Title: Speech at the award of the XVIII King of Spain Prize for Economics
text: 23.03.2022 Address at the presentation of the 18th King of Spain Economics Prize Banco de Espana Pablo Hernandez de Cos Governor Good evening, Your Majesty, Minister, members of the Governing Council of the Banco de Espana, dignitaries, members of the panel, ladies and gentlemen. Firstly, I would like to thank Your Majesty for officiating at todays King of Spain Economics Prize award ceremony. It is an honour for this institution to have Your Majesty here again. As you may know, the King of Spain Economics Prize was established in 1986 by the Fundacion Jose Celma Prieto. I also wish to thank the foundation's president, Javier Celma, for having continued the generous patronage his father began. For this eighteenth edition of the award, the panel, which I had the honour to preside, was made up of alvaro Rodriguez-Bereijo (Deputy Chair), Juan Velarde Fuertes, Jose Ramon alvarez Rendueles, Rodolfo Martin Villa, Jose Luis Feito and Julio Segura. After its deliberations on 8 November last year, the panel decided to award the King of Spain Economics Prize to Professor Manuel Arellano for his outstanding research and teaching. Manuel Arellano is considered one of the worlds most influential economists of recent years in the development of econometric tools. Born in Elda (Alicante) in 1957, he holds a degree from the Universidad de Barcelona and a PhD from the London School of Economics. He began his professional career at the University of Oxford and at the London School of Economics, and has been a professor of econometrics at the Centro de Estudios Monetarios y Financieros (CEMFI) since 1991. Throughout his career, he has been a prolific teacher and researcher, for which he has received a long list of acknowledgements. I shall mention just a few of the most noteworthy ones. Professor Arellano has been editor or co-editor of some of the most prestigious international academic journals, such as the Review of Economic Studies and the Journal of Applied Econometrics. He has been the president of the Econometric Society, the most prestigious international society in the field of economics. He is a member of that society, in addition to being an international honorary member of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences. He has also been president of the European Economic Association and of the Spanish Economic Association, and a member of the Scientific Council of the European Research Council. In 2012 he was awarded the King Jaime I Economics Prize. He is currently Chair of the Scientific and Technical Committee of the Spanish State Research Agency. Professor Arellanos research has centred on the area of microeconometrics. Specifically, he has made a decisive contribution to the development of tools to estimate statistical 1 models using panel data, where records of individuals, households and firms are available over time. The seminal work by Professor Arellano, together with Steven Bond and Olympia Bover, made it possible to develop innovative methods for appropriately processing and harnessing such data. And this has enhanced economists ability to respond more robustly to a diverse range of important economic matters. Included here are employment dynamics, firms productivity, economic growth, changes in income and consumption, and the impact of certain public programmes and policies, to name just a few of their practical applications. These contributions have also become more important over time. Nowadays one of the main pillars for transforming the economy, and society in general, lies precisely in technologys capacity to generate, store and process data. In the 1980s, when Professor Arellano began his research in this field, little panel data were available. But today, they are widely available and used in the vast majority of empirical economics studies. They are also therefore the basis for economic policy decision-making. His publications have had such an impact on all areas of applied economics that he was named Clarivate Citation Laureate in Economics in 2018. Indeed, his 1991 article with Stephen Bond in the Review of Economic Studies presenting a model for estimating dynamic models in the presence of individual heterogeneity, known as the Arellano-Bond estimator, last year became the first publication in history to be cited 10,000 times in the Research Papers in Economics (RePEc) repository. But, aside from his important research work, Professor Arellanos role in furthering economics in recent decades has also included being a real catalyst for new generations of researchers through his methods and teaching. Indeed, one of his books, Panel Data Econometrics (Oxford University Press, 2003), has become one of the main postgraduate econometrics texts at the best universities in the world. In the same vein, he has also carried out noteworthy work supervising PhD theses and mentoring dozens of prestigious researchers currently at institutions across the world (including the Banco de Espana), some of whom are with us here today, either in person or watching via the livestream. I would also like to dedicate a few words to his more personal qualities. Those of us who know Professor Arellano would point out that his humility and altruism surpass even his academic merits. Humility, because he is driven by intellectual curiosity and a desire for learning, rather than by any personal interest in amassing achievements or publications, even though his contributions to economics make them inevitable. And altruism, because he is always ready to listen and give words of encouragement to his colleagues and students, whom he has a genuine interest in helping, even when that means less time to dedicate to his own projects. I mention all this to show his strong personal commitment to excellence in the service of improving society. On more than a few occasions in recent centuries, despite its notable 2 figures, Spanish science has been characterised as lacking the cohesive elements that would make greater success possible through collective effort. Well, Professor Arellano, along with certain other internationally renowned economists, decided in the late 1980s to combine their efforts and dedicate their professional life to making Spain a true centre of global excellence in economics teaching and research. I am referring to CEMFI, the success of which cannot be understood without the work and life-long dedication of Manuel Arellano, under the direction of its first and so far only director, Rafael Repullo, who is also with us today. The impact of this collective effort could be approximated perfectly well by applying the very econometric tools that our prize winner has decisively contributed to developing. But, to be able to fully gauge exactly what it means to Spain to have a centre of excellence of this calibre, it is perhaps still necessary for one of the disciples he has inspired to make another breakthrough in our capacity to extract information from data, like the one made when Professor Arellano developed his methods. Be that as it may, prizes like the one he is receiving today provide public recognition of the scale and significance of his individual contributions and of the collective achievements in which he has participated. Your Majesty, thanking you once again for your presence at this ceremony, it only remains for me, with your permission, to ask the prize winner to step up to receive the 18th King of Spain Economics Prize. 3

Title: Appearance before the Senate Budget Committee
text: Jaime Caruna Governor of the Bank of Spain November 20, 2000 APPEARANCE OF THE GOVERNOR OF THE BANK OF SPAIN, JAIME CARUANA, BEFORE THE SENATE BUDGET COMMITTEE Mr. President, ladies and gentlemen, I am addressing you for the first time, in the hearings prior to the discussion of the General State Budget for 2001, and I do so at a time when the Spanish economy, like most of the economies of the industrialized countries, is in a phase of prosperity and growth that, In our case, it has already lasted for the fourth consecutive year. The macroeconomic stability achieved, the rigour with which the policy of controlling expenditure and reducing the public deficit has been implemented and the favourable expectations of economic agents following our entry into Economic and Monetary Union - in a favourable external context - have allowed the Spanish economy to maintain particularly high rates of economic growth and job creation. which have placed our unemployment rate, according to recent data from the Labour Force Survey, at 13.7%, a figure that has not been reached since 1981 and which should continue to fall in the coming years. In this environment, the objective of budgetary balance is appropriate to the cyclical position of the economy, while it represents an important step forward in achieving the commitments made in the stability programme - the achievement of balance is one year ahead - and represents a historic achievement in consolidating one of the basic pillars of macroeconomic stability. The maintenance of a sound position of public finances in the medium term - a horizon in which a less expansionary context cannot be ruled out and for which further cuts in direct taxation have been advanced - and its sustainability in longer periods - when the ageing of the population determines the need to finance growing public spending - will require continuing to introduce measures that favour the control of expenditure and the increase in fiscal discipline, in line with the announced Budget Stability Law. This favorable environment, which is the one maintained by most international organizations for the world economy in the coming year, is being subjected recently, however, to the incidence of a series of events that are affecting, in a moderate way, the expectations of economic agents, and that if not channeled in the right way could compromise the levels of stability achieved and reduce the growth potential of economies. I am referring, above all, to the sharp rises in oil prices on international markets, which are going on much longer than initially thought and which have placed the price of crude oil above thirty dollars-barrels for several months. So far, the impact of higher energy prices on economic growth rates has been quite limited, but their direct impact on inflation rates is considerable, especially in those economies that are more energy dependent or that are in a more advanced cyclical expansion phase. Along with this factor, and for reasons that may not be entirely alien to it, stock markets around the world have increased their instability, with corrections that, in some cases, have affected household wealth levels and consumer confidence. This is particularly noticeable in the case of the United States economy, but it is also having an impact on European economies, including, as we shall see, ours. The macroeconomic scenario considered by the Bank of Spain for 2001 is very similar to the one incorporated by the Government in the draft budget. Both assume that the rate of growth of the real gross domestic product of the Spanish economy will gradually slow down, reaching growth rates close to 3.5%. This behavior is explained, basically, by the slowdown that national demand is registering, prolonging the trend that has already been observed in the data of recent quarters. On the other hand, the contribution of the net external balance, which has become less negative as exports have recovered the dynamism lost as a result of the international crisis of 1998, will remain at moderate levels in 2001. The slowdown in domestic expenditure in 2000 is mainly explained by the trend in private consumption, although investment in capital goods has also slowed down in its rate of growth. In 2001, private consumption is expected to continue to reduce its rate of change to close to 3%. The factors that determine the slowdown in household consumption expenditure are common to both years and are related to the evolution of both disposable income and household wealth and interest rates. In 2000, disposable income is estimated to be experiencing high growth rates in nominal terms and close to those of previous years; No However, the rising inflation rate has eroded households' purchasing power, inducing a slowdown in their real income. Price increases are expected to moderate by 2001; However, the expected growth in employment, which is still high but at a slower pace, will have an additional restraining effect on income, in real terms. Net interest income is also slowing down, as a result of the rapid increase in consumer indebtedness, which is preferably at variable interest rates. In any case, it is estimated that the household savings rate, after falling substantially in 2000, would tend to stabilize next year. Along with disposable income, there are other determinants that also help explain the slowdown in private consumption in recent years. The wealth gains achieved after the revaluation of financial assets in 1997 and 1998 have been moderating their expansionary effects on spending in 2000, and will continue to do so in 2001; To which should be added the disincentive effect on consumption of the rise in interest rates itself. These same reasons, together with the increase in house prices, affect residential investment in contraction, which, although still considerably high, is also likely to grow less in 2001. The expansionary cycle of the construction sector is being prolonged, however, by the greater growth of public works in recent months. Investment in equipment has also attenuated its high real growth rates in 2000. For next year, its rate of growth is expected to revive, as the financial situation of companies is healthy and their profitability high, which provides an adequate basis for carrying out investment decisions. In addition, the demand outlook underpinning the central forecast scenario for 2001 is also positive and justifies maintaining a high investment rate. However, other types of considerations, such as the profitability of alternative investments abroad, may have induced companies to expand in other markets, making it difficult to assess the effect of this decision on the pace of domestic investment. I believe that the scenario expected for next year is therefore positive: the slowdown in demand, and in particular in consumer spending, would reduce the pressure on prices, and the maintenance of high export growth rates would contribute to a more favourable configuration of final demand, where investment and exports would gain weight compared to consumption; the slowdown in imports, as a result of the lower expected growth rates For demand, it would alleviate the growth experienced by the trade deficit, which will also be helped by the return of import prices towards more moderate growth rates. In this situation, and in view of the resurgence experienced by inflation rates, the single monetary policy implemented for the countries of the euro area has been adopting a stricter tone and has tended to adapt more and more to the requirements of the Spanish economy, and it is expected that it will continue to do so in the future. As is well known, the Eurosystem has been gradually raising interest rates since November 1999, in a context of high economic growth and, especially in the most recent period, deterioration in inflationary expectations, largely induced by the rise in oil prices and the weakness of the euro. The last increase in interest rates took place on 5th October when the Governing Council of the ECB decided to increase its intervention rate by 25 basis points, bringing it to 4.75%. Thus, since November last year, an increase in intervention rates of 225 basis points has accumulated. In any case, even taking this increase into account, real interest rates are still historically low and monetary and financial conditions - determined by the level of both interest rates and the exchange rate - are relatively comfortable. In Spain, monetary and financial conditions have been somewhat more expansionary than in EMU as a whole, reflected in a low level of real interest rates and a fairly strong growth in credit granted to the private sector. In any case, for the macroeconomic scenario that we have defined for next year to become a reality, it is necessary that the macroeconomic stability achieved is not lost and that the efforts made in recent years aimed at containing the prices and costs of the economy, controlling public spending and improving the competitive environment have due continuity. Otherwise, a more negative alternative scenario could be configured, in which the losses in competitiveness that would accumulate would end up affecting the growth rates of exports and investment, reducing the growth potential of the economy and its capacity to create employment. In this sense, the State Budget for 2001 represents a step forward in the line of rigor that it is essential to follow to reduce the resurgence experienced by consumer prices, which, although it has an important transitory component derived from the rise experienced by energy prices, could end up being transferred to other sectors of the economy and entrenched in the expectations of economic agents. At the moment, as you all know, the annual growth rate of the CPI - both the national and harmonised index - is 4%, much higher than expected, since the price of oil has not experienced the slowdown that most analysts expected for the central months of this year. This rate is also influenced by other elements, such as seasonal increases in the prices of some foods or those that, in a context of strong demand growth, have experienced the prices of some services. On numerous occasions the Bank of Spain has drawn attention to the danger posed by the fact that, in the face of a transitory shock of external origin, economic agents - companies and workers - try to avoid the loss of real income that derives from it through increases in margins and wage increases, since this would mean a permanent deterioration of the inflationary situation. with the consequent deterioration of competitiveness and reduction of the pace of economic growth and job creation. In such cases, it was advisable to use, as a reference point for income revisions, a CPI measure from which precisely those transitory elements that had to be avoided were excluded. For next year it is expected that the rate of increase of the CPI will be reduced substantially, and this is reflected in the statistical forecasting models commonly used. The economic reasons for the improvement in the inflationary outlook are diverse: a slowdown in domestic demand, which, as we have seen, will adjust its rate of growth to that of most EU countries; the achievement of the budgetary balance planned for next year and the increasingly tight tone of the area's monetary policy, which shape a set of macroeconomic policies more in line with the needs of the Spanish economy; and, finally, the forecasts on the evolution of the price of crude oil, which, although they continue to place it above 25 dollars-barrel, suppose, in terms of variation rates, a significant slowdown that will be incorporated into the consumer price indices. It also seems reasonable that the foreseeable scenario for the euro values favours the recovery of the European currency, more in line with its fundamentals. Taking into account all these factors, it is difficult to say how far the slowdown in the CPI will go next year, but what is certain is that it will depend, to a large extent, on how economic agents react to the increases, in principle transitory, that the CPI has experienced in the current year. The decisions of private economic operators for the next financial year should therefore not be made with a view to the past. In this sense, that the Government has proposed a CPI growth rate of 2%, not as a forecast, but as a reference for agents Consider it when reviewing their prices and wages, thus determining the growth of the nominal magnitudes of the economy, it seems to me a wise decision. The 2%, as is well known, is the upper inflation threshold for determining the stability of euro area economies, and we must be careful not to depart from it. It makes no sense that, after the effort made by the Spanish economy - companies and workers - to achieve the nominal stability typical of the countries in the area in which we have integrated, we lose the many benefits that have been derived, and continue to be derived, in terms of economic growth and job creation. In the current circumstances, the past is a bad guide to predicting the future, as the inflation rate will tend to flex. The bad thing would be if the reduction in inflation were made difficult by an indication of incomes with past inflation or by a generalized effort to transmit to final prices any increase in costs. That is how I see, ladies and gentlemen, the panorama in which the Spanish economy will develop in the coming year and in which the assessment of the General State Budgets that you have to carry out is framed. I am at your disposal to answer any questions you may have in this regard. Thanks a lot.
text_original: Jaime Caruna Gobernador del Banco de Espaa 20 de Noviembre de 2000 COMPARECENCIA DEL GOBERNADOR DEL BANCO DE ESPAA, JAIME CARUANA, ANTE LA COMISIN DE PRESUPUESTOS DEL SENADO Sr. Presidente, Seoras: Me dirijo por primera vez a ustedes, dentro de las comparecencias previas a la discusin de los Presupuestos Generales del Estado para el ao 2001, y lo hago en un momento en el que la economa espaola, lo mismo que la mayora de las economas de los pases industrializados, se encuentra en una fase de prosperidad y crecimiento que, en nuestro caso, se prolonga ya por cuarto ao consecutivo. La estabilidad macroeconmica alcanzada, el rigor con el que se ha instrumentado la poltica de control del gasto y reduccin del dficit pblico y las expectativas favorables de los agentes econmicos tras nuestra entrada en la Unin Econmica y Monetaria -en un contexto exterior favorable-, han permitido que la economa espaola mantenga ritmos de crecimiento econmico y de creacin de empleo particularmente elevados, que han situado nuestra tasa de paro, segn los datos recientes de la Encuesta de Poblacin Activa, en el 13,7%, un registro que no se alcanzaba desde 1981 y que debe seguir reducindose en los prximos ejercicios. En este entorno, el objetivo de equilibrio presupuestario resulta adecuado a la posicin cclica de la economa, al tiempo que supone un avance importante en la consecucin de los compromisos contrados en el programa de estabilidad -se adelanta un ao la consecucin del equilibrio- y supone un logro histrico en la consolidacin de uno de los pilares bsicos de la estabilidad macroeconmica. El mantenimiento de una posicin saneada de las finanzas pblicas en el medio plazo -horizonte en el que no se puede descartar un contexto menos expansivo y para el que se han avanzado nuevos recortes en la imposicin directa- y su sostenibilidad en perodos ms dilatados -cuando el envejecimiento de la poblacin determine la necesidad de financiar un gasto pblico creciente- requerirn continuar introduciendo medidas que favorezcan el control del gasto y el aumento de la disciplina fiscal, en lnea con la anunciada Ley de Estabilidad Presupuestaria. Este entorno favorable, que es el que mantienen la mayora de los organismos internacionales para la economa mundial en el prximo ao, se est viendo sometido recientemente, sin embargo, a la incidencia de una serie de acontecimientos que estn afectando, de forma moderada, a las expectativas de los agentes econmicos, y que de no encauzarse de la manera adecuada podran comprometer los niveles de estabilidad alcanzados y reducir el potencial de crecimiento de las economas. Me refiero, sobre todo, a las fuertes alzas experimentadas por los precios del petrleo en los mercados internacionales, que se estn prolongando mucho ms de lo que en un primer momento se haba pensado y que han situado el precio del crudo por encima de los treinta dlares-barril desde hace varios meses. Hasta el momento, la incidencia de los mayores precios energticos sobre los ritmos de crecimiento econmico ha sido bastante limitada, pero su impacto directo sobre las tasas de inflacin est siendo considerable, sobre todo en aquellas economas que tienen una mayor dependencia energtica o que se encuentran en una fase de expansin cclica ms avanzada. Junto con este factor, y por razones que posiblemente no le son del todo ajenas, los mercados burstiles de todo el mundo han aumentado su inestabilidad, habindose registrado correcciones que, en algunos casos, han afectado a los niveles de riqueza de las familias y a la confianza de los consumidores. Este hecho est siendo especialmente notable en el caso de la economa de los Estados Unidos, pero est incidiendo tambin en las economas europeas, entre ellas, como ahora veremos, en la nuestra. El escenario macroeconmico que considera el Banco de Espaa para el ao 2001 es muy similaral incorporado por el Gobierno en el proyecto de presupuestos. Ambos suponen que el ritmo de crecimiento del producto interior bruto real de la economa espaola ir desacelerndose paulatinamente, hasta alcanzar tasas de avance prximas al 3,5%. Este comportamiento se explica, bsicamente, por la desaceleracin que est registrando la demanda nacional, prolongando la tendencia que ya se viene observando en los datos de los ltimos trimestres. Por el contrario, la aportacin del saldo neto exterior, que se ha hecho menos negativa a medida que las exportaciones han ido recuperando el dinamismo perdido a raz de la crisis internacional de 1998, se mantendr en cotas moderadas en el ao 2001. La desaceleracin del gasto interior en el ao 2000 se explica, sobre todo, por el comportamiento del consumo privado, aunque tambin la inversin en bienes de equipo ha perdido intensidad en su ritmo de avance. En el ao 2001 se prev que el consumo privado siga reduciendo su tasa de variacin, hasta situarla en cotas prximas al 3%. Los factores que determinan la desaceleracin del gasto de consumo de las familias son comunes a ambos aos y estn relacionados con la evolucin tanto de la renta disponible como de la riqueza de los hogares y los tipos de inters. En el ao 2000 se estima que la renta disponible, en trminos nominales, est experimentando tasas de crecimiento elevadas y prximas a las de los aos anteriores; no obstante, el aumento de la tasa de inflacin ha erosionado el poder de compra de los hogares, induciendo una desaceleracin en su renta real. Para el ao 2001 se espera que los incrementos de precios se moderen; no obstante, el crecimiento previsto para el empleo, todava elevado, pero a ritmo menor, ejercer un efecto de contencin adicional sobre la renta, en trminos reales. Tambin las rentas netas por intereses estn desacelerndose, como consecuencia del rpido aumento que ha experimentado el endeudamiento de los consumidores, que es, preferentemente, a tipo de inters variable. En cualquier caso, se estima que la tasa de ahorro de las familias, tras reducirse sustancialmente en el ao 2000, tendera estabilizarse el prximo ao. Junto con la renta disponible existen otros determinantes que contribuyen tambin a explicar el perfil de desaceleracin del consumo privado en estos aos. Las ganancias de riqueza que se alcanzaron tras la revalorizacin de los activos financieros en 1997 y 1998 han ido moderando sus efectos expansivos sobre el gasto en el ao 2000, y lo seguirn haciendo en el 2001; a lo que habra que aadir el efecto desincentivador que ejerce sobre el consumo la propia subida de los tipos de inters. Estas mismas razones, junto con el aumento experimentado por los precios de la vivienda, afectan contractivamente a la inversin residencial, que, aunque con tasas aun considerablemente elevadas, tambin tendera crecer menos en el ao 2001. El ciclo expansivo del sector de la construccin se est viendo prolongado, no obstante, por el mayor crecimiento de la obra pblica en los ltimos meses. Tambin la inversin en equipo ha atenuado sus altas tasas de crecimiento real en el ao 2000. Para el prximo ao se espera que vuelva a reavivarse su ritmo de avance, ya que la situacin financiera de las empresas es saneada y su rentabilidad elevada, lo que proporciona un fundamento adecuado para llevara cabo decisiones de inversin. Adems, las perspectivas de demanda que sustentan el escenario central de previsin para el ao 2001 tambin son positivas y justifican el mantenimiento de un ritmo inversor elevado. No obstante, otro tipo de consideraciones, como la rentabilidad de inversiones alternativas en el exterior, pueden haber inducido a las empresas a expandirse en otros mercados, siendo difcil valorar el efecto de esta decisin sobre el ritmo de inversin domstica. Creo que el escenario que se espera para el prximo ao es, por tanto, positivo: la desaceleracin de la demanda, y en particular del gasto de consumo, permitira reducir la presin sobre los precios, y el mantenimiento de tasas elevadas de crecimiento de la exportacin contribuira a una configuracin de la demanda final ms favorable, donde la inversin y la exportacin ganaran peso en comparacin con el consumo; la desaceleracin de las importaciones, como consecuencia de los menores ritmos de crecimiento esperados para la demanda, aliviara, por su parte, el crecimiento que ha experimentado el dficit comercial, a lo que tambin colaborar el retorno de los precios de importacin hacia tasas de crecimiento ms moderadas. En esta situacin, y ante el rebrote experimentado por las tasas de inflacin, la poltica monetaria nica instrumentada para los pases de la zona del euro ha ido adoptando un tono ms estricto y ha tendido a acomodarse cada vez ms a los requerimientos de la economa espaola, y as se espera que lo siga haciendo en el futuro. Como es bien sabido, el Eurosistema ha venido subiendo gradualmente los tipos de inters desde noviembre de 1999, en un contexto de elevado crecimiento econmico y, sobre todo en el perodo ms reciente, de deterioro de las expectativas inflacionistas, inducido en buena medida por el ascenso del precio del petrleo y por la debilidad del euro. El ltimo aumento de los tipos de inters tuvo lugar el 5 de octubre, cuando el Consejo de Gobierno del BCE decidi incrementar su tipo de intervencin por una cuanta de 25 puntos bsicos, con lo que este se sita actualmente en el 4,75%. De esta forma, desde noviembre del ao pasado se acumula una subida de los tipos de intervencin de 225 puntos bsicos. En cualquier caso, aun teniendo en cuenta este incremento, los tipos de inters reales muestran todava unos niveles histricamente bajos y las condiciones monetarias y financieras -determinadas por el nivel, tanto de los tipos de inters como del tipo de cambio- resultan relativamente holgadas. En Espaa, las condiciones monetarias y financieras vienen siendo algo ms expansivas que en el conjunto de la UEM, lo que se ha reflejado en un bajo nivel de los tipos de inters reales y en un crecimiento bastante intenso del crdito concedido al sector privado. En cualquier caso, para que el escenario macroeconmico que hemos definido para el prximo ao se haga realidad es necesario que no se pierda la estabilidad macroeconmica alcanzada y que los esfuerzos realizados en estos ltimos aos encaminados a la contencin de los precios y costes de la economa, al control del gasto pblico y a la mejora del entorno competitivo tengan la debida continuidad. De no ser as, podra configurarse un escenario alternativo ms negativo, en el que las prdidas de competitividad que se iran acumulando terminaran por afectar a las tasas de crecimiento de las exportaciones y de la inversin, disminuyendo el potencial de crecimiento de la economa y su capacidad para crear empleo. En este sentido, el Presupuesto del Estado para el ao 2001 supone un paso adelante en la lnea de rigor que resulta imprescindible seguir para reducir el rebrote experimentado por los precios de consumo, que, aunque tiene un componente transitorio importante derivado del alza experimentada por los precios energticos, podra terminar trasladndose a otros sectores de la economa y enquistarse en las expectativas de los agentes econmicos. En este momento, como todos ustedes saben, la tasa de crecimiento interanual del IPC -tanto delndice nacional como del armonizado- es del 4%, muy superior a la que se esperaba, ya que el precio del petrleo no ha experimentado la desaceleracin que prevean la mayora de los analistas para los meses centrales de este ao. En esta tasa influyen tambin otros elementos, como las alzas estacionales de los precios de algunos alimentos o las que, en un contexto de fuerte crecimiento de la demanda, han experimentado los precios de algunos servicios. En numerosas ocasiones se ha llamado la atencin desde el Banco de Espaa sobre el peligro que supone el que, ante un shock transitorio de origen externo, los agentes econmicos -empresas y trabajadores- traten de eludir la prdida de renta real que de l se deriva mediante aumentos de mrgenes e incrementos salariales, ya que ello supondra un deterioro permanente de la situacin inflacionista, con el consiguiente deterioro de la competitividad y reduccin del ritmo de crecimiento econmico y de creacin de empleo. Se aconsejaba, en esos casos, la posibilidad de utilizar, como punto de referencia para las revisiones de rentas, una medida del IPC de la que se excluyeran, precisamente, esos elementos transitorios que haba que procurar no perpetuar. Para el prximo ao se espera que el ritmo de aumento del IPC se reduzca de manera sustancial, y as lo recogen los modelos estadsticos de previsin utilizados habitualmente. Las razones econmicas que avalan la mejora en el panorama inflacionista son de diversa ndole: desaceleracin de la demanda interna, que, como hemos visto, ir acomodando su tasa de avance a la de la mayora de los pases de la UE; el logro del equilibrio presupuestario previsto para el prximo ejercicio y el tono cada vez ms estricto de la poltica monetaria de la zona, que configuran un conjunto de polticas macroeconmicas ms acorde con las necesidades de la economa espaola; y, por ltimo, las previsiones sobre la evolucin del precio del crudo, que, aunque lo siguen situando por encima de los 25 dlares-barril, suponen, en trminos de tasas de variacin, una importante desaceleracin que se ir incorporando en losndices de precios de consumo. Tambin parece razonable que el escenario previsible para la cotizacin del euro favorezca la recuperacin de la moneda europea, ms en lnea con sus fundamentos. Teniendo en cuenta todos estos factores, es difcil decir hasta dnde llegar la desaceleracin del IPC el prximo ao, pero, lo que es seguro, es que depender, en gran medida, de cmo reaccionen los agentes econmicos ante los aumentos, en principio transitorios, que ha experimentado el IPC en el ao actual. Las decisiones de los agentes econmicos privados de cara al prximo ejercicio no deben realizarse, por tanto, mirando hacia el pasado. En este sentido, que el Gobierno haya planteado una tasa de crecimiento del IPC del 2%, no como una previsin, sino como una referencia para que los agentes econmicos la tengan en cuenta en el momento de revisar sus precios y salarios, determinando as el crecimiento de las magnitudes nominales de la economa, me parece una decisin acertada. El 2%, como es bien conocido, es la cota que marca el umbral superior de inflacin para determinar la estabilidad de las economas de la zona del euro y debemos procurar no apartarnos de ella. No tiene sentido que, despus del esfuerzo que ha realizado la economa espaola -las empresas y los trabajadores- para alcanzar la estabilidad nominal propia de los pases del rea en la que nos hemos integrado, perdamos los muchos beneficios que de ello se han derivado, y siguen derivndose, en trminos de crecimiento econmico y creacin de empleo. En las circunstancias actuales, el pasado es una mala gua para predecir el futuro, pues la tasa de inflacin tender a flexionar. Lo malo sera que la reduccin de la inflacin se viera dificultada por una indiciacin de las rentas con la inflacin pasada o por un esfuerzo generalizado de transmitir a los precios finales cualquier encarecimiento de costes. Ases como veo, Seoras, el panorama en el que se desenvolver la economa espaola en el prximo ao y en el que se enmarca la valoracin de los Presupuestos Generales del Estado que sus Seoras tienen que realizar. Estoy a su disposicin para responder a cualquier pregunta que a este respecto quieran realizarme. Muchas gracias.

Title: Closing speech at the "Euro 2002" conference
text: Jaime Caruna Governor of the Bank of Spain April 4, 2001 EURO 2002 CONFERENCE. CLOSING SPEECH BY JAIME CARUANA, GOVERNOR OF THE BANK OF SPAIN Ladies and gentlemen At the close of this conference on the introduction of the euro that the Banco de Espa96a has organised within the framework of the Euro 2002 Information Campaign, I would like to sincerely thank all the speakers and attendees for their contributions, which are very valuable in this final stretch of the process that will lead, in less than nine months' time. in the circulation of the new euro banknotes and coins. The euro has been our currency since 1-January-99. Its beneficial effects both through greater economic stability, which facilitates sustained growth, and the elimination of barriers and uncertainties, which enhance the efficiency and integration of markets, are already a reality. However, we still have an important phase: the physical replacement of peseta banknotes and coins by euro-denominated notes and coins. The replacement of twelve national currencies by a single currency, the euro, is undoubtedly one of the biggest logistical challenges we have ever faced in Spain and the rest of the euro area. In a short period of time, the twelve countries that make up the euro area must produce 16 billion banknotes and 50 billion pieces of currency. To illustrate the magnitude of the task, it is enough to remember that, placed side by side, these banknotes are equivalent to five times the distance separating the Earth from the Moon, or that the coins to be produced in Spain would cover the surface of a football stadium up to a height of twenty meters. Fortunately, today we can say that the production of these billions of banknotes and coins is proceeding satisfactorily overall throughout the euro area, meeting the deadlines. In the case of Spain, the F87brica Nacional de Moneda y Timbre has already produced 44% of the total of 1,924 million euro banknotes that correspond to us, that is, 850 million. And, as for the coins, 80% is already produced, so our Factory is scrupulously complying with the planned programming. But if it is complicated to produce this volume of banknotes and coins, it is also difficult to get them to every corner of Spain. To ensure smooth distribution, the Bank of Spain has already begun to move the thousands of tons of euro banknotes and coins from central warehouses to each of its branches in all provinces. As of September 1, it will be distributed to financial institutions. This operation is of paramount importance for the successful launch of the euro. The role of financial institutions is all the more important since they will in turn be the ones who, through specific agreements, distribute banknotes and coins to the large-scale distribution sector, small businesses and other sectors that need to have a sufficient amount of euros to serve their customers from 1 January 2002. I would like to make special mention of the spirit of collaboration that we have found at all times in the Spanish financial sector, which has been able to understand the magnitude of this event and live up to what is expected of it. I would also like to recall the excellent preparation and success of the financial system in its conversion to the euro in 1999. However, the introduction of the euro is not a challenge that can be limited to certain economic sectors, but it is a task that involves the whole of Spanish society, and that is why I would also like to appeal to all citizens to face it with confidence, with full awareness of the importance of this historic step. The success of the introduction of the euro in our daily lives also depends on the attitude of each of us as consumers and as users of the new currency. That is why I would like to ask from here for the collaboration of citizens with initiatives and attitudes that can help speed up the process of introducing the euro and the correlative withdrawal of pesetas. An example of these initiatives can be to get rid of the coins that almost all of us accumulate at home in advance. Going with the contents of the domestic piggy banks to our financial institution in January 2002 would only complicate the most critical moments of the launch of the new currency. On the other hand, entering these coins into the entity before the end of 2001 does not entail any detriment to the citizen and nevertheless contributes very positively to the streamlining of the process. The same can be said of maintaining a positive attitude towards the redenomination of bank accounts from pesetas to euros, which financial institutions will carry out from September 15, according to the agreement signed by the Banking Associations with the Ministry of Economy and the Bank of Spain. This is not just a necessary measure to facilitate the adaptation of customer accounts, but it will be an excellent way for customers to gradually and progressively become familiar with the new magnitudes in euros. It is also very important that the media continue their reporting, which is essential to bring society the knowledge it needs, and I ask you to continue to intensify your outreach as we approach the key date in this important process. For its part, the Bank of Spain will put all the means at its disposal to ensure that this transition is as smooth as possible for citizens. Our goal is that all Spaniards are duly informed about the appearance of what will be their banknotes and coins from next January 1, about the security elements that will distinguish an authentic banknote from one that is not and about the process of its introduction. To this end, we are participating very actively in the Euro 2002 communication campaign launched by the European Central Bank and the twelve national central banks that make up the Eurosystem. Campaign that complements and coordinates with those carried out by the national governments of the different countries. To date and in our country, more than 30 million leaflets have already been produced and are being distributed to citizens and more than 600,000 information posters are being placed in numerous points of public attention, all with the invaluable help of the more than 200 agencies and public institutions, associations and companies that are actively collaborating in the dissemination of this information to society, To whom I take this opportunity to sincerely thank them for their enthusiasm and effort. In addition to these generalized information actions, we are developing actions aimed at certain groups, such as the elderly, immigrants, the rural population and children and young people. For the latter, in particular and through Collaboration Agreements with the Autonomous Communities and Cities, which have shown extraordinary sensitivity to address different joint actions with the Bank of Spain, training material will be sent to all schools for the organization of didactic days, such as videos, teacher guides and posters, also giving each student a basic informative piece, which means just over 5 million copies. The positive attitude and spirit of cooperation of these Territorial Public Administrations has made it possible to undertake actions of enormous magnitude, for which I am deeply grateful. It is also important to highlight the training program of the Bank of Spain aimed at professionals who must have a good knowledge of the security elements of the new currency, such as Security Forces, ATMs and dependents, or groups that They have greater difficulties in learning it, such as people with visual impairments. This program, which has the very important collaboration of the National Mint and Stamp, will allow us to train more than 1000 trainers who will then transmit their knowledge to other people especially interested, for their professional work, in knowing the security elements. The Bank of Spain, in addition, has a special concern to avoid that the transition to the fiat euro can serve as an excuse for price increases. The substitution of prices in pesetas by prices in euros and the appearance of decimals, can be a temptation for those who intend an upward rounding of their rates. I trust that Spanish entrepreneurs are aware of the importance of the process and that the new prices will be another element of competition between companies. I also hope that consumers will penalise such behaviour and favour those companies and products that are committed to principles such as conversion safety, consumer assistance and advice, etc. Principles for trade that were included in the Code of Good Practice. It is obvious that, in this matter, all public administrations must follow an exemplary conduct, rigorously applying the rules of conversion and rounding, so that there are no artificial increases in the prices and tariffs that apply to all concepts of income within the scope of their respective competences. This will of course be done by the Bank of Spain itself in all the rates and tariffs it applies in its operations and, within the scope of its competences, it will monitor that credit institutions comply with the established conversion rules and will take an active position in the claims of citizens who denounce practices that may be considered abusive. I would like to end these closing remarks of the conference with a twofold message of confidence and attention. Confidence because the process of introducing euro banknotes and coins has been carefully planned and, despite its undoubted complexity, is being rigorously complied with. Citizens can therefore feel reassured At the same time, however, it is our duty to remind all economic operators that, with 272 days to go before the euro arrives, there is no time to lose in making the necessary adaptations. This is a particularly relevant message for all those small and medium-sized companies that, according to opinion studies, have preferred to leave for the end the internal changes forced by the currency exchange. For them, our message is clear: adapting in advance has practical advantages, while waiting until the last moment means taking unnecessary economic risks. And there is no doubt that companies that prepare in advance will be rewarded by the market. Ladies and gentlemen: At this historic moment for Spain and for Europe, we are all obliged to make our contribution, so that the last phase of the birth of the euro is as positive as the successive stages covered since the Delors Group laid the foundations for what economic and monetary union was to be in 1989. agreed in the Maastricht Treaty in 1992. Ten years later, the physical introduction of our common currency is the best symbol of the gradual achievements of half a century of European integration. The Banco de Espa96a, as well as the European Central Bank and the other national central banks of the Eurosystem, will do our best to ensure that, on 1 January 2002, 300 million Europeans greet the euro in the conviction that the phrase we have coined as the slogan of the campaign "The euro, our currency", is finally a tangible reality. Thanks a lot.

DISCURSO DE CLAUSURA PRONUNCIADO POR JAIME CARUANA, GOBERNADOR DEL BANCO DE ESPAA Seoras y Seores, Al clausurar esta conferencia sobre la introduccin del euro que el Banco de Espaa ha organizado en el marco de la Campaa de Informacin Euro 2002, quisiera agradecer muy sinceramente a todos los ponentes y asistentes sus aportaciones, que resultan muy valiosas en esta recta final del proceso que desembocar, dentro ya de menos de nueve meses, en la puesta en circulacin de los nuevos billetes y monedas en euros. Sus efectos beneficiosos tanto a travs de una mayor estabilidad econmica, que facilita el crecimiento sostenido, como la eliminacin de barreras e incertidumbres, que potencian la eficiencia e integracin de los mercados, son ya una realidad. Sin embargo, nos queda una fase importante: la sustitucin fsica de los billetes y monedas en pesetas por los billetes y monedas denominados en euros. En un plazo corto de tiempo, los doce pases que integramos la zona del euro debemos producir 16.000 millones de billetes y 50.000 millones de piezas de moneda. El papel de las entidades financieras es tanto ms importante cuanto que ellas sern a su vez las que, mediante acuerdos especficos, procedan al reparto de billetes y monedas al sector de la gran distribucin, al pequeo comercio y a otros sectores que necesitan contar con una cantidad suficiente de euros para atender a sus clientes a partir del 1 de enero de 2002. Quiero hacer aqu una mencin especial al espritu de colaboracin que hemos encontrado en todo momento en el sector financiero espaol, que ha sabido comprender la magnitud de este acontecimiento y estar a la altura de lo que se espera de l. Tambin quiero recordar la excelente preparacin y xito del sistema financiero en su conversin al euro en 1999. Sin embargo, la puesta en circulacin del euro no es un reto que se pueda circunscribir a determinados sectores econmicos, sino que es una tarea que implica a toda la sociedad espaola, y por eso quiero hacer tambin un llamamiento al conjunto de los ciudadanos para que la afronten con confianza, con plena conciencia de la importancia de este paso histrico. El xito de la implantacin del euro en nuestras vidas cotidianas depende tambin de la actitud de cada uno de nosotros como consumidores y como usuarios de la nueva moneda. Por eso me gustara pedir desde aqu la colaboracin de los ciudadanos con iniciativas y actitudes que pueden ayudar a agilizar el proceso de introduccin del euro y el correlativo de retirada de pesetas. Un ejemplo de estas iniciativas puede ser el desprendernos anticipadamente de las monedas que casi todos acumulamos en casa. Acudir con el contenido de las huchas domsticas a nuestra entidad financiera en enero de 2002 no hara ms que complicar los momentos ms crticos del lanzamiento de la nueva moneda. En cambio, ingresar esas monedas en la entidad antes de la finalizacin del ao 2001, no supone ningn perjuicio para el ciudadano y sin embargo contribuye muy positivamente a la agilizacin del proceso. Otro tanto se puede decir de mantener una actitud positiva ante la redenominacin de cuentas bancarias de pesetas a euros, que las entidades financieras van a llevar a cabo a partir del 15 de septiembre, segn el acuerdo firmado por las Asociaciones Bancarias con el Ministerio de Economa y el Banco de Espaa. No slo se trata de una medida necesaria para facilitar la adaptacin de las cuentas de los clientes, sino que ser una excelente manera de que stos se familiaricen de forma gradual y progresiva con las nuevas magnitudes en euros. Tambin es muy importante que los medios de comunicacin continuen su labor informativa, que es imprescindible para hacer llegar a la sociedad los conocimientos que sta necesita, por lo que les pido que sigan intensificando su labor de difusin a medida que nos vamos acercando a la fecha clave de este importante proceso. Para ello, estamos participando muy activamente en la campaa de comunicacin Euro 2002 lanzada por el Banco Central Europeo y los doce bancos centrales nacionales que componen el Eurosistema. La actitud positiva y el espritu de cooperacin de estas Administraciones Pblicas Territoriales ha hecho posible acometer acciones de enorme envergadura, por lo que les estoy profundamente agradecido. Este programa, que cuenta con la importantsima colaboracin de la Fbrica Nacional de Moneda y Timbre, nos permitir formar a ms de 1000 formadores que despus transmitirn sus conocimientos a otras personas especialmente interesadas, por su quehacer profesional, en conocer los elementos de seguridad. El Banco de Espaa, adems, tiene una especial preocupacin por evitar que la transicin al euro fiduciario pueda servir de excusa para incrementos de precios. Es obvio que, en este asunto, todas las Administraciones Pblicas deben seguir una conducta ejemplar, aplicando con rigor las normas de conversin y de redondeo, de manera que no se produzcan incrementos artificiales en los precios y tarifas que aplican a todos los conceptos de ingresos en el mbito de sus respectivas competencias. As lo har por supuesto el propio Banco de Espaa en todas las tasas y tarifas que aplica en sus operaciones y, en el mbito de sus competencias, vigilar que las entidades de crdito se ajusten a las normas de conversin establecidas y tomar una postura activa en las reclamaciones de ciudadanos que denuncien practicas que puedan considerarse abusivas. Quiero terminar estas palabras de clausura de la conferencia con un doble mensaje de confianza y de atencin. Confianza porque el proceso de introduccin de los billetes y monedas en euros ha sido minuciosamente programado y, a pesar de su indudable complejidad, est siendo rigurosamente cumplido. Para ellas nuestro mensaje es claro: adaptarse con antelacin tiene ventajas prcticas, mientras que esperar hasta el ltimo momento supone correr riesgos econmicos innecesarios. Y no cabe duda de que las empresas que se preparen con antelacin sern recompensadas por el mercado. Seoras y seores: En este momento histrico para Espaa y para Europa, todos estamos obligados a hacer nuestra aportacin, para que la ltima fase del alumbramiento del euro sea tan positiva como lo han sido hasta ahora las sucesivas etapas cubiertas desde que, en 1989, el grupo Delors sent las bases de lo que haba de ser la unin econmica y monetaria, acordada en el Tratado de Maastricht en 1992. Diez aos despus, la introduccin fsica de nuestra moneda comn es el mejor smbolo de los paulatinos logros alcanzados en medio siglo de integracin europea. Desde el Banco de Espaa, como desde el Banco Central Europeo y los dems bancos centrales nacionales del Eurosistema, dedicaremos nuestros mejores esfuerzos para lograr que, el 1 de enero de 2002, 300 millones de europeos saluden al euro con la conviccin de que la frase que hemos acuado como lema de la campaa "El euro, nuestra moneda", es por fin una realidad tangible. Title: Remarks at the presentation of the Germn Berncer Award
text: Jaime Caruna Governor of the Bank of Spain April 6, 2001 REMARKS BY THE GOVERNOR OF THE BANK OF SPAIN, JAIME CARUANA, AT THE PRESENTATION OF THE GERMe7N BERNe7CER AWARD My first words must be to congratulate those who have promoted the Germ87n Bern87cer Prize in order to reward the best work of monetary or banking research in the euro area. The creation of a prize of these characteristics and with the name of one of our economists most linked to the birth of monetary analysis in Spain is an initiative at the height of the radically new reality of the European Economic and Monetary Union, to which the ECB observatory rightly dedicates all its activity. The opportunity to choose the figure of Germ87n Bern87cer to name this distinction is also supported by his relevant role as deputy director of the then newly created Research Service of the Bank of Spain, which has been making such important contributions to the analysis of the Spanish economy and monetary policy. Germ87n Bern87cer, who was born in Alicante in 1883, moved to Madrid to fill the vacancy left by Jos8e Larraz as deputy director of the Research Service of the Bank of Spain in 1931. Together with Olegario Fern87ndez-Ba96os, he would form the tandem that directed the research department of the issuing bank during a period in which the tasks of economic advice and analysis and the promotion of research work began to mark the path of what, over the years, would be hallmarks of this institution. As you will recall, the birth of the Research Service in 1930 was closely linked to the need for an institution in which to prepare reports and to promote studies aimed at advising the authorities of the Bank and the Ministry on how to deal with the protracted aftermath of the international crisis and the problems related to the stability of the peseta exchange rate. The prestige that Germ87n Bern87cer had achieved from his chair at the Higher School of Commerce of Alicante and his deep knowledge of monetary issues -acquired during his training stage in Germany, where he came into contact with the work of Wicksell- they made him the ideal person to, together with Fern87ndez-Ba96os -with a much more statistical and quantitative training-, launch a study center with few precedents, at that time, in our country. There are numerous works that accredit the importance of Bern87cer's work, from the so-called: Interest of capital. The problem of its origins, until, already from its position in the Research Service, The rhythm of the Spanish economic crisis in relation to the world one, which raises with enormous acuteness the difficulties of forecasting and economic analysis in a world subject to intense cyclical fluctuations. The proposal of a set of indicators that would allow us to anticipate cyclical changes in the economy and its denomination as "economic barometers", we must admit that it seems to be taken from the pages of some economic magazine or newspaper of today. But where Bern87cer's interest in the economic problems of the moment is best reflected is in his Collection of chronicles of the weekly Bulletin and in the quarterly reports of the situation published by the Research Service with the title: Economic-financial situation of Spain. Bernacer's analysis of the economic problems of those turbulent years remains enormously current, as evidenced by the following quote: "The action and reaction between the commodity and stock markets plays an important role in the mechanics of the economic fluctuations of the economy." You will not be able to deny that this brief sentence is still fully valid and lucid almost seventy years later. But not only does the choice of the economist who gives name to the newly established prize seem right to me. It is also important to devote it to research on monetary and banking issues within EMU. There is no doubt today that the proper conduct of monetary policy increasingly requires the use of sophisticated analytical tools that are developed inside and outside the realm of central banks. In this way, it is pertinent to promote, as this award intends to do, quality research in this field. This need is particularly pressing when it comes to tackling a project of the magnitude and complexity of Economic and Monetary Union, which involves the application of a single monetary policy in a group of nations that maintain many particular features and that remain sovereign in the management of the other instruments of economic policy. even if it is within certain rules and coordination mechanisms that seek to ensure common objectives. To adequately address all these challenges, all members of the Eurosystem, the ECB and the national central banks devote a great deal of effort to analysis and research in order to adequately inform the monetary policy strategy and the adoption of appropriate decisions. To address all these tasks, the Eurosystem as a whole needs to establish links with academia from which significant improvements can certainly be made for the effective performance of its role. This objective is reflected in numerous initiatives, both by the ECB and the national central banks, for dialogue and cooperation with universities and research centres and is part of the Eurosystem's communication policy. This occasion seems to me to be particularly propitious to address this important subject, to which I would like to devote the second part of my speech. Together with the definition of the objectives pursued and the establishment of the mechanisms and principles on which the decision-making process is articulated, communication policy constitutes one of the basic elements on which the monetary policy strategy of most central banks is based and, in particular, that of the Eurosystem. In our case, there are at least two powerful reasons why the role played by communication policy should become particularly relevant. Firstly, it should be recalled that the Eurosystem enjoys, in the exercise of its tasks, complete independence from other public authorities; The ultimate objective of which is, as you are no doubt aware, to prevent the exercise of monetary policy from being affected by the political cycle, so that its ability to achieve the priority objective of maintaining price stability may be impaired. However, this independence requires, as a logical counterpart, the Eurosystem's accountability for its activities both to the legitimate representatives of society and to public opinion. Secondly, the effectiveness of monetary policy is often conditioned by the way in which economic agents interpret the decisions taken by the responsible central bank. In this sense, the design of a fluid communication policy, which guarantees an adequate degree of transparency, is an indispensable requirement to reduce the risk of forming erroneous expectations that hinder the normal development of the process of transmission of central bank shares to the economy as a whole, thus reducing the effectiveness of monetary policy. It is important, however, to point out that the economic theory and practice of the most successful central banks in meeting their objectives shows that the quality of communication is much more important than its intensity. It is simply inappropriate to base - as has sometimes been done - the assessment of the adequacy of a given communication policy on the mere drawing up of the list of those elements of which A central bank does not report. I believe, on the contrary, that any rigorous analysis of this question must begin with a detailed study of the specific procedures used to communicate and explain to the markets and the general public the objectives pursued and the decisions taken, and, from this point, to ask, in any case, the real added value derived from the adoption of complementary information instruments or procedures. In the case of the Eurosystem, the Treaty on European Union contains in its articles a series of specific accountability requirements. Thus, the ECB is obliged to send an annual report to the European Parliament, the European Council and the Commission and to report to them quarterly on its activities, as well as to publish, on a weekly basis, its consolidated balance sheet. Members of the Executive Board of the ECB must also appear regularly before the various committees of the European Parliament. Finally, the President of ECOFIN has the opportunity to attend meetings of the Governing Council of the ECB. In addition to these legal requirements, the Governing Council has also taken a number of initiatives which have made it possible to considerably increase the amount of information available on the exercise of the single monetary policy and on the rest of the ECB's activities. Thus, firstly, the Governing Council published a specific interpretation of the concept of price stability which, as you all know, is contained in the Treaty as the priority objective of monetary policy. This interpretation - an annual increase in the harmonised index of consumer prices for the euro area of less than 2% - provides society with a precise reference to assess, in the medium term, the effectiveness of the ECB's actions. In the same vein, the Council has announced the basic elements that frame its decision-making process in the field of monetary policy - the well-known first and second pillars - and has decided to give greater specificity to the first of the pillars, that relating to the quantity of money in circulation, specifying both the definition of the basic monetary aggregate - called M3 -, as a reference value for its year-on-year growth rate, which is considered consistent, in the medium term, with the objective of price stability. The ECB also publishes a monthly economic bulletin containing an article containing a detailed analysis of the economic situation in the euro area and an assessment of the possible risks to maintaining price stability. In addition, on a monthly basis and in any event after each movement in the benchmark interest rates, the Governing Council publishes a press release which includes its assessment of the economic situation and outlook for the area and, where relevant, the reasons that have led to the decision to alter the tone of monetary policy. Finally, the ECB carries out extensive outreach and communication work through its website and develops, in collaboration with the national central banks, specific advertising campaigns, such as the launch to disseminate the characteristics of the new euro banknotes. In the field of relations with public authorities, the President of the ECB has undertaken to assist the European Parliament's Committee on Economic Affairs whenever the topics discussed or recent events so warrant and, in any case, once every three months; while also attending the meetings of the Ministers of Economy and Finance of the countries belonging to the Economic and Monetary Union, the so-called Eurogroup. To conclude this review of the additional measures adopted by the Governing Council of the ECB in the interests of greater transparency, I would like to mention the recent decision to publish, on a semi-annual basis, the projections of a wide range of macroeconomic variables made by ECB experts and the national central banks of the EMU countries. Although it does not collect all the information relevant to monetary policy decision-making by the Governing Council of the ECB, the publication of this exercise provides the public with a synthetic view of the Eurosystem economists' technical assessment of the euro area's short- and medium-term outlook. Macroeconomic projections are perhaps the most visible product of a line of work aimed at improving knowledge of all relevant aspects of the euro area economy, involving both the ECB and the Eurosystem national central banks. It should be borne in mind that the latter generally have a long experience in economic and monetary analysis and represent the most authoritative voice as regards their respective national economies. This is the case of the Bank of Spain, which, since Bern87cer's time, has devoted numerous resources to economic studies, which has allowed it to develop a powerful analytical instrument and a deep knowledge of the real and financial sectors of the Spanish economy. This acquis, which, prior to the start of Economic and Monetary Union, proved very useful for the design and implementation of national monetary policy, now enables the Banco de Espa96a to contribute very actively, in collaboration with the rest of the Eurosystem, to the preparation of the technical work of basis for appropriate decision-making by the Governing Council of the European Central Bank. From all that I have said so far, it must be deduced that I consider the flourishing of discussion forums, publications and observatories on the ECB, such as the one co-organising this event, to be very enriching. Interesting and useful ideas can certainly emerge from this, while the Eurosystem obtains relevant information on how the public assesses its operating schemes and welcomes decisions taken. In our country, initiatives such as those mentioned, or such as the establishment of the Germ87n Bern87cer Prize itself, have the added benefit of contributing to promoting the economic debate, which has not always had the desired depth, on the importance and implications of monetary integration.
text_original: Jaime Caruna Gobernador del Banco de Espaa 6 de Abril de 2001 PALABRAS DEL GOBERNADOR DEL BANCO DE ESPAA, JAIME CARUANA, EN LA PRESENTACIN DEL PREMIO GERMN BERNCER Mis primeras palabras han de ser de felicitacin a los que han promovido el Premio Germn Berncer con el fin de recompensar los mejores trabajos de investigacin monetaria o bancaria en el mbito de la zona del euro. La creacin de un premio de estas caractersticas y con el nombre de uno de nuestros economistas ms vinculados al nacimiento del anlisis monetario en Espaa constituye una iniciativa a la altura de la realidad, radicalmente nueva, de la Unin Econmica y Monetaria Europea, a la que el observatorio del BCE dedica con acierto toda su actividad. La oportunidad de la eleccin de la figura de Germn Berncer para dar nombre a esta distincin est avalada tambin por su relevante papel como subdirector del entonces recin creado Servicio de Estudios del Banco de Espaa, que tan importantes contribuciones ha venido realizando al anlisis de la economa espaola y de la poltica monetaria. Germn Berncer, que haba nacido en Alicante en el ao 1883, se traslad a Madrid para cubrir la vacante que haba dejado Jos Larraz como subdirector del Servicio de Estudios del Banco de Espaa en el ao 1931. Junto a Olegario Fernndez-Baos, formara el tndem que dirigi el departamento de estudios del banco emisor durante un perodo en el que las tareas de asesoramiento y anlisis econmico y el impulso de la labor de investigacin empezaron a marcar el camino de lo que, con el transcurrir de los aos, seran seas de identidad de esta institucin. Como ustedes recordarn, el nacimiento del Servicio de Estudios en 1930 estuvo estrechamente relacionado con la necesidad de disponer de una institucin en la que se preparasen los informes y se impulsaran los estudios encaminados a asesorar a las autoridades del Banco y del Ministerio sobre la manera de afrontar las prolongadas secuelas de la crisis internacional y los problemas relacionados con la estabilidad del tipo de cambio de la peseta El prestigio que haba alcanzado Germn Berncer desde su ctedra en la Escuela Superior de Comercio de Alicante y su profundo conocimiento de los temas monetarios -adquiridos durante su etapa de formacin en Alemania, donde entr en contacto con la obra de Wicksell- hacan de l la persona idnea para, junto con Fernndez-Baos -con una formacin mucho ms estadstica y cuantitativa-, poner en marcha un centro de estudios con pocos precedentes, en aquel momento, en nuestro pas. Son numerosos los trabajos que acreditan la importancia de la obra de Berncer, desde el denominado: Inters del capital. El problema de sus orgenes, hasta, ya desde su puesto en el Servicio de Estudios, El ritmo de la crisis econmica espaola en relacin con la mundial, que plantea con enorme agudeza las dificultades de la previsin y el anlisis econmico en un mundo sometido a intensas fluctuaciones cclicas. La propuesta de un conjunto de indicadores que permitiera anticipar los cambios cclicos en la economa y su denominacin como barmetros econmicos, hemos de reconocer que parece sacada de las pginas de alguna revista o peridico econmico de hoy da. Pero donde mejor se plasma el inters de Berncer por los problemas econmicos del momento es en su Coleccin de crnicas del Boletn semanal y en los informes trimestrales de coyuntura que publicaba el Servicio de Estudios con el ttulo de: Situacin econmico-financiera de Espaa. El anlisis de Berncer de los problemas econmicos de aquellos turbulentos aos sigue siendo enormemente actual, como lo prueba la siguiente cita: La accin y reaccin entre los mercados de productos y el de valores juega un papel importante en la mecnica de las fluctuaciones econmicas de la economa. No me podrn negar que esta breve sentencia sigue siendo plenamente vlida y lcida casi setenta aos despus. Pero no solo me parece acertada la eleccin del economista que da nombre al premio recin instaurado. Tambin lo es dedicarlo a la investigacin en temas monetarios y bancarios dentro de la UEM. Es hoy indudable que la adecuada conduccin de la poltica monetaria exige, cada vez ms, el uso de herramientas analticas sofisticadas que son desarrolladas dentro y fuera del mbito de los bancos centrales. De este modo, resulta pertinente fomentar, como pretende hacer este premio, la investigacin de calidad en este campo. Esta necesidad es especialmente acuciante cuando se trata de abordar un proyecto de la envergadura y complejidad de la Unin Econmica y Monetaria, que supone la aplicacin de una poltica monetaria nica en un conjunto de naciones que mantienen muchos rasgos particulares y que siguen siendo soberanas en el manejo de los restantes instrumentos de la poltica econmica, aunque sea dentro de unas ciertas reglas y mecanismos de coordinacin que pretenden asegurar los objetivos comunes. Para afrontar de manera adecuada todos estos retos, todos los miembros del Eurosistema, el BCE y los bancos centrales nacionales dedican un gran esfuerzo al anlisis y a la investigacin, con el fin de fundamentar adecuadamente la estrategia de poltica monetaria y la adopcin de las decisiones oportunas. Para abordar todas estas tareas, el Eurosistema en su conjunto debe establecer vnculos con el mundo acadmico de los que, sin duda, pueden desprenderse mejoras importantes para el eficaz desempeo de su funcin. Este objetivo se plasma en numerosas iniciativas, tanto del BCE como de los bancos centrales nacionales, de dilogo y cooperacin con universidades y centros de investigacin y se enmarca dentro de la poltica de comunicacin del Eurosistema. Esta ocasin me parece especialmente propicia para abordar este importante tema, al que quisiera dedicar la segunda parte de mi intervencin. Junto con la definicin de los objetivos que se persiguen y el establecimiento de los mecanismos y los principios sobre los que se articula el proceso de toma de decisiones, la poltica de comunicacin constituye uno de los elementos bsicos sobre los que se asienta la estrategia de la poltica monetaria de la mayora de los bancos centrales y, en particular, la del Eurosistema. En nuestro caso, existen, al menos, dos poderosas razones para que el papel que desempea la poltica de comunicacin adquiera especial relevancia. En primer lugar, es preciso recordar que el Eurosistema goza, en el ejercicio de sus funciones, de total independencia con respecto al resto de los poderes pblicos; independencia cuyo objetivo ltimo es, como sin duda conocen, evitar que el ejercicio de la poltica monetaria se vea afectado por el ciclo poltico, de modo que pueda mermarse su capacidad para alcanzar el objetivo prioritario de mantener la estabilidad de precios. Sin embargo, esta independencia requiere, como lgica contrapartida, la obligacin del Eurosistema de rendir cuentas de sus actividades tanto ante los legtimos representantes de la sociedad como ante la opinin pblica. En segundo lugar, la eficacia de la poltica monetaria est, a menudo, condicionada por la forma en la que los agentes econmicos interpretan las decisiones adoptadas por el banco central responsable. En este sentido, el diseo de una poltica de comunicacin fluida, que garantice un grado adecuado de transparencia, constituye un requisito indispensable para reducir el riesgo de que se formen expectativas errneas que obstaculicen el normal desenvolvimiento del proceso de transmisin de las acciones del banco central al conjunto de la economa, reduciendo as la efectividad de la poltica monetaria. Es importante, sin embargo, sealar que la teora econmica y la prctica de los bancos centrales que ms xito han cosechado en el cumplimiento de sus objetivos demuestra que la calidad de la comunicacin es mucho ms importante que su intensidad Es simplemente inadecuado basar -como, a veces, se ha hecho- la evaluacin de la idoneidad de una determinada poltica de comunicacin en la mera elaboracin de la lista de aquellos elementos de los que un banco central no informa. Creo, por el contrario, que cualquier anlisis riguroso de esta cuestin debe comenzar por el estudio detallado de los procedimientos concretos utilizados para comunicar y explicar a los mercados y al pblico en general los objetivos que se persiguen y las decisiones que se adoptan, y, a partir de este punto, preguntarse, en todo caso, por el verdadero valor aadido derivado de la adopcin de instrumentos o procedimientos de informacin complementarios. En el caso del Eurosistema, el Tratado de la Unin Europea contiene en su articulado una serie de requerimientos concretos de rendicin de cuentas. As, el BCE est obligado a enviar un informe anual al Parlamento Europeo, al Consejo Europeo y a la Comisin y a informarles trimestralmente de sus actividades, as como a publicar, con carcter semanal, su balance consolidado. Asimismo, los miembros del Comit Ejecutivo del BCE deben comparecer, regularmente, ante los diferentes comits del Parlamento Europeo. Finalmente, el Presidente del ECOFIN tiene la posibilidad de asistir a las reuniones del Consejo de Gobierno del BCE. Ms all de estos requerimientos legales el Consejo de Gobierno ha tomado, adems, una serie de iniciativas que han permitido incrementar considerablemente el volumen de informacin disponible sobre el ejercicio de la poltica monetaria nica y sobre el resto de las actividades del BCE. As, en primer lugar, el Consejo de Gobierno hizo pblica una interpretacin concreta del concepto de estabilidad de precios que, como todos ustedes conocen, figura en el Tratado como el objetivo prioritario de la poltica monetaria. Esta interpretacin -un incremento anual del ndice armonizado de precios de consumo para el rea del euro inferior al 2%- proporciona a la sociedad una referencia precisa para valorar, en el medio plazo, la eficacia de las acciones del BCE. En esta misma direccin, el Consejo ha dado a conocer los elementos bsicos que enmarcan su proceso de toma de decisiones en materia de poltica monetaria -los conocidos primer y segundo pilar- y ha decidido dotar de mayor concrecin al primero de los pilares, el relativo a la cantidad de dinero en circulacin, especificando tanto la definicin del agregado monetario bsico -denominado M3-, como un valor de referencia para su tasa de crecimiento interanual, que se considera consistente, en el medio plazo, con el objetivo de estabilidad de precios. El BCE publica, adems, cada mes, un boletn econmico en el que se incluye un artculo que contiene un anlisis detallado de la situacin econmica en el rea del euro y una valoracin de los posibles riesgos para el mantenimiento de la estabilidad de precios. Adems, con periodicidad mensual y, en todo caso, despus de cada movimiento de los tipos de inters de intervencin, el Consejo de Gobierno hace pblica una nota de prensa donde se recoge su valoracin de la coyuntura y las perspectivas econmicas de la zona y, cuando resulta pertinente, las razones que han llevado a la decisin de alterar el tono de la poltica monetaria. Finalmente, el BCE realiza una amplia labor de divulgacin y comunicacin a travs de su sitio en internet y desarrolla, en colaboracin con los bancos centrales nacionales, campaas de publicidad especficas, como la puesta en marcha para difundir las caractersticas de los nuevos billetes de euros. En el terreno de las relaciones con las autoridades pblicas, el Presidente del BCE se ha comprometido a asistir a la Comisin de Economa del Parlamento Europeo siempre que los temas tratados o los acontecimientos recientes as lo aconsejen y, en todo caso, una vez cada tres meses; al tiempo que asiste tambin a las reuniones de los ministros de Economa y Hacienda de los pases pertenecientes a la Unin Econmica y Monetaria, el llamado Eurogrupo.
