Para concluir esta revisin de las medidas suplementarias que, en aras de una mayor transparencia, ha adoptado el Consejo de Gobierno del BCE, quisiera mencionar la reciente decisin de publicar, con carcter semestral, las proyecciones que de un conjunto amplio de variables macroeconmicas realizan los expertos del BCE y de los bancos centrales nacionales de los pases de la UEM. Aunque no recoge toda la informacin relevante para la toma de decisiones de poltica monetaria por parte del Consejo de Gobierno del BCE, la publicacin de este ejercicio permite al pblico obtener una visin sinttica de la valoracin tcnica que los economistas del Eurosistema realizan de las perspectivas de la zona del euro a corto y medio plazo. Las proyecciones macroeconmicas son, quizs, el producto ms visible de una lnea de trabajo dirigida a perfeccionar el conocimiento de todos los aspectos relevantes de la economa de la zona del euro, en la que participan tanto el BCE como los bancos centrales nacionales del Eurosistema. Ha de tenerse en cuenta que estos ltimos cuentan, en general, con una larga experiencia en el anlisis econmico y monetario y representan la voz ms autorizada en lo que se refiere a sus respectivas economas nacionales. Este es el caso del Banco de Espaa, que, desde los tiempos de Berncer, ha dedicado numerosos recursos a los estudios econmicos, lo que le ha permitido desarrollar un instrumental analtico poderoso y un conocimiento profundo de los sectores real y financiero de la economa espaola. Este acerbo, que, con anterioridad al comienzo de la Unin Econmica y Monetaria, result de gran utilidad para el diseo y la instrumentacin de la poltica monetaria nacional, permite ahora al Banco de Espaa contribuir de manera muy activa, en colaboracin con el resto del Eurosistema, a la elaboracin del trabajo tcnico de base que resulta preciso para la adecuada toma de decisiones por parte del Consejo de Gobierno del Banco Central Europeo. De todo lo que llevo dicho hasta ahora debe deducirse que considero muy enriquecedor el florecimiento de foros de discusin, publicaciones y observatorios sobre el BCE, como el que co-organiza este acto. Sin duda, de todo ello pueden surgir ideas interesantes y tiles, al tiempo que el Eurosistema obtiene informacin relevante sobre la forma en la que el pblico valora sus esquemas de funcionamiento y acoge las decisiones adoptadas. En nuestro pas, iniciativas como las sealadas, o como la propia instauracin del Premio Germn Berncer, tienen el beneficio aadido de contribuir a fomentar el debate econmico, que no siempre ha tenido la profundidad deseable, sobre la trascendencia y las implicaciones de la integracin monetaria.

Title: Speech delivered at the Ordinary General Assembly of the Spanish Confederation of Savings Banks
text: Jaime Caruna Governor of the Bank of Spain April 18, 2001 SPEECH DELIVERED BY JAIME CARUANA, GOVERNOR OF THE BANK OF SPAIN, AT THE ORDINARY GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE SPANISH CONFEDERATION OF SAVINGS BANKS It is a great satisfaction for me to be here today with all of you and to be able to make some reflection on this sector. I would like, on this first occasion, to focus on some basic aspects of the activity of the Savings Banks. 1. Evolution of the sector. Definition of the sector. Let's start, however, with a quick review of what has been the exercise we left behind. In 2000 the savings banks have had good results, although there are signs of exhaustion in the capacity to generate resources and the approximation between pre-tax results and operating margin may indicate tensions in future earnings growth. The aggregate figures for the sector show growth in activity (the average balance sheet has grown by 13.3%), in results (growth of 10.9% in net results over the previous year) and in return on equity that has remained above 14%. Similarly, its solvency continues at high levels, with significant surpluses (above 50% in aggregate terms) over the minimum receivable own resources. However, the year 2000 has also confirmed the tendency to compensate for the fall in margins by shifting to activities which, because of their greater risk, offer higher returns. Thus, the weight of credit investment and equity portfolios has continued to grow significantly at the expense of treasury and fixed income investment. If we look at the evolution of the sector from a longer time horizon, the results of recent years show that the Savings Banks sector has been able to adapt and keep up with changes in the financial markets and the economic environment. The savings banks have contributed to the distribution of market shares among a greater number of entities, favouring the persistence of a high level of competition in our market. On the other hand, the Savings Banks have been able to combine this evolution with the positive social orientation of their activity and with the maintenance of their special link with the regional environment, which has allowed the provision of services to customers and geographical areas that, without their presence, could have been left unattended. In turn, their regional and social proximity gives them greater retail customer loyalty, which adds stability to their banking model. Today, one of every two pesetas deposited by Spaniards is entrusted to a Savings Bank. In short, the Savings Banks have been able to rely on their strengths and have provided the financial system with stability, solvency and competition, as well as playing an important social role. But in periods of intense change, complacency is not a good advisor and it is more constructive to think about its future evolution, under a critical approach, which allows detecting possible weaknesses and specific areas of activity that require special attention. Supervisors have a relatively simple scheme to analyze an entity or a sector. We rely on the so-called supervisory risk profile, which responds to three main categories of factors: . The risk profile, which includes both the activities according to their nature, objectives and strategy, as well as the analysis of the various risks assumed by line of activity. This category also includes business risk, which includes the ability to generate and maintain the entity's results over time. . Quality of management. The supervisory risk of an entity not only depends on the risks it assumes, it also depends on the quality of management. Is the entity and its risks well managed?, Does it have adequate structures consistent with the nature and strategy of the entity? . Finally, quality and quantity of own resources. To cushion unexpected risks, it is necessary to have sufficient own resources. Are there sufficient and good quality resources? 2. Risk profile. Profile of activities and risks in relation to their objectives and strategies. In the specific case of savings banks, the analysis of activities and risks must start from their uniqueness: that of being private credit institutions, but with strong regional and social roots. The savings banks as credit institutions of a private foundational nature, of a social nature, have always been linked to the promotion and mobilization of popular savings and, in general, to the attention of the financial needs of those families and companies that make up the social fabric; Under this anchorage in the retail business, they have traditionally operated as entities that strongly diversified their risks. These defining features and operational characteristics of the Savings Banks are the basis of their legal consideration and are the basis of the structure of their governing bodies and their control and accountability mechanisms. I believe that there is a broad consensus on preserving these characteristics and this requires that the Savings Banks continue to be true to themselves. This implies, on the one hand, reaffirming their character as credit institutions above other considerations, which is what will ensure their future survival and therefore the interests of their depositors. It also involves some degree of self-restraint in those activities and risks furthest from their own nature. If we want to continue creating value for society and for the region in a sustained manner, the Savings Banks must be, above all, solvent entities and managed with correct economic and financial criteria. I would now like to touch briefly on some of the risks. Credit risk. In the last two years, the credit investment of the savings banks has grown by 40%, a very high figure that leads me to reiterate our message of prudence. In favourable circumstances, there is a tendency to underestimate risks and to relax the granting of credit. I believe that each entity should analyze whether its growth in credit investment is compatible with reasonable risk premiums and its ability to manage risks. For the supervisor. The growth of credit above certain levels is a risk factor that requires detailed monitoring of the entity. Industrial investments. The acquisition of shares in companies, as a financial investment, is an alternative by which savings banks can diversify their business structure. Like any credit institution, they are required to have a good knowledge of the sector and the risks and commitments assumed, as well as to have sufficient financial and management capacity. However, permanent fixed assets in investments in industrial companies with a vocation for control or significant influence on management, represent long-term commitments with additional responsibilities and if they exceed certain limits or reach significant relative proportions in the balance sheet they may be extraneous to their nature and objectives. Although such links to industrial companies can be seen as an area generating new business opportunities, they are in exchange for assuming new risks, together with the additional responsibilities that entails the involvement in the shareholding and management. On the other hand, these shares require abundant own resources to comply with the current limits on industrial holdings and risk concentration, and may require the capture of those, through hybrid instruments (such as preferred shares issued by subsidiaries), which do not seem natural in a foundational entity. For all the above, and because such participations can divert the Savings Banks from those characteristics that best correspond to their nature, I believe that this is an area in which prudence, self-moderation to which I referred earlier, as well as great transparency and broad participation in the definition of their strategy, are necessary. Concentration: in groups and sectors. To the extent that the current legislation establishes only minimum levels, it is the managers of the credit institution who must define, with rigour and prudence, their degree of diversification taking into account their management capacity and resources. On the one hand, prudence must lead savings banks, and all credit institutions, to ensure that their concentration on large customers is clearly lower than that laid down in the rules. On the other hand, and even when there is no rule that limits sectoral or business concentration, it is necessary that entities closely monitor this type of concentration, and that their managers pay special attention to adequate sector diversification and effective compliance with it on an ongoing basis. In terms of concentration, the powers of the Banco de Espa96a are and will be exercised with criteria of maximum prudence, that is, from the strictest perspective in order to promote maximum diversification. I would now like to mention two additional issues: Rationalization of costs. This is a traditional and repeated recipe but should not lose validity. It is essential to insist on this, since the mere observation of the costs of the sector leads us to the conclusion that the savings banks must cut their structural costs. The figures for 2000 serve to show that operating expenses are still high, in relation to the balance sheet (2.2% on ATM), in relation to ordinary margin by 65.6% and also that its high growth (8.9%), continues to have a significant negative impact on operating margin, which grew by 4.5%. The effort to rationalize and cut structural costs must continue and this must remain a primary focus for its managers. This rationalisation is not only necessary in the costs associated with the network, which is increasingly focused on commercial aspects, but an in-depth review of the structural costs of central services would be necessary. I believe that this rationalization can be made compatible with the necessary efforts in areas such as improving risk management, the challenge of new technologies and human resources management. The management of the OBS. While attending to objectives that constitute one of their hallmarks, the Savings Banks must manage the resources allocated to social charitable work from the basic perspective of attending, in the first place, to the financial nature of the Fund and its necessary stability and future solvency. From this perspective, special attention and prudence are also required in those commitments that condition the Fund's future capacity for self-financing. In Consequently, the Savings Banks must retain their autonomy in the decision and management of their OBS and minimize those social works that imply the commitment of high future budgetary attentions to their exclusive charge. 3. Management of the institution and risk management structures. The increasing size of the Savings Banks on the one hand, and the growing competence, sophistication and complexity of financial instruments, markets and systems, on the other, place new demands on the quality of management of the entities. We must be aware that the governance structures of the Savings Banks have attracted some attention. It has been repeated on numerous occasions: the need to strengthen the professionalism, stability and control of the management of the Savings Banks, the need to avoid political interference in their management, the risks of confusing social purposes with public policy objectives. In various forums and institutions, the difficulties arising from the lack of identification of ownership and the absence of mechanisms for balancing and controlling the market have been noted. Regardless of the nuances that can be made to some of the previous arguments, I believe that the sector is in a position to consider the challenge of finding formulas for improving the management of the Savings Banks, creating structures that establish counterweights, hinder personalisms and external interferences and facilitate the definition of clear strategies according to their nature and encourage professional and transparent management. I believe that this is a key area in which the sector itself must make a deep reflection that allows arriving at a code of good governance of the Savings Banks, adapted to their characteristics, their needs and their governing bodies. The fact that the sector itself has a code of good governance in line with principles of existing codes, (the Olivencia code, with the principles established in Basel and the OECD), would help the Savings Banks to improve the mechanisms for defining strategies, control and transparency of management, and accountability in accordance with their nature. A starting principle is to make it clear that only a solvent and efficient entity can guarantee, in a sustained manner, the protection of the depositor and the fulfillment of its final objectives. The conclusion of this principle is that the code of good governance should highlight the obligation that the members of the administrative bodies must put, above any other objective, the good management of the entity. Let me quickly recall some of the basic principles of bank governance proposed by Basel: . Establishment of strategic objectives and a corporate culture that is transmitted and communicated to the entire organization of the entity. . Ensure that board members are qualified for their work, have detailed knowledge of their role in the governance of the entity and are not subject to undue influence from managers or subject to interests external to the entity. . Ensure that the entity's senior management has appropriate control of its departments and activities. Key decisions should be made by more than one person. . Carry out the governance of the entity with transparency. The internal measures, within the organization itself, that each entity must take in order to improve management, can be complemented or supported by initiatives of an associative nature, between different entities or through processes of concentration in the sector that serve the same objectives. I think it is important to highlight the merits of the associationist experiences that are being implemented in the sector, which help to minimize size restrictions in areas such as: computer centers, insurance, electronic banking, leasing, risk management, etc. Risk management. A chapter that deserves special attention is the improvement of instruments that ensure adequate knowledge and control of credit, market, and operational risks. Savings banks, like all credit institutions, must devote significant efforts to these aspects in order to keep pace with market changes and advances in management techniques, especially when the use of internal models can be used for prudential purposes and in anticipation of regulatory changes that will result from the application of the new solvency requirements developed by the Basel Committee of Supervisors and by the European Union. To the extent that the main objective of the new control models is to optimise the identification and management of risks, and of the own resources necessary for their coverage, their design and implementation should not await the entry into force of the changes that will allow its use for regulatory purposes, but must be considered, in themselves, as some more elements of necessary adaptation to the demands of all professional management and, therefore, be addressed, with the utmost rigor and as soon as possible. I think this is an issue that would require more time for proper treatment. Today I would simply like to stress its importance and our encouragement and support for the work that the ECSC is promoting in the field of risk control, and to which almost all the savings banks have joined. 4. Own resources. Savings banks, and in general, credit institutions, have been increasingly resorting to the issuance of preferred shares by instrumental subsidiaries abroad to increase their own resources. Although these are instruments whose computability is provided for in solvency rules, their increasingly frequent use means that the percentage they represent of total eligible own resources is very significant in a growing number of institutions. Above certain levels, there are uncertainties about the practical effectiveness of these own resources. This is not an exclusive situation in the savings bank sector, what has been said applies to all credit institutions. Although it has not been incorporated into a standard, I would like to point out the opinion of the Bank of Spain in relation to preferred shares. In our view, preferential share levels above 30% of core own resources are not recommended. We also believe that these instruments should not be used to finance expansion policies in new activities or markets. Consequently, regardless of their special monitoring by the supervisor, it is up to the institutions, for their own security, to avoid their excessive use and, if necessary, to reconsider their growth strategy if this means exceeding the recommended limits. A second aspect to consider is the fact that preferred shares are marketed, in many cases, through the networks of the entities and are acquired by regular customers who approach the product with the perspective of a passive client, who is offered a good return. All of this poses risks to The policyholder implies a certain opacity in prices and involves the assumption of additional risks to the entities, including reputational. Conversion to euros. Finally, I would like to say a few words about the forthcoming process of changing peseta notes and coins from euros to euros. When this meeting is held next year, the dual circulation period will be over, and the peseta will no longer be legal tender, although we will still be at the stage where credit institutions convert national currency for euros. The replacement of twelve national currencies by a single currency, the euro, is undoubtedly one of the greatest logistical challenges we have faced at European level and the role of financial institutions is very important in all its phases. I would like to reiterate our gratitude for the spirit of collaboration that we have found at all times in the Spanish financial sector, which has been able to understand the magnitude of this event. In the case of the Savings Banks, I want to thank them for their special contribution to making the change reach all corners of Spain. I know that I leave many topics and nuances unaddressed, especially in a sector as special, sensitive and complex as the Savings Banks. That is why I want to make myself available to all of you and offer my availability and desire for collaboration and that of the Bank of Spain to continue working together with the sector.
text_original: Jaime Caruna Gobernador del Banco de Espaa 18 de Abril de 2001 DISCURSO PRONUNCIADO POR JAIME CARUANA, GOBERNADOR DEL BANCO DE ESPAA, EN LA ASAMBLEA GENERAL ORDINARIA DE LA CONFEDERACIN ESPAOLA DE CAJAS DE AHORROS Es para mi una gran satisfaccin estar hoy aqu con todos Uds. y poder hacer alguna reflexin sobre este sector. Me gustara, en esta primera ocasin, centrarme en algunos aspectos bsicos de la actividad de las Cajas. 1. Evolucin del sector. Definicin del sector. Comencemos, no obstante, por un rpido repaso de lo que ha sido el ejercicio que dejamos atrs. En el ao 2000 las Cajas han tenido unos buenos resultados, si bien se aprecian seales de agotamiento en la capacidad generacin de recursos y el acercamiento entre resultados antes de impuestos y el margen de explotacin puede indicar tensiones en el crecimiento futuro de resultados. Las cifras agregadas del sector muestran crecimientos en actividad (el balance medio ha crecido un 13,3%), en resultados (crecimiento del 10,9% de los resultados netos sobre el ao anterior) y en rentabilidad sobre recursos propios que se ha mantenido por encima del 14%. Del mismo modo, su solvencia continua en niveles elevados, con supervit significativos (por encima del 50% en trminos agregados) sobre los recursos propios mnimos exigibles. No obstante, el ao 2000 ha confirmado tambin la tendencia a compensar la cada de mrgenes con un desplazamiento a actividades que, por su mayor riesgo, ofrecen rendimientos ms elevados. As, ha seguido creciendo de manera significativa el peso de la inversin crediticia y de la cartera de renta variable a costa de la inversin tesorera y en renta fija. Si observamos la evolucin del sector desde un horizonte temporal ms amplio, los resultados de los ltimos aos muestran que el sector de Cajas ha sabido adaptarse y estar a la altura de los cambios en los mercados financieros y en el entorno econmico. Las Cajas han contribuido a la distribucin de cuotas de mercado entre un mayor nmero de entidades, favoreciendo la persistencia de un elevado nivel de competencia en nuestro mercado. Por otra parte, las Cajas han sabido compaginar esta evolucin con la positiva orientacin social de su actividad y con el mantenimiento de su especial vinculacin con el entorno regional, lo que ha permitido la prestacin de servicios a clientes y zonas geogrficas que, sin su presencia, pudieran haber quedado desatendidos. A su vez, su proximidad regional y social les aportan una mayor fidelidad del cliente minorista, lo que aade estabilidad a su modelo de banca. Hoy, una de cada dos pesetas depositadas por los espaoles es confiada a una Caja de Ahorros. En suma, las Cajas de Ahorro han sabido apoyarse en sus puntos fuertes y han proporcionado al sistema financiero estabilidad, solvencia y competencia, adems de jugar un importante papel social. Pero en perodos de cambios intensos, la complacencia no es buena consejera y es ms constructivo pensar en su evolucin futura, bajo un enfoque crtico, que permita detectar posibles debilidades y reas especficas de actividad que precisen de una especial atencin. Los supervisores tenemos un esquema relativamente sencillo para analizar una entidad o un sector. Nos basamos en el denominado perfil de riesgo supervisor, que responde a tres grandes categoras de factores:  El perfil de riesgos, en el que se incluyen tanto las actividades en funcin de su naturaleza, objetivos y estrategia, como el anlisis de los diversos riesgos asumidos por lnea de actividad. Se recoge tambin en esta categora, el riesgo de negocio, que incluye la capacidad de generar y mantener en el tiempo los resultados de la entidad.  Calidad de la gestin. El riesgo supervisor de una entidad no solo depende de los riesgos que asume, tambin depende de la calidad de la gestin. Se gestiona bien la entidad y sus riesgos?, tiene estructuras adecuadas y consistentes con la naturaleza y estrategia de la entidad?  Finalmente, calidad y cantidad de los recursos propios. Para amortiguar riesgos inesperados, es necesario tener suficientes recursos propios. Se dispone de recursos suficientes y de buena calidad? 2. Perfil de riesgos. Perfil de actividades y riesgos en relacin con sus objetivos y estrategias. En el caso especfico de las Cajas, el anlisis de actividades y riesgos ha de partir de su singularidad: la de ser entidades de crdito privadas, pero con un fuerte arraigo tanto regional como social. Las Cajas como entidades de crdito de naturaleza fundacional privada, de carcter social, han estado desde siempre vinculadas al fomento y movilizacin del ahorro popular y, en general, a la atencin de las necesidades financieras de aquellas familias y empresas que conforman el tejido social; bajo ese anclaje en el negocio minorista, han operado tradicionalmente como entidades que diversificaban fuertemente sus riesgos. Estos rasgos definitorios y caractersticas operativas de las Cajas son el fundamento de su consideracin jurdica y son la base de la estructura de sus rganos de gobierno y la de sus mecanismos de control y rendicin de cuentas. Creo que hay un amplio consenso en preservar estas caractersticas y ello requiere que las Cajas continen siendo fieles a s mismas. Esto implica, por una parte, reafirmar su carcter de entidades de crdito por encima de otras consideraciones, que es lo que asegurar su supervivencia futura y por tanto los intereses de sus depositantes. Supone tambin algn grado de auto moderacin en aquellas actividades y riesgos ms alejados de su propia naturaleza. Si se quiere seguir creando valor para la sociedad y para la regin de forma sostenida, las Cajas deben ser, por encima de todo, entidades solventes y gestionadas con criterios econmicos y financieros correctos. Me gustara ahora referirme brevemente a algunos de los riesgos. Riesgo de crdito. En los dos ltimos aos, la inversin crediticia de las Cajas ha crecido un 40%, cifra muy elevada que me lleva a reiterar nuestro mensaje de prudencia. En coyunturas favorables se tiende a minusvalorar los riesgos y a relajar la concesin de crditos. Creo que cada entidad debe analizar si su crecimiento en inversin crediticia es compatible con primas de riesgo razonables y con su capacidad de gestionar los riesgos. Para el supervisor. el crecimiento del crdito por encima de determinados niveles es un factor de riesgo que obliga a hacer un seguimiento detallado de la entidad. Inversiones industriales. La adquisicin de acciones en empresas, como inversin de carcter financiero, es una alternativa por la que las Cajas pueden diversificar su estructura de negocio. Como a cualquier entidad de crdito se les pide que tengan un buen conocimiento del sector y de los riesgos y compromisos asumidos, as como que cuenten con capacidad financiera y de gestin suficientes. Sin embargo, las inmovilizaciones permanentes en inversiones en empresas industriales con vocacin de control o de influencia notable en la gestin, representan compromisos a largo plazo con responsabilidades adicionales y si sobrepasan determinados lmites o alcanzan proporciones relativas importantes en el balance pueden ser extraas a su naturaleza y objetivos. Aunque tales vinculaciones a empresas industriales puedan verse como un rea generadora de nuevas oportunidades de negocio, lo son a cambio de asumir nuevos riesgos, unidos a las responsabilidades adicionales que conlleva la propia implicacin en el accionariado y gestin. Por otra parte, estas participaciones demandan abundantes recursos propios para cumplir los lmites vigentes a las participaciones industriales y a la concentracin de riesgos, y pueden obligar a la captacin de aquellos, a travs de instrumentos hbridos (como las acciones preferentes emitidas por filiales), que no parecen naturales en una entidad de carcter fundacional. Por todo lo expuesto, y porque tales participaciones pueden desviar a las Cajas de aquellas caractersticas que mejor se corresponden a su naturaleza, creo que este es un terreno en el que son necesarias la prudencia, la auto moderacin a la que antes he hecho referencia, as como una gran transparencia y amplia participacin en la definicin de su estrategia. Concentracin: en grupos y sectores. En la medida que la normativa vigente establece nicamente unos niveles mnimos, son los gestores de la entidad de crdito los que deben definir, con rigor y prudencia, su grado de diversificacin atendiendo a su capacidad de gestin y a sus recursos. Por una parte, la prudencia debe llevar a las Cajas, y a todas las entidades de crdito, a que su concentracin en los grandes clientes sea claramente inferior a la que marcan las normas. Por otra, y an cuando no haya una norma que limite la concentracin sectorial o de negocio, es necesario que las entidades vigilen estrechamente este tipo de concentracin, y que sus gestores presten especial atencin a una adecuada diversificacin sectorial y al efectivo cumplimiento de la misma de manera continuada. En materia de concentracin, las competencias del Banco de Espaa se ejercen y se ejercern con criterios de mxima prudencia, es decir, desde la perspectiva ms estricta a fin de favorecer la mxima diversificacin. Me gustara ahora mencionar dos temas adicionales: Racionalizacin de los costes. Esta es una receta tradicional y reiterada pero que no debe perder vigencia. Es imprescindible insistir en ello, ya que la mera observacin de los costes del sector nos lleva a la conclusin de que las Cajas deben recortar sus gastos de estructura. Las cifras del ao 2000 sirven para mostrar que los gastos de explotacin siguen siendo elevados, con relacin al balance (2,2% sobre ATM), con relacin al margen ordinario un 65,6% y tambin que su alto crecimiento (8,9%), sigue teniendo una relevante incidencia negativa sobre el margen de explotacin, que crece un 4,5%. El esfuerzo para racionalizar y recortar costes de estructura debe continuar y ste debe seguir siendo un elemento de atencin primordial para sus gestores. Esta racionalizacin no es slo necesaria en los costes asociados a la red, cada vez ms volcada en aspectos comerciales, sino que sera necesaria una revisin en profundidad de los costes estructurales de los servicios centrales. Esta racionalizacin creo que puede hacerse compatible con los esfuerzos necesarios en reas como la mejora de la gestin de riesgos, el reto de las nuevas tecnologas y de gestin de los recursos humanos. La gestin de la OBS. Sin dejar de atender unos objetivos que constituyen una de sus seas de identidad, las Cajas deben gestionar los recursos destinados a la obra benfico social desde la perspectiva bsica de atender, en primer lugar, a la naturaleza financiera de la Caja y a su necesaria estabilidad y solvencia futura. Bajo esa perspectiva, se requiere tambin una especial atencin y prudencia en aquellos compromisos que condicionen la capacidad futura de autofinanciacin de la Caja. En consecuencia, las Cajas deben retener su autonoma en la decisin y gestin de su OBS y minimizar aquellas obras sociales que impliquen el compromiso de elevadas atenciones presupuestarias futuras a su exclusivo cargo. 3. Gestin de la entidad y estructuras de gestin de riesgos. El tamao, cada vez mayor de las Cajas por un lado, y la creciente competencia, sofisticacin y complejidad de los instrumentos, mercados y sistemas financieros, por otro, plantean nuevas exigencias en la calidad de gestin de las entidades. Hay que ser conscientes de que las estructuras de gobierno de las Cajas han despertado una cierta atencin. Se ha repetido en numerosas ocasiones: la necesidad de reforzar la profesionalidad, estabilidad y control de la gestin de las Cajas, la necesidad de evitar interferencias polticas en su gestin, los riesgos de confundir fines sociales con objetivos de poltica pblica. En diversos foros e instituciones se han apuntado las dificultades derivadas de la falta de identificacin de la propiedad y de la ausencia de mecanismos de equilibrio y control del mercado. Independientemente de las matizaciones que se pueden hacer a algunos de los argumentos anteriores, creo que el sector est en condiciones de plantearse el reto de buscar formulas de perfeccionamiento de la gestin de las Cajas, creando estructuras que establezcan contrapesos, dificulten personalismos e interferencias externas y faciliten la definicin de estrategias claras acordes con su naturaleza e incentiven la gestin profesional y transparente. Creo que esta es un rea clave en la que el propio sector debe hacer una profunda reflexin que permita llegar a un cdigo de buen gobierno de las Cajas, adaptado a sus caractersticas, a sus necesidades y a sus rganos de gobierno. El que el propio sector se dote de un cdigo de buen gobierno en lnea con principios de cdigos ya existentes, (el cdigo Olivencia, con los principios establecidos en Basilea y la OCDE), ayudara a las Cajas a mejorar los mecanismos de definicin de estrategias, de control y transparencia de la gestin, y de rendicin de cuentas acordes con su naturaleza. Un principio de partida es dejar claro que slo una entidad solvente y eficiente puede garantizar, de manera sostenida, la proteccin del depositante y el cumplimiento de sus objetivos finales. La conclusin de este principio es que el cdigo de buen gobierno, debe destacar la obligacin de que los miembros de los rganos de administracin deben poner, por encima de cualquier otro objetivo, la buena gestin de la entidad. Permtanme rpidamente recordar algunos de los principios bsicos del gobierno de entidades de crdito que propone Basilea:  Establecimiento de objetivos estratgicos y una cultura corporativa que sea transmitida y comunicada a toda la organizacin de la entidad.  Asegurar que los miembros del consejo estn cualificados para su labor, tienen un conocimiento detallado de su papel en el gobierno de la entidad y no estn sujetos a indebidas influencias de los gestores o sometidos a intereses externos a la entidad.  Garantizar que la alta direccin de la entidad tiene un control apropiado de sus departamentos y actividades. Las decisiones clave deben adoptarse por ms de una persona.  Realizar el gobierno de la entidad con transparencia. Las medidas internas, en la propia organizacin, que cada entidad debe tomar con el fin de mejorar la gestin, pueden ser complementadas o apoyadas mediante iniciativas de carcter asociativo, entre distintas entidades o mediante procesos de concentracin en el sector que sirvan a los mismos objetivos. Creo importante destacar los mritos de las experiencias asociacionistas que se estn implantando en el sector, que ayudan a minimizar las restricciones de tamao en reas como: centros informticos, seguros, banca electrnica, leasing, gestin de riesgos etc. Gestin de riesgos. Un captulo que merece atencin especial es el de la mejora de los instrumentos que aseguren un adecuado conocimiento y control de los riesgos, de crdito, de mercado, y operacionales. Las Cajas, al igual que todas las entidades de crdito, deben dedicar importantes esfuerzos a estos aspectos para estar a la altura de los cambios de los mercados y los progresos en tcnicas de gestin, mxime cuando la utilizacin de los modelos internos podr ser utilizada con fines prudenciales y en previsin de los cambios regulatorios que supondr la aplicacin de los nuevos requisitos de solvencia en elaboracin por el Comit de Supervisores de Basilea y por la Unin Europea. En la medida que los nuevos modelos de control tienen como objetivo principal optimizar la identificacin y gestin de los riesgos, y de los recursos propios necesarios para su cobertura, su diseo y puesta en marcha no debe esperar a la entrada en vigor de los cambios que permitirn su uso con fines regulatorios, sino que deben considerarse, en s mismos, como unos elementos ms de adaptacin necesaria a las demandas propias de toda gestin profesional y, por tanto, abordarse, con el mximo rigor y con la mayor brevedad. Creo que este es un tema que requerira ms tiempo para su tratamiento adecuado. Hoy simplemente quiero volver a insistir en su importancia y en nuestro aliento y apoyo a los trabajos que la CECA esta impulsando en materia de control de riesgos, y a los que se han adherido la prctica totalidad de las Cajas. 4. Recursos propios. Las Cajas de Ahorros, y con carcter general, las entidades de crdito, vienen recurriendo de forma creciente a la emisin de acciones preferentes por filiales instrumentales en el extranjero para incrementar sus recursos propios. Aunque se trata de instrumentos cuya computabilidad est prevista en las normas de solvencia, su utilizacin cada vez ms frecuente hace que el porcentaje que representan sobre el total de recursos propios computables sea muy significativo en un nmero creciente de entidades. Por encima de determinados niveles, se plantean incertidumbres sobre la efectividad prctica de estos recursos propios. No se trata de una situacin exclusiva del sector de Cajas, lo dicho es aplicable a todas las entidades de crdito. Aunque no se ha incorporado a una norma, me gustara sealar la opinin del Banco de Espaa con relacin a las acciones preferentes. En nuestra opinin, niveles de acciones preferentes por encima del 30% de los recursos propios bsicos no son recomendables. Adems consideramos que estos instrumentos no deberan usarse para financiar polticas de expansin en nuevas actividades o mercados. En consecuencia, con independencia de su especial seguimiento por parte del supervisor, es a las entidades, a las que por su propia seguridad, corresponde evitar su uso excesivo y si es necesario, reconsiderar su estrategia de crecimiento si esta supone superar los lmites recomendables. Un segundo aspecto a considerar es el hecho de que las acciones preferentes se comercialicen, en muchas ocasiones, a travs de las redes de las entidades y sean adquiridas por clientes habituales que se acercan al producto con la perspectiva de un cliente de pasivo, al que se le ofrece una buena rentabilidad. Todo ello plantea riesgos para el tomador, implica cierta opacidad en los precios y supone la asuncin de riesgos adicionales a las entidades, entre ellos el reputacional. Conversin a euros. Finalmente, quiero dedicar unas palabras al prximo proceso de cambio de billetes y monedas de pesetas a euros. Cuando se celebre esta reunin el ao que viene, el periodo de doble circulacin habr terminado, y la peseta ya no ser moneda de curso legal, aunque todava estaremos en la fase en que las entidades de crdito convierten moneda nacional por euros. La sustitucin de doce monedas nacionales por una moneda nica, el euro, es sin duda uno de los mayores retos logsticos al que nos hemos enfrentado a nivel europeo y el papel de las entidades financieras es muy importante en todas sus fases. Quiero reiterar nuestro agradecimiento por el espritu de colaboracin que hemos encontrado en todo momento en el sector financiero espaol, que ha sabido comprender la magnitud de este acontecimiento. En el caso de las Cajas de Ahorro, quiero agradecer su especial contribucin a que el cambio alcance a todos los rincones de Espaa. S que dejo muchos temas y matices sin tratar, especialmente en un sector tan especial, sensible y complejo como el de las Cajas. Por ello quiero ponerme a disposicin de todos Uds. y ofrecer mi disponibilidad y deseo de colaboracin y la del Banco de Espaa para seguir trabajando conjuntamente con el sector.

Title: Appearance before the Senate Budget Committee
text: Jaime Caruna Governor of the Bank of Spain November 14, 2001 APPEARANCE OF THE GOVERNOR OF THE BANK OF SPAIN, JAIME CARUANA, BEFORE THE SENATE BUDGET COMMITTEE Thank you very much, Mr. President. Dear Senators, I am writing to you in the hearings relating to the discussion of the General State Budget for 2002, at a time of great uncertainty about the intensity and duration of the slowdown in the world economy and about the conditions in which the Spanish economy will develop in the coming quarters. This environment of uncertainty was already present when the macroeconomic scenario for the period 2001-2002 accompanying the General State Budget Project was prepared, but it has worsened considerably, following the dramatic events of 11 September. These have therefore had an impact on an international economic situation in which the American slowdown was already clearly perceived and which, together with the poor situation of the Japanese economy, had fuelled the incipient crisis of many emerging economies. The euro area had also begun to feel the effects of the economic deterioration of its external environment, denoting a lower capacity than expected to develop a pattern of autonomous growth vis-88-vis the American economy. There is a broad consensus that the direct effects of terrorist attacks on activity are likely to be transitory, since the American productive apparatus has not been affected and, therefore, its growth potential remains intact. However, in the short term, an impact on demand of considerable scope is being detected, as a result of the effect of terrorist attacks on the confidence of North American and European businessmen and consumers. All this has transferred the scenario of a possible recovery to, not without uncertainty, already entered next year. In fact, the starting point and intensity of the recovery remain uncertain two months after the terrorist attack, and will not be alien to the development of the war, as well as to the reaction of economic agents to the economic policy decisions taken by the world authorities. In the days immediately following the tremendous upheaval, the monetary authorities' actions were aimed at ensuring the proper functioning of the financial markets, through injections of liquidity into the money markets by the Federal Reserve, the European Central Bank and other central banks, which were carried out with great effectiveness. A few days later, the monetary authorities of the main industrialized economies reduced intervention rates, with the aim of mitigating the possible deterioration in the confidence of economic agents. On 17th September an Extraordinary Council of the ECB agreed, in line with a similar action by the Federal Reserve, to reduce the official rates by half a percentage point to 3.75% in EMU. In the United States, this initial monetary policy reaction was almost immediately reinforced by a series of fiscal policy actions aimed at reducing the tax burden on firms and households and increasing government spending by a relatively large amount, and subsequently by two additional cuts in the target federal funds interest rate. which stood at 2% on November 6. The ECB also lowered its benchmark rate by half a point two days later. International organizations, such as the IMF, the OECD, the European Commission or the ECB itself, are currently reviewing their growth scenarios, which, with great probability, will reflect greater pessimism. For 2001, growth in the United States is quite likely to approach 1%, and the euro area is likely to be below 1.7%, which is the IMF's last official forecast. The revision to be introduced for 2002 is, as can be seen from my previous comments, more difficult to specify, although it is unlikely that the United States and Europe will achieve higher growth rates than in 2001. At present, only the figures for the end of the third quarter for the United States are available, although information on indicators after September 11 referring to the different economies is beginning to be known. In the United States, growth in the third quarter was -0.4% and the data published on confidence indices anticipate a drastic slowdown in consumer spending in the coming months, so the foreseeable fall in this aggregate, together with the prolonged deterioration in private investment and exports, accentuates the risks of the US economy. As for the euro area economies as a whole, the first data on consumer opinions and the business climate predict the intensification of the slowdown in activity that had been taking shape since the second half of last year. EU industry and construction confidence indicators in October were markedly below the levels reached in September, and the consumer confidence indicator prolonged the worsening of recent months. Other indicators related to demand variables, such as the degree of utilization of productive capacity and export expectations, registered a clear decline in the fourth quarter. This confirms that GDP growth in the euro area will be weak in the second half of 2001 and is likely to remain below potential growth for much of next year. As a counterpart to this loss of dynamism in activity - but also as a result of the correction of temporary increases in energy and food prices - the area's inflation rate has shown a downward trend since May, which, in combination with the favourable trend in the commodity markets, has shown a downward trend in the area. It makes it possible to forecast a gradual approximation to the levels of stability established for the whole area, which could be reached in the first months of 2002. This improvement in the medium-term inflation outlook, in a context of loss of momentum in activity, led the European Central Bank to make the last cut of fifty basis points in the rate of the main refinancing operations, on November 8, to 3.25%. Thus, for the fourth time this year, the ECB adjusted monetary conditions in the euro area to an economic environment of more favourable inflationary prospects and lower growth, applying the criteria governing the Eurosystem's monetary policy decisions. In Europe, which has less healthy public finances than the United States, despite the significant consolidation process experienced in the last 5 years, the debate on the margins of action available to fiscal policy has gained renewed prominence after recent events. In this sense, respect for the Stability and Growth Pact, without unnecessary reinterpretations, is essential to preserve the credibility of fiscal policy. But this is compatible with taking advantage of the margins of flexibility that the Pact grants to allow automatic stabilisers to act, provided that this does not jeopardise the consolidation of public finances. In this respect, EMU countries' starting positions differ, as does their ability to adapt fiscal policy to the cyclical situation. Thus, only those countries that have already reached a position close to budgetary balance will be able to allow the automatic stabilisers to operate fully, while those that do not yet have a budget balance close to balance will have to continue their efforts to achieve it, thus limiting the game of stabilisers. The Spanish economy shares with the euro area the trends in terms of slowing growth and reducing the inflation rate. Indeed, in a context of growing uncertainty, in which exports and investment in capital goods show greater sensitivity to the deterioration of the general economic outlook, it is estimated that the Spanish economy reduced the year-on-year growth rate of its Gross Domestic Product in the third quarter to values close to 2.5%. after the 3% reached in the previous quarter and the 4% that was registered, at that time, a year ago. For its part, the rate of change of the CPI has fallen from levels above 4% in the central months of the year to levels of 3.4% in September, and the available forecasts point to additional cuts in price growth in the remainder of the year. In this way, the Spanish economy continues to grow at a faster rate than the rest of EMU, advancing in its process of real convergence, even in a phase of economic slowdown. At the same time, however, it maintains a positive inflation differential with the euro area d0 of almost one percentage point, according to the latest records d0 the persistence of which may end up posing risks to competitiveness and employment growth. The maintenance of a positive growth differential with Europe is a fact that had not occurred in the most recent cyclical slowdowns, which were characterized, as is well known, by drastic downward adjustments in output and employment to correct the imbalances that had been generated during the boom phase. This differential fact is largely attributable to our integration into monetary union, which has protected the economy from certain elements - such as increases in long-term risk premia and movements in exchange rates - that would have contributed to intensifying the slowdown. In any case, the slowdown and recovery profile of the Spanish economy in 2002 will be similar to that of the rest of EMU, and is subject to similar uncertainties as to its temporal sequence and intensity. Spanish exports will be affected by the loss of additional dynamism in their foreign markets. The link with European markets through trade flows is immediate, given the importance of Spanish sales to the countries of the area, and is an important element in the synchronization of the Spanish cycle with the European one; the weakness of exports to EMU will be amplified by the decline in sales to other areas, starting with the US. It is therefore to be expected that the lower dynamism already shown by the latest export data will persist and that foreign demand will become a factor that acts counteractively on growth in the coming quarters: its contribution to growth will become negative in the second half of 2001 and will maintain this sign throughout 2002, although tending to correct itself. With regard to domestic demand, the moderate pattern of slowdown in household spending, both in consumption and residential investment, will be accentuated after the events of September. Deteriorating expectations and, above all, the slowdown in employment have substantial effects on consumer spending patterns; Especially in a context of significant cuts in the value of their net financial wealth, which have been accumulating since the beginning of 2000, and are now tending to strengthen. Despite this weakening, consumption will still register a rate of growth capable of sustaining the growth in demand, especially to the extent that the unemployment rate continues to fall. In any case, household spending will continue to slow down in the coming quarters, so that its growth in 2002 as a whole will be lower than in 2001. In relation to productive investment, although, as has been repeated on numerous occasions, the equity situation and profitability levels of Spanish companies are good, investment has experienced a trend of sharp weakening since last year, and the short-term prospects do not favor a change in these trends either. The slowing trends will, however, be offset by the growth-sustaining effects of lower oil prices and lower inflation, as well as by lower demand stimuli and the play of automatic stabilisers of fiscal policies at European level. For the Spanish economy, the lowering of oil prices is particularly important since, given the still high dependence on imported energy, it usually has a very positive effect on cost formation and income generation. These impulses are more relevant for economic growth in the context of macroeconomic stability and market liberalisation that has accompanied entry into EMU. In summary, the consequences of the terrorist attacks of September have reinforced the slowdown trend in the Spanish economy, so that it does not seem possible for growth on average in 2001 to reach the figure of 3%. With this starting point, it is most likely that the Spanish economy will start 2002 with a moderate growth rate, lower than expected a few months ago, but in any case higher than what can take place in most of the countries around us. It is foreseeable that, during the second part of 2002, the international economic outlook will clear and the Spanish economy will gradually approach its potential growth rate. In any case, the real GDP growth rate that is finally achieved on average next year is surrounded by many Uncertainties, but with the information currently available, a further reduction in the pace of growth seems inevitable, which will tend to reach the area of 2% to 2.5%, with a balance of risks tilted to the downside persisting. The slowdown in economic activity has logically affected the rate of job creation and it is foreseeable that this will continue to do so in the coming quarters, although this process is developing moderately. This is important since the reduced capacity to generate new jobs affects the expectations and income of consumers, and therefore their spending decisions, introducing additional decelerating elements. As has been repeated on numerous occasions, the Spanish economy is following a pattern of intensive growth in job creation, for the maintenance of which it is necessary to have flexible markets, which know how to adapt effectively to the changes that take place in the economic environment, especially in times of sudden changes, such as the current one. It is also necessary that this pattern be accompanied by an investment process that incorporates technological advances that allow increases in productivity. As noted, the inflation rate has begun to ease downwards in the summer months, dragged down by the correction in energy, other commodity and food prices. The slowdown in activity and demand will allow this corrective movement to continue and be passed on to core inflation, which has so far shown strong resistance to moderation. However, as I pointed out earlier, Spain maintains a positive inflation differential with EMU that can only be related, in part, to its status as a country in the process of real convergence, and which also responds to inefficiencies in the functioning of its markets. This differential may end up leading to losses in competitiveness which, in the context of monetary union, could only be recovered by a correction that is probably costly in terms of growth and employment. It is therefore important to take advantage of the current situation to reduce the inflation differential. An essential support to achieve this is the continuation of the current moderation in the behavior of wages and a deepening in the liberalization and flexibility of markets that favors competition and contains the growth of business margins. The budget figures for 2002 are based on a macroeconomic scenario of mild moderation in the rate of growth in activity, which does not incorporate the effects that may result from the worsening of recessionary trends in the international environment in the last months of the current year. They therefore envisage a relatively dynamic behaviour in employment and incorporate, although less intensely than in previous years, a still high growth in income from social contributions and tax collection. In this context, the balance of non-financial operations of general government, in terms of the National Accounts, will remain balanced in 2002, with a composition by agents equal to that foreseen in 2001. Among the main measures contained in the Draft General State Budget I am interested in making special mention of the application of the new system of regional financing of the Autonomous Communities of common regime, which although it should be valued positively in its elements of increase of fiscal co-responsibility, also raises the need to establish the mechanisms that guarantee information transparency in relation to the activities of the Administrations Territorial. This is an essential element for the proper development of any process of fiscal decentralization, but it is reinforced in the Spanish case by the magnitude of the expenditure and tax responsibilities assumed by the Autonomous Communities in relation to all public sector activities. On the other hand, the principle of transparency is intrinsic to the provisions of the Stability and Growth Pact and the Draft Law on Budgetary Stability, which establish strict rules of fiscal discipline. The General State Budget for 2002 extends the fiscal policy strategy developed in recent years, which has consisted of a gradual reduction in the tax burden and control of current public expenditure. This strategy has made it possible to put public finances in a position close to budgetary balance in the medium term, as understood in the Stability and Growth Pact, and to recover the necessary room for manoeuvre to be able to undertake stabilising policies in the event of a possible worsening of the economic situation, without exceeding the 3% threshold established by the Treaty. Achieving budgetary balance in 2002 in the economic context indicated implies a neutral tone to fiscal policy and allows automatic stabilisers to act, in line with the philosophy of the Stability and Growth Pact. This neutral tone, given the slightly restrictive nature of fiscal policy in recent years, seems appropriate in the current circumstances of economic slowdown. As can be seen from my previous considerations, the main risk facing the 2002 Budget arises from a slowdown in output and employment greater than that envisaged by the Government's macroeconomic scenario. If this risk materializes, as seems difficult to avoid, a slight cyclical deficit in the public accounts in 2002 should not be ruled out, as a result of the Set of automatic stabilizers. What is important is that, by accepting the positive role of stabilizers at the current juncture, the neutral tone of the structural component of fiscal policy underlying the 2002 budget figures should be preserved and that no additional discretionary measures should be taken to permanently increase the deficit. There are several reasons for my earlier argument. In the first place, the growth prospects for the Spanish economy at this time do not require discretionary expansionary actions in fiscal policy beyond automatic stabilisers, since the stimulus of these actions would add to the monetary impulse, also expansionary, which derives from the recent decreases in intervention rates by the European Central Bank. On the other hand, maintaining a sound fiscal position is necessary to enable automatic stabilisers to act freely in the event that the economic slowdown becomes more intense than expected or lasts longer than expected, without spilling over fiscal positions. This argument acquires particular relevance in the case of the Spanish economy, given the high inertia shown in the past by certain items of public expenditure in situations of economic slowdown and the high cost of recovering a healthy fiscal position, essential to preserve an environment of macroeconomic stability. Finally, the process of fiscal consolidation carried out in recent years should not be considered concluded, since, on the one hand, it is necessary to continue advancing in the development of public expenditure and revenue strategies that improve the fundamentals of economic growth of the Spanish economy and, on the other, it is necessary to ensure the sustainability of public finances in the medium term, when the population ageing occurs. In this sense, it is necessary to positively assess the allocation made to the pension reserve fund and the improvement in the tax treatment of contributions to pension funds contemplated in the Budgets and its Accompanying Law, respectively. The sustainability of public finances in the medium term requires, however, a more comprehensive and determined strategy that, among other aspects, fully exploits the possibilities provided by the excellent situation that Social Security has been showing in recent years through larger allocations to the reserve fund or the adoption of a faster pace of fiscal consolidation. In summary, the uncertainty surrounding the growth prospects of the world economy in the coming months and its impact on the Spanish economy calls for cautious management of fiscal policy in 2002, which preserves the achievements made in this area, so that, at the same time, it can use the room for manoeuvre provided by a Balanced budget starting position. In this regard, the efforts made in recent years to support the country's productive capacity through research, development and innovation policies and, in general, through public investment should be maintained. On the other hand, the design of economic policies should be strengthened through the deepening of labour market reforms that promote job creation in the economy, and the introduction of new structural reforms that improve the flexibility of markets and their responsiveness to sudden changes in the external environment, like the one that has just taken place. This will ensure that the economy retains the macroeconomic stability necessary to take full advantage of the external economic recovery, when it occurs, while further enhancing its growth potential.
