Acordada la suspensin del expediente administrativo sancionador, no se volvern a reiniciar las actuaciones hasta que no exista sentencia firme en va penal. Futuro de la supervisin prudencial Una vez concluido este resumen de las actuaciones del Banco de Espaa relativas al BBVA, voy a terminar mi intervencin con algunas reflexiones acerca de la evolucin previsible de la supervisin bancaria en el futuro inmediato. Lo sucedido en nuestras fronteras y fuera de ellas requiere un anlisis riguroso que permita extraer conclusiones que ayuden a fortalecer los sistemas financieros. Como punto de partida, me gustara decir que la supervisin bancaria, tal y como se conceba hace unos aos, resulta hoy insuficiente ante las nuevas caractersticas que presentan los sistemas financieros: creciente integracin y complejidad, mayor competencia y una interaccin con el resto de la economa ms variada y potente. Es necesario, por tanto, actualizar constantemente nuestro aparato prudencial, si no queremos que quede desfasado respecto a las nuevas realidades. Una caracterstica importante de este proceso de renovacin es, que no puede, ni debe, plantearse de forma aislada, sino enmarcado en el movimiento de coordinacin internacional al que antes me he referido. Algunos problemas, como son los fallos en el gobierno de las entidades o de los controles internos y externos, trascienden el mbito nacional y precisan soluciones vlidas a nivel internacional. Esto explica nuestra creciente presencia en los foros supervisores internacionales, con el objetivo de participar activamente en la definicin e implantacin de los mejores criterios y prcticas bancarias y de supervisin. Para afrontar los cambios que acabo de mencionar, que sin duda van a ir acelerndose en el futuro, necesitamos una supervisin prudencial con un enfoque ms preventivo e incentivador, tendente a promover la buena gestin de las entidades, al menos por dos vas: "A priori", impulsando la calidad y consistencia de los sistemas, estructuras, tcnicas, procedimientos y cultura de gestin de riesgos; "a posteriori", dedicando ms recursos a complementar la supervisin tradicional con la evaluacin de los aspectos cualitativos antes mencionados. Los cdigos de buen gobierno deben ser mejorados y reforzados mediante estructuras internas y procedimientos que faciliten los controles de administradores y supervisores; la creacin y funcionamiento efectivo de comisiones especializadas, como la de control interno y la de remuneraciones; las reglas internas de funcionamiento del consejo, que promuevan la adecuada informacin, y las decisiones colegiadas; la importancia de las actas y referencias escritas, son ejemplos de cmo las estructuras internas y procedimientos pueden aumentar la eficacia de los cdigos de buen gobierno. Quiero recordar que este enfoque incentivador es una de las caractersticas esenciales del Nuevo Acuerdo de Capital que estamos ultimando en el Comit de Basilea y que se basa en tres elementos: recursos propios suficientes, la accin supervisora y la disciplina de mercado. Esta es la orientacin en la que el Banco de Espaa viene trabajando en los ltimos aos y que se plasma en una metodologa denominada Supervisin de la Actividad Bancaria bajo el Enfoque Riesgo. En sntesis, creo que tenemos que seguir trabajando para conseguir una adecuada combinacin de regulacin, control interno de las entidades, supervisin, coordinacin internacional y disciplina de mercado, que lleve a sistemas bancarios solventes que cumplan su funcin con un alto grado de calidad y servicio.

Title: The presence of Spanish banks in Latin America and the Argentine crisis
text: Encuentro ABOUT "The presence of Spanish banks in Latin America and the Argentine crisis" Santander, 19-21 June 2002 -CLOSING CONFERENCE GONZALO GIL Deputy governor General a5 The expansion of Spanish banking in Latin America is not an isolated event. On the contrary, it is a phenomenon that is fully consistent with the acceleration which, in the second half of the nineties, is undergoing the process of opening up to the outside world not only of our economy, but of Spanish society as a whole. a5 If the growing internationalization of the Spanish economy is to be quantified, it is necessary to resort to balance of payments data. Starting with the current account balance, i.e. our non-financial relations with the outside, Figure 1 shows how, since 1995, the relative importance of our transnational income (blue line) and payments (red line) for these concepts has grown by almost 10 percentage points in terms of GDP, despite the slowdown of the past. consequence of the change in the phase of the cycle at the global level. a5 For its part, to illustrate the internationalization in the financial field, graph 2 shows, in blue, which part of the total financial assets owned by residents in Spain corresponds to investments abroad and, in red, how much of our Total indebtedness has been financed by non-residents. Since 1995, the growth of these relative amounts has been more than 6 percentage points. a5 I am not going to dwell on these general aspects. However, before turning to our financial relations with the outside world and, more specifically, on banking relations, I would like to mention that the full opening of our economy to the outside world also raises great potential, which we must know how to take advantage of, but also possible problems, which must be tackled. a5 Of these scams, I will mention that a more open economy is also an economy more exposed to contagion from external shocks, especially in an international economic system as interdependent as the current one. It is clear that our integration into the Economic and Monetary Union has played a stabilizing role for the Spanish economy in recent shocks. Although this aid will continue to exist in the future, it is still essential to implement realistic and forward-looking national policies to ensure that, when difficulties arise, they can be tackled by having sufficient room for manoeuvre (fiscal, monetary, etc. a5 In order to make it possible to exploit and even expand the possibilities offered by our increasing openness to the outside world, the way forward is obvious: to improve our external competitiveness. To this end, it is necessary to continue to maintain budgetary balance; increase productive investment, especially in cutting-edge technologies; further liberalisation of our real and financial markets; maintain wage moderation and, in general, improve price stability, especially in activities less open to competition. International Investments a5 This frame of reference is the recent evolution of investment from and abroad, the cumulative balance of which, at the end of each year, is shown in graph 3. It shows the strong growth of both Spanish investments abroad (whose total has multiplied by 2.93 in six years) and foreign investments in Spain (which have multiplied by 2.56 in the same period). This uneven growth has led to the coverage ratio (percentage of total capital exported with respect to total imports) has improved by more than 10 percentage points, to 83.4%. a5 In the case of investments from and abroad of other resident sectors, it is customary to separate them into three different groups: (a) direct investments, which flow from the parent companies to the subsidiaries (at least 10% owned) and can be implemented through equities (shares and other forms of participation) or through fixed income (inter-company credits, normally); (b) portfolio investments, which, as the name suggests, do not seek control by the issuer of the securities, so that their time horizon is usually shorter, and are implemented by securities, both variable income (shares and shares in investment funds) and fixed income (public and private); and (c) other investments, which are credit relationships (mainly deposits and loans). a5 Figure 4 shows the great stability of the composition of total foreign investment in Spain during the scams. Within this stability, there is some decrease in the relative importance of direct investments (yellow) in favour of portfolio investments (blue). a5 On the other hand, the composition of the cumulative total of Spanish investment abroad (Graph 5) shows significant changes during the period considered. a5 Throughout this stage, the relative weight of direct investment has almost doubled, reaching 34.8% of the total. Licaly, behind this strong growth is the external expansion of our financial and non-financial companies, which, as shown in graph 6, with data from the end of 2000, has been directed: by area, preferably to Latin America, with 66.5%, followed at a great distance by the European Union, with 32.7%; by issuers, non-financial corporations, which I will later refer to, with 56.9%, and the rest to financial institutions. a5 Portfolio investment, which in 1996 was the least important, has quadrupled to the largest at 37.9 per cent of the total. The fundamental factor that has driven this growth has been the international diversification of the portfolios of collective investment institutions, so the main destination of these capital exports has been the most liquid stock markets in the world. Figure 7 shows the composition by security class of the portfolio investor. It is noted that medium and long-term fixed income is the most important portfolio investment, although during the period considered its weight has fallen 13 percentage points. However, in order to verify the volatility of the composition of these investments, it is sufficient to bear in mind that, as a result of the greater risk uncertainty caused by the increase in all kinds of uncertainties, the portfolio of medium- and long-term fixed-income securities grew by 43.1% during 2001. a5 To be sure, the counterpart to the relative growth in direct and portfolio investment is the decline in the relative importance of "Other investments" (Figure 5), those of a credit nature, as mentioned above, and, therefore, carried out mainly by resident entities (external financing), non-residents (external financing) or both (in interbank operations). Although the absolute amounts grew slightly during the years considered, their relative weight has fallen 46 percentage points. With this, the composition of our investments abroad presents a more balanced structure and in line with the countries of our environment. a5 From this disparate evolution of the different types of investments from and abroad result the net balances, by investment classes, shown in graph 8. Leaving aside once again the Bank of Spain (red line), the change of sign that, in 2000, the net balance of direct investments (blue line) experienced, with which our country becomes a net exporter of capital for this concept. On the other hand, the net balance of portfolio investments (green line) improves significantly during scams. a5 To arrive at the slight worsening of the total net balance (black line), which balances the current balance deficit and capital, the balance of "other investments", those of a credit nature (purple line), remains to be retained. The sharp deterioration in this balance is due to the compensatory action traditionally exercised by this type of investment. For example, its balance was in surplus in 1996. a5 Before commenting on the expansion of our entities in Latin America, I would like to make two observations. The first is to emphasise that, as I said earlier, direct investment by our non-financial companies in the area has been of greater quantitative importance than banking companies. Although the largest non-bank investments are on everyone's mind, in relation to the three most significant scams: in 1999, the purchase of REPSOL from YPF in Argentina, ENDESA's investments in ENERSIS in Mexico and the expansion of TELEFeeNICA in Brazil; in 2000, TELEFeeNICA's takeover bid for all its subsidiaries in the area; and, in 2001, the acquisition by TELEFeeNICA of several thousands of companies in Mexico. a5 The second observation is of a methodological nature. Until now, I have been using data from individual balance sheets, an essential criterion for analysing the evolution of the balance of payments, which is governed by resident/non-resident classification, and til for cross-sectoral comparisons. From now on, to analyse the most characteristic features of the international activity of Spanish banks, I will use exclusively data from the consolidated balance sheets. The reason is that the individual balance sheets include the investments of the parent company in Latin America, but not the activity of the subsidiaries in that area, nor, therefore, their risks. Presence of Spanish banks in Latin America a5 I have already commented that, in the second half of the nineties, the process of opening up our economy to the outside world is dynamized, both in the exchange of goods and services and financial instruments and with the external expansion of Spanish banking in Latin America, through direct investments, is not an isolated phenomenon, but with cutting-edge non-financial companies. However, the case of banks has specific features that are worth remembering. a5 Starting on the demand side, the main driving factor behind the foreign expansion of Spanish banking is the merger process that took place in our country in the second half of the nineties. It will result in two large banking groups, with a high level of own resources and the possibility of expanding them, with significant surpluses of management capacity, with a good knowledge of retail banking technology and with the need to exploit the economies of scale and scope arising from mergers. a5 All this potential cannot be developed in a scenario like the Spanish financial system. The Most High The degree of banking, the high levels of competition, the tendency to fall in all margins, etc. are factors that advise readjustment strategies (rationalization of the management of new structures, improvement of control procedures, purification of duplications of capacity that have arisen, cost savings, etc.) but, of course, they do not offer possibilities for expansion. a5 Both because of geographical proximity and, above all, because of the integration process under way, the European Union could have been a suitable terrain for this expansion. I say theically, because our banks would not have had significant competitive advantages in countries, such as those of the European Union, with excess capacity; because the expansion via the opening of offices had clearly shown its severe limitations, both for foreign banks in Spain and for Spanish banks abroad; and because the purchase of significant holdings in European entities of sufficient size, which is attempted despite the high prices in force, encounters insurmountable institutional difficulties. a5 With these data, Latin America was the "natural" destination of our entities. Although with significant differences between countries, in general the level of banking was low; major privatization processes were under way; the limited efficiency of institutions offered clear opportunities to make management improvements cost-effective; the high margins in force, in addition to reflecting higher levels of risk, offered possibilities to apply technologies that were very well shot in Spain; there was a com language and a close culture, and, moreover, the advantages in terms of geographical, sectoral and cyclical diversification were greater than in relation to Europe. a5 At the same time, competition from other areas to acquire entities was not going to be excessive: US banks were still resentful of the previous Latin American debt crisis; French, Italian and, moreover, the NDICA banks had their own internal problems; German banks looked to the countries of the East; etc. a5 The consequence of all these factors is known, Spanish banking -its two main groups, to be exact- begins a rapid and important process of expansi in Latin America, whose most relevant quantitative results are: direct investments of 25,640 million euros, which have led to more than 35% of the consolidated assets of both groups being in the area, and to the most significant market shares achieved in it are 20% for loans, 21% for loans, 40% for pension funds, and around 15% for collective investment (Table 14). a5 Regarding banking activity, graph 9 shows the distribution by country of the consolidated assets that the two large Spanish groups have in Latin America. It is observed that Mexico represents more than half of these assets, followed at a great distance by Brazil, Chile and Argentina, while the relative importance of the rest of the countries is very limited. a5 Turning to the qualitative aspects, the expansion in Latin America has been based, as is known, not on the opening of branches or the creation of new banks but on the acquisition of shares in pre-existing banks, sidly established and with a deep knowledge of the different national markets. In addition, in almost all cases, groups Espaoles have assumed full control of the management of the investee entities. a5 To be effective, this full control required in the group's matrix, to implement important improvements in the information, management and control systems; In the acquired subsidiaries, the introduction of both drastic processes of rationalization and, in some cases, of reorganization and of profound changes in the management of the institutions and, in particular, of their risks. a5 The predominant activity of the Latin American subsidiaries acquired is retail banking, that is, the activity considered to be of lower risk, generating large margins in the area and where Spanish groups have more experience. I will come back to this topic. a5 The results obtained with this action in 2001 are summarized in graph 10, which compares the cascades of results of the Spanish subsidiaries in Latin America as a whole, with those obtained by our two large groups in their activity in Spain. It is easy to see that all the balances of these waterfalls, that is, the successive margins, are better in Latin America. However, it must be borne in mind that these are purely accounting results, so they do not They include highly significant concepts, such as the risk-adjusted return incurred to achieve it. a5 Nor is the evolution of the different balances parallel (Table 15). Thus, the spread between intermediation margins ( asset remuneration minus cost of liabilities) widens when moving to ordinary margins, as a result of the high amount reached by commissions in Latin America, due to the importance of the management of pension funds and collective investment institutions. a5 Operating expenses are much higher in Latin America, which, on the one hand, explains why the differential between the two operating margins is shortened, and, on the other hand, leads to the efficiency ratio (operating expenses / ordinary margin) being better (less high) in Spain. a5 To arrive at the result before tax, it is necessary to subtract from the operating margin diverse and extraordinary results and the provision of provisions. This scam is significantly higher in Latin America, as a result of its worse (higher) NPL ratio. Consequently, the differential of the results before taxes is lower than that existing between operating margins. a5 As I said before, the results obtained must always be compared with the risks incurred to obtain them. Therefore, before commenting on how these risks have materialized in the case of Argentina, I will pause for a moment to deal with the concentration registered in the international expansion of our banks. a5 Figure 11 shows the worldwide distribution of the consolidated assets of our two large groups. However, to deal with risks, it is more significant to analyze the share of these consolidated assets located in the so-called developing countries, which in our case represents around 35% of total consolidated assets. Figure 12 shows how our two large groups concentrate almost all of their consolidated assets located in developing countries in Latin America. Similarly, this graph shows that this concentration is significantly lower in the case of other countries with internationally active banks. a5 Later, when dealing with the Argentine crisis, I will comment on the possibilities of contagion between the different Latin American economies, an issue that, literally, would aggravate the risk of concentration. Now I am going to comment on a characteristic of the actions of our entities in Latin America, which does not reduce the aforementioned concentration, but it does considerably tie the risk assumed there. a5 The data in Figure 12 I have just mentioned come from the Bank for International Settlements in Basel (BIS) and are the most frequently used in international comparisons. However, these data do not include the total of "foreign assets", but only what the BIS calls "international claims", which do not take into account what I will call "local activity", which includes the part of local assets in local currency that is financed by local liabilities, also in local currency. a5 The great importance of this "local activity" is precisely one of the characteristics of the expansion of our banking in Latin America, since, as I said before, it has been based on acquiring subsidiaries fully settled and specialized in the activity of retail banking. This is shown in Figure 13, which shows, also with data from the BIS, the relative importance that, for different countries, the two components of "foreign assets" have: "international assets" and "local activity"(1). a5 The greater importance of "local activity", characteristic of acting through subsidiaries, represents advantages of different types that transcend the aforementioned subsidiaries and reach the benefit of the entire group. These advantages range from lower country, liquidity and exchange rate risk, to a more direct knowledge of local customers of assets and liabilities, which, apart from being able to generate commissions for banking services, allows a better management of credit risk, by facilitating both the prior selection of borrowers and a greater capacity to react in the event that credit risk materializes. (1) At the time of the charts (December 2001), when much of the banking activity in Argentina was pseudo-dollarized, this part was not considered "local activity" but "international assets". Argentine crisis a5 To comment on the repercussions of the Argentine crisis on Spanish banks, the obligatory starting point is to quantify what the presence of our entities was in that country at the end of 2001, before the crisis broke out. This is the information summarized in Figure 14. a5 The two large Spanish banking groups owned the fourth and fifth of Argentine banks by size. Although on this date the peso/dlar parity officially continued, using a more realistic exchange rate (1 dar 1.7 pesos), it is obtained that our entities had in Argentina just over 2% of their consolidated assets, equivalent to 8% of the assets in all Latin America; almost 2.5% of the total losses of the two groups, and around 3% of their credit investment. Without taking into account the extraordinary write-downs caused by the crisis, the profits obtained in Argentina were almost 3.5% of the total attributable profit of the two groups. It is therefore a relatively small concentration. a5 The characteristics of the performance of the subsidiaries in this country were similar to those I have already mentioned for the whole of Latin America. Therefore, the risks that can be considered microeconomic were conceptually analogous to those of other countries. Regarding its magnitude, it was generally thought to be lower than the Latin American average, since, before the current crisis began to take shape, the solvency and stability of the Argentine banking system were very high and were considered exemplary in the area, after the rigorous sanitation plan adopted to solve the strong crises induced by the so-called "tequila effect", in the mid-nineties. Consequently, the supervisory measures on this type of risk were also similar to those in the rest of the area, which I will summarize. a5 Since the expansion in Latin America has been based almost exclusively on subsidiaries, these, at a consolidated level, are part of Spanish banking groups, although, at the individual level, they continue to be banks of different nationalities, subject, therefore, to the corresponding national rules and supervisors. a5 In situations of this kind, the distribution of responsibilities proposed by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, and universally accepted, is that the host supervisor (the Latin American, in this case) must ensure the individual solvency of the subsidiaries of foreign groups, in exactly the same way as with respect to the other domestically owned banks under its jurisdiction; for its part, the supervisor of origin (the Bank of Spain, in this case) must ensure the solvency of the consolidable group as a whole. a5 From these differentiated responsibilities, since there are mutual channels of contagion between the entity and the group, the need arises for both supervisors to coordinate their actions bilaterally. Formally, the content of this collaboration is set out in the "memoranda of understanding" that both supervisors usually subscribe. a5 Based on this framework, and given the change in the risk profile that the expansion in Latin America meant for the two large groups, Banco de Espaa has based its consolidated supervision on them on the following principles, which, of course, have been communicated to the parent companies: a) Group culture and management information. The Board of Directors of the parent company must implement an international group culture in terms of its Organization, Management, Internal Information System and Controls. In this sense, the parent companies must effectively assume the functions of controlling the management of their subsidiaries, having exhaustive information and systems based on common computer platforms that allow: on the one hand, monitoring, consolidated accounting harmonization, business analysis and control of its risks; on the other hand, that the Bank of Spain can develop its supervisory responsibilities, based on the information held by the parent company. To this end, an intense internal audit work must be carried out from the Central Services in each of the group's entities, with at least an annual cadence. b) Prudent accounting policies. Spanish banking groups with activity abroad must follow a policy of special prudence, rapidly amortizing goodwill and constituting special provisions that cover possible losses arising even from extreme scenarios. In addition, the inclusion in large Spanish banking groups of companies incorporated in other countries and subject to their own legal and accounting standards requires prior harmonization before their Accounting consolidation, adapting the financial statements of foreign subsidiaries to the minimum Spanish standards through the corresponding adjustments, which must be adequately documented and based on prudential criteria. c) Group solvency and individual solvency. The amount, quality and structure of the group's own resources should be strengthened. As for its distribution among the different countries, each subsidiary must have sufficient own resources to cover its risks, with enough slack to face its growth, and always above local standards. That is to say, although normatively the own resources of the groups are measured on a consolidated basis, an adequate management of the risks advises their distribution among the different components of the group, depending on the location of the risks. d) Domain diagram. The domain diagram representative of the group's control structure should be clear and transparent. e) Autonomy and financial independence. Each subsidiary of a Spanish banking group must be financially independent of the parent and other entities of the group and, therefore, be able to obtain its financing and liquidity with full autonomy. In other words, each entity that needs financing must obtain it from the market and pay the risk premium corresponding to its individual situation. Likewise, the coverage that each subsidiary eventually decides to make of its risks, must be carried out in the market, without the parent company or other entities of the group being its counterparty or guarantor. f) Liquidity control. Each group must devise adequate contingency plans for its consolidated position in the currencies in which it operates. In addition, each subsidiary must have its own system of continuous measurement of its liquidity, providing adequate mechanisms to meet the ordinary needs of liquid funds, and credible contingency plans to deal with extraordinary situations. a5 It is not now possible to carry out an exhaustive analysis of the origins and development of the Argentine crisis. I would like to mention two aspects that I consider particularly relevant. The first concerns the fiscal problems, both of the central government and of the provinces, which, despite their gravity, remained for a long time. masked by placid deficits of less than 3% of GDP. This masking, and the consequent postponement of reforms, were made possible, first, by the initial success of the currency board and the strong growth recorded in the early nineties; Then, after the Mexican crisis of 1995 and the consequent "tequila effect", for the income derived from the privatization process. When these supports were exhausted, without having carried out reforms that guaranteed fiscal sustainability, domestic banking was resorted to first, eroding its then foundations, and, then, when the recession was already a fait accompli, to severe fiscal contractions, which aggravated the recession without solving any of the problems raised. a5 The second issue I want to mention is the maintenance of the fixed parity against giving beyond the initial period of adjustment, which weakens Argentina's competitiveness at a time of strong appreciation of the US currency against the euro, with the euro area being Argentina's main trading partner, and of intense depreciation of the Brazilian real. a5 If this is compounded by the great difficulty of designing and implementing a non-destabilizing de-dollarization process, experience that is unprecedented; the international fall in the price of key Argentine export products; the lack of liberalization of internal markets, particularly labour markets; The scarce openness to the outside world of the Argentine economy, which prevents it from benefiting from the current depreciations of its currency, and the radical and growing disagreement between the population and the political class, there are enough elements to understand what is specific about the Argentine crisis and the difficulties that are posing its overcoming. a5 When it comes to drawing conclusions, I will mention just three. With regard to the origins of the crisis, the importance of coherence between the exchange rate regime chosen by each country and all its economic policies and institutional structure, since there is no exchange rate regime that, by itself, is capable of protecting an economy against financial crises, if it is not accompanied by adequate and coherent policies. a5 Regarding the treatment that will end up being given to the crisis, that the existence of an open, stable institutional framework, respectful of property rights is the only way to generate confidence and support from international financial markets that allows financial situations, such as that of Argentina, of serious insufficiency of domestic savings. a5 With regard to the supervisory approach, something as obvious as the importance of sufficiently assessing institutional risks, both when taking external expansion decisions, especially if it is concentrated in developing countries, and afterwards, providing subsidiaries and the solvency group itself with sufficient margin of slack to deal with adverse situations, even unexpected, and attempts to solve them difficult to conceive in more developed and stable institutional environments. a5 In any case, what is clear is that the Argentine crisis has occurred; whereas their treatment has been affected by numerous hesitations, contradictions, backward gears, rules with retroactive effect, etc.; and that its final resolution is still pending and subject to numerous incinitas. a5 What have our entities done so far in this environment? I believe that the answer to this question is that they have done what was appropriate, that is, to provision for all of the losses already expressed and those foreseeable at the moment, with the maximum Prudence and, literally, with not a few uncertainties. Following these criteria, the entire net book value of the Argentine banking subsidiaries has been provisioned in the consolidated balance sheets; all goodwill that was outstanding for amortization; all cross-border risk provisionable according to the regulations of the Bank of Spain; the total subordinated debt capitalized this same a; all intergroup support granted in 2002 and half of previous support; and, finally, the estimated unrealised losses in local financing, both escrow and private, granted by the subsidiaries. a5 The total provisioned is currently close to the 2,825 million euros, a figure that is approximately equivalent to 35% of the total assets of all classes in Argentina. This amount comes entirely from the income statement (a very important part of it having been returned to the end of 2001) with the exception of depreciation due to devaluation of investments, which, due to the requirements of accounting regulations, has been charged against reserves. a5 In summary, the impact of the Argentine crisis has had no impact on the solvency of the affected groups or, even less, on the banking system as a whole. Spanish, and practically no effect in macroeconomic terms (1% of foreign trade, the 3 most important companies .Telefonica, Repsol YPF and Endesa. represent less than 2% of GFCF in Spain). a5 This is confirmed by Figure 15, which shows that our banks maintain a large surplus of own resources, which has increased in 2001, above the legal minimum of 8%, both with the criteria of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision and with the criteria of our prudential regulation, much more demanding. Its impact on the results has been moderate, given that the main reason why the profits of our banks have grown at a slower pace than in previous years is due to the change in the phase of the economic cycle. At the international level, the comparison is even more favourable, as shown in Figure 16, which shows how bank profits in the main neighbouring countries have varied in 2001 compared with 2000. a5 Finally, it remains to assess whether the sanitation effort made is sufficient. First of all, it must be borne in mind that an assessment of this type requires specifying with Sufficient precision is the expected future scenarios, a subject which, as I have already said, is subject to multiple and important incinitas. On the basis of these, the supervisory answer is almost obvious: we consider the provisions constituted to be sufficient, taking into account the information available today; Otherwise, we would have asked to increase the allocations, since the two groups concerned have sufficient results to meet this request. a5 What do the markets think about this? Figure 17 answers this question. It compares the evolution of the share prices of our two large groups with the performance of the Dow Jones Stoxx 600 Bank sector index, which groups the banks with the largest market capitalization around the world. It is observed that from November 2001 to March 2002, that is, since the Argentine crisis begins to be discounted by the markets until its scope is sufficiently specified, our banks move, in relation to this index, jointly and within the margin 5 points, which means that the markets have not penalized our large groups for the crisis in Argentina. a5 For our entities, the main question for the future posed by the situation in Latin America is whether the Argentine crisis will end up infecting other countries in the area. Honestly, I hope not, but I don't like being a prophet. That's why I prefer to let others speak. In graph 18, Moody's, one of the main rating agencies in the world, shows that the fall in Argentina's rating since the beginning of last year has not contaminated the other countries. For their part, in graph 19, the markets speak directly, highlighting the low contagion power they attribute to the Argentine economy, given the low, and also decreasing, correlation presented by its sovereign differential ("spread") with the main countries of the area. a5 Although perhaps there is no "contagion" in the strictest definition of this phenomenon, the truth is that the situation in Argentina, once a model in the region d0 sovereign suspensions, violation of property rights, political uncertainty, etc. d0 worsens the sentiment of the markets about the region and amplifies the problems of each country. In fact, the relationship of the other countries in the area, in relation to the situation in Argentina, has gone through several phases: at the beginning, and during much of 2001, there was a high correlation between the spreads of the region, with depreciation of exchange rates (that is, there was a certain problem of contagion). Markets feared a repeat of the previous crisis. On the other hand, from October 2001, there was a disengagement from Argentina and the markets clearly discriminated between Argentina and the rest. From April-May 2002, spreads and exchange rate depreciation have widened again, especially in Brazil, due to both domestic and international factors (uncertainties USA, Stock Exchanges, Enron).

Este enmascaramiento, y el consiguiente aplazamiento de las reformas, fueron posibles, primero, por el xito inicial del "currency board" y el fuerte crecimiento registrado a principios de los as noventa; luego, tras la crisis mejicana de 1995 y el consiguiente "efecto tequila", por los ingresos derivados del proceso de privatizaciones. Cuando estos soportes se agotaron, sin haber llevado a cabo reformas que garantizaran la sostenibilidad fiscal, se recurri en primer lugar, a la banca domstica, erosionando sus entonces sidos cimientos, y, luego, cuando la recesi ya era un hecho consumado, a severas contracciones fiscales, que agravaron la recesi sin solucionar ninguno de los problemas planteados.  La segunda cuesti que quiero mencionar es el mantenimiento de la paridad fija frente al dar ms all del perodo inicial de ajuste, que debilitla competitividad argentina en momentos de fuerte apreciaci de la moneda estadounidense frente al euro, siendo la eurozona el principal socio comercial de Argentina, y de intensa depreciaci del real brasile.  Si a esto se ade la gran dificultad de diser e implantar un proceso de desdolarizaci no desestabilizador, experiencia que no tiene precedentes; la cada internacional del precio de los productos clave de las exportaciones argentinas; la nula liberalizacin de los mercados internos, en particular los laborales; la escasa apertura al exterior de la economa argentina, que le impide beneficiarse de las actuales depreciaciones de su moneda, y el radical y creciente desencuentro entre la poblaci y la clase poltica, se tienen suficientes elementos para comprender lo que de especfico tiene la crisis argentina y las dificultades que estn planteando su superacin.  A la hora de sacar consecuencias, icamente mencionar tres. Respecto a los orgenes de la crisis, la importancia que reviste la coherencia entre el rgimen de tipo de cambio elegido por cada pas y el conjunto de sus polticas econmicas y su estructura institucional, ya que no hay rgimen cambiario que, por s mismo, sea capaz de proteger a una economa frente a crisis financieras, si no est acompaado de polticas adecuadas y coherentes.  Respecto al tratamiento que se acabe por dar a la crisis, que la existencia de un marco institucional abierto, estable, respetuoso con los derechos de propiedad es el ico camino para generar la confianza y el respaldo de los mercados financieros internacionales que permita financiera situaciones, como la de Argentina, de grave insuficiencia de ahorro interno.  Respecto al enfoque supervisor, algo tan obvio como la importancia de valorar suficientemente los riesgos institucionales, tanto a la hora de adoptar decisiones de expansi exterior, en especial si se concentra en pases en desarrollo, como despus, dotando a las filiales y al propio grupo de solvencia con suficiente margen de holgura como para hacer frente a situaciones adversas, incluso inesperadas, y a intentos de solucionarlas difcilmente concebibles en entornos institucionales ms desarrollados y estables.  En cualquier caso, lo que es evidente es que la crisis argentina se ha producido; que su tratamiento se ha visto afectado por numerosas vacilaciones, contradicciones, marchas hacia atrs, normas con efecto retroactivo, etc.; y que su resoluci definitiva todava est pendiente y sometida a numerosas incnitas.  Qu han hecho hasta ahora nuestras entidades en este entorno?. Creo que la respuesta a este interrogante es que han hecho lo que corresponda, es decir, provisionar la totalidad, tanto de las prdidas ya manifestadas como de las previsibles en estos momentos, con la mxima prudencia y, licamente, con no pocas incertidumbres. Siguiendo estos criterios, se ha provisionado la totalidad del valor neto contable de las filiales bancarias argentinas en los balances consolidados; todos los fondos de comercio que estaban pendientes de amortizar; todo el riesgo transfronterizo provisionable segn la normativa del Banco de Espaa; el total de la deuda subordinada capitalizada este mismo a; todos los apoyos intergrupo concedidos en 2002 y la mitad de los anteriores; y, finalmente, las prdidas latentes estimadas en la financiaci local, tanto plica como privada, concedida por las filiales.  El total provisionado se acerca, en estos momentos, a los 2.825 millones de euros, cifra que aproximadamente equivale al 35% del total de activos de todas las clases en Argentina. Este importe proviene ntegramente de la cuenta de resultados (habindose retrotrado al cierre de 2001 una parte muy importante del mismo) con la ica excepci de la depreciaci por devaluaci de las inversiones, que, por exigencias de la normativa contable, se ha cargado contra reservas.  En resumen, el impacto de la crisis argentina no ha tenido ninguna incidencia en la solvencia de los grupos afectados ni, menos todava, en el conjunto del sistema bancario espaol, y prcticamente ningn efecto en trminos macroeconmicos (1% del comercio exterior, las 3 empresas ms importantes Telfonica, Repsol YPF y Endesa representan menos del 2% de la FBCF en Espaa).  As lo confirma el grfico 15, que muestra co nuestras entidades mantienen un amplio excedente de recursos propios, que ha aumentado en 2001, sobre el mnimo legal del 8%, tanto con los criterios del Comit de Supervisi Bancaria de Basilea como con los criterios de nuestra regulaci prudencial, mucho ms exigentes. Su repercusi en los resultados ha sido moderada, dado que la principal causa de que los beneficios de nuestros bancos hayan crecido a menor ritmo que en as anteriores se debe al cambio en la fase del ciclo econmico. A nivel internacional, la comparaci todava resulta ms favorable, como pone de manifiesto el grfico 16, en el que se muestra co han variado en 2001, respecto a 2000, los beneficios bancarios en los principales pases de nuestro entorno.  Queda, finalmente, por valorar si el esfuerzo saneador realizado es suficiente. Ante todo, hay que tener en cuenta que una valoraci de este tipo exige concretar con suficiente precisi los escenarios futuros previstos, tema que, como ya he dicho, est sometido a mtiples e importantes incnitas. Partiendo de ellas, la respuesta supervisora es casi obvia: las provisiones constituidas las consideramos suficientes, teniendo en cuenta la informaci hoy disponible; en caso contrario, hubiramos solicitado elevar las dotaciones, ya que los dos grupos afectados cuenta con resultados suficientes para afrontar esta petici.  Qu opinan los mercados a este respecto?. El grfico 17 da respuesta a este interrogante. En l, se compara la evoluci de las cotizaciones de las acciones de nuestros dos grandes grupos con la marcha del ndice sectorial Dow Jones Stoxx 600 Bank, que agrupa a los bancos con mayor capitalizaci burstil de todo el mundo. Se observa que desde noviembre de 2001 hasta marzo de 2002, es decir, desde que la crisis argentina comienza a ser descontada por los mercados hasta que se concreta suficientemente su alcance, nuestros bancos se mueven, en relaci a dicho ndice, de forma conjunta y dentro del margen + 5 puntos, lo que equivale a que los mercados no han penalizado a nuestros grandes grupos por la crisis de Argentina.  Para nuestras entidades, la principal incnita de cara al futuro que plantea la situaci en Latinoamrica es si la crisis argentina acabar por contagiar a otros pases de la zona. Sinceramente, espero que no, pero no me gusta ser profeta. Por eso, prefiero dejar que hablen otros. En el grfico 18, lo hace Moody's, una de las principales agencias calificadoras del mundo, poniendo de manifiesto que la cada en la calificaci de Argentina desde comienzos del a pasado no ha contaminado a los dems pases. Por su parte, en el grfico 19, hablan directamente los mercados, poniendo de manifiesto el escaso poder de contagio que atribuyen a la economa argentina, dada la baja, y adems decreciente, correlaci que presenta su diferencial ("spread") soberano con los principales pases de la zona.  Aunque quizs no se est produciendo "contagio" en la definici ms estricta de este feneno, lo cierto es que la situaci de Argentina, en otro tiempo modelo en la regi suspensiones soberanas, quebranto de derechos de propiedad, incertidumbre poltica, etc. , empeora el sentimiento de los mercados sobre la regi y amplifica los problemas propios de cada pas. De hecho, la relaci de los restantes pases del rea, en relaci con la situaci Argentina, ha atravesado diversas fases: al comienzo, y durante buena parte del 2001, se produjo una alta correlaci entre los spreads de la regi, con depreciaci de los tipos de cambio (es decir, s hubo un cierto problema de contagio). Los mercados temieron una repetici de la anterior crisis. En cambio, a partir de octubre de 2001, se produjo un desenganche de Argentina y los mercados discriminaron claramente entre Argentina y el resto. A partir de abril-mayo de 2002, se han vuelto a ampliar spreads y depreciaci del tipo de cambio, especialmente en Brasil, debido tanto a factores domsticos como internacionales (incertidumbres USA, Bolsas, Enron).

Title: Closing conference at the XXIX Conference on Financial Markets
text: Jaime Caruna Governor of the Bank of Spain CLOSING CONFERENCE OF THE GOVERNOR OF THE BANK OF SPAIN, JAIME CARUANA, AT THE XXIX CONFERENCE ON FINANCIAL MARKETS It is a great satisfaction for me to come to Zaragoza to close these days organized by Intermoney, which already have a long tradition and constitute a discussion forum of great interest to all participants in the financial markets. Let me take this opportunity to set out some thoughts on the evolution of monetary policy in the euro area and the recent trajectory of the Spanish economy, dwelling on the new challenges that it will have to face in the near future. The introduction of euro notes and coins at the beginning of this year was perhaps the most visible sign of the establishment of a monetary union in Europe. The exchange of the old national currencies - which has been logistically complex and whose preparations and implementation have absorbed many resources in recent years - was remarkably successful thanks to the work and collaboration provided by the many actors involved in the process, among which financial institutions have played an essential role. I believe that the absence of relevant incidents during the transition period and the good reception of the new currency by European citizens - despite the discomfort of changing the usual unit of account - are the best reward for these efforts. Although for a large part of society monetary union has only been perceived as a reality since 1 January this year, when we have been able to start using the euro in all our daily transactions, the single currency already has, as you know, a history of almost three and a half years, a period in which it has been used in an increasing number of financial transactions in all parts of the world. It has been chosen as the denomination currency for a substantial volume of issues of various financial instruments and has come to occupy a significant part of the portfolios of the main international investors and the foreign reserves of most central banks. Since 1 January 1999, the countries forming Economic and Monetary Union have shared a common monetary policy, the orientation of which has been determined by the priority objective, laid down in the Treaty on European Union, of ensuring price stability. This is due to the conviction - which emanates from both experience and academic research - that, in order to maximize welfare, economic policy actions should not be determined by the attempt to achieve high short-term growth rates at any price, but should focus on achieving sustained and lasting output increases, that is, they should seek, above all, to increase the economy's growth potential. Monetary policy also has limited capacity to modulate cyclical fluctuations in the short term, while it is an effective tool for influencing price developments over the medium term. From the point of view of collective welfare, it is appropriate to assign to monetary policy the mission of achieving and maintaining price stability, since inflation distorts the allocation of resources and thus reduces the potential output of the economy. To facilitate the achievement of this objective, the EU Treaty incorporates a number of principles that inspired the institutional framework for the Eurosystem's monetary policy and its current strategy. Thus, it was advocated that the monetary authorities have a high degree of independence from the public authorities, so as to avoid interference that would alter the normal development of the decision-making process. As a counterweight to this autonomy, it was considered essential for the Eurosystem to be transparent and accountable to society on the extent and manner of carrying out the tasks entrusted to it, explaining the reasons behind its decisions and regularly presenting its assessment of the economic situation. In this respect, I would like to emphasise that transparency should not only be seen as the trade-off required in a democratic system for granting functional independence to a public institution, but is also crucial from the point of view of the effectiveness of monetary policy. It should be stressed that the better actors understand the elements on which the Central Bank relies to make its decisions, the easier it will be for agents' expectations to be based on sound foundations and to evolve in a manner consistent with the objectives of the monetary authority, thus facilitating the proper functioning of the monetary policy transmission mechanism. I believe that the Eurosystem has already shown a proven interest in improving its communication policy. The need to maintain an adequate flow of information with the public on the analysis underpinning decisions is reinforced by the absence of precise quantitative targets in the Eurosystem's strategic outline. Indeed, although monetary policy has an unequivocal priority objective, on which the assessment of the Central Bank's actions must be based, the definition of price stability adopted by the ECB incorporates an appreciable dose of flexibility. In particular, it is established as a medium-term target, therefore compatible with increases in prices that temporarily place inflation above the reference, of 2%, which contains the definition itself. Moreover, the ECB has a certain margin of manoeuvre to decide on the distribution over time of the necessary adjustments in intervention rates in order to adapt the tone of monetary policy to that required for the fulfilment of the objective. It is therefore consistent with the ECB's mandate that such strategic decisions are taken, as is done in practice, taking into account their foreseeable impact on general economic conditions. But, in addition to a certain degree of strategic flexibility, the European Central Bank needs, as a necessary ingredient for the proper performance of its function, sufficient analytical flexibility. This is especially necessary in a world, such as the current one, where changes in economic relations can be rapid and abrupt, due, among other factors, to the growing interdependence of economies and the incorporation of recent technological advances in production processes, whose effects on the development of economic activity are still far from being able to be accurately evaluated. In the case of Europe, moreover, economic integration and the single currency have meant, in all likelihood, a structural change in the determinants of the economic decisions of the agents that makes it difficult, to a greater extent than usual, to use models estimated with historical data in the design of monetary policy. Under these conditions, it is logical for the Eurosystem to use a pragmatic approach that allows for a plurality of indicators and technical tools that can facilitate the assessment of the economy's inflation outlook, and that avoids the mechanistic use of a specific analytical model or scheme. I believe that the monetary policy decisions taken by the Eurosystem - especially in the last year - are a good example of this flexibility to which I have just referred. During 2001, the euro area was impacted by a number of shocks, which were largely common to the world economy, such as higher oil prices, falling stock prices, the crisis in the high-tech and telecommunications sector, and the slowdown in world trade. Finally, the events of September 11 caused a sharp drop in the confidence of businesses and families around the world. Some of these shocks, such as that of oil, together with others specific to the European economy, such as those affecting the livestock sector, led to a marked increase in inflation observed during 2000 and the first months of 2001, coinciding with the first symptoms of weakening activity. Under these conditions, despite the The deterioration of the inflationary situation, the consideration of the eminently transitory nature of the shocks suffered and the signs of a slowdown in domestic demand led the ECB to relax its tone of monetary policy, first modestly in May and August, and then, more intensely, in September and November, following the terrorist attacks in the US and the consequent further deterioration in growth prospects. In addition, an acceleration of M3, which is the monetary aggregate chosen as the main indicator of liquidity developments in the euro area, was observed during 2001. The Eurosystem, however, avoided a mechanistic interpretation of the progressive increase in the deviation in the face of M3 growth and the 4.5% reference value established for this variable. On the contrary, the analysis of the data concluded that, to a large extent, this behaviour of liquid assets was the result of the climate of uncertainty in the financial markets, which had driven portfolio shifts from riskier and less liquid investments d0 such as equities d0 to liquid assets included in the definition of M3. This meant that the sharp increase in this aggregate did not entail the anticipation of potentially inflationary spending decisions, so the evolution of the monetary indicator did not question the advisability of relaxing the tone of monetary policy. At the present time, a complex economic situation is once again present, in which the medium-term assessment of the inflation outlook is, as is usually the case in periods of change in the cyclical phase of the economy, particularly difficult. The latest indicators on activity suggest that the slowdown bottomed out at the end of last year and detect a gradual increase in growth in the euro area, although uncertainties remain about the intensity and extent of the recovery. On the other hand, the recent trajectory of inflation has been worse than expected, although, again, the factors explaining this relative deterioration seem, in principle, transitory. These are the cases of the evolution of the price of crude oil and the possible inflationary effects of the swap process, which, although limited, could be somewhat higher than initially estimated. In the coming months, the Eurosystem will therefore need to remain particularly vigilant in order to ensure compatibility between the tone of monetary policy and the prospects for maintaining price stability. Therefore, wage trends are very relevant, since a break in the moderation pattern of recent years would have a persistent upward impact on the inflation rate. They are not It conceals the fact that wage negotiations in some countries offer somewhat worrying results in this regard. In line with the previous argument, the Governing Council of the European Central Bank at yesterday's meeting, decided not to move interest rates, and in the statement I think three basic ideas can be highlighted: Firstly, despite the latest inflation estimate that represents a drop to 2% in May, the evolution of prices has been worse than expected and the prospects are now less satisfactory than was assumed a few months ago. Second, although the data that are emerging are consistent with the expected scenario of a gradual recovery, the economic outlook maintains elements of uncertainty. Consequently, it argued the need to accumulate more evidence before a full assessment of inflationary risks in the medium term could be made, and stressed the importance of the transitory elements of past price increases not becoming entrenched in our economies. Therefore, the decision was not to move interest rates and remain vigilant to the evolution of the factors that determine the inflation outlook. In any case, the level of interest rates has been and continues to be conducive to an increase in the dynamism of economic activity. From the decision taken in May 2001 to cut interest rates for the first time in the last phase of cyclical slowdown until November, when the ECB applied the last cut, interest rates on the main refinancing operations fell by 150 basis points, bringing real rates close to the lowest levels of recent decades in all the economies that form the EMU. It is undeniable that these monetary conditions have helped to moderate the scope and reduce the duration of the cyclical slowdown. Thus, despite the sharp slowdown in activity, the period of relative weakness in productive activity seems to have been brief and in some countries, including Spain, output has continued to show positive growth rates. In fact, and with this I come to the second part of my speech, if we look closely at the recent evolution of the Spanish economy, we observe that, in recent years, it has shown a more favourable behavior than in previous episodes. In particular, contrary to what had been a regularity of the business cycle in Spain, the slowdown has not prevented maintaining growth rates of output and employment above the EMU averages, so that the process of real convergence towards the highest levels of per capita income in other European countries has not stopped. Behind this change in behaviour are several factors, including the maintenance of a high degree of macroeconomic stability - achieved through nominal convergence and subsequent accession to EMU and progress in fiscal consolidation - relative wage moderation and the implementation of structural reforms in goods and factor markets. These elements meant that during the period of strong GDP growth between 1997 and 2000, large macroeconomic imbalances did not accumulate, as in previous expansionary periods, which, in the past, had to be cleaned up in the phases of slowdown, causing intense falls in demand and employment. In this way, the favourable evolution of the Spanish economy responds, in part, to structural factors associated with the new institutional framework in which it is inserted and which, by themselves, should contribute to facilitating permanent improvements in the well-being of citizens. However, the maintenance of high growth rates in recent years is also the consequence of the expansionary effect of the very process of adapting our economy to the new environment, which should gradually give way to factors of a more stable nature in order to continue advancing in real convergence at a rate no lower than the current one. In particular, the substantial decline in nominal and real interest rates and the improvement in income prospects brought about by EMU membership has led to an increase in the value of private sector wealth and favoured a sharp increase in the indebtedness of households and non-financial corporations. which has resulted in notable increases in consumption and, to a lesser extent, investment. This increase in the use of external financing by agents should be interpreted as a reasonable adaptation of their decisions to the new scenario, where both lower financial costs and better revenue prospects allow the sustainability of higher debt ratios. In fact, it can be seen that the acceleration in the demand for external financing from the private sector in Spain has only brought its debt-to-GDP ratio closer to the higher levels of other European countries. At the same time, the burdens that this greater indebtedness entails, both in terms of interest payments and in terms of amortization of the principal, have increased, in terms of income. available, only moderately, as a result of lower interest rates. However, although the equity position of the private sector has not suffered an appreciable deterioration, given the prospects presented by our economy, the changes in its composition are illustrative from the point of view of economic analysis. Thus, while EMU entry tends to reduce the size and frequency of adverse income or debt cost shocks in general, increased indebtedness necessarily increases agents' exposure to such shocks. On the other hand, to the extent that much of the increase in debt has materialized in the acquisition of real estate, in the case of households, and of participations in foreign companies, in the case of companies, the financial position of the sector is, logically, influenced by the fluctuations experienced by the value of these assets. Finally, although, as I have said, the financial burden, in terms of income, has hardly increased, we can expect a greater sensitivity of consumption and investment to factors that cause an additional increase in the effort required to meet the financial commitments acquired. In any case, there is no doubt that the greater indebtedness of the private sector has helped to sustain domestic demand in recent years, favouring the Spanish economy to grow at a faster rate than that of the euro area, even in a period - such as 2001 - of slowdown. However, increases in indebtedness such as those observed are not sustainable indefinitely. Therefore, it is necessary to ask ourselves about the factors that may allow the Spanish economy to maintain high growth rates, which allow further progress in the process of real convergence. In this sense, the evidence accumulated in recent years offers some elements that invite, at least, reflection. A first element is the performance of investment in capital goods, which showed modest dynamism in the last cycle, despite low interest rates, the favourable trend in the economy's final demand and the spread of new technologies linked to information technology and telecommunications. A very modest increase in labour productivity has also been observed. To some extent, the evolution of this variable reflects a more intensive use of available labour as a result of the reforms undertaken in the labour market, which have allowed a better use of the relative endowment of productive factors of our economy. However, the limited dynamism of investment in equipment in some sectors could make it difficult, in the medium term, to continue the pattern of high growth and strong job creation. In fact, the persistence of an inflation differential with the euro zone points to the possible appearance, in the future, of a problem of competitiveness of the Spanish economy. Although the causes of this differential are diverse, the phenomenon of dual inflation, characterized by significantly higher inflation in sectors protected from competition than that generally shown by other EMU countries and domestic sectors producing tradable goods, has recently regained strength. Resolving these problems requires the continuation of a stability-oriented macroeconomic policy, but also the adoption of further structural reforms. Considering that monetary policy can only respond to the problems posed by the euro area as a whole, and without forgetting the contribution that budgetary policy must make - maintaining sound finances, promoting investment and efficiency in public spending, and eliminating tax distortions - it seems clear that the bulk of efforts must be concentrated on removing the barriers that damage the adjustment mechanisms of the economy and They discourage the expansion and modernization of the productive apparatus. The aim should therefore be to create an investment-friendly environment that promotes productivity and employment growth and improves the adaptability of enterprises to changes in the economic environment. I believe that the extent to which our economy can take full advantage of the considerable opportunities that have opened up with our integration into EMU depends crucially on our ability to meet these challenges. In the development of these challenges, financial markets play a fundamental role. Over the last year, they have shown a remarkable degree of resilience in the face of all the shocks to which they have been subjected and have therefore contributed to the favourable performance of the economy as a whole. The situation of synchronized slowdown in the main economies was joined by such important and varied shocks as those derived from sharp rises in oil prices, the rapid correction of the so-called technological bubble, impacts on the food sector such as foot-and-mouth disease and mad cow disease, on September 11, crisis in Turkey and Argentina, Enron and other major corporate crises. As I said, in the face of these disturbances, the financial markets have functioned satisfactorily, showing the importance of the progress made in terms of market integration, improvements in negotiating capacity, progress in risk management and diversification, in the solvency of its main operators and in terms of transparency. But there have also been shadows in the functioning of the financial markets, I refer to the set of weaknesses highlighted in the so-called Enron case. The relevance and significance of this case is due to the fact that the problems highlighted are not specific to a specific case; on the contrary, the Enron case presents a set of weaknesses of a more institutional and systemic nature, which in one way or another have manifested themselves in other companies and markets; also in some respects, in ours. This case has been analyzed by other speakers in these days and therefore I would only like to add that its analysis should serve as a stimulus for all - companies, regulators, supervisors, analysts and auditors - to seek the most appropriate answers to the problems it poses. The effective good governance of the entities with structures and culture that supports it, the appropriate resolution of conflicts of interest, accounting practices that respond to the principles of prudence and reflection of economic reality, practices of consolidation of the relevant structures of the group that appropriately reflect its risks, quality information transmitted with transparency to the market and analyzed independently by analysts, etc. They are indispensable elements for maintaining confidence and the proper functioning of financial markets. Let me now turn to the last part of my speech, on development in the Spanish financial markets. During the period since the last edition of these conferences, the Spanish financial markets have achieved remarkable achievements in their process of adaptation to the changes registered in Europe. Let us briefly recall the achievements to which I am referring. In June 2001, the "Protocol of Spanish Markets" was signed, which laid the foundations for the integration of the different securities markets and the various Spanish registration, clearing and settlement systems. Eight months later, in February 2002, "Bolsas y Mercados Espa96oles" was formally constituted, the corporate area in which the integration should take place. Naturally, such a broad integration effort has had to develop at different stages. Thus, let us remember that in July of last year the efforts of MEFF, AIAF and SENAF had already borne fruit with the creation of the holding company that grouped these three companies. On the other hand, around the same dates, an important step was also taken in the process of creating the future central securities depository of Spain, when the two main systems of registration and settlement of public and private fixed income that operated in our country were unified under the platform of the Public Debt Book-Entry Center. As a result of all this process, in the near future the holding company "Bolsas y Mercados Espa96oles" will integrate the Citrus Futures market (FC&M), the MEFF-AIAF-SENAF holding, the Securities Clearing and Settlement Service, as well as the Barcelona, Bilbao, Madrid and Valencia Stock Exchanges. The Central de Anotaciones de Deuda P9cblica -CADE- will be incorporated as soon as the parliamentary processing of the Law on Measures to Reform the Financial System is concluded, which must authorize the effective "merger" in the future Iberclear of the central depository managed by the Bank of Spain with the Securities Clearing and Settlement Service. In any case, it should be noted that the Promoter Iberclear has developed the preparatory work that was entrusted to it as the driving company of the future systems management company of the holding. The Bank's special interest in this latest milestone in the integration of Spanish markets will merit specific consideration at a later stage. But first allow me to briefly expose my perception of the context in which the holding company "Bolsas y Mercados Espa96oles" arises. Stock markets around the world have been undergoing profound transformations in recent years as a result of two main forces: globalization and the revolution in information and communication technologies. In Europe, moreover, the launch of the euro has boosted the urgency of a common financial space. The increase in competition that these events have generated has accentuated, in turn, the trend towards the consolidation of the national offer of securities contracting and post-trading services. In short, the "market of markets", a concept in itself elusive, has taken shape in our economic acquis. In this concept we encompass approaches as diverse as the (later failed) merger project between Deutsche B9arse and the London Stock Exchange, the expansion of Euroclear and the Paris Stock Exchange through Euronext horizontally integrating homogeneous sets of contracting or uniform blocks of registration and settlement in independent and specialized companies, the sustained growth of MTS in Europe as a market dedicated solely to the negotiation of public debt or the vertical integration adopted by Deutsche B9arse. In the first presentations of this morning, these aspects have been discussed with the intervention of relevant protagonists in these projects. The diversity of strategies I have outlined shows that the organizational model to which the stock market industry must respond is still an open question. Sometimes, even the role of the various actors does not seem to be clearly defined, as evidenced by the recent controversies in Europe regarding the practices of "internalisation" of orders arising from the project to concentrate the trading of orders on organised securities markets, to the detriment of less formal securities trading systems. And this lack of definition as to the model of the markets, it should be stressed, is not only a European feature. The echoes that reach us from the United States confirm the absence of unequivocal paradigms on this issue. In this context of uncertainty about the future model of integration of European securities markets, the initiative taken by the Spanish markets to equip themselves with size can only be welcomed. It is clear that this directly strengthens its negotiating power for any hypothetical future alliance. However, along with the advantages of this important project, it is important to bear in mind risks that we must avoid. First of all, it should be noted that the acquisition of dimension cannot become an objective in itself, but must be an instrument for improving management. The increase in size could create a purely transitory fiction of success if it does not materialize in strategies, practical advances and concrete results in the improvement of the management and organization of the different grouped companies. Secondly, the corporate structure in the form of a holding company presented by the "Bolsa y Mercados Espa96oles" project should not constitute an impediment to carry out an integral management of the same, taking advantage of the synergies and economies of scale underlying the markets and systems. Judging by the tone of consensus that has presided over the formation of the holding, the best omens in that regard seem to be justified. Finally, let us remember that financial markets can only operate on the basis of transparency and the public's full confidence in an impeccable track record. In this sense, it seems desirable that the creation of the holding company of the Spanish markets and its eventual IPO should be used to increase the confidence in it of the final investors. With this I want to emphasize that the care for the public good that must govern the operation of an official organized market and the level of demand demanded by the supervisors should not be substantially altered by the constitution of the holding. Allow me, now, in line with the previous caution, to explain what the role of the Bank of Spain is in this project. Currently, the Bank has a representative on the Board of Directors of the holding. Naturally, our presence in this management body is a foretaste of the participation that we will maintain in its capital, once the transfer and integration of CADE in the conglomerate of the Spanish markets has taken place. That presence in the capital of the holding company seeks to reflect the contribution of the Bank's assets and, at the same time, to promote an orderly transition in the management of securities registration, clearing and settlement systems. El especial inters para el Banco de este ltimo hito en la integracin de los mercados espaoles merecer unas consideraciones concretas ms adelante. Pero antes permtanme que exponga brevemente mi percepcin del contexto en el que surge el holding "Bolsas y Mercados Espaoles". Los mercados de valores de todo el mundo vienen experimentando en los ltimos aos profundas transformaciones como resultado de dos fuerzas principales: la globalizacin y la revolucin en las tecnologas informticas y de comunicaciones. En Europa, adems, el lanzamiento del euro ha potenciado la urgencia de un espacio financiero comn. El aumento de la competencia que estos hechos han generado ha acentuado, a su vez, la tendencia hacia la consolidacin de la oferta nacional de servicios de contratacin y postcontratacin de valores. En definitiva, el "mercado de mercados", un concepto en s mismo escurridizo, ha tomado cuerpo en nuestro acerbo econmico. En este concepto englobamos planteamientos tan diversos como el (posteriormente fallido) proyecto de fusin entre Deutsche Brse y la London Stock Exchange, la expansin de Euroclear y de la Bolsa de Pars a travs de Euronext integrando horizontalmente conjuntos homogneos de contratacin o bloques uniformes de registro y liquidacin en sociedades independientes y especializadas, el crecimiento sostenido de MTS en Europa como mercado dedicado nicamente a la negociacin de deuda pblica o la integracin vertical adoptada por la Deutsche Brse. En las primeras ponencias de esta maana se han debatido estos aspectos con la intervencin de protagonistas relevantes en estos proyectos. La diversidad de estrategias que he apuntado muestra que el modelo de organizacin al que debe responder la industria de los mercados de valores es una cuestin todava abierta. En ocasiones, ni siquiera el papel de los distintos actores parece estar claramente definido, como demuestran las recientes polmicas suscitadas en Europa respecto a las prcticas de "internalizacin" de rdenes provocadas por el proyecto de concentrar la contratacin de rdenes en los mercados organizados de valores, en detrimento de sistemas menos formales de negociacin de ttulos. Y esta indefinicin en cuanto al modelo de los mercados, conviene subrayarlo, no es nicamente un rasgo europeo. Los ecos que nos llegan de Estados Unidos confirman la ausencia de paradigmas inequvocos sobre esta cuestin. En este contexto de incertidumbre sobre el modelo futuro de integracin de los mercados de valores europeos, la iniciativa adoptada por los mercados espaoles de dotarse de tamao no puede ser sino bienvenida. Resulta evidente que con ello se refuerza directamente su poder negociador de cara a cualquier hipottica alianza futura. Sin embargo, junto con las ventajas de este importante proyecto conviene tener presente riesgos que debemos evitar. En primer lugar, cabe sealar que la adquisicin de dimensin no puede convertirse en un objetivo en s mismo, sino que debe ser un instrumento de mejora en la gestin. El aumento de tamao podra crear una ficcin de xito puramente transitorio si no se materializa en estrategias, avances prcticos y resultados concretos en la mejora de la gestin y de la organizacin de las distintas sociedades agrupadas. En segundo lugar, la estructura corporativa en forma de holding que presenta el proyecto "Bolsa y Mercados Espaoles", no debiera constituir un impedimento para efectuar una gestin integral del mismo aprovechando las sinergias y economas de escala subyacentes en los mercados y sistemas. A juzgar por el tono de consenso que ha presidido la formacin del holding, parecen estar justificados los mejores augurios en ese sentido. Finalmente, recordemos que los mercados financieros solo pueden funcionar sobre la base de la transparencia y de la plena confianza del pblico en una trayectoria impecable. En este sentido, parece deseable que la creacin del holding de los mercados espaoles y su eventual salida a Bolsa debieran aprovecharse para acrecentar la confianza en el mismo de los inversores finales.
