Con ello quiero destacar que el cuidado del bien pblico que debe presidir el funcionamiento de un mercado organizado oficial y el nivel de exigencia demandado por los supervisores no debieran verse sustancialmente alterados por la constitucin del holding. Permtanme, ahora s, que, al hilo de la cautela anterior, explique cul es el papel del Banco de Espaa en este proyecto. Actualmente, el Banco cuenta con un representante en el Consejo de Administracin del holding. Naturalmente, nuestra presencia en ese rgano de direccin constituye un anticipo de la participacin que mantendremos en su capital, una vez que se haya producido el traspaso e integracin de CADE en el conglomerado de los mercados espaoles. Pues bien, esa presencia en el capital del holding trata de recoger la aportacin de activos del Banco y de promover, al tiempo, una transicin ordenada en la gestin de los sistemas de registro, compensacin y liquidacin de valores. Para entender ms claramente este argumento, conviene evocar brevemente los antecedentes del proceso de consolidacin de los sistemas de postcontratacin de valores en Espaa. Desde su creacin, en 1987, el Mercado de Deuda Pblica Anotada ha estado estructurado en torno a CADE, la Central de Anotaciones, un sistema de registro, compensacin y liquidacin que ha recibido el reconocimiento nacional e internacional. Este logro ha sido posible, obviamente, gracias al impulso comn de todas las partes implicadas: el Tesoro Pblico espaol, los miembros del mercado de deuda y el Banco de Espaa. Los nuevos tiempos no han alterado la adecuacin de las soluciones tcnicas de acuerdo a las cuales ha venido siendo gestionado CADE. S resulta algo desfasada, sin embargo, la fragmentacin bajo la que opera en nuestro pas la industria del depsito central de valores, en contraste con la consolidacin que ya hace aos se viene registrando en Europa. En ese contexto, el Banco de Espaa acord, junto con el SCLV, la creacin en junio de 2000 de Iberclear, cuyo papel de promocin ya he mencionado anteriormente. Me interesa destacar de nuevo que el enfoque tcnico desde el que se concibe la gestin de un depositario central y de un sistema de liquidacin no ha variado. En realidad, los sucesivos informes de expertos que, desde distintas perspectivas, han analizado la problemtica de la liquidacin de valores han reforzado nuestra conviccin en la conveniencia de no supeditar la liquidacin de los ttulos a su contratacin y de aplicar los estndares ms modernos a los procesos de registro y anotacin. Ello nos permitir mejorar el asiento de las operaciones transfronterizas y nos dar la base operativa para crear una cmara de contrapartida que cubra no solo derivados, sino tambin valores de renta fija y variable. Es de sobra conocida la importancia que se concede a las contrapartidas centrales en la arquitectura de los mercados financieros europeos. No voy a insistir ms en ello en estos momentos. Tan solo deseo recordar con este ejemplo un principio ms general: la armonizacin de la infraestructura de nuestros mercados con los estndares internacionales exige aceptar compromisos, y cambios y la creacin del holding es un magnfico augurio en este sentido. En el Banco de Espaa estamos convencidos de que los sistemas espaoles de registro, compensacin y liquidacin de valores tienen la capacidad y la potencialidad suficientes para ofrecer servicios de calidad y adaptados a los nuevos tiempos. Naturalmente, este es un reto al que el Banco de Espaa sigue brindando todo su apoyo. Mientras tanto, debemos animar desde aqu a que Iberclear aborde la ltima fase de su proyecto, en la que se debern comenzar a adoptar las medidas e iniciativas que han sido objeto de preparacin mientras ha actuado como promotora.

Title: Appearance in the Budget Committee of the Congress of Deputies
text: Jaime Caruna Governor of the Bank of Spain APPEARANCE OF THE GOVERNOR OF THE BANK OF SPAIN IN THE BUDGET COMMITTEE OF THE CONGRESS OF DEPUTIES A year ago, the world economy was going through a very delicate period, as a result of the dramatic events of the eleventh of September 2001. Subsequently, both in the United States and in Europe, the phase of sluggish productive activity began to overcome relatively quickly, despite the direct impact of terrorist attacks on relevant sectors and the deterioration caused in consumer and investor confidence around the world. However, the recovery phase has begun with little vigour in most countries, with the exception of some of the economies of Southeast Asia. The low dynamism of most advanced economies today is partly linked to sharp falls in prices in major international stock markets, increased uncertainty and risk aversion in financial markets, and international political tension that has slowed the recovery of confidence and led to a significant rebound in oil prices. For its part, the Latin American subcontinent has been subjected in recent months to tensions, which have highlighted the structural weaknesses of some countries, and the vulnerability generated by dependence on foreign savings in a large part of the countries in the area. The high volatility of world stock markets and international political uncertainty make it difficult to assess the prospects for the world economy for the near future. In principle, the most likely scenario is that activity will continue on the path of recovery that has begun, once the adverse effects of the stock market crisis are exhausted, although the risks of a more unfavourable development are not negligible. In this context, the evolution of the euro area economy has experienced a lower dynamism than expected only a few months ago. Although the GDP growth rate seems to have reached its cyclical low in the fourth quarter of last year, the pace at which the recovery has begun has been very modest, with the area's GDP unlikely to increase by more than 1% in the current year. This low level of activity is, above all, the consequence of the direct exposure of the EMU economy to the international stock market crisis and its impact on its export markets. The sharp correction in European stock markets d0 higher than the US so far this year d0 is partly due to the widespread effects of the US stock market crisis, although it also reflects some specific factors. Thus, it has been notorious the difficulty of some important companies to monetize expensive strategic operations, such as mergers or acquisitions, or obtaining third-generation mobile telephony licenses. In addition, the floods that affected much of Central Europe last summer have caused damage to the industrial fabric and deteriorated the financial position of insurance companies, already weakened by the loss of value of their financial assets. Worryingly, gross capital formation in the euro area, with a capital goods component falling at a year-on-year rate of 5% in the second quarter of this year. While this investment sluggishness is largely driven by cyclical factors and the impact of international shocks, it also reflects remaining structural weaknesses that damage the potential profitability of business projects. However, the trajectory of activity in EMU suggests that, from the end of this year or early next year, economic dynamism will increase steadily, so that the area's GDP growth rates will progressively approach those of its potential output, although the risks of a scenario of greater persistence of cyclical weakness should not be underestimated. In this context, the conduct of monetary policy has become somewhat complex. The relatively favourable outlook for price stability over the medium term allowed the ECB to adjust its policy to the cyclical slowdown that the euro area experienced last year. Interest rates were reduced by 1.5 percentage points in 2001 to 3.25% in November, where they remain today. Subsequently, the significant deterioration in the economic situation caused by the evolution of the stock markets, together with the appreciation of the euro, have mitigated, despite the strong growth in liquidity, the inflationary risks that had begun to emerge. Thus, at the last meeting of the Governing Council of the ECB (12 September), it was decided to maintain the current level of interest rates, assessing that their current level was adequately aligned with the balance sheet of risks affecting price stability over the medium term, which is the ECB's priority objective. The public finances of the EMU Member States currently deserve special attention, in view of the difficulties recently shown by some of them - not our own - in meeting their objectives in this area. I believe it is appropriate to reiterate in this Committee on Budgets my conviction that fiscal discipline is an essential ingredient, not only for sustained economic growth, but also for the proper functioning of monetary union. In this sense, the Stability and Growth Pact is an essential tool to promote the necessary orientation of fiscal policies to achieve or maintain balanced budgetary balances, while incorporating sufficient flexibility so that these can be adjusted, in the short term, to the needs of each economy and, in particular, to its cyclical situation. The international and European panorama are conditioning the evolution of the Spanish economy. To the direct impact that is transmitted through the decline in trade flows of goods and services with the rest of the world, we must add the effects of the falls in stock market prices, and the spread of a climate of uncertainty and distrust that retracts the spending decisions of households and the investment plans of companies. Despite this adverse climate, the Spanish economy continues to register positive real growth rates that in the first half of the year have stabilized at 2%. A rate of expansion that, although it has slowed down significantly, is still considerably higher than those registered in most of the countries of our environment, so that, once again, the process of real convergence with the European Union will continue to advance, which is an appropriate reference criterion to assess the behavior of the economy. However, as the external environment has deteriorated, the improvement in the recovery phase has been delayed over time, so it may be necessary to wait until the final months of the year for the Spanish economy to clearly return to a path of expansion, the intensity of which will depend on whether the expectations of recovery of the world economy are confirmed. Thus, the growth of the Spanish economy in the average of 2002 could not exceed 2%, so that it is during the next year when its rate of growth will gradually approach values of the order of 3%, allowing the average rate to exceed 2.5%. The climate of external weakness is manifested in the decline in exports of goods and services and in the cut in the investment plans of companies, with the industrial sector having suffered most directly from the consequences of this situation. They are therefore The components of domestic origin continue to sustain economic growth, among which the dynamism of employment stands out. The fact that the Spanish economy continues to register relatively high employment growth rates in its slowdown phase is an important difference with what happened in previous cycles, in which, as you will recall, there were intense processes of job destruction that ended up plunging the economy into deep recessions. On this occasion, on the contrary, employment is being a key factor in the growth of household disposable income and in the maintenance of spending rates - on consumer goods and services and on the purchase of homes. Household investment in housing continues to experience great strength, which, together with public investment, makes the construction sector the most expansive element in the current situation. But this behavior is also encouraging the price spiral in the housing market d0 which is not exclusive to our economy d0 despite the economic slowdown, introducing a risk factor. In principle, the Spanish economy is in a favourable position to join the global recovery when it is confirmed. The cycle is expected to close with relatively high real GDP growth rates. In addition, employment is a fundamental point of support for the maintenance of activity. The levels of macroeconomic stability achieved in recent years, the consolidation of the balance of public finances, the reforms undertaken in many markets, including the labour market, and wage moderation, are factors that allow us to hope that these new patterns of behaviour will be established. The resurgence experienced by the growth rate of prices in the Spanish economy throughout this year is, however, a cause for concern. There are a variety of reasons, including the rise in the prices of some foods and the rise in crude oil. The growth rate of the CPI at the end of the year will not be far from that recorded at the moment, since, although it is foreseeable that the more stable components of the index will reduce their rate of increase, energy prices are expected to continue to increase as they reflect the base effect that originates as a result of the sharp falls in prices that took place in the final months of last year. year. As these factors subside, as early as 2003, the inflation rate will slow down, but it is necessary that the inflation differential that we maintain with the EMU countries will be persistently reduced because, otherwise, the foundations of competitiveness of the economy will be pierced. The strength that the Spanish economy has maintained d0 even during its recent stage of slowdown d0 together with historically low interest rates, have facilitated the continued increase in the indebtedness of families and companies. In the case of families, the intense recourse to credit in recent years has been associated, basically, with the development of the housing market and the growing appeal to mortgage financing. Although the levels of indebtedness achieved do not differ from the average of the European economies, the pace of growth remains very high, despite the economic slowdown. In turn, corporate indebtedness, in a context of sluggish investment, is closely linked to the foreign asset acquisition operations undertaken in the recent past. In this sense, the problems faced by some Latin American countries are restricting the margin of action of some companies although, on the whole, the financial situation of companies remains solid and profitability ratios high. In short, private sector indebtedness cannot continue to grow at the rates at which it has been doing so, as this would entail a deterioration of its financial situation and an increase in its vulnerability to unexpected shocks. Risks that, if materialized, would erode the future spending capacity of companies and households and therefore limit the internal support of economic growth. It is therefore important that the recovery be compatible with a recovery in private savings and a clear moderation of the use of external financing. From this point of view, an orderly containment of increases in house prices should help curb household indebtedness and preserve their financial position without interfering with their consumption plans. In the macroeconomic scenario described, the 2003 General State Budget renews the commitment to budgetary stability that has been at the heart of fiscal policy in recent years. Its subjection to the Budgetary Stability Law reinforces the elements of discipline necessary to achieve sound public finances that allow, in the face of the appearance of adverse cyclical situations, to use the room for manoeuvre provided by the automatic stabilisers and to keep the public deficit at moderate levels, in line with what is established in the Community commitments. The objective of budgetary balance established by the Budget for 2003 is appropriate, from the point of view of the cyclical position of the Spanish economy, although if the risks of lower growth materialize they could lead to the appearance of a modest deficit. The tone of budgetary policy is also appropriate from the perspective of the commitments made to the Stability and Growth Pact and the challenges that public finances in Spain will have to face in the medium term, since they will reduce the tax burden borne by companies and households and, At the same time, maintain essential public expenditure items to improve the economy's productivity and long-term growth potential. In this sense, the reform of personal income tax is an essential element of the 2003 budget programming, given that it is expected to have beneficial effects on production, employment and disposable income that should lead the Spanish economy to recover its path of potential expansion. The cyclical conditions of this economy are, however, very different from those that prevailed when the last tax reform was undertaken, so it will be very important that, over the next year, its effective cost in terms of reducing revenue is closely monitored. I would like to conclude by reiterating the importance of macroeconomic and financial stability as an essential basis for sustained economic growth. An orientation that has been very fruitful in recent years and that takes on special validity in times of uncertainty and tension in international markets.
text_original: Jaime Caruna Gobernador del Banco de Espaa COMPARECENCIA DEL GOBERNADOR DEL BANCO DE ESPAA EN LA COMISIN DE PRESUPUESTOS DEL CONGRESO DE LOS DIPUTADOS Hace un ao, la economa mundial atravesaba un perodo muy delicado, como consecuencia de los dramticos sucesos del once de septiembre de 2001. Posteriormente, tanto en Estados Unidos como en Europa, la fase de atona de la actividad productiva empez a superarse con relativa rapidez, a pesar del impacto directo de los ataques terroristas sobre sectores relevantes y el deterioro ocasionado en la confianza de consumidores e inversores en todo el mundo. Sin embargo, la etapa de recuperacin se ha iniciado con escaso vigor en la mayor parte de los pases, si exceptuamos algunas de las economas del sudeste asitico. El escaso dinamismo que presentan hoy la mayora de las economas avanzadas est en parte ligado a las fuertes cadas de las cotizaciones en los principales mercados burstiles internacionales, al aumento de la incertidumbre y aversin al riesgo en los mercados financieros, y a la tensin poltica internacional que ha ralentizado la recuperacin de la confianza y ocasionado un repunte significativo del precio del petrleo. Por su parte, el subcontinente latinoamericano ha estado sometido en los ltimos meses a tensiones, que han puesto de manifiesto las debilidades estructurales de algunos pases, y la vulnerabilidad que genera la dependencia del ahorro exterior en gran parte de los pases del rea. La elevada volatilidad que presentan las bolsas mundiales y la incertidumbre poltica internacional, dificultan la evaluacin de las perspectivas de la economa mundial para el futuro prximo. En principio, el escenario ms probable es que la actividad prosiga la senda de recuperacin iniciada, una vez se agoten los efectos adversos de la crisis burstil, aunque los riesgos de una evolucin ms desfavorable no son despreciables. En este contexto, la evolucin de la economa de la zona del euro ha experimentado un dinamismo menor del esperado hace solo unos meses. Aunque la tasa de crecimiento del PIB parece haber alcanzado su mnimo cclico en el cuarto trimestre del pasado ao, el ritmo con el que se ha iniciado la recuperacin ha sido muy modesto, siendo improbable que el PIB del rea aumente ms de un 1% en el ao en curso. Esta escasa expansin de la actividad es, sobre todo, la consecuencia de la exposicin directa de la economa de la UEM a la crisis internacional de las bolsas y a su impacto sobre sus mercados de exportacin. La pronunciada correccin de las bolsas europeas -superior a la estadounidense en lo que va de ao- se debe, en parte, a los efectos generalizados de la crisis burstil americana, aunque refleja tambin algunos factores especficos. As, ha resultado notoria la dificultad de algunas empresas importantes para rentabilizar costosas operaciones estratgicas, como fusiones o adquisiciones, o la obtencin de licencias de telefona mvil de tercera generacin. Adems, las inundaciones que afectaron a gran parte de Europa Central el pasado verano han causado daos en el tejido industrial y deteriorado la posicin financiera de las compaas aseguradoras, ya de por s debilitada por la prdida de valor de sus activos financieros. Resulta preocupante el descenso de la formacin bruta de capital en la zona del euro, cuyo componente de bienes de equipo caa en el segundo trimestre de este ao a una tasa interanual del 5%. Aunque esta atona inversora responde en gran medida a factores cclicos y al impacto de las perturbaciones internacionales, refleja tambin las deficiencias estructurales que subsisten y que daan la rentabilidad potencial de los proyectos empresariales. No obstante, la trayectoria de la actividad en la UEM apunta a que, a partir de finales de este ao o principios del prximo, el dinamismo econmico aumente de modo sostenido, de manera que las tasas de crecimiento del PIB del rea se acerquen progresivamente a las de su producto potencial, aunque no se deben infravalorar los riesgos de un panorama de mayor persistencia de la debilidad cclica. En este marco, la ejecucin de la poltica monetaria ha revestido cierta complejidad. La existencia de unas perspectivas relativamente favorables para la estabilidad de precios a medio plazo, permiti al BCE acomodar su poltica a la etapa de desaceleracin cclica que atraves la zona del euro el pasado ao. As, los tipos de inters se rebajaron en 1,5 puntos porcentuales a lo largo de 2001 hasta alcanzar el 3,25% en noviembre, nivel en el que se mantienen en la actualidad. Posteriormente, el sensible deterioro de la situacin econmica que ocasion la evolucin de las bolsas, junto con la apreciacin del euro, han mitigado, a pesar del fuerte crecimiento de la liquidez, los riesgos inflacionistas que haban empezado a emerger. De esta manera, en la ltima reunin del Consejo de Gobierno del BCE (12 de septiembre), se decidi mantener el nivel actual de los tipos de inters, al valorar que su nivel actual se ajustaba adecuadamente al balance de los riesgos que afectan a la estabilidad de precios a medio plazo, que es el objetivo prioritario del BCE. Las finanzas pblicas de los pases miembros de la UEM merecen en estos momentos una atencin especial, a la vista de las dificultades que recientemente han mostrado algunos de ellos -entre los que no se encuentra el nuestro- para cumplir sus objetivos en este terreno. Creo que es oportuno reiterar en esta Comisin de Presupuestos mi convencimiento de que la disciplina fiscal es un ingrediente imprescindible, no solo para el crecimiento econmico sostenido, sino tambin para el adecuado funcionamiento de la Unin Monetaria. En este sentido, el Pacto de Estabilidad y Crecimiento constituye una herramienta esencial para promover la necesaria orientacin de las polticas fiscales al logro o mantenimiento de saldos presupuestarios equilibrados, al tiempo que incorpora la suficiente flexibilidad para que estos puedan ajustarse, en el corto plazo, a las necesidades de cada economa y, en particular, a su situacin cclica. El panorama internacional y europeo estn condicionando la evolucin de la economa espaola. Al impacto directo que se trasmite a travs del descenso de los flujos comerciales de bienes y servicios con el resto del mundo hay que aadir los efectos de las cadas de las cotizaciones en las bolsas de valores, y la propagacin de un clima de incertidumbre y desconfianza que retrae las decisiones de gasto de las familias y los planes de inversin de las empresas. A pesar de este clima adverso, la economa espaola sigue registrando tasas positivas de crecimiento real que en el primer semestre del ao se han estabilizado en el 2%. Un ritmo de expansin que, aunque se ha desacelerado significativamente, sigue siendo considerablemente ms elevado que los que se registran en la mayora de los pases de nuestro entorno por lo que, un ao ms, continuar avanzando el proceso de convergencia real con la Unin Europea, que es un criterio de referencia adecuado para valorar el comportamiento de la economa. No obstante, a medida que se ha ido deteriorando el entorno exterior, la mejora en la fase de reactivacin se ha ido retrasando en el tiempo, por lo que puede que haya que esperar a los meses finales del ao para que la economa espaola vuelva a tomar con claridad una senda de expansin, cuya intensidad depender de que se vayan viendo confirmadas las expectativas de recuperacin de la economa mundial. As, el crecimiento de la economa espaola en el promedio de 2002 podra no exceder el 2%, de manera que sea a lo largo del prximo ao cuando su tasa de avance vaya aproximndose, paulatinamente, a valores del orden del 3%, permitiendo que la tasa media pueda superar el 2,5%. El clima de debilidad exterior se manifiesta en el descenso de las exportaciones de bienes y servicios y en el recorte en los planes de inversin de las empresas, siendo el sector industrial el que ha sufrido ms directamente las consecuencias de esta coyuntura. Son pues los componentes de origen interno los que siguen sustentando el crecimiento econmico, entre los que destaca el dinamismo del empleo. El que la economa espaola siga registrando tasas de crecimiento del empleo relativamente elevadas en su fase de desaceleracin constituye una importante diferencia con lo que ocurra en ciclos anteriores, en los que, como recordarn, se producan intensos procesos de destruccin de puestos de trabajo que terminaban sumiendo a la economa en recesiones profundas. En esta ocasin, por el contrario, el empleo est siendo un factor clave en el crecimiento de la renta disponible de las familias y en el mantenimiento de unos ritmos de gasto -en bienes y servicios de consumo y en la compra de viviendas- La inversin de las familias en vivienda contina experimentando una gran fortaleza, que, junto con la inversin pblica, hace que el sector de la construccin sea el elemento ms expansivo en la actual coyuntura. Pero este comportamiento est alentando tambin la espiral de precios en el mercado de la vivienda -que no es exclusivo de nuestra economa- a pesar de la desaceleracin econmica, introduciendo un factor de riesgo. En principio, la economa espaola se encuentra en una posicin favorable para incorporarse a la reactivacin mundial cuando sta se confirme. El ciclo se cerrar, previsiblemente, con tasas de crecimiento del PIB real relativamente altas. Adems, el empleo constituye un punto de apoyo fundamental para el sostenimiento de la actividad. Los niveles de estabilidad macroeconmica alcanzados en estos ltimos aos, la consolidacin del equilibrio de las finanzas pblicas, las reformas emprendidas en numerosos mercados, entre ellos el mercado de trabajo, y la moderacin salarial, son factores que permiten confiar en el asentamiento de estas nuevas pautas de comportamiento. El rebrote que ha experimentado la tasa de crecimiento de los precios de la economa espaola a lo largo de este ao es, sin embargo, un motivo de preocupacin. Obedece a razones muy diversas, entre las que cabe mencionar el aumento de los precios de algunos alimentos y las alzas que est experimentando el crudo de petrleo. La tasa de crecimiento del IPC al final del ao no se alejar mucho de la que se registra en este momento, ya que, si bien es previsible que los componentes ms estables del ndice recorten su ritmo de aumento, los precios de la energa se espera que sigan aumentando al recoger el efecto base que se origina como consecuencia de las fuertes cadas de precios que tuvieron lugar en los meses finales del pasado ao. A medida que estos factores vayan remitiendo, ya en el ao 2003, la tasa de inflacin se ir desacelerando, pero es necesario que el diferencial de inflacin que mantenemos con los pases de la UEM se reduzca de forma persistente pues, en otro caso, se estarn horadando las bases de competitividad de la economa. La fortaleza que ha mantenido la economa espaola -incluso, durante su reciente etapa de desaceleracin- junto a tipos de inters histricamente bajos, han facilitado el continuado aumento que ha experimentado el endeudamiento de familias y empresas. En el caso de las familias, el intenso recurso al crdito en estos aos ha estado asociado, bsicamente, con el desarrollo del mercado de la vivienda y la creciente apelacin a la financiacin hipotecaria. Aunque los niveles de endeudamiento alcanzados no difieren de la media de las economas europeas, el ritmo de crecimiento sigue siendo muy elevado, a pesar de la desaceleracin econmica. A su vez, el endeudamiento de las empresas, en un contexto de atona de la inversin, est estrechamente vinculado a las operaciones de adquisicin de activos en el exterior emprendidas en el pasado reciente. En este sentido, los problemas que atraviesan algunos pases latinoamericanos estn restringiendo el margen de actuacin de algunas compaas aunque, en conjunto, la situacin financiera de las empresas sigue siendo slida y las ratios de rentabilidad elevadas. En definitiva, el endeudamiento del sector privado no puede seguir creciendo a los ritmos a los que lo viene haciendo, ya que ello supondra un deterioro de su situacin financiera y un aumento de su vulnerabilidad ante perturbaciones inesperadas. Riesgos que, de materializarse, erosionaran la capacidad futura de gasto de empresas y familias y limitaran, por tanto, el sostenimiento interno del crecimiento econmico. Es importante, por consiguiente, que la reactivacin sea compatible con una recuperacin del ahorro privado y una clara moderacin de la apelacin a la financiacin ajena. Desde este punto de vista, una contencin ordenada de las alzas en el precio de las viviendas debera contribuir a frenar el endeudamiento de las familias y a preservar su posicin financiera sin interferir en sus planes de consumo. En el escenario macroeconmico descrito, los Presupuestos Generales del Estado de 2003 renuevan el compromiso con la estabilidad presupuestaria que ha sido el centro de la poltica fiscal de los ltimos aos. Su sujecin a la Ley de Estabilidad Presupuestaria refuerza los elementos de disciplina necesarios para alcanzar unas finanzas pblicas saneadas que permitan, ante la aparicin de situaciones cclicas adversas, utilizar el margen de maniobra que proporcionan los estabilizadores automticos y mantener el dficit pblico en cotas moderadas, en lnea con lo que establecen los compromisos comunitarios. El objetivo del equilibrio presupuestario que establecen los Presupuestos para el 2003 es apropiado, desde el punto de vista de la posicin cclica de la economa espaola, aunque si se materializasen los riesgos de menor crecimiento podran dar lugar a la aparicin de un modesto dficit. El tono de la poltica presupuestaria tambin es adecuado desde la perspectiva de los compromisos asumidos con el Pacto de Estabilidad y de Crecimiento y de los retos a los que debern enfrentarse las finanzas pblicas en Espaa en el medio plazo, dado que permitirn reducir la carga fiscal que soportan las empresas y las familias y, al mismo tiempo, mantener partidas de gasto pblico esenciales para mejorar la productividad de la economa y su potencial de crecimiento a largo plazo. En este sentido, la reforma del IRPF resulta un elemento esencial de la programacin presupuestaria del 2003, dado que de ella se esperan efectos beneficiosos sobre la produccin, el empleo y la renta disponible que deberan llevar a la economa espaola a recuperar su senda de expansin potencial. Las condiciones cclicas de esta economa son, sin embargo, muy distintas de las que prevalecan cuando se acometi la ltima reforma del impuesto, por lo que ser muy importante que, a lo largo del prximo ao, se realice un seguimiento minucioso de su coste efectivo en trminos de reduccin de la recaudacin. Me gustara terminar reiterando la importancia de la estabilidad macroeconmica y financiera como base imprescindible del crecimiento econmico sostenido. Una orientacin que ha sido muy fructfera en los ltimos aos y que cobra especial validez en momentos de incertidumbre y tensin en los mercados internacionales.

Title: Governor's opening speech LACEA, Palacio de Congresos, October 11, 2002
text: Jaime Caruna Speeches by the Governor Madrid, Palacio de Congresos, 11 de Octubre de 2002 GOVERNOR'S OPENING SPEECH LACEA Ladies and Gentlemen, It is a great honour for me to welcome you to the Annual Meeting of LACEA. I do so in my dual capacity as Governor of the Banco de Espana and President of the Board of Trustees of the Centro de Estudios Monetarios y Financieros (CEMFI), the organiser of this event whose efforts and dedication have been crucial for ensuring the staging of the meeting. LACEA is a relatively young association, created only 10 years ago, but it has already established its credentials in the academic world. I was impressed by the variety, quantity and quality of the papers presented this weekend. The rapid and successful development of LACEA over this short period of time is indicative , in my view, of two facts: the interest among economists in the Latin American region (whose experience and problems are often paradigmatic among emerging markets), and the high calibre of Latin American researchers, whether located in the region or elsewhere. Latin American economies seem to be at a crossroads. After a decade of progress in trade and financial integration, of reforms aimed at enhancing efficiency and of substantial progress in ensuring economic stability, recent crises have introduced some uncertainty to the road ahead in some countries. The crises were a result of domestic shocks in some cases, of external shocks in others, or more frequently of a combination of both. The impact of these shocks was exacerbated by structural vulnerabilities in a number of countries, reflected basically in a strong dependence on foreign capital flows. We should however not overreact to recent crises, serious and painful as they may be. If we look at the sub-continent as a whole taking a longer view, the progress in certain areas over the last decade is remarkable. Macroeconomic stability has, in contrast to a long period of instability, been achieved and maintained in many countries, favoured by sound monetary and fiscal policies; the soundness and efficiency of financial systems have been reinforced; and gains in efficiency, in general, have been observed in many sectors, a process related inter alia to privatisations. Some countries in Latin America seem to be moving remarkably smoothly towards economic integration -in some cases with industrial countries as partners-, a sound macroeconomic setting and progress in welfare. Identifying the key features and factors underlying recent experiences, successful or otherwise, in certain countries is a key contribution researchers can make towards a better understanding of economic development in Latin America. When we look at Latin American economic policies from a European perspective, there is a risk of an insufficient understanding of the environment in which such policies are adopted and implemented. There is perhaps a natural tendency to apply the institutional framework with which we are more familiar to economies that are much more complex from a political, social and institutional standpoint. I have sometimes had the impression that there is some lack of understanding on the European side of the difficulties economic policy-making faces in Latin America, and in emerging markets in general for that matter. The problems related to social inequality; the inadequacy of infrastructures; the weak institutional and political setting; the dependence on raw materials as a source of external income; the exposure to shocks of a varied nature, and the vulnerability to changes in the mood of global capital markets, all have a profound impact on the way economic policies are designed and pursued in such countries, and on the related room for manoeuvre. Without acknowledging these particularities, it is difficult to understand Latin American economic policies. You would not be surprised if I stress, as a central banker, that these difficulties should in no way cast doubt on the desirability of the key objectives of macroeconomic stability and financial system soundness, a message we need to make particularly clear at times of distress like these. Latin American countries have too often paid a high price for monetary laxity and fiscal profligacy. They are therefore well aware of the importance of macro-stability as a prerequisite for growth. The Latin American experience clearly shows that only countries that persevere with sound policies are able to obtain the confidence and credibility of domestic economic agents and the endorsement of global financial markets needed to enter a virtuous circle of economic growth, sustained capital inflows and macroeconomic stability. Experience in the region also shows that there are no short cuts to replacing persistent political resolve aimed at that objective, and no magic devices to deliver such stability without any cost. But an appropriate institutional setting, including central bank independence and rules for fiscal discipline, can certainly reduce such cost substantially. Turning to the financial system, the link between its development and broader economic development has been highlighted by country experiences as well as by the economic literature. Although there are deep-seated differences among Latin American countries, the region as a whole shows a remarkable dependence on foreign capital flows for its investment and development, in contrast to other emerging regions. This dependence, combined in some countries with relatively low degrees of trade openness, a lack of reputation for sound macroeconomic policies and a poor record in the observance of property rights, has created a situation in which changes in the direction of capital flows ("sudden stops") entail a very high cost for a number of Latin American economies in terms of volatility of growth and output loss. The fostering of domestic saving is a high priority in many countries in the region, whose achievement is closely related to the development of sound and efficient financial systems, both as concerns the banking sector and financial markets. The relationship between economic development and financial sector development is bi-directional: growth and economic development stimulate financial deepening, and a sound and resilient financial system helps increase potential economic growth. In particular, a deep financial system acts as a buffer to absorb shocks generated in global financial markets. But financial sector development and a higher level of saving require a legal and institutional framework in which economic agents can operate under the assumption of a lasting and deep-rooted respect of the basic rules of a free market economy, including in particular the protection of property rights, something that is unfortunately not always guaranteed in some countries in the region. Latin America is a fascinating region, with formidable potential, but one in which economic policies face complex challenges. Policy-makers in the region are particularly in need of high-quality economic research, aimed at shedding light on the difficult choices they face. Such well-founded analysis is indeed especially necessary at this crucial juncture, at which economists and the public at large look at recent crises with apprehension and a certain degree of uneasiness. I am glad to observe that this high-quality research is flourishing, as this LACEA Annual meeting confirms. Let me add a few thoughts on the role I consider Spain is playing and can play in fostering mutual understanding between Europe and Latin America. As you know, in Spain we tend to see ourselves as a bridge between Latin America and Europe, a view reinforced over recent years as a result of a considerable deepening of our links with both areas. We also believe that although the experiences of European and Latin American countries differ in many respects, there are interesting lessons to be drawn from the comparison between both areas, in their similarities and differences. And we believe Spain is particularly well placed to contribute to such a debate, because our economic policy objectives in recent decades have many similarities with those of Latin American countries: achieving and maintaining macro-stability, increasing the efficiency of our economy and ensuring successful integration into a wider market, both in the trade and financial spheres. Interestingly, although Latin America is normally seen as an area particularly linked to the US, for geographical, political and historical reasons, the trade and financial relations of many Latin American countries with the European Union are even stronger than those with the US, particularly so in South America. Within Europe, Spain has traditionally had particularly deep ties with Latin America, and these have been reinforced over recent years, specifically as concerns direct investment. It is in this regard very gratifying for Spain that the deepening of our EU dimension over recent years has not been at the expense of our Latin American links. On the contrary, Spain was able to progress remarkably strongly on both fronts, which tends to show that regional integration processes, if carried out properly, do not take place at the cost of lessening links with third countries but rather have the potential to foster international links with a wider array of partners. This was certainly the case for Spain, which witnessed an intensification of its international projection in parallel with deeper integration into the EU. Naturally, as a result of these increasing links with Latin America, the community of Spanish economists developed great interest in economic research in the region. This LACEA meeting provides an excellent opportunity to foster links between Latin American researchers and their European and -in particular- Spanish counterparts. I hope we will all enjoy this opportunity. Thank you.

Title: Reflections on Financial Stability
text: Pedro Barri8e de la Maza Foundation Lecture series LA CORU84A, 16 OCTOBER 2002 REFLECTIONS ON FINANCIAL STABILITY GONZALO GIL Deputy governor I would like to begin my speech by thanking the Pedro Barri8e de la Maza Foundation for the opportunity it gives me to share with all of you some reflections on how financial stability, national and international, has evolved during the scam. Before starting to do so, I think it is appropriate to take a few minutes to comment on some particularly relevant aspects of the concept of financial stability, undoubtedly one of the most important objectives of contemporary economic policy, the safeguarding of which is one of the main tasks entrusted to the Banco de Espaa. 1. Financial stability Without going into greater depth, financial stability can be considered to exist when the necessary conditions are met so that intermediaries and financial markets can fulfill their basic function: to channel savings, allocating it efficiently from a correct formation of prices. Based on this generic definition, there are three aspects of financial stability that I want to highlight: its content, its extensibility and its dynamics. With regard to its content, insofar as the financial system is not an isolated structure, but fully immersed in the economy, and even in society, the conditions that define financial stability are not only financial in the strict sense, but also economic, social and political. This is not a new phenomenon. There have always been mutual relations between the financial world and its environment and, therefore, the possibility that disturbances arising in one of these fields affect the other, even giving rise to a spiral of successive interactions that aggravate all problems. What is new is the great diversity and intensity that, in the scams, the interrelations between the financial sector and the real sector of the economy have been reaching. As a result, it makes less and less sense to treat financial stability and economic stability separately in their various aspects: monetary, exchange rate, fiscal, cyclical, etc. Turning to the issue of extensi, it is clear that, in an economy as globalized and interdependent as the current one, in which growing and more complex conglomerates operate throughout the world and in which the real and financial markets of the various countries are increasingly integrated and better informed, financial stability cannot be approached exclusively with a national perspective. And this is valid both for preventive actions (strengthening of the international financial architecture or anticipating external shocks, for example) and for those aimed at solving crises that may occur. Finally, safeguarding the conditions that define financial stability cannot be approached from a static approach, which considers a smooth functioning of the economy possible. On the contrary, it must be approached from an essentially dynamic approach, which, taking as a starting point the real functioning of the system at all times, its tendencies and its fragilities, considers: firstly, trying to minimize the nero and severity of disturbances, endgenas and exats; Secondly, since these shocks will continue to exist, provide the system with the greatest possible reaction capacity, enhancing its robustness and ensuring that economic and financial authorities have the necessary room for manoeuvre to be able to implement stabilising economic policies. I have highlighted these three aspects of financial stability because they have been particularly important in the twelve-month periods. A period that begins with an event whose drama and significance are difficult to exaggerate: the terrorist attacks of 11 September, to the consequences of which I will devote the first part of my speech. Even before the attacks, there were signs that the international economic situation had changed. After a long bullish period, especially bright for the US economy, a change had emerged in the phase of the cycle, the characteristics and implications for financial stability of which I will discuss below. In times of uncertainty about the intensity and duration of this recessionary phase, a series of serious facts were known, which have come to be personalized in the so-called Enron case, which have questioned key aspects of the functioning of the main stock market in the world: the United States. I will comment on these aspects before, in conclusion, moving on to deal with the situation in Latin America, the disturbance that is most directly affecting our financial system, due to the important presence of Spanish banks in the area. 2. September 11 attacks First, the monetary authorities of the United States, and within a single day of each other the European authorities, reacted appropriately, through a series of actions that avoided a total paralysis of the world financial center, reassuring the markets, preventing the collapse of the international payments system and quickly arbitrating alternative channels to those that had been damaged. These actions lasted for several days and culminated in the opening of the New York Stock Exchange on September 17. It is not a question of analyzing in detail facts already sufficiently known, it is interesting instead to mention "some conclusions" of the events of those days for financial stability. More generally, it has become clear that, even under absolutely extreme conditions, totally unexpected and of unprecedented moral and material gravity, the mechanisms for safeguarding the stability of the system functioned properly, the economic and monetary authorities reacted quickly, imaginatively and correctly, and the evidence of international solidarity went far beyond mere declarations. Finally, another conclusion, which may seem excessive but which I think is remarkable, is the validity of one of the usual recommendations of the Bank of Spain to the entities and groups whose supervision is entrusted to it: the need to have effective contingency plans, which allow facing with the maximum possible guarantees, even the most unforeseen and extreme scenarios that may arise in any geographical area or line of activity. Finally, a tima conclusi must necessarily be an explicit recognition of confidence in financial markets and in the subjects who attend them. 3. International economic situation One of the most remarkable features in the international economic evolution of the last year has been the way in which it has influenced and influenced the stability of financial systems on a global scale. Today we know from the revisions to GDP made by the US statistical office, that the American economy had concluded the long period of economic growth it had enjoyed since the first half of the nineties, several quarters before the events of September 11. This stage had come hand in hand with an unprecedented increase in productivity caused by changes in production and management processes derived from the extensive introduction of new technologies. Thus, contrary to the arguments of some of the defenders of the so-called "new economy", the slowdown in growth came to show that economic cycles continued to exist, although in this case the contractionary phase occurred in a somewhat unexpected way. In fact, unlike in previous cycles, the trigger for the change was not a tightening of monetary policy aimed at controlling inflationary tensions, but a significant fall in corporate profits, in an environment of moderation in demand growth, and high competition in supply, which made it difficult to transfer cost pressures to prices due to the rise in wages and prices of energy. This situation led firms to a drastic process of inventory adjustment and investment in capital goods, with obvious effects on production, which were partially offset by the support of private consumption, which continued to behave surprisingly favourably during the downward phase of the cycle. Two of the factors to which this behaviour of private consumption has been attributed are the wealth effect derived from the continued rise in house prices, and the maintenance of household disposable income resulting from the increase in real wages at least in the initial stages of the slowdown. As a counterpoint, and contrary to some expectations that had been created to date, the European Union did not take over from the US as the engine of the world economy. Nor could Jap do so, mired for as long as an economic-financial crisis that does not finish showing signs of improvement. The result of all this was an economic slowdown in the three main economic areas practically in sync, a situation that although not totally new, had not been witnessed in the timas decades. And as a consequence, emerging economies, both Asia and Eastern Europe or Latin America, also suffered from this slowdown in global activity. The deep crises in Turkey and Argentina are framed in this context of global slowdown, although each has its own features and vulnerabilities that forged a serious loss of confidence in foreign investment. Particularly noteworthy in this context, as was evident at the beginning of the speech, is the appreciable stability shown by the international financial system throughout this phase of slower economic growth. Some of the reasons to which this favourable behaviour of the financial system has been attributed have been, among others, the processes of deregulation and financial innovation carried out in previous years, which have allowed a more effective diversification of risk; the use of new technologies, which have improved access to real-time information for market participants and enabled a faster correction of possible financial imbalances; increased transparency resulting from, inter alia, the introduction of standards and codes of good practice proposed by the International Monetary Fund, the World Bank and the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision; and, finally, the importance given by international financial authorities and regulators to financial stability issues. To these reasons should be added the room for manoeuvre achieved in the upward phase of the cycle, which has subsequently allowed expansionary economic policies to be implemented to stimulate aggregate demand. The monetary and fiscal policies adopted more intensively in the United States, and with some greater moderation in the European Union, are a good example of this. In this context, the equity markets began, after the fall in prices that followed September 11, a recovery in the heat of the improvement in expectations of economic recovery, confidence in the room for maneuver of economic policies (in particular monetary) and the expectation of a short war in Afghanistan. These expectations were supported by the dynamic GDP growth in the first quarter of this year in the US, which has a clearly expansionary effect on much of the world. Emerging Asia, Japan and Europe benefited from the pull in external demand, registering positive growth in activity in that quarter. On the other hand, in the fixed income markets, the declines in interest rates induced by monetary policy were felt, bringing the cost of financing to close to historical lows. It should be noted, however, that the returns on debt and the issuers with the best credit rating differ from those issuers with lower credit ratings or in the sectors hardest hit by the crisis, including telecommunications. In general, however, there were no problems for fundraising, except for the aforementioned exceptions and perhaps that of the US commercial paper market, whose outstanding balance registered the largest drop in its history. With regard to banking activity, the outlook was generally favourable except for investment banking, affected by the drastic decline in corporate activity and the fall in stock market operations. Factors that contributed to a relatively favourable environment for banking include, firstly, their moderate exposure to the boom in new technologies, since it is financed mainly in the stock markets and differentiator with respect to previous expansionary phases of the economic cycle. I refer to the absence of a housing bubble in the non- residential financed by banks, which certainly must have Learned from the experience of the real estate recession at the beginning of The nineties. The third factor is the increase during the expansionary phase of the economic cycle, in the solvency levels of financial institutions both due to the accumulation of provisions for insolvencies and own resources and, especially, due to improvements in the identification and management of risks. This was significantly facilitated by the smooth functioning of derivatives markets, in particular the novel credit derivatives market as mechanisms for the reallocation of credit risk. Credit risk was in many cases assumed by insurance companies in their usual role as risk takers. In this regard, it should be noted that the accumulation of risks in these institutions was added, on the one hand, by the consequences of September 11 and the floods in Central Europe, and, on the other, by the severe cut in their reserves and the negative evolution of stock prices, which show a situation of greater vulnerability that may affect their ability to meet the commitments assumed in pension plans with pre-established benefits. From May onwards, a strong downward movement began in the international equity markets that gained strength in the summer months and was reflected in a parallel decline in yields in the plicos, showing a sharp increase in risk aversi. At the same time, a movement of widening of private bond yield spreads begins, symptomatic of a greater perception of risk by financial markets. Among the factors to which this change in market sentiment can be attributed are the growing risk of armed intervention in Iraq by the US, the widespread doubts about the resilience of the world economy, and the crisis of confidence in corporate accounting generated from the ENRON and WorldCom cases. Uncertainty about the evolution of Brazilian debt towards sustainable levels after the elections adds to this unfavorable outlook for developed and emerging financial markets. 4. The Enron case In the situation that I have just summarized, in December of last year, the bankruptcy of Enron was declared, the largest in history in the United States until then, affecting assets valued in accounting 63.4 billion dares. This amount, which doubled that of the largest bankruptcy until then, that of the oil company Texaco, was, in turn, doubled by that of Worldcom, in July of this year. However, it is not the high figures that have given particular significance to these cases, but the fact that they have become paradigmatic of the serious deficiencies in terms of transparency that have become apparent in the US stock markets during the scam. It is clear that these shortcomings in no way excuse the Very serious responsibilities that managers and senior managers of the affected undertakings have throughout the process which led to their Bankruptcy. The managers of any company, financial or non-financial, They are the most responsible for their activity and they must be attribute to them the successes they achieve, but also the failures in which incur, as well as the consequences that may have the eventual irregular conduct in which they may have incurred. Having established the principle of the maximum responsibility of managers, it must be recognized that the special importance of these corporate scandals is not due to the behavior of those responsible but to two circumstances. The first is that the high number of companies concerned has revealed major shortcomings in the institutional mechanisms designed to prevent, detect and tackle which business behaviour such as those mentioned, which may always exist, is harmful to the not to those who have a direct relationship with the company (workers, creditors, shareholders, etc.) but also, and very especially, to third parties and to the system as a whole. Secondly, these cases are especially important because they have emerged in the United States, the first economy on the planet, within capital markets that are the most important and evolved in the world, and that, until now, were considered as an obligatory frame of reference when establishing comparisons or proposing reforms. In view of this significance, it is necessary to understand what has failed and why. To try this, I will mention the aspects that I consider most relevant to the stability of the system and, at the same time, those least affected by localism, that is, by the non-exportable peculiarities of the American system. All these aspects revolve around a central idea: the need to safeguard that financial markets have the complete, truthful and timely information they need to be able to carry out their most important contribution to financial stability: efficiently allocate resources based on a correct formation of the prices of the instruments exchanged, based on its fundamental analysis, on the correct valuation of its risks and on a rational and prudent behavior of investors. Conceptually, these safeguards are located in two different, yet deeply interrelated, spaces: On the one hand, within the company, where the information is initially generated, the main institutional failure revealed refers, without a doubt, to the governance of companies. Since this is a very broad concept, I will now mention two aspects of it: the system of remuneration of directors and senior managers and the functioning of the audit committee. The criterion followed to set remuneration is simple: align the interests of these senior officials with those of the company, that is, with those of the shareholders. One way to achieve this, which has experienced a strong growth in scams, is the granting of stock options on shares of the company itself. In principle, the mechanism is correct; However, problems may arise depending on whether it is implemented. Of these problems, we should mention: the possible lack of transparency; the possibility that accounting regulations allow, as was the case in the USA, that their cost is not charged to the income statement at the time they are granted, prudently resolving any valuation problems that may arise; and, finally, the problem that arises if the conditions of exercise of the options create perverse incentives for directors and senior executives to temporarily manipulate upwards the accounting results or the price of the shares, to the detriment of future results or even the viability of the company. Another basic aspect of the good governance of the companies that has failed in the companies that I have been commenting on is the presence in its board of directors and in its audit committee of an insufficient number of independent members, so that its function of control of the managers has practically not existed. In this important control function, the action of a audit committee which, having sufficient independence and resources, Take on such critical tasks as ensuring that accounting policies the enterprise, its internal controls and the performance of internal auditors and external parties have the necessary quality to detect possible fraud, to Know the risks of all kinds assumed by the company and for promote the production and transmission of information for one's own Board of Directors, for shareholders and for markets in general. In any case, safeguarding transparency in the markets can never be based on trusting that business behaviour will be ideal in all circumstances. Therefore, failures registered outside the company are particularly worrying. Aspects related to accounting standards The quality of the regulatory body, the adequacy of the principles emanating from it, which, with the exception of casuistics, encourage creative interpretations) have been questioned start from events. It is worth selling just two aspects that have played a crucial role: the definition of the consolidation perimeter (which allows special purpose entities to be left out); the possibility of accounting with the criterion of "fair value" using easily manipulated prices in scarcely liquid markets. The criticisms received by the external audit have been even harsher, as significant problems in their organization and functioning have become apparent. With regard to its organization, the dispersion of bodies that had competence over the supervision of the sector made it practically non-existent. Regarding its operation, the main cause of the failure of the external audit is the poor treatment that the organization of the supervision gave to a double conflict of interest, encouraging tolerance towards the audited company. The first of these arises when It is the managers of the company who hire, pay and can dismiss the auditor, rather than the audit committee, so that This, with its independence from management, is the one who is configured as "the customer" and make demands consistent with the external auditor their culture of control. The second conflict of interest arises when It is the same company that audits the accounts of another and, in addition, provides different services, such as consulting, that report to you substantial income. There has also been no lack of conflicts of interest, similar to those of the cited, in the case of rating companies, which always They gave many of the affected companies the best scores, not even in investment banks. If all this series of failures shows that the supply of information to the market has not worked properly, it is no less true that neither has the demand, an issue that raises two different kinds of responsibilities. The first, of a general nature, refers to all types of investors, because of the relaxation with which they have exercised their necessary contribution to market discipline. Greater significance are the possible responsibilities, of all kinds, of institutional investors, for the carelessness with which they have managed the savings of others, for their uncritical and gregarious use of financial techniques according to fashions, and for their collaboration necessary so that the Enron case, and those that have followed it, have been able to occur, either by ACCI or by Omisi, by not having applied due diligence to the knowledge of its clientele, in this case of asset. All of the above should not serve to question the general validity of the US supervisory model. Its economic foundations are sound and the objectives it sets are fully valid. Between them, there is a complex network of institutions and norms characterized, in the face of systems like ours, by a balance between regulation and self-regulation with a strong weight of this scam. Precisely, this particular balance is one of the most controversial issues and I will return to it in the tima part of my conference. Suffice it to say for now that both regulation and Self-regulation has advantages that it is necessary to know how to maximize, without incur the risks that each one can entail. Self-regulation, Therefore, it cannot be demonized after the failures I am discussing, since, on the one hand, it is closely associated with the achievements obtained. for many years by the Anglo-Saxon stock markets; by other In part, there is nothing to show that the Enron case, and those who have accompanied, they would not have existed if the American system had State, in general, more regulated and less self-regulated. I therefore believe that the fundamental problem is not It arises between regulation and self-regulation but resides in whether one and the other are of sufficient quality, an issue that is undoubtedly a responsibility Plica. From this, I believe that in this attitude of vigilance they have There have been failures of the US authorities, to carry their confidence in the proper functioning of self-regulation far beyond Reasonable limits. In the genesis of these failures, I believe that the An atmosphere of overflowing euphoria that has permeated the economy American as the tide decade progressed. Under A period of unprecedented prosperity and expectations raised by the announced "new economy", which were seen as Its champions have believed to see all kinds of practices legitimized, at the same time that he ceded the supervision of supervisors, perhaps for fear of being considered obstacles to progress. Under these conditions, irregular business behaviour has proliferated; the "creative" accounting practices necessary to hide them; tolerance, if not complicity, of institutions set up to verify, evaluate and analyse the quality of information provided to the market by undertakings; excessive investor complacency; and, in short, the relaxation of market discipline. Of course, the reaction of the US authorities has occurred. Although there is still part of its content to be specified, in view of what is being known, the main problem, the interventionist overreaction, has been ignored; the main conflicts of interest disrupting self-regulation have been addressed; supervision has been morally and materially rearmed to meet its responsibilities with realism and rigour; and the administrative and criminal sanctions regime has been tightened. Despite all this, an element as important to financial stability as investor confidence in business information will continue to suffer, at least in US markets. With regard to our country, although there have been no scandals comparable to those of the United States, the drafting of the new Financial Law, currently pending in Parliament, has significantly improved the regulatory treatment of the main problems highlighted in the Enron case and in those that have followed. 5. The current situation in Latin America and the supervision of Spanish parent banking groups Of the disturbances in the international economy that have affected financial stability in scam a, I still have to comment on the imbalances and, in some cases, crises in Latin American countries, undoubtedly those that are most directly related to Spain, due to the important presence in the area of our two main banking groups. I am not going to talk about the background of these crises, their development, or their foreseeable consequences for the area. I will only focus on analyzing the presence of our banks in Latin America, the safeguards that have been taken so that possible turbulence in the area does not affect our financial stability, and the consequences that these crises are having on the Spanish financial system. In the case of Spanish banks, the main driving factor of its external expansion is the process of mergers that develop our country in the second half of the nineties. It will result in two large banking groups, with a high level of own resources and the possibility of expanding them, with significant surpluses of management capacity, with a good knowledge of retail banking technology and with the need to exploit the economies of scale and scope arising from mergers. All this potential could not be developed in a scenario like the one presented in those years by our financial system. The very high degree of banking of the Spanish economy, a certain oversizing of the installed capacity, the strong levels of competition, the tendency to fall of all margins, etc. were factors that, rather than providing possibilities for expansion, advised readjustment strategies. Similar characteristics of maturity presented the European Union and the other developed areas, so Latin America was the "natural" destination of our entities. Although with significant differences between countries, in general the level of banking was low; major privatization processes were under way; the low efficiency of existing institutions offered clear opportunities to make profitable the improvements in management that were introduced by allowing the application of techniques and technologies that were widely rolled in Spain; the high margins in force, which, in addition to reflecting higher levels of risk, offered the potential for greater results; there was a com language and a close culture, and, moreover, the advantages in terms of diversification d0 geographical, sectoral and cyclical d0 were greater than in relation to Europe. Obviously, it wasn't all advantages. Along with the favorable aspects I have just mentioned, the expansion in Latin America presented the risks that the presence always enters in emerging countries, with economic, social and political structures less stable than those of developed countries. We were all aware of these risks. From there, the fundamental decision about whether the opportunities outweighed the risks rested with the administrators and senior managers of the institutions. Meanwhile, it was up to supervisors to ensure that the decision taken by banks did not jeopardize their future stability and viability, let alone those of the system as a whole, even in the worst-case scenario. The ultimate consequence of all these considerations is known. Spanish banks d0 its two main groups, to be exact d0 began a rapid and important process of expansion in Latin America, whose quantitative results became spectacular: direct investments of 25,560 million euros, which led to approximately 30% of the consolidated assets of both groups being in the area, and to the market shares achieved in it rising to 22% for deposits, 20% for loans, 40% for pension fund management, and around 14% for collective investment management. In the months of timas, some of these figures have decreased, but they do not change the overall picture drawn. Considering banking activity in the strict sense, the distribution by country of the total consolidated assets that the two large Spanish groups have in Latin America is as follows, with data to June: Mexico, with 15%, followed at a great distance by Brazil and Chile, with 4% each, Puerto Rico with 2% and Argentina (slightly less than 1.5%), while the relative importance of the rest of the countries is very limited. Turning to the qualitative aspects, the expansion in Latin America has been based on the acquisition of stakes in important banks pre-existing commercial, generally through brands based in local markets and with a good knowledge of the situation and financial customs of the country. In addition, the Spanish groups from the beginning assumed full control of the management of the investee entities. The activity carried out mainly by the Latin American subsidiaries acquired is retail banking, that is, the banking activity considered to be of lower risk, because it generates wider and more stable margins, as well as a greater link with customers. In this line of business is where Spanish groups have more experience. The changes generated by the process of expansion of Spanish banking in Latin America have required important changes in the way the Bank of Spain supervises the large banking groups. The decisions of the Banco de Espaa in this area require, at least, to consider the following aspects: relations with the supervisors of the host countries, the development of new structures and procedures for the supervision of large groups and, finally, the elaboration of a set of reference rules that establish a general prudential framework for Latin American activities. Let's see them: The first of these is based on the fact that, since the expansion in Latin America is based on subsidiaries, these, at a consolidated level, are part of Spanish banking groups, although, at the individual level, they continue to be banks of different nationalities, subject, therefore, to the corresponding national laws and supervisors. In situations of this type, the distribution of responsibilities proposed by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision in its so-called Basic Principles for Effective Supervision, and which have been universally accepted by the international banking community, is that the host supervisor, the Latin American in this case, it must ensure the individual solvency of its national banks, but these are subsidiaries of foreign groups, in exactly the same way as if they were domestically owned banks; For his part, the supervisor of origin, the Bank of Spain in this case, must ensure the solvency of the Consolidated group as a whole. Despite the fact that the two supervisory responsibilities are Clearly differentiated, it is necessary that the two supervisors coordinate their actions, for which the protocols are signed conocidos como "Memoranda of Understanding". The second aspect concerns supervisory activity in the strict sense. It is evident that groups as large and complex as those that have led the expansion in Latin America cannot be supervised using traditional procedures, even if only because now much of their activity takes place outside Spain. For this reason, a set of procedures has been developed to be able to carry out the supervisory activities from the Central Services in Spain of the large banking groups. This method is being carried out by a specialized monitoring group that consumes a large amount of resources. Its presence in the headquarters of these banking groups is of a permanent nature and has two basic objectives: a general one, which monitors the joint evolution of the entire consolidated group, and a particular one, which reviews the entities and areas in which greater risk is detected. These tasks take into account the work carried out by internal auditors (whose frequency per country must be annual) and of the external audit, especially in their role of verifying harmonization in obtaining consolidated accounts. Despite the high consumption of resources that such an approach demands and its selective action, the effective supervision of such large and complex groups would be impossible without the active and necessary collaboration of the entities themselves. To facilitate it, the development experienced by these groups has been fundamental, becoming true multinationals and, therefore, implementing management structures and procedures supported by advanced technological means, which allow them to adequately control their consolidated activity from their Central Services. By this reason, the Bank of Spain has established a series of reference standards for its international expansion that, at present, are being put into practice by Spanish groups and that are developed in the Banking Supervision Report recently published by the Bank of Spain. These principles cover aspects such as management reporting and control, accounting policies, individual and group solvency, and the desirability of subsidiaries managing their financing and liquidity without dependence on the parent company. These were the most significant quantitative and qualitative aspects of the presence in Latin America of our banks and the way in which we supervised them from Spain when, over the past year, the economic situation began to deteriorate in some countries in the area. As is known, this deterioration has been especially serious in Argentina, then Uruguay and Venezuela spread and more recently it has manifested itself in Brazil. Of these countries, there are two countries that have a significant presence in Spanish banks. In Argentina, the 4th and 5th largest banks in the country are owned by size, representing 4.9% of Spanish assets in Latin America and, as already indicated, just under 1.5% of the total consolidated balance sheet of our two large groups. In Brazil, the 6th and 16th largest banks are owned by Spain, representing 15.2% of assets in the area and approximately 4% of total consolidated assets. Therefore, the concentration in these two countries of assets of the two largest Spanish banking groups is not excessive: just under 6% of their consolidated balance sheets. If in the economic field these two countries present profound Distinctive features, also banking operations are very different between they, since, in the face of the fragility represented by the very high dolarizaci Argentina, in Brazil 82% of the activity corresponds to Investments denominated in local currency, financed with liabilities also in local currency. The reaction of the two large Spanish groups to the crises in these countries has been the one that should be adopted, in the case of solvent and mature entities: to provision the deterioration experienced with criteria of maximum prudence, even if this has meant altering the projected profits downwards. In essence, all these write-downs have been charged to the income statements. This, together with the zero contribution to profits of Argentina, the effects of the depreciation of Latin American currencies, and the lower rate of growth of the business, inside and outside Spain, has led to that, for this year, the expected joint attributable profit of the two large groups has been modified downwards with a decrease of 10%, from 4,900 in December 2001 to an estimated figure of db4,400 million at the end of 2002. Despite this estimated reduction in projected earnings, both the profitability of our two largest banking groups and their solvency remain high. Thus, in June of this year, the returns achieved on equity (R.O.E.), have been higher than 13%, being among the highest internationally and the least decreased.
