On the other hand, the solvency ratios measured with the criteria of the Bank for Settlements of Basel, were above 11%, well above the minimum of 8%, despite the contraction of the business, the write-downs made and the depreciation of Latin American currencies. Finally, measured with the same criterion, first-class equity was above 7.3% of weighted risks. A remarkable general conclusion is that developments in Latin America have not questioned the basic features of the situation of the Spanish banking system, which is characterized by being a healthy, profitable, efficient and stable system. It is healthy due to its excess of own resources, capacity to generate results, high rate of capitalization of profits and good quality of assets. It is profitable due to the strength and recurrence of the income statement structure, based, fundamentally, on the retail and commercial banking business. It is efficient, since in the scams as the increase of the business is being managed with costs of transformation content, which have been reduced in terms of ATMs. And it is profitable as a result of both the quality of the management of the entities themselves and the non-concentration of the market, which gives it a high level of competition. 6. Final Thoughts Finally, I would like to share with you a series of reflections raised by the facts discussed in the previous pages. 1. The strong process of economic expansion, more accentuated in the United States than in other areas, has been accompanied in many cases by features of irrational exuberance in different markets. In these, decisions were often based on unrealistic expectations of present and future benefits under the confidence that cycles were already things of the past. But the situation has changed, what was previously considered as a permanent expansion, is transformed first into a short recession, which would be followed, it was thought, by a rapid recovery, to with the passage of time more affirm the expectation of a prolonged period of slow growth. Since the beginning of this year, all successive forecasts, both national and international, have been delaying the moment of recovery. Along with this macroeconomic situation, very diverse causes have played an important role, some of them already existing in the boom process, but masked by the exaggerated optimism of those as; while others have already materialized with the slow growth process underway. To the first group belong the causes related to failures in the functioning of the markets: fraud, inadequate government gains, violation of accounting standards, false information to the markets, etc. In a recent episode, the weekly The Economist quoted the phrase of a well-known American investor: "Only when the tide goes out, you can see who is swimming naked." Well, when the situation changed, all the known "nakedness" phenomena began to appear, which accentuated the fall in stock prices, and contributed to increasing the uncertainties and vulnerability of the general economic situation. To the second group of aggravating factors belong the crises and tensions in emerging countries, with more direct influence in some countries than in others, but with a general effect of widening the uncertainty that conditions capital flows and not so towards the countries that are directly suffering them. Likewise, this group includes all those "political" developments Israel-Palestine, Iraq, etc. that, again, have an effect on the level of general confidence and in this case also with an upward component of oil prices. 2. In this environment, financial markets in general and banking markets in particular have shown resilience to avoid further deterioration of the problems posed by the situation. Their best disposition to act quickly when necessary and in a cooperative manner d0 remember the above-mentioned reluctance to the attacks of 11 September d0 as well as the margins for manoeuvre gained d0 by better control of credit risks, by the provision of adequate provisions in accordance with the rules of the supervisory authorities, etc. d0 at the previous stage, have led to the maintenance of financial stability at reasonable levels. However, we should not fall back into irrational expectations: the maintenance and improvement of financial stability is an ongoing process since the achievements made do not have an infinite capacity to respond to the continuous materialization of risks. That is why it is always Work needed d0 regulators, institutions and markets d0 to increase the soundness of financial institutions. 3. The moment we live in, with all its uncertainties and vulnerabilities, places in the foreground and concentrates attention on the aspects of risk. This produces an inevitable negative bias in the perception of the situation. At the same time, however, the acute perception of these fragilities can support the adoption of a set of reforms in the fundamentals of the system, and do so in a way that consolidates international coherence. 4. This would therefore be the time to delve into some reforms already undertaken, both by markets and by public regulators, seeking to correct the fundamental aspects that, in the light of recent experiences, have been profoundly eroded, and, at the same time, to do so in a coherent between systems, in such a way that regulatory uncertainties generating gaps that can be used with obvious risks to the system as a whole. 5. Different international institutions and organizations, in addition to the markets themselves, are working on the task of making the foundations of financial markets more sound, while maintaining, at the same time, a certain homogenization of regulations and practices that, due to their differences alone .without taking into account their vulnerability., are prone to originate processes of regulatory arbitrage disruptive to the proper functioning of market discipline. In this double sense of fundamental reform and international coherence, the following can be cited: (a)The International Accounting Standards Board (IASB), which is improving accounting standards and seeking to increase convergence of standards across countries d1 an element of extraordinary importance in an increasingly globalized world and thus with companies operating simultaneously in several countries. It is worth considering, in connection with this matter, the agreement of the aforementioned Agency, applicable from 2005, which will amend the accounting standards currently used by financial institutions. Although this is not the time to dwell on this issue, it is possible to see the fact that accounting standards, in the case of financial institutions, should be a product of the collaboration of accounting and supervisory experts, as a way of ensuring adequate treatment of the specific risks of banking institutions compared to other companies. Accounting homogenization certainly has advantages, but it should accommodate the consideration of these differential aspects. The example of the role of accounting regulator developed by the Bank of Spain, which has produced undoubted advantages in the adequate supervisory control of financial institutions and has served to improve their solvency, should be taken into consideration, in an inevitable structure of accounting standards more homogenized. (b)IOSCO's work on auditor independence, monitoring them and improving information at the market and transparency. c) The revision and expansion of Corporate principles OECD Governance. 6. But perhaps the most representative area of work of this global approach is represented by the one that, for 3 years, has occupied the Basel Committee. A crucial aspect of financial stability is, undoubtedly, that which seeks to improve the analysis of credit risks, and others, in which banks incur, seeking an incentive effect of risk control systems and establishing the appropriate capital requirements for each case, so that unexpected risks can be covered without the entity seeing its operation in danger. This is undoubtedly a fundamental aspect of the current Agreement under development and it is often the "exclusive" agreement that represents the entire Agreement. A small digresi in relation to this issue and to the Spanish regulation: As you know, the strengthening of the own resources of the entities has been in our case a permanent concern that has led us to apply more demanding principles than those internationally admitted. But, apart from own resources, the provision policy (which will allow it to face the expected risks .materialized ono) has been a strong point in the regulation of the Bank of Spain. I believe that these times, and recent experiences, are clearly validating the policy followed by the Bank and assumed by the entities, whose joint effect has led to a sound financial system, with a solvency ratio above 11%, efficient and stable. It is a satisfaction, therefore, to observe that in certain agencies the idea of statistical provisi has penetrated in such a way that the concept, predictably, will be included in international regulations in one way or another. 7. But returning to the Basel Agreement, its content goes beyond the proper valuation of the capital needed to cover risks. No system or financial institution could operate in compliance with the minimum capital requirements. Financial stability is much more than that and, in this sense, the Agreement can be read as a global approach to making it sustainable. Indeed, in addition to the key element mentioned above, which would be the subject of Pillar 1, the aspects related to supervisory policy (Pillar 2) .inevitably linked to the relationship regulaciaut97noma-regulaci-reguladorci.; and market discipline, including the adequate provision of information (Pillar 3), are equally fundamental parts of the Agreement. 8. In this way, the Agreement enters into a crucial aspect relating to the maintenance of the "rules of the game" that should govern the interaction between public supervision, a certain degree of self-regulation and market discipline d0 which have been violated with apparent ease in the recent past, as we have just seen, and whose functioning needs to be improved and ensured. 9. Both the supervisory authorities and the markets themselves, through self-regulation, have initiated to improve the fundamentals of financial stability. Self-regulation through standards and conduct codes are a basic element for the functioning of markets. Its importance in one or the other case depends on the historical evolutions of functioning in each country, and a priori it cannot be qualified as good or bad. The task of self-regulation of markets has, on the other hand, obvious limitations in areas that may give rise to conflict of interest. However well this self-regulation is developed, the presence of the "plica policy" of supervision and regulation is inevitable. The basic task of the latter in the fields that are its own, must be oriented, it is already oriented, in our country among others, towards an assessment of the quality of the internal processes of risk control. On the other hand, its relationship with self-regulation should serve to "fix" standards and good practices in order to favor a more rapid expansion of them and make them become "minimum requirements", from which individual improvements are possible. This would avoid regulatory arbitrage and also the fact that self-regulation also has a high cyclical component that makes self-discipline more difficult to maintain both in bullish phases, due to relaxation and overconfidence, and in the phases of low to try to escape from some hurried situation. 10.La rule of the game that complements the two mentioned is market discipline. This can be the case if there are corporate governance gains with a clear accountability scheme and a transparent incentive scheme with independent internal audit. On the other hand, market discipline is such if good accounting practices are respected, and if the integrity and transparency of the information provided allows investors to make consistent decisions. Again here, the presence of the regulator is also necessary. 11.All of the above is therefore an important agenda which, although exemplified in the Basel Committee, is contributing greatly to its development by national supervisors, international bodies and the markets themselves. The Agreement still has three years left, but it would not make sense to wait, and it is not being done, so that many of the reforms that will eventually be approved, are already beginning to lay their foundations. 12.These moments, as I mentioned earlier, are conducive to taking action and securing a sound and lasting foundation of financial systems. This is everyone's task and it is not a financial issue, but there is one part that concerns us directly, because, as the Chairman of the Basel Committee said at the meeting in Cape Town: "Banking supervisors and central bankers certainly share the objectives [to reduce poverty and promote economic development]. To fulfil our obligation to ensure the safety and solvency of the financial system, we seek to preserve depositors' savings, promote the mobilization of credit, and, ultimately, protect the health and growth of our economies. We really cannot alleviate poverty or promote economic development unless our banks are well run, our financial system is stable, and our markets transparent and open."
text_original: Fundacin Pedro Barri de la Maza Ciclo de conferencias LA CORUA, 16 DE OCTUBRE DE 2002 REFLEXIONES SOBRE LA ESTABILIDAD FINANCIERA GONZALO GIL Subgobernador Quiero empezar mi intervenci agradeciendo a la Fundaci Pedro Barri de la Maza la oportunidad que me brinda para compartir con todos ustedes algunas reflexiones acerca de co ha evolucionado la estabilidad financiera, nacional e internacional, durante el timo a. Antes de empezar a hacerlo, creo conveniente dedicar unos minutos a comentar algunos aspectos especialmente relevantes del concepto de estabilidad financiera, sin duda uno de los objetivos ms importantes de la poltica econica contempornea, cuya salvaguardia constituye una de las principales tareas que tiene encomendadas el Banco de Espaa. 1. Sobre la estabilidad financiera Sin entrar en mayores profundidades, se puede considerar que existe estabilidad financiera cuando se dan las condiciones necesarias para que los intermediarios y mercados financieros puedan cumplir su funci bsica: canalizar el ahorro, asignndolo de forma eficiente a partir de una correcta formaci de los precios. Partiendo de esta definici genrica, hay tres aspectos de la estabilidad financiera que quiero destacar: su contenido, su extensi y su dinmica. Respecto a su contenido, en la medida en que el sistema financiero no constituye una estructura aislada, sino plenamente inmersa en la economa, e incluso en la sociedad, las condiciones que definen la estabilidad financiera, no son icamente financieras en sentido estricto, sino tambin econmicas, sociales y polticas. Este no es un fenmeno nuevo. Siempre han existido las relaciones mutuas entre el mundo financiero y su entorno y, por tanto, la posibilidad de que perturbaciones surgidas en alguno de estos campos afecten al otro, incluso dando lugar a una espiral de sucesivas interacciones que agraven todos los problemas. Lo que s es nuevo es la gran diversidad e intensidad que, en los timos as han ido alcanzando las interrelaciones entre el sector financiero y el sector real de la economa. Como consecuencia de ello, cada vez tiene menos sentido tratar por separado la estabilidad financiera y la estabilidad econmica en sus diversas vertientes: monetaria, cambiaria, fiscal, cclica, etc. Pasando al tema de la extensi, es evidente que, en una economa tan globalizada e interdependiente como la actual, en la que conglomerados cada vez mayores y ms complejos operan en todo el mundo y en la que los mercados reales y financieros de los diversos pases cada vez estn ms integrados y mejor informados, la estabilidad financiera no puede plantearse exclusivamente con una ptica nacional. Y esto es vlido tanto para las acciones preventivas (fortalecimiento de la arquitectura financiera internacional o previsi de shocks externos, por ejemplo) como para las destinadas a solventar las crisis que puedan llegar a producirse. Finalmente, la salvaguardia de las condiciones que definen la estabilidad financiera no puede abordarse desde un planteamiento esttico, que considere posible un funcionamiento de la economa, carente de perturbaciones. Por el contrario, ha de abordarse desde un planteamiento esencialmente dinmico, que, teniendo como punto de partida el funcionamiento real del sistema en cada momento, sus tendencias y sus fragilidades, se plantee: en primer lugar, intentar minimizar el nero y la gravedad de las perturbaciones, endgenas y exenas; en segundo lugar, puesto que estas perturbaciones van a seguir existiendo, dotar al sistema de la mayor capacidad de reacci posible, potenciando su robustez y procurando que las autoridades econmicas y financieras cuenten con el margen de maniobra necesario para poder aplicar polticas econicas estabilizadoras. He destacado estos tres aspectos de la estabilidad financiera porque han revestido especial importancia en los timos doce meses. Un perodo que comienza con un acontecimiento cuyo dramatismo y trascendencia son difciles de exagerar: los atentados terroristas del 11 de septiembre, a cuyas consecuencias dedicar la primera parte de mi intervenci. Ya antes de los atentados eran patentes los indicios de que la coyuntura econica internacional haba cambiado. Tras una larga etapa alcista, especialmente brillante para la economa estadounidense, haba surgido un cambio en la fase del ciclo, cuyas caractersticas e implicaciones para la estabilidad financiera tratar a continuaci. En momentos de incertidumbre sobre la intensidad y duraci de esta fase recesiva, se conocieron una serie de graves hechos, que han venido a personalizarse en el denominado caso Enron, que han cuestionado aspectos claves del funcionamiento del principal mercado de valores del mundo: el estadounidense. Comentar estos aspectos antes de, para terminar, pasar a ocuparme de la situaci en Latinoamrica, la perturbaci que ms directamente est afectando a nuestro sistema financiero, por la importante presencia de la banca espaola en la zona. 2. Atentados del 11 de septiembre En primer lugar las autoridades monetarias de los Estados Unidos, y con un solo da de diferencia las autoridades europeas, reaccionaron adecuadamente, mediante una serie de actuaciones que evitaron una paralizaci total del centro financiero mundial, tranquilizando a los mercados, evitando el colapso del sistema de pagos internacional y arbitrando rpidamente cauces alternativos a los que haban resultado daados. Estas actuaciones se prolongaron durante varios das y tuvieron culminaci en la apertura de la Bolsa de Nueva York el 17 de septiembre. No se trata de analizar con detalle hechos ya suficientemente conocidos, s tiene inters en cambio mencionar algunas conclusiones" de los acontecimientos de aquellos das para la estabilidad financiera. La ms general es que se ha puesto de manifiesto que, incluso en condiciones absolutamente extremas, totalmente inesperadas y de una gravedad moral y material sin precedentes, los mecanismos de salvaguardia de la estabilidad del sistema funcionaron adecuadamente, las autoridades econmicas y monetarias reaccionaron con rapidez, imaginaci y acierto, y las pruebas de solidaridad internacional fueron mucho ms all de simples declaraciones. Finalmente otra conclusi, que puede parecer excesiva pero que creo destacable, es la vigencia de una de las recomendaciones habituales del Banco de Espa a las entidades y grupos cuya supervisi tiene encomendada: la necesidad de contar con planes de contingencias efectivos, que permitan afrontar con las mximas garantas posibles, incluso los escenarios ms imprevistos y extremos que puedan llegar a plantearse en cualquier rea geogrfica o lnea de actividad. Para terminar, una tima conclusi tiene que ser necesariamente un reconocimiento expreso de la confianza en los mercados financieros y en los sujetos que concurren a ellos. 3. Situacin econmica internacional Uno de los rasgos ms destacables en la evoluci econmica internacional del ltimo a ha sido la manera en que sta ha influido y se ha visto influida por la estabilidad de los sistemas financieros a escala global. Hoy sabemos, por las revisiones del PIB efectuadas por la oficina estadstica estadounidense, que la economa americana haba concluido la larga etapa de crecimiento econmico de la que haba disfrutado desde la primera mitad de los noventa, varios trimestres antes de que se produjeran los acontecimientos del 11 de septiembre. Dicha etapa haba venido de la mano de un aumento de la productividad sin precedentes originado por los cambios en los procesos productivos y gerenciales derivados de la introducci extensiva de nuevas tecnologas. As, en contra de lo argumentado por algunos de los defensores de la llamada nueva economa, la desaceleraci del crecimiento vino a poner de manifiesto que los ciclos econmicos seguan existiendo, aunque en esta ocasi la fase contractiva se produjese de una forma un tanto inesperada. De hecho, a diferencia de lo ocurrido en anteriores ciclos, el desencadenante del cambio no fue un endurecimiento de la poltica monetaria destinado a controlar las tensiones inflacionistas, sino una importante cada de los beneficios empresariales, en un entorno de moderaci del crecimiento de la demanda, y de elevada competencia en la oferta, que dificultaba la traslaci a precios de las presiones de costes por la subida de los salarios y los precios de la energa. Tal situaci condujo a las empresas a un proceso drstico de ajuste de existencias e inversi en bienes de equipo, con efectos evidentes sobre la producci, que se vieron compensados so parcialmente por el sostenimiento del consumo privado, que continucomportndose de forma sorprendente favorable durante la fase bajista del ciclo. Dos de los factores a los que se ha atribuido este comportamiento del consumo privado son el efecto riqueza derivado de la continuada subida de los precios de la vivienda, y el mantenimiento de la renta disponible de las familias derivada del aumento de los salarios reales al menos en las etapas iniciales de la desaceleracin. Como contrapunto, y en contra de algunas expectativas que se haban creado hasta la fecha, la Uni Europea no tomel relevo de EE.UU. como motor de la economa mundial. Tampoco Jap pudo hacerlo, sumido desde hace as en una crisis econico-financiera que no termina de presentar indicios de mejora. El resultado de todo ello fue una desaceleracin econmica en las tres principales reas econmicas prcticamente en sincrona, una situaci que si bien no es totalmente novedosa, no se haba presenciado en las timas dcadas. Y como consecuencia, tambin las economas emergentes, tanto Asia como Europa del Este o Latinoamrica, acusaron dicha desaceleraci de la actividad mundial. En Argentina, son de propiedad espaola el 4 y 5 de los bancos del pas por tama, lo que representa el 4,9% de los activos espales en Latinoamrica y, como ya se ha indicado, algo menos del 1,5% del total balance consolidado de nuestros dos grandes grupos. Por su parte, en Brasil son de propiedad espaola el 6 y el 16 de los mayores bancos, representando el 15,2% de los activos en la zona y, aproximadamente, el 4% de los activos totales consolidados. Por tanto, la concentraci en estos dos pases de activos de los dos mayores grupos bancarios espales no es excesiva: algo menos del 6% de sus balances consolidados. Si en el terreno econmico estos dos pases presentan profundos rasgos distintivos, tambin la operativa bancaria es muy diferente entre ellos, ya que, frente a la fragilidad que representaba la altsima dolarizaci Argentina, en Brasil el 82% de la actividad corresponde a inversiones denominadas en moneda local, financiadas con pasivos tambin en moneda local. La reacci de los dos grandes grupos espales ante las crisis de estos pases ha sido la que corresponda adoptar, tratndose de entidades solventes y maduras: provisionar el deterioro experimentado con criterios de mxima prudencia, aunque ello haya supuesto alterar a la baja los beneficios proyectados. En lo esencial, todos estos saneamientos se han hecho con cargo a las cuentas de resultados. Esto, unido a la nula contribucin a beneficios de Argentina, a los efectos de la depreciaci de las monedas latinoamericanas, y al menor ritmo de crecimiento del negocio, dentro y fuera de Espaa, ha llevado a que, para el presente ejercicio, el beneficio conjunto atribuido esperado de los dos grandes grupos haya sido modificado a la baja con un descenso del 10%, pasando de 4.900, en diciembre de 2001, a una cifra estimada para finales de 2002 de 4.400 millones de euros. Pese a esta reducci estimada en los beneficios proyectados, tanto la rentabilidad de nuestros dos mayores grupos bancarios como su solvencia continn siendo elevadas. As, en junio de este a, las rentabilidades alcanzadas sobre fondos propios (R.O.E.), han sido superiores al 13%, siendo de las ms elevadas a nivel internacional y de las que menos han disminuido. Por su parte, los coeficientes de solvencia medidos con los criterios del Banco de Pagos de Basilea, eran superiores al 11%, muy por encima del mnimo del 8%, pese a la contraccin del negocio, a los saneamientos realizados y a la depreciaci de las monedas latinoamericanas. Finalmente, medidos con el mismo criterio, los recursos propios de primera categora estaban por encima del 7,3% de los riesgos ponderados. Una destacable conclusi general es que los desarrollos en Amrica Latina no han cuestionado los rasgos bsicos de la situacin del sistema bancario espaol, que se caracteriza por ser un sistema saneado, rentable, eficiente y estable. Es saneado debido a su exceso de recursos propios, capacidad de generaci de resultados, alta tasa de capitalizaci de beneficios y buena calidad de activos. Es rentable debido a la fortaleza y recurrencia de la estructura de la cuenta de resultados, basada, fundamentalmente, en el negocio de banca minorista y comercial. Es eficiente, ya que en los timos as el incremento del negocio se est gestionando con costes de transformaci contenidos, que se han visto reducidos en trminos de ATMs. Y es rentable como consecuencia tanto de la calidad de la gesti de las propias entidades como por la no concentraci del mercado, lo que le da un elevado nivel de competencia. 6. Reflexiones finales Para terminar me gustara compartir con Uds. una serie de reflexiones suscitadas por los hechos comentados en las pginas anteriores. 1. El fuerte proceso de expansi econmica, ms acentuada en Estados Unidos que en otras reas, ha venido acompaado en muchos casos por rasgos de exuberancia irracional en distintos mercados. En estos, las decisiones se basaron, con frecuencia, en expectativas nada realistas de beneficios presentes y futuros bajo la confianza de que los ciclos ya eran cosas del pasado. Pero la situaci ha cambiado, lo que antes se considercomo una expansi permanente, se transform primero en una recesi corta, que vendra seguida, se pensaba, por una recuperaci rpida, para con el paso del tiempo afirmarse ms la expectativa de un periodo dilatado de crecimiento lento. Desde comienzos del a en curso, todas las sucesivas previsiones, tanto nacionales como internacionales, han venido dilatando en el tiempo el momento de la recuperaci. Junto a esta situaci macroeconmica han jugado un papel importante muy diversas causas, algunas de ellas ya existentes en el proceso de auge, pero enmascaradas por el optimismo exagerado de aquellos as; mientras que otras se han materializado ya con el proceso de crecimiento lento en marcha. Al primer grupo pertenecen las causas relacionadas con fallos en el funcionamiento de los mercados: fraudes, ganos de gobierno inadecuados, vulneraci de normas contables, informaci falsa a los mercados, etctera. En un nero reciente, el semanario The Economist citaba la frase de un conocido inversor norteamericano: "Slo cuando la marea baja, puede verse quin est nadando desnudo". Pues bien, cuando la situaci cambi empezaron a aparecer todos los fenmenos de "desnudez" ya conocidos, que acentuaron la cada de las cotizaciones burstiles, y contribuyeron a acrecentar las incertidumbres y vulnerabilidad de la situaci econmica general. Al segundo grupo de factores agravantes pertenecen las crisis y tensiones en pases emergentes, con influencia ms directa en unos pases que en otros, pero con un efecto general de ampliaci de la incertidumbre que condiciona los flujos de capital y no so hacia los pases que directamente las estn sufriendo. Igualmente, se incluyen en este grupo todos aquellos desarrollos "polticos" Israel-Palestina, Irak, etc. que, de nuevo, tienen un efecto sobre el nivel de confianza general y en este timo caso adems con un componente alcista de los precios del petreo. 2. En este entorno, los mercados financieros, en general, y los bancarios, en particular, han mostrado una capacidad de resistencia que ha permitido evitar un empeoramiento adicional de los problemas que la situacin planteaba. Su mejor disposici para actuar rpidamente cuando ha sido necesario y de manera cooperativarecurdese la reacci, mencionada antes, a los atentados del 11 de septiembre, as como los mrgenes de maniobra ganados por un mayor control de los riesgos de crdito, por la dotaci de provisiones adecuadas siguiendo las normas de las autoridadessupervisoras,etc.en la etapa anterior, han propiciado el mantenimiento de la estabilidad financiera a unos niveles razonables. No se debera caer, no obstante, de nuevo en expectativas irracionales: el mantenimiento y mejora de la estabilidad financiera es un proceso continuo ya que los logros conseguidos no tienen una capacidad de respuesta infinita ante la continua materializaci de riesgos. Por ello siempre es necesario trabajar reguladores, instituciones y mercados para aumentar la solidez de las instituciones financieras. 3. El momento que vivimos, con todas sus incertidumbres y vulnerabilidades, colocan en primer plano y concentran la atenci en los aspectos de riesgo. Esto produce un inevitable sesgo negativo en la percepci de la situaci. Al mismo tiempo, sin embargo, la aguda percepci de estas fragilidades puede respaldar la adopci de un conjunto de reformas en los fundamentos del sistema, y hacerlo de forma que se consolide la coherencia internacional. 4. As pues, este sera el momento para ahondar en algunas reformas ya emprendidas, tanto por mercados como por reguladores plicos, tratando de corregir los aspectos fundamentales que, a la luz de las recientes experiencias, se han erosionado profundamente, y, al tiempo, hacerlo de una manera coherente entre unos sistemas y otros, de tal manera que desaparezcan incertidumbres regulatorias generadoras de vacos que pueden ser utilizados con evidentes riesgos para el sistema en su conjunto. 5. Diferentes instituciones y organismos internacionales, adems de los propios mercados, estn trabajando en la tarea de hacer ms sidos los fundamentos de los mercados financieros, manteniendo, al mismo tiempo, una cierta homogenizaci de normativas y prcticas que, por sus solas diferencias sin tener en cuenta su vulneraci, son proclives a originar procesos de arbitraje regulatorio perturbadores para el adecuado funcionamiento de la disciplina de mercado. En este doble sentido de reforma de fundamentos y coherencia internacional, pueden citarse los trabajos de: a)La International Accounting Standards Board (IASB), que est mejorando las normas contables y tratando de incrementar la convergencia de normas entre los distintos pases un elemento de extraordinaria importancia en un mundo cada vez ms globalizado y, por lo tanto, con empresas que actn simultneamente en diversos pases. Merece la pena selar, en relacin con este asunto, el acuerdo del mencionado Organismo, de aplicaci a partir de 2005, que modificar las normas contables utilizadas en estos momentos por las entidades financieras. Aunque no es el momento de detenerse en este tema, s que puede selarse el hecho de que las normas contables, en el caso de entidades financieras, deberan ser un producto de la colaboraci de expertos contables y supervisores, como ica forma de garantizar un tratamiento adecuado a los riesgos especficos de las entidades bancarias frente a otras empresas. La homogenizacin contable tiene, desde luego, ventajas, pero en ella debera tener cabida la consideraci de dichos aspectos diferenciales. El ejemplo del papel de regulador contable desarrollado por el Banco de Espaa, que ha producido indudables ventajas en el adecuado control supervisor de las entidades financieras y ha servido para mejorar su solvencia, debera tenerse en consideraci, en una inevitable estructura de normas contables ms homogeneizada. b)Los trabajos de IOSCO sobre independencia de auditores, seguimiento de los mismos y mejora en la informacin al mercado y la transparencia. c) La revisi y ampliaci de los principios de Corporate Governance de la OCDE. 6. Pero quizs, el rea de trabajo ms representativa de este enfoque global est representada por aquella que, desde hace 3 as, viene ocupando al Comit de Basilea. Un aspecto crucial de la estabilidad financiera es, indudablemente, aquel que trata de mejorar el anlisis de los riesgos de crdito, y otros, en que los bancos incurren, buscando un efecto incentivador de los sistemas de control de riesgos y estableciendo los requerimientos de capital adecuados para cada caso, de tal forma que los riesgos no esperados puedan ser cubiertos sin que la entidad vea en peligro su funcionamiento. ste es sin duda un aspecto fundamental del actual Acuerdo en elaboraci y, con frecuencia, es ste "en exclusiva" el que viene a representar todo el Acuerdo. Una pequea digresi en relaci con este tema y con la regulaci espala: Como ustedes saben, el fortalecimiento de los recursos propios de las entidades ha sido en nuestro caso una preocupaci permanente que nos ha llevado a aplicar principios ms exigentes que los internacionalmente admitidos. Pero, al margen de los recursos propios, la poltica de provisiones (que permitir hacer frente a los riesgos esperados materializados ono) ha sido un punto fuerte en la regulaci del Banco de Espaa. Creo que los tiempos que corren, y las experiencias recientes, estn validando con claridad la poltica seguida por el Banco y asumida por las entidades, cuyo efecto conjunto ha conducido a un sistema financiero saneado, con un coeficiente de solvencia por encima del 11%, eficiente y estable. Es una satisfacci, por ello, observar co en determinados organismos la idea de la provisi estadstica ha calado de tal forma que el concepto, previsiblemente, ser recogido en la normativa internacional de una manera u otra. 7. Pero volviendo al Acuerdo de Basilea, su contenido va ms all de la adecuada valoraci del capital necesario para cubrir los riesgos. Ning sistema ni entidad financiera podra funcionar so cumpliendo los requisitos mnimos de capital. La estabilidad financiera es mucho ms que eso y, en este sentido, el Acuerdo puede leerse como un enfoque global para hacer aqulla sostenible. En efecto, adems del elemento clave antes mencionado, que sera el objeto del Pilar 1, los aspectos relacionados con la poltica supervisora (Pilar 2) inevitablemente vinculados con la relaci regulaciautorregulaci; y la disciplina de mercado, que pasa por el adecuado suministro de informaci (Pilar 3), constituyen parte igualmente fundamental del Acuerdo. 8. De esta manera, el Acuerdo entra en un aspecto crucial relativo al mantenimiento de las "reglas del juego" que deben regir la interacci entre supervisi pblica, cierto grado de autorregulaci y disciplina de mercado que han sido vulnerados con aparente facilidad en un pasado reciente, tal como acabamos de ver, y cuyo funcionamiento es necesario mejorar y asegurar. 9. Tanto las autoridades supervisoras como los propios mercados, por la va de la autorregulaci, han iniciado la mejora de los fundamentos de la estabilidad financiera. La autorregulaci por la va de estndares y cigos de conducta son un elemento bsico para el funcionamiento de los mercados. Su importancia en unos u otros casos depende de las evoluciones histicas de funcionamiento en cada pas, y a priori no puede ser calificada como buena o como mala. La tarea de autorregulaci de los mercados tiene, por otra parte, limitaciones obvias en reas que pueden suscitar conflicto de intereses. Por muy bien que est desarrollada esta autorregulaci, es inevitable la presencia de la "poltica plica" de supervisi y regulaci. La tarea bsica de esta ltima en los campos que le son propios, debe orientarse, se est orientando ya, en nuestro pas entre otros, hacia una valoraci de la calidad de los procesos internos de control de riesgos. Por otro lado, su relaci con la autorregulaci debera servir para "fijar" los estndares y buenas prcticas con el fin de favorecer una expansi ms rpida de los mismos y hacer que se transformen en "requisitos mnimos", a partir de los cuales sean posibles mejoras individuales. Se evitaran as arbitrajes regulatorios y tambin el hecho de que las autorregulaciones tienen tambin un elevado componente cclico que hace que la autodisciplina sea ms difcil de mantener tanto en fases alcistas, por relajaci y exceso de confianza, como en las fases de baja para intentar escapar de alguna situacin apurada. 10.La regla de juego que complementa a las dos mencionadas es la disciplina de mercado. sta so puede darse si existen unos ganos de gobierno corporativo con un esquema de responsabilidades claro y un esquema de incentivos transparente con auditora interna independiente. Por otro lado, la disciplina de mercado so es tal si se respetan las prcticas contables adecuadas, y si la integridad y transparencia de la informaci suministrada permite a los inversores una toma de decisiones coherente. De nuevo aqu, la presencia del regulador tambin es necesaria. 11.Todo lo anterior constituye, pues, una agenda importante que, aunque ejemplificada en el Comit de Basilea, a su desarrollo estn contribuyendo gran nero de supervisores nacionales, organismos internacionales y los propios mercados. Al Acuerdo le quedan todava tres aos, pero no tendra sentido esperar, y no se est haciendo, de tal forma que muchas de las reformas que sern eventualmente aprobadas, ya estn empezando a sentar sus fundamentos. 12.Estos momentos, como mencion antes, son los propicios para emprender acciones y asegurar unos fundamentos de los sistemas financieros sidos y duraderos. Esta es una tarea de todos y no so un asunto de financieros, pero hay una parte que nos compete directamente, pues, como deca el Presidente del Comit de Basilea, en la tima reuni de Ciudad del Cabo: "Supervisores bancarios y banqueros centrales ciertamente comparten los objetivos [reducir la pobreza y promover el desarrollo econico]. Para cumplir nuestra obligacin de procurar la seguridad y solvencia del sistema financiero, tratamos de preservar los ahorros de los depositantes, promover la movilizaci del crdito y, en ltimo extremo, proteger la salud y el crecimiento de nuestras economas. Realmente, no podremos aliviar la pobreza ni promocionar el desarrollo econmico a menos que nuestros bancos estn bien dirigidos, nuestro sistema financiero sea estable y nuestros mercados transparentes y abiertos".

Title: Conference: Financial Circle of Barcelona, February 10, 2003
text: CONFERENCE OF THE GOVERNOR OF THE BANK OF SPAIN, JAIME CARUANA, AT THE FINANCIAL CIRCLE OF BARCELONA CONFERENCE OF THE GOVERNOR OF THE BANK OF SPAIN, JAIME CARUANA, AT THE FINANCIAL CIRCLE OF BARCELONA 9 1 BANCO DE ESPA84A / ECONOMIC BULLETIN / FEBRUARY 2003 BANCO DE ESPA84A / ECONOMIC BULLETIN / FEBRUARY 2003 Conference of the Governor of the Bank of Spain, Jaime Caruana, at the Financial Circle of Barcelona The Spanish economy at the entrance in 2003 Ladies and gentlemen: I want my first words to be of thanks to the organizers of this conference that gives me the opportunity to share with you some reflections on the current situation of the Spanish economy and the challenges it will face in the future. Uncertainty is undoubtedly the most frequent word today in any analysis of the international environment, largely due to the tensions posed by the possible armed conflict in Iraq. This climate of uncertainty is inhibiting the decisions of economic agents and hindering the implementation of a sustained recovery process. Geopolitical uncertainties are difficult to introduce in economic analysis and therefore, I will focus my presentation on examining the state of the Spanish economy and its capacity to intensify the recovery, once a good part of the aforementioned uncertainties disappear. Let me begin with my final conclusion: the Spanish economy in the difficult context of 2002 has developed with a comparatively favourable balance sheet and is in a good position to resume a more dynamic growth path, once the uncertainties that grip the world economy are cleared. This conclusion is supported by the fact that in the behaviour of our economy during these last two years of global slowdown, significant differences can be seen in relation to previous episodes of slowdown and also in relation to the evolution of the euro area. Likewise, the most recent data show certain changes that, if confirmed in the coming months, would mean a positive turn in the determinants of our growth pattern. There are also risks and challenges that need to be addressed to ensure sustained growth over the medium term. Challenges that have to do with maintaining macroeconomic stability, boosting productive investment and technological dynamism, promoting new technologies and improving the efficiency and flexibility of our markets and institutions. These are some of the aspects that I want to deal with in this presentation and for this it is essential, in a world like ours, increasingly integrated and dependent, that we pause for a few minutes to analyze the complex international economic situation. The year 2003 has begun without being able to clear the uncertainties and geopolitical tensions of last year that have fueled bullish expectations about oil prices, whose market has also been destabilized in recent weeks by the events in Venezuela and also, as I indicated earlier, have affected the confidence of companies and consumers. All this has been reflected in volatility and declines in the prices of the main stock markets, which were already punished by other factors: revision of earnings growth expectations, greater risk aversion of investors, deterioration of confidence in the integrity of accounting information and its control, etc. These declines in international stock markets have devalued the financial assets of households and raised the cost of capital for companies. So far, increases in the prices of energy products have not significantly affected the inflation rates of the main economies, because their economic growth rates are clearly below their potential and, in the case of the euro area, the revaluation of the currency has been an important compensatory factor. Against this background, policymakers have reacted by pursuing growth-sustaining macroeconomic policies that have sought to counteract the contractionary effects of the adverse geopolitical environment. Monetary policies have adopted, almost without exception, a markedly expansionary tone and in many countries budgetary consolidation efforts have been relaxed, with public deficits appearing to be of some consideration in some cases. These actions have helped to sustain household and general government spending, without business investment rates, conditioned by the prevailing uncertainty, having recovered the right tone to promote a phase of sustained cyclical recovery. This is, broadly speaking, the pattern observed in the US economy, where the shortage of savings that had been dragging on since the previous long expansionary period has been accentuated by the disappearance of the large public surpluses that had been registered in those years, and by the persistence of relatively high rates of increase in consumption and home purchases. However, investment in equipment has not yet recovered, influenced by the excess capacity generated in some sectors in the second half of the last decade and by the doubts that corporate results raise about the future evolution of the profitability of capital formation projects. In addition, at a time when interest rates are at historic lows, the wealth situation of households, characterised by high indebtedness, is vulnerable to adverse developments, so that these may erode the resilience shown by private consumption as one of the main supports of growth. Recovery expectations continue to depend largely on the evolution of the US economy since, in addition to this country, the only areas that are currently showing some strength are some Asian and Eastern European countries, but these do not have enough weight to have a significant impact on world trade. In Latin American economies, there are some signs of relief. At least that is what could be deduced from the greater stability that can be seen in the Argentine economy or from the reduction in interest rate differentials on Brazilian debt, after the formation of the new government. However, the region's growth prospects for the current year remain very modest. Activity in the euro area has been severely affected, as it could not be otherwise, by the lack of strength in the global economy, as external demand has not played the leading role expected from it. The most recent data, however, show a revival in exports compared to what happened in the first half of last year, which seems to have favoured an improvement in industrial expectations, which were very depressed. Indicators on investment in equipment have also been less negative than in previous periods, but consumer confidence levels have continued to deteriorate. The European economy is being particularly vulnerable to the uncertainties that accompany geopolitical tensions and the risks of armed conflict, due to the high sensitivity to oil price developments and the depressed state of confidence and expectations. Forecasts suggest that quarter-on-quarter growth in real GDP should have stabilized in the last quarter of last year, so that the rate of increase from the 2002 average will not reach 1%. And the prospects for recovery this year are modest and subject to the aforementioned uncertainties. The inflation rate for the area as a whole, partly reflecting inflationary tensions from abroad, but also encouraged by the rising labour costs that were taking place, remained above 2% last year and ended the year with a year-on-year increase in the HICP for the area as a whole of 2.3%. in the month of December. Productivity gains throughout the year have moderated unit labour cost growth and helped to improve inflationary expectations for 2003. It is foreseeable, therefore, that the behavior of prices will develop within what is considered consistent with the concept of stability, which presides over the objectives of monetary policy, provided that price tensions in international oil markets do not overwhelm the scenarios that are being discounted. In this context, the implementation of monetary policy, unique during the recent period of slowdown and weak economic growth, has been a complex task. The ECB has continuously monitored medium-term price constraints, taking into account, at all times, the risks affecting economic activity in the area. The improved inflation outlook, to which the appreciation of the euro exchange rate has contributed, which has significantly mitigated the impact of oil price increases, the persistence of a climate of uncertainty about the start and intensity of the recovery, led the ECB Council to reduce, last December, reference interest rates by half a percentage point. It should be recalled that rates remained unchanged at 3.25% since November 2001. The role played by public finances in this situation has been conditioned by the different starting point of the economies of the area. Those that had not sufficiently adjusted their budgetary position at the greatest economic boom have seen their public deficits exceed d0 or were about to do so d0 the requirements of the Stability and Growth Pact. In others, with healthier public finances, the operation of automatic stabilisers has, in some cases, generated small deficits, without undermining their structural positions. It is in this particularly uncertain scenario, which I have just outlined, that the Spanish economy must be placed when analysing the results of the year that has just ended and the prospects with which the new year is faced. The international environment has limited the growth of our markets, with the consequent negative impact on the growth of exports of goods and on tourism. The instability of financial markets and the fall in stock prices have reduced the financial wealth of households and have contributed to spreading a climate of uncertainty that has affected the expectations of economic agents, and in particular the particularly sensitive business sectors, when planning their investments, to the context in which they expect their activity to develop. And, finally, the tensions in the oil market, given the still high dependence of our economy on imported energy, have contributed, in the second part of the year, to raise the inflation rate. Taking into account the negative constraints in which it has had to operate, the results achieved by the Spanish economy in 2002, although showing a weakening of the rate of growth and job creation, deserve a positive assessment and, more importantly, open the door to moderately hopeful prospects for the current year. conditioned, however, to what happens in the uncertain international panorama. According to the forecasts that we have at the moment in the Bank of Spain, the growth of real GDP in the average of 2002 has been 2%, a figure that, although lower than that obtained in the previous year, is more than double that expected to have reached the whole of EMU. We will have taken an additional step in our process of real convergence with the countries of the area. In addition, the slowdown in the pace of growth throughout the year has been moderate and, according to available estimates, has tended to dry up in the final months of the year; In fact, year-on-year growth in the fourth quarter, calculated with the seasonally adjusted series, slightly exceeded the average for the year, standing at around 2.1%. The growth of the Spanish economy in 2002 was based on the contribution of domestic demand, while the contribution of net foreign demand to output growth was slightly negative. Within the national demand, it is worth noting the dynamism of investment in the construction sector d0 where the strength of home purchases by families stands out d0 and also, although to a lesser extent, that of household consumption, whose evolution has allowed a certain recovery in the family savings rate. The most depressed tone has been marked by investment in equipment, a feature that, as we have seen, is common to the European economy and the US, which shows the importance of the global expectations factor. The investment activity of the Public Administrations has also played an important role, as well as their consumption expenses. Despite this, the growth recorded by public revenues has allowed to close the year without moving significantly away from the programmed budgetary balance, since the public deficit has been only two tenths of a percentage point of GDP. The increase in employment has been more moderate than in the previous year, although significant d0 of the order of 1.3% (in equivalent jobs) d0 which has allowed a moderate recovery in productivity. In terms of the Labour Force Survey, growth was 1.6%, i.e. 256,000 additional jobs in 2002, but as the activity rate of the population has increased considerably (483,000), unemployment has also increased, moderately, approaching 11.5% of the active population. The agreed wage increases seem to have followed, in general, the agreement adopted between the social partners for collective bargaining last year. It was on the price front that the greatest difficulties were recorded in 2002. As you know, the year-on-year growth in consumer prices last December was 4%, so that our differential with respect to all the countries of the euro area reached a value of 1.7 percentage points; of 1.4 points, if we refer to the average of the year. Although it is true that the behaviour of the CPI has been influenced by some transitory factors related to the evolution of the prices of certain foods or to the resurgence of energy prices, to which I have already referred, we must not forget the persistence of significant price differentials d0 in relation to the euro area d0 in the components of services and non-energy industrial goods. In this regard, it should be noted that unit labour cost pressure over the past year has been relatively intense and differentiated according to sector, although its trend has been towards a certain slowdown, as apparent labour productivity has recovered; This, together with the expansion of margins in the sectors less exposed to competition, or in others where the strength of demand was greater, explain a significant part of the resurgence in the inflation rate of the economy in the past year. These are the main features of the Spanish economy in 2002. The evaluation of the results achieved, as I said before, is still favorable. That is why it is also important to analyse the risks that, to a large extent, are a consequence of the long period of growth that we have gone through and the factors that have driven it, as well as some rigidities that continue to condition the behaviour of some parts of our economy. In this sense, the persistence of high growth rates in consumption and investment in housing have limited the financing capacity of households and have generated significant increases in credit, especially in activities related to home purchases, with the consequent increase in their debt ratios to levels similar to those of the euro area. Various demand and supply factors, the lack of flexibility and complexity that characterize the housing market have facilitated the escalation of prices, which have continued to increase to a greater extent than expected. This process of rising prices has tended to feed itself by boosting investment in the sector, especially at a time when financing costs were particularly low and when the profitability of other alternative forms of investment was being very limited. On occasion I have pointed out the importance of the recovery being compatible with a recovery in private savings and a moderation of the use of external financing. From this point of view, an orderly containment of increases in house prices would be an important contribution to curbing household indebtedness and would make it easier for their financial position not to interfere with spending plans. The increase in corporate indebtedness has also been notable in recent years, due, in some cases, to the financing needs generated by investment flows abroad which, in many cases directed to Latin American countries, have contributed decisively to the internationalization of the Spanish economy. This trend has slowed down throughout 2002, partly as a result of low investment activity. Corporate profits have been adversely affected by the heavy provisions that some companies have had to face for risks incurred in Latin America and by capital losses suffered as a result of the fall in stock prices. However, ordinary yields have continued to grow at high rates, which has allowed historically high levels of profitability to be maintained and much higher than the costs of obtaining financial resources, so conditions are conducive to a recovery of investment when the uncertainty factors that inhibit business decisions at this juncture are cleared. However, possibly the most important challenge facing the Spanish economy is the containment of the inflation differential with the euro zone, since its persistence may end up eroding competitiveness and limiting our growth potential. The forecasts point to a significant improvement in the coming months, especially as some transitory factors related to the prices of energy products and some food products subside. Returning to the analysis of the most recent data, which refer, in most cases, to the last months of last year, we can see, however, certain relevant changes that may mark a turning point with respect to what have been the determining factors of our growth in the recent stage of moderate cyclical slowdown. Merchandise exports have thus begun to show signs of recovery, relative to the low levels reached at the end of 2001 and in the first half of last year. The resurgence of exports has been quickly felt in industrial activity, which also seems to resume positive growth rates, and all this has been reflected, finally, in business confidence indicators, which have improved appreciably. The most recent indicators on the performance of investment in equipment also point to an incipient improvement in this variable, after two long years of very negative results, while the growth of consumption and activity in the construction sector has moderated, although it continues to be very high d0 to which it also collaborates. The dynamism of infrastructure investments shows signs of greater containment. These trends are the ones with which the Spanish economy began in 2003 and its development will depend on how the international environment is configured. It does not seem foreseeable that there will be a significant change in the world economy until well into the year, as is assumed in most of the scenarios with which the different international organizations are working. Then, in the middle of the year, once some of the unknowns that weigh on the present have been cleared, it is expected that the main economies will recover an increasingly sustained tone, so that they will gradually approach their potential growth rate. This is also the most reasonable trajectory that can be expected for our economy this year. Its growth rate does not seem likely to increase significantly in the first half of the year, but it may do so later, as the external context improves and the recovery in investment in capital goods can be confirmed. At this point, I think it is worthwhile for us to delve into the reasons that have allowed the Spanish economy to obtain comparatively favourable results in this last cycle, in which the model of previous cycles in which the strong imbalances that were accumulating in the years of expansion had to be corrected through painful processes of recession and job destruction have been broken. In this way, we will be able to assess the guidelines that should guide our economy to ensure a sustained and stable growth rate in the future. I think we will all agree that Spain's entry into EMU and access to the levels of macroeconomic stability typical of the core countries of the area meant, for our economy, a positive boost that was profitable in terms of gains in competitiveness, improvements in the financing conditions of families and companies, moderation in wage cost growth and strengthening of favourable expectations about future growth possibilities. And all this in a few years in which very important technological changes were taking place in the international arena, which were revolutionizing the world of information and telecommunications and which, by generating very high increases in productivity, were allowing some economies d0 mainly the United States d0 to achieve very high growth, without incurring inflationary tensions. Thus, a pattern of growth was developed in which investment and exports became the main engines of growth and in which job creation was the main support for family expenses, which also found very favorable conditions for financing them. And so that all this could be developed in the right environment, a set of reforms were launched that aimed to adapt our regulatory framework and improve the competitiveness of our markets and institutions, adjusting the Public Administrations to the established postulates of budgetary stability. The favourable impulses received by the Spanish economy had allowed it to maintain relatively high growth rates that lasted until the cyclical slowdown of the world economy began. There was then a change in the pattern of growth of the Spanish economy, in which both exports and business investment were giving prominence and in which the most dynamic factors became, as we have seen, consumption and investment in the construction sector, as a consequence, in part, that employment maintained remarkable, albeit decreasing, growth rates, but, above all, that the monetary conditions established for the countries of the euro area were amply comfortable for our economy, which was in a more advanced cyclical position than most countries in the euro area. The fall in exports followed the pattern set by foreign markets and although there were no losses in the share of presence of our products in world markets, we did not increase it either, as was the usual pattern in previous years. In the case of productive investment, the contraction was more abrupt, as companies were the ones that most quickly felt the change in expectations that destabilized global financial markets. In fact, investment in capital goods began its slowdown in mid-2000, registering negative real rates of change in the following two years. Although the configuration of a growth pattern such as this, in which investment and exports maintain a relatively depressed tone, has been imposed by the events that condition the evolution of the world economy, it is necessary for the Spanish economy to recover, as soon as conditions permit, a growth model in which both variables once again have a prominent role. For this, as we have seen, it is necessary to preserve the levels of macroeconomic stability typical of the area to which we belong, that sufficient savings flows are available so that the levels of indebtedness of economic agents d0 and therefore, of the nation d0 remain within moderate levels and that the improvement in the functioning of our markets and institutions guarantees the most efficient allocation of resources. The deepening of real convergence within the Monetary Union requires the maintenance of competitiveness and a continuous improvement in efficiency, since it is not possible to use the exchange rate as an adjustment variable for the correction of imbalances that may arise. Exports need to increase their share of world markets and ensure that the penetration of imported products into the domestic market allows for greater satisfaction of the needs of firms and households but without diminishing growth potential. And productive investment d0 in equipment and infrastructure d0 has to be a source of productivity and efficiency gains, especially in a world, such as the current one, in which very important technological changes have taken place that are transforming the behavior of companies and consumers. The pattern of growth of the Spanish economy in the recent period has been conditioned by the need to absorb the high unemployment rates that had been achieved as a result of the macroeconomic imbalances and rigidities of the past. To this end, it was essential to maximize the use of the labour factor per unit of output, which led to intense rates of job creation and modest in terms of observed productivity growth. In the current situation, in order to continue narrowing the differences in welfare and income with our community partners, it is necessary to make continuity in job creation compatible with the response to the challenges posed by the accelerated pace of technological innovation and the advancement of the knowledge society. And this requires increasing the pace of investment in physical, technological and human capital and, especially, greater incorporation of information and communication technologies. The diffusion of these new technologies makes it possible to reduce production costs and increase productivity in industries and service branches that increasingly use inputs of this nature, leading to an increase in the productive potential of the economy. One aspect of this process, which is not always sufficiently underlined, is the effect that all this has on the organization of production, making it more flexible, more adaptable to the opportunities that arise in the markets and more efficient in its responsiveness. This reveals the complementarity that must exist between the promotion of the use of new technologies and the effort to provide markets with goods, factors and services with greater flexibility and to promote regulation that favors the creation and establishment of new companies and the development of venture capital markets. These reflections allow me to conclude this conference by pointing out the good position in which the economy is to resume a more dynamic growth path, once the uncertainties that grip the world economy are cleared, and, at the same time, the challenges that must be addressed to ensure its sustainability in the medium term. Challenges that have to do with maintaining macroeconomic stability, boosting productive investment and technological dynamism, promoting new technologies and improving the efficiency and flexibility of our markets and institutions. These are determining factors in competitiveness, which is undoubtedly the strategic variable on which the medium- and long-term success of our accession to the European Union and entry into the euro depends. 10.2.2003.
text_original: CONFERENCIA DEL GOBERNADOR DEL BANCO DE ESPAA, JAIME CARUANA, EN EL CRCULO FINANCIERO DE BARCELONA CONFERENCIA DEL GOBERNADOR DEL BANCO DE ESPAA, JAIME CARUANA, EN EL CRCULO FINANCIERO DE BARCELONA 9 1 BANCO DE ESPAA / BOLETN ECONMICO / FEBRERO 2003 BANCO DE ESPAA / BOLETN ECONMICO / FEBRERO 2003 Conferencia del Gobernador del Banco de Espaa, Jaime Caruana, en el Crculo Financiero de Barcelona La economa espaola en la entrada en el 2003 Seoras y seores: Quiero que mis primeras palabras sean de agradecimiento a los organizadores de esta conferencia que me brinda la oportunidad de compartir con ustedes algunas reflexiones sobre la situacin actual de la economa espaola y los retos a los que se enfrentar en el futuro. Incertidumbre es, sin duda, hoy la palabra ms frecuente en cualquier anlisis del entorno internacional, en buena parte debida a las tensiones que plantea el posible conflicto armado en Irak. Este clima de incertidumbre est inhibiendo las decisiones de los agentes econmicos y dificultando la puesta en marcha de un proceso de recuperacin sostenido. Las incertidumbres geopolticas son difciles de introducir en el anlisis econmico y por ello, voy a centrar mi presentacin en el examen del estado en que se encuentra la economa espaola y su capacidad de intensificar la recuperacin, una vez que desaparezcan buena parte de las incertidumbres mencionadas. Permtanme empezar por mi conclusin final: la economa espaola en el contexto difcil del ao 2002 se ha desenvuelto con un balance comparativamente favorable y est en buenas condiciones para reanudar una senda de crecimiento ms dinmico, una vez que se despejen las incertidumbres que atenazan a la economa mundial. Esta conclusin viene apoyada por la constatacin de que en el comportamiento de nuestra economa durante estos dos ltimos aos de desaceleracin mundial, se pueden apreciar diferencias importantes con relacin a previos episodios de desaceleracin y tambin con relacin a la evolucin de la zona euro. As mismo, los datos ms recientes muestran ciertos cambios que, de confirmarse en los prximos meses, supondran un giro positivo en los determinantes de nuestro patrn de crecimiento. Tambin existen riesgos y retos que es necesario abordar para asegurar un crecimiento sostenido a medio plazo. Retos que tienen que ver con el mantenimiento de la estabilidad macroeconmica, el impulso de la inversin productiva y el dinamismo tecnolgico, el fomento de las nuevas tecnologas y la mejora en la eficiencia y flexibilidad de nuestros mercados e instituciones. Estos son algunos de los aspectos que quiero tratar en esta presentacin y para ello resulta imprescindible, en un mundo como el nuestro, cada vez ms integrado y dependiente, que nos detengamos unos breves minutos en analizar la compleja situacin econmica internacional. El ao 2003 ha comenzado sin que hayan podido despejarse las incertidumbres y tensiones geopolticas del ao pasado que han alimentado expectativas alcistas sobre los precios del petrleo, cuyo mercado se ha visto adems desestabilizado en las ltimas semanas por los acontecimientos que se viven en Venezuela y tambin, como he indicado anteriormente, han incidido en la confianza de las empresas y consumidores. Todo ello se ha reflejado en volatilidad y descensos de las cotizaciones de los principales mercados burstiles, que ya venan castigadas por otros factores: revisin de expectativas de crecimiento de beneficios, mayor aversin al riesgo de los inversores, deterioro de la confianza en la integridad de la informacin contable y su control, etc. Estos descensos en las bolsas internacionales han desvalorizado los activos financieros de las familias y han elevado el coste del capital para las empresas. Hasta el momento, los aumentos en los precios de los productos energticos no han afectado significativamente a las tasas de inflacin de las principales economas, debido a que sus ritmos de crecimiento econmico se encuentran claramente por debajo de su potencial y, en el caso de la zona euro, la revalorizacin de la moneda ha sido un factor compensatorio importante. En esta tesitura, las autoridades econmicas han reaccionado aplicando polticas macroeconmicas sustentadoras del crecimiento que han tratado de contrarrestar los efectos contractivos procedentes del entorno geopoltico adverso. Las polticas monetarias han adoptado, prcticamente sin excepcin, un tono marcadamente expansivo y en muchos pases se han relajado los esfuerzos de consolidacin presupuestaria, apareciendo dficit pblicos de cierta consideracin en algunos casos. Estas actuaciones han ayudado a sostener el gasto de las familias y de las Administraciones Pblicas, sin que las tasas de inversin empresarial, condicionadas por la incertidumbre reinante, hayan recuperado el tono adecuado para impulsar una fase de recuperacin cclica sostenida. Este es, a grandes rasgos, el patrn que se observa en la economa de Estados Unidos, donde la escasez de ahorro que se arrastraba desde la larga etapa expansiva previa, se ha visto acentuada por la desaparicin de los cuantiosos supervit pblicos que se haban registrado en aquellos aos, y por la persistencia de tasas de aumento en el consumo y en la compra de viviendas de las familias relativamente elevadas. Mientras que, sin embargo, la inversin en equipo sigue sin recuperarse, influida por los excesos de capacidad que se generaron en algunos sectores en la segunda mitad de la pasada dcada y por las dudas que los resultados empresariales suscitan sobre la evolucin futura de la rentabilidad de los proyectos de formacin de capital. Adems, en un momento en el que los tipos de inters se encuentran en mnimos histricos, la situacin patrimonial de las familias, caracterizada por un elevado endeudamiento, resulta vulnerable a desarrollos adversos, de manera que estos podrn llegar a erosionar la resistencia que ha mostrado el consumo privado como uno de los principales soportes del crecimiento. Las expectativas de recuperacin siguen dependiendo en buena parte de la evolucin de la economa de los Estados Unidos ya que, adems de este pas, las nicas reas que en el momento actual estn mostrando una cierta fortaleza son algunos pases asiticos y del Este de Europa, pero estas no tienen peso suficiente para incidir de forma significativa en el comercio mundial. En las economas latinoamericanas, se detectan algunos indicios de alivio. Al menos eso es lo que podra deducirse de la mayor estabilidad que se aprecia en la economa argentina o de la reduccin en los diferenciales de los tipos de inters de la deuda brasilea, tras la formacin del nuevo gobierno. No obstante, las perspectivas de crecimiento de la regin para el ao actual siguen siendo muy modestas. La actividad de la zona del euro se ha visto muy afectada, como no podra ser de otra forma, por la falta de vigor de la economa mundial, ya que la demanda exterior no ha desempeado el papel impulsor que de ella se esperaba. En los datos ms recientes se aprecia, sin embargo, una reanimacin de las exportaciones en relacin con lo ocurrido en la primera mitad del ao pasado, lo que parece que ha favorecido una mejora de las expectativas industriales, que estaban muy deprimidas. Tambin los indicadores sobre la inversin en equipo han sido menos negativos que en los perodos precedentes, pero los niveles de confianza de los consumidores se han seguido deteriorando. La economa europea est siendo particularmente vulnerable a las incertidumbres que acompaan a las tensiones geopolticas y a los riesgos de conflictos armados, debido a la elevada sensibilidad a la evolucin de los precios del petrleo y al deprimido estado de la confianza y de las expectativas. Las previsiones apuntan a que el crecimiento intertrimestral del PIB real debe de haberse estabilizado en el ltimo trimestre del pasado ao, con lo que la tasa de aumento del promedio de 2002 no alcanzar el 1%. Y las perspectivas de recuperacin en este ao son modestas y estn sujetas a las incertidumbres mencionadas. La tasa de inflacin del conjunto de la zona, como consecuencia, en parte, de las tensiones inflacionistas procedentes del exterior, pero tambin alentada por las alzas que estaban teniendo lugar en los costes laborales, se ha mantenido por encima del 2% en el pasado ao y ha terminado el ejercicio con un incremento interanual del IAPC del conjunto de la zona del 2,3%, en el mes de diciembre. Las ganancias de productividad que han ido producindose a lo largo del ao han moderado el crecimiento de los costes laborales unitarios y han contribuido a mejorar las expectativas inflacionistas para 2003. Es previsible, por lo tanto, que el comportamiento de los precios se desenvuelva dentro de lo que se considera coherente con el concepto de estabilidad, que preside los objetivos de la poltica monetaria, siempre y cuando las tensiones de precios en los mercados internacionales del petrleo no desborden los escenarios que se estn descontando. En este marco, la instrumentacin de la poltica monetaria, nica durante el reciente perodo de desaceleracin y dbil crecimiento econmico, ha sido una tarea compleja. El BCE ha ejercido una vigilancia continuada de los condicionantes de los precios a medio plazo, teniendo en cuenta, en todo momento, los riesgos que afectaban a la actividad econmica del rea. La mejora de las perspectivas de inflacin, a la que han contribuido la apreciacin del tipo de cambio del euro que ha mitigado apreciablemente el impacto de las alzas del precio del petrleo, la persistencia de un clima de incertidumbre sobre el comienzo y la intensidad de la recuperacin, llev al Consejo del BCE a reducir, el pasado mes de diciembre, los tipos de inters de referencia en medio punto porcentual. Recurdese que los tipos permanecan invariables, en el 3,25%, desde el mes de noviembre del ao 2001. El papel desempeado por las finanzas pblicas en esta situacin se ha visto condicionado por el distinto punto de partida de las economas del rea. Aquellas que no haban ajustado suficientemente su posicin presupuestaria en los momentos de mayor bonanza econmica han visto como sus dficit pblicos desbordaban o estaban a punto de hacerlo los requerimientos del Pacto de Estabilidad y Crecimiento. En otras, con unas finanzas pblicas ms saneadas, la actuacin de los estabilizadores automticos ha generado, en algunos casos, pequeos dficit, sin menoscabo de sus posiciones estructurales. En este escenario, particularmente incierto, que acabo de esbozar, es en el que hay que situar a la economa espaola a la hora de analizar los resultados del ao que acaba de terminar y las perspectivas con las que se afronta el nuevo ejercicio. El entorno internacional ha limitado el cre-cimiento de nuestros mercados, con el consiguiente impacto negativo sobre el crecimiento de las exportaciones de bienes y sobre el turismo. La inestabilidad de los mercados financieros y el descenso en las cotizaciones burstiles han disminuido la riqueza financiera de las familias y han contribuido a propagar un clima de incertidumbre que ha afectado a las expectativas de los agentes econmicos, y de forma muy particular a los sectores empresariales, especialmente sensibles, a la hora de planificar sus inversiones, al contexto en el que esperan se desenvuelva su actividad. Y, en fin, las tensiones en el mercado del petrleo, dada la todava elevada dependencia de nuestra economa respecto de la energa importada, han contribuido, en la segunda parte del ao, a elevar la tasa de inflacin. Teniendo en cuenta los condicionantes negativos en los que se ha tenido que desenvolver, los resultados alcanzados por la economa espaola en 2002, aunque muestran un debilitamiento del ritmo de crecimiento y de creacin de empleo, merecen una valoracin positiva y, lo que es ms importante, abren la puerta a unas perspectivas para el ao en curso moderadamente esperanzadoras, condicionadas, no obstante, a lo que ocurra en el incierto panorama internacional. De acuerdo con las previsiones que tenemos en este momento en el Banco de Espaa, el crecimiento del PIB real en el promedio de 2002 ha sido del 2%, una cifra que, si bien es inferior a la obtenida en el ao precedente, dobla, sobradamente, la que se espera haya alcanzado el conjunto de la UEM, con lo que habremos dado un paso adicional en nuestro proceso de convergencia real con los pases de la zona. Adems, la desaceleracin en el ritmo de crecimiento a lo largo del ao ha sido moderada y, de acuerdo con las estimaciones disponibles, ha tendido a agotarse en los meses finales del ao; de hecho, el crecimiento interanual en el cuarto trimestre, calculado con la serie desestacionalizada, ha superado, ligeramente, al del promedio del ejercicio, situndose en torno al 2,1%. El crecimiento de la economa espaola en el ao 2002 se ha basado en la contribucin de la demanda nacional, mientras que la aportacin de la demanda exterior neta al aumento del producto ha sido ligeramente negativa. Dentro de la demanda nacional, hay que sealar el dinamismo de la inversin en el sector de la construccin donde destaca, a su vez, la pujanza de la compra de viviendas por las familias y tambin, aunque en menor medida, el del consumo de los hogares, cuya evolucin ha permitido una cierta recuperacin de la tasa de ahorro familiar. El tono ms deprimido lo ha marcado la inversin en equipo, rasgo que, como hemos visto, es comn a la economa europea y de los EEUU, lo que muestra la importancia del factor expectativas globales. Tambin ha jugado un papel relevante la actividad inversora de las Administraciones Pblicas, as como sus gastos de consumo.
