A pesar de ello, el crecimiento que han registrado los ingresos pblicos ha permitido cerrar el ao sin alejarse significativamente del equilibrio presupuestario programado, ya que el dficit pblico ha sido de solo dos dcimas porcentuales del PIB. El incremento del empleo ha sido ms moderado que en el ejercicio precedente, aunque significativo del orden del 1,3% (en puestos de trabajo equivalente), lo que ha permitido una moderada recuperacin de la productividad. En trminos de la Encuesta de Poblacin Activa, el crecimiento ha sido del 1,6%, es decir, 256 mil empleos adicionales en el ao 2002, pero como la tasa de actividad de la poblacin ha aumentado considerablemente (483 mil), el paro tambin lo ha hecho, de forma moderada, aproximndose al 11,5% de la poblacin activa. Los incrementos salariales pactados parece que han seguido, en lneas generales, el acuerdo adoptado entre los agentes sociales para la negociacin colectiva en el pasado ao. Ha sido en el frente de los precios donde se han registrado las mayores dificultades en el ao 2002. Como ustedes saben, el crecimiento interanual de los precios de consumo en el pasado mes de diciembre fue del 4%, con lo que nuestro diferencial con respecto al conjunto de pases de la zona euro alcanz un valor de 1,7 puntos porcentuales; de 1,4 puntos, si nos referimos al promedio del ao. Aunque es verdad que en el comportamiento del IPC han incidido algunos factores transitorios relacionados con la evolucin de los precios de ciertos alimentos o con el rebrote de los precios energticos, al que ya me he referido, no debemos olvidar la persistencia de diferenciales de precios importantes en relacin con la zona euro en los componentes de servicios y de bienes industriales no energticos. En este sentido, hay que sealar que la presin de los costes laborales unitarios durante el pasado ao ha sido relativamente intensa y diferenciada segn sectores, aunque su tendencia ha sido hacia una cierta desaceleracin, a medida que se recuperaba la productividad aparente del trabajo; ello, unido a la ampliacin de mrgenes en los sectores menos expuestos a la competencia, o en otros en los que la fuerza de la demanda era mayor, explican una parte importante del rebrote de la tasa de inflacin de la economa en el pasado ao. Estos son los grandes rasgos de la economa espaola en el ao 2002. La valoracin de los resultados alcanzados, como antes dije, no deja de ser favorable. Por ello es importante analizar tambin los riesgos que, en gran medida, son consecuencia del largo perodo de crecimiento que hemos atravesado y de los factores que lo han impulsado, as como de algunas rigideces que siguen condicionando el comportamiento de algunas partes de nuestra economa. En este sentido, la persistencia de tasas de crecimiento elevadas en el consumo y la inversin en vivienda han limitado la capacidad de financiacin de las familias y han generado aumentos importantes del crdito, especialmente en las actividades relacionadas con la adquisicin de viviendas, con la consiguiente elevacin de sus ratios de endeudamiento hasta niveles similares a los de la zona euro. Diversos factores de demanda y de oferta, la falta de flexibilidad y complejidad que caracteriza al mercado de la vivienda han facilitado la escalada de precios, que han seguido aumentando en mayor medida de lo que se esperaba. Este proceso de precios al alza ha tendido a autoalimentarse impulsando la inversin en el sector, especialmente en unos momentos en los que los costes de financiacin eran particularmente reducidos y en los que la rentabilidad de otras formas de inversin alternativas estaba siendo muy limitada. En alguna ocasin he sealado la importancia de que la reactivacin sea compatible con una recuperacin del ahorro privado y una moderacin de la apelacin a la financiacin ajena. Desde este punto de vista, una contencin ordenada de las alzas en el precio de las viviendas sera una importante contribucin al freno del endeudamiento de las familias y facilitara que su posicin financiera no interfiriese con los planes de gasto. El aumento del endeudamiento de las empresas ha sido tambin notable en estos ltimos aos, debido, en algunos casos, a las necesidades de financiacin generadas por los flujos de inversin al exterior que, dirigidos en muchos casos a pases latinoamericanos, han contribuido decisivamente a la internacionalizacin de la economa espaola. Esta tendencia se ha flexionado a lo largo de 2002, como consecuencia, en parte, de la baja actividad inversora. Los beneficios empresariales se han visto negativamente afectados por las fuertes provisiones que algunas empresas han tenido que hacer frente a los riesgos contrados en Latinoamrica y por las prdidas de capital sufridas como consecuencia de la cada de las cotizaciones burstiles. No obstante, los rendimientos ordinarios han seguido creciendo a tasas elevadas, lo que ha permitido mantener unos niveles de rentabilidad histricamente altos y muy superiores a los costes de la obtencin de recursos financieros, por lo que las condiciones son propicias a una recuperacin de la inversin cuando se despejen los factores de incertidumbre que inhiben las decisiones empresariales en la presente coyuntura. Sin embargo, posiblemente el reto ms importante al que se enfrenta la economa espaola es la contencin del diferencial de inflacin con la zona euro, ya que su persistencia puede terminar erosionando la competitividad y limitar nuestro potencial de crecimiento. Las previsiones apuntan a una mejora significativa en los prximos meses, especialmente en la medida en la que algunos factores transitorios relacionados con los precios de los productos energticos y de algunos productos alimenticios vayan remitiendo. Volviendo al anlisis de los datos ms recientes, que se refieren, en la mayora de los casos, a los ltimos meses del ao pasado, se aprecian, sin embargo, ciertos cambios relevantes que pueden marcar un punto de inflexin con respecto a lo que han sido los factores determinantes de nuestro crecimiento en la reciente etapa de moderada desaceleracin cclica. As, las exportaciones de mercancas han comenzado a dar sntomas de recuperacin, en relacin con los bajos niveles que se haban llegado a alcanzar al final de 2001 y en la primera mitad del ao pasado. El rebrote de la exportacin se ha dejado sentir rpidamente en la actividad industrial, que tambin parece retomar tasas de aumento positivas, y todo ello se ha reflejado, en fin, en los indicadores de confianza empresariales, que han mejorado apreciablemente. Los indicadores ms recientes sobre el comportamiento de la inversin en equipo apuntan, igualmente, hacia una mejora incipiente de esta variable, tras dos aos largos de resultados muy negativos, mientras que se ha moderado el crecimiento del consumo y la actividad del sector de la construccin, aunque contina siendo muy elevada a lo que colabora, tambin, el dinamismo de las inversiones en infraestructuras, muestra indicios de una mayor contencin. Estas tendencias son con las que la economa espaola ha comenzado el ao 2003 y su desarrollo depender de cmo vaya configurndose el entorno internacional. No parece previsible que se produzca un cambio significativo en la economa mundial hasta bien avanzado el ao, tal y como se supone en la mayora de los escenarios con los que se est trabajando en los distintos organismos internacionales. Despus, a mediados del ao, una vez que se hayan despejado algunas de las incgnitas que pesan sobre la actualidad, se espera que las principales economas vayan recuperando un tono cada vez ms sostenido, de forma que se vayan aproximando, paulatinamente, a su ritmo de crecimiento potencial. Esta es, tambin, la trayectoria ms razonable que cabe esperar para nuestra economa en el presente ejercicio. No parece probable que su ritmo de crecimiento se acente significativamente en la primera mitad del ao, pero s lo puede hacer posteriormente, a medida que mejore el contexto exterior y se pueda confirmar la recuperacin en la inversin en bienes de equipo. Llegado a este punto, creo que vale la pena que profundicemos en las razones que han permitido a la economa espaola obtener unos resultados comparativamente favorables en este ltimo ciclo, en el que se ha roto el modelo de ciclos anteriores en el que los fuertes desequilibrios que se iban acumulando en los aos de expansin deban corregirse a travs de procesos dolorosos de recesin y destruccin de empleo. De esta forma, estaremos en condiciones de valorar las pautas que deben guiar a nuestra economa para asegurarse un ritmo de crecimiento sostenido y estable en el futuro. Creo que todos estaremos de acuerdo en que la entrada de Espaa en la UEM y el acceso a los niveles de estabilidad macroeconmica propios de los pases centrales del rea supuso, para nuestra economa, un impulso positivo que se fue rentabilizando en trminos de ganancias de competitividad, mejoras en las condiciones de financiacin de familias y empresas, moderacin en el crecimiento de los costes salariales y afianzamiento de unas expectativas favorables sobre las posibilidades de crecimiento futuras. Y todo ello en unos aos en los que se estaban produciendo en el mbito internacional cambios tecnolgicos muy importantes, que estaban revolucionando el mundo de la informacin y las telecomunicaciones y que, al generar aumentos muy elevados en la productividad, estaban permitiendo a algunas economas principalmente a Estados Unidos alcanzar crecimientos muy elevados, sin incurrir en tensiones inflacionistas. Se fue configurando, as, un patrn de crecimiento en el que la inversin y las exportaciones se constituyeron en los principales motores del crecimiento y en el que la creacin de empleo era el sostn principal de los gastos familiares, que encontraron, adems, unas condiciones muy favorables para su financiacin. Y para que todo ello pudiera desenvolverse en el entorno adecuado, se pusieron en marcha un conjunto de reformas que tenan como propsito adecuar nuestro marco regulatorio y mejorar la competitividad de nuestros mercados e instituciones, ajustndose las Administraciones Pblicas a los postulados de estabilidad presupuestaria establecidos. Los impulsos favorables recibidos por la economa espaola le haban permitido mantener ritmos de crecimiento relativamente elevados que se prolongaron hasta que se inici la fase de desaceleracin cclica de la economa mundial. Tuvo lugar, entonces, un cambio en el patrn de crecimiento de la economa espaola, en el que tanto la exportacin como la inversin empresarial fueron cediendo protagonismo y en el que los factores ms dinmicos pasaron a ser, como hemos visto, el consumo y la inversin en el sector de la construccin, como consecuencia, en parte, de que el empleo mantuvo ritmos de crecimiento notables, aunque decrecientes, pero, sobre todo, de que las condiciones monetarias establecidas para los pases de la zona euro resultaron ampliamente holgadas para nuestra economa, que se encontraba en una posicin cclica ms avanzada que la mayora de los pases de la zona. La cada de las exportaciones sigui la pauta marcada por los mercados exteriores y aunque no se registraron prdidas en la cuota de presencia de nuestros productos en los mercados mundiales, tampoco la aumentamos, como era la pauta habitual en aos anteriores. En el caso de la inversin productiva, la contraccin fue ms brusca, pues las empresas fueron las que acusaron ms rpidamente el cambio de expectativas que desestabiliz los mercados financieros mundiales. De hecho, la inversin en bienes de equipo inici su desaceleracin a mediados del ao 2000, registrando en los dos ejercicios posteriores tasas de variacin real negativas. Aunque la configuracin de un patrn de crecimiento como este, en el que la inversin y las exportaciones mantienen un tono relativamente deprimido, ha venido impuesto por los acontecimientos que condicionan la evolucin de la economa mundial, es necesario que la economa espaola recupere, en cuanto las condiciones lo permitan, un modelo de crecimiento en el que ambas variables vuelvan a tener un destacado protagonismo. Para ello, como hemos visto, es necesario preservar los niveles de estabilidad macroeconmica propios de la zona a la que pertenecemos, que se disponga de los flujos de ahorro suficientes para que los niveles de endeudamiento de los agentes econmicos y por ende, de la nacin se mantengan dentro de unas cotas moderadas y que la mejora en el funcionamiento de nuestros mercados e instituciones garantice la asignacin ms eficiente de los recursos. La profundizacin de la convergencia real dentro de la Unin Monetaria requiere el mantenimiento de la competitividad y una mejora continuada de la eficiencia, ya que no es posible utilizar el tipo de cambio como variable de ajuste para la correccin de los desequilibrios que se puedan generar. Las exportaciones tienen que aumentar su participacin en los mercados mundiales y procurar que la penetracin de los productos importados en el mercado interior permita una mayor satisfaccin de las necesidades de empresas y familias pero sin restar potencial de crecimiento. Y la inversin productiva en equipo y en infraestructuras tiene que ser una fuente de ganancias de productividad y eficiencia, sobre todo en un mundo, como el actual, en el que han tenido lugar cambios tecnolgicos muy importantes que estn transformando el comportamiento de empresas y consumidores. El patrn de crecimiento de la economa espaola en el perodo reciente ha estado condicionado por la necesidad de absorber las elevadas tasas de desempleo que se haban alcanzado como consecuencia de los desequilibrios macroeconmicos y las rigideces del pasado. Para ello, era imprescindible maximizar la utilizacin del factor trabajo por unidad de producto, lo que determinaba unos ritmos intensos de creacin de empleo y modestos en cuanto al crecimiento de la productividad observada. En la situacin actual, para seguir acortando las diferencias de bienestar y renta con nuestros socios comunitarios es necesario hacer compatible la continuidad en la generacin de empleo con la respuesta a los retos que plantea el acelerado ritmo de innovacin tecnolgica y el avance de la sociedad del conocimiento. Y ello requiere intensificar los ritmos de inversin en capital fsico, tecnolgico y humano y, especialmente, una mayor incorporacin de las tecnologas de la informacin y las comunicaciones. La difusin de estas nuevas tecnologas permite reducir costes de produccin y aumentar la productividad en las industrias y ramas de servicios que crecientemente utilizan inputs de esta naturaleza, dando lugar a un aumento del potencial productivo de la economa. Un aspecto de este proceso, que no siempre es suficientemente subrayado, es el efecto que todo ello tiene en la organizacin de la produccin, hacindola ms flexible, ms adaptable a las oportunidades que surgen en los mercados y ms eficiente en su capacidad de respuesta. Lo cual revela la complementariedad que debe existir entre el impulso del uso de las nuevas tecnologas y el esfuerzo por dotar a los mercados de bienes, factores y servicios de mayor flexibilidad y por promover una regulacin que favorezca la creacin y establecimiento de nuevas empresas y el desarrollo de los mercados de capital-riesgo. Estas reflexiones me permiten terminar esta conferencia sealando la buena posicin en que se encuentra la economa para reanudar una senda de crecimiento ms dinmico, una vez que se despejen las incertidumbres que atenazan a la economa mundial, y, a la vez, los retos que es necesario abordar para asegurar su sostenimiento a medio plazo. Retos que tienen que ver con el mantenimiento de la estabilidad macroeconmica, el impulso de la inversin productiva y el dinamismo tecnolgico, el fomento de las nuevas tecnologas y la mejora en la eficiencia y flexibilidad de nuestros mercados e instituciones. Factores determinantes de la competitividad, que es sin duda la variable estratgica de la que depende el xito a medio y largo plazo de nuestra incorporacin a la Unin Europea y de la entrada en el euro. 10.2.2003.

Title: Conference: V Information Society 2003. Title: Telecommunications and Economics
text: V INFORMATION SOCIETY 2003 VALENCIA 14 MAY 2003 CONFERENCE OF THE GOVERNOR OF THE BANK OF SPAIN TITLE: TELECOMMUNICATIONS AND ECONOMY Good morning, everyone. It is an honor for me to participate in these days and I am very grateful for the invitation. Information and communication technologies have played a key role in the economic evolution and debate of these scams. In this speech, I will try to present some ideas on the role of information and communication technologies in economic growth and well-being. Although the focus of my presentation is economic, I will begin by acknowledging that the transformations that new information and communication technologies have induced go far beyond the purely economic and include fundamental changes in the way we relate to each other and, also, in the way in which we access and treat information. The world economy is experiencing a situation of low growth and low investment, while uncertainties persist about the extent of the expected recovery, although the central scenario is that of an improvement in the pace of activity in the second part of the year. The decrease in geopolitical uncertainties, the improvement in the situation of financial markets and the decline in oil prices support this scenario. This situation of modest global growth, geographically unevenly distributed, is the result of a set of factors, among which the sum of global shocks to which the economy has been subjected in the scams stands out. Among them is the rise and crisis of the communications and information technology sector. As a result, the telecommunications and new technologies sector has been seriously affected by overinvestment and overcapacity, excessive indebtedness, falls in demand, dramatic changes in expectations and financing difficulties, and capital withdrawals, among others. Many companies have had to make major adjustments, which has limited their ability to invest. In some cases, the question has arisen as to whether the new economy is dead or whether, on the contrary, as I believe, we are faced with a crisis of digesti of past excesses, rather than a crisis of a structural nature. The interrelation between the processes of intense technological renewal and the economy is not new, and history shows how technological revolutions have been accompanied, on many occasions, by periods of excesses and crises in which financial, economic and technological factors are mixed. In this context, and on the occasion of my participation in these conferences on the Information Society, it seemed appropriate to review the role of the new technologies in this phase of cyclical slowdown, in order to assess whether recent events support the role attributed to them as responsible for the appearance of the so-called New Economy, at the end of the millennium. As you probably recall, the basic argument of the New Economy was that the generalization in broad sectors of the use of applications derived from new computer and communication technologies would have caused a change in the pattern of productivity behavior. This change would have been the trigger for the prolonged period of strong economic expansion and low inflation that the US economy experienced in the second half of the nineties. It would be interesting to recall that an increase in productivity is important for several reasons: first, it improves an economy's capacity for growth, that is, its potential growth; Secondly, it simplifies the way in which labour costs are transmitted to prices and, finally, it determines the evolution of real wages and living standards. Some thought that the implications of this paradigm shift would go further, affecting the very intensity of economic cycles d0 for which considerable softening was expected d0 or even the determinants of stock prices. The focus of this debate is therefore in the United States, but it quickly spreads to other geographical areas, where the analysis of the determinants of economic growth and, in particular, of the differences in productivity behaviour between the United States and Europe, happens to occupy a prominent role in economic policy debates. In relation to the explanatory causes of these differences, some agreement was reached on the role that could be played by the lower innovative dynamism d0 which, in turn, would have been reflected in a slower incorporation of new technologies into production processes in Europe d0 and the existence of product markets and less competitive factors. In this conference I propose to recall, briefly, the channels through which the economic effects after the adoption of new technologies run and review the conditions of the success of their implementation. I shall now provide some information on the empirical results obtained in the work carried out by various institutions on the influence of new technologies on output and productivity growth, which have taken into account, where possible, the economic slowdown. I will also try to situate the relative position of the Spanish economy in this area and point out the challenges that will have to be addressed in the future in order to achieve a reasonable development of the Information Society. I shall conclude my speech with a few notes on the prospects for the evolution of new information and communication technologies. * * * * The economic effects linked to the use of new technologies are activated when technological advances translate into decreases in their prices and appreciable improvements in quality. This causes cuts in the production costs of the industries that use them as productive inputs, as well as increases in productivity, which spread to the rest of the economy. As a result, it becomes more productive, increasing its capacity for growth, while inflationary pressures are addressed. Some studies seal three stages in the way in which the effects of these technological revolutions spread: The first phase would be that of technological change that raises productivity in the sector that is innovating. The second stage would be the fall in relative prices as a result of the technological progress mentioned, which would cause greater investment in these cheaper products from other sectors of the economy, that is, a greater increase in capital. The process would conclude with a reorganization facilitated by these increased investments that would determine an increase in productivity. These two elements, deepening of investments and organizational improvements, which occur in the two phases, are key to understanding productivity gains. The effects I have just described are not very different from those detected after the emergence of technological innovations of comparable significance, such as the establishment of the railway or the invention of electricity, both of which have been repeatedly cited in the debates on the New Economy. There are elements common to all these technological revolutions, among which the following can be highlighted: first, in the cases cited the initial productivity gains were due to the increase in investments as a result of the aforementioned price falls. However, the productivity gains derived from the reorganization of production processes happened with delay, a decade later. A second element was the tendency for the processes of technological progress to be accompanied by periods of excesses in the financial markets. There are, however, in the current situation, some differentiating elements that would justify the greater power in the transmission of this generation of innovations. Firstly, it seems that, on this occasion, in the information technology revolution, the fall in prices has been exceptionally greater. The fall in semiconductor prices associated with Moore's law is often mentioned in this regard. Secondly, the increasing globalization of the world economy would have led to a more rapid diffusion of new information and communication technologies. At the same time, its very nature is more conducive to the emergence of innovative forms of production organization, with new rules, principles and institutions, which would have promoted improvements in the efficiency of production processes, also boosting the potential growth of the economy. It is evident, for example, that the generalization in the use of the Internet has created opportunities, businesses and services hitherto non-existent and has allowed a significant reduction in the costs of searching for information and the opening up to competition of services which, until not so long ago, enjoyed elements of local monopoly. From this point of view, it is clear that the widespread use of the Internet encourages the efficiency and competition of the economy. Again, I would like to emphasize that, although I focus on the economy, we cannot lose sight of the importance of these phenomena in the transformation of society: quick access to information, capacity for mass processing, possibility of communication without distance imposing limitations, etc. The transmission of these effects to society as a whole is not, however, automatic and requires that the economy has achieved the degree of competence and flexibility necessary to facilitate organisational changes inherent in the efficient use of new technologies, the adaptation of workers' skills to a changing environment and a dynamic framework for business creation. To illustrate the importance of flexibility at the enterprise level, the example of trade in the United States is often cited, which contributes a relatively important part to its increase in productivity. Trade in the US invested heavily in technology in the second half of the 90s, but its increase in productivity does not result fundamentally from having more fast computers, but from profound transformations in the reorganization of its business, its supply chains, its stock and sales management, etc. In short, it was the result of a process of reorganization that technology made possible. Technology is required, but also the initiative and decision to make changes. In this sense, it is known that technical progress improves the quality of productive capital, but that, at the same time, it generates new demands on the qualifications of workers. Therefore, it is essential to make the necessary investment to make the training adjustments that guarantee that complementary progress is made in both aspects. It is also essential that the regulatory environment favors the access of new business projects to financing. In any case, I would like to recall that the more or less permanent nature of these effects constitutes one of the central elements in the debate on the New Economy. In this sense, its promoters defended the structural nature of the productivity gains experienced by the US economy in the late nineties. Faced with them, another widespread opinion was the one that attributed this strong dynamism of productivity, in addition to the impact of new technologies, to other factors, such as the cyclical expansion itself, the high degree of liberalization of the markets for goods and services in the United States and even to the statistical effect produced by errors in the measurement of the relevant variables. All this led to the prediction of a slowdown in productivity, once cyclical conditions changed, an extreme that has not occurred, as I will comment later, and that shows the solidity of the change in productivity patterns registered in the US economy. * * * * Let me now provide some figures on the size of the ICT sectors in the OECD countries, as well as the investment effort being made in this area. According to the OECD's estimates, the importance of the information and communication technology sector d0 defined in a standard way d0 grew very rapidly in the course of the nineties. Thus, in 2000, the added value generated by these productive branches was between 4% and 17% of the added value of the market economy in the member countries of this organization, and investment in this type of technology between 15% and 30% of non-residential productive investment in the sector. Due to its greater intensity, the investment made by the United States, Australia and Finland stands out, countries that are in the group of those in which, according to OECD estimates, there would have been the greatest contribution of new technologies to aggregate productivity growth. From a sectoral point of view, the greatest contribution of new technologies has occurred in the services sector, especially in trade and financial services, where the greatest productivity gains attributable to this effect are recorded. This result is consistent with the greater possibilities for companies operating in these sectors to use applications derived from new computer and communications technologies in their business area. By timo, the available empirical evidence suggests that, in the most recent years of less investment dynamism, technological change would have continued and Production and investment in new technologies would have continued to boost economic growth and productivity gains in the most advanced countries in this area. Naturally, given the excess capacity that has accumulated over the past decade, the rate of progress in production and in the incorporation of these new technologies into production processes would have decreased. Once I have reviewed the international evidence, I will go on to give some figures on the development of new technologies in Spain and on their economic effects estimated, among other institutions, by the Bank of Spain. This will allow us to know its relative position on the international scene, which I have presented above, and to discuss the challenges it faces in the medium term. I would like to begin by saying that Spain has participated in the general declines in the prices of goods and services constituted by the new information and communication technologies, which, in the case of telecommunications, has been further boosted by the environment of greater competition that has resulted from the liberalization process experienced by the sector in the scams. To obtain a general idea of the magnitude of these decreases, the behavior followed by the corresponding rricas of the CPI can be used as a reference. Thus, the telephony component has fallen by 9.6% since 1999 d0 the first year of liberalization of the sector d0 and that of computers and computer equipment by 50.1% since 1995, although, in this case, the price cuts began before that date. These decreases are more pronounced if the price indices used in this comparison are corrected by the improvements in quality that have been incorporated by the new generations of products, as has been estimated in different works carried out in the Bank of Spain. In the case of computers, for example, these findings indicate that, in the period 1992 to 2000, the usual price measures would have underestimated price declines by around 26% each, a figure sufficiently illustrative of the measurement biases that may be incurred with the usual techniques of estimating deflators and the added value of goods and services subject to major innovations. technolic. This would imply that part of the lack of productivity is purely due to a statistical effect. On the other hand, according to our estimates, the importance of the sector producing this type of goods, estimated by its participation in the added value of the market economy, amounted to 6% in 2001, placing Spain in the group of countries least specialized in this type of production within the OECD. However, in line with the developments that have been observed at the international level, the sector would have followed an upward trajectory during the second half of the nineties, and would have shown a very favorable evolution in the scams, with increases in productivity and employment much higher than those of other sectors. At the same time, the incorporation of new technologies in production processes has advanced at a good pace d0 as reflected in the strong increase in this This type of capital in the investment of Spanish firms in scams and has contributed positively to the growth of added value and aggregate productivity. By scam, and as it was also detected for other countries, certain branches of services d0 in the case of Spain, communications, business services and distribution d0 have benefited particularly from the increases in productivity that the use of new technologies has led. However, despite this progress, there are indications that the development of the Information Society in Spain is lagging behind. As is well known, particularly in this forum, this idea is shared by many analysts and is the main conclusion of the report prepared by the Special Study Committee on the Development of the Information Society, recently published. It identifies three areas in which it is necessary to increase the presence of new information and communication technologies: Firstly, in the Plica Administration, where it is recognized that, despite the progress made in the supply of services, there is, in comparison with other countries in our environment, room to increase their use internally and to increase transactions with citizens. Secondly, in SMEs, where a path is detected to integrate new technologies into their production processes and to increase their online presence. Thirdly, in the incorporation of citizens into the Information Society, since it is significantly behind in various areas. In households, the rate of introduction of PCs and access to the Internet is below the European average, although broadband penetration is one of the highest in Europe. At the same time, there has been a strong growth of thousand telephony, which has been favored by the development of a European standard and a high degree of competition. The report highlights the shortcomings that occur in the educational field in terms of the use of new technologies within educational programs and the existence of a strong potential for expansion in health and judicial environments. These constraints in the development of the information society are taking place despite the many initiatives that have been taken in the scams to promote spending on innovation and development and to encourage the use of new technologies, which have been implemented, to a large extent, through the establishment of generous tax benefits. In this respect, I would like to recall that the Spanish government is particularly involved in the development of the Lisbon Agenda, which was set by the European Council in the spring of 2000 and whose main objective is to make the European Union one of the most competitive economies by 2010, which should be achieved through the achievement of full employment and the development of the Information Society. From this point of view, all the initiatives that have recently been developed to identify the obstacles faced by the full use of new technologies, as well as the actions that have been undertaken in the regulatory field to eliminate these obstacles, are relevant. In particular, I would like to mention the adoption last year of the law that regulates electricity trade and the approval, just a month ago, of the preliminary draft of the electricity signature. The first of these initiatives will provide greater legal certainty for users and service providers and will therefore most likely contribute to promoting the use of the Internet and other interactive services. The second seeks to promote a more widespread use of the electrical firm in order to increase security in telematic communications, as well as to streamline the Electricity Administration and commerce, both aspects susceptible to improvement, as sel8e previously. The relative backwardness of the development of the Information Society in Spain responds, however, to a more structural characteristic, given that this economy has traditionally shown a relatively weak pace in the incorporation of innovations, compared to European standards. This manifests itself in many aspects of Spanish economic life and, in the short term, is also influencing the slow progress of productivity growth in these scams. From this point of view, for the Spanish economy to obtain maximum efficiency in the use of new technologies, it is necessary that the process of liberalization of product markets and the reforms in the labour market undertaken a few years ago continue to advance. Only in this way will the necessary competitive conditions be created to encourage innovation and the degree of flexibility required to facilitate the adaptation of enterprises, productive capital and the capacities of workers to the new productive and organizational processes that new technological applications allow. In addition, education policies must have the capacity to adjust to correct any skills gaps that may be identified. By timo, in line with the regulatory developments to which I referred earlier, the regulatory framework must try to reduce risk and uncertainties -which is not easy in such a dynamic sector-, provide an environment that encourages investment and sustainable competition in the long term, which requires operators with critical mass and investment capacity. To highlight the importance for the Spanish economy of taking this relatively ambitious approach, it is worth recalling the factors that explain American leadership in this area. As previously stated, this has been the result of combining, on the one hand, the significant investment effort made to produce and incorporate these technologies in the different production processes and, on the other, the configuration of a very competitive and flexible economic environment, favoring the diffusion towards the whole of society of organizational changes and the use of applications derived from new technologies. The strength of this approach has been evident during the current cyclical slowdown, in which productivity in the United States has continued to show sustained increases, despite the significant cuts in activity that have occurred in these three scams. On the other hand, the more recent evolution of technological stock prices, showing a slight recovery, may be signalling the end of the process of price correction beginning in spring 2000, which, together with the elimination of some overcapacity and the adjustment of expectations for corporate profits, It highlights the prospects for continued moderate expansion of new technologies and their contribution to economic growth. This lesson is especially important for the Spanish economy in which, in addition to the flexibility improvements that it still has to solve, the business fabric follows a pattern of productive specialization in manufacturing with a very marked orientation towards medium-high technology sectors, in contrast to the lower importance of sectors that produce more technologically advanced goods. However, from a medium-term perspective, it is expected that Spanish companies will continue to demand computer and telecommunications equipment, since they will have to undertake a relatively large catching up process in this area and will have to replace equipment subject to rapid depreciation. In addition, as I have said above, there are sufficient indications that the development of technological improvements has not been exhausted, so that further declines in the prices of these goods must be foreseen to encourage their more intensive use by Spanish companies and families. If, at the same time, the Spanish economy continues to make progress in shaping a more competitive environment, I believe that the prospects for the evolution of the sector will be favourable and that, in great probability, it will contribute positively to the growth and economic well-being of our society. **** Let me conclude this conference by extending some of the reflections on information and communication technologies to the economy as a whole. The Spanish economy has shown remarkable resilience in an international context of cyclical slowdown that has manifested itself in the maintenance of high growth rates in activity and employment, within a relatively moderate slowdown trajectory. This reflects the improvement in their capacity to respond to adverse shocks, which has been achieved as a result of the new macroeconomic stability regime following its accession to EMU and the structural reforms undertaken in the scams. Despite this favourable diagnosis, in order to ensure that a path of sustained growth without inflation is maintained in the medium term that allows adequate competitiveness records to be achieved and to continue to reduce differences in economic well-being with the most advanced countries, the Spanish economy must, however, modify some characteristics of its current growth pattern to meet the challenge of productivity, in line with the recommendations I have just set out in the field of new information and communication technologies. In particular, there is a need for an intensification of investment in capital goods d0 perhaps the weakest aspect of the current economic situation d0 and for the right conditions to be created for the incorporation of technological advances, including, of course, those linked to information and communications. Only in this way will sustained gains in productivity be achieved which, in combination with those generated by a more labour-intensive use, permanently expand the potential growth of this economy. Allow me to make a few thoughtful thoughts on new technologies. The persistence of productivity growth in the American economy, even in times of cyclical slowdown, the fact that technological dynamism has continued even in difficult times and that the number of users and applications continues to grow all suggest that the crisis in information and communication technologies is, as I said earlier, More digesti than structural. Improving society's access to new technologies, which must become normal and everyday, and improving content and the quality of services must be objectives and priorities of the first order: for example, advances in speed, through broadband access, or the consolidation of confidence in the security of transactions, so that more citizens and companies are incorporated into the information society, which will require additional investments. I have mentioned economic, technological and regulatory factors, but communication technologies deal with aspects related to the true essence of human society, such as access to information and communication between people. Therefore, its development will not only depend on technological development, which is undoubtedly important, or on having a flexible economy, which is also vital, but it will depend, to a large extent, on the changes that occur in society. In this sense, education is now more important than ever, but not simply traditional education, but the ability to adapt and use available knowledge. Thanks a lot.
