El que, durante el primer trimestre, las exportaciones espalas dirigidas a los mercados europeos hayan aumentado el 5%, aproximadamente, y que las ventas a otras reas extracomunitarias lo hayan hecho en el 9%, tambin de forma aproximada, son, sin duda, resultados favorables. Ahora bien, hemos de tener en cuenta que para que ello haya sido as, los precios de exportaci han tenido que registrar tasas de variaci prcticamente nulas, y que la penetraci de las importaciones ha sido igualmente apreciable, lo que se explica, a su vez, por el notable abaratamiento de sus precios, acentuado, en los timos meses, por la apreciacin del tipo de cambio. Un comportamiento cuyo alcance desborda el anlisis de la actual coyuntura y sobre el que volver ms adelante. El principal soporte del gasto de los hogares, el pasado a y en el perodo transcurrido del actual ha sido, licamente, el aumento de su renta disponible. El papel del empleo en el sostenimiento de la renta de los hogares es, como bien saben, muy importante. Por eso, el que el ritmo de creaci de puestos de trabajo haya mantenido un tono relativamente elevado durante la fase de desaceleraci ha sido una de las razones que han permitido sostener el crecimiento econico, incluso en la fase de desaceleraci cclica, y a ello han contribuido, tanto las reformas emprendidas en el funcionamiento del mercado de trabajo como la contenci en la tasa de crecimiento de los salarios reales. Las Administraciones plicas han tenido tambin una aportaci destacada al crecimiento de la renta disponible de las familias. En el pasado a destacel papel que, en este sentido, tuvieron las prestaciones sociales, mientras que, en este a, ese impulso procede principalmente de los cambios acordados en el impuesto sobre la renta de las personas fsicas. Como antes deca, el que esto haya tenido lugar sin comprometer la estabilidad presupuestaria -y los datos disponibles para este a sobre la ejecuci del presupuesto del Estado parecen confirmarlo- ilustra la importancia que ha tenido el proceso de consolidaci fiscal realizada en los as recientes y su contribucin a la moderaci de la desaceleraci cclica de la economa espala. Pero la fortaleza del gasto de las familias no podra explicarse sin tener en cuenta las condiciones monetarias que lo han estimulado, sobre todo cuando en dicho gasto se incluye la inversi residencial privada. Los descensos registrados por los tipos de inters en los timos as que, como hemos visto, se han prolongado en el actual ejercicio, han permitido a los agentes econicos privados -y entre ellos a las familias- acceder a unas condiciones de financiaci muy asequibles, lo que ha estimulado el crecimiento del crdito y ha elevado sustancialmente sus niveles de endeudamiento. Los ritmos de crecimiento alcanzados por la inversi en viviendas han sido particularmente elevados y a ello ha contribuido de forma destacada la demanda realizada como una forma de inversi alternativa a la que ofrecen otras formas de colocaci de la riqueza, demanda que se superpone a aquella que se dirige, prioritariamente, a satisfacer las necesidades de los servicios proporcionados por este bien. Las prdidas acumuladas por los mercados burstiles y la incertidumbre que ha prevalecido en el pasado reciente, en un contexto internacional poco favorable, han estimulado adicionalmente la inversi residencial, impulsando fuertes alzas en los precios de la vivienda que han estado realimentando este proceso. A su vez, el aumento en la riqueza inmobiliaria de las familias ha permitido compensar la desvalorizaci de su cartera de activos financieros a la que antes me refera, con la incidencia correspondiente en las decisiones de consumo. Aunque el ritmo de crecimiento de la inversi en viviendas haba tendido a moderarse, hay indicadores que podran estar adelantando cierta reactivaci en la futura construccin de edificios. Los datos ms recientes sobre el crecimiento del crdito parecen confirmar este diagntico, ya que el crdito concedido a empresas y familias aument en el pasado mes de abril , a una tasa prima al 14%, en lnea con su evoluci en los trimestres precedentes, destacando, igualmente, la financiaci destinada a las actividades inmobiliarias y a la adquisici de vivienda. Aunque todo este proceso ha supuesto un rpido aumento de los niveles de endeudamiento de las familias, las ratios correspondientes se encuentran en unas cotas similares a las que registran la mayora de pases de nuestro entorno y reflejan, en parte, la adaptaci a unas condiciones monetarias que, en un contexto de estabilidad macroeconica, son percibidas por los agentes como permanentes. Adems, el crecimiento del endeudamiento no se ha traducido en incrementos en la carga financiera, como consecuencia de los descensos que han tenido lugar en los tipos de inters. A pesar de ello, sigue siendo necesario vigilar muy de cerca los problemas que podran generarse si estos desarrollos tendieran a exacerbarse y si el mercado de la vivienda no facilitara una moderaci adecuada a sus precios. La disponibilidad de unas condiciones de financiaci favorables, y no me refiero solo a las que se derivan de unos tipos de inters reducidos, en comparaci con lo que eran los patrones habituales en nuestra economa, sino tambin al desarrollo de unos mercados eficientes y unas entidades rentables y solventes con capacidad de suministrar los flujos de financiaci, son, sin duda, un activo que se deriva, como digo, de haber alcanzado unos niveles de estabilidad elevados. Pero hay que procurar que las decisiones de gasto del sector privado se acomoden, bsicamente, a unos fundamentos sidos, que en el caso de las familias se deben asentar primordialmente en un alto nivel de empleo y una razonable estabilidad del mismo.. Estos comentarios podran extenderse tambin a la situacin de las empresas, cuyos niveles de endeudamiento han aumentado sustancialmente en estos timos as, en respuesta a unos planteamientos similares a los que acabo de hacer, sin que se hayan visto comprometidas sus ratios de rentabilidad, que siguen siendo elevadas. Existen condiciones, por tanto, para que las empresas puedan afrontar una recuperaci de sus tasas de inversi, a medida que se vayan despejando las incertidumbres que a permanecen, aunque es importante que ello descanse en unos resultados que permitan preservar la solidez de su posici patrimonial y moderar su ritmo de apelaci a la financiaci ajena. Por el momento, solo la actividad inversora del sector de la construccin da muestras de gran dinamismo, tanto en inversi residencial como en infraestructuras y otras obras plicas. Los indicadores ms recientes sobre inversi en bienes de equipo parecen confirmar el comienzo de una recuperaci que ya apuntaban los datos de las cuentas trimestrales a los que antes me refera. Pero se trata a de un proceso incipiente, que se debe confirmar en los primos meses. Para ello, sera necesario preservar la competitividad de nuestro aparato productivo y que el crecimiento de los costes salariales se adapte a la situaci de las empresas. En este sentido, resultan preocupantes las diferencias que siguen observndose en la evoluci de los mrgenes empresariales, segn se trate de sectores expuestos o no a la competencia. Los datos sobre la evoluci reciente de los precios de exportaci a los que antes me refera, con tasas de variaci prcticamente nulas desde hace ms de un a, son elocuentes del esfuerzo que deben realizar las empresas exportadoras para mantenerse en unos mercados que pasan por una situaci particularmente delicada y en los que la competencia es cada vez ms acusada. Paralelamente, otros sectores, menos abiertos a la competencia, siguen registrando ampliaciones en sus mrgenes de explotaci considerables. Creo que hay que destacar la contribuci que ha tenido la moderaci salarial de estos timos as en la desaceleraci de la tasa de inflaci de la economa y, por supuesto, en el crecimiento del empleo. Sin embargo, durante el pasado a, el rebrote que registraron los precios de consumo y la consiguiente reactivaci de las clusulas de salvaguardia en las negociaciones colectivas ha hecho que, aumentos de precios que, en parte, tenan un carcter transitorio y que, de hecho, se estn descontando ya en los primeros meses del a actual, se incorporen en los aumentos salariales, con la consiguiente presi sobre los costes de las empresas. Es necesario superar esta situacin, de forma que las negociaciones colectivas en marcha se acomoden a las nuevas expectativas inflacionistas y que el crecimiento de los costes laborales tenga en cuenta el entorno competitivo en el que se desenvuelven muchas de nuestras empresas. Esta es adems, como hemos visto, una condici necesaria para que el proceso de creaci de empleo no se detenga. La tasa de aumento del IPC se espera que se siga desacelerando en los primos meses, desde el 3,1% en el que se encuentra actualmente. Pero si queremos profundizar en ese proceso y que el ritmo de aumento de nuestros precios se vaya aproximando, paulatinamente, al de los pases de la zona euro, acortando los diferenciales que de ellos nos separan, es necesario que las negociaciones colectivas se acomoden a estas nuevas expectativas inflacionistas y que retomen una senda de moderaci que aten la presi de los costes laborales en los balances de las empresas. Sobre todo, como hemos visto, en aquellas que al estar expuestas a la competencia, en los mercados exteriores o en el mercado interior, no pueden repercutir en sus precios los incrementos de costes y realizan los ajustes a travs de la compresi de sus mrgenes. Y es necesario tambin, evidentemente, que la competencia se extienda a todos los mercados, de forma que la asignaci de los recursos sea la ms eficiente posible. De esta forma, a medida que se vaya consolidando la recuperaci de la economa mundial, las empresas espalas estarn en condiciones de mejorar su cuota de participacin en los mercados exteriores y de liderar un proceso de crecimiento sostenido de la tasa de inversi, necesario para incorporar las mejoras tecnolicas y las consiguientes ganancias de productividad. El balance que se deduce del anlisis de la coyuntura de la economa espala ofrece sobrados argumentos para pensar que se encuentra en una buena posici de partida para incorporarse a la reactivaci econica internacional. Las condiciones monetarias imperantes en el conjunto del rea del euro tendern a favorecer la recuperaci de dichos mercados, que son el destino principal de nuestras exportaciones, lo que permitir amortiguar el impacto de la apreciaci del euro sobre las ventas fuera del rea. Dichas condiciones seguirn siendo holgadas para una economa cuyo crecimiento se basa en un gasto interno comparativamente elevado, apoyado por un alto ritmo de endeudamiento, por lo que la disciplina en la formaci de costes y precios y la flexibilidad de los mercados sern unos determinantes fundamentales de la sostenibilidad de la senda de mayor dinamismo relativo en la que nuestra economa viene mantenindose desde el inicio de la Unin Monetaria. En este entorno de crecimiento mesurado de la economa qu cabe decir sobre la evoluci de los mercados financieros espaoles durante los doce meses transcurridos desde que se celebraron las anteriores Jornadas en Zaragoza?. En las distintas sesiones de trabajo de estas Jornadas ya se han abordado distintas facetas de los mismos y, por ello, me cer a dos aspectos que me parecen actuales y relevantes. Me refiero a los primos retos en la mejora de las infraestructuras de pago que comporta nuestra integraci en el euro y a la participaci del Banco de Espa en el holding Bolsas y Mercados Espales que patrocina este encuentro. Tras el xito en la introducci del euro y extrayendo las consecuencias de dicha unificaci, los ciudadanos europeos exigen unos servicios de pagos transfronterizos modernos que hagan las ventajas de la Uni Monetaria patentes y perceptibles en la vida diaria. El sistema bancario europeo ha respondido a este reto promoviendo un proyecto que estos das comienza a hacerse realidad y en el que estn participando activamente las entidades espalas: el rea ica de pagos (SEPA) en los pases del euro. El proyecto comprende la creaci de una cmara transeuropea para compensar transferencias de peque importe, que empeza funcionar hace un mes; planes para implantar a nivel del rea un sistema equivalente a nuestros recibos domiciliados; un empuje importante a las labores de normalizaci y simplificaci de las redes de transporte de informaci entre los distintos pases; y un tratamiento homogneo de los ingresos y retiradas de monedas y billetes de euro que las entidades de crdito realizan en los bancos centrales nacionales del rea. El Sistema Europeo de Bancos Centrales, por su parte, ha iniciado la reforma del mecanismo TARGET de pagos al por mayor con el horizonte de lanzar un nuevo sistema en el a 2008, mejorando los servicios y reduciendo los costes de utilizaci del mismo. Las entidades espalas y el Banco de Espa estn participando activamente en este proyecto europeo y procediendo a adaptar nuestras infraestructuras de pagos para mantener el buen nivel de calidad con el que hemos operado hasta estos momentos. Qu pasos se han acordado en este mbito? En primer lugar, potenciar el Sistema Nacional de Compensaci Electrica que asienta los pagos al por menor. Dotarlo de personalidad jurdica propia, utilizando para ello el Servicio Espal de Pagos Interbancarios, y limitar los riesgos de las entidades participantes en el sistema. En segundo lugar, participar activamente en la Cmara Europea de Compensaci de Transferencias al por menor STEP2- donde ya operan las cinco entidades espalas ms importantes desde mediados de abril de este a. En tercer lugar, trasladar los pagos de alto importe que circulan en la actualidad por el Sistema Nacional de Compensaci Electrica hacia los procedimientos de liquidaci en tiempo real del Banco de Espa conectados a TARGET. Finalmente, se requerir tambin transformar la red informtica del Banco de Espa para adecuarla a los estndares europeos y reducir el coste de uso de la misma. Todo este conjunto de actuaciones que se extendern durante los tres primos aos buscan mejorar, por un lado, los mecanismos de intercambio de pagos al por menor y controlar sus riesgos. Por otro lado, aspiran a potenciar los enlaces del Banco de Espa con el Sistema TARGET. Dentro de ste y en el marco del BCE se est debatiendo la posibilidad de mantener una estructura confederada, como la actualmente existente, o evolucionar hacia una arquitectura ms centralizada. Independiente del diseo futuro del Sistema TARGET, el esfuerzo que la sociedad espala demanda a las entidades de crdito y al Banco de Espa para mejorar nuestras infraestructuras y sus enlaces con el resto de los pases europeos va a ser muy importante y deberemos afrontarlo con decisi, dejando claro nuestro compromiso de dotarnos de un sistema de pagos moderno y plenamente integrado, como una infraestructura bsica para competir en condiciones de xito en los mercados financieros del euro. El segundo aspecto al que quisiera referirme en estas XXX Jornadas, es el proceso de consolidaci de los mercados de valores espales y el papel que el Banco de Espa ha desempedo en la creaci y la puesta en marcha de la Sociedad que promueve este encuentro. El 1 de octubre de 2002 inicisu actividad legal el holding Bolsas y Mercados Espales y el 1 de abril de 2003 lo ha hecho Iberclear, como gestor nico de los servicios centrales de liquidacin de valores de la naci. Por ahora, quedan fuera los servicios autonicos de liquidaci de valores que podrn libremente integrarse en el proyecto en fechas venideras. Hace unos das la Comisi Ejecutiva de Bolsas y Mercados Espales y el Banco de Espa hemos decidido proponer a la Junta General de accionistas de la Sociedad la entrada del Banco de Espa en Bolsas y Mercados Espales mediante una ampliaci del capital social de la misma y la entrega de las acciones que el Banco posee en Iberclear. Mediante esta operaci, el holding pasara a poseer la totalidad de las acciones de las sociedades que gestionan y liquidan los mercados de valores espales y, en contrapartida, el Banco de Espa pasara a ser accionista de Bolsas y Mercados Espales. Cul es el sentido de esta operacin que cierra la integraci societaria de todos los mercados de valores?. Qu han buscado el Banco de Espa y el Tesoro Plico al aportar al proyecto los procedimientos de la deuda plica?. En primer lugar, se ha querido unificar en una sola sociedad la administraci de todos los mercados e infraestructuras para dotarlos de un enfoque estratgico ico y mejorar su gesti. Esto comprende un doble aspecto: integrar los sistemas de contrataci, liquidaci y registro, y coordinar los esquemas de trabajo de los distintos eslabones de creaci de valor en la cadena de negocio de los valores. En segundo lugar, se ha buscado explotar las diversas sinergias de la organizaci en temas como recursos humanos, contrataci de servicios externos, informtica, redes de comunicacin, servicios de informaci, etc. En tercer lugar, establecer las bases para un engarce futuro con los movimientos equivalentes que se estn registrando en Europa, buscando los contactos y las alianzas ms adecuados para la colaboraci mutua. Podemos y debemos aspirar a mantener nuestra posici en los mercados de valores europeos como una de las plazas relevantes en el contexto del euro. El Banco de Espa ha promovido activamente esta operaci y espera culminarla en los primos das, si cuenta con el acuerdo de los accionistas privados, convencido que es el camino preciso para nuestra consolidacin en el rea. La compaa resultante es una sociedad privada que gestiona un negocio estratgico. Nuestra participaci en ella no responde a un inters de control ni tiene vocaci de perpetuidad. El Banco de Espa siempre ha manifestado que sta es una actuaci temporal que no quiere que se dilate indefinidamente. Una vez que la Sociedad est firmemente asentada y los mercados de deuda plica y su liquidaci queden adecuadamente engarzados en el conjunto de los mercados de valores espales, el Banco de Espa, de acuerdo con el Tesoro Plico y con el resto de los socios privados, dar por finalizada su presencia en la misma. Eso ser ms adelante, ahora lo importante en este proyecto, como en los cambios que ya he comentado en los sistemas de pagos, es realizar un buen trabajo de infraestructura y situar a nuestros mercados en condiciones de competir con eficacia en Europa. Muchas gracias a todos.

Title: Governor's Appearance: Committee on Economy and Finance of the Congress of Deputies
text: Appearance of the Governor of the Bank of Spain before the Committee of Economy and Finance of the Congress of Deputies 18 June 2003 Mr. President, Honourable Members, I am grateful for this opportunity to come again to this Committee on Economy and Finance, within the framework of my regular appearances, to present to your Series the assessment that the Bank of Spain makes of the situation and prospects of the Spanish economy within the framework of its membership of the Economic and Monetary Union. The timing of this hearing is particularly opportune as it coincides practically with the publication of the Annual Report that the Bank of Spain prepares every year, which includes a detailed description of the most recent evolution of our economy as well as the analysis of the challenges and opportunities it faces. I will try to summarize the main features presented in this report and pay particular attention to the monetary policy of the euro area, given its relevant implications for the evolution of key national variables, and my status as a member of the Governing Council of the ECB. As your Serias know, this party is responsible for setting the objectives and taking decisions on the definition of monetary policy, which is implemented through operations carried out, for the most part, by the national central banks of the countries which, like ours, have joined EMU. I shall therefore begin by referring to the economic situation in the euro area, with particular reference to monetary policy and to certain decisions of the Governing Council on the strategy and functioning of the institution. Then I will refer to the Spanish economy and its challenges and, finally, I will devote a section to the issues of financial stability. Euro area and monetary policy. When it appeared before this Commission in the spring of last year, the world economy was subject to a high degree of uncertainty, as a result of a set of shocks that include: the effect of the end of the stock market bubble (especially in technological securities), geopolitical uncertainties, the crisis in emerging countries (specifically, in Argentina), the bankruptcy of some of the world's largest companies and the crisis of confidence in the fundamentals of Western financial markets. This climate of instability, deteriorates the confidence of agents and favors the increase in the price of oil and reinforces the unfavorable evolution of stock prices, which contributes to slowing down productive activity. In recent months, the rapid resolution of the military conflict in Iraq has facilitated an improvement in economic conditions, which has been reflected in the recovery of international stock markets. However, although we do not yet have sufficient data to make an accurate assessment of the new situation, the available indicators do not yet provide clear evidence of an appreciable increase in economic dynamism in the short term, while the intensity of the recovery is constrained by factors such as macroeconomic and financial imbalances in the United States. the lagged effects of the sharp equity price correction in 2000 and 2001 and the low utilization of installed productive capacity still observed in a number of countries. As a result, euro area growth in the first half of the year is very likely to be very weak. The European economy is currently showing a virtual stagnation of its Gross Domestic Product, after experiencing modest growth in 2002, mostly explained by the contribution of the external sector, as domestic demand barely registered a slight increase. In the early months of this year, private expenditure has remained weak while exports have shown limited dynamism in external markets and have begun to reflect the effect of the sharp appreciation of the euro. In the bulletin of the European Central Bank, the new macroeconomic projections have been published that show a decline, on the previous projections, both in growth and inflation figures. Growth for this year would remain in the range 0.4-1% and inflation between 1.8 d0 2.2. In any case, despite the relative weakness of the current economic situation, and the risks facing the major economies, economic activity in the euro area is expected to gradually return to a more expansionary tone from the second half of this year, although it is not likely to approach its potential growth rate until the first financial year. This scenario is supported by external and internal factors; Among the external ones, the ECB bulletin highlights the expected rebound in external demand in the euro zone, which should offset the attenuating effect of the exchange rate. Among the domestic factors, the recovery in domestic consumption from the second half of the year onwards stands out, as a result of the growth in real disposable income supported by the effects of the favourable trade ratio and lower inflation rates. It also highlights that although the contribution of investment is likely to remain modest, the improvement in the global environment and low interest rates should contribute to its improvement. The disappointing performance of the European economy since 2001 raises two types of questions that require rigorous assessment and an appropriate response from the authorities. First, the euro area has been very sensitive to the shocks that have affected the global economy. Both the slowdown in production in the United States, as well as the rise in oil prices, the stock market crisis and geopolitical tension, have had a marked impact on the evolution of activity in the euro area, causing it to deviate from its long-term growth path, which shows the limited strength of the internal springs of economic dynamism. It seems clear that, while some of this pronounced vulnerability to external circumstances may be linked to closer economic, trade and financial relations between Europe and the rest of the world, it reflects both the inadequate functioning of adjustment mechanisms and, in particular, the rigidities that characterise wage and price formation. Thus, an economy's capacity to respond to external shocks is strengthened if its goods and factor markets show a high degree of flexibility, since, in this case, it is the nominal variables that assume the fundamental weight of the adjustment, thus limiting fluctuations in the variables that most directly affect economic well-being. such as activity or employment. It is therefore increasingly imperative to adopt ambitious market reforms to limit the impact of adverse external developments and thus increase the economy's capacity for sustained growth. On the other hand, the recent economic slowdown in Europe has shown that inadequate management of finances can significantly limit the ability of budgetary policy to contribute to growth and job creation. In this sense, it should be seen that the insufficient reduction of imbalances in the tima phase of cyclical expansion in some countries, which, fortunately, Spain is not included, has reduced the power of fiscal policy to soften the scope of the cyclical slowdown, by reducing the room for manoeuvre available in the budgets of the governments concerned. In addition, the limited consolidation of the accounts of various Member States has meant that, in the face of deteriorating economic conditions, their financial deficits have exceeded the limits laid down in the Treaty on European Union, which has led to the activation of the disciplinary procedures provided for in Community legislation. In any case, recent experience confirms that fiscal discipline, far from being a constraint on economic growth, is a necessary condition for its preservation and contributes to the proper functioning of the Economic and Monetary Union. These developments therefore reinforce the validity of the available multilateral surveillance mechanisms for national fiscal policies, and in particular those contained in the Stability and Growth Pact. A favourable development in the last few months has been the improvement in the inflation outlook, partly due to the fall in oil prices and the appreciation of the euro, but also due to sluggish private spending. This moderation of inflationary pressures has allowed the Governing Council of the ECB to adjust monetary conditions to the weak European economic situation, cutting key interest rates by 50 basis points on 5 June, bringing the main monetary policy rate to 2%. the lowest level, not since the beginning of EMU but also for several decades in any of the countries that today make up the Economic and Monetary Union. With this measure, official rates are now 125 basis points below those in force six months ago and accumulate a reduction of almost three percentage points since, two years ago, monetary policy began to ease. This decision underlines the contribution that monetary policy can make to the task of boosting the economic recovery in the area, once inflationary risks are estimated to be under control. It should be remembered, however, that monetary policy alone cannot solve the problems that determine the area's modest growth figures. This interest rate movement agreed by the Governing Council of the ECB has been presented to the opinion following the new communication scheme established following the review of its monetary policy strategy, the results of which were announced last May. This assessment, which provides an overall satisfactory assessment of the operation of the strategy since its adoption shortly before the start of the monetary union, confirmed the definition of price stability adopted at the time by the ECB which, by establishing a quantitative benchmark for its priority objective, constitutes a key element of the rule guiding its monetary policy actions. At the same time, the Governing Council clarifies, taking into account the need to minimise the risks of deflacy, possible biases in price measurement and the implications of national inflation rate differentials, its actions will aim to ensure that inflation is in the medium term at 2%. As your S8eriah know, for some months now we have been witnessing a major review of the institutional framework of the European Union, largely motivated by the need to ensure its operation following the enlargement process to include twenty-five countries. In this area, I would first like to highlight the changes made to the voting system within the Governing Council of the ECB. On the basis of these changes, approved by the European Council in March 1 on the basis of a recommendation by the ECB, the number of Governors with voting rights in the Governing Council will be no later than fifteen, so that, once the number of countries participating in EMU is higher, A rotation system will be activated. In order to maintain at all times the representativeness of the euro area as a whole, the system envisaged assigns to each Governor a frequency of rotation which depends on the size of his country's economy, by creating three different groups according to their voting frequency. Since Spain belongs to the group of five EU countries with the highest economic weight, the Governor of the Bank of Spain is among those who will hold the most frequent voting capacity. But, without a doubt, the most relevant institutional challenge that the European Union has posed at the moment is the elaboration of a Constitutional Treaty, whose draft will be presented by the European Convention at the European Council of the first weekend in Salica. This summit of Heads of State or Government will lead to the convening of an Intergovernmental Conference, whose task will be to propose the drafting of the final text which will be submitted for ratification by the Member States. It is to be hoped that the new Constitution will not only preserve the effective functioning of the EU after the accession of new members but will also strengthen the process of European construction in which the Economic and Monetary Union already occupies a prominent place. That is why the way in which the Convention has dealt with the chapters relating to the institutional design of the Monetary Union is appropriate, which, by respecting the principles agreed upon when the Maastricht Treaty was signed, recognises its validity, which I believe has been fully proven since the introduction of the Maastricht currency in 1999. Spanish economy. Turning now to the focus on the Spanish economy, the Annual Report that I presented last week to the Governing Council of the Bank of Spain contains a detailed analysis of its performance during 2002, which highlights, as the most relevant aspect, the capacity it has shown to overcome the adverse consequences of the low external dynamism and to maintain growth rates significantly higher than those registered in the rest of the Spanish area. euro. Thus, in 2002, economic growth stood at 2%, compared with a scant 0.9% for all the countries with which we share our currency. In Spain, growth was based on the growth of national demand, which increased by 2.2%, and was accompanied by a significant generation of employment, so that employment increased by 1.3% (compared with 0.4% in EMU). The data for the first quarter of 2003, recently known, have confirmed this favourable performance, revealing that the Spanish economy grew by 2.1% in that period, while in the euro area as a whole, as I have already seen, output is growing slightly lower than in the past. During the first months of 2003, domestic demand has intensified its dynamism, offsetting the negative impact that foreign demand has continued to have, in a still depressed international context. In this way, employment generation has remained important and has even intensified. The resilience shown by the Spanish economy in an adverse external context marks an important change in relation to the vulnerability that usually characterized it in previous stages of cyclical slowdown, and that caused the appearance of important imbalances, which resulted in sudden adjustments in production and employment. The Annual Report identifies the main factors behind this improved performance in the current slowdown phase. In this regard, it is worth mentioning, first of all, the macroeconomic stability regime that has prevailed in our country throughout the scams and to which both the anchoring of expectations provided by membership of the Monetary Union and a disciplined fiscal policy that respects the Stability and Growth Pact have contributed. Reforms in certain markets, particularly labour markets, and measures to liberalize and promote competition have also helped to improve the functioning of the economy's supply. In this context of stability and greater efficiency, the expansionary impulses received almost from the entry into the Monetary Union - mainly through significant reductions in interest rates and the reduction in inflation expectations itself - have been transferred to higher growth rates in activity and, above all, in employment. which, together with the play of automatic fiscal policy stabilisers, have provided additional support to domestic demand, at a time when external demand was beginning to weaken. For all these reasons, Spain has continued to progress towards real convergence with the number of more developed European nations, in a process that has not stopped despite the deterioration experienced by the international economy. The growth observed in Spain in the last two years has been based on the strength of consumption, and investment in construction. The creation of employment and the game of transfers with the plico sector have contributed to the expansion of the disposable income of families and have provided solidity to their income expectations, underpinning their spending decisions. The existence of comfortable monetary and financial conditions, both in terms of low interest rates and the availability of credit, have operated in the same direction. To this has been added the effort made in the improvement of infrastructures, making construction the most dynamic component of spending. Productive investment and exports have shown, however, a notable weakness in the slowdown phase -more intense in the case of investment-, although the most recent data are encouraging to point towards a change in trend in both cases. Although the profitability levels of Spanish companies are high, the deterioration in demand expectations and the great uncertainty that have characterized the international context in the two scams have had a discouraging effect on investment plans. In addition, the fall in stock prices and the increase in risk premia traded on the markets have led to financing conditions for companies that are less accommodative than what is implied by interest rate levels. In any case, the signs of rebound that can be seen today are indicative that the financial conditions of companies are not an obstacle to a recovery of investment. For its part, exports suffered the impact of the international crisis, and has not begun to show signs, although somewhat hesitant, of recovery until the second half of last year. Inflation picked up in 2002, driven in part by specific factors associated with the evolution of oil prices, the rise in certain food prices and the introduction of the euro. As expected, to the extent that these elements were transitory, their effect has been discounted in the first months of 2003. To this have been added the appreciation of the European currency and the most recent fall in oil prices, so that inflation stood at 2.7% in May, after having ended 2002 at rates of 4%. It is also noteworthy the slowdown in the prices of services to 3.5% year-on-year variation. Despite this improvement, which has also been reflected in a significant reduction in the inflation differential, this remains positive and, if it continues for a long time, may compromise the competitiveness of our products if it is not accompanied by a faster increase in productivity in the sectors most exposed to competition. In fact, this inflation differential reflects, in part, an equally positive differential in labour costs and, in part, the widening of margins in those sectors with a higher demand pressure and less exposed to competition. These factors point to the need to strengthen the bases of wage moderation, promote productivity gains, and deepen the processes of liberalization and increased competition in the markets of some products, to maintain competitiveness. Challenges of the Spanish economy Following this assessment of the performance of the Spanish economy in 2002 and the first months of 2003, I would like to refer briefly to the prospects and challenges for the future. As I have already said, the pattern of growth that the Spanish economy has followed until now has provided adequate support for the process of real convergence and has allowed a substantial increase in the employment rate, a very important aspect, given the low levels from which our country started. However, the expansionary impulses linked to EMU entry will tend to run out. This makes it necessary for investment and exports to take over as drivers of growth. This is also a more appropriate pattern of growth for a situation in which the Spanish economy will depend to a large extent on its internal mechanisms to grow at rates close to potential and to continue to make progress in real convergence, in the context of an enlarged EU and increasingly globalised markets. The high dynamism experienced by household spending since the last expansionary phase has led to a continuous decline in the savings rate and the financing capacity of this sector - which has only stopped in 2002 - and to a rapid growth in its indebtedness, which has reached levels comparable to those recorded in other EU countries. Although there has not been a similar growth in the financial burden, since declines in interest rates have kept their level stable as a percentage of income, high indebtedness means that household spending decisions may be conditioned, to a greater extent, by movements in interest rates and house prices. Most of the credit granted to families has been directed to finance the purchase of housing. The high demand for real estate assets has led to very strong increases in their prices, which are largely explained by the evolution of their usual determinants -demographic variables, income, interest rates and profitability of alternative assets, basically-. However, it seems to be detected that the upward adjustment of these prices has been greater than that which would justify these determinants in the long term. This overrun, however, has not been broader than that observed in other bullish cycles and it is expected that, as in the past, it can be absorbed in an orderly manner and without too sudden price movements. In any case, the necessary moderation of household indebtedness and the desirable containment in house price hikes suggest that future consumption growth must remain in line with the fundamental determinants of household income, which rests, above all, on the pace of job creation. In this way, the most dynamic impulses must therefore come, as previously seen, from exports and productive investment. The keys to promoting this new pattern of growth are in improving the competitiveness of the economy, and increasing the profitability of companies. A key component of an economy's competitiveness is the relative level of its labour costs, a factor that will gain prominence in the enlarged EU, as the new countries joining in 2004 generally have great advantages in this area. In this perspective, maintaining wage moderation and progress towards a system of determining wages that takes greater account of the specific conditions of enterprises are essential to meet this challenge. At the same time, it is essential to boost productivity growth and the capitalization of the economy. Although infrastructure endowment has increased rapidly, other components of the capital stock, mainly investment in equipment, have not done so to the same extent. It should be borne in mind that this is the main way for the incorporation of technological advances and innovation in production processes. For the greatest effort to have the expected effects on productivity, and to contribute efficiently to the diffusion of technological progress, it must be accompanied by additional improvements in the functioning of markets, both factor and product. Increasing the efficiency and competitiveness of the production structure is particularly relevant in the new context posed by the enlargement of the EU towards Central and Eastern Europe. The expansion will force Spain to compete, in the main markets in which it operates, with countries that have patterns of productive and commercial specialization very close to ours, with a very high growth potential and with a notable attraction for foreign investment flows. The Spanish economy has overcome in its recent past the great challenges posed by integration into the European Union and entry into the euro. Both challenges were a great incentive to face the pending problems and ended up promoting a great step forward in the modernization of the productive system and in the approximation to the levels of welfare of the most advanced countries. The conditions are now in place for something similar to happen with the impact of enlargement, especially if the macroeconomic stability framework achieved is maintained, the advantages of balanced public finances are regained, the role of investment and exports in our growth pattern is strengthened, and job creation is compatible with productivity growth. All this in line with the requirements that derive from the diagnosis that I have just presented to you. Allow me, therefore, before turning to the aspects of financial stability, to conclude that the Spanish economy is in a good relative condition to resume a more dynamic growth path, once the uncertainties gripping the world economy are cleared. Financial stability. I would now like to turn to another area of activity of the Bank of Spain: aspects related to financial stability and banking supervision. But before delving into the description of the evolution of the Spanish financial system, allow me to draw your attention to the second line of the report of banking supervision in Spain. In my appearance before this Committee a year ago, I announced that we were finishing the first copy of the supervisory report of the Bank of Spain which corresponded to the financial year 2001 and which was published a few months later. This has advanced several months its preparation, so that the one corresponding to last year has already been published. As you know, this publication will be mandatory from 2003 by legal imperative. The Bank of Spain has preferred, however, to anticipate this legal requirement and thus contribute to a better knowledge and transparency of the supervisory function. For this reason, let me emphasize that in this report, the Bank of Spain has gone beyond a mere and strict compliance with the legal obligation and has tried to make an exercise of analysis and explanation that, together with the half-yearly reports of financial stability, which I also announced in my previous appearance, allow a follow-up of the evolution of the conditions that determine the stability of our financial system. From an international point of view, 2002 was a tremendously complex one. If the most remarkable feature of the international financial system were to be sealed, the key word would possibly: resistance. Resistance to a wide range of disturbances that I have synthesized in my previous presentation. What are the factors that explain this relative success? A first factor to take into account is that of improvements in risk management, which allow a better diversification of risk and a broader international diffusion. Obviously, no matter how good this management of financial risk is, once assumed, it cannot disappear, but a correct transformation and distribution of it can facilitate the absorption of shocks. Another key element in explaining this success has been the actions of the authorities when deep institutional weaknesses and conflicts of interest were revealed. In short, the international financial system has overcome a complex and difficult period. However, this message of optimism must be qualified, because even if significant shocks have been absorbed, it is inevitable that the resilience of the international financial system to adverse shocks has been diminished. We must therefore remain vigilant, and continue efforts to strengthen the international financial system. In this environment, the Spanish financial entities and markets satisfactorily exceeded the a, so that we can affirm, that the financial conditions in the Spanish economy have not posed restrictions to the process of economic recovery. The evolution of the Spanish entities in 2002 can be summarized by analyzing three specific areas: activity, profitability and solvency. With regard to activity, the banking business, measured by the total resources of assets and liabilities of the consolidated balance sheet, grew by 0.7% in 2002, compared with 7.4% the previous year, thus moderating its growth considerably. However, it is necessary to go a little deeper, since the consolidated balance sheet includes both the evolution of the business in Spain and abroad. Activity abroad fell by more than 23.5%, largely as a result of the evolution of the euro exchange rate, while banking activity in national territory, moderated, continued to grow at higher rates, around 8%, in accordance, to some extent, with the economic dynamism of the Spanish economy. In any case, the basic characteristic of banking developments on the asset side is the dynamism of credit to the resident private sector, which has maintained its growth in figures that move around 14% year-on-year. This evolution is mainly based on mortgage-backed credit whose year-on-year growth remains at around 20%. These figures determine a change in its composition, gaining a greater weight mortgage credit, intended for housing acquisition and the construction sector. This evolution is linked to the evolution of the housing market, as I said before. There are elements that advise prudence and vigilance of entities in the granting of new credits. First, the current rate of growth of mortgage credit does not seem to represent a long-term equilibrium value; It mainly reflects the adjustment of agents' expectations in the face of the new environment of macroeconomic stability, low interest rates and dynamism in job creation. Secondly, although these are secured loans, and when the price of real estate does not fluctuate like that of financial assets, the future value of a guarantee cannot be projected mechanically. The value of the guarantee must therefore be seen in conjunction with its possible future evolution, including in its possible case stress scenarios. Third, although NPL ratios remain at historically low levels, reflecting a substantial improvement in risk management, given the strong growth in credit in scams, banks must consider the difficulties of maintaining such low ratios. Therefore, they should carefully analyze the impact that alternative interest rate scenarios may have on loan delinquency rates. Let me conclude this reflection on the activity of institutions with a brief mention of the area of liabilities. Term deposits have been moderating their growth rate to around 10%, a figure similar to that of total creditors. Although this value is reasonable, and even high, there is a significant and growing gap between loans and debt, financed either by external debt or by increases in own resources. This element, although it does not currently represent an immediate concern, does provide an additional argument in favour of a certain moderation in credit growth rates. In the area of profitability, the banks were no strangers to the complexities and problems of 2002. Thus, the profit fell moderately, around 10%, a figure that has moderated in the first quarter of the year. However, its behavior, in a complex year, was satisfactory, since the falls were smaller than in other countries of our environment and the profitability ratio or ROE, even though it also falls at 12%, which represents a differential against the debt plica to 10 ace of about 8%. Again this figure has improved in the first quarter of this year, with a return on equity of more than 13%. This satisfactory evolution, not without certain weaknesses, shows the advantages, under certain conditions, of the Spanish banking model, with a high retail banking component, as a profitable and stable model, that is, less subject to the variability of results that characterizes, for example, investment banking. In terms of solvency, lenders maintained the usual equity soundness profile, with an average solvency ratio in 2002 of 11.1%, well above the minimum of 8%. If we take into account that the Spanish regulations are more demanding than the Community directive or the solvency rules of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, the situation is more satisfactory. In terms of first-class capital, the Spanish ratio stood at 8.5% in 2002, more than double the minimum requirement of 4%. By scam, Spain has the statistical provision, which obliges entities to provision not only for failed risks, but also for latent ones. Despite this scenario, as supervisors we must flee, as I have already said, from complacency. That is why we have reiterated on several occasions, including the audit report, the importance of a strategic vision of own resources that pays attention to both their sufficiency and their quality. Thus, we have established a limit for so-called preferred shares of 30% of Tier 1 capital, and we have alerted institutions to the risks of their marketing to retail investors, who may not sufficiently understand the risks of the product. In short, and taking into account the three areas of activity, profitability and solvency, we can affirm the good health of the Spanish financial system that, at the moment, is in a position to finance a greater rate of economic reactivation. I would like to conclude this intervention by highlighting that at Banco de Espa we continue to work on the lines of improvement of prudential banking supervision that I mentioned in my last intervention, that is, in a very brief way: international coordination, preventive approach and incentive of good risk management, which complements traditional supervision, attention to qualitative aspects, including governance structures and governance of institutions, etc. so that the combination of regulation, supervisory practices and market discipline, contribute to maintaining and improving the efficiency and solvency of our banking system. Thanks a lot.
