Economa espala. Pasando ahora a centrarme en la economa espala, el Informe Anual que la semana pasada present al Consejo de Gobierno del Banco de Espa contiene un anlisis detallado de su comportamiento durante el a 2002, del que destaca, como aspecto ms relevante, la capacidad que ha mostrado para sortear las consecuencias adversas del escaso dinamismo exterior y para mantener ritmos de crecimiento significativamente ms elevados que los registrados en el resto de la zona del euro. As, en 2002, el crecimiento econico espal se situen el 2%, frente al escaso 0,9% del conjunto de pases con los que compartimos nuestra moneda. En Espa, el crecimiento estuvo basado en el avance de la demanda nacional, que aumentun 2,2%, y vino acompado de una importante generacin de empleo, de forma que la ocupaci se incrementun 1,3% (frente a un 0,4% en la UEM). Los datos del primer trimestre de 2003, recientemente conocidos, han venido a confirmar este comportamiento favorable, al revelar que la economa espala creciun 2,1% en ese perodo, en tanto que en el conjunto de la zona del euro, como ya he selado, el producto avanza tasas ligeramente inferiores a las del pasado a. Durante los primeros meses de 2003, la demanda nacional ha intensificado su dinamismo, compensando el impacto negativo que ha seguido teniendo la demanda exterior, en un contexto internacional todava deprimido. De esta forma, la generaci de empleo ha seguido siendo importante e incluso se ha intensificado. La resistencia mostrada por la economa espala en un contexto exterior adverso marca un cambio importante en relaci con la vulnerabilidad que le caracterizaba habitualmente en anteriores etapas de desaceleraci cclica, y que provocaba la aparici de importantes desequilibrios, que derivaban en ajustes bruscos de la producci y del empleo. En el Informe Anual se identifican los principales factores que estn detrs de este mejor comportamiento en la actual fase de desaceleracin. A este respecto, hay que mencionar, en primer lugar, el rgimen de estabilidad macroeconica que ha prevalecido en nuestro pas a lo largo de los timos as y al que han contribuido, tanto el anclaje de expectativas proporcionado por la pertenencia a la Uni Monetaria como una poltica fiscal disciplinada y respetuosa del Pacto de Estabilidad y Crecimiento. Tambin las reformas introducidas en algunos mercados -en especial, el de trabajo- y las medidas de liberalizaci y de fomento de la competencia, han contribuido a mejorar el funcionamiento de la oferta de la economa. En este marco de estabilidad y de mayor eficiencia, los impulsos expansivos recibidos con ocasi de la entrada en la Uni Monetaria -a travs, fundamentalmente, de descensos significativos de tipos de inters y del propio recorte de las expectativas de inflaci- se han trasladado a mayores tasas de crecimiento de la actividad y, sobre todo, del empleo, que, junto con el juego de los estabilizadores automticos de la poltica fiscal, han proporcionado un sostn adicional a la demanda interna, en el momento en que la demanda exterior comenzaba a debilitarse. Por todo ello, Espa ha seguido progresando hacia la convergencia real con el nleo de naciones europeas ms desarrolladas, en un proceso que no se ha detenido a pesar del deterioro experimentado por la economa internacional. El crecimiento que se ha observado en Espa en los dos ltimos as se ha basado en la fortaleza del consumo, y de la inversi en construcci. La creaci de empleo y el juego de transferencias con el sector plico han contribuido a la expansi de la renta disponible de las familias y han proporcionado solidez a sus expectativas de renta, sustentando sus decisiones de gasto. La existencia de unas condiciones monetarias y financieras holgadas, tanto en trminos de bajos tipos de inters como de disponibilidad de crdito, han operado en el mismo sentido. A ello se ha adido el esfuerzo realizado en la mejora de infraestructuras, haciendo de la construcci el componente ms dinmico del gasto. La inversi productiva y las exportaciones han mostrado, sin embargo, una notable debilidad en la fase desaceleraci -ms intensa en el caso de la inversi-, si bien los datos ms recientes resultan alentadores al apuntar hacia un cambio de tendencia en ambos casos. Aunque los niveles de rentabilidad de las empresas espaolas son elevados, el deterioro de las expectativas de demanda y la gran incertidumbre que han caracterizado al contexto internacional en los dos timos as han tenido un efecto desalentador sobre los planes de inversi. Adems, el descenso de las cotizaciones burstiles y el aumento de las primas de riesgo negociadas en los mercados, han determinado unas condiciones de financiaci para las empresas menos laxas de lo que se desprende de los niveles de tipos de inters. En cualquier caso, los signos de repunte que se aprecian en la actualidad son indicativos de que las condiciones financieras de las empresas no son obstculo para una recuperaci de la inversi. Por su parte, la exportaci sufriel impacto de la crisis internacional, y no ha empezado a mostrar signos, aunque algo vacilantes, de recuperaci hasta la segunda mitad del pasado a. La inflacin experimentun rebrote a lo largo del a 2002, empujada, en parte, por factores especficos, asociados a la evoluci de los precios del petreo, a las alzas de algunos precios alimenticios y a la puesta en circulaci del euro. Como caba esperar, en la medida en que estos elementos eran transitorios, su efecto se ha ido descontando en los primeros meses de 2003. A ello se han adido la apreciaci de la moneda europea y el ms reciente descenso de los precios del petreo, de forma que la inflaci se ha situado, en el mes de mayo, en el 2,7%, tras haber finalizado el a 2002 en tasas del 4%. Es de destacar tambin la desaceleraci de los precios de los servicios hasta el 3.5% de variaci interanual. A pesar de esta mejora, que se ha reflejado tambin en una apreciable reduccin del diferencial de inflaci, este sigue siendo positivo y en caso de mantenerse prolongadamente, puede comprometer la competitividad de nuestros productos si no se ve acompado de un avance ms rpido de la productividad en los sectores ms expuestos a la competencia. De hecho, este diferencial de inflaci refleja, en parte, un diferencial tambin positivo de costes laborales y, en parte, la ampliaci de mrgenes en aquellos sectores con una presi de la demanda ms elevada y menos expuestos a la competencia. Estos factores apuntan hacia la necesidad de reforzar las bases de la moderaci salarial, fomentar las ganancias de productividad, y profundizar en los procesos de liberalizaci y aumento de la competencia en los mercados de algunos productos, para mantener la competitividad. Retos de la economa espala Tras esta valoraci de los resultados de la economa espala en 2002 y en los primeros meses de 2003, quisiera referirme brevemente a las perspectivas y los retos que se plantean para el futuro. Como ya he dicho, el patr de crecimiento que ha seguido la economa espala hasta el momento actual ha proporcionado un soporte adecuado al proceso de convergencia real y ha permitido un aumento sustancial de la tasa de ocupaci, aspecto muy importante, dados los bajos niveles de los que parta nuestro pas. Sin embargo los impulsos expansivos ligados a la entrada en la UEM tendern a agotarse. Ello hace necesario que la inversi y las exportaciones tomen el relevo como impulsores de crecimiento. Es este, adems, un patr de crecimiento ms adecuado para una situaci en la que la economa espala depender en gran medida de sus mecanismos internos para crecer a ritmos cercanos al potencial y seguir progresando en la convergencia real, en el contexto de una UE ampliada y de unos mercados cada vez ms globalizados. El elevado dinamismo que ha experimentado el gasto de los hogares desde la tima etapa expansiva ha dado lugar a un descenso continuo de la tasa de ahorro y de la capacidad de financiaci de este sector -que solo se ha detenido en el a 2002- y a un crecimiento rpido de su endeudamiento, que ha alcanzado niveles equiparables a los que se registran en otros pases de la UE. Aunque no se ha producido un crecimiento similar de la carga financiera, ya que los descensos de tipos de inters han mantenido estable su nivel como porcentaje de la renta, el elevado endeudamiento hace que las decisiones de gasto de los hogares puedan verse condicionadas, en mayor medida, por movimientos en los tipos de inters y en los precios de la vivienda. La mayor parte del crdito concedido a las familias se ha dirigido a financiar la adquisici de vivienda. La elevada demanda de activos inmobiliarios ha propiciado incrementos muy fuertes de sus precios, que se explican en gran medida por la evoluci de sus determinantes habituales -variables demogrficas, renta, tipos de inters y rentabilidad de activos alternativos, bsicamente-. No obstante, parece detectarse que el ajuste al alza de estos precios ha sido superior al que justificaran dichos determinantes en el largo plazo. Esta sobrerreacci, sin embargo, no ha sido ms amplia que la observada en otros ciclos alcistas y cabe esperar que, al igual que en el pasado, pueda ser absorbida de manera ordenada y sin movimientos demasiado bruscos de los precios. En cualquier caso, la necesaria moderaci del endeudamiento de los hogares y la deseable contenci en las alzas de los precios de la vivienda, apuntan a que el crecimiento futuro del consumo debe mantenerse en lnea con los determinantes fundamentales de la renta de las familias, que descansa, sobre todo, en el ritmo de creaci de empleo. De esta manera, los impulsos ms dinmicos deben proceder, por tanto, como selaba anteriormente, de la exportaci y la inversi productiva. Las claves para impulsar este nuevo patr de crecimiento estn en la mejora de la competitividad de la economa, y el aumento de la rentabilidad de las empresas. Un componente fundamental de la competitividad de una economa es el nivel relativo de sus costes laborales, un factor que ganar relevancia en la UE ampliada, ya que los nuevos pases que se incorporarn en 2004 parten, en general, con grandes ventajas en este terreno. En esta perspectiva, el mantenimiento de la moderaci salarial y el progreso hacia un sistema de determinaci de los salarios que tenga en cuenta, en mayor medida, las condiciones especficas de las empresas resultan fundamentales para afrontar este reto. Paralelamente, es imprescindible impulsar el aumento de la productividad y la capitalizaci de la economa. Aunque la dotaci de infraestructuras ha aumentado con rapidez, otros componentes del stock de capital, principalmente la inversi en equipo, no lo han hecho en la misma medida. Debe tenerse en cuenta que esta es la va principal para la incorporacin de avances tecnolicos y de innovaci en los procesos productivos. Para que el mayor esfuerzo tenga los efectos esperados sobre la productividad, y contribuya eficientemente a la difusi de progreso tecnolico, es necesario que vaya acompado de mejoras adicionales en el funcionamiento de los mercados, tanto de factores como de productos. El aumento de la eficiencia y de la competitividad de la estructura productiva cobra especial relevancia en el nuevo contexto que plantea la ampliaci de la UE hacia el centro y el este de Europa. La ampliaci obligar a Espa a competir, en los principales mercados en los que opera, con pases que presentan patrones de especializaci productiva y comercial muy primos a los nuestros, con un potencial de crecimiento muy elevado y con una notable atracci para los flujos de inversi extranjera. La economa espala la superado en su pasado reciente los grandes desafos que plantean la integraci en la Uni Europea y la entrada en el euro. Ambos retos supusieron un gran acicate para afrontar los problemas pendientes y terminaron impulsando un gran paso adelante en la modernizaci del sistema productivo y en la aproximaci a los niveles de bienestar de los pases ms avanzados. Hoy se dan las condiciones para que algo parecido suceda con el impacto de la ampliaci, sobre todo si se conserva el marco de estabilidad macroeconica alcanzado, se aprovechan las ventajas de unas finanzas pblicas equilibradas, se afianza el papel de la inversi y de las exportaciones en nuestro patr de crecimiento, y se hace compatible la generaci de empleo con el avance de la productividad. Todo ello en lnea con los requerimientos que se derivan del diagntico que les acabo de presentar. Permtanme pues, que antes de pasar a los aspectos de estabilidad financiera concluya que la economa espala est en buenas condiciones relativas para reanudar una senda de crecimiento ms dinmico, una vez que se despejen las incertidumbres que atenazan a la economa mundial. Estabilidad financiera. Seras, me gustara ahora pasar a referirme a otra rea de actividad del Banco de Espa: los aspectos relacionados con la estabilidad financiera y la supervisi bancaria. Pero antes de adentrarme en la descripci de la evoluci del sistema financiero espal, permtanme que llame su atenci sobre el segundo nero de la memoria de la supervisi bancaria en Espa. En mi comparecencia ante esta Comisi hace un a, anunci que estbamos terminando el primer ejemplar de la memoria de supervisi del Banco de Espaa que corresponda al ejercicio 2001 y que fue publicada unos meses despus. Este a hemos adelantado varios meses su elaboraci, de forma que ya ha sido publicada la correspondiente al ejercicio pasado. Como ustedes saben, esta publicacin ser obligatoria a partir del a 2003 por imperativo legal. El Banco de Espa ha preferido, no obstante, adelantarse a ese requisito legal y contribuir, de esa manera, a un mejor conocimiento y trasparencia de la funci supervisora. Por timo, djenme destacar que en dicha memoria, el Banco de Espaa ha ido ms all de un mero y estricto cumplimiento de la obligaci legal y ha tratado de hacer un ejercicio de anlisis y explicaci que, junto con los informes semestrales de estabilidad financiera, que tambin anuncie en mi anterior comparecencia, permiten un seguimiento de la evoluci de las condiciones que determinan la estabilidad de nuestro sistema financiero. Desde un punto de vista internacional, el a 2002 fue un a tremendamente complejo. Si hubiese que selar el rasgo ms notable del sistema financiero internacional, la palabra clave sera posiblemente: resistencia. Resistencia ante un conjunto amplio de perturbaciones que he sintetizado en mi exposici anterior. Cules son los factores que explican ese relativo xito? Un primer factor a tener en cuenta es el de las mejoras en la gesti del riesgo, que permiten una mejor diversificacin del mismo y una difusi internacional ms amplia. Evidentemente, por muy buena que sea esa gesti del riesgo financiero, una vez asumido, ste no puede desaparecer, pero una correcta transformaci y distribucin del mismo puede facilitar la absorci de perturbaciones. Otro elemento clave a la hora de explicar ese xito ha sido la actuaci de las autoridades plicas cuando se pusieron de manifiesto debilidades institucionales profundas y conflictos de intereses. En definitiva, el sistema financiero internacional ha superado un periodo complejo y difcil. No obstante, este mensaje de optimismo debe ser matizado, pues aun cuando se hayan absorbido perturbaciones de calado considerable, es inevitable que la capacidad de resistencia del sistema financiero internacional, ante perturbaciones adversas ha quedado mermada. Por tanto, debemos permanecer alerta, y continuar con los esfuerzos para fortalecer el sistema financiero internacional. En ese entorno, las entidades y mercados financieros espales superaron satisfactoriamente el a, de forma que podemos afirmar, que las condiciones financieras en la economa espala no han planteado restricciones al proceso de recuperaci econica. La evoluci de las entidades de depito espalas en el 2002 puede resumirse analizando tres reas concretas: actividad, rentabilidad y solvencia. Por lo que respecta a la actividad, el negocio bancario, medido por los recursos totales de activos y pasivos, del balance consolidado, crecien 2002 un 0,7%, frente a un 7,4% el a anterior, moderndose por tanto de manera considerable su crecimiento. No obstante, es necesario profundizar un poco ms, pues el balance consolidado incluye tanto la evoluci del negocio en Espa, como en el extranjero. La actividad en el extranjero cayms de un 23,5%, en buena parte como resultado de la evoluci del tipo de cambio del euro, mientras que la actividad bancaria en territorio nacional, a moderndose, siguicreciendo a tasas ms elevadas, en torno al 8%, en concordancia, hasta cierto punto, con el dinamismo econico de la economa espala. En cualquier caso, la caracterstica bsica de la evoluci bancaria por el lado del activo es dinamismo del crdito al sector privado residente, que ha mantenido su crecimiento en cifras que se mueven en torno al 14% interanual. Esta evoluci se sustenta fundamentalmente en el crdito con garanta hipotecaria cuyo crecimiento interanual se mantiene en torno al 20%. Estas cifras determinan un cambio en su composici, ganando un mayor peso el crdito hipotecario, destinado a adquisici de vivienda y al sector de la construcci. Esta evoluci est ligada a la evoluci del mercado de la vivienda, como antes he comentado. Existen elementos que aconsejan prudencia y vigilancia de las entidades en la concesi de nuevos crditos. En primer lugar, el ritmo de crecimiento actual del crdito hipotecario, no parece representar un valor de equilibrio a largo plazo; refleja principalmente el ajuste de las expectativas de los agentes ante el nuevo entorno de estabilidad macroeconica, bajos tipos de inters y dinamismo en la creaci de empleo. En segundo lugar, aunque se trata de crditos con garanta real, y a cuando el precio de los inmuebles no oscila como el de los activos financieros, el valor futuro de una garanta no puede ser proyectado de manera mecnica. El valor de la garanta debe verse, pues, en conjunci con su posible evoluci futura, incluyendo en su posible caso escenarios de estrs. En tercer lugar, aunque los ratios de morosidad permanecen a niveles histicamente bajos, lo que refleja una sustancial mejora en la gesti de riesgos, dado el fuerte crecimiento del crdito en los timos as, las entidades deben considerar las dificultades de mantener ratios tan bajos. Por ello conviene que analicen con cuidado el impacto que escenarios alternativos de tipo de inters pueden tener sobre las tasas de morosidad de los crditos. Permtanme que termine esta reflexi sobre la actividad de las entidades con una breve menci al rea del pasivo. Los depitos a plazo han ido moderando su tasa de crecimiento hasta cifras en el entorno del 10%, cifra similar a la de los acreedores totales. Si bien ese valor es razonable, e incluso elevado, existe una brecha importante, y creciente, entre crditos y depitos, financiado bien con endeudamiento externo, bien con aumentos de recursos propios. Este elemento, a cuando no representa hoy por hoy una preocupacin inmediata, s que ade un argumento adicional en favor de una cierta moderaci de las tasas de crecimiento del crdito. En el rea de rentabilidad, los bancos espales no fueron ajenos a las complejidades y problemas del a 2002. As, el beneficio caymoderadamente, en torno al 10%, cifra que se ha moderado en el primer trimestre del a. No obstante, su comportamiento, en un a complejo, fue satisfactorio, pues las cadas fueron menores que en otros pases de nuestro entorno y el ratio de rentabilidad o ROE, aun cuando tambin cay se situen un 12%, lo que representa un diferencial frente a la deuda plica a 10 as de cerca del 8%. De nuevo esta cifra ha mejorado en el primer trimestre del presente a siendo la rentabilidad sobre recursos propios superior a un 13%. Esta evoluci satisfactoria, no exenta de ciertas debilidades, muestra las ventajas, en determinadas condiciones, del modelo bancario espaol, con un elevado componente de banca al por menor, como un modelo rentable y estable, esto es, menos sometido a la variabilidad de resultados que caracterizpor ejemplo, a la banca de inversi. En cuanto a la solvencia, las entidades de depito mantuvieron el perfil de solidez de recursos propios habitual en ella, con un ratio de solvencia medio en el 2002 del 11,1%, muy por encima del mnimo del 8%. Si tenemos en cuenta que la normativa espala es ms exigente que la directiva comunitaria o que las reglas de solvencia del Comit de Supervisi Bancaria de Basilea, la situaci es a ms satisfactoria. En trminos de capital de primera categora, el ratio espal se situen el 2002 en un 8,5%, esto es, ms del doble del requerimiento mnimo del 4%. Por timo, Espa cuenta con la provisi estadstica, que obliga a las entidades a provisionar no so por los riesgos fallidos, sino tambin por los latentes. A pesar de este panorama, como supervisores debemos huir, como ya he dicho, de la complacencia. Por ello, hemos reiterado en diversas ocasiones, incluida la tima memoria de supervisi, la importancia de una visi estratgica de los recursos propios que preste atenci tanto a su suficiencia como a su calidad. As, hemos establecido un lmite para las llamadas participaciones preferentes del 30% del capital Tier 1, y hemos alertado a las entidades de los riesgos de su comercializaci entre inversores minoristas, que pueden no entender suficientemente los riesgos del producto Por otra parte, estamos revisando el tratamiento a efectos de recursos propios de las titulizaciones para ponerlo en lnea con la futura normativa de capital de Basilea. En definitiva, y teniendo en cuenta las tres reas de actividad, rentabilidad y solvencia, podemos afirmar la buena salud del sistema financiero espal que, en estos momentos, est en disposici de financiar un mayor ritmo de reactivaci econica. Me gustara terminar esta intervenci destacando que en el Banco de Espa continuamos trabajando en las lneas de mejora de la supervisi prudencial bancaria que mencion en mi pasada intervenci, es decir, de forma muy resumida: coordinaci internacional, enfoque preventivo e incentivador de buena gesti de riesgos, que complemente la supervisi tradicional, atenci a los aspectos cualitativos, incluidas las estructuras y cigos de buen gobierno de las entidades, etc. de forma que la combinaci de regulaci, practicas supervisoras y disciplina de mercado, contribuyan a mantener y mejorar la eficiencia y solvencia de nuestro sistema bancario. Muchas gracias.

Title: The enlargement of the European Union: economic, monetary and financial aspects. Complutense University. Summer Courses. El Escorial.
text: The enlargement of the European Union: economic, monetary and financial aspects (summary) Complutense University. Summer Courses El Escorial, 9 July 2003 Jos8e Vi96als, General Manager of Banco de Espa96a a5 EU enlargement is not only an economic but also a political and institutional milestone, bringing great challenges but also opportunities for Europe. a5 The main challenge is to achieve real convergence of the new Member States towards the European average, as they currently have an average GDP per head of 44% of the GDP of the current EU but nevertheless have approximately 28% of its population. Given the starting conditions, it will still be many years before full convergence is achieved, but what is important is that convergence is as fast and sustainable as possible, in order to facilitate the smooth functioning of the enlarged EU. a5 In addition to deepening structural reforms, there are two conditions needed to enhance the processes of real convergence in the new Member States: 1) strengthening macroeconomic stability and nominal convergence; and 2) develop their financial systems. a5 With regard to macroeconomic stability, the acceding countries have adopted different monetary and exchange rate regimes that have helped them to reduce their inflation rates, although they face the challenges of further reducing their often high government deficits. The timing of whether to enter the euro area will vary from country to country. In any case, the entry of a particular country into the euro area must respect compliance with the conditions of Maastricht. The "best moment" is also the one that guarantees the best prospects for real convergence. a5 More developed financial systems support growth processes by mobilizing savings, allocating it to the most efficient investment projects, and managing and distributing risks more effectively. The development of the financial systems of the acceding countries is therefore essential for achieving real convergence. Currently, the financial systems of these countries are characterized by: low levels of development, weak role of capital markets, scarcity of domestic credit and high participation of foreign capital in the ownership of banks. Therefore, it is necessary to enhance the size and quality of financial systems, so as to increase domestic credit to the private sector and the role of markets, in a framework of greater competition, solidity, efficiency and legal stability.
text_original: La ampliacin de la Unin Europea: aspectos econmicos, monetarios y financieros (resumen) Universidad Complutense. Cursos de Verano El Escorial, 9 de julio de 2003 Jos Vials, Director General de Banco de Espaa  La ampliacin de la UE supone un hito no solo econmico, sino tambin poltico e institucional, que entraa grandes desafos pero tambin oportunidades para Europa.  El principal reto es lograr la convergencia real de los nuevos estados miembros hacia la media europea, ya que actualmente tienen un PIB per capita, por trmino medio, del 44% del PIB de la actual UE pero, sin embargo, cuentan aproximadamente con un 28% de su poblacin. Dadas las condiciones de partida, pasarn an bastantes aos hasta que se logre la plena convergencia, pero lo importante es que esta sea lo ms rpida y sostenible posible, con objeto de facilitar el buen funcionamiento de la UE ampliada.  Adems de profundizar en las reformas estructurales, dos son las condiciones que se precisan para potenciar los procesos de convergencia real de los nuevos estados miembros:1) fortalecer la estabilidad macroeconmica y la convergencia nominal; y 2) desarrollar sus sistemas financieros.  Por lo que respecta a la estabilidad macroeconmica, los pases en adhesin han adoptado distintos regmenes monetarios y cambiarios que les han ayudado a reducir sus tasas de inflacin, si bien tienen los retos de seguir reduciendo sus, en muchos casos, elevados dficit pblicos. Acerca del momento oportuno para entrar en el rea del euro, este variar segn uno u otro pas. En cualquier caso, la entrada de un determinado pas en el rea del euro debe respetar el cumplimiento de las condiciones de Maastricht. El mejor momento es, adems, el que garantiza las mejores perspectivas para la convergencia real.  Unos sistemas financieros ms desarrollados favorecen los procesos de crecimiento al movilizar el ahorro, asignarlo a los proyectos de inversin ms eficientes y gestionar y distribuir los riesgos ms eficazmente. De ah que, el desarrollo de los sistemas financieros de los pases en adhesin resulte fundamental para lograr la convergencia real. Actualmente, los sistemas financieros de estos pases se caracterizan por: niveles de desarrollo reducidos, escaso papel de los mercados de capitales, escasez de crdito interno y elevada participacin de capitales extranjeros en la propiedad de los bancos. Por ello, resulta necesario potenciar el tamao y calidad de los sistemas financieros, de forma que se incremente el crdito interno al sector privado y el papel de los mercados, en un marco de mayor competencia, solidez, eficacia y estabilidad jurdica.

Title: The challenges of banking supervision and the new perspectives of Basel II
text: BANK OF SPAIN THE CHALLENGES OF BANKING SUPERVISION AND THE NEW PROSPECTS OF BASEL II GONZALO GIL Deputy governor September 2003 1. Introduccin Banks have special characteristics that require the existence of a specific regulatory and supervisory framework. Firstly, their function of producing liquidity for the economy: banks transform demand from their customers into loans, usually in the medium and long term. Secondly, the characteristics of the banking business translate into the existence of asymmetric information between depositors and bank managers. The interaction of the two previous elements can lead to doubts (founded or not) about the situation of the entity, depositors decide massively to withdraw their deposits from the entity. Faced with the avalanche of depositors, the bank does not have enough liquid assets to deal with the deposits and may be forced to sell, at a loss, the rest of the assets. Finally, the entity goes bankrupt because the realizations of assets are insufficient to cover the deposits. The bankruptcy of one entity can cause those of others with which it had credit and credit operations and, in extreme, although not impossible, cases, the bankruptcy of the entire banking system with the result of the complete collapse of the payment system. Therefore, the special characteristics of banking companies (exposure to bank panics) can translate into a very negative externality on the economy as a whole. The welfare costs that this would entail justify the existence and need for adequate regulation of tax entities. Of all banking regulation, the regulation of banks' own resources stands out for its relevance. An appropriate level of capital can contribute to: partially correcting institutions' assumption of excessive risk; ensure a buffer to cope with negative shocks to your bottom line; facilitate raising funds to deal with liquidity shocks and, finally, deal with unexpected losses. It should be borne in mind that this regulation/supervision cannot replace the internal elements of corporate governance (managers, administrators, boards of directors, audit committee...) or the disciplining role of market competition. Clearly, responsibility for the situation of entities lies with their managers. 2. Objectives of banking supervision The actions of the supervision are carried out in accordance with a legal mandate that gives force and, at the same time, limits the actions of the Bank of Spain, responsible for the supervision of credit institutions. Following this mandate, it directs its attention, first of all, to the solvency and performance of institutions with the aim of avoiding the emergence of systemic risks and minimizing, as far as possible, individual crises. This is done through compliance with established rules, which also include customer protection and transparency towards the market. It is always advisable to be clear about the limitations imposed on the Bank by its legal system. The precision of the limits is perceived more clearly if we relate their functions with those of other sectoral supervisors and with the actions of other bodies. Thus, with respect to other entities with adjoining competences (tax authorities, CNMV, DGS, Comisi de Prevencin de Blanqueo), the relationship is one of collaboration (through the signing of agreements that formalize it) and communication when in the development of its own competences the Bank knows some relevant information. It is appropriate to clearly demarcate some functions of the Bank that have concomitance with those of other entities, also essential. Without wishing to be exhaustive: the Bank of Spain does not manage or administer the entities, if it verifies the solvency of the entity, although without an exhaustive review of the operations carried out. Unlike the external auditors, the Bank of Spain carries out the valuation of the entity without any time limit, its information is reserved and does not examine the financial statements. It is the responsibility of the internal audit of the entities to review the internal controls established by the Board of Directors, which is very helpful, but not part of the task of the supervisor. Finally, the Bank does not guarantee in its own sense the deposits of the entities since that is the task of the deposit guarantee fund, with the corresponding coverage limits established by the corresponding legislation. The basic objectives of supervision will not change with the approval of the new Basel capital agreement, known as Basel II. 3. Basic structure of the existing Agreement (Basel I) The objective of Basel I (agreement signed in 1988) was, on the one hand, to strengthen solvency after a period of rapid deregulation and liberalization of financial systems and, on the other hand, to level the competitive playing field of internationally active banks. The agreement establishes a minimum capital ratio of 8% of weighted assets, with a harmonised definition of capital and asset weights. By way of illustration, cash and debt issued by OECD governments is 0 per cent, equivalent to 0 per cent capital consumption; exposures to banks whose registered office is in an OECD country are weighted 20% (minimum capital of 1.6%); loans with mortgage guarantee 50% (consumption of 4%) and the rest of exposures are weighted 100% with a capital requirement of at least 8%. Among the merits of the 1988 agreement is its simplicity and that it has contributed significantly to the harmonization of banking regulation between countries (more than 100 countries have acceded to the agreement), has improved competitive equality and, above all, has strengthened the stability of the international financial system, through an increase in the capital ratios maintained by institutions. However, despite its contributions, the agreement was becoming outdated due to the new possibilities offered to banks by innovation in products and financial markets and the considerable improvement in risk management that institutions have carried out since 1988 (more precise risk measurement, better coverage, consideration of new risks, etc.). In addition, the connection between capital requirements and the risk assumed by institutions was somewhat crude (for example, all exposures to non-financial corporations were required to have the same capital, without differentiating according to their credit quality) and was beginning to be exploited by institutions (regulatory arbitrage). In short, loss of significance and the diminishing comparability of capital ratios raise the need to revise the old agreement of 1988. 4. New Basel Accord (Basel II) The objectives of the new agreement continue to be the promotion of the solvency of banking systems and the promotion of equality in competition, as well as the better hedging of risks and the extension of this to others not explicitly considered in the current Agreement (in particular operational risk). Basel II seeks to link capital requirements much more closely to the risk incurred and become a stimulus for banks to improve their risk management. The new agreement gives a broader role to banking supervisors and financial markets. The elaboration of the new agreement has been a complex process but open to the entities that have participated in the different calibration exercises carried out by the Basel Committee as well as through countless suggestions to improve the agreement, many of which have been incorporated. The road has been long. The first concept paper is from June 1999. From then until now: 3 impact studies, 2 additional consultative documents, numerous working groups set up by the Committee, hundreds of meetings with representatives of banks, etc. After each consultative document, an extensive discussion process has been developed with more than 300 banks around the world, including five Spanish banks, which have collaborated on the quantitative impact studies necessary to properly calibrate the required capital curves and, at the same time, ensure that the reform was consistent, with the aim of maintaining the level of own resources. Spain began to participate in this process in 1999 as a guest country to the credit risk working group, the key group of the Agreement, and joined it fully from the moment it was selected as a member of the Basel Committee (February 2001). Since July of this year, the Governor chairs the Committee. The date established for the closing of the Agreement is December of this year and from that point the process of implementing three ace of duration will begin, which, given the complexity of the Agreement, will require intense work from entities and supervisors. In principle, the date of entry into force of the new agreement is the end of 2006. STRUCTURE OF THE AGREEMENT: THE THREE PILLARS. Basel II is structured around three pillars. Pillar 1 provides for minimum capital requirements to cover three categories of risks: credit risk, for which three approaches are allowed, market risk (unchanged from the current situation) and operational risk coverage. Pillar 2 contains the review of the capital adequacy by the supervisor and, finally, Pillar 3 promotes market discipline through the requirement of greater transparency of information to institutions. a5 Pillar 1: minimum capital requirements The numerator of the capital ratio; that is, the definition of regulatory capital remains unchanged in relation to Basel I. The minimum 8% does not change either. What changes is the definition of weighted assets; that is, the calculation of the risks incurred by banks. New in Pillar 1 are substantial changes in the treatment of credit risk and the explicit treatment of operational risk. In both cases there are three possible options, each of which increases the sensitivity to risk and the sophistication of the measurement methods so that each bank chooses the most appropriate. For credit risk, the most important from a prudential point of view, Basel II proposes three approaches: standard approach and internal rating models (IRB) approach with two variants, basic approach and advanced approach. The standard approach establishes greater sensitivity to risk through the use of external ratings (provided by rating agencies authorized for this purpose by supervisors). It also establishes, as in the previous Agreement, portfolios (sovereign, banks, non-financial companies and retail business) with weightings that depend on external ratings and also on the existence or not of mortgage guarantees. Additionally, the treatment of risk compensation techniques (guarantees, credit derivatives, etc.) is improved. In the IRB approach, the fundamental difference is that the calculation of capital requirements is based on the measurement of the risk factors (probability of default, loss in case of default, exposure at the time of default and maturity) provided by the entity itself and result of its internal models used for the measurement and management of its risks. However, banks do not determine all the elements necessary for the calculation of own resources since the fmulas that relate risk factors to the level of capital are provided by supervisors. These fmulas translate quantitative data into capital requirements. The difference between the basic and advanced approaches lies in the nero, greater in the advanced case and minor in the basic case, of factors from the entity itself that are used for the calculation of its own resources. There is also recognition of the risk mitigation techniques used by institutions and specific treatment for asset securitisation. Operational risk is defined as the likelihood of incurring losses due to inadequacy or failures in internal processes, personnel or systems or as a result of external events. Legal risk is included but not strategic or reputational risk. There are also three alternatives to measure this risk: Basic, Standard and Advanced approach. Again the difference is based on a greater sophistication of calculations and an increasing finesse in risk measurement. In the basic and standard ones, which will be applied to banks with lower risks in this area, they are required to maintain a level of capital directly proportional to a variable representative of their turnover, given that the greater the volume, the greater the possibility of incurring such risk. a5 Pillar 2: Supervisory review Capital adequacy goes beyond meeting the minimum requirements set out in Pillar 1. The complexity and rapid change of markets and products as well as changes in risk management by institutions could cause the Pillar 1 Agreement to fall behind what would be the best risk control practices. It is therefore necessary to strengthen the role of the supervisor (Pillar 2) in order to make the necessary corrections. Pillar 2 is based on four key principles and additional, more specific elements. Principle 1 states that banks should have procedures for assessing their level of capital in relation to their risk profile and a strategy for maintaining their capital levels. Principle 2 requires supervisors to assess the adequacy of institutions' capital and their ability to meet minimum capital ratios. Principle 3 authorizes supervisors to impose capital levels above the minimum. Finally, Principle 4 states that supervisors should intervene quickly to prevent capital from falling below the level appropriate to each institution's risk profile. As regards the specific elements, Pillar 2 can be used to cover risks not covered in Pillar 1 and in particular, issues related to securitisations (effective or non-effective transfer of risk) and to the economic cycle (performance and verification of stress test exercises developed by institutions). Regulators/supervisors should provide explicit views on the adequacy of capital levels above the Pillar 1 regulatory minimum. To do this, they will have to proactively assess the policies of the banks, the evolution of economic capital and the control of risks by the company. All this will involve an intense effort on the part of supervisors to develop technological capacities, increase staff, etc. There is a risk that the more sophisticated supervisor will tend to give more flexibility to its entities while the less prepared will tend to be more conservative, putting its banks at a competitive disadvantage. The solution to this question is achieved through the convergence of supervisory practices, something that the Committee is already working on, following the developments of other committees in the timand years. a5 Pillar 3: Market discipline It is an essential complement to the two previous pillars. It establishes a series of requirements that allow market participants to properly assess the risk profile of the entity and its capitalization. Transparency in this regard is a balancing component of the Agreement's increased emphasis on internal methodologies that give banks a greater degree of discretion in calculating their capital needs. The transparency policy must be formally approved by the Board of Directors. It will apply at a consolidated level, but supervisors will have the capacity to require it at a sub-consolidation level. Detailed information should be provided on own resources and their components, on the relationship between capital and risks, on risks. The publication of financial accounts is not a substitute for any of the above requirements. The frequency will differ according to the nature of the information. 5. Characteristics and nature of the Basel Committee rules They provide a framework for effective banking supervision that helps protect the stability of financial systems. Although the rules drawn up cover many different aspects related to the general objective mentioned, it is worth mentioning here only those of a more general nature: firstly, the 25 core principles which constitute the requirements for achieving effective banking supervision, secondly, the Basel Accord of 1988, which is still in force and, finally, the Basel II Accord that replaces the previous one and that has been explained in the previous section. The Basel Committee on Banking Supervision is a body created in 1974 to coordinate the supervision of internationally active banks. It is made up of representatives of central banks and supervisors (group of 10, plus Luxembourg and Spain since January 2001). It is not an international organization nor does it have its own legal entity. Its recommendations are not international standards although they have extraordinary influence. This means that the process of drafting the Agreement in which the Committee is involved is of a completely different nature from that of the national supervisory standard-setting processes. The Committee is responsible for developing international standards and identifying best practices for the development of effective supervision and regulation, from a technical point of view. Apart from this process is the work of parliamentary representatives who are the ones who will freely decide on the rules to be approved. This means that the set of rules that constitute the Agreement do not have legal force until the parliamentary bodies have decided on them in each country. The same was of course true of the Basel I Agreement in force, which has become a legal norm, in whole or in part, in virtually all countries on the basis of the prestige of the members of the Committee. a5 Process in the European Union The beginning of the discussion of the new Agreement coincides with the date on which the first steps in the creation of the European Single Market began to be taken. Therefore, the treatment of the issue is integrated into the Financial Services Action Plan. Through the groups of the Commission in which members and non-members of Basel participate, the European regulatory framework is being developed, which proposes the adaptation of the Agreement to the specificities of the Uni (greater presence of SMEs in the European productive fabric, banks of very different size, etc.). As in Basel, there has been a very fluid dialogue with industry. As with the other directives, this one must also apply to all financial institutions (banks and investment companies). Regulations do not have to lead to an increase in capital requirements. There are incentives for non-specialist local entities to adopt the standard approach, small specialisers to adopt the basic IRB, and large international banks to operate with the advanced approach. The retail portfolio makes the difference between one entity and another. The Directive (which should be ready in the first quarter of 2004 and transposed into national law by 2006) also sets out an appropriate regulatory framework for small, securities-focused institutions. The directive will incorporate some nuances with respect to Basel II: more attention to mortgage loans, treatment of mortgage and territorial bonds, broader treatment of mitigation elements, greater flexibility in the treatment of operational risk in ESIS. Its preparation is already following the Lamfalussy scheme: level 1 and level 2, of a legal nature, approved by codecisi (Council and Parliament), level 3, which is not part of positive law (convergence of supervisory practices). Level 1 is the body of the directive and contains the basic principles of regulation and the elements considered essential from the point of view of legal certainty. Level 2 is articulated through annexes and incorporates technical issues and other aspects that may need to be changed flexibly. Level 3 seeks homogenization in its application to the different topics through supervisory convergence. Outside the European Union there is also debate and the necessary steps are being taken to adapt to Basel II. Specifically, an extraordinarily intense parliamentary debate on Basel II is currently taking place in the United States. The European case is different and the rules contained in the Agreement will only be in force in the countries of the Union when the European legislative process is closed, which will lead to a directive implementing in all countries, which may finally follow the Agreement or in all probability making differences. 6. Implementation of the new Agreement The process of implementing the Agreement shall in no case be an automatic process in which entities freely choose the approach that suits them best. On the contrary, the requirements for the use of internal models (IRB approach) are very demanding. These are both quantitative (data for long periods of time, requirements determined to rating systems, etc.) and qualitative. Among these scams stands out that the models used are practically integrated into the management of the entity itself. Risk assessment will not be something isolated from management but a direct product of it. Models developed exclusively for the calculation of regulatory own resources shall not be authorised. Application may be uneven between countries and, within a country, between banks. In the United States, supervisors have already announced that they will only require Basel II from about 10 entities, the most sophisticated and those that concentrate the largest part of international assets. In Europe, it will apply to all banks and investment companies, regardless of size. Supervisors will have to decide between possible options. Basel II is focused, in its advanced variants, on the most sophisticated banks with an international presence. There is also no need to automatically move to Basel II in 2006. Emerging countries that have recently implemented Basel I can postpone change by acting in the meantime by incorporating pillar 2 and 3 elements into their systems. This flexibility and adaptability of the Agreement (which results in greater complexity) requires particular attention to cross-border consistency issues, in particular for multinational banks in different jurisdictions. There is a Working Group for the Implementation of the Agreement (AIG) which, on the basis of the above fact, will closely monitor the implementation of the Agreement, providing a space in which problems are analysed and responses to the inevitable problems posed by its implementation are coordinated. The degree of consistency should be maintained based on the task of supervisors. Supervisors will continue to frame their activity and carry out their responsibilities within the framework set out by the core principles. The new situation suggests, however, that these should be strengthened, with emphasis on the exchange of information and coordination, as well as the elaboration of practical plans. Thus, the AIG has developed six additional basic principles, which reinforce the aspects discussed: 1) The Agreement does not change responsibilities. 2) The home country supervisor of the bank (home supervisor in Basel jargon) is responsible for the implementation of the Agreement on a consolidated basis. 3) The supervisor of the host country of the institution (host supervisor), in the case of subsidiaries, has responsibilities that must be considered 4) Increase the cooperative effort, led by the home. 5) Avoid redundancies in the validation and approval of models. 6) Communication as clearly as possible, to the entities, of the respective roles. 7. Basel Challenges a5 Challenges for banks The literature around the Accord often focuses on its effects on risk measurement and financial stability, but Basel will also be one of the largest structural shocks to the banking industry in recent decades as the new Accord will influence its business strategies (consolidations, mergers, emphasis on certain lines of business, etc.). In addition, banks will need to improve the measurement, management and control of risks. As for their internal models, they must live up to the technical and data requirements and meet the quantitative and qualitative requirements for their use. At the same time, they will have to combine the new agreement with the significant change in accounting rules since 2005. It should be stressed that it is a mistake to have a purely mechanistic view of the new agreement. It is not enough to have a well-designed internal rating system, it is necessary to have it well integrated into the daily risk management process. In addition, it is not enough to have a sufficient volume of own resources, there must be a strategy (permanence of them, capacity to access the market, balance between shareholder remuneration and capitalization, etc.) and an assessment of the level and composition of capital in the medium and long term. a5 Challenges for supervisors The first challenge is to implement Basel II in 3 aces, task nothing Easy due to the inevitable greater complexity that will entail Basel II. Secondly, it is necessary to prepare to comply with the requirements of Pillar 2: assess the adequacy of capital to the risk profile of each institution, which will require detailed knowledge of the risks, including their evolution throughout the economic cycle, the interaction between the different risks as well as assessing the ability of the managers of the institution to manage and control these risks. The supervisor will need to judge the quantity and quality of the institution's own resources and understand, assess and validate the internal credit risk and operational risk models. Since if the regulatory capital raised from Pillar 1 does not appear to the supervisor to be appropriate to the level of risk, the supervisor may require more capital through Pillar 2, it increases the supervisor's discretion. This greater discretion of the supervisor requires greater transparency towards supervisees and an increase in the convergence of supervisory practices to avoid discrimination between countries. The supervisor should pay greater attention to qualitative elements. While inspecting the asset quality and profitability of institutions, it should evaluate the information provided by institutions to the specifications, study the risk management principles applied by each entity, analyse their corporate governance mechanisms and their information and internal control systems. In addition to the above challenges, the supervisor should also add the Basel II interface with the new accounting rules. To this end, a permanent dialogue has been opened between accountants and banking supervisors. The entry into force of the IAS standards in the European Union in 2005 will require preferential attention to be devoted to the valuation of assets and provisions for risks since they affect the definition of the capital of institutions. In fact, the Basel Committee has been working with the International Accountancy Standard Board (IASB) to ensure consistency between Basel II reporting and compliance obligations with accounting standards (IAS). In this sense, the most important IAS standards are 32 and 39, which deal with the valuation of financial assets and liabilities. As with the capital agreement, IAS also go far beyond a regulatory or circular alteration. They are real innovations that will affect not only transparency, but business strategies themselves. Although the Bank of Spain as supervisor, with legitimate interests in accounting, will continue to play an active role in the configuration of the regulations, it is important that the entities assume the qualitative changes that it will entail. It imposes greater responsibility on institutions and their managers by providing greater flexibility. Accounting rules now limited discretion. The biggest impact will undoubtedly come from the change in approach. It should be noted, first of all, the greater interpretative breadth, open principles with accounting treatment options. Secondly, the financial information will be higher than the current one and with a clear orientation towards investors. Making provisions will require stronger doses of estimates than the current model which is very mechanical. The increased use of fair value will introduce greater sensitivity to accounts and equity as a result of the evolution of financial markets. It should be noted, finally, that accounting standards interact directly with the 3 pillars of Basel reinforcing the effects of the Agreement: they will increase the standardization of accounting and the development of valuation methodologies that must take into account the effect of volatility, they will have to transmit to the agencies the true sense of the greatest predictable volatility although they could increase cyclicality, They will help smooth out legal problems with credit derivatives and make it easier for regulators to assess whether risk is actually transferred when the supervisory review of securitisations takes place. 8. Banco de Espaa's supervisory approach Finally, I would like to conclude by assessing, even briefly, the situation in which the Bank of Spain finds itself with a view to Basel II. The supervision has been developed histicamente in 3 phases. In the first, until the banking crisis of the late 70s of the last century, supervision focused on revising a set of rules that severely restricted banking activity. The second phase, after the aforementioned crisis, is based on a complete liberalization of the financial system and begins to emphasize quantitative aspects. In the third stage, Banco de Espa's supervisory methodology has been reoriented towards risks, their management and control. In this third stage, to face the new challenges of supervision, the bank has developed what it calls the SABER approach (Supervision of Banking Activity under the Risk Approach). It is worth briefly remembering how it works. First, the level of inherent risk assumed by an entity in the different areas is quantified (credit, market, interest rate risk are considered, among others, etc.). Secondly, this level is linked to the quality of the control systems in place. In this way, the residual risk of the entity is obtained. The comparison between this residual risk and the solvency of the institution (level and quality of own resources) is what determines the risk for the supervisor. This risk-focused supervision scheme puts us squarely on the Basel II line. In addition to the SABER approach, the existence of the statistical provision established in 2000 and based on the use, with due controls, of internal models to calculate the expected losses in all the operations of the entities, has allowed us to gain experience on internal models of credit risk the scams, even before Basel II closes. The fact that we have been working during the scams on these principles and concepts will undoubtedly facilitate our adaptation to the new scheme. In the same sense, the existence of the CIR and its exploitation for the construction of reference models for the measurement of risk with companies. Basel II will undoubtedly be more sensitive to risk than Basel I. However, it will also be more complex. This greater complexity will force an internal reorganization of the supervisor that will require the adaptation of means and personnel to the new tasks. If we are able to complete this task successfully, we will have taken a major step towards the stability of the Spanish financial system that will benefit society as a whole.
