Deben ser totalmente comprendidos por los banqueros y por los supervisores. En segundo lugar, el Comit pretende (y la industria tambin demanda) que el nuevo Acuerdo pueda ser aplicable a la mayor cantidad de entidades y de pases posible. No se quiere renunciar a que el Acuerdo siga siendo un elemento de referencia del mercado internacional. Por este motivo, las entidades pueden optar entre un conjunto de mtodos para valorar sus riesgos, que pueden utilizar dependiendo de su nivel de sofisticacin. De hecho, en estos momentos, el Acuerdo en su Pilar 1 prev 3 mtodos, con diferente nivel de complejidad (incorporando de forma creciente valoraciones internas de las propias entidades) para que las entidades puedan medir su riesgo de crdito y otros 3 mtodos para hacer lo mismo con el riesgo operacional. Es decir, se ha buscado una mayor cobertura, contemplado opciones diferentes, lo cual inevitablemente conduce a ms complejidad. En tercer lugar, el nuevo Acuerdo, al querer ser ms sensible al riesgo realmente asumido por las entidades que el Acuerdo actual, genera ganadores y perdedores; es decir, hay entidades que necesitarn menos capital regulatorio que en la situacin actual, pero tambin habr entidades a las que suceda lo contrario, por ejemplo, porque su cartera tenga un nivel de riesgo ms elevado. Evidentemente, estas ltimas entidades tratan de que las nuevas propuestas les perjudiquen lo menos posible, aunque esto suponga una renuncia, al menos parcial, a uno de los objetivos bsicos perseguidos por el Comit, esto es, a que los requerimientos de capital sean sensibles al riesgo asumido. Finalmente, los procesos consultivos y los anlisis de impacto que canalizan las opiniones de la industria requieren mucho tiempo. Analizar los cientos de comentarios recibidos, intentando buscar una solucin razonable para todos ellos, as como para llevar a cabo estudios del impacto cuantitativo de las propuestas del Comit, son procesos llevados con extrema seriedad que han permitido incorporar observaciones muy vlidas de la industria. 4. CARACTERSTICAS Y NATURALEZA DE LAS NORMAS DEL COMIT DE BASILEA Estas constituyen un marco de referencia para una supervisin bancaria efectiva que ayude a proteger la estabilidad de los sistemas financieros. Aunque las normas elaboradas por el Comit abarcan muy distintos aspectos relacionados con el objetivo general mencionado, merece la pena citar aqu slo las de carcter ms general: en primer lugar, los 25 principios bsicos (core principles) que constituyen los requisitos para alcanzar una supervisin bancaria efectiva; en segundo lugar, el Acuerdo de Basilea de 1988, todava vigente y, finalmente, el Acuerdo de Basilea II que sustituye al anterior y que se ha explicado en el epgrafe anterior. El Comit de Supervisin Bancaria de Basilea es un organismo creado en 1974 para coordinar la supervisin de los bancos activos a nivel internacional. Est formado por representantes de los bancos centrales y de los supervisores (grupo de los 10, adems de Luxemburgo y Espaa desde enero del 2001). No es un organismo internacional ni tiene entidad jurdica propia. Sus recomendaciones no son normas internacionales aunque tienen extraordinaria influencia. Lo anterior quiere decir que el proceso de elaboracin del Acuerdo en el que el Comit est involucrado es de una naturaleza completamente distinta de la de los procesos nacionales de elaboracin de normas supervisoras. El Comit se ocupa de elaborar estndares internacionales e identificar las mejores prcticas para el desarrollo de una supervisin y regulacin efectiva, desde un punto de vista tcnico. Al margen de este proceso est la labor de los representantes parlamentarios que son los que libremente decidirn sobre las normas a aprobar. Quiere esto decir que el conjunto de normas que constituyen el Acuerdo no tienen fuerza legal hasta que las instancias parlamentarias hayan decidido sobre ellas en cada pas. Lo mismo ocurri, por supuesto, con el Acuerdo hoy vigente de Basilea I, que se ha transformado en norma legal, en todo o en parte, en prcticamente todos los pases en base al prestigio de los miembros del Comit. 5. EL ESTUDIO DE IMPACTO QIS3 Y EL TERCER DOCUMENTO CONSULTIVO (CP3) Este tercer estudio de impacto, que contcon los datos proporcionados por las entidades a finales del ao pasado, ha sido el ms completo y sofisticado de todos y ha permitido al Comit refinar las propuestas que incluyen el tercer documento consultivo. Los resultados obtenidos en el QIS3 son satisfactorios y consistentes con los objetivos anunciados por el Comit. Es decir, en trminos generales, las propuestas del Comit generan unas exigencias de capital regulatorio que, en media, se mantienen en los niveles actuales y, adems, existen ciertos incentivos, en trminos de menores exigencias de capital, para que las entidades adopten mtodos ms sofisticados para medir sus riesgos. El tercer documento consultivo recoge muchas de las peticiones de la industria en sus respuestas al segundo proceso consultivo. Es particularmente relevante la mejora en el tratamiento de las PYMEs y la inclusin de un tratamiento completo del riesgo operacional y de la titulizacin. Sin duda, el tratamiento de los crditos a la pequea y mediana empresa ha sido una de las cuestiones ms relevantes en Europa dado que se trata de un sector bsico para nuestras economas. Por ello me voy a detener brevemente en el tratamiento de estas en el proyecto actual. Las propuestas que realizel Comit en su segundo proceso consultivo generaban unas exigencias de capital significativamente mayores que las actuales y suscitaron un amplio debate entre reguladores y la industria. El Comit se hizo eco de las crticas y realiznuevos estudios que pusieron de manifiesto la necesidad de tener en cuenta la mayor diversificacin de esta cartera y, por tanto, su menor riesgo relativo. Las nuevas propuestas consistieron, bsicamente, en la posibilidad de incluir a las PYMEs en la cartera minorista, donde hay menores exigencias de capital regulatorio, y en reducir la pendiente de la curva de capital que debe aplicarse a todas las empresas, introduciendo un ajuste por tamao para aquellas empresas con un tamao inferior a 50 millones de euros. Adems, en el enfoque IRB bsico se introduce un mayor reconocimiento de colaterales utilizados tpicamente por este sector como son el descuento de efectos y de recibos y los colaterales fsicos. Parece que estos cambios han sido acogidos con satisfaccin por la industria. Tambin merece la pena decir algunas palabras acerca de la cartera de participaciones accionariales, que es importante para muchas entidades espaolas, y a las que las nuevas normas imponen unos requerimientos de capital superiores a los actuales, lo que ha constituido una de las crticas al nuevo proyecto recogido en el CP3. No obstante hay que sealar que este tratamiento es necesario porque las normas actuales, en su sencillez, no valoran adecuadamente este riesgo. Por otra parte, est prevista una transicin suave, de manera que todas las inversiones accionariales existentes a la fecha de aprobacin del nuevo Acuerdo dispondrn de un perodo transitorio de 10 aos durante el cual podrn seguir aplicando las normas existentes en la actualidad. 6. SITUACIN ACTUAL Acercndome al final de mi intervencin, me gustara comentar brevemente en qu situacin nos encontramos en la actualidad. Como ya saben, el tercer perodo consultivo terminel pasado 31 de julio. Se han recibido un nmero muy elevado de comentarios, que pueden consultarse en la pgina Web del BIS, dando muestra una vez ms del gran deseo de transparencia con el que el Comit ha desarrollado todo este proceso. La mayor parte de los comentarios, no slo destacan que se comparten los objetivos generales del nuevo Acuerdo, sino que tambin aceptan que se ha producido una mejora sustancial de las propuestas desde el anterior proceso consultivo, reconociendo adems que el nuevo Acuerdo representa un gran paso adelante en la normativa de solvencia. No obstante, no se debe desconocer que ha habido una gran cantidad de observaciones a elementos particulares de las propuestas, las cuales tienen que ser analizadas y a las que se debe dar una respuesta adecuada. Algunas de estas crticas son de carcter general y, como ya les he anticipado, son de difcil solucin. Se refieren a la complejidad y al conservadurismo de las propuestas, as como a la necesidad de promover la igualdad competitiva. Indudablemente, el nuevo Acuerdo es ms complejo que el actual, pero esta mayor complejidad es el resultado tanto de los deseos del Comit de ofrecer un esquema adaptable a entidades con diferente grado de sofisticacin (Basilea I ofreca homogeneizacin y Basilea II ofrece diferenciacin) como de las peticiones de la propia industria que siempre ha querido que se tengan en cuenta las complejidades especficas de sus negocios y que los requerimientos de capital sean ms sensibles al riesgo. 7. IMPLANTACIN DEL NUEVO ACUERDO El proceso de aplicacin del Acuerdo no ser en ningn caso un proceso automtico en el que las entidades libremente escojan el enfoque que ms les conviene. Al contrario, los requisitos para la utilizacin de los modelos internos (enfoque IRB) son muy exigentes. Se trata de requisitos tanto cuantitativos (datos para largos periodos de tiempo, exigencias determinadas a los sistemas de rating, etc.) como cualitativos. Entre estos ltimos destaca el que los modelos que se utilicen estn prcticamente integrados en la propia gestin de la entidad. La valoracin de riesgos no ser algo aislado de la gestin sino producto directo de la misma. No se autorizarn modelos desarrollados exclusivamente para el clculo de los recursos propios regulatorios. El Acuerdo se basa en una discrecin nacional que requiere una consistencia transfronteriza. La aplicacin podr ser desigual entre pases y, dentro de un pas, entre bancos. En Estados Unidos, los supervisores han anunciado ya que solo exigirn Basilea II a unas 10 entidades, las ms sofisticadas y las que concentran la mayor parte de activos internacionales. En Europa, se aplicar a todos los bancos y a las sociedades de inversin, sin distincin de tamao. Los supervisores debern decidir entre las opciones posibles. Basilea II est enfocado, en sus variantes avanzadas, a los bancos ms sofisticados y con presencia internacional. Tampoco es necesario pasar automticamente a Basilea II en 2006. Los pases emergentes que tengan muy reciente la implantacin de Basilea I pueden posponer el cambio actuando mientras tanto mediante la incorporacin a sus sistemas de elementos de los pilares 2 y 3. Esta flexibilidad y adaptabilidad del Acuerdo (que tiene como consecuencia una mayor complejidad) requiere prestar atencin especial a los problemas de consistencia transfronteriza, en particular, en el caso de bancos multinacionales sometidos a diferentes jurisdicciones. Existe un grupo de trabajo, Grupo para la implantacin del Acuerdo (AIG), que, partiendo del hecho anterior, va a seguir con atencin la implantacin del Acuerdo, proporcionando un espacio en el que se analicen los problemas y se coordinen las respuestas a los mismos. El grado de consistencia debe ser mantenido en base a la tarea de los supervisores. Los supervisores seguirn desarrollando su actividad y sus responsabilidades en el marco sealado por los core principles. La nueva situacin aconseja, no obstante, un refuerzo de los mismos, haciendo nfasis en el intercambio de informacin y coordinacin, as como en la elaboracin de planes prcticos. As, el AIG ha elaborado y publicado seis principios bsicos adicionales, que refuerzan los aspectos comentados: 1) El Acuerdo no cambia las responsabilidades. 2) El supervisor del pas de origen del banco (home supervisor en la jerga de Basilea) es responsable de la aplicacin del Acuerdo en base consolidada. 3) El supervisor del pas de acogida de la entidad (host supervisor), en el caso de filiales, tiene responsabilidades que deben considerarse. 4) Incrementar el esfuerzo de cooperacin, liderado por el home. 5) Evitar las redundancias en la validacin y la aprobacin de los modelos. 6) Comunicacin lo ms clara posible, a las entidades, de los respectivos papeles. Por otra parte, pero en clara vinculacin con lo anterior, el Comit est trabajando en la mayor cooperacin con los supervisores de los pases no pertenecientes al Comit, pues si bien las entidades en las que se centra el nuevo Acuerdo y que, en principio, se veran afectados por la reforma siguen siendo los bancos internacionalmente activos, el Comit espera que el nuevo Acuerdo siga siendo una norma internacional de referencia en materia de solvencia. 8. ASUNTOS MS ESPECFICOS Aparte de estas criticas que afectan al carcter general del Acuerdo, me gustara resaltar algunos temas tcnicos ms especficos que han surgido en el proceso de consulta y que estn siendo en estos momentos objeto de anlisis por los distintos grupos de trabajo implicados en la reforma del Acuerdo. Respecto a la crtica sobre el calibrado del Acuerdo, algunas entidades siguen creyendo que las propuestas actuales no les proporcionan los incentivos apropiados para pasar a los mtodos de clculo ms sofisticados, y otras han mostrado de nuevo su desacuerdo con la solucin de compromiso adoptada en el mtodo IRB de cubrir con capital tanto las prdidas esperadas como las inesperadas y defienden que slo las prdidas inesperadas deberan cubrirse con capital. Tambin se ha planteado el tema del doble impago en las tcnicas de mitigacin de riesgo. En la normas sobre mitigacin de riesgos recogidas en el CP3, un prstamo con una garanta recibe la ponderacin del garante (tratamiento de substitucin). La industria ha considerado dicho tratamiento muy conservador, ya que no tiene en cuenta el hecho de que para que dicho prstamo resulte impagado se debe producir el impago tanto del obligado como del garante de manera simultnea. No obstante, si bien desde un punto de vista terico es clara la reduccin de la probabilidad de impago, su aplicacin prctica se ve dificultada por la no disponibilidad de datos sobre correlaciones entre garantes y obligados. Tambin hay propuestas concretas para modificar el tratamiento del riesgo operacional, del que ya muy pocos discuten que el tratamiento correcto de este riesgo debe darse en el pilar 1, es decir, con exigencias explcitas de capital. Por ltimo destacar los numerosos comentarios de la industria sobre el tratamiento de la titulizacin. En ellos se critica el gran conservadurismo de las propuestas actuales y su gran complejidad y dificultad de interpretacin, lo que ha llevado a proponer una simplificacin en el tratamiento que afectara a varios de los aspectos bsicos del tratamiento de la titulizacin en el nuevo Acuerdo, como es el caso de las ponderaciones del mtodo basado en rating externos (RBA) o la frmula supervisora. Todos estos comentarios realizados por la industria sern analizados y algunos de ellos es muy probable que generen cambios en las propuestas, dado el lgico inters que se tiene por lograr el mejor acuerdo de capitales posible en un perodo de tiempo, que ya debe ser razonablemente corto. Aunque existe la preocupacin de que los plazos estimados para la finalizacin del Acuerdo (finales de este ao) son demasiado estrechos, lo que podra poner en peligro la calidad del Acuerdo, es importante finalizar esta fase de discusiones y de propuestas y abrir el camino a la implementacin efectiva del Acuerdo. Sin embargo, en mi opinin, la credibilidad del nuevo Acuerdo y su xito ciertamente no depende tanto del cumplimiento estricto de unos determinados compromisos en cuanto a fechas, sino que deber medirse teniendo en cuenta las mejoras que haya podido introducir en la gestin interna que las entidades hagan de sus riesgos y por el logro de una mayor fortaleza del sistema financiero mundial que le haga ms resistente a situaciones econmicas de crisis. En conclusin, tenemos delante de nosotros un nuevo Acuerdo de Capitales que ha sido el producto de varios aos de trabajo duro y que, en mi opinin, va a ser muy positivo para mejorar la fortaleza y solidez de las entidades de crdito y del sistema econmico en general. No obstante, conviene recordar que este Acuerdo es slo un paso ms en el intento de acercar lo mximo posible el capital regulatorio a los riesgos realmente asumidos por las entidades. Es importante ser conscientes que hay ciertos temas adicionales que no se ha considerado conveniente incluir en las propuestas actuales pero que sern objeto de estudio en los siguientes pasos que el Comit en su intencin de mejorar progresivamente la normativa de solvencia de las entidades de crdito. Entre estos temas adicionales, se pueden destacar, por ejemplo, la posibilidad de reconocer totalmente los efectos de diversificacin y concentracin de las carteras o la necesidad de buscar la armonizacin de las normas de solvencia con el tratamiento contable de las provisiones. Seguirn dndose pasos adicionales pero no duden que la lnea elegida es la correcta.

Title: Governor's Appearance: Committee on Economy and Finance of the Congress of Deputies, to report on the actions carried out by the Bank of Spain in relation to the entity Eurobank del Mediterrneo S.A.
text: APPEARANCE OF THE GOVERNOR OF THE BANK OF SPAIN IN THE COMMITTEE ON ECONOMY AND FINANCE OF THE CONGRESS OF DEPUTIES Madrid, 17 September 2003 Introduction. To be President, you would be, I would like to begin the hearing by thanking you for the opportunity to explain the actions of Banco de Espa in its functions as banking supervisor in relation to Eurobank del Mediterr87neo, S.A.. First of all, let me stress that our banking system is in excellent health and a high level of solvency. In this context, Eurobank's intervention and the fact that this entity is immersed in a payment suspension procedure represents an occasional, punctual and isolated episode, which has neither affected nor endangered the stability of our banking system. Eurobank's intervention has occurred in time, after impeccable inspection work, with respect to current legislation and trying to mitigate the possible risks for depositors of that entity. The decisive intervention of the Bank of Spain, through various measures that ended in the intervention of the entity on July 25, has stopped, a few months after its inception and detection, a practice that grew at a dizzying pace and that if it had not intervened in time, would have resulted in enormous damage to the clients of that entity. Eurobank, is a small credit institution that comes from the transformation into a bank of the former Caja Hipotecaria S.A.. Sociedad de Cr8edito Hipotecario, in 1989, and which has been controlled since 1996 by the group of who until recently was its president. It is important to note that since 1996, Eurobank has been experiencing regulatory difficulties and has been closely monitored by supervisor. The type of difficulties experienced by the entity, allows to distinguish clearly different stages, being precisely in the last of them, which begins at the end of 2002, when the difficulties in capitalizing the bank are manifested, and the entity embarks on the realization of a series of activities that are those that aggravate its risk profile and that will lead to the intervention of last July. In this last stage, Eurobank begins to market among its customers a series of products under the combined name of "growing investment", which by their nature and characteristics fall within the category of insurance products known as Unit Linked. I would like to emphasize that this category of products called Unit Linked, are frequently marketed, both in our financial environment and in other financial systems. The differential fact, in this case, has been given by the way in which those products were marketed among Eurobank's depositor customers, and in particular, the lack of transparency about the type of product marketed. The supervision detects in the manner and circumstances in which the commercialization of the products of 'growing investment' by Eurobank took place, there were irregularities and circumstances that justified, among other reasons and after the appropriate requirements made to the entity, the adoption of sanctioning and precautionary measures. Before reviewing the last stage of Eurobank's evolution, I would also like to stress that given the characteristics of the bank's operations in this period, it has been necessary to maintain close cooperation with other financial supervisors, national and foreign. This collaboration was made public in the statement of the Bank of Spain, immediately after the intervention, in which it was stated that the intervention was agreed prior to '... coordination with the supervisory authorities and in particular with the Generalitat de Catalu and its Directorate General of Insurance.' Last stage of Eurobank's evolution. Eurobank has been the subject of concern for the supervisor from an early stage. For six years, this entity has been the subject of special monitoring by the supervisory units. I shall shortly refer in detail to what these actions have been. But it is in the analysis of the evolution of the bank at this stage where the key is found to explain the measures adopted and the present situation of the entity. Let me refer to this latest evolution of Eurobank successively and as succinctly as possible. It is my duty to anticipate that the complexity of the operations carried out by Eurobank, makes it necessary to summarize and simplify the analysis of the facts and the actions carried out by the supervisor, whose most technical and precise description, in some cases still subject to evaluation, is found in the documentation of the inspection and in the one sent to the judge. The next stage, which is the key and foundation of the supervisory actions recently carried out by the Bank of Spain, starts at the end of last year. Previously, the entity had been the subject of a reprimand, published in November 2002 and agreed by the Banco de Espa as a result of the disciplinary proceedings initiated on 26 May 2000. At the end of 2002, Eurobank had been showing insufficient equity and began to market highly profitable deposits, which in many cases were reinvested in products called 'increasing investment'. As regards the insufficiency of own resources, the Banco de Espa, as soon as it received the entity's financial statements for 31 December 2002, immediately began an inspection visit in February 2003 which concluded with significant capital adjustments that reduced its own resources to 12 million. I want to emphasize the importance of this data, because it implied that the entity had remained more than six months with own resources below the legal minimum, set at 18 million euros by Royal Decree 1245/1995, of July 14, which is considered a very serious offense by the law of discipline and intervention of credit institutions. The situation of insufficient own resources has not been remedied by the entity and has persisted until now. As a result of the inspection of the entity, the Banco de Espa agreed to disciplinary proceedings against the entity, its administrators and general manager, in May 2003. At the same time, the board of directors of the entity, responsible for its management, was requested to adopt a series of measures aimed at: a) modify your income statement (recording a number of unaccounted adjustments); b) capitalize the entity, so that it has own resources of not less than the 18 million established by the regulations; and that c) provide certain information, repeatedly requested by the inspection services and, until then, not provided. In addition to the above, on February 21 and April 30, disciplinary proceedings were agreed against the president of Eurobank, several of its subsidiaries and collaborators and the entity itself, for carrying out certain operations on Eurobank shares without previously informing Banco de Espa, or for carrying them out in a manner other than that reported. Among the companies issued was Excell Life International S.A., a Luxembourg insurance company, controlled by the Chairman of Eurobank. On the same day, April 30, Banco de Espa opposed Excell increasing its 14.99% stake in Eurobank's capital, due to lack of suitability. With regard to the marketing of products, during the inspection visit, Banco de Espa learned that, in the weeks of 2002, the Bank had marketed 'Growing Investment' products in the form of Unit-Linked, products outside the bank's balance sheet, where the risk of investment is assumed by the subscriber of the product. These products had been issued by mutual societies of autonomous operational scope, which ensure the payment of the agreed interest and a risk of death. The management of the mutual societies was influenced by the dominant shareholding group. The insurance product marketed as "growing investment" involved the placement among customers of financial assets of various kinds, including those issued by the Luxembourg company EXCELL, controlled by the president of Eurobank. I must insist on the normal and regular nature of these Unit linked products in general and on the fact that only in the subsequent investigation, when analyzing the conditions of marketing, evidence of breach of the duty of transparency of information with the clientele among which said product was placed was found. As soon as the Bank of Spain became aware of this, during the inspection that had begun in February 2003, it requested the Entity on 21 March 2003 to cease marketing until it was guaranteed by the entity that customers had sufficient information on the nature of the product and the economic and patrimonial characteristics of the issuer of the investment. Specifically, the entity is required: A) The inclusion in the documentation initially provided to the client in the new operations, as well as in the contract or page that he must necessarily subscribe, of clauses that inform about (1) the nature of the investment and emphasise that this product does not constitute a bank deposit in Eurobank; (2)the absence of additional commitments or guarantees by Eurobank; (3)the nature of Excell Life Internacional SA as a Luxembourg company majority controlled by the Chairman of Eurobank, 4)equity and financial information of Excell and its group. (In case of being placed in financial assets issued by other companies, alternative wordings to these clauses would be proposed). B) For those customers who had already subscribed to these products, it was required that the aforementioned information be sent in a personalized way and with acknowledgment of receipt. C) Finally, Eurobank was required to establish a register, ico in the bank, in which under sequential numbering, these operations were registered. This requirement was reiterated on May 6. Finally, on July 14 it was known that despite the statements of the directors of the entity that the requirement of the Bank of Spain was being fulfilled, the commercialization of these products had continued without complying with the aforementioned transparency requirements. As a result of all the above, on July 15, 2003, the inspection of the Entity began, whose actions continue and have coincided with the work of the intervention agreed on July 25. Situation of the entity On July 25, the Executive Committee of the Bank of Spain, in view of the seriousness of the situation existing in Eurobank del Mediterr87neo detected by the successive inspections carried out, and decisively in the one initiated at the beginning of a on financial statements on December 31, 2002, as well as the request received from the representative of the majority of the share capital, acordsu intervenci, designating for the appropriate purposes the corresponding auditors, one of whom was proposed by the Generalitat de Catalu. The intervention was agreed under the provisions of Articles 31 and 32 of Law 26/1988, of 29 July, on discipline and intervention of credit institutions. Those articles state that the intervention of a credit institution may be carried out when it is in a situation of exceptional gravity which jeopardizes the effectiveness of its own resources or its stability, liquidity or solvency, provided that, in such a situation, the institution itself may request the measure. Concurrently with the process of adopting the decision to impose an exceptional precautionary measure on Eurobank, the majority of the capital of the informal entity Banco de Espa of its owner that Eurobank renounce its authorization to continue exercising the banking activity and assumes, in writing, the irrevocable commitment of said majority of the capital to vote, in favor of the necessary measures for this in the mandatory General Meeting of Shareholders, also requesting the replacement of the directors or the intervention of the Entity by the Bank of Spain. Considering the concurrent extremes, and after an assessment of the situation of the entity, the Bank of Spain agrees to intervene in the bank without replacing the administrators. This measure maintains the exercise and responsibility of management in the statutory bodies of the Entity, but obliges them to submit their decisions to the auditors, who do not have active management capacity, but can veto the acts that the managers intend to carry out if it is considered that they may harm the entity itself or its depositors. In short, the Bank of Spain considers the intervention measure appropriate and proportionate because the situation in which Eurobank found itself in the second quarter of this year had no comparison with that of previous quarters, which could be described as what in financial jargon is known as the flight forward. I would like to highlight the five main elements that will help to shape the decision to adopt, in particular, the intervention measure. A) the opacity of information that the dominant shareholding group showed timately, B) the significant marketing of 'growing investment' products among its customers without adequate transparency for the subscriber C) the diversion of resources to Excell, a company that is outside the scope of Spanish supervision. D) the persistent lack of own resources and the minimum capital deficit to operate as a credit institution. At 31 December 2002, Eurobank had positive accounting own resources, but following the adjustments made by the inspectorate, it became clear that these were actually well below those required by the law in force to operate as a credit institution. Eurobank thus saw the situation presented in previous years, in which capitalization needs were covered by capital increases, worsen. But where a situation as serious as the one had not been presented, both from the patrimonial point of view and the financing and investment structure of the dominant or majority group. E) the announcement of renunciation of the banking license and of initiating the orderly liquidation of the entity. On July 24, the Chairman and controlling shareholder of Eurobank addressed Banco de Espa expressly indicating his irrevocable will to renounce the banking license and liquidate the entity in an orderly manner, requesting the adoption of one of the precautionary measures referred to above. That announcement was obviously nothing more than a clear confirmation of the situation of weakness that Eurobank was going through, which made the adoption of precautionary measures inevitable. On the other hand, the irrevocable decision to liquidate the bank in an orderly manner announced by the person who controls this scam, advises to rule out the replacement of administrators to opt for the intervention measure, as an ideal means to guarantee strict control of the liquidation operations that the entity intended to undertake. As is known, the controlling shareholder failed a month later to comply with the announcement made to the supervisor, by not supporting at the Meeting convened for that purpose on August 25 its own liquidation proposal. On that date, however, the corresponding request for suspension of payments was requested, which would be admitted for processing one day later, on August 26, with which the administration of the entity would be under the tutelage of the competent judicial authority. At the date of the intervention, Eurobank del Mediterr87neo, S.A., had total assets of 240 million euros and customer losses of 209 million, liquid assets of 128 million, 4 offices, 55 employees. It had adjusted accounting own resources, at 31 December 2002, of EUR 12 million which, although lower than the EUR 18 million required by the regulations in force (Royal Decree 1245/1995, of 14 July) to carry out the banking activity, could be sufficient to absorb any losses that could be generated in the orderly liquidation of the assets and thus be able to satisfy the receivables recorded in its balance sheet, provided that the occurrence of contingent liabilities not accounted for by the Entity, or unforeseen impairments in assets, does not prevent it. On the evening of the same day, July 25, the Banco de Espa summons the Chairman of the Board of Directors of the bank and its General Manager, to personally notify them of the intervention agreement as well as the reasons for it. On Monday, July 28, before the start of operations, the bank's administrators already had a communication from the appointed auditors, in which they were instructed on the operational procedures to be followed during the intervention and in which they were informed of the obligation to attend, without excuse or delay, to the request for the return of the complaints in sight, and even to the advance payment of the installment payments, provided that the clauses of the contracts of the same contemplated this possibility in favor of the depositor. On the same day, July 28, the first day of the intervention, the Banco de Espa established a wide range of devices to respond to requests for information that may occur through the Banco de Espa telefica headquarters in Madrid. On 8 August 2003, the Supervisory Services requested greater diligence from the Entity in the provision by the Entity of its television and Internet banking services, in view of complaints received from numerous Eurobank customers who had difficulties in contacting their bank. On 13 August 2003, the financial controllers wrote to the President of the bank instructing them to inform the Board of Directors of the urgent communication to the Board of Directors, upon learning of the existence of transfer notices received by the depositors' bank which had not been processed, requesting him to do so immediately. Likewise, in said letter the Entity was obliged to undo all automatic renewals of the term depitos, made from the date of the intervention, which did not have written authorization from the holders thereof. On 14 August 2003, the Board of Directors of Eurobank filed an application for a declaration of suspension of payments in the Courts of Madrid, which was admitted for processing by the Judicial Authority on 26 August 2003 and ratified by the General Shareholders' Meeting on 15 September. therefore, the judicial protection of the Entity, established by the law of suspension of payments of 1922, is effective. In the period between the date of the Bank's intervention, July 25, 2003 until the closing of the windows decided by the Board of Directors on August 18, following the filing of a demand for a declaration in suspension of payments, there was a withdrawal of customer deposits for approximately 73 million euros. This withdrawal has reduced such losses and total assets to db136 million and db157 million, respectively, and liquid assets to db59 million. On August 20, 2003, two days after the situation of non-payment of monetary deposits by the Entity, decided by the managers of the same on the 18th of that month, and pending the application for suspension of payments in court, the Executive Committee of Banco de Espa adopted the agreement provided for in article 8.1.c. of Royal Decree 2606/1996, of 20 December, in order for the Guarantee Fund for Depitos in Credit Establishments to pay the amounts guaranteed by it, 20,000 euros per cash depositor, since Eurobank was unable to return the monetary deposits to their holders in the immediate future. According to the latest estimates, of the 12,800 customers who currently maintain depitos in the Entity, 85% of them will be fully covered by this guarantee. I would also like to inform you that the Depitos Guarantee Fund has already started sending letters to depositors and starting to pay the guaranteed amounts. On 3 September 2003, the Executive Committee of the Banco de Espa, taking into account the important facts detected by the Supervisory Services of the Bank of Spain in the initial inspection of the Entity, which began on 15 July 2003, coinciding with the intervention work since 25 July, 2003, and reflected in the minutes of July 24 and September 2, to agree disciplinary proceedings against Mr. Eduardo Pascual Arx8e, Chairman of the Board of Directors of Eurobank del Mediterr87neo, S.A., and the Eurobank entity itself, provisionally suspending said being as administrator of the Entity; likewise, to transfer the facts now known to the competent Judicial Authority in the process of suspension of payments of Eurobank, and to inform said authority of the previous agreements. Among the important facts detected by the ongoing inspection, the breaches of requirements made by the Bank of Spain to preserve information transparency before customers in marketing operations of "growing investment" products stand out; the lack of accounting records of certain bonding operations; the forgiveness of guarantees received in favour of Eurobank and other irregularities related to the disposal of funds and sales of real estate assets. The Bank of Spain has required Eurobank to increase its own resources through an increase in its share capital of 6.5 million euros, in order to place these above the minimum 18 million to operate as a bank. None of the current shareholders has attended the subscription of the capital increase in exercise of their right of preferential subscription, whose deadline expires on September 8. At present, a period is open for interested third parties to subscribe to this extension, without the Bank of Spain having so far received any formal request from an investor, so that this Agency can study and process the necessary prior authorization that requires any acquisition of a significant participation in Eurobank. Background and previous actions. Mr. Eduardo Pascual is, since March 1996, the first shareholder of Eurobank del Mediterr87neo, S.A., and since June of that same year he heads the group that controlled said Entity, holding his Presidency from September 1999 until September 3, date on which he was provisionally suspended as a director by agreement of the Executive Committee of Banco de Espa. Mr Pascual is the direct owner of 33.9% of the capital and majority shareholder of a Luxembourg insurance company, in turn the holder of 14.9% of Eurobank. In addition, another 12.2% is owned by three mutual insurance companies, whose management has been influenced very significantly by Mr. Pascual. The rest of the capital is very diversified. Since 1996, Eurobank has been the subject of treatment in 29 sessions of the Executive Committee, with a high number of resolutions, sixty-eight, binding on the entity. These decisions are not made by imperative of the provisions of article 6 of Royal Legislative Decree 1298/1986 of June 28, as they are affected by the professional secrecy imposed on the supervisor. In addition, 9 "in situ" inspections have been carried out, plus another one initiated on July 15 not yet concluded. The most relevant aspects detected in each of them were the following: 1st Inspection, carried out to the Entity on situation at March 31, 1996, coinciding with the entry of Mr. Pascual in the shareholding of the bank, concluded with equity adjustments for 1.8 million euros, coming to place the real profits of the Entity very close to zero. In addition, at that time, the Entity had computable own resources of 13.7 million euros, lower than the 18 necessary. Therefore, in accordance with the first transitional provision of Royal Decree 1245/1995, of July 14, the existence of new partners determines the requirement to place such resources in an amount not less than the aforementioned limit of 18 million euros, necessary to exercise banking activity according to article 2.b. of the aforementioned Royal Decree, the Banco de Espa selal Board of Directors of the Entity, already controlled by the new shareholders, in a letter of 26 July 1996 and reiterated by another of 20 December 1996. After successive disbursements by the shareholders, the amount of the aforementioned 18 million euros was reached. 2nd Inspection. The first inspection visit following the abovementioned takeover, carried out at the beginning of 1997, on the financial statements of 31 December 1996, found that there was a concentration of risks with a certain group equivalent to 40.3% of own resources, which exceeded the legal maximum then fixed at 40% of those resources. The same inspection showed that the Entity was financing the entire cost of a real estate project managed by the group linked to the new dominant shareholders, this risk being the second in importance after the aforementioned concentration, with which Eurobank del Mediterr87neo assumed all the business risk inherent in that project. By letter of 7 March 1997, Banco de Espa set up the Board of Directors of the Entity to reconsider its actions, to return to the sound principle of risk diversification and to distinguish the interests of the Entity from those of the group linked to the new dominant shareholders. 3rd Inspection, on the situation at 31 March 1997, showed that the Bank's main activity had become the implementation of certain operations related to staff regulation processes, basically consisting of long-term depositions, in the name of different holders, and of credits with a long calendar of provisions, in the name of other holders, that was expected to be canceled at maturity, affecting the first collateral. In those operations, which corresponded to a certain activity carried out by the group linked to Mr Pascual, numerous and important defects of formalization were detected, with potential economic repercussions for the Bank. For this reason, Banco de Espa issued a communication on 15 October 1997, by which, in addition to requiring the correction of certain perceived deficits in its hedge funds and other deficiencies, the Board of Directors of the Entity was warned that its activity could not be instrumental auxiliary to that of the group linked to the dominant shareholders 4th Inspection, on the situation as of June 30, 1998, showed that the aforementioned operations already accounted for 60% of customer losses and that the same anomalies and consequent possible contingencies for the Entity, which were used during the previous visit, continued to occur. In addition, a coverage deficit of EUR 3 million is estimated. In this same inspection it was detected that most of the disbursement of the shares subscribed by Mr. Eduardo Pascual in the capital increase through which he had acquired his participation in the Entity, approved in 1995 to be carried out in cash and in several passive dividends, had been carried out with funds obtained shortly before from the Bank itself, in the sale to him of different properties. Additionally, regardless of other extremes, the inspection detected a concentration of risks with a certain business group equivalent to 56.6% of the equity declared by the Entity, which exceeded the legal maximum of 40%. On March 16, 1999, Banco de Espa sent a letter to the Entity assessing the seriousness of the facts detected, formulating the appropriate requirements and warning about the worrying situation of the Entity so that its Board of Directors could evaluate its future viability, an analysis in which the safeguarding of customer deposits should be especially taken into account. 5th Inspection, on the situation as of September 30, 1999, with the objective of verifying compliance with the requirements previously formulated. Although in this inspection visit it was possible to verify the observance of some of the requirements made previously, it is observed, among other anomalies, a strong increase in credit activity with companies and doubtful risks, concluding the need for equity adjustments of 12.4 million euros; The existence of a concentration of risks was detected with two mutual societies of social provision, whose management was decisively influenced by the group linked to the President of the Bank. All this determines the opening of disciplinary proceedings against the Entity, Administrators and General Manager, by agreement of the Bank of Spain of May 26, 2000, regardless of the processing of different requirements urging the correction of the aforementioned irregularities. As already mentioned, this case was resolved in November 2001 with the maximum penalties provided for by the Law on Discipline and Intervention of Credit Institutions for the facts detected. 6th Inspection, on the situation at 31 December 2000, showed high growth in consumer credit and factoring operations, managed under conditions that had triggered the claims of the loan, concluding equity adjustments of 3.7 million euros. It also detects the high concentration of customer deposits, of which 49% corresponded to mutual societies whose management was decisively influenced by the group linked to the President of the bank, and the beginning of an aggressive campaign to capture deposits through high profitability accounts. On July 6, 2001, the Bank of Spain sent a communication to the Entity requesting the regularization of the anomalies detected, as well as the assurance of liquidity, and transferring to the Board of Directors the concern about its situation. The subsequent monitoring of the Entity showed rapid growth in deposits through high-remuneration accounts and consumer loans at high interest rates, so that, on November 16, 2001, the Bank of Spain issued a letter urging them to reconsider the policy of assets and liabilities developed. 7th Inspection, on the situation at 30 September 2001, concluded equity adjustments of EUR 2.3 million and also found that the actual shortcoming observed in transactions with consumer credit defaults was much higher than the level of coverage that the Entity had been applying, equivalent to the regulatory minimum, so that it had to assess precisely whether that shortcoming in order to assess such coverage. On 11 April 2002, Banco de Espa sent a communication to Eurobank requesting the correction of the deficiencies detected which, with regard to the restructuring of the capital adjustments specified in this seventh inspection, the Entity had ignored in its annual accounts for the year 2001, reason for which rectification of those annual accounts is required to incorporate said reorganization. 8th Inspection, on statements of 30 June 2002, concluded equity adjustments of 3.5 million euros and other infringements, among which the existence of a significant real estate investment, in which the Entity assumed all the inherent risk, in the form of mortgage loans in favour of several owners. The Bank of Spain, on October 18, 2002, sent a letter to the Entity with requirements urging the regularization of such extremes, as well as the reconsideration of the policy of assets and liabilities followed. On the other hand, on December 26, 2002, the informal entity Banco de Espa began an activity of purchase of plots and development of real estate developments on them, which would be carried out with the collaboration of third parties, but whose business risk would fall on the Entity. The Bank of Spain, after analyzing the information received, on February 21, 2003 issued a communication warning that such investments did not correspond to its policy of collecting losses, based on high-remunerative accounts, presumably very volatile, and reiterating reconsider the policy of assets and liabilities followed. 9bb Inspection and completed scam, which, as I have already mentioned, referred to statements of 31 December 2002, concluded with equity adjustments of 5.4 million euros that reduced its own resources to 12 million, thus resulting in the Entity has remained six months with own resources below the legal minimum to obtain authorization as a bank, set at EUR 18 million. In addition, in that inspection it was learned that the entity had begun to market to its customers, in the weeks of 2002, insurance products issued by mutual societies operating in an autonomous area, whose management was influenced by the President, which involved the placement among customers of bonds issued by a Luxembourg insurance company controlled by Mr Pascual, with evidence that the duty of transparency of information with customers had been breached. As you know, those extremes led to the opening of disciplinary proceedings against the Entity, Administrators and General Manager on May 9, 2003, the date on which the Bank of Spain also required the regularization of the capital adjustments, correcting for that purpose the annual accounts provisionally approved, and compliance with the level of own resources legally required. In addition, as I have already indicated, on 21 March 2003, before the end of the inspection, Banco de Espa urged the Bank to suspend the marketing of insurance products of the type referred to, until it adopted certain transparency measures on the nature of the product and the economic and patrimonial situation of the issuer. Finally, Inspection 10 is the inspection initiated on 15 July on which I have already reported. This description of the inspections allows, on the one hand, to show the various stages in terms of the activity through which the entity has passed and also how the supervisory action has allowed to send the appropriate recommendations and requirements to the Entity to correct the deficiencies detected, corrections that have been subject to subsequent verification. Thanks to the supervisory action: inspections, requirements and their subsequent verification, situations and practices that posed a risk to the entity and depositors have been corrected. To summarize, the Bank of Spain: -In the first place, it has forced the Entity to establish provisions of very high amounts necessary for different coverage of losses detected in different assets, reaching, in the scams exercises, to urge the Entity to reformulate the previously published income statement and, in this way, surface undeclared losses or increase those recorded. Thus, the losses of 1.8 million euros declared by Eurobank at the end of 2001, were raised by the supervision to 4.1 million, and in 2002 losses initially declared were passed from 3.2 million to a negative result of 8.5 million. With these corrections, the Bank of Spain has required that the Entity's plicos financial statements reflect, at all times, the true image of its economic and patrimonial situation. -Secondly, Banco de Espa has repeatedly required increases in equity (nine times since 1996), as a result of which Eurobank has been forced to carry out successive capital increases that have meant that, in the four cases, shareholders have contributed more than 15 million euros. -Thirdly, Banco de Espa has urged the Entity to abandon certain operations due to the contingencies involved for it, to cancel risk concentrations, not to undertake investment projects inappropriate for the Entity or to keep certain precautions and not to market certain types of products. In my opinion, in each case, compliance with the request has most likely prevented unwanted situations or reduced situations of undue risk; specifically, the high degree of liquidity that the Entity had when it was intervened d0 which has been cited above d0 responds to such requirements. -Fourthly, Banco de Espa has issued a letter to the Bank and its administrators on four occasions: first, as a result of the inspection carried out at the end of 1999, the following two, as a result of the visit on financial statements at the end of 2002 and on the monitoring carried out on the entity; and the scam, for the inspection not yet completed, started on July 15. Thus, in May 2000, proceedings were initiated against the Entity and its directors for acts relating, inter alia, to the actions of the Entity, its credit investment or its patrimonial situation, a file that ended with the imposition of fines and warnings to the Entity and several fines to the President and other administrators of the same; In February 2003, a file was initiated for movements in its shareholding without the required authorization; in May 2003, a case for various financial adjustments and other matters concerning lack of transparency with customers; and, the scam, of September 3, for facts now known as a result of the visit in progress, transferring them to the competent Judicial Authority in the process of suspension of payments. Within the framework of the principle of coordination that governs the relations of the Bank of Spain with other supervisory bodies, its supervisory services have been informing them of the relevant facts that could affect them as they became known for their inspection work. The fines imposed on the Entity and its President for the commission of very serious infractions were the maximum provided for in the applicable regulations for the infringements detected. On the other hand, the imposition of the sanctions of warning to the Entity acquires a special importance, given that it is a measure that aims to correct the actions of the Entity through a sanci that is known by the markets and customers. The file from May to 2000 ends in November 2001, after having extended, at the request of the files, the deadlines for its processing. The sanctions were implemented immediately, although some of them, in particular the sanctions of warning, were not published in the Official State Gazette until November 2002, as a result of the various appeals lodged by the proceedings before the Audiencia Nacional. With regard to the other three proceedings initiated against the Entity in 2003, one of them followed against the Entity and its administrators, the other against the Entity and some of its most significant shareholders and, finally, as already indicated, that of September 3 against the Entity and Mr. Eduardo Pascual Arx8e, which is provisionally suspended from its status as Director and President of the Entity, are currently in the processing phase, given the marked guarantee nature of these sanctioning procedures, which, as can not be less, allow the presentation of allegations by the interested parties in different procedures. In this sense, emphasize that the processes of inspection and, where appropriate, servicing a financial institution, require deadlines that are determined by strict compliance with the Spanish regulatory framework of banking supervision, emanating in a large part of the community directives. The supervisor does not have to guarantee the legitimate right of defence of the parties concerned, but must ensure the maximum solidity of the procedure, which implies supporting with the utmost documentary rigor each of its actions, even at the cost of the desire for speed. Fifthly, from 1996, when the current dominant shareholding group took control of Eurobank del Mediterr87neo until 2002, the Bank's economic trajectory has been characterised, on the one hand, by the inability to generate ordinary income to compensate for the increasing structural costs, so that the operating margin obtained has been recurrently negative; and on the other, by the growing needs for write-downs, which in large part the managers have registered after their relevance in successive inspections of the Bank of Spain became clear. Both effects have determined the recording of losses, more significant in the scams, and especially at the end of 2002, as the Entity increases the volume of its operations. However, the effect of this economic deterioration was covered by shareholders contributing new equity, thanks to the disbursement of passive dividends or the subscription of new capital increases. We have witnessed, therefore, a reality of losses covered by the determination and will of the shareholders. In general, in a free market environment, if the owners trust their project and want to continue carrying it out, they cannot find objections or restrictions on the part of the supervisor, provided that their action does not collide with the applicable regulations and there are no faults, objective situations, included in the Law on discipline and intervention of credit institutions. Sixthly, the supervisory presidency of Banco de Espa has been constant, especially relevant in the current year due to the seriousness of the facts known in its first semester, and has resulted throughout these scams as, frequent actions, requirements or initiation of files in order to: - The patrimonial situation required by law will be reinforced, which has been fulfilled with the exception of the timo requirement on the situation of the Entity at December 31, 2002. - The annual accounts shall be redrawn in view of the lack of accounting in the profit and loss account of the adjustments detected during inspection visits, mainly due to the need to establish provisions to cover credit risk. - Certain credit investment policies were abandoned due to the contingencies they implied for Eurobank, characterised by concentrations of risks or high credit risk. - An adequate financial balance was maintained between the peculiarities of the deposits taken by the bank (in the very short term and at high cost, therefore, very volatile) and the investments made in order to preserve the liquidity of the Entity, actions that have placed its liquidity at very high levels. -And, finally, the necessary transparency of information in the marketing of products among its customers will be respected. I reiterate that compliance with the request has avoided, at least, undesirable situations and, in any case, has reduced scenarios of disproportionate risk. In fact, Eurobank del Mediterr87neo had high liquidity and positive accounting equity at the time of the intervention, provided that there are no contingent liabilities not accounted for by the Entity. It is noteworthy that the greatest intensity of the supervisor's action has occurred in the current year, when the situation of the bank worsens, since of the four files initiated against the Entity and administrators, three have been initiated in 2003. Final thoughts.- I wanted to tell you about the supervisory actions of the Banco de Espa in relation to Eurobank since 1996 so that you have a precise knowledge of our proceed, which I hope has been able to clarify to Your Ser92as, the scope and meaning of the measures adopted by the Bank of Spain. From his report, the increase in the frequency of supervisory actions and the severity of the disciplinary measures adopted by Banco de Espa are perceptible, which are directly related, as it cannot be otherwise, with the rate of aggravation of the bank's supervisory risk profile, as the facts were detected and the economic and patrimonial evolution of the entity were known. In short, if in the early stages of the bank the difficulty of finding an adequate business model that provides recurrence to income and sufficient solvency margin is manifested, it is in the tima stage of the Eurobank bank, in this to 2003, in which the risk factors that I explained in my intervention that make action necessary, that the norm itself qualifies as exceptional, the intervention. The response times are marked by the procedures themselves and by the need to act on the basis of contrasted elements, once the facts have occurred. Any application of exceptional measure of the Bank of Spain must be scrupulously respectful of the letter of the Law, without it being possible to apply anticipated actions not foreseen in it, since the Plica Administration, by imperative of the principle of legality, can only do what the Law allows it, This determines that, outside of measures of general financial policy, and the practice of prudential requirements, Banco de Espa cannot "anticipate" precautionary measures if the factual assumption provided for in the standard has not occurred, even if there are indications that the alleged event may occur in the future. The entire process described above reflects the operating framework of the supervisory mechanisms of Banco de Espa, whose main objective is to safeguard the stability of the Spanish Financial System, monitoring the solvency and performance of credit institutions, which means, in short, the defense of their depositors. It is recognized that the regulatory and supervisory framework of Spanish banking is very rigorous, in which the minimum requirements of own resources required by our regulations are notoriously higher than those established in the Community directives; The provisioning obligations, against the income statement, of the entities are more demanding than those established in other countries of our environment; and supervision procedures are very intense, with the characteristic of frequent "in situ" contrast inspection visits. All this contributes to the fact that our financial system currently enjoys very high solvency (with a BIS ratio of 12.4% over the minimum 8%); high profitability (ROE of 14.1%) and great efficiency, as evidenced by the fact that operating expenses account for only 58% of the ordinary margin obtained in banking activity. But unfortunately, and the Bank of Spain is the first to feel it, this does not mean that it is always possible to avoid totally and at all times the consequences of the existence of poorly managed or inefficient entities -in which case the market discipline itself must act-, but that the Bank of Spain must try to minimize the probability and effects of that eventual crisis of a bank. In this sense, they have been able to verify, with the detailed account set out above, that the supervisory actions and the requirements made by the Bank of Spain have decisively mitigated the negative effects of Eurobank's situation, since it is obliged to recapitalize repeatedly, for the administrators to change their management and investment policy towards more solvent and very liquid assets, considerably raising the level of liquidity with which the bank has tended to operate, and above all to rectify public financial statements, making losses appear or considerably raising those previously published, so that these reflect the true image of its economic equity situation, and could be known by its clientele, by the market and by the public in general. In addition to the efforts made to ensure that the faithful image of the entity's economic situation was a plea, the Bank of Spain agreed to publicize the situation imposed on Eurobank and the persons who held positions of administration and direction of the Entity for the commission of serious infringements. That publicity was made in the Official State Gazette of 6 November 2002, once the disciplinary proceedings initiated by the Banco de Espa in May 2000 had become final through administrative channels. In addition, Eurobank is a very small credit institution within our Spanish financial system that, although it has had problems in compliance with prudential regulations, at no time has it involved any systemic risk and whose potential exit from the system should not diminish confidence in it. In advanced financial systems like ours, the legal framework of guarantees to depositors is based on the existence of Deposit Guarantee Funds similar to ours. Allow me to quote a judgment of the National High Court regarding the scam crisis of a bank, prior to this one, in which it is stressed that "the bad management of a banking entity has its direct cause in the decisions of its administrators; The risk of bad management exists and it is about amortization, creating a guarantee fund for this purpose. But this is an inevitable risk." The existence of a solvent, profitable and efficient Financial System, as is currently the ESPAL, does not eliminate the possibility that, despite the efforts of the Supervisor, some entity may enter into crisis. To minimize the destabilizing effects that individual crises may cause, the 1977 Guarantee Fund for Deposits in Credit Establishments was created, which currently guarantees, up to 20,000 euros, to each of the depositors of any Spanish credit institution. To think that the existence of a supervisor, however effective it may be, can, in all cases, prevent the crisis of a financial institution due to inadequate management policies or irregular actions, does not conform to the reality or the objectives of the supervisors of the countries of our environment where the market economy operates. As for the future that foreseeably awaits Eurobank depositors of the Mediterranean, indicate that after receiving shortly the 20,000 euros contemplated by current regulations, those (around 2,000 depositors) whose balance exceeds the aforementioned amount, will become part, together with the Depitos Guarantee Fund, of the group of creditors of the Entity, for the amount not paid by it, pending the corresponding realization of assets or as a result of what is appropriate, where appropriate, in the agreement agreed in the process of suspension of payments. The Depitos Guarantee Fund has sent letters to 10,500 holders, leaving to send just over 2,000 to holders with depitos less than 6 euros and as of yesterday, payments have been made to 2,842 customers for a total of 13 million euros. Also indicate again that, except for the appearance of contingencies not recorded in the balance sheet of the bank by its administrators, the net accounting assets declared by it could be sufficient to absorb possible losses of value in the realization of its assets and thus be able to meet the return of the deposits that are currently recorded in the bank's balance sheet. But I insist again that the total satisfaction of its losses by the bank will depend on the fact that no liabilities or contingencies now appear not recorded in the accounts. A little thought before concluding, although, as I have indicated, the size and situation of Eurobank has not at any time raised a situation of risk for the financial system, it has presented some aspects in terms of its complexity that deserve reflection. The operations carried out by the bank in terms of product marketing confirm the growing complexity of financial supervision as a result of the sophistication of financial and insurance products, the existence of various sectoral legislations and jurisdictions in different countries. The response to such international and multisectoral situations is adequate supervisory coordination and greater transparency. Banco de Espa has promoted collaboration and coordination with other financial supervisors throughout its actions and our assessment of it is positive and has allowed an early response. To conclude my intervention, I would like to reiterate that the Institution I represent has detected the situation early, has acted diligently and has promptly addressed the rapid deterioration of the entity in its last phase, complying in its actions with its legal mandate and the current legal system and thus contributing decisively to the stability of the Spanish Financial System. the protection of depositors, and encouraging cooperation with other sectoral financial supervisors as necessary. These are the points I wanted to make in my speech and I remain at your disposal to answer any questions you may wish to ask me.

Ser Presidente, Seras, Quiero empezar la comparecencia agradecindoles la oportunidad que me brindan para explicar la actuaci del Banco de Espa en sus funciones de supervisor bancario en relaci con Eurobank del Mediterrneo, S.A.. Ante todo, permtanme subrayar que nuestro sistema bancario goza de una inmejorable salud y de un elevado nivel de solvencia. Dentro de ese contexto, la intervenci de Eurobank y el hecho de que dicha entidad se encuentre inmersa en un procedimiento de suspensi de pagos, supone un episodio ocasional, puntual y aislado, que ni ha afectado, ni ha puesto en peligro la estabilidad de nuestro sistema bancario. La intervenci de Eurobank se ha producido en tiempo, tras una labor inspectora impecable, con respeto a la legalidad vigente y tratando de mitigar los posibles riesgos para los depositantes de dicha entidad. La decisiva intervenci del Banco de Espa, mediante diversas medidas que terminaron en la intervenci de la entidad el pasado 25 de julio, ha atajado, a los pocos meses de su inicio y detecci, una practica que creca a un ritmo vertiginoso y que de no haber intervenido a tiempo, se hubiera traducido en enormes perjuicios para los clientes de dicha entidad. Eurobank, es una peque entidad de crdito que proviene de la transformaci en banco de la antigua Caja Hipotecaria S.A.. Sociedad de Crdito Hipotecario, en 1989, y que ha estado controlada desde 1996 por el grupo de quin hasta hace poco era su presidente. Es importante destacar que desde 1996, Eurobank ha venido presentando dificultades regulatorias siendo objeto de estrecho seguimiento supervisor. El tipo de dificultades atravesadas por la entidad, permite distinguir ntidamente diversas etapas, siendo precisamente en la ltima de ellas, que comienza a finales de 2002, cuando se manifiestan las dificultades en capitalizar el banco, y la entidad se embarca en la realizaci de una serie de actividades que son las que agravan su perfil de riesgo y que abocarn en la intervenci del pasado mes de julio. En esta ltima etapa, Eurobank comienza a comercializar entre su clientela una serie de productos bajo la denominaci pliza combinada de inversi creciente, que por su naturaleza y caractersticas se engloban en la categora de los productos de seguros conocidos como Unit Linked. Me gustara subrayar que esta categora de productos denominados Unit Linked, son de frecuente comercializaci, tanto en nuestro entorno financiero como en otros sistemas financieros. El hecho diferencial, en este caso, ha venido dado por el modo en que dichos productos fueron comercializados entre la clientela de depositantes de Eurobank, y en particular, la falta de transparencia sobre el tipo de producto comercializado.
