Entre esos elementos hay que mencionar un proceso de rpida apreciacin del euro, la posibilidad de que las empresas europeas no hayan completado todava el ajuste de sus balances y los efectos que la incertidumbre sobre el comportamiento del empleo y la situacin de las finanzas pblicas nacionales pueda tener sobre el gasto de los consumidores. A este respecto, es evidente que una fuente importante de preocupacin proviene del comportamiento de las polticas fiscales en algunos pases de la zona, que no avanzaron suficientemente en el proceso de consolidacin, en la fase de crecimiento ms intenso, y que no han sido capaces de contener los dficit pblicos dentro de los lmites legalmente establecidos. Estos desarrollos han puesto a prueba la eficacia de los mecanismos correctivos previstos en el Tratado de la UE y en el Pacto de Estabilidad y Crecimiento. En este sentido, cabe lamentar, tal y como lo han hecho la Comisin Europea y el Consejo de Gobierno del Banco Central Europeo, las conclusiones del Consejo de Ministros de la UE del pasado 25 de noviembre, relativas a los procedimientos de dficit excesivo abiertos a Alemania y a Francia. Estas conclusiones, al no ajustarse a las normas de disciplina vigentes, suponen un riesgo para el mantenimiento de la credibilidad del marco institucional y de la confianza en la solidez de las finanzas pblicas de los Estados Miembros de la zona del euro. Por ello, resulta perentorio que las autoridades nacionales adopten acciones efectivas que limiten los efectos adversos que estos acontecimientos hayan podido generar. Por su parte, la poltica monetaria nica ha aprovechado que las perspectivas sobre la tasa de inflacin de la zona han evolucionado en torno a niveles compatibles con la estabilidad de precios para mantener un tono apropiado para superar la situacin de estancamiento de la economa. Cabe sealar, sin embargo, que, a pesar del bajo dinamismo registrado, la tasa de inflacin de la zona del euro ha mostrado cierta persistencia, que se ha visto favorecida por el comportamiento de los precios alimenticios, y que puede verse alentada por las subidas de los impuestos indirectos introducidas en algunos pases para contener los dficit pblicos en 2004. En esta situacin, las autoridades europeas se enfrentan en los prximos trimestres al reto de hacer compatibles la recuperacin de la economa de la zona con el retorno a los valores de referencia establecidos por el Pacto de Estabilidad y Crecimiento, preservando el marco de consolidacin fiscal, e impulsar, de forma decidida, las medidas de reforma estructural que permitan elevar la capacidad de crecimiento de la economa europea. En Espaa, como dije al principio, el comportamiento de la economa ha sido considerablemente ms dinmico. En el tercer trimestre de 2003, la tasa interanual de crecimiento del PIB se ha situado en el 2,4%, con un avance intertrimestral del 0,7%, cifras ligeramente superiores a las del trimestre anterior, que confirman la continuidad de una senda de reanimacin gradual, una vez que se super un mnimo cclico en los meses centrales del ao anterior. Estos datos indican, adems, que el diferencial de crecimiento con la zona del euro, que se ampli en la primera mitad del ao, ha seguido aumentando en la segunda parte, an cuando la economa europea ha comenzado ya a superar su fase de crecimiento ms dbil. A su vez, el empleo ha continuado creciendo en Espaa a ritmos comparativamente elevados, marcando tambin una diferencia notable con la zona del euro. El crecimiento del PIB continua estando sostenido por la demanda interna y, dentro de ella, por el consumo y la construccin. La generacin de rentas de los hogares apoyada principalmente en la creacin de empleo, la mejora de las bolsas, los aumentos en el valor del patrimonio inmobiliario de las familias y los bajos tipos de inters han seguido contribuyendo, en diferente medida, a mantener, e incluso a intensificar, el crecimiento del consumo privado. Adems, la adquisicin de viviendas, influida tambin por el aumento de la renta, por las favorables condiciones de financiacin, por factores demogrficos y demanda procedente del exterior, ha mantenido un ritmo muy vivo, en un contexto de aumento de la edificacin, por lo que el endeudamiento de los hogares y los precios de la vivienda han mantenido las pautas de los trimestres precedentes. El empuje de la obra civil tambin ha confluido en el impulso de la inversin en construccin, que ha seguido registrando aumentos elevados en los meses recientes, aunque los indicadores ms inmediatos apuntan hacia una suave desaceleracin, que tiene su origen en el tramo de la construccin privada no residencial. Por su parte, las compras de bienes de equipo, que ya haban salido del bache que sufrieron en el ao 2001, han frenado, sin embargo, su ritmo de expansin en ese perodo. A ello pueden haber contribuido diversos factores, como la dbil recuperacin en los pases europeos ms prximos a Espaa. Sin embargo, la situacin de las empresas espaolas sigue siendo saneada y sus niveles de rentabilidad altos, por lo que cabe esperar que se trate de un episodio pasajero, de manera que la inversin productiva retome un mayor impulso cuando se consolide la recuperacin internacional. Las exportaciones, por su parte, que se haban fortalecido notablemente desde el verano de 2002 y que han mantenido ritmos elevados de crecimiento en el primer semestre de este ao, tambin se desaceleraron en verano. La informacin disponible indica que esta prdida de dinamismo adquiri mayor intensidad en las ventas dirigidas a la zona del euro y que fue mucho ms suave en las destinadas a otras reas geogrficas. En este ltimo caso, debe tenerse en cuenta que, debido a la apreciacin del euro, los exportadores espaoles a estos mercados han tenido que asumir descensos de precios para proteger sus cuotas. El menor dinamismo de las exportaciones en los ltimos meses parece reflejar principalmente la atona del mercado europeo, aunque la compresin de mrgenes en el sector ha podido empezar a jugar un papel tambin. En todo caso, este comportamiento, junto con un perfil de desaceleracin menos acentuado de las importaciones cuyo avance se ha visto respaldado por la pujanza de la demanda interna y por la propia apreciacin del euro se ha traducido en una aportacin negativa de la demanda externa al crecimiento del PIB. De este panorama se desprende que las perspectivas de crecimiento de la economa espaola en el horizonte ms cercano estn asentadas sobre bases slidas, puesto que sus principales apoyos el consumo y la construccin mantienen ritmos de avance estables y elevados, y los otros componentes se vern alentados a medida que la recuperacin internacional y la de la zona del euro, en especial se vaya reforzando. Cabe esperar, por tanto, que en lnea con el diagnstico que esboc en el Congreso, la economa espaola cierre el ao 2003 con un avance medio del PIB del orden del 2,3% o incluso algo ms elevado-, resultado que proporciona el punto de partida adecuado para que, en un contexto de expansin exterior, en el ao 2004 se alcancen tasas de crecimiento en el entorno del 3%, en coherencia con las cifras incorporadas en el cuadro macroeconmico en el que se basa la programacin presupuestaria. Ello no obvia, sin embargo, la existencia de algunos rasgos en el comportamiento de la economa espaola que se deben mejorar para aprovechar mejor el impulso exterior y proporcionar una mayor sostenibilidad al crecimiento en el medio plazo. Las vacilaciones mostradas, en el periodo ms reciente, por la inversin en equipo y las exportaciones ilustran la necesidad de que la recuperacin se asiente en la competitividad de aquellos sectores ms abiertos al exterior, sobre los que debera descansar el peso de la fase expansiva, para evitar que se acumulen presiones sobre los sectores que ms han contribuido al crecimiento hasta ahora. Reviste particular importancia que la evolucin de los precios y de los costes en Espaa se alinee con la de nuestros principales socios comerciales. El crecimiento de los costes laborales en la economa espaola contina siendo superior al observado en la zona del euro, como consecuencia tanto de las ganancias reducidas que registra la productividad del trabajo como de un crecimiento de los salarios ms elevado, a pesar de las pautas de moderacin que se han ido aceptando. A este respecto, la inversin productiva debe desempear un protagonismo destacado, pues slo un avance de la misma puede hacer compatible el mantenimiento de la generacin de empleo con unas ganancias de productividad ms elevadas. En cuanto a los salarios, conviene evitar que las desviaciones transitorias de la inflacin realimenten presiones alcistas sobre los mismos. Para ello es necesario limitar los mecanismos de indiciacin que perviven en la negociacin colectiva y que dificultan los procesos de reduccin de la tasa de inflacin. En cualquier caso, no son slo los diferenciales de costes laborales por unidad de producto los que explican el diferencial de inflacin que Espaa mantiene con la zona del euro, tambin las ampliaciones de mrgenes en algunos sectores, ligadas tanto a la presin de la demanda como al funcionamiento poco eficiente de algunos mercados, estn contribuyendo a mantener las alzas de precios. Por ello es fundamental seguir profundizando en la flexibilizacin de los mercados de productos y de la economa, en general. En el perodo transcurrido de 2003, la tasa de inflacin espaola, medida por el IPC, ha experimentado una notable reduccin, desde los niveles del 4% con que finaliz el ao 2002 hasta la cifra del 2,6% que alcanz en octubre. Este significativo recorte refleja, en parte, el descuento de una serie de factores, que incidieron sobre los precios durante el pasado ao como ciertos aumentos de la imposicin indirecta, o la introduccin de los billetes y monedas de euro, cuyos efectos sobre la tasa de inflacin se han ido reabsorbiendo en la primera parte de 2003. A pesar de ello, el diferencial de inflacin con la UEM contina situado en siete dcimas de punto porcentual, indicando la pervivencia de algunos factores que tienden a limitar la necesaria reduccin del mismo. Cabe mencionar, a ste respecto, las clusulas de revisin salarial, cuyos efectos sobre el proceso de formacin de precios tardarn en ser absorbidos, y la persistencia de incrementos de precios relativamente elevados en los servicios y en la distribucin comercial, que, como acabo de mencionar, en algunos casos estn ligados a la fortaleza de la demanda y, en otros, reflejan la existencia de estructuras de mercado insuficientemente competitivas. En este momento, en el que la economa espaola reanuda una senda de aceleracin gradual, en una coyuntura europea que permite prever unas condiciones monetarias que seguirn siendo holgadas para las necesidades interiores, reviste gran importancia que la poltica fiscal preserve su orientacin estabilizadora y ayude a atemperar las presiones de demanda, contribuyendo tambin al reequilibrio en la composicin del gasto. En este marco hay que valorar positivamente la previsin del Gobierno, anunciada en el Congreso durante el debate de los Presupuestos Generales del Estado para el ao 2004, de un ligero supervit en el cierre de las cuentas pblicas del ejercicio 2003. Este resultado, mejor que el anticipado en el Proyecto de Presupuestos sujeto a debate, est en lnea con la funcin estabilizadora de la poltica fiscal y pone de manifiesto la posibilidad de compatibilizar dicha funcin con el cumplimiento del Pacto de Estabilidad y de Crecimiento. De hecho, en los aos en los que la economa espaola experiment una cierta desaceleracin cclica, las Administraciones Pblicas espaolas siguieron avanzando en la consolidacin presupuestaria, a la vez que contribuan de forma positiva al sostenimiento de la actividad, a travs de su influencia sobre la renta disponible de las familias y, por esta va, sobre el consumo privado y mediante una aportacin significativa al desarrollo de la inversin en infraestructuras. No hay que olvidar, sin embargo, que esta orientacin estabilizadora de la poltica fiscal no habra sido posible sin el esfuerzo de consolidacin realizado durante la fase cclica precedente, en la cul se registraron importantes incrementos en la recaudacin, incluso en los aos de reforma impositiva, al tiempo que se proceda a efectuar ajustes importantes en el gasto corriente primario. Esta estrategia contrasta, como seal anteriormente, con la que han seguido otros pases europeos, con resultados mucho menos positivos para el margen de maniobra de la poltica fiscal. Para el ao 2004 los Presupuestos Generales del Estado establecen el objetivo de situar las cuentas pblicas en una posicin de equilibrio. Este objetivo sera compatible con una cierta orientacin expansiva en determinadas partidas de gasto prestaciones sociales, empleo pblico, remuneracin de los salariados e inversin pblica y, por el lado de los ingresos, con algn efecto tambin expansivo derivado de la reforma del IRPF, instrumentada en el ao 2003. Sin embargo, al partir de una situacin de supervit como la prevista en el ejercicio 2003, puede ser conveniente que se profundice en el papel estabilizador que la poltica fiscal viene desempeando, especialmente cuando se prev un repunte cclico. En esta coyuntura sera conveniente -sobre todo, si se acenta el perfil de aceleracin del gasto interno- que durante el prximo ao se obtuviera un supervit de magnitud similar al ya alcanzado. De esta manera, continuara la mejora del saldo corregido del efecto cclico y de los tipos de inters (lo que se conoce como saldo estructural primario). Este tipo de actuacin permitira, adems, afrontar los retos que, en el corto plazo, supone avanzar en el proceso de separacin de las fuentes de financiacin del Estado y de la Seguridad Social, tal y como estipula el reciente acuerdo sobre las pensiones en el marco del Pacto de Toledo y, ms en el medio plazo, mejorar la calidad de las finanzas pblicas y profundizar en la consolidacin presupuestaria, aspectos necesarios para superar con xito los retos asociados al envejecimiento de la poblacin. De esta manera la poltica presupuestaria continuara desempeando el papel que se requiere de ella, una vez que la poltica monetaria, al venir dictada por las necesidades del conjunto del rea del euro, no puede atender las necesidades de estabilizacin especficas de la economa espaola.

Title: Intervention: ABC Forum. "Notas sobre la economa espaola"
text: NOTES ON THE SPANISH ECONOMY ABC FORUM March 22, 2004 Jaime Caruana, Governor of the Bank of Spain INTRODUCTION First of all I would like to thank you for the invitation to participate in the ABC Forum in which I have been preceded by important personalities, for which I feel very honored. I would like to take this opportunity to try to make a calm analysis of the situation of the Spanish economy and I trust that during Question Time I will have the opportunity to know the vision of many of those present at this table. I am aware of the importance and difficulty of a serene and objective analysis given the tragedy of the brutal terrorist attack that we have recently suffered and that we all feel very close to us; I don't even think the analysis of the economic impact is the most relevant given the immense suffering it has caused. However, it is necessary to do so, as financial markets reacted and some debate was opened in various areas about the possible implications, relating to economic developments at a time when the modest recovery of the world economy is gaining strength. I would like to start by moving forward to one of the conclusions I will reach later: the Spanish economy is in a good position to overcome the challenges it faces, including the potential impact that could result from the terrorist attack. The main channel of influence is its possible impact on the confidence of economic agents that can alter their spending decisions. It is not yet possible to have reliable indicators of its effect on confidence and additional time will be needed to determine its transmission to economic variables. At the moment, the only indicators we have are the derivatives of the financial markets, which have reacted by seeking security, which caused bonds to reach new profitability lows and the stock markets to register significant falls. The exchange rate has not been significantly affected. During the six days following the attack of September 11, the IBEX gave up approximately 8%, the following month the fall had been reduced to just under 2%. In the present case, the IBEX has lost approximately 5%. Obviously, it is difficult to extract relevant information from these markets that tend to overreact in the short term and that are subject to the influence of many fundamental and technical factors. Also, I think the comparison with September 11 can be misleading. On this occasion, neither the damage to the infrastructures and settlement systems of the main markets and financial companies has occurred, nor has the situation of the main economies in the same cyclical position. At that time, on September 11, the world economy was in full slowdown, while now we are in a recovery, which, although modest, is expanding its base and gaining strength. It seems less likely that any of these regions, such as Asia, will be affected by these events. Similarly, in September 11 the stock markets had been falling for a year and a half, while today they have been rising for about a year. All this advises caution in comparisons so as not to exaggerate the possible effects and the need for more information. Last week, the possible economic impact of the attack in Madrid was discussed in the General and Governing Councils of the ECB. In addition to receiving condolences and solidarity for what happened, the general feeling was to corroborate the need for more time to assess the possible impact on economic variables. At the next meeting, as part of our usual economic review, we will be able to carry out a first analysis, which will undoubtedly remain preliminary. Although the analysis of the economic impacts will require more time, much can be said about the degree of preparation of the Spanish economy, about our room for maneuver. In this regard, I believe that there are solid reasons, based on the recent positive performance of our economy, that allow us to have confidence in our ability to address challenges and to take advantage of the impulses of international reactivation that have been consolidating from an advantageous position. Therefore, I will focus my reflections on the Spanish economy, its environment, its strengths, challenges and also on the balance of risks. The Spanish economy undoubtedly has challenges - they are not new - and the Bank of Spain has not hesitated to fulfill its role of highlighting the elements of risk that should be borne in mind if we want to continue the path of real convergence. Its solution requires resolutely continuing with the policies of stability and reforms that give our economy flexibility and capacity to maneuver and react to adverse situations. In a situation of change of government, which always generates some uncertainty, the unequivocal manifestations of the new team regarding its commitment in economic policy with the aforementioned principles of stability, non-interventionism and reforms add one more reason for confidence. This confidence can be increased when the development of the measures allows the markets, in their continuous monitoring work, to know the details of the measures and the consistency of their execution. Throughout my presentation I will combine short-term analyses with medium and long-term reflections and this is because I am convinced that the best economic policy in the short term is one that is consistent with the medium and long term. As we will see, part of the problems facing Europe today are associated with a lack of confidence resulting from insecurity in the approach and solution of long-term challenges. I will begin by briefly analysing the external context, I will dwell especially on the euro area given its relevance for our economy, and finally I will refer to the Spanish economy. 1. Outdoor environment The world economy is in a phase of recovery that began in 2002 and in 2003 consolidated and expanded its base to the main geographical areas, with the exception of the euro area, which recorded growth of only 0.4%. If we remember the debates a few months ago, the world economy was compared to an airplane flying with a single engine, which, obviously, was the American economy. Since then, in general and with the exception of the euro area, the growth forecasts of the various international organizations have been revised upwards significantly. In addition, the American economy is being complemented by growth in other parts of the world, mainly Asia and especially China. Integration into the world economy and its pronounced expansion figure in 2003 d0 over 9% d0 is allowing this country to achieve an increasingly important role in international trade and financial exchanges. Japan's GDP also grew much higher than the average over the last decade last year, supported by the expansionary nature of monetary policy and, above all, progress in the financial consolidation of the corporate sector. The positive evolution of the world economy has been supported by the recovery of international financial markets in an environment of expansionary monetary and budgetary conditions, without inflationary tensions appearing in the main economies. Entering into the analysis of the balance of risks, the pattern of recovery that the world economy is following incorporates some elements of risk for its sustainability. Thus, the economic dynamism of the United States in recent years has been driven by some factors whose expansionary action cannot be maintained indefinitely. Such is the case with the exceptional easing of monetary policy, tax cuts and the increase in the propensity to spend of households. The deterioration in the equity balances of the private sector d0 especially households d0 and the public sector, which has accompanied the action of these factors, has manifested itself in an increase in the current account deficit to levels above 5% of GDP. External imbalances cannot continue to grow unlimitedly, so prospects for consolidating global economic growth depend on how they can be corrected. It will also be necessary to follow the evolution of the price of oil, which is above the upper limit of the band set by OPEC. The euro area lags behind the dynamism of the global economy. The main cause of the persistent weakness of its economic activity is to be found in sluggish domestic spending, weighed down by successive falls in productive investment from 2001 to 2003 and sluggish private consumption. In addition, however, the appreciation of the exchange rate has been felt in the evolution of the area's net foreign sales, particularly in the last quarter of 2003, after several years of loss of export shares on the world market. According to the first estimate, euro zone growth in the fourth quarter was 0.3% quarter-on-quarter, confirming that the recovery began in the third quarter, after the first two recorded slightly negative growth. It is worth noting that weakness in private consumption persisted (0.1 per cent) and, on a positive note, gross fixed capital formation registered a positive growth rate for the first time since the fourth quarter of 2002. The decline in investment has been linked, in part, to poor corporate performance and the clean-up undertaken by some major companies. However, as we will see later, this explanation is not enough. As regards the trend in private consumption in the first months of 2004, consumer confidence improved slightly in January and February, while data for car registrations for February and retail sales were relatively favourable. This information allows us to have certain expectations of recovery of this component of demand since the beginning of the year. All this is compatible with the scenario of gradual recovery, with a more balanced balance of risks and with an inflation outlook that, although volatile due to the base effect, is considered compatible with the definition of price stability. In any case, the difficulty of establishing the growth of domestic demand contrasts with the maintenance of conditions conducive to its expansion. Thus, the low level of nominal and real interest rates, which remained close to the lows of recent decades, was joined in 2003 by the intense recovery of the stock markets and the reduction of corporate bond rate differentials. At the same time, household disposable income was strengthened by the performance of employment, more favourable than in other stages of slowdown, and the tax cuts implemented in many countries. In the same vein, the improvement in the international environment has contributed to increasing the external demand of European companies, mitigating the opposite effect of exchange rate appreciation. But although there are some specific factors that may partially explain the sluggishness of consumption and investment over the past two years, these are not enough to justify by themselves the low momentum of private sector spending when the aforementioned favorable conditions are met, so it is clear that what lies behind it is, First and foremost, weak consumer and investor confidence. It is not easy to unravel precisely the factors underlying the weak confidence of economic agents, but it is quite likely that they are linked to structural fragilities in the economy that erode expectations about the future behavior of labour and capital incomes. Consequently, when, as in the current phase, the lack of momentum in the economy is largely due to pessimism in expectations and the persistence of structural problems, the ability of monetary authorities to influence agents' spending decisions is limited and it is of great importance that their conduct gives rise to confidence in maintaining price stability, Essential condition to achieve sustained growth. At the same time, structural reform policies are gaining importance; In this regard, I would like to make two additional comments: First, the importance of giving the necessary priority to achieving balanced budgets that provide room for manoeuvre to economies, allowing the free operation of automatic stabilizers when they need it. It is also necessary, from the point of view of the functioning of a monetary union, to avoid the costs of fiscal indiscipline being shared by the members of the area. It is therefore particularly important to maintain and respect rules, such as those contained in the Treaty on European Union and in the Stability and Growth Pact, regardless of whether formulas can be studied to improve their functioning in practice. In addition, supposedly expansionary budget deficits that are perceived with distrust and as unsustainable may have opposite effects, that is, contractionary by not being transferred to additional spending decisions. The second point I would like to make is a more medium- to long-term reflection on growth in the EU. As I said before, the current central scenario is one of moderate recovery, so that throughout this year growth would gradually tend to approach its potential growth. In my opinion, the main problem is not that the EU is growing below its potential; I think the problem is that the growth potential is as low as around 2% or somewhat higher. I know that I am opening another front in this presentation, but I think it is important to pause for a moment because it is directly related to the need to decisively implement the Lisbon and Barcelona agendas and improve productivity. These last aspects are also relevant to our economy. This reduction in our ability to grow in the EU has been occurring slowly and systematically over the past 30 years and has meant that we have slowly separated ourselves from the potential growth of the US. This has given rise to an interesting debate, particularly since 1995, on the determinants of growth, and especially the differences in apparent productivity and its components between the two areas. The US economy, unlike the European Union, has shown a degree of efficiency that has allowed it to achieve notable and persistent increases in productivity and, in addition, make them compatible with increases in employment. This statement must be qualified with the data of this last phase of recovery, in which employment is behaving significantly below expectations according to previous patterns. There is no time to delve into this debate, which is complex and comprises elements as varied as statistical measurement problems in Europe; the pace of progress in investment, mainly in information technology; the improvement in human capital and in the ability to incorporate technical progress and new technologies into the organization and processes of companies, etc. A final thought on this point: the materialization and transmission of the potential effects of investments in new technologies to society as a whole is not automatic and requires that the economy has reached the degree of competence and flexibility necessary to facilitate organisational changes, the adaptation of workers' skills to a changing environment and a dynamic framework for business creation. The announcements and actions on reforms in some of the main EMU countries represent a window of opportunity that should hopefully serve to accumulate sufficient critical mass to improve the confidence of agents and to reduce the vulnerability of the EMU economy to shocks in confidence. 2. Spanish economy I want to move on to the analysis of the Spanish economy, not without highlighting that the behaviour of the external environment is an important determinant of our evolution. Despite the low dynamism of the euro area, the Spanish economy continued during 2003 and the elapsed part of 2004 a path of gradual expansion, in line with the notable improvement in the world economy. This behaviour of the Spanish economy throughout 2003 has confirmed some previous analyses that the Bank of Spain has been carrying out, to which I will refer briefly. The Spanish economy closed 2003 with an average growth of 2.4%, which is broken down into an increase in domestic demand of 3.3% and a negative contribution of the net external balance of one percentage point. This growth was again accompanied by significant job creation (1.8% average for the year). Data for the fourth quarter indicate that the most dynamic components have continued to be private consumption and construction, although they have registered a slight slowdown. Investment in capital goods, which has grown positively since mid-2002, also slowed its rate of growth. On the other hand, the slowdown in imports was greater than that of exports, which allowed the contribution of the foreign sector to be less negative. The growth profile of the economy throughout the four quarters of last year was upward: 2.2-2.3-2.4 and 2.7. The most recent indicators do not seem to point to significant changes in the trends observed in previous quarters and remain consistent with an average growth scenario approaching 3%. As for inflation, after three months of consecutive reductions, the latest figure for February, which reached 2.1% in year-on-year terms, represents the lowest rate since the beginning of 1999 and brings the differential with EMU to 0.6. Monitoring this variable, given its persistence, remains key to detecting potential competitiveness problems. If we take a certain perspective in our analysis, the Spanish economy has experienced in recent years a period of continuous growth, which has meant significant progress in the field of real convergence, so that the gap between Spanish per capita income and the EMU average has been reduced by more than seven percentage points in the last eight years. This process has not been interrupted in the recent economic slowdown, despite the fact that our main EMU partners are going through a phase of weak growth, which has hindered the growth of Spanish exports. This is a new, different positive behaviour, not only in relation to the evolution of our European partners but also in relation to past experiences of slowing down our economy. This prolonged phase of growth, where the Spanish economy has been less vulnerable than in the past to adverse external shocks, has benefited greatly from the expansionary effect on agents' spending decisions of the consolidation of the macroeconomic stability environment caused by our entry into EMU and the reduction in nominal and real interest rates. But, in addition, the domestic policies carried out, in particular the notable effort made in terms of budgetary consolidation and the adoption of reforms that have boosted the expansionary impulses on activity and employment generated by the institutional changes that occurred with the introduction of the euro. The important thing is that the same factors that have given the Spanish economy considerable resistance to the cyclical weakening phase allow us to approach from an advantageous position the impulses of international reactivation that have been consolidating and generalizing over the last year. This conclusion, which I already advanced in my introduction, is not only based on the significant differential behavior of recent years, but is also supported by a medium-term analysis, which confirms the profound changes in the fundamentals of the Spanish economy. Over the last twenty-five years the Spanish economy has undergone transformations of great importance and depth, which have taken place in line with a growing integration into the world economic fabric, which culminated four years ago with its incorporation into the group of founding countries of the Economic and Monetary Union, and which has been able to boost its presence on the international stage, until reaching a relevant position in the new globalized economy. In this chapter of relevant transformations that have strengthened our economy, the Spanish financial system deserves recognition for its progress in areas such as solvency, efficiency and risk management. We have a competitive banking system, with solvency ratios, a capacity to generate recurring resources and risk management that place it in the first places of the advanced countries. An additional reason for confidence, given the importance of the banking system being able to function properly and finance the development of our economy in favorable and adverse cyclical conditions. Thus, the main features of the recent evolution of the Spanish economy confirm the existence of solid foundations for the continuation of a path of gradual expansion, probably more moderate than that registered during the previous cycle over the horizon of the coming years, if there are no serious unexpected shocks. However, the pattern of growth followed in the most recent period, which has been driven mainly by consumer and construction spending in a context of historically low interest rates, may generate some risks for its longer-term projection. When such a pattern of expenditure is prolonged over time, it can lead to the emergence of difficulties for the financial balance of households and societies and for the competitiveness of the economy. I have had the opportunity to point out on previous occasions that, now that the signs of recovery in the international economy are taking hold, it is appropriate that this growth be based to a greater extent on the impulse from external demand, surpassing the pattern followed so far, in which domestic demand has played a preponderant role. This change in composition would favour the intensification of productive investment and avoid the imbalances that a low diversification of sources of growth can entail. To promote sustained growth, our economy must move towards a more diversified pattern of growth, with a greater weight of productive investment and exports, which contributes to the financial balance of companies and households and strengthens the foundations of competitiveness. To this end, it is essential to deepen the stabilising role of fiscal policy and structural reforms that increase the flexibility and efficiency of the economy. These changes are necessary to further close the gap that, in terms of well-being, still separates us from the average of the euro area countries. With regard to the conditions of investment, it should be remembered that monetary and financial conditions in Spain are particularly favourable. This slack of financial conditions has resulted in an intense recourse of companies and, above all, of families to obtain external resources to support their spending decisions. Under these conditions, the financial position of enterprises does not impede greater dynamism in capital goods investment and employment. However, the levels of indebtedness achieved imply, as in the case of households, a greater relative exposure of companies to a possible increase in the costs of refinancing their liabilities or to an unfavourable evolution of their results and, consequently, have increased the dependence of their spending decisions on the behaviour of the variables that determine that financial situation The existence of a framework conducive to the expansion of productive capital, such as that arising from the financial situation of enterprises, tends to facilitate the gradual transition towards a pattern of growth in which investment in equipment d0 together with exports d0 acquires a greater role. This transition is necessary to address the risks to long-term growth prospects that may result from a prolonged weakness in this type of investment that could adversely affect innovation and productivity and, therefore, the competitiveness of the economy. The dynamism of the other key variable, exports, requires taking care of the competitiveness of the economy, which may be hampered in the medium term by certain characteristics of the functioning of factor and product markets, which hinder efficiency in the processes of cost and price formation. The ability to transfer wage increases to prices and maintain the operating margins of companies is much lower in the branches most exposed to external competition or in those where demand is weaker, so excessive homogenization in wage behavior can erode their profitability and competitiveness. The analysis of the industrial sector more open to external competition seems to indicate that after several years of margin compression it has had to resort to productivity increases through the adjustment in employment. This cost-cutting strategy has made it possible to maintain competitiveness in export markets but can hardly be prolonged indefinitely. The above considerations point to the challenge for economic policy posed by the need to move towards a pattern of growth in which the risks of financial imbalances in firms or households or deterioration of the competitiveness of the economy are reduced. More specifically, the sustainability of economic dynamism requires a fiscal policy capable of sufficiently offsetting the pressures generated by a relatively loose common monetary policy for our cyclical position and a further deepening of the reform process to provide the supply with an appropriate degree of flexibility. Recognising the difficulties that have become apparent in Europe in complying with the Stability and Growth Pact in a context of low growth, it should be stressed that the importance of an orthodox fiscal policy does not arise, or at least not only, from compliance with the European coordination framework but from the very needs of our economy. Since Spain's entry into the EMU, budgetary policy has borne the brunt of macroeconomic stabilisation, offsetting, at least partially, the expansionary impulses on domestic demand that have resulted from the single monetary policy. In this context, the public accounts have recorded increasingly favourable results, reaching surplus positions in 2002 and 2003 and falling levels of public debt, progressively far from the threshold of 60% of GDP. This behaviour has been greatly facilitated by institutional designs that have had an impact on the budgetary system and culminated in the entry into force of the Budget Stability Act in 2003. Over the medium term, however, the slack in monetary conditions cannot be expected to change significantly, so that even the maintenance of contractionary fiscal impulses, of a similar magnitude to those of recent years, could prove insufficient to provide the macroeconomic policies (monetary and fiscal) as a whole consistent with the phase of expansion in activity expected in the coming years. Fiscal discipline will also make it possible to better address other medium-term considerations, such as the impact of population ageing on public spending. This restrictive stance, which is necessary for the proper management of aggregate demand, should be combined with the objective, in terms of composition, of improving the quality of public finances so that the public sector can drive the necessary productivity gains. Naturally, this requirement affects both the composition of expenditure and that of government revenue. A fiscal policy which takes account of these objectives would also make it possible to contribute to the achievement of the objectives set for the EU by the Lisbon European Council in spring 2000, confirmed and subsequently concretised at the Barcelona Summit. In short, the Spanish economy has shown in its recent evolution adequate conditions to continue a path of gradual expansion that will allow it to move towards the standards of progress and well-being typical of the most advanced European countries. For this trend to continue in the longer term, it will be necessary for productive investment and exports to play a greater role as engines of growth, for the growth rate of financing to the private sector to moderate and for the foundations of the economy's competitiveness to be strengthened. These are the challenges faced by economic policy instruments such as fiscal policy or supply-side policies that remain under the responsibility of national authorities. Whether the current favourable prospects can be projected in the longer term will depend on its ability to maintain a sufficiently stabilising fiscal tone and to make decisive progress in meeting the objectives set out in the Lisbon agenda. With regard to the impact of the terrorist attack, I believe that an analysis of the foundations on which our economy rests and the short-term prospects allow us to reaffirm our confidence.

Adems de recibir el psame y solidaridad por lo ocurrido, el sentimiento general fue de corroborar la necesidad de ms tiempo para evaluar el posible impacto sobre las variables econmicas. En la prxima reunin, dentro de nuestro habitual examen econmico, podremos realizar un primer anlisis, que indudablemente seguir teniendo un carcter preliminar. Aunque el anlisis de los impactos econmicos requerir ms tiempo, s se puede decir mucho sobre el grado de preparacin de la economa espaola, sobre nuestro margen de maniobra.
