Esta confianza se podr ver acrecentada cuando el desarrollo de las medidas permitan a los mercados, en su continua labor de seguimiento, ir conociendo los detalles de las mismas y la consistencia de su ejecucin. A lo largo de mi exposicin combinar anlisis coyunturales con reflexiones de medio y largo plazo y ello porque estoy convencido de que la mejor poltica econmica en el corto plazo es aquella que es consistente con el medio y largo plazo. Como veremos, parte de los problemas a los que se enfrenta Europa hoy estn asociados a falta de confianza derivada de la inseguridad en el planteamiento y solucin de retos de largo plazo. Empezar analizando brevemente el contexto exterior, me detendr especialmente en la zona euro dada su relevancia para nuestra economa, y finalmente me referir a la economa espaola. 1. Entorno exterior La economa mundial se encuentra en una fase de recuperacin que se inicia en 2002 y que en 2003 se afianz y ampli su base a las principales reas geogrficas, con la excepcin de la zona del euro, que registr un crecimiento de tan solo el 0,4%. Si recordamos los debates de hace unos meses, la economa mundial se comparaba a un avin volando con un solo motor, que, obviamente, era la economa americana. Desde entonces, con carcter general y con la excepcin de la zona del euro, las previsiones de crecimiento de los diversos organismos internacionales se han ido revisando al alza de manera significativa. Adems, la economa americana est siendo complementada por el crecimiento en otras partes del mundo, principalmente Asia y muy especialmente China. La integracin a la economa mundial y su pronunciada cifra de expansin en 2003 superior al 9%, est permitiendo a este pas alcanzar un papel cada vez ms relevante en los intercambios comerciales y financieros internacionales. Asimismo, el PIB de Japn experiment el pasado ao un aumento muy superior a la media del ltimo decenio, apoyado en el carcter expansivo de la poltica monetaria y, sobre todo, en los avances en el saneamiento financiero del sector empresarial. La positiva evolucin de la economa mundial ha estado apoyada por la recuperacin de los mercados financieros internacionales en un entorno de condiciones monetarias y presupuestarias expansivas, sin que hayan aparecido tensiones inflacionistas en las principales economas. Entrando en el anlisis del balance de riesgos, el patrn de recuperacin que est siguiendo la economa mundial incorpora algunos elementos de riesgo para su sostenibilidad. As, el dinamismo econmico de Estados Unidos en los ltimos aos ha estado impulsado por algunos factores cuya actuacin expansiva no se puede mantener de manera indefinida. Tal es el caso de la excepcional relajacin de la poltica monetaria, las rebajas de impuestos y el aumento de la propensin al gasto de las familias. El deterioro de los balances patrimoniales del sector privado especialmente de los hogares y del sector pblico, que ha acompaado a la accin de estos factores, se ha manifestado en un incremento del dficit por cuenta corriente hasta niveles superiores al 5% del PIB. Los desequilibrios externos no pueden seguir creciendo de manera ilimitada, por lo que las perspectivas de consolidacin del crecimiento econmico mundial dependen de la forma en la que puedan corregirse los mismos. Tambin habr que seguir la evolucin del precio del petrleo, que se encuentra por encima del lmite superior de la banda fijada por la OPEP. La zona del euro evoluciona con retraso respecto al dinamismo de la economa mundial. La causa principal de la persistente debilidad de su actividad econmica se encuentra en la atona del gasto interno, lastrado por las sucesivas cadas de la inversin productiva desde 2001 a 2003 y la atona del consumo privado. Pero, adems, la apreciacin del tipo de cambio se ha dejado sentir en la evolucin de las ventas exteriores netas de la zona, particularmente en el ltimo trimestre de 2003, despus de varios aos de perdidas de cuotas de exportacin en el mercado mundial. De acuerdo con la primera estimacin, el crecimiento de la zona euro en el cuarto trimestre fue de un 0.3% en trminos inter trimestrales, confirmando que la recuperacin se inici en el tercer trimestre, despus de que los dos primeros registraran crecimientos ligeramente negativos. Merece la pena destacar que persisti la debilidad del consumo privado (0,1%) y, como dato positivo, que la formacin bruta de capital fijo registr una tasa de crecimiento positiva por primera vez desde el cuarto trimestre de 2002. La cada de la inversin ha estado vinculada, en parte, a los pobres resultados empresariales y a los procesos de saneamiento emprendidos por algunas compaas importantes. Sin embargo, como veremos posteriormente, esta explicacin no es suficiente. En cuanto a la evolucin del consumo privado en los primeros meses de 2004, la confianza de los consumidores experiment una ligera mejora en enero y febrero, en tanto que los datos de matriculacin de automviles de febrero y ventas minoristas fueron relativamente favorables. Esta informacin permite albergar ciertas expectativas de recuperacin de este componente de la demanda desde el inicio del ao. Todo lo dicho es compatible con el escenario de recuperacin gradual, con un balance de riesgos ms equilibrado y con unas perspectivas de inflacin que aunque voltiles por el efecto base, se estima compatibles con la definicin de estabilidad de precios. En cualquier caso, la dificultad de asentar el crecimiento de la demanda interna contrasta con el mantenimiento de condiciones propicias para su expansin. As, al reducido nivel de los tipos de inters nominal y real que permanecieron cercanos a los mnimos de las ltimas dcadas, se uni en 2003 la intensa recuperacin de las bolsas y la reduccin de los diferenciales de tipos de los bonos corporativos. Al mismo tiempo, la renta disponible de los hogares se vio fortalecida por el comportamiento del empleo, ms favorable que en otras etapas de desaceleracin, y las rebajas impositivas instrumentadas en numerosos pases. Y en la misma lnea, la mejora del entorno internacional ha contribuido a aumentar la demanda exterior de las empresas europeas, mitigando el efecto contrario de la apreciacin del tipo de cambio. Pero aunque existan algunos factores especficos que pueden explicar parcialmente la atona del consumo y la inversin en los ltimos dos aos, estos no son suficientes para justificar por s solos el escaso impulso del gasto del sector privado cuando se dan las condiciones favorables mencionadas, por lo que resulta evidente que lo que subyace detrs de la misma es, ante todo, una confianza endeble de consumidores e inversores. No es fcil desentraar con precisin los factores que subyacen a la dbil confianza de los agentes econmicos, pero resulta bastante probable que estn ligados a fragilidades estructurales de la economa que erosionan las expectativas sobre el comportamiento futuro de las rentas del trabajo y del capital. En consecuencia, cuando como ocurre en la fase actual- la falta de pulso de la economa se debe, en gran parte, al pesimismo de las expectativas y a la persistencia de problemas estructurales, la capacidad de las autoridades monetarias para influir sobre las decisiones de gasto de los agentes es limitada y adquiere, en cambio, gran relevancia que su conducta suscite confianza en el mantenimiento de la estabilidad de precios, condicin imprescindible para lograr un crecimiento sostenido. Simultneamente, ganan importancia la polticas de reformas estructurales; en este sentido me gustara hacer dos comentarios adicionales: En primer lugar, la importancia de otorgar la prioridad necesaria al logro de presupuestos equilibrados que proporcionen mrgenes de maniobra a las economas, permitiendo el funcionamiento libre de los estabilizadores automticos cuando lo necesiten. Tambin es necesario, desde el punto de vista del funcionamiento de una Unin Monetaria, para evitar que los costes de la indisciplina fiscal sean compartidos por los miembros de la zona. Por lo tanto, resulta particularmente importante mantener y respetar reglas, como las contenidas en el Tratado de la Unin Europea y en el Pacto de Estabilidad y Crecimiento, con independencia de que puedan ser estudiadas frmulas que permiten mejorar su funcionamiento en la prctica. Adems, puede suceder que dficit presupuestarios pretendidamente expansivos que sean percibidos con desconfianza y como no sostenibles, tengan efectos contrarios, es decir, contractivos al no trasladarse a decisiones adicionales de gasto El segundo punto al que me gustara referirme es una reflexin ms de medio-largo plazo sobre el crecimiento en la UE. Como he dicho antes, el escenario central actual es de moderada recuperacin, de forma que a lo largo de este ao el crecimiento tendera de forma gradual a acercase a su crecimiento potencial. En mi opinin, el principal problema no es que la UE est creciendo por debajo de su potencial; ciertamente es preocupante su dificultad para dinamizar la demanda interna, creo que el problema radica en que el potencial de crecimiento se site en una cifra tan baja como el entorno del 2% o algo superior. Se que estoy abriendo otro frente en esta presentacin, pero creo que es importante detenerse un momento porque est directamente relacionado con la necesidad de poner decididamente en marcha las agendas de Lisboa y Barcelona y mejorar la productividad. Estos ltimos aspectos son tambin relevantes para nuestra economa. Esta reduccin de nuestra capacidad de crecer en la UE ha venido producindose lenta y sistemticamente en los ltimos 30 aos y ha hecho que nos hayamos ido separando lentamente de los crecimientos potenciales de los EEUU. Ello ha originado un debate interesante, sobre todo a partir de 1995, sobre los determinantes del crecimiento, y especialmente las diferencias en la productividad aparente y sus componentes entre las dos zonas. La economa de los EEUU, a diferencia de la Unin Europea, ha mostrado un grado de eficiencia que le ha permitido conseguir notables y persistentes incrementos de productividad y, adems, hacerlos compatibles con incrementos de empleo. Esta afirmacin hay que matizarla con los datos de esta ltima fase de recuperacin, en la que el empleo est comportndose significativamente por debajo de lo esperado segn patrones anteriores. No hay tiempo para profundizar en este debate, que es complejo y que comprende elementos tan variados como problemas estadsticos de medicin en Europa; el ritmo de avance en la inversin, principalmente en tecnologas de la informacin; la mejora en capital humano y en la capacidad de incorporar el progreso tcnico y nuevas tecnologas a la organizacin y procesos de las empresas, etc. Una reflexin final en este punto: la materializacin y transmisin de los efectos potenciales de las inversiones en nuevas tecnologas hacia el conjunto de la sociedad no es automtica y requiere que la economa haya alcanzado el grado de competencia y de flexibilidad necesarios para facilitar cambios organizativos, la adaptacin de las capacidades de los trabajadores a un entorno cambiante y un marco dinmico de creacin de empresas. Los anuncios y acciones en materia de reformas en algunos de los principales pases de la UEM representan una ventana de oportunidad que deseablemente debera servir para ir acumulando suficiente masa crtica para mejorar la confianza de los agentes y para reducir la vulnerabilidad de la economa de la UEM ante perturbaciones de confianza. 2. Economa espaola Quiero pasar al anlisis de la economa espaola, no sin destacar que el comportamiento del entorno exterior es un importante condicionante de nuestra evolucin. A pesar del escaso dinamismo de la zona euro, la economa espaola ha proseguido durante 2003 y la parte trascurrida de 2004 una senda de gradual expansin, en sintona con la notable mejora de la economa mundial. Este comportamiento de la economa espaola a lo largo de 2003 ha venido a confirmar algunos anlisis previos que el Banco de Espaa ha venido realizando, a los que me referir brevemente. La economa espaola ha cerrado el ao 2003 con un crecimiento medio del 2.4%, que se descompone en un aumento de la demanda nacional del 3.3% y una contribucin negativa del saldo neto exterior de un punto porcentual. Este crecimiento fue acompaado nuevamente de una importante creacin de empleo (1.8% promedio del ao). Los datos del cuarto trimestre indican que los componentes ms dinmicos han continuado siendo el consumo privado y la construccin, si bien han registrado una ligera desaceleracin. La inversin en bienes de equipo que registra crecimientos positivos desde mediados de 2002, tambin disminuy su ritmo de avance. Por otra parte la desaceleracin de las importaciones fue superior a la de las exportaciones, lo que permiti que la aportacin del sector exterior fuese menos negativa. El perfil de crecimiento de la economa a lo largo de los cuatro trimestres del ao pasado fue ascendente: 2,2-2,3-2,4 y 2,7. Los indicadores ms recientes no parecen apuntar a cambios relevantes en las tendencias observadas en los trimestres precedentes y siguen siendo consistentes con un escenario de crecimiento medio que se aproxime al 3%. En cuanto a la inflacin, tras tres meses de reducciones consecutivas, la ltima cifra correspondiente a febrero, que alcanz un 2.1% en trminos interanuales, representa la tasa ms baja desde principios de 1999 y lleva el diferencial con la UEM a un 0,6. El seguimiento de esta variable, dada su persistencia, sigue siendo clave para detectar posibles problemas de competitividad. Si tomamos una cierta perspectiva en nuestro anlisis, la economa espaola ha experimentado en los ltimos aos, una etapa de crecimiento continuado, que ha supuesto avances significativos en el terreno de la convergencia real, de modo que la brecha entre la renta per-capita espaola y la media de la UEM se ha reducido en ms de siete puntos porcentuales en los ltimos ocho aos. Este proceso no se ha interrumpido en la etapa de desaceleracin econmica reciente, a pesar de que nuestros principales socios de la UEM atraviesan una fase de crecimiento dbil, que ha dificultado el avance de las exportaciones espaolas. Este es un comportamiento positivo nuevo, diferente, no solo en relacin a la evolucin de nuestros socios europeos sino tambin en relacin a experiencias pasadas de desaceleracin de nuestra economa. Esta prolongada fase de crecimiento, donde la economa espaola se ha mostrado menos vulnerable que en el pasado a perturbaciones exteriores adversas, se ha beneficiado en gran medida del efecto expansivo que sobre las decisiones de gasto de los agentes ha tenido la consolidacin del entorno de estabilidad macroeconmica que ha ocasionado nuestro ingreso en la UEM y la reduccin de los tipos de inters nominales y reales. Pero, adems, las polticas domsticas llevadas a cabo, en particular el esfuerzo notable realizado en materia de consolidacin presupuestaria y la adopcin de reformas que han potenciado los impulsos expansivos sobre la actividad y el empleo generados por los cambios institucionales acaecidos con la introduccin del euro. Lo importante es que los mismos factores que han dotado a la economa espaola de una considerable resistencia frente a la fase de debilitamiento cclico, nos permiten abordar desde una posicin ventajosa los impulsos de reactivacin internacional que se han ido afianzando y generalizando a lo largo del ltimo ejercicio. Esta conclusin, que ya avanzaba en mi introduccin, no solo se basa en el significativo comportamiento diferencial de los ltimos aos, sino que tambin viene avalada por un anlisis de medio plazo, que permite confirmar los profundos cambios en los fundamentos de la economa espaola. A lo largo de los ltimos veinticinco aos la economa espaola ha experimentado transformaciones de gran trascendencia y profundidad, que han transcurrido al hilo de una creciente integracin en el entramado econmico mundial, que culmin hace cuatro aos con su incorporacin en el grupo de pases fundadores de la Unin Econmica y Monetaria, y que ha sido capaz de impulsar su presencia en el escenario internacional, hasta alcanzar un puesto relevante en la nueva economa globalizada. En este capitulo de transformaciones relevantes que han fortalecido nuestra economa, el sistema financiero espaol merece un reconocimiento en sus avances en reas como la solvencia, eficiencia y gestin de riesgos. Tenemos un sistema bancario competitivo, con unos ratios de solvencia, una capacidad de generacin de recursos recurrentes y una gestin de riesgos que lo colocan en los primeros lugares de los pases avanzados. Una razn adicional para la confianza, dada la trascendencia de que el sistema bancario sea capaz de funcionar correctamente y financiar el desarrollo de nuestra economa en condiciones cclicas favorables y adversas. As pues, los principales rasgos de la evolucin reciente de la economa espaola confirman la existencia de unas bases slidas para la continuidad de una senda de expansin gradual, probablemente ms moderada que la registrada durante el ciclo anterior en el horizonte de los prximos aos, si no se producen graves perturbaciones inesperadas. Sin embargo, el patrn de crecimiento seguido en el periodo ms reciente, que ha estado impulsado principalmente por el gasto en consumo y en construccin en un contexto de tipos de inters histricamente bajos, puede generar algunos riesgos para su proyeccin a ms largo plazo. Cuando se prolonga en el tiempo un patrn de gasto de estas caractersticas, puede dar lugar a la aparicin de dificultades para el equilibrio financiero de hogares y sociedades y para la competitividad de la economa. Ya en ocasiones anteriores he tenido la oportunidad de sealar que, ahora que los signos de recuperacin de la economa internacional se afiancen, conviene que este crecimiento se base en mayor medida en el impulso proveniente de la demanda exterior, superando el patrn seguido hasta este momento, en el que la demanda interna ha tenido un papel preponderante. Este cambio de composicin favorecera la intensificacin de la inversin productiva y evitara los desequilibrios que puede acarrear una escasa diversificacin de fuentes del crecimiento. Para propiciar el crecimiento sostenido, nuestra economa debe avanzar hacia un patrn de crecimiento ms diversificado, con mayor peso de la inversin productiva y de las exportaciones, que contribuya al equilibrio financiero de las empresas y de los hogares y fortalezca las bases de la competitividad. Para ello resulta fundamental profundizar en el papel estabilizador de la poltica presupuestaria y en las reformas estructurales que incrementen la flexibilidad y la eficiencia de la economa. Estos cambios son necesarios para seguir cerrando la brecha que, en trminos de bienestar, nos separa an de la media de los pases del rea del euro. En cuanto a los condicionantes de la inversin, conviene recordar que en Espaa las condiciones monetarias y financieras son particularmente favorables. Esta holgura de las condiciones financieras se ha traducido en un intenso recurso de las empresas y, sobre todo, de las familias a la obtencin de recursos ajenos para sustentar sus decisiones de gasto. En estas condiciones, la posicin financiera de las empresas no supone ningn obstculo para un mayor dinamismo de la inversin en bienes de equipo y del empleo. No obstante, los niveles de endeudamiento alcanzados suponen, como en el caso de los hogares, una mayor exposicin relativa de las sociedades a un posible aumento de los costes de refinanciacin de sus pasivos o a una evolucin desfavorable de sus resultados y, consiguientemente, han elevado la dependencia de sus decisiones de gasto al comportamiento de las variables que determinan dicha situacin financiera La existencia de un marco propicio para la ampliacin del capital productivo, como el que se desprende de la situacin financiera de las empresas, tiende a facilitar la transicin gradual hacia un patrn de crecimiento en el que la inversin en equipo junto con las exportaciones- adquiere un mayor protagonismo. Esta transicin es necesaria para afrontar los riesgos que, para las posibilidades de crecimiento a largo plazo, se pueden derivar de una prolongada debilidad de este tipo de inversin que pudiera llegar a afectar negativamente a la innovacin y a la productividad y, por tanto, a la competitividad de la economa. El dinamismo de la otra variable clave, la exportacin, requiere cuidar la competitividad de la economa, que puede verse obstaculizada a medio plazo por ciertas caractersticas del funcionamiento de los mercados de factores y de productos, que dificultan la eficiencia en los procesos de formacin de costes y de precios. La capacidad para trasladar incrementos salariales a precios y mantener los mrgenes de explotacin de las empresas es muy inferior en las ramas ms expuestas a la competencia exterior o en las que la demanda presenta una mayor debilidad, por lo que la excesiva homogenizacin en el comportamiento salarial puede erosionar su rentabilidad y competitividad. El anlisis del sector industrial ms abierto a la competencia exterior, parece indicar que tras varios aos de compresin de mrgenes ha debido recurrir a incrementos de productividad mediante el ajuste en el empleo. Esta estrategia de reduccin de costes ha permitido mantener la competitividad en los mercados de exportacin pero difcilmente puede prolongarse de manera indefinida. Las consideraciones anteriores apuntan al reto que para la poltica econmica supone la necesidad de avanzar hacia un patrn de crecimiento en el que se reduzcan los riesgos de desequilibrios financieros en las empresas o los hogares o de deterioro de la competitividad de la economa. Ms concretamente, la sostenibilidad del dinamismo econmico requiere una poltica fiscal capaz de compensar suficientemente las presiones que genera una poltica monetaria comn relativamente laxa para nuestra posicin cclica y una mayor profundizacin del proceso reformador que permita dotar a la oferta de un grado idneo de flexibilidad. Reconociendo las dificultades que se han puesto de manifiesto en Europa para cumplir el Pacto de Estabilidad y Crecimiento en un contexto de bajo crecimiento, conviene destacar que la importancia de una poltica fiscal ortodoxa no surge, o al menos no nicamente, del cumplimiento del marco de coordinacin europeo sino de las propias necesidades de nuestra economa. Desde el ingreso de Espaa en la UEM, la poltica presupuestaria ha llevado el peso de la estabilizacin macroeconmica, compensando, al menos parcialmente, los impulsos expansivos sobre la demanda interna que se han derivado de la poltica monetaria nica. En este contexto, las cuentas pblicas han registrado resultados cada vez ms favorables, hasta alcanzar posiciones excedentarias en 2002 y 2003 y niveles de deuda pblica descendentes, progresivamente alejados del umbral del 60% del PIB. Este comportamiento se ha visto favorecido, en gran medida, por diseos institucionales que han incidido en el sistema presupuestario y que han culminado con la entrada en vigor de la Ley de Estabilidad Presupuestaria en 2003. A medio plazo, no obstante, no cabe esperar que la holgura de las condiciones monetarias vare significativamente, por lo que incluso el mantenimiento de impulsos fiscales contractivos, de magnitud similar a los de los ltimos aos, podra resultar insuficiente para dotar al conjunto de polticas macroeconmicas (monetaria y fiscal) del tono coherente con la fase de expansin de la actividad que se prev para los prximos aos. La disciplina fiscal permitir tambin enfrentar mejor otras consideraciones de medio plazo como el impacto del envejecimiento de la poblacin sobre el gasto pblico. Esa orientacin restrictiva, necesaria para una gestin adecuada de la demanda agregada, debera simultanearse con el objetivo, en trminos de composicin, de mejorar la calidad de las finanzas pblicas, de manera que el sector pblico impulse los incrementos de productividad necesarios. Naturalmente este requisito afecta tanto a la composicin del gasto como a la de los ingresos pblicos. Una poltica fiscal que tenga en cuenta estos objetivos permitira, adems, contribuir al logro de los objetivos establecidos para la UE por el Consejo Europeo de Lisboa en la primavera del 2000, confirmados y concretados posteriormente en la cumbre de Barcelona. En definitiva, la economa espaola ha mostrado en su evolucin reciente unas condiciones adecuadas para proseguir una senda de gradual expansin que le permitir avanzar hacia los estndares de progreso y bienestar propios de los pases europeos ms avanzados. Para que esta tendencia se mantenga a ms largo plazo ser necesario que la inversin productiva y las exportaciones desempeen un mayor protagonismo como motores del crecimiento, que se modere el ritmo de crecimiento de la financiacin al sector privado y que se fortalezcan las bases de la competitividad de la economa. Estos son los retos a los que se enfrentan los instrumentos de poltica econmica que, como la poltica fiscal o las polticas de oferta, se mantienen bajo la responsabilidad de las autoridades nacionales. De su capacidad para mantener un tono fiscal que sea suficientemente estabilizador y para avanzar decididamente en el cumplimiento de los objetivos planteados en la agenda de Lisboa, depender el que las favorables perspectivas actuales se puedan proyectar a ms largo plazo. En cuanto al impacto del atentado terrorista, creo que el anlisis de las bases en las que se apoya nuestra economa y las perspectivas a corto plazo permiten reafirmar nuestra confianza.

Title: Speech: VI Annual Meeting of Senior Executives of Latin American Banks (Santiago, Chile)
text: VI Annual Meeting of Senior Executives of Latin American Banks Santiago, March 26, 2004 Speech by Jaime Caruana, Governor of the Bank of Spain and President of the Basel Committee. Before starting, I would like to thank the Institute of International Finance (IIF) and Banco de Chile for kindly inviting me to participate in this meeting and to share with all of you the work that the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision is carrying out for the update of the Capital Agreement. Work that currently absorbs a large part of the Committee's efforts. In particular, I would also like to thank Charles Dallara for all his support over the years in promoting a smooth dialogue between the IIF and the Committee. Looking only at the new forms of collaboration and communication that have been established between regulators and regulated, we could conclude that the work for the revision of the Basel Agreement has been an effort that has already borne fruit. The Bank of Spain has an excellent relationship with the Central Bank of Chile and with the Superintendency of Banks and Financial Institutions and this is an additional reason to thank this opportunity to be in Santiago de Chile today with all of you. As is already known to all, the new Agreement aims to establish capital requirements that are more reasonably adjusted to the underlying risk borne by each institution. However, it would not be wise to reduce the merits of the new Agreement to a better quantification of capital requirements, which in itself is a significant achievement. The Committee is convinced that the new capital rules also introduce the right incentives to improve banking risk management. Because the main risk of banking activity is not credit risk or operational risk, which the new Agreement develops extensively. The main risk d0 and all countries have witnessed this in one way or another d0 is that the banker does not have sufficient capacity to measure and manage the risks he assumes. Therefore, it is expected that the implementation of the new Agreement will help to improve the measurement and management of banking risks, key elements for a greater solidity of the banking sector and, therefore, to favor greater financial stability, especially in regions such as Latin America, where the banking sector has a decisive weight in the functioning and development of the financial sector. Banking plays a fundamental role in the sustained growth of the region. Access to credit, particularly for small and medium-sized enterprises, and the availability of other banking services, together with macroeconomic stability and legal certainty, are a solid basis for economic growth. But in the same way, poorly managed and undercapitalized banking, coupled with imperfect knowledge on the part of supervisors and bankers of the risks assumed, can make any attempt at financial stability impossible. The benefits of implementing the new Agreement are thus clear. It would therefore be expected that the various national regulators would be able to offer, at least to their banks with a higher degree of sophistication in their activities and risk management, the possibility of accessing the more advanced options proposed by the new Agreement. However, this does not mean that the Committee advises non-members to implement the new Agreement automatically, and within the deadlines set for Committee members. The Committee, on the other hand, insists that individual regulators need to pay particular attention to their specific circumstances when designing the implementation of the new Agreement. Thus, individual regulators will have to carefully decide on its implementation by considering, for example, other regulatory priorities, their experience with the 1988 Agreement or the resources available for effective supervision under Basel II. In some cases, it may be advisable to defer the date of entry into force of the new Agreement; in others, the current Agreement may be a valid solution for less sophisticated banks. In this regard, the Fund and the World Bank have recently expressed their intention to base their assessment of a country's capital standards on national policy: that it is best suited to the state of the local banking system. Basel II is therefore a tool for regulating and promoting the financial system, not for evaluation. At this point, what would be expected from the Committee? Above all, clarity in enactment and scope of the proposals, so that both supervisors and bankers can continue to advance in the work necessary for their entry into force. In recent months, significant progress has been made in a number of important areas: The focus of the agreement was modified to bring it closer to industry practices by establishing in advanced approaches calibration only on unexpected losses, significant progress has been made in risk mitigation, the securitization chapter is practically complete, progress has been made in operational risk management for groups with a presence in different countries and some elements of pillar II have been clarified. Detailed descriptions of these developments can be found on the BIS website where the latest press releases and explanatory notes can be found. We continue to work on the outstanding issues and in this regard, the Committee remains firmly committed to publishing the new Agreement by the middle of this year. This document will serve as the basis for the various national regulations. However, there is no need to wait for the publication of the new Agreement before starting the preparatory work. The Third Consultative Document, published in May last year and widely discussed with the members of the IIF, together with the agreements of the Committee in its last two meetings, are already a solid basis on which to continue basing the work. There are some issues to be closed, but in no way do I expect that the results of these discussions will invalidate the efforts that banks and supervisors are making or plan to make to prepare for their entry into force. In any event, the Committee has stressed on numerous occasions the evolving nature of the Basel II process. From the moment it was decided that the New Capital Agreement would approach industry best practices, we are aware that we will have to evolve, in an orderly manner, when practices change. The Committee is also aware that the successful implementation of the new Agreement depends on its consistent application among the various national regulators. A proposed international standard that presents a varied menu of options and includes both quantitative and qualitative factors, it is not surprising that it is a frequent cause of anxiety for banking groups operating in different countries. The Committee was keenly aware from the outset of the need to promote consistent implementation of the new Agreement and to that end, for the first time in its history, established a working group whose mandate is focused on promoting consistent implementation of Basel II. This group, the Accord Implementation Group, chaired by Nick Le Pan, focuses its work on the exchange of information on the different approaches that each member country of the Committee intends to follow for the implementation of the new Agreement. It is precisely through the exchange of information that the Committee hopes to achieve the consistency that both supervisors and bankers desire. On the other hand, I would like to make it clear that the work of the Committee, directly or through the AIG, does not seek to achieve total uniformity. Among the members of the Committee, as well as outside it, there are different monitoring practices, all of which are valid, which the Committee expects to continue. Last August, as a result of the work of the aforementioned group, the Committee published six high-level principles that provide a framework for cooperation for the implementation of the agreement at the international level. These principles do not alter the responsibilities of origin and destination supervisors, but recognise the need for greater cooperation between supervisors, to facilitate consistency and reduce unnecessary costs for banking groups operating in different countries. To try to achieve the greatest possible international consistency, the Committee has asked the AIG to extend its dialogue to other supervisors and, in general, to the banking sector. In this regard, I would like to thank again the active contribution of the IIF to the work of the AIG. I would also like to thank in particular the supervisors of the region who, directly and through the Core Principles Liaison Group, the main forum for regular discussion of the Committee's work with the other supervisors, the Fund and the World Bank, are collaborating in order to better understand the different positions for the implementation of the new Agreement. Finally, what is expected of banks? To be sure, the new capital rules call on banks to raise the bar on their internal risk management and measurement procedures. Is banking in Latin America ready to face the challenge? That is something I would very much like to be able to discuss today. At this meeting are the most qualified voices to give a good account of the initial situation and the necessary work. Banks need to know what plans regulators have to implement the new capital rules, as we mentioned earlier. But equally, regulators need to know the plans and possibilities of banks in order to give an adequate regulatory response. This is a necessary dialogue between banks and regulators that I wish was already taking place. Finally, I would like to conclude this intervention by encouraging everyone to continue working on strengthening Latin America's financial systems; and there is no doubt that the Committee's new proposals go in this direction. I hope that as a result of this meeting we can continue to strengthen everyone's commitment to support the Committee's efforts, thereby ensuring that the implementation of the new Capital Accord is the success we all hope for. Thanks a lot.
text_original: VI Reunin Anual de Altos Ejecutivos de Bancos de Latinoamrica Santiago, 26 de marzo de 2004 Intervencin de Jaime Caruana, Gobernador del Banco de Espaa y Presidente del Comit de Basilea. Antes de comenzar, quisiera agradecer al Institute of International Finance (IIF) y al Banco de Chile la amabilidad de haberme invitado a participar en esta reunin y poder, as, compartir con todos Uds. los trabajos que el Comit de Supervisin Bancaria de Basilea est llevando a cabo para la actualizacin del Acuerdo de Capital. Unos trabajos que en estos momentos absorben buena parte de los esfuerzos del Comit. De manera especial, tambin quisiera agradecerle a Charles Dallara todo su apoyo durante estos aos para promover un dilogo fluido entre el IIF y el Comit. Fijndonos tan slo en las nuevas formas de colaboracin y comunicacin que se han establecido entre reguladores y regulados, podramos concluir que los trabajos para la revisin del Acuerdo de Basilea han sido un esfuerzo que ha ya dado sus frutos. El Banco de Espaa tiene una excelente relacin con el Banco Central de Chile y con la Superintendencia de Bancos e Instituciones Financieras y ello supone una razn adicional para agradecer esta oportunidad de estar hoy en Santiago de Chile con todos ustedes. Como ya es conocido por todos, el nuevo Acuerdo pretende establecer unos requerimientos de capital que se ajusten de una manera ms razonable al riesgo subyacente que soporta cada entidad. Sin embargo, no sera acertado reducir los mritos del nuevo Acuerdo a una mejor cuantificacin de las exigencias del capital, lo que de por s ya es un logro significativo. El Comit est convencido de que mediante las nuevas normas de capital tambin se introducen los incentivos correctos para mejorar la gestin de los riesgos bancarios. Porque el principal riesgo de la actividad bancaria no es el riesgo de crdito o el riesgo operacional, que el nuevo Acuerdo desarrolla ampliamente. El principal riesgo y todos los pases de una forma u otra hemos sido testigos de esto, es que el banquero no tenga la capacidad suficiente para medir y gestionar los riesgos que asume. As pues, es de esperar que la aplicacin del nuevo Acuerdo ayude a mejorar la medicin y gestin de los riesgos bancarios, elementos clave para una mayor solidez del sector bancario y, por tanto, para favorecer una mayor estabilidad financiera, especialmente en regiones como Latinoamrica, donde el sector bancario tiene un peso decisivo en el funcionamiento y desarrollo del sector financiero. La banca juega un papel fundamental en el crecimiento sostenido de la regin. El acceso al crdito, en particular para la pequea y mediana empresa, y la disponibilidad del resto de servicios bancarios, unido a una estabilidad macroeconmica y seguridad jurdica, son una base slida para el crecimiento de la economa. Pero del mismo modo, una banca mal gestionada e infra-capitalizada, unida a un conocimiento imperfecto por parte de supervisores y banqueros de los riesgos que se asumen, pueden hacer imposible cualquier intento de estabilidad financiera. Los beneficios de la aplicacin del nuevo Acuerdo, pues, quedan claros. Cabra esperar, por lo tanto, que los distintos reguladores nacionales pudieran ofrecer, al menos a sus bancos con un mayor grado de sofisticacin en sus actividades y gestin de riesgos, la posibilidad de acceder a las opciones ms avanzadas que propone el nuevo Acuerdo. Sin embargo, esto no quiere decir que el Comit aconseje a los pases no miembros que apliquen el nuevo Acuerdo de forma automtica, y dentro de los plazos establecidos para los miembros del Comit. El Comit, por el contrario, insiste en que los distintos reguladores han de prestar especial atencin a sus circunstancias especficas a la hora de disear la aplicacin del nuevo Acuerdo. As, los distintos reguladores debern decidir cuidadosamente su puesta en prctica considerando, por ejemplo, otras prioridades de regulacin, su experiencia con el Acuerdo de 1988 o los recursos disponibles para una supervisin efectiva de acuerdo con Basilea II. En algunos casos, puede resultar aconsejable diferir la fecha de entrada en vigor del nuevo Acuerdo; en otros, el Acuerdo actual puede ser una solucin vlida para la banca menos sofisticada. En este sentido, el Fondo y el Banco Mundial han expresado recientemente su intencin de fundamentar en la normativa nacional su evaluacin de las normas de capital de un pas: que sta sea la que mejor se adapte a la situacin del sistema bancario local. Basilea II es, por tanto, una herramienta de regulacin y de promocin del sistema financiero, no de evaluacin. Llegados a este punto, qu cabra esperar del Comit? Sobre todo, claridad en promulgacin y alcance de las propuestas, de modo que tanto a supervisores como a banqueros puedan seguir avanzando en los trabajos necesarios para su entrada en vigor. En los ltimos meses se ha avanzado significativamente en un conjunto de reas importantes: Se modific el enfoque del acuerdo para hacerlo mas prximo a las prcticas de la industria al establecer en los enfoque avanzados la calibracin nicamente sobre perdidas inesperadas, se ha progresado significativamente en la mitigacin de riesgos, el captulo de titulizacin est prcticamente completo, se ha avanzado en la gestin del riesgo operacional para grupos con presencia en diferentes pases y se han clarificado algunos elementos del pilar II. Existen descripciones detalladas de estos avances en la Web del BIS donde se encuentran los ltimos comunicados de prensa y notas explicativas. Continuamos trabajando en los temas pendientes y en este sentido, el Comit mantiene firme su compromiso de publicar el nuevo Acuerdo a mediados de este ao. Este documento servir de base para las distintas regulaciones nacionales. Sin embargo, no hace falta esperar a la publicacin del nuevo Acuerdo para iniciar los trabajos preparatorios. El Tercer Documento Consultivo, publicado en mayo del ao pasado y ampliamente discutido con los miembros del IIF, junto con los acuerdos del Comit en sus dos ltimas reuniones, son ya una base slida sobre las que seguir fundamentando los trabajos. Quedan algunos temas por cerrar, pero de ningn modo espero que los resultados de estas discusiones invaliden los esfuerzos que la banca y los supervisores estn haciendo o tienen pensado hacer para preparar su entrada en vigor. En cualquier caso el Comit ha insistido en numerosas ocasiones en el carcter evolutivo del proceso de Basilea II. Desde el momento en el que se decidi que el Nuevo Acuerdo de Capital se aproximase a las buenas prcticas de la industria, somos conscientes de que deberemos evolucionar, de forma ordenada, cuando las prcticas cambien. Tambin el Comit es consciente de que el xito de la puesta en marcha del nuevo Acuerdo pasa por su aplicacin consistente entre los distintos reguladores nacionales. Una propuesta de norma internacional que presenta un variado men de opciones y que incluye tanto factores cuantitativos como cualitativos, no es de extraar que sea motivo frecuente de ansiedad para los grupos bancarios operativos en distintos pases. El Comit fue muy consciente desde el principio de la necesidad de promover una aplicacin consistente del nuevo Acuerdo y para ello, y por primera vez en su historia, creo un grupo de trabajo cuyo mandato se centra en la promocin de una aplicacin consistente de Basilea II. Este grupo, el Accord Implementation Group, presidido por Nick Le Pan, asienta su trabajo en el intercambio de informacin sobre los distintos enfoques que cada pas miembro del Comit tiene pensado seguir para la aplicacin del nuevo Acuerdo. Es precisamente mediante el intercambio de informacin como el Comit espera alcanzar esa consistencia que tanto supervisores como banqueros desean. Por otra parte, quisiera dejar claro que los trabajos del Comit, directamente o a travs del AIG, no buscan alcanzar una uniformidad total. Entre los miembros del Comit, as como fuera de l, existen distintas prcticas de supervisn, todas ellas vlidas, que el Comit espera que continen. El pasado mes de agosto, como consecuencia del trabajo del citado grupo, el Comit publico seis principios de alto nivel que facilitan un marco de cooperacin para la puesta en marcha del acuerdo a nivel internacional. Estos principios no alteran las responsabilidades de los supervisores de origen y destino, pero reconocen la necesidad de una mayor cooperacin entre supervisores, para facilitar la consistencia y reducir costes innecesarios a los grupos bancarios que operan en diferentes pases. Para tratar de alcanzar la mayor consistencia internacional posible, el Comit ha pedido al AIG que extienda su dilogo al resto de supervisores y, en general, al sector bancario. En este sentido, quisiera agradecer de nuevo la activa contribucin del IIF a los trabajos del AIG. Tambin quisiera agradecer de forma especial a los supervisores de la regin que directamente y a travs del Core Principles Liaison Group, el principal foro para discutir de forma regular los trabajos del Comit con el resto de supervisores, el Fondo y el Banco Mundial, estn colaborando en aras de un mejor entendimiento de las distintas posturas para la aplicacin del nuevo Acuerdo. Por ltimo, qu es lo que se espera de las entidades bancarias? Sin duda, las nuevas normas de capital piden a las entidades que suban el listn en cuanto a sus procedimientos internos de gestin y medicin de riesgos. Est la banca en Latinoamrica preparada para afrontar el reto? Eso es algo que me gustara mucho poder discutir hoy. En esta reunin se encuentran las voces ms cualificadas para dar buena cuenta de la situacin de partida y de los trabajos necesarios. La banca necesita conocer qu planes tienen los reguladores para aplicar las nuevas normas de capital, como ya hemos mencionado antes. Pero del mismo modo, los reguladores necesitan conocer los planes y posibilidades de los bancos para poder dar una respuesta de regulacin adecuada. Este es un dilogo necesario entre la banca y los reguladores que deseara que ya se estuviera llevando a cabo. Finalmente, quisiera concluir esta intervencin animando a todos a seguir trabajando en el fortalecimiento de los sistemas financieros de Latinoamrica; y que duda cabe que las nuevas propuestas del Comit van en esta direccin. Espero que como fruto de este encuentro podamos seguir afianzando el compromiso de todos de apoyar los esfuerzos del Comit, y de este modo asegurar que la aplicacin del nuevo Acuerdo de Capital sea el xito que todos esperamos. Muchas gracias.

Title: Speech: Ordinary General Assembly of the Spanish Confederation of Savings Banks, Madrid
text: Savings Banks, 21 April 2004 Jaime Caruana. Governor of the Bank of Spain It is a pleasure for me to be with all of you again today and to be able to participate in the celebration of your Ordinary General Assembly. Since my previous speech in this forum, three years ago, the conditions under which the world economy has developed, and in particular those that have affected the financial systems, have not, you will agree with me, been simple. The world economy is currently going through a phase of recovery which, although not without risks, was able to take hold in 2003, not only in terms of its intensity, but also in terms of its geographical scope, as a greater number of regions participated in it. The euro area was, however, an exception, with growth of just 0.4%, confirming that the area's recovery is continuing at a modest pace. In this context of low dynamism in the euro area, the Spanish economy has been able to maintain positive differential growth in relation to our neighbouring countries and to continue during 2003 and the elapsed part of 2004 a path of expansion, which confirms a better performance of our economy even in environments of economic slowdown. This new performance of our economy allows us to approach from an advantageous position the impulses of international reactivation that have been consolidating throughout the financial year. This global economic recovery began in 2002, after a period marked by a series of shocks and uncertainties that led to a slowdown in the world economy and also tested both the scope for action and the adaptability of financial systems. resilience, successfully facing the difficult adverse events that have been taking place. This behavior is due to a wide set of factors, of which I would like to highlight two. In the first place, the implementation by the entities, throughout the scams, of important improvements in their control and risk management systems. Undoubtedly, technological advances and the possibility of having more sophisticated analytical tools and databases, as well as the introduction of organizational improvements and greater investment in human capital, have allowed remarkable progress in understanding the risks assumed as well as in their management. Secondly, financial institutions enjoyed a healthy starting position. The experience of scams has confirmed that, when dealing with periods of cyclical shocks or downturns, it is important to have high levels of solvency as well as room for manoeuvre. Appropriate solvency levels should be based on prudent valuation and good asset quality, maintaining not an adequate volume of provisions but also ample and quality own resources, commensurate with the risk profile assumed. For its part, the room for manoeuvre necessary to successfully deal with complex situations is not determined by the aforementioned level of solvency but, fundamentally, by the capacity of the institution to generate resources, especially recurrent, and to improve its efficiency. That is, for the solidity and quality of the income statement. This has undoubtedly been the experience of Spanish banking, and I think we will agree that, in our country, there has been an adequate functioning of the three basic lines of defense of any banking system: risk management, capacity to generate resources and level of solvency. of savings have not been an exception, but rather an example of solidity in a complex environment, as evidenced by the fact that in these scams, and despite the pressure suffered both in terms of margins and results, the profitability of the sector's own resources has remained above 12%. Moreover, savings banks have been operating with NPL ratios at minimum levels and with a high percentage of coverage of doubtful assets, while maintaining their own resources significantly above the regulatory minimum. Throughout 2003, and in line with a better economic and financial climate, the Spanish savings banks have only reaffirmed themselves in this direction. For all these reasons, I can only congratulate myself on the achievements obtained in this regard, given that savings banks are a fundamental and valuable part of the Spanish financial system and their good results say a lot about the level of management achieved by the professionals who are in charge of them. However, as I emphasised in my previous speech to you, there is still a body of information about the profile of the risks taken and the management of savings banks which, in my view, deserve special consideration by the directors of the banks. Today, however, I do not intend to review these aspects, although I do want to reiterate, once again, the need for prudent and responsible action on the part of managers. Developments such as those observed in relation to the high rate of growth of mortgage financing, and to the sectors of construction and real estate development, especially when these growths have been accompanied by a significantly lower increase in deposits, show the need for the management of entities not to be limited to a mere adaptation to events as they happen, rather, managers must try to anticipate possible changes in both the cycle and asset prices. We all know that these exist. Therefore, it is necessary to permanently monitor the administrators of the entities, based on the development of both business strategies and risk management, own resources and liquidity that are dissected with a medium and long-term visi. These strategies should also be based on the analysis of the impact of possible changes in the time horizon of the cycle, being consistent with past experience and the present situation. However, it is not my intention to delve into the risks derived from cyclical changes, but today, throughout my speech, I would like to share with you some reflections on two regulatory reforms whose entry into force will undoubtedly encourage better management of entities, strengthening the financial system as a whole. The implementation of the above-mentioned reforms is increasingly imminent and, in the light of the challenges that we all have to face in order to adapt to them successfully, we need to redouble our efforts. As you may have anticipated, I am referring to the New Capital Agreement and the process of harmonising accounting standards within the European Union. I'll start with this scam. International Accounting Standards (IAS or IAS) As you know, the European Union takes the decision that the consolidated annual accounts of groups with securities listed on any regulated market of the Uni, are prepared in accordance with the International Accounting Standards emanating from the IASB. In addition, the legislative instrument chosen is the Regulation which, unlike the Directives, which require transposition, is directly applicable, general and national regulatory authorities and facilitates uniformity in its application. The acceptance of international accounting standards was a decision that will have great implications. Thus, the cousin a, more than 7,000 European companies will have to adapt their accounting standards to the new standards designed by the IASB and adopted by the Commission. On the other hand, these new rules introduce significant changes in aspects as important for the management of companies as provisions, consolidation, amortization of goodwill, market valuation of financial instruments or accounting of pension funds, among others. By this reason, the role traditionally assumed by both the directors of the entities and the auditors in the preparation of financial information will be modified. In the future, in the context of a relatively more open accounting framework, their responsibility for the information provided to the market by institutions and thus for the proper application of accounting standards will increase. The adoption of these new standards is undoubtedly a complex process, which is compounded by the scheduling difficulties arising from the fact that some of them, namely IAS 39, are still subject to consultation. Therefore, in order to facilitate the transition and add certainty to it, I would like to set out the main lines of the Bank of Spain's policy regarding these accounting standards, reaffirming, first of all, the unquestionable support that the two main objectives underlying the International Accounting Standards will receive. On the one hand, the consolidation of the financial market within the European Union, which will bring considerable advantages, and in the process of construction it is of enormous importance to ensure that market participants have access to a possible homogenization. On the other hand, the medium-term convergence between IAS standards and Anglo-American accounting standards, which offers the possibility of strengthening the integration of the international financial system. The recent corporate scandals, which have subjected accounting standards to review worldwide, offer an opportunity to make significant progress in this process of convergence. The IASB has been working hard to develop these standards and, as it has developed them, has subjected them to scrutiny by securities market regulators, accountants and other stakeholders. As a result of the comments received on the previously existing standards, the IASB decided as early as 2002 to initiate a process of improving existing IAS, including the rules relating to financial instruments, in order to reduce certain alternatives offered, as well as to eliminate the existence of redundancies and internal conflicts within the standards themselves. This process of improvements has been completed, partly in December 2003 and part in March of this year, so that, pending the resolution of some still relevant aspect, such as the fair value option, the set of rules to be applied in 2005 is already definitively completed. For its part, the European Union, maintaining the objective of applying the IAS since 1 January 2005, has to approve the changes that the IASB has developed since July 2003, the date on which, with the exception of the rules relating to financial instruments, it approved all the IAS existing at that time. From a supervisory point of view, accounting represents an essential piece of the regulatory and prudential framework of credit institutions. Accounting standards should facilitate the transparency and comparability of institutions and simultaneously In this way, they can contribute to the creation of a prudential framework that supports the stability of banking institutions, which is particularly desirable, taking into account the specific characteristics of the sector and especially the objective of protecting depositors. The experience of the espal supervisory model, which has been based on prudent accounting standards, has been positive and it is therefore appropriate to continue in the new IAS environment. Therefore, and given that the new European accounting regulation is a relatively open conceptual framework designed for all types of companies, it is necessary that its application in credit institutions takes into account the need to promote the strength of the banking system and financial stability. In our view, the IASB's recent proposal to explicitly recognise the role of the prudential supervisor in monitoring fair value estimates, as well as financial risk management policies and systems, is particularly noteworthy. In this new accounting regulatory environment, Banco de Espa, recognizing the benefits derived from this process of harmonization within the European Union, and in accordance with its competences in terms of accounting regulation of Spanish credit institutions, has decided to carry out a renewal of its current regulations, represented by Circular 4/91. Thus, Banco de Espa, with the aim of giving certainty to this complex process, is working on a new accounting circular compatible with IAS, although in those cases in which different alternatives are proposed in the International Accounting Standards, appropriate prudence will be chosen for the banking sector. The new accounting circular will facilitate several simultaneous objectives: first, entities, by adopting it, will be complying with the IAS regulation; Secondly, it will include the prudential options necessary in the recognition of the particularities operating under the same rules and, therefore, that the choice of accounting options is not a factor of distortion of competition between entities. Finally, the new accounting circular will allow the IAS criteria to be extended to all states; individual and consolidated, as well as reserved and plicos. The Banco de Espa will therefore offer both credit institutions and their auditors a framework for adapting to the IAS that combines, on the one hand, continuity with the special role played by accounting aspects in the Spanish banking supervision model and, on the other hand, a deep, homogeneous and coherent adaptation to the new European accounting framework represented by the IAS. Banco de Espa, as I mentioned, is working on this new circular and hopes to be in a position to discuss its content with the sector immediately. However, it must be reiterated that there are problems of delay in the approval of certain standards, mainly IAS 39, which are affecting the entire process of adoption of International Accounting Standards by the European Union. Despite this, we are in a position to advance some aspects about the direction of the new Circular in certain areas that we know concern the entities. I am not going to mention all the substantial changes or go into too much detail but, despite how dry it may be, I do think it is important to highlight some of those aspects. 1. Credit risk coverage. Provisions. The experience of the espal provisioning system, based on the specific, generic and statistical provisions, has been very positive. prudent of the world and that has required from the entities a superior effort to that of the competing companies at the international level. I also believe that it has contributed to the strength of our system and that, today, it has wide international recognition. As regards the current level of provisions and its periacy allocation regime, the Bank of Spain considers that, for the sector as a whole, the magnitude of the current figures is appropriate. The principles of its regulatory framework are also considered appropriate, primarily the need to promptly record impairments on assets, as well as the recognition that even portfolios that do not yet show impairment have an inherent risk, i.e. an expected loss, which needs to be provisioned in advance. Moreover, the compatibility of the framework currently in force with International Accounting Standards is reinforced by recent amendments to IAS 39, such as the obligation to when the loss has not been individually identified, the obligation of in all groups of loans, and not in the most impaired and the use of expert judgement in calculating levels. adequate provisi. 2. Associated companies and equivalence As mentioned above, the introduction of IAS will place greater responsibility on the part of both managers and auditors. The accounting treatment of associated enterprises is another example of the fact that their judgement is particularly important in the application of accounting standards. Thus, in the current regulations a series of presumptions of an objective nature are contemplated on the existence of actuality, in the Spanish regulations, those participations in listed entities greater than 3% are assumed under the method of putting in equivalence, threshold clearly lower than the 20% contemplated in the IAS. This important change implies that, in determining the existence or not of significant influence, subjective considerations become more relevant, which, however, must not be forgotten, already exist today. In any case, the entities must comply with the provisions of the commercial legislation in this regard and, in the future Circular, no quantitative criteria will be collected. However, in its application, Banco de Espa will objectify situations that show the existence of a notable influence through elements such as, for example, presence on boards (seniority in them, etc.) or active participation in the policies of the investee. The Bank of Spain will seek to facilitate the transition to the new system, as abrupt implementation could have important strategic and economic implications. 3. Classification of financial assets The classification of financial assets will not imply a particularly significant change with respect to the portfolios currently included in the Circular in force, there being small differences in the definition of the same and, especially, in the trading book. Within this aspect, the fair value option, included in the current IAS 39, is of special relevance, and which enables the entity to designate, from the moment of initial recognition, any financial instrument at fair value, recording the variations that occur in the income statement. Such is the relevance of this option that, in view of the opinions expressed mainly by the consultative period. This amendment limits its use to certain specific cases, reinforces the need for a reliable measure of fair value and, finally, recognises the role of supervisors in financial institutions. 4. Depreciation of goodwill Another change to which it is necessary to draw attention is that of the accounting of goodwill. The new accounting framework calls for the abolition of the obligation to depreciate, but an annual audit of the impairment loss is required. The importance of this verification of impairment loss and, above all, its potential impact should not be underestimated. In fact, the new accounting scheme may require the charging of all goodwill to be charged to the income statement of an a, if the annual audit results in a null value, without there also being the possibility of activating that depreciated goodwill later. In addition, it is not difficult to imagine situations in which there is a simultaneous deterioration of several goodwills, which would force them to be cleaned up in the income statement of the same year. In short, the proposed new regime may facilitate the initial absorption of goodwill, but the rigour required by the application of such a rule can greatly complicate the management of its deterioration. 5. Loan fees The IAS establishes the obligation to accrue the income from loan commissions that form an integral part of the effective interest rate, as well as the expenses directly attributable to its concession. This represents an important change with respect to the current Circular, which allows the accounting of the entire commission as income and does not contemplate the accrual of costs. additions related to the operation, will be distributed throughout the life of the loan, so that the periodic return of the operation is estimated in the income statement from the effective interest rate of the same and not through the contractual interest rate as, basically, occurs under the current Circular 4/91. However, from the point of view of the verification of the Bank of Spain, and in order to simplify procedures, we consider that in certain cases the presumption of the existence of a direct cost and, therefore, the non-need for accrualization can be introduced. This would be the case of moderate amounts, that is, those up to 0.20% of the nominal loan, with a maximum amount of db 300, in which the immediate recognition of the commission as an income in the income statement will be accepted, provided that it has been invoiced to the borrower. On the other hand, commissions above this amount should be accrued and if the entity considers that there are also costs higher than the aforementioned amount that must also be accrued, the estimate of the direct costs added must be justified by an analytical accounting of the entity. 6. The accounting of the OBS in the Savings Banks and Credit Cooperatives Allow me to finish this section, dedicated to the new accounting regulations, mentioning the accounting of the Social Work, an aspect very typical of our system. We consider, in this regard, that there is no reason to change the current accounting treatment when the allocations to the OBS are not mandatory. The new accounting circular will contemplate its accounting as an application of the benefit. The Basel Committee, as is well known, is developing a process of reform of the 1988 Capital Accord, which will lead to a New Agreement that will be a step forward in the design of prudential regulation, while making a determined commitment to promoting financial stability. This is based on the conviction that when banks are individually well capitalized and managed, they become more stable and have a greater capacity to successfully overcome adverse events. More importantly, when all institutions have the right incentives and maintain adequate capital levels, the financial system as a whole becomes more resilient, less responsive to cycle changes, and better able to support economic growth. With the aim of enhancing financial stability, the New Agreement has developed a broad set of mechanisms, many of them completely new, which are articulated through the joint action of the famous three pillars: minimum requirements, supervisory review and market discipline. Given that the structure of the New Agreement is well known to all of you, I will take advantage of my intervention today to update you on the important progress that has been made in the past few months, as well as on the most relevant aspects in relation to the imminent process of implementation of the Agreement. However, it should be remembered that Basel II will be the fruit of an intensive effort developed by the Committee over the past five years, during which time the permanent dialogue with industry, as well as with various organizations and academics, has been of great importance. This collaboration has been fundamentally reflected in a series of quantitative impact studies and advisory documents. I want to take this opportunity to show my appreciation for the participation of savings banks in this process. summer, and the approximately 200 comments received, first of all, the recognition of the industry about the improvements achieved with respect to the proposals presented previously. At the same time, a number of aspects, mainly of a technical nature, were identified about which there was a certain degree of concern. The Committee paid its utmost attention to the comments received and, in October 2003, at a meeting in Madrid, set out a plan to resolve the outstanding issues no later than the middle of this year. I will now briefly review the most important developments that have taken place since then. Treatment of expected and unexpected losses The proposal in CP3 regarding the treatment of credit risk losses in the internal models approach, known in Basel II as the IRB approach, implied that banks should hold capital to deal with both unexpected and expected losses. It was a compromise solution intended to alleviate the disadvantages arising from the existence of different accounting practices in terms of provisions. However, industry comments, as well as the Committee's own research work, have highlighted the need to change the approach initially adopted, so that the calculation of risk-weighted assets should only take into account the part of the calculations reached with the IRB that correspond to unexpected losses. Notwithstanding the above, it is necessary that institutions have the appropriate incentives to supply correctly. For this reason they have to compare the expected losses obtained through the IRB approach with the total provisions actually made: if the former are greater than the latter, there will be a shortfall in provisions, provisions must be deducted from capital, both basic and second-category, while excesses are considered eligible as second-category own resources, always with a maximum limit. Asset securitization One of the areas in which more progress has been made in the months and in which work continues to be done, is that of asset securitization. The comments received acknowledged the efforts made by the Committee in this area, but the proposal put forward at COP3 was described as excessively complex, while some concern was expressed about the high operational burdens related to its implementation. Given the very complexity of securitisation structures, their treatment in the New Deal should not be expected to be straightforward. Despite this, the Committee has intensified its work to address these potential problems identified in the so-called IRB approach to securitisation. Progress has been made in developing a more risk-sensitive treatment for certain exposures without credit ratings, albeit relatively low risk, in very specific securitisations. Thus, the Committee introduced the possibility of using a new method based on internal valuations of institutions themselves to determine the capital charges associated with liquidity lines provided in commercial paper securitisations. Progress has also been made in making the operational requirements of the approach used to calculate the expected loss on portfolios of credit rights that will subsequently be securitized, so as to facilitate the use of the supervisory fmula. Finally, some modifications have also been developed for credit rating exposures, which are aimed at reducing the asymmetries in the existing treatment for banks that originate the securitization and those that the calibration of risk weights in the RBA method goes through ensuring greater alignment with the level of risk inherent in those positions. Operational Risk As you all know, one of the modifications of the New Deal has been to require a portion of capital to cover operational risk separately. This advance aims, on the one hand, to recognize the efforts made by the industry to improve the measurement and control systems of operational risk, while rewarding entities that implement improvements in their measurement. The so-called internal measurement approach, or AMA in Basel II parlance, is the one that will be applied by the most advanced institutions and the one that will make it possible to achieve the objectives to which I referred earlier. However, the industry, mainly the largest internationally active institutions, has expressed concern about allocating capital requirements arising from the AMA approach among its subsidiaries located in different countries. In this regard, four principles have been published that aim to clarify allocation criteria and ease implementation efforts. The intention is to reduce the burden on those institutions that apply this approach between different jurisdictions, while respecting the legislation of different countries, which may require compliance with minimum standards. In general, further work is needed on coordination mechanisms between supervisors, group and subsidiaries, so that, while respecting everyone's responsibilities, these mechanisms are improved and that Basel II is properly applied to international banks. Risk mitigation With the aim of deepening the approximation of regulatory capital to economic capital, Basel II has recognized a wide range of risk mitigation techniques. Although a number of aspects remain open, significant progress has been made in recent months, despite which the treatment of risk mitigation must continue to evolve to reflect, to a greater extent, the practices developed by the industry. Let me remind you, however, that the Basel II approach is evolutionary, implying, among other things, that there will be areas to be considered as part of the Committee's future work. Planned timetable and implementation process It follows from my words that the more technically complex aspects arising from the comments received following COP3 have been resolved. Although some aspects are still being finalized, there is no doubt that the commitment made at the Madrid meeting is still fully valid: to have, by the middle of this year, a sufficiently established text to serve as a basis for the national implementation process, as well as for the industry to continue its efforts to successfully face the challenges implied by the New Agreement. Compliance with this objective is compatible with the date of implementation originally set, i.e. the end of 2006. With regard to the implementation of the New Agreement, it is necessary to remember that this is the responsibility of each country. In this area, the European Union must transform the Basel II recommendations into a legislative text. The New Agreement must therefore include a new Directive which will subsequently have to be transposed into national law. At present, the European Commission expects to be sent to the Council and the European Parliament in the first few months. In parallel to these developments that I have mentioned, the industry must redouble its efforts and implement investments in the necessary systems and processes. In order to ensure that the lack of certainty about the details of certain rules does not act as a disincentive mechanism, having a sufficiently agreed text by mid-2004 is important. It is not only the institutions that have to move in this direction, but the supervisors must also do so. The Committee itself has redoubled its efforts in this area and the Implementation Group has for two years allowed supervisors to exchange their experiences and methodologies, in such a way as to promote consistency in the application of the different approaches. In this sense, from the recognition that the different countries will be able to apply alternative approaches in compliance with the principles emanating from the New Agreement, what I think is really important is the exchange of views that, enhanced by pillar 2, will be developed between the different supervisors. In this area of cooperation between countries, I would like to mention in the process of organisational restructuring that banking supervision is undergoing in the European Union, the creation of the Committee of European Banking Supervisors (CEBS), whose basic objectives include contributing both to the consistent implementation of Community directives and to the convergence of supervisory practices between Member States. while encouraging the increase and improvement of cooperation between supervisors. In this context, at its first meeting, held in Barcelona, one of the main priorities of the CEBS was set as the implementation in Europe of Basel II, as well as the treatment of accounting issues and, in particular, those relating to the new International Accounting Standards, to which I referred earlier. The adaptation to these changes in the immediate future by the entities will require a significant effort, being necessary the implementation of internal processes that ensure an effective and complete transition to the new reality. Finally, I would like to refer to an aspect that is becoming increasingly important: the need to align the regulatory framework more closely with the accounting framework. This need for approximation is not only because the New Capital Arrangement has introduced a set of requirements on the need to provide information to the markets, but because there are other areas, such as the treatment of provisions and the valuation of financial instruments, where supervisors and those responsible for accounting standards should achieve a greater degree of approximation. The dialogue between the credit institution sector itself, supervisory bodies, and those responsible for designing accounting standards should continue and allow progress to be made in regulatory frameworks that facilitate financial stability without limiting or hindering the ability of financial systems to progress and innovate. Savings banks have a long history during which they have been able to adapt, rely on their strengths and overcome the challenges that technological, regulatory and economic changes have posed. I am convinced that in this occasion, in which the sector faces challenges on the three fronts mentioned, it will know how to live up to the task. Thanks a lot.

Tratamiento de las prdidas esperadas e inesperadas La propuesta recogida en el CP3 respecto al tratamiento de las prdidas por riesgo de crdito en el enfoque de los modelos internos, conocido en Basilea II como el enfoque IRB, implicaba que los bancos deban mantener capital para hacer frente tanto a las prdidas inesperadas, como tambin a las esperadas. Se trataba de una soluci de compromiso que pretenda de paliar los inconvenientes derivados de la existencia de diferentes prcticas contables en materia de provisiones. Sin embargo, los comentarios de la industria, as como el trabajo de investigaci desarrollado por el propio Comit, han puesto de manifiesto la necesidad de modificar el enfoque inicialmente adoptado, de tal modo que en el cputo de los activos ponderados por riesgo so se ha de tener en cuenta la parte de los clculos alcanzados con el IRB que correspondan a prdidas no esperadas.
