Por esta raz han de comparar las prdidas esperadas obtenidas a travs del enfoque IRB con el total de provisiones realmente efectuado: si las primeras son mayores que las segundas existir un defecto de provisiones provisiones han de deducirse del capital, tanto del bsico como del de segunda categora, mientras que los excesos se consideran elegibles como recursos propios de segunda categora, siempre con un lmite mximo. Titulizaci de activos Uno de los mbitos en el que ms se ha avanzado en los timos meses, y en el que se contin trabajando, es el de la titulizaci de activos. Los comentarios recibidos reconocieron el esfuerzo realizado por el Comit en esta materia, pero la propuesta planteada en el CP3 fue calificada de excesivamente compleja, al tiempo que se manifestun cierto grado de preocupaci por las elevadas cargas operativas relacionadas con su implementaci. Dada la propia complejidad de las estructuras de titulizaci, no se debera esperar que su tratamiento en el Nuevo Acuerdo fuera sencillo. A pesar de ello el Comit ha intensificado su trabajo para paliar estos posibles problemas detectados en el denominado enfoque IRB de titulizaci. Se ha avanzado en el desarrollo de un tratamiento ms sensible al riesgo para ciertas exposiciones sin calificaci crediticia, aunque de riesgo relativamente reducido, en titulizaciones muy concretas. As, el Comit ha introducido la posibilidad de emplear un nuevo mtodo basado en valoraciones internas de las propias entidades para determinar las cargas de capital asociadas a lneas de liquidez aportadas en las titulizaciones de papel comercial. Tambin, se ha avanzado en la flexibilizaci de los requerimientos operacionales del enfoque utilizado para el clculo de la prdida esperada en carteras de derechos de crdito que posteriormente sern titulizadas, de tal modo que se facilite el uso de la fmula supervisora. Finalmente, se han desarrollado tambin algunas modificaciones para las exposiciones con calificaci crediticia, que estn encaminadas a reducir las asimetras en el tratamiento existente para los bancos que originan la titulizaci y aquellos otros que la calibraci de las ponderaciones al riesgo en el mtodo RBA, pasa asegurar un mayor alineamiento con el nivel de riesgo inherente a esas posiciones. Riesgo Operacional Como todos ustedes saben, una de las modificaciones del Nuevo Acuerdo ha sido exigir una parte de capital para cubrir el riesgo operacional de forma separada. Este avance pretende, por una parte, reconocer los esfuerzos realizados por la industria para mejorar los sistemas de medici y control del riesgo operacional, al tiempo que premiar a las entidades que implementen mejoras en su medici. El denominado enfoque de las mediciones internas, o AMA en el lenguaje de Basilea II, es el que aplicarn las instituciones ms avanzadas y el que permitir en mayor medida alcanzar los objetivos a los que anteriormente me he referido. Ahora bien, la industria, principalmente las instituciones internacionalmente activas de mayor tama, ha expresado su preocupaci a la hora de asignar los requerimientos de capital surgidos del enfoque AMA entre sus filiales emplazadas en distintos pases. En este sentido, se han publicado cuatro principios que pretenden clarificar los criterios de asignaci y aliviar los esfuerzos de implementaci. La intenci es reducir la carga de aquellas instituciones que apliquen este enfoque entre diferentes jurisdicciones, al tiempo que se respete la legislaci de los distintos pases, que podrn exigir el cumplimiento de estndares mnimos. En general, es necesario seguir trabajando en los mecanismos de coordinaci entre supervisores, el del grupo y los de las filiales, de forma que, respetando las responsabilidades de todos, se mejoren dichos mecanismos y se permita una aplicaci adecuada de Basilea II a los bancos internacionales. Mitigaci de riesgos Con el objetivo de profundizar en la aproximaci del capital regulatorio al capital econico, en Basilea II se han reconocido un amplio conjunto de tcnicas de mitigaci de riesgos. Aunque permanecen abiertos una serie de aspectos, en los timos meses se han logrado significativos avances, a pesar de los cuales el tratamiento de la mitigaci de riesgos debe seguir evolucionando para reflejar, en mayor medida, las prcticas desarrolladas por la industria. Ahora bien, permtanme recordarles que el enfoque de Basilea II es evolutivo, lo que implica, entre otras cuestiones, que habr mbitos que han de considerarse como parte del trabajo futuro del Comit. Calendario previsto y proceso de implementaci De mis palabras se deduce que se han solucionado los aspectos tcnicamente ms complejos que se desprendan de los comentarios recibidos a raz del CP3. A pesar de que algunos aspectos estn todava cerrndose, no cabe duda de que el compromiso adquirido en la reuni de Madrid sigue plenamente vigente: disponer, a mediados de este a, de un texto suficientemente sido que sirva de base para el proceso de implementaci nacional, as como para que la industria contin sus esfuerzos para afrontar con xito los retos que implica el Nuevo Acuerdo. As pues, el Nuevo Acuerdo ha de recogerse un una nueva Directiva que, posteriormente, habr de transponerse a las propias legislaciones nacionales. En la actualidad, la Comisi Europea espera de, en los primos meses, ser enviada al Consejo y al Parlamento Europeo. En paralelo a estos desarrollos que he venido mencionado, la industria debe redoblar sus esfuerzos y poner en marcha las inversiones en los sistemas y procesos necesarios. A fin de que la falta de certidumbre sobre los detalles de ciertas normas no act como un mecanismo desincentivador, disponer de un texto consensuado suficientemente sido a mediados de 2004 es importante. No so las entidades han de avanzar en esta direcci, sino que los supervisores tambin hemos de hacerlo. El propio Comit ha redoblado sus esfuerzos en este terreno y el Grupo de Implementaci permite, desde hace dos as, que los supervisores intercambien sus experiencias y metodologas, de tal modo que se promueva la consistencia en la aplicaci de los distintos enfoques. En este sentido, desde el reconocimiento de que los diferentes pases podrn aplicar enfoques alternativos en el cumplimiento de los principios emanados del Nuevo Acuerdo, lo que creo realmente importante es el intercambio de puntos de vista que, potenciado por el pilar 2, se desarrollar entre los diferentes supervisores. En este mbito de la cooperaci entre pases, no querra dejar de mencionar, dentro del proceso de reestructuraci organizativa que la supervisi bancaria est viviendo en la Uni Europea, la creaci del Comit Europeo de Supervisores Bancarios (CEBS), que tiene entre sus objetivos bsicos el contribuir tanto a la ejecuci consistente de las Directivas comunitarias como a la convergencia de las prcticas supervisoras entre los estados miembros, al tiempo que fomentar el incremento y la mejora de la cooperaci entre supervisores. En este contexto, en su primera reuni, celebrada en Barcelona, se fijcomo una de las principales prioridades del CEBS la aplicaci en Europa de Basilea II, as como el tratamiento de las cuestiones contables y, en particular, las referentes a las nuevas Normas Internacionales de Contabilidad, a las que anteriormente me he referido. La adaptaci a estos cambios en el futuro inmediato por parte de las entidades exigir un importante esfuerzo, siendo necesaria la puesta en prctica de los procesos internos que aseguren una transici eficaz y completa a la nueva realidad. Para finalizar, querra referirme a un aspecto que cada da cobra una mayor importancia: la necesidad de alinear en mayor medida el marco regulatorio con el contable. Esta necesidad de acercamiento no so se debe a que en el Nuevo Acuerdo de Capital se hayan introducido un conjunto de requerimientos sobre la necesidad de aportar informaci a los mercados, sino porque existen otros mbitos, como el tratamiento de las provisiones y la valoraci de los instrumentos financieros, en los que los supervisores y los responsables de la normativa contable deberamos alcanzar un mayor grado de acercamiento. El dilogo entre el propio sector de las entidades de crdito, los organismos supervisores, y los responsables del dise de las normas contables deber continuar y permitir avanzar en marcos regulatorios que faciliten la estabilidad financiera sin limitar o dificultar la capacidad de los sistemas financieros de progresar e innovar. Las Cajas de ahorro tienen una larga trayectoria durante la cual han sabido adaptarse, apoyarse en sus puntos fuertes y superar los desafos que los cambios tecnolicos, regulatorios y de entorno econico han planteado. Title: Closing Conference: XI Meeting of the financial sector: "Management strategies in a context of profound changes in business models", Madrid
text: XI Meeting of the financial sector Management strategies in a context of profound changes in business models. 28 April 2004 Closing Conference Jaime Caruana. Governor of the Bank of Spain In its eleventh edition, the celebration of the meeting of the financial sector has allowed, once again, a fruitful exchange of ideas about the central aspects that affect the financial markets. My first words are therefore congratulations to the organizers and participants, as well as thanks for their kind invitation to participate in this meeting. Throughout these two days, important aspects have been pointed out that, given the changes produced in business models, must be taken into consideration in the design of successful management strategies. In the design of these strategies, it must be borne in mind that, in recent decades, the physiognomy of the economic and financial environment in which we live has changed substantially. Although the changes in the financial system are numerous, allow me simply to mention some of those that, in my opinion, are most relevant. Firstly, there has been a greater internationalisation of financial institutions, both in terms of the fundraising process and in terms of their asset instruments. Undoubtedly, this phenomenon is part of a growing process of financial globalization that, having generally benefited the countries that participate in it, implies new challenges. Suffice it to recall how the increased interrelationships between actors operating in different markets contributes to the fact that disturbances can spread very quickly, including phenomena of low probability, but with very negative potential consequences. Secondly, the significant technological advances that have occurred in recent years have made it possible to develop increasingly sophisticated and complex products based on previously unthinkable data processing. Perhaps the most representative example is the derivative products that, apart from other considerations, have allowed investors to better manage both their portfolios and the risks associated with their operations. In particular, the development of credit derivatives as well as asset securitisation has allowed important advances in the transfer of credit risk, without forgetting those other mechanisms, increasingly important, that allow the transfer of market and operational risks. Thirdly, the changes that have occurred in financial systems and the increasing complexity with which they have been operating, have highlighted the importance of a set of risks that until not long ago it was not possible to quantify or were simply treated as a cost. Operational risk, those associated with off-balance sheet operations and reputational are three examples and, given their growing importance, I will refer to them in a little more detail later. Finally, and this is an aspect that specifically affects Spain, it must not be forgotten that our integration into an area of stability, such as the euro zone, has led to profound positive changes in the behaviour of our economy, while providing our financial system with a framework for action that offers more opportunities. In fact, by enabling Spanish credit institutions to go to the European financial markets in better conditions and assuming fewer risks, not only has the internationalization of Spanish banks been favored, but the financing of credit growth and expansion processes such as the one we are currently experiencing has been facilitated, alleviating the potential tensions associated with the fact that this credit expansion has not been accompanied by dynamism. analogue of tanks. This does not imply, however, that the rapid growth of credit that has been observed in Spain, in an environment of low interest rates, does not require prudent and responsible action on the part of credit institutions, since it is not possible to rule out that at some point throughout the cycle there will be a return to a context of rates more in line with what would indicate both European historical experience and the prospects for economic recovery. Likewise, the return to more sustainable growth figures in mortgage credit also poses business challenges for Spanish entities that should not be underestimated. In my speech today, however, I do not intend to address short-term issues, but rather to raise some elements that should integrate the strategic response that we must all offer in order to promote financial stability in a world not without risks. This response must occur at three levels. First, on the part of financial institutions, which with a vision not short-term, but of medium and long term, must have management strategies that allow them, on the one hand, to know their clients adapting, among other issues, to their needs, and their ability to assume risks, and, on the other, to have solid risk management systems, incorporated into the usual decision-making processes and based on efficient corporate governance structures, which respond to the best standards of integrity and prudence. This good risk management must be supported by a strategy of own resources that, depending on the profile of risks assumed, guarantees its slack and quality throughout an economic cycle and especially in the most difficult moments of it. The second level at which a response must occur is that of banking regulators and supervisors, who must promote the financial stability of the system, encouraging innovation and improving the financial services offered to society as a whole. To this end, I believe that regulation and supervision must be based on the introduction of appropriate incentive systems and try to avoid excessive interventionism. Third, on the part of consumers, from those who, in a world in which there is no zero probability or zero risk, can expect an active attitude in the analysis of the information relevant to the understanding of the products and financial investments they have to undertake. Acknowledging the effects on institutions of responses from regulators and supervisors, as well as from consumers, let me now refer to them in a little more detail. The response of the entities Financial institutions, as I mentioned earlier, must offer a strategic response based both on the knowledge of their customers and on a solid and prudent risk management, adopting, in the design of that strategic response, a medium and long-term vision. In any business activity, knowledge of the client, their needs and constraints, is of vital importance in the design of management strategies. Credit institutions should not only be aware of the preferences and characteristics of consumers of financial products, but they also have a key role to play in enabling consumers to correctly assess the risks they assume in relation to their degree of risk tolerance and their ability to assume risk. This is necessary, especially in sophisticated liability and investment products, but also in asset products, where it is necessary to carefully assess the capacity to meet the future commitments that have been acquired, especially in a context of rapid credit expansion and low interest rates, such as the one currently experienced in Spain. The knowledge of banking customers by the entities presents, however, a second dimension, which in recent years has received greater attention from different supervisory bodies at international level, including that of the Bank of Spain. I am referring to the need for financial institutions to ensure, to the best of their ability, that the banking services offered by them are not used in the development of illicit activities which, even without their knowledge, could promote, in particular, money laundering or the financing of terrorism. We live in a varied and complex world, not without risks. These risks are also present, even more intensely, in the development of banking activity, to the extent that, rightly, it is stated that they are its very essence. In the development of banking activity, a broad and differentiated set of strategies have been developed that aim to understand, measure, limit and control risk, in short, incorporate risk into decision-making processes, so that the premiums applied to the various products and services incorporate the corresponding measure of the associated risk. A common element in all entities is that it has become aware that proper management inexorably involves the provision of the necessary technical and human resources to identify risks and quantify the exposures involved. The necessary investment in systems and human capital poses the additional challenge of doing so without jeopardizing the continuous improvement of the entity's efficiency necessary to strengthen the income statement. In recent years, there have been significant advances in risk measurement and management systems, which supervisors must recognize and encourage by providing the right incentives. Nevertheless, there is a need to further develop such measurement and management systems, while recognizing that, while the main banking risks remain credit risks and those associated with fluctuations in financial markets, significant changes in the financial system have intensified the importance of other risks that were traditionally not quantified or addressed, Simply, as a cost. It is not my intention to address in detail what these types of risks are, but I would like to mention three that, as I have already advanced, are of particular relevance. First, operational risk, which has received increased attention from major banks, to be treated as a distinct and proprietary risk class, rather than as a residue arising after credit and market risk are taken into account. These efforts have led to the considerable development of operational risk measurement and management mechanisms, although there is still a long way to go. Secondly, the growing importance of off-balance sheet transactions, that is, those in which balances representing rights, obligations and other legal situations are included that, in the future, may have financial repercussions, as well as those balances that are necessary to reflect all the operations of an entity, even if they do not compromise its assets. Managers of institutions need to pay particular attention to them, as many of the activities recorded here, such as contingent liabilities, guarantees or forward transactions, incorporate risks that are not always easy to assess. Finally, I would like to emphasise that the recent international scandals in the business world highlight the growing importance of reputational risk. A factor that has been frequently repeated in these international scandals has been the excessively complex and non-transparent organizational structure of the companies involved, which have employed vehicle companies domiciled in opaque jurisdictions. The operations carried out under these conditions also contribute to promoting operational risk and, logically, hinder the appropriate knowledge of the clientele to which I have just referred as essential on the part of the entities. In any case, the foregoing highlights the importance of having organizational structures that provide transparency and the necessary mechanisms so that information, knowledge and, in general, the risk culture of the entity flow in an agile way among all its members. Moreover, proper risk management will not be possible without the implementation of good corporate governance, the implementation of which will be the ultimate responsibility of the top management of the entities, which must advocate a healthy, prudent and transparent management of them. Finally, allow me to say a few words about the importance of an adequate time horizon in business management. I have previously pointed out that, in strategic design, it is essential that both incentive systems, for example remuneration, and control and management mechanisms are designed and aligned with a medium and long-term orientation. An incentive structure or a business vision excessively close to the short term, such as a continuous and excessive concern about the next profit figure to be published, can lead to costly strategic mistakes in the medium term. Likewise, the absence of an adequate evaluation of the changes in economic conditions that usually occur throughout a cycle can induce excessively pro-cyclical behavior. Suffice it to recall that, although risks tend to materialize in the slowdown phases, banks' credit policy mistakes tend to be made in the expansionary phases of the cycle, when the prevailing optimism leads to the relaxation of the requirements of the credit policies practiced by the entities. That said, it is difficult to separate the cyclical elements from the genuinely structural improvements, for example, in the case of the Spanish system, I think it is fair to recognize that the low delinquency that is registering, is not only based on the fact that the slowdown of the cycle in our economy has been very moderate and has occurred in an environment of very favorable monetary conditions, It must also be attributed to the significant improvements in risk management implemented by our entities, something for which they are to be congratulated. The response of regulators and supervisors Today, there is widespread recognition of the benefits of a stable functioning of the financial system. Regulators and supervisors are firmly committed to preserving and, furthermore, promoting financial stability. This commitment must be compatible with an action that stimulates a permanent improvement of the financial system, so that it continues to improve the services it provides to society. This requires a certain balance that avoids imposing unnecessary burdens on financial institutions or excessive interventionism that introduces organisational barriers that hinder financial innovation. Moreover, regulators and supervisors need to assess a given policy not only in the light of the expected benefits but also in the light of its costs. Let me remind you that such considerations have been present at all times throughout the process of gestation of the New Basel Capital Accord. Suffice it to recall, in this regard, the intensive efforts and rigorous analyses implemented by the Committee with the aim of preventing the proposed measures from generating, for example, procyclical effects, by making it difficult for credit to flow to the real economy during recessionary phases, or that such measures could have perverse implications as regards the granting of financing to small and medium-sized enterprises. The main mission entrusted to us today by regulators and banking supervisors is to create the appropriate incentive systems, systems that are not only compatible but reinforce positive market incentives. A good example of incentive-based regulation is the New Capital Deal, which seeks to approximate regulatory capital and economic capital. Undoubtedly, a greater link between regulatory capital and the level of risk borne by an entity provides an incentive for managers to improve their risk measurements. This incentive will be reinforced to the extent that, as future regulation envisages, institutions are allowed to use their own calculations and, based on a set of general parameters defined by regulators, determine the level of capital requirements associated with their risks. Indeed, as we all know, Basel II proposes several alternatives to institutions for the calculation of regulatory capital related to credit risk, from the application of a standard system based on external credit ratings to the possibility of using internal rating systems, designed by the entity itself. However, it seems to me that there is a tendency to underestimate the set of requirements necessary for an entity to be able to use the most advanced approaches or even to be interested in doing so. These advanced approaches, internal credit rating systems, are not just a set of more or less complex formulas that allow a better calculation of regulatory capital; Qualitative requirements are very important in aspects such as data collection, the design of internal rating systems, in their validation and maintenance, but, above all, in the aspects of corporate governance and effective use of systems. In summary, not all entities should aspire, at least in the short term, to use advanced approaches, nor is it even obvious that these are the best solution for small or medium-sized entities or whose degree of sophistication in terms of products or markets in which they operate is high. In any case, those who already have some experience in risk-focused management and perform economic capital calculations and decide to take the step of going to the advanced approaches of Basel II, have to be aware of the investments in technology, human capital and organization that may be necessary are important. Finally, it should not be forgotten that the minimum capital required of institutions is not designed to cover all the risks they face. For this reason, financial institutions are expected to recognise the strategic dimension of a medium-long term own resources policy, and maintain a level of capital above the regulatory minimum, with supervisors having the necessary capacity to require them to operate with additional capital. This process requires continuous dialogue between institutions and supervisors and facilitates the establishment of appropriate incentives for institutions to make their internal assessments based on the best standards. However, recognising the importance of the level of capital, let me simply mention other significant aspects, such as the importance of the quality and composition of own resources and also the need for a prudent and early pre-capital provisioning system. The regulatory and supervisory framework must be based on a broad approach and based on several pillars that act together. Today, it is particularly important that prudential regulation and supervision is supported by the disciplinary effect played by the markets, collaborating, in this sense, in the generation of the appropriate incentives for bank managers to behave judiciously in terms of risk management. To this end, analysts, minority shareholders, depositors and holders of debt, whether subordinated or not, must have the capacity to evaluate institutions, and it is necessary for this to have sufficient transparency of information on the part of the entities. In other words, institutions must publish within a reasonable period of time that information, both quantitative and qualitative, that enables financial market participants to make such assessments, information that must not only be reliable, but also relevant and based on generally accepted valuation principles. From what has been said so far, many will have recognized some of the principles that inspire the New Capital Accord, which will undoubtedly be a step forward in prudential regulation, contributing significantly to promoting financial stability. Let me now make a few thoughts on the response that consumers must offer in order to promote the proper functioning of the financial system. Consumer response Today, banking customers face a wide range of complex financial products and services, offered by a large number of entities. In this context, they are expected to be proactive in the search for information that allows them to make their decisions from the assessment of the different alternatives available to them. Consumers of financial products and services must also bear in mind that in our system there are a set of mechanisms designed with the aim of defending their legitimate interests, such as the existence of a guarantee fund that covers deposits made by customers, up to a limit of 20,000 euros. However, to the extent that the amounts are higher than those I have just referred to or more complex products are used, such as subordinated or structured debt, it is necessary for consumers to increase their efforts to achieve sufficient knowledge of the risk profile of the product and the operation being carried out. In short, in a world in which zero risk does not exist, consumers must seek to have the necessary information that allows them to make their decisions responsibly, taking into account, in addition, that the conditions, both their personal, and the economy in general, can change over time, so they have to assume debt levels according to both their present ability to pay, as with the estimate for the future, considering for it different potential scenarios. Such an attitude on the part of consumers requires not only that they have access to information, but also that they have sufficient capacity to understand the products offered to them, as well as the consequences of the commitments made. Entities have a fundamental role, to the extent that they have to offer them those products that suit their needs, while contributing to their availability of the necessary information and helping them understand the products and investments that are offered. Well-informed consumers are necessary for the efficient functioning of the market and for the maintenance and improvement of a good individual reputation of the financial institution and the sector as a whole. In short, entities must assume their mission of knowing, informing, educating and advising their customers. I believe that we can all contribute to this work. The Banco de Espa96a therefore intends to promote the education of users of banking services through the development of a project through the Internet, of which I hope its first phase will be operational at the beginning of 2005. And again the entities Let me say my last words about some challenges that banks will face in the short term that have strategic implications. The New Basel Capital Accord will, and indeed is exerting, considerable influence over them. Moreover, changes in accounting rules will pose strategic challenges for institutions. It is not my intention to address now the changes that will be introduced by the adaptation of the Spanish accounting framework to International Accounting Standards, an issue that I already dealt with in some detail last week in my participation in the Ordinary General Assembly of the ECSC and that we focused on trying to add certainty and prudential criteria to the process. I would, however, like to conclude my speech by referring, as an example of the impact of accounting standards on the strategic decisions of institutions, to two specific aspects of International Accounting Standards: the treatment of associated companies and that of consolidation goodwill. In the accounting treatment of associated companies, the current regulations contemplate a series of presumptions of an objective nature about the existence of significant influence, an issue that will change in the future framework of IAS. Currently, in Spanish regulations, those participations in listed corporations greater than 3% are assumed under the equity method, a threshold clearly lower than the 20% contemplated in the IAS. This important modification implies that, when determining the existence or not of significant influence, subjective considerations become more relevant, which, however, must not be forgotten, already exist today. The Bank of Spain will not include in its accounting-prudential standard any quantitative criteria; however, in its application, the Banco de Espa96a will take into account, in the most objective way possible, those situations that show the existence of a notable influence through different elements. As regards the treatment of consolidation goodwill, the new accounting framework calls for the abolition of the obligation to write it down until there is an impairment to be verified annually. I would like to reiterate the need not to underestimate the importance of this impairment loss check and, above all, its potential impact. The rigor required by the application of a rule such as this can greatly complicate the management of situations of impairment of goodwill. Conclusion Let me conclude by pointing out that the Spanish financial system has been able to face important challenges in recent years and therefore deserves our recognition and confidence that it will also know how to face present and future challenges, preserving its important contribution to growth and the improvement of its services to Spanish society. This requires a strategic response from all of us: entities, regulators and supervisors, and consumers. Thank you very much for your attention.
