De este modo, aunque la trayectoria reciente y las perspectivas sobre la evolucin en el futuro prximo de la economa espaola son ms favorables que las del conjunto de la UEM, los retos que tiene planteados no son de una naturaleza muy distinta. En particular, nuestra economa requiere, como la europea, un aumento de la productividad que exige algunos cambios en su patrn de especializacin y mejoras progresivas en la calidad de los factores que emplea en los procesos productivos. Adems, tal y como ocurre en la mayor parte de los pases europeos, Espaa debe realizar un esfuerzo para seguir incrementando la intensidad de utilizacin del factor trabajo, a pesar de que sta ha crecido en los ltimos aos de manera muy superior a la media de la UE. Debe recordarse, en este sentido, que la economa espaola mantiene tasas de participacin y de empleo inferiores a las de los principales pases de la UE y una evolucin demogrfica que le exige prestar una atencin especial al equilibrio financiero de su sistema pblico de pensiones. Por lo tanto, desde la perspectiva de nuestro pas, no resulta difcil identificarse con la demanda de polticas reformadoras por parte de las autoridades europeas que estn a la altura de la importancia de los problemas que deben afrontar. En las circunstancias actuales no caben actitudes pasivas ya que la Unin Europea parece cada vez menos capaz de mantener incrementos continuados del bienestar colectivo si no logra aumentar la eficiencia de su economa y lograr un uso ms intenso de sus recursos disponibles. Al contrario de lo que en ocasiones se ha defendido, no tengo ninguna duda de que estos objetivos resultan perfectamente compatibles con la estructura de las preferencias de los ciudadanos europeos, y creo algo exagerado el peso que algunos dan a la idea de que los europeos ponderan el ocio y la cohesin social en mayor medida que los habitantes de otras reas. De hecho, la preservacin del bienestar colectivo puede exigir reformas de aquellos aspectos del funcionamiento de los mercados, el sistema fiscal o los esquemas de proteccin que distorsionan las decisiones individuales y reducen artificialmente la demanda de empleo y la participacin y, de este modo, dificultan tanto la prosperidad econmica como la sostenibilidad de los mecanismos pblicos de apoyo a los sectores sociales ms vulnerables. Creo pues que preservar exige reformar y el mejor momento es ahora. El momento actual resulta particularmente propicio para que las autoridades incrementen el grado de ambicin de sus programas reformadores. En primer lugar, la Unin Europea cuenta con un instrumento muy til, como es el conjunto de compromisos y objetivos establecidos por el Consejo Europeo de Lisboa en la primavera del 2000. En aquel momento, las autoridades europeas disearon una estrategia encaminada a lograr unos objetivos muy ambiciosos. La experiencia muestra que habr que reorganizar prioridades y mejorar los mecanismos para que las polticas se lleven a cabo a nivel nacional de forma efectiva, pero tambin creo que los elementos bsicos de estrategia siguen siendo validos y necesarios. Entre ellos cabe destacar el diseo de reformas estructurales que favorecieran la competitividad y la innovacin, el desarrollo de polticas dirigidas a fortalecer la sociedad de la informacin y los gastos en inversin y desarrollo, la culminacin del mercado interior, el perfeccionamiento del capital humano y, todo ello, en un entorno de estabilidad macroeconmica. Pero, adems, en los aos transcurridos de la presente dcada ha continuado el proceso de globalizacin de la economa internacional y han surgidos nuevas reas de expansin que han supuesto una intensificacin de las presiones competitivas en las que se desenvuelve la economa mundial y que supusieron la principal motivacin de los acuerdos de Lisboa. Asimismo, los avances en el mbito de las nuevas tecnologas de la informacin y de las comunicaciones, tras una breve pausa en los primeros aos de la presente dcada, parecen haber retomado su dinamismo. Finalmente, los signos de recuperacin que viene mostrando la economa europea en el ltimo ao, tras un prolongado perodo de escaso crecimiento deben contribuir a impulsar reformas que pudieran resultar ms costosas en un entorno de atona de la actividad y el empleo. La confluencia de todos estos factores hacen prever que la revisin de los avances realizados en la Agenda de Lisboa, que se ha de llevar a cabo en la primavera del ao prximo sirva de reflexin sobre el origen de los retrasos acumulados y revitalice el debate en torno a las condiciones necesarias para que la UE supere sus deficiencias estructurales y de este modo, incremente su capacidad para competir en los mercados internacionales como frmula para elevar progresivamente el bienestar colectivo. Parte de esta Agenda est dedicada a las reformas necesarias en sistema financiero y me gustara terminar con dos reflexiones sobre este aspecto. El papel de un sector financiero eficiente en la correcta asignacin de recursos y por tanto en la consecucin de un mayor crecimiento potencial es muy relevante y aunque los progresos en materia de integracin a nivel de la Unin Europea han sido notables, debemos seguir trabajando para reducir la fragmentacin de los mercados financieros, que sigue siendo un factor de desventaja competitiva de la economa europea. El segundo comentario se refiere a la importante reforma en la regulacin bancaria que supondr la nueva directiva sobre capital, una vez que el Comit de Supervisin Bancaria de Basilea ha presentado Basilea II y se inicia la fase de adopcin de la regulacin a nivel nacional. Basilea II supone un nuevo enfoque regulador mucho mas completo al estar basada en reforzar los incentivos de mercado para la mejora de la gestin de riesgos. Concretamente a travs de sus tres pilares, requerimientos de capital ms sensibles al riesgo, supervisin coordinada y mayor transparencia, no solo se consiguen establecer niveles adecuados de capital, sin que tambin, y esto es una gran innovacin respecto al acuerdo de 1988, se establecen incentivos para que las entidades bancarias continen con su proceso de mejora en la gestin de riesgo. El resultado ser un sistema financiero ms slido y estable que ser capaz de contribuir de forma ms eficaz al crecimiento de la economa en su conjunto. Muchas gracias

Title: Governor's Appearance: Committee on Economy and Finance of the Congress of Deputies
text: Madrid, 30 June 2004 Appearance of the Governor of the Bank of Spain Commission of Economy and Finance of the Congress of Deputies. Jaime Caruana Governor Ladies and gentlemen, I would like to begin by expressing my satisfaction at appearing once again before this Committee. I believe that these hearings contribute significantly to achieving the transparency with which central banks must act, as a necessary complement to the autonomy with which we carry out the functions entrusted to us, particularly when they are integrated into an institutional scheme as complex as that of the European Economic and Monetary Union. As is traditional at this time, the Annual Report for 2003 has just been presented to the Governing Council of the Banco de Espa96a and it is therefore a good time to reflect on the situation of the Spanish economy and its medium-term prospects, with particular attention to the monetary policy of the Eurosystem. which is relevant to our economy. We are now in the sixth year of existence of the European Economic and Monetary Union, of which Spain has been part since its establishment. The establishment of the single currency on 1 January 1999 meant, as you know, that the common monetary policy for the area would eventually be determined by the Governing Council of the European Central Bank d0 which is the decision-making body of the Eurosystem d0 taking into account the situation and needs of the area as a whole. The monetary and financial conditions in which the Spanish economy operates d0 the level of short- and long-term interest rates and the exchange rate d0 are therefore determined by the economic evolution and prospects of EMU. Over the past three years, activity in the euro area has shown little dynamism. While some economies, notably the United States, were more willing to overcome the depressive shocks that hit the global economy at the beginning of the decade, EMU was highly vulnerable to such shocks, despite the expansionary nature of macroeconomic policies on both sides of the Atlantic. In particular, the Eurosystem gradually relaxed the tone of its monetary policy, so that, between mid-2001 and mid-2003, key interest rates were reduced by a cumulative amount of 275 basis points, to 2%, which is the minimum level reached by interest rates in Europe in recent decades and at which they have been remained until now. European countries' fiscal policies also helped to moderate external depressive effects, as automatic stabilisers generally played their role in dampening cyclical swings. However, in some countries, the expansionary stance of fiscal policies during previous periods of expansion did not allow them to accumulate the necessary room for manoeuvre to be able to respond adequately to the impact of the economic slowdown on the budget, leading to the emergence of excessive deficits and non-compliance with the discipline rules agreed at European level, This has made the management of budgetary policy extremely complicated. These imbalances have also opened a debate on the appropriateness or content of fiscal rules which, from the Eurosystem's point of view, I consider unfocused and inopportune, since fiscal discipline is an essential ingredient for the proper functioning of a monetary union and the existing rules are generally appropriate. It also diverts the debate on weak growth in monetary union from what I believe should be at the heart of it, namely the structural weaknesses in the functioning of the European economy and the necessary reforms to improve its long-term growth capacity. Despite the expansionary tone of the policies implemented, the first signs of recovery that began to be felt in the main economies of the euro zone in the middle of last year came from the impulses received from abroad. The return of the world economy and markets to high growth rates made it possible to compensate - at least partially - for the significant appreciation accumulated by the euro during 2002 and 2003 and stimulated the growth of European exports. Domestic demand and, in particular, private consumption remained, however, a depressed tone, in line with the pessimism shown by the indicators of confidence in families and companies. Throughout 2003 and as 2004 progresses, the recovery of the world economy has been based, basically, on the strong growth recorded in the United States and the exceptional dynamism of the Chinese economy, although Japan and other emerging countries are also contributing to the shaping of a more favourable international environment. It is foreseeable that these areas will continue to boost world trade in the near future, which will favor the recovery of European economies. The situation, however, is not without uncertainties, insofar as notorious imbalances persist that have not been corrected d0 such as the existence of high external and public deficits in the United States, or the symptoms of overheating that can be seen in the Chinese economy. The increases that are taking place in the price of oil and other raw materials, as a result of geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and the pressure on demand in some of the aforementioned economies, are another factor of uncertainty about the intensity and extent that the current cyclical recovery phase may reach. In this situation, the euro area's performance during the first quarter of 2004 has been generally encouraging. Real GDP growth has been 0.6%, in quarter-on-quarter terms, a figure that can be considered close to what would be the potential expansion of the area's economy. In addition, growth is on a relatively diversified basis, since the positive contribution of net exports is compounded by some improvement in private consumption and investment. The Eurosystem's assessment of the outlook for the area as a whole is moderately optimistic. The recovery will advance gradually and to finish settling down it needs to eliminate the elements of uncertainty and lack of confidence that are conditioning the spending decisions of families and companies. In addition, there may be significant differences in the pace of recovery across economies. For example, domestic demand continues to show considerable weakness in Germany, where the burden of the recovery continued to be based on the pull of foreign trade; in France and Italy, however, private consumption has begun to gain greater vitality. In the field of inflation, the harmonised index of consumer prices has risen significantly in recent months, bringing its annual growth rate to 2.5% in May, above the definition of price stability established by the European Central Bank, which, as you know, corresponds to a rate close to, but less than, 2%. The increase in inflation is related to the sharp rise in oil prices and its year-on-year rate of change has been exacerbated as a result of the price declines that took place in the same months last year. Although, as I have already said, higher oil prices open up new uncertainties about price developments and the recovery of European economies, the impression is that, in principle, the effects in terms of inflation and growth of the price increases observed so far will be moderate. The inflation rate in the euro area is therefore expected to return to levels consistent with the definition of price stability in the near future. For this reason, the Governing Council of the European Central Bank has not substantially changed its diagnosis of the situation in recent months and has maintained key interest rates at 2%. In any case, in situations such as this, monetary policy must remain vigilant, because there is a danger that increases in prices that are, in principle, transitory, end up being incorporated into the process of income formation in economies, and become more persistent. It is therefore to be expected that the financial conditions prevailing in the area as a whole will continue to support the recovery process that is already under way, but without compromising price stability. This is ultimately, as you all know, the commitment and main objective of the Eurosystem, and is based on the belief that maintaining macroeconomic stability is a necessary condition for achieving a path of sustained growth. The monetary policy implemented by the ECB therefore plays a fundamental role in macroeconomic management and is the focus of all its efforts on this, but we should also be aware of its limitations. The ECB's monetary policy has changed its tone in recent years so that monetary and financial conditions have adapted to the cyclical weakness of all the economies in the area, bringing interest rates to historically low levels, which are very favourable to promote agents' spending. But monetary policy cannot solve the confidence or structural problems afflicting many European economies, which cannot be solved through further monetary easing, but through measures to provide EMU with more effective mechanisms to respond flexibly to shocks and to build confidence in its ability to grow. On the fiscal front, it is imperative that countries engaged in excessive deficit procedures meet their commitments and correct these imbalances as soon as possible. The recovery that is beginning to manifest itself must be used in that direction. In addition, the European authorities must address the medium-term problems affecting their public finances, taking the necessary measures to ensure that social protection mechanisms are consistent with the financial capacity of public administrations, in a context of population ageing. Finally, it should be noted that the structural reform agenda has been very limited in recent years, since the ambitious objectives set at the Lisbon Council, planned for 2010, have not been matched in practice with the appropriate decisions and seem, at present, difficult to achieve. Ladies and gentlemen, it is in this context and in this environment of economic policies that we must analyse the evolution and prospects of the Spanish economy, to which I shall now refer. Faced with the hesitant nature of the recovery in EMU, the Spanish economy has maintained a comparatively high real growth rate over the last few years. In the first quarter of 2004, the annual rate of change in GDP was 2.8 per cent, extending the period of moderate expansion already observed last year, after overcoming a cyclical low in the second half of 2002. Thus, the growth differential with respect to the euro area has been above 1.5 percentage points in recent quarters. Although the recovery trend observed over the past year was associated, to some extent, with the expansion of the world economy, the main element that has continued to sustain Spanish growth in the most recent period has been domestic demand. The factors that explain the good performance of the Spanish economy are not new, but have been operating for several years. They originate, on the one hand, in the favourable monetary and financial conditions d0 in terms of low interest rates, high rates of credit expansion and revaluation of wealth d0 which have characterized, with greater or lesser intensity, the entire period of membership of the monetary union, since the end of the previous decade. These comfortable financial conditions, operating in a context of macroeconomic stability and fiscal discipline, have provided a solid and firm foundation for the expansion of domestic spending. On the other hand, mention should be made of the good performance of supply policies, which have allowed a relatively flexible response of output and, above all, employment to the expansion of demand, reinforcing it and limiting price pressures. Fiscal policy has maintained a stabilizing tone d0 thanks to which it reached a surplus of 0.3% of GDP in 2003 d0 which could be made compatible with the introduction of a reform of personal income tax that has been boosting the growth of household disposable income. In this situation, the Spanish economy grew throughout 2004 with a growth pattern similar to that of previous years, based, fundamentally, on household consumption d0 which has even accentuated its rate of increase d0 and activity in the construction sector, although, in this case, with a slight slowdown trend in recent months. The strength of residential investment stands out, which, like that of consumption, continues to be sustained by the strength of disposable income and the gains in wealth d0 financial and non-financial d0 of households. As for the rest of the investment, public works are supporting the progress of construction and certain signs of recovery continue to be seen in the productive investment of companies. This is possibly the most relevant and hopeful fact of recent months since, so far, business investment has maintained a very moderate tone linked, possibly, to the financial consolidation in which some business groups are immersed and to the uncertainty that still surrounds the process of economic recovery in Europe. The notable strength of domestic demand in the first months of the year has been offset by the negative contribution of net foreign demand, as a result of the increase in imports. Exports have managed to maintain a growth rate close to that of their markets, despite the losses in competitiveness induced by the past appreciation of the euro. The most recent data show no signs that anticipate sudden changes in the trends that can be seen in the Spanish economy in the first half of 2004 and that I have just commented; provided, of course, that the world economy maintains the expected tone of recovery. The impact of the recent increases in oil prices should not seriously affect our growth rate, although, in the short term, the incidence of a shock of this nature affects the Spanish economy more than other European economies, as a result of their greater energy dependence. We have already seen this in the resurgence experienced by inflation rates, which has revealed the persistence of some upward biases. In any case, if these tensions do not worsen, Spanish GDP growth can be expected to remain close to 3% in 2004 and 2005, a value that is close to what can be considered its potential growth rate and that could give continuity to the process of real convergence. Despite these favourable prospects, further progress in real convergence in the medium term, beyond 2005, should be supported by a pattern of growth different from the current one, which depends less on the components of expenditure that have driven the growth of demand in the past and relies more on those that contribute most to raising productive potential, such as investment and export. It should be borne in mind that the prolongation over time of the growth scheme that the economy has been following involves some risks that derive, fundamentally, from the losses of competitiveness that have been incubating since our entry into EMU and the persistence of some trends that may compromise the financial balance of companies and families. These are risks whose effects could also be exacerbated by the return to more neutral monetary conditions or by a possible decrease in the generation of employment in the economy. The losses in competitiveness have their origin, both in the positive inflation differential and in the slow growth of productivity. The inflation rate experienced a downward trend throughout 2003, which lasted until last March, when it reached 2.1%. Since then, however, the impact of recent oil price rises and the pick-up in food prices have led to a further significant rise in the rate of price increase, so that the narrowing in the spread with the euro area that had been achieved could not be consolidated. it has once again widened towards the percentage point level, where it has been, on average, since the start of monetary union. This inflation differential has resulted in higher cost growth in Spain and, in particular, wages, to which the collective bargaining system endows with a certain inertial behavior, which ends up having an impact on new price increases. Higher wage growth in Spain, compared to the euro area, has affected different sectors of the economy differently. The sectors most exposed to external competition, which cannot sustain systematically higher price increases than their competitors, have had to compensate for higher wage growth in various ways. At the outset of monetary union, reductions in the financial burden resulting from interest rate declines provided sufficient scope to accommodate higher wage increases; Subsequently, however, operating margins began to suffer and a downward adjustment in employment has already begun to be observed in some industrial branches, reflecting a reaction to generate productivity gains as a means of lowering unit costs. In the most protected sectors, however, insufficient competitive pressure in some markets continues to allow higher costs to be covered by price increases that are contributing to the maintenance of the inflation differential. The adjustment that the sectors most open to competition have begun to undertake is also due to the low growth that productivity has been registering in the Spanish economy, following a pattern that it shares with most European economies. The causes are diverse and the diagnosis complex. On the one hand, it is indisputable that wage moderation and labour market reforms in the nineties led to a pattern of employment-intensive growth, which was d0 and still is d0 necessary to increase the economy's per capita income. However, it must be recognized, on the other hand, that, together with this positive aspect, this behavior also reflects the difficulties that have been incubated as a result of the low rate of growth of productive investment, which has not allowed more permanent increases in productivity, by limiting the growth of the capital stock and the incorporation of new technologies. Another risk that has been emerging during the long expansion of domestic demand is related to the rapid growth of debts incurred by both non-financial corporations and households. It is true that this increase in indebtedness has been accompanied by a revaluation of the assets of these sectors d0 so that their net worth, in fact, has continued to grow d0 and that it has not led to an excessive increase in the debt burden in proportion to their income, thanks to the low levels of interest rates. In this way, the increase in the financial balance sheets of companies and households must be interpreted, above all, as the adjustment of these sectors to more stable financial conditions, so it does not represent a problem in itself. But this should not hide the fact that the increase in debt itself and the changes in the composition of assets and liabilities, with equities among the former, and variable-rate loans, among the latter, make the financial position of companies and households more sensitive to any adverse disturbance or to a possible tightening of monetary conditions. In the case of households, moreover, the increase in indebtedness is closely linked to the notable increase in house prices in recent years, a sector in which there is evidence that, as often happens in its expansionary stages, a certain overvaluation has been reached that needs to be absorbed through a prompt moderation of the increases that continue to be registered. to avoid future corrections that could affect the spending capacity of the sector. I believe, ladies and gentlemen, that we are at a moment of great importance for the future of our economy, which will face major challenges in the coming years. The European Union is transforming into an increasingly large economic area, forcing the Spanish economy to compete with new countries that have productive structures relatively similar to ours. To address these challenges, policies that remain under the control of national authorities have important tasks to play in strengthening competitiveness and ensuring adequate control of domestic demand. To strengthen competitiveness, it is necessary to improve those aspects of the process of cost and price formation that encourage its inertial growth. In the field of wage formation, the collective bargaining system should be adapted, since the current design tends to favour the fixing of wage increases that are too homogeneous. The defence of competitiveness requires that wage behaviour be as close as possible to the specific conditions of firms and workers, so that it is more closely linked to productivity. It would also be desirable to decouple wage developments from external shocks affecting inflation, unlike what is currently the case with wage review clauses, which reinforce the persistence of inflationary shocks. On the other hand, the proper functioning of distribution channels and the promotion of competitive behaviour in product markets are aspects that can facilitate the absorption of price tensions. In this respect, the regulation on retail trade should be aimed at promoting competition and avoiding market partitioning. To achieve a more productive economy, through an expansion of its growth potential, not only requires the return to higher investment rates, which allow the renewal of the stock of physical capital and the incorporation of new technologies, as well as greater investment in human capital, it is also necessary to promote a more efficient and competitive behavior of some markets that are fundamental, from network industries to the labour market itself. With regard to the latter, in addition to the reform of collective bargaining, it is necessary to continue with measures aimed at reducing the duality created by the high rate of temporary employment, with a view to providing greater stability to employment, which favours investment in human capital. I think it is important to emphasise that these reforms should not only not result in less flexibility in this market, but on the contrary, they should be used to introduce additional elements of flexibility. For its part, developments in the housing market highlight the need to introduce some reforms that increase the flexibility of supply and help moderate episodes of price increases. Specifically, a less restrictive regulation of the land market and a relaxation of the procedures for disposing of building land, as well as a promotion of the rental market are actions that contribute to stabilizing the price of housing. I would like to conclude my speech by underlining the fundamental role of fiscal policy in establishing a stable economic framework that promotes growth, both in the short and long term. I believe, ladies and gentlemen, that the good results achieved by the Spanish economy in the most recent period cannot be explained without the help of disciplined fiscal action, which has actively contributed to maintaining an environment of macroeconomic stability. Spain is among the few countries that have fulfilled the fiscal commitments acquired in the Stability and Growth Pact and that have reached a fiscal position "close to balance or in surplus". In the current situation, given the slack that characterizes the monetary and financial conditions of the countries of the euro zone, it is not only European commitments, but the very stability of the Spanish economy and long-term challenges, which determine the need for fiscal policy to continue adopting a strict tone. In this regard, I would like to reiterate that, as I had occasion to explain in my appearances before the Congressional Budget Committee and the Senate Budget Committee last year, it may be appropriate for fiscal policy to deepen the stabilizing role it has been playing. This requires further improvement in the balance of public accounts, currently in surplus, since the action of the automatic stabilization mechanisms, by itself, cannot be considered sufficient to play the stabilizing role of domestic demand that is needed in the current circumstances. In the longer term, the challenges that Spanish finances will have to face in various areas d0 such as those arising from the ageing of the population d0 advocate the generation of surpluses in public accounts. In this sense, the systematic contribution of resources to the pension reserve fund is an important line of action that must be maintained with determination and constancy. The discipline of public finance requires the collaboration of all administrations that make up the public sector. In this sense, the growing weight of regional governments d0 both in terms of income and expenditure d0 makes their commitment to the transparency of their actions and to the individual monitoring and set of the budgetary discipline rules in force in our country acquire extraordinary importance. Ladies and gentlemen, I indicated earlier that we are at a moment of great importance for the future of our economy. The Spanish economy has reduced its differences in income and welfare with the countries of the European Union in the last 10 years; However, the continuation of this convergence process requires that the aforementioned risks and challenges be adequately addressed without delay. If we fail to do so, we run the risk that we will slowly lose the comparative advantage of recent years and in a monetary union the way out of this situation may be longer and more costly than in the past. Thanks a lot.
text_original: Madrid, 30 de junio de 2004 Comparecencia del Gobernador del Banco de Espaa Comisin de Economa y Hacienda del Congreso de los Diputados. Jaime Caruana Gobernador Seoras: Quisiera empezar expresando mi satisfaccin por comparecer una vez ms ante esta Comisin. Creo que estas comparecencias contribuyen significativamente a alcanzar la transparencia con la que los bancos centrales han de actuar, como complemento necesario de la autonoma con la que desempeamos las funciones que tenemos encomendadas, particularmente cuando estn integrados en un esquema institucional tan complejo como el de la Unin Econmica y Monetaria Europea. Como es tradicional en estas fechas, se acaba de presentar ante el Consejo de Gobierno del Banco de Espaa el Informe Anual del ao 2003 y es un buen momento, por tanto, para reflexionar sobre la situacin de la economa espaola y sus perspectivas a medio plazo, con especial atencin a la poltica monetaria del Eurosistema, que es la relevante para nuestra economa. Nos encontramos ya en el sexto ao de existencia de la Unin Econmica y Monetaria Europea, de la que Espaa forma parte desde su constitucin. El establecimiento de la moneda nica el 1 de enero de 1999 supuso, como sus seoras saben, que la poltica monetaria comn para la zona pasara a estar determinada, en cada momento, por el Consejo de Gobierno del Banco Central Europeo que es el rgano rector del Eurosistema- , atendiendo a la situacin y a las necesidades del conjunto del rea. Las condiciones monetarias y financieras en las que se desenvuelve la economa espaola el nivel de los tipos de inters a corto y largo plazo y del tipo de cambio- vienen determinadas, por tanto, por la evolucin y perspectivas econmicas de la UEM. En los tres ltimos aos, la actividad en la zona euro ha dado pruebas de un escaso dinamismo. Mientras que algunas economas en particular, Estados Unidos mostraron una mayor disposicin para superar los shocks de carcter depresivo que afectaron a la economa mundial al comienzo de la dcada, la UEM manifest una elevada vulnerabilidad frente a esas perturbaciones, a pesar del carcter expansivo adoptado por las polticas macroeconmicas a uno y otro lado del atlntico. En particular, el Eurosistema fue relajando paulatinamente el tono de su poltica monetaria, de modo que, entre mediados de 2001 y mediados de 2003, los tipos de inters oficiales se redujeron por una cuanta acumulada de 275 puntos bsicos, hasta situarse, desde el da 6 de junio del pasado ao, en el 2%, que es el nivel mnimo alcanzado por los tipos de inters en Europa en las ltimas dcadas y en el que han permanecido hasta ahora. La poltica presupuestaria de los pases europeos tambin contribuy a moderar los efectos depresivos externos, ya que, en general, los estabilizadores automticos desempearon su papel amortiguador de las oscilaciones cclicas. Sin embargo, en algunos pases, la orientacin expansiva de las polticas fiscales durante los perodos de expansin anteriores no permiti acumular el margen de maniobra necesario para poder responder adecuadamente al impacto de la desaceleracin econmica en el presupuesto, lo que les condujo a la aparicin de dficit excesivos y al incumplimiento de las normas de disciplina acordadas en el mbito europeo, lo que ha complicado extraordinariamente la gestin de la poltica presupuestaria. Esos desequilibrios han abierto, adems, un debate sobre la conveniencia o el contenido de las reglas fiscales que, desde el punto de vista del Eurosistema, considero desenfocado e inoportuno, pues la disciplina fiscal es un ingrediente esencial para un funcionamiento adecuado de una unin monetaria y las normas vigentes resultan, en general, apropiadas. Adems desva el debate sobre el dbil crecimiento de la unin monetaria de lo que en mi opinin debera ser el centro del mismo, es decir, las debilidades estructurales del funcionamiento de la economa europea y las necesarias reformas que mejoren su capacidad de crecimiento a largo plazo. A pesar del tono expansivo de las polticas instrumentadas, los primeros signos de recuperacin que comenzaron a percibirse en las principales economas de la zona euro a mediados del pasado ao provenan de los impulsos que se reciban del exterior. El retorno de la economa y los mercados mundiales a tasas de crecimiento elevadas permiti compensar -al menos, parcialmente- la significativa apreciacin acumulada por el euro durante 2002 y 2003 y estimul el crecimiento de las exportaciones europeas. La demanda interna y, en especial, el consumo privado mantuvieron, sin embargo, un tono deprimido, en lnea con el pesimismo que mostraban los indicadores de confianza de familias y empresas. A lo largo de 2003 y a medida que avanza el ao 2004, la recuperacin de la economa mundial se ha ido asentando, bsicamente, en el fuerte crecimiento que se registra en Estados Unidos y en el excepcional dinamismo de la economa China, aunque Japn y otros pases emergentes estn contribuyendo tambin a la configuracin de un entorno internacional ms favorable. Es previsible que estas reas sigan impulsando los intercambios mundiales en el futuro prximo, lo que favorecer la recuperacin de las economas europeas. La situacin, sin embargo, no est exenta de incertidumbres, en la medida en que persisten notorios desequilibrios que no han sido corregidos como la existencia de elevados dficit exterior y pblico en Estados Unidos, o los sntomas de recalentamiento que se aprecian en la economa china. Las alzas que se estn produciendo en el precio del petrleo y de otras materias primas, como consecuencia de las tensiones geopolticas de Oriente Medio y de la presin de la demanda de algunas de las economas citadas son otro factor de incertidumbre sobre la intensidad y la extensin que pueda alcanzar la fase de recuperacin cclica actual. En esta situacin, los resultados de la zona euro durante el primer trimestre de 2004 han sido, en general, esperanzadores. El crecimiento del PIB real ha sido del 0,6%, en trminos intertrimestrales, una cifra que puede considerarse prxima a lo que sera la expansin potencial de la economa del rea. Adems, el crecimiento se asienta en unas bases relativamente diversificadas, pues, a la contribucin positiva de las exportaciones netas hay que aadir una cierta mejora en el consumo privado y en la inversin. La valoracin que se hace desde el Eurosistema sobre las perspectivas para el conjunto del rea es moderadamente optimista. La recuperacin avanzar gradualmente y para acabar de asentarse necesita que se vayan eliminando los elementos de incertidumbre y falta de confianza que estn condicionado las decisiones de gasto de familias y empresas. Adems, puede haber diferencias apreciables en el ritmo de recuperacin de las distintas economas. As, por ejemplo, la demanda interna contina dando muestras de una debilidad considerable en Alemania, donde el peso de la recuperacin sigui basndose en el tirn del comercio exterior; en Francia e Italia, sin embargo, el consumo privado ha empezado a cobrar una mayor vitalidad. En el terreno de la inflacin, el ndice armonizado de precios de consumo ha registrado un repunte significativo en los ltimos meses, que ha situado su tasa de crecimiento interanual en el 2,5% en el mes de mayo, por encima de la definicin de estabilidad de precios establecida por el Banco Central Europeo, que, como ustedes saben, se corresponde con una tasa prxima, pero inferior, al 2%. El aumento de la inflacin est relacionado con la brusca subida de los precios del petrleo y su ritmo de variacin interanual se ha visto agudizado como consecuencia de los descensos de precios que tuvieron lugar en los mismos meses del pasado ao. Aunque, como ya he dicho, el encarecimiento del petrleo abre nuevas incertidumbres sobre la evolucin de precios y la recuperacin de las economas europeas, la impresin es que, en principio, los efectos en trminos de inflacin y crecimiento de las alzas de precios observadas hasta ahora sern moderados. Se espera, por tanto, que la tasa de inflacin de la zona euro vuelva a situarse en niveles compatibles con la definicin de estabilidad de precios en un futuro cercano. Por ello, el Consejo de Gobierno del Banco Central Europeo no ha modificado sustancialmente en los meses recientes su diagnstico de la situacin y ha mantenido los tipos de inters oficiales en el 2%. En cualquier caso, en situaciones como esta, la poltica monetaria debe permanecer vigilante, pues existe el peligro de que aumentos en los precios que tienen, en principio, un carcter transitorio, terminen incorporndose al proceso de formacin de rentas de las economas, y se hagan ms persistentes. Cabe esperar, por tanto, que las condiciones financieras que prevalezcan en el conjunto de la zona sigan favoreciendo el proceso de recuperacin que ya est en marcha, pero sin comprometer la estabilidad de precios. Este es en ltimo trmino, como todos ustedes saben, el compromiso y el objetivo principal del Eurosistema, y se basa en el convencimiento de el mantenimiento de la estabilidad macroeconmica es una condicin necesaria para alcanzar una senda de crecimiento sostenida. La poltica monetaria instrumentada por el BCE tiene, por tanto, un papel fundamental en la gestin macroeconmica y a ello encamina todos sus esfuerzos, pero tambin conviene que seamos conscientes de sus limitaciones. La poltica monetaria del BCE ha ido modificando su tono en los ltimos aos para que las condiciones monetarias y financieras se fueran adaptando a la posicin de debilidad cclica del conjunto de economas del rea, hasta situar los tipos de inters en unos niveles histricamente bajos, muy favorables para promover el gasto de los agentes. Pero la poltica monetaria no puede resolver los problemas de confianza o de naturaleza estructural que aquejan a muchas economas europeas, que no pueden solucionarse a travs de una mayor relajacin monetaria, sino mediante la adopcin de medidas que permitan dotar a la UEM de unos mecanismos ms eficaces para responder con flexibilidad a las perturbaciones y para generar confianza en su capacidad de crecimiento. En el mbito fiscal, es imprescindible que los pases inmersos en procedimientos de dficit excesivo hagan frente a sus compromisos y corrijan esos desequilibrios a la mayor brevedad. La recuperacin que empieza a manifestarse debe aprovecharse en esa direccin. Adems, las autoridades europeas deben afrontar los problemas de medio plazo que aquejan a sus finanzas pblicas, adoptando las medidas necesarias para asegurar que los mecanismos de proteccin social sean coherentes con la capacidad financiera de las Administraciones Pblicas, en un contexto de envejecimiento de la poblacin. Finalmente, es preciso destacar que la agenda de reformas estructurales ha tenido un desarrollo muy limitado en los ltimos aos, ya que los ambiciosos objetivos fijados en el Consejo de Lisboa, previstos para 2010, no se han visto correspondidos en la prctica con las decisiones oportunas y parecen, en el da de hoy, difciles de alcanzar. Seoras, es en este contexto y en este entorno de polticas econmicas donde debemos analizar la evolucin y perspectivas de la economa espaola, a las que paso a referirme a continuacin. Frente al carcter vacilante de la recuperacin en la UEM, la economa espaola ha mantenido un ritmo de crecimiento real comparativamente elevado a lo largo de los ltimos aos. En el primer trimestre de 2004, la tasa de variacin interanual del PIB ha sido del 2,8%, prolongando la etapa de moderada expansin que ya se observ durante el pasado ao, tras superar un mnimo cclico en la segunda mitad de 2002. De esta forma, el diferencial de crecimiento respecto al rea del euro se ha situado, en los ltimos trimestres, por encima de 1,5 puntos porcentuales. Aunque la tendencia a la recuperacin observada a lo largo del pasado ao estuvo asociada, en alguna medida, a la expansin de la economa mundial, el principal elemento que ha seguido sustentando el crecimiento espaol en el perodo ms reciente ha sido la demanda interna. Los factores que explican el buen comportamiento de la economa espaola no son nuevos, sino que han estado operando desde hace varios ejercicios. Tienen su origen, por un lado, en las favorables condiciones monetarias y financieras en trminos de bajos tipos de inters, tasas elevadas de expansin crediticia y revalorizacin de la riqueza que han caracterizado, con mayor o menor intensidad, toda la etapa de pertenencia a la unin monetaria, desde finales de la dcada anterior. Estas condiciones financieras holgadas, al operar en un contexto de estabilidad macroeconmica y disciplina fiscal han proporcionado una base slida y firme a la expansin del gasto domstico. Por otro lado, hay que mencionar el buen resultado de las polticas de oferta, que han permitido una respuesta relativamente flexible del producto y, sobre todo, del empleo ante la expansin de la demanda, reforzndola y limitando las presiones sobre los precios. La poltica fiscal ha mantenido un tono estabilizador gracias al cual alcanz un supervit del 0,3% del PIB en 2003, que pudo compatibilizarse con la introduccin de una reforma del IRPF que ha estado impulsando el crecimiento de la renta disponible de los hogares. En esta situacin, la economa espaola avanza a lo largo de 2004 con un patrn de crecimiento similar al de los aos anteriores, basado, fundamentalmente, en el consumo de los hogares que incluso han acentuado su ritmo de aumento y la actividad del sector de la construccin, aunque, en este caso, con una ligera tendencia a la desaceleracin en los meses ms recientes. Destaca la fortaleza que conserva la inversin residencial, que, como la del consumo, contina sustentndose en la solidez de la renta disponible y en las ganancias de riqueza financiera y no financiera de las familias. En cuanto al resto de la inversin, la obra pblica est respaldando al avance de la construccin y se continan apreciando ciertos signos de recuperacin en la inversin productiva de las empresas. Este es, posiblemente, el hecho ms relevante y esperanzador de los ltimos meses ya que, hasta ahora, la inversin empresarial ha mantenido un tono muy moderado ligado, posiblemente, al saneamiento financiero en el que se encuentran inmersos algunos grupos empresariales y a la incertidumbre que an rodea al proceso de recuperacin econmica en Europa. La notable firmeza de la demanda interna en los primeros meses del ao se ha visto compensada por la aportacin negativa de la demanda exterior neta, como consecuencia del incremento de las importaciones. Las exportaciones han conseguido mantener un ritmo de crecimiento prximo al de sus mercados, a pesar de las prdidas de competitividad inducidas por la pasada apreciacin del euro. En los datos ms recientes no se aprecian signos que anticipen cambios bruscos en las tendencias que se aprecian en la economa espaola en esta primera mitad del ao 2004 y que acabo de comentar; siempre, claro est, que la economa mundial mantenga el tono de recuperacin previsto. El impacto de las recientes subidas del precio del petrleo no tendra que afectar de forma grave a nuestro ritmo de crecimiento, aunque, a corto plazo, la incidencia de un shock de esta naturaleza afecta ms a la economa espaola que a otras economas europeas, como consecuencia de su mayor dependencia energtica. Esto hemos podido apreciarlo ya en el rebrote que han experimentado las tasas de inflacin, que ha puesto de manifiesto la persistencia de algunos sesgos alcistas. En cualquier caso, si estas tensiones no se agravan, cabe esperar que el crecimiento del PIB espaol se mantenga prximo al 3% en 2004 y 2005, un valor que est en el entorno de lo que puede considerarse su ritmo de crecimiento potencial y que podra dar continuidad al proceso de convergencia real. A pesar de estas perspectivas favorables, la consecucin de nuevos avances en la convergencia real en el medio plazo, ms all del ao 2005, deber apoyarse en un patrn de crecimiento diferente al actual, que dependa menos de los componentes del gasto que han impulsado el avance de la demanda en el pasado y se apoye ms en aquellos otros que ms contribuyen a elevar el potencial productivo, como la inversin y la exportacin. Debe tenerse en cuenta que la prolongacin en el tiempo del esquema de crecimiento que viene siguiendo la economa supone algunos riesgos que se derivan, fundamentalmente, de las prdidas de competitividad que se han ido incubando desde nuestra entrada en la UEM y de la persistencia de algunas tendencias que pueden comprometer el equilibrio financiero de empresas y familias. Son riesgos cuyos efectos podran verse agudizados, adems, por la vuelta a unas condiciones monetarias ms neutrales o por una eventual disminucin de la generacin de empleo de la economa. Las prdidas de competitividad tienen su origen, tanto en el diferencial positivo de inflacin como en el lento avance de la productividad. La tasa de inflacin experiment una trayectoria descendente a lo largo de 2003, que se prolong hasta el pasado mes de marzo, cuando lleg a situarse en el 2,1%. A partir de ese momento, sin embargo, la incidencia de las alzas recientes del precio del petrleo y el repunte de los precios alimenticios han determinado una nueva y significativa subida de la tasa de aumento de los precios, de manera que el recorte en el diferencial con la zona del euro que se haba conseguido no ha podido consolidarse, sino que ha vuelto a ampliarse hacia la cota del punto porcentual, nivel en el que se ha situado, por trmino medio, desde el inicio de la Unin Monetaria. Ese diferencial de inflacin se ha traducido en un mayor crecimiento de los costes en Espaa y, en particular, de los salarios, a los que el sistema de negociacin colectiva dota de un cierto comportamiento inercial, que termina repercutiendo en nuevas alzas de precios. El mayor crecimiento de los salarios en Espaa, en comparacin con el rea del euro, ha afectado de forma diferente a los distintos sectores de la economa. Los sectores ms expuestos a la competencia externa, que no pueden mantener aumentos de sus precios sistemticamente ms elevados que los de sus competidores han tenido que compensar el mayor crecimiento salarial por distintas vas. Al inicio de la unin monetaria, las reducciones de la carga financiera a que dieron lugar los descensos de los tipos de inters proporcionaron un margen suficiente para acomodar los mayores incrementos salariales; posteriormente, sin embargo, se empezaron a resentir los mrgenes de explotacin y ya ha comenzado a observarse en algunas ramas industriales un ajuste a la baja del empleo, que refleja una reaccin para generar ganancias de productividad como medio de abaratar los costes unitarios. En los sectores ms protegidos, en cambio, la insuficiencia de la presin competitiva en algunos mercados sigue permitiendo que el encarecimiento de los costes se cubra con aumentos de precios que estn contribuyendo al mantenimiento del diferencial del inflacin. El ajuste que han empezado a emprender los sectores ms abiertos a la competencia se debe tambin al bajo crecimiento que ha venido registrando la productividad en la economa espaola, siguiendo una pauta que comparte con la mayor parte de las economas europeas. Las causas son diversas y el diagnostico complejo. Por un lado, es indiscutible que la moderacin salarial y las reformas del mercado de trabajo de los aos noventa dieron lugar a un patrn de crecimiento intensivo en empleo, que era y sigue siendo necesario para incrementar la renta per capita de la economa. Sin embargo, hay que reconocer, por otro lado, que, junto a esta vertiente positiva, este comportamiento refleja tambin las dificultades que se han incubado como consecuencia del reducido ritmo de crecimiento de la inversin productiva, que no ha permitido aumentos de la productividad de carcter ms permanentes, al limitar el crecimiento del stock de capital y la incorporacin de nuevas tecnologas. Otro de los riesgos que han ido emergiendo durante la etapa de larga expansin de la demanda interna est relacionado con el rpido crecimiento de las deudas contradas tanto por las empresas no financieras como por los hogares. Es cierto que este aumento del endeudamiento ha venido acompaado de una revalorizacin de los activos de estos sectores de forma que su patrimonio neto, de hecho, ha seguido creciendo y que no ha supuesto un incremento excesivo de la carga de la deuda en proporcin con su renta, gracias a los bajos niveles de los tipos de inters. De esta manera, el incremento de los balances financieros de empresas y familias debe interpretarse, sobre todo, como el ajuste de estos sectores a unas condiciones financieras ms estables, por lo que no representa por si mismo un problema. Pero ello no debe ocultar que el propio incremento de la deuda y los cambios en la composicin de activos y pasivos, con ms peso de la renta variable, entre los primeros, y de los crditos a tipo de inters variable, entre los segundos, hacen que la posicin financiera de empresas y familias sea ahora ms sensible frente cualquier perturbacin adversa o ante un eventual endurecimiento de las condiciones monetarias. En el caso de las familias, adems, el aumento del endeudamiento est estrechamente ligado al notable aumento que han experimentado los precios de las viviendas en los ltimos aos, un sector en el que existe evidencia de que, como suele ocurrir en sus etapas expansivas, se ha alcanzado una cierta sobrevaloracin que es necesario absorber mediante una pronta moderacin de las alzas que se siguen registrando, para evitar correcciones futuras que pudieran afectar a la capacidad de gasto del sector. Creo, seoras, que nos encontramos en un momento de gran importancia para el futuro de nuestra economa, que se ha de enfrentar en los prximos aos a retos importantes. La Unin Europea se est transformando en un espacio econmico cada vez ms amplio, que obliga a la economa espaola a competir con nuevos pases que tienen unas estructuras productivas relativamente parecidas a las nuestras. Para encarar estos retos, las polticas que se mantienen bajo el dominio de las autoridades nacionales tienen importantes tareas que desempear para fortalecer la competitividad y asegurar el adecuado control de la demanda interna. Para reforzar la competitividad es necesario mejorar aquellos aspectos del proceso de formacin de costes y precios que incentivan su crecimiento inercial. En el terreno de la formacin de los salarios, habra que adaptar el sistema de negociacin colectiva, ya que el diseo actual tiende a favorecer la fijacin de incrementos salariales demasiado homogneos. La defensa de la competitividad requiere que el comportamiento salarial se aproxime en la mayor medida posible a las condiciones especficas de las empresas y de los trabajadores, de manera que est ms estrechamente vinculado a la productividad. Asimismo, sera conveniente desligar la evolucin salarial de las perturbaciones externas que afectan a la inflacin, al contrario de lo que sucede en la actualidad con las clusulas de revisin salarial, que refuerzan la persistencia en las perturbaciones inflacionistas. Por otra parte, el buen funcionamiento de los canales de distribucin y el fomento de un comportamiento competitivo en los mercados de productos son aspectos que pueden facilitar la absorcin de las tensiones de precios. A este respecto, la regulacin relativa al comercio minorista debe estar orientada a favorecer la competencia y a evitar la compartimentacin del mercado. Para conseguir una economa ms productiva, a travs de una ampliacin de su potencial de crecimiento, no slo se requiere el retorno a tasas de inversin ms elevadas, que permitan renovar el stock de capital fsico y la incorporacin de nuevas tecnologas, as como una mayor inversin en capital humano, tambin es preciso fomentar un comportamiento ms eficiente y competitivo de algunos mercados que resultan fundamentales, desde las industrias de red al propio mercado de trabajo. En relacin con este ltimo, adems de la reforma de la negociacin colectiva es necesario continuar con los medidas tendentes a reducir la dualidad creada por la elevada tasa de temporalidad, con vistas a proporcionar una mayor estabilidad al empleo, que favorezca la inversin en capital humano. Creo importante destacar que estas reformas no slo no deberan redundar en una menor flexibilidad de este mercado, si no que por el contrario, deberan aprovecharse para introducir elementos adicionales de flexibilidad. Por su parte, la evolucin del mercado de la vivienda pone de manifiesto la necesidad de introducir algunas reformas que aumenten la flexibilidad de la oferta y ayuden a moderar los episodios de alzas de precios. En concreto, una regulacin menos restrictiva del mercado del suelo y una flexibilizacin de los trmites para disponer de terreno edificable, as como una promocin del mercado de alquiler son actuaciones que contribuir a estabilizar el precio de la vivienda. Quisiera finalizar mi intervencin subrayando el papel fundamental que tiene la poltica fiscal en el establecimiento de un marco econmico estable que promueva el crecimiento, tanto a corto como a largo plazo. Creo, seoras, que los buenos resultados alcanzados por la economa espaola en el perodo ms reciente no pueden explicarse sin el concurso que ha prestado una accin fiscal disciplinada, que ha contribuido activamente a mantener un entorno de estabilidad macroeconmica. Espaa se encuentra entre los pocos pases que han cumplido con los compromisos fiscales adquiridos en el Pacto de Estabilidad y Crecimiento y que han alcanzado una posicin fiscal "prxima al equilibrio o en supervit". En la coyuntura actual, dada la holgura que caracteriza a las condiciones monetarias y financieras de los pases de la zona euro, no son slo los compromisos europeos, sino la propia estabilidad de la economa espaola y los retos a largo plazo, los que determinan la necesidad de que la poltica fiscal siga adoptando un tono estricto. En este sentido me gustara reiterar que, como tuve ocasin de exponer en mis comparecencias ante la Comisin de Presupuestos del Congreso y ante la Comisin de Presupuestos del Senado, el ao pasado, puede ser conveniente que la poltica fiscal profundice en el papel estabilizador que viene desempeando. Ello requiere profundizar en la mejora del saldo de las cuentas pblicas, en este momento en supervit, ya que la actuacin de los mecanismos de estabilizacin automtica, por s sola, no puede considerarse suficiente para desempear el papel estabilizador de la demanda interna que se necesita en las actuales circunstancias. A ms largo plazo, los retos a los que en diversos mbitos debern hacer frente las finanzas espaolas como los derivados del envejecimiento de la poblacin abogan por la generacin de excedentes en las cuentas pblicas. En este sentido, la aportacin sistemtica de recursos al fondo de reserva de las pensiones es una lnea de actuacin importante que se debe mantener con determinacin y constancia. La disciplina de las finanzas pblicas requiere la colaboracin de todas las administraciones que integran el sector pblico. En este sentido, el creciente peso que tienen los gobiernos autonmicos tanto en la vertiente de ingresos como de gastos hace que su compromiso en la transparencia de su actuacin y en el seguimiento individual y conjunto de las reglas de disciplina presupuestaria vigentes en nuestro pas adquiera una importancia extraordinaria. Seoras, indiqu anteriormente que nos encontramos en un momento de gran importancia para el futuro de nuestra economa. La economa espaola ha recortado en los ltimos 10 aos sus diferencias de renta y bienestar con los pases de la Unin Europea; sin embargo, la continuidad de este proceso de convergencia requiere que sin demora se enfoquen adecuadamente los riesgos y retos antes mencionados. Si no lo logramos, corremos el riesgo de que lentamente perdamos la ventaja comparativa de estos ltimos aos y en una unin monetaria la salida de esta situacin puede ser ms larga y costosa que en el pasado. Muchas gracias.

Title: Opening Speech: IV International Financial Meeting of Caja Madrid, Madrid
text: Madrid, 5 July 2004 Keynote address IV International Financial Meeting of Caja Madrid. Jaime Caruana Governor Ladies and gentlemen: I want to thank the organizers for the opportunity to address you on this opening day of the Fourth International Financial Meeting of Caja Madrid. For two days they will discuss the situation in which the world economy finds itself, its new rules and its new protagonists, and the stability and legal security that are needed so that the process of economic recovery that we are experiencing is based on increasingly solid foundations that consolidate and strengthen it. For this, they will have the presence of very outstanding personalities and specialists who will make them participants in their experience and knowledge. It is not risky to predict a great success to these meetings. In recent days, I have had the opportunity to express my opinion on the situation in which our economy finds itself and what is the international environment in which it operates. I did so on the occasion of the presentation of the Annual Report for 2003 to the Governing Council of the Banco de Espa96a and, more recently, on the occasion of my appearance before the Congressional Committee on the Economy. I do not want, therefore, to be repetitive and repeat a diagnosis that I am sure many of you know and, possibly, share. I would like to take this opportunity to focus on some ideas, specifically on four themes, which may be illustrative of the problems we have to face and which we should bear in mind in any debate on the future of the world economy and its implications for the Spanish economy. The program of these days asks if the recovery is already a reality. I believe that the world economy is entering a phase of clear expansion, led by the United States and with the collaboration of other prominent players; Among them, most especially, some Asian economies. The most recent data also indicate that this recovery process is spreading to the main European economies and that the group of countries in the euro zone seems to be finally abandoning the stagnation of recent years. The Spanish economy is in an advantageous position to take advantage of this stimulating environment. It has shown a great capacity for resilience during the last phase of cyclical slowdown and has maintained a sustained growth rate for several quarters now. It could be that we are, therefore, at the beginning of a relatively generalized growth stage. We cannot say, however, that this scenario is free of uncertainties and that the economic recovery phase is guaranteed. The US economy has entered a new phase of growth that confirms its extraordinary vitality, but drags significant imbalances that, if not straightened, could compromise its momentum. Europe continues to show signs of rigidities that limit its capacity for expansion, and which must be corrected so that it can develop its full potential and contribute, as far as it is due, to more balanced global growth. Spain, in short, faces the challenge of maintaining and intensifying its process of real convergence with the most prominent economies in our environment, for which it needs to strengthen its competitive position. So, on this occasion, I preferred to choose the three economic themes that I have outlined plus a financial theme, rather than trying to make an extensive analysis of the economic situation. The four cases are: In international economics, the global economic imbalances that persist despite the recovery, their possible adjustment paths and their implications for the recovery. I find it interesting to reflect on the situation of the European economy on the relationship between the structural challenges facing the area, a medium-term issue, and the difficulties that confidence is showing in resuming a dynamism similar to other similar cyclical situations. In the Spanish economy, I believe that a central issue for the near future, beyond 2005, is competitiveness. Finally, in the financial area, I would like to explain the favourable treatment of small and medium-sized enterprises in Basel II. 1) Global economic imbalances. The current phase of growth of the world economy is characterized by the presence of notable imbalances in international savings and investment flows, of which the current account deficit of the United States is the main exponent. To date, the financing of the US deficit has not posed any problem, due to the willingness of foreign investors to continue absorbing assets issued by the economic agents of that country. This phenomenon has been encouraged by several factors, including the productivity gains of the American economy since the second half of the 90s that have increased the expected return on its assets, the development and efficiency with which world financial markets act, reinforced, in the case of the United States, by the preponderant role of the dollar within the international monetary system. In addition, the exchange rate policies pursued by many Asian countries d0 aimed at preventing the appreciation of the exchange rates of their currencies and continuing to support the recovery of their economies d0 have led them to exert a strong demand for dollar-denominated assets. Although the confluence of these factors has been, to date, fruitful, we should not think that this situation can last indefinitely and introduces an element of risk in the process of global recovery. As you know, the classic ways of absorbing current account imbalances are basically two. The first runs through exchange rate movements and their impact on the relative prices of tradable goods. The second relates to demand-side stimulus policies implemented in the various areas. Countries that have accumulated trade surpluses must boost the growth of their economies to balance flows of goods and services with deficit areas, and allow their currencies to appreciate. Both adjustment mechanisms are, to some extent, complementary, so both can play an important role in correcting imbalances. In any case, the expected contribution of exchange rate movements to the correction of global external imbalances is limited, and adjustments in the economic policies of the major countries are therefore necessary. The experience of the last two years is sufficiently illustrative in this respect: the loss of value of the US currency coexisted with a widening of the deficit in the United States and the surpluses of Japan and the rest of Asia, mainly because the depreciation of the dollar was not concentrated in the currencies of these regions. which are the ones that cause, to a greater extent, the North American trade imbalance, but, above all, against the euro, the currency of a region with a relatively balanced external balance. It cannot be excluded, therefore, that an adjustment of this type, far from solving the US external imbalance, will end up affecting the recovery of the European economies, which are those that are in a more delayed cyclical phase. Achieving a more balanced distribution of global growth with more balanced external positions without jeopardizing the recovery is therefore one of the main challenges facing the global economy. A first risk is that the persistence of current account imbalances could exacerbate volatility in international exchange and financial markets. For these reasons, it seems advisable that the economic policies of the different world areas adopt an orientation that allows mitigating the risks associated with global imbalances, without compromising their stability. Thus, in the United States, the gradual withdrawal of the fiscal stimulus introduced in recent years could make a fundamental contribution to moderating the growth of domestic demand and, therefore, to containing the high needs for appealing to global savings that has been registered. Not surprisingly, the terminology of "twin deficits" has been coined to refer to the double imbalance of this economy, since, although private agents have also contributed to the external imbalance, this has been, above all, the counterpart of the high public deficit. For its part, the contribution of euro area economic policies to the correction of global imbalances depends on the determined implementation of product market reforms and factors that will raise their potential growth and demand for foreign-produced goods. The evolution of the euro area over the last few years has been somewhat disappointing. Its rate of growth has remained virtually stagnant and many of the welfare gains expected from the adoption of a single currency and the deepening of a single market have not yet been realised. Highlighting the importance of the economic policies of the various areas in the orderly adjustment of global imbalances, the important contribution that higher growth in the euro area would have in this process, allows me to focus on the second of the issues I wanted to address. 2) Reforms and confidence in Europe In recent years, a broad consensus has been forged on the causes of this difficult situation to boost its growth, as well as on possible remedies. I would like to highlight, in this regard, two points which, in my opinion, are very relevant. First, the modest growth of productivity, which could be related, in turn, to the low rate of generation of technological innovations and the difficulties in the diffusion of existing ones, well below, both, those that have taken place in other geographical areas. This may have been helped by the relative regulatory and administrative rigidity faced by European companies. In addition, the efficiency of the functioning of European labour markets continues to offer ample room for improvement. A more intensive and efficient use of the labour factor requires a deepening of the reforms undertaken and, in particular, in the implementation of measures to reduce recruitment costs, in the implementation of reforms of tax systems and, in particular, in the revision of those elements of the mechanisms of social benefits that, Having been conceived at a time of higher economic growth, they now reveal their high costs in terms of a distortion of incentives for an efficient allocation of resources. However, the consensus which, as I have indicated, has been building around this diagnosis and which was enshrined in the ambitious objectives of the Lisbon agenda, has not been matched by decisive action on the part of the national authorities, which have generally adopted a hesitant attitude in applying the catalogue of measures drawn up. In my view, one of the reasons for the weakness of the reform drive lies in the fact that the authorities have not always been able to convey to citizens that reforms are presented as an opportunity for greater future growth and not as a loss of well-being. The idea that the costs of reforms are felt quickly while their fruits take years to arrive d0 or even in the case of pension reforms, decades or generations d0 has been exaggerated. I believe that this idea must be qualified a lot because progress in the reform agenda and in its understanding by the citizen would help to increase potential growth and also to spur the weak confidence of European agents that has inhibited their propensity to spend in recent years. A more determined will to reform is a necessary ingredient to underpin the current phase of greater dynamism of activity. In this respect, the hopeful recovery in EMU output that began in the middle of last year provides an opportunity for the acceleration of reforms that must not be wasted, as improved employment and income prospects help mitigate potential costs in the shorter term. 3) The competitiveness of the Spanish economy In relation to the Spanish economy, I have preferred to choose competitiveness as the most relevant element for the future of our economy. The Spanish economy has managed to stay out of the unstimulating tone experienced by the main European economies in recent years and has been able to benefit from the stable environment in which it has been developing since our entry into EMU. This has allowed it to continue narrowing its income and welfare differences with the most advanced countries in the EU. This dynamism is based on relatively solid foundations. On the one hand, favourable monetary and financial conditions and buoyant employment continue to underpin the expansion of household spending on consumer goods and housing. On the other hand, it is to be hoped that, in the coming months, the healthy financial situation of Spanish companies and the expansion of the world economy, which, as I have already said, is increasingly intense and widespread, will tend to broaden the foundations of our growth pattern, so that it will be sustained, to an increasing extent. in those components of expenditure that contribute to raising productive potential, such as investment and exports. In this sense, there are already signs of recovery in the productive investment of companies, once the phase of financial consolidation that some large business groups have had to face has passed, while exports may be favored by the better tone of international markets. This favourable behaviour should not, however, diminish the importance of the need to preserve the levels of macroeconomic stability achieved and to deepen and broaden the structural reforms that the economy needs. I would like to refer today, as I did on the occasion of the presentation of the Annual Report, to the need to address certain elements of risk that have been brewing over recent years and which, if materialized, could hinder the full incorporation of the Spanish economy into the phase of global economic expansion and the continuity of the process of real convergence. I am alluding, in particular, to the persistence of inflation differentials with all the countries of the euro area and the low growth of productivity, two factors that may end up damaging the competitiveness on which the future growth of our economy must be based. The persistence of a positive inflation differential vis-88-vis the euro zone countries responds, in part, to the more advanced cyclical position maintained by the Spanish economy, but also reflects the presence of imperfections and rigidities that are evident in more noticeable increases in those sectors, such as services, which are protected by external competition. In addition, as some of these activities are suppliers of intermediate inputs, their price increases are transmitted to the rest of the productive network, which accentuates the cost pressure, with the consequent deterioration of the conditions of competition of those companies that compete in international markets. This situation has forced many industrial sectors, especially those with a greater export vocation, to adjust, after several years of compression of their operating margins, the growth of employment, in order to reduce their costs per unit of product and defend their market shares. Cost and price stability is an essential element of the economic policy strategy within EMU, and preserving it is a key challenge for our economy. But we must not forget that, in a context of increasing internationalization, the competitive advantages that the Spanish economy has traditionally enjoyed, based on lower price and cost levels than those of our main competitors, may be affected by those of those countries of more recent industrialization that are rapidly incorporating into export activity. In this way, the defence of the competitive position of the Spanish economy is increasingly linked to improvements in efficiency and productivity, a challenge that we share with other European countries, along the lines outlined in the first part of my speech. As I have already explained on numerous occasions, the low growth in productivity in the Spanish economy in recent years is undoubtedly related to the strength and intensity of the job creation process, which has been boosted by the flexibility measures adopted in the labour market. The strength of employment has not only made it possible to significantly reduce our high unemployment rate, but has also sustained the growth of household disposable income. We can, however, identify some other factors, of a more structural nature, which also help to explain the lower dynamism of productivity, even in relation to the other countries of the euro area, and which must be adequately addressed, if we do not want to see our medium-term growth capacity constrained. Among them, due to its importance, we must highlight the scarce role of technological innovation and the role of the dissemination of knowledge in the modernization of the productive apparatus. For the Spanish economy to achieve genuine increases in productivity, it must decisively increase the capitalization of its production processes, strengthening, in particular, those transport and telecommunications infrastructures, which have such an influence on long-term growth. At the same time, the innovative effort, the level of education and the qualification of the workforce must be intensified, in order to improve the capacity of Spanish companies to adapt their productive and commercial structure to the patterns of international demand, promoting a growing specialization in those products with greater added value and more dynamic markets. The experience of other countries shows the importance of combining, on the one hand, the significant investment effort necessary to produce and incorporate new technologies in the different production processes and, on the other, the configuration of a competitive and flexible economic environment, favoring the diffusion towards the whole of society of organizational changes and the use of applications derived from new technologies. In this way we will be able to cope with the increasingly intense competitive pressure exerted by the countries that have recently joined the EU, with productive and commercial structures similar to ours and which are undertaking intense capitalization processes, financed, in large part, from abroad. The Spanish economy is therefore faced d0 like the rest of the European economies d0 with the need to advance in the necessary reforms to improve its productive structures and make the functioning of the markets for goods and services more flexible. In turn, macroeconomic policies must continue to ensure the current stable environment. In this regard, it is appropriate to reiterate once again the importance for Spain of maintaining a disciplined budgetary policy that allows the balance of public accounts to continue improving, so that, in the face of the comfortable monetary conditions that will prevail, consistent with the requirements of the euro area as a whole, expansionary impulses can be moderated and budgetary stability preserved in the medium and long term. Only with this orientation will it be possible to avoid the medium-term risks to which I have referred, and to take advantage of the opportunities offered by the new stage of generalized growth that the world economy can enjoy and on whose perspectives you will reflect throughout these days, so I do not want to take away more time than you promise to be fruitful working sessions. 4) Basel II and SMEs. Taking advantage of the opportunity offered by this meeting and continuing with the idea of focusing on specific issues, I would like to jump from the macro to the micro and from the real economy to the financial one, to dedicate my last words to the Basel II agreement, approved the last week of June and specifically to its favorable treatment of small and medium-sized enterprises. something that we all recognize as very necessary for economic development.
