text_original: Madrid, 13 de octubre de 2004 COMPARECENCIA DEL GOBERNADOR DEL BANCO DE ESPAA ANTE LA COMISIN DE PRESUPUESTOS DEL CONGRESO CONGRESO DE LOS DIPUTADOS Jaime Caruana Gobernador del Banco de Espa Sr. Presidente, Sras. y Sres. Diputados: Es muy grato para m comparecer ante esta Comisi de Presupuestos del Congreso, con ocasin de la presentacin de los Presupuestos Generales del Estado de 2005. Se trata de los primeros presupuestos de la nueva legislatura, que responden a las directrices de poltica econica establecidas por el nuevo Gobierno. Se presentan, adems, en un momento crucial para la evoluci futura de la economa espala, en el que el tono que adopte la poltica econica y la poltica fiscal en particular ser muy influyente sobre sus posibilidades de crecimiento y de convergencia con Europa. Mi contribuci bascular, como es habitual, sobre la valoraci de la situacin de la economa en el actual entorno internacional y la poltica monetaria del Eurosistema que compartimos con los dems miembros de la zona. Comenzar, por tanto, comentando el contexto externo y, dentro de l, las perspectivas para el rea del euro. En los timos meses, la fase de recuperacin ha seguido consolidndose en la economa internacional y generalizndose a las diferentes regiones, a pesar de las tensiones experimentadas por el precio del petreo. Las previsiones ms recientes discutidas en diversos foros internacionales siguen siendo cautamente optimistas sobre las perspectivas de expansin continuada en 2005, destacando especialmente los crecimientos esperados en Estados Unidos y en los pases asiticos as como la progresiva ampliaci de la base geogrfica sobre la que se asienta el crecimiento mundial. La aceleraci ms intensa del crecimiento de la economa mundial que tuvo lugar desde mediados de 2003 permitique la zona del euro iniciara una recuperaci gradual, que en los timos cuatro trimestres ha mostrado unos ritmos de expansi prximos a la tasa de crecimiento potencial de esta regin. De acuerdo con los ltimos datos disponibles, el producto del rea se expandia una tasa interanual del 2% en el segundo trimestre de 2004 y se prev que el crecimiento alcance en el conjunto del presente a una cifra similar, tras tres as de escaso dinamismo de la actividad. En cualquier caso, no se ha absorbido todava la brecha de produccin acumulada en los timos aos. La recuperaci se apoy inicialmente en la demanda externa, dado el fuerte tir del comercio mundial, pero el gasto interior tambin ha experimentado ms recientemente un mayor empuje, aunque la mejora de la demanda interna est siendo relativamente lenta, sin que los indicadores de confianza hayan mostrado avances significativos en los timos meses. En todo caso, la evoluci del conjunto de la zona del euro es el resultado de comportamientos bastante dispares, pues hay pases (como Espaa o Francia) con tasas de expansin primas al 3% y con una aportacin significativa de la demanda interna, mientras en otros (como Holanda o Alemania) el crecimiento ha sido ms dbil y ha descansado de forma significativa en la demanda exterior. En este panorama internacional, relativamente positivo pero no exento de desequilibrios, la principal fuente de incertidumbre a corto plazo es el comportamiento del precio del petreo, tras el significativo encarecimiento que ha experimentado en los timos meses, si bien es difcil detectar, por el momento, un impacto apreciable de esa perturbaci sobre el crecimiento en la UEM. Las previsiones apuntan a un fortalecimiento de la actividad en la zona del euro en los primos trimestres, gracias al soporte que continuar proporcionando la expansi del comercio mundial, si, como parece probable, los principales pases industrializados mantienen ritmos de crecimiento relativamente elevados. Tambin cabe esperar que la demanda interna de las economas ms rezagadas de la UEM comience a mostrar un mayor dinamismo, a medida que el impulso del comercio exterior alimente la inversi y el empleo, y estas variables, a su vez, favorezcan las expectativas de renta y el gasto de las familias. En el mbito de la inflacin, por el contrario, los efectos del encarecimiento del petreo han sido ms rpidos y perceptibles. La inflacin en la UEM se ha situado por encima del 2% en los timos meses y, probablemente, no disminuir por debajo de esa cifra hasta la primera mitad de 2005, y ello siempre que no se produzcan los denominados efectos de segunda ronda, como consecuencia de los intentos de los agentes de proteger sus rentas mediante incrementos de sus demandas salariales o de sus mrgenes. Es obvio que el BCE vigilar si esos mecanismos de defensa se ponen en marcha, pues en ese caso habra riesgos sustanciales para el mantenimiento de la estabilidad de precios. En este contexto, el Eurosistema ha mantenido, desde junio de 2003, los tipos de inters a corto plazo en el 2%, un nivel que representa un mnimo histrico y que, en trminos reales, supone, para la mayor parte de los pases, tasas primas a cero o negativas. Los tipos de inters a largo plazo, por su parte, tambin se encuentran en unos niveles muy reducidos. De modo que las condiciones monetarias y financieras se han mantenido muy favorables para el afianzamiento de la recuperaci. Estos comentarios sobre la situaci europea no pueden pasar por alto el debate que est teniendo lugar en los timos meses acerca del seguimiento de las polticas econicas y, en particular, de la poltica presupuestaria dentro de la Uni Europea, tras los incumplimientos que se han producido en la aplicaci del procedimiento de dficit excesivo previsto en el Pacto de Crecimiento y Estabilidad en los casos de Alemania y Francia. En primer lugar, es importante dejar constancia de que, pese a las dificultades que se han presentado, el marco europeo de disciplina fiscal, aunque no ha actuado con el rigor esperado, ha servido como freno del deterioro de las posiciones presupuestarias en la fase de desaceleraci cclica, que en ausencia de dicho Pacto habra sido incluso ms grave. Sin embargo, es obvio que se han puesto de manifiesto serios problemas en la aplicaci de estos mecanismos de disciplina que es necesario corregir, para salvaguardar su eficacia y credibilidad. Recientemente, la Comisi Europea ha lanzado una serie de propuestas en torno a las cuales se est desarrollando el debate en las instituciones europeas. Sin entrar a valorar detalladamente dichas propuestas, me gustara recalcar que, en mi opinin, a la vista de la experiencia reciente, resulta crucial realizar una vigilancia estricta de la poltica presupuestaria en las fases de auge, pues so si entonces se produce el ajuste adecuado, las finanzas plicas estarn preparadas para afrontar las etapas de desaceleraci sin generar dficit plicos excesivos. Asimismo, me parece adecuado prestar ms atenci al criterio de deuda a la hora de evaluar las polticas presupuestarias, pues, en ocasiones, este criterio suministra informaci muy valiosa sobre la autntica situaci de las finanzas plicas. Obviamente, esa labor de vigilancia y coordinacin solo podr ejercerse si se dispone de informaci fidedigna y puntual sobre la evolucin presupuestaria, que atienda a los criterios contables y a los calendarios establecidos. La discusin sobre estas cuestiones continuar durante los primos meses y mantengo una fundada esperanza en que se encuentre la forma de mejorar la aplicaci del Pacto por la Estabilidad y el Crecimiento, de manera que se reestablezca la eficacia y la credibilidad de los imprescindibles mecanismos de disciplina fiscal y que ello sirva de marco para una coordinacin suficiente de las polticas econicas de los pases de la zona del euro. De todos modos, estas revisiones no requieren cambios normativos que, en todo caso, se encuentran restringidos por las disposiciones del Tratado vigente recogidas tambin en el nuevo Tratado Constitucional-, seg las cuales los lmites del 3% del PIB para el dficit plico y del 60% del PIB para la ratio de deuda pblica no pueden ser modificados. Tambin quiero selar que la revisi del avance en los objetivos marcados en la agenda de Lisboa, apunta a un resultado claramente insuficiente, por lo que resulta prioritario reestablecer el impulso reformador. Del xito de esta estrategia depender la capacidad de alcanzar un crecimiento alto y sostenido a medio plazo en la zona del euro. En este contexto de expansin de la economa mundial y de progresivo afianzamiento de las perspectivas econicas en Europa, la economa espala ha tendido a estabilizar su tasa de crecimiento en torno a los niveles comparativamente elevados que haba alcanzado al finalizar el a pasado. Concretamente, segn las estimaciones ms recientes de la Contabilidad Trimestral, en el segundo trimestre de 2004 el incremento interanual del PIB fue del 2,6%, tras haber registrado aumentos ligeramente ms elevados en los dos trimestres anteriores del 2,8% y del 2,7%, respectivamente. Estas estimaciones indican que el diferencial de crecimiento con la zona del euro sigue siendo positivo y que, por tanto, la economa espala sigue convergiendo, en trminos reales, con los niveles de renta de los pases ms avanzados de la zona, aunque el ritmo de convergencia sea ahora menor, debido a que el ligero debilitamiento reciente de nuestro ritmo de expansi ha coincidido con la recuperacin que estn experimentando estas economas. El crecimiento sigue estando acompaado de una generaci de empleo comparativamente elevada. De hecho, los timos indicadores del mercado laboral apuntan a una estabilizaci del ritmo de creaci de empleo, que aumentun 2% en el segundo trimestre. No obstante, estas estimaciones confirman tambin que el ritmo de avance de la productividad aparente del trabajo sigue siendo reducido. El aspecto, sin duda, ms positivo de la coyuntura reciente ha sido el avance de la inversi en equipo en el segundo trimestre de 2004, perodo en el que ha empezado a superar el estancamiento que vena registrando desde 2003. La informaci coyuntural parece confirmar la continuidad de esta mejora. Sin embargo, otros aspectos de los factores que impulsan el crecimiento resultan menos novedosos. El consumo privado ha mantenido tasas de aumento superiores al 3%, ms elevadas que las observadas en 2003; el avance del consumo plico ha superado el 4%; y la construcci, con aumentos en el entorno del 4,2%, ha seguido proporcionando un soporte bsico a la expansi del gasto, impulsada por la obra plica y por la inversi residencial. Esta tima sigue progresando, a pesar de los elevados niveles que ya haba alcanzado en los as precedentes. La demanda exterior, por su parte, ha acentuado su carcter contractivo de forma significativa en los primeros trimestres de 2004, frenando el avance de la actividad. Por un lado, los datos de la Contabilidad Trimestral indicaran que las exportaciones de bienes han comenzado a beneficiarse del impulso del comercio mundial, creciendo a tasas similares a ste, y parece que los datos ms actualizados de comercio exterior reflejan este impulso. Sin embargo, en contraposici, el turismo ha registrado unos resultados bastante dbiles en el segundo trimestre de 2004 que, segn todos los indicios, se han extendido de forma algo atenuada a la campa de verano. Ms importante a, las importaciones han repuntado fuertemente desde el inicio del ao, contribuyendo a frenar el producto. En definitiva, los resultados de la economa espaola se siguen asentando en un patrn de crecimiento muy similar al de los timos aos. El avance de la demanda se basa en gran medida en el soporte que las holgadas condiciones financieras prestan al gasto de las familias en consumo e inversi residencial y en el avance del gasto en obra civil y en consumo plico. Aunque la inversi productiva y las exportaciones han tendido a recuperarse, lo han hecho con una intensidad todava inferior a lo deseable. El dinamismo del gasto de los hogares ha generado tensiones sobre los precios, en especial, en aquellos sectores con menor flexibilidad de oferta. Los datos recibidos desde la primavera han mostrado un repunte significativo de la tasa de inflacin, en un contexto de presiones provenientes de los mercados de materias primas singularmente, del petreo y de algunos alimentos. Concretamente, la tasa de inflaci se ha situado en el 3,1% en septiembre, seg el avance preliminar, con lo que el diferencial con el rea del euro habra vuelto a la zona de un punto porcentual. Es probable que el alza del precio del petreo haya tenido un impacto relativamente ms intenso en nuestra economa que en otras economas europeas. Sin embargo, el nleo ms permanente del diferencial de inflaci procede de los componentes ms estables del IPC: la inflacin subyacente espaola se ha aproximado al 3% en los timos meses, en torno a seis o siete dcimas por encima de su nivel en la eurozona, y en el caso de los servicios, el diferencial se mantiene en torno a un punto porcentual. La persistencia de este comportamiento est teniendo efectos negativos sobre la competitividad que empiezan a ser perceptibles en el dficit comercial y en el debilitamiento del turismo. Por lo que se refiere a las implicaciones financieras del comportamiento de los hogares, cabe selar que no se percibe todava un cambio en la tendencia creciente del endeudamiento. De hecho, la financiacin a los hogares se ha acelerado en la primera parte de 2004, impulsada por el fuerte crecimiento del crdito hipotecario. Asimismo, los diversos indicadores sobre el esfuerzo que representa la adquisici de vivienda muestran que este sigue aumentando, sin que, por otra parte, se haya reducido la presin sobre el precio de estos activos, que so ha dado tibias seles de moderaci. Aunque la posici patrimonial de las familias sigue siendo sida, el peso de la carga financiera en relaci a la renta se ha incrementado. Por su parte, la financiacin a las empresas, que haba mantenido un tono ms moderado, se ha acelerado en los timos meses, posiblemente como reflejo del repunte de la inversi, que cuenta para su continuidad con el apoyo de una situacin financiera y unos niveles de rentabilidad elevados. Las informaciones disponibles permiten prever que la economa contin creciendo en el segundo semestre a ritmos similares a los de la primera parte del a. De esta forma, el ejercicio podra cerrarse con un crecimiento del PIB ligeramente por debajo del 2,8%, dependiendo, sobre todo, de cual sea el efecto contractivo de la demanda exterior neta. Y a partir de aqu, el escenario para 2005 vendr condicionado por la intensidad de los impulsos procedentes del contexto exterior y por la evoluci de las condiciones internas de la economa. Si la zona del euro sigue ganando fortaleza, en un entorno internacional expansivo, la economa espaola tendra tambin la oportunidad de reforzar su dinamismo y alcanzar ritmos de crecimiento que se podran acercar al 3%. Sin embargo, en las circunstancias actuales, dicha tasa se encuentra, ms bien, en la zona alta del rango posible de previsi. En esa direcci apunta el riesgo de que el encarecimiento del petreo se prolongue o incluso alcance una intensidad superior a la inicialmente prevista o de que la recuperacin de las economas europeas muestre mayores vacilaciones. Las implicaciones de un comportamiento adverso del precio del petreo en nuestra economa, tanto en la reducci del ritmo de crecimiento econico y de creacin de empleo como en su presi alcista sobre los precios, depende, en buena medida, del comportamiento de los agentes econicos. En la medida en que estos empresas y trabajadores traten de eludir la prdida de renta real, que supone el aumento del precio del petreo, mediante aumentos de mrgenes e incrementos salariales se tendern a producir deterioros ms duraderos de la situacin inflacionista, crecimiento y empleo. Conviene, sin embargo, no olvidar que diversos factores, como son la menor dependencia del petreo y el menor incremento de precios en trminos reales, matizan el impacto directo en relacin a pasadas experiencias; por ello es importante evitar los efectos de segunda ronda mencionados y posibles compensaciones que podran disminuir los incentivos necesarios para la mejora de la eficiencia energtica. A nivel interno, tambin existen factores que pueden actuar frenando el crecimiento, como es el caso de la posible materializacin de algunos riesgos que subyacen al patr de crecimiento que ha seguido la economa espala o con el agotamiento de algunos de los impulsos recibidos tras su ingreso en el euro. Son estos riesgos los que reclaman una respuesta activa de la poltica econica que permita mitigarlos y establecer las mejores condiciones para aprovechar los impulsos procedentes del exterior. Los instrumentos disponibles a nivel nacional deben orientarse a preservar el marco de estabilidad macroeconica, a moderar la demanda de los hogares y a fomentar, simultneamente, la inversi productiva y la competitividad, de manera que se reequilibren los componentes del gasto que sustentan el avance de la demanda y se favorezca las ganancias de productividad y la competitividad. La poltica monetaria nica ha determinado, hasta el momento, unas condiciones monetarias y financieras relativamente holgadas para las necesidades de la economa espaola. Es previsible que, a medida que la situaci general de la economa de la zona del euro vaya mejorando, el tono de las condiciones monetarias retorne gradualmente hacia pautas ms neutrales, de manera que se podr ir absorbiendo, al menos en parte, la holgura financiera que ha prevalecido. No obstante, aunque la orientacin de la poltica monetaria se mueva en una direcci ms acorde con las necesidades domsticas, es ms que probable que este cambio no sea suficiente para alcanzar el tono global de polticas que en este momento necesita la economa, por lo que reviste gran importancia la funcin que corresponde a las polticas internas. En la situacin que he descrito sobre la poltica presupuestaria recae la tarea de tratar de encauzar la demanda y el gasto de manera coherente con la contencin de los riesgos que han empezado a emerger y para ello resulta imprescindible que se profundice en la senda de consolidacin presupuestaria de los timos as. Como dije el a pasado en esta misma Comisi, los Presupuestos Generales para el ao en curso, que entonces se discutan, tenan un objetivo de equilibrio de la cuenta del conjunto de las Administraciones Plicas, que en aquellas circunstancias cclicas tena un carcter moderadamente expansivo, lo que aconsejaba utilizar cualquier margen disponible para una instrumentacin ms ajustada y para avanzar ms decididamente hacia el supervit, en lnea con requerimientos de la situaci macroeconmica. Las cifras sobre la ejecucin presupuestaria en 2004 estn afectadas por el reconocimiento de algunos ajustes en el gasto de las Administraciones Plicas en trminos de Contabilidad Nacional que no estaban contempladas por los Presupuestos y la asunci de deuda de algunas empresas plicas, como RTVE y RENFE. Como consecuencia de ello, el saldo estimado ha resultado deficitario en una cuanta que, en lo fundamental, refleja estas operaciones puntuales, que pretenden reflejar de manera ms exhaustiva la situaci de las finanzas plicas. La apuesta por la mejora de la transparencia en las cuentas plicas, manifestada en la presentaci de presupuestos como un objetivo necesario para mejorar la eficiencia del sector plico, debe valorarse positivamente dado que ste es un elemento esencial para garantizar la disciplina fiscal. En este sentido, cualquier esfuerzo de transparencia debe servir para reforzar los mecanismos de disciplina y evitar la continuidad de las tendencias al gasto de las unidades saneadas. Ello pone de manifiesto la conveniencia de que vaya acompado de las reformas necesarias que eviten la reaparicin futura de los desequilibrios surgidos en el pasado en empresas plicas, como las anteriormente mencionadas, que han motivado los ajustes en 2004, de forma que estos ajustes no sirvan para dotar de una mayor holgura al presupuesto que pudiera favorecer un incremento permanente del gasto plico. La transparencia como mecanismo de disciplina tiene particular importancia cuando la estructura del gasto est fuertemente descentralizada, como ocurre en Espa. Es imprescindible que la situacin de las finanzas del conjunto de las Administraciones Plicas se conozca con una frecuencia y una puntualidad similar a la del Estado, para lo que se requiere una mayor transparencia de las Comunidades Automas. Igualmente resulta importante que, ms all del propio rigor de los criterios contables, las distintas administraciones pblicas expliciten aquellos compromisos o actividades que no consolidan dentro del sector pero que pueden representar riesgos de mayores pagos o deudas en el futuro. En cualquier caso, una vez que se tienen en cuenta los ajustes contables realizados, la valoracin del tono de la ejecucin presupuestaria en el a 2004 apunta, de acuerdo con las previsiones de cierre del ejercicio disponibles, a que ste ha resultado efectivamente expansivo, incluso si se tiene en cuenta el ligero debilitamiento de la recuperaci. De modo que el esfuerzo de consolidaci presupuestaria habra quedado por debajo de lo que hubiera sido deseable para alcanzar una sida protecci frente a los factores de riesgo que se estaban haciendo presentes. Los Presupuestos Generales para el ao 2005 presentan un objetivo de supervit para el conjunto de las Administraciones Plicas de una dcima de PIB, que es compatible con los criterios de estabilidad presupuestaria y que permitira a Espa estar entre el reducido nero de pases del rea del euro con saldo excedentario en sus cuentas plicas. Desde el punto de vista de sus efectos macroeconmicos, con todas las cautelas que se derivan de un anlisis que en esta ocasi esta rodeado de mayor incertidumbre de la habitual como consecuencia de los ajustes contables realizados, esta cifra podra significar que no se corrige suficientemente la mencionada orientacin moderadamente expansiva de la poltica fiscal, resultando una contribuci a la estabilidad que podra ser inferior a la deseable en la situacin actual de la economa espala. Dada la ausencia de un suficiente margen de maniobra en el presupuesto para 2005, es especialmente importante que la ejecuci de la misma por parte de las diferentes administraciones plicas sea especialmente rigurosa, que se aprovechen todas las oportunidades para profundizar la senda de consolidaci presupuestaria y que se eviten desbordamientos de las cifras programadas, incluso en el caso de que el crecimiento econico o los ingresos sean ligeramente inferiores a los contemplados en la planificaci presupuestaria. El tono de poltica fiscal que requiere la economa espala no se circunscribe a un saldo global que resulte apropiado para la actual coyuntura, sino que tambin se refiere a la composici y calidad de los ingresos y gastos plicos. Polticas que favorezcan el aumento del crecimiento potencial de la economa permiten tambin que se pueda financiar el gasto social de forma sostenida, por ello es necesario priorizar adecuadamente el fomento de la inversi y del aumento de la productividad y una contenci de otras rbricas de gasto, especialmente si se pretende potenciar paralelamente algunos componentes del gasto social. En conjunto, una combinacin de polticas, monetaria y fiscal, menos holgada es la respuesta macroeconica adecuada para abordar los riesgos que se presentan en el terreno de la competitividad, de las alzas de los precios de la vivienda y del endeudamiento de las familias. Ello plantea una especial exigencia y responsabilidad en el campo fiscal, un tono ms estricto favorecer la contencin de incrementos de precios y de costes en los sectores menos expuestos a la competencia, la contenci gradual de los precios de la vivienda hacia una senda compatible con la evolucin de sus fundamentos y la desaceleraci del ritmo de endeudamiento de los hogares hacia pautas ms sostenibles. Pero tan importante como el tono agregado de la poltica macroeconmica es el impulso de las reformas estructurales que aborden los problemas de rigideces o de inadecuaci de la regulaci en algunos mercados. Dichas reformas son tambin imprescindibles para impulsar el crecimiento de la productividad, al que tanta relevancia concede el Proyecto de Presupuestos y para ello deben contribuir, en timo trmino, a dinamizar la iniciativa empresarial y la capacidad de innovaci de la economa en su conjunto. La actuaci plica se debe orientar, sobre todo, a crear las condiciones para que los agentes puedan tomar sus decisiones en un entorno suficientemente competitivo, evitando caer en un intervencionismo que dificulte el dinamismo y la capacidad de adaptaci de nuestra economa. Es muy importante mantener un impulso liberalizador que despeje las dudas que se han podido suscitar sobre el carcter de algunas regulaciones, como en el caso de los horarios de apertura de los establecimientos comerciales, que afectan a un sector que desempe un papel destacado en la difusi de las ganancias de productividad y en la formaci de los precios finales. El impulso reformador debe abarcar un abanico de sectores y medidas muy amplio en respuesta a los problemas especficos de la economa espala y en lnea con los objetivos de la agenda de Lisboa. En relacin con propuestas relativas a sectores especficos, en el terreno de la vivienda, por ejemplo, es necesario que las medidas orientadas a favorecer el acceso vayan acompadas de reformas que incrementen efectivamente la flexibilidad de la oferta, cuesti que depende fundamentalmente de la regulacin del mercado del suelo, pues de otro modo las presiones siempre terminarn manifestndose a travs de las subidas de precios. Debe concederse gran importancia a las medidas encaminadas a consolidar las bases para un crecimiento que permita mejoras de productividad y paralelamente la generaci continuada de empleo en la economa. Las reformas introducidas en los aos noventa permitieron reducir significativamente la tasa de desempleo y, al aumentar el potencial de creaci de empleo, han contribuido a sostener el dinamismo econico. Sin embargo, la inercia y la rigidez que siguen presentando los mecanismos de determinaci salarial y los elementos de inflexibilidad que persisten en otros aspectos del mercado de trabajo hacen necesaria una profundizaci en las reformas en este mercado, clave para el funcionamiento de la economa. La estrategia de mejora de la competitividad debe adoptar un enfoque general, que abarque desde el fomento de la inversi en capital fsico y humano, base de las ganancias de productividad, a la revisi de algunas estrategias sectoriales y al propio patrn de especializaci productiva. Pero estas son cuestiones de gran alcance que desbordan el marco de esta comparecencia. Permtanme terminar insistiendo en la importancia del papel que le corresponde a la poltica presupuestaria, a la hora de aprovechar la mejora del contexto externo y de asegurar que los riesgos que estn emergiendo no pongan en peligro la continuidad de la recuperaci y de la convergencia. As mismo, la profundizacin en la consolidaci presupuestaria es necesaria para afrontar con mayores garantas los retos de largo plazo a los que las cuentas plicas habrn de enfrentarse, en especial aquellos asociados al efecto del envejecimiento de la poblaci.

Title: Conference "Transparency and Market Discipline: Corporate Governance"
text: - Cultural Center of Caixanova, Vigo, 11 November 2004 Transparency and Market Discipline: Corporate Governance Business Conference "Reflections on business problems in the regulatory and financial framework of 2005", APIE Gonzalo Gil Deputy governor SUMMARY The common thread of my lecture is the effect that the imminent regulatory changes .NIC. Basel. will produce on all aspects of the life of entities. Indeed, both regulatory changes are of a magnitude and complexity that will affect everything from the measurement of risks to the form of governance of the entities. As the territory thus defined is unfathomable, a drastic limitation is necessary: to focus attention on the part of these changes that will affect transparency, market discipline and, ultimately, the Government of the entities. Of course, the follow-up of this common thread will be altered on those occasions when a detour seems convenient to clarify a specific point or comment on some specific or more detailed development. All the changes will affect, of course, all the entities that participate in the financial markets .and in some cases even companies from different sectors., but given the program of these Days, the central point will be the Savings Banks. A first part will point out the position of the Savings Banks in our financial system, following two lines: the evolution of their business and importance within the system and the qualitative aspects that make some difference with the other participants in the system. The second part will focus on those aspects of IAS and Basel directly related to aspects of transparency, governance, etc. It is not a question of describing the content of new rules, but of touching on some aspects of them: those, on the other hand, which have been less dealt with up to now. The objectives and general characteristics of the new 4/91 will receive some attention here. The third part will focus on Transparency, Market Discipline and Corporate Governance. It will reflect on the situation of the Savings Banks in this area and the potential effects of the aforementioned rules on transparency and good governance. (PART 1) FEATURES OF THE EVOLUTION OF THE BOXES AND QUALITATIVE ASPECTS Within the framework of the expansion of our financial system, savings banks have experienced an operational development and an adaptation of their corporate governance rules that have facilitated, despite their peculiar nature, a more complete identification with private entities and has allowed them to act in the markets following criteria of economic rationality. Operational characteristics of the Savings Banks The Financial Stability Report, soon to be published, when analyzing the evolution of the system, indicates the features of the evolution of the Savings Banks in different areas: In terms of size, savings banks have significantly increased their number of offices and employees in recent years. The number of employees already exceeds that of banks. On the other hand, its market share has also increased both in terms of credit (49.6% of the total) and deposits (61% of the total). Its financing to the private sector has grown at rates above 15% since 1997 (18% in June '04). Within this, the credit with mortgage guarantee stands out, which already accounts for more than 60% of the financing granted by the Savings Banks. With regard to efficiency, margin data (intermediation, ordinary and operational) show an increase over the previous year. The slowdown in operating expenses is reflected in improvements in the efficiency ratio, which stood at 60% in July '04. Profitability is also showing favourably. Margin growth, cost containment and lower allocations to other specific funds explain the increase in the group's attributable profit, and ROA and ROE have remained stable. The solvency ratios (total and core) maintain the downward trend of recent years. Despite the growth in equity (12.2%), due to the acceleration of Tier 1 and, to a lesser extent, Tier 2, requirements have grown at a higher rate (15%) due to the strong increase in the loan granted. However, the solvency ratios, total (approximately 11%) and basic (greater than 8%), are above the required regulatory minimums (8% and 4%) and are higher than those maintained by banks. There is, therefore, nothing in the operational development of the Savings Banks that allows to establish a distinction of any kind with the other financial institutions of the system. Qualitative aspects With regard to these aspects, different from the previous ones, and related to ownership and government, the Savings Banks have some peculiarities that, as we have just seen, have not hindered at any time their performance as market entities. These characteristics exist, and I would like to make some initial reflections on them. They have some peculiarities related to their origin and history: a significant social content in their actions and strong regional roots, which has not prevented them from developing their operations with great success and in competitive conditions. In depository institutions, savings banks play a very significant role, and their contribution is decisive in maintaining competition between markets and in a sector in which the fundamental point [being more important in savings banks than in other financial institutions, since they do not have shareholders] is the confidence of depositors; properly directed boxes reinforce the stability of the system. It is precisely through the control of risks, maintaining a high level of profits and a level of solvency appropriate to their risk profile, that the Savings Banks model will be able to prosper. Only by acting with business and efficiency criteria, basing its direction on professional criteria of economic rationality, can this be achieved, creating value for society as a whole and the regions. I believe that there is a broad consensus on preserving the characteristics of the savings banks, and this implies reaffirming their character as credit institutions above other considerations, which is what will ensure their future survival and therefore the interests of their depositors. It also implies a certain degree of moderation in those activities and risks furthest from their nature. As such private depository institutions, their contribution to the financial system as a whole must be articulated around the concepts of profit generation, solvency and management with (appropriate) economic and financial criteria. The above considerations that I have just made, together with its operational development, should serve as a basis for future developments, which will be conditioned by macroeconomic uncertainties and global developments and by considerations regarding the development of the business itself based on an increasingly competitive and globalized environment, both at European and international level. But in addition to these uncertainties and possibilities typical of the cyclical evolution of its economy, in the coming years in financial institutions, and of course the Savings Banks, they will face a series of regulatory changes that will redefine not only the characteristics of their business, but also the very nature of their management. I am referring to the Basel II Capital Arrangement and International Accounting Standards (IAS), which enter into force in January 2005. * * * (PART 2) THE CAPITAL AGREEMENT AND INTERNATIONAL ACCOUNTING STANDARDS Before pointing out the most outstanding features of this regulation, on the other hand already well known, I would like to emphasize an important fact, which is the nature and scope of these regulatory changes. It is a question of emphasizing once again that its repercussions are not limited to a mere instrumental change or compliance with some regulations to traditional use; Its qualitative components are essential and its implementation will change, they are already changing it, the nature of the business, the way of dealing with risks and their measurement (and coverage). But, at the same time, all the mechanisms of internal functioning of the entities: the management, the work of the commissions, the form of decision-making, the information to be provided, etc., will have to go a step further on what has already been achieved so far. Basel Was there a need for new solvency regulation? Yes, despite the positive elements of the current regulation, . Due to its shortcomings after more than 14 years of validity: it does not take into account the improvements produced in the methodologies for measuring and managing risks; It creates perverse incentives, encouraging regulatory arbitrage. . The need to provide adequate incentives and recognition of new and more effective risk management techniques. What are the most innovative aspects of Basel II? The newest aspects of Basel II/Directive are: . All risks are covered. . It is based on the 3 mutually reinforcing pillars and each of them represents a supervisory policy approach. . A menu of options is offered to entities, who have the option to choose based on their degree of sophistication. . The norm has an evolutionary character, not closed. I believe that in expert analysis, in public communication, etc. the predominance and attention paid to purely quantitative and regulatory elements has obscured what is probably the greatest virtue of the Agreement: its qualitative aspects. Indeed, together with the markedly comprehensive approach, embodied through a series of elements (joint action of the 3 pillars, the consideration of a broad set of risks, attention to evolution, and increasing operational complexity, etc.), the Agreement introduces the necessary incentives to motivate appropriate behavior on the part of managers. Of all of them, I would like to focus on those fundamentally related to Pillar 3, since the Agreement reinforces the necessary involvement of the senior management of the entities in the implementation of solid principles of good corporate governance. This is a necessary requirement to achieve a real improvement in risk management systems. From this recognition, incentives are introduced to encourage the commitment of senior management in the aforementioned field. Banking supervisors want to incorporate market discipline as a necessary complement to the supervisory structure. Market discipline and transparency, which is necessary for it to function, contribute to stable and resilient financial markets. This is because it allows better access to the information provided by financial institutions. It facilitates the analytical capacity of rating entities, investors and depositors to assess the risk profile of institutions. Market discipline can only work if there is transparency, and this is a fundamental task of corporate governance of entities. Thus, the Agreement has been intended to be a compendium of rules, supervision and market discipline, trying to reconcile the advantages of all. Rules, discretion and market discipline. . Rules have the advantage that they provide institutions with great clarity about what supervisors expect. "Rules only" has disadvantages, since they can produce rigidity and discourage innovation, preventing them from capturing the peculiarities of different types of risk and their development over time. . The complement with the discretionary approach, which allows specific situations to be taken into account, is necessary, and this role is fulfilled by the supervisory review. . Not everything ends with these two approaches, since market participants may have problems in comparability between institutions. The predominance of internal information provided by banks for capital requirements d0 the more intense the more advanced the approach chosen d0 and the bank-supervisor relationship, requires an additional compensatory approach: Pillar 3. . To achieve this, Pillar 3 contains a series of transparency requirements d0 it is in a way a refinement of accounting standards. The information decisions that Basel II requests entities to provide are based on the following principles: Market participants should know and understand how capital requirements are applied in the consolidated; they should know what risks institutions face; how and to what extent they approach them; the characteristics of the capital and the amount they maintain. Capital is the institution's last defense, intended to cover unexpected losses. . In addition, the formal aspects of the transparency policy are reinforced. Transparency policy formally approved by the Council. That the instruments to promote them are credible (functioning of Commissions). Daily use of them as an integrated part of management. * * * If I mentioned earlier that the quantitative aspects of the Basel Agreement have received much greater attention than the qualitative ones, the same is true of another aspect of the implementation of the Agreement, which is receiving little attention despite the progress of the process. The rules of the Agreement have no legal force and their effective implementation depends on national authorities, which can give them legal force. The case of the European Union is peculiar and the Agreement will be implemented by means of a directive that is already well developed. I would like to make a few comments on this, to serve as a wake-up call on a subject that deserves it. Why is the European case peculiar? For the existence of a single market in the EU: . The Directive applies to all credit institutions and investment firms, irrespective of their size, legal nature and level of sophistication of their internal systems and operations. This is not the case in Basel (designed for large internationally active entities) and explains some of the differences between EU regulation and Basel II. . In addition, in the EU, trends towards greater integration have led to strong pressure from pan-European banking groups to reduce the administrative burdens of being subject to different regulatory and supervisory authorities. This pressure, which already existed, has been accentuated with the excuse of greater discretion and scope for divergence from the new regulations. Therefore, the Directive contains some elements for implementation that "force" greater coordination and exchange of information between supervisors. It goes beyond Basel's principles on cross-border activity. What specific features will the implementation of the Directive have? The implementation of the Directive is complex, because: . The framework is flexible: entities are given the possibility to choose different methods. . The qualitative elements are very important. . There is a potential uneven application of the Agreement, due to the existence of a large number of areas of national discretion. Work is under way to reduce these areas of national discretion by, for example, convergence in their application in all countries. However, in some cases their elimination is not appropriate because they reflect the diversity between different domestic markets. . The different levels to which the various requirements contained in the Directive should apply have been fully and systematically developed. The obligations of credit institutions are established, distinguishing between those that must be met at the individual level (all individual institutions are subject to capital requirements, with some exceptions if strict requirements are met) and at the consolidated level. . To deal with cross-border groups: the role of the consolidating supervisor is developed and rules are established for the exchange of information between supervisors (apart from the extension to other authorities, in emergency situations). . Market reporting requirements for EU supervisory authorities are specified in order to facilitate convergence in the interpretation of the Directive and improve transparency. What settings s/ the Basel text? The Directive also contains some adjustments arising from both the scope and the different characteristics of EU markets. Those derived from the different scope of application. Adjustments necessary to ensure that rules are proportionate to the reality and complexity of small institutions: . The Directive has allowed small banks to use the Standardised Approach on a permanent basis for their sovereign and interbank exposures, even if they are material exposures, and to use the IRB Approach for the rest of their exposures, provided that they meet 2 requirements: that they are a small number of material exposures and that it is very expensive for the institution to develop an internal rating method for these exhibitions. . The possibility for institutions to estimate risk factors in the IRB method using joint data from several entities (the so-called "data pool") is further developed: Important for similar small entities that would not be able to obtain meaningful estimates of their risk factors on their own and that can join and aggregate their data and means to obtain them. Save costs since the development of the methodology can be done jointly. They must demonstrate that the rating systems and criteria of other entities are similar to their own; The pool used for estimates is representative of the portfolio for which it is to be used and is used consistently over time. The entity remains responsible for the integrity of its rating system and must sufficiently understand the methodology used, being able to control and audit the rating process. . Small investment firms have a specific treatment for the application of operational risk requirements. Those derived from the different characteristics of EU markets: . To stimulate SME financing: Some requirements are relaxed in the general framework of risk mitigation techniques (CRM): operations guaranteed by SGRs, re-endorsement is allowed. The treatment of venture capital operations is improved when the portfolio is sufficiently diversified: the capital requirements of venture capital funds are lowered. . Requirements are relaxed so that bank bonds can be used as collateral. . The favorable treatment of "covered bonds" (bonds guaranteed with mortgage securities or with risks with sovereigns, such as our mortgage and territorial bonds) is maintained. . Wider recognition of mortgages on commercial premises is envisaged. . Requirements are reduced in some aspects of securitization, particularly in the standard method, by setting a ceiling on requirements. * * * INTERNATIONAL ACCOUNTING STANDARDS In the effectiveness and control of risks, accounting standards also have a decisive influence. The interaction of these with the different pillars of the Capital Agreement is very intense and in fact transparency begins with the way in which financial data is recorded and communicated. In this sense, care has always been taken to ensure that the requirements of Pillar 3 do not conflict with the IAS. This change in the regulatory environment will affect practically all sectors, since the rules are general. The European Union decided that the consolidated annual accounts of groups with securities listed on any regulated market in the European Union should be drawn up, since January 2005, in accordance with the rules approved by the Commission and drawn up by the IASB. Two objectives are pursued by generally approved IAS: 1. They promote the consolidation of the European single market, which requires for its constitution the guarantee that all participants have access to financial information as homogenised as possible. 2. On a broader level, the new standards represent a step forward in convergence with Anglo-American standards. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the fact is that the application of accounting standards to financial institutions poses some specific problems arising from the peculiar nature of the latter (the possibility of producing systemic risks is not the least) and the high degree of regulation of the same d0 not comparable with that existing in other sectors d0 by supervisors with explicit legal mandates. Supervisors are therefore legitimately obliged to analyse the effects that may result from accounting rules in certain areas. Accounting rules can be expected to favour market discipline and effective risk control. In the area of transparency and market discipline, the Committee has made efforts d0 in collaboration with the authors of accounting standards d0 to avoid that the requirements of Pillar 3 could conflict with the rules arising from the application of IAS. In this connection, it is necessary to underline that, in a complementary and consistent way with Basel Pillar 3, IAS represent a further reinforcement of institutions' obligations in this area. This is well evidenced in our own Circular, which will be mentioned later, since transparency is one of the greatest novelties, not only because of the difference it presents with respect to the current information model (more or less extensive breakdowns of balance sheet headings), but also because of the amount of information that must be provided (the transparency standards .59th to 62nd. represent more than 17% of the Circular in number of pages). The information to be provided refers, among other things, to: . Description of the different financial risks (credit, interest, market and liquidity risk) and management and hedging policies used by the group, as well as the amounts represented by their exposure. . Description of the methods and models used to estimate the fair value of financial instruments that are not listed on active markets, as well as the most significant assumptions that such models use. . Description and nature of the transactions carried out with the related parties of the entity (subsidiaries, associates and multigroup, as well as with the members of the board of directors and key management personnel), indicating the policy followed in the granting of loans, etc. unless they have been carried out under market conditions. The remuneration received by Board members (individually) and key management personnel (globally) should also be reported. There are other areas of interaction between the two standards that are of interest and sometimes concern to supervisors. The establishment of provisions, changes in valuation of financial instruments, the potential effect of accounting rules on the solvency ratio and the definition of own resources, etc., advise that supervisors should implement certain supervisory filters that maintain the calculations of regulatory capital and the adequate provision of provisions. Issues that are still under discussion and that will continue in the future. * * * THE BANK OF SPAIN AND THE NIC: THE NEW CIRCULAR 4/91 The Bank of Spain has already carried out a first public consultation process of the new Circular 4/91, and at this time, once the comments received have been analyzed and the pertinent modifications made, it has been sent for consultation following the formal procedure established, and it has also been reposted on the Web. Some brief comments on the Circular: 1. Actions of the Banco de Espa96a The actions of the Bank of Spain are part of broader processes. Firstly, the existence of a Community Regulation, which implies an immediate entry into force. Secondly, the future existence of a General Accounting Plan, not yet drawn up, in accordance with IAS standards. The White Paper established a procedure of approval similar to the European one: The ICAC will submit the Circular to a double contrast: 1st, the Accounting Committee, and 2nd, Accounting Commission. The results of the first consultative process: more than 600 comments that have improved the quality of the new text. In any case, good general reception of the Circular and recognition of the effort made by the Bank of Spain. 2. Criteria for its elaboration The Bank of Spain has sought to offer a guide that allows banks to approach the transition to the new system with a greater degree of certainty. Minimize discrepancies in criteria between Spanish standards (mandatory in individual public states) and IAS (mandatory in the consolidated public states of listed entities), and thus the workload. Combine IAS requirements with maintaining the BE's prudent attitude, avoiding sudden breakdowns. Maintain as before the consistency of criteria between public and reserved states (for reasons of banking supervision and EMU statistics). In the area of provisions, this orientation translates into maintaining high levels of provisions and preserving the idea that the deterioration of credits occurs before it manifests. In the other areas, compatibility with IAS is sought, trying to find a balance between the different options proposed by the Regulation. Equalization of the competitive terrain for entities. 3. Entry into force The Circular will enter into force on 1 January 2005; however, since the annual accounts must be presented with comparative information for two full years using the same accounting criteria, entities, when preparing the annual accounts for 2005 (to be presented at the beginning of 2006), must present the comparative information for the year 2004 with the criteria of the new Circular. Therefore, the date of adjustment of the differences between the criteria of Circular 4/91 and those of the new Circular must be made on January 1, 2004, and all adjustments, with certain exceptions, will be made directly against the reserves of the entities. 4. General content of the Circular Two parts, with an equivalent legal enforceability. The main text tries to use language as compatible as possible with IAS, and the Annexes, which can be described as "supervisory guides", introduce traditional elements in our regulation, adapted to the new IAS environment. It will not be in any case a "frozen" text and will be subject to adaptations promoted both by changes in IAS, changes derived from the preparation of the General Accounting Plan or self-generated changes by its application. (Coverage of core deposits, PV in liabilities) The Circular implies new definitions, and important changes in formats, with the appearance of new accounts (changes in equity), new statements of provisions, etc. Extension of the IAS principles to individual and sub-consolidated reserved balance sheets (with the lower costs that this entails for institutions), but always choosing those options within the most prudent IAS and often offering practical reference guides (provisions, commissions, etc.) or presumptions, in technical language. Scope of consolidation: expands to approximate the IAS definition. This includes non-financial companies and insurance companies. Related to the new 4/91, there is the necessary modification, under study, of Circular 5/93, of own resources. The definition or elements to be included in PR or capital will necessarily vary. Among the most important changes can be mentioned: those arising from the treatment of securitisations in Basel II and the recognition of excess provisions over the expected loss level, both in Basel I (we do not recognize it now) and in Basel II. 5. Particular content This is not the time to describe the changes contained in the Circular, which, on the other hand, is on the Web; It is worth commenting on an issue that was not included in the first public consultation process and that has attracted a great deal of attention from entities: provisions. The current philosophy is maintained but with somewhat lower levels of demand. Generally speaking, IAS originally only supported the concept of "loss incurred". Subsequently, the intervention with the Basel Committee led him to make the position somewhat more flexible: . Supports provisioning portfolios even if the damaged credit is not individualized. . You have to check all the credits, even if they are apparently fine. . Gives a role to the supervisor in the issue of credit valuation. The new provisioning scheme will include: A SPECIFIC provision with a matrix approach with calendars. Based on information from the CIR. . Separate treatment PF and PJ (includes individual companies.), with consideration of security interests and within them housing (up to 80% of LTV). . They will be applied to the entire amount of the operation, and not only to the defaulter, with anticipation of calendars and customer drag effect, as before. A GENERIC provision . Under this denomination, the old Generic and the old Statistics, reformed, will be merged into a single Fund. The new Fund will take into account the inherent loss as well as the evolution of risk factors over the cycle. . In general, the new system implies a reduction over the previous levels and its application is conditioned at the beginning by the level that the entities would have reached with the previous system. In any case: Although it is not convenient to have a discussion in terms of high or low provisions, but in terms of well-provisioned and poorly provisioned entities (or sufficient or insufficiently provisioned), it can be said that, on average, the system will replicate a smaller volume of background and flow than the previous ones. The dispersion in the new system will be less than in the previous one, and there will be entities (those with the greatest endowment of old statistics) that will release more; and others that will release less. * * * (3rd PART) TRANSPARENCY AND MARKET DISCIPLINE: CORPORATE GOVERNANCE Thus, it seems quite clear that the imminent regulatory changes discussed above will have a powerful influence on risk management structures and, more generally, on the overall management of the entity itself and its transparency. The whole stream of reforms of recent years will be reinforced and stimulated by the announced changes. Given this aspect of the new changes that are coming, how are the Boxes prepared? If a few years ago our Governor, in the ECSC Assembly, said that: "the governance structures of the savings banks have attracted a certain attention... and the need to strengthen the professionalism, stability and control of the management of the Savings Banks has been repeated on occasions ...", the truth is that the situation has improved significantly, and the Savings Banks have been equipped with structures that, although they can be improved, as is logical, are far from the situation that was pointed out in the previous paragraph. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the basic principle that was formulated on that occasion is still valid: as a rule of action of all entities, and, of course, the Savings Banks. "A starting principle is to make it clear that only a solvent and efficient entity can guarantee, in a sustained manner, the protection of the depositor and the fulfillment of its final objectives. The conclusion of this principle is that the Code of Good Governance should highlight the obligation that the members of the administrative bodies must put the good management of the entity above any other objective." What are the features of the current situation? Two preliminary considerations: 1) The Government of the Savings Banks is essentially an autonomous competence, therefore all observations are made from the supervisory point of view; (2) Although competing on the same markets, the governing bodies of savings banks have different characteristics from those of banks, which are public limited companies. The previous years, especially 2002 and 2003, have been fruitful in the adoption of rules relating to transparency and good governance of savings banks. They have been oriented in several directions: . Accentuate the role of market discipline: transparency of corporate governance, participatory quotas. [Annual report of the Savings Banks, with securities admitted to trading: pending] . All the abundant legislation of the last two years regarding the good governance of the Savings Banks has insisted on a specific line: to strengthen the character of financial institution of the same, establishing the mechanisms and controls so that their investment policy is governed by the criteria of the other financial institutions with which they compete. . Their independence and professionalism have been strengthened: 50% limit on public representation, irrevocability of positions during their mandate, term limits by age, greater general proportionality. Investment Committee, Audit Committee, etc. What to say from the supervisor's perspective? First. The above guidelines are reasonable, although the legal developments already approved have yet to be completed. Therefore, it seems appropriate that, in addition to adapting to the potential changes that occur in the European Union, the effort is concentrated on developing and really assimilating all the changes approved. Secondly, it is necessary to continue to insist on the key role of the Directors-General, but also on that of the administrative bodies and the various committees emanating from them. It is worth mentioning: 1. The responsibility of the directors in the management decisions they adopt, which may be legally required. 2. The creation of the Investment Committee (within the Board of Directors), which is responsible for reporting on the investments made by the fund, their financial viability and their adequacy to the foundational objectives. Important, although still pending, is the annual report that must be made on these points (which will be incorporated into the corporate governance report). 3. The Control Committee (or the Audit Committee), with very broad functions, which may go as far as suspending the effectiveness of the Council's decisions. Third, that the managers, in addition to adopting measures to ensure a genuine consolidation of governance structures in the operation of the Fund, should focus on strengthening society's confidence in the Savings Banks as a necessary element for the preservation of the Savings Bank model. For this, a firm commitment to the instruments that allow the exercise of effective market discipline is of the utmost importance for all entities and, of course, the savings banks. An important part in the preservation of the same, from the supervisory point of view, is an adequate control of the risks that the entity incurs due to its investment policy. Although it is not only about credit risk, this is fundamental, and in this sense, the draft of the new Circular 4/91, which is in the final consultation process, reinforces in its annex IX the requirements for an "analysis and coverage of credit risks". The evolution of mortgage credit has been the subject of analysis and valuation on several occasions by the Bank of Spain. The persistence of its growth in the latest available data makes it necessary, at a time like this, in which we are reflecting on good governance, to emphasize that it serves as a basis for the adequate assessment of risks and their follow-up. The duration of the period of maintenance of high rates of growth of mortgage credit affects all the variables related to it: evolution of prices, wealth and indebtedness of families, characteristics of loans, almost absolute predominance of variable rates, etc., increasing the degrees of vulnerability. Therefore, and apart from the arguments already known, it is necessary to draw the attention of all entities to the need to put more emphasis on factors that, such as those mentioned, acquire greater significance with the duration of the bullish period. . It is necessary to ensure that the fixing of the maximum loan amount, depending on the guarantee provided, does not exceed the prudent measure (fixed by accounting regulations) of 80%. It is essential to preserve the value of the collateral, which can be altered by market conditions. . In addition, the deferral of principal payments and the lengthening of maturities, together with the increasing volume of promotional credit investment, introduces risks that require careful assessment in the face of the potential materialization of unfavorable circumstances. . Such strong and persistent growth rates are forcing an increasing appeal to financing in the debt and interbank markets, which may affect the structural balance of banks. It is therefore necessary to implement diversification policies, debt limits in wholesale markets, merger surveillance, etc., and to avoid the possible impact of these liability policies on solvency ratios. * * * In summary, repeat once again the need for institutions to accentuate their active policies to strengthen the credit quality of mortgage operations. It is not a question here of detailing the requirements that the Circular establishes as necessary for adequate risk control. What ultimately worries the Circular is that this policy is properly implemented with a clear scheme of responsibilities and commissions that allow assessing each potential credit investment from the point of view of guaranteeing the solvency of the entity. This discipline cannot be exercised effectively if transparency is deficient, so an orientation, in this sense, that goes beyond the prescriptive rules, and that anticipates to offer information regarding those aspects in which the Savings Banks differ more from their competitors, will constitute an important element for the strengthening of their character as a private credit institution, shared with other basic characteristics such as the solvency of the institution and the protection of its depositors. This active approach to corporate governance and transparency policy is all the more necessary given the increasing complexity of many of the financial products they distribute on their networks. Adequate and understandable information, probably not necessary for a professional investor but necessary for network placements, is crucial for the characteristic clientele of the Savings Banks, who must be clear d0 in their own interest and that of the Fund d0 what is the nature of their relationship with it.
