Title: Procyclicality of the financial system and regulation. Presentation at the International Conference on Financial Procyclicality, organized by the International Monetary Fund and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority. Hong Kong. Only in English.
text: Hong Kong, 22 November 2004 Procyclicality of the financial system and regulation* Conference Managing Procyclicality of the Financial System: Experiences in Asia and Policy Options. Hong Kong Monetary Authority and the International Monetary Fund Jose Vils Director General International Affairs * The views expressed are purely personal. Introduction As the most insightful paper by Ashley Taylor and Charles Goodhart (2005) that has provided the background for our session clearly demonstrates, there are concerns both in academia and in the banking sector regarding the potential costs of greater procyclicality that could come together with Basel II and IAS39. The question is to what extent these concerns are really well founded, and I aim to address this issue. I will start with a discussion of cyclicality, both in general and in the financial system in particular. I will next go on to explain what the main likely consequences of Basel II are regarding the volatility of the financial cycle and procyclicality. I will turn then to discussing how excessive procyclicality can be fixed if it were to eventually arise and will conclude with some remarks on the likely impact of IAS39 on procyclicality and on how restrictive the new accounting standards are concerning the implementation of some of the best remedies for the procyclicality problem, should it finally arise. What is cyclical? When discussing cyclicality, it is very important to remember that this is by no means a concept that just applies to the financial sphere. Indeed, the economy is also cyclical and, going further, one can confidently say that human behaviour is cyclical and that as we are all well aware even life is cyclical. In the financial sphere, a certain degree of procyclicality is a natural, sensible and desirable outcome as it reflects the extent to which the financial sector is influenced by developments in the real economy and viceversa. The issue is nevertheless to what extent there is an excessive degree of procyclicality. The financial system is excessively procyclical when it unnecessarily amplifies swings in the real economy and/or reduces the stability and soundness of the financial sector. As Borio, Furfine and Lowe (2001) have explained, since shifts in risk attitudes initiated by the state of the economy are inherent in the nature of human behaviour, there is a tendency for economic agents both lenders and borrowers to systematically misperceive risks over the cycle. This leads to over-optimism in booms which tends to be followed by over-pessimism in downturns. This, in turn, sets in motion the well-known financial accelerator, where the real and financial cycles tend to reinforce each other through the traditional interactions between asset prices and credit, thus planting the seeds for financial instability and their associated economic and social costs (Bernanke, Gertler and Gilchrist, 1999). In light of the above, it is clear that even without regulation there will be excessive procyclicality both in the financial system and in the real economy. Yet regulation has, in principle, the potential for either increasing or decreasing procyclicality. If so, how should the financial and economic impact of Basel II be assessed in this regard? A framework for assessing the consequences of Basel II The main goal of Basel II is to enhance financial stability by introducing incentives for banks to better measure and manage risks, to hold appropriate, more sensitive capital and to improve the transparency of their risk profile. From the viewpoint of a central banker it is interesting to note a certain parallelism between modern thinking in monetary policy and the framework depicted for financial stability in Basel II. In particular, the modern approaches to monetary and financial stability have three key characteristics in common. First, they are both forward-looking in nature and have a medium-term horizon, all of which departs from the backward-looking, myopic behaviour observed in the past. Second, as a result of the above, they both have an anticipatory character that seeks prevention rather than cure. And, finally, both attempt to incorporate market views through the role played by expectations and market discipline. When assessing the value added of Basel II, and in order to put the analysis of procyclicality into perspective, we must take into account its impact on both 'financial output trend' and 'volatility'. For instance, Figure 1 provides an impressionistic description of the potential impact of Basel II compared to Basel I. It tries to convey the now generally accepted idea that by introducing risksensitive capital requirements, Basel II can enhance the efficiency and the stability of the banking system relative to Basel I. This is represented by a higher and faster growing 'financial output' in Basel II relative to Basel I, as shown by the two 'trend' lines in the Figure. Despite this significant improvement, there is a heated debate about whether Basel II will increase financial volatility and, as a result, procyclicality with the real economy, as shown by the two alternative oscillating lines around the 'trend' corresponding to Basel II. Does Basel II add to procyclicality? In the discussion about the impact of Basel II on procyclicality, there are several views. A first view, neatly put forward in the paper by Taylor and Goodhart (2005), is that a close scrutiny of Basel II and of the available empirical evidence suggests that, overall, Basel II is likely to exacerbate procyclicality although it is unclear what the size of this effect would be. Figure 2 illustrates the several causal links that have to be followed for Basel II to increase procyclicality. Namely, Basel II would increase the risk-sensitiveness of minimum capital requirements which, in turn, would lead to higher cyclicality of the overall regulatory capital and to more procyclical capital. Consequently, this would be reflected onto more procyclical lending and onto a higher degree of procyclicality in the real economy. Clearly, for Basel II to ultimately result in higher real procyclicality, none of the causal links in the chain has to be broken. A different view is the so-called 'neutrality' view, which considers that some of the causal links in the chain are most likely to be broken. Specifically, while there is almost no discussion that the minimum capital requirements will be more procyclical through Pillar 1, and while regulatory capital might admittedly still be more procyclical under Basel II in spite of the mitigants provided by Pillar 2, it must nevertheless be recognised that lending practices are much more closely linked to economic capital than to regulatory capital and, therefore, are not likely to be significantly influenced by Basel II, since economic capital should not be much affected. Indeed, according to proponents of this view what Basel II will do is to align regulatory capital more closely to current banking practices and thus to economic capital, thereby not affecting lending policies. Moreover, banks hold significant capital buffers that although moving procyclically lead to an overall moderate effect (Ayuso, Perez and Saurina, 2004). But one could go even further and argue that Basel II will not only not raise procyclicality but will actually help reduce it since there is nothing more procyclical than a poorly run bank. By contributing to a better assessment and management of risks, Basel II should reduce the scope for surprises and thus for procyclicality. This is, for example, the view taken by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision as clearly stated by its Chairman: 'When banking systems are adequately capitalised, well-managed and risks are correctly assessed within the appropriate time horizon, the financial system becomes more stable, less procyclical, better able to promote sustainable growth, and more resilient during periods of stress.' (Caruana, 2004). I think it is fair to say that, given the uncertainties posed by the Lucas critique, we are not likely reasonably to know what the effects of Basel II on procyclicality will be until the system has actually been up and running for some time. Still, I think that it is important to stress that it is by no means clear that Basel II will exacerbate procyclicality and, if it did, that this effect would be significant. How to fix excessive procyclicality? Since central banks and banking regulators are paid to worry, it is always necessary to be prepared for the worst even if this is not the most likely scenario. Let me thus come to the issue of how to fix excessive procyclicality arising from the financial system. A first line of defence -and an important one- has to do with macroeconomic policies. Specifically, a stability-oriented monetary policy and a fiscal policy that can be made to work in a countercyclical fashion around a trend-path of fiscal rectitude are powerful tools for combating excessive procyclicality, both by preventing financial instability from arising and by allowing greater room for manoeuvre to deal with episodes of instability should they materialise. Let me focus, however, on the prudential policies and, in particular, on the role that can be played by what I consider to be a first-best remedy for excess procyclicality: namely, the introduction of forward-looking or dynamic provisioning, as practised in Spain over the past few years (Fernandez de Lis, Martinez-Pages and Saurina, 2000). Without going into too much detail, the key purpose of such a system is to correct the basic market failure mentioned earlier whereby risk tends to be underestimated in good times and overestimated in bad times. The underlying philosophy of forward-looking provisioning is not that risk arises in bad times but rather that risk increases in good times but only materialises in bad times (Crockett, 2001). As a result, it is useful to build up provisions in times of plenty (i.e. when risk increases through the expansion of credit but is underestimated) that can be drawn on in downturns (when risk materialises). Accountants have often criticised forward-looking provisioning arguing that setting up a provision when credit is granted implies that credit is priced below its face value. This accountants claim distorts the book value of banks assets and results in losses in accuracy and transparency. These criticisms have led to proposals (Borio, Furfine and Lowe, 2001 and Goodhart, 2004) to have as a second-best option some sort of countercyclical capital charges that share the basic philosophy of forward-looking provisioning. However, as I will presently argue, even taking into account potential accounting issues should not lead to the abandonment of forward-looking provisions as the first-best solution to procyclicality. The new international accounting standards and procyclicality Let me tackle, albeit rather briefly, the issue of the relationship between IAS39 and procyclicality. I cannot agree more with the basic conclusion of Taylor and Goodhart (2005) that IAS39 adds to procyclicality in the financial system through the introduction of fair-value accounting, notwithstanding its virtues in terms of transparency and market discipline. Unlike the case of Basel II, where as I have argued its procyclical impact is not so clear, the procyclical consequences of IAS39 are quite evident. Consequently, it is an irony that, even if the introduction of IAS39 will have far-reaching repercussions for the financial system, so little analysis has been made to date of the potential efficiency and macroeconomic impact of the new accounting rules. There is also a serious risk that, if the new rules are interpreted too rigidly, they could discourage, complicate and even prevent the implementation of some solutions to the procyclicality problem such as forward-looking provisioning. Consequently, IAS39 might not only exacerbate procyclicality but also make it more difficult for regulatory policy to deal with procyclicality. In particular, Basel II is mainly about capital (to cover unexpected losses) and thus does not deal in depth with provisions (e.g. to cover expected losses, as in the case of forward-looking provisions). In turn, IAS39 contemplates only 'incurred losses' as far as provisions are concerned. Hence, under a rigid interpretation, IAS39 would not be compatible with a system of forward-looking provisions. However, while IAS39 contemplates only 'incurred losses', it leaves some margin for manoeuvre that can be used to implement a system of forward-looking provisioning. Specifically, homogeneous group provisioning is possible even if individual losses are not yet individually identified, and provisioning can be made for all groups of loans and not only for those affected by incurred and already identified losses in an individual loan. Finally, it is pertinent also to recall that Basel II stipulates that the difference between total expected losses and total provisions be reflected in regulatory capital, thus squaring the circle. Conclusions There are several conclusions I would like to draw concerning the impact of regulation on the procyclicality of the financial system. First, while procyclicality is certainly an important issue, it is not just due to regulation. Second, a certain degree of procyclicality is natural, sensible and desirable as it reflects behaviour that is risk-sensitive. Third, when assessing the overall impact of regulation, one should look both at trend (efficiency effects) and cycle (procyclicality). In this respect, while most would agree that Basel II is clearly better in terms of trend given its effects from the standpoint of efficiency, transparency, stability, etc. its cyclical impact is still subject to debate. Indeed, it is not clear whether Basel II will add to procyclicality or, even if it did, what the size of the effect would be. Fourth, contrary to Basel II, the 'case for procyclicality' is very clear for the new accounting standards (in particular, IAS39). And finally, the authorities in charge of financial stability should, in any case, be ready to counter excessive procyclicality. For this purpose, I have advocated forward-looking provisioning as a first-best option from the regulatory viewpoint and made the case for avoiding too rigid an interpretation of the new accounting standards that could hinder the implementation of such an effective measure to deal with procyclicality. Title: Governor's Appearance: Senate Budget Committee, Madrid
text: Madrid, 24 November 2004 Appearance of the Governor Committee on Budgets. Senate Jaime Caruana Governor of the Bank of Spain Mr. President, Senators, I am very pleased to appear before you again on the occasion of the presentation of the 2005 General State Budget Project. This is a good time to analyze the situation in which our economy finds itself, what its future prospects and its most important challenges are, and what should be the tone adopted by economic policies so that the current stage of expansion is consolidated and we can continue advancing in the process of real convergence with the countries of our environment. I believe that, from my position as Governor of the Bank of Spain, the best contribution I can make to this debate is to analyse the Spanish economy within the international context in which it operates, paying particular attention to the euro area, whose evolution, as you know, sets the tone for the common monetary policy. Overall, 2004 has been a good year for the world economy, which has shown one of the highest growth rates in recent decades. This expansion has also been shared by various regions, among which Asian countries and the United States stand out. As on other occasions, the dynamism of activity has been accompanied by an acceleration of trade, which highlights the intensity and scope of the processes of globalization and economic integration in today's world. However, this favourable trend in the world economy for the year as a whole hides a certain loss of vigour in recent months, which is undoubtedly related to higher oil prices. Although the increase in the prices of petroleum products has been lower, in real terms, than in other similar episodes, it is still significant. Part of this increase can be explained, precisely, by the strong pressure of global demand d0 especially by some Asian economies d0 but supply factors are also important, so oil prices are expected to remain high in the medium term. It is this perception that is most affecting growth expectations, since, for the moment, the direct impact of price increases on energy indices d0 and on household spending decisions d0 has been relatively limited. The slowdown in activity in some countries may also be related to the application of somewhat more restrictive demand policies, as is the case in the United States, where the Federal Reserve has raised interest rates by one percentage point in recent months; or that of China, with a return to more moderate rates of growth, after a period of intense expansion, difficult to sustain. Although there is currently some uncertainty about the future evolution of economic activity in the main countries of the world, it is foreseeable that during 2005 a fairly acceptable rate of growth will be maintained in most regions, although the rates of expansion will be somewhat lower than this year. This is being collected by most international organizations, such as the IMF, which has just reduced its global growth forecast for next year by three tenths, to 4%. The recent moderation in oil prices could mark some normalisation of that market, especially if supply conditions tend to normalise, although it is most likely that, as I said, prices will remain at relatively high levels next year. On the other hand, this phase of recovery is proceeding without resolving the global macrofinancial imbalances that have been accumulating and that may jeopardize the sustainability of global economic growth. In this sense, the episode of depreciation of the dollar that has taken place in recent weeks has revived the risk represented by the significant external deficit in the United States and that the euro area is the main affected by the exchange rate movements of that currency, given the absence of flexibility in the exchange rate of the currencies of some Asian countries of great relevance. The euro area has broadly shared the developments in the world economy described above, although it has also shown some specific characteristics. During the first part of 2004, the economic recovery in this region continued, with growth around its potential output, supported by the contribution of net exports, while domestic demand maintained the trend of weakness of recent years. In the third quarter, growth is expected to have slowed as a result of the impact of the lower dynamism of the world economy on European exports, which has not been offset by stronger domestic demand. The weakness in domestic spending in the euro area is due to a number of causes, although it is likely to have a significant structural component, linked to the lack of expectations of job and wealth creation in some euro area economies. This component is more visible if one considers the favourable financial conditions that exist in the area, since short- and long-term interest rates are at historically low levels, whether measured in nominal or real terms. These conditions, which should favour agents' spending, have only allowed a slow recovery in demand, suggesting that obstacles of different kinds hinder the expansion process. Obviously, the increase in energy prices due to its negative effects on confidence and on the real income of households is also hindering the take-off of domestic demand. I would also like to point out, and this is important to understand what is happening in the area as a whole, that not all countries show a similar evolution. In this sense, the dynamism of some economies has not been able to prevent the slow process of recovery in other States - such as Germany, Italy or the Netherlands - from characterizing the area as a whole. Nor can we lose sight of the high synchrony that exists among most economies in the area and their dependence on the evolution of foreign demand. All this helps to explain why some countries, such as France, have registered a very poor growth figure in the third quarter of this year, after the strong momentum they had exhibited in the first half of the year. In this context of high oil prices and weak domestic demand, the appreciation of the euro exchange rate is helping to significantly moderate the cost of energy imports, but it may also lead to a decrease in net international demand for European products, at a time when domestic spending has not fully consolidated. With all this, it is likely that this year will close with euro area growth of around 2%. The outlook for 2005 points to a continuation of the economic recovery on the basis of relatively high growth in world trade and a gradual improvement in agent confidence, although the expansion process appears to be slow, with output expected to increase at a rate of no more than 2 per cent. It therefore seems difficult to absorb the negative output gap that has accumulated in recent years in Economic and Monetary Union. Higher oil prices have had a significant impact on the annual rate of inflation in the euro area, which has been above 2% in recent months. With current energy price levels, it is unlikely for the Harmonized Index of Consumer Prices to return to rates below 2% in the coming months. However, it should be noted that, for the time being, it is not apparent that agents have reacted to this direct impact of higher energy prices on consumer prices by demanding higher wage increases, or by causing unjustified price increases in other goods or services, to which the weak situation in which the labour market finds itself has contributed, on the one hand, and on the other, the lower dependence on petroleum products of most European economies. For the absence of these second-round effects to be consolidated, the authorities must not adopt fiscal measures that, in order to alleviate the impact of the increase in energy prices, delay the adjustment period, and that the wage negotiations that will take place in the coming months are carried out with moderation. In this situation, the Governing Council of the ECB has been able to maintain key interest rates at 2% - the level at which short-term rates have been located since June last year - although it has been recalling in recent months the work of strict surveillance it is carrying out, to prevent the short-term inflationary effects that inevitably cause the rise in energy prices from taking root in the expectations of Agent inflation. In this quick review of the situation in the euro area, I cannot fail to refer to the budgetary developments in its Member States. It is clear that the economic slowdown and the slow recovery process have made it difficult for some countries to comply with the Stability and Growth Pact. Despite this, I would like to emphasise that the European framework for fiscal discipline contained in the Treaty on European Union and in that Pact has helped to halt the deterioration of the budgetary positions of European countries during this period of low growth. Certainly, some economies should have been more ambitious in correcting their imbalances this year, although, in general, the neutral tone that fiscal policy will show in most States for the year as a whole seems appropriate. All this is not intended to detract from the serious problems that exist for the implementation of the Stability and Growth Pact, which must be corrected so that its effectiveness and credibility can be safeguarded. The European Union's Economy and Finance Ministers are currently working on these ideas and it is hoped that in the first months of 2005 we will have the first results of these discussions. Given the difficulties encountered, it is difficult not to emphasize the need for reliable and up-to-date information on budgetary positions as a prerequisite for rigorous monitoring and surveillance of fiscal positions. It also seems essential to establish mechanisms to allow strict surveillance of fiscal policy in the boom phases, since only if appropriate adjustments are made in times of expansion will it be possible to prepare public finances to face the stages of slowdown without generating excessive public deficits. In sum, the euro area is in a relatively favourable international growth scenario, although there is great uncertainty about the future evolution of the oil price and the dollar exchange rate, which are two crucial variables in shaping the area's recovery path. In any case, even if these variables evolve favourably, it is undeniable that the European economy has a low growth potential, which must be boosted by reforms in the markets for goods and productive factors, as recently analysed by the Heads of State and Government at the European Council last October. While there is a high consensus on this diagnosis, a similar determination is lacking to implement measures to make the European economy more dynamic. I would like to turn now to the situation in which the Spanish economy finds itself, placing special emphasis on its most recent evolution. The first thing that is striking is that, faced with the difficulties that, as we have seen, other European economies have to face in order to strengthen their expansionary phase, the Spanish economy has continued to maintain a comparatively high rate of growth in the period since 2004. According to the advance published by the INE . and which has just been confirmed by the data of the Quarterly National Accounts that have just been known ., the year-on-year growth rate of Spanish real GDP in the third quarter of the year has been 2.6%, the same as in the previous period, and it is possible that the rate reached in the average of the year does not differ, significantly, of this. For next year, the results we can expect in terms of real GDP growth will depend on how the world economy develops and, in particular, how European economies evolve. I believe that, in this situation, it is most likely that the Spanish economy will maintain a relatively stable growth path, not far from the current one, which could accelerate, gradually, as the uncertainties surrounding the international environment are cleared. The positive growth differential between Spain and the euro area has continued to underpin the process of real convergence, and is expected to continue in 2005. A fundamental difference between our growth pattern and that of the euro area as a whole is the considerable capacity of the Spanish economy to generate employment, and this has been confirmed by the data from the Labour Force Survey referring to the third quarter and the other available indicators on the evolution of the labour market, as well as, I hope, the data from the CNTR. This process needs to continue in the coming quarters and the persistence of high employment growth rates needs to be consistent with an improvement in productivity gains. These results, comparatively positive for the Spanish economy, do not prevent less favourable aspects in its behaviour that must be pointed out, in order to redirect them and thus guarantee, precisely, the continuity of the expansionary phase. In particular, the support provided by the comfortable monetary and financial conditions that have prevailed in the euro area as a whole has led to the consolidation, in recent years, of a growth pattern that combines a great strength of domestic demand with a very contractionary contribution of external demand, so it contains potential elements of imbalance that, At the moment, it does not seem that they are being drawn. Growth has been systematically based on the dynamism of household spending, on residential consumption and investment, and on high investment in civil works. The most recent data confirm that these trends are maintained, and this has been reflected in the figures of the National Accounts for the third quarter to which I referred earlier. But, perhaps, the most outstanding feature of the recent situation, in view of the desirable recomposition of the structure of spending, is the significant rebound that investment in capital goods is registering, leaving behind the recessionary behavior that it had been showing since the beginning of this decade. The healthy financial position in which companies find themselves and the good conditions that prevail in the economy point to the continuity of this process, which is also very sensitive, we must not forget, as the international environment evolves. As I have already said, the considerable dynamism of domestic demand is limited by the contractionary nature of external demand, which does not seem to have subsided. Although exports of goods have benefited from the boost of world trade and have grown at rates similar to those of external markets, tourism has recorded a rather weak performance, even if we take into account the slight improvement experienced since the summer months. But, above all, it has been imports that have maintained very high growth rates, increasing their presence in the internal market and helping to slow down the recovery of the product. The strength of domestic spending has generated tensions over the final prices of the economy, focused on those sectors with less flexibility of supply or that operate in less competitive conditions. In terms of consumer prices, the data received since spring have reflected a significant upswing in the inflation rate, in the context, which I have already described, of strong pressures in the oil market and d0 although in an increasingly less intense way d0 of higher food prices. Specifically, the inflation rate stood at 3.6% in October, bringing the spread with the euro area to 1.2 percentage points. Although this differential is due, in part, to specific factors such as the varying intensity of the transfer of the increase in oil prices, it reflects, above all, the persistence of higher inflation rates in the sectors most protected from competition. In this sense, the inflation differential has its origin in the notable differences observed in the growth rates of unit labour costs, much higher in our economy and also tending to accentuate in recent years. It is precisely in the service sectors where the increase in labour costs is being most intense, and it is these sectors, too, that can most easily pass them on to prices, without having to reduce their commercial margins. This is not the case for industrial sectors, especially exporters, which see their rates of profitability diminished. The persistence of these spreads is therefore having negative effects on competitiveness, and this is beginning to be reflected in the significant increase in the trade imbalance and the weakening of tourism. On the other hand, the prolonged strength of domestic spending and, in particular, household spending also has implications for the financial balance of these agents, as has been highlighted by the Bank of Spain on numerous occasions. In this respect, there is still no change in the growing trend of indebtedness. On the contrary, financing to households has accelerated in the intervening months of 2004, driven by the strong growth of mortgage credit, despite the fact that the weight of the financial burden as a percentage of income has increased. This growth in mortgage credit is closely linked to the pressure that housing demand continues to exert on the price of real estate assets, which has also shown no signs of moderation. Therefore, although the equity position of households remains solid, mainly due to the revaluation of real estate assets, the sensitivity of spending decisions in this sector to a possible increase in interest rates -which significantly increases their financial burden-, to a slowdown in employment or to a correction of the overvaluation of housing, has continued to grow. In general, it can be said, however, that in the context of the continuation of the global expansion that today appears to be more likely, the growth prospects for the Spanish economy over the coming quarters are favourable, although they are not exempt from risks from both the external and domestic environments. Among the first: an additional increase in oil prices, a scenario of greater hesitation in the recovery of European economies, or an early adjustment of the large imbalances observed today worldwide, through an excessive appreciation of the euro, would undoubtedly have negative consequences on Spanish growth. Internally, the possible materialisation of some risks underlying the growth pattern followed by the Spanish economy and the exhaustion of some of the expansionary impulses received after entering the Monetary Union could also attenuate our growth rate. We can do little from Spain to limit the risks that come from abroad. However, it is possible and necessary to address those that have a domestic origin, through the design of economic policies aimed at preserving macroeconomic stability, directing household demand and promoting productive investment and competitiveness, so as to rebalance the components of spending that sustain the growth in demand. A looser monetary and fiscal policy mix is the appropriate macroeconomic response to address competitiveness challenges d0 as it will help contain price and cost increases in less competitive sectors d0 house price rises d0 by seeking a gradual convergence of house price increases towards fundamental-consistent rates. and household indebtedness d0 by encouraging their slowdown towards more sustainable patterns. In this area, although it is possible that, as the euro area recovers, the tone of monetary conditions will acquire a less expansionary tone, it is not foreseeable that the change will be sufficient to meet the requirements of containment of domestic spending in the Spanish economy. That is why, as I pointed out in my appearance in the Congress of Deputies in October, and I would like to reiterate before you today, budgetary policy must actively contribute to addressing some of the imbalances that are emerging. The fiscal policy defined in the General State Budget Project for 2005 generally implies a maintenance of the budgetary stability policy. The objectives established d0 which set the achievement of a slight surplus for all the Public Administrations d0 should be achievable, even in the case of a macroeconomic scenario of lower growth than the one contemplated in the budget projections. However, it should be borne in mind that programming seems to have been carried out more tightly than in previous years, so it provides little scope to accommodate possible deviations. The objective set for 2005 is compatible with the internal criteria of budgetary stability and with Spain's continued membership of the group of euro area countries that comfortably meet the commitments of the Stability and Growth Pact, as reflected in the favourable evolution of structural balances . which discount the effect of the economic cycle on fiscal performance . and the ratio of public debt to the to GDP, which in 2005 could be below 50%. It is also noteworthy the effort made to reflect more exhaustively the situation of public finances, although it has meant the recognition of some expenses that were not programmed in the 2004 budgets and the assumption of the debt accumulated by some public companies, such as RTVE and RENFE. It is necessary that these recognitions are accompanied by the necessary reforms so that imbalances do not occur again in the healthy units and that, from all administrations, extreme rigor is extreme when undertaking spending programs, so that similar situations do not arise again in the future. In a situation such as the current one, in which, as I have already pointed out, domestic demand remains very dynamic and membership of EMU reduces the capacity to implement autonomous demand-side policies, the assessment of the most appropriate tone of fiscal policy has to take into account its contribution to the correction of internal imbalances. From this point of view d0 and taking into account the looseness of monetary conditions that the common monetary policy represents for Spain d0 the tone of the fiscal policy programmed for 2005 could be insufficient to correct the moderately expansionary stance that it is having during this year. In any case, it is essential that every opportunity be taken to deepen budgetary consolidation, avoiding overflows of the programmed figures, even if economic growth is somewhat lower than that contemplated in the macroeconomic table accompanying the Budget. When a longer-term perspective is adopted, the desirability of deepening the process of fiscal consolidation is accentuated, given the need to take into account the pressure that an ageing population can generate on public spending. We are in a moment of uncertainty about the absolute magnitude of this phenomenon, due to the difficulty of projecting the future evolution of some recent events, such as the phenomenon of immigration. However, even the most favourable demographic projections point to strong growth in dependency ratios and pension spending, as well as an increase in public spending linked to elderly care. In a scenario of these characteristics, the dynamics of the pension reserve fund in recent years, which accumulates financial assets for an amount higher than initially established, should be positively assessed. In any case, this dynamic is strongly influenced by a very favourable labour market situation and by demographic developments that cannot be maintained indefinitely, so that, in addition to addressing the necessary reforms, it is necessary to deepen the consolidation of public finances in order to generate greater savings with which to face future spending commitments. Just as important as the aggregate tone of macroeconomic policy is the introduction of structural reforms that boost productivity growth, boost entrepreneurship, and enhance the innovation capacity of the economy as a whole. In this area, it is important that public action is directed, above all, to create the conditions for actors to make their decisions in a sufficiently competitive environment. In the field of housing, it is necessary that measures aimed at promoting access be accompanied by reforms that increase the flexibility of supply, an issue that depends fundamentally on the regulation of the land market, otherwise pressures will always end up manifesting themselves through price increases. Measures aimed at consolidating the foundations for continued employment generation in the economy are of great importance. The reforms introduced in the nineties made it possible to significantly reduce the unemployment rate and, by increasing the potential for job creation, have helped to sustain economic dynamism. However, the inertia and rigidity that wage determination mechanisms continue to present and the elements of inflexibility that persist in other aspects of the labour market make it necessary to deepen the reforms in this market, key to the functioning of the economy. In general, the reform drive must cover a very wide range of sectors and measures in response to the specific problems of the Spanish economy and in line with the objectives of the Lisbon agenda. The strategy to improve competitiveness should adopt a general approach, ranging from the promotion of investment in physical and human capital, the basis of productivity gains, to the revision of some sectoral strategies and to the pattern of productive specialization itself. I believe, ladies and gentlemen, and I conclude with this, that we are at a very important moment for the future of our economy, which we must not miss. Over the last few years, the Spanish economy has received the benefits of macroeconomic stability, which brought about our membership of EMU, and which we must preserve. But if we are to make further progress in our process of real convergence, it is imperative that economic policies remain firmly oriented towards stability and address the challenges that are being posed and to which I have referred throughout this speech.

Aunque este diferencial se debe, en parte, a factores especficos como la diversa intensidad en la traslacin del aumento de los precios del petrleo, refleja, sobre todo, la persistencia de tasas de inflacin ms elevadas en los sectores ms protegidos a la competencia. En este sentido, el diferencial de inflacin tiene su origen en las notables diferencias que se observan en los ritmos de crecimiento de los costes laborales unitarios, muy superiores en nuestra economa y con tendencia, adems, a acentuarse en los ltimos aos. Es, precisamente, en los sectores de servicios donde el aumento de los costes laborales est siendo ms intenso, y son estos sectores, tambin, los que con mayor facilidad pueden repercutirlos en los precios, sin tener que reducir sus mrgenes comerciales. No es este el caso de los sectores industriales, sobre todo de los exportadores, que ven disminuida, as, sus tasas de rentabilidad. La persistencia de estos diferenciales est teniendo, por tanto, efectos negativos sobre la competitividad, y as empieza a reflejarse en el notable aumento del desequilibrio comercial y en el debilitamiento del turismo. Por otra parte, la prolongada fortaleza del gasto interno y, en especial, del gasto de los hogares tiene tambin implicaciones para el equilibrio financiero de estos agentes, tal como han sido puestas de manifiesto por el Banco de Espaa en numerosas ocasiones. A este respecto, no se perciben an cambios en la tendencia creciente del endeudamiento. Bien al contrario, la financiacin a los hogares se ha acelerado en los meses transcurridos de 2004, impulsada por el fuerte crecimiento del crdito hipotecario, a pesar de que el peso de la carga financiera en porcentaje de la renta se ha incrementado. Este crecimiento del crdito hipotecario est estrechamente vinculado a la presin que la demanda de viviendas sigue ejerciendo sobre el precio de los activos inmobiliarios, que tampoco ha dado seales de moderacin. Por tanto, aunque la posicin patrimonial de las familias sigue siendo slida, debido, fundamentalmente, a la revalorizacin de los activos inmobiliarios, ha continuado creciendo la sensibilidad de las decisiones de gasto de este sector ante un eventual aumento de los tipos de inters -que incrementase significativamente su carga financiera-, ante una desaceleracin del empleo o ante una correccin de la sobrevaloracin de la vivienda. En general, puede afirmarse, sin embargo, que en el contexto de continuidad de la expansin global que hoy aparece como ms probable, las perspectivas de crecimiento de la economa espaola durante los prximos trimestres son favorables, aunque no estn exentas de riesgos procedentes tanto del entorno exterior como del mbito domstico. Entre los primeros: un encarecimiento adicional de los precios del petrleo, un escenario de mayor vacilacin en la recuperacin de las economas europeas, o un ajuste temprano de los grandes desequilibrios que se observan hoy a nivel mundial, a travs de una apreciacin excesiva del euro, tendran, sin duda, consecuencias negativas sobre el crecimiento espaol. A nivel interno, la eventual materializacin de algunos riesgos que subyacen al patrn de crecimiento que ha seguido la economa espaola y el agotamiento de algunos de los impulsos expansivos recibidos tras la entrada en la Unin Monetaria tambin podran atenuar nuestro ritmo de crecimiento. Poco podemos hacer desde Espaa para limitar los riesgos que provienen del exterior. Sin embargo, s es posible y necesario afrontar aquellos que tienen un origen interno, mediante el diseo de unas polticas econmicas orientadas a preservar la estabilidad macroeconmica, a encauzar la demanda de los hogares y a fomentar la inversin productiva y la competitividad, de manera que se reequilibren los componentes del gasto que sustentan el avance de la demanda. Una combinacin de polticas monetaria y fiscal menos holgada resulta la respuesta macroeconmica apropiada para abordar los problemas planteados en el terreno de la competitividad pues favorecer la contencin de incrementos de precios y de costes en los sectores menos expuestos a la competencia, de las alzas de los precios de la vivienda al procurar una gradual convergencia de los aumentos de precios de la vivienda hacia tasas compatibles con la evolucin de sus fundamentos y del endeudamiento de las familias al incentivar su desaceleracin hacia pautas ms sostenibles. En este mbito, aunque es posible que, a medida que se recupere la zona del euro, el tono de las condiciones monetarias se vaya adquiriendo un tono menos expansivo, no es previsible que el cambio sea suficiente para afrontar los requerimientos de contencin del gasto interno en la economa espaola. Por ello, como seal en mi comparecencia en el Congreso de los Diputados, en octubre, y quiero reiterar hoy ante ustedes, la poltica presupuestaria tiene que contribuir activamente a encauzar algunos de los desequilibrios que estn emergiendo. La poltica fiscal que define el Proyecto de Presupuestos Generales del Estado para el ao 2005 supone, en lneas generales, un mantenimiento de la poltica de estabilidad presupuestaria. Los objetivos establecidos que fijan el logro de un ligero supervit para el conjunto de las AAPP deberan ser alcanzables, incluso en el caso de un escenario macroeconmico de menor crecimiento al que contemplan las proyecciones del presupuesto. No obstante, debe tenerse en cuenta que la programacin parece que se ha realizado de forma ms ajustada que en aos anteriores, por lo que proporciona un escaso margen para acomodar posibles desviaciones. El objetivo fijado para el 2005 es compatible con los criterios internos de estabilidad presupuestaria y con el mantenimiento de Espaa en el grupo de pases del rea del euro que cumplen con holgura los compromisos del Pacto de Estabilidad y de Crecimiento, tal y como reflejan la favorable evolucin de los saldos estructurales que descuentan el efecto del ciclo econmico sobre los resultados fiscales  y de la ratio de deuda pblica con respecto al PIB, que en 2005 podra situarse por debajo del 50 %. Es reseable, tambin, el esfuerzo realizado para reflejar de manera ms exhaustiva la situacin de las finanzas pblicas, aunque haya supuesto el reconocimiento de algunos gastos que no estaban programados en los presupuestos de 2004 y a la asuncin de la deuda acumulada por algunas empresas pblicas, como RTVE y RENFE. Es preciso que estos reconocimientos, vayan acompaados de las reformas necesarias para que no vuelvan a producirse desequilibrios en las unidades saneadas y que, desde todas las administraciones, se extreme el rigor a la hora de acometer los programas de gasto, para que no vuelvan a surgir situaciones similares en el futuro. En una coyuntura como la actual, en la que, como ya he sealado, la demanda interna conserva un gran dinamismo y la pertenencia a la UEM reduce la capacidad de instrumentar polticas autnomas de demanda, la valoracin sobre el tono ms apropiado de la poltica fiscal tiene que tener en cuenta la contribucin que la misma presta a la correccin de los desequilibrios internos. Desde este punto de vista y teniendo en cuenta la holgura de las condiciones monetarias que la poltica monetaria comn representa para Espaa- el tono de la poltica fiscal programado para 2005 podra resultar insuficiente para corregir la orientacin moderadamente expansiva que la misma esta teniendo durante el presente ejercicio. En cualquier caso, es fundamental que se aprovechen todas las oportunidades para profundizar en la consolidacin presupuestaria, evitando desbordamientos de las cifras programadas, an cuando el crecimiento econmico fuera algo inferior al contemplado en el cuadro macroeconmico que acompaa a los Presupuestos. Cuando se adopta una perspectiva de ms largo plazo, la conveniencia de profundizar en el proceso de consolidacin fiscal se acenta, ante la necesidad de tener en cuenta la presin que puede generar sobre el gasto pblico el envejecimiento de la poblacin. Nos encontramos en un momento de incertidumbre en torno a la magnitud absoluta de este fenmeno, por la dificultad de proyectar la evolucin futura de algunos hechos recientes, como puede ser el fenmeno de la inmigracin. Con todo, incluso las proyecciones demogrficas ms favorables apuntan a un fuerte crecimiento de las tasas de dependencia y del gasto en pensiones, as como un incremento del gasto pblico vinculado al cuidado de los mayores. En un escenario de estas caractersticas, cabe valorar positivamente la dinmica del fondo de reserva de las pensiones en estos ltimos aos, que acumula activos financieros por un importe superior al establecido inicialmente. En todo caso, esta dinmica est muy influida por una coyuntura muy favorable del mercado de trabajo y por unos desarrollos demogrficos que no se pueden mantener de forma indefinida, por lo que, adems de abordar las reformas necesarias, es preciso profundizar en el saneamiento de las finanzas pblicas con el fin de generar un mayor ahorro con el que afrontar los compromisos futuros de gasto. Tan importante como el tono agregado de la poltica macroeconmica es la introduccin de reformas estructurales que impulsen el crecimiento de la productividad, dinamicen la iniciativa empresarial y favorezcan la capacidad de innovacin de la economa, en su conjunto. En este mbito, es importante que la actuacin pblica se dirija, sobre todo, a crear las condiciones para que los agentes puedan tomar sus decisiones en un entorno suficientemente competitivo. En el terreno de la vivienda, es necesario que las medidas orientadas a favorecer el acceso vayan acompaadas de reformas que incrementen la flexibilidad de la oferta, cuestin que depende fundamentalmente de la regulacin del mercado del suelo, pues de otro modo las presiones siempre terminarn manifestndose a travs de las subidas de precios. Tienen gran importancia las medidas encaminadas a consolidar las bases para la generacin continuada de empleo en la economa. Las reformas introducidas en los aos noventa permitieron reducir significativamente la tasa de desempleo y, al aumentar el potencial de creacin de empleo, han contribuido a sostener el dinamismo econmico. Sin embargo, la inercia y la rigidez que siguen presentando los mecanismos de determinacin salarial y los elementos de inflexibilidad que persisten en otros aspectos del mercado de trabajo hacen necesaria una profundizacin en las reformas en este mercado, clave para el funcionamiento de la economa. En general, el impulso reformador debe abarcar un abanico de sectores y medidas muy amplio en respuesta a los problemas especficos de la economa espaola y en lnea con los objetivos de la agenda de Lisboa. La estrategia de mejora de la competitividad debe adoptar un enfoque general, que abarque desde el fomento de la inversin en capital fsico y humano, base de las ganancias de productividad, a la revisin de algunas estrategias sectoriales y al propio patrn de especializacin productiva. Creo, seoras, y con esto concluyo, que nos encontramos en un momento muy importante para el futuro de nuestra economa, que no debemos desaprovechar. La economa espaola ha recibido a lo largo de los ltimos aos los beneficios que comporta la estabilidad macroeconmica, que trajo consigo nuestra pertenencia a la UEM, y que hemos de preservar. Pero para que podamos seguir avanzando en nuestro proceso de convergencia real es imprescindible que las polticas econmicas mantengan una firme orientacin hacia la estabilidad y aborden los retos que se estn planteados y a los que he hecho referencia a lo largo de esta intervencin.

Title: Speech: Eugenio Domingo, the central banker (Tribute to Eugenio Domingo Solans, organized by the College of Economists at the Bank of Spain, Madrid)
text: Madrid, 21 February 2005 Eugenio Domingo, the central banker Tribute to Eugenio Domingo Solans, organized by the College of Economists. Bank of Spain Jaime Caruana Governor of the Bank of Spain The highlights of Eugenio Domingo's personality, as well as the wide range of his interests and activities, have already been conveniently underlined by those who have preceded me in this rostrum. But it is obvious that justice is only done to the personality of Eugenio Domingo if his outstanding role as a central banker is sufficiently highlighted. It is in this facet of Eugenio's professional activity where I want to focus my words. Eugenio Domingo held positions of maximum responsibility both in the Bank of Spain, first, and in the European Central Bank, later, for a total period of ten years. This allowed him to participate actively from different positions in the project of creating a monetary union in Europe; This required close collaboration between the national central banks to prepare the conceptual foundations and technical procedures required for the effective exercise of a common monetary policy implemented within a federally cut institutional scheme embodied in what is now known as the Eurosystem. In this way, the national central banks played an essential role in the discussions on the strategy and operational framework of the single monetary policy that took place in the second half of the decade of the nineties, and which led to a model where the main decisions are taken by a central body, the Governing Council of the ECB, made up of the executive directors of the ECB and the governors of the national central banks, and where implementation tasks are mainly carried out in a decentralised manner. In addition, it was agreed to maintain within the Eurosystem a network of committees and working groups dedicated to specific topics, where central banks could exchange their views, thus taking into account the views of national experts and drawing on the experience and knowledge accumulated by all Eurosystem members in making final decisions. The ECB's own Executive Board was nourished by people who, like Eugenio Domingo, not only had great prestige but also brought together diverse backgrounds, sensitivities and criteria. This has allowed the resulting entity to be much more than the sum of its parts and, in particular, the strategic and operational framework of the single monetary policy to compare favourably with that available to the main central banks. When Eugenio Domingo arrived at the European Central Bank, as a member of the Executive Board, at the time of its foundation in June 1998, the challenge facing this institution was considerable. It is true that the European Monetary Institute had already made progress in some important aspects of the design of the single monetary policy and the organization of the entity that should lead it, but the concreteness and formal adoption of all the many pieces required for the implementation of the new monetary authority would only take place after the establishment of the European Central Bank. The functions that were then directly assigned to Eugenio Domingo were, moreover, particularly relevant. As responsible for issues related to Banknotes, Statistics and Information Systems, it could be said that Eugenio Domingo had to directly take charge of much of the basic infrastructure of the operation of the single monetary policy. Thus, among the competences of Eugenio Domingo was that of guaranteeing adequate technological support for the European Central Bank, which presented great needs in this area, as a result of the technical complexity of its functions and the objective difficulty of operating with a high degree of decentralization, which required the adoption of sophisticated harmonisation protocols and interconnection procedures between national computer systems. Within the orbit of functions of Eugenio Domingo was also to ensure the availability of the broad statistical base required for the adoption of monetary policy decisions. This involved the implementation of a complex decentralized system for collecting information d0 particularly in the monetary and financial field d0 and agile procedures for continuous and timely updating of a wide range of indicators. Finally, Eugenio Domingo assumed, as director of the ECB, the important responsibility of managing the banknote area, to which I will refer later. If I may go back a little further in time, I would like to recall that it was not the first time that Eugenio Domingo faced major challenges in his role as a central banker. As you know, Eugenio Domingo was a member of the Governing Council and the Executive Committee of the Banco de Espa96a between 1994 and 1998. Perhaps, the main challenge that the Bank of Spain had to undertake had to do with the design of a monetary policy strategy that would serve the priority objective of economic convergence with the main EU countries. After the crisis of the exchange rate mechanism of the European Monetary System in 1992, which had led to several devaluations of the peseta, monetary policy was at a crossroads in 1994: it was clear that its strategy could not rest on exchange rate objectives d0 unable to sufficiently anchor the expectations of agents after the devaluations. nor in monetary aggregates, since since the end of the eighties there had been a progressive deterioration of its informative content on the foreseeable evolution of prices or activity. Stabilizing inflation expectations was also an urgent task for monetary policy in a context of weak public finances, manifested in a substantial public deficit and a growing stock of public debt. In the debate that took place within the Bank of Spain on the monetary policy strategy that could best adapt to these circumstances, Eugenio Domingo played a very important role, showing what I believe was a prominent feature of his personality: his ability to combine deep intellectual convictions with an appreciable dose of pragmatism. In particular, Eugenio Domingo supported the establishment of a strategy of direct inflation targets, so that monetary policy decisions and their communication would be more focused on the foreseeable evolution of this variable in the medium term, which would allow the Bank's commitment to achieving price stability to be more evident. which was the primary objective of monetary policy according to the recently passed Law of Autonomy. However, Eugenio also defended the need to preserve the role of the evolution of money in circulation as a privileged indicator because, although it was clear that monetary aggregates could not act as an intermediate objective of monetary policy, it was also true that they could collect and synthesize relevant information on the inflationary situation and provided an element of continuity with the analytical approach followed until that moment. Years later, Eugenio Domingo participated in a similar debate within the European Central Bank when the Eurosystem's monetary policy strategy was discussed, in a context in which, once again, neither the exchange rate nor monetary aggregates were variables that could be chosen as intermediate objectives. For this reason, he was surely satisfied when he found that the strategy finally adopted by the new European institution had many similarities with the one that the Bank of Spain applied between 1995 and 1998 and that he actively contributed to design. In particular, the Eurosystem's monetary policy strategy quantifies the inflation rate it considers compatible with the price stability objective and monitors the various factors that may affect its evolution over the medium term, while giving an important role to the trajectory of monetary aggregates in the analysis of the inflationary outlook. One of the main advantages of this strategy is that it allows a flexible management of monetary policy without compromising the commitment to maintaining price stability. Some flexibility for monetary policy to pursue its objectives is essential as information on the economic situation is always incomplete, subject to a degree of uncertainty, and the links of observed indicators to final targets may also change. To overcome these difficulties, the strategy places in the medium term the relevant horizon in which the objectives must be achieved, and emphasizes the diversity of variables that are subject to observation and the variety of analytical approaches used in the assessment of inflationary perspectives. Similarly, the growth rates of monetary aggregates d0 which have been unusually high in recent years d0 must also be subject to careful interpretation to extract their possible implications for price developments in the medium and long term, as they are variables sensitive to changes in agents' preferences for the demand for liquid assets. The Eurosystem's monetary policy strategy can therefore allow for short-term deviations in inflation developments from its target, such as those that have taken place in the euro area in recent months, considering that they are, above all, the result of temporary shocks d0 such as that caused by higher oil prices d0 and, They are therefore consistent with the return to more moderate price growth rates in the future. In fact, the current outlook for inflation developments is relatively favourable, suggesting a return to year-on-year rates below 2% in the coming months. The outlook for the evolution of activity in the euro area is somewhat more uncertain, following the slump experienced in the second half of 2004, although the recovery is expected to gradually strengthen during 2005. But perhaps the most important milestone in Eugenio Domingo's fruitful professional career d0 for which he will surely be most remembered by the international financial community d0 was the putting euro banknotes and coins into circulation, a task for which he was responsible as a member of the Executive Board of the European Central Bank between 1998 and 2004. It thus played a leading role in the design and supervision of preparations for the production of the new banknotes and coins and the process of exchanging national coins for euro banknotes from 1 January 2002. On that date, a long and costly process, launched several years earlier, was completed to determine the design of banknotes, paper support and security mechanisms that would be able to achieve easy recognition by the public and reduce the chances of counterfeiting to a minimum. As we get used to the use of euro cash in transactions, we may also lose perspective of what the introduction of the new currency meant. I would therefore like to recall here the merit of those who had to coordinate the procedures required to replace the banknotes and coins used by more than 300 million Europeans with the new euro-denominated ones in a very short period of time, and to coordinate the management of the complex processes of mass production, storage and distribution. By way of example, suffice it to note that before 1 January 2002, EUR 145 billion had already been distributed between banknotes and coins to credit institutions so that the exchange process could begin on the same night of 31 December 2001 and that a high percentage of the approximately 200 000 ATMs operating in the euro area were able to provide euro banknotes already in the euro area. the first week of January 2002. In that month alone, almost 8 billion new banknotes were put into circulation, worth a total of 220 billion euros, representing more than two-thirds of the cash in circulation at the end of the previous year. By the first quarter of 2002, the withdrawal of the old national currencies was almost complete: by the end of March, more than 90% of the cash was euro-denominated banknotes. Symbolically, those days will be hard to forget. The undeniable success of the exchange operation and the favourable reception of the new banknotes by European citizens allowed them to perceive more palpably the reality of the process of economic and monetary integration. Indeed, for many, the physical presence of the new currency was the most unmistakable sign that the process of European integration was advancing irreversibly despite its considerable complexity. I am sure that he felt the satisfaction of his contribution, so concrete and, at the same time, so essential, to that process with which he was firmly identified and personally committed. It is evident that his professional successes were the direct consequence of his considerable personal qualities. As he pointed out, he knew how to combine a great analytical capacity with a strong practical sense, which allowed him to contribute significantly to decision-making, both from the point of view of his own responsibilities and in the collegial scope of the Committees and Councils in which he participated, and of which he was always a fundamental piece. These features were compounded by a great ability to manage projects and human teams, as brilliantly demonstrated in the direction of the process of introducing euro banknotes to which I referred earlier. All these aspects of his personality made Eugenio Domingo an excellent central banker and an effective public servant. If you add to these professional traits his great human qualities, evident to anyone who has treated him personally, you will understand perfectly why I consider it a privilege to have worked with Eugenio for many years and an honor to have been able to establish a friendly relationship with him. Thanks a lot.
text_original: Madrid, 21 de febrero de 2005 Eugenio Domingo, el banquero central Homenaje a Eugenio Domingo Solans, organizado por el Colegio de Economistas. Banco de Espaa Jaime Caruana Gobernador del Banco de Espaa Los aspectos ms destacados de la personalidad de Eugenio Domingo, as como el amplio rango de sus intereses y actividades, han sido ya convenientemente subrayados por los que me han precedido en esta tribuna. Pero es obvio que solo se hace justicia a la personalidad de Eugenio Domingo si se destaca suficientemente su papel sobresaliente como banquero central. Es en esta faceta de la actividad profesional de Eugenio donde quiero centrar mis palabras. Eugenio Domingo ocup cargos de mxima responsabilidad tanto en el Banco de Espaa, primero, como en el Banco Central Europeo, despus, durante un perodo total de diez aos. Esto le permiti participar activamente desde distintas posiciones en el proyecto de creacin de una unin monetaria en Europa; misin que exigi la colaboracin estrecha entre los bancos centrales nacionales para preparar los fundamentos conceptuales y los procedimientos tcnicos requeridos para el ejercicio eficaz de una poltica monetaria comn instrumentada dentro de un esquema institucional de corte federal plasmado en lo que hoy se conoce como Eurosistema. De este modo, los bancos centrales nacionales desempearon un papel esencial en las discusiones sobre la estrategia y el marco operativo de la poltica monetaria nica que tuvieron lugar en la segunda mitad de la dcada de los aos noventa, y que condujo a un modelo donde las decisiones principales son asumidas por un rgano central, el Consejo de Gobierno del BCE, formado por los consejeros ejecutivos del BCE y los gobernadores de los bancos centrales nacionales, y donde las labores de instrumentacin son fundamentalmente realizadas de manera descentralizada. Adems, se acord mantener en el Eurosistema una red de comits y grupos de trabajo dedicados a temas especficos, donde los bancos centrales pudieran intercambiar sus puntos de vista, con lo que se tendran en cuenta las opiniones de los expertos nacionales y podran aprovecharse la experiencia y conocimiento acumulado por todos los miembros del Eurosistema a la hora de adoptar las decisiones finales. El propio Comit Ejecutivo del BCE se nutri de personas que como Eugenio Domingo, no solo tenan un gran prestigio sino que, adems, reunan diversas procedencias, sensibilidades y criterios. Todo ello ha permitido que la entidad resultante sea mucho ms que la suma de sus partes y que, en particular, el marco estratgico y operativo de la poltica monetaria nica se compare favorablemente con el que disponen los principales bancos centrales. Cuando Eugenio Domingo llega al Banco Central Europeo, como miembro del Comit Ejecutivo, en el momento de su fundacin en junio de 1998, el reto que tena ante s esta institucin era considerable. Es cierto que el Instituto Monetario Europeo ya haba avanzado en algunos aspectos importantes del diseo de la poltica monetaria nica y de la organizacin de la entidad que debera dirigirla, pero la concrecin y adopcin formal de todas las numerosas piezas que requera la puesta en funcionamiento de la nueva autoridad monetaria solo se efectuaran tras el establecimiento del Banco Central Europeo. Las funciones que fueron directamente asignadas entonces a Eugenio Domingo eran, adems, particularmente relevantes. Como responsable de las cuestiones relacionadas con Billetes, Estadsticas y Sistemas de Informacin, se podra decir que Eugenio Domingo tuvo que hacerse cargo directamente de gran parte de la infraestructura bsica del funcionamiento de la poltica monetaria nica. As, entre las competencias de Eugenio Domingo se encontraba la de garantizar el soporte tecnolgico adecuado para el Banco Central Europeo, que presentaba unas grandes necesidades en esta materia, como consecuencia de la complejidad tcnica de sus funciones y de la dificultad objetiva que supona operar con un alto grado de descentralizacin, que requiri la adopcin de sofisticados protocolos de armonizacin y procedimientos de interconexin entre los sistemas informticos nacionales. Dentro de la rbita de funciones de Eugenio Domingo se encontraba tambin asegurar la disponibilidad de la amplia base estadstica que requera la adopcin de las decisiones de poltica monetaria. Esto supuso la puesta en marcha de un complejo sistema descentralizado de recogida de informacin en particular en el mbito monetario y financiero- y de procedimientos giles de actualizacin continua y puntual de una amplia gama de indicadores. Finalmente, Eugenio Domingo asumi, como consejero del BCE, la importante responsabilidad de gestionar el rea de billetes, a la que me referir ms adelante. Si me permiten remontarme un poco ms en el tiempo, me gustara recordar que no era la primera vez que Eugenio Domingo se enfrentaba a retos de envergadura en su faceta de banquero central. Como ustedes saben, Eugenio Domingo fue miembro del Consejo de Gobierno y de la Comisin Ejecutiva del Banco de Espaa entre 1994 y 1998. Quizs, el principal reto que debi acometer el Banco de Espaa tuvo que ver con el diseo de una estrategia de poltica monetaria que sirviera al objetivo prioritario de la convergencia econmica con los principales pases de la UE. Tras la crisis del mecanismo de tipos de cambio del Sistema Monetario Europeo en 1992, que haba provocado varias devaluaciones de la peseta, la poltica monetaria se encontraba en 1994 en una encrucijada: era evidente que su estrategia no poda descansar en objetivos cambiarios incapaces de anclar suficientemente las expectativas de los agentes tras las devaluaciones-, ni tampoco en los agregados monetarios, ya que desde finales de la dcada de los aos ochenta se vena observando un deterioro progresivo de su contenido informativo sobre la previsible evolucin de los precios o de la actividad. La estabilizacin de las expectativas de inflacin era, adems, una tarea urgente de la poltica monetaria en un contexto de debilidad de las finanzas pblicas, que se manifestaba en un dficit pblico sustancial y en un saldo creciente de deuda pblica. En el debate que tuvo lugar en el seno del Banco de Espaa sobre la estrategia de poltica monetaria que mejor poda adaptarse a esas circunstancias, Eugenio Domingo desempe un papel muy relevante, dando muestras de lo que creo fue un rasgo destacado de su personalidad: su capacidad para combinar unas profundas convicciones intelectuales con una dosis apreciable de pragmatismo. En particular, Eugenio Domingo apoy el establecimiento de una estrategia de objetivos directos de inflacin, de modo que las decisiones de poltica monetaria y su comunicacin bascularan en mayor medida sobre la evolucin previsible de esta variable en el medio plazo, lo que permitira que se hiciera ms patente el compromiso del Banco con el logro de la estabilidad de precios, que era el objetivo primordial de la poltica monetaria de acuerdo con la Ley de Autonoma recin aprobada. Sin embargo, Eugenio tambin defendi la necesidad de conservar el papel de la evolucin del dinero en circulacin como indicador privilegiado pues, aunque era claro que los agregados monetarios no podan actuar como objetivo intermedio de la poltica monetaria, tambin era cierto que podan recoger y sintetizar informacin relevante sobre la situacin inflacionista y proporcionaban un elemento de continuidad con el enfoque analtico seguido hasta ese momento. Aos ms tarde, Eugenio Domingo particip en un debate similar en el seno del Banco Central Europeo cuando se debati la estrategia de poltica monetaria del Eurosistema, en un contexto en que, de nuevo, ni el tipo de cambio ni los agregados monetarios eran variables susceptibles de ser elegidas como objetivos intermedios. Por ello, seguramente se sinti satisfecho cuando comprob que la estrategia finalmente adoptada por la nueva institucin europea guardaba bastantes similitudes con la que el Banco de Espaa aplic entre 1995 y 1998 y que l contribuy activamente a disear. En concreto, la estrategia de poltica monetaria del Eurosistema cuantifica la tasa de inflacin que juzga compatible con el objetivo de estabilidad de precios y realiza un seguimiento de los diversos factores que pueden afectar a su evolucin a medio plazo, al tiempo que otorga un papel relevante a la trayectoria de los agregados monetarios en el anlisis de las perspectivas inflacionistas. Una de las principales ventajas de esta estrategia es que permite un manejo flexible de la poltica monetaria sin que esto ponga en entredicho el compromiso con el mantenimiento de la estabilidad de precios. Disponer de un cierto margen de flexibilidad para que la poltica monetaria persiga sus objetivos es esencial por cuanto la informacin sobre la situacin econmica siempre es incompleta, est sujeta a un cierto grado de incertidumbre y los vnculos de los indicadores observados con las metas finales tambin pueden ser cambiantes. Para superar estas dificultades, la estrategia sita en el medio plazo el horizonte relevante en el que hay que alcanzar los objetivos, y pone nfasis en la diversidad de variables que estn sujetas a observacin y en la variedad de enfoques analticos que se utilizan en la valoracin de las perspectivas inflacionistas. De la misma forma, los ritmos de crecimiento de los agregados monetarios que han sido inusualmente altos en los ltimos aos- tambin deben estar sujetos a una interpretacin cuidadosa para extraer sus posibles implicaciones sobre la evolucin de los precios a medio y largo plazo, pues son variables sensibles a cambios en las preferencias de los agentes por la demanda de activos lquidos. La estrategia de poltica monetaria del Eurosistema puede admitir, por tanto, desviaciones a corto plazo de la evolucin de la inflacin respecto a su objetivo, como las que han tenido lugar en la zona del euro durante los ltimos meses, al considerar que son, sobre todo, el resultado de perturbaciones transitorias como la causada por el encarecimiento del petrleo- y, por tanto, son coherentes con el retorno a tasas de incremento de los precios ms moderadas en el futuro. De hecho, las actuales perspectivas sobre la evolucin de la inflacin son relativamente favorables, pues sugieren el retorno a tasas interanuales inferiores al 2% en los prximos meses. El panorama sobre la evolucin de la actividad en la zona del euro es algo ms incierto, tras el bache experimentado en la segunda mitad de 2004, aunque cabe esperar que la recuperacin vaya fortalecindose progresivamente durante 2005. Pero, quizs el hito ms importante en la fructfera carrera profesional de Eugenio Domingo aquello por lo que ser seguramente ms recordado por la comunidad financiera internacional- fue el de la puesta en circulacin de los billetes y monedas en euros, cometido del que fue responsable como miembro del Comit Ejecutivo del Banco Central Europeo entre 1998 y 2004. De este modo, desempe un papel protagonista en el diseo y supervisin de los preparativos para la produccin de los nuevos billetes y monedas, as como del proceso de canje de las monedas nacionales por los billetes en euros a partir del 1 de enero de 2002. En esa fecha culmin un largo y costoso proceso, puesto en marcha varios aos antes, para determinar el diseo de los billetes, el soporte en papel y los mecanismos de seguridad que fueran capaces de lograr un fcil reconocimiento por parte del pblico y de reducir las posibilidades de falsificacin al mnimo. A medida que vamos acostumbrndonos al uso del efectivo en euros en las transacciones, es posible que tambin vayamos perdiendo la perspectiva de lo que supuso la introduccin de la nueva moneda. Por ello, me gustara recordar aqu el mrito de quien debi coordinar los procedimientos que requera la sustitucin de los billetes y monedas utilizados por ms de 300 millones de europeos por los nuevos denominados en euros en un perodo muy reducido de tiempo, y coordinar la gestin de los complejos procesos de produccin masiva, almacenaje y distribucin. A modo de ejemplos, baste sealar que antes del 1 de enero de 2002 ya se haban distribuido 145 mm de euros entre billetes y monedas a las entidades de crdito para que el proceso de canje pudiera comenzar la misma noche del 31 de diciembre de 2001 y que un alto porcentaje de los aproximadamente 200.000 cajeros automticos que estaban en funcionamiento en la zona del euro pudieron proporcionar billetes en euros ya en la primera semana del mes de enero de 2002. En el primer trimestre del ao 2002 la retirada de las antiguas monedas nacionales se haba completado prcticamente: as, a finales de marzo, ms del 90% del efectivo corresponda a billetes denominados en euros. Desde el punto de vista simblico, aquellos das sern difciles de olvidar. El xito incontestable de la operacin de canje y la favorable acogida de los nuevos billetes por parte de los ciudadanos europeos permitieron que estos percibieran de modo ms palpable la realidad del proceso de integracin econmica y monetaria. De hecho, para muchos, la presencia fsica de la nueva moneda fue la seal ms inequvoca de que el proceso de integracin europea avanzaba de modo irreversible a pesar de su considerable complejidad. Estoy seguro de que l sinti la satisfaccin de su contribucin, tan concreta y, al mismo tiempo, tan esencial, a ese proceso con el que se encontraba firmemente identificado y personalmente comprometido. Es evidente que sus xitos profesionales fueron la consecuencia directa de sus considerables cualidades personales. Como sealaba, saba combinar una gran capacidad analtica con un acusado sentido prctico, lo que le permita contribuir de modo destacado a la toma de decisiones, tanto desde el punto de vista de sus propias responsabilidades como en el mbito colegiado de los Comits y Consejos en los que particip, y de los que fue siempre una pieza fundamental.
