This higher level of risk explains the higher margins of the banking business and, therefore, throws some uncertainty about the final impact on profitability, once the higher level of risk is taken into account. In addition to monitoring credit and market risk in each country, banks should pay attention to the greater operational risk involved in managing an entity with a larger asset size and, above all, greater complexity, due to the presence in many countries, with macroeconomic environments, regulatory and accounting frameworks and technological development very different between them. Likewise, in an increasingly interconnected and global world, internationalization can lead to an increase in reputational risk, so that the difficulties in a country translate into greater distrust towards the entity as a whole, without even the quantitative impact of these difficulties being significant. To date, Spanish entities have demonstrated a high management capacity in their internationalization processes, even when they have had to face very complex situations in some of the countries in which they are present. This is due to the highly competitive environment in which they have operated in Spain, their previous experience of mergers and acquisitions, and also their ability to operate under high prudential standards and banking supervision. The existence of a competitive market for banking products and services, the experience gained in merger processes, and the consequent restructuring, and the supervisory pressure in Spain have forged a management capacity exportable to other banking markets and systems. A second element of reflection is the capacity in terms of own resources that entities must show to support their internationalization process. The acquisition of foreign banks puts pressure on their own resources (through the goodwill generated) and increases their risk-weighted assets, for which they must have sufficient own resources. Shareholders must commit to the internationalization process through their willingness to carry out capital increases and to strengthen the entity's reserves by retaining results. Capital and reserves are the two defining elements of the quality of the equity available to an entity. From a prudential point of view, in the medium term, an institution's own resources must have a sufficient level of quality and, therefore, the lower quality elements that make up its regulatory own resources (subordinated financing and preferred shares) must be limited. A high presence of innovative instruments in core own resources ends up translating into an increase in the cost of financing that has a negative impact on the profitability of institutions. Therefore, although the Bank of Spain can recognize innovative instruments in regulatory own resources (for example, allowing preferential shares that incorporate a remuneration increase clause after 10 years to be computed as basic equity), it would always limit their relative weight (for example, around 15%), and without forgetting that there is already a limit of 30% on traditional preferred shares. The combination of the significant process of opening up the Spanish banking system and membership of the euro zone have allowed the Spanish economy to finance without stress the growing gap that exists between the growth of credit to the resident private sector, largely linked to the financing of housing purchases, and bank deposits from this sector. Access to the European interbank market has allowed Spanish banks to supplement the funds they obtain from their depositors in order to lend Spanish families the amounts they need to buy their home. However, this poses challenges to the Spanish economy and entities. Firstly, the indebtedness of Spanish families already exceeds the Community average and is growing at a very high rate. Spanish families should be reminded that when contracting their mortgages they are aware of the impact that a future rise in interest rates may have on their monthly disposable income and, therefore, on their ability to repay said mortgage loan. In particular, the warning is even more relevant for those with less room for manoeuvre (instability in employment, high level of indebtedness, very long-term mortgage, etc.). Entities must also analyze this situation carefully, applying a strict policy of admission, granting and monitoring of their risks with mortgage guarantee, both with families and with real estate developers. The latter have historically shown themselves to be a very risky sector, with a high delinquency rate in recessionary phases. In addition, the dependence on the European banking market to finance the gap between investment and financing from the resident private sector will end up putting pressure on the costs of financing and, therefore, on the profitability of Spanish entities. Finally, as a fourth element of prudential reflection on the internationalization of Spanish banks, there is a need to increase coordination between banking supervisors. This coordination is both facilitated and demanded by the convergence in the accounting framework that will bring the new international accounting standards (IAS, International Accounting Standards, or IFRS, International Financial Reporting Standards) and by the development of a common framework of own resources requirements (Basel II). In addition, this cooperation and increasing interaction between supervisors must take place, with differential elements, both at global level and at EU level. As mentioned above, the implementation of IAS and Basel II is an enabler of such cooperation. In the case of IAS, because their implementation (initially in the EU and in the future worldwide) involves the development of a common financial reporting language that greatly facilitates cooperation and, where appropriate, the development of a common supervisory approach. In the case of Basel II, because it represents a shift towards risk-based supervision, that is, a development of a new common supervisory culture at global level. Moreover, in the case of Basel II, this global coordination effort does not start from scratch. Indeed, since Basel I has been applied to more than one hundred countries, the importance of a sound and well-capitalized international financial system for the proper functioning of the world economy is fully recognized. Even so, Basel II requires supervisors to further strengthen their cooperation and coordination to achieve an effective implementation of the new Basel II capital arrangement, which constitutes an important step forward in the measurement, management and supervision of banking risks. At the level of the European Union, this need for coordination is even greater, because we are talking about a single financial market, with a common regulation through directives but with an execution of that regulation carried out by local supervisory authorities of each of the member states. Coordination to ensure a homogeneous application of Community rules is therefore essential in the European context. This differential element of the European context is reflected in initiatives such as the creation of the so-called level 3 committees within the Lamfalussy approach (CESR for securities, CEBS for banking and CEIOPS for insurance), which are responsible for coordination between supervisors and for advancing the convergence of supervisory practices. In addition, the current proposal for a Directive on the implementation of Basel II contains specific elements of reinforcement, such as the increased role of the consolidated supervisor (the parent parent home supervisor), the creation of colleges of supervisors (i.e. a grouping with the supervisors of a specific consolidated group) or the strengthening of supervisory transparency. In short, this greater international cooperation will contribute to the growing internationalization of banking in Spain, Europe and the world without undermining the solvency and stability of the financial system.
text_original: Madrid, 24 de junio de 2005 Internacionalizacin de la banca espaola La empresa espaola ante los nuevos retos de la internacionalizacin. APIE Gonzalo Gil Subgobernador del Banco de Espaa El sistema financiero espaol ha experimentado una profunda transformacin desde que inici su proceso de desregulacin y liberalizacin, a mediados de la dcada de los setenta. Uno de los aspectos ms destacados de dicha transformacin es su apertura al exterior, tanto por la entrada de bancos extranjeros en Espaa como por la creciente actividad en el exterior de las entidades nacionales. Desde finales de la dcada de los setenta, la banca extranjera ha ido entrando en nuestro pas y contribuyendo al aumento de la competencia y de la eficiencia del sistema bancario espaol. Al principio, la banca extranjera se centr en el negocio mayorista, pero luego, progresivamente, fue aumentando su presencia en el negocio minorista, de particulares y de empresas medianas y pequeas. Los bancos extranjeros han aportado innovacin en productos y en canales de distribucin que han mejorado la prestacin de servicios bancarios a los clientes, tanto de activo (prstamos) como de pasivo (depsitos), del conjunto de entidades de crdito que operan en Espaa. Las entidades espaolas han sido capaces de asimilar la entrada de la banca extranjera, adaptarse a sus innovaciones y mantener una cuota de mercado elevada. Algunos bancos extranjeros han abandonado el mercado espaol, bien por cambios de estrategia de su casa matriz, bien por el elevado grado de competencia y eficiencia que han dificultado su expansin. Otras entidades, en cambio, han sabido adaptarse especializndose en segmentos de mercado especficos o desarrollando un modelo de banca universal por todo el territorio. Los bancos espaoles, en particular, los de mayor tamao, han desarrollado en la ltima dcada un proceso intenso de internacionalizacin, proceso que todava contina. La maduracin del negocio, el estrechamiento de mrgenes y la elevada competencia que existe entre las entidades en el mercado domstico ha llevado a algunas de ellas a comprar bancos en Latinoamrica y en Europa, exportando sus plataformas tecnolgicas, su capacidad de gestin y su visin del negocio bancario, buscando aprovechar el potencial de crecimiento que ofrecen algunos pases menos bancarizados o buscando una mayor diversificacin del riesgo. Los protagonistas de este proceso de internacionalizacin se han convertido en entidades multinacionales, con un tamao del activo muy elevado y una capitalizacin burstil que los sita entre los diez primeros del ranking europeo. El proceso de internacionalizacin de la banca espaola, un proceso rpido, intenso y relativamente reciente, plantea a las entidades involucradas y al supervisor bancario espaol una serie de consideraciones prudenciales. En primer lugar, la internacionalizacin de las entidades espaolas exige una elevada capacidad de gestin y un reforzamiento de la funcin de control de los diferentes riesgos asumidos. Los bancos adquiridos en los diferentes pases necesitan, normalmente, un proceso intenso de saneamiento y/o un vuelco en sus planteamientos estratgicos y en su gestin del negocio. Para ello, hay que contar con equipos humanos en la matriz dispuestos a trasladarse al pas en cuestin y a permanecer el tiempo que sea necesario para implantar el nuevo concepto de negocio bancario en toda la organizacin adquirida, gestionar y controlar la transicin y hacer frente a las dificultades especficas que puedan ir surgiendo. Adems de la estrategia comercial de refocalizacin del negocio y la de saneamiento, hay que proceder, normalmente, a la implantacin de las plataformas tecnolgicas de la matriz que permiten generar economas de escala, con el consiguiente ahorro de costes. Todo lo anterior requiere una capacidad de organizacin elevada, una cierta flexibilidad en los recursos humanos gestionados y una inversin en sistemas de control. La capacidad de gestin debe extenderse tambin al control de los riesgos. Es cierto que la diversificacin de la actividad bancaria a nivel internacional contribuye a disminuir el riesgo, pero, no obstante, tambin es cierto que algunos de los pases en los que las entidades espaolas han entrado son economas emergentes, sujetas a una mayor volatilidad de su actividad econmica y, por tanto, a un mayor nivel de riesgo. Dicho mayor nivel de riesgo explica los mayores mrgenes del negocio bancario y, por tanto, arroja cierta incertidumbre sobre el impacto final en la rentabilidad, una vez tenido en cuenta el nivel de riesgo mayor. Adems del seguimiento del riesgo de crdito y de mercado en cada pas, los bancos debern prestar atencin al mayor riesgo operacional que supone gestionar una entidad con un mayor tamao del activo y, sobre todo, de una mayor complejidad, por la presencia en numerosos pases, con entornos macroeconmicos, marcos regulatorios y contables y desarrollo tecnolgico muy dispar entre ellos. Asimismo, en un mundo cada vez ms interconectado y global, la internacionalizacin puede llevar a aumentar el riesgo reputacional, de tal forma que las dificultades en un pas se traduzcan en una mayor desconfianza hacia el conjunto de la entidad, sin que ni siquiera el impacto cuantitativo de dichas dificultades sea significativo. Hasta la fecha, las entidades espaolas han demostrado una elevada capacidad de gestin en sus procesos de internacionalizacin, incluso cuando han tenido que afrontar situaciones muy complejas en algunos de los pases en los que estn presentes. Ello se debe al entorno fuertemente competitivo en el que se han desenvuelto en Espaa, a su experiencia previa de fusiones y adquisiciones, y tambin a su capacidad para desenvolverse bajo unas normas prudenciales y una supervisin bancaria exigentes. La existencia de un mercado de productos y servicios bancarios competitivo, la experiencia adquirida en procesos de fusin, y la consiguiente reestructuracin, y la presin supervisora en Espaa han forjado una capacidad de gestin exportable a otros mercados y sistemas bancarios. Un segundo elemento de reflexin es la capacidad en trminos de recursos propios que deben mostrar las entidades para soportar su proceso de internacionalizacin. La adquisicin de bancos extranjeros presiona sobre sus recursos propios (a travs de los fondos de comercio generados) y aumenta sus activos ponderados por riesgo, para los que deben de disponer de suficientes recursos propios. Los accionistas deben comprometerse en el proceso de internacionalizacin a travs de su disposicin a realizar ampliaciones de capital y a reforzar las reservas de la entidad mediante la retencin de resultados. Capital y reservas son los dos elementos definitorios de la calidad de los recursos propios que dispone una entidad. Desde un punto de vista prudencial, en el medio plazo, los recursos propios de una entidad deben tener un nivel suficiente de calidad y, por lo tanto, los elementos de menor calidad que conforman sus recursos propios regulatorios (financiacin subordinada y participaciones preferentes) deben ser limitados. Una presencia elevada de instrumentos innovativos en los recursos propios bsicos se acaba traduciendo en un aumento del coste de la financiacin que repercute negativamente en la rentabilidad de las entidades. Por ello, aunque el Banco de Espaa pueda reconocer los instrumentos innovativos en los recursos propios regulatorios (por ejemplo, permitiendo computar como recursos propios bsicos las participaciones preferentes que incorporan una clusula de aumento de la remuneracin transcurridos 10 aos), siempre sera limitando su peso relativo (por ejemplo, en torno al 15%), y sin olvidar que existe ya un lmite del 30% sobre las participaciones preferentes tradicionales. La combinacin del significativo proceso de apertura del sistema bancario espaol y la pertenencia a la zona euro han permitido a la economa espaola financiar sin tensiones el creciente desfase o gap que existe entre el crecimiento del crdito al sector privado residente, en buena medida vinculado a la financiacin de la adquisicin de vivienda, y los depsitos bancarios provenientes de dicho sector. El acceso al mercado interbancario europeo ha permitido a los bancos espaoles complementar los fondos que obtienen de sus depositantes para poder prestar a las familias espaolas los importes que necesitan para adquirir su vivienda. No obstante, lo anterior plantea retos a la economa espaola y a las entidades. En primer lugar, el endeudamiento de las familias espaolas ya supera a la media comunitaria y est creciendo a un ritmo muy elevado. Conviene recordar a las familias espaolas que al contratar sus hipotecas sean conscientes del impacto que una elevacin futura de los tipos de inters puede tener sobre su renta mensual disponible y, por tanto, sobre su capacidad de devolucin de dicho prstamo hipotecario. En particular, la advertencia es ms relevante, si cabe, para aquellas con menor margen de maniobra (inestabilidad en el empleo, elevado nivel de endeudamiento, hipoteca a muy largo plazo, etc.). Las entidades tambin deben analizar esta situacin con detenimiento, aplicando una estricta poltica de admisin, concesin y seguimiento de sus riesgos con garanta hipotecaria, tanto con las familias como con los promotores inmobiliarios. Estos ltimos histricamente se han mostrado como un sector muy arriesgado, con una elevada morosidad en las fases recesivas. Adems, la dependencia del mercado bancario europeo para financiar el gap entre inversin y financiacin proveniente del sector privado residente va a acabar por presionar en los costes de la financiacin y, por tanto, en la rentabilidad de las entidades espaolas. Finalmente, como cuarto elemento de reflexin prudencial en torno a la internacionalizacin de la banca espaola, aparece la necesidad de aumentar la coordinacin entre supervisores bancarios. Dicha coordinacin se ve a la vez facilitada y demandada por la convergencia en el marco contable que van a traer las nuevas normas internacionales de contabilidad (las IAS, International Accounting Standards, o los IFRS, International Financial Reporting Standards) y por el desarrollo de un marco comn de requerimientos de recursos propios (Basilea II). Adems, esta cooperacin y creciente interaccin entre los supervisores se ha de producir, con elementos diferenciales, tanto a escala global como en el mbito de la UE. Como ya se ha mencionado, la implantacin de las IAS y Basilea II suponen un elemento facilitador de esa cooperacin. En el caso de las IAS, porque su implantacin (inicialmente en la UE y en el futuro a nivel mundial) supone el desarrollo de un lenguaje comn de informacin financiera que facilita enormemente la cooperacin y, en su caso, el desarrollo de una aproximacin supervisora comn. En el caso de Basilea II, porque representa un cambio hacia la supervisin basada en el anlisis del riesgo, esto es, un desarrollo de una nueva cultura de supervisin comn a nivel global. Adems, en el caso de Basilea II, este esfuerzo de coordinacin global no parte de cero. En efecto, dado que Basilea I se ha aplicado a ms de cien pases, la importancia que un sistema financiero internacional slido y bien capitalizado tiene para el correcto funcionamiento de la economa mundial, est plenamente reconocido. Aun as, Basilea II exige a los supervisores estrechar an ms su cooperacin y coordinacin para conseguir una implantacin efectiva del nuevo acuerdo de capital de Basilea II, que constituye un importante paso adelante en la medicin, gestin y supervisin de los riesgos bancarios. En el mbito de la Unin Europea, esa necesidad de coordinacin es an mayor, pues estamos hablando de un mercado financiero nico, con una regulacin comn mediante directivas pero con una ejecucin de esa regulacin realizada por autoridades supervisoras locales de cada uno de los estados miembros. Resulta, pues, esencial en el contexto europeo una coordinacin que garantice una aplicacin homognea de la regulacin comunitaria. Este elemento diferencial del contexto europeo se refleja en iniciativas como la creacin de los llamados comits de nivel 3 dentro del enfoque Lamfalussy (CESR para valores, CEBS para banca y CEIOPS para seguros), y que se encargan de la coordinacin entre supervisores y de avanzar en la convergencia de las prcticas supervisoras. Adems, la actual propuesta de Directiva sobre la implantacin de Basilea II contiene elementos especficos de reforzamiento, como el mayor papel del supervisor consolidado (el supervisor de origen de la matriz), la creacin de los colegios de supervisores (esto es, una agrupacin con los supervisores de un grupo consolidado especfico) o el reforzamiento de la transparencia del supervisor. En definitiva, esta mayor cooperacin internacional va a contribuir a que la internacionalizacin creciente de la banca en Espaa, en Europa y en el mundo se haga sin menoscabo de la solvencia y la estabilidad del sistema financiero.

Title: Introduction: IV Germn Berncer Prize Ceremony (Bank of Spain)
text: Madrid, 29 June 2005 Introduction of the Governor at the ceremony of the IV Germ87n Bern87cer Prize Bank of Spain Jaime Caruana Governor of the Bank of Spain First of all, I would like to congratulate the sponsors of the Germ87n Bern87cer Prize for their continued work in supporting economic research. Having completed its fourth edition, I would like to highlight four highlights of this award that make it especially appreciated in this institution: This is an award aimed at relevant contributions in the area of monetary and financial economics and, in particular, in monetary matters within EMU. There are many issues on the research agenda of the academic community in this field that are particularly close to the concerns of the Eurosystem central banks. It is logical, therefore, that the Banco de Espa96a pays special attention to all research topics that have a special importance for the functioning of the euro area, the conduct of monetary policy and the other tasks entrusted to us. Secondly, throughout its four editions, the Germ87n Bern87cer Prize has distinguished European economists who, despite their youth, have managed to establish an outstanding international reputation by making important contributions to Monetary and Financial Economics. The list of winners that includes professors Phillip Lane, Jose Manuel Campa, Luigi Zingales and, this year, Stephanie Schmitt-Grohe is an unequivocal sign of the commitment to academic excellence of the organizers, sponsors and members of the jury of this award. Ms. Stephanie Schmitt-Groh8e, this year's laureate, is a German-born young professor of economics who earned her Ph.D. in economics from the University of Chicago in 1994 and currently holds an academic position at Duke University in North Carolina. Prof. Schmitt-Groh8e's main contributions relate to the assessment of monetary and fiscal policies in economies with real and nominal rigidities. These contributions allow a better understanding of the implications of these policies on social welfare. In this regard, I would like to emphasize, as a central banker, that the results obtained by Prof. Schmitt-Groh8e allow to substantiate theoretically the objective of price stability in economies with a certain degree of nominal rigidity, although it is not for me to gloss the many important contributions of the research work of the laureate. My third comment relates precisely to the importance of recognizing the research work of a young economist in the early stages of her professional career. The promotion of research for the development of knowledge of socioeconomic reality is especially successful when the contribution to knowledge of young economists whose work does not always obtain the same public impact, at least outside the academic community, as that of economists with more years of experience is rewarded. Finally, and fourthly, I would like to recall, once again, that this award is named after a prominent Spanish economist who worked at the Bank of Spain, heading the research department from 1931. His works were a milestone in the economic analysis of the time and obtained a certain international recognition. Which adds a reason for satisfaction to all of us who work in this house. I would like to conclude my brief speech by congratulating Prof. Schmitt-Groh8e and pointing out that her work has not only won this award, but that, from the perspective of a central bank, it is an example of how to optimally combine rigorous economic analysis, the development of new theories and economic models together with new methodologies for their analysis, and the relevance of the results for the conduct of monetary and fiscal policies. Thanks a lot.
text_original: Madrid, 29 de junio de 2005 Introduccin del Gobernador en el acto de entrega del IV Premio Germn Berncer Banco de Espaa Jaime Caruana Gobernador del Banco de Espaa En primer lugar, quisiera felicitar a los patrocinadores del Premio Germn Berncer por su continuada labor de apoyo de la investigacin econmica. Habiendo cumplido su cuarta edicin, me gustara resaltar cuatro aspectos destacados de este premio que lo hacen especialmente apreciado en esta institucin: Se trata de un premio dirigido a las contribuciones relevantes en el rea de la economa monetaria y financiera y, en particular, en asuntos monetarios dentro de la UEM. Son muchas las cuestiones en la agenda investigadora de la comunidad acadmica en este campo que son especialmente cercanas a las preocupaciones de los bancos centrales del Eurosistema. Es lgico, por tanto, que el Banco de Espaa preste especial atencin a todos los temas de investigacin que tienen una trascendencia especial para el funcionamiento del rea del euro, la conduccin de la poltica monetaria y las restantes tareas que tenemos encomendadas. En segundo lugar, a lo largo de sus cuatro ediciones, el premio Germn Berncer ha distinguido a economistas europeos que, a pesar de su juventud, han logrado establecer una sobresaliente reputacin internacional realizando contribuciones importantes a la Economa Monetaria y Financiera. La lista de premiados que incluye a los profesores Phillip Lane, Jose Manuel Campa, Luigi Zingales y, este ao, Stephanie Schmitt-Grohe constituye una seal inequvoca de la apuesta por la excelencia acadmica de los organizadores, patrocinadores y miembros del jurado de este premio. Ms. Stephanie Schmitt-Groh, premiada este ao, es una joven profesora de economa nacida en Alemania, que obtuvo su doctorado en economa por la Universidad de Chicago en 1994 y que actualmente ocupa una posicin acadmica en la Universidad de Duke en Carolina del Norte. Las principales contribuciones de la Prof. Schmitt-Groh se refieren a la evaluacin de las polticas monetaria y fiscal en economas con rigideces reales y nominales. Estas contribuciones permiten una mejor comprensin de las implicaciones de estas polticas sobre el bienestar social. A este respecto, me gustara destacar, como banquero central, que los resultados obtenidos por la Prof. Schmitt-Groh permiten fundamentar tericamente el objetivo de la estabilidad de precios en economas con un cierto grado de rigidez nominal., aunque no me corresponde a m glosar las muchas e importantes contribuciones del trabajo de investigacin de la premiada. Mi tercer comentario se refiere precisamente a la importancia que tiene el reconocimiento de la labor investigadora de una joven economista en una primera etapa de su carrera profesional. La promocin de la investigacin para el desarrollo del conocimiento de la realidad socioeconmica es especialmente acertada cuando se premia la contribucin al conocimiento de jvenes economistas cuyos trabajos no siempre obtienen la misma repercusin pblica, al menos fuera de la comunidad acadmica, que la de economistas con ms aos de experiencia. Finalmente y, en cuarto lugar, me gustara recordar, un ao ms, que este premio lleva el nombre de un destacado economista espaol que trabaj en el Banco de Espaa, dirigiendo el departamento de estudios a partir de 1931. Sus trabajos supusieron un hito en el anlisis econmico de la poca y obtuvieron un cierto reconocimiento internacional. Lo que aade un motivo de satisfaccin a todos los que trabajamos en esta casa. Quisiera finalizar mi breve intervencin felicitando a la Prof. Schmitt-Groh y sealando que su trabajo, no solo se ha hecho merecedor de este premio, sino que, desde la perspectiva de un banco central, constituye un ejemplo de como combinar ptimamente el anlisis econmico riguroso, el desarrollo de nuevas teoras y modelos econmicos junto con nuevas metodologas para su anlisis, y la relevancia de los resultados para la conduccin de las polticas monetaria y fiscal. Muchas gracias.

Title: Governor's Appearance: Budget Committee of the Congress of Deputies
text: Madrid, 10 October 2005 Appearance before the Congressional Budget Committee Jaime Caruana Governor of the Bank of Spain Ladies and gentlemen, I appear, as usual, before this Congressional Budget Committee, within the framework of the deliberations that precede the approval of the General State Budget, in order to contribute to the point of view of the Bank of Spain on the economic situation and the challenges arising from it. I will begin by framing the external context, paying particular attention to developments in the euro area, an area in which monetary policy relevant to Spain is set. The most outstanding fact of the recent evolution of the international economy has been the sharp increase in the price of oil, which since the beginning of 2004 has more than doubled as a result of the strong growth of its demand (especially by the US and China) and the limited surplus capacity of production and refining. Thus, during the summer, the price of a barrel of crude oil has reached historical highs in nominal terms. In real terms, however, the current price level continues to be lower than the levels observed twenty-five years ago, in the early eighties. However, in 2005 the world economy continued to show high dynamism in a context of moderate inflation, with GDP reaching a growth rate of over 4 per cent (although below the 5.1 per cent observed in 2004). This rate of growth hides, however, quite marked differences between the different economic areas, depending, in large part, on the unequal degree of vulnerability to increases in the price of oil and other raw materials, the different degree of exposure to world trade and, of course, factors specific to each area. Thus, the expansion continues to be led by the United States and emerging Asia (including China and India). It is noteworthy that the euro area economy has shown a lack of dynamism, to which I will go into more detail later. It is important to note that the sharp increase in the price of crude oil is not having the intense effects on activity and inflation that were observed in previous episodes. This is due, among other reasons, to the fact that the increase in prices responds, in large part, to the increase in oil demand in a situation of general economic boom, rather than to cuts in production, such as those that characterized the increases of 1973-74, 1978-80 and 1989-90. Moreover, the changes of recent years have made the world economy more resilient to deal with the adverse consequences of higher oil prices. For their part, governments have avoided d0 in general terms d0 the application of compensatory policies for the increase in crude oil that they achieved such poor results in the past. And, fortunately, the absence of second-round effects on wages has helped contain underlying inflationary tensions, allowing monetary policies to continue to be encouraging growth. Despite the relatively satisfactory performance of the global economy in the early months of the year, downside risks to growth have been accentuated in 2005. First, the most recent analyses available suggest that the price of oil will remain at current high levels for an extended period of time and occasional spikes are even possible, given the limited spare production capacity. Second, global imbalances and, in particular, the US external deficit, have continued to widen, so that the risk that they could end up affecting the stability of foreign exchange markets and global growth has increased. The euro area, for its part, has not been able to benefit from the boom in the world economy in 2005. During the first half of the year, growth in the area remained at very moderate levels, similar to those recorded in the latter part of 2004, and growth prospects for the year as a whole have been progressively lowered as the months have passed. The latest predictions point to modest average GDP growth of around 1.3% in 2005, reflecting the notable weakness in domestic demand. Over the medium term, I believe that the existing favourable monetary and financial conditions, together with relatively strong growth in world trade, should allow a sustained recovery in economic activity to begin to reach rates around 2% in line with potential growth. This recovery would be based, in the first instance, on exports and investment. However, this scenario is subject to downside risks related to energy price developments and existing global imbalances. With regard to prices, the evolution of the Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices in the euro area has been marked by the upward trajectory of the energy component. Thus, the year-on-year inflation rate has been above 2% and the latest data show a trend towards rebounding, which has reached 2.5% in September's advance. It does not therefore seem possible that area inflation could soon return to rates below 2%, given the combined effect of higher oil prices and, to a lesser extent, exchange rate depreciation. It is not easy to diagnose the extent of this uptick. So far, no conclusive evidence of inflationary tensions has been found in the medium term. The year-on-year rate of change of the index, which excludes unprocessed foods and energy, has remained at moderate levels of around 1.5%, which would indicate that the increase in energy prices would not be transferred to other components of the aggregate index. For their part, inflationary expectations remain contained and wage growth is moderate in a context of weakness in aggregate demand and the labour market. However, high energy price levels and their potential second-round effects on wages represent significant upside risks to inflation in the euro area, which we at the European Central Bank scrupulously monitor. In this situation, in line with the prospects for gradually overcoming the current phase of sluggish economic activity, the Governing Council of the ECB considered that, despite the pressure that oil prices are exerting on prices, the monetary policy stance is still in line with the objective of price stability over the medium term. For all these reasons, it has been decided to keep official interest rates unchanged at 2%, but reinforcing its vigilant attitude towards the possible materialization of the risks that are becoming visible in the latest inflation figures. The low economic dynamism, despite the favourable conditions for growth resulting from low interest rates, the sound equity situation of companies, the moderate trend in labour costs and strong external demand, underlines d0 beyond short-term factors d0 the need to undertake decisive structural reforms to increase the potential growth capacity of the European economy. In July, the Commission presented the Community Lisbon Programme, which contained a set of eight key measures in three main areas: fostering knowledge and innovation for growth, making Europe a more attractive place to invest and work, and creating more and higher quality jobs. The Community programme must now be complemented by national reform plans to be submitted by the Member States in the autumn. It is difficult to overstate the importance of achieving concrete progress in these areas at both national and European level. Finally, in this rapid review of the situation in the euro area, I cannot fail to refer to the budgetary developments in its Member States, characterised, as in previous years, by insufficient fiscal consolidation efforts and the persistence of high structural deficits. Thus, the evolution of public finances in EMU indicates that the deficit and debt targets of the stability programmes in most countries will not be met in 2005 either. In fact, according to the European Commission's spring estimate, a total of four countries will be in excessive deficit in 2005. As we have repeatedly pointed out from the European Central Bank, it is crucial that the new framework of the Stability and Growth Pact is applied as strictly as possible and that countries show greater commitment to its compliance than in the past. From the point of view of the Spanish economy, the main features of the international economic outlook that I have just described are an environment of moderate strength in external markets and, above all, of slack in monetary and financial conditions, given its advanced cyclical position and the higher inflation rates it has been registering. Allow me to draw up a brief overview of the economic situation and its prospects for the coming quarters, which will serve to frame the analysis and assessment of the 2006 Budget. In the first half of 2005, Spanish GDP growth rose slightly, following the trend already observed throughout 2004, reaching a year-on-year increase of 3.4% in the second quarter. The information available on the evolution of the economy over the summer, still quite incomplete, indicates that growth has remained high, although it seems to have stabilized. I would like to recall that these estimates correspond to the new National Accounts, base 2000, which the INE published a few months ago and which have led to a significant upward revision d0 of around half a percentage point per year d0 of Spanish growth in the last five years. This revision mainly reflects the incorporation into these estimates of updated population and employment figures, which reflect the strong impact of immigration. Output expansion continues to be accompanied by a high capacity for employment generation. The quarterly accounting data have placed the year-on-year increase in the number of jobs at 3.1% in the second quarter, following a trend of moderate acceleration similar to that of activity. It is also true that, as I have already pointed out in other hearings, these estimates indicate that labour productivity gains continue to be very small. In the first half of 2005, domestic demand has reinforced its high dynamism, registering increases of close to 5.5%. Investment in equipment has risen sharply, which, following the strong recovery shown throughout 2004, has stabilised at rates of change close to 10% during the first half of the year. The prospects for demand growth, favourable financing conditions and the good performance of corporate profits have contributed to this investment boom, which has been joined by other components of investment, such as non-residential construction, which has increased its dynamism in the first half of 2005 due to the construction of infrastructure. It should be noted, however, that according to the most up-to-date indicators, spending on capital goods would have moderated its expansionary impulse in the summer months. Household consumption continues to grow at a significantly higher rate than their disposable income, reflecting the importance of the revaluation of household wealth d0 both financial and, especially, real estate d0 as a driver of spending. In particular, consumption grew at rates close to 5% in the first half of 2005, although it maintained a path of slight slowdown compared with the end of 2004, which would have continued throughout the summer. In turn, residential investment continues to grow at rates of 6%, very similar to those registered last year. The favourable mortgage financing conditions are combined with the effects, already mentioned, of the revaluation of household assets to explain the prolongation of the intense boom in housing investment. The boost in domestic demand is being compensated, however, by the large detraction exerted by foreign demand on the growth rate of output. Part of this drain comes from the relatively more advanced cyclical position maintained by the Spanish economy, compared to its main trading partners, and from the import intensity of investment in equipment, but it is also a consequence of the losses in competitiveness that have been accumulating in recent years. The external contribution reached strongly negative levels in the first quarter of 2005, clearly exceeding two points of GDP, as an abnormally weak performance of exports was combined with the effect of the recovery of investment in equipment on imports. Since the second quarter, as exports of goods and tourism receipts have been recovering, the contractionary effect of the external contribution has been somewhat mitigated, although it continues to be very bulky. In this regard, it should be noted that the contribution of inflation differentials to the deterioration of competitiveness has not slowed. The inflation rate measured by consumer prices increased in September to 3.7% (four tenths more than in August), as a result of the rise in food and, above all, energy prices, as well as the inertia of inflation in services. To all this may have been added an increase of one tenth attributable to the increase in indirect taxes on tobacco and alcohol. The inflation differential with the euro area as a whole remains above one percentage point and has even tended to widen with the resurgence linked to oil prices to reach 1.2 points, according to the advance data for September. The wage increases agreed in collective agreements continue to be at rates similar to those registered the previous year, of 2.9%, giving rise to a generally moderate growth in remuneration, which has helped to contain increases in labour costs. However, it should be borne in mind that in the most exposed sectors prices are subject to strong competitive pressures and that cost growth, as in the case of prices, is still above that observed in other competing countries. In recent quarters, therefore, the Spanish economy has continued to advance in an expansionary stage that generates employment, in which, among the most recent positive results, the recovery of productive investment stands out, although the most recent data introduce some doubts about the intensity of its continuation. In any case, there are still not sufficiently strong signs of a significant change in the composition of growth, which is based excessively on consumption and construction, while external demand exerts a large contractionary effect, so risks arising from accumulated competitiveness losses and rapid growth in household debt remain present, linked to the continued real estate boom. The sharp widening of the external imbalance observed since last year should be interpreted as an indication that the risks associated with losses in competitiveness have begun to materialize. Imports, encouraged by the growth in domestic demand, continue to increase their degree of penetration into the domestic market. At the same time, it is very likely that exports, despite the timid improvement recorded in the second quarter, will lose share again in 2005, as happened last year. In these circumstances, the most exposed industrial activities are struggling to cope with increasing external competition, and both the trade deficit and financing needs have increased sharply. On the other hand, the high growth in household spending, especially in residential investment, continues to be supported by rising credit indebtedness, and house prices continue to rise at high rates, despite being at higher average levels than can be explained by the evolution of its fundamental determinants. According to the financial accounts, households have continued to reduce their savings rate and have begun to be net fund-seekers. However, short-term forecasts remain buoyant. The trends observed in the Spanish economy today are, in principle, compatible with the estimate incorporated in the macroeconomic scenario that has served as the basis for the 2006 Draft Budget of GDP growth focused on 3.3% in the whole of 2005, although it may be that the main components of demand continue to show the push, Despite its recent slowdown, it translates into a few more tenths of growth. The scenario envisaged for next year is surrounded by greater uncertainties, which stem in part from the external environment that I described at the beginning of my speech d0 particularly from oil price increases whose impact is usually manifested with prolonged lags d0 but also from the internal risks that I have identified. The expansion of the Spanish economy is expected to continue to be influenced by the extraordinarily low levels of interest rates and the increase in the active population, so it is expected that in the short term the current dynamic scenario will continue, along the lines foreseen in the macroeconomic table accompanying the Budget. However, if the imbalances that have been dragging continue to increase, they may, as I have said on previous occasions, be an obstacle to the sustainability of growth in the medium term. This is the main challenge facing economic policy. The consolidation of the current economic dynamism in the medium term requires a rebalancing of the pattern of domestic spending that combines a certain slowdown in household spending on consumption and residential investment d0 which would facilitate the moderation of credit growth and the orderly absorption of housing overvaluation d0 with a strengthening of productive investment. On the supply side, employment growth needs to be accompanied by a stronger pace of productivity growth and a moderation in price and cost hikes that allow competitiveness to recover. Only in this way will it be possible to halt the deterioration of the external balance and reduce the strong contractionary effect that net foreign demand has been exerting. Under these conditions, demand policies, and in particular fiscal policy, should help to steer domestic spending towards more moderate growth rates in line with the economy's potential growth. We cannot forget that within monetary union, budgetary policy is the main instrument available to influence aggregate demand, and therefore the internal absorption of the economy and the external deficit. However, as I have pointed out on other occasions, demand policies are not sufficient if they are not supported by structural reform policies that improve the functioning of markets for goods and services, encourage improvements in competitiveness and sustain labour supply growth and job creation. The fiscal forecasts for 2005 point to a surplus in the balance of the Public Administrations of 0.1% of GDP, in line with the objectives budgeted at the beginning of the year. A closure of the public accounts in this environment makes it possible to comfortably meet the fiscal requirements established by the European commitments in the scope of the Stability and Growth Pact, as well as to deepen the downward trajectory of public debt, whose ratio as a proportion to GDP could be below 45% by the end of 2005. These good results should not hide, however, that the fiscal effort has experienced a certain slowdown this year and that budgetary policy has acquired an expansionary tone that would not have contributed to the extent that it could have moderated the pressures of domestic demand and contained the risks present in the Spanish economy. Given the strong dynamism shown by tax collection, with records that exceed the estimates that were handled when the Budgets were prepared, it should be possible to end this year with a surplus also higher than budgeted, which would be more in line with the requirements of the economy. The 2006 Budget presents a surplus target for general government as a whole of 0.2% of GDP. Taking into account that the cyclical position will be similar to that of this year, the tone of fiscal policy, estimated from the usual indicators, could be moderately expansionary. The budgeting of a growth in public expenditure of the State significantly above the expected increase in nominal GDP points in the same direction. It does not seem, therefore, that the fiscal policy scheduled for 2006 will sufficiently correct the expansionary stance. It is very important that if the dynamism of revenue exceeds the forecasts of the Budget, as has happened in 2005, this translates into a higher surplus and not into additional increases in expenditure. The priorities of the expenditure policies incorporated in the Budgets seem to be adequately oriented towards areas that are particularly important for improving productivity, such as promoting innovation, increasing investment in infrastructure, increasing resources for education and boosting quality public services, but entail significant increases in the corresponding budgetary allocations, to which are added the spending commitments that have been assumed in the field of housing, minimum pensions or health financing. On this last point, it is worrying that the agreement reached is fundamentally based on greater recourse to State financing, compared to the use of complementary financing channels offered by the current regional financing system and that it does not address the introduction of measures to improve efficiency in health spending. In the phase that the Spanish economy is going through, it is very important that budgetary policy plays an effective role in containing the risks behind the strong dynamism of spending, so it would be highly desirable, as I have already said, to move towards a greater surplus in the public accounts. The fiscal contribution must come not only from the improvement of the budget balance but also from the increase in efficiency in the performance of the public sector, through the revision of spending policies and tax figures that can help improve incentives. The tax reforms announced must take these objectives into account and must be well calibrated so as not to entail excessive collection costs. In this sense, we must not forget that the current dynamism of public revenues may incorporate some transitory component that could disappear in less favorable circumstances. These considerations are reinforced when Spanish demographic prospects are taken into account. These point to an intense process of population ageing, despite the intense immigration flows that have been recorded in recent years. Budgetary policy needs to anticipate well in advance the pressures on public spending that an ageing society will generate, both in terms of pensions and dependency coverage, by adopting more ambitious fiscal targets and addressing the necessary reforms in social protection systems. The institutional framework within which fiscal policy operates is of great importance in ensuring disciplined developments in public finances. Discussions are currently under way to reform the Budget Stability Laws, which provide the basis for limiting undisciplined conduct and distributing the established fiscal policy objective by agents. The most innovative aspect of the reform project is the introduction of greater flexibility in the definition of budgetary stability rules, allowing the State and the Autonomous Communities to adapt their deficit or surplus target to the cyclical situation of the economy. This amendment to the Law is aimed at allowing the operation of existing automatic stabilisers, although it does not introduce sufficient incentives for the generation of adequate surpluses in favourable cyclical situations. In addition, the Reform Bill strengthens fiscal discipline by introducing specific requirements for different public sector actors. These requirements are clearly defined in the case of the Central Administration, whose balance, for the purposes of fulfilling the objective of budgetary stability, will be computed independently of that of Social Security, but in the case of the Autonomous Communities there is no transparent distribution of the fiscal effort that corresponds to each of them, which may entail some risk of deviations. Finally, I would like to place particular emphasis on the provisions incorporated in the regulation to improve transparency and the availability of information on public accounts, an objective that has been unsuccessful on previous occasions, but which I consider to be of vital importance as an element of discipline in tax structures in which spending is strongly decentralised, as is the case in Spain. In terms of structural reforms, the Government has taken a series of initiatives over the past year aimed at boosting productivity and innovation with the aim of laying the foundations for solid growth in the long term. I am referring to the Plan for the Revitalization of the Economy, the Ingenio 2010 Program and, soon, the National Economic Reform Plan. These initiatives establish an appropriate orientation for economic policy to address the challenges facing the Spanish economy, in particular, the need to boost productivity and establish the foundations for solid growth in the long term that allows sustained improvements in the economic well-being of Spanish society. It is necessary, however, to make the commitments made more concrete and deeper, and at the same time to undertake other more far-reaching reforms, which are of vital importance in the case of the labour market. These reforms are essential to maintain dynamism in employment and promote innovation in the business fabric, particularly in companies in the service branches and in those of reduced size, which represent a very important part of the business landscape of this country and which are the ones that accumulate the greatest innovation and technological gap. To this end, the labour market must provide sufficient flexibility to enable firms to organise the use of factors of production efficiently and the processes of liberalisation of markets for goods and services undertaken in recent years must continue. It is also of great importance that the decentralization of competences that characterizes the autonomous structure of the State does not generate regulatory discrepancies that could lead to an erosion of the unity of the national market, as has already happened in some areas such as retail trade. Such a development would be contradictory to the processes of European integration and globalisation and would damage the competitive position of the Spanish economy. In relation to this issue, no one escapes the enormous importance of the debate on possible reforms of the institutional framework of the Autonomous Communities and, in particular, of the proposal of the Statute of Autonomy of Catalonia. This proposal entails political, cultural and social modifications, on whose constitutionality and convenience the competent parliamentary and jurisdictional bodies will pronounce. From the point of view of economic policy, in addition, the current wording entails alterations in the distribution of competences between the State and the Autonomous Communities and in the financing systems of the latter that may affect, not only internal cohesion, but also the capacity of public policies to maintain market integration and efficiency in the functioning of the economy. These are far-reaching decisions that may have an impact on the medium and long-term position of the Spanish economy in a world scenario characterized by fierce competition and increasing openness and integration. Institutional changes of this nature can have important and lasting economic consequences, weaken the efficiency and capacity to grow of the economy and affect the well-being of all Spaniards. Therefore, special care must be taken that institutional design allows effective management of economic policies, promotes an environment that favors private initiative and competition, avoids excessive interventionism, as well as uncertainties and regulatory risks and is finally consistent with full economic integration. The Bank of Spain views with particular concern the proposals to modify the system of regulation and supervision of credit institutions that involve a fragmentation of competences, which could be interpreted as contrary to the copious jurisprudence of the Constitutional Court, particularly with regard to the stability and solvency of the financial system. This disintegration could fragment the Spanish financial system, generate conflicts of interest in the governance and supervision of savings banks, (as the regional public authorities that are already present in the governing bodies of these institutions gain supervisory powers), could compromise the effectiveness of financial supervision and would hinder progress in the direction of convergence and coordination in this area, demanded by the European authorities and international financial stability forums. In short, in the panorama that I have tried to outline, economic policy has a special responsibility, in multiple areas, to promote the establishment of adequate bases so that the dynamism that the Spanish economy is experiencing can be projected in a sustainable way into the future.
text_original: Madrid, 10 de octubre de 2005 Comparecencia ante la Comisin de Presupuestos del Congreso Jaime Caruana Gobernador del Banco de Espaa Seoras: Comparezco, como viene siendo habitual, ante esta Comisin de Presupuestos del Congreso, en el marco de las deliberaciones que preceden a la aprobacin de los Presupuestos Generales del Estado, con la finalidad de contribuir con el punto de vista del Banco de Espaa sobre la situacin econmica y los retos que se derivan de la misma. Comenzar enmarcando el contexto exterior, prestando particular atencin a la evolucin de la zona del euro, mbito en el que se establece la poltica monetaria relevante para Espaa. El hecho ms destacado de la evolucin reciente de la economa internacional ha sido el fuerte aumento del precio del petrleo, que desde principio del ao 2004 se ha ms que duplicado como consecuencia del fuerte crecimiento de su demanda (especialmente, por parte de EEUU y China) y de la limitada capacidad excedente de produccin y refino. As, durante el verano, el precio del barril de crudo ha alcanzado mximos histricos en trminos nominales. En trminos reales, sin embargo, el nivel de precios actual contina siendo inferior a los niveles observados hace veinticinco aos, a principios de la dcada de los aos ochenta. Con todo, en 2005 la economa mundial ha continuado mostrando un elevado dinamismo en un contexto de inflacin moderada, pudiendo alcanzar el PIB una tasa de crecimiento superior al 4% (aunque por debajo del 5,1% observado en 2004). Este ritmo de avance esconde, no obstante, diferencias bastante acusadas entre las distintas reas econmicas dependiendo, en gran parte, del desigual grado de vulnerabilidad frente a los aumentos del precio de petrleo y de otras materias primas, del diverso grado de exposicin al comercio mundial y, por supuesto, de factores especficos de cada zona. As, la expansin sigue estando liderada por Estados Unidos y las economas emergentes de Asia (incluyendo China e India). Es de destacar la falta de dinamismo que ha mostrado la economa del rea del euro, a la que luego me referir ms detenidamente. Es importante destacar que el fuerte incremento del precio del crudo no est teniendo los intensos efectos sobre la actividad y la inflacin que se observaron en episodios anteriores. Ello se debe, entre otras razones, a que el encarecimiento responde, en gran parte, al incremento de la demanda de petrleo en una situacin de bonanza econmica general, ms que a recortes en la produccin, como los que caracterizaron las alzas de 1973-74, 1978-80 y 1989-90. Adems, los cambios de los ltimos aos han dotado a la economa mundial de una mayor resistencia para afrontar las consecuencias adversas de la subida del precio del petrleo. Por su parte, los gobiernos han evitado en trminos generales la aplicacin de polticas compensatorias del incremento del crudo que tan malos resultados cosecharon en el pasado. Y, afortunadamente, la ausencia de efectos de segunda ronda sobre los salarios ha permitido contener las tensiones inflacionistas subyacentes, propiciando que las polticas monetarias hayan continuado siendo alentadoras del crecimiento. A pesar de los resultados relativamente satisfactorios de la economa mundial en los primeros meses del ao, los riesgos a la baja sobre el crecimiento se han ido acentuando en 2005. En primer lugar, los anlisis ms recientes disponibles apuntan a que el precio del petrleo permanecer en los niveles elevados actuales por un perodo prolongado y es incluso posible que se produzcan repuntes ocasionales, dada la limitada capacidad excedente de produccin. En segundo lugar, los desequilibrios globales y, en particular, el dficit exterior americano, han seguido amplindose, de tal forma que el riesgo de que puedan terminar afectando a la estabilidad de los mercados cambiarios y al crecimiento global se ha incrementado. La zona del euro, por su parte, no ha sido capaz de beneficiarse en 2005 de la bonanza de la economa mundial. Durante la primera mitad del ao, el crecimiento del rea se ha mantenido en cotas muy moderadas, similares a las registradas en la ltima parte de 2004, y las perspectivas de crecimiento para el conjunto del ao se han visto rebajadas progresivamente segn han ido transcurriendo los meses. Las predicciones ms recientes apuntan hacia un modesto crecimiento medio del PIB en torno al 1,3 % en 2005, reflejo de la notable debilidad que muestra la demanda interna. Ms a medio plazo, creo que las favorables condiciones monetarias y financieras existentes, junto con un crecimiento relativamente intenso del comercio mundial, deberan permitir el inicio de una recuperacin sostenida de la actividad econmica hasta alcanzar tasas alrededor del 2% en lnea con el crecimiento potencial. Esta recuperacin estara basada, en primera instancia, en las exportaciones y en la inversin. No obstante, este escenario est sujeto a riesgos a la baja relacionados con la evolucin de los precios energticos y con los desequilibrios globales existentes. Por lo que respecta a los precios, la evolucin del ndice Armonizado de Precios de Consumo en la zona euro ha venido marcada por la trayectoria ascendente del componente energtico. As, la tasa interanual de inflacin se ha situado por encima del 2% y los ltimos datos muestran una tendencia al repunte, que ha llegado al 2,5% en el de avance del mes de septiembre. No parece, por tanto, posible que la inflacin del rea pueda volver pronto a tasas inferiores al 2%, dado el efecto combinado del aumento de los precios del petrleo y, en menor medida, de la depreciacin del tipo de cambio. No es fcil diagnosticar el alcance de este repunte. Hasta ahora no se ha encontrado evidencia concluyente de tensiones inflacionistas a medio plazo. La tasa interanual de variacin del ndice, que excluye los alimentos no elaborados y la energa, se ha mantenido en niveles moderados en torno al 1,5%, lo cual indicara que el encarecimiento de los precios energticos no se estara trasladando a otros componentes del ndice agregado. Por su parte, las expectativas inflacionistas permanecen contenidas y los crecimientos salariales son moderados en un contexto de debilidad de la demanda agregada y del mercado de trabajo. Sin embargo, los elevados niveles de los precios energticos y sus posibles efectos de segunda ronda sobre los salarios representan importantes riesgos alcistas para la inflacin en la zona del euro, que en el Banco Central Europeo vigilamos escrupulosamente. En esta situacin, acorde con las perspectivas de superacin gradual de la fase actual de atona de la actividad econmica, el Consejo de Gobierno del BCE ha considerado que, a pesar de la presin que los precios del petrleo estn ejerciendo sobre los precios, todava la orientacin de la poltica monetaria est en lnea con el objetivo de estabilidad de precios a medio plazo. Por todo ello, se ha decidido mantener inalterados los tipos de inters oficiales en el 2%, pero reforzando su actitud vigilante ante la eventual materializacin de los riesgos que se estn haciendo visibles en las ltimas cifras de inflacin. El escaso dinamismo econmico, a pesar de las favorables condiciones para el crecimiento que se derivan de los reducidos tipos de inters, de la saneada situacin patrimonial de las empresas, de la evolucin moderada de los costes laborales y de la vigorosa demanda exterior, subraya ms all de factores coyunturales la necesidad de acometer de forma decidida reformas estructurales que aumenten la capacidad de crecimiento potencial de la economa europea. En julio, la Comisin present el programa comunitario sobre la estrategia de Lisboa, que contena un conjunto de ocho medidas claves en tres reas principales: fomentar el conocimiento y la innovacin para el crecimiento, hacer de Europa un lugar ms atractivo para invertir y trabajar, y crear ms empleo y de ms calidad. El programa comunitario ha de ser complementado ahora por planes nacionales de reforma que los Estados Miembros han de presentar en otoo. Resulta difcil exagerar la importancia de lograr avances concretos en estas reas tanto a nivel nacional como europeo. Finalmente, en este rpido repaso de la situacin en la zona del euro no puedo dejar de referirme a la evolucin presupuestaria de sus Estados Miembros, caracterizada, como en aos anteriores, por un insuficiente esfuerzo de consolidacin fiscal y la persistencia de elevados dficit estructurales. As, la evolucin de las finanzas pblicas en la UEM indica que no se cumplirn tampoco en 2005 los objetivos de dficit y deuda de los programas de estabilidad en la mayor parte de los pases. De hecho, de acuerdo con la estimacin de primavera de la Comisin Europea, un total de cuatro pases estarn en situacin de dficit excesivo en 2005. Tal como hemos venido sealando reiteradamente desde el Banco Central Europeo, resulta crucial que el nuevo marco del Pacto de Estabilidad y Crecimiento sea aplicado del modo ms estricto posible y que los pases muestren un mayor compromiso con su cumplimiento que en el pasado. Desde el punto de vista de la economa espaola, los principales rasgos del panorama econmico internacional que acabo de describir conforman un entorno de moderada fortaleza de los mercados externos y, sobre todo, de holgura de las condiciones monetarias y financieras, dadas su avanzada posicin cclica y las mayores tasas de inflacin que viene registrando. Permtanme que trace, a continuacin, un breve repaso de la situacin coyuntural de la economa y de sus perspectivas para los prximos trimestres, que sirva para enmarcar el anlisis y la valoracin de los Presupuestos del ao 2006. En la primera mitad de 2005, el crecimiento del PIB espaol se elev suavemente, siguiendo la tendencia ya observada a lo largo de 2004, hasta alcanzar un incremento interanual del 3,4% en el segundo trimestre. La informacin disponible sobre la evolucin de la economa a lo largo del verano, todava bastante incompleta, indica que el crecimiento ha continuado siendo alto, si bien parece haberse estabilizado. Quisiera recordar que estas estimaciones corresponden a la nueva Contabilidad Nacional, base 2000, que el INE public hace pocos meses y que han supuesto una significativa revisin al alza de en torno a medio punto porcentual por ao del crecimiento espaol en el ltimo quinquenio. Esta revisin refleja, principalmente, la incorporacin en estas estimaciones de cifras actualizadas de poblacin y empleo, que reflejan el fuerte impacto de la inmigracin. La expansin del producto sigue estando acompaada por una elevada capacidad de generacin de empleo. Los datos de la Contabilidad trimestral han situado el incremento interanual del nmero de puestos de trabajo en el 3,1%, en el segundo trimestre, siguiendo una tendencia de moderada aceleracin similar a la de la actividad. Es cierto tambin que, como ya he sealado en otras comparecencias, estas estimaciones indican que las ganancias de productividad del trabajo continan siendo muy reducidas. En la primera mitad de 2005, la demanda interna ha reforzado su elevado dinamismo, registrando incrementos cercanos al 5,5%. Es de destacar el avance de la inversin en equipo, que, tras la intensa reactivacin mostrada a lo largo de 2004, se ha estabilizado en tasas de variacin prximas al 10% durante el primer semestre. Las perspectivas de crecimiento de la demanda, las favorables condiciones de financiacin y el buen comportamiento de los beneficios empresariales han contribuido a este auge inversor, al que se han unido otros componentes de la inversin, como la construccin no residencial, que ha incrementado su dinamismo en la primera mitad de 2005 debido a la realizacin de infraestructuras. Hay que sealar, sin embargo, que segn los indicadores ms actualizados el gasto en bienes de equipo habra moderado su impulso expansivo en los meses del verano. El consumo de los hogares contina avanzando a un ritmo significativamente superior al de su renta disponible, reflejando la importancia que est teniendo la revalorizacin de la riqueza de los hogares -tanto la financiera como, especialmente, la inmobiliaria- como elemento impulsor del gasto. En concreto, el consumo ha crecido a tasas cercanas al 5% en la primera mitad de 2005, aunque mantiene una senda de ligera desaceleracin en relacin con el final de 2004, que habra continuado a lo largo del verano. A su vez, la inversin residencial contina creciendo a tasas del 6%, muy similares a las registradas el pasado ao. Las favorables condiciones de financiacin hipotecaria se unen a los efectos, ya mencionados, de la revalorizacin del patrimonio de los hogares para explicar la prolongacin del intenso auge de la inversin en vivienda. El empuje de la demanda interna se est viendo compensado, sin embargo, por la abultada detraccin que ejerce la demanda exterior sobre la tasa de crecimiento del producto. Parte de este drenaje procede de la posicin cclica relativamente ms avanzada que mantiene la economa espaola, en comparacin con sus principales socios comerciales, y de la intensidad importadora de la inversin en equipo, pero tambin es consecuencia de las prdidas de competitividad que se han ido acumulando en los ltimos aos. La contribucin exterior alcanz cotas fuertemente negativas en el primer trimestre de 2005, superando claramente los dos puntos del PIB, al unirse en ese perodo un comportamiento anormalmente dbil de las exportaciones con el efecto de la recuperacin de la inversin en equipo sobre las importaciones. A partir del segundo trimestre, a medida que las exportaciones de bienes y los ingresos por turismo se han ido recuperando, el efecto contractivo de la aportacin exterior se ha mitigado algo, aunque contina siendo muy abultada. A este respecto, cabe sealar, que la contribucin de los diferenciales de inflacin al deterioro de la competitividad no se ha aminorado. La tasa de inflacin medida por los precios de consumo se ha incrementado en septiembre hasta el 3,7% (cuatro dcimas ms que en agosto), como consecuencia del encarecimiento de los alimentos y, sobre todo, de la energa, as como de la inercia de la inflacin en los servicios. A todo ello se puede haber unido un aumento de una dcima atribuible a la subida de los impuestos indirectos que gravan el tabaco y el alcohol. El diferencial de inflacin con el conjunto de la zona del euro se mantiene por encima de un punto porcentual e incluso ha tendido a ampliarse con el rebrote vinculado a los precios del petrleo hasta alcanzar los 1,2 puntos, segn los datos de avance del mes de septiembre. Los incrementos salariales pactados en convenios colectivos continan situados en tasas similares a las registradas el ao anterior, del 2,9%, dando lugar a un crecimiento, en general, moderado de las remuneraciones, que ha ayudado a contener los aumentos de costes laborales. No obstante, debe tenerse en cuenta que en los sectores ms expuestos los precios estn sujetos a fuertes presiones competitivas y que el crecimiento de costes, al igual que en el caso de los precios, sigue estando por encima del observado en otros pases competidores. En los ltimos trimestres, por tanto, la economa espaola ha seguido avanzando en una etapa expansiva generadora de empleo, en la que destaca, entre los resultados positivos ms recientes, la recuperacin de la inversin productiva, aunque los datos ms recientes introducen algunas dudas sobre la intensidad de su continuacin. En cualquier caso, todava no hay signos suficientemente slidos de un cambio significativo en la composicin del crecimiento, que se basa en exceso en el consumo y la construccin, mientras que la demanda externa ejerce un abultado efecto contractivo, por lo que siguen estando presentes los riesgos que se derivan de las prdidas de competitividad acumuladas y del rpido crecimiento de la deuda de los hogares, vinculado al continuado auge inmobiliario. La fuerte ampliacin del desequilibrio exterior que viene observndose desde el pasado ao debe interpretarse como una indicacin de que los riesgos asociados a las prdidas de competitividad han comenzado a materializarse. Las importaciones, alentadas por el crecimiento de la demanda interna, siguen aumentando su grado de penetracin en el mercado interior. Paralelamente, es muy probable que las exportaciones, a pesar de la tmida mejora registrada en el segundo trimestre, vuelvan a perder cuota en 2005, como ya sucedi el ao pasado. En estas circunstancias, las actividades industriales ms expuestas estn teniendo dificultades para afrentar la creciente competencia externa, y tanto el dficit comercial como las necesidades de financiacin han experimentado un aumento pronunciado. Por otra parte, el elevado crecimiento del gasto de los hogares, especialmente en inversin residencial, sigue estando sustentado en un creciente endeudamiento crediticio, y el precio de la vivienda sigue aumentando a tasas elevadas, a pesar de encontrarse en niveles medios superiores de los que cabe explicar por la evolucin de sus determinantes fundamentales. Segn las cuentas financieras, las familias han continuado reduciendo su tasa de ahorro y han comenzado a ser demandantes netos de fondos. No obstante, las previsiones de corto plazo siguen siendo de un dinamismo continuado. Las tendencias que se observan en la economa espaola en la actualidad son, en principio, compatibles con la estimacin incorporada en el escenario macroeconmico que ha servido de base al Proyecto de Presupuestos de 2006 de un crecimiento del PIB centrado en el 3,3% en el conjunto de 2005, aunque puede que el empuje que siguen evidenciando los principales componentes de la demanda, a pesar de su reciente desaceleracin, se traduzca en alguna dcima ms de crecimiento. El escenario previsto para el prximo ao est rodeado de mayores incertidumbres, que provienen en parte del entorno exterior que he descrito al comienzo de mi intervencin particularmente de los aumentos del precio del petrleo cuyo impacto se suele manifestar con desfases prolongados-, pero tambin de los riesgos internos que he sealado. La expansin de la economa espaola, previsiblemente, seguir contando con la influencia expansiva de los niveles extraordinariamente bajos de los tipos de inters y del aumento de la poblacin activa, por lo que cabe esperar que a corto plazo se prolongue el escenario de dinamismo actual, en la lnea prevista en el cuadro macroeconmico que acompaa a los Presupuestos. Sin embargo, si los desequilibrios que se vienen arrastrando siguen aumentando pueden llegar a suponer, como ya he dicho en ocasiones anteriores, un obstculo para la sostenibilidad del crecimiento a medio plazo. Este es el principal reto que tiene planteado la poltica econmica. La consolidacin del actual dinamismo econmico en el medio plazo requiere un reequilibrio del patrn de gasto interno que combine una cierta desaceleracin del gasto de las familias en consumo e inversin residencial -lo que facilitara la moderacin del crecimiento del crdito y la absorcin ordenada de la sobrevaloracin de la vivienda- con un fortalecimiento de la inversin productiva. A su vez, por el lado de la oferta, es necesario que el crecimiento del empleo venga acompaado por un ritmo ms vivo de crecimiento de la productividad y de una moderacin de las alzas de precios y costes que permitan una recuperacin de la competitividad. Slo de esta manera ser posible detener el deterioro del saldo exterior y reducir el fuerte efecto contractivo que la demanda exterior neta viene ejerciendo. En estas condiciones, las polticas de demanda y, en particular, la poltica fiscal, deben contribuir a encauzar el gasto interno hacia ritmos de crecimiento ms moderados y acordes con el crecimiento potencial de la economa. No podemos olvidar que dentro de la unin monetaria, la poltica presupuestaria constituye el principal instrumento disponible para influir sobre la demanda agregada, y por lo tanto sobre la absorcin interna de la economa y el dficit exterior. No obstante, como ya he sealado en otras ocasiones, las polticas de demanda no son suficientes si no estn apoyadas por polticas de reforma estructural que mejoren el funcionamiento de los mercados de bienes y servicios, fomenten las mejoras de competitividad y permitan mantener el crecimiento de la oferta de trabajo y la generacin de empleo. Las previsiones fiscales para el 2005 apuntan a un supervit del saldo de las AAPP del 0,1% del PIB, en lnea con los objetivos presupuestados al inicio del ejercicio. Un cierre de las cuentas pblicas en este entorno permite cumplir con holgura los requerimientos fiscales que establecen los compromisos europeos en el mbito del Pacto de Estabilidad y de Crecimiento, as como profundizar la trayectoria descendente de la deuda pblica, cuya ratio en proporcin al PIB podra situarse por debajo del 45% al concluir el 2005. Estos buenos resultados no deben ocultar, sin embargo, que el esfuerzo fiscal ha experimentado una cierta ralentizacin este ao y que la poltica presupuestaria ha adquirido un tono expansivo que no habra contribuido en la medida que podra haberlo hecho a moderar las presiones de la demanda interna y a contener los riesgos presentes en la economa espaola. Dado el fuerte dinamismo que ha mostrado la recaudacin tributaria, con registros que exceden las estimaciones que se manejaron cuando se elaboraron los Presupuestos, debera ser posible culminar este ejercicio con un supervit tambin superior al presupuestado, que se ajustase ms a los requerimientos de la economa. Los Presupuestos para el ao 2006 presentan un objetivo de supervit para el conjunto de las Administraciones Pblicas del 0,2% del PIB. Si se tiene en cuenta que la posicin cclica ser similar a la del presente ejercicio, el tono de la poltica fiscal, estimado a partir de los indicadores habituales, podra resultar moderadamente expansivo. La presupuestacin de un crecimiento del gasto pblico del Estado significativamente por encima del incremento previsto del PIB nominal apunta en esta misma direccin. No parece, por tanto, que la poltica fiscal programada para el 2006 vaya a corregir suficientemente la orientacin expansiva. Es muy importante que si el dinamismo de los ingresos supera las previsiones de los Presupuestos, como ha ocurrido en 2005, ello se traduzca en un supervit ms elevado y no en aumentos adicionales del gasto.
