Resulta pertinente, no obstante, sealar, tambin desde esta perspectiva, que el comportamiento expansivo del gasto privado habra requerido, y todava requiere como he dicho recientemente en la Comisin de Presupuestos del Congreso-, un mayor grado de restriccin fiscal que contribuya en mayor medida a mitigar los desequilibrios macroeconmicos y financieros observados. En definitiva, los desequilibrios que acompaan al patrn actual de crecimiento de nuestra economa estn generando unas necesidades anuales netas de financiacin para el conjunto de la nacin que pueden situarse en el entorno del 6% del PIB. Ya sea por su relativa proximidad al nivel que actualmente exhibe la economa norteamericana, a la que todos los analistas tienden a atribuir un problema de desequilibrio exterior agudo; ya sea por ser superiores a las cotas alcanzadas por nuestra propia economa en momentos histricos anteriores que desembocaron en episodios de crisis cambiaria, este dato es contemplado con especial atencin por los analistas. En este sentido, es importante tener presente antes de nada que la pertenencia de Espaa a la zona euro ha modificado sustancialmente la forma en que deben contemplarse los riesgos derivados del dficit por cuenta corriente de nuestra economa. En una economa abierta con soberana monetaria y precios poco flexibles, el mecanismo habitual de correccin de un nivel excesivo de dficit exterior discurre a travs de una depreciacin del tipo de cambio, que permite restaurar la competitividad-precio de la economa. Visto desde una perspectiva puramente financiera, el desequilibrio tiende a generar una prdida de atractivo de los activos emitidos en la moneda domstica para los ahorradores no residentes, lo que hace reducir su valor relativo frente a instrumentos similares emitidos en otras monedas. La depreciacin del tipo de cambio reduce, entonces, la demanda de fondos en moneda extranjera que requiere la financiacin del dficit domstico y facilita la correccin paulatina del desequilibrio comercial. Es preciso observar, asimismo, que, en esas condiciones, la incertidumbre sobre la evolucin cambiaria tiende a encarecer el coste de la financiacin exterior y, de este modo, limita la capacidad de la economa para mantener, de modo persistente, saldos negativos en su balanza por cuenta corriente que ocasionen un aumento sostenido de sus deudas frente a no residentes. La pertenencia a un rea monetaria comn como la UEM cortocircuita, obviamente, el mecanismo anterior puesto que el vnculo se establece, en este caso, entre el tipo de cambio del euro y el dficit exterior no de la economa espaola individualmente considerada sino de la zona euro en su conjunto. De este modo, el aumento de las necesidades de financiacin de una economa no dispone del freno que representa la incertidumbre cambiaria y el aumento de los costes de financiacin. Consecuentemente, la conexin entre un dficit por cuenta corriente y las posibles dificultades para su financiacin discurre ahora a travs de un canal mucho ms indirecto que pasa, primero, por las implicaciones del desequilibrio sobre la capacidad de crecimiento de la economa y, despus, por la incidencia de esta ltima sobre la posicin patrimonial de cada prestatario. Es importante recalcar que esto no significa en absoluto que los problemas derivados de un elevado nivel de dficit por cuenta corriente desaparezcan. Se trata ms bien de un cambio en su naturaleza. Si me permiten que utilice aqu un smil mdico, cabra decir que el dficit exterior deja de ser una enfermedad en s mismo para pasar a constituir, principalmente, el sntoma de una enfermedad diferente. Una enfermedad que consiste en la paulatina prdida de competitividad. Los sntomas, en todo caso, son relevantes y hay que observarlos con detenimiento, ya que aportan una valiosa informacin sobre la evolucin del problema subyacente. Pero adems, hay que analizarlos con detalle porque requieren un tratamiento, tanto en el problema de fondo, como para ayudar a prevenir la aparicin de dificultades complementarias que compliquen el diagnstico. Desde esta perspectiva, querra dedicar los siguientes minutos de mi exposicin a analizar brevemente cmo se est financiando el dficit corriente de la economa espaola y a analizar sus implicaciones para la conduccin de las polticas pblicas. A comienzos de la presente dcada, cuando las necesidades de financiacin de la economa espaola se situaban en el entorno del 3% del PIB, nuestra Balanza de Pagos mostraba un reparto aproximadamente equitativo entre los tres componentes principales de las entradas netas de financiacin: la inversin directa; la inversin en cartera; y el resto de inversiones, que incluyen principalmente prstamos, depsitos y operaciones temporales de instituciones financieras. A partir de 2003, sin embargo, hemos asistido a una paulatina contraccin de la inversin directa que, de acuerdo con la ltima informacin disponible, apenas ha supuesto el 6% de las entradas de recursos durante los primeros seis meses de este ao. En un principio, el hueco dejado por la menor inversin directa exterior fue ocupado, principalmente, por el avance de las otras inversiones, es decir, por un mayor recurso de las entidades de crdito a los mercados interbancarios internacionales. Con posterioridad, hemos asistido a un crecimiento muy importante de la inversin en cartera, que acapara ahora aproximadamente las tres cuartas partes del total de fondos captados del resto del mundo. Un anlisis ms pormenorizado de esta partida revela, no obstante, que el reciente auge responde fundamentalmente al comportamiento expansivo de la adquisicin por parte de inversores extranjeros de valores de renta fija emitidos tanto por las entidades de crdito como por los fondos de titulizacin. De este modo, los recursos financieros exteriores necesarios para financiar el dficit corriente de la economa espaola se estn canalizando hacia sus destinatarios ltimos a travs, principalmente, de la intermediacin de las entidades de crdito espaolas. Estas estn apelando a los mercados internacionales con el fin de cubrir la creciente brecha existente entre la demanda de crdito y la evolucin de los pasivos bancarios tradicionales. De este modo, la expansin de la demanda domstica y el desequilibrio exterior que ha generado, han conllevado un aumento notable tanto de la cartera crediticia como de los pasivos frente al exterior del sector bancario residente, que ha aumentado la complejidad de la gestin y control de riesgos de un modo que no puede pasar desapercibido a quienes tenemos la tarea de velar por la buena salud y eficiencia de esta pieza fundamental del sistema financiero espaol. A este respecto, debo sealar que las entidades estn respondiendo con diligencia a la evolucin del escenario en el que operan. Ante el fuerte crecimiento de la demanda de crdito y el consiguiente incremento de los requerimientos derivados de los diferentes coeficientes de solvencia, las entidades han hecho un cierto uso del colchn que les proporciona el tradicional mantenimiento de unos niveles de recursos propios sustancialmente superiores a los legalmente exigibles. De este modo, pese a la ligera tendencia bajista que muestran las ratios en estos ltimos aos, sus niveles actuales continan situndose cmodamente por encima de los mnimos exigidos. Simultneamente, tanto el propio dinamismo del crdito como la continuada expansin de la economa y sus consiguientes efectos contractivos sobre la morosidad han venido acompaados por importantes avances de las provisiones mantenidas por las entidades y, por tanto, de la cobertura disponible frente a potenciales insolvencias. Este proceso, en el que la provisin estadstica ha desempeado un importante papel, est sirviendo para reforzar la solidez de las entidades en un contexto en el que el fuerte crecimiento de los prstamos aconseja extremar las precauciones ante los riesgos de impagos futuros. Paralelamente se han producido progresivos avances de sus resultados, que sitan actualmente a las instituciones espaolas entre las ms rentables del concierto europeo, en un contexto no fcil para la banca como es el de bajos tipos de inters. Esta tendencia se ha visto, sin duda, propiciada por el propio dinamismo de la actividad de intermediacin. Pero es importante observar, asimismo, que se ha beneficiado tambin de un importante esfuerzo en la contencin de costes cuyo reflejo ms evidente se halla en la continuada mejora de la ratio media de eficiencia del sector. Una importante conclusin de todo lo dicho es la importancia de haber contado y poder contar en el futuro con un sistema financiero integrado, eficiente y solvente para la financiacin del crecimiento de nuestra economa. Crecimiento que ha permitido acercar nuestros niveles de bienestar al de nuestros socios europeos. Ha sido la integracin del mercado financiero europeo, en el marco de la moneda nica, la que ha permitido la financiacin de nuestra economa sin las restricciones a las que estaba acostumbrada en el pasado. Adems el sistema financiero espaol ha sabido adaptarse a las nuevas circunstancias y al igual que en el pasado ha sabido no slo canalizar el ahorro interno hacia las asignaciones ms rentables, contribuyendo as al desarrollo, sino tambin protagonizar un proceso de expansin internacional con notable xito. Un sistema financiero integrado, eficiente y competitivo, proporciona las mejores condiciones para depositantes e inversores y contribuye a una mayor solidez desde una perspectiva prudencial. En estas condiciones, corresponde al Banco de Espaa vigilar que el marco regulatorio vigente favorezca la preservacin de la solidez, rentabilidad y eficiencia del sector, en un contexto caracterizado por una creciente complejidad de los instrumentos financieros y una progresiva internacionalizacin de los flujos de capitales. Dicho marco, adems, debe fomentar la integracin de los mercados, configurarse respetando los principios bsicos de mercado de manera que se reduzcan al mnimo imprescindible las interferencias en su normal funcionamiento y tener como referencia bsica a la hora de definir estrategias y prioridades, los retos que plantea la globalizacin y las ventajas que proporciona el mercado nico europeo. El Banco de Espaa est realizando notables esfuerzos en este terreno, que, se enmarcan dentro de procesos ms amplios desarrollados a nivel europeo e internacional. En el mbito europeo se plantean retos importantes. Por una parte, la creacin del euro y las iniciativas regulatorias europeas (entre las que destacan el Plan de Accin de Servicios Financieros de la Comisin Europea) ha conseguido la integracin en un muy corto espacio de tiempo de los mercados mayoristas, como el monetario y el interbancario. No obstante, esa integracin avanza mucho ms lentamente en el rea de banca minorista, y no son pocas las resistencias que todava se suscitan en operaciones bancarias transfronterizas. Creo que el enfoque de la Comisin Europea de considerar la nueva fase de su plan de accin en el mbito de los servicios financieros como parte integral y fundamental de su agenda econmica y social es muy adecuado. Efectivamente, retos como la globalizacin, la necesidad de aumentar su crecimiento potencial, de crear un entorno que favorezca capacidad emprendedora y la innovacin, la sostenibilidad de las tensiones que el envejecimiento de la poblacin plantea en la financiacin de los sistemas de pensiones y de salud, exigen que la UE acometa reformas y una de las principales es la de perfeccionar un mercado financiero nico, integrado y dinmico que canalice el ahorro, diversifique riesgos y proporcione a las empresas los medios para invertir y crecer. La responsabilidad en estas reas no solo recae en los organismos y autoridades comunitarios, sino tambin, y en muchos casos, muy especialmente, en las autoridades de los pases miembros. Creo que todas las autoridades debemos empujar en la misma direccin: integracin de mercados, mejor regulacin que disminuya costes a las empresas, incentivos a la mejor gestin de riesgos, supervisin en base a riesgo, coordinacin y convergencia supervisora, mejora de las estructuras de gobierno corporativo, transparencia, disciplina de mercado, etc. La lista es larga y variada, por ello, me gustara dedicar el final de mi intervencin a comentar de forma esquemtica alguno de esos aspectos, cuya eleccin responde a su particular relevancia en una situacin como la actual en la que, como he venido sealando a lo largo de mi exposicin, ha aumentado sensiblemente la complejidad del negocio como consecuencia de las transformaciones de nuestra economa y del sistema financiero nacional e internacional. En el marco regulador conocido como Lamfalusy, el denominado CEBS (Comit europeo de supervisores bancarios), presidido por el Banco de Espaa en sus dos primeros aos de existencia, ha venido trabajando, creo que de forma reconocidamente eficiente, en varias de las lneas de actuacin: Coordinacin y convergencia de las prcticas supervisoras. Algo especialmente relevante para lograr consistencia en la implementacin de Basilea II, cuya directiva, como ustedes saben, ha sido recientemente aprobada por el Parlamento Europeo. Basilea II y ms especialmente la directiva europea de capital refuerza el papel del supervisor de origen, tanto como dinamizador de la coordinacin de los supervisores de destino, como en los procesos de validacin de modelos. En el mercado financiero europeo nico, en el que coexisten 25 autoridades supervisoras nacionales junto con bancos de vocacin paneuropea, no basta con una regulacin comn, sino que es necesario un amplio consenso entre los supervisores sobre cmo se va a aplicar en la prctica esa directiva. Este proceso, denominado convergencia de prcticas supervisoras, es imprescindible para no impedir los procesos de integracin entre instituciones y para ofrecer a la industria bancaria un sistema de supervisin europea eficiente en trminos de coste. CEBS ha lanzado tambin dos iniciativas en el terreno de la informacin y transparencia al buscar unos formatos comunes en la Unin Europea para los requerimientos de informacin en materia contable y de capital, conocidos como FINREP y COREP. Es la primera vez que los supervisores financieros europeos logran establecer unos requerimientos de informacin comunes para toda la UE, con evidentes ventajas de coste para la industria. Adems, esta armonizacin de la informacin favorecer tambin la de las prcticas supervisoras. Por ltimo, estas iniciativas incluyen desarrollos informticos utilizando las ltimas tcnicas en transmisin de informacin financiera, como XBRL. Con la Directiva de Basilea II recientemente aprobada por el Consejo y el Parlamento Europeo, creo que es conveniente dedicarle un poco de tiempo a reflexionar sobre su papel en el fortalecimiento del sistema financiero por varias vas. Por un lado, Basilea II proporcionara incentivos para una mejor gestin de riesgos y va a propiciar que los consejeros de las entidades asuman una mayor responsabilidad en su control efectivo. Por otro, se incrementarn sustancialmente los requisitos de transparencia lo que, entre otras cosas, har mucho ms visibles las decisiones de gestin de riesgos adoptadas, amplificando, de este modo, la capacidad de los mercados para premiar, en forma de unos menores costes de financiacin, a aquellas instituciones que persigan con mayor empeo y acierto el objetivo de crear valor con una perspectiva de medio y largo plazo. La mejora en la gestin de riesgos debe estar anclada en un buen gobierno corporativo. Aunque Basilea II conformar un marco general propicio para un mejor gobierno de las entidades, ser preciso que cada regulador perfile los elementos concretos que permiten adaptarse a las caractersticas especficas de entidades o grupos de entidades. La necesidad de articular normativamente una serie de principios de buen gobierno corporativo surge cuando los mecanismos de mercado, incluida la posibilidad de la propia autorregulacin por parte del sector, no son suficientes para garantizar una correcta alineacin de los intereses de los gestores de las empresas con los de sus propietarios ltimos. Tambin es razonable pensar que la existencia de unos slidos principios de buen gobierno contribuir positivamente a aumentar la confianza de quienes, sin convertirse necesariamente en propietarios de las sociedades, contribuyen de un modo u otro a financiar su actividad. La importancia del buen gobierno societario es, en mi opinin, aun mayor en el caso del negocio bancario ya que la esencia del mismo consiste precisamente en tomar fondos de unos agentes y canalizarlos hacia terceros. Trminos como confianza y reputacin adquieren, por lo tanto, una dimensin adicional. En este sentido me gustara recordar que el Comit de Supervisores Bancarios de Basilea ha publicado un documento consultivo en el que se ha tratado de adaptar el cdigo de buen gobierno de la OCDE a las especificidades de las entidades de crdito. Estas iniciativas que he resumido de forma esquemtica: la convergencia y cooperacin supervisora, la implantacin de Basilea II y las iniciativas para reforzar el buen gobierno de las entidades financieras son solo algunos ejemplos que van en las direcciones antes mencionadas de profundizar en la integracin y competencia de los mercados financieros y en la eficiencia y solvencia de las entidades de crdito. Terminar recordando que el largo periodo de crecimiento de la economa espaola ha requerido un acceso al ahorro exterior que ha sido posible, sin introducir restricciones al crecimiento, gracias principalmente al mercado financiero europeo en el contexto del euro, destacando el relevante papel jugado por las entidades de crdito espaolas. Esta facilidad de financiacin no debe ocultar la necesidad de corregir los desequilibrios subyacentes si se quiere prolongar el periodo de convergencia con nuestros socios europeos. En este proceso, las polticas presupuestarias y de reformas estructurales son claves. Asimismo, no debemos ignorar que la forma concreta en la que se est instrumentando la entrada de este mayor volumen de ahorro exterior supone una presin adicional sobre la capacidad de las entidades de crdito espaolas para intermediar de manera eficaz los flujos de recursos financieros entre ahorradores y prestamistas y un cambio en su perfil de riesgos. Un ejercicio de mnima prudencia exige, pues, vigilar con especial atencin la evolucin este proceso en el futuro y continuar avanzando en las lneas de accin antes mencionadas. Muchas gracias por su atencin.

Title: Securitization of assets: perspectives from a Central Bank
text: Marrakech, 11 November 2005 Asset securitization: perspectives from a Central Bank First Spanish Securitization Forum. EBN Bank D. Gonzalo Gil Deputy Governor of the Bank of Spain I would like to begin my speech by thanking the organizers of this conference for the opportunity to share with you some reflections on recent trends and future developments that asset securitization processes may pose for the banking sector. In recent decades, financial markets have undergone important changes that have substantially altered their physiognomy. Thus, for example, there has been a growing internationalization of entities, which must be framed in a context of greater financial globalization. Likewise, in recent years there have been important technological advances that have allowed the development of more sophisticated and complex products. This type of products, which pose a greater difficulty of treatment precisely related, at least in part, to their greater complexity, allow entities to develop new lines of business, while facilitating them to adapt to the needs of their customers. Asset securitisation has to be seen in this context. Throughout my speech, I intend to share with you some reflection on the evolution of asset securitization over the last few years, understanding this activity as the process of transforming a set of assets on the balance sheet of an entity, typically illiquid, such as mortgage loans, into securities that can be transferred, sold or assigned. I would also like to analyse the benefits it poses for banks, as well as some of the potential risks from the point of view of financial stability. Finally, I intend to comment briefly on the latest developments in prudential regulation in this area, especially those related to the revised Framework for International Capital Convergence of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, better known as Basel II, and its influence on Spanish regulation and on the foreseeable development of the market. Evolution of asset securitisation in the banking sector The evolution of securitisation is determined by a wide range of factors, including the degree of development of bond markets, in terms of their narrowness and liquidity. However, the securitization of assets, by its very nature, is an activity that depends, to a large extent, on the evolution of existing regulations in this area. In Spain, the 1981 law on the mortgage market allowed entities to issue bonds, bonds and mortgage participations, which were guaranteed by the loans and mortgage credits that appeared on their balance sheet. Mortgage holdings, unlike bonds and bonds, opened up the possibility of off-balance sheet securitizations, but their initial success was very limited. In 1992, the mortgage securitisation law, linked to a wider market reform initiated in 1991, was a first step towards advancing the development of so-called off-balance sheet securitisations. Through this law, the Mortgage Securitization Funds (FTH) are created with the objective, among others, of stimulating specialization and competition in the mortgage market and of favoring the emergence of a long-term private fixed income security. These are assets without legal personality that acquire mortgage loans from entities, through mortgage participations, and that, simultaneously, issue mortgage-backed bonds, which must be rated by a rating agency. These bonds involve the grouping of mortgage loans of different characteristics (interest rate, term, etc.), which are transferred off the balance sheet of the entities and transformed into negotiable, standardized and homogeneous securities. The fact that the development of securitization begins in the mortgage market is not a novelty in the Spanish case. In fact, the first process of this kind took place in that market in the United States in 1970. Moreover, there are reasons that have to do with the very characteristics of mortgage loans that make them relatively homogeneous products that can be securitized more easily: reduced probabilities of default, value of the guarantee of the loans easily knowable or long repayment period, among others. However, despite the creation of mortgage securitisation funds in 1992, this activity had a rather limited development in Spain, until in 1998 a set of factors occurred that triggered a growing dynamism in the Spanish securitisation market. On the one hand, Royal Decree 926/1998 regulated asset securitisation funds (FTAs), similar to mortgage securitisation, but with the capacity to acquire not mortgage loans suitable for mobilisation in the mortgage market, but any credit right, present, and which therefore appears on the balance sheet of an entity, or future. In addition, this new regulation allowed greater flexibility and freedom to the agents involved in the securitisation processes. Some examples of asset securitisations other than mortgage loans that have become particularly important in the Spanish case are securitisations of loans to SMEs and, fundamentally, mortgage bonds, which have experienced a notable expansion in recent years. But the dynamism of securitisation in Spain since 1998 is not only due to the aforementioned legislative changes. In that year, as I have pointed out, there were a series of circumstances that made us think about the future growth of this market. In the first place, the very development of financial markets in Spain, in a context of greater financial culture, allowed the growing importance of, among others, investment funds. These funds covered the need of many savers to include in their portfolios more sophisticated instruments that could provide a higher return than traditional bank deposits. The managers of the investment funds would channel part of the funds' assets to the fixed income markets. Secondly, in the context of monetary union, the weight of public debt in fixed income financial markets would tend to be reduced, with asset-backed securities, mortgage or not, being able to act as an alternative for a group of investors looking for substitutes for public bonds. Finally, and related to the above, a low nominal return on lower-risk assets was expected, and asset-backed securities could be converted into a reasonable alternative for certain investors. The subsequent confirmation of many of these factors helps to explain the aforementioned dynamism observed in the area of asset securitisation. This dynamism has been reflected in Spain over the last five years, during which the growth of emissions has always been higher, in annual terms, to 45%. Thus, in 2004 the volume issued was just over six times higher than in 2000. This strong issuing activity means that the total balance of asset-backed securities has also grown continuously, at rates above 50%, reaching 120 billion euros in 2004, almost seven times more than in 2000. The data available in 2005, which in September showed a growth in the volume of emissions of just over 26% compared to the same period of the previous year, suggest that the dynamism of the sector will continue for another year. In fact, this year has seen the largest securitization of mortgage bonds to date due to their size. Of the previous total, the securitization of mortgage bonds has been very notable in recent years. In 2004 they represented 31% of the outstanding balance of the liabilities of Spanish securitization funds, with their volume issued on that date growing by 73% compared to the previous year, and four times more than with respect to what was issued in 2001. However, the securitisation of mortgage bonds has different characteristics compared to other securitisations, insofar as private sector assets are not securitized, but bank liabilities. Moreover, the mortgage loans that back these bonds remain on bank balance sheets. Excluding the securitisation of mortgage bonds, the sector has been dynamic, but to a lesser extent: the outstanding balance of liabilities of Spanish securitisation funds increased between 2004 and 2000 by almost five times, instead of seven; while the volume issued in 2004, compared to 2003, goes from growing 45% to 33%. The dynamism of the securitisation market is also reflected in the percentage of securitised assets, including securitised mortgage bonds, on credit under management, which rose from almost 5% in 2000 to around 14% in 2004. Limiting these calculations to the mortgage portfolio, these percentages would be 9% in 2000 and 18% in 2004. However, and despite this evolution, the data indicate, even for the mortgage market, a still limited mobilization. In the European context, the asset securitisation market has also been very dynamic in recent years, with a new all-time high in terms of volume issued in 2004. The data available up to the second half of 2005 indicate that this year this maximum could even be exceeded, since the volume issued in the first half of the year was 18.3% higher than in the same period of the previous year. In this context, according to data from the first half of 2005, Spain ranked third in Europe, with 14% of total emissions, and only behind the United Kingdom and Italy. The dynamism of asset securitisation in Spain is mainly due to financial institutions, and increasingly to savings banks. In December 2004, outstanding balances show that 54% of market-backed securities come from assets securitized by savings banks. Likewise, in recent years there has also been a process of deconcentration of issuances, which implies that the outstanding balance of securitization bonds in the hands of larger entities is decreasing. So far I have explained the evolution of securitisation by referring to the development of regulation in this area and to a set of factors that could be considered demand. However, it is not possible to understand this phenomenon in Spain without taking into account the remarkable dynamism of financing to the resident private sector, and especially mortgage financing in recent years. I have already pointed out that in recent years the main protagonist of securitisation has been mortgage bonds, which in 2004 represented 31% of the outstanding balance of liabilities of Spanish securitisation funds, and which currently make up the most active market in Europe in this product. Moreover, by type of securitised asset, the relative importance of mortgage loans, issued through both FTH and FTA, stands out, with a weight of 41% of the outstanding balances of liabilities of Spanish securitization funds in 2004. Today, and after its prominence in previous years, the outstanding balance of issues through FTH is slightly lower than through FTA, which reflects the increase in the securitization of mortgage loans of amounts greater than 80% of the appraised value. In short, and taking into account that 83% of the new issues in 2004 were supported, in some way, by mortgage loans, a good part of the growth in the securitisation market is related to the dynamism of the mortgage market in Spain. In fact, and unlike what has happened in other European markets in recent years, in Spain the development of new securitization models, such as synthetic ones, has been almost non-existent. Having a complete view of the causes of this strong expansion of the securitisation market in Spain requires dwelling on some factors that we could call supply. In fact, this brings me to the second of the points of my speech: the analysis of the advantages that asset securitisation presents for institutions. Benefits of asset securitisation for institutions As I have already pointed out, through asset securitisation, institutions sell part of their loans to third parties, which allows them to restructure their balance sheet without having to wait passively for the maturity of the asset. At the same time, they usually maintain asset management, receive commissions, which are reflected in their income statement, and maintain the commercial relationship with their clients. In addition to these considerations, there are other advantages. I will point out the three that I consider most relevant from the point of view of credit institutions, the predominant actors in this activity. First, asset securitisation can be used as a mode of credit risk management, through its transfer to a third party. Like other instruments that enable this type of transfer, such as credit derivatives, it is a mechanism that allows active risk management without, as I have pointed out, the commercial relations of the entity being negatively affected. It also facilitates efficient comprehensive credit risk management at the banking group level, becoming a useful tool, for example, to deal with concentration risk. With regard to the transfer of risks, however, let me remind you that Spanish legislation has always been demanding. In particular, the full transfer of risks is required in order not to make the corresponding provisions for insolvencies. Thus, for example, in cases where the entity accompanies the sale of the assets of a subordinated loan to the fund, in order to absorb a certain level of losses due to credit risk, the obligation to provision for that risk remains. This prevents securitisation from being used as a means of arbitrating provisions. The requirement regarding the transfer of risks will continue to be the trend after the recent entry into force of the new accounting circular, circular 4/2004, which, as you know, adapts the International Financial Reporting Standards to the peculiarities of the Spanish banking system. Under the new accounting framework, it is established that the reduction of the balance sheet only occurs when the transferor has substantially transferred the risks and benefits associated with the asset in question. This implies that it will be necessary to analyse each assignment contract individually. The data available for 2005 show that the new circular, as expected, has not had a direct impact on the issuance of securitised assets, which continues, as I have pointed out, to increase. However, the information available to date shows that a significant amount (about db25 billion out of a total of db73 billion) of securitisations carried out (remember that the rule does not have full retroactive effects) has had to be returned to the balance sheet. The second advantage of asset securitisation is that it allows institutions to transform illiquid assets, such as mortgage loans, into more liquid ones, such as mortgage-backed securities. Some banks have found the securitisation process beneficial simply as a mechanism that enables the creation of a cushion of easily convertible assets into liquidity, for example by offering them as collateral at the ECB. In a context such as Spain's, characterised by the strong expansion of credit to the private sector, together with the slower rate of growth of deposits from this sector, the liquidity reason provided by securitisation is an important explanatory factor. In fact, within the mortgage portfolio, securitized assets over total assets managed, which indicate the risk transferred to the market, was 8.3% in December 2004. If the mortgage bonds issued are included in the numerator, thus obtaining an indicator of the liquidity obtained by the entities, the percentage stood at 18%. In this sense, the strong dynamism shown by mortgage bonds, as I have said enabled for securitization since 1998, has to do with the capture of financing by entities, mainly by those that found it complex to place the issued bonds on the market. However, since the loans backing the bonds remain on the balance sheet, this type of securitisation cannot be understood as a risk management and transfer mechanism. Finally, a third element that could make asset securitisation attractive to entities is the possibility of managing regulatory own resources. That is, by deregistering assets from the balance sheet, it is possible to develop the same volume of activity, but appealing to a smaller amount of equity. However, this practice can lead to behaviour that is difficult to reconcile with prudent risk management and solvency. In particular, the self-serving choice of loans to be securitised may lead to an average decline in the credit quality of banks' portfolios. However, it does not seem that this has been the case in Spain, where, although these advantages have existed and still exist in that regulatory framework, depository institutions, banks, savings banks and cooperatives have come to this market, fundamentally, for the above reasons. Some potential risks Transfer of risks Among the advantages I mentioned earlier about asset securitization, I pointed out the possibilities it allows as a risk management mechanism. Undoubtedly, from the point of view of the stability of the financial system as a whole, to the extent that institutions have more and better ways to manage the risks they face, this is a positive element. In fact, through securitization, credit risk is more manageable, since it is transformed, we could say, into a tradable good. On the other hand, risk no longer accumulates on the balance sheet of a group of entities, but is dispersed among a greater number of investors. The process of dispersing risk among a wider range of actors is beneficial from the point of view of financial stability. Moreover, to the extent that this process of dispersion of risks is not only carried out between banks, but also between different sectors within the financial field, it makes it possible to manage the excessive concentrations (geographical, product, maturities, currencies, etc.) that the banking sector could maintain. In any case, the final result for the financial stability of risk transfer processes, including asset securitization, also depends on the management that arises on a set of non-negligible challenges. Let me simply point out a few of them. The distribution of risks among a greater number of actors, which, as I have pointed out, can be positive for financial stability, could be neutralised by the fact that, in some markets, the concentration of trading was excessive. In this sense, the organisational structure of markets must be an area to be considered and monitored on an ongoing basis. I also pointed out that the transfer of risks outside the banking sector could be an advantage. However, this is not always the case, in particular where such risks are assumed by non-regulated entities. Not only does this mean that the extent of crises may be greater, to the extent that imbalances may become easier and more difficult, but that their resolution may also be hampered. In line with the above, there has recently been a growing degree of concern about hegde funds, which can act as investors interested in asset transfer processes that involve a higher level of risk. While these funds provide liquidity and offer different views from those prevailing in the markets, favouring efficiency, their high leverage and their ability to change their positions very quickly are financial stability concerns. It should not be forgotten that, to the extent that market participants purchasing asset-backed securities or other risk transfer instruments rely on the opinion issued by rating agencies, these agencies play a central role in the proper functioning of such instruments. Asset securitisation processes as risk transfer mechanisms may involve systemic risks, insofar as the default suffered by an institution is likely to cause a chain reaction affecting other institutions. Likewise, the traditional role of banks as institutions that monitor the behavior of borrowers can be diluted. Last but not least, today there is no adequate level of transparency in risk transfer markets, which can limit their capacity as instruments capable of enhancing the efficiency and stability of financial markets. Consequently, it seems necessary to advance in the achievement of greater information transparency, at least in two directions: in the information provided by the entities themselves at the individual level, and in the creation of statistics and databases at the aggregate level that enable analysis. In this regard, it is worth mentioning the initiative of the European Committee of Banking Supervisors (CEBS) to create a common supervisory information framework derived from the new Solvency Directives that incorporate Basel II, known as COREP ("Common Reporting") by the working group that is carrying it out. The proposal, almost definitive, includes a table of individualized information on the securitisations carried out by credit institutions and their fundamental characteristics which, for those supervisors who make use of it (I remind you that the application will be voluntary for supervisors) will be an important source of knowledge that complements the information provided by the two tables, also from COREP, with information on capital requirements arising from exposures of any kind related to securitisations. Complexity of securitisations Let me now raise a second set of elements that may involve challenges to be considered in the medium term. These elements have to do with the complexity of the structures with which asset securitisations are developed. On the one hand, the securitisation of assets is carried out, on numerous occasions, through vehicles. To date, this has not been a problem in Spain, but in other countries. Operating through these complex structures, which sometimes hinder or prevent transparency, poses additional challenges for the entities that use them in the development of their activity. Although these are legitimate business decisions in the vast majority of cases, it is no less true that they incorporate legal and reputational risks that will have to be considered. Therefore, institutions are expected to act with an appropriate degree of responsibility, identifying the risks associated with the use of these structures, establishing appropriate procedures for their management and evaluating at all times that they are used for the purposes initially intended. This approach is being shared by several regulators internationally, including the Bank of Spain. More recently, the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision has published for its public consultation, which ended on October 31, a document on corporate governance principles, which analyzes these issues in depth, from the perspective of good governance needs. The complexity of asset securitisation processes, however, goes beyond the fact that the activity is carried out through these vehicles and, without a doubt, implies management risks that will have to be properly considered. A good example of this complexity is found in the lengthy and difficult process that has taken place to satisfactorily accommodate the securitization of assets within Basel II. Allow me to devote the last few minutes of my speech to this issue. The new regulation of securitisation in Basel II As is well known, the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision promotes the international harmonization of prudential regulations, with the aim of strengthening the solvency of the financial system as well as leveling the competitive playing field of internationally active credit institutions. As a result of this objective, the 1988 Capital Agreement (Basel I) was born, which established a simple calculation of the necessary prudential capital. This simplicity facilitated its general acceptance beyond the group of members of the Committee and the group of banks to which the Agreement was originally addressed, resulting in an overall improvement in the solvency of the financial system while leveling the playing field between entities from different countries in a world that was already tending towards financial globalization, it is a precursor, to a large extent, of the other forms of globalization. However, Basel I became obsolete due to its own simplicity that progressively distanced it from the objectives it pursued. That is, the great transformation that took place in the international financial markets, in their various agents, in the operations carried out and in the management of risks did not fit adequately in Basel I, especially for the internationally active banks to which the Agreement was addressed, apart from the subsequent generalization. In addition, one of the aspects whose management has become more active in recent years has been, precisely, the management of own resources. It is clear that a simple solvency ratio gave opportunities for the most aggressive managers to improve the apparent solvency of institutions, opportunities that have been taken advantage of in certain cases. Basel II takes a step forward, while maintaining the same objectives as its predecessor. It pursues a stable financial system through a more adequate capitalization of the entities, that is, the prudential regulations are more sensitive to the level of risks assumed as well as to the internal risk management systems of each entity. In this way, regulatory capital is brought closer to economic capital while seeking, as far as possible, to maintain the level of capitalization reached by the financial system. In relation to the issue that specifically concerns us, securitization, the absence of a specific treatment in Basel I is notorious. In turn, Basel II establishes general rules that are also not suitable for securitisations, since the general treatment is aimed at individual loan portfolios that, although it is true that they can be considered jointly, it is no less true that they are not adequate to face the treatment of the stratified risks of a portfolio. Stratification that can be associated with securitization and that causes different degrees of participation in losses. Basel II has therefore created a specific framework for any position held in a securitisation, a framework to which I will briefly refer. But first, it is again necessary to define the concept of securitisation subject to specific treatment in Basel II. In this context, securitisation is defined as the flow of payments from an underlying portfolio of assets that is distributed in at least two different stratified risk positions, in which we find different collection capacities on the part of its holders. In this sense, payments to investors depend on the behavior of the underlying assets, i.e. they do not derive from an obligation of the originator, while subordinated tranches can absorb losses without interrupting the contractual flow of payments to the best-positioned, or more senior, tranches, as they are commonly called in the market. The concept of securitisation under Basel II also includes the significant and stratified mobilisation of a portfolio's credit risk through financial derivatives, i.e. synthetic securitisation. In the latter case, the credit risk of an underlying portfolio of assets is transferred, in whole or in part, through the use of credit derivatives or collateral that serve to hedge the credit risk of the portfolio, in this way and as in traditional securitisation, the investor's risk depends on the behaviour of the underlying portfolio. The term significant risk transfer is very relevant, both in traditional and synthetic securitisations. Despite its importance, it is not perfectly defined, but we nevertheless find some support in Pillar II of the Agreement. Its relevance lies in the fact that the application of the specific methods of securitisation requires that the aforementioned significant transfer of risk has occurred, in addition to other requirements having to be met depending on whether the traditional or synthetic securitisation is (for example, not maintaining effective control over the transferred assets or that investors only have rights over the underlying assets and not over the assets of the risk-transferring bank). And what are the specific methods envisaged by Basel II for securitisations? As in the case of the methodologies applicable to the remaining exposures, Basel II distinguishes between a Standard Method and Internal Rating Based (IRB) methods for the treatment of securitisations for the purpose of calculating capital requirements. As for the possibility of applying or not of these methods, tell them that the Standard method is mandatory for those banks that apply this approach for the type of assets that make up the securitized portfolio. On the other hand, the IRB method is mandatory for banks that have received the necessary authorisation to apply it for the type of assets that make up that securitised portfolio. In fact, the distinction here between the standard method and the IRB is less relevant, since we can consider that there is a range of methods whose sophistication and sensitivity to risk is increasing starting from a standard method linked to external credit ratings. There are three methods under the IRB designation: the method also based on external ratings, although with greater flexibility than the standard method, the supervisory formula method and the internal valuation method. The internal valuation method is a very specific system only applicable for exposures in commercial paper programs. The IRB method based on external ratings confers a little more risk awareness than the Standard, while the supervisory formula method is only used when there is no external rating or cannot be inferred from the established tranches. By the latter method, the capital requirement depends on what was available before the securitisation as well as on additional elements. Such external rating shall, where appropriate, be obtained from among the rating entities (ECAIS) considered to be "eligible" for general purposes, but which shall comply with certain additional conditions in the case of securitisation. It should be remembered that the IRB method establishes a ceiling as far as capital requirements are concerned, since they cannot exceed the requirement that would be required of the exposures of the portfolio if the portfolio had not been securitized. And it is also worth noting that, in general, in the event that none of the above IRB methods are applicable, the position will be deducted from regulatory capital in the same way as is done for the Standard Model in the absence of external ratings. This deduction is made, in equal parts, of first- and second-category capital. In relation to the revision of the current Spanish solvency regulations, which are clearly insufficient for the proper treatment of securitisations, it seems the most convenient thing to wait for the implementation of the new solvency directives that reflect the changes introduced by Basel II. This is because the horizon for implementing the new directives is very close. And also because we could do little in the interim until that implementation. That is, the awareness of the capital requirements of securitization positions would be only partial, given certain limitations in the current regulation that is above the Circulars and, therefore, the powers of the Bank of Spain. It was under these considerations that the Bank of Spain Circular 3/2005, of 30 June, to credit institutions, which also modifies 5/1993, was drawn up, and whose main objective was to address and clarify the effects on eligible own resources and risk assets subject to weighting had produced the important reform of the accounting standards of these entities undertaken by Bank of Spain Circular 4/2004, of 22 December. The review undertaken has basically intended that the application of the new accounting regulations maintain the current definition of computable own resources and the accounting basis for calculating risks, avoiding a significant alteration of the minimum own resources requirements to which credit institutions are subject and thus ensuring adequate coordination between the new accounting concepts and the definitions and mandates of the rules governing the requirements solvency. The accounting changes made in the field of securitisations, with more stringent requirements for their decommissioning, have not been reflected in Circular 3/2005 because, in the light of the considerations I have made above, the implementation costs might not justify the extent of the improvements that could be made at this time. Conclusions Let me conclude by simply providing a final thought on the securitisation process. Throughout my speech, I pointed out that asset securitisation, like other risk transfer mechanisms, has different aspects that can promote financial stability. However, I also pointed out some factors that can contribute to their positive effects not only being diluted, but even counteracted: from the complexity of these instruments, to the transfer of risks to non-regulated financial institutions, to the lack of transparency of this type of operation. My personal impression, however, is that the net balance of these positive and negative effects must be favourable from the point of view of financial stability. And this is not because the risks are lower, but because we all have to assume our degree of responsibility and find formulas that allow us to enjoy the benefits derived from better risk and liquidity management, minimizing potential risks. In fact, this is not unique to asset securitisations or other risk transfer mechanisms, but we have been doing so in many other areas of the financial sector. Thank you very much for your attention

Evolucin de la titulizacin de activos en el sector bancario La evolucin de la titulizacin viene determinada por un conjunto amplio de factores, entre ellos el propio grado de desarrollo de los mercados de renta fija, en trminos de su estrechez y liquidez. No obstante, la titulizacin de activos, por sus propias caractersticas, es una actividad que depende, en gran parte, de la evolucin de las regulaciones existentes en la materia. En Espaa, la ley de 1981 del mercado hipotecario permita a las entidades emitir bonos, cdulas y participaciones hipotecarias, que quedaban garantizados por los prstamos y crditos hipotecarios que figuraban en su balance. Las participaciones hipotecarias, a diferencia de los bonos y las cdulas, abran la posibilidad a las titulizaciones fuera de balance, pero su xito inicial fue muy limitado. En 1992, la ley de titulizacin hipotecaria, vinculada a una reforma ms amplia del mercado iniciada en 1991, supone un primer paso para avanzar en el desarrollo de las denominadas titulizaciones fuera de balance. A travs de esta ley se crean los Fondos de Titulizacin Hipotecaria (FTH) con el objetivo, entre otros, de estimular la especializacin y la competencia en el mercado hipotecario y de favorecer la aparicin de un ttulo de renta fija privada a largo plazo. Se trata de patrimonios sin personalidad jurdica que adquieren a las entidades, a travs de participaciones hipotecarias, los prstamos hipotecarios y que, simultneamente, emiten bonos de titulizacin hipotecaria, que obligatoriamente han de ser calificados por una agencia de calificacin. No obstante, a pesar de la creacin de los fondos de titulizacin hipotecaria en 1992, esta actividad tuvo un desarrollo bastante limitado en Espaa, hasta que en 1998 concurrieron un conjunto de factores que desencadenaron un dinamismo creciente en el mercado de titulizaciones espaol. Por una parte, el Real Decreto 926/1998 regul los fondos de titulizacin de activos (FTA), anlogos a los de titulizacin hipotecaria, pero con capacidad para adquirir no ya prstamos hipotecarios aptos para su movilizacin en el mercado hipotecarios, sino cualquier derecho de crdito, presente, y que por lo tanto figure en el balance de una entidad, o futuro. Adems, esta nueva regulacin permita una mayor flexibilidad y libertad a los agentes participantes en los procesos de titulizacin. Algunos ejemplos de titulizaciones de activos distintos de los prstamos hipotecarios que han cobrado especial importancia en el caso espaol son las titulizaciones de prstamos a PYMES y, fundamentalmente, las cdulas hipotecarias, que han experimentado una notable expansin en los ltimos aos. Pero el dinamismo de la titulizacin en Espaa a partir de 1998 no solo se debe a los mencionados cambios legislativos. En ese ao, como he sealado, se daban una serie de circunstancias que hacan pensar en el futuro crecimiento de este mercado. En primer lugar, el propio desarrollo de los mercados financieros en Espaa, en un contexto de mayor cultura financiera, permita la creciente importancia de, entre otros, los fondos de inversin. Dichos fondos cubran la necesidad de muchos ahorradores de incluir en sus carteras instrumentos ms sofisticados que pudieran aportar una mayor rentabilidad que los depsitos bancarios tradicionales. Los gestores de los fondos de inversin, canalizaran parte de patrimonio de los fondos hacia los mercados de renta fija. En segundo lugar, en el contexto de la Unin Monetaria, el peso de la deuda pblica en los mercados financieros de renta fija tendera a reducirse, pudiendo actuar los bonos de titulizacin, hipotecaria o no, como una alternativa para un conjunto de inversores en busca de sustitutos para la renta fija pblica. Finalmente, y relacionado con lo anterior, se esperaba una reducida rentabilidad nominal de los activos de ms bajo riesgo, pudiendo convertirse los bonos de titulizacin en una alternativa razonable para determinados inversores. La posterior confirmacin de buena parte de estos factores contribuye a explicar el mencionado dinamismo que se ha observado en el mbito de la titulizacin de activos. Este dinamismo se plasma en Espaa a lo largo de los ltimos cinco aos, durante los cuales el crecimiento de las emisiones ha sido siempre superior, en trminos anuales, al 45%. As, en 2004 el volumen emitido superaba en algo ms de seis veces el de 2000. Esta fuerte actividad emisora lleva a que el saldo total de los bonos de titulizacin haya crecido tambin de forma continua, a tasas superiores al 50%, hasta alcanzar en 2004 los 120 mil millones de euros, casi siete veces ms que el registrado en 2000. Es ms, los prstamos hipotecarios que respaldan dichas cdulas permanecen en los balances bancarios. Excluyendo la titulizacin de cdulas hipotecarias el sector se ha mostrado dinmico, pero en menor medida: el saldo vivo de los pasivos de los fondos de titulizacin espaoles se increment entre 2004 y 2000 casi en cinco veces, en lugar de en siete; mientras que el volumen emitido en 2004, respecto a 2003, pasa de crecer el 45% a hacerlo el 33%. Restringiendo estos clculos a la cartera hipotecaria, dichos porcentajes seran del 9% en 2000 y del 18% en 2004. Con todo, y a pesar de esta evolucin, los datos indican, incluso para el mercado hipotecario, una movilizacin todava limitada. En el contexto europeo, el mercado de titulizacin de activos tambin se ha mostrado muy dinmico en los ltimos aos, registrndose en 2004 un nuevo mximo histrico en trminos del volumen emitido. Los datos disponibles hasta el segundo semestre de 2005 indican que en este ao ese mximo podra incluso ser superado, ya que el volumen emitido en la primera mitad del ejercicio era un 18,3% superior al del mismo perodo del ao precedente.
