The presence of services among the most inflationary items of the Spanish economy is not surprising, since this type of productive activities is more protected against external competition than manufacturing, and companies and suppliers can exercise greater market power, especially when consumer demand is buoyant. There is a range of services present in the shopping basket that are scarcely marketable, and in addition some of these markets are, in general, more regulated, so that, although the liberalization process has advanced substantially in the last two decades, the degree of competition in some branches of this sector is still insufficient. The inflation differential with EMU should also be examined from the perspective of the contribution of labour costs and corporate margins. In a first approximation and from an internal point of view, the evolution of wage costs in our country could be described as moderate, in the sense that it has not hindered the expansion of margins or the maintenance of the profitability ratios of companies at relatively high levels, in recent years d0 as shown, for example, information from the Central Balance Sheet of the Bank of Spain. However, a closer examination of the information reveals some less flattering aspects. Thus, it is worth noting the particularly expansionary evolution that margins are having in the construction and services branches, which have benefited from strong growth in house prices and lower competitive pressures, respectively. In turn, wage increases, combined with the low growth in productivity, have led to a persistently higher growth in unit labour costs than in our trading partners, which has been able to reduce the competitiveness of Spanish companies in domestic and foreign markets. On the other hand, the widespread application of safeguard clauses in collective agreements tends to prolong the inflationary impact of energy price increases and hinder the necessary adjustment to this shock. In addition, the current collective bargaining system encourages the application of homogeneous wage increases in large sectors and geographical areas, which may not be suitable for the productivity conditions of relevant groups of companies. This accumulation of factors tends to discourage the use of the labour factor and may end up affecting job creation and growth in the medium term. As I mentioned at the beginning of my speech, the low dynamism of productivity and the strong development of labour-intensive activities d0 especially construction and services d0 are characteristics that can be expected in an economy, such as Spain's, which over the last decade has experienced a large surplus of labour .in terms of a high unemployment rate. which, In addition, it has been fueled by the arrival of numerous immigrants. However, the evolution of productivity is not limited to reflecting the intensity of employment generation. Thus, if we look at the evolution of total factor productivity d0 a variable that reflects the extent to which the increase in production is not simply the result of providing more employment and capital, but of technological and efficiency improvements d0 it is observed that this variable has been slowing down in the last decade to reach very low rates. In addition, there are abundant indications that the rigidities of operation in some markets, the insufficient preparation of the workforce or the imbalance between the training required by companies and that offered by workers, as well as the scarce effort to invest in new technologies and R D i are factors that may be reducing the productivity of the economy as a whole, damaging the ability of companies to compete and even favoring the allocation of resources towards activities with lower added value. This relative lag in the implementation of technological improvements and in capitalizing the economy may not affect growth and job creation in the short term, but, since productivity is the fundamental variable that determines long-term economic growth, maintaining current trends would limit the chances of achieving greater growth potential over a longer horizon. In short, in order to ensure high and sustained growth in the long term, which allows further progress in real convergence, it is necessary to balance the current growth model, curb losses in competitiveness and promote productivity gains. This must be done by taking advantage of the opportunities offered by participation in monetary union, but also within the constraints arising from it. The macroeconomic and financial stability provided by the area is a major help to achieve sustained growth paths. At the same time, however, the lack of availability of a fundamental instrument, such as monetary policy, to deal with the specific problems of national economies forces the authorities to make more intensive and effective use of the instruments at their disposal. I have said before that the recent quarter-point increase in the European Central Bank's basic intervention rate responds to the overall needs of the euro area and is therefore appropriate for both the area and Spain. In addition, it will help to alleviate somewhat the slack of monetary conditions in which the Spanish economy has been developing, although these will continue to be considerably expansionary, so the role of the other components of economic policy continues to be very important. In the area of demand-side policies, budgetary policy is the main tool for modulating internal tensions. In the current circumstances, in which spending is growing at very high rates, fiscal policy should aim to temper the momentum of demand, maintaining a stabilizing tone. The most recent information on the evolution of the State's collection and payment figures would make it possible to anticipate, for the general government sector as a whole, a surplus higher than that forecast for 2005. Similarly, the extrapolation of these trends in the context of the budgetary scenario foreseen for 2006 in the draft Budget points to the possibility of obtaining more ambitious results for next year, so that the tone of fiscal policy is more adjusted to the requirements of the economic situation. On the other hand, a relatively restrictive stance on fiscal policy is desirable, not only cyclically, but also for structural reasons, as it represents the appropriate response to prepare public finances for the future budgetary impact of population ageing. Within the Monetary Union, competitiveness plays a key role in the adjustment of participating economies, so it is crucial to monitor public policies that encourage income moderation, productivity growth, and the establishment of mechanisms that promote flexible adaptation to adverse economic shocks or external technological or commercial challenges. This is part of the National Reform Plan, which the Government has recently approved and which contains measures to boost productivity, innovation and real convergence. The emphasis placed by this Plan on complementary action in various fields, over a relatively long horizon, is adequate to introduce the modifications of the productive structure, which are essential to sustain growth in the medium and long term. In this sense, the importance given to the improvement of physical and human capital, investment in R D i or the business environment are very relevant. The establishment of concrete objectives for the different axes around which the Plan is articulated and the regular evaluation that is announced for its follow-up can also help to make progress in these areas more palpable. It is desirable, therefore, that the proposals made materialize in a decisive government action that establishes a timetable for its implementation. And we must not forget that there are crucial aspects for the flexibility and improvement of the functioning of the Spanish economy d0 such as the labour market d0 that would require progress d0 for example, in the field of collective bargaining d0 that go beyond what is included in this Plan. In short, in the year that is now ending, the Spanish economy has continued to show a high rate of growth. However, for this expansion to consolidate in the future, it is necessary for economic policy to adequately address the imbalances that have been generated in this period of high growth, which requires both measures to moderate demand and modify its composition, and actions to strengthen supply flexibility. Only with a significant and well-targeted effort in these two aspects of economic policy can the remarkable process of economic growth that we have enjoyed in the last decade be prolonged.
text_original: 12 de diciembre de 2005 III Congreso de Economa de la Comunidad Valenciana Jaime Caruana Lacorte Gobernador del Banco de Espaa Me complace mucho participar en estas Jornadas de Economa Regional Valenciana y agradezco a sus organizadores que me hayan encargado pronunciar unas palabras al comienzo de las mismas. Ms probable resulta en mi opinin que este fenmeno se deba, sobre todo, a los desincentivos generados por los sistemas impositivos, de seguridad social y de pensiones, lo que invita a la adopcin de medidas reformadoras adicionales que permitan seguir disminuyendo la distancia que separa a Estados Unidos y la zona del euro en la intensidad de utilizacin de los recursos humanos disponibles. El crecimiento de los mrgenes empresariales, los bajos costes de financiacin, la solvente situacin financiera de las empresas tras el saneamiento del fuerte endeudamiento que acumularon algunas empresas en la segunda mitad de los aos noventa y la pujanza de la demanda estn impulsando el esfuerzo inversor. Sin embargo, una parte significativa del incremento de la demanda interior se ha seguido filtrando hacia el exterior. As, la aportacin negativa de las exportaciones netas al crecimiento del producto, que continu amplindose a lo largo de 2004, se ha mantenido en cotas prximas a los dos puntos porcentuales, aunque en ligero retroceso, a lo largo de 2005. Esta evolucin se explica tanto por el comportamiento de las exportaciones como de las importaciones. El deterioro de la aportacin del sector exterior y el creciente desequilibrio de balanza de pagos obedecen a diversas causas, en parte de carcter coyuntural, como el hecho de que la posicin cclica espaola est ms avanzada que la de las economas ms prximas, pertenecientes principalmente a la zona del euro. Tambin el encarecimiento de la energa y los mayores flujos de inversin contribuyen a incrementar el dficit exterior. Con todo, la cada de la cuota de mercado de las exportaciones espaolas desde 2004 indica que nuestras empresas tienen dificultades para competir en los mercados internacionales, en un contexto de fuerte dinamismo internacional de algunos pases emergentes -China es quiz el caso ms paradigmtico- y de evolucin comparativamente alcista de los costes internos. En este sentido, el diferencial acumulado de crecimiento de los precios de consumo respecto al resto de la zona del euro no ha dejado de ampliarse desde la introduccin de la moneda nica. Ciertamente, si se mide en trminos de los precios de exportacin, la prdida de competitividad-precio parece menos intensa. Sin embargo, es posible que los precios de exportacin que fijan las empresas espaolas sean, sobre todo, el resultado de la fuerte presin de la competencia internacional y, de este modo, solo puedan mantenerse asumiendo un recorte de los mrgenes empresariales es decir, aceptando incrementos de precios inferiores al aumento de los costes internos, que podra poner en cuestin la propia sostenibilidad de la actividad exportadora. Por todo ello, el mantenimiento de un diferencial de inflacin relativamente elevado, en trminos de precios de consumo, frente a la zona del euro es posiblemente uno de los rasgos ms preocupantes de la actual situacin de la economa espaola. Este diferencial, como he sealado, se ha situado de forma persistente en torno a un punto porcentual desde el comienzo de la tercera fase de la Unin Econmica y Monetaria, en 1999. Adems, es generalizado entre los distintos componentes del ndice armonizado de precios de consumo, si bien alcanza una magnitud particularmente elevada en el caso de los alimentos no elaborados y de los servicios. La presencia de los servicios entre las partidas ms inflacionistas de la economa espaola no es sorprendente, pues este tipo de actividades productivas se encuentra ms protegido frente a la competencia exterior que las manufacturas, y las empresas y proveedores pueden ejercer un mayor poder de mercado, sobre todo cuando la demanda de consumo es boyante. Existe una gama de servicios presente en la cesta de la compra que son escasamente comercializables, y adems algunos de estos mercados se encuentran, en general, ms regulados, de modo que, aunque el proceso de liberalizacin ha avanzado sustancialmente en las dos ltimas dcadas, el grado de competencia en algunas ramas de este sector es todava insuficiente. El diferencial de inflacin con la UEM tambin debe examinarse desde la perspectiva de la contribucin de los costes laborales y los mrgenes empresariales. En una primera aproximacin y desde un punto de vista interno, la evolucin de los costes salariales en nuestro pas podra calificarse de moderada, en el sentido de que no ha entorpecido la ampliacin de los mrgenes ni el mantenimiento de las ratios de rentabilidad de las empresas en niveles relativamente elevados, en los ltimos aos como muestra, por ejemplo, la informacin de la Central de Balances del Banco de Espaa. Sin embargo, un examen ms riguroso de la informacin revela algunos aspectos menos halageos. As, cabe sealar la evolucin particularmente expansiva que estn teniendo los mrgenes en las ramas de construccin y servicios, que se han beneficiado del fuerte crecimiento de los precios de la vivienda y de unas menores presiones competitivas, respectivamente. A su vez, los aumentos salariales, en combinacin con el escaso avance de la productividad, han determinado un crecimiento de los costes laborales unitarios persistentemente superior al de nuestros socios comerciales, que ha podido reducir la competitividad de las empresas espaolas en los mercados interiores y exteriores. Por otra parte, la aplicacin generalizada de clusulas de salvaguarda en los convenios colectivos tiende a prolongar el impacto inflacionista de los incrementos del precio de la energa y a entorpecer el necesario ajuste frente a esa perturbacin. Adems, el actual sistema de negociacin colectiva propicia la aplicacin de incrementos salariales homogneos en amplios sectores y zonas geogrficas, que pueden no ser adecuados para las condiciones de productividad de grupos relevantes de empresas. Este cmulo de factores propende a desincentivar la utilizacin del factor trabajo y puede acabar afectando a la generacin de empleo y al crecimiento a medio plazo. Como coment al principio de mi intervencin, el escaso dinamismo de la productividad y el fuerte desarrollo de actividades intensivas en la utilizacin del factor trabajo en especial, la construccin y los servicios son caractersticas que cabe esperar en una economa, como la espaola, que durante la ltima dcada ha experimentado un amplio excedente de mano de obra en trminos de una elevada tasa de paro que, adems, se ha visto alimentado por la llegada de numerosos inmigrantes. Sin embargo, la evolucin de la productividad no se limita a reflejar la intensidad en la generacin de empleo. As, si se atiende a la evolucin de la productividad total de los factores variable que refleja en qu medida el aumento de la produccin no es simplemente el resultado de aportar ms empleo y capital, sino de mejoras tecnolgicas y de eficiencia, se observa que esta variable ha ido desacelerndose en la ltima dcada hasta alcanzar tasas muy reducidas. Adems, hay abundantes indicios de que las rigideces de funcionamiento en algunos mercados, la insuficiente preparacin de la mano de obra o el desequilibrio entre la formacin requerida por las empresas y la ofrecida por los trabajadores, as como el escaso esfuerzo de inversin en nuevas tecnologas y en I+D+i son factores que pueden estar mermando la productividad del conjunto de la economa, daando la capacidad de competir de las empresas e, incluso, favoreciendo la asignacin de recursos hacia actividades con menor valor aadido. Este relativo retraso en la aplicacin de mejoras tecnolgicas y en la capitalizacin de la economa podra no afectar a corto plazo al crecimiento y a la creacin de empleo, pero, dado que la productividad es la variable fundamental que determina el crecimiento econmico a largo plazo, el mantenimiento de las tendencias actuales limitara las posibilidades de alcanzar un mayor potencial de crecimiento en un horizonte ms prolongado. En definitiva, para asegurar un crecimiento elevado y sostenido a largo plazo, que permita seguir progresando en la convergencia real, es necesario equilibrar el actual modelo de crecimiento, poner freno a las prdidas de competitividad y fomentar las ganancias de productividad. Y ello ha de hacerse aprovechando las oportunidades que ofrece la participacin en la Unin Monetaria, pero tambin dentro de las limitaciones que se derivan de la misma. La estabilidad macroeconmica y financiera que suministra el rea es una ayuda de primera magnitud para alcanzar sendas de crecimiento sostenido. Pero, a la vez, la no disponibilidad de un instrumento fundamental, como es la poltica monetaria, para afrontar los problemas especficos de las economas nacionales obliga a las autoridades a hacer un uso ms intenso y eficaz de los instrumentos a su alcance. Ya he dicho antes que la reciente subida de un cuarto de punto en el tipo bsico de intervencin del Banco Central Europeo responde a las necesidades globales de la zona del euro y es, por lo tanto, adecuado tanto para el rea como para Espaa. Adems, ayudar a aliviar algo la holgura de las condiciones monetarias en las que viene desenvolvindose la economa espaola, aunque estas seguirn siendo considerablemente expansivas, por lo que el papel de los restantes componentes de la poltica econmica contina siendo muy importante. En el mbito de las polticas de demanda, la poltica presupuestaria constituye la principal herramienta para modular las tensiones internas. En las circunstancias actuales, en las que el gasto crece a ritmos muy elevados, la poltica fiscal debe orientarse a atemperar el empuje de la demanda, manteniendo un tono estabilizador. La informacin ms reciente acerca de la evolucin de las cifras de recaudacin y pagos del Estado permitira anticipar, para el conjunto del sector de Administraciones Pblicas, un supervit ms elevado que el previsto para 2005. De igual forma, la extrapolacin de estas tendencias en el marco del escenario presupuestario previsto para 2006 en el proyecto de Presupuestos apunta a la posibilidad de obtener unos resultados ms ambiciosos para el prximo ao, de manera que el tono de la poltica fiscal se ajuste en mayor medida a los requerimientos de la situacin econmica. Por otra parte, una orientacin relativamente restrictiva de la poltica fiscal resulta conveniente, no solo desde el punto de vista cclico, sino tambin por motivos estructurales, pues representa la respuesta adecuada para preparar a las finanzas pblicas con vistas al impacto presupuestario que ejercer en el futuro el fenmeno del envejecimiento de la poblacin. Dentro de la Unin Monetaria, la competitividad desempea un papel fundamental en el ajuste de las economas participantes, por lo que resulta crucial el seguimiento de polticas publicas que fomenten la moderacin de las rentas, el avance de la productividad, y el establecimiento de mecanismos que promuevan una adaptacin flexible ante perturbaciones econmicas adversas o ante retos externos de orden tecnolgico o comercial. En este mbito se inscribe el Plan Nacional de Reformas, que el Gobierno ha aprobado recientemente y que contiene medidas para impulsar la productividad, la innovacin y la convergencia real. El nfasis que pone este Plan en la actuacin complementaria en diversos campos, a lo largo de un horizonte relativamente prolongado, resulta adecuado para introducir las modificaciones de la estructura productiva, que son imprescindibles para sostener el crecimiento a medio y largo plazo. En este sentido, la importancia concedida a la mejora del capital fsico y humano, la inversin en I+D+i o el entorno empresarial son muy pertinentes. El establecimiento de objetivos concretos para los distintos ejes entorno a los que se articula el Plan y la evaluacin regular que se anuncia para su seguimiento pueden tambin ayudar a que el progreso en esos mbitos sea ms palpable. Es deseable, por tanto, que las propuestas realizadas se concreten en una decida accin de gobierno que se establezca un calendario para su instrumentacin. Y no hay que olvidar que existen aspectos cruciales para la flexibilizacin y mejora del funcionamiento de la economa espaola como el del mercado de trabajo que exigiran avances por ejemplo, en el mbito de la negociacin colectiva que van ms all de lo recogido en este Plan. En definitiva, en el ao que ahora termina, la economa espaola ha seguido mostrando un ritmo de crecimiento elevado. Sin embargo, para que esta expansin se consolide en el futuro, es necesario que la poltica econmica atienda adecuadamente a los desequilibrios que han ido generndose en esta etapa de alto crecimiento, lo que exige tanto medidas para moderar la demanda y modificar su composicin, como actuaciones para reforzar la flexibilidad de la oferta. Solo con un esfuerzo significativo y bien orientado en estas dos vertientes de la poltica econmica podr prolongarse el notable proceso de crecimiento econmico del que hemos disfrutado en la ltima dcada.

Title: The XBRL Standard and Banking Supervision
text: Buenos Aires, 20 April 2006 The XBRL standard and banking supervision I International Congress of XBRL in Ibero-America Gonzalo Gil Deputy Governor of the Bank of Spain Introduction I would like to begin my speech with a few words of thanks to the organizers of this meeting for the kind invitation they extended to me to participate in it. It is a pleasure for me to be here today and to be able to share with all of you some reflections on the XBRL standard and its implications from the point of view of banking supervision. I am aware that the interest that the Bank of Spain has been demonstrating in a computer language from its role as prudential supervisor can be, in the first instance, somewhat shocking. Let me therefore give an initial thought on why the development and use of XBRL is in the public interest. I do not discover anything new if I tell you that the efficient functioning of financial markets depends on the prices that are formed in them reflecting all the information about the financial asset that is traded. For this to be so, that is, for a market to be efficient, it is a necessary condition that information flows with sufficient abundance and speed. However, information does not arise, let alone is transmitted, by spontaneous generation. That is, it is necessary to generate the information, find the appropriate channels so that it reaches the agents that participate in the markets and, finally, they have to incorporate it into their decision-making processes. A standard such as XBRL, which is a system designed for the exchange of information by establishing a way of sending and representing it, is called to play a central role in promoting the smooth flow of financial information. This is precisely where its public utility lies, since it will allow the generating units of the information to contact the users of the same accurately, reliably and quickly. The speed and reliability of the information will be increased because XBRL not only cares about the transmission of the data, but also with establishing its definition through a predefined protocol. This undoubtedly contributes to minimizing potential errors contained in financial information. In short, XBRL proposes a common language for financial information and, in this way, contributes to the greater efficiency of the markets. In this sense, it will mean an improvement in terms of price formation, since in this process, the agents participating in the markets will have more accurate and timely information, which will allow to reflect to a greater extent, and with more precision, the underlying economic-financial reality. Precision, reliability and speed in the transmission of information are the three aspects provided by the XBRL standard and that justify its interest from the point of view of public policies. Having said that, allow me to elaborate on these ideas throughout my speech. To this end, I will begin by presenting the main initiatives of the Committee of European Banking Supervisors (CEBS) in the field of information transmission, and their link with the XBRL language. From there, I will emphasize the advantages of adopting this standard at European level at a time, moreover, especially. I will also argue that these advantages provided by XBRL are not constrained at European level, but that other countries could also benefit from them. Finally, I will conclude my speech by sharing with you our experience in Spain, and in particular I will focus on some recent initiatives developed by the Banco de Espa96a. The Committee of European Banking Supervisors (CEBS): initiatives in the field of information generation and transmission Before analysing the main initiatives of the CEBS in the field of the generation and transmission of information, allow me to say a few words to place this body in the European framework. In 2003, the European Commission decided to adopt the Lamfalussy approach, initially developed in the field of securities, to the regulation of the banking and insurance sectors. This approach, which owes its name to the chairman of the group of experts that developed it in 2000, offers a response to the need to create in Europe a regulatory framework that would contribute to the promotion of an integrated capital market. Within this framework, the CEBS, which formally began its functions in January 2004, acts as a committee bringing together high-level representatives of the banking supervisory authorities and central banks of the European Union, including the European Central Bank. The main functions of the CEBS are grouped around three main areas. Firstly, this body provides advice, advising the European Commission on banking policy issues, and in particular on the preparation of preliminary measures regarding the implementation of European Union legislation. Secondly, it contributes to the consistent implementation of Community directives by establishing guidelines, recommendations and principles. Last but not least, CEBS's tasks also consist of promoting cooperation between the various banking supervisors in the European Union, maintaining and encouraging the exchange of information between them. Allow me to refer to this last area, and to share with you some initiatives that the CEBS has developed in the field of the generation and exchange of information. If you consider that the European Union currently consists of 25 countries, you can imagine without much effort that the initial situation involved a certain degree of complexity. That is, each of these countries requested different information from the entities. The differences, in fact, were not limited to the different definitions used by each Member State, but also affected the information systems, the technologies used or the formats used, for example. While diversity is often a value in itself, in this area I believe that the difficulties and additional costs involved, both for institutions and supervisors are obvious. Within this framework, CEBS is carrying out two main initiatives to promote the harmonization of the information requirements required of entities. On the one hand, through a project called COREP, work has been done on the development of common reports in the field of the solvency ratio, which have been published in January 2006. On the other hand, the project called FINREP adopts the same line of work in the field of financial information, and the joint reports were published in December last year. These common reports have been developed at a particularly convenient time, since both the introduction of International Financial Reporting Standards and the implementation of Basel II are forcing supervisors to modify, to some extent, the requirements and information systems that were in force to date. In the development of these projects, FINREP and COREP, the XBRL standard provides the appropriate technology. What's more, it does so at a time when it is most needed. For these reasons, CEBS has recommended, in both initiatives, to promote the use of the XBRL standard, creating two taxonomies. Benefits associated with implementing XBRL in Europe The benefits of adopting XBRL have to do with the benefits you expect from a common information system. Having a common information framework throughout the European Union will contribute not only to promoting the playing field in which institutions operate or, if you like, to promoting a greater competitive balance, but is a very important ingredient when it comes to eliminating potential obstacles to the integration of the financial market. The benefits of a common reporting framework are palpable for both the information generating entities and banking supervisors. From the point of view of institutions, there is no doubt that, mainly cross-border banks, the administrative costs they face will be reduced. For supervisors, the advantages have to do with the greater possibilities and facilities in the field of information exchange. In this respect, an important element that will contribute to increasing the cost-effectiveness of supervisory activities is the greater flexibility which, in turn, makes such a framework possible. Thus, in this context, requesting additional information or slightly modifying that which is being requested entails lower costs. Again, entities will benefit from this. This set of positive effects will ultimately have an impact on a higher quality of the information flows generated. What, in this context, is the contribution of XBRL? The answer can be summarized by saying that it is a standard that, due to its speed, flexibility and precision, characteristics to which I have already referred, contributes to the materialization of the aforementioned positive effects. First, XBRL will enable banks to meet the information needs of European Union supervisory authorities by applying a single information systems standard. Therefore, the costs associated with the implementation of common reports arising from projects initiated by CEBS in the area of information relating to the solvency of institutions, as well as their financial statements, will be reduced for cross-border banking groups. Thus, XBRL will contribute to reducing the administrative and implementation costs associated with the process. Second, smaller institutions will be able to benefit from XBRL for two reasons. On the one hand, because it is a standard in which royalties do not have to be paid, that is, it is a free standard. Secondly, to the extent that CEBS develops XBRL taxonomies, those entities will be able to take advantage of the economies of scale associated with that process. Logically, this will result in lower costs when implementing both Basel II and International Financial Reporting Standards. Third, supervisors will also derive benefits from the use of XBRL, and in particular, from the resulting economies of scale. Undoubtedly, the use of this standard will contribute to improving the cost effectiveness of supervisory activities. Fourthly, XBRL will facilitate the use and transmission of homogeneous definitions that are expressed in the European Union's joint reports. This will undoubtedly have a positive impact on the achievement of one of the benefits to which I referred earlier: financial integration. In short, supervisors will benefit from a decentralized information collection system, while benefiting from the benefits of centralized databases. Indeed, the comparability of formats, content and information systems supported by XBRL will allow supervisors to decentralise the way in which information is collected, but at the same time that they can retain all functionalities as if there were a centralised database. The improvement this brings in terms of additional flexibility therefore seems clear. Earlier I referred to the timing of XBRL implementation. We are currently in a process of changing reporting requirements, both due to the introduction of International Financial Reporting Standards and Basel II. Allow me just two words on the latter. At present, and once the Basel Committee published the text of the Agreement, the next step, at European level, was its transfer to the Community Directive, which, without going into further detail, I would like to point out that it is practically compatible with Basel II. From there, the next step is its transposition into the national legislation of each of the Member States and its development into what could be called secondary regulation. For example, the Bank of Spain is developing a new circular in this area. This is undoubtedly a challenge for the XBRL language. However, as is often the case in most cases where major challenges need to be addressed, there is also an opportunity. In this case, the opportunity is, from my point of view, unbeatable. In fact, some years before the process was not mature enough, and perhaps it was a little early not for XBRL, but even for CEBS. However, next year, in terms of the implementation of Basel II and International Financial Reporting Standards, it will be too late. In the European context, the opportunity is there, and I would venture to say that it is a question of now or never. XBRL and its role in the global economy So far I have referred to the European context, and I have tried to highlight the advantages associated with the XBRL standard. Allow me, before entering into assessing our experience in Spain, to devote some reflection to the role of XBRL in the global economy. To be more specific, is what I have told you so far relevant to Argentina and other Latin American countries? From my point of view the answer is yes, and, at least, there are three compelling reasons. Firstly, and although it may seem obvious, the unstoppable process of financial globalisation that we have been witnessing in recent decades is not a phenomenon exclusive to Europe, but is taking place on a global scale. In fact, Europe, due to its special political characteristics, could be considered as a laboratory in which to test the necessary developments in the global financial system in order to successfully reconcile, on the one hand, national sovereignties, and on the other, the efficient functioning of financial markets and the entities that operate in them. Secondly, because the two major regulatory developments driving interest in the possibilities of XBRL technology in Europe are two phenomena whose scope is global. In other words, Basel II and International Financial Reporting Standards have a universal scope and, in this sense, also affect this region. Thirdly, because the increasing demands for information from supervisors and markets mean greater complexity, both for the generators of information, that is, for institutions, and for its users. That is, even ignoring the globalization processes to which I have referred, XBRL makes sense as a mechanism for rationalizing the management of financial information. In this sense, if finally the XBRL standard were only applied in Spain for the information that banks send to the Bank of Spain, there is no doubt that even so, it would be a huge improvement for our entities and for the institution that I represent. XBRL in Spain and Bank of Spain projects in this regard Allow me to address, briefly, the last of the aspects I would like to deal with today, which is none other than to share with you the Spanish experience. Spain became an XBRL jurisdiction in 2004, creating the association XBRL Spain. I began my speech by noting and motivating the commitment that the Bank of Spain is putting into promoting the XBRL language. Proof of this, insofar as its adoption is considered to be in the public interest, is that this association is chaired, precisely, by the Bank of Spain. The main objective of the association is to promote the introduction, adoption and development, both nationally and internationally, of the XBRL language, with the purpose that I have already been exposing to you: to unify the principles applicable in financial information. Behind this objective is what could be considered the primary objective of this whole process, and from which important benefits are undoubtedly expected for those who participate in it: to facilitate the integration of both Spanish and European financial markets. Since XBRL Spain was created, we have experienced a strong growth in the number of members, totaling about 40 today. The activities of the association have been, and are, related to cooperation between the various regulatory agencies, which has been established as a main objective. Work is also underway on the development of a number of taxonomies, in addition to the determined and intensive cooperation that has been carried out with international ones (for example, in the context of the aforementioned COREP and FINREP projects). In fact, XBRL has been implemented and is now in use. For its part, the Bank of Spain has initiated a series of projects in the field of the application of the XBRL language. The first one is related to the prudential information that entities must send to the Bank of Spain and, in particular, consists of receiving the declarations of those listed in XBRL language. In its initial phase, the project is limited to the main banking groups, but the objective is that progressively the rest of the banking groups end up joining the project. The entities that participate in it, and this is an example of the cost savings involved in the adoption of XBRL, can reuse the information to inform other agencies such as, for example, the National Securities Market Commission. The second of the projects to which I would like to refer has to do with the reception of the information that in the field of solvency is required by the Community Directive implementing Basel II. This is a project that has been, since its origins, led by XBRL, and the intention is to materialize its development throughout this year to, in the next, begin to receive information already applying this standard. To influence the benefits that this new approach will bring, think that Spanish cross-border entities will be able to report the same information to other supervisors in the European Union, with the consequent cost savings that this entails. Finally, the third project to be developed by the Bank of Spain is aimed at receiving supervisory accounting information in XBRL, to the extent that a harmonised financial reporting framework is being implemented in the European Union. In this sense, and as I have already mentioned, we are actively participating in the creation of the FINREP taxonomy and the project expects to be developed throughout 2007. Conclusions In short, and as you can see, the involvement of the Bank of Spain in this area is being very relevant and this for the reasons that, throughout my speech, I have tried to convey to you. XBRL is a tool, as I have already said, that provides accuracy, reliability and speed in the transmission of financial information, characteristics that will undoubtedly contribute to promoting a more efficient functioning of financial markets. Moreover, XBRL provides very important operational advantages since, one of its great virtues, is that it only needs a small critical mass to make its implementation worthwhile. That is also why the Bank of Spain has shown its interest in this standard. That is, from the Spanish perspective, simply the success in the projects initiated by my institution with respect to the way in which the entities communicate information to us will be a great step forward. Now, it is no less true that if we think about the set of initiatives that are being developed in this area d0 in Spain, in the European Union through CEBS or elsewhere, such as the initiatives of the SEC d0 we have a tool of enormous power that, I am sure, will bring important benefits to those who decide to use it. Thank you very much for your attention.
