Una tendencia reciente en este sentido es la contratacin de proveedores externos de tecnologa (outsourcing), lo cual aporta ventajas para las entidades. Es una frmula que permite acceder al conocimiento en determinados terrenos, al tiempo que puede ser eficiente en trminos de costes y aportar flexibilidad. No obstante, estos procesos pueden llevar aparejados ciertos riesgos para las entidades, entre ellos la inconsistencia con sus planes estratgicos y una cierta prdida de control sobre los procesos externalizados. Las entidades han de asegurar que esto no sea as, al tiempo que han de aplicar medidas para limitar otro tipo de riesgos que pudieran surgir, por ejemplo los relacionados con cuestiones de seguridad, de integridad de los sistemas empleados, de confidencialidad de la informacin e, incluso, de cumplimiento de las normas y regulaciones aplicables. En este sentido, el hecho de contratar determinados servicios con terceros no exime de su responsabilidad a las entidades. Por lo tanto, las entidades deben definir con claridad los servicios a externalizar, escoger adecuadamente a la empresa que se encargar de proveerlos e implantar los controles necesarios para reducir los riesgos asociados. Por nuestra parte, los supervisores hemos de estar atentos a los potenciales riesgos que pudieran surgir y asegurar que la transferencia de estos servicios no reducir la capacidad de la entidad para cumplir con las exigencias regulatorias. * * * * * En definitiva, los procesos de transferencia de riesgos, los desarrollos demogrficos y la innovacin tecnolgica son algunos de los elementos que contribuirn a modificar el panorama del sector bancario en el medio plazo. Soy consciente de que, como ya les avanc en mi introduccin, dejo muchas cosas en el tintero, pero no querra olvidarme del creciente proceso de internacionalizacin del sector bancario, tanto a nivel global, como dentro de la Unin Europea. Desde mi punto de vista, este proceso, incentivado en buena medida tras la introduccin del euro, continuar en Europa a lo largo de los prximos aos, planteando retos adicionales para las entidades. As, la competencia, cada vez en mayor medida, est adquiriendo una dimensin ms internacional. Cul es la respuesta que han de ofrecer las entidades? El fenmeno de la internacionalizacin de nuestro sistema financiero no debe verse como un desarrollo aislado o especfico de nuestro pas. Al contrario, nuestros bancos no han hecho sino incorporarse a una tendencia global, si bien es cierto que lo han hecho con especial acierto y, por qu no reconocerlo, arrojo. No es mi intencin reflexionar sobre los aspectos positivos de la globalizacin financiera, que los tiene y son bien conocidos, sino centrarme en lo que implica para el entramado de regulacin y supervisin. En efecto, tenemos bancos globales, gestionados desde la casa matriz, con funciones centralizadas como el control de riesgos operativos o la gestin de la liquidez, y regulaciones y supervisores locales, esto es, con atribuciones y obligaciones legales que no encajan con la operativa de estos bancos globales. A una nica gestin se corresponden una multiplicidad de reguladores. No slo se plantean problemas desde el punto de vista del gestor. Tambin el supervisor debe estar convencido de que todas las actividades y riesgos estn siendo supervisados de manera adecuada y esto es as tanto para el supervisor de origen como de destino. Por ltimo, la propia naturaleza de las nuevas regulaciones, como Basilea II, facilita en parte la labor, al proporcionar una base regulatoria homognea a nivel mundial. Pero la propia naturaleza de esas normas, pensadas para ser aplicadas a nivel consolidado, dificulta su aplicacin basada en la entidad legal, esto es, al nivel de la filial individual. En los siguientes prrafos me voy a concentrar en analizar este problema en el mbito de la Unin Europea. A nivel mundial, las soluciones a este problema son, si cabe, an ms complejas, y tan slo iniciativas como las del Comit de Basilea (a travs del AIG, o Accord Implementation Group) pueden tener xito. Slo a travs del dilogo intenso entre bancos, supervisores de la matriz y supervisores de destino se pueden paliar las complejidades que introduce la gestin global del sistema financiero con su supervisin realizada a escala local. La Unin Europea tiene caractersticas nicas, no slo econmicas, sino tambin polticas e institucionales, que en este punto se centran en un reforzado inters por lograr una profundizacin y plena integracin del mercado financiero europeo, que ya est dando frutos en reas como los mercados monetarios e interbancarios, la titulizacin, amn de incentivar la realizacin de grandes operaciones transfronterizas de adquisiciones bancarias. De hecho, si se observan los cambios experimentados por el mercado financiero de la UE en los ltimos seis aos, no puede sino calificarse como revolucin: creacin de una moneda nica en parte de la UE, integracin plena de los mercados monetarios e interbancarios, profundizacin de los mercados de activos titulizados y de financiacin de grandes empresas, aparicin de nuevos grandes bancos verdaderamente paneuropeos, aparicin de organismos de cooperacin entre supervisores, creacin de estructuras polticas en el Consejo Europeo dedicadas exclusivamente a impulsar la creacin del mercado financiero nico (El Comit de Servicios Financieros), anlisis de la gestin de crisis con impacto paneuropeo (MOUs de gestin de crisis entre Ministerios, Bancos Centrales y Supervisores y ejercicios de simulacin de crisis a nivel de la UE y del eurosistema), etc. Pero la principal revolucin es, quizs, que por primera vez desde la constitucin de la UE, se ha identificado el rea financiera como una de las claves para cerrar la brecha de productividad de la UE frente a otras reas econmicas. La cuestin, pendiente en gran medida de resolucin, es qu estructuras supervisoras tiene que tener la UE para atender las crecientes exigencias de ese mercado nico, sin descuidar al mismo tiempo las necesidades de unos mercados financieros que tambin siguen siendo locales en su naturaleza (pensemos, por ejemplo, en la banca retail o al por menor). Querra despejar dos opciones que me parecen imposibles en la actual coyuntura del mercado interior. La primera a rechazar es la opcin de la inaccin: el mercado nico est cambiando y con l debe hacerlo nuestro esquema de regulacin y supervisin. La segunda, la de crear un supervisor a nivel europeo, es igualmente improbable por la imposibilidad prctica de llevarla a cabo dadas las actuales infraestructuras institucionales. Vayamos, pues, a una solucin pragmtica, diseada en funcin de las necesidades actuales, y capaz tambin de adaptarse a la evolucin de dichas necesidades y a la evolucin del mercado financiero nico. Los elementos de esa solucin pragmtica seran varios. El primero de ellos, por su importancia, es el de la certidumbre legal, para supervisores y para las entidades, de cualquier solucin que se adopte, sea esta centralizada o descentralizada. En otras palabras, en supervisin el terreno medio no representa un compromiso, sino tierra de nadie. El segundo elemento de la solucin pragmtica es que la misma debe tener en cuenta la diversidad de realidades dentro de ese mercado nico, con entidades paneuropeas presentes casi en todos los pases de la UE pero tambin con entidades de escaso tamao, y con unos pocos empleados. Para todos ellos, es imprescindible garantizar un equilibrio del terreno de juego. El tercer elemento es, quizs, de una importancia terica limitada, pero de una relevancia prctica muy importante. Dada la diversidad de la organizacin de la supervisin en la UE, con supervisores nicos en algunos pases, bancos centrales supervisores de la banca en otros y twin peaks en el resto, la solucin diseada debe respetar esa diversidad que est basada en un conjunto de factores, comerciales, institucionales, de estructura de mercados, etc. Y no por algn principio sacrosanto, sino porque si la homogeneidad institucional nacional fuera un prerrequisito de la organizacin de la supervisin del mercado nico, habra que esperar no menos de una dcada. Pero la diversidad en la supervisin nacional no slo se refleja en la organizacin, sino que tambin tiene su reflejo en cuestiones como el uso de la supervisin in situ, el papel de los auditores externos, etc. La neutralidad respecto a los modelos de organizacin y gestin de la supervisin nacional aparece, pues, como un aspecto a garantizar. El cuarto prerrequisito no es sino una versin del anterior: la necesidad de que se respeta al mximo la subsidiariedad (las soluciones deben ser nacionales en la medida de lo posible) y la proporcionalidad (instituciones sencillas no deben ser sometidas a soluciones complejas y costosas). La nueva directiva de Basilea II ya marca algunas direcciones interesantes. Se introduce el concepto de cooperacin multilateral, con la creacin del colegio de supervisores (esto es, la presencia de todos los supervisores, el de origen y los de destino), y el reconocimiento del papel lder del supervisor en base consolidada. A estos cambios, de carcter legal (y, por tanto, de obligado cumplimiento), se une el papel creciente que est jugando el Comit Europeo de Supervisores Bancario, conocido como CEBS. En efecto, este comit, en sus primeros dos aos y medio de vida, ha efectuado un importante trabajo de cooperacin supervisora que permitir una aplicacin de la Directiva de Basilea II en la UE ms homognea. Pero donde realmente tiene que proporcionar resultados es en lograr la convergencia de las prcticas supervisoras en los pases de la UE. O, en lenguaje ms llano, lograr que exista una cultura de supervisin comn donde hasta ahora ha habido 25. El proceso puede ser largo y complicado pero, al mismo tiempo, inevitable. De hecho, la transformacin profunda del modelo supervisor hasta ahora vigente ya ha comenzado. III. Conclusiones Concluir mi intervencin enfatizando las dos grandes ideas que he tratado de transmitirles el da de hoy. Primero, que durante los ltimos seis aos el sector bancario espaol se ha consolidado, en trminos de su eficiencia, rentabilidad y solvencia, en el grupo de cabeza de los pases europeos. Este logro, sin duda contribuye a la estabilidad de nuestro sistema financiero, y por lo tanto favorece el buen funcionamiento de la economa. Segundo, afianzar lo conseguido hasta ahora exige no caer en la autocomplacencia, sino que se precisa de una accin diaria encaminada a afrontar los cambios que estn por venir. Mi experiencia como Subgobernador del Banco de Espaa durante estos aos me dice que entre esta institucin y las entidades de crdito espaolas ha existido una relacin fluida y, en trminos generales, ausente de especiales tensiones. Es ms, y al margen de las posibles discrepancias de criterio que, puntualmente, puedan haber existido, creo que la relacin se ha basado en la confianza mutua y en la colaboracin estrecha. Afrontar con xito los retos de futuro exigir mantener ese espritu de colaboracin mutua, asumiendo con profesionalidad, cada uno desde el ejercicio de sus funciones, las tareas que le competen. Aprovechando la oportunidad que me brinda este foro para dirigirme a los periodistas de informacin econmica, querra recordarles que ustedes juegan tambin un papel activo y muy relevante, en la medida en la que contribuyen a la transparencia informativa. Preservar esta tarea, intensificando la profesionalidad con la que la vienen desarrollando, repercutir positivamente en el mejor funcionamiento de nuestro sistema financiero. No me cabe ninguna duda de que esto ser as en el futuro y que cada uno de nosotros asumiremos con responsabilidad nuestro cometido. Desde esa conviccin me reafirmo en la creencia de que el sistema bancario espaol abordar con xito las transformaciones que le deparar el futuro. Muchas gracias por su atencin.

Title: Speech delivered at the public ceremony held on the occasion of the inauguration as the new Governor of the Bank of Spain
text: Madrid, 18 July 2006 Inauguration Speech Miguel Fern87ndez Ord9796ez Governor of the Bank of Spain Dear Vice President, authorities, friends. First of all, thank you. Thank you, for your presence at this event, to all the authorities and to all of you who have wanted to join us today in the presentation of the new Governing Council of the BDE. My thanks to the President of the Government for his decision, which has allowed me to accede to this responsibility. Thank you to the Vice-President because he was the one who proposed my name to him and thank you to the spokesmen of the political groups in the House who welcomed the proposal. Thanks also to those who did not, Miguel Arias Ca96ete, because, despite his discrepancies, he has always publicly recognized my technical competence and sufficient experience to exercise these functions. Thank you to the members of the Governing Council, my colleagues during this year. Special thanks to Angel Luis L97pez Roa, with whom I have also shared during this period the tasks of the Executive Committee and with whom I have exchanged many ideas in order to improve the governance of the Bank that I will develop in the coming months. As of today, he will be accompanied on the Executive Committee by Vicente Salas, probably the most prestigious professor of business economics in the country, whom I also thank for having agreed to replace me in that position. Thanks to Jaime Caruana and Gonzalo Gil, outgoing governor and deputy governor, whose work, and I share this judgment with the Vice President, has been excellent. If with words you can not say more, yes you can with the facts because today I have shown my appreciation for their work by having confirmed their general directors: Malo de Molina, Ar92ztegui, Rold87n, and the Secretary General, Alepuz. In addition, the Council of Ministers was kind enough to accept my proposal that one of those directors, Jos8e Vi96als, be the Deputy Governor. Thanks to all of them for accepting in this new stage to continue being part of the management team of the house. Of all the Directors appointed or confirmed by my predecessors, the only one who will not continue with us, having been appointed Secretary General of the AEB yesterday, is Pedro Pablo Villasante, who, together with its President, Miguel Mart92n, are a guarantee of understanding and efficiency in the implementation of the entire regulatory paradigm shift that is Basel-II. I want to leave here testimony of my respect for Villasante's decision, which I know has not been easy for him to take, my recognition of the work done by a great professional and my personal thanks because, given the importance I attach to supervision, it is the Director that I have stolen more hours of conversation and meetings during the last months. Thank you to the heads of department and division who are with us today as representatives of all those who work at the Bank, because they are the foundations of this house and because in a continuous dialogue throughout this period they have helped me a lot to understand the strengths of the institution and the challenges we are going to face. Finally, I would like to welcome the first woman in the history of the BDE to join the Governing Council as an unborn member. Just this morning, the Executive Committee also decided to appoint a woman who will be the first to reach the post of Director-General of the Bank and another woman who will also be the first to enter a Deputy Directorate-General. The Bank thus begins to take some first steps in overcoming this prejudice of male superiority so deeply rooted in Spain, which leads to the selection of less prepared men for managerial positions preventing the promotion of the most competent women which, apart from injustice, has harmful economic effects by hindering the increase in productivity of companies and institutions in our country. In recent months, the importance of this institution being independent has been stressed, and I think it is necessary to say today what I think of it. Well, very simple, bluntly, clearly, I believe that nothing is more necessary, nothing is more inexcusable, that the BDE acts autonomously if it wants to adequately fulfill its purposes. Autonomy was already prescribed in the 1980 law and was secured in 1994 when, among many other reforms, the legislator took away from the Executive the possibility of changing the Bank's governing bodies at its discretion. Our entry into the Eurosystem has further strengthened this autonomy by prescribing that national governments cannot replace the Governor who will be part of the ECB's Governing Council, who is the one who decides monetary policy, not only for Spaniards, but for the more than 300 million Europeans who have the euro as their currency. However, this emphasis that has legitimately been placed these months on the autonomy of the Bank should not lead us to the point of forgetting that autonomy is a fundamental characteristic, but it has an instrumental character. The word north that should guide our actions is that of service, since the EDB is a public service, - certainly different in its form of exercise from that of the central administration - but public service in any case. To give just a few examples, the EDB must defend the interests of depositors and, therefore, in its regulation and supervision it must think first of all, but it must also do so without harming the activity of banks and other private institutions because the more efficient, profitable and solvent our entities are, the more protected users will be. And the BDE must be understood with the Autonomous Communities in the exercise of those competences that they have in our system and the BDE must continue to offer its advice to the Government, to Parliament and to inform public opinion, because the public interest is nothing but the sum of the interests of all those people and institutions. The BDE must act autonomously but it cannot forget that it is at the service of Spain, of this Spain that combines many interests and visions, of this rich and complex Spain that we must serve. Another inexcusable station in the words of an inauguration is the reference to the main challenges of the new stage, but since I aim not to tire you, I will use the wise technology of the catechism, that of summarizing them in two. Our first challenge is to further increase the Bank's international prestige in these areas of analysis, support for the member of the Governing Council of the ECB and in the operations of the federated central bank of the European System of Central Banks. The second major challenge is to adapt financial supervision/regulation to the new global scenario, to the unstoppable globalization of entities and of supervisory activity itself. Let me use a bullfighter simile. In recent years, the work of supervisors and central banks has focused on the design of the rules and principles that must govern the new regulation. The BDE has played an important role in this process with its participation in all international design forums. Although this task is not over, the essential thing is done: we have designed the size of the crutch, its color, the suit of lights, etc. The weight and brave of the bull has also been outlined. But now we have to fight it. In 2008 the new system will have to operate in Spain. And this challenge is not only for the EDB, because, given that the new regulation has a very important self-regulation component, it is the private entities themselves that are obliged to radically transform their risk control. We will have to do it together as we would all fail if any fail. In the face of these challenges, it is essential that the Bank succeeds in its response to globalization. And in my decision to elect a Deputy Governor has undoubtedly weighed the special sensitivity of Jos8e Vi96als to the phenomenon of internationalization. Today's world is transforming at a rapid pace and is rapidly making the rules, decisions, criteria and actions of regulators obsolete. But, together with an attentive flexibility in the face of changes in the global economy, it is essential to have permanent references that prevent us from getting lost in a meaningless tacticism, it is necessary to be clear about the principles that should guide us while we adapt to changes. And although the world is changing, the principles have not changed, so it is advisable to learn from those who preceded us. Here we are accompanied, and I appreciate it, ex-governors, ex-general directors, ex-counselors, and we must all learn something, but let me evoke Luis Angel Rojo today because he is someone who has been everything in this house and not just governor, and therefore he is a reference that can be worth us, not only to those who are going to be in the governing bodies. but to all the others, bringing together the three characteristics that, in my opinion, should serve as a guide for action: competence, integrity and institutional sense. First of all, professional competence, passion for excellence. There are many who have worried about this in the Bank but no one can forget Rojo's level of demand on those around him and his concern that the EDB not only applied existing economic knowledge but that the Bank was also a generator of that knowledge. That demand, six years after he left the Bank, remains and it is our obligation to preserve it. But, in public service, competition is of little value if it is not accompanied by integrity. Those who put their self-interests above public interests can be even more dangerous to the community when they are most capable. Finally, there is a third characteristic that I think is essential to maintain as a guide for our action, and that is the institutional sense. In an autonomous institution such as the BDE it is crucial that those who work in it, in addition to the passion for excellence and integrity, are loyal to the institution. We must be vigilant so that the main defects that threaten all autonomous entities do not arise in the Bank: corporatism, unnecessary opacity or the pure defense of comfortable bureaucratic positions, but, at the same time, we must never be ashamed of developing a solid institutional sense because it is essential to ensure that the EDB, as I said, be always at the service of Spain. Thanks again to all.
text_original: Madrid, 18 de julio de 2006 Discurso de Toma de Posesin Miguel Fernndez Ordez Gobernador del Banco de Espaa Querido Vicepresidente, autoridades, amigos. En primer lugar, gracias. Adems el Consejo de Ministros tuvo a bien aceptar mi propuesta de que uno de esos directores, Jos Vials, fuera el Subgobernador. Gracias a todos ellos por aceptar en esta nueva etapa seguir formando parte del equipo directivo de la casa. De todos los Directores nombrados o confirmados por mis antecesores, el nico que no seguir con nosotros, al haber sido nombrado ayer Secretario General de la AEB, es Pedro Pablo Villasante, quien, junto a su Presidente, Miguel Martn, son una garanta de entendimiento y de eficacia en la puesta en marcha de todo el cambio de paradigma regulador que es Basilea-II. Quiero dejar aqu testimonio de mi respeto a la decisin de Villasante, que s que no le ha sido fcil tomar, mi reconocimiento al trabajo hecho por un gran profesional y mi agradecimiento personal pues, dada la importancia que concedo a la supervisin, es al Director al que he robado ms horas de conversacin y reuniones durante los ltimos meses. Gracias a los jefes de departamento y de divisin que hoy nos acompaan como representantes de todos los que trabajan en el Banco, porque ellos son los cimientos de esta casa y porque en un dilogo continuado a lo largo de este perodo me han ayudado mucho a entender los puntos fuertes de la institucin y los retos que vamos afrontar. Finalmente quiero dar la bienvenida a la primera mujer en la historia del BDE que entra en el Consejo de Gobierno como vocal no nato. Esta misma maana la Comisin ejecutiva ha decidido nombrar tambin a una mujer que ser la primera que accede a un puesto de Director General del Banco y a otra mujer que ser tambin la primera en acceder a una Direccin General Adjunta. El Banco empieza as a dar unos primeros pasos en la superacin de ese prejuicio de superioridad masculina tan arraigado en Espaa, que lleva a seleccionar a hombres menos preparados para puestos directivos impidiendo la promocin de las mujeres ms competentes lo cual, al margen de la injusticia, tiene efectos econmicos perjudiciales al obstaculizar el aumento de productividad de las empresas e instituciones de nuestro pas. En los ltimos meses se ha subrayado la importancia de que esta institucin sea independiente, y creo que es obligado decir en este da lo que pienso de ello. Pues muy simple, sin rodeos, claramente, creo que nada es ms necesario, nada es ms inexcusable, que el BDE acte con autonoma si quiere cumplir adecuadamente sus fines. La autonoma estaba ya prescrita en la ley de 1980 y, qued asegurada en 1994 cuando, entre otras muchas reformas, el legislador le quit al Ejecutivo la posibilidad de cambiar a su discrecin los rganos de gobierno del Banco. Nuestro ingreso en el Eurosistema ha reforzado an ms esta autonoma pues prescribe que los gobiernos nacionales no puedan sustituir al Gobernador que va a formar parte del consejo de Gobierno del BCE, que es quien decide la poltica monetaria, no solo para los espaoles, sino para los ms de 300 millones de europeos que tienen como moneda el euro. No obstante, este nfasis que legtimamente se ha puesto estos meses en la autonoma del Banco no debera llevarnos al punto de olvidar que la autonoma es una caracterstica fundamental, pero tiene carcter instrumental. La palabra-norte que debe orientar nuestras actuaciones es la de servicio, ya que el BDE es un servicio pblico, - ciertamente distinto en su forma de ejercicio al de la Administracin central - , pero servicio pblico en cualquier caso. Por dar solo unos ejemplos, el BDE debe defender los intereses de los depositantes y, por tanto, en su regulacin y supervisin debe pensar en primer lugar en ellos, pero tambin debe hacerlo sin perjudicar la actividad de bancos y otras instituciones privadas pues cuanto ms eficientes, rentables y solventes sean nuestras entidades, ms protegidos estarn los usuarios. Y el BDE ha de entenderse con las CCAA en el ejercicio de aquellas competencias que tienen en nuestro sistema y el BDE debe seguir ofreciendo su asesoramiento al Gobierno, al Parlamento e informando a la opinin pblica, porque el inters pblico no es sino la suma de los intereses de todas esas personas e instituciones. El BDE debe actuar con autonoma pero no puede olvidar que est al servicio de Espaa, de esta Espaa que ana muchos intereses y visiones, de esta Espaa rica y compleja a la que debemos servir. Otra inexcusable estacin en las palabras de una toma de posesin es la referencia a los principales retos de la nueva etapa, pero como tengo por objetivo no cansarles, voy a utilizar la sabia tecnologa del catecismo, la de resumirlos en dos. Nuestro primer reto es el de aumentar an ms el prestigio internacional del Banco en esas reas de anlisis, de apoyo al miembro del consejo de Gobierno del BCE y en las operativas de banco central federado del Sistema Europeo de Bancos Centrales. El segundo gran reto es el de adecuar la supervisin/regulacin financiera al nuevo escenario mundial, a la imparable globalizacin de las entidades y de la propia actividad supervisora. Permtanme utilizar un smil torero. Estos aos el trabajo de los supervisores y bancos centrales se ha concentrado en el diseo de las normas y principios que han de presidir la nueva regulacin. El BDE ha jugado un papel importante en este proceso con su participacin en todos los foros internacionales de diseo. Aunque esta tarea no ha acabado, lo esencial est hecho: hemos diseado el tamao de la muleta, su color, el traje de luces, etc. Tambin se ha perfilado el peso y brava del toro. Pero ahora hay que torearlo. En el 2008 tendr que funcionar el nuevo sistema en Espaa. Y este reto no es solo para el BDE, porque, dado que la nueva regulacin tiene un componente de autorregulacin muy importante, son las propias entidades privadas las que estn obligadas a transformar radicalmente su control de riesgos. Tendremos que hacerlo juntos ya que fallaramos todos si falla alguno. Ante estos retos es capital que el Banco acierte en su respuesta a la globalizacin. Y en mi decisin de elegir un Subgobernador ha pesado sin duda la especial sensibilidad de Jos Vials al fenmeno de la internacionalizacin. El mundo actual est transformndose a una velocidad trepidante y est volviendo obsoletas rpidamente las normas, decisiones, criterios y actuaciones de los reguladores. Pero, junto a una atenta flexibilidad ante los cambios en la economa global, es fundamental contar con unas referencias permanentes que nos eviten perdernos en un tacticismo sin sentido, es necesario tener claros los principios que nos deben guiar mientras nos adaptamos a los cambios. Y aunque el mundo est cambiando, no han cambiado los principios, por lo que es recomendable aprender de los que nos precedieron. Aqu nos acompaan, y yo lo aprecio, ex-gobernadores, exdirectores generales, exconsejeros, y de todos debemos aprender algo, pero djenme evocar hoy a Luis Angel Rojo porque es alguien que ha sido todo en esta casa y no solo gobernador, y por tanto es una referencia que nos puede valer, no slo a los que vamos a estar en los rganos de gobierno, sino a todos los dems, reuniendo las tres caractersticas que, en mi opinin, deben servirnos de gua de actuacin: competencia, integridad y sentido institucional. En primer lugar la competencia profesional, la pasin por la excelencia. Son muchos los que se han preocupado de ello en el Banco pero nadie puede olvidar el nivel de exigencia de Rojo sobre los que le rodeaban y su preocupacin de que el BDE no solo aplicara el conocimiento econmico existente sino que el Banco fuera tambin un generador de ese conocimiento. Esa exigencia, seis aos despus de que dejara el Banco, se mantiene y es nuestra obligacin preservarla. Pero, en el servicio pblico, de poco vale la competencia si no va acompaada de la integridad. Quienes ponen sus intereses propios por encima de los intereses pblicos pueden ser an ms peligrosos para la comunidad cuando son ms capaces. Finalmente, hay una tercera caracterstica que me parece fundamental mantener como gua de nuestra actuacin y es el sentido institucional. En una institucin autnoma como el BDE es trascendental que los que trabajen en ella, adems de la pasin por la excelencia y de la integridad, sean leales a la institucin. Debemos estar alerta para que no surjan en el Banco los principales defectos que acechan a todos los entes autnomos: el corporativismo, la innecesaria opacidad o la pura defensa de posiciones burocrticas cmodas, pero, a la vez, no debemos avergonzarnos nunca de desarrollar un slido sentido institucional porque es esencial para conseguir que el BDE, como he dicho, est siempre al servicio de Espaa. Gracias otra vez a todos.

Title: Appearance before the Congressional Budget Committee
text: Madrid,10 October 2006 Appearance before the Congressional Budget Committee Miguel Fern87ndez Ord9796ez Governor of the Bank of Spain ladies and gentlemen, This appearance, which is part of the parliamentary discussion of the General Budget of 2007, is my first appearance as Governor of the Bank of Spain before the Congress of Deputies. Allow me, as the first, to refer to the specific content of the report on the importance I attach to relations with Parliament. The Banco de Espa96a is assigned functions related to macroeconomic and financial stability of great scope for the development of the economy, economic growth and the well-being of citizens. To be able to carry out these functions, it has a framework of great institutional independence, in the terms established by the Law of Autonomy and the Treaties of the European Union, which constitutes its main hallmark. The responsibility involved in the exercise of such independence requires an adequate explanation of the lines of action followed in relation to the objectives entrusted and transparency mechanisms that facilitate monitoring by society, economic agents and financial markets. From this perspective, the appearances of the Governor before the representative body of popular sovereignty are of great importance and play a privileged role in communicating the analysis of the economy on which the actions of the Bank of Spain are based. I am convinced that these appearances will be very fruitful for the fulfillment of the mission entrusted to us by the Laws. I appear at a time when the latest data reveal the consolidation of the European recovery, within the expansive climate of the world economy, and which, in our case, have led to an upward revision of the growth rate of the Spanish economy. The latest data published by the Spanish National Accounts have exceeded the forecasts of the various bodies and provide a table confirming the prolongation, with renewed dynamism, of its long phase of expansion. In addition to the continuation of the expansionary factors that have accompanied the establishment of a regime of macroeconomic stability, there has been the intensification of the demographic impulse resulting from immigration and the growing participation of women and, more recently, the recovery of the euro area. In relation to this last factor, I think it is important to highlight that this recovery and the gradual withdrawal of the expansionary tone of the single monetary policy, which logically accompanies it, are taking place at a particularly opportune moment for the Spanish economy. The combination of the two movements tends to sustain growth by boosting external demand, while adjusting monetary conditions helps contain domestic demand and helps balance the composition of growth. We are, therefore, faced with conditions that, in principle, allow us to project the current scenario of economic dynamism towards the horizon of the coming years, although it is a scenario that is not exempt from risks, both external and internal, especially in terms of its sustainability in the long term. These risks require early and effective economic policy action to prevent their potential realisation. In order to deepen this analysis, I will refer first to the situation of the euro area, in the current international context, and to the single monetary policy, which is our monetary policy, and then to the analysis of the situation of the Spanish economy in which the general budgets for next year are inserted. ***** Throughout this year, the international economic outlook is characterized by the maintenance of the remarkable strength that world activity and trade have been exhibiting in recent years, and which is being common to most of the main geographical areas. This dynamism has continued despite prices of a barrel of oil and non-energy raw materials that remain high, although they have eased significantly from the highs reached during the summer. The outlook for a medium-term horizon points to the continuation of the expansionary phase of the world economy, albeit at somewhat more moderate rates. These forecasts are surrounded by uncertainties due to the persistence of macro-financial imbalances, the uncertain trajectory of oil prices d0 despite the recent moderation d0 in a somewhat unstable geopolitical framework, and the possibility that the slowdown in the US economy will be more significant than currently anticipated. Therefore, although the most plausible scenario is encouraging, there are some downside risks. In this global context, we have witnessed in the course of the current year the long-awaited consolidation of the recovery of the euro area economy. After the sluggishness observed in recent years, activity has gained increasing strength, so that output has accelerated to an increase of around 2.5% at the end of the first half of the year. It should be noted that, following the initial boost in the foreign sector, the strengthening of domestic demand has begun to take over, supported mainly by the dynamism of investment, which has been encouraged by favourable financial conditions and, in addition, by the recovery of corporate profits and the clean-up of their balance sheets. For its part, private consumption has also experienced a certain improvement, still hesitant, which will have to be consolidated to the extent that the recovery in employment is confirmed. In the medium term, the phase of economic strength is likely to continue over the coming quarters, so that GDP will maintain growth rates in the vicinity of potential output. Logically, this favourable outlook broadly shares the same risks that are written for the international environment. As regards inflation, the HICP growth rate had remained persistently above 2% until August, which, let me remind you, is the numerical benchmark used in the definition of the Eurosystem's price stability objective, although it has eased to 1.8% in September following the recent correction in energy commodity prices, since the indices referring to baskets of products that exclude these goods had, in general, a more favorable behavior. The absence, for the time being, of underlying inflationary tensions can also be seen in the moderate evolution of labour costs and indicators of inflationary expectations. However, there are upside risks to inflation over the short and medium term, as the more dynamic economic backdrop could favour the gradual materialisation of the spillover effects on the non-energy components of the HICP of past oil prices and rising wage demands. The monetary policy implemented in recent years has effectively contributed to the improvement in the economic situation and outlook for the euro area as a whole that I have just described. In particular, despite the recurrence of upward shocks in the headline price level, the ECB has managed to keep inflation expectations at levels consistent with its priority objective, reflecting the high credibility it enjoys. This has favoured the containment of company costs, the strengthening of the confidence of agents and, as a result, the moderation of the adverse effects of the rise in crude oil prices. All these developments prove the benefits associated with the independence of the central bank and the clarity of its strategic objectives. The economic policies of the euro area also face three very important challenges, such as population ageing, globalisation and technological change. Firstly, the expected budgetary impact of the coming changes in the demographic structure of the population attaches great importance to measures aimed at counteracting these effects and to the implementation of the institutional framework in place following the reform of the Stability and Growth Pact. In this respect, it is particularly important for countries in excessive deficits to take advantage of improved economic developments to reduce their imbalances in a lasting way. Secondly, technological changes and those introduced by the incorporation of new geographical areas into the global economic scenario require the implementation of structural reforms that favour competitiveness. These are essential if the transformation of the current phase of recovery of activity into a sustainable expansion is to be achieved. The unsatisfactory evolution of euro area GDP since the beginning of the current decade reflects both a slowdown in labour productivity and, despite more recent progress, the still insufficient degree of utilization of this productive factor. In order to reverse this trend, some aspects of the regulation of product and labour markets need to be reviewed in order to facilitate the reallocation of resources in the manner required by the twin phenomena of globalisation and technological change. Europe has decided to move forward in this area through the reforms and deadlines contained in the Lisbon Agenda. This is an excellent programme whose implementation requires, however, the determination of national economic decision-makers and the support of a broad political and social consensus. The sustained improvement of the well-being of European citizens requires, in any case, the participation of all areas of public policies. That is why it seems to me essential to ensure that the existing institutional relations framework between the central bank and the national and Community economic authorities should function smoothly. This operation is based on the monthly presence of the President and Vice-President of the ECB at Eurogroup meetings, and of the President of the Eurogroup and the European Commissioner for Economic Affairs at meetings of the Governing Council of the ECB. Experience shows that interaction is very fruitful when it proceeds in accordance with the established distribution of responsibilities and, in particular, with the necessary respect for the independence of the monetary authority, which constitutes the basic basis of sucredibility. As I pointed out, it is precisely the credibility acquired that has allowed the central bank to adjust monetary conditions in the recent past to the weakness of the economy without threatening the fulfillment of its priority objective. Similarly, if current expectations of growth in economic activity are confirmed, monetary policy should continue to gradually remove the accommodative nature it still maintains. The process of normalising monetary conditions can therefore be seen as the logical outcome of the phase of economic dynamism in which we find ourselves and of the need to ensure its compatibility with the maintenance of price stability. ***** From the point of view of the Spanish economy, the improvement experienced by the euro area and the gradual normalisation of monetary conditions, to which I have just referred, form a propitious scenario for the prolongation of the dynamism of activity and employment. In the first half of 2006 the Spanish economy continued to show great strength, with a profile of a gentle acceleration in activity in the second quarter of the year, which placed GDP at a year-on-year growth rate of 3.7%. In fact, the latest figures available from the Quarterly National Accounts are some tenth higher than the growth previously forecast for the first two quarters of the year, although this mainly reflects, both in its intensity and composition, the revisions in the rate of GDP growth in 2004 and 2005, for which there is a somewhat less negative contribution from the external sector than initially estimated. The continuation of the expansion in 2006 has continued to be based on the strength of domestic demand, which has begun a certain slowdown that has been offset by the gradual improvement in the contribution of the foreign sector to growth. These data suggest the beginning of an incipient rebalancing process in the composition of growth, to which the still moderate effect of the adjustment of monetary and financial conditions on expenditure is reportedly contributing on the one hand and, on the other, the economic recovery in the euro area. Of the different components of domestic demand, only private and public consumption have shown signs of a slight slowdown in the elapsed part of the year; while investment in construction has remained remarkably strong and investment in equipment has intensified its pace of increase in the second quarter, following the slight inflection of mid-2005. The slowdown in private consumption has been the result of factors that have acted in a counter-manner. Among those that have been able to curb household consumption can be mentioned the erosion of purchasing power that has occurred in the face of high inflation rates recorded in the first half of the year, as well as the effect of the rise in interest rates, which could be inducing a certain correction of the trend of recent years to decline in the household savings rate. On the contrary, the dynamism that maintains job creation d0 with rates around 3% d0 and the persistence of a wealth effect that could still be powerful would have continued to sustain the dynamism of household consumption. In this regard, it should be remembered that although the revaluation of real estate wealth is beginning to show some signs of slowdown, in recent months there have been significant stock market increases that could have counteracted this effect. As regards the various components of gross capital formation, investment in construction has maintained, as I mentioned a moment ago, considerable stability, with growth rates above 5%, in a context in which demand for housing has continued to show great strength and the segments of non-residential building and civil works have continued to show signs of intense activity. It is also worth mentioning the upturn in investment in equipment, which remains the most dynamic component of demand, reflecting greater export activity and the improvement of the industrial sector in an environment of business profitability and financial conditions very favorable to the expansion of productive capacity. But perhaps the most remarkable aspect of the current economic situation is the relief that is beginning to occur in the pressure of net external demand, whose negative contribution to output growth has fallen in recent quarters to around one percentage point. The recovery in exports of goods, driven by strong growth in world trade and the take-off in economic activity in the euro countries, almost entirely explains the easing of the negative contribution of net external demand. Imports, meanwhile, have maintained a strong dynamism, reflecting the growth in final demand. In this context, export quotas appear to have stabilised, following last year's decline, although import penetration has continued to increase. It is not easy to diagnose the extent of this improvement in the external sector, but the absence of significant changes in the trajectory of competitiveness-price indicators, which, in general terms, have continued to deteriorate so far this year, could slow down and even interrupt the improvement in the external sector. The Spanish economy has continued to show in the elapsed part of this year an intense capacity to generate employment, so that the labour market has continued to absorb a very dynamic labor supply, while the unemployment rate fell to levels not known since the seventies, with records of 8.5% in the second quarter. The most recent labour market situation indicators confirm the continuation of this trend. Labour costs picked up slightly in the first part of 2006, with increases of around 3%, which, in any case, are lower than those negotiated in the agreement when the effect of safeguard clauses is taken into account. This discrepancy may be due to the effect on aggregate wage growth of lower wages from the important inflows into the labour market, in which immigration plays an important role. Despite the small upward revision in the rate of productivity growth implied by the latest figures from the National Accounts, labour costs per unit of product have continued to widen their differential with EMU, although in the manufacturing sector, where productivity gains are being significant, it can be seen, For the first time, a stabilization. On the price front, the inflation rate has followed an upward trajectory in the first part of the year, driven by the evolution of labour costs and the widening of margins, but, above all, by the rise in oil prices, to which I have already referred. In this context, the rate of year-on-year increase in the CPI remained at levels close to 4% until July, although in August it eased to 3.7% and the advance of the harmonised index for September points to an additional cut to 3.0%, mainly due to the sharp decline in energy prices in the last two months. It cannot be ignored, however, that core inflation has remained persistently at around 3% rates, above the levels of the last two years, and that the consumer price differential with EMU has remained high. Despite the improvement in export performance and the slowdown in expenditure, the external deficit has continued to increase both in nominal terms and as a percentage of GDP during the first half of 2006, albeit at rates lower than those observed in the last two years. Here, too, higher oil prices have played an important role in this deterioration. The economic information available for the third quarter of 2006, which is still partial and fragmentary, points to the continued strength of economic activity, suggesting that GDP growth on average in 2006 could be slightly higher than in 2005. For its part, the outlook for 2007 points to a slight slowdown in output growth and to the continuation of the patterns observed in recent quarters. Domestic demand is expected to continue the trend of a gentle slowdown and further improvements in the contribution of net foreign demand. This profile would be in line with the macroeconomic scenario on which the General State Budget for 2007 has been prepared, although it would be based on somewhat higher growth rates in 2006. With regard to inflation, the outlook for the remainder of the year points to a slowdown in the annual rate of the CPI, which would be largely explained by the decline in the contribution of energy prices to the headline index, although average growth will eventually be higher than in 2005. Finally, I have outlined a picture of sustained growth and the beginning of a gradual correction of imbalances throughout 2006 and in the first quarters of 2007, which is not, however, without medium-term risks. At international level, I have already mentioned those relating to the prospects for the world economy and the uncertainty that still surrounds the intensity of the European recovery. In the domestic sphere, I would like to point out in particular those that emanate from the maintenance of the inflation differential and the high indebtedness of households. The continuation of price increases higher than those in the euro area is worrying in the event that the indexation mechanisms incorporated in the negotiation collectively prolong the inertia of price increases with the consequent negative impact on competitiveness. In turn, the stabilization of core inflation at relatively high rates suggests that some effects of higher oil prices may be being passed on more permanently to other prices. All this could adversely affect the improvement in exports. In this context, the containment of inflation and its approximation to rates compatible with the concept of price stability is necessary to continue the rebalancing between domestic and external demand and to ensure the continuity of economic dynamism over the medium term. With regard to the considerations relating to the risks arising from the increase in private sector indebtedness d0 especially of households d0 and the sharp growth in residential investment, I would like to begin by recalling that these phenomena are consistent with the recent transformations in our economy and, most notably, with the low level of interest rates. However, the financial position of agents and, therefore, their propensity to spend, has become more sensitive to the evolution of their income, interest rates and house prices. A sensitivity that becomes more relevant when interest rates are in a phase of rising house prices tend to slow down. However, the equity position of firms and households is sound and provides a solid basis for their adaptation to interest rate levels corresponding to the greater economic dynamism of the euro area. It cannot be ruled out, however, that a part of indebted households with lower income levels and real estate service companies may be vulnerable. In any case, the environment of price stability, which limits the foreseeable path of interest rates, and the forecast of a gradual slowdown in house prices d0 to which the latest official data published point d0 contribute to alleviating the elements of risk indicated. In addition, the solvency of the financial system and the sound state of public finances, to which I shall refer later, constitute an important safety valve for maintaining the overall stability of the economy. Finally, the Spanish economy shows relatively healthy growth prospects in the coming quarters, whose continuity in the medium term requires further progress in containing domestic demand and expanding the response capacity of aggregate supply. In this context, economic policies should contribute to achieving these objectives. I have already referred to the single monetary policy stance and have mentioned the fact that the gradual withdrawal of its expansionary tone is taking place at a particular time. timely for the Spanish economy; for the adjustment of monetary conditions helps contain domestic demand and helps to balance the expansion. With regard to fiscal policy, the latest forecasts for the balance of public accounts in 2006 point to a surplus of 1.1%, two tenths higher than that set in the last update of the Stability Programme, of 0.9% of GDP. A closure of the public accounts in this environment would be sufficient to comfortably meet the fiscal requirements set out in the European commitments under the Stability and Growth Pact and to prolong the downward trajectory of public debt, whose ratio as a proportion to GDP could be below 40% by the end of the year. This improvement in the fiscal position reflects the fact that the Spanish economy has been growing more than expected as well as that tax collection in the main tax figures has comfortably exceeded the estimates made in the budget programming exercise. The General State Budget Project for 2007 establishes a surplus target for all Public Administrations of 0.7% of GDP in a macroeconomic scenario that, as I have already mentioned, represents a slight slowdown in GDP. The continuation of the economic boom scenario and the foreseeable prolongation of the revenue dynamism should make it possible to exceed this objective despite the confluence in 2007 of a series of factors that will tend to reduce revenue, such as the entry into force of the reform of personal income tax and corporate tax, the new EU Financial Perspectives or certain elements of the labour reform that came into force last July. The achievement of a surplus higher than programmed, in line with what has happened in recent years, would be more in line with the role that corresponds to fiscal policy in the current situation of the Spanish economy. This is an orientation that should not be relaxed. The good results obtained by the Spanish economy in recent years are a clear example of how fruitful budgetary stability strategies can be and their full compatibility with the maintenance of prolonged phases of economic growth. The priorities of the spending policies incorporated in the Budgets are oriented towards areas of great importance for improving productivity, such as increasing resources for education and innovation or increasing investment in infrastructure. It is important, therefore, to ensure the efficiency of the actions undertaken in such a way as to ensure that the increase in resources is reflected in effective improvements in capitalization and productivity in the medium term. To continue advancing in improving the structural fiscal position, it is essential to increase efficiency in the management of expenditure by the different levels of government of the Public Administrations. In In this sense, it should be remembered that the State executes only 20% of the public expenditure of the Public Administrations and that according to the latest estimates it will show in 2006, for the second consecutive year, a surplus fiscal position, which will be extended in 2007 according to the forecasts of the General State Budget Project for that year. It is therefore important to seek the support of the Autonomous Communities, whose overall budget balance continues to be in deficit d0 and will continue to be so in 2007 d0 not only to continue making progress in improving the fiscal position of the Public Administrations but also to achieve a more efficient management of expenditure, for which they are responsible for just over 35% of the total. These efforts will help to create a better basis for meeting the challenges of ageing and the commitment made to address protection needs in situations of dependency. On the supply policy side, the effort must focus on achieving more flexible factor and product markets that help the Spanish economy adapt to an increasingly competitive environment and make efficient use of available productive resources. This requires maintaining the current capacity for job creation while generating productivity gains. The National Reform Plan articulates a set of actions oriented in this direction that must be applied with determination and ambition. However, there are some areas of the economy, such as the labour market, which should be further reformed. The picture that emerges from the recent information I have just commented on is that of an economy that maintains renewed dynamism and has a tendency to rebalance the factors supporting growth. However, the elements of risk for its long-term sustainability, on which the Bank of Spain has been warning, remain in force, so it is still pertinent to remain cautious and deepen the agenda of pending reforms. In this way, the Spanish economy could take advantage of the opportunities offered by the prolongation of the long phase of expansion that it is experiencing and could continue to make progress in the medium and long term in convergence with the welfare levels of the most advanced economies.
text_original: Madrid,10deoctubre de2006 Comparecencia ante la Comisin de Presupuestos del Congreso Miguel Fernndez Ordez GobernadordelBancode Espaa Seoras: Esta comparecencia, que se enmarca en la discusin parlamentaria de los Presupuestos Generales de 2007, es mi primera comparecencia como Gobernador del Banco de Espaa ante el Congreso de los Diputados. Desde esta perspectiva, tienen gran trascendencia las comparecencias del Gobernador ante el rgano representante de la soberana popular y desempean un papel privilegiado a la hora de comunicar el anlisis de la economa en el que se basan las actuaciones del Banco de Espaa. Los ltimos datos publicados de la Contabilidad Nacional de Espaa han superado las previsiones de los distintos organismos y suministran un cuadro que confirma la prolongacin, con un renovado dinamismo,de suya larga fasedeexpansin. A la continuidad de los factores expansivos que han venido acompaando al establecimiento de un rgimen de estabilidad macroeconmica se han aadido la intensificacin del impulso demogrfico derivado de la inmigracin y de la creciente participacin de la mujer y, ms recientemente, la recuperacin del rea del euro. En relacin con este ltimo factor, me parece importante destacar, que dicha recuperacin y la retirada gradual del tono expansivo de la poltica monetaria nica, que lgicamente la acompaa, se estn produciendo en un momento especialmente oportuno para la economa espaola. La combinacin de ambos movimientos tiende, por un lado, a sostener el crecimiento a travs del impulso de la demanda externa, mientras que, por otro, el ajuste de las condiciones monetarias favorece la contencin de la demandainterna yayudaareequilibrar lacomposicin delcrecimiento. Nos encontramos, por tanto, con unas condiciones que, en principio, permiten proyectar el escenario actual de dinamismo econmico hacia el horizonte de los prximos aos, aunque se trata de un escenario que no est exento de riesgos, tanto externos como internos, sobre todo en lo que se refiere a su sostenibilidad en el largo plazo. Estos riesgos requieren una accin tempranayeficazde lapolticaeconmicaqueevite opalie suposiblematerializacin. Para profundizar enesteanlisisme voyareferiren primer lugar alasituacin del readeleuro, en el actual contexto internacional, y a la poltica monetaria nica, que es nuestra poltica monetaria, para pasar posteriormente al anlisis de la situacin de la economa espaola en la que se insertan lospresupuestos generales parael aoprximo. ***** A lo largo del presente ejercicio, el panorama econmico internacional se est caracterizando por el mantenimiento de la notable fortaleza que la actividad y el comercio mundiales han venido exhibiendo en los ltimos aos, yque est siendo comn ala mayor parte de las principales reas geogrficas. Este dinamismo se ha mantenido a pesar de unos precios del barril de petrleo y de las materias primas no energticas que continan siendo elevados, aunque han flexionado significativamentedesde los mximos alcanzados duranteel verano. Las perspectivas para un horizonte de medio plazo apuntan a la continuidad de la fase expansiva de la economa mundial, si bien a tasas algo ms moderadas. Estas previsiones estn rodeadas de incertidumbres debidas a la persistencia de los desequilibrios macro-financieros, la incierta trayectoria de los precios del petrleo a pesar de la moderacin reciente-en un marco geopoltico algo inestable, y la posibilidad de que la desaceleracin de la economa estadounidense revista una mayor entidad de la anticipada actualmente. Por ello, aunque el escenarioms verosmil resultaalentador, existen algunosriesgos alabaja. En este contexto global, hemos asistido en el transcurso del ao en curso a la consolidacin largamente esperada-de la recuperacin de la economa del rea del euro. Tras la atona observada en los ltimos aos, la actividad ha cobrado un vigor creciente, de forma que el producto se ha acelerado hasta alcanzar un incremento en torno al 2,5% al final del primer semestre del ao. Cabe destacar que, tras el impulso inicial del sector exterior, el fortalecimiento de la demanda interna ha comenzado a tomar el relevo, apoyada sobre todo en el dinamismo de la inversin, que se ha visto alentada por unas condiciones financieras favorables y, adems, por la recuperacin de los beneficios de las empresas yel saneamiento de sus balances. Por su parte, el consumo privado ha experimentado tambin una cierta mejora, an titubeante, que habr de ir consolidndose en la medida que se confirme la recuperacin del empleo. A medio plazo, lo ms probable es que se prolongue la fase de vigor econmico en los prximos trimestres, de forma que el PIB mantenga tasas de crecimiento en el entorno de las del producto potencial.
