La creciente independencia de los bancos centrales y su orientacin al logro de la estabilidad de precios ha reducido considerablemente en los ltimos aos la probabilidad de brotes inflacionistas en la mayor parte de los pases de la regin. Las tasas de inflacin de un dgito han pasado de ser la excepcin a ser la norma y, en el promedio de Amrica Latina, han sido inferiores al 6% en los dos ltimos aos. En los meses ms recientes, se han alcanzado adems registros mnimos por debajo del 5% en el agregado- desde que se llevan estadsticas fiables. Desde luego, siempre puede argumentarse que no ha sido slo la credibilidad de los bancos centrales el motivo del buen comportamiento de la inflacin, en comparacin con tiempos pasados, y que otros factores, entre ellos, el aumento de la competencia derivado de la globalizacin, han contribuido a este logro. Pero ustedes entendern que conceda un mrito importante a la mejora de la credibilidad antiinflacionista de los bancos centrales, en general, y de los latinoamericanos, en particular, que partan de una situacin de escasa reputacin. El descenso de las tasas de inflacin se ha traducido tambin en un mayor desarrollo y una mayor profundizacin de los sistemas financieros. La menor incertidumbre sobre la evolucin futura de los precios y los tipos de inters facilita la toma de decisiones de inversin y financiacin a largo plazo en condiciones de mayor certeza. Esa mayor estabilidad monetaria debe haber repercutido tambin favorablemente en el crecimiento. Otra aportacin clave dentro del mbito de las responsabilidades de los bancos centrales y en general de los supervisores bancarios es la correcta regulacin y supervisin del sistema financiero, en la medida en que ambas refuerzan la confianza de los agentes en su buen funcionamiento y contribuyen a reducir su vulnerabilidad. La estabilidad del sistema financiero y su eficiencia en la provisin de servicios financieros son especialmente importantes para las clases medias, pues, a diferencia de las capas de poblacin con mayor poder adquisitivo no tienen prcticamente acceso a servicios financieros en el exterior. En lo que se refiere a las clases con bajos niveles de renta, aunque a menudo no tienen acceso a los canales financieros formales, los bancos centrales pueden tambin colaborar activamente en facilitar el acceso al crdito y a los servicios financieros, por ejemplo aunque no slo, facilitando la bancarizacin de las remesas. En definitiva, en los ltimos aos se han dado en Amrica Latina grandes avances en trminos de estabilidad macroeconmica y, en particular, en el mbito de la inflacin y de fortalecimiento de los sistemas financieros, mejoras que deben consolidarse. Conclusiones Me gustara concluir esta intervencin subrayando los progresos econmicos de la regin en los ltimos aos, y la oportunidad que ello supone para mejorar el funcionamiento de la sociedad y de las instituciones. Amrica Latina atraviesa una fase de crecimiento favorable y de mejora de las condiciones externas, que est siendo aprovechada en mayor medida que en el pasado para reforzar las polticas econmicas internas y la estabilidad. Sin embargo, las debilidades de fondo de la regin solo podrn ser superadas definitivamente con una reactivacin ms intensa de los procesos de reformas, que eleven el crecimiento a largo plazo y lleven, a la vez, a una distribucin ms equilibrada del mismo. El actual perodo de bonanza econmica ofrece una nueva y excelente oportunidad para reforzar las polticas y las instituciones en este sentido, y prepararlas para tiempos ms difciles, que no debe desaprovecharse. Muchas gracias

Title: Appearance before the Senate Economy and Finance Committee
text: Madrid, 27 September 2007 Appearance of the Governor of Banco de Espa before the Committee of Economy and Finance of the Senate Miguel Fernandez Ordez Governor You would be: Last week I had the opportunity to address the Committee on Economy and Finance of the Congress to present my assessment of the Spanish and international economic situation, especially in light of the episodes of instability registered in the financial markets in recent weeks. Given the short time that has elapsed since that hearing, there is hardly any new relevant information on this issue, so you will allow me to approach my presentation basically following an approach similar to the one I used in Congress. This episode of turbulence in the financial markets has arisen at a time of strong expansion of the world economy, which has been growing for several years above 5% and that in 2006 closed the three-year period of greater expansion of activity since the seventies. Moreover, in 2006, the dynamism of the world economy was fairly broad-based, with the United States growing at a rate of more than 3% and the euro area recovering to similar rates, while emerging economies - particularly in Asia - continued to show strong dynamism. In the first half of 2007 this trend continued albeit with some slowdown in the US economy, but the appearance of this episode of turbulence in financial markets has now introduced a substantial element of uncertainty about the chances of this global economic strength remaining unchanged in the future. The element that has triggered this episode has been the increase in delinquency in the United States of a specific type of mortgage loans, which are characterized by their high vulnerability, since they are granted to people with a high risk profile and, sometimes, in fairly lax conditions. This has meant that, as I mentioned before, when the US economy has slowed down, the delinquency rate of these debtors has increased, which has led to intermediaries specializing in this type of mortgage have begun to experience losses and some of them have had to recognize their inability to meet their payment commitments. The origin of the turbulence is therefore very specific, as it is concentrated in a limited number of US financial institutions specializing in the riskiest mortgage segment. Perhaps most striking about this process are the factors that have led to this very specific disruption spreading rapidly and intensely to international financial markets. Obviously, the prominence of the US economy in the world and the high financing needs that this country has presented in recent years have intensified the exposure of markets and financial intermediaries around the world to economic developments in North America. The increasing globalization observed in financial transactions has also been the breeding ground for the initial shock to end up affecting institutions of various kinds and from different countries. The proliferation of structured financial instruments, with some exposure to these subprime mortgages, and whose complexity makes it difficult to properly assess their implicit risks, has been, finally, a very relevant driving factor, to which I will refer later. The effects of this episode of financial instability are well known to all of you: in the face of uncertainty and loss of confidence, many investors have liquidated their positions in the riskiest assets and shifted them towards safe and liquid instruments. As a result, there has been a decline in stock prices in the main financial centres and an increase in the credit risk premia required in private bond markets. By contrast, interest rates on public debt have fallen. These movements contain, in part, positive elements, insofar as they represent a more realistic assessment of the financial risks of many investments, which had probably been judged very optimistically in recent years. In this regard, a more reasonable assessment of these risks should result in a better allocation of financial resources and, ultimately, in greater sustainability of economic growth in the medium and long term. However, together with this change in the valuation of risk, this episode of turbulence is also leading to a tightening of both the price and the availability of financing, which, if it becomes entrenched or more intense, could have unfavorable implications for the confidence of economic agents. At the moment, very little data is available on the possible economic consequences of this shock. After August, one of the few sources of information available is data from opinion polls, although, in general, these still do not show substantial changes compared to the previous month. It is therefore premature to attempt to assess with any precision the foreseeable effect of these shocks on world economic growth. The forecasts made in the coming weeks by the main international organizations suggest that the turbulence will have some negative impact on the growth of the world economy, especially in 2008, although of limited magnitude, so that the global dynamism observed by the scams will continue, although at a more moderate pace. However, they also acknowledge that the current uncertainty in making economic projections has increased significantly and that the risks of any forecast are predominantly on the downside. One of the sources of uncertainty I mentioned earlier is that the United States will develop in the first quarters, because a bad performance of the US economy would drag down other countries. In contrast, recent good developments in emerging economies, which have been relatively insulated from these financial problems, are a factor that gives rise to some optimism about the resilience of the global economy. Indeed, unlike other episodes of financial turbulence in the past, which affected countries in Asia, Latin America and Eastern Europe, in this case it has been the Western industrialized countries that have been most affected by the crisis, in particular, the United States and the most developed European countries. Given the importance that the euro area has for the Spanish economy, both because of the magnitude of economic relations and because it is the area for which the monetary policy that binds us is defined, I find it interesting to examine, first of all, the prospects for this area in the light of this episode of financial instability. Before delving into the possible repercussions on the Spanish economy. In the European case there have been no problems in the mortgage markets, among other things because there are hardly any products of such high risk as that marketed by some entities in the United States, so that the intermediaries affected have been, in the first instance, to the extent that they had acquired securities linked to the subprime mortgage loans granted in that economy. However, this has only been the germ of a complex process that has ended up affecting the financial conditions of the European economy. As I recalled earlier, one of the first effects of mortgage problems in the United States is that it has triggered a global process of upward revision of credit risk premiums. In part, this review was reasonable d0 and perhaps even appropriate d0 given that its low level had probably driven overinvestment in high-risk potential activities. These investments had been boosted by the proliferation of new financial intermediaries specializing in credit risk transfer markets. These markets favor the diversification of investments, but also present some drawbacks due to the complexity of the instruments negotiated, which hinders their proper valuation, and the weak incentives that entities active in this operation may have to evaluate risks that they may not have to assume finally. In particular, in the current episode, some institutions that had been financing themselves through the issuance of very short-term fixed-income securities and using the funds raised to acquire structured products linked to long-term credit operations, including US subprime mortgages, have played an important role. This is one of the fundamental aspects of the turbulence observed, because when investors have detected the presence of subprime mortgages in the assets of these intermediaries, they have been reluctant to renew their assets against them. Since some credit institutions have made a commitment to provide liquidity to these specialised institutions in the event that, when maturity, they are unable to renew the financing they raise through the issuance of securities, investor distrust of these intermediaries has ended up affecting some credit institutions, while they have found themselves in need of additional liquidity to cover these positions. Faced with these liquidity problems, which are palpable in the euro area money markets, as well as in those of a good range of industrialized economies, central banks, and the ECB in particular, have reacted quickly, providing the market with the liquidity demanded both through regular operations and through extraordinary injection mechanisms, with the aim of calming existing tensions in the market. While this has prevented the crisis from deepening and sent a message of security, it has not prevented a certain lack of confidence from prevailing, as a result of difficulties in valuing structured products linked to subprime mortgages. This has hampered trading in money markets, especially in their longer maturities, where the financing exchanged has been substantially reduced and where interest rates have increased significantly. Although, as I said before, it is still too early to offer an accurate assessment of the possible impact of these turbulences on economic activity, it is a fact that this phenomenon has manifested itself at a time when the European economy is showing remarkable dynamism, which gives us hope that the eventual impact of this financial instability will be assimilable. In particular, the business situation is very solid, both from the equity point of view, after the balance sheet clean-up that took place in the scams, and from the perspective of expected profitability, which continues to boost productive investment. Private consumption is perhaps the least strong variable, although it is expected that increases in employment in the quarters will also promote household spending. With all this, growth in the euro area should remain around its potential rate, although slightly lower rates of expansion than expected a few months ago cannot be ruled out. There are no significant changes in the inflation outlook, as it would be around 2% in the medium term, with a lower contribution from indirect taxes d0 following the high contribution represented by the increase in the VAT rate in Germany in 2007 d0 but with higher growth in wages and, consequently, in unit labour costs, due to the greater dynamism that is expected in the labour market. The possibility of stronger than expected wage pressures if job creation continues to strengthen or margins in some sectors protected from international competition would jeopardise price stability in the euro area, which is also threatened by the expansionary bias shown by oil and other commodity prices. In any case, it is clear that the financial problems that arose last summer constitute an element that hinders the decision-making process of monetary policy, since it introduces greater doses of uncertainty when drawing up prospects for both growth and inflation. While this episode of turbulence has increased downside risks to growth, it is difficult to determine the intensity of that review, as well as the extent to which this can alleviate the inflationary risks I noted earlier. Given this uncertainty, the Governing Council of the ECB decided to hold its first meeting this September to keep interest rates unchanged, while recognising the need to accumulate more information on this episode and to study it in detail before taking any decision. It therefore seems necessary to gather information on various factors which may affect the evolution of the European economy. Some relate to the rest of the world, perhaps including monitoring the development of the U.S. economy, the transmission of this evolution to the world economy and the possible repercussions on financial markets and the exchange rate. Until now, the United States had managed to cope with a slowdown in residential investment while maintaining a certain dynamism in activity. In addition, it is necessary to know how strongly this episode of turbulence can be transferred to credit markets in Europe, both in terms of the cost of financing and the availability of funds for investment projects by companies and families. Also important is the perception that private sector agents have of this phenomenon of instability, since the loss of confidence in the prospects of demand in the case of companies or in future incomes in the case of households can cause spending decisions to be delayed, affecting growth. I believe that this is an opportune moment to reiterate the firm commitment of monetary policy to the objective of price stability, since we are certain that maintaining that stability is the best contribution that monetary policy can make to promote sustained growth in output and employment. therefore, the well-being of citizens. In the case of Spain, these events have occurred while our economy has continued to show remarkable dynamism, within a phase of growth that has lasted for more than a decade. In the first half of 2007, activity grew by around 4 per cent, similar to that recorded in 2006, the highest rate observed since 2000. In addition, it should be noted that in recent quarters there has been a certain rebalancing in the sources of growth, with a lower contribution of domestic demand and an improvement in the contribution of the foreign sector. Even within the slight moderation of domestic demand, some positive seles are perceived, since business investment d0 which, possibly, is the component that best anticipates the support of production in the future d0 has remained very strong, while private consumption and, above all, residential investment d0 whose evolution had absorbed a growing part of spending in recent years d0 are the variables where the slowdown has been most noticeable. This more balanced composition of expenditure has been partly the result of the gradual retreat since late 2005 of the accommodative tone of monetary and financial conditions in the euro area, which had boosted private sector spending and borrowing in Spain in previous years. The increase in key interest rates by the ECB has not, in any case, been unrelated to the recovery observed in the euro area, which, together with the good performance of the world economy, has been a fundamental element in encouraging Spanish exports since 2006, after some sluggishness in our sales abroad. But it is not only the conditions of demand that explain the recent evolution of the Spanish economy, since it seems clear that without a significant expansion of supply it would not have been possible to maintain such intense economic growth for such a long period. In this sense, the increase in the supply of labour, linked both to migratory flows and to the increase in the participation of women in the labour market, has made it possible to sustain a high rate of growth without generating excessive cost and price pressures. In recent months, the inflation rate, as measured by the CPI, has fallen to close to 2% (2.2% in July and August), although this reduction is partly a consequence of the evolution of energy prices and a certain rebound can be expected in the first few months. Private consumption appears to have responded smoothly to changes in financial conditions, from growing slightly above 4 per cent in 2004 and 2005 to growing at a rate of 3.3 per cent in the second quarter of 2007. The increase in interest rates has increased the cost of financing borne by families indebted at variable rates, which has been able to affect the dynamics of spending in a segment of the population. Likewise, the slowdown in house prices has been reducing the possible expansionary influence that wealth has been able to have on consumption. Other elements, however, have supported household consumption, among which we must highlight the dynamism of employment, which has continued to expand at high rates, above 3%, which has reinforced the confidence of agents in their prospects for future income. The slowdown in investment in housing since the beginning of 2006 is also due to the increase in interest rates and lower expectations of revaluation of this rate. active, which have meant a certain cooling of the strength so intense that this component of demand had shown in recent years. As in the case of private consumption, the slowdown recorded has also been mild, since the dynamism of the population has provided a very relevant demand support. But the most remarkable thing about the recent evolution of the Spanish economy is that other factors have compensated for the lower contribution to the growth of these two components of domestic spending, so that activity has not only not suffered, but has shown renewed dynamism. The first of these factors is the productive investment of companies, which, despite the tightening of financial conditions, has experienced a strong strength, thanks to high profitability and favourable business expectations, which the recovery in the euro area has reinforced in both scams. In fact, while in the period 2001-2004, investment in construction was the most dynamic component of demand, since 2005 it has been investment in capital goods that has shown the highest growth rates, reaching expansion rates of around 13% in the timour quarters. The second relevant factor has been the improvement in the contribution of net foreign demand to growth, with a better performance of exports since 2006 and a certain moderation of purchases abroad already in 2007. The data of the National Accounts, which refer to the second quarter, support this tendency to rebalance in the composition of expenditure, although with a lower rate of growth in activity, which reached 4% in that quarter, one tenth below that registered in the first months of the year. The indicators available for the third quarter d0 although scarce and incomplete d0 also suggest that this trend towards less dynamism in domestic demand and growth in activity will continue. Although, as I said at the outset, it is too early to assess precisely whether the implications for the Spanish economy of the period of financial instability that emerged in August, it is likely that private consumption and investment in housing will not suffer sharp deviations from their path of gradual deceleration, especially in light of the expected maintenance of a robust pace of job creation and population growth. The change in the real estate cycle, which seems to be already underway, will moderate investment in construction, although the other components of this variable d0 civil works and non-residential buildings d0 whose evolution is due to different factors, linked to the decisions of the authorities and companies, could maintain some strength, which would alleviate the negative impact of housing on growth. It is foreseeable that business investment will continue to be the most dynamic element of domestic demand, although it is difficult for it to maintain the very high rates of growth that it now shows, so it will hardly be able to counteract the slowdown in household spending. All of this It assumes, in short, that net external demand will play a crucial role in ensuring that the moderation of expenditure does not lead to an excessive slowdown in activity. We have already seen that in the evolution of this external demand, the effects of the turbulence on the world economy, particularly in the United States, and their repercussions on the exchange rate are fundamental, since they can directly affect the growth of Spain's export markets and the possibilities of competing in them. This is probably the fundamental channel through which the recent episode of financial instability and greater international uncertainty could affect the growth scenario expected for the Spanish economy. The fact that these factors are outside our area of influence only underlines the importance of improving the mechanisms that allow Spanish companies to increase their ability to compete in international markets. Along with the influence of turbulence on the external sector, it is also worth assessing the possible effects on domestic demand of a possible tightening of financial conditions. As I explained at the beginning of my speech, this episode of instability has led to increases in money market interest rates and problems in trading long-term liquidity. The transfer of these financial difficulties to economic actors will basically depend on the situation and decisions of national credit institutions, which are the ones that mostly provide the financing demanded by the private sector. Therefore, properly understanding the current situation of Spanish banks is key to determining the extent of the impact of turbulence on our economy. I would like to reiterate here in the Senate that we have ample evidence that confirms the position of strength with which Spanish credit institutions face these turbulences, based on their high levels of profitability, comfortable levels of solvency, clearly above the minimum required by regulation; and broad coverage of NPLs. In addition, there are other factors that have limited the exposure of Spanish entities to current shocks. First, the credit quality of Spanish mortgages is high, with no high-risk segment in the mortgage markets similar to the North American one. NPL ratios are low and the average ratio between the volume of loans granted and the value of collateral required is moderate. Second, exposure to subprime mortgages on banks' balance sheets is completely marginal. Spanish institutions have not acquired subprime mortgages or credit commitments with other financial intermediaries that could have such assets. In fact, these types of intermediaries have not proliferated in our financial system. Finally, a fundamental feature that provides reassurance about the quality of the assets of the Spanish financial system is the traditional banking model followed, which is characterized by the fact that entities have resorted to the securitization of credits mainly to finance the expansion of activity and not in order to transmit to third parties the risks associated with the loans in their portfolio. This assumes that credit risks have been kept on the balance sheet itself, so that quality controls on those risks have continued to function properly. In addition, the securitisation processes used by Spanish institutions have materialised in instruments that have a low degree of complexity and are much easier to assess than the structured products to which I referred earlier. This does not mean, obviously, that the Spanish economy and its financial system can feel completely safe from the repercussions that may arise from this process of financial instability. In particular, if this episode were to drag on excessively, it could end up affecting investor confidence and trading on the financial markets, regardless of the true credit quality of the different instruments. If this were to happen, the fact that our economy needs to be financed in international markets could act as an obstacle to maintaining the high rates of growth observed in scams. In short, the outlook for the Spanish economy points to a certain moderation in growth, from the current high rates of expansion, although the recent episode of financial instability has increased, as elsewhere, the uncertainty surrounding them. The underlying dynamism of the economic situation d0 which may show a gradual slowdown although with a more balanced composition d0 and the strength of financial institutions provide some certainty about the ability of this economy to cope with the impact of turbulence. However, should this episode prove to be prolonged and intense, external demand could struggle to offset the foreseeable moderation in domestic demand, especially if financial instability substantially affects our main export markets. Let me end this speech by referring to the important role that the authorities must play in these circumstances. Indeed, I believe that good management of economic policy is crucial and should be aimed at providing confidence to the agents, preserving sufficient room for action in the face of possible future events. In the area of budgetary policy, this translates into the need to maintain its current orientation, which is proving beneficial for the stability of the economy, achieving a sufficiently comfortable budget surplus and avoiding expenditure deviations, so that, should conditions deteriorate, there would be sufficient room for manoeuvre to help stabilise the economic situation. Finally, the latent uncertainty in the international economic and financial environment cannot put in the background the initiatives for the implementation of the structural reforms that have already been identified, both in the aspects to improve the functioning of the markets for goods and productive factors, and in the area of increasing the productive capital of the Spanish economy. In times of uncertainty such as the present, these reforms are essential because they can provide the flexibility needed to reduce the costs of reallocation of factors between activities d0 for example, from construction to industry and services d0 and boost the ability of Spanish companies to compete in both the internal market and international markets. Thanks a lot.

En el mbito de la poltica presupuestaria, esto se traduce en la necesidad de mantener su orientaci actual, que est siendo beneficiosa para la estabilidad de la economa, alcanzando un saldo presupuestario superavitario suficientemente holgado y evitando desviaciones de gasto, de modo que, si las condiciones se deterioraran, se dispusiera de un margen de maniobra suficiente para contribuir a estabilizar la situaci econica. Finalmente, la incertidumbre latente en el entorno econico y financiero internacional no puede poner en segundo plano las iniciativas para la aplicaci de las reformas estructurales que ya se han identificado, tanto en los aspectos para mejorar el funcionamiento de los mercados de bienes y factores productivos, como en el mbito del incremento del capital productivo de la economa espala. En momentos de incertidumbre como los actuales, estas reformas son bsicas porque pueden proporcionar la flexibilidad necesaria para reducir los costes de reasignacin de factores entre actividades por ejemplo, desde la construccin hacia la industria y los servicios- e impulsar la capacidad de las empresas espalas para competir tanto en el mercado interior como en los mercados internacionales. Muchas gracias.

Title: Appearance before the Senate Budget Committee
text: Madrid, 23 November 2007 Appearance of the Governor of the Bank of Spain before the Senate Budget Committee Miguel Fern87ndez Ord9796ez Governor As you are well aware, the international financial markets were affected over the past summer by an episode of turbulence whose duration and consequences cannot yet be determined. My appearance before this Committee on Budgets is therefore taking place at a time when the analysis of the economic outlook is surrounded by a greater degree of uncertainty than usual. I do not think it is necessary to reiterate here the analysis of the main triggers of the turbulence, an aspect that I have already addressed in detail in my recent appearances both in this House and in Congress, so I will limit myself to recalling the aspects that may be of greater relevance to better understand what are the conditions that make it difficult for the situation in the financial markets to normalize fully. This episode of instability had its origin in a profound deterioration in the credit quality of certain highly complex financial assets associated with the financing of subprime mortgages in the United States. In principle, the losses suffered by all holders of these products are not of a considerable magnitude, when considering the international financial system as a whole, but the direct or indirect exposure of financial agents has been revealed in an unexpected and widespread way, leading to a deterioration in the confidence of participants in some markets. The consequence has been a significant decline in activity not only in the markets in which these products are traded, but also in the money markets where the liquidity provided by central banks is redistributed. The rapid interventions of the latter, which provided liquidity on an extraordinary basis, have eased tensions in interbank markets, although these have not completely dissipated. The definitive normalization of the situation still requires a better knowledge and a greater assimilation of the degree of exposure of the different agents. In any case, as I have had the opportunity to say on previous occasions, the financial system of our country is facing these events with firm support as a result, on the one hand, of the virtual absence of exposure of our entities to instruments of this nature and, on the other, of their solid equity position and high profitability. Fortunately, the turbulence was triggered at a time of remarkable strength in global activity, driven notably by the continued dynamism of emerging economies, whose financial markets, unlike in developed countries, are proving relatively immune to this phase of instability. This episode of financial turmoil introduces some uncertainty about the continuation of a period of strong global growth that has lasted for five years. In any case, the most likely scenario handled by most institutions and analysts for the next horizon projects a sustained increase in world output, although at a somewhat more moderate pace than in the recent past. The potential impact of the outbreak of financial instability on global dynamism should not lead us to lose sight of some positive effects that accompany the market correction when viewed from a lengthy time perspective. Indeed, in recent years, the world economy has been characterized by the maintenance of very low levels of interest rates and an abundance of global liquidity, in a context of robust growth and moderation of inflation. These conditions, together with low NPL ratios, had contributed to a sharp decline in risk premia, which the very search for higher yields probably fed back. In fact, well before the summer, there were already numerous voices pointing to the existence of a significant underestimation of risks in some segments of the international financial system. From this perspective, the turbulence episode, when the most critical phase is overcome, can be expected to lead to a tighter assessment of risk and increased discipline in financial markets, which will tend to strengthen the foundations of global activity in the longer term. The euro area faces this period of financial instability from a fairly favourable starting position, although it should be remembered that some signs had already emerged before the start of the period that suggested that the pace of expansion of the euro area's activity may have already reached its cyclical maximum and that pointed towards a moderation more in line with its potential growth rate. However, by the time the shocks hit, the euro area had accumulated a year and a half of strong growth and the continued dynamism of the various components of demand was on solid footing. In particular, the gradual strengthening of labour markets was helping to sustain consumer spending, and sound balance sheets and the high profitability of firms in the area augured a remarkable dynamism in productive investment. On the external side of the economy, the boost in world activity and trade created a favorable scenario for the advance of sales abroad. In addition, the implementation of more disciplined macroeconomic policies in the institutional framework of EMU was making the area more resilient to these or other shocks compared to past eras. The events of this summer have not affected the dynamism of the area during the third quarter, which has been more intense than initially expected, but it is highly likely that they will end up having an impact on a slowdown in growth rates greater than anticipated then, although within perspectives that remain generally favorable. Internally, one of the main consequences of the turbulence may be a certain tightening of the standards for granting financing to families and companies. On the external side, although emerging economies can be expected to continue to lead global growth, the forecasts are much less rosy with regard to the United States, since the difficulties experienced by its real estate sector are greater than those anticipated a few months ago. In any case, the difficulties in accurately gauging the magnitude of the effects on activity in the medium term are evident. The data accumulated since the beginning of this episode are still too scarce to allow us to clear the uncertainty about two aspects that may condition the final scope of this episode. I am referring, of course, to the resilience of the US economy and, with it, to the possible evolution of trade flows in the area and, above all, to the time that the return of international financial markets to a situation of normality will take place, because it is no secret from anyone that the more persistent the tensions in these markets, Greater will be its effects on the confidence of families and businesses in the area. On the price side, inflationary pressures in the euro area had remained relatively contained until September, and one might even expect, in the first instance, that by tending to dampen the pace of expansion of activity, the episode of financial turbulence could help to mitigate some of the risks to price stability. However, new sources of inflationary pressures linked to oil and food price developments have recently emerged, leading to a pick-up in HICP rates in October. Crude oil prices are, in fact, at levels close to their all-time highs. In addition, unprocessed food prices have accelerated significantly, which may reflect global demand pressures, but is likely to respond to unfavourable supply conditions arising from weather developments in some geographical areas. It is true that in the recent past we have seen sharp rises in oil prices without this leading to substantial increases in wage demands and core inflation. However, the accumulation of these increases may end up triggering propagation processes that make the resurgence of inflation more persistent. This risk may also be increased in the current context of limited slack in the area's labour markets. The coincidence in time of the effects of the financial turmoil and the movements underlying this inflationary resurgence has introduced greater complexity into monetary policy decision-making. Uncertainty about the effects of the turbulence has led the Governing Council of the ECB to halt the process of phasing out monetary stimulus that it had been carrying out progressively since the end of 2005, keeping interest rates unchanged at the three meetings held between September and November. At the same time, however, the Governing Council drew attention to the increase in inflationary risks over the medium term and reiterated its full commitment to act, when and as necessary, to ensure that inflation expectations remain firmly anchored at levels consistent with price stability. Let me now focus on the highlights of recent developments in the Spanish economy. Since I appeared in this very Chamber, almost two months ago, the diagnosis of the short-term outlook for the Spanish economy has not changed substantially. As indicated by the information just published by the INE referring to the third quarter, the Spanish economy continued the path of gradual slowdown in activity that had begun in the second, placing year-on-year GDP growth at 3.8%, compared to rates of around 4% in the first half of the year. The mild moderation in domestic demand continued over this period, reflecting the process of normalization of monetary conditions initiated almost two years ago, as well as the improvement in the contribution of net foreign demand to growth, in the face of an external environment that has remained favourable. Overall, this has allowed further progress towards a more balanced composition between domestic and external sources of expenditure and, within domestic demand, business investment has gained weight compared to household spending, especially in its residential investment component. Household consumption has continued the process of gradual moderation that began a few quarters ago, although within a pattern of dynamism that is supported by population expansion and solid employment. This trend reflects the normal adaptation of households to less comfortable monetary and financial conditions and the lower intensity of wealth appreciation, given the slowdown in house price increases. Residential investment, on the other hand, is moderating its rate of growth somewhat more markedly, prolonging the pattern of gradual slowdown that it has been showing since the beginning of 2006, also in response to the increase in interest rates and lower expectations of revaluation of real estate prices, despite the fact that demographic dynamism tends to limit the effect of these two factors on housing demand. The lower momentum in spending and the increase in financing prices are leading to a containment in household demand for credit and a slowdown in their debt ratios in terms of disposable income. Overall, the household savings rate moderated again in the first part of the year and their financing needs remained stable in GDP terms, but the change in financial conditions is likely to lead to a stabilization of the savings rate in the future. Business spending, on the other hand, maintained a strong trend, although in the central months of the year it showed signs of a slight slowdown. In particular, the strength of investment in equipment in a situation of high profitability both present and expected and favorable business expectations stands out. In recent months, the use of external financing by companies began to reflect the relative tightening of financial conditions, observing a slight inflection in the rate of indebtedness as well as an incipient change in composition according to their purpose, being able to appreciate a slowdown in the funds directed to finance real estate and construction activities, compared to an increase in those destined to industrial companies and service activities. Net foreign demand has continued to cushion the impact of the slowdown in spending on growth, due to a more dynamic performance of exports than that of purchases abroad, particularly pronounced in the third quarter. Despite this, the rate of growth of sales abroad so far this year is somewhat lower than the previous year, in a context in which export markets are showing a somewhat less expansionary behavior and in which the appreciation of the euro exchange rate could be affecting, to some extent, to extra-Community sales. Although the evolution of the euro value is helping to make purchases abroad cheaper, imports of goods are growing less than the previous year, consistent with the slight slowdown shown by final demand. However, the trade deficit has continued to widen, albeit at slower rates than in the past, and the nation's financing needs have also continued to increase at a more attenuated pace. On the supply side, the slight slowdown in GDP mainly reflects a certain loss of dynamism in the construction sector, while industry continued to show signs of strength, albeit somewhat more contained throughout the third quarter. Employment has been adjusting to the evolution of activity, observing, from the second quarter, a small reduction in the rate of job creation, also somewhat more pronounced in the construction sector. And all this in a population context that has continued to be very dynamic, an aspect that, from a broader temporal perspective, has been crucial for activity to adjust to the dynamism of demand, avoiding the generation of excessive cost pressures and prices throughout the prolonged phase of expansion that the Spanish economy has experienced. Labour costs throughout this year are following a path of moderation, with growth somewhat lower than the previous year, which is being transferred to unit labour costs, given the upswing in productivity. Unfortunately, on the other hand, consumer prices have been performing less favourably in recent months, as a result of the significant increases in crude oil prices and food commodity prices on international markets. This negative impact is also occurring when the CPI began to pick up as a result of a base effect, associated with the behaviour of oil prices in the first half of 2006. In this context, the annual rate of the consumer price index rose in October to 3.6% and the inflation differential with EMU increased to 1 pp, from the minimum of 0.5 pps reached in summer. Although core inflation remains at levels similar to those of the first half of the year, the increase in inflationary pressures, although transitory, increases the risk of its spread to the economy as a whole, particularly as a result of the existence of indexation mechanisms and practices in the setting of prices and incomes. A close to the current year such as the one I have just described allows us to draw a macroeconomic scenario for 2008 that, in its basic lines, should not differ substantially from that projected by the Bank of Spain in the forecasts that we published last spring and in which, as will be recalled, a gradual approximation of GDP towards growth rates of around 3% was contemplated. It is true, however, that these projections rest on the reasonable assumption that the turbulence will have a limited duration, as reflected in most forecasts made after the summer for the world economy by the main international organizations. It is interesting to review the factors underpinning a scenario of a mild slowdown for the Spanish economy in 2008, compatible with the maintenance of a high dynamism of activity and employment. On the one hand, the normalisation of the tone of monetary policy should facilitate a smooth adjustment towards more sustainable rates of private sector spending and indebtedness over the medium term. On the other hand, the real estate market is expected to continue to evolve in line with the patterns it has followed so far, i.e. with a gradual slowdown in house prices and a gentle adjustment in demand, which would continue to be supported by the high rate of population growth. Moreover, although it will probably be difficult to maintain the growth rates of business investment and investment in non-residential construction as strong as those of recent quarters, the outlook for both expenditure components also remains favourable. In any case, it seems difficult for productive investment to compensate, by itself, for the lower contribution of household spending. That is why, as I pointed out during my last appearance in this very House, the role of net external demand is crucial to reconcile a certain containment of expenditure with the maintenance of growth rates of around 3%. As we have seen in recent years, the contribution of this variable to growth depends closely on the performance of our export markets but also on the competitiveness of our production. Therefore, a scenario of recovery of net exports such as the one I have just described requires continuity in improving the competitiveness of Spanish companies, in response to changes in world trade as a result of the entry of new and powerful competitors. At the same time, the lower boost in final demand should materialize in a certain slowdown in imports, reducing the filtering of spending abroad. Domestically, maintaining the dynamism of employment and gradually normalising the real estate market are essential to sustain income expectations and, consequently, agents' spending plans within a pattern of mild deceleration. I have already given the arguments that facilitate an orderly adjustment of the real estate market. As for the employment response, there are indications that in recent years there have been improvements in the overall functioning of the labour market that are behind the enormous capacity of the Spanish economy to generate employment and that should continue in the future. In any case, the return to more normal patterns in the construction sector and the high incidence of this sector on employment behaviour attribute great importance to the existence of a sufficient degree of flexibility in the functioning of the economy to facilitate the reallocation of resources towards industrial activities and services that have to take over, giving continuity to the change in product composition that has occurred in recent quarters. The best contribution that economic policies can make in a situation such as the current one of mild slowdown and increasing uncertainty is to ensure commitment to budgetary stability and to deepen structural policies aimed at rebalancing the sources of growth. The General State Budget Project aims to achieve a surplus in 2007 of 1.3% in the accounts of all Public Administrations. The information available on budget implementation so far this year seems to suggest, however, that the positive balance at the end of the year may be higher than the last official forecast and of a similar magnitude to that of the previous year. As in previous years, these results, better than initially expected, would be due to a favourable trend in tax revenues, mainly from direct taxes, in a context of economic growth also higher than expected. As for the 2008 financial year, the General State Budget Project places the general government surplus target at 0.9%. This figure complies with the European commitments derived from the Stability and Growth Pact and respects the budgetary stability objectives set by the Chambers of Congress and the Senate in June 2007, in compliance with the provisions of the new Budgetary Stability Laws, which enter into force precisely for the first time in 2008. The programmed reduction of the surplus would be based on some tax cut measures, while, on the expenditure side, the Draft Budget sets a growth rate for the State in line with the expected evolution of nominal GDP, which means strictly complying with the limit that was established in June in the context also of the provisions of the Budget Stability Law. It should be borne in mind that, as I pointed out earlier, the objectives set are based on a very cautious forecast for the end of 2007 on the revenue side. It is conceivable that if there were a result in the collection figures for 2007 that was more comfortable than expected in the Advance of Liquidation of the Budgets, this better record should be transferred to the budget forecast for 2008 and therefore allow the achievement of a surplus also higher. As in previous years, the important thing is that the additional margins that may arise on the revenue side do not result in an increase in expenditure but in the generation of a greater surplus. I would like to emphasise that the current government surplus has a certain temporal component that must be taken into account when carrying out budgetary programming. On the one hand, the prolonged period of dynamism of the economy and, in particular, of the real estate sector has generated a strong growth in tax collection that will tend to reduce in a phase of economic slowdown. On the other hand, it should be borne in mind that the Multiannual Financial Framework of the European Union for the period 2007-2013 provides for a progressive reduction of funds allocated to Spain, which still has a reduced impact in these first years, which are transitional. In this context, maintaining a sufficient level of government surplus seems to be the most appropriate strategy in the short, medium and long term. On the one hand, because it provides the tone that fiscal policy must maintain in a cyclical situation in which economic growth is expected to be similar to its potential. On the other hand, because in a context of uncertainty it is especially relevant to maintain the stabilizing potential of the Budgets so that it can be used in case the slowdown is greater than expected. Finally, maintaining a high public surplus would make it possible to better cope with the foreseeable impact of population ageing on public finances in the medium term. I would like to stress, in any case, that all administrations and, in particular, the Autonomous Communities should contribute to the achievement of this strategy. The official forecast is, however, that all these Territorial Entities still present in this year a public deficit balance despite the good economic situation of recent years. In this context, the reform of the financing system of these administrations is pending discussion. Given the experience of recent years, this reform should be carried out in such a way as to generate adequate incentives for sound behaviour of their public finances. On the supply policy side, the key is to achieve an improvement in the economy's ability to adapt, which allows us to respond flexibly to the changing and highly competitive environment, favours the efficient allocation of resources and increases our growth potential. The National Reform Plan approved in 2005 articulated a set of actions that were oriented in the direction I have mentioned. The Progress Report of the Programme presented last October shows that the implementation of the Plan has gone at a good pace and that convergence in terms of GDP per capita with the European Union has been maintained. This approximation in the levels of economic well-being has been based, however, essentially, on the increase in the employment rate, so it seems necessary to continue deepening reforms that allow both preserving the strength in job creation and increasing, at the same time, the efficiency gains of the economy. In this sense, the spending priorities incorporated in the draft Budget are oriented, as in past years, towards areas of great importance for improving productivity, such as research and development, education and infrastructure. It is important, however, to ensure that the expected increase in the allocation of resources is managed efficiently, for which the most appropriate mechanisms for evaluating and selecting public policies must be used, so that they result in real increases in productivity. At the same time, it is necessary to continue deepening measures to increase the flexibility and efficiency of the labour market in order to facilitate the reallocation of employment between productive sectors and to prevent the cyclical change of phase from causing declines in the level of employment as used to happen in the past. Special attention should be paid, among other aspects, to those institutional elements that could reduce the sensitivity of wages to the cycle, such as safeguard clauses. Similarly, revisions of the minimum wage should be considered with caution because of the impact they may have on cost and price formation and job creation. Finally, in the field of structural policies aimed at making product markets more flexible, it is necessary to persevere and extend the liberalization processes undertaken in recent years and to make progress in defining a simpler and more transparent regulatory framework. In relation to the latter, the commitment made by the central government to reduce the administrative burden on companies resulting from national legislation by 25% by 2012 should be highly appreciated. An ambitious transposition of the Services Directive, currently under discussion, could allow an important advance in this area. The role of the Territorial Administrations is, again, crucial in the achievement of these objectives, since they enjoy regulatory capacity on the regulation of a wide set of economic sectors. An example is internal trade, a sector of great relevance, not only because of the weight that its activity represents in the economy as a whole, but also because of the role played by distribution channels in the behavior of productivity and in price formation processes. In recent years, however, there has been an increase, in general, in the degree of regulatory restriction in this sector, as highlighted in a recent article published in our Economic Bulletin. In any case, the opportunities offered to the Spanish economy to prolong the trajectory of modernization and economic dynamism well deserve the necessary efforts of economic policy to overcome the uncertainties and challenges that arise. Thanks a lot.
text_original: Madrid, 23 de noviembre de 2007 Comparecencia del Gobernador del Banco de Espaa ante la Comisin de Presupuestos del Senado Miguel Fernndez Ordez Gobernador Como ustedes conocen bien, los mercados financieros internacionales se vieron afectados a lo largo del verano pasado por un episodio de turbulencias cuya duracin y consecuencias an no se pueden precisar. Mi comparecencia ante esta Comisin de Presupuestos tiene lugar, por tanto, en un momento en el que el anlisis de las perspectivas econmicas est rodeado de un grado de incertidumbre mayor del habitual. No creo que sea necesario reiterar aqu el anlisis de los principales desencadenantes del las turbulencias, aspecto que ya he abordado con detenimiento en mis comparecencias recientes tanto en esta Cmara como en el Congreso, por lo que me limitar a recordar los aspectos que pueden resultar de mayor relevancia para comprender mejor cules son los condicionantes que dificultan que la situacin en los mercados financieros se normalice plenamente. Este episodio de inestabilidad tuvo su origen en un profundo deterioro de la calidad crediticia de determinados activos financieros de gran complejidad asociados a la financiacin de hipotecas de alto riesgo en Estados Unidos. En principio, las prdidas sufridas por el conjunto de tenedores de estos productos no son de una magnitud considerable, cuando se considera el sistema financiero internacional en su conjunto, pero la exposicin directa o indirecta de los agentes financieros se ha revelado de forma inesperada y muy extendida, por lo que ha conducido a un deterioro de la confianza de los participantes en algunos mercados. La consecuencia ha sido una importante disminucin de la actividad no solo en los mercados en los que se negocian esos productos, sino tambin en los mercados monetarios en los que se redistribuye la liquidez proporcionada por los bancos centrales. Las rpidas intervenciones de estos ltimos, que suministraron liquidez con carcter extraordinario, han permitido aliviar las tensiones en los mercados interbancarios, aunque estas no se han disipado por completo. La normalizacin definitiva de la situacin requiere todava un mejor conocimiento y una mayor asimilacin del grado de exposicin de los distintos agentes. En todo caso, como ya he tenido la oportunidad de decir en ocasiones anteriores, el sistema financiero de nuestro pas est afrontando estos acontecimientos con soportes firmes como resultado, por una parte, de la prctica ausencia de exposicin de nuestras entidades a los instrumentos de esta naturaleza y, por otra, de su slida posicin patrimonial y su elevada rentabilidad. Afortunadamente, las turbulencias se desencadenaron en un momento de notable fortaleza de la actividad mundial, impulsada de manera destacada por el continuado dinamismo de las economas emergentes, cuyos mercados financieros, a diferencia de lo ocurrido en los pases desarrollados, estn resultando relativamente inmunes a esta fase de inestabilidad. Este episodio de perturbaciones financieras introduce alguna incertidumbre sobre la continuacin de un perodo de slido crecimiento mundial que se prolonga ya por un lustro. En cualquier caso, el escenario ms probable que manejan la mayor parte de las instituciones y los analistas para el prximo horizonte proyecta un avance sostenido del producto mundial, aunque a un ritmo algo ms moderado que en el pasado reciente. El posible efecto del brote de inestabilidad financiera sobre el dinamismo mundial no debe llevar a perder de vista algunos efectos positivos que acompaan a la correccin de los mercados cuando se considera desde una perspectiva temporal dilatada. En efecto, en los ltimos aos, la economa mundial se haba venido caracterizando por el mantenimiento de unos niveles muy reducidos de tipos de inters y una abundancia de liquidez global, en un marco de crecimiento robusto y moderacin de la inflacin. Estas condiciones, junto a unas tasas de morosidad reducidas, haban contribuido a un pronunciado descenso de las primas de riesgo, que la propia bsqueda de mayores rentabilidades probablemente realiment. De hecho, bastante antes del verano, eran ya numerosas las voces que sealaban la existencia de una importante infravaloracin de los riesgos en algunos segmentos del sistema financiero internacional. Desde esta perspectiva, cabe esperar que el episodio de turbulencias, cuando se supere la fase ms crtica, conduzca a una valoracin ms ajustada del riesgo y a un aumento de la disciplina en los mercados financieros, que tendern a fortalecer los cimientos de la actividad mundial a ms largo plazo. El rea del euro afronta este periodo de inestabilidad financiera desde una posicin de partida bastante favorable, si bien es preciso recordar que ya antes del inicio del mismo haban surgido algunas seales que hacan pensar que el ritmo de expansin de la actividad del rea podra haber alcanzado ya su mximo cclico y que apuntaban hacia una moderacin ms en lnea con su tasa de crecimiento potencial. No obstante, en el momento en que se desencadenaron las perturbaciones, la eurozona haba acumulado ao y medio de crecimiento vigoroso y la continuacin del dinamismo de los distintos componentes de la demanda se asentaba sobre bases slidas. En particular, el gradual fortalecimiento de los mercados de trabajo estaba contribuyendo al sostenimiento del gasto de los consumidores y los balances saneados y la elevada rentabilidad de las empresas del rea auguraban un dinamismo notable de la inversin productiva. En la vertiente externa de la economa, el empuje de la actividad y el comercio mundiales configuraban un panorama propicio para el avance de las ventas al exterior. Adems, la aplicacin de polticas macroeconmicas ms disciplinadas en el marco institucional de la UEM estaba dotando al rea de una mayor resistencia ante estas u otras perturbaciones, en comparacin con pocas pasadas. Los acontecimientos de este verano no han afectado al dinamismo del rea durante el tercer trimestre, que ha resultado ms intenso de lo inicialmente esperado, pero es altamente probable que terminen repercutiendo en una ralentizacin de las tasas de crecimiento mayor de lo que se anticipaba entonces, aunque dentro de unas perspectivas que siguen siendo globalmente favorables. En el mbito interno, una de las principales secuelas de las turbulencias puede ser un cierto endurecimiento de los estndares de concesin de financiacin a familias y empresas. En la vertiente externa, aunque cabe esperar que las economas emergentes continen liderando el crecimiento mundial, las previsiones son bastante menos halageas en lo que respecta a Estados Unidos, ya que las dificultades por las que atraviesa su sector inmobiliario son mayores que las anticipadas hace unos meses. En cualquier caso, las dificultades para calibrar de forma precisa la magnitud de los efectos sobre la actividad en el medio plazo son evidentes. Los datos acumulados desde el inicio de este episodio resultan an demasiado escasos para permitir despejar la incertidumbre sobre dos aspectos que pueden condicionar el alcance final de este episodio. Me refiero, naturalmente, a la capacidad de resistencia de la economa norteamericana y, con ella, a la posible evolucin de los flujos comerciales del rea y, sobre todo, al tiempo que tomar el retorno de los mercados financieros internacionales a una situacin de normalidad, porque a nadie se le oculta que cuanto ms persistentes sean las tensiones en esos mercados, mayores sern sus efectos sobre la confianza de las familias y las empresas del rea. En el mbito de los precios, las presiones inflacionistas en el rea del euro se haban mantenido relativamente contenidas hasta el mes de septiembre e incluso cabra esperar, en primera instancia, que al tender a atemperar el ritmo de expansin de la actividad, el episodio de turbulencias financieras pudiera contribuir a mitigar algo los riesgos para la estabilidad de precios. Sin embargo, recientemente han aparecido nuevos focos de presiones inflacionistas ligados a la evolucin de los precios del petrleo y de los alimentos que han motivado ya en octubre un repunte de las tasas de variacin del IAPC. Los precios del crudo se encuentran, de hecho, en niveles cercanos a sus mximos histricos. Adems, los precios de los alimentos no elaborados han experimentado una notable aceleracin, lo que puede reflejar las presiones de demanda a nivel global, pero seguramente responde tambin a las desfavorables condiciones de oferta derivadas de la evolucin meteorolgica en algunas reas geogrficas. Es cierto que en el pasado reciente hemos asistido a fuertes elevaciones de los precios del crudo sin que ello haya comportado incrementos sustanciales de las demandas salariales y la inflacin subyacente. Sin embargo, la acumulacin de dichos incrementos puede terminar desencadenando procesos de propagacin que hagan ms persistente el rebrote de la inflacin. Este riesgo, adems, puede verse acrecentado en el contexto actual de limitada holgura en los mercados de trabajo del rea. La coincidencia en el tiempo de los efectos de la perturbacin financiera y los movimientos que subyacen a este rebrote inflacionista ha introducido una mayor complejidad en la toma de decisiones de poltica monetaria. La incertidumbre acerca de los efectos de las turbulencias ha llevado al Consejo de Gobierno del BCE a detener el proceso de retirada gradual del estmulo monetario que haba venido llevando a cabo de manera progresiva desde finales de 2005, manteniendo sin cambios los tipos de inters en las tres reuniones celebradas entre septiembre y noviembre. Al mismo tiempo, sin embargo, el Consejo de Gobierno ha llamado la atencin sobre el aumento de los riesgos inflacionistas a medio plazo y ha reiterado su pleno compromiso a actuar, cuando y cuanto sea preciso, para asegurar que las expectativas de inflacin permanecen ancladas slidamente en niveles coherentes con la estabilidad de precios. Permtanme ahora que me centre en los aspectos ms destacados de la evolucin reciente de la economa espaola. Desde que comparec en esta misma Cmara, hace ahora casi dos meses, el diagnstico sobre las perspectivas a corto plazo de la economa espaola no se ha modificado sustancialmente. Como indica la informacin que acaba de publicar el INE referida al tercer trimestre, la economa espaola continu la senda de gradual desaceleracin de la actividad que haba iniciado en el segundo, situando el crecimiento interanual del PIB en el 3,8%, frente a tasas en el entorno del 4% en la primera mitad del ejercicio. A lo largo de este perodo prosigui la suave moderacin de la demanda interna, reflejando el proceso de normalizacin de las condiciones monetarias iniciado hace casi dos aos, as como la mejora de la aportacin de la demanda exterior neta al crecimiento, ante un entorno exterior que ha continuado siendo favorable. En conjunto, ello ha permitido nuevos avances hacia una composicin ms equilibrada entre las fuentes internas y externas del gasto y, dentro de la demanda interna, que la inversin empresarial haya ganado peso frente al gasto de las familias, sobre todo en su componente de inversin residencial. El consumo de los hogares ha continuado el proceso de moderacin gradual que inici hace unos trimestres, aunque dentro de una pauta de dinamismo que se apoya en la expansin de la poblacin y en la solidez del empleo. Esta evolucin refleja la normal adaptacin de las familias a unas condiciones monetarias y financieras menos holgadas y la menor intensidad de la revalorizacin de la riqueza, dada la atenuacin de los incrementos de los precios de la vivienda. La inversin residencial, por su parte, est moderando su ritmo de avance de forma algo ms marcada, prolongando la pauta de desaceleracin gradual que viene mostrando desde principios de 2006, en respuesta tambin al aumento de los tipos de inters y las menores expectativas de revalorizacin de precios de los inmuebles, a pesar de que el dinamismo demogrfico tiende a limitar el efecto de estos dos factores sobre la demanda de vivienda. El menor impulso del gasto y el encarecimiento de la financiacin estn propiciando una contencin en la demanda de crdito de los hogares y una ralentizacin de sus ratio de endeudamiento en trminos de la renta disponible. En conjunto, la tasa de ahorro de las familias volvi a moderarse en la primera parte del ao y sus necesidades de financiacin se mantuvieron estables en trminos del PIB, pero es posible que el cambio en las condiciones financieras conduzca a una estabilizacin de la tasa de ahorro en el futuro. El gasto de las empresas mantuvo, por su parte, una tnica de fortaleza, aunque en los meses centrales del ejercicio dio muestras de una leve desaceleracin. Destaca, en particular, la pujanza de la inversin en equipo en una situacin de elevada rentabilidad tanto presente como esperada y de favorables expectativas de negocio. En los ltimos meses, el recurso a la financiacin ajena de las empresas empez a reflejar el endurecimiento relativo de las condiciones financieras, observndose una ligera inflexin en el ritmo de endeudamiento as como un incipiente cambio de composicin segn su finalidad, pudindose apreciar una desaceleracin de los fondos dirigidos a financiar actividades inmobiliarias y de construccin, frente a un incremento de los destinados a empresas industriales y a las actividades de servicios. La demanda exterior neta ha seguido contribuyendo a amortiguar el impacto de la desaceleracin del gasto sobre el crecimiento, debido a un comportamiento de las exportaciones ms dinmico que el de las compras al exterior, particularmente acusado en el tercer trimestre. Pese a ello, el ritmo de avance de las ventas al exterior en lo que va de ao est siendo algo inferior al del ejercicio previo, en un contexto en el que los mercados de exportacin estn mostrando un comportamiento algo menos expansivo y en el que la apreciacin del tipo de cambio del euro podra estar afectando, en alguna medida, a las ventas extracomunitarias. A pesar de que la evolucin de la cotizacin del euro est contribuyendo a abaratar las compras en el exterior, las importaciones de bienes estn creciendo menos que el ao precedente, en coherencia con la suave desaceleracin que muestra la demanda final. Con todo, el dficit comercial ha seguido aumentando, aunque a ritmos ms reducidos que en el pasado y las necesidades de financiacin de la nacin tambin han continuado incrementndose a ritmos ms atenuados. Por el lado de la oferta, la suave desaceleracin del PIB refleja, principalmente, una cierta prdida de dinamismo en el sector de la construccin mientras que la industria sigui dando muestras de fortaleza, si bien de forma algo ms contenida a lo largo del tercer trimestre. El empleo se ha ido ajustando a la evolucin de la actividad, observndose, a partir del segundo trimestre, una pequea reduccin en el ritmo de generacin de empleo, tambin algo ms acusado en el sector de la construccin. Y todo ello en un contexto poblacional que ha continuado siendo muy dinmico, aspecto que, desde una perspectiva temporal ms amplia, ha sido crucial para que la actividad se fuera ajustando al dinamismo de la demanda, evitando que se generaran presiones de costes y precios excesivas a lo largo de la prolongada fase de expansin que ha vivido la economa espaola. Los costes laborales a lo largo del presente ejercicio estn siguiendo una trayectoria de moderacin, con crecimientos algo inferiores a los del ao previo, que se est trasladando a los costes laborales unitarios, dado el repunte de la productividad. Desafortunadamente, en cambio, los precios de consumo estn teniendo un comportamiento menos favorable en estos ltimos meses, como consecuencia de las importantes elevaciones de los precios del crudo y de los precios de las materias primas alimenticias en los mercados internacionales. Este impacto negativo se est produciendo adems cuando el IPC empezaba a repuntar como consecuencia de un efecto base, asociado al comportamiento del precio del petrleo en la primera mitad de 2006. En este contexto, la tasa interanual de ndice de precios de consumo se elev en octubre hasta el 3,6% y el diferencial de inflacin con la UEM aument hasta 1 pp, desde el mnimo de 0,5 pp alcanzado en verano. Si bien la inflacin subyacente permanece en niveles similares a los de la primera mitad del ejercicio, el incremento de las presiones inflacionistas, aunque tenga un carcter transitorio, aumenta el riesgo de su propagacin al conjunto de la economa, particularmente como consecuencia de la existencia de mecanismos y prcticas de indiciacin en la fijacin de precios y rentas. Un cierre del ao corriente como el que acabo de describir permite dibujar un escenario macroeconmico para 2008 que, en sus lneas bsicas, no debera diferir sustancialmente del que proyectaba el Banco de Espaa en las previsiones que publicamos la pasada primavera y en las que, como se recordar, se contemplaba una aproximacin gradual del PIB hacia tasas de crecimiento en el entorno del 3 %. Es cierto, sin embargo, que estas proyecciones descansan en el supuesto razonable de que las turbulencias tengan una duracin limitada, tal y como recogen la mayora de previsiones realizadas despus del verano para la economa mundial por los principales organismos internacionales. Tiene inters repasar los factores que sustentan un escenario de desaceleracin suave para la economa espaola en 2008, compatible con el mantenimiento de un elevado dinamismo de la actividad y el empleo. Por una parte, la normalizacin del tono de la poltica monetaria debe facilitar un ajuste suave hacia ritmos de gasto y de endeudamiento del sector privado ms sostenibles en el medio plazo. Por otra, cabe esperar que el mercado inmobiliario contine evolucionando segn las pautas que ha seguido hasta ahora, esto es, con una desaceleracin gradual del precio de la vivienda y un ajuste suave de la demanda, que seguira estando apoyada por el elevado ritmo de crecimiento de la poblacin. Adems, aunque probablemente ser difcil mantener ritmos de expansin de la inversin empresarial y de la inversin en construccin no residencial tan intensos como los de los ltimos trimestres, las perspectivas de evolucin de ambos componentes de gasto siguen siendo tambin favorables. En todo caso, parece difcil que la inversin productiva pueda compensar, por si misma, la menor aportacin del gasto de las familias. Por ello, como ya seal durante mi ltima comparecencia en esta misma Cmara, el papel de la demanda exterior neta resulta crucial para compatibilizar una cierta contencin del gasto con el mantenimiento de ritmos de crecimiento en el entorno del 3%. Como hemos podido ver en estos ltimos aos, la contribucin de esta variable al crecimiento depende estrechamente del comportamiento de nuestros mercados de exportacin pero tambin de la competitividad de nuestra produccin. Por ello, un escenario de recuperacin de las exportaciones netas como el que acabo de describir requiere la continuidad en la mejora de la competitividad de las empresas espaolas, en respuesta a los cambios del comercio mundial a raz de la entrada de nuevos y potentes competidores. Al mismo tiempo, el menor empuje de la demanda final debera materializarse en una cierta ralentizacin de las importaciones, disminuyendo la filtracin de gasto hacia el exterior. En el mbito interno, el mantenimiento del dinamismo del empleo y la normalizacin gradual del mercado inmobiliario resultan fundamentales para el sostenimiento de las expectativas de renta y, en consecuencia, de los planes de gasto de los agentes dentro de una pauta de desaceleracin suave. Ya he dado los argumentos que facilitan un ajuste ordenado del mercado inmobiliario. En cuanto a la respuesta del empleo, existen indicios de que en estos ltimos aos se han producido mejoras en el funcionamiento global del mercado de trabajo que estn detrs de la enorme capacidad de la economa espaola para generar empleo y que deben continuar en el futuro. En todo caso, la vuelta a pautas ms normales en el sector de la construccin y la elevada incidencia de este sector en el comportamiento del empleo atribuyen gran importancia a la existencia de un grado de flexibilidad suficiente en el funcionamiento de la economa que facilite la reasignacin de recursos hacia las actividades industriales y los servicios que han de tomar el relevo, dando continuidad al cambio de composicin del producto que se ha producido en los ltimos trimestres. La mejor contribucin que las polticas econmicas pueden prestar en una situacin como la actual, de suave desaceleracin y aumento de la incertidumbre, consiste en garantizar el compromiso con la estabilidad presupuestaria y profundizar en las polticas estructurales orientadas a reequilibrar las fuentes del crecimiento. El Proyecto de Presupuestos Generales del Estado apunta a la consecucin de un supervit en 2007 del 1,3% en las cuentas del conjunto de las Administraciones Pblicas. La informacin disponible sobre la ejecucin presupuestaria en lo que va de ao parece sugerir, no obstante, que el saldo positivo al concluir el mismo puede ser ms elevado que la ltima previsin oficial y de magnitud similar a la del ao anterior. Como en ejercicios pasados, estos resultados, mejores que los previstos inicialmente, se deberan a una favorable evolucin de los ingresos impositivos, principalmente de los impuestos directos, en un contexto de un crecimiento econmico tambin superior al previsto. En cuanto al ejercicio 2008, el Proyecto de Presupuestos Generales del Estado sita el objetivo de supervit de las Administraciones Pblicas en el 0,9%. Esta cifra cumple con los compromisos europeos derivados del Pacto de Estabilidad y Crecimiento y respeta los objetivos de estabilidad presupuestaria fijados por las Cmaras del Congreso y del Senado en junio de 2007, en cumplimiento con lo establecido en la nuevas Leyes de Estabilidad Presupuestarias, que entran precisamente en vigor por primera vez en el ejercicio 2008. La programada reduccin del supervit se basara en algunas medidas de recorte de impuestos, mientras que, por el lado del gasto, el Proyecto de Presupuestos fija una tasa de crecimiento para el Estado en lnea con la evolucin esperada del PIB nominal, lo que supone cumplir estrictamente con el lmite que se estableci en junio en el contexto tambin de las provisiones de la Ley de Estabilidad Presupuestaria. Debe tenerse en cuenta que, como seal con anterioridad, los objetivos marcados estn basados en una previsin de cierre del ao 2007 muy prudente por el lado de los ingresos. Cabe pensar que si se produjera un resultado en las cifras de recaudacin del ao 2007 ms holgado que el previsto en el Avance de Liquidacin de los Presupuestos, este mejor registro se debera trasladar a la previsin presupuestaria para 2008 y permitir, por tanto, la consecucin de un supervit tambin ms elevado.
