Gracias al esfuerzo conjunto de todos hemos sido capaces de desemper satisfactoriamente, un a ms, las tareas que esta instituci tiene encomendadas. Estoy seguro de que ese mismo espritu de trabajo en com nos permitir afrontar con xito los importantes retos que tenemos por delante.

Title: The international dimension of the Spanish banking sector. Closing conference of the course organized by the Association of Economic Information Journalists at the Menndez Pelayo International University
text: Santander, 20 June 2008 The international dimension of the Spanish banking system Closing conference of the course organized by the Association of Journalists of Ecological Information (APIE) at the Men8endez Pelayo International University Jose Vils Deputy Governor of Banco de Espa I would like to thank the Association of Journalists of Ecological Information and the Men8endez Pelayo International University for their invitation to deliver this closing conference at a Meeting that, after year, proposes topics for debate of remarkable topicality and of special relevance for the Spanish economy, its development potential and its future prospects. "The international expansion of the Spanish company", the theme of this summer's call, responds in its formulation to the growing external dimension of our companies and the challenge posed by their participation in increasingly integrated, efficient and mature markets. A review of the program of the course and the list of prestigious speakers who have preceded me reveals that during these four days both the process of internationalization of the industrial and commercial company and the expansion abroad of the Spanish financial sector have been extensively addressed. Both processes share common characteristics and respond to similar motivations of shareholders and managers, but also present some specific features that explain the different rhythm that, with a historical perspective, we can appreciate in the degree of international penetration of both sectors. In the case of non-financial enterprises, the beginning of this process can be placed in 1986. In that year, with the entry of Spain into the European Union, the long period of international isolation of the Spanish economy is definitively concluded, although direct investments abroad were at first very moderate and only reached greater relevance as the Spanish company modernized and focused its objectives on new markets. Spanish banks had to wait another decade to begin their expansion abroad. On the way in which the international dimension of Spanish banking has been configured and the supervisory implications of this process, my reflections today will turn. * * * * Currently, around 22% of the consolidated assets of our banking system are abroad, a very significant figure if we take into account that this percentage is highly concentrated in the two large Spanish groups. Although the entities of our country had previously made some investments in other geographical areas, in general through the opening of branches or subsidiaries to serve the Spanish population resident abroad or Spanish companies in their foreign trade activities, it is not until the mid-nineties when the main banks implement expansion strategies in other markets that make them play, for the first time in their history, a relevant role in the international financial panorama. This process of expansion is then directed almost exclusively towards Latin America. Several factors help to understand why it was at that time and why towards that geographical area. After the crisis affecting the Spanish banking sector between 1978 and 1985, the priority shared between the bankers and the authorities was the consolidation of a strong and stable banking system. Improvements in management systems, in the training of managers and in the regulatory and supervisory framework made it possible to complete this process in a relatively short time. From 1988 onwards, major mergers began between the largest Spanish banks, with the uni of Banco de Bilbao and Banco de Vizcaya. This process continues over the following decade, in which the banking sector of our country is reaching the solidity, size and confidence sufficient to open up to the outside. The Spanish entities had at that time two important stimuli. On the one hand, mergers brought with them the availability of a high number of managers with high capacity and qualifications, who are well suited to pilot acquisition operations. And on the other hand, Spanish banking had specialized in a specific business model, that of retail banking, in which it had achieved a high degree of experience and quality, developing forms of relationship with customers that could be valid in other markets. The mid-nineties was, therefore, the opportune date. With regard to the objective of investments, the choice of Spanish bank managers was clear: Latin America, a region that exerted the following attraction factors on Spanish institutions: a5 An economic situation that had experienced a clear improvement in its fundamentals a5 The suitability of the retail banking business model for the characteristics of the countries of the area a5 The wide financial margins with which it operated a5 And the comparative advantage provided by cultural and language affinities However, the process was not without significant risks, and proof of this was, for example, the Argentine crisis at the end of the last century. From the first half of the nineties onwards, a series of important purchases of Spanish banks in Latin America took place in a very relevant process both for the Spanish groups and for the financial systems of these countries. The investment of Spanish banks abroad undertook new routes at the beginning of this century: the most relevant acquisition in Europe, in the United Kingdom, dates from 2004, although before that there had already been some significant acquisition in Portugal. Since then, other important operations have been carried out in countries such as Germany and there have also been some other frustrated approaches. After the Latin American experience, the time had come for expansion in Europe. On the one hand, Spanish banking had laid the foundations to try to participate successfully in the most competitive European markets, as a result of the experience gained after several operations in Latin America, the improvement of efficiency, which had continued at a good pace, and the international prestige achieved by the Spanish banking sector. On the other hand, the specialized management of the risks of the most complex groups required an adequate geographical diversification of investments abroad. And finally, the fusi operations or acquisition at European level was but the corollary of progress in European convergence and measures to strengthen an ICO financial market. The most recent stage, in which some purchases have continued to be made in Latin America and Europe, is also characterized by the incorporation of a new geographical objective: since 2005, important acquisitions have been made in the United States, and the most vigorous economies in Asia are also in the focus of attention of our entities. * * * * Already with a certain historical perspective, we can conclude that the process of expansion of Spanish banks abroad is proving very satisfactory. In my view, there are three reasons for this. In the first place, the sequence of ideas for the correct internationalization of any economy emerging from a protectionist phase has been respected: liberalization and trade openness, first; and liberalization of capital movements and direct investment thereafter, once the domestic financial system has become sound. Secondly, the conception of the process on the part of the managers of the Spanish banks has been correct. The operations undertaken have always been based on a clear business logic, avoiding any speculative temptation in favour of the basic principle of bank risk management: prudence. The strategies developed have focused on extending in other countries the business model that constitutes its specialty, retail banking, renouncing the introduction in more volatile market segments that a priori could have been considered more complementary, such as investment banking activity. Thirdly, as is the case, Banco de Espa has also applied high standards in authorising and assessing these operations, ensuring that they do not adversely affect the group's financial situation or management capacity, and ensuring that both the effective individual supervision of the subsidiary and the supervision of the group as a whole are ensured. These ideas also explain why, so far, it has been only the two largest Spanish banking groups that have been almost exclusive protagonists of the acquisitions that we have been discussing. Thus, at the end of 2007, 97% of the total assets abroad of the Spanish banking system were on the balance sheets of both groups. In any case, it should be noted that some operations have already been carried out by other entities and that new projects are being addressed, which will always be assessed by the Bank of Spain applying uniform criteria regardless of the type of credit institution that promotes the initiative, whether it is a bank or a savings bank. I would like to dwell briefly on some of these criteria, which relate to the entities themselves. I think it is important to mention that any expansion strategy in the international market must be preceded by a prior extension of the business in Spain. The assumption of more complex risks or in different jurisdictions that present local peculiarities is a process that has to be approached in a staggered manner, from the simplest to the most sophisticated, from the most primal to the most differentiated, without jumps that add uncertainties about its viability in the short, medium and long term. In turn, the financial capacity of an entity that develops an international expansion strategy is a key element to gauge its chances of success. It is not only a question of proving purchasing power, but of having a clear strategy in the short, medium and long term on the business model to be developed, on its impact on the generation of profits and on the mechanisms established to mitigate both the most typical risks of the banking business and those derived from participation in foreign markets. At the same time, it is necessary to have an appropriate management capacity, based on the absence of any type of agreements that hinder the effective exercise of control. The integration of the investee in the entity's own circuits, the displacement of expert personnel, the incorporation of the acquired subsidiary into the internal audit plans, or the progress towards the application of internal risk management models for regulatory purposes, are some elements that allow an objective analysis of the degree of management capacity available. By this point, I would like to recall the importance of the acquiring entity being subject to appropriate market discipline, capable of contributing to appropriate external control and assessment of the evolution of the business. In the case of savings banks, as the Bank of Spain has already stated on other occasions, this discipline can be achieved through various methods. So far, the fmulas that some savings banks have proposed have been the issuance of participatory quotas or the listing of shares of a subsidiary holding company with significant weight in all the consolidated statements. * * * * Another noteworthy aspect of the process of international expansion of the Spanish banking system refers to the supervisory implications. The Bank of Spain, in the 2001 Supervisory Report, presented some recommendations on the management of groups with an international presence. Next, I will refer to some of the most relevant points in relation to this question. Firstly, the new risks involved in participating in markets that are less close and with new levels of complexity require sufficient capitalisation, for which it is necessary to strengthen the amount and quality of own resources within the group and to ensure their distribution according to risks. Secondly, an adequate level of transparency and financial autonomy must be achieved. On the basis of a rational dominance structure, each subsidiary is an active participant in its country's financial system that has to demonstrate its ability to effectively finance its activity and independently cover its risks in the market. Thirdly, effective risk management systems adapted to the group's new international projection must be put in place. This requires the definition of common high-level criteria on organisation, management and internal information systems, within which each subsidiary is able to individually manage the risks of its activity. Fourthly, in the field of internal control, it is advisable to establish a culture of effective control both in the group and in each of its units, together with an independent internal audit that covers the entire perimeter of consolidation and strengthens the performance in each unit of the group of local internal audit services. In the field of liquidity management control, each banking subsidiary must have a system of continuous measurement of its own liquidity, both in local currency and in other currencies, and design contingency plans to deal with possible extraordinary situations. The presence abroad of a country's banks also implies the need to deepen relations between the supervisors of the different entities of the group. In this respect, the division of responsibilities laid down in 1977 in the Basel Committee's so-called "Concordat", according to which the individual supervision of the credit institution is the responsibility of the supervisory authority of the country which granted the licence and the supervision of the group on a consolidated basis by the supervisory authority of the country of the parent company, remains valid. However, once the legal terms for the division of competences have been established, it is necessary to establish the bases for effective collaboration between the different supervisory authorities involved and to guarantee exchanges of information that allow the best performance of the respective functions. To this end, Banco de Espa has signed cooperation agreements with 9 countries in the Americas, 7 European countries and one Asian country. Their scam, with Puerto Rico, was signed just last week. Also last week, the incorporation into Spanish law of the new regulatory framework for the capital of credit institutions, known as Basel II, was completed with the publication in the BOE of the Bank of Spain's circular on this matter. The new framework brings advantages that, in the case of international banking groups, are particularly palpable, since it incorporates greater sensitivity to risk, recognition of the most advanced management systems and the need for its own systems of self-assessment of capital. After the first phase of implementation of the so-called IRB models by the Spanish groups with management systems better adapted to the new regulations, the basic criteria that the Bank of Spain will apply in relation to future applications are the following: the entities will have to maintain prior contacts with the Bank of Spain to evaluate the real situation of the models and the reasonableness of their approaches, since the models submitted will have to be actually used at the time of the application and must have adequate and contrasted levels of quality and control; the formal application and the information that must accompany it will follow the specific formats established by the Bank of Spain, with complete documentation that allows the models to be validated; The formal validation process, which will last six months, will start from that moment. In this second phase, the same methodology that has been used so far will be applied to the validation processes, whose duration will already be less than that required by the revision of the first models, and the Bank of Spain will continue to work on the issuance and updating of guides or specific validation documents to facilitate the knowledge by the entities of the criteria used. The implementation of common rules governing banking activity in a very large number of countries, such as Basel II (or its predecessor, Basel I, of 1988) is the response of international regulators to the phenomenon of the internationalization of business and banking in the world, and is part of a broad set of global initiatives. Some of these are highly developed, such as the unification of financial reporting criteria within the framework of international accounting standards, while others are in the study and development phase, such as proposals in different areas developed by different international forums, including the recent recommendations of the Financial Stability Forum. The phenomenon of financial internationalization has, of course, a European dimension of its own, which means that within the framework of the institutions of the European Union a broad process of reflection and debate is also being addressed on how to deal more efficiently with the processes of convergence in regulation and supervisory practices, and coordination between supervisors. It is both a question of responding to the phenomenon of the growing integration in Europe in the retail banking sector, and of promoting this process. The debate is broad and is aimed at the many facets of the structure of financial supervision, with the aim of also deepening the most appropriate schemes for the treatment of crises of entities that are part of groups at European level. In this sense, on June 1, the new cooperation agreement on international financial stability was signed between the financial supervisory authorities, central banks and finance ministers of the European Union, which addresses, among other issues, such relevant aspects as the common principles of transnational financial crisis management, cooperation agreements, forms of activation of procedures and responsibilities in a crisis, exchange of information and coordinated transparency of information. This is one of the steps being taken in the direction of ensuring that the exercise by the supervisory authorities of each country of their respective competences takes into account the European dimension of the main banking groups on the continent and is exercised with a perspective that goes beyond national limits. * * * * I would like to devote the last few minutes of my speech to commenting on a few aspects relating to the disturbances in the international financial markets, which began last summer and are still continuing. These disturbances are, in my opinion, the first important test for the new international financial system that has been brewing in recent years, in line with the processes of financial innovation and the increasing globalization of markets. In the origin and development of turbulence, both novel and other more traditional features can be appreciated. Among the first, the fact that the epicenter of the turbulence has been located in the US, the main world economy, stands out and that the problems have moved very quickly to other latitudes, especially to the main European countries, as a result of the globalization of financial markets and the opening of new channels through which risk circulates. At this time, the transfer of risks has occurred through the bundling of the original loans through securitization vehicles and other complex structures in which acquirers from distant geographical areas have ended up investing. Among the most traditional features of the current financial turmoil, the most remarkable thing is that its origin is in the relaxation of criteria in the granting of mortgage loans in the United States, with the application of unwise credit policies, this being a typical factor of generating difficulties in banking systems. In general, risk transfer mechanisms have a great capacity to provide stability to the financial system, since they allow originator banks to manage their own resources needs, help diversify liquidity sources and make it possible for the risks granted to be finally assumed by other agents, distributing them more widely. But misuse of risk transfer mechanisms also makes them potentially harmful. Current circumstances have shown that the risks were not as dispersed as assumed, as the transmission that had taken place was often more nominal than effective. In addition, pockets of vulnerability were being created where risk accumulated: for example, in vehicles that structured complex operations, which were often financing short-term positions in the short term, and generating high liquidity commitments for banks providing emergency lines. In these cases, the complexity and lack of transparency have made it difficult to diagnose the situation in time and have favored that, in many cases, the risks ended up in the hands of investors less prepared to understand, value and manage them. Financial innovation processes are profound phenomena that cannot be reversed, since they contribute very positively to the improvement of efficiency in the allocation of capital and to economic growth in the medium and long term. But innovations sometimes include spurious instruments that propose, through opaque mechanisms, combinations of risk and return that are far from the real level of risk. For this reason, innovations are periodically tested by the market to, in a process analogous to that of natural selection, identify the novelties that deserve to survive in the future because they involve sustainable and efficient improvements, those that have to modify some of their elements to be viable, and those that will end up in oblivion. Now, for example, certain facets of the banking business model known as "originate to distribute" and more sophisticated structured financial products are going through such a process. The current episode shows us that in an increasingly complex world, in which internationalization and innovation simultaneously provide opportunities and risks, it is a priority that credit institutions engage in a process of permanent improvement that allows them to properly identify and understand the risks, both traditional and new, as well as the implementation of prudent management and control systems. For their part, regulators and supervisors also have to respond actively to the phenomenon of innovation, adapting our systems and standards to the reality of each moment, with the ability to anticipate and apply corrective measures to practices that may hinder financial stability. And, in the presence of transnational groups, international cooperation needs to be turned into a pillar of supervision. The most recent initiatives of the Basel Committee or the Financial Stability Forum are in this direction. It is true that Spanish credit institutions have been absent from the most uncertain phenomena of the current situation: their banking model has focused on traditional financial intermediation, both in Spain and abroad; they have not entered the "originate to distribute" business, and therefore have not had inadequate incentives to relax their lending policies; nor have they developed structured products whose complexity would make it difficult to understand and assess risks, because Spanish securitisations have been characterised by simplicity and high quality; nor have they invested in complex structured products. In addition, the management of credit institutions has been supported by a framework of accounting regulation and demanding solvency, which has led to a prudent valuation of assets and risks as well as the accumulation of provisions to cover losses in the downward phase of the cycle. But Spanish banks are not, of course, immune to the indirect effects that financial shocks are bringing about: first, disruption in the functioning of international private money and bond markets; and, secondly, its harmful impact on global economic growth, which coincides with the end of the long shock wave that the Spanish economy has gone through and which, therefore, complicates the adjustment process in our country. From now on, it is to be hoped that financial resources will no longer be available on international markets at reduced cost, with the risk premiums so little penalizing that had been accepted in the previous situation. Above all, the evolution of the banking business in Spain cannot be expected to continue at the pace of the past, since it must be accompanied by considerably lower nominal GDP growth rates. Therefore, it is necessary for entities to update their business plans and adapt them to the present circumstances, especially in those cases in which a greater specialization had been chosen in the financing of residential investment, the sector of activity most affected at the moment. In defining their strategies, it will also be important to seek a rebalancing between their sources of financing and their assets, taking into account current market conditions. Likewise, managers need to find new ways to efficiency, which compensate for the foreseeable lasting increase in financing costs, which are difficult to transfer automatically to customers, by controlling expenditure and rationalizing the structures, systems and processes that channel banking activity. The search for efficiency is undoubtedly a basic principle of business management, but it is even more so at a time when the growth of profitability based on turnover is no longer a realistic possibility, and in which the increase in NPL ratios will exert a greater pressure on the margins and profits of the entities. At the moment, as always, it is necessary for Spanish institutions to maintain the quality of their management systems, both to adequately protect their activity in Spain and to establish their growing presence in other geographical markets, and to maintain the necessary balance between policies for the assumption of new risks and the implementation of strict control mechanisms. And, by surprise, no one escapes the fact that due to the new economic and financial circumstances, both institutions and supervisors have to carry out our work in an increasingly demanding environment, with less margin for error and with more need to develop prudent, preventive and effective approaches. Thanks a lot.
text_original: Santander, 20 de junio de 2008 La dimensi internacional del sistema bancario espal Conferencia de clausura del curso organizado por la Asociaci de Periodistas de Informaci Econica (APIE) en la Universidad Internacional Menndez Pelayo Jos Vils Subgobernador del Banco de Espa Quisiera agradecer a la Asociaci de Periodistas de Informaci Econica y a la Universidad Internacional Menndez Pelayo su invitacin para pronunciar esta conferencia de clausura en un Encuentro que, a tras ao, propone temas para el debate de notable actualidad y de especial relevancia para la economa espala, su potencial de desarrollo y sus perspectivas de futuro. La expansin internacional de la empresa espala, el tema de la convocatoria de este verano, responde en su formulacin a la creciente dimensin exterior de nuestras empresas y al reto que supone su participaci en mercados cada vez ms integrados, eficientes y maduros. Un repaso al programa del curso y a la lista de prestigiosos ponentes que me han precedido revela que durante estos cuatro das se han abordado extensamente tanto el proceso de internacionalizaci de la empresa industrial y comercial como la expansin en el exterior del sector financiero espal. Ambos procesos comparten caractersticas comunes y responden a anlogas motivaciones de los accionistas y gestores, pero tambin presentan algunos rasgos especficos que explican el diferente ritmo que, con perspectiva histica, podemos apreciar en el grado de penetracin internacional de uno y otro sector. En el caso de la empresa no financiera el inicio de este proceso puede situarse en 1986. En ese ao, con la entrada de Espa en la Uni Europea se da definitivamente por concluido el largo perodo de aislamiento internacional de la economa espala, si bien las inversiones directas en el exterior fueron al principio muy moderadas y slo alcanzaron mayor relevancia a medida que la empresa espala se modernizy enfocsus objetivos hacia nuevos mercados. La banca espala hubo de esperar todava una dcada ms hasta dar comienzo a su expansin en el exterior. Sobre la forma en que se ha ido configurando la dimensin internacional de la banca espala y las implicaciones supervisoras de este proceso van a girar mis reflexiones de hoy. * * * * Actualmente en torno al 22% de los activos consolidados de nuestro sistema bancario se encuentra en el exterior, una cifra muy significativa si se tiene en cuenta que este porcentaje est muy concentrado en los dos grandes grupos espales. Aunque las entidades de nuestro pas haban realizado anteriormente algunas inversiones en otras zonas geogrficas, en general mediante la apertura de sucursales o filiales para dar servicio a la poblaci espaola residente en el extranjero o a las empresas espaolas en sus actividades de comercio exterior, no es hasta mediados de los aos noventa cuando los principales bancos ponen en prctica estrategias de expansi en otros mercados que les hacen jugar, por primera vez en su historia, un papel relevante en el panorama financiero internacional. Este proceso de expansi se dirige entonces casi exclusivamente hacia Amrica Latina. Diversos factores ayudan a comprender por qu fue en ese momento y por qu hacia esa zona geogrfica. Tras la crisis que afectal sector bancario espal entre 1978 y 1985 la prioridad compartida entre los banqueros y las autoridades fue la consolidacin de un sistema bancario fuerte y estable. Las mejoras en los sistemas de gesti, en la capacitacin de los administradores y en el marco de regulacin y supervisin permitieron culminar este proceso en un tiempo relativamente breve. A partir de 1988 se inician las grandes fusiones entre los mayores bancos espales, con la uni del Banco de Bilbao y el Banco de Vizcaya. Este proceso contina a lo largo de la dcada siguiente, en la que el sector bancario de nuestro pas va alcanzado la solidez, el tama y la confianza suficientes para abrirse al exterior. Las entidades espalas contaban en ese momento con dos estmulos importantes. De una parte, las fusiones trajeron consigo la disponibilidad de un nero elevado de gestores de alta capacidad y cualificacin, ideos para pilotar las operaciones de adquisicin. Y de otra, la banca espala se haba especializado en un modelo concreto de negocio, el de banca minorista, en el que haba alcanzado un alto grado de experiencia y calidad, desarrollando formas de relacin con la clientela que podan ser vlidas en otros mercados. Mediados de los as noventa era, por lo tanto, la fecha oportuna. Por lo que se refiere al objetivo de las inversiones, la elecci de los gestores bancarios espales fue clara: Amrica Latina, una regi que ejerca sobre las entidades espalas los siguientes factores de atraccin:  Una situacin econica que haba experimentado una clara mejora en sus fundamentos  La idoneidad del modelo de negocio de banca al por menor espal para las caractersticas de los pases de la zona  Los amplios mrgenes financieros con que se operaba  Y la ventaja comparativa aportada por las afinidades culturales y de idioma No obstante, el proceso no estaba exento de riesgos significativos, y prueba de ello fue, por ejemplo, la crisis Argentina de fin del siglo pasado. A partir de la primera mitad de los as noventa se sucediuna serie de compras importantes de la banca espala en Latinoamrica en un proceso muy relevante tanto para los grupos espales como para los sistemas financieros de estos pases. La inversin de la banca espala en el exterior emprendinuevas rutas en los comienzos del presente siglo: la adquisicin ms relevante en Europa, en el Reino Unido, data de 2004, aunque antes ya se haba producido alguna adquisici significativa en Portugal. A partir de entonces se realizan otras operaciones importantes en pases como Alemania y se producen tambin algunos otros acercamientos frustrados. Tras la experiencia latinoamericana, haba llegado el momento de la expansi en Europa. Por un lado, la banca espala haba sentado las bases para intentar participar con xito en los mercados europeos ms competitivos, como consecuencia de la experiencia ganada tras varios as de operaciones en Latinoamrica, de la mejora de la eficiencia, que haba continuado a buen ritmo, y del prestigio internacional logrado por el sector bancario espal. Por otro lado, la gesti especializada de los riesgos de los grupos ms complejos demandaba una adecuada diversificacin geogrfica de las inversiones en el exterior. Y, finalmente, las operaciones de fusi o adquisici en el mbito europeo no eran sino el corolario de los avances en la convergencia europea y de las medidas para potenciar un mercado financiero ico. La etapa ms reciente, en la que han continuado realizndose algunas compras en Amrica Latina y en Europa, se caracteriza tambin por la incorporacin de un nuevo objetivo geogrfico: desde 2005 se vienen realizando adquisiciones importantes en Estados Unidos, y las economas ms vigorosas de Asia estn tambin en el foco de atencin de nuestras entidades. * * * * Ya con una cierta perspectiva histica, podemos concluir que el proceso de expansin de la banca espaola en el exterior est resultando muy satisfactorio. A mi juicio, hay tres razones que lo explican. En primer lugar, se ha respetado la secuencia idea para la correcta internacionalizacin de cualquier economa que sale de una fase proteccionista: liberalizaci y apertura comercial, primero; y liberalizaci de los movimientos de capitales y de las inversiones directas despus, una vez que el sistema financiero nacional ha adquirido la solidez necesaria. En segundo lugar, la concepci del proceso por parte de los gestores de la banca espala ha sido acertada. Las operaciones emprendidas se han fundamentado siempre en una lgica empresarial clara, evitando toda tentaci especulativa en beneficio del principio bsico de la gesti de riesgos bancarios: la prudencia. Las estrategias desarrolladas se han enfocado a extender en otros pases el modelo de negocio que constituye su especialidad, la banca minorista, renunciando a la introduccin en segmentos de mercado ms voltiles que a priori podran haberse considerado ms complementarios, como la actividad de banca de inversi. En tercer lugar, como es lgico, el Banco de Espa tambin ha aplicado criterios exigentes en la autorizacin y valoraci de estas operaciones, asegurndose de que las mismas no afectaran negativamente a la situacin financiera del grupo o a su capacidad de gesti, y cerciorndose de que quedara asegurada tanto la supervisi individual efectiva de la filial como la supervisin del grupo en su conjunto. Estas ideas explican tambin que, hasta el momento, hayan sido so los dos grupos bancarios espales de mayor dimensi los que han sido protagonistas casi exclusivos de las adquisiciones que hemos venido comentando. As, a finales de 2007, el 97% de los activos totales en el exterior del sistema bancario espaol se encontraba en los balances de ambos grupos. En todo caso, hay que destacar que ya se han realizado algunas operaciones por otras entidades y que se estn abordando nuevos proyectos, que siempre sern valorados por el Banco de Espaa aplicando criterios uniformes con independencia del tipo de entidad de crdito que promueva la iniciativa, ya se trate de un banco o de una caja de ahorros. Quisiera detenerme brevemente en comentar algunos de estos criterios, que se refieren a las propias entidades. Creo que es importante mencionar que cualquier estrategia de expansi en el mercado internacional debe ir precedida de una previa extensi del negocio en Espaa. La asuncin de riesgos ms complejos o en jurisdicciones diferentes que presentan peculiaridades locales es un proceso que tiene que abordarse de forma escalonada, de lo ms sencillo a lo ms sofisticado, de lo ms primo a lo ms diferenciado, sin saltos que aadan incertidumbres sobre su viabilidad a corto, medio y largo plazo. A su vez, la capacidad financiera de una entidad que desarrolla una estrategia de expansi internacional es un elemento clave para calibrar sus posibilidades de xito. No se trata solamente de acreditar la capacidad de compra, sino de disponer de una estrategia clara a corto, medio y largo plazo sobre el modelo de negocio a desarrollar, sobre su impacto en la generaci de beneficios y sobre los mecanismos establecidos para mitigar tanto los riesgos ms tpicos del negocio bancario como los derivados de la participacin en mercados exteriores. Junto a ello, resulta necesario contar con una apropiada capacidad de gesti, sobre la base de la inexistencia de cualquier tipo de acuerdos que supongan una traba al ejercicio efectivo del control. La integracin de la participada en los circuitos propios de la entidad, el desplazamiento de personal experto, la incorporaci de la filial adquirida a los planes de la auditora interna, o el avance hacia la aplicacin de modelos internos de gesti de riesgos a efectos regulatorios, son algunos elementos que permiten un anlisis objetivo del grado de capacidad gerencial disponible. Por timo, quisiera recordar la importancia de que la entidad adquirente est sometida a una adecuada disciplina de mercado, capaz de contribuir a un apropiado control y valoracin externos de la evolucin del negocio. En el caso de las cajas de ahorros, como ya ha sealado el Banco de Espa en otras ocasiones, dicha disciplina puede llegar a alcanzarse mediante fmulas diversas. Hasta el momento, las fmulas que algunas cajas han propuesto han sido la emisi de cuotas participativas o la cotizacin de acciones de una sociedad holding filial con un peso significativo en el conjunto de los estados consolidados. * * * * Otro aspecto destacable del proceso de expansin internacional del sistema bancario espal se refiere a las implicaciones supervisoras. El Banco de Espa, en la Memoria de Supervisin de 2001, expuso algunas recomendaciones sobre la gesti de grupos con presencia internacional. A continuaci, voy a referirme a alguno de los puntos ms relevantes en relaci con esta cuestin. En primer lugar, los nuevos riesgos que implica la participaci en mercados menos cercanos y con nuevos niveles de complejidad exigen contar con una capitalizacin suficiente, para lo que es necesario reforzar el importe y calidad de los recursos propios dentro del grupo y procurar su distribuci en funci de los riesgos. En segundo lugar, ha de lograrse un adecuado nivel de transparencia y autonoma financiera. Sobre la base de una estructura de dominio racional, cada filial es un participante activo en el sistema financiero de su pas que tiene que demostrar su capacidad para financiar autnomamente su actividad y cubrir independientemente sus riesgos en el mercado. En tercer lugar, han de implantarse unos sistemas de gesti del riesgo eficaces y adaptados a la nueva proyeccin internacional del grupo. Para ello se precisa la definicin de unos criterios comunes de alto nivel sobre organizaci, gestin y sistemas de informaci interna, en cuyo marco cada filial sea capaz de gestionar individualmente los riesgos de su actividad. En cuarto lugar, en el mbito del control interno, lo recomendable es establecer una cultura de control efectiva tanto en el grupo como en cada una de sus unidades, junto con una auditora interna independiente que cubra todo el permetro de la consolidaci y refuerce la actuaci en cada unidad del grupo de los servicios locales de auditora interna. En el mbito del control de la gesti de la liquidez, cada filial bancaria ha de contar con un sistema de medicin continua de la propia liquidez, tanto en moneda local como en otras monedas, y disear planes de contingencia para afrontar eventuales situaciones extraordinarias. La presencia en el exterior de la banca de un pas supone tambin la necesidad de profundizar en las relaciones entre los supervisores de las distintas entidades del grupo. A este respecto sigue siendo vlido el reparto de responsabilidades que quedfijado en 1977 en el denominado Concordato del Comit de Basilea, de acuerdo con el cual la supervisin individual de la entidad de crdito corresponde a la autoridad supervisora del pas que haya concedido la licencia y la supervisin del grupo de forma consolidada a la autoridad supervisora del pas de la matriz. Pero una vez fijados los trminos legales de reparto de competencias, se hace preciso establecer las bases para una colaboraci efectiva entre las distintas autoridades de supervisi implicadas y garantizar intercambios de informaci que permitan el mejor desempeo de las respectivas funciones. A tal fin el Banco de Espa ha firmado convenios de cooperacin con 9 pases del continente americano, 7 pases europeos y un pas asitico. El timo de ellos, con Puerto Rico, se firmprecisamente la semana pasada. Tambin la semana pasada se completla incorporaci al derecho espal del nuevo marco regulatorio del capital de las entidades de crdito, conocido como Basilea II, con la publicaci en el BOE de la circular del Banco de Espaa sobre esta materia. El nuevo marco aporta ventajas que, en el caso de los grupos bancarios internacionales, son especialmente palpables, pues incorpora una mayor sensibilidad al riesgo, un reconocimiento de los sistemas ms avanzados de gesti y la necesidad de contar con sistemas propios de autoevaluaci del capital. Tras la primera fase de implantacin de los denominados modelos IRB por los grupos espales con sistemas de gesti mejor adaptados a la nueva normativa, los criterios bsicos que aplicar el Banco de Espaa en relacin con futuras solicitudes son los siguientes: las entidades habrn de mantener contactos previos con el Banco de Espaa para evaluar la situaci real de los modelos y la razonabilidad de sus planteamientos, ya que los modelos presentados tendrn que estar siendo efectivamente utilizados en el momento de la solicitud y debern tener unos niveles de calidad y control adecuados y contrastados; la solicitud formal y la informaci que debe acompaarla seguirn los formatos especficos establecidos por el Banco de Espaa, con una documentaci completa que permita validar los modelos; el proceso de validaci formal, que durar seis meses, comenzar a partir de ese momento. En esta segunda fase se aplicar a los procesos de validaci, cuya duracin ser ya inferior a la que ha precisado la revisi de los primeros modelos, la misma metodologa que se ha utilizado hasta el momento, y el Banco de Espaa seguir trabajando en la emisin y actualizaci de guas o documentos especficos de validaci para facilitar el conocimiento por las entidades de los criterios utilizados. La implantaci de normas comunes que regulan la actividad bancaria en un nmero muy amplio de pases, como es el caso de Basilea II (o su precedente, Basilea I, de 1988) es la respuesta de los reguladores internacionales ante el feneno de la internacionalizacin de la empresa y de la banca en el mundo, y forma parte de un conjunto amplio de iniciativas globales. Algunas de stas estn muy desarrolladas, como la unificacin de los criterios de informaci financiera en el marco de las normas internacionales de contabilidad, mientras que otras a se encuentran en fase de estudio y desarrollo, como las propuestas en diferentes mbitos que elaboran distintos foros internacionales entre las que pueden citarse las recientes recomendaciones del Foro de Estabilidad Financiera (Financial Stability Forum). El feneno de la internacionalizacin financiera tiene, claro est, una dimensi europea propia, lo que hace que en el marco de las instituciones de la Uni Europea tambin se est abordando un proceso amplio de reflexin y debate sobre la manera de abordar ms eficientemente los procesos de convergencia en regulaci y prcticas supervisoras, y de coordinacin entre supervisores. Se trata tanto de dar respuesta al feneno de la creciente integracin en Europa en el sector de banca minorista, como de impulsar el citado proceso. El debate es amplio y va dirigido a las mtiples facetas de la estructura de la supervisin financiera, con el objetivo de profundizar tambin en los esquemas ms adecuados para el tratamiento de las crisis de entidades que formen parte de grupos de nivel europeo. En este sentido, el pasado 1 de junio se firmel nuevo convenio de cooperaci sobre estabilidad financiera internacional entre las autoridades de supervisi financiera, los bancos centrales y los ministros de finanzas de la Uni Europea, que aborda, entre otras cuestiones, aspectos tan relevantes como los principios comunes de gesti de crisis financieras transnacionales, los acuerdos de cooperacin, las formas de activacin de procedimientos y las responsabilidades en una crisis, el intercambio de informacin y la transparencia informativa coordinada. Este es uno de los pasos que se estn dando en la direccin de asegurar que el ejercicio por las autoridades supervisoras de cada pas de sus competencias respectivas tenga en cuenta la dimensin europea de los principales grupos bancarios del continente y se ejerza con una perspectiva que vaya ms all de los lmites nacionales. * * * * Quisiera dedicar los timos minutos de mi intervencin a comentar algunos aspectos relacionados con las perturbaciones de los mercados financieros internacionales, iniciadas durante el pasado verano y que an persisten. Estas perturbaciones constituyen, a mi juicio, el primer test importante para el nuevo sistema financiero internacional que ha venido gestndose en los ltimos aos, al hilo de los procesos de innovacin financiera y de la creciente globalizaci de los mercados. En el origen y el desarrollo de las turbulencias pueden apreciarse tanto rasgos novedosos como otros de carcter ms tradicional. Entre los primeros, destaca el hecho de que el epicentro de las turbulencias se haya situado en EEUU, la principal economa mundial, y que los problemas se hayan trasladado de manera muy rpida a otras latitudes, especialmente a los principales pases europeos, como consecuencia de la globalizaci de los mercados financieros y de la apertura de nuevos canales por donde circula el riesgo. En esta ocasin, la transmisi de los riesgos se ha producido mediante el empaquetamiento de los prstamos originales a travs de vehculos de titulizaci y otras estructuras complejas en las que han acabado invirtiendo adquirentes de zonas geogrficas lejanas. Entre los rasgos ms tradicionales de las actuales perturbaciones financieras, lo ms reseble es que su origen est en la relajacin de criterios en la concesi de crditos hipotecarios en Estados Unidos, con la aplicaci de polticas crediticias poco prudentes, siendo ste un factor tpico de generaci de dificultades en los sistemas bancarios. En general, los mecanismos de transferencia de riesgos tienen una gran capacidad para dotar de estabilidad al sistema financiero, puesto que permiten a los bancos originadores gestionar sus necesidades de recursos propios, ayudan a diversificar las fuentes de liquidez y hacen posible que los riesgos concedidos sean finalmente asumidos por otros agentes, distribuyndolos ms ampliamente. Pero un uso indebido de los mecanismos de transferencia de riesgos los convierte tambin en potencialmente nocivos. Las circunstancias actuales han puesto de manifiesto que los riesgos no se encontraban tan dispersos como se supona, ya que la transmisi que se haba realizado era, a menudo, ms nominal que efectiva. Adems, se estaban creando bolsas de vulnerabilidad donde se acumulaba el riesgo: por ejemplo, en los vehculos mediante los que se estructuraban operaciones complejas, que muchas veces estaban financiando a corto plazo posiciones a largo plazo, y generando compromisos elevados de liquidez para los bancos proveedores de lneas de emergencia. En estos casos, la complejidad y la falta de transparencia han dificultado un diagntico a tiempo de la situacin y han favorecido que, en numerosas ocasiones, los riesgos acabasen en manos de los inversores menos preparados para comprenderlos, valorarlos y gestionarlos. Los procesos de innovacin financiera son fenmenos profundos que no tienen marcha atrs, puesto que contribuyen muy positivamente a la mejora de la eficiencia en la asignaci del capital y al crecimiento econico a medio y largo plazo. Pero entre las innovaciones figuran a veces instrumentos espurios que proponen, a travs de mecanismos opacos, combinaciones de riesgo y rentabilidad alejadas del nivel real de riesgo. Por eso, las innovaciones son periicamente sometidas a prueba por el mercado para, en un proceso anlogo al de la selecci natural, identificar las novedades que merecen pervivir en el futuro por suponer mejoras sidas y eficientes, las que han de modificar algunos de sus elementos para resultar viables, y las que acabarn en el olvido. Ahora, por ejemplo, ciertas facetas del modelo de negocio bancario conocido como originar para distribuir y de los productos financieros estructurados ms sofisticados, estn pasando por un proceso de este tipo. El episodio actual nos ense que en un mundo cada vez ms complejo, en que la internacionalizaci y la innovacin aportan simultneamente oportunidades y riesgos, resulta prioritario que las entidades de crdito se involucren en un proceso de mejora permanente que les permita una adecuada identificaci y comprensin de los riesgos, tanto de los tradicionales como de los nuevos, as como la implantaci de prudentes sistemas de gesti y control. Por su parte, los reguladores y supervisores tenemos tambin que responder de manera activa al feneno de la innovacin, adaptando nuestros sistemas y normas a la realidad de cada momento, con capacidad de anticipacin y de aplicacin de medidas correctoras ante prcticas que puedan obstaculizar la estabilidad financiera. Y, ante la presencia de grupos transnacionales, se necesita convertir la cooperaci internacional en un pilar de la supervisin. En este sentido van las iniciativas ms recientes del Comit de Basilea o del Foro de Estabilidad Financiera. Es cierto que las entidades de crdito espalas han estado ausentes de los fenenos ms inciertos de la situacin actual: su modelo de banca se ha centrado en la intermediacin financiera tradicional, tanto en Espa como en el exterior; no se han introducido en el negocio de originar para distribuir, y por lo tanto no han tenido incentivos inadecuados para relajar sus polticas de concesi de crditos; ni han desarrollado productos estructurados cuya complejidad dificultara la comprensin y valoraci de los riesgos, porque las titulizaciones espaolas se han caracterizado por su sencillez y elevada calidad; ni han invertido en productos estructurados complejos. Adems, la gesti de las entidades de crdito se ha apoyado en un marco de regulaci contable y de solvencia exigente, que ha propiciado una valoracin prudente de los activos y de los riesgos as como la acumulacin de provisiones para cubrir prdidas en la fase bajista del ciclo. Pero las entidades espaolas no son inmunes, claro est, a los efectos indirectos que las perturbaciones financieras estn trayendo consigo: en primer lugar, la alteracin en el funcionamiento de los mercados monetarios y de renta fija privada internacionales; y, en segundo lugar, su impacto nocivo sobre el crecimiento econico global, que coincide con el fin de la larga onda expansiva por la que ha atravesado la economa espala y que, por tanto, complica el proceso de ajuste en nuestro pas. A partir de ahora, cabe esperar que no se pueda volver a disponer de recursos financieros en los mercados internacionales a coste reducido, con las primas de riesgo tan poco penalizadoras que se venan aceptando en la situaci anterior. Y sobre todo, tampoco cabe esperar que la evolucin del negocio bancario en Espa contin a los ritmos del pasado, puesto que debe acompasarse a unas tasas de crecimiento del PIB nominal considerablemente menores. Por todo ello, es necesario que las entidades actualicen sus planes de negocio y los adapten a las circunstancias presentes, especialmente en aquellos casos en que se haba optado por una especializacin mayor en la financiacin de la inversi residencial, el sector de actividad ms afectado en estos momentos. En la definicin de sus estrategias, ser importante tambin la bqueda de un reequilibrio entre sus fuentes de financiaci y sus activos, que tenga en cuenta las condiciones actuales de los mercados. Asimismo los gestores necesitan encontrar nuevos caminos para la eficiencia, que compensen el previsible incremento duradero de los costes de la financiaci, difcilmente trasladables de forma automtica a la clientela, mediante el control del gasto y la racionalizacin de las estructuras, sistemas y procesos que canalizan la actividad bancaria. La bsqueda de la eficiencia es, sin duda, un principio bsico de la gestin empresarial, pero lo es ms en estos momentos en que el crecimiento de la rentabilidad basado en el volumen de negocio ha dejado de ser una posibilidad realista, y en el que el aumento de las tasas de morosidad ejercer una mayor presi sobre los mrgenes y los beneficios de las entidades. En estos momentos, como siempre, es preciso que las entidades espalas mantengan la calidad de sus sistemas de gesti, tanto para proteger adecuadamente su actividad en Espa como para asentar su creciente presencia en otros mercados geogrficos, y que se guarde el necesario equilibrio entre las polticas de asuncin de nuevos riesgos y la implantaci de mecanismos sidos de control. Y, por timo, a nadie escapa que debido a las nuevas circunstancias econicas y financieras, tanto las entidades como los supervisores hemos de realizar nuestro trabajo en un entorno cada vez ms exigente, con menos margen de error y con ms necesidad de desarrollar enfoques prudentes, preventivos y eficaces. Muchas gracias.

Title: Appearance before the Committee on Economy and Finance of the Congress
text: Madrid, 24 June 2008 Appearance of the Governor of the Bank of Spain before the Committee of Economy and Finance of the Congress Miguel Fernandez Ordez Governor of the Bank of Spain The economic climate, national and international, that frames this appearance before His Offices is markedly different from that which serves as a reference to previous appearances. The upward trend in the prices of crude oil, other raw materials and food, the deterioration of the cyclical situation of the US economy, and the serious turbulence that emerged in the international financial markets since last summer have slowed down the growth of the world economy and are strongly conditioning the outlook for its future evolution. At the same time, the confluence of these three far-reaching shocks has reopened long-standing debates on the use to be made in these circumstances of different economic policy tools and has raised new questions in the area of maintaining macroeconomic and financial stability. All this is taking place, moreover, at a time when the European economy maintains the dynamism of activity but under the threat of greater risks to price stability, while in our country the economy, after an exceptionally long period of remarkably high GDP expansion rates, has entered a phase of slowdown and adjustment. There is no way to deal with such a variety and complexity of topics in sufficient detail in the limited time frame of this hearing. Let me therefore confine my comments to those which, in my opinion, are most relevant at the moment. Starting with the international context in which the Spanish economy operates, I will begin by recalling that for the fourth consecutive year the growth rate of the world economy is around 5% in 2007. This behavior was quite widespread, but it was the emerging economies that once again stood out from the rest, contributing almost 70% of the advance in world GDP. These figures, however, hide important differences between before and after the summer. In fact, since then we have been witnessing a process of downward revision of the short-term outlook for the global economy, accompanied, in addition, by the recognition of a growing level of uncertainty around them. The elements that explain this greater uncertainty are multiples. On the one hand, there are doubts about the resilience of the industrialized economies and, in particular, the US economy, whose pattern of exit from the situation of weakness is the subject of intense debate. The real resilience of emerging economies to a longer loss of dynamism in developed countries is also uncertain, nor are there greater certainties about the behaviour of exchange rates and their influence on global imbalances to be corrected. But, in my opinion, the greatest risks remain related, firstly, to the outcome of the episode of international financial tensions. Allow me, Your Sir8es, to now address this issue from an international perspective and leave its impact on the Spanish financial system for later. The crisis in the US subprime mortgage market would not have generated an episode of this gravity if there had not been certain structural weaknesses in the international financial framework. International financial stability reports dated before the turbulence warned, in fact, against underestimating risks in the markets, encouraged and hidden at the same time by the good cyclical moment experienced by the world economy. The events of the summer dismantled investor overconfidence and laid bare the underlying problems. I think it may be useful to mention, at least, the most relevant. In the first place, there has been insufficient capacity to adapt the regulatory framework of some countries to the appearance of increasingly sophisticated products and vehicles outside the consolidation perimeters of the entities. As is well known, ill-conceived regulation can facilitate artificial financial innovation processes that do not add value. Nor do financial products add value that, like some of those that have emerged in these times in the field of credit securitization, end up being so complex and opaque that it is not possible to correctly assess the risks assumed when acquiring them. This is one of the areas in which the competent international financial authorities and institutions will have to concentrate their efforts. It will also be necessary to make more decisive progress at the international level in the area of cooperation between supervisors. In order to supervise global actors operating in markets that are also global in nature, supervisory authorities of the same size are required. I believe that progress can be made with certainty in this direction if cooperation between national supervisors is increased and the exchange of information between them is intensified. Another risk factor worldwide that requires special attention at this time is the upward trend in the price of raw materials, particularly energy, and food. After the strong upswing in these prices, it is easy to identify elements of demand linked to significant changes in emerging economies. But neither should we ignore some relevant limitations on the supply side, such as the low excess capacity of production and refining, in the case of crude oil, or the effects of particularly adverse weather conditions, in the case of food. In the short term, these factors are unlikely to reverse significantly, so there is a growing risk that this adjustment in relative commodity prices will be perceived as a permanent, rather than temporary, increase in inflation. If this risk materializes and ends up affecting the mechanisms of wage negotiation and margin formation, inflationary spirals would be set in motion at the international level, highly harmful to employment and welfare. Inflationary tensions, downward revisions to activity and risks to financial stability constitute a scenario of enormous complexity for the exercise of monetary policy, a scenario to which the Eurosystem has not been alien. EMU GDP grew by more than 2.5% for the second consecutive year, but the effects of shocks and the appreciation of the euro began to be felt in the quarter as a whole. EMU is certainly showing a remarkable capacity to withstand tensions, which is based above all on the dynamism that the labour market has maintained to date. But uncertainty about the behavior of the European economy in the medium term has increased, and in recent months private institutions and international organizations have revised downwards their growth forecasts for this year and the next. The Eurosystem has also made its own proposals, which point to advances of around 1.8% in 2008 and 1.5% in 2009. In both cases, in addition, predominantly downside risks are contemplated. As it could not be otherwise, the behavior of inflation is strongly influenced by what happened in the international markets of raw materials and food and has ended up standing above 3%. These levels, which are exceptional for EMU standards, are expected to continue for some time to later and it will not be until the last part of the year that gradual declines will begin to be recorded throughout 2009. But, in addition, this is a scenario subject to upside risks that emanate mainly from the possibility of second-round effects on the fixing of wages, margins and prices. However, the choice of the most appropriate tone for monetary policy is not the only difficulty that the Eurosystem is facing. The loss of liquidity and the increase in risk premia in the European interbank markets, a fundamental element in the implementation and transmission of monetary policy, required great attention and special efforts. Efforts should be focused, and this has been the case for the Eurosystem, on enabling banks to meet their liquidity needs. In view of the results, I do not think it is an exaggeration to say that this area has been done with remarkable effectiveness. During this period of uncertainty, the Governing Council of the ECB has so far kept key interest rates unchanged, although the increase in risk premia in the money market, the rise in corporate bond spreads, the tightening of loan supply conditions revealed by the results of the Bank Lending Survey and the appreciation of the euro have introduced some tightening of the conditions of financing of the area, which was considered necessary to counteract inflationary tensions. However, the recent uptick in inflation in the area, largely attributable to upward external price pressures, has increased the risks of second-round effects on wage negotiations and pricing, and of a loss of anchoring expectations, prompting the Council to announce that it is on high alert and determined to act in order to prevent such risks from materializing. Having reviewed the international framework in which the analysis of the situation of the Spanish economy must be contextualized, I will focus on this for the rest of my appearance. As is well known, our economy began to experience over the past year a period of slowdown in activity that, although initially due to the maturation of the long expansionary cycle that began in the mid-nineties, has been accentuated by the appearance of the disturbances that have afflicted the world economy as a whole. All these events have occurred after a long period of expansion and high employment generation that have allowed a notable advance in the approximation to the average level of income of the countries of our environment. These results are closely linked to the benefits of Spain's entry into EMU and to the efforts made to achieve a sound budgetary position and to increase the flexibility of the economy through the introduction of liberalisation and structural reform measures. However, the very maturation of this cycle, together with the pattern of growth followed during it, has finally led to a change of phase and the beginning of a process of adjustment of the economy. As is known, the dynamism of demand was based, among other factors, on high consumption growth and strong and prolonged real estate expansion, encouraged by interest rates that remained at low levels for a long period of time. In fact, it has been in this sector that the effects of a long expansion in comfortable monetary and financial conditions had been most felt, which had led to a growth of the nero of built homes and their prices at rates hardly sustainable in the long term. In these circumstances, the change in the monetary policy stance, through the interest rate hikes implemented since December 2005 by the ECB, discourages purchase of housing and the indebtedness of families, leading to the beginning of the necessary adjustment of the real estate sector, which begins to manifest itself in more moderate growth in the price of housing. At the same time, the combined effect of the normalization of monetary conditions and lower expectations of appreciation of financial wealth was felt in a loss of momentum in private consumption. In the middle of the past, the abrupt unleashing of the episode of instability in the financial markets contributed to intensifying the adjustment, by inducing a generalized deterioration of confidence when private agents had already begun a process of correcting their spending patterns. At the same time, the increase in the average cost of obtaining funds by financial institutions has led to an increase in the cost of financing granted to private agents, as entities have adopted more demanding criteria for granting credit. Although it is true that during the past year the worsening of the economic context was already evident in a certain moderation of the year-on-year rates of growth of the product, it has been in the first months of this year when the slowdown of the Spanish economy has been becoming more pronounced. Specifically, the components of demand representative of household consumption and housing expenditure, the main driving force of activity during the long expansionary phase, have also shown the greatest weakness since the adjustment process began. For its part, productive investment is maintaining a reasonable strength, although it has also lost some of its strength over the most recent quarters. The improvement in the contribution of the net external balance to GDP growth is a positive feature of recent developments in economic activity, as a result of the remarkable pace of expansion that our exports are maintaining. The downward flexion of spending by companies and, above all, by households has been reflected in the rate of growth of credit demanded by the private sector, which has continued to slow down to approach that of the incomes of these agents, thus interrupting the trend of increasing indebtedness that had been observed in scams. The Spanish economy has also had to face the increase in the price of oil and other raw materials. The upswing in inflation that has occurred in this context, with rates above 4%, as recorded in the months of the month, has deteriorated the purchasing power of Spanish households, discouraging consumption and eroding their confidence. The external origin of the inflationary episode we are witnessing, however, should not lead us to consider this evolution as something outside the sphere of influence of the authorities and social agents. In particular, attempts to avoid the real income losses that the increase in the price of imported goods entails, either through price or cost increases, as a result of existing indiciacin mechanisms, may end up generating greater inflationary tensions and negatively affect job creation, which would tend to intensify and prolong the adjustment. Efforts to maintain a path of moderation of corporate margins and wages are even more important in a situation such as the current one in which the main destination countries of our exports are also immersed in a phase of slowdown, so that the behavior of competitiveness is a crucial element for the contribution of the external sector to counteract the loss of vigor of domestic demand. The outlook for the Spanish economy points to a period of moderation in growth in the immediate future, in which, however, there are elements that should make it possible to cushion the impact of the shocks I have just described. In particular, our country now has an institutional environment much more prone to macroeconomic stability, a balanced budget position and factor and product markets that, although still suffering from certain rigidities, are more flexible than they were a decade and a half ago. On the other hand, the soundness of the Spanish financial system represents an important support to mitigate the effects derived from the prolonged phase of international financial instability. However, it must be recognized that the uncertainties surrounding this central scenario are mostly downward and originate, above all, from abroad. In our case, given our dependence on external savings, a return to a more normal functioning of international capital markets would help smooth the adjustment by reducing financing costs and lengthening financing terms. However, the materialization of the central scenario in which the slowdown in activity has a moderate intensity and duration depends not only on the extent of external shocks, but also on the effort made by all public administrations and social partners, each in its field of action. In particular, it seems to me of particular importance that the design of economic policy in the current situation is based on the maintenance of budgetary stability and an effort to make the markets more flexible. The achievement of budgetary stability throughout the previous expansionary phase has made it possible to face the slowdown in activity from a position in which automatic stabilisers can deploy their countercyclical potential. On the other hand, discretionary policies that compromise the stability gains achieved and may exhaust the room for manoeuvre that might be necessary in the event of any of the risks I have just described materialise, should be avoided. In this sense, it should not be forgotten that, although all public administrations face this phase of slowdown from a favorable position, such a position is not without risks, as shown by the weakening of collection, mainly that corresponding to the tax figures that are most linked to the developments of the housing market. Therefore, any measure adopted should be selective in nature and be accompanied by an effort to contain other budgetary areas that are susceptible to cost reductions. I would like to draw attention, at this point, to the effort to rationalise expenditure that the Autonomous Communities have to make in this new stage, especially in view of the notable slowdown observed in the taxes transferred. Another crucial element is the strengthening of flexibility and efficiency in the functioning of factor and product markets, which should facilitate the transfer of resources from the adjustment sectors to those that will take over. The economic slowdown is already being felt in the employment data for the months of the scams, so it is urgent to strengthen incentives for the active search of a job, promote the generation of stable employment and facilitate the geographical and sectoral mobility of workers, through the relevant reforms. But the elements of evidence present in the collective bargaining system, which contribute to converting transitory episodes of inflationary rebound into lasting departures from the path of wage moderation, must also be reviewed. In reducing the duration and intensity of the adjustment as much as possible and in addressing the future recovery from a favourable starting point, progress in liberalising goods and services markets will play a key role. In this sense, there are several areas that, in my opinion, require special attention. Firstly, there is scope for deepening consumer services, the use of which at this juncture may prove particularly fruitful. The Services Directive approved at European level must be ambitiously transposed into the Spanish legal system. In addition, the important role played by distribution channels in the price formation process calls for the dismantling of the constraints currently imposed on retail trade. In the situation that the real estate sector is going through, it seems essential to promote the development of the rental market, which involves an increase in the legal certainty of landlords and the elimination of the restrictions that currently weigh on the duration of contracts. These actions can potentially exert very beneficial effects to smooth the adjustment of the housing market and accommodate the demand for existing accommodation. One area in which product market reforms should have an impact is the network industries (particularly in the energy sector), as the efficient provision of these services has a favourable effect on the overall efficiency of the economy. Nor should it be forgotten that raising the economy's long-term growth potential requires economic policies to foster physical and human capital, for which it is necessary to decisively promote the improvement of the education system and innovative efforts. In the final part of this hearing, I would now like to turn to the Spanish banking system. I will begin by noting that the direct impact of financial turbulence on our entities has been limited. Firstly, because the activity of our banks, savings banks and cooperatives rests on the traditional financial intermediation system between depositors and borrowers. The issuance of securitized assets, particularly mortgage bonds, has also been an important source of financing for the Spanish banking system in these scams, but, in our case, securitization has followed simple and transparent processes, in which especially complex and difficult to value products have not been generated and the external "vehicles" that we have known in other latitudes have not been created. Likewise, the massive transfer of risks outside the banking system of the "originate to distribute" model itself has not been carried out here. In this way, the entities have continued to manage their lending operations with the professionalism and diligence of those who continue to base a central part of their results on the correct valuation of the risks assumed. The direct impact of shocks has also been cushioned by the existence of stringent accounting and solvency regulations and supervisory practices that are particularly sensitive to the evolution of risks. This has led institutions to follow prudent criteria in the valuation of their assets and has allowed important forecast bags to accumulate during good times with which to face losses that may arise in times of greater difficulties. Spanish banks thus maintained reasonable liquidity and a wide diversification of maturities and financing segments when the wholesale markets in which they had been capturing a significant part of their resources collapsed. Their capacity to respond in this difficult environment has been evident in the adaptation they have carried out of their sources of financing, struggling to capture traditional liabilities, moving towards shorter maturities and, in the final stretch of last year, increasing their use to the Eurosystem, although from a limited level and without moving away from the participation equivalent to the "key" of the Bank of Spain in the capital of the ECB. For some months now, we have been witnessing the first symptoms of the reactivation of the primary markets of simple bank obligations and mortgage bonds, in which Spanish entities have managed to place a very significant volume of issues in a short time. It is important that our entities increase their presence in these markets and adjust to an environment of higher financing costs and business growth rates much higher than those of national GDP. And they will have to do so under cyclical conditions that will tend to add pressure on their margins. In these circumstances, improvements in the efficiency of the organization that result in a more adjusted management of costs acquire special relevance. The Bank of Spain, for its part, will continue to ensure that these new challenges are faced without jeopardizing the stability of the system. In the field of accounting provisions, we will continue to rely on preventive schemes compatible with international accounting standards and with the acceptance of the most advanced internal models of the entities, schemes that have proven themselves illegitimate in the current circumstances and that are gaining international acceptance in a progressive manner. In the field of supervisory regulations, and with this reminder I conclude my intervention, on May 22 the Governing Council of the Bank of Spain approved a circular that involves the implementation in Spain of the new solvency regulations known as Basel II, whose entry into force will increase the prudential tools available to the supervisor. Thank you very much for your attention.

En la parte final de esta comparecencia quisiera ocuparme ahora del sistema bancario espaol. Comenzar sealando que el impacto directo de las turbulencias financieras sobre nuestras entidades ha sido limitado. Primeramente, porque la actividad de nuestros bancos, cajas y cooperativas descansa en el sistema de intermediacin financiera tradicional entre depositantes y prestatarios. La emisin de activos titulizados, particularmente cdulas hipotecarias, ha sido tambin una importante fuente de financiaci para el sistema bancario espaol en estos timos as, pero, en nuestro caso, la titulizacin ha seguido procesos sencillos y transparentes, en los que no se han generado productos especialmente complejos y de difcil valoraci y no se han creado los vehculos externos que hemos conocido en otras latitudes. Asimismo, tampoco se ha llevado a cabo aqu la transferencia masiva de los riesgos fuera del propio sistema bancario propia del modelo originar para distribuir. De este modo, las entidades han continuado gestionando sus operaciones de prstamo con la profesionalidad y la diligencia propias de quien contin basando una parte central de sus resultados en la correcta valoraci de los riesgos asumidos. El impacto directo de las perturbaciones ha resultado amortiguado tambin por la existencia de una exigente regulacin contable y de solvencia y de unas prcticas de supervisi particularmente atentas a la evoluci de los riesgos. Esto ha propiciado que las entidades sigan criterios prudentes en la valoracin de sus activos y ha permitido que durante los tiempos de bonanza se acumulen importantes bolsas de previsiones con las que hacer frente a las prdidas que puedan surgir en momentos de mayores dificultades. Las entidades espaolas mantenan as una liquidez razonable y una amplia diversificaci de plazos y segmentos de financiacin cuando los mercados mayoristas en los que venan captando una parte notable de sus recursos colapsaron. Su capacidad de respuesta en este entorno de dificultad ha quedado patente en la adaptacin que han llevado a cabo de sus fuentes de financiaci, pugnando por captar pasivos tradicionales, desplazndose hacia plazos ms cortos y, en el tramo final del pasado ejercicio, elevando su recurso al Eurosistema, aunque a partir de un nivel limitado y sin alejarse de la participaci equivalente a la clave del Banco de Espa en el capital del BCE. Desde hace unos meses, venimos asistiendo a los primeros sntomas de reactivacin de los mercados primarios de obligaciones bancarias simples y cdulas hipotecarias, en los que las entidades espalas han conseguido colocar un volumen de emisiones muy importante en poco tiempo.
