I will then devote the remainder of my speech to commenting on the main regulatory initiatives currently underway, within the framework of the work carried out in the field of the European Union, the Financial Stability Forum and the Basel Committee. * * * During the fourteen years of prosperity that the Spanish economy has experienced, Spanish credit institutions have been ensuring a positive position, which is reflected in their solvency, profitability and efficiency ratios, so the outbreak of turbulence in international financial markets, in the summer of 2007, surprised our banking system well prepared to face its effects. The experience in past crises helps us maintain a financial regulation and a supervisory model that, together with the business model of our banks and savings banks, have contributed to the current position of the Spanish banking system. Thanks to the prudential criteria maintained in the accounting rules applicable to Spanish institutions and, in particular, with regard to provisions for credit risk, Spanish institutions have had greater strength and room for manoeuvre to deal with the deterioration of credit market conditions. These same criteria have been decisive so that our entities have not maintained, either, relevant off-balance sheet positions through certain vehicles, a procedure that for entities in other countries has been enormously harmful because, under an apparent effective transfer of risk, it contributes to creating stock exchanges where losses accumulated that then returned to the entity. The demanding regulation on control and management of credit risk, and supervisory practices particularly attentive to the evolution of risks, have favoured that our Entities remain mostly focused on the traditional banking business, which has moved them away from the most complex financial engineering and the "originate to distribute" model that is, along with other relevant factors, at the origin of the turbulence of last summer and the financial crisis that we are now going through. On the contrary, the patterns followed in securitisations in Spain have normally been based on simple structures in which, in addition, the retention in bank balance sheets of the most relevant risks of the underlying assets has contributed to institutions having the same incentives to properly assess the credit quality of loan holders as if the portfolio had not been securitized, avoiding that, in this way, the criteria for granting credits have been relaxed. Likewise, in strengthening its structural position, we must not forget the important effort made by Spanish credit institutions to implement the complex regulatory and far-reaching changes developed in scams, before the financial storm of the summer of 2007. These changes have had a high level of demand in terms of organizational, personal and technological resources. I think it is fair to acknowledge that the Spanish entities have undertaken this process satisfactorily, professionally and diligently. First, they had to deal with the adoption of the new accounting framework of international financial reporting standards. Then, preparations for the major reform of solvency regulations, driven by the agreement known as Basel II; and, almost coinciding in time, the practical implementation of the requirements of the Financial Markets Directive, known as MiFID. International accounting standards have been incorporated into our regulations by Bank of Spain Circular 4/2004, in which a notable effort was made to maintain prudent criteria in those areas in which these standards allowed several options. A clear example of this is the rules on provisions for credit risk which, on the one hand, establishes the criteria that determine the provisions to be made in relation to losses incurred and identifiable in specific transactions. And on the other, it establishes the need to make provisions to cover losses, also incurred and inherent to the portfolio, but not yet identifiable individually. From a conceptual point of view, these provisions reflect the fact that, for banking systems, risks tend to accumulate over expansionary cycles, and to manifest themselves when these end, that is, they have to do with the procyclical behavior that characterizes financial markets. The system is designed in such a way that it has forced institutions to set up funds that will allow them to absorb the impact of a potential increase in specific provisions. Basel II, which has been regulated in Bank of Spain Circular 3/2008, but which had already been influencing the behaviour of our institutions long before, represents a notable advance in the management of the risks faced by credit institutions. This has allowed, and will allow in the future, because it is a system that is fed back with experience, that managers know better the business and operation of the entities, and that they can control to a greater extent the risks they incur. The new solvency regulations aim to make it more rigorous and sensitive to risk, while encouraging better risk management. It should not be forgotten that the worst risk that a bank manager can incur is his inability to identify, understand or measure with prudence the risks of the business he undertakes. I will not dwell on the three pillars on which the solvency treatment is based, as they are already well known, but I will stress the importance of these being observed together, so that the entities reach a level of own resources in accordance with their overall risk profile. By timo, in this review of the most recent regulations, Spanish credit institutions have also faced the test of incorporating the mandates of the so-called MIFID. One of MIFID's objectives is to improve investor protection in two ways: strengthening the organisational and operational requirements of investment service providers, and improving the rules of conduct governing their customer relations. The improvement of investor protection, apart from being a legitimate objective in itself, serves to favor a better organization and a more severe internal control, which is a requirement of good management that results in an operational improvement with positive effects on the efficiency and credibility of the entity. On the other hand, from the point of view of integral risk management, it serves to raise awareness and sensitize about the importance of reputational risk. This is particularly important risk for credit institutions, whose business is based precisely on trust. * * * Legitimately proud of what has been done so far, however, we must not become complacent. The current situation presents important challenges and new elements both for our banks and savings banks and for regulators and supervisors, which must be assessed in a weighted manner. It is clear that the strong growth of the Spanish economy in recent years has also led to various imbalances. The enormous use of foreign financing to meet the credit needs with which to support this growth, and the rapid growth of household and corporate indebtedness, together with other well-known factors, such as the essential role played by the real estate market in our growth, are elements that we must bear in mind, as they will determine our future cousin. To these imbalances, whose correction process had begun in 2006, have now been added global events that have intensified the adjustment creating a situation in which the sharp increase in non-performing loans and the contraction of the business pose challenges that must be addressed without delay. Although the increase in non-performing loans was foreseeable and although it has not yet reached alarming levels, it must be addressed by combining high doses of flexibility in its management and the maintenance of the quality and quantity of provisions and own funds; On the other hand, the contraction of the business will inevitably force entities to promote greater control of costs and the rationalization of processes. Both banking and regulatory activity will have to adapt to the new framework, forcing entities and regulators to undertake initiatives that allow maintaining and strengthening the foundations of our banking system and boosting its growth in a globalized market. In this same direction of strengthening the soundness and stability of the banking system as a whole, it is necessary to place the initiatives that, in different international forums, are being addressed to modify financial regulation and that are focusing on: - strengthening the solvency of institutions and continuing to contribute to better banking risk management; - improve transparency for investors, markets and regulators, as well as valuation standards, particularly when markets become illiquid; - increase cooperation and convergence between supervisors to ensure effective prudential control of large transnational groups, - crisis prevention and management where necessary; and - improving the functioning of markets, including the role of credit rating agencies and the existing incentive structure. In order to strengthen the solvency of institutions, continuing with regulatory harmonisation and supervisory convergence, and with the aim of contributing to financial stability, the European Commission, culminating initiatives launched prior to the turbulence of summer 2007, has just presented a proposal for a Directive that modifies the solvency regulation currently in force in the areas that I will comment on below. First, it is intended to improve some elements of the regulation applicable to securitisations and structured products, especially where turbulence has highlighted the need to review the existence of certain potentially adverse incentives. Thus, to address the conflicts of interest present in the originate-to-distribute model, it is proposed that originators and sponsors of instruments with non-transparent structures retain a portion of the risk transferred to investors. This new requirement is complemented, on the part of investors, with the obligation on the part of these to have a complete knowledge of the risks they assume both by the characteristics of the complex structures in which they are investing and of the underlying assets. The extension of the originate-to-distribute model has also led to a strong growth in the assets included in the trading book, whose risk had not been correctly taken into account in the current regulations, which has advised a substantial increase in the capital requirements for these assets, in particular, to adequately cover their credit risk. At the same time, there is a proposal to strengthen the quality of banks' core own resources, so that the hybrid instruments that are now computed together with ordinary capital and reserves, will withstand strict and harmonised limits, and will have characteristics that make them truly ile in the event of a crisis of an institution. It also addresses the revision of the regulation of concentration risk with a single client or group of related clients, in order to make it more consistent with the methods applied for the calculation of capital requirements and to tighten the treatment of various exposures and counterparties, in particular interbank exposures, previously excluded from these limits in many countries, although not in Spain. More innovative is the establishment of detailed principles for proper liquidity risk management and supervision. The aim is to encourage banks to gain a better understanding of their risk profile. Thus, the Board of Directors will be responsible for establishing the appropriate level of tolerance for liquidity risk. On the other hand, entities must carry out stress exercises and implement the corresponding contingency plans. Emphasis is also placed on the desirability of maintaining an appropriate cushion of high-quality liquid assets to deal with stressful situations. Finally, much of the reform is devoted to improving the supervisory mechanisms of large cross-border banking groups; the legal recognition of colleges of supervisors, measures to facilitate the exercise of the powers of the supervisors concerned, to coordinate their activity and to enable them to share their information with other authorities, which should make the supervision of these groups more effective, especially in the event of an emergency situation in an entity with a presence in several countries. In addition, it is intended to strengthen the role of the European committees of supervisors and, in particular, that of the banking supervisors (the so-called CEBS) who are assigned specific tasks in addition to those they have already been carrying out technical advice to the Commission in relation to the legislative initiatives I have just mentioned; or the development of supervisory guides to ensure convergence in the implementation of European standards. Alongside these initiatives in Europe, the Basel Committee of Banking Supervisors is also nearing completion of work that will contribute, globally, to reducing system leverage and excessive risk concentration within large international banks. These works range from the specific measures that will contribute to refining the so-called Pillar 1 in those points that have been most decisive in the losses suffered by financial institutions during the turbulence, to the improvement of risk management and the increase of transparency to the market. To this end, the requirements for so-called resecuritisations or those of the trading book will increase in order to adequately capture certain elements of credit risk that the usual models have not adequately valued, and in this way regulatory capital will be aligned with the risk inherent in these positions. Also in this same direction is the guide just published by the Committee on liquidity risk management, which is intended, fundamentally, to increase the capacity of banks to face possible situations of liquidity stress, through, among other factors, a prudent buffer of high quality liquid assets. The current crisis has shown the importance of integrating liquidity management into the bank's overall risk management processes. But the crisis has also opened up for reflection numerous areas that I will only mention, for example, - the harmonization of crisis prevention and management measures, in which cooperation and convergence will play an essential role, both between supervisors and between supervisors and other actors. - the improvement of the functioning of the markets, which includes, among other initiatives, that of the European Commission on the possible regulation of credit rating agencies. - the revision of asset valuation standards, including the adoption of a method of valuing illiquid assets in financial statements. -the analysis of the possible procyclical effects of financial regulation, in particular the possible procyclical effect of solvency rules, accounting regulations and even staff remuneration policies. By the way, another area that will undoubtedly reach great importance is that of strengthening the infrastructures on which the financial system is built. There is a growing need for us to reassess the soundness of our derivatives markets, especially credit derivatives markets where a huge volume of risk is transferred, and of our settlement and clearing systems, together with the main participants in them, in order to ensure that they fulfil their function (to provide liquidity and price to products) both in normal times and in stressful situations. * * * Also because of its importance in terms of promoting appropriate financial infrastructures and its enormous relevance on an essential part of the business of our banks, I want to highlight the creation of an ICO market for payment services linked to the Single Euro Payments Area, known by its acronym in English, SEPA, and the recently adopted directive on payment services. The harmonization of the rules of conduct with customers with regard to payments will benefit the user of financial services, who will have a wider range of suppliers at his disposal, with the consequent increase in efficiency via price and / or quality of the service received, and in conditions of protection that allow an adequate level of confidence and security. The purpose of this Payment Services Directive is to establish a common legal framework for the provision of payment services, which should at the same time: - Provide payment service users with a sufficient degree of protection of their interests to ensure that they have the level of security necessary to rely on the cross-border service provision of the ICO market. - Create a playing field that favors the competitive offer of these services, both for the possibility of access for all types of solvent intermediaries, and for the absence of national obstacles that give the provision of these services. Preparing for the correct application of this standard, which will mean a significant change in our most common banking practices and uses, is a new challenge that our banks must address in the first months, once again testing the ability to adapt their structures. The involvement of the organisation as a whole in its implementation will undoubtedly contribute to increasing its strength, especially in relations with retail customers. In the same vein, the recent Consumer Credit Directive deepens the retail services market while ensuring a high level of consumer protection. Both by way of greater transparency in the conditions, and by the right of the consumer to withdraw from the credit during a regulated period, at no cost to him and without the need to prove any reason, will also favor a greater responsibility of the entities in the rigorous granting of these credits. I have intended with this intervention to provide an overview of past, present and future regulatory challenges. But let me end with a general reflection on reforms of the regulatory framework. We must prevent the current crisis from leading us to react pendulously towards hyperregulation. The exceptional circumstances we are experiencing cannot make us forget a principle that seems to me to be essential, and that is that any regulatory initiative, before being approved, must be properly considered and subjected to a demanding examination of its purpose and necessity. Thanks a lot
text_original: Madrid, 9 de octubre de 2008 Perspectivas regulatorias en el sistema bancario espal II Foro Cajas de Ahorros. CECA Miguel Fernndez Ordez Gobernador del Banco de Espa En primer lugar, quiero agradecer a los organizadores de esta jornada su amable invitaci a participar en este foro para pronunciar algunas palabras sobre las perspectivas regulatorias del sistema bancario espal. Dados los acontecimientos que da a da se vienen sucediendo en el sistema financiero internacional, este tema podra parecer de menor importancia. Pero precisamente la calidad de nuestro sistema de regulacin y supervisi nos est permitiendo enfrentar esta situacin desde una posici de fortaleza. En mi intervenci comenzar centrndome en la situaci del sistema bancario espal, su posici ante las perturbaciones de los mercados financieros y las condiciones en que afronta los retos e incertidumbres del nuevo entorno econico, subrayando el papel que en todo ello ha jugado, y est jugando nuestro marco regulatorio. Despus dedicar el resto de mi intervenci a comentar las principales iniciativas regulatorias actualmente en curso, enmarcadas en los trabajos desarrollados en el mbito de la Unin Europea, el Foro de Estabilidad Financiera y el Comit de Basilea. * * * Durante los catorce aos de bonanza que ha vivido la economa espala las entidades de crdito espalas han ido asegurando una sida posici, que se refleja en sus ratios de solvencia, de rentabilidad y de eficiencia, por lo que el estallido de las turbulencias en los mercados financieros internacionales, en el verano de 2007., sorprendi a nuestro sistema bancario bien preparado para afrontar sus efectos. La experiencia en crisis pasadas nos ayuda mantener una regulacin financiera y un modelo de supervisin que, unidos al propio modelo de negocio de nuestros bancos y cajas, han contribuido a la sida posicin actual del sistema bancario espaol. Gracias a los criterios de prudencia mantenidos en la normativa contable aplicable a las entidades espalas y, en particular, en lo que se refiere a las provisiones por riesgo de crdito, las entidades espalas han dispuesto de una mayor fortaleza y margen de maniobra para afrontar el deterioro de las condiciones de los mercados del crdito. Esos mismos criterios han sido decisivos para que nuestras entidades no hayan mantenido, tampoco, posiciones relevantes fuera de balance a travs de determinados vehculos, procedimiento que para las entidades de otros pases ha resultado enormemente lesivo porque, bajo una aparente transmisi efectiva del riesgo, contribuya crear bolsas donde se acumulaban prdidas que luego retornaban a la entidad. La exigente regulaci sobre control y gestin del riesgo de crdito, y unas prcticas de supervisin particularmente atentas a la evolucin de los riesgos, han favorecido que nuestras entidades sigan mayoritariamente centradas en el negocio bancario tradicional, lo que les ha alejado de la ingeniera financiera ms compleja y del modelo de originar para distribuir que est, junto a otros factores tambin relevantes, en el origen de las turbulencias del verano pasado y de la crisis financiera que ahora estamos atravesando. Por el contrario, los patrones seguidos en las titulizaciones en Espa se han basado normalmente en estructuras sencillas en las que, adems, la retencin en los balances bancarios de los riesgos ms relevantes de los activos subyacentes ha contribuido a que las entidades tengan los mismos incentivos para evaluar adecuadamente la calidad crediticia de los titulares de los prstamos que si la cartera no se hubiera titulizado, evitando que, por esta va, se hayan relajado los criterios de concesin de crditos. Asimismo, en el reforzamiento de su posicin estructural no hay que olvidar el importante esfuerzo que han realizado las entidades de crdito espalas para implantar los complejos cambios regulatorios y de gran calado desarrollados en los timos as, antes de la tormenta financiera del verano de 2007. Estos cambios han tenido un alto nivel de exigencia en trminos de recursos organizativos, personales y tecnolicos. Creo que es justo reconocer que las entidades espaolas han acometido este proceso de forma satisfactoria, con profesionalidad y diligencia. Primero tuvieron que afrontar la adopcin del nuevo marco contable de las normas internacionales de informacin financiera. Despus, los preparativos para la importante reforma de la normativa de solvencia, impulsada por el acuerdo conocido como Basilea II; y, casi coincidiendo en el tiempo, la implantacin prctica de las exigencias de la Directiva de mercados financieros, la conocida como MiFID. Las normas internacionales de contabilidad han sido incorporadas a nuestra regulaci por la circular del Banco de Espa 4/2004, en la que se hizo un notable esfuerzo por mantener criterios de prudencia en aquellos mbitos en los que dichas normas permitan varias opciones. Un ejemplo claro de ello es la normativa en materia de provisiones por riesgo de crdito que, por una parte, establece los criterios que determinan las provisiones que deben realizarse en relaci con las prdidas incurridas e identificables en operaciones concretas. Y por otra, establece la necesidad de hacer provisiones para cubrir las prdidas, tambin incurridas e inherentes a la cartera, pero todava no identificables de manera individualizada. Desde un punto de vista conceptual, estas provisiones reflejan el hecho de que, para los sistemas bancarios, los riesgos tienden a acumularse a lo largo de los ciclos expansivos, y a manifestarse cuando estos se acaban, es decir, tienen que ver con el comportamiento procclico que caracteriza a los mercados financieros. El sistema est disedo de tal modo que ha obligado a las entidades a constituir fondos que les permitirn absorber el impacto de un potencial incremento de las provisiones especficas. Basilea II, que ha sido objeto de regulaci en la circular del Banco de Espa 3/2008, pero que ya vena influyendo desde mucho antes en los comportamientos de nuestras entidades, supone un notable avance en la gesti de los riesgos que afrontan las entidades de crdito. Esto ha permitido, y va a permitir en el futuro, porque es un sistema que se realimenta con la experiencia, que los gestores conozcan mejor el negocio y funcionamiento de las entidades, y que puedan controlar en mayor medida los riesgos en los que incurren. La nueva normativa de solvencia tiene como objetivo hacerla ms rigurosa y sensible al riesgo, a la vez que incentivar una mejor gestin del mismo. No hay que olvidar que el peor de los riesgos en que puede incurrir un gestor bancario es su incapacidad de identificar, comprender o medir con prudencia los riesgos del negocio que acomete. No me detendr en comentar los tres pilares en que se asienta el tratamiento de la solvencia, por ser ya sobradamente conocidos, pero s destacar la importancia de que stos se observen conjuntamente, a fin de que las entidades alcancen un nivel de recursos propios acorde con su perfil de riesgos global. Por timo, en este repaso de la normativa ms reciente, las entidades de crdito espalas tambin se han enfrentado a la prueba de incorporar los mandatos de la denominada MIFID. La MIFID tiene como uno de sus objetivos la mejora de la protecci del inversor a travs de dos vas: el refuerzo de los requisitos organizativos y operativos de los proveedores de servicios de inversi, y el perfeccionamiento de las normas de conducta que rigen sus relaciones con la clientela. La mejora de la protecci del inversor, aparte de ser un objetivo legtimo en s mismo, sirve para favorecer una mejor organizacin y un control interno ms severo, lo que es una exigencia de buena gestin que redunda en una mejora operativa con efectos positivos sobre la eficiencia y la credibilidad de la entidad. Por otro lado, desde el punto de vista de gestin integral de riesgos, sirve para concienciar y sensibilizar acerca de la importancia del riesgo de reputaci. Riesgo especialmente importante en el caso de las entidades de crdito, cuyo negocio est basado precisamente en la confianza. * * * Legtimamente orgullosos de lo hecho hasta hoy no debemos, sin embargo, caer en la autocomplacencia. La coyuntura actual presenta retos importantes y elementos nuevos tanto para nuestros bancos y cajas como para los reguladores y supervisores, que deben ser valorados de forma ponderada. Es evidente que el fuerte crecimiento de la economa espala en estos ltimos as tambin ha dado lugar a diversos desequilibrios. El enorme recurso a la financiacin exterior para atender las necesidades de crdito con que apoyar dicho crecimiento, y el rpido crecimiento del endeudamiento de las familias y empresas, junto a otros factores bien conocidos, como el papel esencial que ha desempeado el mercado inmobiliario en nuestro crecimiento, son elementos que debemos tener muy presentes, pues van a determinar nuestro primo futuro. A esos desequilibrios, cuyo proceso de correcci se haba iniciado en 2006, se han sumado ahora acontecimientos mundiales que, han intensificado el ajuste creando una situaci en la que el pronunciado aumento de la morosidad y la contracci del negocio plantean retos a los que hay que hacer frente sin tardanza. Aunque el aumento de la morosidad era previsible y aunque todava no ha alcanzado niveles alarmantes, hay que hacerle frente aunando elevadas dosis de flexibilidad en su gesti y el mantenimiento de la calidad y cantidad de las provisiones y fondos propios; por su parte, la contracci del negocio obligar inevitablemente a las entidades a promover un mayor control de los costes y la racionalizacin de los procesos. Tanto la actividad bancaria como la regulatoria tendrn que adaptarse al nuevo marco, forzando a entidades y reguladores a abordar iniciativas que permitan mantener y reforzar las sidas bases de nuestro sistema bancario e impulsar su crecimiento en un mercado globalizado. En esta misma direccin de reforzar la solidez y estabilidad del sistema bancario en su conjunto, hay que situar las iniciativas que, en diferentes foros internacionales, se estn abordando para modificar la regulaci financiera y que se estn centrando en: - reforzar la solvencia de las entidades y seguir contribuyendo a la mejor gestin de los riesgos bancarios; - mejorar tanto la transparencia para inversores, mercados y reguladores, como los estndares de valoraci, en particular cuando los mercados se vuelven ilquidos; - incrementar la cooperaci y convergencia entre supervisores para asegurar la eficacia en el control prudencial de los grandes grupos transnacionales, - la prevenci de situaciones de crisis y su gesti en caso necesario, y - la mejora del funcionamiento de los mercados, incluyendo el papel de las agencias de calificaci crediticia y de la estructura de incentivos existentes. En orden a reforzar la solvencia de las entidades, prosiguiendo con la armonizacin regulatoria y la convergencia supervisora, y con el objetivo de contribuir a la estabilidad financiera, la Comisi Europea, culminando unas iniciativas puestas en marcha con anterioridad a las turbulencias del verano de 2007, acaba de presentar una propuesta de Directiva que modifica la regulaci de la solvencia actualmente en vigor en las reas que a continuaci paso a comentarles. En primer lugar, se pretende mejorar algunos elementos de la regulacin aplicable a las titulizaciones y los productos estructurados, especialmente donde las turbulencias han puesto de manifiesto la necesidad de revisar la existencia de determinados incentivos potencialmente adversos. As, para hacer frente a los conflictos de inters presentes en el modelo originar para distribuir, se propone que los originadores y los patrocinadores de instrumentos con estructuras poco transparentes retengan una parte del riesgo transferido a los inversores. Este nuevo requisito se complementa, por el lado de los inversores, con la obligaci por parte de estos de tener un conocimiento completo de los riesgos que asumen tanto por las caractersticas de las complejas estructuras en que estn invirtiendo como de los activos subyacentes. Tambin la extensin del modelo de originar para distribuir ha producido un fuerte crecimiento de los activos incluidos en la cartera de negociaci, cuyo riesgo no haba sido correctamente tenido en cuenta en la normativa actual, lo que ha aconsejado un aumento sustancial de los requerimientos de capital para estos activos, en particular, para cubrir adecuadamente su riesgo de crdito. Al mismo tiempo se plantea un reforzamiento de la calidad de los recursos propios bsicos de las entidades bancarias, de forma que los instrumentos hbridos que ahora se computan junto con el capital ordinario y las reservas, van a soportar lmites estrictos y armonizados, y dispondrn de caractersticas que los hagan verdaderamente iles en caso de crisis de una entidad. Tambin se aborda la revisi de la regulaci del riesgo de concentraci con un solo cliente o grupo de clientes vinculados entre s, con el fin de hacerla ms coherente con los mtodos aplicados para el clculo de los requerimientos de capital y de endurecer el tratamiento de diversas exposiciones y contrapartes, en particular las interbancarias, antes excluidas de estos lmites en muchos pases, aunque no en Espaa. Ms novedoso es el establecimiento de principios detallados para una adecuada gestin y supervisin del riesgo de liquidez. El objetivo es incentivar a los bancos a que adquieran un mejor conocimiento de su perfil de riesgo. As, el consejo de administraci ser el encargado de establecer el nivel apropiado de tolerancia frente al riesgo de liquidez. Por otro lado, las entidades debern realizar ejercicios de estrs e implantar los correspondientes planes de contingencia. Asimismo, se hace hincapi en la conveniencia de mantener un colchn apropiado de activos lquidos de alta calidad para hacer frente a situaciones de estrs. Finalmente, buena parte de la reforma se dedica a mejorar los mecanismos de supervisi de los grandes grupos bancarios transfronterizos; el reconocimiento legal de los colegios de supervisores, las medidas destinadas a facilitar el ejercicio de las competencias de los supervisores implicados, a coordinar su actividad y a permitir que compartan su informaci con otras autoridades, que deberan dotar de mayor eficacia a la supervisin de dichos grupos, especialmente en caso de una situaci de emergencia en una entidad con presencia en diversos pases. Adems, se pretende fortalecer el papel de los comits europeos de supervisores y, en particular el de los supervisores bancarios (el denominado CEBS) a los que se asignan tareas especficas adicionales a las que ya venan realizando de asesoramiento tcnico a la Comisi en relacin a las iniciativas legislativas que acabo de comentar; o del desarrollo de guas supervisoras para asegurar la convergencia en la implantaci de las normas europeas. Junto a estas iniciativas en Europa, el Comit de supervisores bancarios de Basilea tambin est a punto de finalizar diversos trabajos que contribuirn, globalmente, a reducir el apalancamiento del sistema y la concentracin excesiva de riesgos dentro de los grandes bancos internacionales. Esos trabajos van, desde las medidas puntuales que van a contribuir a refinar el denominado Pilar 1 en aquellos puntos que han sido ms determinantes en las prdidas sufridas por las entidades financieras durante las turbulencias, a la mejora de la gesti de riesgos y el incremento de la transparencia al mercado. Con este fin, aumentarn los requerimientos exigibles en las llamadas retitulizaciones o los de la cartera de negociaci con el fin de capturar adecuadamente ciertos elementos de riesgo de crdito que los modelos al uso no han valorado adecuadamente y de esta forma se alinear el capital regulatorio con el riesgo inherente a estas posiciones. Tambin en esta misma direccin va la gua que acaba de publicar el Comit sobre la gesti del riesgo de liquidez, donde se pretende, fundamentalmente, elevar la capacidad de los bancos para enfrentarse a posibles situaciones de estrs de liquidez, mediante, entre otros factores, un prudente colchn de activos lquidos de elevada calidad. La crisis actual ha mostrado la importancia de integrar la gesti de la liquidez en los procesos globales de gesti de riesgos de la entidad. Pero tambin la crisis ha abierto a la reflexin numerosas reas que slo voy a mencionar, por ejemplo, - la armonizacin de las medidas de prevenci y gesti de situaciones de crisis, terreno en el que jugar un papel esencial la cooperacin y convergencia, tanto entre supervisores como entre los supervisores y otros actores. - la mejora del funcionamiento de los mercados, donde se inserta, entre otras iniciativas, la de la Comisi Europea sobre la eventual regulaci de las agencias de calificacin crediticia. - la revisin de los estndares de valoraci de los activos, incluyendo la bqueda de un mtodo com de valorar los activos ilquidos en los estados contables. -el anlisis de los posibles efectos procclicos de la regulaci financiera, especialmente el posible efecto procclico de la normativa de solvencia, de la contable e, incluso de las polticas de retribucin al personal. Por timo, otra rea que sin duda alcanzar gran importancia es la de reforzar las infraestructuras sobre las que est construido el sistema financiero. Hay una necesidad creciente de que volvamos a evaluar la solidez de nuestros mercados de derivados, muy en especial los de derivados de crdito en los que se transfieren un volumen enorme de riesgos, y de nuestros sistemas de liquidacin y compensacin, junto a los principales participantes en los mismos, con el fin de asegurar que cumplen su funci (dar liquidez y precio a los productos) tanto en tiempos normales como en situaciones de estrs. * * * Tambin por su importancia en orden a la promoci de infraestructuras financieras apropiadas y por su enorme relevancia sobre una parte esencial del negocio de nuestras entidades bancarias, quiero destacar la creaci de un mercado ico de servicios de pago ligado a la Zona nica de Pagos en euros, conocido por sus siglas en ingls, SEPA, y la directiva de reciente aprobacin sobre servicios de pago. La armonizaci de las normas de conducta con la clientela en lo que se refiere a los pagos redundar en beneficio del usuario de servicios financieros, que tendr una ms amplia gama de proveedores a su disposici, con el consiguiente incremento de la eficiencia va precio y/o calidad del servicio recibido, y en unas condiciones de protecci que le permiten una adecuado nivel de confianza y seguridad. La finalidad de esta Directiva de servicios de pago es establecer un marco jurdico comn para su prestacin, marco jurdico que debe a la vez: - dotar a los usuarios de servicios de pago de un grado de proteccin de sus intereses suficiente para que dispongan del nivel seguridad necesario para confiar en la prestaci de servicios transfronterizos propia del mercado ico. - crear un terreno de juego que favorezca la oferta competitiva de estos servicios, tanto por la posibilidad de acceso de todo tipo de intermediarios solventes, como por la ausencia de trabas nacionales que dan la prestaci de estos servicios. Prepararse para la correcta aplicacin de esta norma, que supondr un cambio importante en nuestras prcticas y usos bancarios ms habituales constituye un nuevo reto que debern abordar nuestras entidades bancarias en los primos meses poniendo una vez ms a prueba la capacidad de adaptacin de sus estructuras. La implicaci del conjunto de la organizaci en su puesta en marcha contribuir sin duda a incrementar su solidez especialmente en las relaciones con los clientes minoristas. En esta misma lnea, la reciente Directiva de crdito al consumo profundiza en el mercado ico de servicios al por menor garantizando a la vez un elevado nivel de proteccin de los consumidores. Tanto por la va de una mayor transparencia en las condiciones, como por la del derecho del consumidor a desistir del crdito durante un plazo reglado, sin coste alguno para l y sin necesidad de acreditar motivo alguno, se favorecer adems una mayor responsabilidad de las entidades en la concesi rigurosa de estos crditos. He pretendido con esta intervenci proporcionar una perspectiva general de los retos regulatorios pasados, presentes y futuros. Pero djenme terminar con una reflexi general sobre las reformas del marco de regulacin. Tenemos que evitar que la crisis actual nos lleve a reaccionar pendularmente hacia la hiperregulacin. Las excepcionales circunstancias que estamos viviendo no pueden hacernos olvidar un principio que me parece esencial y es el de que toda iniciativa regulatoria, antes de aprobarse debe ser convenientemente ponderada y someterse a un examen exigente sobre su finalidad y necesidad. Muchas gracias

Title: Presentation of the Financial Stability Review devoted to Valuation. Intervention in the framework of the meetings of the Annual Meeting of the International Monetary Fund. English only
text: Washington, 12 October 2008 Presentation of the Financial Stability Review of the Banque de France devoted to Valuation Internacional Monetary Fund Jose Vils Deputy Governor of the Banco de Espa Let me start by congratulating the Banque de France for this impressive issue of the Financial Stability Review. It couldnt be more timely and right to the point. Valuation issues are at the centre of the current crisis and, certainly, understanding them better will be one of the pillars with which we will be able to build up the new regulatory framework of the future. The current crisis has revealed a series of flaws in various areas of the international financial system. One topic on which regulators, supervisors and the industry are focusing is the application of fair value, especially when there are no deep and liquid markets. Another topic is the interaction between valuation and the procyclicality of the financial system. The adverse consequences of procyclicality tend to be more intense at times, as at present, when the interplay between asset valuation and leverage has become more important. If valuation methods tend to introduce incentives to increase leverage and mispricing risks, the adjustment process when economic conditions change will be more pronounced, amplifying its adverse impact on the economy. Fair value would need to be perfected in several areas. In particular, it should allow a better evaluation of risks and profits over the business cycle and it should be compatible with promoting financial stability. Pros and cons of fair value The advantages of fair value are clear: a) fair value has proven to be the only method capable of offering a transparent, relevant and reliable valuation of a series of financial products (e.g. derivatives) b) fair value offers a closer view of the actual situation of financial markets which is closer to the view institutions use for management purposes c) fair value is associated with greater market discipline However, no valuation method is free from limitations: a) there are not always active markets, and prices are therefore not always available for use in applying fair value which means that estimating fair value involves the use of valuation methods, which in turn implies some subjectivity in their design b) When there are incentives to manipulate the information reported to the markets, the use of valuation models opens up the possibility of institutions cherry-picking specific parameters or assumptions, thereby accentuating information asymmetry problems c) Fair value increases volatility on bank balance sheets, on profit and loss accounts, and consequently on the levels of regulatory capital that banks must hold. This would intensify the procyclicality of financial markets d) As a result of the greater volatility induced in banks' profits and loss accounts, the use of fair value might create perverse incentives in banks' management decisions, placing excessive emphasis on the short term, in particular if compensation is linked to short term accounting results Furthermore, the current financial crisis has highlighted significant weaknesses regarding the implementation of fair value in at least three areas: 1) shortcomings in the design of valuation models, which have not properly captured the characteristics of the most complex products 2) it has highlighted governance problems since systems have not been appropriately designed to verify and test the valuations made 3) the information reported to the market has not been understood Is it possible to improve fair value? A return to valuation at cost is neither feasible nor desirable. Yet the application of fair value under very adverse financial market conditions has highlighted significant limitations which bear negatively on financial stability. Improving its functioning would appear to be necessary. I turn now to describing two of the potential avenues that can be explored in order to improve fair value: dynamic provisions and valuation reserves. Dynamic provisions The first mechanism that might help improve fair value is dynamic provisions. These are a good measurement of the fair value of a loan portfolio. Conceptually, provisions should be understood as adjustments to the book value of the loans. These adjustments take into consideration the impact that the credit risk borne by the institution entails for these loans. Therefore, a correct valuation of loans in the credit portfolio should also include the factors of risk which, though they have not been specified at the level of individual loans, can in fact be quantified through statistical procedures. The absence of value corrections for these reasons distorts the true and fair view that financial information should provide, hampering decision-making by investors. Dynamic provisions, as an approximation to the fair value of banks' loan portfolios, mitigate the fact that, at favourable times in the cycle, risks are taken and build up but are only disclosed with a delay in financial institutions' profit and loss accounts. Valuation reserves1 As a second improvement in fair value, institutions could set aside valuation reserves for those more complex structured products that are mark-to-model. These reserves would entail the recognition, in accounting terms, of the uncertainty associated with the calculation of fair value under specific circumstances. Banks should have different estimates of the fair value of the instrument depending on the various values these inputs may take given different assumptions and scenarios. Institutions should reflect in their accounts the estimation of the fair value of the instrument, along with a valuation reserve that reflects the uncertainties surrounding this estimation. The valuation reserves should be objective and transparent. Moreover, and this is most important, they should be symmetrical. That is, these reserves have to function both in good times and in bad times. In other words, it is not a question of generating buffers to face difficulties, but of improving the valuation of complex financial instruments by explicitly and transparently incorporating the uncertainty that surrounds the valuation. Fair value implementation problems do not emerge ex novo when economic and financial conditions turn adverse; they already exist in good times. It is precisely in these periods when agents act with excessive optimism, valuing risks inappropriately. As the current financial difficulties clearly show, the losses being posted now stem from the excesses committed in the prior years of strong economic growth. There are two further arguments in favour of valuation reserves and of dynamic provisions. If managers fail to take into account risks and profits over the cycle in their decision-making, the introduction of the proposed changes to fair value will help them do so. And that is good for risk management while, at the same time, investors are offered better information. Valuation reserves and dynamic provisions are mechanisms that also contribute to mitigating the current procyclicality of accounting rules. Both measures favour a longer-term view, and in 1 An example of how these valuation reserves could work is the following: In the valuation of complex models, the assumptions regarding asset correlations are very important and there is significant uncertainty on how and at what speed those correlations might change. Therefore, the idea would be to incorporate such an uncertainty in the valuations. In good times, when risk premiums and correlations are very low, the valuation reserve would increase while in bad times, when risk premiums and correlations overshoot, valuation reserves will decline. Alternatively, we would be marking down some complex (i.e. difficult to value) financial products in good times and marking them up in bad times. In a sense, it is an extension of the dynamic provision philosophy to other financial products. particular one through the cycle, both for managers and for those who need to evaluate the risk profile of banks. General principles for the review of fair value Beyond the specific instruments that may be considered, there is a series of general guiding principles that are relevant for reviewing fair value: 1) Search for better valuations This principle should apply both to the more quantitative aspects referring to valuation models and as regards providing a more realistic view of the risks and profits associated with business activity throughout the cycle (e.g. through dynamic provisions and valuation reserves). 2)Minimise the procyclical impact induced by fair value It should be acknowledged that, during the favourable phases in the cycle, financial market participants display a natural behaviour that leads them to build up a series of risks which, when the situation turns adverse, tend to materialise. Accounting rules should not encourage this type of behaviour. From the standpoint of the application of fair value, the use of dynamic provisions and of valuation reserves may contribute to mitigating such risks. 3)Governance Both quantitative and qualitative aspects are relevant in the implementation of valuation models. Sufficient resources should be set aside, and models should be revised and tested by independent units and subjected to different stress tests, among other considerations. 4)Transparency Investors need to be able to receive the necessary information. It will not only be important to know the volume of exposures valued by means of fair value, but also matters relating to the valuation method and inputs used, to the assumptions made and to those aspects that may contribute to users' better understanding of the financial information. Conclusion Fair value is the best standard for providing final users of financial statements with relevant, reliable and comparable information. However, fair value needs to be improved in order to strengthen the relevance, reliability and comparability of information. This can be done through two specific mechanisms (dynamic provisions and valuation reserves) within the framework of some more general guiding principles for this review process. Both share important characteristics that are relevant in terms of their effectiveness and usefulness for market participants: objectiveness, transparency and symmetry throughout the business cycle. While fair value is a clear step forward when compared, for instance, with cost valuation, the current crisis very clearly shows that it is by no means the end of the road. To continue along it, we need to effectively engage in a multilateral dialogue among accountants, regulators, supervisors and market participants so as to incorporate the much needed macro-prudential dimension both in financial regulation and accounting standards.

Title: Conference on Immigration - Presentation of the I FEDEA Report
text: Madrid, 16 October 2008 Conference on Immigration - Presentation of the I FEDEA Report Miguel Fernandez Ordez Governor of the Bank of Spain Good afternoon. Welcome to this act of presentation of the I FEDEA Report. Since its foundation in 1985, FEDEA's raison d'90tre has been to generate quality economic analyses. In all this time, FEDEA's research agenda has addressed the most relevant socio-economic problems that, at all times, the Spanish economy has faced, highlighting, among others, the labor market, pensions, or the financial situation of Spanish companies. In a more recent stage, which began last year, research at FEDEA is structured through Research Programs, which are called Research Chairs. The Bank of Spain contributes, like other employers, by financing one of these chairs, the Fuentes Quintana Chair, which is responsible for conducting and promoting research on Education and Human Capital and organizes its activities around three research themes: i) educational growth and the mismatch between the supply and demand of labor, (ii) women's labour participation and (iii) immigration. For its first annual report, the theme chosen by FEDEA has been the impact of immigration on the Spanish economy and society. In this report, as in all the others, FEDEA researchers have expressed the result of their analytical work and their opinions with total independence from the sponsoring institutions, including the Bank of Spain, which today has the satisfaction of officiating as host of this act. With this we intend to show support for the research work of the Foundation, but it should not be interpreted as an assumption of the opinions contained in the report, which belong exclusively to its authors. Before closing this event, allow me to refer in a few words to the content of this report produced by FEDEA. That the choice for FEDEA's annual report was immigration is not surprising, given that the arrival of immigrants has been one of the main events that has marked the behavior of the Spanish economy during the last decade. After this experience, it is important to draw some conclusions about the socio-economic consequences of immigration that may contribute to the process of decision-making of policies, especially in the process of economic adjustment in which the Spanish economy is immersed. In this regard, I will make four reflections that, in my opinion, should be taken into account when assessing what immigration has meant, and can mean, in the socio-economic development of our country: 1. In the first place, from a quantitative point of view, during the tima decade of the twentieth century and what we have of the first of the twenty-first century, the flows of immigrants to Europe have grown significantly, with Spain being the main receiving country. In fact, since the beginning of the twenty-first century, Spain has had an immigration rate, close to 1.5%, which has rarely been observed in other countries, except on exceptional occasions. In recent times, we can only compare such an influx of immigrants to what happened in Portugal, in the mid-1970s, after decolonization, in Israel after the fall of the Soviet regimes, or in Ireland during the economic expansion that began in the mid-80s. In the case of Espal, this arrival of immigrants explains much of the demographic momentum of the tima decade. According to the data of the Register of Inhabitants, on January 1, 2008 the non-Spanish population resident in Spain accounted for 11.33% of the total population, having increased by about 4.7 million people since 1996, a period in which the growth of the total resident population in Spain was approximately 7 million people. The foreign population resident in Spain has somewhat different individual characteristics from the Spanish population. Restricting ourselves to the immigrant population from non-EU countries(27), this is a relatively younger population with slightly lower levels of education. By having a greater weight among working-age population groups and having shown a higher activity rate than that of the Spanish population, the immigrant population has contributed to raising the employment rate. It is mainly this effect on the employment rate that has led several studies to conclude, under conservative assumptions about the relationship between immigration and productivity, that approximately 25% of the growth in per capita income during the present decade can be attributed to immigration. 2. Secondly, it must be argued that the effects of immigration on the labour market are not reduced to the employment rate. The arrival of immigrants has contributed to changing the functioning of the labour market. Too often, the labor impact of immigration is presented exclusively as competition between natives and immigrants for the same jobs. The idea that the level of employment is fixed and that, therefore, the arrival of immigrants, or their return to their countries of origin, improves the employment opportunities of the native population is a mistake from the economic point of view, as is the argument that by expelling older workers from employment, With early retirement and early retirement, the job opportunities of the jenes are improved, or that the greater labor participation of women harms the employment opportunities of men. In fact, several studies that have addressed the relationship between immigration and unemployment have not been able to find empirical evidence to support this idea. With regard to the immigrant population that has arrived in Spain, due to its individual characteristics mentioned above and its patterns of labour participation, it has proved to be complementary to the native population, engaging in activities in which the national labour supply was scarce and showing much higher levels of geographical and sectoral mobility. This has enabled job creation in labour-intensive regions and sectors. In short, immigration has helped to make the labour market more flexible and, possibly, has favoured that certain groups of the population may have improved their productivity. 3. There is another common error in economic debates, the so-called "fallacy of composition", which consists in attributing something to a phenomenon as a whole, when that attribution may only be correct in relation to one of the parts of that phenomenon. For example, a decrease in the average income at a given time and country is interpreted as a decrease in the income of all individuals in that country, although what may have happened is that, having increased the income of many or all individuals, the percentage of the population with the lowest income has also increased. By ignoring these compositional effects, causal relationships are usually established between two variables, without taking into account that the supposed cause is the result of adding heterogeneous observations. Consequently, the fact that the immigrant population has somewhat different individual characteristics from the native population is also relevant for the analysis of other socio-economic consequences of immigration as varied, such as, for example, the demand for services and social benefits or their impact on the exchange relationship between unemployment and inflation. A very relevant issue for the tasks entrusted to the Central Banks. For example, a working paper recently published in the Bank of Spain series concludes that the different labour behaviour of immigrants, in terms of their labour supply, explains why, during the recent economic expansion in which the unemployment rate fell by more than 10 percentage points, The inflation rate has remained about two percentage points below what would have resulted in the absence of immigration. There is another example of the importance of taking into account heterogeneity in the analysis of the impact of immigration: when it is stated that the immigrant population is more likely to demand certain social services than the native population, it is usually done, incorrectly, by comparing the average demand of all immigrants and that of natives. not comparing the demand for such services from immigrants and natives of the same individual characteristics. Consequently, the analysis of the socio-economic consequences of immigration must recognize individual heterogeneity and establish causal relationships from microeconomic data that allow these relationships to be adequately identified. The use of databases that allow these empirical exercises and the application of appropriate methods of analysis are the basis for a better understanding of the phenomenon of immigration. 4. Finally, in the analysis of immigration, as in that of many other issues with economic impact, it is necessary to clarify the time horizon in question. Results or implications that are true in the short term are not necessarily true in the long term. For example, it is well known that an increase in the savings rate, by reducing consumption, tends to slow down the growth of economic activity in the short term. However, in the long run, only a higher rate of savings can allow the accumulation of capital and knowledge leading to greater production. In the case of immigration, there is an optimistic view, But erring, that the arrival of immigrants helps significantly to solve the problem of financing pensions in the face of the aging process of the population in which we are immersed. While it is true that, in the short term, being a relatively young population with a high employment rate, their contributions to Social Security far exceed the benefits received in the form of retirement pensions, the same will not happen, in a period of two or three decades, when immigrants currently active in the labour market retire and begin to receive the benefits generated by their contributions. In more general terms, there are many aspects that can condition its socio-economic consequences in the medium and long term. The patterns of return of immigrants to their countries of origin, the process of assimilation of immigrants who remain in our country, or the behavior of the second generation of immigrants in the educational system and in the labor market are the most important. As you can see, the analysis of the socio-economic consequences of immigration is an arduous task that must take into account many dimensions and should be addressed with sufficient statistical information and rigorous methods of analysis, such as that contained in the Report we are presenting today. Only in this way can we obtain a reliable knowledge of this phenomenon so important for the current Spain. Thank you very much for your attention and I close this act of presentation of the Annual Report of FEDEA.
text_original: Madrid, 16 de octubre de 2008 Jornadas sobre Inmigraci - Presentaci del I Informe FEDEA Miguel Fernndez Ordez Gobernador del Banco de Espa Buenas tardes. Bienvenidos a este acto de presentaci del I Informe FEDEA. Desde su fundacin en 1985, la raz de ser de FEDEA ha sido generar anlisis econicos de calidad. En todo este tiempo, la agenda investigadora de FEDEA ha abordado los problemas socioeconicos ms relevantes que, en cada momento, ha afrontado la economa espaola, destacando, entre otros, el mercado de trabajo, las pensiones, o la situaci financiera de las empresas espaolas. En una etapa ms reciente, que se iniciel ao pasado, la investigacin en FEDEA se estructura a travs de Programas de Investigaci, que se denominan Ctedras de Investigacin. El Banco de Espaa contribuye, al igual que otros patronos, financiando una de dichas ctedras, la ctedra Fuentes Quintana, que se ocupa de realizar y promover la investigacin sobre Educacin y Capital Humano y que organiza sus actividades alrededor de tres temas de investigaci: i) el incremento educacional y el desajuste entre la oferta y la demanda de trabajo, ii) la participaci laboral de la mujer y iii) la inmigracin. Para su primer informe anual, el tema elegido por FEDEA ha sido el impacto de la inmigracin sobre la economa y la sociedad espalas. En este informe como en todos los dems, los investigadores de FEDEA han plasmado el resultado de su trabajo analtico y sus opiniones con total independencia respecto de las instituciones patrocinadoras, incluido el Banco de Espa, que hoy tiene la satisfaccin de oficiar como anfitri de este acto. Con ello pretendemos mostrar el respaldo a la labor investigadora de la Fundacin, pero licamente no debe interpretarse como una asunci de las opiniones recogidas en el informe, que pertenecen exclusivamente a sus autores. Antes de clausurar este acto, permtanme que me refiera con unas breves palabras al contenido de este informe realizado por FEDEA. Que la elecci para el informe anual de FEDEA haya sido la inmigracin no resulta sorprendente, dado que la llegada de inmigrantes ha sido uno de los principales acontecimientos que ha marcado el comportamiento de la economa espala durante la tima dcada. Tras esta experiencia, es importante extraer algunas conclusiones sobre las consecuencias socioeconmicas de la inmigraci que puedan contribuir al proceso de decisi de polticas plicas, en especial en el proceso de ajuste econico en el que se encuentra inmersa la economa espaola. A este respecto, realizar a continuacin cuatro reflexiones que, a mi juicio, deberan ser tenidas en cuenta a la hora de valorar lo que ha supuesto, y puede suponer, la inmigracin en el desarrollo socioeconico de nuestro pas: 1. En primer lugar, desde un punto de vista cuantitativo, durante la tima dcada del siglo XX y lo que llevamos de la primera del siglo XXI, los flujos de inmigrantes hacia Europa han crecido notablemente, siendo Espa el principal pas receptor. De hecho, desde el inicio del siglo XXI, Espaa ha tenido una tasa de inmigracin, cercana al 1,5%, que raramente se ha observado en otros pases, salvo en ocasiones excepcionales. En pocas recientes, solo cabe comparar tal flujo de inmigrantes a lo sucedido en Portugal, a mediados de los 1970s, tras la descolonizacin, en Israel tras la cada de los regmenes soviticos, o en Irlanda durante la expansin econica que se inicia mediados de los 80. En el caso espal, esta llegada de inmigrantes explica buena parte del impulso demogrfico de la tima dcada. Seg los datos del Padr de Habitantes, a 1 de enero de 2008 la poblacin no espala residente en Espa supona el 11,33% de la poblaci total, habindose incrementado en alrededor de 4,7 millones de personas desde 1996, periodo en el cual el crecimiento de la poblacin total residente en Espaa fue de aproximadamente 7 millones de personas. La poblacin extranjera residente en Espa tiene unas caractersticas individuales algo distintas de la poblacin espala. Restringindonos a la poblaci inmigrante de pases que no pertenecen a la UE(27), se trata de una poblaci relativamente ms joven y con niveles educativos ligeramente inferiores. Al tener mayor peso los grupos de poblacin en edad de trabajar y haber mostrado una tasa de actividad ms elevada que la de la poblacin espala, la poblacin inmigrante ha contribuido a elevar la tasa de empleo. Es principalmente este efecto sobre la tasa de empleo lo que ha llevado a varios estudios a concluir, bajo supuestos conservadores acerca de la relaci entre la inmigracin y la productividad, que aproximadamente un 25% del crecimiento de la renta per cpita espala durante la presente dcada se puede atribuir a la inmigraci. 2. En segundo lugar, hay que selar que los efectos de la inmigracin sobre el mercado de trabajo no se reducen a la tasa de empleo. La llegada de inmigrantes ha contribuido a cambiar el funcionamiento del mercado de trabajo. En demasiadas ocasiones, el impacto laboral de la inmigracin se presenta exclusivamente como la competencia entre nativos e inmigrantes por los mismos puestos de trabajo. La idea de que el nivel de empleo est fijo y de que, por tanto, la llegada de inmigrantes, o su retorno a sus pases de origen, mejora las oportunidades de empleo de la poblaci nativa es un error desde el punto de vista econmico, como lo es sostener que expulsando del empleo a los trabajadores mayores, con prejubilaciones y jubilaciones anticipadas, se mejora las oportunidades laborales de los jenes, o que la mayor participaci laboral de las mujeres perjudica las oportunidades de empleo de los varones. De hecho, varios estudios que han abordado la relacin entre inmigracin y desempleo no han podido encontrar evidencia emprica que permita sostener esta idea. Por lo que respecta a la poblacin inmigrante que ha llegado a Espaa, por sus caractersticas individuales mencionadas anteriormente y por sus pautas de participaci laboral, ha resultado ser complementaria a la poblacin nativa, ocupndose en actividades en la que la oferta de trabajo nacional era escasa y mostrando unos niveles de movilidad geogrfica y sectoriales muy superiores, lo que ha permitido la creaci de empleo en regiones y sectores intensivos en mano de obra. En definitiva, la inmigracin ha contribuido a flexibilizar el mercado de trabajo y, posiblemente, haya favorecido que determinados grupos de la poblaci puedan haber mejorado su productividad. 3. Existe otro error com en los debates econicos, la denominada falacia de la composici, que consiste en atribuir algo a un fenmeno en su conjunto, cuando dicha atribuci puede que solo sea correcta en relaci a una de las partes de dicho feneno. Por ejemplo, una disminucin de la renta media en un determinado momento y pas se interpreta como una disminucin de la renta de todos los individuos de dicho pas, aunque puede que lo ico que haya ocurrido es que, habiendo aumentado la renta de muchos o todos los individuos, tambin se haya incrementado el porcentaje de la poblacin con menor renta. Al ignorar estos efectos de composici, se suelen establecer relaciones causales entre dos variables, sin tener en cuenta que la supuesta causa es el resultado de agregar observaciones heterogneas. En consecuencia, el hecho de que la poblaci inmigrante tenga caractersticas individuales algo distintas de la poblaci nativa resulta tambin relevante para el anlisis de otras consecuencias socioeconmicas de la inmigracin tan variadas, como, por ejemplo, la demanda de servicios y de prestaciones sociales o su impacto sobre la relaci de intercambio entre desempleo e inflaci, una cuesti muy relevante para las labores que tienen encomendadas los bancos centrales. Por ejemplo, en un documento de trabajo recientemente publicado en la serie del Banco de Espa se concluye que el distinto comportamiento laboral de los inmigrantes, en lo que se refiere a su oferta de trabajo, explica que, durante la reciente expansin econica en la que la tasa de desempleo se redujo en ms de 10 puntos porcentuales, la tasa de inflacin se haya mantenido alrededor de dos puntos porcentuales por debajo de lo que hubiera resultado en ausencia de la inmigraci. Hay otro ejemplo sobre la importancia de tener en cuenta la heterogeneidad en el anlisis del impacto de la inmigraci: cuando se afirma que la poblaci inmigrante es ms proclive a demandar determinados servicios sociales que la poblaci nativa, se suele hacer, incorrectamente, comparando la demanda media del conjunto de inmigrantes y la de los nativos, no comparando la demanda de dichos servicios de inmigrantes y nativos de las mismas caractersticas individuales. En consecuencia, el anlisis de las consecuencias socioeconmicas de la inmigracin debe reconocer la heterogeneidad individual y establecer relaciones causales a partir de datos microeconmicos que permitan identificar adecuadamente dichas relaciones. La utilizacin de bases de datos que permitan estos ejercicios empricos y la aplicaci de los mtodos de anlisis apropiados son la base para la mejor comprensin del feneno de la inmigracin. 4. Finalmente, en el anlisis de la inmigraci, al igual que en el de muchos otros asuntos con impacto econico, conviene aclarar el horizonte temporal en cuesti. Resultados o implicaciones que son ciertas en el corto plazo, no necesariamente lo son en el largo plazo. Por ejemplo, es bien sabido que un incremento de la tasa de ahorro, al reducir el consumo, tiende a ralentizar el crecimiento de la actividad econica en el corto plazo. Sin embargo, en el largo plazo, solo una mayor tasa de ahorro puede permitir la acumulaci de capital y de conocimientos que den lugar a una mayor producci. En el caso de la inmigracin, existe la visin optimista, pero errea, de que la llegada de inmigrantes ayuda significativamente a resolver el problema de financiaci de las pensiones ante el proceso de envejecimiento de la poblaci en el que estamos inmersos. Siendo cierto que, en el corto plazo, al tratarse de una poblacin relativamente joven y con una tasa de empleo elevado, sus contribuciones a la Seguridad Social superan con creces las prestaciones recibidas en forma de pensiones de jubilacin, no ocurrir lo mismo, en un periodo de dos o tres dcadas, cuando los inmigrantes actualmente activos en el mercado de trabajo se jubilen y pasen a recibir las prestaciones generadas por sus contribuciones. En trminos ms generales, hay muchos aspectos que pueden condicionar sus consecuencias socioeconmicas a medio y largo plazo. Las pautas de retorno de los inmigrantes a sus pases de origen, el proceso de asimilacin de los inmigrantes que permanezcan en nuestro pas, o el comportamiento de la segunda generaci de inmigrantes en el sistema educativo y en el mercado de trabajo son los ms importantes. Como ven, el anlisis de las consecuencias socioeconicas de la inmigracin es una tarea ardua que debe contemplar numerosas dimensiones y conviene abordarlo contando con la suficiente informacin estadstica y mtodos de anlisis rigurosos, como el contenido en el Informe que hoy presentamos. Solo as podremos obtener un conocimiento fiable de este feneno tan importante para la Espa actual. Muchas gracias por su atencin y doy por clausurado este acto de presentaci del Informe Anual de FEDEA.

Title: Reflections on the international financial crisis. Intervention at the "V Meeting of the banking sector: The global opportunity" organized by IESE
text: Madrid, 28 October 2008 "Reflections on the international financial crisis" V Meeting of the banking sector: The global opportunity of the event/IESE Business School Jose Vils Deputy Governor of Banco de Espa I would like to begin by thanking IESE and, in particular, the organizers, Professors Nueno and Toribio, for their invitation to deliver this inaugural conference at a meeting that revolves around the financial system, at a time when international markets are going through a time of turmoil and when news agency teletypes have become accustomed to causing us a shock without giving us time to recover from the previous one. No one doubts that the current international financial crisis is the most important, complex, profound and with the greatest global repercussions of the past decades. The difficulties experienced by the financial systems of the main countries in the last fifteen months highlight the inability of the new international financial system, which has been confirmed in recent years in the wake of the processes of integration, globalization and innovation, to face major shocks without resisting their stability. And if we had to choose a word to define the situation of the markets in the timas weeks, it would be none other than "vertigo", given the materialization of numerous extreme and very costly events, which only a few months before would have been considered highly unlikely and that have affected a wide spectrum of financial institutions. In order to address these issues, I shall divide my speech into two parts. In the first, I will review the main features of the global financial situation, focusing on the analysis of the problems and the solutions that have been designed to overcome them. And then I will turn to the challenges that the current financial turmoil poses to stability, with particular emphasis on some initiatives undertaken at global and European level with a medium-term perspective to lay the foundations for a more stable financial system that avoids the repetition of crises such as the current one. * * * * * * If there is a characteristic that distinguishes this crisis from other episodes recorded in recent decades, it is that its epicenter has not been located in fragile or emerging economies, but in the US, the world's leading economy. It is also remarkable the speed and virulence with which its effects have spread geographically, which is explained by the intensity of the processes of financial innovation and globalization, a positive trend from many points of view but which today decreases the capacity of borders to act as firewalls and opens circuits through which risk circulates fluidly. The new globalized and innovative international financial system has been subjected, for the first time, to a serious test, since until now it had been consolidating in an era of unusually prolonged prosperity. However, it is clear that the test has not been passed. The current situation does not, of course, refute the concepts of globalization and innovation, but it does force us to rethink some of the paths they had entered. This crisis also has traditional elements, among which the lack of prudence of too many banks in their credit operations and other investments, which has led to the existence of given assets as a result of the mistakes made in the decisions that have been taken. The subprime mortgages, the American subprime mortgages that we have been talking about so much, should never have gone beyond the client's proposal phase. But, unfortunately, the subprime problem is only the tip of the iceberg of forms of behavior widespread in the current financial system. The factor that best explains the breakdown of the line of prudence required in bank management is the presence of the new banking model known as "originate to distribute", in which some entities approve operations whose risk is transferred to third parties through the capital markets. In this model, there has been a chain failure in the incentive systems of all the agents involved: borrowers who have assumed loans improperly; lenders who have granted them recklessly; the intermediaries who have distributed them; rating agencies that have incorrectly assessed the risk of complex structured products; and private investors d0 both individuals and entities d0 who have acquired them by relying excessively on such valuations without carrying out a proper analysis of the risk incurred. For all the above, it is clear that the regulatory and supervisory systems have not worked as would have been desirable in many countries, since they have not treated with the necessary rigor the risks and off-balance sheet structures, which really acted as parallel banks but without capital. With this base of weaknesses of a microeconomic nature, the problem has been able to reach the current magnitude thanks to the macroeconomic environment in which it has been brewing: a situation of abundant international liquidity at a very low cost, which has boosted the possibility of borrowing and the desire to do so by bidding and demanding agents who discounted, with little historical perspective and some ignorance of the fundamentals of the economy, that the low-risk expectations quoted by the markets were to remain continuously in a kind of new beneficial and peaceful world economic order. These expectations d0 which were neither rational nor reasonable d0 have favoured the excessive growth of indebtedness and the parallel increase in asset prices in a procyclical process in which both tendencies were mutually reinforcing while the parties watched it serenely, as if it were a virtuous circle, when in reality it was forming a spiral of danger. One of the reasons behind this serenity was the conviction that the financial system distributed risk effectively outside the banking system, which increased its capacity to withstand shocks of various kinds and high magnitude without jeopardizing its stability. However, one of the lessons we have learned from the onset of the crisis is that risk transfer markets have not served to distribute risk outside the banking system as effectively as previously thought. Thus, many of the risks that had been transferred nominally were not effectively transferred, eventually becoming re-intermediated on the balance sheets of many of the world's major banks, which exerts a strong pressure on their capital ratios. But even in those cases where the risks were effectively distributed, they ended up falling not so much on the agents best placed to absorb them but on those with the least capacity to understand them. On the other hand, more recent events highlight the need to distinguish between genuine and spurious financial innovations; that is, between those that really offer investors new combinations between risk, profitability and liquidity, and those that do so. Consequently, it is not surprising that the financial storm in which we are immersed is carrying out a selection process, in which the financial innovations that have been questioned disappear and others survive after making the relevant modifications. * * * * * * The dizzying pace of events in recent weeks and, in particular, after the bankruptcy of Lehman Brothers, has meant the erosion of the basic pillar of any financial system or market: confidence. Erosi is also widespread in multiple directions, since it affects poorly sophisticated actors, such as retail depositors of banks, but also professional managers, such as the treasurers of large banking entities.
