And it also occurs globally, once the financial systems of the main European countries and, in these days, the emerging economies have also been affected. As a result, financial systems do not operate normally and do not fulfil their function of efficiently allocating available resources, with consequent dangers for the real economy and for global economic growth, which are reflected, among others, in the Evolution of the stock markets. It is in this difficult context that we must analyze the measures recently announced, both by various central banks and by the G8 and the European Union, to try to reactivate the markets and transmit confidence to economic agents. On the one hand, the main central banks of the world (among which are the Federal Reserve, the ECB and the Bank of England) have been acting in coordination in these months in the provision of dares, while they have been opening new possibilities for entities to obtain liquidity in their respective markets. On the other hand, a concerted reduction in intervention interest rates of 50 basis points has been carried out in concert for several weeks, an unprecedented action which demonstrates the understanding that global problems in turn require global responses. In addition to this interest rate set, the ECB made significant changes to the instrument of monetary policy in order to stabilise short-term market interest rates, so that it has moved from fully meeting the demand for liquidity at the official rate in its auctions, to narrowing the corridor between the rates of credit and deposit facilities, and to expand the range of eligible collateral. But there has been no coordination on the part of central banks. In the EU, following steps to increase depositor guarantees, and in the light of ongoing initiatives in the United States and the United Kingdom, the highest policy makers in member countries have set out five general principles for action. Firstly, after showing its full support for the measures adopted by the ECB to ensure liquidity, mechanisms are designed to facilitate financing for credit institutions, establishing the possibility for the State to guarantee medium-term debt issues made by banks. Secondly, Member States may strengthen the capital of credit institutions, and in particular tier 1 capital, through the acquisition of preferred shares or any other instrument with similar characteristics. Thirdly, there is an explicit commitment to prevent the failure of relevant financial institutions, protecting the interests of taxpayers and ensuring that the shareholders and managers of these institutions bear the consequences of the intervention. Fourth, competent authorities are called upon to provide sufficient flexibility in the implementation of valuation accounting standards in the currently exceptional circumstances of market uncertainty. Fifthly, it highlights the need to improve cooperation procedures between European countries in order to achieve efficient crisis management. The Spanish authorities, within the framework of European cooperation described above and in line with the presentation of the national plans that the governments of the EU countries are carrying out In these days, they have also announced, as you know, a set of measures to increase confidence and help restore the functioning of the markets. All the measures that have been taken in the main countries and economic areas, extraordinary for their magnitude and also for their symbolic significance, are intended to send a clear and forceful message to all market agents regarding the attitude of the public authorities. That is, that one is aware of the gravity of the situation and that one is prepared to do what is necessary to avoid the risk of a collapse of the international financial system. What is needed now is to implement the agreed measures diligently and effectively so that they can contribute to restoring normality. * * * * * * Having examined the factors underlying the international financial crisis and the authorities' exit programmes, I will now turn to the proposals currently being developed, with a medium-term perspective, to strengthen financial stability. The development of the crisis makes it necessary to strike a balance between the need to stabilise the situation in the short term and to introduce appropriate measures in the medium term in order, on the one hand, to avoid similar problems in the future; and, on the other, to recover a fully market framework but correcting the excesses of the past. The global nature of the crisis calls for intensified coordination and cooperation between national authorities d0 governments, central banks and supervisors d0 international financial institutions, standard-setting agencies and the private sector. I will therefore devote this second part of my speech to reviewing the various initiatives, global and European, that are under way to strengthen the international financial system. I believe that, with the crisis, part of the achievements of previous years in the area of financial integration have been affected. Thus, a process of renationalization of the markets has been observed with a decline in activity in the markets of international financing. In addition, contagion has led to cross-border financial operations practically disappearing. Finally, the extent of the contagion from the US crisis to the European banking sector has been greater than expected. There is no doubt that the current difficulties constitute a very demanding test for the process of financial globalization. Indeed, recent months have revealed shortcomings in the international financial system that illustrate the difficult relationship between the process of globalization and financial stability. In any case, turbulence cannot act. as a brake on globalisation and, in particular, on the integration of markets, but by On the contrary, they should be a stimulus for the achievement of global solutions that allow increasing the resilience of the financial system. Global solutions to which Europe must contribute in a relevant way by virtue of its weight in the international context. The crisis has provoked a broad debate on the functioning of the financial system, ranging from aspects such as supervisory structures, financial regulation and market infrastructures, to banks' risk management processes or business strategies. This has led to different initiatives to address the new challenges that are at different stages of preparation. However, the fact that the crisis is in full swing means that the lessons to be learned and the recommendations that can be made are necessarily preliminary. I will mention just some of these initiatives, which cover many fronts and at the head of which are those promoted by the Financial Stability Forum, at global level, and by ECOFIN, within the framework of the European Union, without forgetting that, in recent days, a process has also been launched to reformulate the international financial architecture on the basis of the guidelines that come out of the summit that will take place in Washington on November 15. In particular, the ECOFIN of October 2007 decrees a roadmap to respond to malfunctioning markets, which is updated periodically and is in line with the recommendations made by the Financial Stability Forum. The actions and recommendations set out in the roadmap are addressed not only to the committees of supervisors, the European Central Bank and the Commission itself, but also to industry, and cover not only a wide spectrum of market participants, but also a wide range of areas such as transparency, valuation standards, prudential regulation, rating agencies and coordination between supervisors. Let me, therefore, now turn briefly to each of these aspects. The restoration of market confidence and the increased resilience of the financial system require the strengthening of transparency and information to the market of the risks actually assumed and of the valuation standards of financial instruments. The International Accounting Standards Board (IAS Board), in this regard, has established a panel of experts to assist in the review of good practices in the area of valuation techniques for financial instruments when markets are not active. In addition, it is revising the accounting framework for off-balance sheet vehicles which will clarify the principle that institutions should consolidate all entities they control. The turbulence has also highlighted the need to strengthen some aspects of the prudential framework, risk management and supervision in the financial sector. In particular, it aims to increase capital requirements for certain complex structured products, such as resecuritisations, and seeks to overcome an inadequate incentive structure associated with structured loans and securitisations. In particular, incentives for originators to transfer the full risk of securitised assets to investors should be reduced. In addition, principles have been published that seek to strengthen the standards for prudent liquidity risk management. The role and use of ratings by both bank managers and the regulatory framework is also the subject of in-depth debate. There has been much discussion about the role that rating agencies have had in the development of the crisis and the international gain that groups securities supervisors (IOSCO) publish May a review of the Conduct of Rating Agencies to protect the quality and integrity of the rating process. This is intended to ensure the independence of rating agencies and avoid conflicts of interest. In addition, it is intended to strengthen the supervision (oversight) of these entities and anticipates the possibility of the existence of a register of rating agencies. The lack of confidence of market players in structured products requires particular attention, given the very important role they have played in the financing of banks. One way to contribute to the recovery of confidence would be through product standardization. A further step would be taken by addressing weaknesses in the operational infrastructures of over-the-counter (OTC) derivatives markets. In particular, the creation of a central settlement system for credit default swaps (CDS), which reduces counterparty risk from a greater automation in clearing and settlement systems would help to activate the market. In addition, it would allow to know almost instantaneously the distribution of losses associated with any credit event, something that is impossible today. On the subject of supervisory coordination, the Financial Stability Forum has set up a small group of supervisors to develop the necessary protocols for the establishment of international supervisory colleges for large financial institutions. This is important given that schools have great flexibility in order to adapt to the characteristics of the different members of the group. Finally, I think it is very important to mention the initiatives underway to address the problems of procyclicality of the financial system and the regulatory and accounting framework. When I speak of procyclicality, as you know, I am referring to the vicious circles that originate in the phases of expansion through the mutual reinforcement of the increase in indebtedness and asset prices, the easing of credit policies and the assumption of increasing levels of risk. These phenomena have their inevitable and painful corollary d0 as we are currently seeing d0 in contractionary phases, in the form of falls in asset prices, tightening of the conditions of access to credit, deleveraging and fear of risk. Since, as experience shows, the market is not able to provide compensation mechanisms for excessive procyclicality, it is up to the public authorities to correct them. However, we must be aware that one of the weaknesses of the financial system that the current situation has revealed is the lack of a fine-tuned link between regulation and supervision that are structured around individual entities and the collective objective of guaranteeing the financial stability of the system. Hence, based on the consensus that the procyclicality of the financial system has played a fundamental role in the origin and development of the crisis, it is essential to intensify the dialogue between regulators and supervisors, accounting standard-setting bodies and industry in order to reduce procyclicality. And this dialogue must, necessarily, allow the introduction of the macroprudential dimension in regulation and accounting standards. In my view, dynamic provisions for loans, such as shovel provisions, the establishment of valuation reserves for mark-to-model assets and the introduction of countercyclical elements in capital regulation can make an important contribution to this objective. * * * * * * In conclusion, in the course of my intervention I have highlighted how the financial crisis is testing the resilience of the global financial system and the robustness of national and international policy mechanisms in the area of financial stability. Recalling the famous phrase of the President of the United States Franklin Delano Roosevelt during the difficult times of the Great Depression, it is true that in the current circumstances: "What is most to be feared is precisely fear". To combat this fear and restore the confidence that will allow us to emerge from the crisis, the authorities of different countries have adopted measures that in many cases can only be described as extraordinary. And, at the same time, an important number of proposals have been formulated and developed to strengthen the financial system in the medium term, enhancing its most stabilizing elements through the lessons of the crisis. As a supervisor and as a central banker, I want to convey to you a final message of realistic serenity: although the situation we are going through is unparalleled, I believe that the existing problems, whose seriousness is evident, have a solution. Or, in other words, although it will not be quick or easy, I am convinced that we will overcome this global financial crisis. I believe that we must trust that the instruments of intervention in the markets (novel, comprehensive and powerful) that are being used by the authorities of many countries (governments, central banks and supervisors) in a framework of close cooperation and dialogue with private actors, will contribute to restoring normality in the functioning of markets and the financial system. But these public actions must not lead to a weakening of the commitment of the private sector. That is why it is essential for shareholders and bank managers to assume the appropriate responsibilities. At the same time, it is vital that the room for manoeuvre gained thanks to public intervention does not lead to a relaxation of the attitude of private managers, especially if we take into account the complex environment in which entities will operate in the first months. That is, they must take advantage of the respite allowed by the measures being taken to undertake those actions, for example cost containment and restructuring, that allow this cyclical phase to be successfully overcome. Obviously, public intervention is in this case a necessary, but not sufficient, condition for success. By scam, I think this is not the time to conclude that the time of the market has already passed and that of the State has arrived. To deduce from what has happened that, once the crisis is over, we must go to more State and less market would, in my opinion, be an erroneous and dangerous lesson. What we need is not more, but better state, and not less, but better market. And this requires an improved system of financial regulation and supervision, which corrects the incentives of private agents to incur in the excesses of the past and allows financial markets to function well. Markets that must be increasingly global, effectively distribute resources and have a degree of stability that they have lacked so far. This, then, is the pending task: to improve the process of financial globalisation and not to conclude it or, much less, to set it back. Thanks a lot.
text_original: Madrid, 28 de octubre de 2008 Reflexiones sobre la crisis financiera internacional V Encuentro del sector bancario: La oportunidad global del acto/IESE Business School Jos Vils Subgobernador del Banco de Espa Quiero comenzar agradeciendo al IESE y, en particular, a los organizadores, Profesores Nueno y Toribio, su invitacin para pronunciar esta conferencia inaugural en un encuentro que gira en torno al sistema financiero, en unos momentos en que los mercados internacionales atraviesan una poca de convulsin y en que los teletipos de las agencias de noticias se han acostumbrado a causarnos un sobresalto sin darnos tiempo para recuperarnos del anterior. Nadie duda ya de que la actual crisis financiera internacional es la ms importante, compleja, profunda y de mayores repercusiones globales de las timas dcadas. Las dificultades por las que han atravesado los sistemas financieros de los principales pases en los ltimos quince meses ponen de manifiesto la incapacidad del nuevo sistema financiero internacional que se ha ido confirmando en los ltimos aos al hilo de los procesos de integracin, globalizacin e innovaci, para hacer frente a perturbaciones de envergadura sin que se resista su estabilidad. Y si hubiera que escoger una palabra para definir la situaci de los mercados en las timas semanas, sta no sera otra que vrtigo, dada la materializacin de numerosos eventos extremos y muy costosos, que tan so unos meses antes se hubieran considerado como altamente improbables y que han afectado a un amplio espectro de instituciones financieras. Con objeto de abordar estas cuestiones, voy a dividir mi intervencin en dos partes. En la primera, repasar los principales rasgos de la situacin financiera global, centrndome en el anlisis de los problemas y de las soluciones que se han disedo para superarlas. Y, posteriormente, pasar a examinar los retos que las actuales perturbaciones financieras entraan para la estabilidad, haciendo especial hincapi en algunas iniciativas emprendidas a nivel global y europeo con una perspectiva de medio plazo para sentar las bases de un sistema financiero ms estable que evite la repeticin de crisis como la actual. * * * * * * Si hay una caracterstica que distingue esta crisis de otros episodios registrados en las timas dcadas es que su epicentro no se ha situado en economas frgiles o emergentes, sino en EEUU, la primera economa mundial. Tambin es reseble la rapidez y virulencia con que se han extendido sus efectos geogrficamente, lo que se explica por la intensidad de los procesos de innovaci financiera y globalizaci, una tendencia positiva desde muchos puntos de vista pero que disminuye hoy en da la capacidad de las fronteras para actuar como cortafuegos y abre circuitos por donde circula el riesgo con fluidez. El nuevo sistema financiero internacional globalizado e innovador ha sido sometido, por primera vez, a un test serio, pues hasta ahora se haba venido consolidando en una poca de bonanza inusualmente prolongada. Sin embargo, resulta evidente que el test no ha sido superado. La situaci actual no refuta, desde luego, los conceptos de globalizaci e innovaci, pero s obliga a replantear algunos de los caminos por los que se haban adentrado. Tambin esta crisis presenta elementos tradicionales, entre los que destaca la falta de prudencia de demasiados bancos en sus operaciones de crdito y otras inversiones, que ha dado lugar a la existencia de activos dados como consecuencia de los errores cometidos en las decisiones que se han tomado. Las hipotecas de alto riesgo, las hipotecas subprime americanas de las que tanto venimos hablando, no deberan haber pasado nunca de la fase de propuesta del cliente. Pero, desafortunadamente, el problema del subprime es solo la punta del iceberg de unas formas de comportamiento muy extendidas en el sistema financiero actual. El factor que mejor explica la quiebra de la lnea de prudencia exigible en la gestin bancaria es la presencia del nuevo modelo de banca conocido como originar para distribuir, en el que algunas entidades aprueban operaciones cuyo riesgo se transfiere a terceros a travs de los mercados de capitales. En dicho modelo se ha producido un fallo en cadena en los sistemas de incentivos de todos los agentes involucrados: los prestatarios que han asumido crditos indebidamente; los prestamistas que los han concedido imprudentemente; los intermediarios que los han distribuido; las agencias de rating que han valorado incorrectamente el riesgo de los productos estructurados complejos; y los inversores privados tanto particulares como entidades que los han adquirido findose en exceso de dichas valoraciones sin llevar a cabo un anlisis adecuado del riesgo contrado. Por todo lo anterior, resulta evidente que tampoco han funcionado como hubiera sido deseable los sistemas de regulacin y supervisin en no pocos pases, al no haber tratado con el necesario rigor los riesgos y las estructuras fuera de balance, que realmente actuaban como bancos paralelos pero sin capital. Con esta base de debilidades de carcter microeconico, el problema ha podido alcanzar la magnitud actual gracias al entorno macroeconico en que se ha ido gestando: una situaci de abundante liquidez internacional a coste muy reducido, que ha impulsado la posibilidad de endeudarse y el deseo de hacerlo por agentes oferentes y demandantes que descontaban, con escasa perspectiva histrica y cierto desconocimiento de los fundamentos de la economa, que las expectativas de bajo riesgo cotizadas por los mercados iban a permanecer de manera continuada en una especie de nuevo orden econico mundial benfico y apacible. Estas expectativas que no eran ni racionales ni razonables han favorecido el crecimiento excesivo del endeudamiento y el incremento paralelo del precio de los activos en un proceso procclico en que ambas tendencias se iban realimentando mutuamente mientras las partes lo observaban con serenidad, como si se tratara de un crculo virtuoso, cuando en la realidad iba conformando una espiral de peligro. Una de las razones en las que se fundamentaba dicha serenidad era el convencimiento de que el sistema financiero distribua el riesgo eficazmente fuera del sistema bancario, lo que aumentaba su capacidad para resistir perturbaciones de diversa naturaleza y elevada magnitud sin ver peligrar su estabilidad. Sin embargo, una de las lecciones que hemos aprendido tras el inicio de la crisis es que los mercados de transferencia de riesgos no han servido para distribuir el riesgo fuera del sistema bancario tan eficazmente como se pensaba. As, muchos de los riesgos que se haban transferido de forma nominal no lo estaban de forma efectiva, con lo que eventualmente se vieron re-intermediados en los balances de muchos de los principales bancos mundiales, lo que ejerciuna fuerte presi sobre sus ratios de capital. Pero incluso en aquellos casos en que los riesgos fueron efectivamente distribuidos, estos terminaron recayendo no tanto en los agentes mejor situados para absorberlos sino en aquellos con menor capacidad para entenderlos. De otra parte, los acontecimientos ms recientes ponen de manifiesto la necesidad de distinguir entre las innovaciones financieras genuinas y las espurias; esto es, entre aquellas que realmente ofrecen a los inversores nuevas combinaciones entre riesgo, rentabilidad y liquidez, y aquellas que so lo aparentan. En consecuencia, no es de extraar que la tormenta financiera en la que nos encontramos inmersos est llevando a cabo un proceso de seleccin, en el que las innovaciones financieras que se han visto cuestionadas desaparezcan y otras so sobrevivan tras realizar las modificaciones pertinentes. * * * * * * El vertiginoso ritmo de los acontecimientos en las timas semanas y, en particular, tras la quiebra de Lehman Brothers, ha supuesto la erosin del pilar bsico de todo sistema o mercado financiero: la confianza. Erosi que es generalizada, adems, en mtiples direcciones, puesto que afecta a actores escasamente sofisticados, como los depositantes minoristas de los bancos, pero tambin a gestores profesionales, como los tesoreros de grandes entidades bancarias. Y se produce, adems, de manera global, una vez que tambin han sido afectados los sistemas financieros de los principales pases europeos y, en estos timos das, las economas emergentes. Como consecuencia, los sistemas financieros no operan con normalidad y no cumplen su funcin de asignar eficientemente los recursos disponibles, con los consiguientes peligros para la economa real y para el crecimiento econico global, que tienen su reflejo, entre otros, en la evolucin de los mercados burstiles. Es en este difcil contexto en el que hay que analizar las medidas recientemente anunciadas, tanto por diversos bancos centrales como por el G8 y la Uni Europea, para tratar de reactivar los mercados y transmitir confianza a los agentes econmicos. Por un lado, los principales bancos centrales del mundo (entre los que se encuentran la Reserva Federal, el BCE y el Banco de Inglaterra) han venido actuando coordinadamente en estos meses en la provisin de dares, al tiempo que han ido abriendo nuevas posibilidades a las entidades para obtener liquidez en sus mercados respectivos. Por otro lado, hace varias semanas se lleva cabo de forma concertada una reducci de los tipos de inters de intervenci de 50 puntos bsicos, una accin sin precedentes y que demuestra la comprensi de que problemas globales requieren a su vez de respuestas globales. Adems de esta seal de tipos de inters, el BCE introdujo importantes cambios en la instrumentaci de la poltica monetaria con objeto de estabilizar los tipos de inters de mercado de corto plazo, de forma que ha pasado a satisfacer plenamente la demanda de liquidez al tipo oficial en sus subastas, a estrechar el corredor entre los tipos de las facilidades de crdito y depsito, y a ampliar la gama de colaterales admisibles. Pero no so ha existido coordinaci por parte de los bancos centrales. En la UE, tras haberse tomado medidas para incrementar las garantas de los depositantes, y a la vista de las iniciativas en marcha en los Estados Unidos y en Reino Unido, los mximos responsables polticos de los pases miembros han fijado cinco principios generales de actuaci. En primer lugar, tras mostrar su apoyo pleno a las medidas adoptadas por el BCE para asegurar la liquidez, se disen mecanismos que facilitan la financiacin a las entidades de crdito, estableciendo la posibilidad de que el Estado garantice las emisiones de deuda a medio plazo realizadas por las entidades. En segundo lugar, los Estados podrn reforzar el capital de las entidades de crdito, y, en particular, el de primera categora (tier 1), a travs de la adquisicin de acciones preferentes o algn otro instrumento de caractersticas similares. En tercer lugar, se plantea un compromiso explcito para evitar la quiebra de instituciones financieras relevantes, protegiendo los intereses de los contribuyentes y asegurando que los accionistas y gestores de estas instituciones cargan con las consecuencias de la intervencin. En cuarto lugar, se emplaza a las autoridades competentes a que concedan una flexibilidad suficiente en la implementaci de las normas contables de valoraci en las actualmente excepcionales circunstancias de incertidumbre en los mercados. Y, en quinto lugar, se destaca la necesidad de mejorar los procedimientos de cooperaci entre los pases europeos para lograr una gesti eficiente de la crisis. Las autoridades espalas, en el marco de cooperaci europeo antes descrito y en lnea con la presentacin de los planes nacionales que los gobiernos de los pases de la UE estn llevando a cabo en estos timos das, han anunciado tambin, como saben, un conjunto de medidas para aumentar la confianza y contribuir a restablecer el funcionamiento de los mercados. Todas las medidas que se han venido tomando en los principales pases y reas econicas, extraordinarias por su magnitud y tambin por su significado simbico, tienen por objeto mandar un mensaje claro y contundente a todos los agentes del mercado respecto a la actitud de las autoridades pblicas. Esto es, que se es consciente de la gravedad de la situacin y que se est dispuesto a hacer lo necesario para evitar el riesgo de un colapso del sistema financiero internacional. Ahora, lo que se precisa es instrumentar las medidas acordadas de forma diligente y eficaz con objeto de que vayan contribuyendo a recuperar la normalidad. * * * * * * Tras haber examinado los factores que subyacen a la crisis financiera internacional y los programas de las autoridades para salir de ella, voy a pasar a continuaci a analizar las propuestas que actualmente se estn elaborando, con una perspectiva de medio plazo, para afianzar la estabilidad financiera. El desarrollo de la crisis hace necesario encontrar un equilibrio entre las necesidades de estabilizar la situacin en el corto plazo y de introducir las medidas adecuadas a medio plazo con objeto, por una parte, de evitar en el futuro problemas similares; y, por otra, de recuperar un marco plenamente de mercado pero corrigiendo los excesos del pasado. El carcter global de la crisis exige una intensificacin de la coordinacin y la cooperaci entre las autoridades nacionales gobiernos, bancos centrales y supervisores, las instituciones financieras internacionales, los organismos encargados de la fijacin de estndares y el sector privado. En consecuencia, voy a dedicar esta segunda parte de mi intervenci a revisar las distintas iniciativas, globales y europeas, que estn en marcha para fortalecer el sistema financiero internacional. Creo que, con la crisis, parte de los logros de aos anteriores en el rea de integracin financiera se han visto afectados. As, se ha observado un proceso de renacionalizaci de los mercados con un retroceso en la actividad en los mercados de financiaci internacional. Adems, el contagio ha llevado a que la operativa transfronteriza financiera haya desaparecido prcticamente. Finalmente, la magnitud del contagio de la crisis estadounidense al sector bancario europeo ha sido mayor de lo esperado. No cabe duda de que las dificultades actuales constituyen una prueba muy exigente para el proceso de globalizaci financiera. En efecto, en los ltimos meses se han puesto de manifiesto fallos en el sistema financiero internacional que ilustran las difciles relaciones entre el proceso de globalizacin y la estabilidad financiera. En cualquier caso, las turbulencias no pueden actuar como un freno a la globalizaci y, en particular, a la integraci de los mercados sino que, por el contrario, deben constituir un estmulo para la consecuci de soluciones globales que permitan incrementar la resistencia del sistema financiero. Soluciones globales a las que Europa debe contribuir de manera relevante en virtud del peso que le corresponde en el contexto internacional. La crisis ha provocado un amplio debate sobre el funcionamiento del sistema financiero, que abarca desde aspectos como las estructuras supervisoras, la regulaci financiera y las infraestructuras de mercado, hasta los procesos de gestin de riesgos de los bancos o las estrategias de negocio. Esto ha dado lugar a diferentes iniciativas para hacer frente a los nuevos retos planteados que estn en distintas fases de preparaci. No obstante, el hecho de que la crisis est an en pleno desarrollo hace que las lecciones que puedan aprenderse y las recomendaciones que puedan formularse sean necesariamente preliminares. Mencionar slo algunas de estas iniciativas, que abarcan muchos frentes y a cuya cabeza estn las impulsadas por el Foro de Estabilidad Financiera, a nivel global, y por el ECOFIN, en el marco de la Uni Europea, sin olvidar que, en los timos das, tambin se ha lanzado un proceso para reformular la arquitectura financiera internacional a partir de las directrices que salgan de la cumbre que tendr lugar en Washington el 15 de noviembre. En concreto, el ECOFIN de octubre de 2007 decretuna hoja de ruta para responder al mal funcionamiento de los mercados, que se actualiza periicamente y est en consonancia con las recomendaciones realizadas por el Foro de Estabilidad Financiera. Las acciones y recomendaciones recogidas en la hoja de ruta van dirigidas no slo a los comits de supervisores, al Banco Central Europeo y a la propia Comisin, sino tambin a la industria, Y no slo cubren un amplio espectro de participantes en los mercados, sino tambin un amplio abanico de reas como la transparencia, los estndares de valoracin, la regulaci prudencial, las agencias de rating y la coordinacin entre supervisores. Permtanme, por tanto, que a continuacin pase a referirme brevemente a cada uno de estos aspectos. El restablecimiento de la confianza del mercado y el incremento de la resistencia del sistema financiero requieren el reforzamiento de la transparencia e informaci al mercado de los riesgos que realmente se asumen y de los estndares de valoraci de instrumentos financieros. El Consejo Internacional de Estndares Contables (IAS Board), en este sentido, ha establecido un panel de expertos para que le ayude en la revisi de las buenas prcticas en el rea de las tcnicas de valoracin de instrumentos financieros cuando los mercados no son activos. Adems, est revisando el marco contable para los vehculos fuera de balance que aclarar el principio de que las instituciones deben consolidar todas las entidades que controlen. Las turbulencias tambin han puesto de manifiesto la necesidad de fortalecer algunos aspectos del marco prudencial, de la gesti de riesgos y de la supervisin en el sector financiero. En particular, se propone aumentar los requerimientos de capital para ciertos productos estructurados complejos, como las retitulizaciones, y se busca superar una estructura inadecuada de incentivos asociados a los crditos estructurados y las titulizaciones. En concreto, deben reducirse los incentivos para que los originadores transfieran el riesgo ntegro de los activos titulizados a los inversores. Adems, se han publicado unos principios que buscan fortalecer los estndares para una gesti prudente del riesgo de liquidez. El papel y el uso de los ratings tanto por parte de los gestores bancarios como en el marco regulatorio tambin est siendo objeto de un profundo debate. Se ha discutido mucho el papel que las agencias de calificaci han tenido en el desarrollo de la crisis y el gano internacional que agrupa a los supervisores de valores (IOSCO) publicen Mayo una revisin del Cigo de Conducta de las agencias de rating para proteger la calidad e integridad del proceso de calificacin. Con ello, se persigue asegurar la independencia de las agencias de rating y evitar los conflictos de intereses. Adems, se pretende fortalecer la supervisi (oversight) de estas entidades y se anticipa la posibilidad de la existencia de un registro de agencias de calificaci. La falta de confianza de los agentes del mercado en los productos estructurados requiere especial atencin, habida cuenta del papel tan importante que estos han jugado en la financiaci de las entidades bancarias. Una forma de contribuir a la recuperacin de la confianza sera por la va de la estandarizacin de productos. Se dara un paso adicional abordando las debilidades en las infraestructuras operativas de los mercados de derivados over the counter (OTC). En concreto, la creacin de un sistema de liquidacin central para los credit default swaps (CDS), que reduzca el riesgo de contraparte a partir de un mayor automatismo en los sistemas de compensacin y liquidacin contribuira a activar el mercado. Adems, permitira conocer de manera casi instantnea la distribuci de prdidas asociadas a cualquier evento de crdito, algo que hoy es imposible. En el tema de la coordinaci de la supervisi, el Foro de Estabilidad Financiera ha constituido un peque grupo de supervisores para desarrollar los protocolos necesarios para el establecimiento de colegios supervisores internacionales para las grandes instituciones financieras. Esto es importante dado que los colegios presentan una gran flexibilidad de cara a adaptarse a las caractersticas de los distintos miembros del grupo. Por ltimo, creo que es muy importante mencionar las iniciativas en curso para abordar los problemas de prociclicidad del sistema financiero y del marco regulatorio y contable. Cuando hablo de prociclicidad, como saben, me refiero a los crculos viciosos que se originan en las fases de expansi mediante el reforzamiento mutuo del aumento del endeudamiento y de los precios de los activos, del relajamiento de las polticas crediticias y de la asunci de cotas de riesgo cada vez mayores. Estos fenenos tienen su corolario inevitable y doloroso como estamos viendo actualmente en las fases contractivas, en forma de cadas de los precios de los activos, endurecimiento de las condiciones de acceso al crdito, desendeudamiento y miedo al riesgo. Puesto que, como la experiencia demuestra, el mercado no es capaz de ofrecer mecanismos de compensacin a la excesiva prociclicidad, corresponde a las autoridades pblicas su correcci. Ahora bien, hay que ser consciente de que una de las debilidades del sistema financiero que la actual situaci ha puesto de manifiesto es la falta de un engarce afinado entre una regulaci y una supervisi que se estructuran en torno a entidades individuales y el objetivo colectivo de garantizar la estabilidad financiera del sistema. De ah que, a partir del consenso que existe de que la prociclicidad del sistema financiero ha desempeado un papel fundamental en el origen y desarrollo de la crisis, resulte indispensable intensificar el dilogo entre los reguladores y supervisores, los rganos encargados de establecer estndares contables y la industria con objeto de reducir la prociclicidad. Y ese dilogo debe, necesariamente, permitir la introduccin de la dimensin macroprudencial en la regulacin y en las normas contables. A mi juicio, las provisiones de carcter dinmico para los crditos como las espalas, la constituci de reservas de valoracin para los activos mark-to-model y la introducci de elementos contracclicos en la regulacin del capital pueden contribuir de forma importante a este objetivo. * * * * * * Para concluir, en el curso de mi intervenci he resaltado co la crisis financiera est poniendo a prueba la resistencia del sistema financiero global y la robustez de los mecanismos de poltica nacional e internacional en el rea de la estabilidad financiera. Recordando la famosa frase del Presidente de los Estados Unidos Franklin Delano Roosevelt durante los difciles tiempos de la Gran Depresi, es cierto que en las circunstancias actuales: A lo que ms hay que temer es precisamente al miedo. Para combatir este miedo y restablecer la confianza que nos permita salir de la crisis, las autoridades de distintos pases han adoptado medidas que en muchos casos slo pueden calificarse de extraordinarias. Y, al mismo tiempo, se ha ido formulando y desarrollando un importante nero de propuestas para reforzar el sistema financiero en el medio plazo, potenciando sus elementos ms estabilizadores a travs de las enseanzas de la crisis. Como supervisor y como banquero central deseo transmitirles un mensaje final de serenidad realista: aunque la situacin por la que estamos atravesando no tiene parang, creo que los problemas existentes, cuya seriedad es patente, tienen soluci. O, en otras palabras, aunque no ser rpido ni ser fcil, estoy convencido de que superaremos esta crisis financiera global. Creo que debemos confiar en que los instrumentos de intervencin en los mercados (novedosos, amplios y potentes) que estn siendo empleados por las autoridades de numerosos pases (gobiernos, bancos centrales y supervisores) en un marco de estrecha colaboracin y dilogo con los agentes privados, contribuyan a restablecer la normalidad en el funcionamiento de los mercados y del sistema financiero. Pero estas actuaciones pblicas no deben llevar a un debilitamiento del compromiso del sector privado. De ah que sea imprescindible la asunci de las responsabilidades oportunas por parte de los accionistas y los gestores bancarios. A su vez, es vital que el margen de maniobra ganado gracias a la intervencin pblica no lleve a una relajacin de la actitud de los gestores privados, mxime si tenemos en cuenta el complejo entorno en el que las entidades van a operar en los primos meses. Esto es, deben aprovechar el respiro permitido por las medidas que se estn adoptando para acometer aquellas acciones, por ejemplo de contencin de costes y de reestructuraci, que permitan superar esta fase cclica con xito. Como es evidente, la intervencin pblica es en este caso una condici necesaria, pero no suficiente, para el xito. Por timo, creo que no es este el momento de concluir que el tiempo del mercado ya ha pasado y el del Estado ha llegado. Deducir de lo sucedido que, una vez superada la crisis, debemos ir a ms Estado y menos mercado sera, a mi juicio, una lecci errea y peligrosa. Lo que necesitamos no es ms, sino mejor Estado, y no menos, sino mejor mercado. Y para ello se precisa un sistema de regulaci y supervisi financiera mejorado, que corrija los incentivos de los agentes privados a incurrir en los excesos del pasado y que permita un buen funcionamiento de los mercados financieros. Mercados que deben ser cada vez ms globales, distribuir eficazmente los recursos y contar con un grado de estabilidad del que han carecido hasta el momento. Esta es, pues, la tarea pendiente: mejorar el proceso de globalizacin financiera y no darlo por concluido o, mucho menos, hacerlo retroceder. Muchas gracias.

Title: Appearance before the Senate Budget Committee
text: Madrid, 19 November 2008 Appearance of the Governor of the Bank of Spain before the Senate Budget Committee Miguel Fernandez Ordez Governor Your Series will agree with me that, on this occasion, the economic and financial context in which the budgetary discussion is framed is extraordinarily complex. After more than a year of strong convulsions in the international financial markets, in these weeks we have witnessed a severe worsening of the situation, with effects that are beginning to be visible in the real economies of a large number of countries and that make up a scenario dominated by the presence of recessionary trends worldwide. The threat that these trends could, in turn, feed back into financial tensions has led the international economic authorities to adopt, within a framework of coordination, extensive packages of exceptional measures. This is the complex context in which the adjustment process of the Spanish economy is developing. An adjustment that the very maturation of the cycle had already set in motion, but which is proving much more pronounced and complicated than one might have expected. It is therefore clear that the debate on economic policy takes on the occasion of the preparation and approval of budgets is particularly important in this ocasi case. The Spanish economy has undergone profound transformations that offer springs to overcome this difficult stage and resume a path of growth and progress in our convergence process. But for them to work, all the actors involved, including, of course, the economic authorities, will have to adapt their behaviour to the efforts required to avoid setbacks and facilitate reactivation. As usual, my intervention will focus on the diagnosis of the state of the Spanish economy and its economic policy implications. But today more than ever, reference to the deteriorating international context and the economic outlook in the euro area underlying the conduct of monetary policy is unavoidable. According to the IMF's most recent forecasts, the world economy will grow by approximately 3.7% this year, which represents a decline of more than one percentage point compared to the previous year's growth. And the deterioration will be greater in 2009, when world output will expand just two tenths above 2% and most advanced economies will be in recession, in a scenario unknown since the end of World War II. The factors that explain this sharp deterioration are multiple. Among them, there is undoubtedly the negative performance of the American economy, weighed down by a continued decline in its real estate sector that depresses the confidence of families and investors. There are also increases in the prices of oil and raw materials that were experienced until the summer, when they began to reverse; as do the difficulties that emerging economies have begun to show. But above all of them, it is necessary to highlight the effects of the severe worsening of a financial crisis that has already acquired a global dimension. A year ago, financial tensions seemed to be confined to just a few investment funds and some relatively minor U.S. mortgage lenders. Later, however, the list of affected institutions begins to expand to include large investment banks, which as a business model has succumbed to shocks; mortgage agencies backed by the United States Government, one of the world's leading insurers and even American credit institutions that could hardly be described as "minor" anymore. Tensions also spilled over to Europe, where sporadic episodes began to emerge involving English, Danish, Icelandic banks and, finally, also institutions in several euro area countries. The truth is that without practical continuity solution, we began to witness nationalizations, interventions of entities, important limitations of market practices such as those that have affected the short sale of shares and also some bankruptcies. It was, in fact, a bankruptcy, that of Lehman Brothers last September, which seems to have acted as a trigger for the severe worsening of the situation that we have witnessed since then, with a further deterioration of the situation in wholesale financing markets that were almost paralyzed, with large declines in stock values and strong rises in price volatilities and credit spreads. and with an extension, in short, of the list of entities in difficulty, which has accentuated the eminently systemic nature of the risks. This is the framework in which it is necessary to contextualize the different high-level international meetings that have taken place these months and the unprecedented actions that have resulted from them. I believe that we must appreciate very positively the fact that it has been understood that a crisis of global dimension cannot be faced on the basis of measures adopted from eminently national approaches. Fortunately, the meetings that have taken place within the framework of the G10, ECOFIN and the Eurogroup have served to agree on common principles and objectives that provide a global frame of reference for the actions of the different States. A framework that, in essence, is defined by the objectives of: ensuring the liquidity conditions of financial institutions, facilitating the financing of credit institutions and encouraging financial intermediaries to strengthen their capital resources. This process of coordinated global response has been particularly reinforced by the recent world summit in Washington, at which a set of guidelines were agreed to boost economic recovery and inspire the necessary process of reform of international financial markets based on a series of common principles such as greater transparency, improving regulation, protecting market integrity, strengthening international cooperation and reforming major international financial institutions such as the Financial Stability Forum or the International Monetary Fund itself. In any case, I think it is important to underline that this crisis is profoundly altering some of the fundamental coordinates of financial development in recent decades. Thus, from a generalized situation of underestimation of risks in international financial markets has passed to another dominated by an extraordinary, and surely excessive, caution in the evaluation of them. In the future, even taking into account this element of overreaction, it cannot be expected that we will be able to return to the extremely benevolent international financing conditions that existed until the summer of 2007. Moreover, the current process of financial deleveraging is likely not only to include a clear component of correction of past excesses but also to reflect a broader move towards a broad-based reduction in the levels of indebtedness of financial intermediaries and a restriction of domestic and international credit flows, the extent and effects of which on firms and households will depend to a large extent on the capacity of the measures. Rushes to modulate the transition to the new situation. In the euro area, as in the rest of the world, financial conditions have recently tightened markedly and led to a very profound change in the macroeconomic scenario. In the second quarter of the year, there was a decline of 0.2% of GDP compared to the previous quarter, which reduced the year-on-year growth rate to 1.4%, below its potential. The most recent available indicators point to a further deterioration in the second half of the year, which is already reflected in the projections made in recent weeks by the OECD, the European Commission or the IMF. At our first meeting of the Governing Council of the ECB in December, we will have a new projection exercise in the Eurosystem, which will surely also involve a review of the ranges published last September. Until well into the summer, the slowdown in growth had not been enough to break inflationary tensions and stop a process of upward revision of price expectations that increased the risk of price unanchoring. Since then, however, the effects of the deepening financial crisis on demand and the decline in commodity prices have substantially relaxed the existing pressure on prices, costs and wages. In these challenging conditions, we in the Governing Council of the ECB have modulated monetary policy decisions taking into account at all times the evolution of the financial situation and its possible implications for the dynamism of demand and, therefore, prices, while ensuring the supply of liquidity demanded by financial institutions. In this way, the official interest rate has been reduced, in two separate movements for a period of only 21 working days, by 1 percentage point to 3.25%. The first of these cuts also took place within the framework of a coordinated movement with other major central banks. Likewise, the commitment to provide all the required liquidity for as long as necessary has materialized in the implementation of a system of supply of the same without limit of quantity and in terms covering up to 6 months, in the expansion of the currencies in which the loans are granted to include the US dollar and the Swiss franc and in a significant extension of the set of eligible assets. as a guarantee for loans granted. And I'm going to focus on the Spanish economy. As I have had the opportunity to explain in my recent hearings, Spain has not been able to escape the effects of the instability in the financial markets, which have complicated and accentuated the adjustment in which it was already immersed. Unfortunately, the sharp deterioration in financial markets over the past few months has aggravated the uncertainty situation and led to a further tightening of financing conditions. The adjustment had begun through an initially gradual correction of the excesses in the real estate sector that had been generated in a global context of financial easing and underestimation of risk and under monetary and financial conditions that were particularly comfortable for Spain. The dynamism of the residential sector had moderated as the change in the monetary policy stance initiated at the end of 2005 was transferred to the cost of financing for households and firms and expectations of house price appreciation were reduced. However, this gradual pattern was altered when the outbreak of the international financial crisis in the summer of last year raised credit risk premiums across the board, blocked a very significant part of banks' wholesale financing mechanisms and spread uncertainty and mistrust. In this context, the demand for housing fell sharply and its prices, after several years of increasingly moderate increases, began to show declines in real terms. This abrupt change of scenery caused a very significant cut in the initiation of housing and leads many real estate companies to have to restructure, some of them entering bankruptcy. This set of factors contributes to the correction of the residential sector, with adverse implications on the total employment of the economy, which goes from growing at premium rates to 3% in the second half of last year, to which a process of destruction of jobs began this summer, for the first time in the fourteen years. Employment is thus acting as the main channel for propagating the adjustment of the real estate sector to the rest of the economy. Indeed, household consumption is rapidly reflecting the abrupt change in employment trends, as well as the deterioration in confidence, in a context of significant financial tensions and adverse developments in household wealth, as a result of falling stock prices and falling property prices. Overall, this scenario of greater uncertainty and financing difficulties is leading to the recovery of the household savings rate. Business investment is also experiencing a rapid slowdown: if the maintenance of exports is providing some support to companies' spending plans. The progressive weakening of domestic expenditure throughout this year has been partially cushioned by an improvement in net foreign demand, which in the second quarter was positive, for the first time since 2001, although in the context of the spread of the financial crisis that I have just described, One cannot be very optimistic about the potential for export support in the short term. However, net foreign demand can be expected to continue to provide a resistance line to the general weakening trend. On the supply side, the fact that the intense adjustment in employment is taking place at the same time as there are high increases in labour costs is particularly relevant, because collective bargaining throughout 2008 has been incorporating the deterioration in inflation expectations that occurred at the end of last year and the first half of this year and because the activation of the safeguard clauses has Transferred to wages the deviation in inflation that occurred in 2007. On the other hand, this wage upswing has not been accompanied by similarly large increases in productivity, so increases in unit labour costs continue to be higher than those of our trading partners. If, in addition, business margins continued to expand in certain activities, as has been observed, the difficulties of the economy to compete abroad would increase, undermining one of the possible springs of reactivation. Fortunately, the inflation outlook has improved significantly in recent months, once commodity costs, and in particular the price of oil, began to ease in mid-July, and much more decisively following the worsening of financial tensions. The CPI has cut its annual growth rate from the annual peak in July to 3.6% in October, bringing the HICP inflation differential to EMU at 0.4%, the lowest level since the start of EMU. Given the role that tightening financial conditions are playing in weakening spending, I think it is appropriate to devote a few minutes to analysing the behaviour of credit in Spain. Before the delinquency of subprime mortgages in the United States soared, credit growth rates in Spain had already begun to modulate in response to the gradual increase in financing costs, the downward revision of expectations of future income and the revaluation of wealth and the levels of indebtedness achieved after a long period with rates of growth of the loans that were hardly sustainable. Developments since then, and in particular the marked reassessment of risks and the severe reduction in international financing flows, have added additional elements of supply-side constraint. As a result of the two forces together, the most recent data, which do not fully cover the stage of aggravation of financial tensions, show growth rates of financing to Spanish firms and households that are much lower than a few years ago and that are progressively approaching nominal GDP growth. The trajectory described by the figures known so far reflected a behavior consistent with the adjustment process of the Spanish economy and with the prevailing conditions of high financial costs, accentuated risk awareness and greater difficulties in obtaining resources in international financial markets. However, it is clear that in recent weeks these global conditions have worsened significantly and have accentuated the downward trend in credit. Faced with this, it is expected that this effect will be counteracted, to an extent and with time lags difficult to foresee, by the unprecedented measures adopted in Spain, as in the rest of the economies of our environment, to mitigate the negative effects of the financial crisis on the availability of credit. Measures that include the creation of the Fund for the Acquisition of Financial Assets and the authorization to the Ministry of Economy and Finance to guarantee new issues of credit institutions and to acquire, if necessary, shares or other types of participations in credit institutions. In any case, I would not want to fail to seal that as you know Your Ser92as, the Spanish entities are demonstrating a greater capacity for resistance to this situation than in other latitudes. It is gratifying to note that our system of regulation and supervision has led, in conjunction with other factors, to the fact that our entities have not been involved in the generation, marketing or acquisition of the financial products that have contaminated the international financial system. Likewise, due to their levels of efficiency, profitability and solvency, they are facing events from a position of relative strength. Although, as I have repeated on several occasions, a crisis such as the one that is shaking financial markets around the world today cannot be neutral for those who depend on them to a greater extent. In any case, from a macroeconomic point of view, the implications of the international financial crisis necessarily lead to a downward revision of the growth prospects of the Spanish economy in the first quarters, while introducing great uncertainty about its medium-term prospects, in line with that observed worldwide. In this context, GDP sharply reduced its year-on-year growth rate in the third quarter, reaching a rate of change of 0.9%, equivalent to a negative quarter-on-quarter rate of .0.2%. The most recent information points to a behaviour in the same direction in the final months of the year and the prolongation of the adjustment process in 2009. It is expected that the process of correcting residential investment will be intensified, since the records of the work in execution will reflect the coming year of the slowdown in initiations. The slowdown in consumption is also expected to continue, mainly due to weak employment, and that business investment will reflect the decline in activity. According to all this, the contribution of domestic demand to output growth is likely to be negative and could only be mitigated by the external sector if exports maintain a certain dynamism and if, as seems logical, the slowdown in imports. For its part, the foreseeable trend in inflation points towards increasingly moderate price increases in the remainder of the year as a result, above all, of the sharp declines in the price of crude oil in the months of the last few months. This trajectory should be prolonged along the cousin ao, supported, additionally, by the very sluggishness of demand. However, in order to achieve more complete and sustainable convergence with the euro area, it is necessary that price contention is also transferred to core inflation and that upside risks arising from the indirect and second-round effects of cost and price increases in the euro area do not materialise. The macroeconomic framework on which the government has prepared the General State Budget Project for 2009 also includes an adjustment trajectory However, in view of the deterioration of the economic climate in the two months, and, as has happened with the projections of most analysts, it has become outdated. In this way, economic growth in 2009 is likely to be lower than expected in the Draft Budget and, moreover, risks remain on the downside, risks that will become all the more important the longer the downward cycle of the world economy becomes. The evaluation of the draft budget must take into account this sharp change in the cyclical situation of the economy and, in particular, the sharp decline in tax collection. These factors, together with the significant tax collection impact of the measures to boost activity that have been taken throughout this year, lead to a deficit closure of the accounts in 2008, as already announced by the Government in the Presentation of the Draft General State Budget for 2009. Budget performance figures published since then seem to point to a somewhat worse balance in 2008 than projected by these official figures, so that the flat deficit will reach an already significant magnitude. In this context, the weakness of activity in 2009 generates a dynamic of widening of the deficit that leads in itself to also exceed the deficit foreseen in the Draft Budget, to the point of approaching the reference thresholds established by the European commitments. These developments come at a time of international debate on the degree of activism that fiscal policy should adopt in the current economic circumstances, culminating in the Washington World Summit with the commitment to implement fiscal measures to stimulate domestic demand in different countries. without compromising the sustainability of finances in the medium term. It must be recognized that in the present circumstances there are a number of exceptional factors, and notably the severity that the global slowdown is reaching, which could justify the implementation of more expansionary fiscal policies in some countries. However, in Spain, there are a number of conditions that advise that the possible adoption of additional measures to stimulate activity should be framed within an obligatory framework of fiscal prudence. It should not be lost sight of the fact that the budgetary situation in our country is deteriorating rapidly, tax revenues show a high sensitivity to the contractionary cycle and the expansionary measures already approved by the Government have yet to be reflected in the public accounts. In less than a year we will go from a surplus of 2% of GDP to a deficit that could approach 3%. It is essential that, in view of the prospects of a prolonged weakening of the global growth scenario, fiscal policy maintains some room for action in the face of possible situations of further deterioration, since nothing would be worse than having to face new shocks when there is no other option than to reduce the deficit, as happened to us in the past or as has happened more recently to other countries in our environment. Nor can it be ruled out that the sensitivity of debt risk premia to countries' macroeconomic and fiscal conditions will increase, so that those that suffer a further deterioration in their financial envelopes could be subject to a further tightening of financing conditions, contrary to what is desirable in the current circumstances. All this suggests that the measures that can be adopted to boost activity or to promote the normalization of financing flows be designed in such a way that they are consistent with the maintenance of a healthy fiscal position in the medium term, in line with the recommendations of the Washington Summit, and favor the potential growth of the economy. To this end, it is important to ensure that measures are selected very carefully so as not to generate a permanent deterioration in the budgetary situation and contribute to improving the efficiency of the economy, without compromising the necessary adjustments. The State Budgets must, in my opinion, comply with these premises but the Autonomous Communities and Local Corporations also have a great responsibility in this task because the most important part of public expenditure - and, in particular, investment - is executed by the Territorial Administrations and these are also facing a stage of rapid decline in their collection capacity. On the other hand, the emphasis that has been placed in recent months on short-term measures to deal with the current global economic slowdown risks delaying or forgetting the need for structural reforms. Its importance is, however, crucial if high growth rates are to be recovered in the medium and long term. Even from a short-term point of view, these reforms can have positive effects insofar as they improve the confidence and expectations of agents. This importance of structural measures applies particularly to the Spanish case. The speed and intensity of the employment response in the current phase of slowdown is only a reflection of the persistence of weaknesses in the functioning of factor and product markets, which leads to inappropriate behaviour in wage costs and corporate margins, and which places the burden of adjustment on the level of employment, It hinders the necessary realignment of productive factors between sectors and harms the competitiveness of the economy. In the current circumstances, therefore, it is a priority to undertake reforms that make the economy more flexible, liberalise certain sectors and markets and increase competition. In my first appearance at the Congress, I made a summary of those which, in my view, are most urgent. Let me remind you. In the labour market, a softer reduction in employment in stages of cyclical slowdown is a priority, and to this end ways must be explored to facilitate the response of wages to changes in the economic environment, adapt them to productivity gains and avoid upward inertia in the face of external shocks introduced by mechanisms such as safeguard clauses. It is also essential to preserve long-term unemployment at low levels and to this end the transition from unemployment to employment must be made as easy as possible by improving the functioning of employment services and the effectiveness of active policies. It is precisely in relation to the policies that affect the unemployed where some of the scams approved by the Government have been concentrated, although for the moment only in order to alleviate the financial restrictions that could be affecting certain groups. In the housing market, rental regulation must be improved to make it more flexible and profitable, so as to encourage the acquisition of housing for investment purposes, thus helping to reduce excess supply. In addition, the placing on the rental market of these homes would expand the possibilities of satisfying the demand for residential services of the population. In services activities and, in particular, commercial distribution, there is also scope to introduce a more competitive environment and to achieve significant efficiency gains. The transposition of the services directive, the draft of which has recently been presented, offers a unique opportunity to make progress towards achieving the objective of reducing our inflation rate and increasing the competitiveness of the economy and the purchasing power of families in a context in which their incomes have been reduced mainly by the slowdown in employment. With the same objectives, improvements should be made in the regulation of network industries and, in particular, the energy sector, which favour competition and increase energy efficiency, as well as in port, airport and rail freight services, sectors that in Spain are essential to strengthen the competitiveness of industrial and export sectors. Let me conclude by emphasizing that it is these timid reforms that the Spanish economy needs to face the adjustment and recover growth as soon as possible. Its implementation requires the initiative of the authorities, but also the close collaboration of the social partners. This would be its best contribution to the Spanish economy being able to continue reducing in the medium term the welfare differences with the most advanced countries. .
