En cualquier caso, como consecuencia de la moderaci del crecimiento del crdito, del incremento de la morosidad y de las mayores dificultades de financiaci, cabe esperar que desciendan los resultados de nuestras entidades. Por el lado del activo, un menor volumen de actividad tender a reducir el margen de intermediacin. Por el lado del pasivo, el continuo incremento del coste de la financiaci, tanto por la tensi en los mercados mayoristas como por la competencia en la captaci de los depitos a plazo, contribuir a minorar la rentabilidad. Pero el mayor riesgo para la evolucin de los resultados en el futuro primo es el incremento de la morosidad, si bien las provisiones dinmicas contribuirn a amortiguar el impacto del aumento de dudosos sobre los beneficios, sobre todo en las fases iniciales de aumento de la morosidad. Ante esta situaci de mayores presiones sobre las cuentas de resultados en un entorno menos dinmico del negocio bancario, cabe esperar un compromiso firme de nuestras entidades para la contencin de costes, lo que puede instrumentarse a travs de diversos canales, incluyendo los procesos de consolidaci bancaria. So ese esfuerzo de contenci permitir, en el medio plazo, hacer compatible el descenso de la actividad y el aumento de los costes financieros con el mantenimiento de niveles adecuados de rentabilidad. A su vez, las incertidumbres que planean sobre la actividad bancaria deberan inducir a las entidades a incrementar su fortaleza financiera a travs de cualquiera de las diferentes vas que existen para ello. * * * * * Una vez valorada la situaci actual del sistema bancario espaol e identificados los principales retos a los que nuestras entidades deben enfrentarse en las difciles circunstancias actuales, voy a dedicar el resto de mi intervencin a compartir con ustedes algunas reflexiones bsicas acerca de los principios que, a mi juicio, deben regir el sistema bancario en el futuro una vez se recupere la estabilidad. A recuperar la estabilidad van dirigidas las medidas de carcter extraordinario que han tomado los bancos centrales y los gobiernos de las principales economas en las timas semanas y meses y que han tenido su culminaci en los resultados de la Cumbre de Washington del 15 de noviembre. Con el fin de no detenerme en exceso en la descripcin de estas medidas, tan solo quiero recordar que stas han tendido a articularse en torno a varias lneas de defensa: -la disminuci de tipos de inters oficiales y el suministro de amplios volenes de liquidez en condiciones ms favorables por parte de los bancos centrales; - el aumento de las garantas a los depsitos del plico en las entidades bancarias - la adquisicin con cargo a fondos plicos de activos en poder de los bancos; -la concesin de avales o garantas pblicas a las emisiones de deuda realizadas por los bancos; - la capitalizacin de los bancos incluso con fondos pblicos, tanto para remediar situaciones de insuficiencia de capital manifiesta como con fines preventivos; - la adaptacin de las normas contables de valoracin para tener en cuenta las excepcionales circunstancias de incertidumbre en los mercados; - y, finalmente, la puesta en marcha de paquetes de estmulo presupuestario y fiscal que van orientados a reanimar la demanda agregada. Como ustedes pueden comprender, la adopci de estas medidas extraordinarias, que suponen una intervenci del sector plico en los sistemas financieros de los principales pases a una escala sin precedentes en las timas dcadas, solo puede explicarse por la seriedad de la crisis financiera internacional y por el convencimiento de que una crisis global requiere una respuesta coordinada a escala global. Sin embargo, junto a estas medidas tambin se estn dando los pasos necesarios para asegurar que su vigencia es temporal y que, una vez superada la crisis, se retorne a un sistema financiero de mercado competitivo y bien regulado pero no sobreregulado, que no solo asigne eficazmente los recursos sino que, adems, evite incurrir en los excesos del pasado que tantos problemas nos estn causando actualmente. Como he dicho en alguna otra ocasin, sera un error deducir de lo sucedido que, una vez superada la crisis, debemos ir a ms Estado y menos mercado. Porque lo que necesitamos no es ms, sino mejor Estado, y no menos, sino mejor mercado. Esta es la tarea que debe llevarse a cabo tras la cumbre de Washington mediante la configuraci de un nuevo marco de regulaci y supervisin financiera que no solo asegure la eficiencia del sistema financiero sino que impida la repeticin de crisis como la actual. Pero, junto a todo lo que vaya a hacerse en el mbito del marco normativo, resulta indispensable que las entidades de crdito adopten una serie de principios que, a mi juicio, deben estar presentes en cualquier concepcin asumible del negocio bancario. Principios que son muy sencillos pero cuyo abandono por numerosas entidades en muy diversos pases nos ha llevado a los problemas actuales. El primero es el de la prudencia, principio que tiene que inspirar de forma permanente no solo la regulaci y la supervisin financiera de todos los pases sino tambin la gestin privada de las entidades. Al igual que para referirse a la funcin de las autoridades hablamos de supervisin prudencial, deberamos acostumbrarnos a hablar de gesti prudente de los bancos como sinimo de gesti bancaria. La prudencia es un principio hacia el que el Banco de Espaa ha mostrado siempre el mximo respeto, como en estos momentos se viene reconociendo internacionalmente. Ahora esto puede resultar obvio, pero cranme cuando les digo que hasta poco antes del inicio de la crisis la prudencia era vista en no pocos mbitos como un concepto anticuado, como una excusa para la ineficiencia. El segundo principio es la confianza. ste es el principal activo a proteger en las entidades bancarias, habiendo factores bajo el control de los gestores que contribuyen a apuntalarla, como la recurrencia de los resultados, el cumplimiento normativo, el servicio al cliente o el modelo de negocio tradicional. Pero tambin hay otros factores bajo el control de los gestores que erosionan la confianza, como la falta de transparencia, los modelos de negocio bancario ms arriesgados o la comercializaci de productos financieros opacos y complejos. En banca debe percibirse confianza cuando se mira la calidad de los activos, la situaci de liquidez, las prcticas de gesti, la rentabilidad y el capital de las entidades. En tercer lugar, voy a referirme a la eficiencia. La batalla por la eficiencia es fundamental para proteger la posicin competitiva de las entidades. Lo es hoy y lo ser cada vez ms en el futuro, especialmente cuando se avance hacia una mayor integracin europea del mercado minorista bancario y hacia una mayor consolidacin mundial de la banca. En cuarto lugar se encuentra la palabra responsabilidad. Nadie discute la funcin del beneficio como el principal incentivo a la producci eficiente de bienes y servicios y, por tanto, a la creacin de riqueza. Pero el beneficio a corto plazo no puede convertirse en el objetivo nico de la gesti empresarial. En el caso de la banca, la dimensi plica de la funcin de intermediaci financiera impone criterios de actuacin a los gestores bancarios especialmente exigentes, de acuerdo con cigos inspirados en las mejores prcticas de gobierno corporativo. Confo en que, cada vez ms, la sociedad demande de las autoridades la vigilancia del cumplimiento de los cigos para una administraci sana y eficiente de las entidades. Fundamentos de tica, deontologa y responsabilidad deben primar en cuestiones tales como las remuneraciones a los directivos y altos cargos, en el desarrollo de tcnicas de innovacin financiera, en la actuacin en los mercados de derivados, y en el propio modelo bancario de originar para distribuir. El quinto principio es la memoria. No se puede olvidar la realidad de los ciclos econicos, haciendo caso omiso a las lecciones aprendidas de las crisis pasadas. En pocas de bonanza prolongada hay una tendencia a bajar la guardia y a minusvalorar los riesgos. Frente a ello, la evidencia histica nos recuerda que es precisamente en pocas de bonanza cuando deben vigilarse ms de cerca los riesgos, incluyendo los riesgos globales de orden macroeconico, incorporando a la gestin y a la regulaci financiera los mecanismos contracclicos que favorezcan la superacin de una visi miope y cortoplacista en la medici de los riesgos y la valoraci de los activos. Por timo, creo que es importante recalcar la transparencia, que debe orientarse hacia todos los usuarios de la informaci financiera, inversores, mercados y reguladores, con objeto de mejorar la eficiencia y evitar la inestabilidad. * * * * * Y concluyo. A lo largo de mi intervenci he pasado revista a la situacin actual del sistema bancario espaol y a su capacidad para hacer frente a los desafos que se derivan de un entorno econico y financiero tan complicado como el actual. Tal y como he tratado de poner de manifiesto, aunque los retos son considerables nuestras entidades parten de una buena posicin para superarlos. Pero para que esto pueda conseguirse realmente har falta seguir trabajando para mejorar la eficiencia, vigilar los riesgos e incrementar la fortaleza financiera de nuestros bancos y cajas. La historia de los timos veinticinco aos del sistema bancario espal es una historia de xito basada en el seguimiento por parte de las entidades de los principios que deben guiar el negocio bancario y en la estrecha colaboracin con los ganos de regulaci y supervisin. Sigamos pues trabajando juntos para superar, como lo hemos hecho en ocasiones anteriores, las dificultades a las que nos enfrentamos y para que, de esta forma, demos continuidad a esa historia de xito que tanto ha contribuido a impulsar el crecimiento econico espal en el pasado. Muchas gracias.

Title: Spain at the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank: Fifty years of relationship
text: Madrid, 15 December 2008 Spain at the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank: Fifty Years of Relationship Conference organized by the Ministry of Economy and Finance and the Bank of Spain Miguel Fernandez Ordez Governor I would like, first of all, to welcome you and thank you for your presence today at the headquarters of the Bank of Spain, to share this day of commemoration of the 50th anniversary of Spain's entry into the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank, organized jointly by the Ministry of Economy and the Bank of Spain. It is a satisfaction for me to be able to count among the attendees of this conference a large group of people who have been directly involved in the activity of both institutions throughout these 50 years. Some of them, for having worked d0 or being working d0 in the Fund or in the Bank, in positions of various responsibilities; others, such as those responsible for the representation of Spain before both institutions; others, in short, for being professionals from the academic and business world linked to them, in some way. A commemorative meeting, such as this one, is first and foremost an opportunity to reflect on the future on the basis of past experience. Let me, therefore, begin these opening remarks by reviewing Spain's relationship with the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank over the past five decades. The history of our relationship with the Bretton Woods institutions begins in January 1958 with the application for membership. A few months later, on September 15, 1958, Spain would sign in Washington the accession to the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank, becoming its sixty-sixth member. Spain's entry into the Fund and the World Bank is not a sign of political openness, in the face of the traditional international isolation maintained by our country. It was, in fact, a key element for the change of direction that occurred in the development of the Spanish economy from that moment on. As you know, as early as 1959 the National Stabilization Plan was drawn up together with the Fund, which was a turning point in our economic policy. The Stabilization Plan ended a period of autarky and strong State interventionism, beginning a process of economic reforms and integration into the international economy that a quarter of a century later would receive a definitive boost with the incorporation of Spain into the European Union. Over the past half century, the IMF has played a very important role in the development of the Spanish economy, maintaining an ongoing dialogue with economic policymakers, mainly through its supervisory work, embodied in the well-known Articles IV. In these years, the Fund has carried out forty-one Article IV missions d0 the last culminating last Tuesday d0 that have provided a detailed analysis of the Spanish economy and have included constructive recommendations on the measures to be taken at any given time. Another recent example of this supervisory relationship, which is especially relevant in the current situation, has been Spain's participation in the Financial Sector Valuation Program: in our case, the FSAP will be developed in 2006 and conclude with a favorable evaluation of the Spanish financial system. The rapid development experienced by the Spanish economy in these 50 years has had a clear reflection in the financial relationship of our country with the Fund and the Bank. When the IMF and the World Bank came in, Spain could not contribute financially to these institutions, but had to maintain a debtor position with both until the late 1970s, as a result of the implementation of various support programs. But once the economic take-off was consolidated, Spain has been able to firmly assume its responsibility as an advanced economy, actively participating in the financing of the IMF and the World Bank since the late 1980s. In 1988, Spain began to commit resources to the Fund's account to finance its programmes for growth and poverty reduction, the PRGFs. In 1998, Spain signed its participation in the New Loan Agreements, which make it possible to supplement the Fund's resources if necessary. More recently, in 2004, a technical assistance account has been opened at IMF for projects in Central America. At the World Bank, Spain continues to increase its contributions to the multiple funds managed by the Bank, such as the Environment, Climate Change, the Special Fund for Least Developed Countries or the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria. In December 2007, Spain was one of the countries that most increased its contribution to the International Development Agency, contributing 3% of the total, more than 640 million euros. Spain's presence at the IMF and the World Bank Our growing contribution to IMF and World Bank financing responds to a strategic commitment to multilateralism in international economic relations. This commitment is also manifested in a growing commitment to improving the governance of both institutions. Looking back, Spain's presence in the governance of the Fund and the Bank has been strengthened as our economic potential and international weight have increased. In 1978, we had the first Spanish Executive Director at the Fund, Joaqu92n Muns, whom we will have the opportunity to hear at today's first session. Later, in 1983, Miguel Boyer presided for the first time the Annual Meetings of the Fund and the World Bank and, in 1991, Carlos Solchaga, was appointed president of the then called Interim Committee, today, International Monetary and Financial Committee. Spain has also had an important presence in the staff of both institutions. The Fund you will always remember the passage of Professor Manuel Guiti87n as director of the Department of Monetary and Exchange Affairs. More recently, two spales have been placed at the highest levels of the Fund's management: Rodrigo de Rato, as Managing Director between 2004 and 2007, and Jaime Caruana, as Director of the Monetary and Capital Markets Department. We will also hear both in the third session of the day. At the World Bank, Ana de Palacio and Manuel Conthe have held positions of maximum responsibility in the last decade, from the Legal and Financial Vice-Presidencies of the Bank. However, in all long relationships, even the most fruitful ones, there are also elements of some frustration or discontent. In our case, we must once again point out that the evolution and dynamism of the Spanish economy in recent decades have not been fully reflected in the increase in voting power in both institutions. Spain's share in the Fund and the Bank is not aligned with the importance of our economy in the global context. However, it is fair to recognize that this misalignment has been partially corrected in the tima reform of quotas approved this year in the IMF, and we trust that it will continue to be corrected in the future. The future of the IMF and the World Bank In short, after 50 years, Spain has consolidated an important presence and an active participation in the promotion of the policies of the IMF and the World Bank, and is firmly committed to guaranteeing the strength of both institutions in the face of the new challenges that they face in the future. This commitment is particularly important in the current context of the international financial crisis. The IMF and the World Bank are called upon to play a central role in the future of the international financial system, the reform of which is currently under discussion. Both institutions must emerge stronger from reform because they have access to the resources, mandate and global legitimacy granted by the representation of more than 180 countries around the world and because of the enormous potential of their human capital. The challenges are many. The IMF and Bank will have to review their policies and their own internal governance. As the Washington summit last November made clear, the IMF, together with the Financial Stability Facility, must assume initial responsibility for recommending appropriate measures to restore confidence and stability to the global financial system, and to ease the effects of the financial crisis on the real economy. Both institutions must also ensure that emerging economies and developing countries in difficulty have access to the financial resources they need. In this difficult task, the IMF and the World Bank will count on Spain's strong support to ensure that the reform of the global financial system provides them with the appropriate resources and instruments to face these new challenges. As you can see from the conference agenda, throughout the day we will have the magnificent opportunity to listen to the opinion and analysis of some of the main actors that have developed the relations between Spain, the IMF and the World Bank, as well as some of the main leaders of these institutions, including: the Fund's own Managing Director. a5 In the first session, the beings SACCHETTI, VARELA, VAN HOUTVEN and MUNS will elaborate on the 50 ace of relationship between Spain and the International Monetary Fund. All of them have actively participated in these relations, including the Stabilization Plan of '59. a5 In the second and third sessions, STRAUSS-KAHN, first, and CAMDESSUS, DE RATO and CARUANA, next, will present the great challenges facing the IMF in the future, which will give us the opportunity to hear first-hand the point of view of those responsible for facing and overcoming these challenges. a5 In the fourth session, Mr. MUASHER, Mr. Perry and Mr. Mart92 will present the challenges facing the World Bank. The three have been protagonists, from their work in the Bank, of the changes underway in that institution. You will allow me to end this speech with a personal note. For me, today's conference acquires a certain sentimental value, because these dates also mark 20 years d0 it is said soon d0 since I was in Washington, on the Board of the IMF, participating in the decisions of the policies of that time. I remember it as one of the most enriching professional and personal experiences of my life. I now give the floor to the Second Vice-President of the Government and Minister for the Economy and Finance, Pedro Solbes, with whom I have the honour of presiding over this opening session, and whom I thank for his presence in this House today. Thanks a lot.
text_original: Madrid, 15 de diciembre de 2008 Espa en el Fondo Monetario Internacional y el Banco Mundial: Cincuenta as de relacin Conferencia organizada por el Ministerio de Economa y Hacienda y el Banco de Espa Miguel Fernndez Ordez Gobernador Quiero, en primer lugar, darles la bienvenida y agradecerles su presencia hoy en la sede del Banco de Espaa, para compartir esta jornada de conmemoracin del 50 aniversario de la entrada de Espaa en el Fondo Monetario Internacional y el Banco Mundial, organizada conjuntamente por el Ministerio de Economa y el Banco de Espa. Es para m una satisfaccin poder contar entre los asistentes a esta conferencia con un nutrido grupo de personas que han estado involucradas directamente en la actividad de ambas instituciones a lo largo de estos 50 as. Algunas de ellas, por haber trabajado o estar trabajando-en el Fondo o en el Banco, en cargos de diversa responsabilidad; otras, como encargadas de la representaci de Espaa ante ambas instituciones; otras, en fin, por ser profesionales del mundo acadmico y empresarial vinculados a ellas, de alguna manera. Una sesin conmemorativa, como esta, constituye ante todo una oportunidad para reflexionar sobre el futuro a partir de la experiencia pasada. Permtanme, por ello, comenzar estas palabras de apertura repasando la relaci de Espaa con el Fondo Monetario Internacional y el Banco Mundial a lo largo de las cinco dcadas pasadas. La historia de la nuestra relaci con las instituciones de Bretton Woods comienza en enero de 1958 con la solicitud de incorporaci. Unos meses despus, el 15 de septiembre de 1958 Espaa suscribira en Washington la adhesi al Fondo Monetario Internacional y al Banco Mundial, convirtindose en su sexagsimo sexto miembro. El ingreso de Espaa en el Fondo y el Banco Mundial no so constituyuna sel de apertura poltica, frente al tradicional aislamiento internacional mantenido por nuestro pas. Fue, en realidad, un elemento clave para el cambio de direcci que se produjo en el desarrollo de la economa espala a partir de ese momento. Como bien saben, ya en 1959 se dise, conjuntamente con el Fondo, el Plan Nacional de Estabilizacin, que supuso un punto de inflexin en nuestra poltica econica. El Plan de Estabilizacin finalizuna etapa de autarqua y fuerte intervencionismo del Estado, dando comienzo a un proceso de reformas econicas e integraci en la economa internacional que un cuarto de siglo ms tarde recibira un impulso definitivo con la incorporaci de Espa a la Unin Europea. Durante el timo medio siglo, el FMI ha jugado un papel muy importante en el desarrollo de la economa espala, manteniendo un dilogo continuado con los responsables de la poltica econica, fundamentalmente a travs de su labor supervisora, materializada en los conocidos Artculos IV. En estos aos, el Fondo ha realizado cuarenta y una misiones del Artculo IV la ltima culminel martes pasado que han aportado un anlisis detallado de la economa espala y han incluido recomendaciones constructivas sobre las medidas a tomar en cada momento. Otro ejemplo reciente de esta relaci supervisora, que resulta especialmente relevante en la coyuntura actual, ha sido la participaci de Espa en el Programa de Valoracin del Sector Financiero: en nuestro caso, el FSAP se desarrollen 2006 y concluy con una evaluaci favorable del sistema financiero espal. El rpido desarrollo experimentado por la economa espala en estos 50 as ha tenido un claro reflejo en la relacin financiera de nuestro pas con el Fondo y con el Banco. Cuando entren el FMI y el Banco Mundial, Espaa no poda contribuir financieramente a estas instituciones, sino que tuvo que mantener una posicin deudora con ambas hasta finales de la dcada de 1970, como resultado de la implementacin de distintos programas de apoyo. Pero una vez consolidado el despegue econico, Espaa ha sabido asumir con firmeza su responsabilidad de economa avanzada, participando activamente en la financiacin del FMI y del Banco Mundial desde finales de la dcada de 1980. A partir de 1988, Espa empieza a comprometer recursos en la cuenta del Fondo destinada a financiar sus programas para el crecimiento y la reduccin de la pobreza, los PRGF. En 1998, Espa suscribisu participaci en los Nuevos Acuerdos de Prstamos, que permiten suplementar los recursos del Fondo en caso de necesidad. Ms recientemente, en 2004, se ha abierto una cuenta de asistencia tcnica en el FMI, destinada a proyectos en Centroamrica. En el Banco Mundial, Espaa contina aumentando sus contribuciones a los mtiples fondos gestionados por el Banco, como los de Medioambiente, Cambio Climtico, el Especial para Pases Menos Avanzados o el Fondo Global contra el SIDA, la Tuberculosis y la Malaria. En Diciembre del 2007, Espa fue uno de los pases que ms aument su contribuci a la Agencia Internacional de Desarrollo, aportando el 3% del total, ms de 640 millones de euros. La presencia de Espaa en el FMI y el Banco Mundial Nuestra aportacin creciente a la financiaci del FMI y del Banco Mundial responde a una apuesta estratgica a favor del multilateralismo en las relaciones econicas internacionales. Esta apuesta se manifiesta tambin en un compromiso creciente con la mejora de la gobernabilidad de ambas instituciones. Volviendo de nuevo la vista atrs, la presencia de Espaa en los ganos de gobierno del Fondo y del Banco ha ido fortalecindose a medida que se han incrementado nuestro potencial econico y nuestro peso internacional. En 1978, tuvimos el primer Director Ejecutivo espal en el Fondo, Joaqun Muns, al que tendremos la oportunidad de escuchar en la primera sesi de hoy. Ms adelante, en 1983, Miguel Boyer presida por primera vez las Reuniones Anuales del Fondo y el Banco Mundial y, en 1991, Carlos Solchaga, era nombrado presidente del entonces llamado Comit Interino, hoy, Comit Monetario y Financiero Internacional. Espaa tambin ha tenido una presencia importante en el staff de ambas instituciones. El Fondo siempre recordar el paso del profesor Manuel Guitin como director del Departamento de Asuntos Monetarios y Cambiarios. Ms recientemente, dos espales se han situado en los niveles ms elevados de la direcci del Fondo: Rodrigo de Rato, como Director Gerente entre 2004 y 2007, y Jaime Caruana, como Director del Departamento de Mercados Monetarios y de Capital. Escucharemos tambin a ambos en la tercera sesi del da. En el Banco Mundial, Ana de Palacio y Manuel Conthe han ocupado puestos de mxima responsabilidad en la tima dcada, desde las Vicepresidencias jurdica y Financiera del Banco. Sin embargo, en todas las relaciones largas, incluso en las ms fructferas, hay tambin elementos de cierta frustracin o descontento. En nuestro caso, debemos volver a sealar que la evolucin y el dinamismo de la economa espala en las timas dcadas no se han visto plenamente reflejados en el aumento del poder de voto en ambas instituciones. La cuota de Espa en el Fondo y el Banco no est alineada con la importancia de nuestra economa en el contexto mundial. Sin embargo, es justo reconocer que ese desalineamiento ha sido parcialmente corregido en la tima reforma de cuotas aprobada este mismo ao en el FMI, y confiamos en que seguir corrigindose en el futuro. El futuro del FMI y del BM En definitiva, despus de 50 as, Espaa ha consolidado una importante presencia y una participaci activa en el impulso de las polticas del FMI y el Banco Mundial, y est firmemente comprometida con garantizar la fortaleza de ambas instituciones ante los nuevos retos que se les plantean en el futuro. Este compromiso adquiere especial importancia en el actual contexto de crisis financiera internacional. El FMI y el Banco Mundial estn llamados a jugar un papel central en el futuro del sistema financiero internacional, cuya reforma se est discutiendo en estos momentos. Ambas instituciones deben salir reforzadas de la reforma porque tienen el acceso a los recursos, el mandato y la legitimidad global que les otorga la representaci de ms de 180 pases en todo el mundo y por el enorme potencial que representa su capital humano. Los retos son muchos. El FMI y el Banco tendrn que revisar sus polticas y su propia gobernabilidad interna. Como se puso de manifiesto en la cumbre de Washington del pasado noviembre, el FMI debe asumir, junto con el Fondo de Estabilidad Financiera, la responsabilidad inicial de recomendar las medidas adecuadas para restablecer la confianza y la estabilidad del sistema financiero global, y para suavizar los efectos de la crisis financiera sobre la economa real. Ambas instituciones deben adems garantizar que las economas emergentes y los pases en desarrollo en dificultades tengan el acceso a los recursos financieros que precisan. En esta difcil labor, el FMI y el Banco Mundial contarn con el firme apoyo de Espaa para que la reforma del sistema financiero global les dote de los recursos e instrumentos adecuados para afrontar estos nuevos retos. Como pueden ver en la agenda de la conferencia, a lo largo del da tendremos la magnfica oportunidad de escuchar la opini y el anlisis de algunos de los principales actores que han desarrollado las relaciones entre Espa, el FMI y el Banco Mundial, as como de algunos de los principales responsables de estas instituciones, entre ellos, el propio Director Gerente del Fondo.  En la primera sesi, los seres SACCHETTI, VARELA, VAN HOUTVEN y MUNS elaborarn sobre los 50 as de relaci entre Espa y el Fondo Monetario Internacional. Todos ellos han participado activamente en estas relaciones, incluido el Plan de Estabilizacin del 59.  En las sesiones segunda y tercera, los seres STRAUSS-KAHN, primero, y CAMDESSUS, DE RATO y CARUANA, a continuacin, presentarn los grandes retos a los que se enfrenta el FMI hacia el futuro, lo que nos dar la oportunidad de escuchar de primera mano el punto de vista de los responsables de afrontar y superar esos retos.  En la cuarta sesi, los seores MUASHER, PERRY y MART expondrn los retos que afronta el Banco Mundial. Los tres han sido protagonistas, a partir de su trabajo en el Banco, de los cambios en marcha en esa institucin. Me van a permitir que termine esta intervencin con un apunte personal. Para m la conferencia de hoy adquiere un cierto valor sentimental, porque en estas fechas tambin se cumplen 20 aos se dice pronto desde que estuve en Washington, en el Directorio del FMI, participando en las decisiones de las polticas de entonces. Lo recuerdo como una de las experiencias profesionales y personales ms enriquecedoras de mi vida. Paso ahora la palabra al Vicepresidente Segundo del Gobierno y Ministro de Economa y Hacienda, Pedro Solbes, con quien tengo el honor de presidir esta sesi de apertura, y a quin agradezco su presencia hoy en esta casa. Title: Appearance before the Congressional Economic Commission
text: Madrid, 25 February 2009 Appearance of the Governor before the Congressional Economic Committee Miguel Fernandez Ordez Governor of the Bank of Spain I appear before this Committee at the request of Your Ser92as, in order to inform you of the management that the Bank of Spain has been developing for the Fund for the Acquisition of Financial Assets and to share with you the analysis of the current situation of credit flows. As you know, the Fund for the Acquisition of Financial Assets is attached to the Ministry of Economy and Finance, to which the law assigns its administration, management and direction through a Governing Council and its Executive Committee. In all that refers to the direction of the Fund is inscribed yesterday's Appearance of the Secretary of State for the Economy before this same Commission. The function of the Bank of Spain is limited to the implementation of its operations in the selection and acquisition of financial assets and its performance as depositary bank of its portfolio. The Bank of Spain reports the details of the execution of operations to the Executive Committee on a bimonthly basis, through a report containing detailed information on the implementation of the Fund. The first of these periodic reports has already been submitted by the Bank of Spain to the Executive Committee of the Fund, and is known to His Ser92as. As detailed in this report, to date four auctions have been held, in which a total figure close to 20,000 million euros has been awarded. The instrumentation of the Fund has consisted in the formalization and liquidation of operations, which is carried out through the purchase, temporary or at maturity, of the financial assets that are thus integrated into the assets of the Fund. At the same time, the maintenance tasks of the portfolio of the acquired securities have been carried out. It is no secret to any of us that this hearing is taking place at a particularly delicate time not only for the Spanish economy but also for the world economy. It would be necessary to go back at least eighty years to find a situation of global risk comparable to this. Under these conditions, it is necessary to flee from simplistic approaches, focused on isolated plots of reality and the complex context in which they are inserted. You will understand, therefore, that I direct my appearance not only to expose and analyze the information we have at the moment but also to contextualize it adequately in the context of the developments that are taking place in the international financial and credit markets and in the Spanish economy itself. Allow me, therefore, to begin by reviewing the most recent data available to the Banco de Espa96a in its dual capacity as supervisor of credit institutions and producer of monetary and financial statistics, statistics which we make available to society on a regular basis through our publications and our website. As without a doubt include, however, the process of collecting and processing basic information. That serves to compile these statistics takes time, so that, at the moment, the most current data that we can handle correspond to the month of January, although I must warn that they are still eminently provisional. The Order of the Ministry of Economy and Finance 3118/2008, which develops Royal Decree-Law 6/2008, has recently entrusted the Bank of Spain with the realization of "a quarterly analysis of the general financial conditions in which the activity of the Financial Assets Acquisition Fund is framed as well as the evolution of bank credit", which will be sent to the Government, which in turn will send it to Congress within the framework of the programmed activities of parliamentary control of the activity of said Fund. It will be then when we have the complete information corresponding to the first quarter of this year. Taking January as the reference month, credit to Spanish households and companies would be growing at a year-on-year rate of almost 6% [5.8%]. In net terms, that is, discounting the effect of past loan repayments, this sector received financing worth approximately 110,000 million euros in the twelve months. If we go down to the breakdown of these figures by market segments, we find differences of a certain magnitude between companies and families. Loans to households for the purchase of housing showed a growth rate close to 4% [4.2%], which was higher than that for consumer and other purpose credit [3.0%]. The funds granted to companies, however, showed a greater dynamism, with rates around 6% [6.1%]. Although it is necessary to specify that this rate hides important differences between different productive sectors. I must point out that the information that allows us to carry out this sectoral breakdown is available with a little more delay but nothing indicates that the previous trends, which have been showing a much more pronounced slowdown in financing of construction companies and those dedicated to real estate development services, will be broken. and a lower loss of dynamism for industry and other service companies. It is quite possible, in any case, that part of this growth in corporate credit reflects not so much the most recent concession decisions of banks and savings banks as a more intensive use by non-financial corporations of credit lines opened in the past, under less demanding conditions than the current ones. on which entities have little or no margin of action. In the same vein, I would like to point out that the dynamism reflected in year-on-year growth rates is significantly modulated when a shorter time perspective than that of a is adopted. Thus, if we look at the three months from November 2008 to January of this year, the growth rate of credit to the other resident sectors, raised in year-on-year terms to facilitate its comparison with the previous figure, is practically reduced to values slightly above 2% [2.1%]. Or, what is the same, some 10,000 million euros of increase in the outstanding balance of the total credit granted by entities resident in our country in the third quarter of last year that, raised to annual figures, would mean just over 40,000 million euros. To contextualize this behavior of credit in Spain it may be useful, as a first reference, to compare it with the evolution of bank loans in other relevant countries in our environment, with the exception, which we must bear in mind, that in some of them, specifically in the United States, credit institutions play a much less active role in the financing of companies, that go directly to the markets to a much greater extent than in our country. For the sake of conciseness, allow me to spare you the detail of the figures and simply emphasise that what this comparison shows is that the process of loss of credit dynamism is common to most economies and, in particular, to those of EMU, the United Kingdom. or the United States. In our country the slowdown has been more marked because we came from higher rates, but the depth acquired by the process has so far been less than in those other economies. Another key reference is the behavior of credit in other phases of cyclical weakness. From this perspective, the adjustment of credit should not surprise us, since it is a variable that is characterized by a markedly cyclical behavior: when the economy grows, bank loans tend to do so at a comparatively higher rate, so that the debt ratios of the private sector increase. On the contrary, the downward phases of the cycle are accompanied by rapid contractions in the rate of credit growth, whose expansion tends to be below that corresponding to GDP itself, and the relative indebtedness of firms and households falls. The behaviour of Spanish credit and GDP is in line with absolute precision with the pattern I have just described. During the recession of our economy, bank lending contracted year-on-year at the end of 1993 by just over 2 percentage points [2.2%], shortly after nominal GDP growth reached a minimum or slightly above zero. And this when there were no financial tensions comparable to those we are experiencing today. In just one month, we will make our growth forecasts for the Spanish economy, thus continuing the practice we started two years ago. As you will no doubt understand, I am not in a position to provide any specific figures. But even without refining the neros too much, it is easy to anticipate that these mark a recession of a certain magnitude, as the forecasts that have been advanced by other organizations such as the International Monetary Fund, the European Commission or the OECD are already doing. There is no doubt that the Spanish economy is immersed in a period of contraction with low inflation, which will determine a very modest, if not negative, nominal growth rate. As we have seen in the past, such a situation should lead, by itself, to a very weak, or even negative, behavior of credit expansion. Against this scenario, we must now superimpose the equally contractionary effects on lending resulting on the one hand from the severity of the crisis of confidence accompanying the current recession and, on the other, from the high financial tension that inevitably accompanies the serious events that have taken place worldwide. with major episodes of bank failures that have already required voluminous and exceptional rescue plans in the affected countries. In this way, Ser92as, I want to begin my assessment of the credit situation in Spain by stopping, first of all, to explain the reasons why the strong contraction that the Spanish economy is experiencing inevitably drags credit. I leave to consider the effects that derive most directly from the crisis situation in the international financial markets. As in the case of so many other goods and services, the observed behavior of credit responds to the pressure of different forces that operate on both the demand and supply sides and which, in this case, are particularly in tune with the cyclical situation of the economy. The downward stages of the cycle are characterized, firstly, by a general retreat in household and business spending, which translates into a lower need for funds with which to finance these expenditures. Likewise, the expectations of employers and workers about their future incomes and, in the case of these scams, about their employment prospects, tend to be revised downwards in times of recession, especially if this results from the need to correct imbalances accumulated during the expansionary phase of the cycle. It is clear that this revision of its own future capacity to pay also has contractionary effects on the demand for credit. As your Ser92as are no doubt aware, since the beginning of 2003, the Bank of Spain, in coordination with the other central banks of the Eurosystem, has carried out a regular quarterly survey of banks in order to better understand the evolution of credit markets in the euro area: the Bank Lending Survey. This is one of the few instruments we have at our disposal to separate the demand and supply components underlying the observed behavior of credit. Well, the Survey clearly shows that the demand for loans from the private sector has been falling in Spain since the end of 2006, thus before the outbreak of the international financial crisis and more in line with the first incipient signs of a process of adjustment of the Spanish economy that the same crisis has come to accelerate later. The decline in demand, however, is insufficient to explain, by itself, the sharp slowdown observed in credit. The cyclical position of the economy also plays a central role in the behaviour of the supply of finance. When GDP growth enters negative territory and unemployment increases, companies and households find it more difficult to meet the payments derived from their debts and this forces credit institutions to divert funds towards the coverage of a growing delinquency that, in other circumstances, They could have been used to fuel the flow of credit. This increase in delinquency is evident in our country, although it is certainly starting from fairly moderate initial levels and Spanish banks and savings banks have had an important cushion of provisions with which to face this increase in defaults. From a more medium-term perspective, the same phenomenon of revising downwards expectations about the future dynamism of the economy that negatively affects the demand for loans also affects the entities, which, faced with the change of cycle, will tend to correct upwards the assessment of the risks implicit in their operations and, therefore, to tighten its conditions for offering new funds. The banks' responses to the Bank Lending Survey confirm that these supply effects are also playing an important role in the recent evolution of credit in Spain. More specifically, the Survey shows that the tightening that is taking place is motivated, fundamentally, by a revision of the expectations of banks and savings banks about economic growth, in general; on the future of specific markets of high relevance to credit, such as housing; or on the solvency of consumers. Other factors such as difficulties in financing loans or potential constraints associated with desired levels of capitalization, which are more directly linked to the current crisis situation in international financial markets, play a much less prominent role, although their influence may be beginning to grow. This would thus add to the traditional cyclical constraints of the supply of credit. In past appearances I have had to comment in detail for various reasons, this international financial crisis reaches the Spanish credit institutions in a position of relative strength that will allow them to withstand without major setbacks the first onslaught. However, the prolongation of these tensions and, above all, the feedback process between the financial and real aspects of the different economies to which they have given rise have generated a second round of effects, indirect or induced. Circumventing any of these indirect effects is going to be more complicated. Among those that should not give rise to greater concern are the effects linked to the persistence of a problem of illiquidity in money markets. When liquidity tensions become critical, the danger of them eventually degenerating into insolvency increases. In substance, however, this risk has been covered by the actions undertaken by the Eurosystem, which has substantially increased the volume of liquidity it provides to institutions, while also extending the range of securities it accepts as collateral in these lending operations. The manifest desire to maintain this policy as long as tensions persist reinforces my conviction that such risks should no longer act as a determining constraint. But beyond liquidity problems, the obvious excesses committed in many countries during a long period of markedly accommodative financial conditions are now forcing a generalized process of deleveraging among financial intermediaries, who now find in their capital levels a limitation in their ability to lend. The information we have at the moment does not suggest that this effect in Spain can be important, but it is clear that it is a source of risks that must be taken into account. Likewise, the collapse of the international wholesale markets in which our entities had been capturing most of the external resources necessary to finance excess domestic spending continue to pose significant challenges for our financial system. The transitional solutions put in place in the face of the first wave of direct effects of the crisis, and I am referring, of course, to the use of the Eurosystem and the issuance of commercial paper, are useful but have a limited path. As in the case of deleveraging, our analysis does not reveal that financing difficulties are playing a decisive role at the moment, but suggest that they may be increasing their influence on banks' credit policy. However, but no less important, the beginning of a period of economic recession, especially in the context of a financial crisis, offers a breeding ground for the overrevival, which is so common in the financial markets. The tendency to overreact can lead to an exaggeration of the risks of borrowers by institutions and, consequently, to an excessive contraction of their credit supply. All these credit crunch risks, as a result of the need for deleveraging, the insufficient resources available on wholesale markets and the tendency towards over-reaction, are by no means exclusive to Spanish banks. On the contrary, some of them have already materialized, with certainly severe effects, for certain entities in other countries. In response, exceptional measures have been adopted in several States and progress has been made in the design of common agreed guidelines in some areas such as the European Union. The different experiences of these interventions allow us to compose a kind of "recipe book" of the arsenal used, which makes sense to review synthetically in order to better understand what tools are available and what is their potential effectiveness to correct the adverse conditions in which the availability of credit develops. A first group of actions is aimed at stopping the extension of the process of distrust in the banking system that is beginning to be implemented as a result of the tensions to which some specific banks, none of them espal, were subjected in the initial phase of the crisis. Faced with the imminent danger of a bank panic episode, which could have led to the collapse of the financial system simultaneously in several countries, the coverage of the guarantee funds of deposits was extended and, more generally, the authorities undertook not to allow possible failures to be detrimental to depositors. I do not think I am optimistic if I say that this objective was fully achieved. In the area of liquidity, it is also possible to identify a number of actions undertaken with the aim of ensuring liquidity availability at longer maturities than those currently envisaged in monetary policy operations, even after the increase in the amounts and timing of the usual Eurosystem tenders. The creation, in our country, of the Fund for the Acquisition of Financial Assets is a good example of the type of specific instruments that have been designed in this context for the provision of liquidity to longer horizons. In the countries most affected by the crisis, measures have also been taken to prevent banks' deleveraging process from having a negative impact on their ability to finance spending projects through the recapitalization of banks with placid funds and the implementation of given bank asset purchase programmes. As your Ministers know, none of these actions has been necessary in the Espal case, although the Royal Decree-Law of last October has established the legal basis for, if necessary, recapitalization operations. Given the enormous uncertainty surrounding the future of this international financial crisis, closing the door to the possible use of such measures later in the process would not seem prudent. As is well known, Spanish institutions do not have assets on their balance sheets that have come to be called "ticos", which has provided an important factor of resistance to the first blow of the crisis that has made a very relevant difference with what is happening in the most severely affected national financial systems. However, this does not mean that our financial system will be immune to the processes that the financial crisis has unleashed. In any case, if the depth of the financial crisis and the deterioration of the macroeconomic environment that accompanies it end up materializing a process of restructuring in the Spanish financial system, we must not forget the existence of another singular strength in our institutional framework. In Spain, unlike other countries, we have Depitos Guarantee Funds, which are financed through contributions from the sector itself and can play, if necessary, an important role in possible restructuring operations of some entity. Their assistance in this type of situation has been effective in the past, which is an asset in terms of experience and reputation that can be very useful. It would be, almost 20 months have passed since the outbreak of the international financial crisis and the Spanish banking system has demonstrated during this time its solidity and solvency. But this does not mean that it is immune to the biggest global economic and financial crisis of recent times. It is possible, as I said before, that the depth of it may imply a process of restructuring our banking system. If it occurs, Banco de Espa will act in the way it has always done: with the aim that neither depositors nor creditors are affected at all. And, of course, with discretion and professionalism. Turning now to the review of the arsenal of measures adopted, it is worth highlighting those aimed at addressing financing difficulties in international wholesale markets by granting public guarantees to bond issues by entities that meet certain requirements. The European Commission has drawn up a common framework for the granting of these guarantees in Europe in order to minimise the possible effects on competition and a level playing field. There are many countries, including ours, in which entities are already making use of these facilities and, although their introduction is not without complications, it can be said that this has begun to restore the possibilities of resorting to financing through the markets, overcoming one of the most serious blocking factors. This does not prevent the available financing from remaining scarce and onerous because savers continue to provide financing with great caution and demand higher remuneration. This brief review would not be complete if it did not even mention the existence of another set of measures, also important, whose objective is to mitigate the effects that the tightening of credit conditions may generate on specific sectors or agents particularly vulnerable to this type of tension. This type of action includes, for example, the various measures adopted to facilitate access to funds for small and medium-sized enterprises or the renegotiation of loan conditions for families in particularly difficult situations. In our country, very substantial financing programmes aimed at these sectors have been undertaken along these lines through the Official Credit Institute. The set of measures available is therefore very extensive. The challenges and complications are so great that the most severely affected countries are still struggling to find appropriate solutions, so not a day goes by without hearing about some new proposal. However, none of these measures is without risk, and not only in terms of their possible negative effects on competition or equal opportunities. Most of these actions require, in one way or another, a great budgetary effort on the part of the States, so it is essential to address it in such a way that it does not pose a serious danger to the long-term soundness of the finances. Great attention should also be paid to the appropriate conditions to be required in return for the entities favoured by the measures or to the design of appropriate mechanisms for monitoring the proper use of aid. * * * * * * * * * Having completed the analysis of the recent credit evolution and the measures with which we are trying to address the existing financial tension, I am particularly interested in dedicating the beginning of this hearing to make some considerations about the perspective from which the credit restrictions that the Spanish economy is experiencing at the current crossroads should be analyzed. That analysis, in my view, must be based on two basic premises. The first is the recognition that the evolution of credit in our country cannot be separated from the existence of a financial crisis of a global nature, over whose solution we have no significant margin of influence. The second is that this crisis comes to our country when the economy was already in the midst of an adjustment process that, in any case, would have had significant contractionary effects on the supply and demand of financial resources. If these premises are ignored, we can easily slide, pushed by the lica anxiety to find a way out of the financial tensions experienced by companies and families, towards wrong diagnoses, based on simplistic explanations, which lead us to believe that the solution is found in mechanical fmulas that far from providing relief can result, in the end, Counterproductive. It is no longer difficult to identify some of these dangers in the voices and proposals that are raised in certain countries in favour of economic nationalism and protectionism, based on the false belief that the return to the defence of national interests can protect each economy from the effects of a global contractionary spiral. The results of that strategy are well known: when each country embarks on a dynamic of protecting itself, the result is an amplification of global recessionary impulses. That was the most destructive force of the Great Depression. That is a lesson that should not be forgotten. The easing of tensions necessarily requires concerted and coordinated action among the largest possible number of countries, capable of restoring confidence in financial markets, promoting a dynamic of consolidation of financial institutions and boosting the dynamism of spending. Within a framework of freedom of trade and financial transactions, the coordination of national policies reinforces and multiplies their effects, thus amplifying the expansionary impulses that flow from them. The obvious corollary of this reasoning is that any action plan undertaken must, necessarily, be articulated and accommodated within the framework of internationally adopted agreements. And neither can we make the mistake of separating the trajectory of credit in our country from the rest of the factors that converge in the severe adjustment that the Spanish economy is going through. Nothing would be more counterproductive than to fall into the erroneous simplification that the way out of the crisis depends exclusively on the existence of an abundant availability of credit financing. Before anglicisms such as "subprime", "conduit" and many others became part of our common vocabulary, the Spanish economy accumulated a series of internal imbalances that had been undermining its dynamism and that made inevitable an adjustment that could have been gradual if international circumstances had not changed so dramatically. In any case, in a situation in which there is the unfortunate coincidence of internal adjustment with extraordinarily adverse external conditions, the recovery of confidence, in addition to the exceptional events that are taking place on a world scale, and the revival of expenditure, on which many contractionary factors have accumulated, will not be possible if the prospect of an absorption of accumulated imbalances does not open up. The revival of credit is undoubtedly part of the solution, but this is not possible if the right conditions are not in place for companies and families to regain confidence in their future incomes and have a solid basis on which to base their plans for consumer or investment spending, or job creation in the case of companies. On previous occasions I have referred to the phenomena that we are experiencing as a result of the confluence of a series of vicious circles that feed off each other. Consumers spend less because they fear for the future of their incomes. Companies invest less and hire fewer workers because they expect less demand and face greater financial difficulties. Banks and savings banks lend less because they attract fewer resources and fear for the solvency of borrowers. They are vicious circles that can hardly be broken by a single point. The state of confidence and the tone of expectations are determinants not only of spending decisions and demand for financing but also of the perception of risk and the requirements required in the granting of credit. And the recovery of confidence and the improvement of expectations, although not independent of the evolution of the international crisis, will depend to a large extent on the capacity that the economy shows to face the adverse circumstances and overcome the present challenges. We must also be aware that in any of the possible scenarios of overcoming this crisis, credit conditions will necessarily have to be more limited and more restrictive than before it. During the long phase of expansion, the indebtedness of Spanish households and companies grew at a rate that the Bank of Spain repeatedly described as unsustainable. It is very difficult, in my opinion, for this economy to rediscover a path of sustained and sustained recovery of spending without first having advanced the process of consolidating the equity position of the private sector that is already underway. The Spanish financial system will also have to adapt to these new conditions. Its good global health is a major asset for the Spanish economy, but we must ensure that this solidity is preserved in the conditions of financial stress and macroeconomic deterioration that we are experiencing. It is not plausible to think of scenarios of revival of financing flows if they are not based on a system of intermediaries that is and profitable. If the Spanish financial system were to weaken severely, as has happened in other countries, financing the economy would become more difficult and growth would suffer greater. On the other hand, the restoration of adequate foundations for the restoration of confidence and the revival of private sector spending plans relies to a large extent on the fact that the adjustment of the economy will result in an improvement in competitiveness and labour market conditions. After several years of vigorous job creation, we have entered a process of job destruction and unemployment rising more than previous recessions. This reflects the persistence of some structural features of our labour market that are not problematic when the economy expands, but which tend to unload the burden of adjustment excessively on employment when the cycle changes. And this contributes to the fact that consumption contracts more sharply than disposable income and that the contraction in investment is not limited to the residential component, where the need for adjustment is evident, but also affects intensely the rest of productive investment. The propagating effect of the contractionary trends exerted by the increase in unemployment is also transmitted to non-performing loans, to the quality of bank assets and, ultimately, has an impact on the tightening of conditions in the granting of credit. And under these conditions it is very likely that an important part of the possible expansionary impulses that can be generated will be slowed down in their effective transfer to spending. All this is sufficiently illustrative of the complexity underlying the economic and financial contraction we are experiencing, in the context of the first global credit crisis in recent economic history. I hope I have been able to convey to you the impossibility of treating credit tensions as if they were an isolated phenomenon. The corollary of this, and with this I end Seor92as, is that any effective action program must contemplate coordinated actions on various fronts that allow to jointly address the many challenges facing the Spanish economy at this time. This is the approach adopted at international level, which we too must follow, adapting it to the particularities of the adjustment process undertaken and the differentiated situation of our financial system. Thanks a lot.

De este modo, Seras, quiero comenzar mi valoracin de la situacin del crdito en Espaa detenindome, en primer lugar, en explicar las razones por las que la fuerte contraccin que est experimentando la economa espala arrastra de manera inevitable al crdito. Dejo as, para ms adelante, la consideraci de los efectos que se derivan ms directamente de la situaci de crisis que se vive en los mercados financieros internacionales. Como en el caso de tantos otros bienes y servicios, el comportamiento observado del crdito responde a la presi de distintas fuerzas que operan tanto por el lado de la demanda como por el de la oferta y que, en este caso, se mueven en particular sintona con la situaci cclica de la economa. Las fases bajistas del ciclo se caracterizan, en primer lugar, por un retraimiento generalizado del gasto de las familias y las empresas que, licamente, se traduce en una menor necesidad de fondos con los que financiar esos gastos. Asimismo, las expectativas de empresarios y trabajadores sobre sus rentas futuras y, en el caso de estos timos, sobre sus perspectivas de empleo, suelen revisarse a la baja en momentos de recesin, sobre todo si sta resulta de la necesidad de corregir desequilibrios acumulados durante la fase expansiva del ciclo. Es evidente que de esta revisin de su propia capacidad futura de pago se derivan igualmente efectos contractivos sobre la demanda de crdito. Como seguramente conocen sus Seras, desde comienzos del a 2003, el Banco de Espa, en coordinaci con el resto de los bancos centrales del Eurosistema, lleva a cabo una encuesta trimestral regular entre las entidades de crdito con objeto de comprender mejor la evoluci de los mercados crediticios en el rea del euro: la Encuesta de Prstamos Bancarios. Este es uno de los pocos instrumentos de los que disponemos para separar los componentes de demanda y de oferta que subyacen al comportamiento observado del crdito. Pues bien, la Encuesta muestra claramente que la demanda de prstamos del sector privado viene reducindose en Espaa desde finales de 2006, antes, pues, del estallido de la crisis financiera internacional y ms en lnea con los primeros signos incipientes de un proceso de ajuste de la economa espaola que esa misma crisis ha venido ms tarde a acelerar. El retroceso de la demanda, sin embargo, resulta insuficiente para explicar, por s solo, la fuerte desaceleracin observada en el crdito. La posici cclica de la economa desempea igualmente un papel central en el comportamiento de la oferta de financiaci. Cuando el crecimiento del PIB se adentra en territorio negativo y aumenta el desempleo, las empresas y las familias encuentran mayores dificultades para atender a los pagos que se derivan de sus deudas y esto obliga a las entidades de crdito a derivar hacia la cobertura de una creciente morosidad los fondos que, en otras circunstancias, podran haberse destinado a alimentar el flujo de crdito. Este incremento de la morosidad es patente en nuestro pas, aunque se parte, ciertamente, desde unos niveles iniciales bastante moderados y los bancos y cajas espaoles han dispuesto de un importante colchn de provisiones con el que hacer frente a este aumento de los impagos. Desde una perspectiva ms de medio plazo, el mismo feneno de revisi a la baja de las expectativas sobre el dinamismo futuro de la economa que afecta negativamente a la demanda de prstamos incide tambin sobre las entidades, que, enfrentadas al cambio de ciclo, tendern a corregir al alza la evaluacin de los riesgos implcitos en sus operaciones y, por tanto, a endurecer sus condiciones de oferta de nuevos fondos. Las respuestas de las entidades a la Encuesta de Prstamos Bancarios confirman que estos efectos de oferta estn desempeando un papel importante tambin en la evoluci reciente del crdito en Espaa. Ms concretamente, la Encuesta evidencia que el endurecimiento que est teniendo lugar viene motivado, fundamentalmente, por una revisi de las expectativas de bancos y cajas sobre el crecimiento econico, en general; sobre el futuro de mercados concretos de gran relevancia para el crdito, como el de la vivienda; o sobre la solvencia de los consumidores. Otros factores como las dificultades para financiar los prstamos o las potenciales limitaciones asociadas a los niveles deseados de capitalizacin, que estn ms directamente vinculados a la situaci de crisis que se vive actualmente en los mercados financieros internacionales, desempen un papel bastante menos destacado, a pesar de que su influencia podra estar comenzando a crecer, con lo que vendran as a sumarse a los condicionantes cclicos tradicionales de la oferta de crdito. En pasadas comparecencias he tenido ocasi de comentar con detenimiento cmo, por distintos motivos, esta crisis financiera internacional alcanza las entidades de crdito espalas en una posici de relativa fortaleza que les permitiresistir sin mayores contratiempos el primer embate. Sin embargo, la prolongaci de esas tensiones y, sobre todo, el proceso de retroalimentaci entre las vertientes financiera y real de las distintas economas a que han dado lugar han generado una segunda ronda de efectos, indirectos o inducidos. Eludir alguno de estos efectos indirectos va a resultar ms complicado. Entre los que no deberan generar mayor preocupaci figuran los efectos ligados a la persistencia de un problema de falta de liquidez en los mercados monetarios. Cuando las tensiones de liquidez se vuelven cricas, aumenta el peligro de que terminen degenerando en situaciones de insolvencia. En lo sustancial, sin embargo, este riesgo ha sido cubierto por las acciones acometidas por el Eurosistema, que ha ampliado sustancialmente el volumen de liquidez que presta a las entidades, al tiempo que ha extendido, de manera amplia tambin, el rango de valores que admite como garantas en esas operaciones de prstamo. La voluntad manifiesta de mantener esta poltica mientras perduren las tensiones refuerza mi convencimiento de que este tipo de riesgos no debe actuar ya como una restricci determinante. Pero ms all de los problemas de liquidez, los excesos evidentes cometidos en muchos pases durante una larga etapa de condiciones financieras marcadamente laxas estn forzando ahora un proceso generalizado de desapalancamiento entre los intermediarios financieros, que encuentran ahora en sus niveles de capital una limitaci en su capacidad para conceder prstamos. La informacin de la que disponemos en estos momentos no hace pensar que en Espaa este efecto pueda ser importante an, pero es evidente que se trata de una fuente de riesgos que debe tenerse en cuenta. Asimismo, el colapso en el que continan sumidos los mercados mayoristas internacionales en los que nuestras entidades haban venido captando la mayor parte de los recursos externos necesarios para financiar el exceso de gasto interno plantean retos importantes para nuestro sistema financiero. Las soluciones transitorias puestas en prctica ante la primera ola de efectos directos de la crisis, y me refiero, naturalmente, al recurso al Eurosistema y a la emisin de papel comercial, estn siendo de utilidad pero tienen un recorrido limitado. Como en el caso del desapalancamiento, nuestros anlisis no revelan que las dificultades de financiacin estn desempeando un papel determinante en estos momentos, pero apuntan a que podran estar aumentando su influencia en la poltica crediticia de las entidades. Por timo, aunque no por ello menos importante, el comienzo de un periodo de recesin econica, sobre todo cuando se enmarca en un contexto de crisis financiera, ofrece un caldo de cultivo propicio para la sobrerreacci, tan habitual, por otra parte, en los mercados financieros. La tendencia a la sobrerreacci puede llevar a exagerar los riesgos de los prestatarios por parte de las entidades y, consecuentemente, traducirse en una contracci excesiva de su oferta de crdito. Todos estos riesgos de restricci crediticia, como consecuencia de la necesidad de desapalancamiento, de la insuficiencia de recursos disponibles en los mercados mayoristas y de la tendencia hacia la sobrerreaccin, no son, en modo alguno, exclusivos de las entidades espalas. Antes al contrario, alguno de ellos se ha materializado ya, con efectos ciertamente severos, para determinadas entidades de otros pases. En respuesta a los mismos, se han adoptado medidas excepcionales en varios Estados y se ha avanzado en el dise de orientaciones concertadas comunes en algunas reas como la Uni Europea. Las distintas experiencias de esas intervenciones permiten componer una especie de recetario del arsenal utilizado, que tiene sentido revisar de manera sinttica con objeto de comprender mejor cules son las herramientas disponibles y cul es su potencial eficacia para corregir las adversas condiciones en las que se desenvuelve la disponibilidad de crdito. Un primer grupo de actuaciones se encamina detener la extensi del proceso de desconfianza en el sistema bancario que comenza ponerse en marcha como resultado de las tensiones a las que se vieron sometidos algunos bancos concretos, ninguno de ellos espal, en la fase inicial de la crisis. Ante el peligro inminente de un episodio de pnico bancario, que podra haber llevado al colapso del sistema financiero de manera simultnea en varios pases, se ampliaron las coberturas de los fondos de garantas de depitos y, con carcter ms general, las autoridades se comprometieron a no permitir que eventuales quiebras pudieran redundar en perjuicio para los depositantes. No creo pecar de optimista si afirmo que este objetivo fue plenamente alcanzado. En el mbito de la liquidez, es posible identificar tambin varias acciones emprendidas con el objetivo de asegurar la disponibilidad de la misma a plazos superiores a los que actualmente se contemplan en las operaciones de poltica monetaria, incluso despus del aumento de las cantidades y de los plazos de las subastas habituales del Eurosistema. La creaci, en nuestro pas, del Fondo para la Adquisicin de Activos Financieros constituye un buen ejemplo del tipo de instrumentos especficos que se han diseado en este contexto para el suministro de liquidez a horizontes ms dilatados. En los pases ms afectados por la crisis, se han adoptado tambin medidas para prevenir que el proceso de desapalancamiento de las entidades de crdito repercuta negativamente sobre su capacidad para financiar proyectos de gasto mediante la recapitalizaci de los bancos con fondos plicos y la puesta en marcha de programas de compra de activos bancarios dados. Como conocen Sus Seoras, ninguna de estas acciones ha sido necesaria en el caso espal, aunque el Real Decreto-Ley del pasado mes de octubre ha establecido la base legal para, si fuera necesario, realizar operaciones de recapitalizacin. Habida cuenta de la enorme incertidumbre que contina envolviendo el futuro de esta situacin de crisis financiera internacional, cerrar la puerta al posible uso de medidas de este tipo en alg momento posterior del proceso no parecera una actitud prudente. Como es bien conocido, las entidades espaolas no tienen en sus balances activos de los que se han venido en denominar ticos, lo que ha suministrado un importante factor de resistencia frente al primer embate de la crisis que ha marcado una diferencia muy relevante con lo que est sucediendo en los sistemas financieros nacionales ms severamente afectados. Sin embargo, ello no supone que nuestro sistema financiero vaya a ser inmune frente a los procesos que la crisis financiera ha desatado. En todo caso, si la profundidad de la crisis financiera y el deterioro del entorno macroeconico que la acompaa terminan por materializar un proceso de reestructuracin en el sistema financiero espal, no debemos olvidar la existencia de otra fortaleza singular en nuestro marco institucional. En Espa, a diferencia de otros pases, contamos con Fondos de Garanta de Depitos, que se financian mediante las contribuciones del propio sector y que pueden desempear, llegado el caso, un papel importante en posibles operaciones de saneamiento de alguna entidad. Su concurso en este tipo de situaciones se mostreficaz en el pasado, lo que supone un activo en trminos de experiencia y de reputacin que puede resultar de gran utilidad. Seras, han pasado casi 20 meses desde que estallla crisis financiera internacional y el sistema bancario espaol ha demostrado durante este tiempo su solidez y su solvencia. Pero esto no significa que sea inmune a la mayor crisis econmica y financiera mundial de los ltimos tiempos. Es posible, como he dicho anteriormente, que la profundidad de la misma pueda implicar un proceso de reestructuracin de nuestro sistema bancario. De producirse, el Banco de Espa actuar de la forma que lo ha hecho siempre: con el objetivo de que ni los depositantes ni los acreedores se vean en absoluto afectados. Y, por supuesto, con discreci y profesionalidad. Volviendo ahora al repaso del arsenal de medidas adoptadas, hay que destacar las destinadas a afrontar las dificultades de financiaci en los mercados mayoristas internacionales mediante la concesi de garantas pblicas a las emisiones de bonos de las entidades que cumplen unos determinados requisitos. La Comisin Europea ha diseado un marco comn para la concesi de estas garantas en Europa con el fin de reducir al mnimo los posibles efectos dainos sobre la competencia y la igualdad de condiciones. Son numerosos los pases, incluido el nuestro, en los que entidades estn haciendo uso ya de estas facilidades y, aunque su introducci no est libre de complicaciones, puede afirmarse que con ello se ha empezado a restablecer las posibilidades de recurrir a la financiacin a travs de los mercados, superndose uno de los factores ms graves de bloqueo. Lo cual no evita que la financiacin disponible siga siendo escasa y onerosa pues los ahorradores siguen proporcionando financiaci con mucha cautela y exigiendo mayor remuneraci. Este breve repaso no sera completo si no mencionara siquiera la existencia de otro conjunto de medidas, importante tambin, cuyo objetivo es paliar los efectos que el endurecimiento de las condiciones de concesin de crdito puede generar sobre sectores o agentes concretos particularmente vulnerables a este tipo de tensiones. Dentro de este tipo de acciones se sitan, por ejemplo, las diversas medidas adoptadas para facilitar el acceso a los fondos de las pequeas y medianas empresas o la renegociaci de las condiciones de los prstamos de las familias en situaci de especial dificultad. En nuestro pas, se han emprendido, en esta lnea, programas muy cuantiosos de financiacin orientados a estos sectores a travs del Instituto de Crdito Oficial. El conjunto de medidas disponible es, por lo tanto, muy extenso. Los retos y las complicaciones son tan grandes que los pases ms severamente afectados siguen batallando por encontrar fmulas apropiadas, por lo que no pasa un da sin que oigamos hablar de alguna propuesta nueva. Sin embargo, ninguna de estas medidas est exenta de riesgos, y no slo en trminos de sus posibles efectos negativos sobre la competencia o la igualdad de oportunidades. La mayor parte de estas acciones requiere, de uno u otro modo, un gran esfuerzo presupuestario por parte de los Estados, por lo que resulta imprescindible abordarlo de manera que no suponga un grave peligro para la solidez a largo plazo de las finanzas plicas. Igualmente, debe prestarse gran atencin a las condiciones adecuadas que se han de exigir en contrapartida a las entidades favorecidas por las medidas o al dise de los mecanismos apropiados de control del buen uso de las ayudas. * * * * * * * * * Una vez completado el anlisis de la evolucin crediticia reciente y de las medidas con las que se est tratando de abordar la tensin financiera existente, me interesa especialmente dedicar la tima parte de esta comparecencia a hacer algunas consideraciones sobre la perspectiva desde la que se deben analizar las restricciones crediticias que vive la economa espaola en la actual encrucijada. Dicho anlisis, a mi juicio, debe asentarse sobre dos premisas bsicas. La primera es el reconocimiento de que la evolucin del crdito en nuestro pas no se puede desligar de la existencia de una crisis financiera de naturaleza global, sobre cuya soluci no tenemos margen de influencia significativo. La segunda es que esa crisis llega a nuestro pas cuando la economa se encontraba ya en medio de un proceso de ajuste que, en cualquier caso, habra tenido efectos contractivos importantes sobre la oferta y la demanda de recursos financieros. Si se ignoran estas premisas podemos deslizarnos fcilmente, empujados por la lica ansiedad por encontrar una salida a las tensiones financieras que viven las empresas y las familias, hacia diagnticos equivocados, basados en explicaciones simplistas, que lleven a creer que la soluci se encuentra en fmulas mecnicas que lejos de proporcionar alivio pueden resultar, a la postre, contraproducentes.
