On the other hand, lending activity has slowed substantially, reflecting both demand and supply factors, and credit can be expected to grow at a slower pace than GDP in the first few months, as has happened in other similar cycles. These two elements d0 the slower rate of growth of the banking business and the increase in non-performing loans d0 put pressure on the income statements of Spanish banks and savings banks in 2008. However, the traditional banking model, much less dependent on the evolution of the financial markets, together with the maintenance of still favourable rate differentials, allowed the results to be positive, despite the difficult economic situation. However, this pressure on the results of Spanish banks is expected to continue in the future, both due to the foreseeable increase in non-performing loans and, more in the medium term, because competition for financing will put downward pressure on operating margins, in a context of deleveraging of the financial sector and, in general, of the economy, which is taking place both in Spain and globally and which cannot be considered as something transitory. I am convinced that the Spanish financial system can overcome these challenges, although, as I have repeated on several occasions, banks will not be immune to the crisis and not all banks start from the same position when facing this difficult stage, since they followed different credit policies in the past and managed their risks differently. In any case, it is essential for institutions to adapt to new circumstances, rationalizing their operating cost structures and correcting excess capacity in the sector. The financial system plays a central role in any economy, as it is the key element in the allocation of financial resources. This role is what justifies that the Spanish State, as other governments have done, has shown itself willing to provide capital to viable credit institutions that need it. This must not, of course, be an unconditional contribution, but requires a restructuring of the institutions that receive these public resources, which will reduce the cost for taxpayers and result in an improvement in the efficiency of the system. It is important to emphasise that, moreover, this approach is fully in line with the common principles agreed in international for a and which have been expressly endorsed in this House with a broad consensus. I am confident that these principles and this spirit of cooperation in matters of general interest relating to the stability and strength of our financial system can soon materialise into a set of provisions that will strengthen the capacity to act in the face of problems that may arise, in line with the tradition of the Bank of Spain and in accordance with the specificity of the serious tensions we are experiencing.

El origen de la crisis que se remonta al verano de 2007-fue eminentemente financiero y la globalizaci de la actividad financiera propicisu rpida propagaci. La actividad de los mercados financieros internacionales se resintiseveramente, llegando a su prctica paralizaci en algunos de ellos. El grado de tensi financiera alcanzsu mximo en octubre de 2008 y, aunque en los ltimos meses ha disminuido, se mantiene todava en niveles relativamente elevados. La gravedad de las perturbaciones financieras desembocen una profunda crisis real, que afecta la economa mundial con una intensidad y simultaneidad inditas, colocando a la mayora de los pases desarrollados en una situaci recesiva a finales de 2008. A partir del cuarto trimestre de 2008 se observaron contracciones tanto de la actividad en muchos pases como del comercio mundial, que se agudizaron en el primer trimestre del presente ao. Sin embargo, en dicho perodo podra haber alcanzado ya el mnimo en el descenso de la actividad, ya que los indicadores ms recientes muestran que, aunque la producci seguir probablemente descendiendo, lo har a un ritmo ms contenido, lo que parece alejar el riesgo de que se produzca una espiral recesiva en la economa mundial. La dimensi que ha alcanzado esta crisis y la multiplicidad de sus ramificaciones suscitan la necesidad de reaccionar en diversos frentes para evitar que se vuelva a producir. Es evidente que la crisis financiera ha puesto al descubierto numerosas lagunas en la regulaci financiera que deben afrontarse con prontitud. Asimismo, es necesario analizar por qu las debilidades estructurales de las economas y de los sistemas financieros no se detectaron o se corrigieron a tiempo, lo que permitila propagaci de efectos en cadena de una magnitud considerable. Con la ventaja que proporciona echar ahora la vista atrs, parece claro que las polticas econicas adoptadas en los ltimos aos fueron, en lneas generales, demasiado permisivas durante esa etapa de alto crecimiento respecto a los desequilibrios que generaba el creciente endeudamiento. Resulta, por tanto, indispensable que las autoridades examinen con ojos crticos los marcos institucionales y regulatorios de sus economas y de sus sistemas financieros y diseen mecanismos para reforzarlos, de forma que pueda prevenirse la repetici de una crisis como la actual. Esa revisi deber abarcar diversos mbitos fundamentales. Dejar para ms adelante los referidos a las polticas de regulaci y supervisi financieras, para centrarme ahora en la necesidad de realizar una reflexi sobre el papel de las polticas macroeconmicas, que evale su protagonismo en la gestaci de la crisis y analice su diseo ms adecuado para corregir desequilibrios como los observados en los ltimos aos. En el mbito de la poltica fiscal se ha echado de menos un papel estabilizador ms intenso en los aos de alto crecimiento, que habra equilibrado el empuje del gasto privado y contribuido a mantener las finanzas pblicas en una senda ms sostenible a medio y largo plazo. En cuanto a la poltica monetaria, deber profundizarse en el papel que corresponde a los bancos centrales en las estrategias de estabilidad. Muchas de las medidas adoptadas en los ltimos meses por las autoridades econicas y monetarias se articularon a partir de unos principios comunes acordados conjuntamente en el marco de distintos foros internacionales. En el caso del Banco Central Europeo, se han puesto en marcha medidas expansivas sin precedentes, que tratan de aliviar las tendencias contractivas que se han percibido tanto en el plano real como en el financiero. La provisi de liquidez se hizo ms flexible ya desde el verano de 2007, aunque fue a partir de octubre de 2008 cuando los cambios fueron ms sustanciales, pues las peticiones de liquidez de las entidades comenzaron a satisfacerse en su totalidad y se ampliel conjunto de activos financieros admitidos como garanta de esas operaciones. Desde el verano de 2008, el tipo oficial de intervencin se ha reducido 325 puntos bsicos, hasta alcanzar, tras la reuni del pasado mes de mayo, un mnimo histico del 1%. En el terreno de las medidas excepcionales habra que mencionar, entre otras, la ampliaci de los plazos a los que se inyecta liquidez, que ahora abarcan hasta los doce meses, y la reciente decisi de adquirir en firme cdulas hipotecarias. Los Gobiernos tambin han adoptado numerosas medidas para afrontar la crisis financiera, que pueden agruparse en dos grandes bloques: las destinadas a dar soporte a los sistemas financieros y las orientadas a impulsar el gasto. En el primer grupo, se ha actuado con una amplia batera de instrumentos, que abarcan desde la ampliaci de las garantas de los depitos bancarios, a la concesi de avales estatales a las emisiones bancarias, las inyecciones de capital pblico en algunas entidades y la compra de activos problemticos que se encontraban en las carteras de los bancos. Entre las medidas de estmulo de la demanda habra que destacar tanto la propia actuaci de los estabilizadores fiscales automticos, que son muy relevantes en las economas europeas, como las medidas especficas orientadas a apoyar mediante aumentos del gasto pblico o reducciones de impuestos a los colectivos o los sectores ms castigados por la crisis. Las medidas que las autoridades espaolas han adoptado responden, en general, a esta misma orientaci. As, en nuestro pas se amplila garanta de los depitos; se creun Fondo para la Adquisici de Activos Financieros, con el fin de comprar a las entidades espaolas activos de elevada calidad; se estn concediendo avales para la emisi de bonos bancarios; se aprobla apertura de diversas lneas de financiaci especial a travs del ICO; se introdujeron nuevas deducciones en el IRPF y se puso en marcha el denominado Fondo Estatal de Inversi Local y del Fondo Especial del Estado para la dinamizaci de la economa. Ms recientemente se han anunciado nuevas medidas de impulso de la demanda (como las ayudas para la adquisici de automiles), al tiempo que se estn ultimando los detalles para el establecimiento de un Fondo de Reestructuraci y Ordenaci Bancaria (FROB) que sirva de herramienta para la remodelaci de nuestro sistema financiero. Permtanme que centre ahora mi atenci en la situaci de la economa espaola. La crisis internacional surgien un momento especialmente delicado para Espaa, pues la economa se estaba ya adentrando en un proceso de ajuste de algunos desequilibrios que se haban acumulado durante la larga etapa de elevado crecimiento que tuvo lugar desde mediados de los aos noventa. Unos desequilibrios que tenan algunos puntos en comn con los detectados a nivel global, pero que tambin mostraban rasgos especficos. Al igual que en otros pases, el dinamismo del gasto del sector privado en Espaa se asenten un rpido incremento del endeudamiento de familias y empresas, alentado por los bajos niveles de deuda de los que se parta y por unas condiciones financieras favorables, propiciadas por un tono de la poltica monetaria que durante ese perodo fue demasiado laxo para las condiciones de nuestra economa. La holgura financiera facilit adems, una concentraci excesiva de recursos econicos y financieros en el sector inmobiliario, que habra de aadir severidad a la fase de ajuste. La poltica fiscal, por su parte, afrontun proceso de consolidaci significativo, pero su contribuci a la moderaci de la demanda nacional no fue suficiente para compensar los efectos de la laxitud monetaria. Como bien conocen ustedes, la economa espaola experimenten la segunda mitad de 2008 un ajuste muy severo: el PIB mostrcrecimientos intertrimestrales negativos a partir del tercer trimestre, que se fueron haciendo ms intensos hasta el primer trimestre de 2009, en el que la actividad se redujo un 1,9% respecto al trimestre anterior, que se sumal retroceso del 1% observado en los tres ltimos meses del pasado ao. Esta contracci se tradujo en una cada interanual del PIB del 3% en el primer trimestre de 2009. Los datos de la coyuntura correspondientes al segundo trimestre son todava poco concluyentes, pero sugieren, en cualquier caso, que el ritmo de contracci de la actividad est siendo menos acusado que en el trimestre anterior. En la recesi espaola el fuerte impacto de la crisis financiera internacional vino a superponerse al ajuste inmobiliario, que ya haba comenzado a desplegar sus efectos con anterioridad. La magnitud de la perturbaci resultante ha sido sustancial y ha afectado profundamente a la confianza de los agentes y ha deprimido las decisiones de gasto y el comportamiento del empleo. A lo largo de 2008 sobresaliel acusado descenso del gasto de las familias, tanto en consumo como en inversi residencial. Pero la profundizaci de la crisis financiera a partir del verano y el deterioro de las expectativas macroeconicas provocaron que otras partidas tambin se vieran afectadas, como es el caso de la inversi empresarial. Esta fuerte cada de la demanda nacional se tradujo en un descenso sustancial de las importaciones, de manera que la aportaci de la demanda exterior neta al PIB mejor amortiguando el retroceso de la actividad. La contracci del gasto privado permitique comenzaran a ajustarse algunos de los desequilibrios acumulados en los aos previos. La capacidad de financiaci de las familias ha aumentado, con un incremento notable de la tasa de ahorro, y la necesidad de financiaci de las empresas se ha reducido, reflejndose todo ello en un descenso de las necesidades de financiaci de la naci, que ha ido hacindose paulatinamente ms intenso en los ltimos trimestres. El debilitamiento de la actividad se fue trasladando gradualmente a todas las ramas productivas, con descensos del empleo, inicialmente, en la construcci, que afectaron despus a la industria y, finalmente, a los servicios. De esta forma, se produjo un proceso generalizado de destrucci de empleo, que alcanzuna gran intensidad en los meses finales de 2008 y en los primeros de 2009, y un incremento muy sustancial de la tasa de paro, hasta el 17,4% en el primer trimestre de este a. Mientras que el alcance de la recesi en Espaa, en trminos de crecimiento del PIB, es incluso inferior al que aqueja a otros pases europeos, el fuerte incremento de la tasa de paro es un rasgo caracterstico de nuestra evoluci particularmente perjudicial y revela una de las debilidades fundamentales de nuestro entramado institucional que es preciso corregir. Uno de los problemas del funcionamiento del mercado de trabajo est relacionado con la escasa sensibilidad de los costes laborales a las condiciones particulares de cada empresa o a la evoluci cclica. En concreto, en 2008 los costes laborales mostraron incrementos elevados, como reflejo del deterioro que ocasionel fuerte encarecimiento del petrleo en la situaci inflacionista en la primera parte del ejercicio. Aunque parece que la presi de los costes salariales ha empezado a remitir en 2009, su evoluci resulta insuficiente en relaci con la trayectoria de la inflaci y con el momento recesivo que vive la economa, de modo que crecimiento del salario real resultante no ser favorecedor de la creaci de empleo. En los ltimos meses se viene observando que la recesi en curso, que est afectando intensamente al consumo de las familias, tambin est provocando revisiones a la baja de precios y mrgenes. As, en mayo la tasa interanual del IPC se situen el -0,9%, el nivel ms bajo desde mediados del siglo pasado, nueve dcimas por debajo de la tasa de inflaci en la zona del euro. Aunque se prev que a finales de ao esas tasas interanuales retomen valores positivos, una vez que desaparezca el efecto estadstico vinculado al encarecimiento del petrleo en los meses iniciales de 2008, no deja de ser destacable el hecho de que en mayo se registraron descensos interanuales en los precios de los alimentos y de los bienes industriales. Tambin en los servicios, que constituyen el componente tradicionalmente ms inflacionista de la economa espaola, se est produciendo una gradual moderaci. Este comportamiento de los precios se inserta en la lnea apropiada para mejorar la competitividad de la economa, reducir los costes de la recesi e iniciar una recuperaci slida. Las perspectivas para la economa espaola apuntan a que el PIB podra continuar contrayndose en lo que resta del ao, de modo que en el conjunto de 2009 su cada ser muy sustancial, aunque probablemente inferior a la que muestren otros pases europeos, ms afectados por el desplome del comercio mundial en los ltimos meses. Aunque el PIB podra seguir cayendo en 2010 en media anual, lo hara a una tasa menos pronunciada, pues la amplia batera de medidas instrumentadas debera ir moderando gradualmente la intensidad de los impulsos restrictivos sobre la actividad. No obstante, dada la intensidad de los ajustes que recaen sobre el empleo, es posible que la tasa de paro mantenga todava una senda ascendente. Es cierto que algunos desequilibrios acumulados durante la expansi se estn corrigiendo. Como acabo de mencionar, el diferencial de inflaci respecto a la zona del euro es ahora favorable a Espaa, mientras que el dficit exterior est disminuyendo intensamente, y cabe esperar que mantenga esa trayectoria, de modo que su ratio sobre el PIB se reduzca en 2010 a menos de la mitad de lo que supona en 2007. Aunque deberamos ahondar en la reabsorci de estos desequilibrios, es innegable que las mejoras obtenidas estn ligadas a una contracci muy brusca de la demanda, con efectos muy negativos sobre la tasa de paro y el tejido productivo. Por ello, es imprescindible revisar algunos elementos de nuestro entramado institucional para evitar que esas prdidas de empleo y de capacidad productiva se enquisten y entorpezcan la recuperaci, as como para prevenir la reaparici de desequilibrios similares a los detectados en los ltimos aos cuando la demanda comience a crecer de nuevo. En la recuperaci de la economa espaola, como en el caso de la economa mundial, ser muy relevante la contribuci de las excepcionales medidas adoptadas tanto en el mbito de las polticas de demanda monetaria y fiscal-como en apoyo del sistema financiero. Pero, en Espaa, con una demanda nacional muy afectada por la necesidad de sanear la posici patrimonial del sector privado y por el impacto de la elevada tasa de paro, ser imprescindible contar con la recuperaci de la demanda externa como principal apoyo para impulsar el gasto. El aprovechamiento de la mejora de la demanda externa cuando esta se produzca exigir que las empresas sean capaces de ofrecer productos competitivos y para ello tendrn que aumentar su productividad y ajustar sus costes, mrgenes y precios de forma flexible. Los sustanciales descensos practicados en los tipos oficiales de los bancos centrales de todo el mundo a lo largo del ltimo ao han propiciado un significativo descenso en el coste de la financiaci. En Espaa, su estmulo expansivo es particularmente poderoso como consecuencia del predominio de la financiaci a tipo de inters variable. Ese impulso ser especialmente relevante en algunos sectores, como el de la construcci residencial, en el que la combinaci de tipos de inters ms bajos y el ajuste de los precios harn ms accesible para las familias la adquisici de una vivienda. Como en otros pases, tambin la poltica fiscal en Espaa ha contribuido a amortiguar el descenso de la actividad, a travs tanto del funcionamiento de los estabilizadores automticos como de la adopci de diversas medidas discrecionales. La magnitud de este esfuerzo fiscal est siendo muy importante y mayor que en los pases de nuestro entorno. Adems, en el caso de Espaa, a la prdida de recaudaci vinculada a la debilidad del gasto, se ha unido la desaparici de los ingresos extraordinarios que el auge inmobiliario haba permitido obtener en la ltima dcada. Por todo ello, el deterioro del saldo de las Administraciones Pblicas ha sido considerable, pasando de un supervit superior al 2% del PIB en 2007 a un dficit que, segn las timas cifras anunciadas por el Gobierno, podra situarse cerca del 10% del PIB en el presente ejercicio. Con esta evoluci se han agotado las posibilidades de actuaci expansiva de la poltica fiscal. El desequilibrio fiscal ha alcanzado un nivel que exige una estrategia de correcci, que debe ser creble, para que los agentes confen en el mantenimiento de la estabilidad presupuestaria a medio plazo. En este sentido, el Gobierno acaba de anunciar los objetivos de estabilidad presupuestaria para el perodo 2010-2012, que comprometen un esfuerzo enorme de consolidaci fiscal, pues aspiran a recortar el dficit desde casi el 10% del PIB que podra alcanzar en 2009 hasta el 3% en 2012, cumpliendo as con las directrices establecidas para Espaa por el Consejo Europeo en relaci con el cumplimiento del Pacto de Estabilidad y Crecimiento. La magnitud de la correcci prevista en tan corto espacio de tiempo exige una ejecuci presupuestaria muy estricta y la adopcin de medidas enrgicas. El reciente incremento de algunos impuestos indirectos es un primer paso en esta direcci, aunque la experiencia del pasado muestra que para que los procesos de consolidaci fiscal sean exitosos deben centrarse en recortes del gasto pblico y, en particular, del gasto improductivo. En este sentido, las comunidades automas, dada su participaci en el gasto pblico, debern contribuir activamente a la recuperaci de la senda de consolidaci fiscal y de estabilidad presupuestaria. En todo caso, aunque las polticas monetaria y fiscal han desempeado un papel muy relevante para compensar los tremendos impulsos contractivos que han sufrido las economas, no se puede seguir descansando en esos apoyos cuando se inicie la recuperaci. Gobiernos y bancos centrales deben preparar el diseo de estrategias de salida del actual marco de actuacin extraordinaria de las polticas fiscal y monetaria, con el fin de evitar que germinen procesos futuros de inestabilidad econica. Por ello, resulta imprescindible que el esfuerzo de poltica se concentre en las reformas que pueden contribuir a mejorar la productividad y el comportamiento de los mercados de factores y productos. Al contrario que en el campo de las polticas de demanda, aqu el margen de actuaci es amplio y, adems, sus efectos potenciales son muy significativos. En el caso espaol, como antes record, uno de los principales problemas de nuestra economa reside en el mercado de trabajo. La actual crisis ha vuelto a generar un incremento fortsimo de la tasa de paro, que nos recuerda que el ajuste en esta economa se produce fundamentalmente mediante la destrucci de puestos de trabajo. Es necesario actuar para evitar que el aumento del nmero de desempleados se enquiste y su grado de empleabilidad disminuya rpidamente. Y tambin para permitir una rpida reasignaci de recursos entre sectores, que facilite el relevo de la actividad inmobiliaria por otras ramas productivas. La reforma laboral resulta ineludible y debera atender a diversos mbitos. En el terreno de la negociaci colectiva, parece necesario que las condiciones laborales y retributivas se ajusten con ms flexibilidad a la situacin econica, especialmente, a la que atraviesan las empresas o los sectores productivos especficos. Tambin es vital introducir cambios en los sistemas de contrataci y una mejora de los sistemas de intermediaci en el mercado laboral y de la movilidad y formaci de los desempleados, para que los trabajadores que han perdido su empleo encuentren pronto nuevas oportunidades. Estas reformas, no solo mejoraran las perspectivas de crecimiento a medio plazo de esta economa, sino que tambin contribuiran a evitar el deterioro del tejido productivo. Obviamente, el mercado de trabajo, con ser importante, no es la nica rea que debera merecer la atenci reformadora de nuestras autoridades. Muy vinculado al mercado laboral se encuentra la cuesti del capital humano y la educaci, donde debe reiterarse que, aunque los rditos son, sobre todo, a medio plazo, la puesta en prctica de reformas es urgente. Finalmente, es imprescindible que Espaa se dote de un entorno competitivo mucho ms sido, en el que nuestras empresas puedan desenvolverse de forma ms eficiente y en igualdad de condiciones con las compaas de otros pases. Dentro de ese entorno, el papel de los servicios es fundamental, dada su imbricaci creciente con las actividades industriales. Adems, la falta de liberalizaci de algunos segmentos puede estar limitando su expansi, lo que resulta especialmente pernicioso dado que este es un sector que engloba algunas de las actividades ms dinmicas y con mayor capacidad de generaci de empleo. En este sentido, la iniciativa recientemente planteada por el Gobierno para implementar la Directiva de Servicios a travs de un proyecto de ley que ree actuaciones en numerosos mbitos, debera ser aplicada de forma decidida, para lo que es preciso que las Comunidades Automas y las Corporaciones Locales colaboren en sus reas de responsabilidad. Tambin avanzar en el impulso de la competencia en las industrias de red permitira que se suministraran inputs al resto de actividades productivas en condiciones ms competitivas. Para finalizar esta intervenci, permtanme que realice un breve repaso de la situaci del sistema bancario espaol. Un rasgo diferenciador de la situaci espaola es que pudo afrontar esta crisis con una posici relativamente fuerte de sus entidades de crdito. El modelo de negocio que estas han venido siguiendo ha sido el tradicional, enfocado en el segmento minorista, de modo que hemos sido ajenos al desarrollo de esos modelos ms sofisticados que han daado profundamente a las entidades de otros pases e incluso a sistemas financieros por completo-, lo que explica que el peso de los activos ticos en los balances de las entidades espaolas sea irrelevante. Tambin la actuaci del Banco de Espaa ayuda que la posici de partida de las entidades fuera ms sida ante la crisis, al exigir la constituci de unas provisiones anticclicas, que pudieran amortiguar la presi en las etapas negativas, y al definir permetros de consolidaci suficientemente amplios para los grupos bancarios, que permitieran una correcta valoraci de los riesgos asumidos. Estas buenas condiciones de partida permitieron que el sistema financiero espaol resistiera la primera oleada de la crisis financiera y siguiera canalizando la necesaria entrada de ahorro exterior aunque por vas diferentes, pues la paralizaci de los mercados de activos titulizados exigila apelaci a fuentes alternativas, como las emisiones de papel a corto plazo y los prstamos del BCE. Los depitos, por otra parte, ganaron tambin peso relativo durante esta primera fase de las tensiones. Sin embargo, la transformaci de la crisis financiera en recesi ha dado lugar a una segunda oleada de riesgos para la estabilidad financiera, cuya naturaleza es, esta vez, eminentemente macroeconmica. Aunque nuestro sistema financiero afronta esta segunda oleada con la ventaja relativa de haber sido menos daado por la primera, es indudable que el deterioro de la economa espaola presiona, por distintas vas, sobre las cuentas de resultados de bancos y cajas. En concreto, la destruccin de empleo est empeorando la capacidad de pago de algunas familias, mientras que el descenso de la actividad est siendo especialmente acusado en el sector inmobiliario, que precisaba de abundante financiaci y que haba adquirido un elevado peso relativo en los balances de algunas entidades. De este modo, tras un largo perodo de expansi econica, en el que las ratios de morosidad alcanzaron niveles histicamente bajos, desde 2008 vienen mostrando repuntes significativos y cabe prever que la presi no se ha agotado todava. Por otro lado, la actividad crediticia se ha ralentizado sustancialmente, como consecuencia de factores tanto de demanda como de oferta, y cabe esperar que el crdito crezca a un ritmo inferior al del PIB en los primos meses, como ha ocurrido en otros ciclos similares. Estos dos elementos -el menor ritmo de crecimiento del negocio bancario y el aumento de la morosidad-presionaron sobre las cuentas de resultados de los bancos y cajas de ahorros espaoles en 2008. Sin embargo, el modelo de banca tradicional, mucho menos dependiente de la evoluci de los mercados financieros, junto con el mantenimiento de unos diferenciales de tipos todava favorables, permitique los resultados fueran positivos, pese a la difcil situaci econica. Sin embargo, cabe esperar que esta presi sobre los resultados de las entidades espaolas vaya a continuar en el futuro, debido tanto al incremento previsible de la morosidad como, ms a medio plazo, porque la competencia por la financiaci presionar los mrgenes operativos a la baja, en un contexto de desapalancamiento del sector financiero y, en general, de la economa, que est teniendo lugar tanto en Espaa como a nivel global y que no cabe considerar como algo transitorio. Estoy convencido de que el sistema financiero espaol puede superar estos retos, aunque, como he repetido en distintas ocasiones, las entidades no van a ser inmunes a la crisis y no todas las entidades de crdito parten de una misma posici a la hora de afrontar esta difcil etapa, ya que siguieron polticas crediticias distintas en el pasado y gestionaron sus riesgos de forma diferente. En todo caso, es ineludible que las entidades se adapten a las nuevas circunstancias, racionalizando sus estructuras de costes operativos y corrigiendo el exceso de capacidad del sector. El sistema financiero desempea un papel central en toda economa, pues es la pieza clave en la asignaci de los recursos financieros. Este papel es el que justifica que el Estado espaol, como han hecho otros gobiernos, se haya mostrado dispuesto a aportar capital a las entidades de crdito viables que lo necesiten. Esta no debe ser, desde luego, una aportaci incondicional, sino que exige una reestructuraci de las instituciones que reciban esos recursos pblicos, lo que reducir el coste para los contribuyentes y redundar en una mejora de la eficiencia del sistema. Es importante recalcar que, adems, esta aproximaci se ajusta plenamente a los principios comunes acordados en los foros internacionales y que han sido respaldados expresamente en esta Cmara con un amplio consenso. Confo en que estos principios y este espritu de cooperaci en los asuntos de inters general relacionados con la estabilidad y fortaleza de nuestro sistema financiero puedan materializarse pronto en un conjunto de disposiciones que refuercen la capacidad de actuaci ante los problemas que se puedan presentar, en lnea con la tradici del Banco de Espaa y de acuerdo con la especificidad de las graves tensiones que estamos viviendo.

Title: Opening speech at the IX International Financial Meeting Caja Madrid
text: Madrid, 7 July 2009 Keynote address IX International Financial Meeting Caja Madrid Miguel Fernandez Ordez Governor Thank you very much for inviting me to inaugurate this IX International Financial Meeting that is unfortunately in the midst of an intense global financial and economic crisis. The Spanish economy, in addition, has to face some imbalances of its own that were generated during the 15 years of scams. In fact, the international crisis affected our economy at a very delicate moment, when the process of adjusting the imbalances accumulated in that long period of growth had begun, which has caused, among other effects, an extraordinary increase in the number of unemployed. The Spanish situation requires structural measures to address reforms, both in the labour market and in other productive sectors that require a more competitive and flexible framework. At the same time, the banking sector will have to go through a restructuring from which it should emerge resized and strengthened. And all this without forgetting the necessary measures to recover the essential budgetary balance in the medium term. In my timid public speeches I have dwelt on these issues, because I believe that it is essential to adopt reforms now, so that, when the international economy recovers, Spain does not encounter serious difficulties in converging with the more developed countries. Today, however, I will focus my intervention on the two aspects that give title to your Meetings: the financial and the international. The current crisis has starkly exposed the weaknesses of the model of the financial system that had developed spectacularly over the course of the scams. A system based on a growing degree of globalization and a continuous process of financial innovation, and therefore, in principle, capable of allowing greater efficiency and favoring greater economic growth. During that it was so. But in the end it has been found that this increasingly global and sophisticated model had many weaknesses and that the authorities were not able to adapt quickly and flexibly enough to these new realities. Today we know quite well the failures and errors that have led us to the crisis. Central banks thought that fighting inflation was enough, resulting in a long period of very low interest rates in the United States, but also in Europe and the rest of the world. This globally expansionary policy stimulates economic growth, but it helps to create the perception, patently wrong, that these rates of growth were sustainable over time. Eco-brokers, faced with abundant liquidity and such low interest rates, sought higher yields, largely underpinning ample leverage. Excessive optimism, poor risk assessment and high leverage are ingredients present in almost all episodes of financial crises and are undoubtedly at the origin of the current one. Financial regulators and supervisors have also made mistakes during these years. Regulation failed to introduce incentives for those participating in financial markets to take the cycle into account. When things are going well, everyone wants to participate in the party. The problem is when you end up thinking that the party has no end, or worse, that every time the fun will be greater. Therefore, financial regulation must introduce mechanisms that reduce the tendency of financial market participants to think about the short term, ignoring the economic cycle. Another prominent example of regulatory failures is the way in which the asset securitization process has been developed, under the originate-to-distribute model. Thus, loans were granted to customers whose ability to repay was more than doubtful, loans that were packaged and distributed throughout the financial system. This seemed to favor a more efficient and flexible risk management, but the truth is that these risks did not end up with those who could manage them better, but with those who had a greater appetite to assume them. And in many cases the entities that originated or distributed these products were not subject to any type of regulation or supervision. It also failed to take sufficient account of certain risks, such as liquidity, which had clearly been underestimated. Nor were common risks sufficiently taken into account; Sometimes, individual institutions are not particularly exposed to a certain risk, but the system as a whole is. In other words, the perspective of the risk of the system is lost, accepting the fallacy that if each entity is sufficiently robust, then so is the system as a whole. On other occasions the correct regulation existed, but its application was incorrect, as in the case of structures created outside bank balance sheets. International accounting regulations required consolidation, but the standard was not interpreted as such in many countries. In the end, parallel banks were created acting outside the regulatory and supervisory sphere, which assumed very large risks, with financial structures that were misaligned in terms and which nevertheless were supported by financial entities integrated into the regulated system. When exposures to these products proved problematic, they had to be assumed by these financial institutions causing the problems known to all. Finally, the principles of good corporate governance that had been approved in recent years by different national and international institutions have not worked as they should. It has become clear that the senior management of many financial institutions did not fully understand the products in which they were investing, nor the risks that the institution was assuming. That is, they failed in their task of administration and control. And to this must be added remuneration schemes that were based excessively on the achievement of accounting results in the short term, regardless of the risk they left behind and far from objectives with a broader horizon and more consistent with the function that financial institutions must fulfill. You will have seen that I have mentioned mistakes made by the authorities, that is, by central bankers, governments, regulators and supervisors. And it is precisely because it is precisely these errors that we must correct. It is true that behind this crisis is also the greed of many private sector agents, which explains, for example, the conduct of both those who were in charge of the entities that encouraged investment in Costa Rican products, and that of many of those who invested in these Costa Rican products. On the other hand, it is undeniable that the behavior of many families and companies, which in some countries borrowed excessively, has also contributed to aggravating the crisis and will delay the recovery. All this is true: it is true that behind the crisis is the behavior of many market participants, but, for a long time, we have known that the obligation of the State and the authorities in general, when designing their regulations, is to take into account these human weaknesses and that irrepressible desire to earn more money or more power. Adam Smith, the father of economic science, warned us in his famous book of how nothing should be expected from the benevolence of the butcher, but that society should be concerned with establishing a framework that would oblige those who participate in the markets to serve the interests of all. The sermons we have heard in the timour on the need for businessmen and bankers to reduce their desire to make money are very noble, but let us not forget that good regulations are what ensure that the greed of some does not give the welfare of the rest of the citizens. The damage caused by the crisis has been quite widespread and most, if not all, countries are responsible for at least some of the mistakes made. In Spain we can congratulate ourselves for having had a fairly conservative banking regulation and supervision, but in view of what happened it also seems clear that, despite the efforts of the different governments, the fact of having kept public accounts in the red until 2004 and having had modest surpluses from then until 2007 was not enough to compensate for the effect that, On the levels of indebtedness of all agents, they had the reduced rates that the monetary uni brought us. But today I want to draw your attention to something very positive that is taking place at the moment, and that should feed a certain optimism about the human species. Because, although it is clear that we are suffering the consequences of many past mistakes of authorities and governments, it is also true that the current reaction to the crisis on the part of all is going in the right direction, and I think we should celebrate it. Let us recall for a moment the reaction unleashed by the crisis of 1929, perhaps the most comparable to the one we are currently experiencing, and we will see that we can congratulate ourselves in seeing that this time the mistakes of then have not been made. The crisis of the thirties gave rise to two kinds of disastrous reactions that fortunately have not occurred on this occasion. On the one hand, there was a generalized backlash against the market economy, which resulted in an extraordinary increase in state intervention in the allocation of resources. Nationalizations, interventions or state planning were imposed in almost all economies. On the other hand, there was also another unfortunate reaction, the tendency of all countries to close in on themselves to find solutions to the crisis, embarking on an economic nationalism whose most visible feature was the explosion of protectionism, and which was undoubtedly another of the factors that served to intensify and prolong the economic crisis of the thirties. I am not saying that among the reactions to the present crisis we cannot find some examples of having fallen into the temptation of seeking purely national solutions or of having increased state interventionism. Thus, in the first moments, some countries that were in a very complicated situation, reacted alone, for example, in terms of giving absolute guarantee to all the depitos. Others nationalized banks or recapitalized them by introducing distorting elements of the necessary competitive equality. But the truth is that, so far, the authorities in most countries have resisted interventionist and nationalist tendencies with remarkable success, and decisive steps have been taken in the search for cooperative solutions in the financial field. The G20 summits of heads of state and government, the first of which took place in November 2008, are perhaps the best symbol that the response to the crisis has been guided by the idea that international cooperation is essential. But there have been many more performances along those lines. At the beginning of the crisis, central banks acted cooperatively to inject liquidity. In Europe, in October 2008, Heads of State and Government reached agreements on a coordinated programme of action measures in the financial system and subsequently transformed the G20 work programme into a roadmap for the EU. With a view to the necessary reforms in the financial system, the Larosi8fre report proposed creating two structures to coordinate macroprudential surveillance and microprudential supervision in Europe, the implementation of which is being developed through interinstitutional work between the European Commission, the Council and Parliament, with the collaboration of the ECB, supervisory committees and national supervisors and central banks. Work is underway in the Basel Committee at global level and in the CEBS at European level to revise the Basel II agreements, and the International Accounting Standards Board is making progress in revising and standardizing accounting standards. For its part, the International Monetary Fund is designing an exercise that should allow anticipating the sources of risk and vulnerability d0 global, national or individual institutions d0 that could lead to a crisis, thus providing a preventive tool to the authorities. The Financial Stability Board (FSB) is another example of the international cooperation effort in the face of the crisis. In this body, heir to the Financial Stability Forum now sit governors of central banks, supervisors and secretaries of state of the Ministries of Economy of the G20 countries, including Spain, as well as some representatives of international organizations. On June 26, their first meeting took place in their new format and their work can serve as an example of that spirit of working together at a global level. At that meeting, there was agreement on the need to consult with the rest of the members to develop plans on possible exit strategies from the policies that were adopted in response to the crisis in the financial system. On the other hand, experiences were exchanged on the stress exercises that they have already carried out or that they plan to carry out, and it was agreed to continue exchanging information on the assumptions and methodologies used in these exercises. In addition, the Council took stock of progress in implementing the recommendations made earlier in this same forum and at the G20 level. Among other topics discussed, it is worth mentioning the assessment of the process of revising international accounting standards, which in recent months has advanced in the line of improving and simplifying the accounting of financial instruments and provisions for unpaid loans. In this area, it reiterates the need for major economies to converge on accounting regulation, to take into account the possible procyclical effects of accounting standards and to explore avenues for technical dialogue between accounting regulators on the one hand and financial market regulators and prudential supervisors, of another. Progress in the development of tools to implement what is known as the macroprudential approach to regulation and supervision was also reviewed. The current financial crisis has shown that until now regulation and supervision have focused excessively on individual institutions, without sufficiently considering the risks to the system as a whole. The FSB also analyses the process of reviewing the scope or scope of application of financial regulation, which, according to the general opinion, should include within its limits institutions, such as hedge funds and rating agencies, and financial products and markets that have hitherto been subject to excessively lax regulations; The importance is also stressed, not that there are international standards of regulation and supervision, but that these standards are observed in a homogeneous way; Ongoing initiatives for the creation of colleges of supervisors in different countries were analysed, which should allow much more effective supervision of entities operating on a global scale; and by Timo, initiatives to establish more reasonable remuneration systems in the financial sector were reviewed. As you can see, the mere account of what was discussed at the FSB meeting can serve as an example of how international cooperation is progressing in multiple forums and institutions with the aim of building together a more slid global financial system. On the other hand, the crisis is forcing us to review some paradigms of regulation that were in force before it. What seemed certain about what was considered to be the proper functioning of the financial markets are now under profound revision. But happily this process of revision is being carried out pragmatically, avoiding the excesses that derive from dogmatic or ideological positions. Undoubtedly, when the crisis erupted in all its harshness, some voices emerged asking for "more State and less Market", but it must be recognized that they have since been relegated to the marginal pages of the periicos. If one pays attention to how this process of revising the regulation of the financial markets is taking place, one will observe that one is not acting with a pretentious or grandiloquent mood, but with the modest attitude of identifying what has failed and seeking solutions to problems, always adopting a pragmatic and non-ideological position. Sometimes I think that, in this process of revision of paradigms in which we are immersed, the reason why no one has seriously raised the idea of the thirties of having more State and less market is due, in large part, not because we have all learned from the past, but because the main feature that has characterized this crisis has been precisely the interruption of the smooth functioning of the markets, to the point that some of them, such as securitization, have practically disappeared. If we were to describe what is the main problem of the current moment of the crisis of the financial system, it is not precisely that there is too much market, but, unfortunately, that there is too little. Some markets continue to malfunction and others, unfortunately, have ceased to exist. It is therefore reassuring that all the countries of the Group of 20 stated in their first communiqu8e that measures to stabilize financial markets and ensure that a crisis such as the current one does not recur must be guided by the belief shared by all its members that market principles, Open trade and investment regimes, as well as effectively regulated financial markets, promote dynamism, innovation and entrepreneurship, and these are the essential elements for economic growth, employment and poverty reduction. And it is that the function of the State is not to replace the Market; that is, to the individuals and companies that act in it, but to take care precisely that the markets function normally, to ensure that they are not paralyzed, that they serve the general interest. Exceptionally or temporarily, the State must intervene in the allocation of an economy's resources. The essential task of the State is to establish the rules of the game and not to intervene in it, leaving it to the market, that is, individuals and companies, to decide on the allocation of resources. The State must not interfere in the management of airlines or canned food factories, but must take care of their regulation, that no Costa Rican products are introduced into cans and that aircraft safety is respected. In this way it ensures something that is fundamental to the functioning of markets: the confidence of those who participate in them. On the other hand, many of the problems that have been detected in financial regulation and supervision come from the other extreme, from those who denied the State its function of promoting the proper functioning of the markets and proclaimed that self-regulation of them was sufficient. And just as the market is key to the proper functioning of economies and no better model has been invented when it comes to allocating economic resources, it is wrong to think that markets can work spontaneously, without the State being behind, defending and promoting their proper functioning through regulation and supervision. Referring to the financial system, there are many examples that could be given of this necessary work of the State to ensure that there are more and better markets but, for the sake of brevity, I will comment on the promotion of transparency. The functioning of financial markets, like that of all markets, is the result of economic decisions made by private actors. But it is obvious that to make a correct decision it is necessary to have the relevant information. This does not mean that there is no uncertainty, but that decisions must be well founded. Therefore, financial regulation must ensure that entities transfer to the market all the information that is relevant for informed decision-making. And to ensure that this information is also reliable and transmitted on time. This requires institutions to disclose quantitative information about their activity that allows them to know what risks they are assuming, what capacity they have to face them and what results they are obtaining. But this being important, it is equally the qualitative information that allows to properly interpret the figures, to know with what criteria they are being prepared, that make it possible to understand the business strategy and that also reflects the processes and means available to the entity to properly manage the elements of risk inherent in the development of its activity. The current financial crisis has shown that there has not been sufficient transparency. The information does not reach the market. A clear example is that relating to the most complex financial products developed in scams. When the problems became more pressing in late 2008, it was not known what risks different financial institutions were taking. In reality, it was not known who was taking those risks. Faced with this situation, market participants reacted as they always do in the face of the unknown: with distrust. If it is not possible to discriminate between those who are most exposed to risk and those who are less exposed to risk, between those who have acted prudently and those who have not, the consequence is that everyone is treated equally. Many financing markets that until then had been key were closed or stopped working properly due to the absence of the necessary information and were treated indiscriminately, fomenting problems in entities and institutions that, probably, did not have them or suffered to a lesser extent. Regulators and supervisors are taking all this into account. Work is under way in different areas, such as the development of Basel II, the third pillar of which addresses precisely the need to inform markets. Accounting regulators and rating agencies are also concerned with these issues, and attach increasing importance to requiring an adequate explanation of how and under what criteria the information transmitted to the market is generated. This collective effort to improve transparency is an example of the remarkable international cooperation effort that is being developed to move towards a new model of financial system, to identify failures and to propose changes in regulation and supervision with the aim of solving these deficiencies. And this process of transformation is being carried out on the basis of the principles to which I referred earlier: to promote the functioning of the market by correcting the problems that are detected, and at the same time, to try to ensure that national responses do not slow down the desirable globalisation of the financial system. More and better markets, more and better international cooperation is what we need and what, happily, we are trying to build together. It is true that few of these proposals for changes in regulation and supervision will serve to get out of the crisis. Most are designed to prevent another of similar characteristics from occurring again. The way out of the crisis has more to do with the success of macroeconomic policies - monetary and fiscal - as well as in those to support the financial system or structural reforms, so essential in many countries. Today, most of the institutions that draw up forecasts agree that the recovery of the world economy could occur around the beginning of the coming one. But the levels of uncertainty are enormous. There is a Chinese proverb that says that you can not say that a man has been happy until he has fulfilled the scam day of his life. And we should probably show the same caution when it comes to certifying the exit from the crisis. But the fact that the authorities of the world's leading countries have agreed on the direction of efforts to improve the regulation and supervision of the financial system d0 more international cooperation and more market economy d0 is very positive and we should welcome it. This moves away from what could be the worst scenario of reaction to the crisis: the deglobalization of the financial system. We seem to have learned from the thirties that the worst consequences of a crisis come not so much from the crisis itself as from the inadequate reactions to it, which can aggravate and prolong it. Therefore, in the event that the crisis lasts longer than we want, we should continue to resist calls for isolationism and interventionism. To date, the pessimists have been wrong. Humanity has not stumbled twice on the same stone. For now. Thanks a lot.
