Tambin se revisaron los progresos en el desarrollo de instrumentos que sirvan para aplicar lo que se denomina enfoque macroprudencial de la regulacin y la supervisi. La actual crisis financiera ha puesto de manifiesto que hasta ahora la regulaci y la supervisi se haban centrado en exceso en las entidades individuales, sin considerar suficientemente los riesgos para el conjunto del sistema. Asimismo, el FSB analiz el proceso de revisi del mbito o alcance de aplicaci de la regulaci financiera, que, de acuerdo con la opinin generalizada, debe incluir dentro de sus lmites a instituciones, como los hedge funds y las agencias de rating, y a productos y mercados financieros que hasta ahora han estado sujetos a regulaciones excesivamente laxas; tambin se insistien la importancia, no so de que existan unos estndares internacionales de regulaci y supervisin, sino de que esos estndares se observen de una forma homognea; se analizaron las iniciativas en curso para la creacin de colegios de supervisores de distintos pases, que deben permitir una supervisin mucho ms efectiva de las entidades que operan a escala global; y por timo, se revisaron las iniciativas para establecer unos sistemas de retribucin ms razonables en el sector financiero. Como ven, el solo relato de lo tratado en la tima reuni del FSB puede servir de ejemplo de co la cooperaci internacional est progresando en mtiples foros e instituciones con el objetivo de construir entre todos un sistema financiero global ms slido. Por otra parte, la crisis est obligando a revisar algunos paradigmas de la regulaci que estaban vigentes antes de la misma. Las que parecan certezas sobre lo que se consideraba un funcionamiento correcto de los mercados financieros estn sometidas hoy a profunda revisin. Pero felizmente este proceso de revisin est llevndose a cabo de forma pragmtica, evitando los excesos que se derivan de posturas dogmticas o ideologizadas. Sin duda, cuando la crisis irrumpicon toda su crudeza surgieron algunas voces pidiendo ms Estado y menos Mercado, pero hay que reconocer que despus han quedado relegadas a las pginas marginales de los periicos. Si uno presta atencin a cmo se est produciendo ese proceso de revisin de la regulaci de los mercados financieros, observar que no se est actuando con un talante pretencioso o grandilocuente, sino con la modesta actitud de identificar lo que ha fallado y buscar soluciones a los problemas, adoptando siempre una postura pragmtica y no ideologizada. A veces pienso que, en este proceso de revisi de paradigmas en el que estamos inmersos, la razn por la cual nadie ha planteado seriamente la idea de los aos treinta de contar con ms Estado y menos Mercado se debe, en buena parte, no so a que todos hemos aprendido del pasado, sino a que el principal rasgo que ha caracterizado a esta crisis ha sido justamente la interrupcin del funcionamiento fluido de los mercados, hasta el punto de que algunos de ellos, como el de la titulizaciones, prcticamente han desaparecido. Si tuviramos que describir cul es el principal problema del momento actual de la crisis del sistema financiero, no es precisamente que haya mucho mercado, sino, lamentablemente, que hay demasiado poco. Algunos mercados siguen funcionando mal y otros, para nuestra desgracia, han dejado de existir. Por ello es tranquilizador que todos los pases del Grupo de los 20 declararan en su primer comunicado que las medidas orientadas a estabilizar los mercados financieros y a asegurar que no vuelva a repetirse una crisis como la actual deben guiarse por la creencia compartida por todos sus miembros en que los principios del mercado, los regmenes abiertos de comercio y de inversi, as como los mercados financieros regulados de forma efectiva, son los que promueven el dinamismo, la innovaci y la actividad emprendedora, y estos son los elementos esenciales para favorecer el crecimiento econico, el empleo y la reducci de la pobreza. Y es que la funci del Estado no es la de sustituir al Mercado; esto es, a los individuos y empresas que actan en l, sino ocuparse precisamente de que los mercados funcionen con normalidad, de asegurar que no se paralicen, de que sirvan al inters general. So excepcionalmente o transitoriamente, el Estado debe intervenir en la asignacin de los recursos de una economa. La tarea esencial del Estado es la de establecer las reglas del juego y no la de intervenir en el mismo, dejando al mercado, esto es a los individuos y las empresas, decidir sobre la asignaci de recursos. El Estado no debe entrometerse en la gesti de las compaas areas o las fbricas de alimentos enlatados, sino que debe ocuparse de su regulacin, de que no se introduzcan productos ticos en las latas y se respete la seguridad de las aeronaves. De esta forma asegura algo que es fundamental para el funcionamiento de los mercados: la confianza de los que en ellos participan. Por otra parte, muchos de los problemas que se han detectado en la regulacin y la supervisi financiera provienen del otro extremo, de quienes negaban al Estado su funci de promover el adecuado funcionamiento de los mercados y proclamaban que bastaba con la autorregulaci de los mismos. Y es que as como el mercado es clave para el buen funcionamiento de las economas y no se ha inventado otro modelo mejor a la hora de asignar los recursos econicos, es equivocado pensar que los mercados pueden funcionar espontneamente, sin que el Estado est detrs, defendiendo e impulsando su buen funcionamiento a travs de la regulacin y la supervisin. Refirindonos al sistema financiero, son muchos los ejemplos que se podran dar de esa necesaria labor del Estado de ocuparse de que haya ms y mejores mercados pero, en aras de la brevedad, comentar so uno: la promoci de la transparencia. El funcionamiento de los mercados financieros, como el de todos los mercados, es el resultado de las decisiones econicas que toman los agentes privados. Pero es obvio que para tomar una decisi correcta es necesario contar con la informacin relevante. Esto no quiere decir que no exista incertidumbre, sino que las decisiones han de estar bien fundadas. Por lo tanto, la regulaci financiera ha de asegurar que las entidades trasladen al mercado toda la informacin que es relevante para la toma informada de decisiones. Y que se garantice que esa informacin sea adems fiable y transmitida a tiempo. Esto exige que las entidades revelen informacin cuantitativa sobre su actividad que permita conocer qu riesgos estn asumiendo, qu capacidad tienen para hacerles frente y qu resultados estn obteniendo. Pero siendo esto importante, lo es en igual medida la informaci cualitativa que permita interpretar adecuadamente las cifras, conocer con qu criterios se estn elaborando, que posibiliten entender la estrategia de negocio y que refleje tambin los procesos y medios de los que la entidad dispone para gestionar adecuadamente los elementos de riesgo inherentes al desarrollo de su actividad. La crisis financiera actual ha demostrado que no ha existido la transparencia suficiente. La informacin no llegbien al mercado. Un ejemplo claro es el relativo a los productos financieros ms complejos desarrollados en los timos as. Cuando los problemas se tornaron ms acuciantes, a finales de 2008, no se saba qu riesgos estaban asumiendo las diferentes instituciones financieras. En realidad, no se conoca quin estaba asumiendo esos riesgos. Ante esta situaci, los participantes en los mercados reaccionaron como se hace siempre frente a lo desconocido: con desconfianza. Si no se puede discriminar entre quienes estn ms expuestos a los riesgos y quienes lo estn menos, entre quienes han actuado con prudencia y los que no lo han hecho, la consecuencia es que se trata a todos por igual. Muchos mercados de financiaci que hasta entonces haban sido clave se cerraron o dejaron de funcionar correctamente por la ausencia de la informacin necesaria y se tratindiscriminadamente a unos y a otros, fomentando problemas en entidades e instituciones que, probablemente, no los tenan o los padecan en menor medida. Los reguladores y supervisores estn teniendo todo esto en cuenta. Se est trabajando en diferentes mbitos, como por ejemplo en el desarrollo de Basilea II, cuyo tercer pilar aborda precisamente la necesidad de informar a los mercados. Los reguladores contables y los de las agencias de rating tambin se preocupan de estas cuestiones, y conceden una importancia creciente a exigir una explicacin adecuada acerca de cmo y bajo qu criterios se generan la informacin que se transmite al mercado. Esta labor colectiva orientada a mejorar la transparencia es so un ejemplo del notable esfuerzo de cooperaci internacional que se est desarrollando para avanzar hacia un nuevo modelo de sistema financiero, para identificar los fallos y para proponer cambios en materia de regulacin y supervisin con el nimo de solventar dichas deficiencias. Y ese proceso de transformacin se est realizando sobre la base de los principios a los que me he referido anteriormente: favorecer el funcionamiento del mercado subsanando los problemas que se detecten, y a la vez, intentar que las respuestas nacionales no frenen la deseable globalizacin del sistema financiero. Ms y mejores mercados, ms y mejor cooperaci internacional es lo que necesitamos y lo que, felizmente, se est tratando de construir entre todos. Es cierto que pocas de estas propuestas de cambio en la regulaci y la supervisi van a servir para salir de la crisis. La mayora estn pensadas para evitar que se vuelva a producir otra de similares caractersticas. La salida de la crisis tiene ms que ver con el acierto en las polticas macroeconmicas -la monetaria y la fiscal,- as como en las de apoyo del sistema financiero o en las reformas estructurales, tan imprescindibles en muchos pases. Hoy la mayora de las instituciones que elaboran previsiones coincidimos en que la recuperaci de la economa mundial se podra producir en torno al principio del a que viene. Pero los niveles de incertidumbre son enormes. Hay un proverbio chino que cuenta que no se puede decir que un hombre ha sido feliz hasta que haya cumplido el timo da de su vida. Y probablemente deberamos mostrar la misma cautela a la hora de certificar la salida de la crisis. Pero el hecho de que las autoridades de los principales pases del mundo hayan coincidido en la orientacin de los esfuerzos para mejorar la regulaci y la supervisi del sistema financiero  ms cooperacin internacional y ms economa de mercado -es muy positivo y debemos celebrarlo. Con ello se aleja el que podra ser el peor de los escenarios de reaccin a la crisis: la desglobalizaci del sistema financiero. Parece que hemos aprendido de los aos treinta que las peores consecuencias de una crisis no vienen tanto de la crisis en s como de las inadecuadas reacciones a la misma, que la pueden agravar y prolongar. Por ello, en el caso que la crisis se prolongara ms de lo que deseamos, deberamos seguir resistiendo las llamadas al aislacionismo y al intervencionismo. Hasta la fecha los pesimistas se han equivocado. La humanidad no ha tropezado dos veces en la misma piedra. De momento. Muchas gracias.

Title: Closing speech of the course "Global Crisis: towards a new economic and social model". University of the Basque Country - Federation of Basque-Navarre Savings Banks
text: San Sebastian, September 11, 2009 Closing of the course "Global Crisis: towards a new economic and social model" University of the Basque Country - Federation of Basque-Navarre Savings Banks Miguel Fernandez Ordez Governor of Banco de Espa Good morning, I want to begin by expressing my gratitude to the organizers for the opportunity they give me to close this day and to share with you my reflections on the main challenges facing credit institutions in our country. This summer has marked two years since the beginning of the turbulence in the financial markets, and in a few days a year will have passed since the announcement of the bankruptcy of the US bank Lehman Brothers, which gave the crisis an extension and depth that nobody would have imagined. We are beginning to have some perspective over the time that has elapsed and it is not risky to say that this crisis will drive significant changes in financial regulation and supervision, and will entail a profound restructuring of the financial system on a global scale. The public debate focused tirelys on the measures that different governments and central banks have adopted to deal with the crisis, as well as on the need to modify the structures of international regulation and supervision to prevent a situation such as the current one from happening again in the future. To this end, a broad program of reforms is being discussed that includes, among other aspects: the inclusion in the perimeter of regulation and supervision of all those agents whose behavior affects the financial markets; a new supervisory structure in the world, with a regime of more intensive cooperation between the authorities of different countries; a broader conception of supervision, in which the macroprudential approach should gain weight; more prudent risk measurement; the introduction of countercyclical mechanisms in accounting and solvency rules to favour a smoother journey through the undulations of cycles; setting requirements for complex and interconnected entities; revitalization of asset securitization markets; and the promotion of managerial remuneration systems that do not introduce inadequate incentives for excessive risk-taking. All these issues have monopolized the debate in recent months. Today, however, I do not want to focus on the financial crisis, nor on the debate on regulation and supervision that has arisen as a result. I do not want to downplay these aspects. The international consensus is that they must be addressed urgently, and the Bank of Spain is participating very actively in the international forums in which the reforms to be carried out are being discussed. These are changes that will undoubtedly mark new paths for the future. But today I would like to highlight that, beyond regulatory and institutional reforms, what will really determine the future of our country's financial system will be the capacity of credit institutions to respond to the challenges posed by the current scenario. And I am not referring only to those that may see their viability compromised as a result of the crisis, but also to that vast majority of entities that, thanks to their good management, are well positioned to successfully overcome this difficult stage. It is a widely acknowledged fact, and in this room we have some excellent examples, that the general state of our country's financial institutions is reasonably good. This has a lot to do with the fact that all actors in the system have learned from the crises of the past. The severe financial crisis of the late 70s and early 80s is not so far away, caused by liberalizing measures that were not well accompanied by a correct monitoring of the suitability of the new bankers, nor by prudent rules that adequately channeled the strategies of the managers, in an environment -until then unknown- of progressive operational freedom and prices. As a result, many entities did not withstand the onslaught of the economic crisis of that period and went through significant problems. The development since then of our financial system and our supervisory model reveals that Spain knew how to assimilate well the lessons of this traumatic process. In the following years, the banking system was slowly consolidated, through a progressive modernization of activity and a continuous improvement in efficiency, with an increasingly higher quality management and a competitive environment that acts as a catalyst for progress, with milestones such as the concentration operations between the largest institutions undertaken since the late 80s. and the international expansion of the main Spanish groups that began in the mid-90s. This trajectory has been accompanied, and in a certain sense fostered, by a regulation in which the prudential approach has predominated, both in the definition of accounting and solvency rules, and in the criteria for their application, and supervision exercised through continuous monitoring enhanced by intense on-site review programs, which has asserted the advantages of closeness and intensity in the exercise of the surveillance function. And if in this way there have not been shocks of complicated digesti, it has also been because the entities, with good strategic vision, have undertaken their modernization step by step, without adventures not based on firm foundations, and sharing d0 and not only tolerating d0 the prudential approach of the regulator. This process has made it possible for the Spanish banking system to show reasonable solidity at the beginning of the international financial crisis, based on its ability to operate efficiently and profitably, with a set of very competitive entities within our borders and with top-level participants in the international arena. One of the factors that has contributed most to this good result is the business model developed by Spanish banks: retail banking. On the one hand, this model promotes a way of acting oriented to the clientele, and prone to weave bonds of loyalty between the user and the entity and, on the other hand, leaves the profit and loss accounts less exposed to the ups and downs of the markets. As a consequence of this strategic vocation, institutions have stayed away from some practices of financial innovation that have been revealed as particularly harmful and that had the effect of masking the level, location and nature of risks. Unlike what happened in other developed countries, our entities have not invested in the so-called Costa Rican assets, based on American subprime mortgages. Nor have they facilitated the concealment of risks by creating conduit vehicles that escape the supervisor's accounting and prudential control. Another essential element for the good state of our financial system has been the effort in the area of efficiency, which compares with the entities of the main countries of the euro area is very favourable. To this has contributed the effort in the containment of costs and the ability to innovate in the mechanisms of control and risk management, in the commercialization of products and in the implementation of organizational and technological improvements. In this sense, it highlights the growing use of the possibilities offered by information technologies, both to innovate in the processes of provision of traditional financial services and to offer new products and channels of relationship with customers. On the other hand, on the liability side, and despite the significant development of capital markets, Spanish institutions have not neglected to maintain a broad base of deposits. In addition, when our banks raised financing in international markets, they focused on relatively long maturities, which has given a certain margin in the worst moments of the financial crisis. All these factors, together with the well-known work of supervision and regulation of the Bank of Spain, have made it possible for us to have an advanced, efficient, competitive and profitable financial system, a crucial support element for the growth of our economy in the last few years, and at the same time, that we have found ourselves at the beginning of the crisis with a well-provisioned and well-capitalized banking system in relation to those of other countries. However, it is clear that, within this general picture, not all credit institutions have been managed with the same diligence, nor have they been affected to the same extent by the crisis. The vast majority, including those who, due to their size, have systemic relevance, are well positioned to face this stage. However, it is no less true that our system has some entities more exposed to the difficulties that the current economic environment raises, especially in those cases in which riskier credit policies have been developed. Given this scenario, the entities with the greatest difficulties must urgently adopt decisive measures to try to rebuild their viability in the short and medium term. And those who are in a more favorable situation, far from falling into complacency, must take the necessary steps to ensure their adaptation to changes of a structural nature in the environment in which they operate. In this regard, there are several factors, to which I will refer below, that pose significant challenges for Spanish banks, especially those that have developed less prudent strategies or have shown other weaknesses in internal governance. A year ago I referred in another intervention to some of these challenges as the "future challenges" of the Spanish banking system. Well, I very much fear that the future is already here, and that these challenges are already those of the present. What are the challenges that Spanish banks have to face immediately? First, press it on margins. In recent years, margins have increased significantly as a result of the increase in the volume of activity. However, in a new environment in which activity will presumably behave much less dynamically, this channel for obtaining profitability seems exhausted. In the current context, margin pressure reaches banks' income statements in at least three ways: the general environment of low interest rates in which we operate, which limits the ability of managers to obtain spreads - as wide as in the past between the return on investments and the cost of liabilities; the increase in the cost of financing in wholesale markets, due to the increase in risk perception; and the escalation of non-performing assets, as a result of non-performing loans. Secondly, the challenge of financing. Over-reliance on capital markets has emerged as a source of vulnerability. Liquidity risk management takes on a relevance that it had not had for many years, when banks had become accustomed to having abundant financing at reduced costs. Now, on the contrary, they face the need to seek a rebalancing in their financial structure and to ensure reasonable access to financing in wholesale markets. Thirdly, the challenge of capital. This crisis has not only opened the debate among the authorities on the capital that banks should have, but has revealed a general tendency of the markets to require them to operate at higher levels than hitherto, and achieved with better category instruments. Entities must, therefore, reflect on their ability to generate new equity resources of the highest quality in a stable manner, both through the capitalization of profits and through the use of the market, and on the limitations that this capacity imposes on the development of their business. On the part of the Bank of Spain, the capital review process d0 Pillar 2 d0 is also being implemented to ensure that each institution sets its own resources objectives consistent with its risk profile and the economic environment in which it operates. Fourthly, the challenge of efficiency. The competitive capacity of entities depends on their potential to deliver services efficiently. Hence, entities must develop appropriate plans to rationalize their technological processes and to reduce their costs, while improving or maintaining the quality of the services provided. Fifth, institutions must address a challenge that in the current context is perhaps the most important: that of asset quality. In particular, at this time, an adequate management of late payment is decisive to promote an effective recovery of claims which, in the event that the award of guarantees is chosen as a contractual or judicial form of recovery, should not be understood as concluded until the disposal of the assets. To this end, many entities are participating in projects that involve the contribution of the assets received to instrumental companies, owned or created together with other credit institutions. These are initiatives that should be applauded to the extent that they are based on the search for synergies for a better professionalized management of these assets, but which, literally, must be neutral in terms of their equity effects - accounting or solvency. By this reason, among the challenges facing our financial system, I would like to highlight the need for institutions to adapt to the new financial landscape so that they can continue to satisfactorily fulfil their economic function as providers of financing for the economy as a whole. In this regard, we must not forget that a weak financial system can increase constraints in the supply of credit and hinder the chances of recovery. All the above challenges converge, directly or indirectly, in a fundamental concept: the income statement. Given the presence of the exenos factors described, which limit the capacity to generate benefits, it is more necessary than ever to underline their importance. In scams, financial institutions have obtained significant returns that, although explained in part by some atypical factors, have been achieved in a highly competitive context. This is an excellent symptom because, in a competitive environment, results are the best indicator that things are being done well. However, these returns were also obtained in an environment in which domestic demand was growing at a much faster rate than GDP. This resulted in a growing indebtedness of the private sector, associated with credit growth figures that, with rates of around 20% at the top of the expansionary cycle, far exceeded those of the advance in the income of these agents. This process generates some structural imbalances in our banking sector. In this economic expansionary cycle and accelerated credit growth, in many cases very focused on real estate and construction activities, there was a significant expansion of banking structures, whose ability to operate profitably is now suffering from the adjustment in the size of the business. Possibly also the inertia of a form of gregarious competition based on the volume of activity has led some entities to forget that the most effective competitive factor in the medium term is the quality of management, an attribute on which the battle to differentiate and obtain a comparative advantage should focus. The profitability of banks in the scams has been largely based on the intense expansion of financial activity, but all prospects suggest that, after the crisis, growth in activity will be below those of the 2007 peak area. Now, faced with this much less expansive scenario, in which private sector agents are immersed in a process of deleveraging, in which various structural factors contribute to the compression of margins, in which capital requirements increase and in which the management of non-performing loans still has an important way to go, It is essential that, as they did in the past, financial institutions find ways to sustain their income statements, and at the same time there is a process of resizing and restructuring of the banking sector in our country. Success in this task is important for institutions and for the supervisor, because recurring solvency can only be built on the basis of results in the medium and long term. And it is also true for society as a whole, because a consistent and solvent financial system is an essential support for economic growth and makes it possible to avoid the costs that could arise if some entities have to come to the aid. For all these reasons, it is essential that the entities continue to deepen the processes of cost containment and improvement of efficiency and productivity to which I referred earlier, while ensuring the correct functioning of their internal control and guarantee mechanisms, such as risk, remuneration and appointment committees, audit or regulatory compliance. Entities can also exploit the benefits of economies of scale. In this sense, some d0 not all d0 have generated efficiency gains and better diversification through internationalization processes. However, given the excess capacity in the domestic market, it is desirable that the search for economies of scale in our country goes through restructuring and consolidation processes, provided that they contribute to reducing excess capacity in the sector and to exploiting synergies between different entities to the maximum. The authorities, for their part, must ensure that adequate levels of competition are maintained, which must remain, as has happened in Spain to date, an incentive for the modernisation and competitiveness of our financial system. In short, most of the credit institutions in our country, despite not having the problems that have been observed in other countries, must face the certainly pressing challenge of adapting to a new scenario in which new strategies will be necessary to obtain returns that guarantee their future in the medium and long term. On the other hand, those entities with the greatest difficulties will urgently have to undertake serious restructuring processes. For this, they will have a fundamental instrument: the Fund for Orderly Bank Restructuring (FROB), approved by the Government and validated in July by Parliament, with the agreement, in addition, of the main opposition party. In this sense, it is worth highlighting the broad parliamentary support achieved by the FROB, in which a strategy, in my opinion correct, is drawn to address the restructuring of the financial system of our country. The FROB regulations ratify the traditional approach applied in Spain in the treatment of entities with problems: a case-by-case approach, not based on the application of uniform fmulas. It consists of the use of the precautionary mechanisms available to the Bank of Spain for crisis resolution, including measures of intervention and replacement of administrators, and the participation of the guarantee funds of depitos, which have functions not only compensatory but also of contribution to sanitation. On these bases, the FROB has received a double mandate: to manage the restructuring processes of entities that present viability difficulties, and to strengthen the own resources of entities that participate in integration processes. As its name suggests, it puts the means so that these processes, necessary in the historical moment in which we live, can be concluded in an orderly manner, without risks to the stability of our system. With regard to the first mandate of the FROB d0 its possible participation in the restructuring of entities with viability problems d0 I would like to emphasize that its intervention is planned in the event that both a first phase of a strictly private solution and a second phase based on the traditional mechanism of the guarantee funds of depitos are exhausted without success. that are not financed with public contributions but with funds from their member entities. For this second phase, it is necessary for the entity to present a viability plan, which must be approved by the Bank of Spain. The latter will be rigorous in its analysis of the plan, which will have to be realistic taking into account the current economic context and the foreseeable new competitive environment in which the banking sector will operate in the ace cousins. In the event that the entity does not present the plan or it is not viable, that the Depitos Guarantee Fund has not accepted the conditions or aid provided for in the plan, or that the execution of the measures provided for in it is seriously breached, then the third phase of the process detailed in the new regulations would begin: the direct intervention of the FROB. In this case, following a principle of assumption of responsibilities, the Bank of Spain will agree, by impossibility of the Law, the measure of substitution of the old administrators, who will be replaced in this function by the FROB itself. Its first mission will be to prepare a report on the situation of the entity and submit to the approval of the Bank of Spain a restructuring plan, which will include measures of merger or cessions of the business. In addition, it must submit to the Minister of Economy and Finance an economic report referring to the financial impact of the restructuring plan on the funds contributed from the General Budget. The execution by the FROB of the restructuring alternative provided for in the Plan, once approved, will always be done through procedures that ensure competition and minimize the cost to the public treasury. The second mandate of the FROB, which is expected to concentrate most of its actions, is to support the integration processes between entities that, without being in a situation of pressing difficulty, address the improvement of their efficiency, the rationalization of their administration and the resizing of their productive capacity to improve their future prospects. The initiative, in this case, corresponds to the entities participating in the integration process, whether it is a fusi, an absorcin, an institutional protection system or other fmulas in accordance with the Espal legal system. The participation of the FROB will require the prior approval of an integration plan presented to Banco de Espa. Again I want to emphasize that the level of rigor in the evaluation of the plan will be high, both by the Bank of Spain and by the FROB, because the principle of efficient use of plastic resources requires that the use of aid is justified by a business plan that contributes to the strengthening of our financial system and that is accompanied by measures aimed at a realistic adaptation of the installed capacity to new market conditions. It is not a question of replacing the Spanish banking model, based on the importance of contact with customers through a network of branches, but of dispensing with duplicate or unprofitable units and, above all, of trying to adjust the central services of the new entities to the different reality of the business of the next years and to the limitations imposed by the search for maximum efficiency. By timo, it should be noted that the temporary disposition by the entities of instruments subscribed by the FROB that will be computable as own resources, will not, far from it, be free, since their remuneration will be set taking into account the principles established by the European Commission in order to avoid distortions in competition, aimed at ensuring that prices are applied in accordance with normal market conditions. In short, I would like to reiterate my confidence in this instrument, which has been designed taking into account the situation of the Spanish financial system and adapted to the specific characteristics of the crisis in our country and which, therefore, is potentially very useful to contribute to the stability of our system. Parliament has already approved the legal instrument and now it is the turn of the entities and the Bank of Spain. In this regard, it is essential that the administrators of our country's credit institutions understand the enormous responsibility they assume at this decisive moment for our financial system and act accordingly. Indeed, after the approval of the FROB, directors and administrators have, if possible, a greater obligation to evaluate the state of their entities and identify the best strategy to ensure their future. In the case of entities in difficulty, it is urgent that they examine their situation realistically and that viability strategies be considered, without loss of time, in line with the provisions of the royal decree that regulates the FROB, in search of the least traumatic solutions, which avoid the intervention of the Bank of Spain. Undoubtedly, also before July of this year and although perhaps some were not fully aware of it, the directors and administrators of savings banks and other entities had the obligation to ensure the proper administration of their institutions. But now, the legislator, when approving the FROB, demands from them a series of additional actions that, if not fulfilled properly, would lead them to incur a great responsibility. The restructuring of entities through the FROB is undoubtedly the issue that most attracts the interest of public opinion, something that is understandable given that these processes could involve the use of taxpayers' resources. However, I do not believe that this is the most relevant issue for the future of the Spanish financial system, as I have tried to explain in this speech. In the current context, what is really important is that the bulk of our financial system, that vast majority of well-managed, efficient and profitable entities, understand that to achieve results like those of the past, new strategies and an effort to resize and rationalize the banking sector of our country will probably be necessary. Success in this task will depend to a large extent on whether within a few years our country continues to have a financial system that can continue to support economic growth. In short, we must aim for our banking system to emerge stronger from the difficult economic and financial situation in which the developed world is immersed, with full capacity to continue to efficiently provide its services to the community and the economy. But the future cousin is not without risks. That is why it is essential that we all, entities and authorities, face the challenge of the first months joining forces, developing our responsibilities diligently, accepting the sacrifices that are necessary. At a time when the levels of uncertainty are still very high, someone has recalled what Cervantes said and that seems especially timely when asking us about the future of our financial system: "there is no more certain astrology than prudence". Thanks a lot.
text_original: San Sebastin, 11 de septiembre de 2009 Clausura del curso Crisis Global: hacia un nuevo modelo econico y social Universidad del Pas Vasco - Federaci de Cajas de Ahorro Vasco-Navarras Miguel Fernndez Ordez Gobernador del Banco de Espa Buenos das, Quiero comenzar expresando mi agradecimiento a los organizadores por la oportunidad que me brindan de clausurar esta jornada y de compartir con ustedes mis reflexiones acerca de los principales retos a los que se enfrentan las entidades de crdito de nuestro pas. Por un lado, este modelo promueve una forma de actuar orientada a la clientela, y proclive a tejer lazos de fidelidad entre el usuario y la entidad y, por otro lado, deja las cuentas de prdidas y ganancias menos expuestas a los vaivenes de los mercados. Adems, cuando nuestras entidades captaron financiaci en los mercados internacionales se centraron en plazos de vencimiento relativamente dilatados, lo que ha conferido un cierto margen en los peores momentos de la crisis financiera. Todos los retos anteriores convergen, directa o indirectamente, en un concepto fundamental: la cuenta de resultados.
