Este es un objetivo que se debe mantener pues, como se ha demostrado en nuestro pas, la competencia entre entidades es algo muy positivo. Djenme terminar volviendo a la macroeconoma. Como est ocurriendo en los pases de nuestro entorno, los datos ms recientes indican que la fase ms aguda de la contraccin de la economa espaola ya ha pasado. Las perspectivas apuntan a que a lo largo de este ao podra iniciarse una fase de crecimiento gradual, basado en el mantenimiento de una contribucin positiva de la demanda externa. Esto hay que celebrarlo pues significa que nuestras empresas ya no van a experimentar la cada libre de las ventas que se produjo el pasado ao. Sin embargo, lo relevante para resolver nuestros dos principales problemas  el paro y el dficit pblico - es aumentar el potencial de crecimiento con el que nuestra economa afrontar el nuevo ciclo expansivo. Como he explicado en numerosas ocasiones y tampoco repetir aqu, hay muchas razones que justifican que Espaa pueda crecer ms que otros pases europeos. Pero a nadie se le escapa que el optimismo que he proclamado es un optimismo condicionado. Estamos en uno de esos momentos histricos en los que, si hacemos lo que tenemos que hacer, podemos aumentar nuestro potencial de crecimiento y emprender de nuevo la senda del desarrollo y la convergencia. Por el contrario, si las reformas llegan tarde o son insuficientes, nuestro futuro es, sin duda, preocupante. Pero confo en que acometeremos las reformas. Mi confianza reposa principalmente en la poblacin espaola, que durante los ltimos 30 aos ha sido favorable a las reformas y sabe que este es el verdadero secreto del ascenso continuado de bienestar. Estoy convencido que la mayora del pueblo espaol es consciente de que nuestro progreso se ha basado en cambiar, en reformar, en adaptar nuestras instituciones ms caducas a aquellas ms modernas que imperan en los pases ms ricos que el nuestro. El xito indiscutible de estos ltimos 30 aos no ha venido cado del cielo sino de un continuo proceso de reformas. Y no veo la razn por la cual ahora, de repente, nos paremos y aceptemos que sin hacer nada sustancial saldremos adelante. Lo que s quiero recalcar es que las tareas que tenemos ante nosotros son de tal entidad que no corresponden a uno solo o varios de los actores o de los responsables del pas. Es una tarea que nos corresponde a todos: gobierno central, comunidades autnomas, corporaciones locales, reguladores y supervisores, trabajadores y empresarios, sindicatos y patronales, partidos que gobiernan y partidos que estn en la oposicin de los distintos parlamentos, etc. Es verdad que unos deben proponer y otros deben apoyar. Que unos deben dirigir y otros deben ayudar con sus ideas, que unos deben liderar y otros colaborar. Pero no creo que en la situacin actual nadie pueda escapar a la responsabilidad de resolver unos problemas que hoy son slo econmicos pero que -no podemos cerrar los ojos- si no los atajamos pronto, podran en algn momento rebasar ese terreno. Muchas gracias.

Title: Conference-lunch organized by the Association for the Progress of the Management of Valencia. "The current situation of the Spanish economy. The difficulties of SMEs"
text: Valencia, 24 March 2010 The current situation of the Spanish economy. The difficulties of SMEs. Conference-lunch organized by the Association for the Progress of the Directorate of Valencia Miguel Fernandez Ordez Governor I would like to begin by thanking the Association for the Progress of the Directorate for its kind invitation to participate in this luncheon and share with you some reflections on the situation that the Spanish economy is going through and the challenges that derive from it. Everything seems to indicate that the world economy has already overcome the most critical moments of the severe crisis we are experiencing and has even begun to take its first steps towards recovery. These are certainly uneven steps, firmer in emerging economies than in more developed economies, and they are also insecure steps, still supported by monetary and fiscal impulses of unprecedented intensity, but which have in many cases exhausted the available room for manoeuvre. But it is a fact that the improvement evidenced by the different indicators of activity and confidence and the gradual normalization of international financial markets have led to an upward revision of growth forecasts for this year and next. These signs of improvement have been reflected in the evolution of the Spanish economy in the quarters. Since the most acute moment of the crisis, a year ago, the recovery of the external environment, the gradual normalization of financial markets and the effect of fiscal stimuli and the reduction in interest rates, have gradually eased the contraction in GDP, which will end up practically stabilizing at the end of the year. The outlook now points to the beginning of a phase of recovery that is likely to be weak and gradual and that can only be consolidated if supported by major reforms. The Bank of Spain will disseminate in a few days the forecasts that we publish once a year, as required by the current General Law of Budgetary Stability. Given the depth of the recession experienced on an international scale, the challenges facing the Spanish economy are not alien, literally, to those that plan on the world economy. But our challenges contain above all unique elements, derived from the specific behavior of the economy before and during the response to it. It is therefore essential to correctly diagnose the nature of the problems we face so that economic policies can react accordingly and prevent the economy from being trapped in a situation of low growth. The Spanish economy will be able to recover sufficient medium-term growth rates to continue the process of real convergence if the necessary policies are implemented decisively and ambitiously. In the comments that follow I will try to develop these lines of reflection. The particular difficulties presented by the recovery in Spain have to do, in the first place, with the imbalances that had accumulated during the previous expansionary phase in terms of an excessive concentration of resources in the real estate sector, a high indebtedness of companies and households and potential risks to competitiveness as a result of a decade of cost increases and prices higher than those of the Monetary Union. The inevitable correction of these imbalances had begun to occur gradually before the onset of the international financial crisis, but is intensifying as a result of their spread into the real economy. Some of the adjustments now taking place are part of the process needed to restore the conditions for a sustainable economic recovery, even if they are holding back the necessary revival of domestic spending. The residential sector will have to reach a size commensurate with the new situation, and this requires that a good part of the existing excess supply be absorbed, which will undoubtedly limit the expansion of residential investment for some time. Similarly, as long as the restructuring of assets of companies and families is not completed, consumption and investment patterns will remain moderate. In a more hopeful direction, it is worth noting the significant decline in underlying inflation, which has occurred as a result of the notable increase in price sensitivity to cyclical conditions. This is making it possible to achieve gains in competitiveness, which, if consolidated, will be decisive for the recovery of growth. But as I said at the beginning of my speech, the development of the crisis has complicated the adjustment with two additional imbalances: the rapid deterioration of public accounts and the sharp increase in unemployment, much higher than that recorded by other countries in our environment. Two problems that, if not addressed soon, could seriously reduce the chances of recovery of the economy. In the case of finance and public debt, it is well known that high levels of public deficit and debt have a significant impact on interest rates, especially when markets are sensitive to the possibility of fiscal crises. But, in addition, they represent important mortgages for the future behavior of the budget, since they force to finance a growing burden of interest on public debt and reduce the capacity of the economy to face future shocks. It must be borne in mind that all historical experiences, own and others, show that the tendencies to increase public deficit and debt take root quickly and then are very difficult to break, due to the important factors of inertia that determine their dynamics. For its part, the disproportionate response of unemployment during the contractionary phase of the cycle reveals the persistence in Spain of important institutional deficiencies, particularly severe in the labour market, which also have a serious impact on the business fabric. The reduction of staff and the closure of companies have had a very negative impact on confidence and expectations, and have amplified recessionary trends. And all this constitutes an additional obstacle to the adjustment of public finances, the consolidation of financial institutions and, ultimately, to the recovery of growth. In these circumstances, it is essential to implement strictly the plan for reducing the deficit under the Stability Programme (2009-2013), since any significant deviation from the announced commitments will give rise to significant credibility problems that could give rise to the chances of recovery. These are ambitious objectives, the fulfilment of which will require significant efforts from all administrations Tenders and sacrifices to many groups potentially affected by the cuts, but the benefits will more than compensate them. It is equally urgent to undertake in parallel a broad set of reforms to mitigate the structural deficiencies that hinder the recovery and reduce the growth potential of the Spanish economy. As I have been insisting in my public interventions, the range of reforms needed is extensive and I will not repeat them today. But of all of them, particularly urgent are those that can contribute to halting the destruction of the business fabric and jobs, as well as facilitating business dynamism and accelerating the absorption by the labour market of the high number of unemployed that has arisen with the crisis, thus preventing long-term unemployment from continuing to rise. This orientation is particularly appropriate for a sector that is of great importance in our country and that is being particularly affected by the economic crisis. I am referring to the small and medium-sized enterprise sector, to which I would like to pay particular attention to this business forum in the remainder of my speech. The relevance of SMEs in the Spanish productive fabric is well known. And not only because of the high percentage they represent of the total number of companies, but also because they are responsible for a high percentage of the creation of new jobs in our country. These characteristics are shared with other developed economies, although in Spain the average size of companies is somewhat lower than the European average. The economic crisis is affecting this business sector particularly hard. By way of illustration, in 2008, more than 98% of business casualties were companies with less than ten employees, a percentage clearly higher than the weight of this type of company in the Spanish productive fabric (which is around 90%). These data make us wonder about the factors underlying the greater vulnerability of SMEs to the economic recession. Although at least a part, possibly not trivial, of the companies that have disappeared in these years may have done so in response to the sectoral readjustment being carried out by the Spanish economy, it is important to elucidate to what extent in this differential behavior of SMEs regulatory and institutional aspects converge that amplify the difficulties of these companies in a climate of macroeconomic deterioration. Undoubtedly, there are some aspects linked to the size of the companies themselves that explain this cyclical behavior. However, the fact that the fall in corporate profits during the crisis has been particularly high in small companies indicates the presence of some structural deficiencies that affect this type of company more negatively and whose effects are exacerbated asymmetrically during recession phases. From this perspective, the adoption of the structural reforms to which I referred earlier acquires an additional dimension of urgency insofar as it can provide a very promising way to solve the problems of this important segment of business demography, particularly hard hit by the crisis. Labour market reforms, which I have been stressing in many public interventions for the economy as a whole, would be particularly beneficial for small enterprises. In our collective bargaining system, only relatively large medium-sized companies with more than 300 employees have their own collective agreement, while those of lower size have to comply with the provisions of higher-level sectoral agreements, set at provincial or national level. With this institutional framework, it is very difficult for wage levels determined at the sectoral level, based on relatively generic considerations of growth, productivity and inflation, to be adapted in a sufficiently differentiated way to the different work and productive environment faced by smaller companies. Not to mention something that is fundamental at this time, such as internal flexibility, which by improving productivity can help to get out of the crisis with fewer adjustments in wages and employment. And if this feature of our collective bargaining system is inefficient under macroeconomic conditions that can be considered "normal", it is particularly damaging in situations of economic contraction such as those experienced by the Spanish economy in the two years, in which the impact of the crisis has fallen very unevenly on companies and sectors, This has caused the adjustment to take place through the expulsion from the market of a good number of companies and workers. An expulsion in many cases unnecessary, because it could have been avoided with a more flexible framework, but which, once it has occurred, has caused a lasting damage on productive capacity and human capital. Disaggregated information on the behaviour of the agreement rates of the two years corroborates this. In general, sectoral collective agreements have been setting wage increases higher than those established at the individual company level, so that small and medium-sized enterprises have been subject to greater cost pressures in a particularly adverse context for them and have lacked alternative adjustment mechanisms such as those that have been able to use some of the larger ones. A reform of the collective bargaining system which, inter alia, would make it possible to make the application of collective agreements more flexible and which would provide employers and workers with the possibility of reaching agreements which, as is being done in many large enterprises, take into account their specific situation, would help to resolve adjustment needs in a less traumatic and more efficient manner. better preserving employment and productive capacity. In this sense, the possibility of using take-down clauses, as contemplated in the Agreement for employment and collective bargaining that has just been signed by the social partners, represents a step in the right direction, but only if an effective application of the same is guaranteed, at least until the necessary reform of the collective bargaining system provided for in said Agreement is concluded. Indeed, the lack of flexibility in fixing a core part of working conditions, in particular that relating to wages, could explain the greater recourse of small companies to temporary hiring. And this is a second factor that, with great probability, is helping to amplify the effects of cyclical counter-reaction on the behavior of SMEs. In order to prevent these companies from being forced to dismiss temporary workers when their contracts expire and having to resort to temporary contracts en masse in the future, greater internal organisational capacity should be facilitated and permanent recruitment arrangements introduced that can be used in general. A review of the structural barriers that condition the activity of SMEs cannot be concluded without making a reference, even if brief, to the administrative environment in which they operate. The costs arising from this environment are more burdensome for small enterprises because of their fixed component. In this sense, the reduction of administrative burdens borne by companies, regulatory simplification, especially tax and labor, and the elimination of the overlap of state, regional and local regulations are crucial to improve the competitiveness of small companies. As is the improvement of competition and sectoral liberalization policies, to the extent that the lack of competition can be particularly detrimental to the development of the activities of SMEs, which are more conditioned by the decisions of companies with greater market control, usually also of greater size. All these structural reforms are also essential to alleviate the financial tensions that continue to be experienced in the economy and that affect SMEs more intensely. A higher level of employment and higher potential growth would immediately translate into an increase in the expected incomes of Spanish households and companies, and this would help them to reduce the still high debt ratios of the sector in a way that is not traumatic for the dynamism of consumption and productive investment. Improving the equity position of the private sector would undoubtedly improve the solvency of its demands for funds and thus expand its ability to access credit. SMEs are, in general, much more dependent on bank credit than larger companies, for which it is less expensive to go directly to the markets. This asymmetry is aggravated in situations such as the current one of great uncertainty and high risk aversion since, due to its size, its number and its high heterogeneity, the assessment of its individual solvency is in itself particularly complex. Credit to all companies is behaving in Spain in a similar way to the rest of Europe, where there are falls between 2.5% and 4.5%, far from the 17% decline observed in the US. Having overcome the financing problems of the past, these figures reflect a greater impact of demand factors d0 if sales and investment fall, the demand for credit for working capital and investment falls d0 but the different surveys carried out among SMEs show the perception of a marked deterioration in their conditions of access to credit. It is reasonable to think, and this is reflected in some of these surveys, that a part of the greatest difficulties encountered in obtaining financing is not unrelated to the strong impact that the crisis is having on its results, and therefore, on its future payment capacity. In this sense, part of the biggest difficulties of SMEs to obtain financing at this juncture has to do with the weakening of their position during the crisis. But another part of this tightening is surely linked to the increase in difficulties in assessing, in this context of great uncertainty, the solvency of individual projects and this can be interpreted as a greater incidence of restrictions on the supply of credit on this segment of the business fabric, which justifies the special measures adopted to alleviate it. It is in this line that initiatives are inserted to strengthen the role played by the ICO in mitigating the information problems that usually limit access to credit for SMEs. But beyond sectoral measures of a palliative nature, their access to credit will depend closely on improving financing conditions for the economy as a whole. It is clear that a weak fiscal position ends up translating into higher financing costs, not only for the public sector, but also for the private sector and, above all, for the segments most vulnerable to credit supply constraints, such as SMEs. In any case, the improvement of financing conditions in our country also involves a restructuring of the financial system that allows entities to adjust effectively to conditions that will clearly be more demanding than before the crisis. Since the beginning of the financial turbulence, which will meet three as the summer cousin, I have explained ad nauseam why the Spanish financial system has resisted with a great The international financial crisis was solid, while we saw the most important banks of some developed countries collapse. But I have also been solving my own problems (digest of real estate excesses, reduction of activity and margins, difficulties in wholesale financing, greater capital requirements by regulators and markets, etc.) that forced serious restructuring efforts by all our entities as soon as possible. I would say that most Spanish entities are doing their homework. In the first place, those entities that in the future analyses carried out by the supervision of the Bank of Spain do not show viability problems but that, nevertheless, need to be restructured by reducing costs, improving their efficiency and profitability, increasing their capital, etc. In this group are the banks, but also the larger savings banks and many other savings banks that have a very strong position. There is another group of entities, mainly savings banks, which are viable today but which, subject to these analyses, show problems in the future. A majority of this group - and you can follow this in the press - are also setting in motion integration processes which, helped by the plastic resources approved by Parliament, will facilitate their restructuring. But unfortunately, there is a minority of boxes that are delaying these processes, either by their own decisions, or by the interference of the governments of their autonomous communities. Although in my previous appearances I have explained the damage caused by these delays in restructuring, I want on this occasion, as emphatically as possible, to call on the responsibility of these savings banks and the autonomous communities that are harming these processes so that they change their attitude immediately, not because of the damage they do to themselves and their region. but for the damage caused to the rest of the credit institutions that are doing their homework. They are few, it is true, and their weight in the system as a whole is small, but the image of slowness and inability to solve their problems is transmitted to the whole of the Spanish banking system, spreading suspicion about the soundness of the other institutions and making their financing more expensive. To this minority of savings banks and governments of autonomous communities, we must tell them clearly that they are not only creating difficulties for others, but also harming themselves and their territories. It is true that these entities are now still viable, but you should know that, as soon as they cease to be, Parliament has provided the Bank of Spain with sufficient instruments so that beyond what the assemblies of these savings banks and the regional governments think, these entities are intervened and subsequently liquidated or sold in the manner provided for by the FROB. This means the opening of the file to the directors and other management gains of the savings banks, and a much more traumatic reduction in employment and financial services in their region than would have occurred in the case of having undertaken orderly integration processes, and all this regardless of the increase in cost to the Spanish taxpayer, for which they will undoubtedly be responsible. But while these attitudes change, and hopefully change soon, we must all continue to explain the fundamental soundness of most Spanish entities. The Director of Regulation of the Bank of Spain dedicates his tima intervention - which can be consulted on our website - and shortly the Bank will advance the publication of the financial stability report. But those who can best explain their situation are the entities themselves, so they should redouble their efforts to show their reality to analysts and plico in general. Furthermore, in addition to speeding up restructuring, I must reiterate the need to adopt as soon as possible a reform of the financial system which will enable the savings banks to provide themselves with quality own resources, if we are not only to prevent problems such as those we are experiencing from arising in the future, but also to ensure that the best savings banks can be sufficiently capitalised and thus be able to continue contributing in the future to the provision of credit and financial services to the Member States. Spanish families and companies. The good progress of financial restructuring and the reform of savings banks will be fundamental for the Spanish economy, its business fabric in general and SMEs in particular. But neither these nor other reforms will achieve their objectives if they are not accompanied by an essential labor reform that stops the bleeding of unemployment and favors hiring, as well as if concrete measures are not adopted soon to comply with the ambitious fiscal consolidation plan sent to Brussels. To do this, and I will not tire of repeating it, the first thing is to avoid falling into the serious mistake of thinking that the exit from the international crisis will solve our problems without the need for reforms. No doubt that recovery will help, but it will not solve our problems. If there are reforms in the areas I have mentioned, we will soon be able to achieve reasonable employment growth. Without reforms, we will face a long period of mediocre employment growth, with future consequences for public finances, the financial system, social protection and, in general, the standard of living and well-being of the people. Thanks a lot.
text_original: Valencia, 24 de marzo de 2010 La situaci actual de la economa espala. Las dificultades de las pymes. Conferencia-almuerzo organizado por la Asociaci para el Progreso de la Direcci de Valencia Miguel Fernndez Ordez Gobernador Quisiera comenzar agradeciendo a la Asociacin para el Progreso de la Direcci su amable invitaci para participar en este almuerzo y compartir con ustedes algunas reflexiones sobre la situaci por la que atraviesa la economa espaola y los retos que de ella se derivan. Todo parece indicar que la economa mundial ha superado ya los momentos ms crticos de la severa crisis que estamos viviendo y que incluso ha comenzado a dar sus primeros pasos hacia la recuperaci. Son, ciertamente, unos pasos desiguales, ms firmes en las economas emergentes que en las ms desarrolladas, y son tambin unos pasos inseguros, apoyados todava en unos impulsos monetarios y fiscales de una intensidad sin precedentes, pero que han agotado en muchos casos los mrgenes de maniobra disponibles. Pero es un hecho que la mejora que evidencian los distintos indicadores de actividad y de confianza y la paulatina normalizacin de los mercados financieros internacionales han llevado a revisar al alza las previsiones de crecimiento para este ao y el siguiente. Estos signos de mejora han ido teniendo su reflejo en la evoluci de la economa espala en los timos trimestres. Desde el momento ms agudo de la crisis, hace ahora un ao, la recuperacin del entorno exterior, la progresiva normalizacin de los mercados financieros y el efecto de los estmulos fiscales y de la reduccin de los tipos de inters, fueron aliviando poco a poco la contracci del PIB, que terminprcticamente estabilizndose al concluir el ejercicio. Las perspectivas apuntan, en la actualidad, al inicio de una fase de recuperacin que ser probablemente dbil y gradual y que so podr consolidarse si se apoya con importantes reformas. El Banco de Espa difundir en unos das las previsiones que publicamos una vez al a, tal como exige la vigente Ley General de Estabilidad Presupuestaria. Dada la profundidad de la recesi vivida a escala internacional, los retos a los que se enfrenta la economa espaola no son ajenos, licamente, a los que planean sobre la economa mundial. Pero nuestros desafos contienen sobre todo elementos singulares, derivados del comportamiento especfico de la economa antes de la crisis y durante la respuesta a la misma. Por ello es esencial diagnosticar acertadamente la naturaleza de los problemas a los que nos enfrentamos para que las polticas econicas puedan reaccionar en consonancia y evitar que la economa quede atrapada en una situacin de escaso crecimiento. La economa espala so podr recuperar ritmos de crecimiento a medio plazo suficientes para continuar el proceso de convergencia real si se instrumentan con decisi y ambici las polticas necesarias. En los comentarios que siguen tratar de desarrollar estas lneas de reflexi. Las dificultades particulares que presenta la recuperacin en Espaa tienen que ver, en primer lugar, con los desequilibrios que se haban acumulado durante la fase expansiva previa en trminos de una concentraci excesiva de recursos en el sector inmobiliario, un elevado endeudamiento de empresas y familias y unos riesgos potenciales para la competitividad como consecuencia de una dcada de aumentos de costes y precios superiores a los de la Unin Monetaria. La inevitable correcci de estos desequilibrios haba comenzado a producirse de forma gradual antes de que se iniciara la crisis financiera internacional, pero se intensifica raz de su propagaci hacia la economa real. Algunos de los ajustes que estn teniendo lugar ahora forman parte del proceso necesario para restablecer las condiciones de una recuperaci econmica sostenible, aunque estn frenando la necesaria reanimaci del gasto interno. El sector residencial deber alcanzar una dimensin acorde con la nueva situaci, y esto exige que una buena parte del exceso de oferta existente se vaya absorbiendo, lo que limitar indudablemente la expansin de la inversi residencial durante alg tiempo. De igual modo, mientras no termine el saneamiento patrimonial de empresas y familias, las pautas de consumo y de inversin seguirn siendo moderadas. En una direccin ms esperanzadora hay que anotar la significativa disminucin de la inflaci subyacente, que se ha producido como consecuencia del notable incremento en la sensibilidad de los precios a la situaci cclica. Ello est permitiendo lograr ganancias en la competitividad, que, si se consolidan, sern decisivas para la recuperaci del crecimiento. Pero como he dicho al principio de mi intervenci, el desarrollo de la crisis ha venido a complicar el ajuste con dos desequilibrios adicionales: el rpido deterioro de las cuentas pblicas y el intenso aumento del desempleo, muy superior al que han registrado otros pases de nuestro entorno. Dos problemas que, si no se encauzan pronto, pueden mermar gravemente las posibilidades de recuperaci de la economa. En el caso de las finanzas plicas, es bien conocido que niveles de dficit y de deuda pblicos elevados tienen un impacto significativo sobre los tipos de inters, sobre todo cuando los mercados estn sensibilizados frente a la posibilidad de que se produzcan crisis fiscales. Pero, adems, suponen importantes hipotecas para el comportamiento futuro del presupuesto, dado que obligan a financiar una carga creciente de intereses de la deuda pblica y reducen la capacidad de la economa para enfrentarse a perturbaciones futuras. Hay que tener presente que todas las experiencias histicas, propias y ajenas, muestran co las tendencias al aumento del dficit y la deuda pblicos se arraigan con rapidez y luego son muy difciles de quebrar, debido a los importantes factores de inercia que determinan su dinmica. Por su parte, la desproporcionada respuesta del desempleo durante la fase contractiva del ciclo revela la persistencia en Espaa de deficiencias institucionales importantes, singularmente severas en el mercado laboral, que tienen adems un grave impacto sobre el tejido empresarial. La reduccin de plantillas y el cierre de empresas han afectado muy negativamente a la confianza y las expectativas, y han amplificado las tendencias recesivas. Y todo ello constituye un obstculo adicional para el ajuste de las finanzas pblicas, el saneamiento de las instituciones financieras y, en definitiva, para la recuperaci del crecimiento. En estas condiciones, resulta inexcusable ejecutar de forma estricta el plan de reducci del dficit plico que contempla el Programa de Estabilidad (2009-2013), ya que cualquier desviaci significativa respecto a los compromisos anunciados suscitar importantes problemas de credibilidad que podran dar las posibilidades de recuperacin. Son objetivos ambiciosos, cuyo cumplimiento exigir esfuerzos notables a todas las Administraciones Plicas y sacrificios a numerosos colectivos potencialmente afectados por los recortes, pero los beneficios los compensarn con creces. Igualmente apremiante resulta acometer en paralelo un amplio conjunto de reformas que permita mitigar las deficiencias estructurales que lastran la recuperacin y reducen el potencial de crecimiento de la economa espaola. Como he venido insistiendo en mis intervenciones pblicas, el abanico de reformas necesarias es extenso y no voy a repetirlas hoy. Pero de todas ellas, son particularmente urgentes aqullas que pueden contribuir a detener la destrucci de tejido empresarial y de puestos de trabajo, as como a facilitar el dinamismo empresarial y acelerar la absorcin por el mercado laboral del elevado nmero de desempleados que ha surgido con la crisis, evitando as que contine aumentando el paro de larga duraci. Esta orientaci es particularmente adecuada para un sector que tiene gran importancia en nuestro pas y que se est viendo afectado de manera especial por la crisis econmica. Me refiero al sector de las pequeas y medianas empresas, al que quiero dedicar, ante este foro de carcter empresarial, una especial atencin en el resto de mi intervenci. La relevancia de las pymes en el tejido productivo espal es bien conocida. Y no solo por el elevado porcentaje que representan sobre el total del nero de empresas, sino tambin porque son responsables de un porcentaje elevado de la creaci de nuevos puestos de trabajo en nuestro pas. Estas caractersticas son compartidas con otras economas desarrolladas, aunque en Espaa el tama medio de las empresas es algo inferior a la media europea. La crisis econica est afectando de manera particularmente intensa a este sector empresarial. A modo de ilustracin, en 2008, ms del 98% de las bajas empresariales fueron empresas con menos de diez asalariados, un porcentaje claramente superior al peso de este tipo de empresas en el tejido productivo espal (que se sit alrededor del 90%). Estos datos obligan a preguntarse por los factores que subyacen a la mayor vulnerabilidad de las pymes frente a la recesin econica. Aunque al menos una parte, posiblemente no trivial, de las empresas que han desaparecido en estos as pueda haberlo hecho en respuesta al reajuste sectorial que est realizando la economa espaola, es importante dilucidar en qu medida en este comportamiento diferencial de las pymes confluyen aspectos regulatorios e institucionales que amplifican las dificultades de estas empresas en un clima de deterioro macroeconmico. Indudablemente, existen algunos aspectos ligados al propio tama de las empresas que explican este comportamiento cclico. Sin embargo, el hecho de que la cada de los beneficios empresariales durante la crisis haya sido singularmente elevada en las empresas de reducida dimensin, indica la presencia de algunas deficiencias estructurales que afectan de forma ms negativa a este tipo de empresas y cuyos efectos se agudizan de forma asimtrica durante las fases de recesi. Desde esta perspectiva, la adopci de las reformas estructurales a las que antes haca referencia adquiere una dimensin de urgencia adicional en la medida en la que puede suministrar una va muy prometedora para la soluci de los problemas de este importante segmento de la demografa empresarial, especialmente castigado por la crisis. Las reformas del mercado de trabajo, sobre cuya necesidad para el conjunto de la economa he venido insistiendo en numerosas intervenciones pblicas, seran particularmente beneficiosas para las empresas de reducida dimensin. En nuestro sistema de negociaci colectiva solo las empresas de tama medio relativamente elevado a partir de 300 empleados disponen de convenio colectivo propio, mientras que las de dimensi inferior se han de atener a lo establecido en los convenios sectoriales de mbito superior, fijados a nivel provincial o nacional. Con este entramado institucional, resulta muy difcil que los niveles salariales que se determinen a escala sectorial, a partir de consideraciones relativamente genricas sobre crecimiento, productividad e inflaci, se adecuen de forma suficientemente diferenciada al distinto entorno laboral y productivo al que se enfrentan las empresas ms pequeas. Por no hablar de algo que es fundamental en este momento, como la flexibilidad interna, que al mejorar la productividad puede ayudar a salir de la crisis con menores ajustes de salarios y empleo. Y si este rasgo de nuestro sistema de negociaci colectiva es poco eficiente en condiciones macroeconmicas que puedan considerarse normales, resulta particularmente perjudicial en situaciones de contraccin econica como las que ha vivido la economa espala en los dos timos aos, en las que el impacto de la crisis ha recado de forma muy desigual sobre empresas y sectores, lo que ha provocado que el ajuste se produzca mediante la expulsin del mercado de un buen nmero de empresas y de trabajadores. Una expulsin en muchos casos innecesaria, porque se podra haber evitado con un marco ms flexible, pero que, una vez que se ha producido, ha causado un da duradero sobre la capacidad productiva y el capital humano. La informaci desagregada sobre el comportamiento de las tarifas de convenio de los dos timos aos corrobora este extremo. Con carcter general, los convenios colectivos de mbito sectorial han venido fijando crecimientos salariales ms elevados que los establecidos en los de mbito individual de empresa, por lo que las pequeas y medianas empresas han estado sometidas a mayores presiones de costes en un contexto particularmente adverso para ellas y han carecido de mecanismos de ajuste alternativos como los que han podido utilizar algunas de las de mayor dimensi. Una reforma del sistema de negociaci colectiva que, entre otros aspectos, permitiera flexibilizar la aplicaci de los convenios colectivos y que proporcionara a empresarios y trabajadores la posibilidad de alcanzar acuerdos que, como se est haciendo en muchas grandes empresas, tengan en cuenta la situaci especfica de las mismas, ayudara a resolver de manera menos traumtica y ms eficiente las necesidades de ajuste, preservando mejor el empleo y la capacidad productiva. En este sentido, la posibilidad de utilizar clusulas de descuelgue, tal y como contempla el Acuerdo para el empleo y la negociacin colectiva que acaban de firmar los agentes sociales, supone un avance en la direcci correcta, pero solo si se garantiza una aplicacin efectiva de la misma, al menos hasta que concluya la necesaria reforma del sistema de negociaci colectiva prevista en dicho Acuerdo. Precisamente, la falta de flexibilidad para fijar una parte nuclear de las condiciones laborales, en particular la relativa a los salarios, podra explicar el mayor recurso de las empresas pequeas a la contratacin temporal. Y este es un segundo factor que, con gran probabilidad, est contribuyendo a amplificar los efectos de la contraccin cclica sobre el comportamiento de las pymes. Para evitar que estas empresas se vean abocadas a despedir a los trabajadores temporales cuando vencen sus contratos y que en el futuro tengan que volver a recurrir de forma masiva a los contratos temporales se ha de facilitar una mayor capacidad de organizacin interna e introducir modalidades de contrataci permanente que puedan utilizarse con carcter general. No se puede concluir una revisi de las barreras estructurales que condicionan la actividad de las pymes sin hacer una referencia, aunque sea breve, al entorno administrativo en el que stas se desenvuelven. Los costes que se derivan de dicho entorno resultan ms gravosos para las empresas pequeas debido al componente fijo de los mismos. En este sentido, la disminuci de las cargas administrativas que soportan las empresas, la simplificacin regulatoria, en especial la fiscal y laboral, y la eliminacin de la superposici de normas estatales, autonicas y locales resultan cruciales para mejorar la competitividad de las empresas de reducida dimensin. Como tambin lo es la mejora de la competencia y las polticas de liberalizacin sectorial, en la medida que la falta de competencia puede ser particularmente daina para el desarrollo de las actividades de las pymes, que se ven ms condicionadas por las decisiones de las empresas con mayor control de mercado, normalmente tambin de mayor tama. Todas estas reformas estructurales son fundamentales tambin para aliviar las tensiones financieras que se siguen viviendo en la economa y que afectan de manera ms intensa a las pymes. Un mayor nivel de empleo y un crecimiento potencial ms elevado se traduciran inmediatamente en un incremento de las rentas esperadas de las familias y de las empresas espalas y ello les ayudara a reducir las todava elevadas ratios de endeudamiento del sector de un modo no traumtico para el dinamismo del consumo y de la inversin productiva. El saneamiento de la posici patrimonial del sector privado mejorara, sin duda, la solvencia de sus demandas de fondos y ampliara as su capacidad de acceso al crdito. Las pymes son, en general, mucho ms dependientes del crdito bancario que las compaas de mayor tama, para las que resulta menos costoso acudir directamente a los mercados. Esa asimetra se agrava en situaciones como la actual de gran incertidumbre y elevada aversin al riesgo ya que, por su dimensin, su nmero y su elevada heterogeneidad, la valoraci de su solvencia individual resulta de por s particularmente compleja. El crdito al conjunto de las empresas se est comportando en Espa de forma parecida al resto de Europa, donde se registran cadas entre el 2,5% y el 4,5%, muy alejadas del descenso del 17% observado en EEUU. Superados los problemas de financiacin del pasado a, estas cifras reflejan un mayor impacto de los factores de demanda  si caen las ventas y la inversin, licamente cae la demanda de crdito para el circulante y para la inversi , pero las distintas encuestas realizadas entre pymes muestran la percepcin de un acusado deterioro de sus condiciones de acceso al crdito. Es razonable pensar, y as lo refleja alguna de estas encuestas, que una parte de las mayores dificultades encontradas para obtener financiaci no es ajena al fuerte impacto que la crisis est teniendo sobre sus resultados, y por tanto, sobre su capacidad de pago futura. En este sentido, parte de los mayores aprietos de las pymes para obtener financiaci en la presente coyuntura tiene que ver con el debilitamiento de su posici durante la crisis. Pero otra parte de ese endurecimiento est seguramente ligada al incremento de las dificultades para valorar, en este contexto de gran incertidumbre, la solvencia de los proyectos individuales y ello puede interpretarse como una mayor incidencia de las restricciones de oferta de crdito sobre este segmento del tejido empresarial, que justifica las medidas especiales adoptadas para paliarla. Es esta lnea se insertan las iniciativas para reforzar el papel que desempea el ICO en la mitigacin de los problemas de informaci que habitualmente limitan el acceso al crdito de las pymes. Pero, ms all de las medidas sectoriales de carcter paliativo, su acceso al crdito depender estrechamente de las mejora de las condiciones de financiaci del conjunto de la economa. Es evidente que una posicin fiscal dbil termina traducindose en mayores costes de financiacin, no solo para el sector plico, sino tambin para el sector privado y, sobre todo, para los segmentos ms vulnerables a las restricciones de oferta de crdito, como es el caso de las pymes. En todo caso, la mejora de las condiciones de financiacin en nuestro pas pasa tambin por una reestructuraci del sistema financiero que permita que las entidades puedan ajustarse de manera eficaz a unas condiciones que sern a todas luces ms exigentes que antes de la crisis. Desde el inicio de las turbulencias financieras, que cumplirn tres as el primo verano, he explicado hasta la saciedad por qu el sistema financiero espaol ha resistido con una gran solidez la crisis financiera internacional, mientras veamos derrumbarse los bancos ms importantes de algunos pases desarrollados. Pero tambin he ido selando los problemas propios (digesti de los excesos inmobiliarios, reducci de actividad y mrgenes, dificultades en la financiacin mayorista, mayores exigencias de capital por reguladores y mercados, etc.) que obligaban a acometer cuanto antes esfuerzos serios de restructuraci por parte de todas nuestras entidades. Yo dira que la mayora de las entidades espaolas est haciendo sus deberes. En primer lugar, aquellas entidades que en los anlisis a futuro que realiza la supervisi del Banco de Espaa no muestran problemas de viabilidad pero que, sin embargo, requieren reestructurarse reduciendo costes, mejorando su eficiencia y rentabilidad, aumentando su capital, etc. En este grupo estn los bancos, pero tambin las cajas de mayor dimensi y otras muchas cajas de ahorro que tienen una posicin muy sida. Hay otro grupo de entidades, fundamentalmente cajas de ahorro, que son viables hoy pero que, sometidas a esos anlisis, muestran problemas en el futuro. De este grupo son tambin mayora -y ustedes lo pueden seguir por la prensa  las que estn poniendo en marcha procesos de integracin que, ayudados con los recursos plicos aprobados por el Parlamento, facilitarn su reestructuracin. Pero desafortunadamente, hay una minora de cajas que est retrasando estos procesos, bien por sus propias decisiones, bien por la interferencia de los gobiernos de sus comunidades automas. Aunque en mis anteriores comparecencias he explicado el dao que producen estos retrasos en la reestructuraci, quiero en esta ocasi, con la mayor rotundidad posible, hacer una llamada a la responsabilidad de esas cajas y de las comunidades automas que estn perjudicando esos procesos para que cambien su actitud inmediatamente, no so por el da que se hacen a s mismas y a su regi, sino por el perjuicio que causan al resto de las instituciones de crdito espalas que s estn haciendo sus deberes. Son pocas, es verdad, y su peso en el conjunto del sistema es reducido, pero la imagen de lentitud e incapacidad de resolver sus problemas se trasmite al conjunto del sistema bancario espal, extendindose la sospecha sobre la solidez de las dems instituciones y encareciendo su financiaci. A esa minora de cajas y de gobiernos de comunidades autnomas hay que decirles con claridad que no solo estn creando dificultades a las dems, sino que adems se perjudican a ellas mismas y a sus territorios. Es verdad que esas entidades ahora son todava viables, pero deben saber que, en cuanto dejen de serlo, el Parlamento ha dotado al Banco de Espaa de suficientes instrumentos para que ms all de lo que piensen las asambleas de esas cajas y los gobiernos autonicos, esas entidades sean intervenidas y posteriormente liquidadas o vendidas en la forma que prev el FROB. Esto significa la apertura de expediente a los consejeros y dems ganos de gobierno de las cajas, y una reducci mucho ms traumtica del empleo y los servicios financieros en su regin que la que se hubiera producido en el caso de haber acometido procesos ordenados de integraci, y todo ello independientemente del aumento del coste para el contribuyente espal, del que sin duda ellos sern responsables. Pero mientras estas actitudes cambian, y esperemos que cambien pronto, todos debemos seguir explicando la fundamental solidez de la mayora de las entidades espalas. El Director de Regulaci del Banco de Espa dedica ello su tima intervenci -que pueden consultar en nuestra pgina web- y en breve el Banco adelantar la publicacin del informe de estabilidad financiera. Pero quienes pueden explicar mejor su situaci son las propias entidades, por lo que deberan redoblar sus esfuerzos para mostrar su realidad a analistas y plico en general. Por otra parte, adems de acelerar la restructuracin, debo reiterar la necesidad de aprobar cuanto antes una reforma del sistema financiero que permita a las cajas dotarse de recursos propios de calidad si queremos no solo evitar que en el futuro surjan problemas como los que estamos viviendo, sino que las mejores cajas puedan capitalizarse suficientemente y as poder seguir contribuyendo en el futuro a la provisi de crdito y de servicios financieros a las familias y empresas espaolas. La buena marcha de la reestructuraci financiera y la reforma de las cajas de ahorro sern fundamentales para la economa espaola, su tejido empresarial en general y las pymes muy en particular. Pero ni estas ni otras reformas alcanzarn sus objetivos si no vienen acompadas por una imprescindible reforma laboral que detenga la sangra del desempleo y favorezca la contratacin, as como si no se adoptan pronto medidas concretas que permitan cumplir con el ambicioso plan de consolidaci fiscal enviado a Bruselas. Para ello, y no me cansar de repetirlo, lo primero es evitar caer en el grave error de pensar que la salida de la crisis internacional resolver nuestros problemas sin necesidad de hacer reformas. Sin duda esa recuperacin ayudar, pero no resolver nuestros problemas. Si hay reformas en los campos que he mencionado, podremos alcanzar pronto un crecimiento razonable del empleo. Si no hay reformas, nos enfrentaremos a un perodo largo de crecimiento mediocre del empleo, con las consecuencias que ello tendr en el futuro sobre las finanzas pblicas, el sistema financiero, la protecci social y, en general, el nivel de vida y bienestar de los espales. Muchas gracias.

Title: The Spanish banking sector in the face of the international financial crisis: diagnosis and measures adopted. Intervention at the Meeting of Presidents of Committees of Economy and Finance of National Parliaments of the European Union. Congress of Deputies.
text: LOGO_3_Negro_300 Madrid, 15 April 2010 The Spanish banking sector in the face of the international financial crisis: diagnosis and measures adopted Meeting of Chairmen of Economic and Finance Committees of National Parliaments of the European Union/Congress of Deputies Javier Ar92ztegui Deputy governor Introduction I would like my first words to be of thanks for the opportunity you give me to address all of you, representatives of the Economic and Monetary Affairs Committees of the European Parliaments; I would like to take this opportunity to explain the measures that have been taken to enable the Spanish banking system to continue contributing to the growth of the economy in the context of the international financial crisis. The crisis that broke out in the summer of 2007 is undoubtedly the most serious recorded since the 30s of the 20th century. Its intensity and scope are unprecedented and have required extraordinary interventions by public authorities. Faced with a situation of such gravity, it is difficult to speak of positive aspects, but I believe that at least one deserves our recognition. And it is precisely the reaction of the public authorities and, in particular, the degree of cooperation and coordination that has finally been achieved at international level. On our continent, the commitment to the common project that is the European Union has contributed decisively to this coordinated action of the authorities. The actions of public officials have revolved around two axes. One, the interventions aimed at preventing the collapse of the financial system, which have materialized in recapitalizations and in the granting of guarantees so that banks can continue to issue their liabilities in the stock markets. And another, the reform of financial regulation to avoid the mistakes of the past. This regulatory change, on which the Bank of Spain is actively working, will have more medium-term effects, since its objective is to limit the possibility of the crisis repeating itself and, in any case, if it is repeated, that it surprises us better prepared to face it with the least damage to our citizens. But I will not address this issue today. My objective is to analyze the situation of the Spanish banking sector in the face of the crisis and the measures that have been adopted in Spain. For this I will structure my words in three parts. In the first I will describe the basic features of Spanish entities that have avoided having to carry out massive recapitalizations. In the second, I will focus on several relevant imbalances that the banking system will have to face in the immediate future. And finally, I will convey to you what strategy has been developed to address these problems. Before dealing in detail with each of these issues, allow me to convey to you the thrust of my speech. The main characteristic of the Spanish banking system is that it has developed a typical "traditional retail banking" business, which is defined by its simplicity and proximity to the customer. This way of doing banking, which before the outbreak of the crisis some defined as outdated, has largely prevented the collapse of the Spanish banking system. But given the duration and magnitude of the crisis and some structural imbalances in our economy in which the banking sector also participated, it has been necessary to implement two actions. One, to facilitate the issuance of bank debt in the international markets of the euro, markets that closed suddenly in the summer of 2007. And another, the creation of the so-called Fund for Orderly Bank Restructuring (FROB) that fulfills a double objective: it allows a quick and effective action of the Bank of Spain in case it is necessary to intervene and sell any entity that could go through viability problems; and, secondly, it facilitates the restructuring of banks and savings banks which, although viable, may require some help in their rationalisation process. The banking model in Spain: traditional retail business As I have pointed out, the most remarkable feature of the Spanish banking sector is its specialization in "traditional retail banking". This banking model is the one we all have in mind: credit institutions that are financed mainly with deposits and that lend long-term to their asset customers. The closeness to the client and the permanence of this relationship are also defining aspects of this model of banking. They are very important because they not only facilitate customer loyalty, but also contribute to the entity and the customer getting to know each other better. The bank is concerned with looking for clients who have an adequate risk profile and, from that selection, manages and controls that risk while the relationship is still alive. The importance of this way of doing business and its capacity to resist the current crisis are better understood if, in contrast, the basic features of the alternative model, which was developed with intensity in different countries, mainly in the United States, and which has been called "originate to distribute" are analyzed. The reason for this designation is that the bank acts as a mere intermediary and does not maintain a customer relationship. Simply put: a bank makes loans to customers, but those loans and therefore the associated default risk are "packaged", restructured and transformed into securities, which are then sold on the financial markets. What does this imply in the bank-customer relationship, as opposed to what happens in a retail banking model? It implies, first, that since the bank "packages" the loans and sells the securities resulting from the transformation, it does not retain the risk. Loans are not held on banks' balance sheets, so banks have less incentive to correctly select customers. And for the same reason, that is, because the risk has been transferred to a third party, banks do not have a reason to worry about the evolution of the credit quality of the customers to whom they granted the financing. The situation is significantly complicated by the degree of complexity that has accompanied the process of "bundling" the loans for later sale. The products used in this process became more and more complicated, and the risk was distributed throughout the market. The problem is that this risk did not end, as was thought, in the hands of those who had more capacity to manage it, but in the hands of those who sought a higher interest rate, or those who simply did not understand the implications of the complex assets they were acquiring. In the retail banking model, such as the Spanish one, that degree of complication and sophistication in the development of new products has simply not been part of the business and, consequently, in the summer of 2007 Spanish banks had not incurred the dangers that finally demanded massive bailouts in other countries: - Spanish entities did not participate in the generation of complex assets, those that have commonly been called "toxic". Spanish banks have bundled loans, selling the resulting securities on the market. But this process has little to do with that developed by banks that have participated in the "originate to distribute" model. And this is because the loans were not deregistered from the bank balance sheets, that is, the risk was not transferred. Therefore, the perverse incentives to which I referred earlier were not generated. In addition, securitization in Spain has been based on products that are very simple and easy to evaluate by end customers. - The Spanish entities also did not invest in these toxic products and, in particular, in those related to the US "sub-prime". Other entities that did acquire them have suffered huge losses. - And finally, Spanish entities did not create structures or vehicles outside bank balance sheets. I am referring to those known as Conduits and SIVs, structures conceived in the heat of the "originate to distribute" model and that in their creation were, in one way or another, supported by financial institutions. The outbreak of the crisis has shown that these off-balance sheet vehicles actually acted as "shadow banks": they were financed in the short term on international markets, based on the reputation of the promoter bank, and invested in the long term. The fundamental problem is that, acting as such, they were subject to neither regulation nor prudential supervision: and no capital was required of them. Regulation and supervision of the Spanish banking system have also helped prevent the collapse of the sector. As deputy governor of the Bank of Spain, the authority responsible for the regulation and supervision of the banking sector, I am not the best person to make this assessment but, leaving aside the failures that every institution always has, I believe that there are three characteristics of our supervisory system that are now internationally recognized as positive: - One is the treatment in Spain of the structures outside the bank balance sheets to which I have just referred. We demand their consolidation in the balance sheets, subjecting them, therefore, to prudential regulation and supervision. Simply put: if a Spanish bank wanted to set up one of these vehicles, that activity was subject to the corresponding capital requirements. The reality has been that this decision acted as a definitive brake on the creation of these innovations. - The second is a very close and demanding supervisory model, which relies on permanent control of bank accounting. The Bank of Spain is the accounting regulator of the individual financial statements that are used for simple banks or as a basis for preparing the financial information of complex groups listed on the Stock Exchange. This facilitates a firm supervision of banks and savings banks based on a clear criterion: institutions must compete openly with each other but this competition must pivot on a common basis of prudence and conservatism in the generation, recognition and distribution of results, which must be respected by all competitors and which is monitored by the Bank of Spain. - The third is the system of "countercyclical provisions". Its philosophy, beyond technicalities, is that entities generate a cushion at the favorable moment of the cycle charged to the results. This buffer was designed to explicitly recognize the credit risks (and therefore the implicit costs) that boil over at the good times of the cycle, and then materialize when the cycle changes. Entities will be able to use it in the recessionary phases of the economy. Its existence has allowed Spanish banks to better cope with the period of strong upswing in non-performing loans that has been recorded in our market over the last three years. In terms of provisions, the body that sets international accounting standards, namely the International Accounting Standards Board (IASB), is evolving towards a new methodology for determining the level of provisions for insolvencies. If this approach finally succeeds, the calculation method would not be based on the "loss incurred", but on the "expected loss", a concept that has characterized the Spanish provision model since mid-2000. In short, the development of a "traditional retail banking" model and the insistence on accounting and supervisory work have contributed to Spanish banks barely incurring the dangers that have eventually led to massive recapitalizations in other countries. A banking model based on these principles is not synonymous with being uncompetitive and inefficient. On the contrary, the Spanish banking sector faced the crisis that erupted in the summer of 2007 from the position of being one of the most profitable and efficient in its environment, while having a high volume of provisions and a level of capital that was well above the regulatory minimums. Imbalances that the sector will have to reabsorb But the Spanish banking system has not remained immune to the crisis since it has incurred a series of imbalances that it will necessarily have to solve. Before describing which imbalances I consider most relevant, and which largely justify the measures that have been adopted, allow me briefly to give you some data that serve to frame the evolution of the sector in the last three years. Credit granted to the private sector resident in Spain, which had grown at rates of over 20% year-on-year from 2005 to mid-2007, has maintained a downward trend and registered slightly negative rates of change in December 2009 (-2%). The difficult economic situation explains this evolution. On the one hand, because companies and families demand less financing. And, on the other, because given the deterioration of the credit quality of customers, entities have increased their requirements for granting loans. The credit slowdown is relatively widespread for the different economic sectors, but more intense in those where growth was stronger in the past or which, by their nature, are more linked to the evolution of the cycle. Non-performing assets in the resident private sector and, consequently, NPL ratios have performed the opposite way to credit: they have grown sharply. Thus, the NPL ratio rose from 0.6% in December 2006 to 5% in December 2009. The increase in the ratio is being more pronounced in sectors whose evolution is more linked to the economic cycle, such as credit to households for purposes other than the purchase of housing and, in particular, to the construction and real estate development sectors. This upward trend in non-performing loans is expected to continue in the coming months but, over the last few quarters, its rate of increase, which is very intense at the beginning, has gradually moderated. Although non-performing loans are closely linked to the performance of the economy, and hence increase more intensely in the most cyclical sectors, there is also a high degree of dispersion between entities. And this does not only depend on their relative sector exposures: even in the construction and real estate development sector, entities with similar exposures have significantly different NPL ratios. This is explained by differences in credit and risk management policies. In summary, on the asset side, the sharp slowdown in activity and the sharp increase in non-performing loans should be highlighted as the most noteworthy facts. On the liability side, it is worth highlighting the difficulties of institutions in accessing wholesale financing markets: some market segments simply stopped working and others have been doing so with difficulties. In addition to the aid that banks have received from the public sector to facilitate their access to markets, which I will discuss in detail later, Spanish depository institutions have increased the collection of deposits in the internal market. Competition for deposit-taking has intensified significantly and is expected to persist while banks and savings banks adapt their business strategies to the new situation in the emissions market. The consolidated results of Spanish banks, despite continuing to be favourable when analysed in comparison with those recorded in other countries, have fallen by 20% between December 2008 and December 2009. The return on equity, which stood at 20% in December 2006, now stands at 9%. The income statements, therefore, have been subject to strong downward pressures. These pressures materialise, mainly, in the increase in provisions for insolvencies, as a result of the increase in non-performing loans, and have offset the evolution of recurring revenues which, favoured by the more traditional business and the containment of operating costs, increased by 18% between December 2008 and December 2009. The sector as a whole closed 2009 by strengthening its solvency ratios: the total ratio stood at 12% (it was 11% in December 2006), the core ratio reached 10% (it was 7% in December 2006) and the core capital ratio 8% (it was 6% in 2006). The solvency ratios have been strengthened thanks to the increase in own resources and, in particular, the increase in higher quality ones. In summary, in recent years, the Spanish banking system has developed its activity in a difficult situation. It has reacted in the right direction, containing operating costs, stepping up traditional retail deposits and bolstering its higher-quality equity. The general parameters under which the sector operates show that it is, in general, healthy. But the pressures arising from the poor performance of the real economy, which are materialized in lower volumes of activity and an increase in non-performing loans, and the difficulties in obtaining financing in the international wholesale markets are still in force today. And to these are added several imbalances of a structural nature that will necessarily have to be adjusted. In the last part of my speech I will address what measures have been put in place to alleviate this situation, but for your better understanding I will first refer to the structural imbalances that I have pointed out: - Firstly, the Spanish banking sector suffers from excess installed capacity. The run-up to the summer 2007 crisis was characterised by downward pressure on income statements. Banks tried to offset this trend by increasing their efficiency, but also by increasing the volume of loans. In a business model that relies on retail banking and customer proximity, and that is very competitive, this led to the growth of the number of branches and, in many cases, their geographical expansion outside their known and traditional environment. This expansion cannot be profitable by requiring a reabsorption of excess installed capacity. - Secondly, Spanish banks financed credit growth by intensifying their use of international financial markets. In the sector's liability structure, the weight of the traditionally strong retail deposit base has been declining in favour of funding from institutional investors. The structure of the maturities of these issues is concentrated in the medium and long term, but today it is clear that the weight of wholesale financing held by Spanish entities in their balance sheets, in relation to traditional deposits collected from retail clients, exceeds the threshold that international markets are willing to admit at the current level of appetite for risk. There is no doubt that the closure of financial markets in the face of a widespread loss of confidence has hindered, and in some cases impeded, access to wholesale financing. This is a permanent change and Spanish banks have to rebalance their liability structures, which is a difficult and gradual process that will take some time to materialize. - The third imbalance to which I will refer is related to the situation of the real estate market in Spain. It is a sector that until 2006 grew excessively and that, since then, is subject to a very marked adjustment process. The Spanish banking system, with differences between banks, financed this excessive growth and now suffers the consequences of the adjustment, which materialize in an intense increase in doubtful loans. Especially those credits that were granted to finance companies related to real estate development activities, which is where the greatest risk currently lies. The financing granted to households for the purchase of housing, due to the very characteristics of this type of loan and the importance for households of the well-financed, is less subject to the cyclical problems that are traditional in the development sector. The volume of bank investment in real estate development is not, however, equivalent to the potential losses that entities will eventually have to assume. Such equivalence is erroneous, first, because it implies that no customer will be able to meet its contractual obligations. And second, that banks will not have the capacity to recover a part, greater or less, of the value of the loans granted, knowing that it is a type of financing that is backed by mortgage guarantees that always have a residual value. But that said, the volume of investment in the real estate development sector is high and poses a risk to manage and rebalance. Diagnosis and strategy designed by the authorities Allow me to summarize what has been said so far in a very schematic way in order to, from there, convey to you the diagnosis of the situation made by the Spanish authorities and, consequently, detail the measures adopted. First, Spanish banks develop a traditional business model that has protected them from the most damaging effects of the financial crisis. And second, the banking sector has incurred imbalances that it must reabsorb: excess capacity, a high weight of wholesale financing and a marked exposure to the real estate development sector. This comes against a backdrop of downward earnings pressures that will persist. From this emerges some common element with what happened in other countries, but also some differences. The common element is that Spanish entities had been resorting to a greater extent than in the past to a type of financing, the wholesale, which was blocked when international financial markets were closed. This posed a risk of strangulation for the banking sector. There are two differentials; one positive and one negative. The positive is the traditional retail banking model that has been a protection. The second differential, negative element derives from overcapacity and intense investment in the real estate development sector. This requires reabsorbing these imbalances. As in any industrial restructuring process, these adjustments are difficult and time-consuming. The authorities' objective in this regard is to ensure that the banking sector is in a position to continue contributing to the growth of the Spanish economy as it emerges from the recessionary phase. And no less important, that this means the lowest possible costs for taxpayers. From this diagnosis, it is easy to understand the measures that have been adopted: aid for the financing of entities and the creation of the Fund for Orderly Bank Restructuring. As I have indicated, the closure of international financial markets implied a risk of strangulation of the sector on the liability side. In mid-October 2008, the granting of State guarantees for new fixed-income issues made by banks was approved. In "community jargon" this is known as "guarantees" to private debt. It is a measure that is part of the decisions taken by the European Heads of State and Government, who at their meeting on 12 October 2008, will insist on their commitment to preserve the stability of the financial system by facilitating the financing of the institutions. The implementation of this measure in Spain authorized the granting of State guarantees for new financing operations carried out by credit institutions resident in Spain -Spanish or foreign-, with the maximum maturity of said operations being five years. It is a measure that has managed to mitigate the liability problems of various entities, while the risks for the State have been limited, especially since a commission is included in the cost of the guarantees that reflects the risk assumed in each operation. The second set of measures, which revolve around the creation of the FROB, have a more structural character and support an adjustment of the sector. It could be argued that this process should be based exclusively on traditional individual crisis resolution mechanisms, with the participation of Deposit Guarantee Funds, whose functions also include sanitation, and which in Spain are constituted ex-ante by the contributions made by the entities. Why then has the creation of the FROB been chosen? It has been considered that the exceptional situation implied by the international financial crisis required, as a preventive measure, the creation of this new instrument, which should allow the orderly reduction of installed capacity. In this sense, the FROB has been constituted with resources that should clear doubts about the viability of the process: if necessary, it plans to reach 99,000 million euros of available resources, equivalent to 9.5% of GDP. Committing that amount does not, however, correspond to an exercise of estimating the potential losses of the Spanish banking sector but, as I have said, is due to the interest of the Spanish State in transmitting the necessary confidence to the market that more than sufficient resources are available. The FROB is designed for two functions: to intervene and sell those entities that may not be viable and, second, to facilitate the restructuring processes of the sector. As for its function as an intervention mechanism in non-viable entities, the FROB has been designed for fast, effective action and in which private solutions prevail over the intervention of the Bank of Spain. Schematically, its way of acting under this modality is conceived on two levels: - First, the entity that is experiencing problems will have to look for a private solution that implies strengthening its solvency, and therefore, correcting the deficiencies that endanger its viability. If you need additional resources, you can be helped by the corresponding Guarantee Fund that is nourished with private resources and reach an agreement with the sector for "mutual" support. - The second level involves the direct action of the FROB at the request of the Bank of Spain that intervenes the entity and changes the administrators. The FROB assumes the provisional administration and puts up for sale, totally or partially, the intervened entity. To meet this function, the FROB can mobilize the 100,000 million euros that I have mentioned. The second leg of the FROB contemplates the stimulation of merger and rationalization processes of credit institutions to improve their efficiency in the medium term and strengthen their own resources. In this case, the entities must present an integration plan detailing the entities that merge and under what conditions and in what evolutions and what they consist of and how the efficiency improvements and the resizing of their productive capacity will be achieved. If the plan is approved by the Bank of Spain as supervisor, the help provided by the FROB consists of strengthening own resources through the subscription of preferred shares. These own funds have a remuneration of 7.75% and will have to be repaid in five years. I insist that, in order to grant them, the merger and, where appropriate, the disappearance of entities, the rationalization of the business and the reduction of installed capacity are required. The FROB is, therefore, an instrument that tries to ensure that the process occurs in an orderly manner and that the entities assume the corresponding cost. Sometimes the pace at which the FROB is acting has been discussed since some have considered that it was too slow. I will make several considerations in this regard: - I have already explained that the Spanish banking sector is in a reasonably good position. The impact of the financial crisis did not result in massive losses requiring massive recapitalizations. The emphasis of the instrument created d0 the FROB d0 is to facilitate the process of reabsorption of imbalances that the sector has to undertake, reinforcing its profitability and solvency in the medium term. - Among the entities that have incurred greater imbalances are some savings banks. These entities, which at the operational, regulatory and supervisory levels are fully equated with commercial banks, have some peculiarities in relation to their ownership and governance structure. These particularities add some element of difficulty and slowness in the restructuring process. - And third, but no less relevant, the FROB is structured around several levels of action, giving primacy to the restructuring operations that entities decide to carry out on a voluntary basis. In other words, while the entities are viable, they have the initiative and they set the times, since the objective is to minimize the use of public resources. Obviously, if they get into difficulties, the initiative is from the Bank of Spain and it marks the times. But we are not in that case, but in the voluntary actions of integration. In any case, and as I have already mentioned, a majority of entities have already initiated different strategic actions aimed at adapting and rationalizing their structures to operate in the new environment. This has led them to increase their own resources, especially those of higher quality, to raise more deposits and to contain their operating expenses, in particular through the closure of offices. Likewise, the FROB has also initiated its actions. On March 25, 2010, the Governing Committee of the FROB, after the approval of the Bank of Spain, decided to financially support three integration processes, which involve the disappearance of eight savings banks to create three new entities. The total amount of aid provided by the FROB amounts to 2,155 million euros. The support is materialized through the subscription by the FROB of preferred shares convertible into participatory quotas, and is subject to the execution of the integration processes in the terms approved by the Bank of Spain.
