Today, more than 80% of the existing savings banks in Spain are facing integration processes, which represents approximately 90% of their assets. The processes in which they are immersed are of different nature. - Three integrations approved by the Bank of Spain have requested resources from the FROB: Two other integration processes are being finalized without requesting any public aid. - Also different in terms of their appeal or not to the resources of the FROB are the integration processes that are already agreed by the Boards of Directors and that have not yet been approved by the Bank of Spain: some will require aid from the FROB and in other cases will not be necessary. - Finally, as you know, two entities have been intervened and their administrators have been changed: CCM and CajaSur. Here, too, there are differences in processes. In the first case, that of CCM, which was intervened on March 29, 2009, there was no public aid, but the Deposit Guarantee Fund was used, which since 1994 has been nourished with the contributions of the savings banks. The assembly that completes its restructuring will take place in eleven days. The second case, that of CajaSur, is the first intervention of the Bank of Spain under the FROB scheme. At the moment several national and foreign banks and savings banks are studying the sales documentation and it is expected to award the entity in the first half of July 2010. A first reading of the above reinforces the ideas I have already outlined. When banks find voluntary integration solutions to which the Bank of Spain agrees, that is the natural path, which may or may not involve the mobilization of public resources. When an entity is not able to solve its problems, and reaches a point where it ceases to be viable, then the Bank activates the other operational mode of the FROB and the credit institution is intervened and subsequently awarded in a competitive procedure that seeks to minimize the public resources used, assigning it to another bank or savings bank, Spanish or foreign, solvent and able to manage the draft resolution. Advancing a step further in this update of the process, I think it is interesting to draw some brushstrokes on the likely physiognomy of the box sector in the future. Firstly, the reform will entail a reduction in the number of banks and, in particular, savings banks. Secondly, the capacity of the sector will not only be rationalised by the decrease in the number of institutions, but also by the reductions resulting from the merger processes in terms of operating and office costs. Each specific case presents differences that derive from the integration plan and business that they are going to develop. But some data serve as a reference: in cases where integration processes are carried out through the FROB, the average decrease in the number of offices is between 20-25%, in central services in 18-20%, and in the number of employees between 15-18%. And thirdly, the integration processes that are being carried out through the FROB imply recognizing additional losses in bank balance sheets since in the business combination possible adjustments due to insolvency and illiquidity are anticipated in an environment of tension. This means that the resulting entity is born with a stronger balance sheet, with more capital and with fewer expectations of future losses. Additionally, the Bank of Spain is carrying out stress exercises for all entities of the Spanish banking system that are expected to be published in the coming weeks. I conclude with these brushstrokes on the future physiognomy of the savings bank sector alluding to the upcoming legislative changes that have been agreed between the two largest political parties in the nation. It is well known that savings banks do not have the capacity to issue capital. This not only reduces their possibilities to strengthen their own resources, but also limits the power of the market to discipline them. The new regulations to be developed, insofar as they make it possible to issue capital instruments of the highest quality, with voting rights, represents a very important step forward in overcoming the deficiency I have mentioned. In this regard, it can be ventured that the introduction of these regulatory changes will probably seek optionality. That is, the boxes themselves will have to decide what they want to be. For some, their choice will likely be to approach the banking model. For others, it will go through the issuance of capital instruments with voting rights. Another group will probably decide to concentrate on a tighter geographical area and continue using the more classic model. But ultimately, as I have indicated, savings banks must be able to have instruments that facilitate their capitalization. And the boxes, regardless of their options, must be fully subject to market discipline. Thanks a lot.
text_original: LOGO_3_Negro_300 Santander, 18 de junio de 2010 El sector bancario espaol: situacin, perspectivas y evolucin del proceso de reestructuracin APIE/UIMP Javier Arztegui Subgobernador Quisiera, en primer lugar, agradecer la invitacin que me han trasladado la Asociacin de Periodistas de Informacin Econmica y la Universidad Internacional Menndez Pelayo para clausurar estas jornadas. Cuando particip en este foro el ao pasado, las jornadas estuvieron dedicadas a la repercusin de la crisis en la industria en general. Ahora, un ao despus, la crisis sigue vigente, constatando que vivimos tiempos difciles. La crisis financiera internacional que se desat en el verano de 2007 ha atravesado diferentes fases, que a riesgo de ser en exceso simplista, se pueden caracterizar del siguiente modo. - Primero, desde el verano de 2007 y, en especial, desde septiembre de 2008, se registr una prdida de confianza en el sistema bancario, que le llev a las puertas del colapso. En un perodo de tiempo muy corto, entidades de diferentes pases consideradas de primer orden necesitaron ser rescatadas por sus gobiernos. - En segundo lugar, a medida que la economa mundial entr en una fase recesiva, la menor actividad y el debilitamiento de la calidad crediticia de los clientes bancarios han deteriorado los balances de las entidades y han aadido ms presin a sus resultados. - Y tercero, los esfuerzos de los gobiernos por evitar el colapso del sistema bancario, las medidas de estmulo y la propia debilidad de la economa real han implicado un rpido deterioro de las finanzas pblicas, obligando a poner en marcha potentes planes de consolidacin fiscal. En mi intervencin abordar cmo est transitando el sistema bancario espaol por estas aguas turbulentas. En trminos generales, cabe destacar que su salud es buena, lo que no quiere decir que no est afrontando una coyuntura difcil. Y por otro lado, una parte del sector, especialmente las cajas de ahorros, estn inmersas en un proceso de reestructuracin. Sobre esta cuestin centrar mi intervencin, ordenndola en tres apartados: Primero, reflexionar brevemente sobre el punto de partida de los bancos y cajas espaoles ante el estallido de la crisis. Segundo, analizar cul es su situacin actual. Y en el tercer apartado tratar de debatir la oportunidad de las medidas adoptadas por las autoridades y su ritmo de avance. El punto de partida Antes del estallido de la crisis, el sistema bancario espaol era considerado como uno de los ms eficientes y rentables de nuestro entorno. Este logro se alcanz desarrollando una forma de hacer negocio que suele denominarse banca tradicional y minorista. No eran pocos los que en ese momento consideraban que esta forma de hacer banca estaba anticuada. La alternativa era un modelo bancario que se ha venido en denominar originar para distribuir. Esta forma de hacer banca creci con intensidad en los aos anteriores a 2007 principalmente en los Estados Unidos y supona, en principio, una respuesta vlida para gestionar el negocio en una sociedad rica y con altos costes de estructura. Su aplicacin prctica, sin embargo, ha supuesto, un desarrollo un tanto alocado que ha generado sobresaltos. La realidad de los tres ltimos aos ha mostrado que la banca tradicional minorista ha estado mejor equipada para afrontar la crisis que la banca del originar para distribuir, que ha terminado con no pocas entidades rescatadas por sus gobiernos. Hoy, desde diferentes mbitos, se reclama que el sector vuelva a lo bsico, o dicho de forma sencilla, que los bancos vuelvan a ser bancos cuidadosos con sus riesgos. El modelo de originar para distribuir se basa en que las entidades conceden prstamos que empaquetan, se reestructuran y posteriormente se venden en los mercados como valores negociables. El negocio tradicional, que es el desarrollado por las entidades espaolas, se basa en la idea que ms o menos todos tenemos de un banco clsico: financiarse fundamentalmente a travs de depsitos minoristas para conceder crditos a los clientes. Y ello potenciando la cercana a la clientela y el establecimiento de relaciones permanentes con ella, de tal modo que se reduzcan los incentivos a mirar para otro lado en lo relativo a la calidad crediticia de los acreditados y de su evolucin. La gestin del riesgo de crdito es el ncleo esencial de la banca tradicional. Asentadas en estos pilares, las entidades de crdito espaolas han evitado generar, e invertir, en los activos que se han venido en denominar txicos. Los bancos espaoles no participaron de ese negocio, no entraron en esa carrera de complejidad en la generacin de los productos y no crearon estructuras de inversin fuera de sus balances (conduits y SIVs). La regulacin y la supervisin de nuestro pas trataron de reforzar los aspectos positivos de esta forma de hacer banca. Ahondando en esta lnea, el Banco de Espaa est extrayendo lecciones adicionales de la crisis. Los cambios del Anejo IX de la Circular contable que recientemente se han presentado a consulta pblica son una muestra de su preocupacin por el reconocimiento temprano del riesgo y del deterioro, y su plasmacin fiel en las valoraciones de los activos. Para confirmar este criterio de prudencia simplemente apuntar tres ejemplos. Las provisiones dinmicas que han protegido a las entidades de crdito en el momento de mayor repunte de la morosidad; la exigencia del regulador de consolidar estructuras fuera de los balances (conduits y SIVs) que de facto ha evitado su desarrollo; y una supervisin prxima a la banca y exigente, que descansa en un control permanente de su contabilidad. Situacin actual del sector: desequilibrios abiertos Como ya he sealado, el sistema bancario espaol est, en su conjunto, sano, si bien existen diferencias en la posicin econmico-financiera de las entidades. Estos contrastes responden, en gran parte, a las diferentes polticas crediticias y de gestin de riesgos desarrolladas por las distintas empresas durante el largo perodo expansivo que culmin en el ao 2007. Por otra parte, la gran mayora de las entidades estn haciendo los deberes, es decir, estn respondiendo a las dificultades presentes adoptando medidas que van en la direccin correcta: incrementando su base de depsitos minoristas; racionalizando sus costes de estructura, y reforzando significativamente su capital. Pero an as, el sector ha de afrontar la reabsorcin de tres desequilibrios estructurales. Primero, una fuerte dependencia de los mercados mayoristas internacionales. Segundo, una excesiva inversin en el sector de promocin inmobiliaria. Y tercero, un excedente de capacidad instalada. - Desde la creacin de la moneda nica, las entidades espaolas financiaron una parte de su crecimiento acudiendo a los mercados de capitales, a travs de la emisin de valores suscritos principalmente por no residentes. Y, en consecuencia, su base de depsitos minoristas ha perdido peso frente a la financiacin mayorista. El peso relativo de los pasivos instrumentados mediante valores, especialmente los suscritos por no residentes, ha alcanzado un nivel que resulta elevado para la aversin al riesgo dominante en la actualidad. La mayor apelacin a los mercados mayoristas no es un desarrollo exclusivamente espaol pero, dentro del rea del euro, probablemente nuestra banca es la que ha avanzado ms rpidamente en esta direccin. No obstante, las entidades espaolas se han aproximado a estas fuentes de financiacin de un modo que se puede considerar prudente, al estar la mayora de los vencimientos concentrados en plazos medios y largos. An as, las entidades, en funcin de sus propias caractersticas, precisan modificar su estructura de pasivo para basarla ms en depsitos interiores. Pero este proceso inevitablemente llevar su tiempo. - La inversin en el sector de promocin inmobiliaria residencial tambin ha sido excesiva y supone un riesgo. Ello es as porque es una industria que est muy vinculada al ciclo econmico y que experimenta un fuerte proceso de ajuste. De lo anterior no se puede deducir que las prdidas potenciales para el sistema bancario sean iguales al volumen de la inversin realizada en promocin. Aunque sea algo obvio, en ocasiones se olvida que la prdida final depender de que se materialicen los impagos y de la capacidad de recuperacin de las garantas hipotecarias de respaldo. Y adems hay que descontar las provisiones ya constituidas. Desde el punto de vista de la absorcin de este desequilibrio es razonable que las entidades utilicen las herramientas a su alcance para minimizar las prdidas. Pero cabe exigir que ello no implique que se dilate su reconocimiento. El Banco de Espaa, a travs de la supervisin y de ajustes en la regulacin, no aceptar dilaciones. - El tercer desequilibrio que he sealado es el exceso de capacidad instalada. Un proceso expansivo de la actividad bancaria durante un largo perodo de tiempo, en un negocio basado en la proximidad al cliente, ha dado como resultado una densidad de oficinas y un tamao de los servicios centrales que no son funcionales. Hay que reducir la capacidad instalada para asegurar la rentabilidad en el medio plazo, ya que esta es la primera lnea de defensa de la banca. Para aadir dificultades a este proceso de absorcin de desequilibrios, el entorno sigue siendo turbulento. La economa real est atravesando un momento complicado y esto incide por dos vas en el sector bancario. Una, a travs del deterioro de la calidad crediticia de empresas y familias, que se traduce en ratios de morosidad ms elevados y, por lo tanto, en la necesidad de mayores provisiones para insolvencias. Y otra, porque la dbil actividad econmica presiona a la baja la cuenta de resultados. A lo largo de 2009, las entidades espaolas fueron capaces de incrementar su margen de intereses, gracias a que los bajos tipos de inters se trasladaron ms rpidamente a los costes de financiacin que a los productos del activo. No obstante, esta ampliacin del margen de intereses habr de perder fuelle, y ello supone un elemento de presin adicional sobre los beneficios. Medidas adoptadas por las autoridades y ritmo de implantacin de las mismas Recapitular las ideas centrales que les he querido transmitir hasta ahora. Primero, el sector bancario espaol ha evitado las recapitalizaciones masivas que han sido necesarias en otros pases. Segundo, el sistema est sano en su conjunto. Y tercero, las entidades de crdito, con claras diferencias entre ellas, afrontan la necesidad de absorber diversos desequilibrios en un contexto econmico y financiero complicado. Este diagnstico justifica las medidas adoptadas por las autoridades y su ritmo de avance. Las medidas adoptadas por las autoridades espaolas han sido bsicamente dos: primero, aliviar las dificultades de acceso a los mercados de financiacin; y segundo, poner sobre la mesa medios y recursos para reestructurar el sistema y, en particular, el sector de las cajas de ahorros. Facilitar el acceso a la financiacin fue una medida adoptada por el Gobierno espaol de forma coordinada con el resto de gobiernos de la Unin Europea. La retirada de los inversores del mercado mayorista, en un clima de prdida de confianza, no slo ha presionado a las entidades espaolas. Al contrario, en la medida en la que han accedido a estas fuentes de financiacin de una forma prudente, concentrando la vida de las emisiones en plazos medios y largos, esto les ha dado un mayor margen de maniobra que a entidades de otros pases. El mecanismo empleado en Espaa, como en el resto de Europa, es el otorgamiento de avales a las emisiones de nuevas obligaciones, incluyendo un coste que trata de reflejar el distinto perfil de riesgo de los emisores. De este modo, el riesgo que finalmente ha asumido el Estado ha sido limitado. La medida ha funcionado bien y distintas entidades, con diferente intensidad en funcin de sus necesidades, la han utilizado. La segunda medida, destinada a facilitar la reestructuracin del sector bancario espaol, se puso en marcha en el verano de 2009 y consiste en el establecimiento del Fondo de Reestructuracin Ordenada Bancaria (FROB). El FROB tiene capacidad para disponer de fondos por un importe de hasta 99 m.m. de euros. Para entender la importancia de los recursos destinados a esta finalidad hay que tener en cuenta que, cuando el FROB fue aprobado, muchas instituciones en Europa y en Estados Unidos precisaron de rescates muy cuantiosos. Por ello, se comprometi un importe que diera plena certidumbre al proceso. Dicho de otro modo, la cuanta deba disipar las dudas que pudieran existir respecto al compromiso de las autoridades espaolas para abordar la reestructuracin. Pero haber asignado un importe elevado no quiere decir que este refleje una estimacin del coste del proceso y, mucho menos, que ste deba utilizarse en su totalidad. Tampoco quiere decir que no se acte desde el mximo rigor en el uso de los fondos pblicos. De hecho, el FROB, por mandato explcito de la ley, ha de facilitar la reestructuracin del sector bancario minimizando los costes para los contribuyentes. Este segundo aspecto no es una cuestin menor y explica que en el diseo del FROB se d prioridad a las soluciones de carcter privado en sus dos modos de actuacin: - El primer modo de actuacin del FROB, el de intervencin y cambio de administradores, rest concebido como un mecanismo de resolucin rpida de bancos inviables. Su aplicacin se articula en dos niveles: primero, la entidad que atraviesa problemas de viabilidad busca una solucin privada que implique reforzar su solvencia y subsanar sus deficiencias. Si esta falla, se activa la actuacin del FROB a instancias del Banco de Espaa, sustituyendo a los administradores. - El segundo modo de actuar del FROB consiste en facilitar integraciones de carcter preventivo de entidades que son viables. Aspira a favorecer procesos de fusin y racionalizacin para reforzar los recursos propios y mejorar su eficiencia. Al solicitar la ayuda del FROB, los bancos y las cajas deben presentar un plan detallado de las condiciones de la fusin, que seale en qu consisten y cmo se esperan lograr las mejoras en la eficiencia y en la reduccin de la capacidad productiva. Si el plan es aprobado por el Banco de Espaa, el FROB refuerza los recursos propios mediante la suscripcin de participaciones preferentes, que las entidades habrn de devolver en cinco aos y cuyo coste es el 7,75%.. Como ya conocen, el plazo para este segundo modo de actuacin del FROB finaliza dentro de doce das. En diferentes ocasiones se ha sealado que la actuacin del FROB ha sido ms lenta de lo necesario. Y en diversas ocasiones he expuesto las razones que explican el ritmo al que se ha avanzado. Que el conjunto del sector est en una posicin sana y no hayan sido necesarias intervenciones masivas y fulminantes, al contrario de lo sucedido en otros pases, contribuye a esa percepcin de lentitud. Adems, a nadie se le oculta que en el proceso estn inmersas las cajas de ahorros, entidades que por su naturaleza presentan particularidades que han ralentizado las actuaciones. Finalmente, y no menos relevante, dar prioridad a la bsqueda de soluciones privadas, con el objetivo de minimizar el recurso a los fondos pblicos, ha incidido tambin en el ritmo de ejecucin de las operaciones. Hoy no voy a ahondar en estas razones, sino que les pondr al da de lo que se est haciendo y dibujar el camino previsible en el futuro. A da de hoy, ms del 80% de las cajas existentes en Espaa estn afrontando procesos de integracin, lo que representa aproximadamente el 90% de sus activos. Los procesos en los que estn inmersas son de distinta naturaleza. - Tres integraciones de las aprobadas por el Banco de Espaa han solicitado recursos del FROB: Otros dos procesos de integracin se estn finalizando sin solicitar ninguna ayuda pblica. - Tambin son diferentes en cuanto a su apelacin o no a los recursos del FROB los procesos de integracin que ya estn acordados por los Consejos de Administracin y que todava no han sido aprobados por el Banco de Espaa: algunos precisarn de ayudas del FROB y en otros casos no sern necesarias. - Finalmente, como saben, se han intervenido dos entidades y se han cambiado sus administradores: CCM y CajaSur. Tambin en este caso hay diferencias en los procesos. En el primer caso, el de CCM, que fue intervenida el 29 de marzo de 2009, no hubo ayudas pblicas, sino que se acudi al Fondo de Garanta de Depsitos que desde 1994 se ha nutrido con las aportaciones de las cajas de ahorro. La asamblea que culmina su reestructuracin se llevar a cabo dentro de once das. El segundo caso, el de CajaSur, es la primera intervencin del Banco de Espaa bajo el esquema del FROB. En estos momentos diversos bancos y cajas nacionales y extranjeros estn estudiando la documentacin de venta y se espera adjudicar la entidad en la primera mitad del mes de julio de 2010. Una primera lectura de lo anterior refuerza las ideas que ya he sealado. Cuando las entidades encuentran soluciones de integracin voluntaria a las que el Banco de Espaa da su conformidad, ese es el camino natural, que puede implicar o no la movilizacin de los recursos pblicos. Cuando una entidad no es capaz de solucionar sus problemas, y llega a un punto en el que deja de ser viable, entonces el Banco activa el otro modo operativo del FROB y la entidad de crdito es intervenida y posteriormente adjudicada en un procedimiento competitivo que busca minimizar los recursos pblicos utilizados, asignndola a otro banco o caja, espaol o extranjero, solvente y capaz de gestionar el proyecto de resolucin. Avanzando un paso ms en esta actualizacin del proceso, creo interesante trazarles algunas pinceladas sobre la fisonoma probable del sector de cajas en el futuro. En primer lugar, la reforma implicar una reduccin en el nmero de entidades y, en particular, de cajas de ahorros En segundo lugar, la capacidad del sector no solo se ver racionalizada por el descenso del nmero de entidades, sino tambin por las reducciones que resulten de los procesos de fusin en trminos de costes de explotacin y oficinas. Cada caso concreto presenta diferencias que se derivan del propio plan de integracin y negocio que van a desarrollar. Pero sirvan unos datos como referencia: en los casos en los que los procesos de integracin se realizan a travs del FROB, la disminucin media del nmero de oficinas est entre el 20-25%, en los servicios centrales en el 18-20%, y en el nmero de empleados entre el 15-18%. Y en tercer lugar, los procesos de integracin que se estn realizando a travs del FROB implican reconocer prdidas adicionales en los balances bancarios ya que en la combinacin de negocios se anticipan posibles ajustes por insolvencia e iliquidez en un entorno de tensin. Esto supone que la entidad resultante nace con un balance ms slido, con ms capital y con menos expectativas de prdidas futuras. Adicionalmente el Banco de Espaa est realizando ejercicios de estrs para todas las entidades del sistema bancario espaol que se esperan publicar en las prximas semanas. Concluyo con estas pinceladas sobre la futura fisonoma del sector de las cajas de ahorro aludiendo a los prximos cambios legislativos que se han acordado entre los dos mayores partidos polticos de la nacin. Es bien conocido que las cajas no tienen capacidad para emitir capital. Esto no slo reduce sus posibilidades de reforzar sus recursos propios, sino que, adems, limita la potencia del mercado para disciplinarlas. La nueva normativa que se ha de desarrollar, en la medida en la que posibilite la emisin de instrumentos de capital de la mxima calidad, con derechos de voto, supone un avance muy importante para solventar la deficiencia que he mencionado. A este respecto cabe aventurar que la introduccin de estos cambios normativos probablemente buscar la opcionalidad. Es decir, las propias cajas tendrn que decidir qu quieren ser. Para algunas, su opcin posiblemente discurrir por aproximarse al modelo bancario. Para otras, pasar por la emisin de instrumentos de capital con derecho de voto. Otro grupo probablemente decidir concentrarse en un mbito geogrfico ms ceido y continuar utilizando el modelo ms clsico. Pero en definitiva, como he indicado, las cajas deben poder disponer de instrumentos que faciliten su capitalizacin. Y las cajas, independientemente de sus opciones, deben estar plenamente sometidas a la disciplina del mercado. Muchas gracias.

Title: Intervention at the "IX Santander - Latin America Meeting"
text: Santander, 6 July 2010 The debt crisis and the restructuring of savings banks IX Santander d0 Latin America/UIMP Meeting Javier Ar92ztegui Deputy Governor of the Bank of Spain Introduction For me it is an immense pleasure to be this summer again in the capital where my parents brought me as a child to the gardens of Piqu92o. Santander is the province where I studied until I was 18 years old and it is an environment for which I confess weakness. Many thanks to the organizers d0 Banco Santander and Universidad Internacional Men8endez Pelayo d0 for having offered me the opportunity to be with you d0 American media professionals d0 who are so important for the analysis and knowledge of Spanish banking in the world. I propose to dedicate a few words to the sovereign debt crisis in Europe and to the restructuring of the banking system in Spain, especially of the savings banks, which, as you know, has been the segment of our financial institutions hardest hit by the turbulence. To begin with, I will give a short account of the crisis and the Spanish Government's response to it. I will focus later on the restructuring and capitalization of savings banks and on the legal changes that must mark a new legal "status" for these entities. I will comment on the stress exercise in which the Banco de Espa96a is embarking with its European banking supervisor colleagues and I will conclude with a few words about the time horizon in which we want to complete this task. The "sovereign debt" crisis and Spain's response Throughout the first half of 2010, a problem of credibility and financial stability of the euro as the second reference currency of international finance has been incubating and growing. When the "single currency" - the euro - was designed, which began in 1999, a common monetary policy and a "Stability and Growth Pact" were established, which aimed to provide the right fiscal conditions for the smooth future of the "single currency". The Pact ensured that the various countries in the area would maintain fiscal discipline, so that the euro would operate on an environment of stability in the aggregate spending of the economies. The euro generated a common financial market in the area and within it the member countries exchanged savings from one country to another in the Union to finance their real investments in a strong integrated financial market. This was the case of Spain which, over a ten-year shock wave, accumulated a net international investment position of 93% of GDP, whose financing was achieved smoothly in European capital markets. In our case, the private sector was the main demander of external funds, since the public sector was reducing its ratio of debt to GDP over these years until ending in 2007 with a level of 36%, thirty points below the average of our partners in the area. After the so-called "punto.com" crisis, fiscal discipline was weakened by incidents caused by France and Germany in 2004, which were not penalized. And in the last quarter of 2009, the new government revealed that Greece had breached the Stability and Growth Pact and had systematically altered its fiscal statistical information to the Brussels Commission. The European response was delayed, showing that it was necessary to reaffirm the conditions of stability and discipline of the area. The agreed solution has been a bailout of Greece strongly conditional on a rapid and determined rectification of imbalances. Europe offered the Greek government a db110 billion aid package designed on this basis. Subsequently, in the first decade of May 2010, it accelerated the fiscal adjustments of the member states of the area and prepared with the IMF a European Financial Stability Facility that accumulates 60,000 million euros of immediate availability of the budget of the European Commission, 440,000 million in a special vehicle, capable of issuing these amounts with an overguarantee of 120% of the Member States, and db250 billion available from the International Monetary Fund. In this environment, the Spanish Government pledged to accelerate fiscal adjustment and approved cuts in public spending and tax increases that will take the general government deficit from 11.2% of GDP, reached in 2009, to 6% in 2011 and 3% in 2013. This remarkable anticipation of fiscal adjustment is complemented by three structural reforms that are in different stages of implementation: - A change in the institutions and rules governing the labour market that Parliament has already approved at first reading, through an emergency Royal Decree Law, and which will be finalised in a new law before the end of next August. - A pension reform with an extension of the retirement age from 65 to 67 years that has already been sent for discussion to Parliament, within the "so-called" Toledo Pact. - And a restructuring of the banking system d0 especially of the savings banks d0 which has already been completed and to which I will refer below. I would like to emphasize to conclude this quick review of the main events of the "sovereign debt" crisis, that these actions are not rhetorical, but are in the process of execution: - Public employees have already received the June payroll with salary cuts that, on average, mean a drop in remuneration of 5%. - The new labor regulations have been in force since June 23 and companies can now apply it in their hiring and collective bargaining. Thirty-eight of the 45 savings banks have already agreed to join or merge. The State has already approved its recapitalisation and the Brussels Commission has authorised these integrations. With this set of structural reforms, Spain aims to accelerate its fiscal adjustment and stimulate its growth, providing greater flexibility and potential to its economy to face our responsibilities as members of the area, helping to restore the credibility of the single currency and the proper functioning of the euro markets. In this environment of reforms, let's delve a little deeper into the restructuring of savings banks. The restructuring and capitalization of savings banks The crisis found the Spanish banking system in a healthy position, with prudent and well-managed entities, and with a way of doing retail banking that has been reasonably resistant to financial turbulence. Within this fundamentally solid group, savings banks, which represent half of the Spanish banking system, suffered from peculiarities that have made them more vulnerable to the turbulence of the environment. I will highlight four of them: -First. Since the creation of the single currency, savings banks have financed a significant part of their growth by going to the euro markets through the issuance of securities subscribed mainly by "non-resident investors". As a result, its retail deposit base lost weight to international financing. The relative share of securities-instrumented liabilities has reached a level that is now high for the risk-aversion dominant in financial markets following the crisis of the past three years. This greater appeal to wholesale markets has been carried out with prudence, since most maturities are concentrated in medium and long maturities. Even so, savings banks need to modify the structure of their liabilities to base it more on internal deposits. But this change will take time in an environment in which the country, in net terms, continues to absorb foreign savings to finance its spending, at a sharply decreasing rate. -Second. Investment in the residential real estate development sector has been excessive and is a drag on the balance sheets of savings banks. This is because it is an industry that is closely linked to the economic cycle and that is currently experiencing a strong correction process. -Third. Excess installed capacity. A long and powerful expansion of activity, in a business based on customer proximity, has resulted in a density of bank branches and a size of central services that are not functional. Productive capacity must be reduced to ensure the profitability of the banking industry. - A fourth and final characteristic is that savings banks cannot generate their own resources of the highest quality (core capital) by methods other than the retention of profits. In other words, they cannot go to the financial markets to issue shares and raise capital. To solve these problems, in June of last year the Fund for Orderly Bank Restructuring (FROB) was established, which began its journey in September 2009 and has already done a very significant job. The FROB has the capacity to dispose of funds for an amount of up to 99 m.m. of euros. To understand the importance of the resources allocated to this purpose, we must bear in mind that, when the FROB was approved, many institutions in Europe and the United States required very large rescues. Therefore, an amount was committed that would give full certainty to the process. In other words, the amount should dispel any doubts that might exist as to the commitment of the Spanish authorities to address the restructuring. But having allocated a high amount does not mean that it reflects an estimate of the cost of the process, much less that it should be used in its entirety. Nor does it mean that we do not act from the utmost rigor in the use of public funds. Indeed, by explicit mandate of the law, it must facilitate the restructuring of the banking sector by minimising costs for taxpayers. The FROB has two modes of action: - The first mode, that of intervention and change of administrators, is conceived as a mechanism for the rapid resolution of failing banks. In the last year, two entities have been intervened: Caja Castilla-La Mancha has been absorbed by Banco Liberta and has disappeared as a credit institution and CajaSur is for sale. Eight credit institutions have shown interest in making an offer for it and next week it will be awarded to the national or foreign institution that, being solvent, offers a better price for its acquisition. - The second way of acting of the FROB is to facilitate preventive integrations of entities that are viable and capitalize them. It aims to promote merger and rationalisation processes in order to strengthen own resources and improve efficiency. Banks and savings banks must submit a detailed plan of the conditions of the merger, indicating what they are and how improvements in efficiency and reduction of installed capacity are expected to be achieved. If the plan is approved by the Bank of Spain, the FROB reinforces the resulting institution's own resources by subscribing to preferred shares, which the entities will have to repay in five years and whose cost is 7.75%. The restructuring of the savings banks is being articulated through twelve integration processes in which 38 of the 45 Spanish savings banks participate, including CajaSur in this process. Only 6 savings banks, representing 8% of the banks' total assets as of December 31, 2009, have remained outside these merger movements. Of the 12 processes indicated, 7 of them have been raised with a request for aid to the FROB, whose total amount amounts to 10,200 million, and another 5 are addressed without public aid. The FROB, in addition, will allocate the necessary support in the restructuring process of CajaSur, which will be specified next week within the framework of the ongoing competitive procedure for the award to a bidder of recognized solvency. In addition, the Deposit Guarantee Fund in Savings Banks has allocated almost 4,000 million to the "resolution" of Caja Castilla la Mancha. Consequently, the amount of resources of the FROB and the Deposit Guarantee Funds that have been approved for this recapitalization and restructuring process will be between 15 and 16 billion euros. That is, approximately 1.5 points of Spanish GDP. The Savings Banks Act As agreed by the two main Spanish political parties, this reform will be completed with a change in the Law that regulates the boxes and that is expected to be outlined before the end of this month of July 2010. It is well known that savings banks do not have the capacity to issue capital. This not only reduces their ability to strengthen their own resources, but also limits the market's power to discipline them. The new regulations to be approved by the Spanish Parliament, insofar as they make it possible to issue capital instruments of the highest quality with voting rights, will be a very important step forward in filling the gap I have mentioned. Likewise, corporate governance and the degree of professionalization of its management will have to be strengthened. In short, as I have pointed out, savings banks must be able to have instruments that facilitate their capitalization and subject them to market discipline. The Bank of Spain is contributing to this reform within the function that the Law of Autonomy grants it to "advise" the Government. El stress test Finally, I would like to point out that Spain has led Europe in carrying out and publishing 'stress tests' to assess the quality of the balance sheets and solvency of credit institutions in a situation in which the market value of the portfolios of public securities of the countries most affected by the 'sovereign debt' crisis has fallen. In spring 2009, the Committee of European Banking Supervisors conducted "stress tests" on the 2008 closing balance sheets of the 26 largest European banks, but decided not to publish the individual results of these stress tests. In June 2010, these tests were repeated for large banks and it was decided to extend them to other credit institutions, medium and small, taking special care to measure the "sovereign risk" implicit in the balance sheets. The individual results of these "stress tests", which will include more smaller banks, will be made public in the second half of this month of July. In Spain, in addition to the two large institutions d0 Santander and BBVA d0 that already participated in last year's stress tests, the other listed banks and all the savings banks will be added, with almost total coverage of banking activity in our country. Conclusion I have tried to show you the work of adapting the banking system that has been carried out in Spain in the first half of 2010 and how it fits into the tax cut, the labor reform and the planned adjustment of pensions. With a fundamentally healthy banking system, especially in the case of the two large international banks, the change has focused on merging savings banks and reducing their size, capitalizing them and requiring them to improve their efficiency and productivity. Throughout this month of July, it is expected to culminate the reform with a proposal to modify the Law of savings banks, which will allow them to obtain their own resources of the highest quality and put on the table more hopeful future projects. Likewise, the publication of the results of the "stress tests" that, in our country, will be especially extensive due to the coverage of the year and the communication effort that the Bank of Spain intends to make, will show the solvency of the Spanish banking system. The authorities are carrying out reform and transparency work to put our banks in optimal conditions to return to the wholesale markets of the euro to renew external financing and obtain new capital resources. With this effort they hope to contribute to the restoration of the securities issuance markets in the single currency which, in May and June 2010, have significantly reduced their activity due to a problem of uncertainty and widespread distrust among investors. May we succeed. I hope I haven't bored you too much. Thank you all very much for your attention.
text_original: Santander, 6 de julio de 2010 La crisis de la deuda y la reestructuracin de las cajas de ahorro IX Encuentro Santander  Amrica Latina/UIMP Javier Arztegui Subgobernador del Banco de Espaa Introduccin Para m es un inmenso placer estar este verano otra vez en la capital donde mis padres me traan de pequeo a los jardines de Piquo. Santander es la provincia donde yo estudi hasta los 18 aos y es un entorno por el que confieso debilidad. Muchas gracias a los organizadores Banco Santander y Universidad Internacional Menndez Pelayo- por haberme ofrecido la oportunidad de estar con ustedes profesionales americanos de los medios de comunicacin- que son tan importantes para el anlisis y el conocimiento de la banca espaola en el mundo. Me propongo dedicar unas palabras a la crisis de la deuda soberana en Europa y a la reestructuracin del sistema bancario en Espaa, especialmente de las cajas de ahorro que, como ustedes conocen, ha sido el segmento de nuestras instituciones financieras ms castigado por las turbulencias. Realizar para empezar un relato corto de la crisis y de la respuesta a la misma del Gobierno espaol. Me centrar posteriormente en la reestructuracin y capitalizacin de las cajas de ahorro y en los cambios legales que han de marcar un nuevo status jurdico para estas entidades. Comentar el ejercicio de stress en el que el Banco de Espaa est embarcado con sus colegas supervisores bancarios europeos y concluir con unas palabras sobre el horizonte temporal en el que queremos culminar esta tarea. La crisis de la deuda soberana y la respuesta espaola A lo largo del primer semestre de este ao 2010, se ha ido incubando y agrandando un problema de credibilidad y estabilidad financiera del euro como segunda moneda de referencia de las finanzas internacionales. Cuando se dise la moneda nica -el euro-, que inici su andadura en 1999, se estableci una poltica monetaria comn y un Pacto para la estabilidad y el crecimiento que aspiraba a proporcionar las condiciones fiscales idneas para el devenir sin sobresaltos de la moneda nica. El Pacto aseguraba que los distintos pases del rea mantendran la disciplina fiscal, de modo que el euro discurriera sobre un entorno de estabilidad en el gasto agregado de las economas. El euro gener un mercado financiero comn en el rea y en su interior los pases miembros intercambiaron ahorro de unos pases a otros de la Unin para financiar sus inversiones reales en un mercado financiero integrado de gran pujanza. Este fue el caso de Espaa que, a lo largo de una onda expansiva de diez aos, acumul una posicin de inversin internacional neta del 93% del PIB, cuya financiacin logr con fluidez en los mercados de capitales europeos. En nuestro caso, el sector privado fue el principal demandante de fondos exteriores, ya que el sector pblico fue reduciendo a lo largo de estos aos su proporcin de deuda en relacin al PIB hasta terminar en 2007 con un nivel del 36%, treinta puntos por debajo de la media de nuestros socios del rea. Tras la crisis denominada de las punto.com, la disciplina fiscal se debilit con incidentes ocasionados por Francia y Alemania en el ao 2004, que no fueron penalizados. Y en el ltimo trimestre de 2009, el nuevo Gobierno revel que Grecia haba incumplido el Pacto de Estabilidad y Crecimiento y haba alterado sistemticamente sus informaciones estadsticas fiscales a la Comisin de Bruselas. La respuesta europea se fue demorando, poniendo en evidencia que era necesario reafirmar las condiciones de estabilidad y disciplina del rea. La solucin acordada ha sido un rescate de Grecia fuertemente condicionado a una rpida y decidida rectificacin de los desequilibrios. Europa ofreci al Gobierno griego un paquete de ayuda de 110.000 m de euros diseado sobre esta base. Posteriormente, en la primera decena de mayo de 2010, aceler los ajustes fiscales de los estados miembros del rea y prepar con el FMI un Fondo Europeo de Estabilidad Financiera que acumula 60.000 millones de euros de disponibilidad inmediata del presupuesto de la Comisin Europea, 440.000 millones en un vehculo especial, capaz de emitir esos importes con una sobregaranta del 120% de los Estados miembros, y 250.000 millones de euros disponibles del Fondo Monetario Internacional. En este entorno, el Gobierno espaol se comprometi a acelerar el ajuste fiscal y aprob recortes en los gastos pblicos y subidas de impuestos que llevarn el dficit de las Administraciones Pblicas desde el 11,2% del PIB, alcanzado en el ao 2009, hasta el 6% en 2011 y el 3% en 2013. Esta notable anticipacin del ajuste fiscal se complementa con tres reformas estructurales que estn en distinta fase de instrumentacin: - Un cambio en las instituciones y en las normas que regulan el mercado de trabajo que ya ha aprobado el Parlamento en una primera lectura, mediante un Real Decreto Ley de urgencia, y que terminar de perfilar en una nueva ley antes de que termine el prximo mes de agosto. - Una reforma de las pensiones con extensin de la edad de jubilacin desde los 65 a los 67 aos que ya se ha enviado para su discusin al Parlamento, dentro del denominado Pacto de Toledo. - Y una reestructuracin del sistema bancario especialmente de las cajas de ahorro- que ya est culminada y a la que me referir a continuacin. Quisiera resaltar para terminar este rpido repaso de los principales eventos de la crisis de la deuda soberana, que estas actuaciones no son retricas, sino que estn en proceso de ejecucin: - Los empleados pblicos ya han cobrado la nmina de junio con recortes salariales que, en promedio, suponen una cada en las retribuciones del 5%. - La nueva normativa laboral est vigente desde el pasado da 23 de junio y las empresas ya pueden aplicarla en su contratacin y en la negociacin colectiva. - Treinta y ocho de las 45 cajas de ahorro ya han acordado integrarse o fusionarse. El Estado ya ha aprobado su recapitalizacin y la Comisin de Bruselas ha autorizado dichas integraciones. Con este conjunto de reformas estructurales Espaa aspira a acelerar su ajuste fiscal y a estimular su crecimiento, dotando de mayor flexibilidad y potencialidad a su economa para afrontar nuestras responsabilidades como miembros del rea, ayudando a restaurar la credibilidad de la moneda nica y el buen funcionamiento de los mercados del euro. En este entorno de reformas, ahondemos un poco ms en la reestructuracin de las cajas de ahorros. La reestructuracin y capitalizacin de las cajas de ahorro La crisis encontr al sistema bancario espaol en una posicin sana, con unas entidades prudentes y bien gestionadas, y con una forma de hacer banca al por menor que se ha mostrado razonablemente resistente a las turbulencias financieras. Dentro de este conjunto fundamentalmente slido, las cajas de ahorro, que representan la mitad del sistema bancario espaol, adolecan de unas peculiaridades que les han hecho ms vulnerables a las turbulencias del entorno. Resaltar cuatro de ellas: - Primera. Desde la creacin de la moneda nica, las cajas de ahorro financiaron una parte relevante de su crecimiento acudiendo a los mercados del euro a travs de la emisin de valores suscritos principalmente por inversores no residentes. En consecuencia, su base de depsitos minoristas perdi peso frente a la financiacin internacional. La proporcin relativa de los pasivos instrumentados mediante valores alcanz un nivel que, en la actualidad, resulta elevado para la aversin al riesgo dominante en los mercados financieros tras la crisis de los tres ltimos aos. Esta mayor apelacin a los mercados mayoristas se ha realizado con prudencia, al estar la mayora de los vencimientos concentrados en los plazos medios y largos. Aun as, las cajas de ahorro precisan modificar la estructura de su pasivo para basarla ms en depsitos interiores. Pero este cambio llevar su tiempo en un entorno en el que el pas, en trminos netos, sigue absorbiendo ahorro exterior para financiar su gasto, a un ritmo fuertemente decreciente. - Segunda. La inversin en el sector de promocin inmobiliaria residencial ha sido excesiva y supone un lastre en los balances de las cajas. Ello es as porque es una industria que est muy vinculada al ciclo econmico y que experimenta un fuerte proceso de correccin en la actualidad. - Tercera. El exceso de capacidad instalada. Una larga y potente expansin de la actividad, en un negocio basado en la proximidad al cliente, ha dado como resultado una densidad de sucursales bancarias y un tamao de los servicios centrales que no son funcionales. Hay que reducir la capacidad productiva para asegurar la rentabilidad de la industria bancaria. - Una cuarta y ltima caracterstica es que las cajas de ahorro no pueden generar recursos propios de la mxima calidad (core capital) por mtodos diferentes de la retencin de beneficios. Dicho en otras palabras, no pueden acudir a los mercados financieros para emitir acciones y obtener capital. Para resolver estos problemas, en junio del pasado ejercicio se estableci el Fondo de Reestructuracin Ordenada Bancaria (FROB) que inici su andadura en septiembre de 2009 y que ya ha realizado un trabajo muy significativo. El FROB tiene capacidad para disponer de fondos por un importe de hasta 99 m.m. de euros. Para entender la importancia de los recursos destinados a esta finalidad, hay que tener en cuenta que, cuando el FROB fue aprobado, muchas instituciones en Europa y en Estados Unidos precisaron de rescates muy cuantiosos. Por ello, se comprometi un importe que diera plena certidumbre al proceso. Dicho de otro modo, la cuanta deba disipar las dudas que pudieran existir respecto al compromiso de las autoridades espaolas para abordar la reestructuracin. Pero haber asignado un importe elevado no quiere decir que ste refleje una estimacin del coste del proceso y, mucho menos, que ste deba utilizarse en su totalidad. Tampoco quiere decir que no se acte desde el mximo rigor en el uso de los fondos pblicos. De hecho, por mandato explcito de la ley, ha de facilitar la reestructuracin del sector bancario minimizando los costes para los contribuyentes. El FROB tiene dos modos de actuacin: - El primer modo, el de intervencin y cambio de administradores, est concebido como un mecanismo de resolucin rpida de bancos inviables. En el ltimo ao, se han intervenido dos entidades: Caja Castilla-La Mancha ha sido absorbida por Banco Liberta y ha desaparecido como entidad de crdito y CajaSur est en venta. Ocho entidades de crdito han mostrado inters en hacer una oferta por la misma y la prxima semana ser adjudicada a la institucin nacional o extranjera que, siendo solvente, ofrezca un mejor precio por su adquisicin. - El segundo modo de actuar del FROB consiste en facilitar integraciones de carcter preventivo de entidades que son viables y capitalizarlas. Aspira a favorecer procesos de fusin y racionalizacin para reforzar los recursos propios y mejorar la eficiencia. Los bancos y las cajas deben presentar un plan detallado de las condiciones de la fusin, que seale en qu consisten y cmo se espera lograr las mejoras en la eficiencia y en la reduccin de la capacidad instalada. Si el plan es aprobado por el Banco de Espaa, el FROB refuerza los recursos propios de la institucin resultante mediante la suscripcin de participaciones preferentes, que las entidades habrn de devolver en cinco aos y cuyo coste es el 7,75%. La reestructuracin de las cajas de ahorros se est articulando a travs de doce procesos de integracin en los que participan 38 de las 45 cajas espaolas, incluyendo en este proceso a CajaSur. nicamente 6 cajas de ahorros, que representan el 8% de los activos totales de las cajas a 31 de diciembre de 2009, se han mantenido al margen de estos movimientos de fusin. De los12 procesos sealados, 7 de ellos se han planteado con peticin de ayudas al FROB, cuyo importe total asciende a 10.200 millones, y otros 5 se abordan sin ayudas pblicas. El FROB, adems, destinar los apoyos precisos en el proceso de reestructuracin de CajaSur, que se concretarn la prxima semana en el marco del procedimiento competitivo en curso para la adjudicacin a un oferente de reconocida solvencia. Adems el Fondo de Garanta de Depsitos en las Cajas de Ahorro ha destinado casi 4.000 millones a la resolucin de Caja Castilla la Mancha. En consecuencia, la cantidad de recursos del FROB y de los Fondos de Garanta de Depsitos que se han aprobado para este proceso de recapitalizacin y reestructuracin estar entre 15 y 16 mil millones de euros. Es decir, aproximadamente 1,5 puntos del PIB espaol. La Ley de Cajas de Ahorros Segn han acordado los dos principales partidos polticos espaoles, esta reforma se completar con un cambio en la Ley que regula las cajas y que se espera que est perfilado antes de que termine este mes de julio de 2010. Es bien conocido que las cajas de ahorro no tienen capacidad para emitir capital. Esto no slo reduce su capacidad de reforzar sus recursos propios, sino que, adems, limita la potencia del mercado para disciplinarlas. La nueva normativa que ha de aprobar el Parlamento espaol, en la medida en la que posibilite la emisin de instrumentos de capital de la mxima calidad con derecho de voto, supondr un avance muy importante para solventar la carencia que he mencionado. Asimismo, habr que reforzar el gobierno corporativo y el grado de profesionalizacin de su gestin. En definitiva, como he sealado, las cajas han de poder disponer de instrumentos que faciliten su capitalizacin y las sometan a la disciplina del mercado. El Banco de Espaa est contribuyendo a esta reforma dentro de la funcin que la Ley de Autonoma le otorga de asesorar al Gobierno. El stress test Quisiera destacar, por ltimo, que Espaa ha liderado dentro de Europa la realizacin y publicacin de pruebas de esfuerzo que sirvan para evaluar la calidad de los balances y la solvencia de las entidades de crdito en una coyuntura en la que ha descendido el valor de mercado de las carteras de ttulos pblicos de los pases ms afectados por la crisis de la deuda soberana. En la primavera de 2009, el Comit Europeo de Supervisores Bancarios realiz pruebas de esfuerzo con los balances de cierre del ao 2008 de los 26 mayores bancos europeos, pero decidi no publicar los resultados individuales de estos stress test. En el pasado mes de junio de 2010 se han repetido estas pruebas para los grandes bancos y se ha decidido extenderlas a otras entidades de crdito, medianas y pequeas, poniendo especial cuidado en medir el riesgo soberano implcito en los balances. Los resultados individuales de estos stress test, que incluirn a ms entidades de crdito de menor tamao, se harn pblicos en la segunda mitad de este mes de julio. En Espaa, adems de las dos grandes instituciones Santander y BBVA- que ya participaron en las pruebas de esfuerzo del ao pasado, se aadirn los dems bancos cotizados y todas las cajas de ahorro, con una cobertura casi total de la actividad bancaria en nuestro pas. Conclusin He tratado de mostrarles el trabajo de adecuacin del sistema bancario que se ha llevado a cabo en Espaa en esta primera mitad del ejercicio 2010 y cmo se encuadra en el recorte fiscal, en la reforma laboral y en el ajuste previsto de las pensiones. Con un sistema bancario fundamentalmente sano, especialmente en el caso de los dos grandes bancos internacionales, el cambio se ha centrado en fusionar las cajas de ahorro y reducir su tamao, capitalizndolas y exigindoles mejorar su eficiencia y productividad. A lo largo de este mes de julio, se espera culminar la reforma con una propuesta de modificacin de la Ley de cajas, que les permitir obtener recursos propios de la mxima calidad y poner sobre la mesa proyectos de futuro ms esperanzadores. Asimismo, la publicacin de los resultados de los stress tests que, en nuestro pas, sern especialmente amplios por la cobertura del ejercicio y por el esfuerzo de comunicacin que se propone realizar el Banco de Espaa, mostrarn la solvencia del sistema bancario espaol. Las autoridades estn llevando a cabo un trabajo de reformas y transparencia que site a nuestras entidades de crdito en unas condiciones ptimas para volver a acudir a los mercados mayoristas del euro a renovar la financiacin ajena y obtener nuevos recursos de capital. Con este esfuerzo esperan contribuir a la restauracin de los mercados de emisiones de valores en la moneda nica que, en los meses de mayo y junio de 2010, han reducido notablemente su actividad por un problema de incertidumbre y desconfianza generalizada entre los inversores. Ojal tengamos xito. Espero no haberles aburrido demasiado. Muchas gracias a todos por su atencin.

Title: Speech at the launch of the PwC-IE Center for the Financial Sector, organized by PricewaterhouseCoopers and IE Business School. The Spanish banking system
text: Madrid, 9 September 2010 The Spanish banking system Presentation by the PwC-IE Center for the Financial Sector/PricewaterhouseCoopers and IE Business School Miguel Fernandez Ordez Governor of the Bank of Spain 1. INTRODUCTION First of all, I would like to thank Luis de Guindos for his kind invitation to the presentation of this Financial Sector Centre at the Instituto de Empresa, which I am sure will contribute to bringing new ideas at such a crucial time for the Spanish financial system. Today I am going to share with you some reflections on the situation of the Spanish banking system at the beginning of the crisis, its behavior during it and the main challenges it will have to face in the future cousin. Given the characteristics of this highly regulated sector, I will take this opportunity to comment on the actions and reactions of governments, regulators and supervisors to manage the crisis, as well as to prevent it from being repeated in the future. 2. SITUATION OF THE SPANISH BANKING SYSTEM AT THE BEGINNING OF THE CRISIS In the middle of 1994, the serious employment crisis of the early 90s was left behind and the Spanish economy began to create some 400,000 jobs a year. This spectacular pace was maintained practically until the beginning of the current international crisis, although some signs of exhaustion of this long expansionary period had already begun to appear before, in mid-2006, such as the reduction in credit growth rates and house prices. What in its first phase was a soft adjustment, later became an abrupt contraction, as a result of the effects of the biggest international financial crisis since the Great Depression. In some countries (such as the United States, Ireland or the United Kingdom), the bursting of the housing bubble put their main banks in danger and forced governments to help them with huge amounts of public resources. But also in other countries that did not have a real estate boom (such as Germany, Holland or Belgium), many entities had to be rescued, because they had accumulated in their balance sheets massive amounts of the so-called Costa Rican assets. Why does the Spanish banking system withstand the first two ace of crises without needing significant injections of capital to which this year has been supplied as part of the process of restructuring savings banks? It has been explained many times: factors such as good regulation, intense supervision and special dedication to a well-managed retail business, generated supports such as the provision system or the absence of investment in complex operations and financing instruments, which served so that our banks did not collapse, as many of the most developed countries do. But it is clear that the twelve years of vigorous expansion generated many imbalances in the economy and in the banking sector. The rapid increase in credit, at rates that were unsustainable in the long term, was accompanied by a significant increase in installed capacity, a growing concentration of risks in the real estate sector and greater recourse to external financing. These imbalances affected the whole system, but more significantly the savings banks, which generally granted more credit than banks, were more exposed to the real estate sector and had a lower level of diversification, as well as clearly improvable governance in some cases. 3. THE SPANISH BANKING SYSTEM DURING THE CRISIS In the first phase of the crisis, various measures were taken to avoid the consequences of the collapse of wholesale financing. Both those adopted at the national level, among which the approval of the Financial Assets Acquisition Fund and the issues guaranteed by the State stand out, and those adopted by the ECB d0 mainly guaranteeing unlimited financing d0 were measures that played an important role in preventing the collapse of the system. But the most important challenge during the crisis has been to undertake the process of restructuring savings banks. To carry it out, the FROB was created, which facilitates restructuring in two ways: on the one hand, it will allow to help those solvent entities that accept to undertake integration processes and reduce their capacity; on the other hand, the FROB also served to facilitate the rapid intervention of entities that were not viable. The Bank of Spain had a great tradition of banking crisis management, but the instruments available were not adapted to the changes brought about by the entry into the euro. On the other hand, the existing instruments were not designed for the intervention and restructuring of the savings banks, since until now this sector had solved its problems without the need for public aid. In the twelve months that followed the approval of the FROB Law, this restructuring process has been developed, which has allowed to reduce the nero of entities, increase their size and establish plans to reduce offices, personnel and general structures, to adapt them to a new situation in which presumably the growth of the business will be much lower than in the past. The public aid committed, mainly through preferential shares, is important - in the order of 11,000 million euros - but it is still small compared to that provided by the States of other developed countries. At the end of the restructuring process, it was important to show the markets where the savings banks were, since the news of interventions or the disappearance of certain entities had fed a much more negative view of the sector than its real situation. Therefore, this year, in the presentation of the annual report, I announced that the Bank of Spain was going to carry out stress tests of Spanish institutions and that it would make its results public. Immediately, this idea was welcomed by our European partners and it was decided to carry out an exercise at the level of the whole of the European Union. From the Bank of Spain we strongly support the elaboration of this exercise at European level, because the existence of a common methodology would make it more credible and internationally comparable. The uncertainty in the markets since the spring of this year made it difficult for Spanish institutions - and not only the savings banks - to obtain financing, which had forced them to increase their use of financing from the European Central Bank, a situation which, although normal, should not become a permanent financing channel. For all these reasons, it was decided to exploit the possibilities of these stress tests to the maximum, by including all savings banks and all listed banks, and offering more detailed information for Spanish institutions than that agreed at European level. The results of the tests are well known and show the solidity of the Spanish banking system: all banks in our country were above the target set of Tier 1 and, after the FROB aid, only four savings banks were below that threshold. But most importantly, there is now transparent information on banks' exposure to major asset classes, and with this, analysts can assess their resilience to different hypothetical shocks. The stress tests have allowed the stress in the public debt markets to be lowered, and have helped to reopen some financing channels for our banks. 4. THE FUTURE OF THE SPANISH BANKING SYSTEM 4.1 The macroeconomic and financial environment Following the restructuring process of the savings banks, the Spanish banking system as a whole is well positioned to overcome the current crisis and to contribute actively, as it has done in the past, to the growth of our economy. But the future of the banking system will not depend exclusively on the implementation of these restructuring processes. The episodes of market instability in the months were mainly due to doubts about the ability of national governments to deal with their structural and public deficit problems, as well as to the difficulties that the European Union was experiencing in managing the Greek crisis and in devising a financing mechanism that could be used in other possible cases. Added to all this was the uncertainty about the European Central Bank's ability to react to this new wave of financing difficulties for European banks. Fortunately, throughout the scams, these incnitas have been resolved. The ECB has adopted measures that have contributed to the better functioning of its markets and has provided institutions with unlimited financing. The changes in the Uni have also gone in the right direction. And some countries, including Spain, have adopted serious measures to reduce the deficit and have planned to or even approved some structural reforms. All this has led to an improvement in the functioning of wholesale markets, although certain cautions must be maintained, because it is clear that potential new episodes of financial instability at the international level that hinder the normalization of the markets cannot yet be completely ruled out, so in any case, banks and savings banks should continue thinking about strengthening their financing structure. The recent crisis has highlighted the intense interaction between banks, financial markets and the real economy. Problems in the banking system are quickly transmitted to the functioning of financial markets and the economy as a whole, and, conversely, a non-growing economy ends up seriously affecting the banking system. Therefore, in addition to the essential measures that have been adopted in the financial field, it is necessary to address reforms in other areas, which contribute to improving confidence, macroeconomic and financial stability, and increasing productivity. As the events of the months have shown, healthy and sustainable public accounts are an essential ingredient to have the confidence of the markets and other economic agents. In this area, the Government has approved an ambitious set of measures that advances a significant part of the effort to reduce the deficit to 2010 and 2011, to this scam for which the deficit target has been set at 6% of GDP. This fiscal consolidation effort, exceeding 5 pp of GDP in only two years, is exceptional, but it was inexcusable if we wanted to return to a path of stability in public finances and dispel doubts about their sustainability. And if these credibility gains are to be long-lasting, it is essential that the announced objectives are strictly met, correcting any possible deviations from them if necessary. In addition, given the high degree of decentralization of our country, it is crucial that the Autonomous Communities and municipalities are seriously involved in achieving these goals. In the same direction, but with a focus more on the medium and long term, a reform of the pension system aimed at improving the fairness of the system and guaranteeing its viability must also be addressed as soon as possible within the framework of the Toledo Pact. These measures to improve our public accounts are essential. But it is also necessary to adopt structural reforms that encourage job creation, facilitate the transfer of resources to the most productive activities and increase the productivity and efficiency of our economy. Labour market reform figures prominently among them. Experience shows that the Spanish labour market model has been a hindrance to competitiveness and hinders the creation of stable employment. With the aim of correcting these inefficiencies, last June the Government approved and sent Parliament a set of measures aimed mainly at reducing duality in contracting and strengthening the instruments of internal flexibility of companies. The proposed reform, although it does not change all the elements of the previous system, contains positive developments, which make it possible for those companies that find themselves in difficulty to adopt, in agreement with their workers, conditions better adapted to their situation, which favour the preservation of jobs. Now it is essential that these possibilities of improving our productive apparatus that the labor reform opens up are used to the maximum. There are many other areas of structural reform that are essential for growth. Education is the most important. It is a fact that in recent decades the level of education of citizens in our country has improved considerably, but there has been a slowdown in the advancement of the educational level of the workforce, which must be addressed through policies that contribute to improving the quantity and quality of education at all levels and, in particular, to reduce the high rates of early leaving in secondary education. This increase in investment in human capital is essential to take advantage of the increases in investment in technological capital and continue to reduce the gap that our economy still drags in this area. Of course, it is essential to insist on the liberalisation of all markets for goods and services, with the aim of increasing competition in these sectors. In this direction it is necessary to complete decisively the process of liberalization of the services sector and it would be desirable to advance in the effective liberalization of the network industries, which provide essential inputs to the rest of the productive sectors. In short, in the future cousin, the key factor for our banking system is the recovery of growth. To achieve this, in addition to the specific measures that have been adopted in the financial field, a set of fiscal, labour and structural measures has been identified, which must be decisively developed by all public administrations. And, as I said, the most important thing at the moment is that the possibilities opened up by this new framework are quickly exploited by workers and employers. 4.2 The main challenges for the banking sector The recovery of confidence in the growth of the Spanish economy, as well as in its ability to reduce the deficit demand, will be essential to normalize the access of Spanish institutions to wholesale and interbank markets and thus facilitate the most pressing task for institutions: adapting their financing structure to the new times. Stress tests can also help, and the restructuring processes under way will certainly increase the soundness of the Spanish financial system. However, in the future, our banking system will also have to face other challenges of the first magnitude, related, both to the nature of the banking business in the new economic context that opens up for cousins, and to the appearance of novelties in the field of regulation and supervision that will determine its framework of action. First, the evolution of asset quality will remain a priority. The scams indicate that the trend of increasing non-performing assets has stopped (they had been increasing since 2007). This could indicate that most of the adjustment has already been made, but there is still a long way to go in the area of asset management. In this area, the Bank of Spain has recently decided to increase its requirements, which will mean, ceteris paribus, an increase of 2% in the level of provisions during 2010. Secondly, exposure to the real estate development sector is a problem that will not be completely solved in the short term, although recent statistics show that the decline in house prices is starting to slow down. The Bank of Spain is urging banks to maintain caution in their risk management policies, taking into account that the adjustment in this sector may continue for some time. - The third aspect is the reduction of capacity of the sector as a whole, while increasing the size of the entities. Spain has been the European country with the highest density of bank branches, which, together with the oversizing of central services, means costs in terms of efficiency. In this sense, one of the objectives of the FROB has been to adjust the business structure to the foreseeable future income. Some steps have been taken in the right direction, as shown by the reduction in the number of branches (-3.5% in 2009). In the case of integration operations approved within the scope of the FROB, the plans include a decrease of 10% to 30% in the number of branches and from 11% to 27% in the staff. - The fourth element to take into account for the future is the ability of banks to increase their capital base and adjust their leverage ratios. This point It will become particularly important in the future cousin because of the introduction of stricter international provisions, which I will comment on later. In the Espal case, the current regulatory framework has so far limited the ability of savings banks to issue own resources of the highest quality. However, Parliament has recently approved a legal reform that will allow these entities to obtain quality capital resources. The reform is proposed as a men and will have the additional advantage of increasing market discipline for savings banks, since surely among the factors that explain the worse performance in general of the savings banks compared to the banks, could be that of having less market discipline. -By this reason, I do not want to fail to mention the challenge that the introduction of new liquidity requirements in the Basel framework will pose for banks (and also for Banco de Espa as supervisor) in the form of two new ratios. These developments have sometimes been the subject of criticism. However, I think it is worth remembering that the current crisis has shown how important it is not for institutions to have sufficient liquid assets to deal with a situation of stress in the short term, but also for them to have a financing structure appropriate to their business. And these are the objectives of these coefficients. Whatever the final details of this regulation, it is clear that this new regulation will require a significant improvement in the systems of information, collection and analysis of liquidity data. Many entities have already started this process that, since the summer of last year, the Bank of Spain has encouraged for being a fundamental piece for a good management of liquidity risk by the entities and an adequate follow-up by the supervisor. 4.3 Reform of regulation and supervision at an international level In parallel to the internal changes in our banking system, substantial changes are taking place in international regulation, which will undoubtedly also determine the future of our entities. Before commenting on some of these changes, let me highlight the way in which these reforms are being agreed upon globally. The meetings of the G20, the creation of the Financial Stability Board (FSB), of which Spain becomes a member and whose origin was the Financial Stability Forum, composed mainly of G10 countries, the revitalization of the group of regulators and heads of supervision of the Basel Committee (GHOS), changes in the governance structure of the BIS and the governance of the IMF are all milestones in what will one day be seen as a revolution in global economic governance. G20 leaders agreed at their Pittsburgh Summit that capital and liquidity regulatory reform (known as Basel III) should be completed by the end of 2010 and enter into force by the end of 2012. In this sense, it is essential to properly calibrate the different measures to achieve the desired objectives. On the other hand, it is aware that the new standards could have a high cost for institutions, for the financial system and the economy in general, if they were applied with all their rigor in a complicated situation such as the current one. For this reason, they also made clear the need for a sufficiently long transitional period, and the necessary grandfathering rules, so that the reform is implemented progressively as financial conditions improve and the economic recovery is assured. To assist in the difficult decisions on calibration and implementation, an impact study has been carried out, and two reports have been published analysing the macroeconomic effects of the proposals in both the transitional and long-term periods. The final decision on when the reform should be fully implemented and on the details of the implementation process has not yet been taken, although progress will be made in this regard shortly. At European level, work is also underway to ensure that the reform of solvency regulations comes into force at the same time as in the rest of the G20 countries. The European Commission is already preparing its legislative initiative, known as "CRD 4" (Capital Requirement Directive). The reform will have a significant impact on the European financial system, and obviously also on the ESPAL. However, it is important to highlight that the changes that are being proposed in the areas of regulation and supervision are in line, in general terms, with practices that were already common in our country, so it seems reasonable to think that Spanish banks are affected to a lesser extent than those of other countries. One example is countercyclical measures. The international community is developing regulatory tools to act against the inherent cyclical fluctuations of the banking system. As you know, in Spain, in the time of Governor Luis e7ngel Rojo, a system of provisions was designed based on an explicit and transparent rule, which requires entities to accumulate a mattress in good times, in which risks typically accumulate, which could be released when these risks materialize. This system has been very useful in the current crisis, since banks had a significant margin, which they have been able to use to absorb losses. If this previous buffer had not existed, there would undoubtedly have been significantly more plastic resources for the recapitalisation of institutions. Other regulatory changes aim to limit certain high-risk activities, reducing incentives to perform them through higher capital requirements or new remuneration criteria. The business model of Spanish banking d0 traditional and prudent d0 has happily left them out of high-risk activities, although obviously the new and greater regulatory requirements will also affect our entities. Another key area of discussion is that of systemic risk and, in particular, the treatment of so-called systemically important financial institutions, or "SIFIs".
