Title: Speech at the "X International Financial Meeting Caja Madrid". Teatros del Canal. "La reforma del sistema financiero espaol"
text: Madrid, 15 November 2010 The reform of the Spanish financial system X International Financial Meeting Caja Madrid Miguel Fern87ndez Ord9796ez Governor Good morning to all and thank you very much to the organizers of this event for inviting me to participate in its inauguration. More than three years ago, at a time when the expansionary cycle of the Spanish economy showed signs of exhaustion, the most serious international financial crisis since the Great Depression began. In 2008 the turbulence hit some major international banks hard, and their governments were forced to bail them out to prevent the collapse of the entire financial system. The Spanish banking sector reasonably withstood that first wave of the crisis. In the first place, because the entities had not participated in the generation or invested in the more complex structured credit products that we baptized as . Our banks practiced, and still do, a retail and customer-friendly business model, which before the summer of 2007 some described as traditional or outdated, but which over time has proven to be an enormously valuable asset. The second reason that explains the good performance of the Spanish banking system in the first two years of the global crisis is our regulatory and supervisory regime, which in some important aspects was more prudent than that of other developed countries. Good examples of this are the system of provisions in force for a decade, which requires a buffer in the expansionary phase of the economic cycle, or the requirement to consolidate any structure outside the bank balance sheets that implies a risk for the entity. As Spain did not offer the incentives provided by other more lax regulatory and supervisory regimes, neither products nor highly vulnerable businesses were developed here. However, at the beginning of the crisis, the Spanish banking system also had some imbalances that had accumulated in the previous long expansionary period. During that period, both the installed capacity in the sector and credit for construction and real estate development activities grew continuously since the late 90s, at rates that were unsustainable from a long-term perspective. Second, this expansion was largely financed by turning to international markets, since deposits raised from firms and households were not sufficient to accommodate such intense credit growth. This led to a dependence on wholesale financing that increased the vulnerability of our institutions to possible shocks in the financial markets. With these imbalances of their own, and faced with a crisis of unprecedented intensity in modern history, it was clear that the Spanish banking sector could not remain immune to the cataclysm experienced by the world economy. Savings banks were particularly affected, or to be more precise, a good part of them. The reason is that these entities accumulated imbalances in a more intense way, and therefore their correction is now more significant. The magnitude of the crisis forced all economic authorities to react quickly, energetically and imaginatively. Governments and central banks adopted exceptional liquidity provision measures to mitigate financing problems in the short term, and immediately set about designing changes in the international regulatory and supervisory framework, aimed at preventing the recurrence of similar crises and improving the resilience of the financial system for the future. These include the new regulatory scheme known as Basel III, advances in the treatment of so-called systemic institutions, increasing the intensity of supervision or the introduction of a new supervisory framework in Europe. Macroeconomic measures still pose significant challenges, such as defining exit strategies to withdraw economic stimuli at the right time. But perhaps even more important for the banking sector is the impact of the profound review of regulation and supervision schemes that has been outlined in the main international forums and organizations in the last two years. In particular, Basel III will require more and better capital from banks depending on the risk of their activities, to which will be added additional requirements depending on the risk of liquidity and long-term financing, as well as to mitigate the procyclicality associated with the banking business. The message of all these changes is clear: banks will have to significantly increase the quantity and quality of their capital. These changes could have a high cost to the global economy, if demanded immediately, given the fragility of current economic and financial conditions. That is why an implementation timetable has been approved that does not jeopardize economic recovery. As I said, Basel III also incorporates new liquidity and leverage ratios. However, regulatory experience with these new instruments is limited, making them difficult to calibrate. Consequently, the concrete proposals for these ratios are not yet fully defined and therefore long adaptation periods have been established as well as review clauses in the event that their application results in unintended consequences. Finally, the new regulatory framework contemplates the creation of countercyclical capital buffers, following a philosophy similar to that of the generic provisions system in force in Spain. A proposal on these buffers has already been published and should be definitively agreed by the end of this year. In addition to the progress of Basel III, in recent months the Financial Stability Board (FSB) has made progress in the treatment of systemically important institutions (SIFIs). The public cost of bailouts of major international banks in the most acute phase of the crisis reopened an old debate on banking regulation: what should be done about entities that are too important to fail, that is, those that can be considered systemic because of their size, the level of complexity of their operations or their degree of interconnectedness with other participants in the financial system. The G-20 summit in Seoul has supported this work, which should conclude by ensuring that the highest regulatory and supervisory requirements are modulated according to the type of activity carried out by the entities, the complexity of that activity and the operational structure of each institution. Obviously, the regulatory changes underway will require a significant effort from the Spanish banking sector, which like that of other countries will have to face the new capital requirements. However, there are factors that should contribute to its impact on the entities of our country remaining within reasonable limits. For example, the new rules set higher capital requirements for riskier assets, but given the nature of our banks' business, which is mainly based on retail banking, these requirements cannot be expected to have an unbearable impact. On the other hand, in the context of the discussion on systemically important institutions, crisis resolution plans aimed at ensuring that any institution can be liquidated or restructured with as little disruption as possible to the whole system play a fundamental role. In this sense, the structure of Spanish cross-border banks is a positive asset, given that their activities abroad are mainly carried out through subsidiaries, which have financial autonomy. In short, the novelties in the regulation and supervision schemes advance in a line that is consistent with some of the practices that were already being developed in our country, and there are reasons to trust in the ability of Spanish entities to adapt to these new requirements. The main challenges Therefore, the most important challenges facing the Spanish banking sector today do not come from changes in international financial regulation, but from its own vulnerabilities, those derived from almost fourteen years of expansion based on a growing debt obtained outside our borders in a significant proportion. In this regard, asset quality remains a priority. The magnitude of increases in non-performing assets has gradually slowed down over the last few months, to now be similar to those at the beginning of 2008. It cannot be ruled out that non-performing loans will continue to pick up in the coming months, although the available information suggests that the most severe part of the adjustment has already been made. In relation to asset quality, exposure to the real estate development sector stands out. This sector has a marked cyclical behaviour, and is currently continuing its adjustment process. The results of the stress tests that were made public in July showed that the hypothetical losses in a very adverse scenario would come mostly from the exposures maintained with this sector, but at the same time they reflected that the Spanish banking sector has sufficient strength to absorb them. However, the Bank of Spain is focusing on two issues in relation to the investment of entities in the real estate sector. First, try to ensure that entities, when managing the risks arising from their exposure to this sector, and in particular when accepting real estate as payment of debts, do not defer the recognition of losses. This translates, on the one hand, into detailed supervision of these operations, and on the other, into the change in the general estimation criteria included in the accounting regulations of the Bank of Spain, which, based on accumulated historical experience, establish minimum percentages of specific coverage for foreclosed assets. The other issue related to exposures with the real estate development sector in which the Bank of Spain is affecting is the need for entities to be more transparent. At a time of adjustment in the real estate sector and confidence in the banking sector is still weak, the lack of information only serves to paint a worse picture than reality itself. A second vulnerability has to do with the financing of entities in wholesale markets. From a medium-term perspective, it is necessary to recompose the liabilities of institutions, reducing their dependence on this type of financing. Inevitably this will take time. Meanwhile, it is key to strengthen the improvement in investor confidence that has been observed since July of this year, and which resulted in the ability of banks to return to the interbank and issuance markets, reducing ECB financing very substantially. It is true that the maturities of Spanish debt are concentrated in medium and long maturities, but banks will have to lengthen maturity structures to the extent that the markets allow it. Another important challenge for the Spanish banking sector is to absorb the excess installed capacity for it as a whole and at the same time increase the critical mass of banks. This process is imperative in the case of savings banks because they are the ones with the greatest imbalances: a very dense network of offices and an oversizing of central services, to which in many cases is added the fact that many entities had a small size. These problems have been addressed using the FROB, an instrument that empowers an orderly reabsorption of excess installed capacity in the banking sector, minimizing the cost of this process for the public treasury. To achieve its objectives, the FROB was constituted with two modalities of action. One, aimed at entities that, being viable, needed to undertake integration processes to guarantee their return to a path of sustainable profitability in the future, through the strengthening of their solvency. The other modality aimed to facilitate a rapid and effective intervention of those entities that presented viability problems. Since the FROB Law was approved, 40 boxes out of a total of 45 are participating in some integration process, which represents 94% of the assets of that subsector. In total, 13 integration processes are underway, of which 8 have requested aid from the FROB, for an amount of 10,581 million euros. This aid is highly conditional. First, temporarily, since they will have to be returned in a period, in general, of 5 years. Second, in terms of its cost, because the FROB requires a minimum annual remuneration of 7.75%. And also for the commitments included in the integration plans that have been approved and are being supervised by the Bank of Spain, which will monitor quarter by quarter the fulfillment of the agreements reached. These agreements involve significant reductions in installed capacity which, for example in terms of the number of offices, entail reductions ranging from 10% to 30%. The amount of public resources mobilized may seem small when compared to other countries, but this is partly due to the high generic provisions that the system had at the outset and the compensation involved, in terms of own resources, by the fact that integrations have been made between entities that had to strengthen their capital and others that did not. With regard to non-viable entities, two savings banks have been intervened since the crisis began. One, Caja Castilla-La Mancha, when the FROB was not yet approved. The other, Cajasur, when that Law had entered into force. The Bank of Spain has explained all the details of these two interventions on numerous occasions. The restructuring of savings banks was a necessary condition to ensure the viability of this sector, but to ensure its future, it was also necessary to undertake the reform of its legal regime, since the legal framework in force until now prevented savings banks from strengthening their higher quality capital in the way that banks do. for they could only increase their capital through the profits generated. The main novelty incorporated in the new legislation on savings banks is that it gives these entities the ability to issue capital instruments of the highest quality. They will have the possibility of issuing participatory quotas with voting rights, which will allow investors who acquire them to enter the decision-making bodies of the savings banks. In addition, for those entities that have business concerns that involve operating beyond their traditional markets and businesses, two possible modifications are opened in their structure: their integration into institutional protection systems and the transfer of their financial business to a bank. It should be noted that through these new organizational models, entities will be able to issue shares, which allow raising capital of the best quality, while forcing the holders of securities to be integrated into their governance structures. As a result of this reform, savings banks will not only be able to cope with the higher capital requirements required by the new regulatory framework, but will also be subject to greater and better market discipline. To the extent that these entities issue securities that incorporate voting rights, surveillance and monitoring by financial agents will be greater, which will result in improvements in their management. And the new legislation has also incorporated some specific elements aimed at professionalizing its management. In addition to providing liquidity to the sector and enabling mechanisms for its orderly restructuring, public authorities have sought to strengthen the transparency of the banking sector. The publication of the stress tests on 23 July is the best example of this. In the presentation of the Annual Report for 2009, I announced the Banco de Espa96a's commitment to carry out stress tests on our banks and to publish their results. The announcement came at a time of high distrust of international markets regarding the situation of the Spanish banking sector, and in particular about savings banks and their exposure to the real estate sector. In these circumstances, and given the noise created by the merger processes and the news derived from the adjustment of the real estate sector, the Bank of Spain considered that the vision that some investors had about our entities was strongly distorted. The lack of information translated into a perception of their situation that was clearly worse than reality itself. The initiative to carry out and publish the stress tests was well received by our European colleagues, and finally led to an exercise carried out by the whole of the European Union, which the Bank of Spain valued very positively because it reinforced the transparency and comparability of the tests. And we were able to keep intact our efforts to provide the market with maximum information. The European exercise was not limited in Spain to examining the entities representing 50% of the sector, but all listed banks and all savings banks were tested. In addition, very detailed quantitative information was given entity by entity, including aspects as relevant as the distribution of hypothetical losses by different portfolios, the funds available to cover these losses, and the public aid already received or committed before the stress tests were carried out. The results showed that, even considering the most unfavorable stress scenario, with a practically zero probability of occurrence, the Spanish banking sector was solid. But perhaps the best thing was that enough information was provided to the market so that analysts could assess the situation of each entity according to their own assumptions. The consequence was that, since the end of July, the international financial markets began to reopen, both the interbank and the issuance of bonds and obligations. There were several Spanish entities that, with differences between them in terms of volume issued and price, were able to access these primary emission markets. These improvements were not only the result of the publication of the stress tests. On the one hand, it was essential that before its realization the processes of integration of savings banks had been agreed. But, it must be recognized that the markets improved above all because the Government put on the table a serious plan of fiscal consolidation and structural reforms, and in particular of the labor market, transmitting to investors greater confidence about the possibilities of the Spanish economy to return to a path of growth. In recent weeks, new market uncertainties have resurfaced regarding the fiscal and banking situation in Ireland as well as doubts about the design of the permanent crisis resolution mechanism. It is hoped that an appropriate reaction by the Irish authorities, as well as clarification by ministers from France, Germany, the United Kingdom, Italy and Spain at the G20 meetings in Seoul on the nature and scope of EU crisis resolution mechanisms, will help calm markets and allay unfounded concerns. I think it is important to underline that the changes that could be introduced in these mechanisms to make them permanent will not take effect before mid-2013, and therefore in no case will they affect either the current outstanding debt or the programs that are addressed with the existing instruments. And so it seems that the markets have begun to understand it. Final Thoughts As I have said on several occasions, and the recent crisis has made it clear, the financial economy and the real economy are not two different and disconnected worlds. The reality is the opposite: the interaction is mutual. There is no doubt that it is essential that the banking sector be in a position to channel credit towards productive activities so that when the recovery arrives it can meet any increase in demand for solvent credit. But this relationship also works in the opposite direction: if the so-called real economy does not soon overcome its own imbalances, low growth, unemployment and delinquency could end up affecting the financial system very negatively and in this way would prevent banks and savings banks from helping the economic recovery. That is why our main objective today must be to consolidate the recovery and achieve sustainable growth rates that will allow us to generate jobs again. For this, it is essential to correct the main imbalances that were generated in the last expansionary phase, as well as those that have appeared with the development of the crisis. The problem of competitiveness and the external deficit needs to be addressed; correcting the high indebtedness of the private sector; reduce the concentration of resources in the real estate market; cutting the public deficit towards more sustainable levels; complete the process of restructuring and reducing the capacity of our banking system; and reducing the unemployment rate from the intolerable levels it currently records. The correction of some of these imbalances has already begun, in some cases as a result of the weakness in demand itself, and in others as a result of economic policy measures d0 such as budgetary consolidation or the restructuring of the banking system. However, and beyond the necessary stabilizing role of demand policies, for the economic recovery to materialize and be sustainable, measures must be adopted to help complete the process of correcting the imbalances in our economy, favoring job creation, facilitating the replacement of productive activities and increasing the efficiency and productivity of the economy as a whole. All actors in our economy should be sufficiently aware that in order to improve competitiveness within a system of fixed exchange rates, it is essential d0 and urgent d0 to provide the economy with more flexible adjustment mechanisms and improve productivity through well-designed supply-side policies. At the same time, the process of restructuring the Spanish banking system must be completed and for this not only the restructuring processes of savings banks that have received public aid must be strictly complied with. Even those entities that, having been successful with their management in the past, have not needed aid, must also react to an environment that is increasingly pushing down profits. The digestion of the real estate adjustment, the increase in the cost of external and internal financing, the low level of interest rates for a large part of the asset as well as a recovery in economic activity that will inevitably be gradual as a result of a long and unbalanced expansionary cycle, configure a scenario in which, if institutions do not react quickly, They will suffer in the level and quality of their income statements. Over the last few years, the Bank of Spain has been warning about the weakening of the income statement and has urged a decisive reaction from the entities themselves. Those who did not prepare sufficiently for this fall in margins and activity and for the exhaustion of generic provisions have no choice but to use all possible energy to increase efficiency by reducing costs of all kinds and use imagination to continue innovating and moving forward. While it is true that Spanish entities have proven to have much more appropriate models than those of other competitors, they have learned a lot during the crisis and at this moment nobody in the world is standing still when it comes to improving the profitability and financial strength of their entities. Banks should not ignore the fact that markets judge in relative terms d0 we have seen this in the case of sovereign risk d0 and therefore, they must not only increase their financial strength and profitability, but they must do so at least at the same speed as their competitors. In summary, the current reform, restructuring or reconversion -whatever you want to call it- of the Spanish banking system is at a crucial moment in which each and every one has to do their job: - The government will have to maintain the tension and direction of its recent economic policy based on budgetary austerity and structural reforms, and Parliament should support them despite the fact that the current situation makes it more attractive to propose increasing expenditure, reducing revenues or delaying reforms. - Regulators and supervisors must diligently implement what the Government and Parliament have approved. - The savings banks that have borrowed public resources must quickly and scrupulously comply with the agreed integration schedules, because they will result in synergies and capacity reorganization processes that will alleviate the income statements, and because the entities will gain critical mass, which will also favor their access to financing. In this sense, all the mergers of savings banks that are already underway and all the SIPs must have constituted the banks that function as the central body of the same and must make public their Board and their new executive team before Christmas. - The rest of the entities, that is, those banks and savings banks that, due to their correct management in the past, did not receive public aid, cannot stand still either. The current pressure on results makes it imperative to reduce costs, increase efficiency and counteract as far as possible the downward trend in profits. Many of these measures and actions are extraordinary, exceptional, require serious efforts and will take time to have an effect. But they are in the right direction. It is now essential to persevere in these tasks, establishing changes in the economy and in the entities that allow us to establish solid foundations for our country to return to a path of sufficient growth and for the banking sector to be in a position to contribute positively to that recovery. Thanks a lot.

Adems, para aquellas entidades que tengan inquietudes empresariales que impliquen operar ms all de sus mercados y negocios tradicionales, se abren dos posibles modificaciones en su estructura: su integracin en sistemas institucionales de proteccin y la cesin de su negocio financiero a un banco. Cabe destacar que a travs de estos nuevos modelos organizativos las entidades podrn emitir acciones, que permiten captar capital de la mejor calidad, al tiempo que obligan a integrar a los tenedores de los ttulos en sus estructuras de gobierno. Como consecuencia de esta reforma, las cajas de ahorros no slo podrn hacer frente a las mayores exigencias de capital que exigir el nuevo marco regulatorio, sino que tambin quedarn sometidas a una mayor y mejor disciplina de mercado. En la medida en la que estas entidades emitan ttulos que incorporan derecho de voto, la vigilancia y el seguimiento por los agentes financieros ser mayor, lo que redundar en mejoras en su gestin. Y la nueva legislacin ha incorporado tambin algunos elementos especficos destinados a profesionalizar su gestin. Adems de facilitar liquidez al sector y de habilitar mecanismos para su reestructuracin ordenada, las autoridades pblicas han intentado reforzar la transparencia del sector bancario. La publicacin de las pruebas de resistencia el pasado 23 de julio es el mejor ejemplo de ello. En la presentacin del Informe Anual relativo al ejercicio 2009 anunci el compromiso del Banco de Espaa de realizar pruebas de resistencia a nuestras entidades, y de publicar sus resultados. El anuncio se produjo en un momento de elevada desconfianza de los mercados internacionales respecto de la situacin del sector bancario espaol, y en particular sobre las cajas de ahorros y su exposicin al sector inmobiliario. En tales circunstancias, y ante el ruido creado por los procesos de fusiones y las noticias derivadas del ajuste del sector inmobiliario, el Banco de Espaa consider que la visin que tenan algunos inversores sobre nuestras entidades estaba fuertemente distorsionada. La falta de informacin se traduca en una percepcin de su situacin que era claramente peor que la realidad misma. La iniciativa de realizar y publicar las pruebas de resistencia fue bien acogida por nuestros colegas europeos, y finalmente deriv en un ejercicio realizado por el conjunto de la Unin Europea, que el Banco de Espaa valor muy positivamente porque as se reforzaba la transparencia y la comparabilidad de las pruebas. Y pudimos mantener intacto nuestro empeo de proporcionar al mercado la mxima informacin. El ejercicio europeo no se limit en Espaa a examinar las entidades que representasen el 50% del sector, sino que se sometieron a prueba todos los bancos cotizados y todas las cajas de ahorros. Adems se dio una informacin cuantitativa muy detallada entidad a entidad, incluyendo aspectos tan relevantes como la distribucin de las prdidas hipotticas por distintas carteras, los fondos disponibles para cubrir dichas prdidas, y las ayudas pblicas ya recibidas o comprometidas antes de la realizacin de las pruebas de resistencia. Los resultados demostraron que, aun considerando el escenario de tensin ms desfavorable, con una probabilidad de ocurrencia prcticamente nula, el sector bancario espaol era slido. Pero quiz lo mejor fue que se aport suficiente informacin al mercado para que los analistas pudieran evaluar la situacin de cada entidad con arreglo a sus propias hiptesis. La consecuencia fue que, desde finales del mes de julio, los mercados financieros internacionales comenzaron a reabrirse, tanto el interbancario, como los de emisiones de cdulas y bonos y obligaciones. Fueron varias las entidades espaolas que, con diferencias entre ellas en cuanto al volumen emitido y al precio, pudieron acceder a estos mercados primarios de emisiones. Estas mejoras no slo fueron fruto de la publicacin de las pruebas de resistencia. Por una parte, fue esencial que antes de su realizacin se hubieran acordado los procesos de integracin de las cajas de ahorros. Pero, hay que reconocer que los mercados mejoraron sobre todo porque el Gobierno puso sobre la mesa un plan serio de consolidacin fiscal y de reformas estructurales, y en particular del mercado de trabajo, transmitiendo a los inversores una mayor confianza sobre las posibilidades de la economa espaola para retornar a una senda de crecimiento. En las ltimas semanas han vuelto a surgir nuevas incertidumbres en los mercados en relacin con la situacin fiscal y bancaria en Irlanda as como las dudas sobre el diseo del mecanismo permanente de resolucin de crisis. Cabe esperar que una adecuada reaccin por parte de las autoridades irlandesas as como la clarificacin que han efectuado los ministros de Francia, Alemania, Reino Unido, Italia y Espaa, en el marco de las reuniones del G20 en Sel, sobre la naturaleza y alcance de los mecanismos de resolucin de crisis de la UE, ayuden a calmar los mercados y a disipar inquietudes infundadas. Me parece importante subrayar que los cambios que se pudieran introducir en dichos mecanismos para hacerlos permanentes no tendrn efecto antes de mediados del 2013, y por lo tanto en ningn caso afectarn ni a la deuda viva actual ni a los programas que se aborden con los instrumentos vigentes. Y as parece que lo han empezado a entender los mercados. Conclusiones finales Como he dicho en diversas ocasiones, y la reciente crisis ha puesto de manifiesto de forma evidente, la economa financiera y la economa real no son dos mundos diferentes e inconexos. La realidad es la contraria: la interaccin es mutua. Qu duda cabe que es fundamental que el sector bancario est en condiciones de canalizar el crdito hacia las actividades productivas para que cuando llegue la recuperacin pueda atender todo aumento de demanda de crdito solvente. Pero esta relacin tambin funciona en el sentido inverso: si la denominada economa real no superara pronto sus propios desequilibrios, el bajo crecimiento, el desempleo y la morosidad podran acabar afectando muy negativamente al sistema financiero y de esta forma impediran que bancos y cajas pudieran ayudar a la recuperacin econmica. Por ello, nuestro principal objetivo hoy debe ser consolidar la recuperacin y alcanzar de forma sostenible unas tasas de crecimiento que permitan volver a generar empleo. Para ello es fundamental corregir los principales desequilibrios que se generaron en la ltima fase expansiva, as como los que han aparecido con el desarrollo de la crisis. Es necesario afrontar el problema de la competitividad y el dficit exterior; corregir el elevado endeudamiento del sector privado; reducir la concentracin de recursos en el mercado inmobiliario; recortar el dficit pblico hacia situarlo en niveles ms sostenibles; completar el proceso de reestructuracin y reduccin de capacidad de nuestro sistema bancario; y reducir la tasa de paro desde los niveles intolerables que registra en la actualidad. La correccin de algunos de estos desequilibrios ya se ha iniciado, en ciertos casos como consecuencia de la propia debilidad de la demanda, y en otros como resultado de medidas de poltica econmica como es el caso de la consolidacin presupuestaria o la reestructuracin del sistema bancario-. Sin embargo, y ms all del necesario papel estabilizador de las polticas de demanda, para que la recuperacin econmica se materialice y sea sostenible deben adoptarse medidas que ayuden a completar el proceso de correccin de los desequilibrios de nuestra economa, favoreciendo la creacin de empleo, facilitando el relevo de las actividades productivas y aumentando la eficiencia y la productividad de la economa en su conjunto. Todos los actores de nuestra economa deberan ser lo suficientemente conscientes de que para poder mejorar la competitividad dentro de un sistema de tipos de cambio fijos es imprescindible y urgente dotar a la economa de mecanismos de ajuste ms flexibles y mejorar la productividad a travs de unas polticas de oferta bien diseadas. Paralelamente, se debe completar el proceso de reestructuracin del sistema bancario espaol y para ello no slo se deben cumplir estrictamente los procesos de reestructuracin de las cajas de ahorro que han recibido ayudas pblicas. Incluso aquellas entidades que, al haber acertado con su gestin en el pasado no han necesitado ayudas, tambin deben reaccionar ante un entorno que cada vez presiona ms a la baja de los beneficios. La digestin del ajuste inmobiliario, el encarecimiento de la financiacin externa e interna, el reducido nivel de tipos para buena parte del activo as como una recuperacin de la actividad econmica que inevitablemente ser gradual como consecuencia de un largo y desequilibrado ciclo expansivo, configuran un escenario en el que, si las entidades no reaccionan rpidamente, lo sufrirn en el nivel y calidad de sus cuentas de resultados. A lo largo de estos ltimos aos el Banco de Espaa ha venido alertando sobre el debilitamiento de la cuenta de resultados y ha urgido una reaccin decidida de las propias entidades. A aqullos que no se prepararon suficientemente para esta cada de mrgenes y de actividad y para el agotamiento de las provisiones genricas no les queda ms remedio que emplear ya toda la energa posible para aumentar la eficiencia reduciendo costes de todo tipo y utilizar la imaginacin para seguir innovando y avanzando. Si bien es verdad que las entidades espaolas han demostrado tener unos modelos mucho ms adecuados que los de otros competidores, estos han aprendido mucho durante la crisis y en este momento nadie en el mundo est quedndose parado a la hora de mejorar la rentabilidad y fortaleza financiera de sus entidades. Las entidades no deberan ignorar que los mercados juzgan en trminos relativos -lo hemos visto en el caso del riesgo soberano- y por tanto, no slo deben aumentar su fortaleza financiera y su rentabilidad, sino que deben hacerlo al menos a la misma velocidad que sus competidores. En resumen, la actual reforma, reestructuracin o reconversin -como quieran Vds. denominarla- del sistema bancario espaol est en un momento crucial en el que todos y cada uno tienen que hacer su trabajo: - El Gobierno habr de mantener la tensin y direccin de su reciente poltica econmica basada en la austeridad presupuestaria y las reformas estructurales, y el Parlamento debera apoyar las mismas a pesar de que la coyuntura actual haga ms atractivo proponer aumentar los gastos, reducir ingresos o retrasar las reformas. - Los reguladores y supervisores debemos aplicar con diligencia lo que el Gobierno y el Parlamento han aprobado. - Las cajas que han recibido en prstamo recursos pblicos debern cumplir rpida y escrupulosamente los calendarios de integracin acordados, porque de ellos se derivarn sinergias y procesos de reordenacin de la capacidad que aliviarn las cuentas de resultados, y porque las entidades ganarn masa crtica, lo que tambin favorecer su acceso a la financiacin. En este sentido todas las fusiones de cajas que ya estn en marcha y todos los SIPs debern tener constituidos los bancos que funcionen como organismo central del mismo y debern hacer pblico su Consejo y su nuevo equipo ejecutivo antes de Navidades. - El resto de las entidades, esto es, aquellos bancos y cajas que por su acertada gestin en el pasado no recibieron ayudas pblicas, tampoco pueden quedarse quietos. La actual presin sobre los resultados obliga imperiosamente a reducir costes, a aumentar la eficiencia y contrarrestar en la medida de lo posible la tendencia a la baja de los beneficios. Muchas de estas medidas y actuaciones son extraordinarias, excepcionales, requieren serios esfuerzos y tomarn tiempo en surtir efectos. Pero estn en la direccin adecuada. Ahora es esencial perseverar en estas tareas, asentando los cambios en la economa y en las entidades que permitan establecer bases slidas para que nuestro pas vuelva a una senda de crecimiento suficiente y para que el sector bancario est en disposicin de contribuir positivamente a esa recuperacin. Muchas gracias.

Title: Appearance of the Governor of the Bank of Spain before the Senate Budget Committee
text: Madrid, 23 November 2010 Appearance of the Governor before the Senate Budget Committee in relation to the 2011 General State Budget Project Miguel Fern87ndez Ord9796ez Governor Ladies and gentlemen, I appear before you in the context of the discussion in this House of the General State Budgets for 2011, which are called to be an essential piece in the design of our country's economic policy. In conditions as unique as the current ones, both Spanish citizens and the international financial and economic community and, in particular, our European partners, are going to be very demanding with budgets that have to contribute decisively to establishing a solid basis for growth, job creation and economic stability. In recent weeks we have witnessed a new episode of tension in the European public debt markets, the immediate origin of which was Ireland's budgetary and banking situation. The contagion has spread, once again, rapidly, and the effects have been felt on the Greek debt, on the Portuguese debt and also, although to a lesser extent, on ours, the Italian or even the Belgian. Given these developments, last Sunday the Irish government formally requested financial assistance from the member states of the European Union and the euro area. The financial support and economic programme needed to resolve the fiscal and banking challenges of the Irish banking sector which, in accordance with the principle of strict conditionality established in May, will have to accompany it should facilitate the progressive normalisation of the situation in that country and, by extension, contribute to greater financial stability in Europe. Since the Greek fiscal crisis broke out last spring in European debt markets, periods of relative calm have alternated with periods of tension, which have always affected more those economies with greater deterioration of their public finances or with more pronounced macroeconomic and financial imbalances. I am convinced that part of these financial tensions are due to an overreaction on the part of the financial markets, which have not always been able to correctly assess the relative strengths and weaknesses of the different economies. But it would be a mistake to blame the markets alone for these developments. It is clear that the European Stability and Growth Pact, and, in general, the European framework for economic governance, have proved clearly insufficient to limit the accumulation of excessive macroeconomic imbalances, the destabilising effects of which we are now suffering from the area-wide. This is the main reason why an in-depth review of European governance mechanisms is being carried out on the twin fronts of crisis prevention and resolution. In the first, the proposals recently made by the European working group led by the President of the Council, Mr Van Rompuy, represent an effective strengthening of the processes for reviewing the policies and economic conditions of the Member States, although, in my opinion, the scale of the challenges would have required a higher degree of ambition in the proposals. In the area of crisis resolution, a broad consensus has emerged on the need for a permanent resolution mechanism, which gives continuity to the current European Financial Stability Facility and, like this one, is subject to a strict principle of conditionality of financial support. The discussion of the details of this mechanism is still in its infancy, yet some proposals generated confusion and contributed to increasing market nervousness at a very inopportune time. The subsequent clarification by ministers from France, Germany, Italy, Spain and the United Kingdom, on the sidelines of the G20 meetings in Seoul, on the scope of possible reforms helped to allay unfounded concerns. I think it is important to underline that the changes that may be introduced in the crisis resolution mechanisms to make them permanent will not take effect before mid-2013, and therefore will not affect either the current outstanding debt or the programs that are addressed with the existing instruments. In Spain, as in other neighbouring countries, budgetary policy responded with significant expansionary stimuli to deal with the economic crisis, which, together with the sharp fall in tax revenue, ended up weakening the situation of public accounts. After several years of running surpluses, public finances ran substantial deficits and, although Spain's debt level started from low levels, the debt-to-GDP ratio increased very rapidly. The consequences of the change in the fiscal position were exacerbated, in an environment of severe volatility in the financial markets, by the emergence of some elements of possible vulnerability of the Spanish economy, which had been maintained as a result of the insufficient progress of some of the structural reforms in the boom years. In particular, the dysfunctions of the labour market were felt to their full extent during the crisis and generated an increase in the unemployment rate much higher than that observed in other neighbouring countries. In turn, the Spanish economy's high dependence on external financing, the result of many years of growth in expenditure necessitating the appeal to external savings, made it particularly sensitive to any disturbance that hindered confidence and banks' access to international financial markets. These elements of weakness facilitated the contagion of the sovereign debt crisis, unleashed in Greece, to the Spanish economy, which translated, between the months of May and July, into serious difficulties in obtaining the necessary external financing, which were amplified by a climate of distrust in the Spanish banking system based, To a large extent, on unsubstantiated assumptions. The economic authorities reacted forcefully to break this adverse dynamic, adopting important fiscal, labor and financial measures. In the budgetary area, the government strengthened and accelerated the implementation of the fiscal consolidation program that, in compliance with community commitments, it had announced in January. To this end, in May it approved a new set of measures that entailed a cut in spending to be undertaken between 2010 and 2011 (for an amount of around 1.5% of GDP). In this way, the Government defined a new path of fiscal consolidation that entailed deficits of 9.3% of GDP in 2010, 6% in 2011, 4.4% in 2012 and 3% of GDP in 2013. The immediate entry into force of this adjustment package d0 some measures were already implemented in June of this year d0 and its content d0 which affected variables as sensitive as the salary of civil servants, social benefits or public investment d0 were fundamental to give credibility to the commitment to reduce the public deficit. In the labour field, as is well known, the government approved a labour market reform on 16th June, which concluded its parliamentary process two months later, on 17 September. The approved reform aims to encourage permanent contracts and increase the internal flexibility of companies, and comes to step out of two of the most relevant deficiencies of our labor market that hindered the maintenance and creation of employment. I have already set out in this House the various actions that have been taken to manage the restructuring of the Spanish banking system, which was an essential condition for ensuring a solid and sustainable recovery of the economy. Allow me to confine myself in this hearing to highlighting the important role played by the stress tests to which the banking system was subjected at the end of July. This was an exercise in transparency that undoubtedly contributed to breaking the aforementioned cycle of mistrust. As will be recalled, when I presented the Annual Report for 2009 on 16 June, I announced the Bank's intention to publish the stress tests of all Spanish banks and savings banks. This initiative was taken up at European level by the European Council held under the Spanish Presidency, and the results of the exercise, harmonised by the European Committee of Banking Supervisors, were published on 23rd July. In the case of Spanish banks, the stress tests covered practically the entire financial system and were carried out in greater detail and disaggregation and with a high degree of transparency, providing extensive information on their exposure to the main asset classes. The results showed a solid position of the system as a whole. The adoption of a stronger policy stance to address fiscal consolidation and structural reforms, reinforced by the publication of the results of financial institutions' stress tests, facilitated the recovery of international investor confidence and an improvement in the perception of the solvency of our financial system. This led to the normalisation of the financing channels of credit institutions and a significant reduction in the Treasury's financing costs. That situation prevailed until the end of October. Since then, however, financial tensions have resurfaced in the euro area, reflecting events in Ireland and some confusion over European support mechanisms, which reignited uncertainties and contagion channels. When I appeared before the Congress of Deputies at the beginning of October, I insisted that, despite the improvement experienced, it was necessary to remain vigilant because there could be new episodes prone to the spread of mistrust. For this reason, I stressed the importance of keeping intact the credibility gained and strengthening it through continuous progress in the development of the announced program. The developments of recent weeks reinforce the validity and timeliness of this message. This is the complex situation in which the Government had to design the General State Budget for 2011 and it is the one that prevails during its parliamentary processing. It is clear that against this background, the correction of the public deficit is an unavoidable priority of economic policy that must be addressed with ambition and energy. In my opinion, the measures proposed by the General State Budget Project adequately address this challenge. But the effort must not stop there. In order to dispel any hint of doubt about the reaction capacity of the Spanish economy, it is essential to interweave fiscal policy with other economic policy tools, in particular with supply-side and structural reform policies, aimed at improving the capacity to generate employment and the recovery of output. The cyclical moment in which the Budgets for 2011 have been defined is marked by the timid beginning of a recovery phase that began to be glimpsed in the first months of this year and that should continue, once the episode of stagnation that has been registered during the third quarter has been overcome, which has been due to transitory factors such as the anticipations of expenditure to the previous quarter or the end of some stimulus programs. The existing prospects for a gradual recovery are, however, surrounded by uncertainties. In an environment where financing conditions are expected to remain restrictive and where both the public and private sectors are facing a pressing need to consolidate their financial position, household consumption is expected to slow its rate of growth compared to the figures for the first half of the year, in line with the slowdown in the growth rate of disposable income and a predictably moderate trend in wealth. This response of consumption would be compatible with a downward trajectory of the savings rate, in line with the changes observed since the beginning of the year, after almost two years of successive increases in this variable. The remaining components of domestic demand are still likely to reflect the weakness of their main determinants. Net foreign demand, however, could show greater dynamism, once imports return to lower growth rates, as seems to have happened in the third quarter, and exports continue their upward trajectory. But for this it is necessary to persevere in consolidating the improvements in competitiveness that have been achieved in the field of costs and prices in recent quarters and strengthen them with genuine gains in productivity. In sum, activity is expected to return to the path of gentle recovery that it had begun at the beginning of the year, although it will still take some time to reach sufficient tone to generate employment. The restoration of confidence, the reduction of uncertainty about the labour market and the financial consolidation of the private sector should be the fundamental ingredients of a sustained recovery in activity, which should have as main drivers the boost in net foreign demand and the progressive dynamism of the private sector. Public sector action has already begun to reflect the impact of the austerity plans that were addressed in the first half of the year. The strength of revenues and the somewhat more incipient inflection of expenditure are in principle compatible with the deficit target stipulated in the Draft Budget for 2010, at least for the State Administrations and Social Security, for which sufficiently up-to-date information is available. For its part, the restrictive stance contemplated in the Budgets for 2011 d0 which, as will be recalled, establishes a deficit for all the Public Administrations of 6% of GDP for that year (and a public debt ratio of 68.7%) d0 should allow progress to be made in achieving the commitments made at European level, although the path of programmed budgetary consolidation is not without risks. Therefore, strict compliance requires rigorous monitoring and control of deviations in income and expenses that may occur and, if necessary, implement appropriate measures. The success of budgetary consolidation also requires the support of each and every one of the levels of government that make up the Public Administrations in Spain. And not only because the high decentralization of public spending in our country makes the participation of these Administrations essential. Also because it must be avoided that the breach of commitments by any of them, if it occurs, could lead to questioning the scope of the Government's commitment to the established objectives. In this sense, over the last month the drafts of the Budgets for 2011 of most of the Autonomous Communities have been released. Overall, they foresee a reduction in non-financial payments of around 8%. As in the case of the State, what is relevant now is to ensure that there are no deviations from the commitments made. To facilitate this task, further strengthening of budgetary frameworks could be useful, in particular in the case of territorial administrations. In this regard, as I have already pointed out on previous occasions, I believe that there is room to improve the transparency of public information of territorial administrations, particularly at a time like the present in which the lack of information can result in a distrust of the markets that manifests itself in a certain additional premium in the cost of financing. Specifically, it would be desirable to correct these shortcomings through the regular publication of the budget execution of the whole and of each of the Autonomous Communities with the same periodicity, degree of detail, lag and ease of access with which the State does. On the other hand, consideration could be given to strengthening mechanisms to avoid budgetary deviations in implementation. In this sense, the parliaments of the Autonomous Communities should consider the establishment of annual spending limits, an instrument that has proven very useful in the case of the State. Likewise, medium-term planning that requires an analysis of the structural dynamics of the different items of public revenue and expenditure and that allows the identification of niches where the margins for rationalization and adjustment are higher may be particularly appropriate when adjustment measures are required that go beyond a temporary correction of imbalances. In this context, the reform of the pension system under discussion is of particular importance, especially if it is carried out immediately and its content is sufficiently ambitious. Decisive action on this front would not only ensure the long-term sustainability of our pension system but would also serve to reaffirm the authorities' commitment to budgetary discipline and their capacity to carry out far-reaching structural reforms, which could have a positive impact on the cost of financing the Treasury. and therefore of all economic agents. In particular, an appropriate combination of substantial changes in some parameters of the system, raising the statutory retirement age, the minimum number of years needed to access the benefit and the period of calculation of the pension, would substantially alleviate the pressure on future public expenditure on pensions. The long-term effects of fiscal consolidation will also be stronger if it is accompanied by structural reforms that increase the economy's growth potential. Among these reforms, those that encourage job creation, enable the achievement of competitiveness gains and improve the efficiency and productivity of the economy in the long term are of transcendental importance. In this area, the reform of the labour market occupies a prominent place, in which, as I have already said, progress has been made with the recent adoption of the Law on urgent measures for the reform of the labour market, which, among other things, includes a series of provisions, among which those aimed at increasing the internal flexibility of companies stand out. granting greater facilities so that they can agree with their workers conditions that deviate from some clauses of the sectoral agreements. The reform of collective bargaining, still pending, should deepen in this direction, allowing a greater adaptation of wages and other working conditions to the individual situation of companies. Internal flexibility is necessary to establish a closer relationship between productivity developments and labour market behaviour and is an essential tool for restoring competitiveness and increasing the dynamism of economic growth. The new labor framework of our country should allow these advantages to be fully exploited. Finally, to the increase in flexibility and the efforts of wage moderation in those companies that need it to recover their competitiveness, a genuine improvement in productivity based on efficiency gains will have to be added, since so far its expansionary behavior mainly reflects the severity in the adjustment of employment. This improvement in productivity also requires deepening other structural reforms with more prolonged effects, including sectoral liberalization, the rationalization of the role of the public sector in economic activity and the improvement of the education system.
text_original: Madrid, 23 de noviembre de 2010 Comparecencia del Gobernador ante la Comisin de Presupuestos del Senado en relacin con el Proyecto de Presupuestos Generales del Estado 2011 Miguel Fernndez Ordez Gobernador Seoras: Comparezco ante ustedes en el marco de la discusin en esta Cmara de los Presupuestos Generales del Estado para 2011, que estn llamados a ser una pieza esencial en el diseo de la poltica econmica de nuestro pas. En unas condiciones tan singulares como las actuales, tanto los ciudadanos espaoles como la comunidad financiera y econmica internacional y, muy en particular, nuestros socios europeos, van a ser muy exigentes con unos presupuestos que tienen que contribuir de manera decisiva a establecer una base slida para el crecimiento, la creacin de empleo y la estabilidad econmica. Hemos asistido en las ltimas semanas a un nuevo episodio de tensin en los mercados de deuda pblica europeos, cuyo origen inmediato se encontraba en la situacin presupuestaria y bancaria de Irlanda. El contagio se ha extendido, una vez ms, de manera rpida, y los efectos se han dejado sentir sobre la deuda griega, sobre la deuda portuguesa y tambin, aunque en menor medida, sobre la nuestra, la italiana o, incluso, la belga. Ante estos desarrollos, el pasado domingo el gobierno irlands solicit formalmente la asistencia financiera de los Estados miembros de la Unin Europea y del rea del euro. El apoyo financiero y el programa econmico necesario para resolver los retos fiscales y del sector bancario irlands que, de acuerdo con el principio de estricta condicionalidad establecido en mayo, tendr que acompaarlo deben facilitar la progresiva normalizacin de la situacin en ese pas y, por extensin, contribuir a una mayor estabilidad financiera en Europa. Desde que en la pasada primavera se desatara la crisis fiscal griega en los mercados de deuda europeos se han venido alternando perodos de relativa calma con otros de tensin, que siempre han afectado ms a aquellas economas con mayor deterioro de sus finanzas pblicas o con desequilibrios macroeconmicos y financieros ms pronunciados. Estoy convencido de que una parte de estas tensiones financieras responde a una sobrerreaccin de los mercados financieros, que no siempre han sabido valorar correctamente las fortalezas y las debilidades relativas de las distintas economas. Pero sera un error achacar exclusivamente a los mercados la responsabilidad de estos desarrollos. Es evidente que el Pacto de Estabilidad Europeo y Crecimiento, y, en general, el marco europeo de gobernanza econmica, se han revelado claramente insuficientes para limitar la acumulacin de desequilibrios macroeconmicos excesivos, cuyos efectos desestabilizadores sobre el conjunto del rea estamos padeciendo ahora. Esta es la principal razn por la que se est llevando a cabo una revisin en profundidad de los mecanismos de gobernanza europeos en el doble frente de la prevencin y la resolucin de las crisis. En el primero, las propuestas recientemente realizadas por el grupo de trabajo europeo dirigido por el Presidente del Consejo, el Sr. Van Rompuy, suponen un reforzamiento efectivo de los procesos de revisin de las polticas y las condiciones econmicas de los Estados miembros aunque, en mi opinin, la magnitud de los desafos habra requerido un grado mayor de ambicin en las propuestas. En el mbito de la resolucin de crisis, se ha generado un consenso amplio en torno a la necesidad de contar con un mecanismo permanente de resolucin, que d continuidad a la actual Facilidad Europea de Estabilidad Financiera y que, como esta, est sujeto a un principio estricto de condicionalidad del apoyo financiero. La discusin de los detalles de este mecanismo est an en una fase incipiente, a pesar de lo cual algunas propuestas generaron confusin y contribuyeron a aumentar el nerviosismo de los mercados en un momento muy inoportuno. La clarificacin posterior que efectuaron los ministros de Francia, Alemania, Italia, Espaa y Reino Unido, en el marco de las reuniones del G20 en Sel, sobre el alcance de las posibles reformas ayud a disipar inquietudes infundadas. Me parece importante subrayar que los cambios que se puedan introducir en los mecanismos de resolucin de crisis para hacerlos permanentes no tendrn efecto antes de mediados del 2013, y por lo tanto no afectarn ni a la deuda viva actual ni a los programas que se aborden con los instrumentos vigentes. En Espaa, como en otros pases de nuestro entorno, la poltica presupuestaria respondi con importantes estmulos expansivos para hacer frente a la crisis econmica, lo que unido a la brusca cada de la recaudacin impositiva termin debilitando la situacin de las cuentas pblicas. Tras varios aos de registrar supervits, las finanzas pblicas pasaron a tener dficits sustanciales y, aunque el nivel de deuda espaola parta de niveles reducidos, la ratio de endeudamiento sobre el PIB aument con gran rapidez. Las consecuencias del cambio en la posicin fiscal se vieron agudizadas, en un entorno de severa volatilidad de los mercados financieros, por el afloramiento de algunos elementos de posible vulnerabilidad de la economa espaola, que se haban mantenido como consecuencia del insuficiente avance de algunas de las reformas estructurales en los aos de bonanza. En particular, las disfuncionalidades del mercado laboral se dejaron sentir en toda su extensin durante la crisis y generaron un aumento de la tasa de paro muy superior al observado en otros pases de nuestro entorno. A su vez, la elevada dependencia de la economa espaola de la financiacin exterior, resultado de muchos aos de un crecimiento del gasto necesitado de la apelacin al ahorro externo, la hizo particularmente sensible a cualquier perturbacin que obstaculizase la confianza y el acceso de las entidades de crdito a los mercados financieros internacionales. Estos elementos de debilidad facilitaron el contagio de la crisis de la deuda soberana, desencadenada en Grecia, a la economa espaola, lo cual se tradujo, entre los meses de mayo y julio, en serias dificultades para la consecucin de la financiacin externa necesaria, que se vieron amplificadas por un clima de desconfianza en el sistema bancario espaol basado, en gran medida, en suposiciones poco fundamentadas. Las autoridades econmicas reaccionaron con contundencia para quebrar esta dinmica tan adversa, adoptando importantes medidas de carcter fiscal, laboral y financiero. En el mbito presupuestario, el gobierno reforz y aceler la implementacin del programa de consolidacin fiscal que, en cumplimiento de los compromisos comunitarios, haba anunciado en enero. Con este objetivo, en mayo aprob una nueva batera de medidas que comportaba un recorte del gasto a acometer entre 2010 y 2011 (por un importe en torno al 1,5% del PIB). De este modo, el Gobierno defina una nueva senda de consolidacin fiscal que comportaba dficits del 9,3% del PIB en 2010, 6% en 2011, 4,4% en 2012 y 3% del PIB en 2013. La entrada en vigor de forma inmediata de este paquete de ajuste algunas medidas se pusieron ya en marcha en junio de este ao- y su contenido -que incida sobre variables tan sensibles como el sueldo de los funcionarios, las prestaciones sociales o la inversin pblica-, fueron fundamentales para dotar de credibilidad al compromiso de reduccin del dficit pblico. En el mbito laboral, como es bien sabido, el Gobierno aprob el 16 de junio una reforma del mercado de trabajo, que concluy su trmite parlamentario dos meses ms tarde, el 17 de septiembre. La reforma aprobada tiene como objetivo incentivar la contratacin indefinida e incrementar la flexibilidad interna de las empresas, y viene a salir al paso de dos de las deficiencias ms relevantes de nuestro mercado laboral que obstaculizaban el mantenimiento y la creacin de empleo. Ya he expuesto en esta Cmara las distintas actuaciones que se han ido realizando para gestionar la reestructuracin del sistema bancario espaol, que constitua una condicin imprescindible para asegurar una recuperacin slida y sostenible de la economa. Por ello, permtanme que en esta comparecencia me limite a destacar el importante papel que desempearon las pruebas de resistencia a las que se someti el sistema bancario a finales de julio. Este fue un ejercicio de transparencia que contribuy sin duda a romper el crculo de desconfianza mencionado. Como se recordar, cuando present el pasado 16 de junio el Informe Anual correspondiente a 2009, anunci la intencin del Banco de publicar las pruebas de resistencia de todos los bancos y cajas espaoles. Dicha iniciativa fue asumida a nivel europeo por el Consejo Europeo celebrado bajo Presidencia Espaola, y los resultados del ejercicio, armonizado por el Comit Europeo de Supervisores Bancarios, fueron publicados el 23 de julio. En el caso de las entidades espaolas las pruebas de resistencia cubrieron prcticamente la totalidad del sistema financiero y se llevaron a cabo con mayor detalle y desagregacin y con un elevado grado de transparencia, proporcionando amplia informacin sobre su exposicin a las principales clases de activos. Los resultados mostraron una posicin slida del conjunto del sistema. La adopcin de una orientacin ms decidida de la poltica econmica para abordar la consolidacin fiscal y las reformas estructurales, reforzada por la publicacin de los resultados de las pruebas de resistencia de las entidades financieras, facilit la recuperacin de la confianza de los inversores internacionales y la mejora en la percepcin de la solvencia de nuestro sistema financiero. Con ello se logr la normalizacin de los canales de financiacin de las entidades de crdito y una significativa reduccin de los costes de financiacin del Tesoro. Esa situacin prevaleci hasta finales de octubre. Desde entonces, sin embargo, las tensiones financieras volvieron a resurgir en la zona del euro, como consecuencia de los acontecimientos en Irlanda y de cierta confusin sobre los mecanismos de ayuda europeos, que reactivaron las incertidumbres y los canales de contagio. Cuando comparec ante el Congreso de los Diputados a principios de octubre insist en que, a pesar de la mejora experimentada, era necesario mantenerse vigilantes porque podan producirse nuevos episodios proclives a la propagacin de la desconfianza. Por este motivo subray la importancia de mantener intacta la credibilidad ganada y de reforzarla a travs de un avance continuo en el desarrollo del programa anunciado. Los desarrollos de las ltimas semanas refuerzan la validez y la oportunidad de este mensaje. Esta es la compleja situacin en la que el Gobierno hubo de disear los Presupuestos Generales del Estado para 2011 y es la que prevalece durante su tramitacin parlamentaria. Es evidente que con este trasfondo, la correccin del dficit pblico es una prioridad ineludible de poltica econmica que se ha de abordar con ambicin y energa. A mi juicio, las medidas que plantea el Proyecto de Presupuestos Generales del Estado afrontan adecuadamente ese reto. Pero el esfuerzo no debe quedarse ah. Para despejar cualquier atisbo de duda sobre la capacidad de reaccin de la economa espaola resulta fundamental la imbricacin de la poltica fiscal con otras herramientas de poltica econmica, muy en particular, con las polticas de oferta y de reforma estructural, orientadas a mejorar la capacidad de generacin de empleo y la recuperacin del producto. El momento cclico en el que se han definido los Presupuestos para el 2011 est marcado por el tmido inicio de una fase de recuperacin que comenz a vislumbrarse en los primeros meses de este ao y que debera proseguir, una vez superado el episodio de estancamiento que se ha registrado durante el tercer trimestre, que se ha debido a factores transitorios como las anticipaciones de gasto al trimestre anterior o la finalizacin de algunos programas de estmulo. Las perspectivas existentes de recuperacin gradual estn, no obstante, rodeadas de incertidumbres. En un entorno en el que previsiblemente las condiciones de financiacin continuarn siendo restrictivas y en el que tanto el sector pblico como el privado se enfrentan a la necesidad apremiante de sanear su posicin financiera, cabe prever que el consumo de los hogares atene su ritmo de avance en comparacin con los registros de la primera mitad del ao, en lnea con la aminoracin del ritmo de crecimiento de la renta disponible y de una evolucin previsiblemente moderada de la riqueza. Esta respuesta del consumo sera compatible con una trayectoria descendente de la tasa de ahorro, en lnea con los cambios que se observan desde principios de ao, tras casi dos aos de aumentos sucesivos en esta variable. El resto de componentes de la demanda interna reflejar todava con gran probabilidad la debilidad de sus determinantes principales. La demanda exterior neta podra mostrar, en cambio, mayor dinamismo, una vez que las importaciones retornen a ritmos de crecimiento ms bajos, como parece haber ocurrido en el tercer trimestre, y que las exportaciones prolonguen su trayectoria ascendente. Pero para ello es necesario perseverar en la consolidacin de las mejoras de competitividad que se han ido alcanzando en el mbito de los costes y de los precios en los ltimos trimestres y afianzarlas con ganancias genuinas en la productividad. En suma, cabe prever que la actividad vuelva a la senda de suave recuperacin que haba iniciado a comienzos de ao, aunque tardar todava algn tiempo en alcanzar el tono suficiente para generar empleo. El restablecimiento de la confianza, la reduccin de la incertidumbre sobre el mercado laboral y el saneamiento financiero del sector privado habrn de ser los ingredientes fundamentales de una recuperacin sostenida de la actividad que debera tener como motores principales el impulso de la demanda exterior neta y el progresivo dinamismo del sector privado. La actuacin del sector pblico ha comenzado a reflejar ya el impacto de los planes de austeridad que se abordaron en la primera mitad del ao. La fortaleza de los ingresos y la inflexin del gasto, algo ms incipiente, resultan en principio compatibles con el objetivo de dficit que estipula el Proyecto de Presupuestos para 2010, al menos para las Administraciones del Estado y la Seguridad Social, para las que se dispone de informacin suficientemente actualizada. Por su parte, la orientacin restrictiva que contemplan los Presupuestos para 2011 que como se recordar establecen un dficit para el conjunto de las AAPP del 6% del PIB para ese ao (y una ratio de deuda pblica del 68,7%)- debera permitir avanzar en el logro de los compromisos adquiridos a nivel europeo, si bien la senda de consolidacin presupuestaria programada no est exenta de riesgos, por lo que su estricto cumplimiento exige un seguimiento y un control riguroso de las desviaciones de ingresos y gastos que se pudieran producir y, si fuera necesario, instrumentar las medidas adecuadas. El xito de la consolidacin presupuestaria requiere, adems, el apoyo de todos y cada uno de los niveles de gobierno que integran las AAPP en Espaa. Y no solo porque la elevada descentralizacin del gasto pblico en nuestro pas hace que el concurso de estas Administraciones sea esencial. Tambin porque se ha de evitar que el incumplimiento de los compromisos por parte de alguna de ellas, en caso de producirse, pudiera llevar a cuestionar el alcance del compromiso del Gobierno con los objetivos establecidos. En este sentido, a lo largo del ltimo mes se han ido dando a conocer los borradores de los Presupuestos para 2011 de la mayora de las CCAA. En su conjunto prevn una reduccin de los pagos no financieros de en torno al 8%. Como en el caso del Estado, lo relevante es ahora garantizar que no se produzcan desviaciones en relacin con los compromisos adquiridos. Para facilitar esta tarea, podra ser til un fortalecimiento adicional de los marcos presupuestarios, en particular en el caso de las Administraciones Territoriales. En este sentido, como ya he sealado en ocasiones previas, creo que hay margen para mejorar la transparencia de la informacin pblica de las Administraciones Territoriales, en particular en un momento como el actual en el que la falta de informacin puede redundar en una desconfianza de los mercados que se manifieste en una cierta prima adicional en el coste de financiacin. En concreto, sera deseable subsanar estas carencias a travs de la publicacin regular de la ejecucin presupuestaria del conjunto y de cada una de las CCAA con la misma periodicidad, grado de detalle, desfase y facilidad de acceso con que lo hace el Estado. Por otra parte, podra considerarse la posibilidad de reforzar los mecanismos para evitar que se produzcan desviaciones presupuestarias en la ejecucin. En este sentido, los parlamentos de las CCAA deberan plantearse el establecimiento de lmites de gasto anual, instrumento que se ha demostrado muy til en el caso del Estado. Asimismo, una planificacin de medio plazo que obligue a analizar la dinmica estructural de las distintas partidas de los ingresos y gastos pblicos y que permita detectar los nichos donde los mrgenes para la racionalizacin y ajuste son superiores puede resultar especialmente apropiada cuando se requieren medidas de ajuste que van ms all de una correccin transitoria de los desequilibrios. En este marco, la reforma del sistema de pensiones que se encuentra en discusin tiene una especial trascendencia, sobre todo si se efecta de una manera inmediata y su contenido es suficientemente ambicioso. Una actuacin decidida en este frente no solo permitira garantizar la sostenibilidad a largo plazo de nuestro sistema de pensiones sino que tambin servira para reafirmar el compromiso de las autoridades con la disciplina presupuestaria y con su capacidad de efectuar reformas estructurales de calado, lo que podra repercutir favorablemente en el coste de financiacin del Tesoro, y por ende de todos los agentes econmicos. En concreto, una adecuada combinacin de modificaciones sustanciales en algunos parmetros del sistema, que eleven la edad legal de jubilacin, el mnimo nmero de aos necesario para acceder a la prestacin y el perodo de clculo de la pensin, permitira aliviar de manera sustancial la presin sobre el futuro gasto pblico en pensiones. Los efectos a largo plazo de la consolidacin fiscal sern adems ms potentes si va acompaada de reformas estructurales que incrementen el potencial de crecimiento de la economa. Entre estas reformas tienen una importancia trascendental aquellas que incentivan la creacin de empleo, posibilitan el logro de ganancias de competitividad y mejoran la eficiencia y productividad de la economa a largo plazo. En este terreno ocupa un lugar destacado la reforma del mercado de trabajo, en la que se ha producido, como ya he dicho, un avance con la reciente aprobacin de Ley de medidas urgentes para la reforma del mercado de trabajo, que, entre otras cosas, incluye una serie de disposiciones, entre las que destacan las dirigidas a incrementar la flexibilidad interna de las empresas, otorgando mayores facilidades para que puedan pactar con sus trabajadores condiciones que se aparten de algunas clusulas de los convenios sectoriales. La reforma de la negociacin colectiva, an pendiente, debera profundizar en esta direccin, permitiendo una mayor adecuacin de los salarios y otras condiciones laborales a la situacin individual de las empresas. La flexibilidad interna es necesaria para establecer una relacin ms estrecha entre la evolucin de la productividad y el comportamiento del mercado de trabajo y constituye una herramienta esencial para recuperar competitividad e incrementar el dinamismo del crecimiento econmico. El nuevo marco laboral de nuestro pas debera permitir que estas ventajas se puedan aprovechar al mximo. Finalmente, al incremento de la flexibilidad y a los esfuerzos de moderacin salarial en aquellas empresas que lo necesiten para recuperar su competitividad tendr que sumarse una mejora genuina de la productividad basada en ganancias de eficiencia, pues hasta el momento su comportamiento expansivo refleja principalmente la severidad en el ajuste del empleo. Esta mejora de la productividad requiere, asimismo, profundizar en otras reformas estructurales con efectos ms dilatados en el tiempo, entre las que destacan la liberalizacin sectorial, la racionalizacin del papel del sector pblico en la actividad econmica y la mejora del sistema educativo.

Title: Intervention at the Vialogos Day
text: April 13, 2011 The consolidation of the Spanish financial sector Travelers Day Javier Ar92ztegui Deputy Governor of the Bank of Spain I would like to begin by thanking Banca C92vica for its invitation to be in Pamplona today and to present my ideas on the consolidation of the Spanish financial sector. My gratitude is double for the opportunity of returning to Navarra, the place where I have my roots and whose visit, whether for personal or professional reasons, is always a reason for satisfaction. I would like to start with a terminological precision. The concept of "consolidation of the financial sector" can be understood in a double sense: as concentration of the sector, or process of integration between entities to reduce the number of participants and increase their average size; and, in a sense more linked to the etymology of the term itself, as a process of reinforcing its "solidity". Although related, each perspective highlights a different aspect of the issue. This interrelation of efficiency and solvency is very noticeable in the restructuring of the savings bank sector. In the first sense, the consolidation of the Spanish banking sector has been accentuated in the last two years. It is not, however, a new phenomenon, but has been a constant since the liberalization of the financial sector initiated in the democratic transition. In this regard, it should be remembered that the entities carried out an intense process of concentration from 1988, which extended throughout the 90s, with mergers between the large banks that meant the rupture of the "status quo". The integration of banking favoured a strong international expansion of the main resulting groups. In the last two years it has been the turn of the savings banks. Perhaps the distinctive thing about this transformation is that it has occurred in a particularly difficult situation, with a set of forces pressuring at the same time on the situation of the entities: international financial tensions, the economic crisis in Spain, the real estate bubble, the exacerbation of sovereign risk, the crisis of confidence, etc. Therefore, the characteristic of this process of concentration of savings banks is that it has had to be encouraged with regulatory measures, including public support, to protect internal financial stability and, of course, it has been promoted by the Bank of Spain as a necessary condition to strengthen the future. Concentration understood as an increase in size should not be an end in itself, but should be accompanied by a deep internal restructuring of institutions, which reduces costs, generates synergies and improves profitability. This idea links with the second meaning of the "consolidation of the banking sector", as an improvement of its solidity, of its solvency. In this sense, the ultimate goal of the current process is to ensure the long-term viability of this sector.
