To ensure that it adapts its structure to the foreseeable turnover, its efficiency to the demands of the market and its solvency to the demands of investors, taxpayers and regulators. These three agents want institutions to operate with a substantially higher level of capital in the future. At this point, the following question should be asked: why was it necessary to face this process of concentration in savings banks? To answer we are going to go back a little in time. We are at the beginning of this twenty-first century, when the situation of the savings bank sector was very different from today. As entities closely linked to their territory, the evolution of their business was stable and was linked to the situation of the Spanish economy. In order to broaden their business base and to take advantage of the opportunities provided by the entry into the euro and the foreseeable fall in interest rates, savings banks began an intense credit expansion in the mid-nineties that culminated in the summer of 2006. This advance generated a set of imbalances with the following characteristics: - It was closely linked to the housing boom, so it was exposure to the real estate sector that grew more pronounced. - Their financing could not be served only through the retail network, so entities increasingly went to the wholesale market, mainly through mortgage bonds or securitizing assets. As a result, the weight of financing via bond issues on the markets multiplied. - The growth of the business meant an increase in structural expenses due to the creation of extensive networks of branches that, once the adjustment of activity began, were oversized. - In some cases, this expansion was not based on sound credit risk management practices. Unfortunately, certain banks favoured growth over other variables and, in setting the conditions of operations, underestimated risk premia and relaxed controls. - Finally, the legal nature of savings banks imposed limitations on access to external sources of capital of the highest quality and determined a governance regime that was less flexible than that of listed companies and less valued by investors. As a result, the boxes had less responsiveness and were subject to less market discipline. Both factors proved to be a major obstacle when high rates of dependence on wholesale funding markets and increased uncertainty typical of any crisis were combined. The greater or lesser influence of these factors established the vulnerability of each entity. And this is what happened from the summer of 2007, with the beginning of the subprime mortgage crisis and the closure of the financing markets. To all this was added the beginning of the recession of the world economy and that of the Spanish one. The liquidity of the entities suffered, as the wholesale markets were weighed down. This shortage became especially acute after the Lehman Brothers crisis. In Spain, it was decided to address the situation through the creation of the Financial Asset Acquisition Fund, designed to provide liquidity to entities through temporary securities acquisition programs. In addition, a programme to grant public guarantees for the issuance of securities was launched. These actions were not enough to cover the financing needs, so the sector seemed to rediscover retail financing channels. All this generated commercial offensives to capture deposits with attractive remuneration conditions that added new and dangerous tensions in the income statements. On the other hand, the delinquency of loan portfolios began a rapid deterioration process from the end of 2007, as a result of the economic recession and the growth of unemployment. The starting situation of Spanish banks was reasonable to face this deterioration in solvency, given the significant effort made by the sector with the constitution of the generic provision in previous years. However, the existence of this provision was not, in some cases, sufficient to stop the logical impact of the economic deterioration. In this context, the initiatives adopted by the Banco de Espa96a were of a diverse nature. First, in order to adopt a more prudent approach to portfolio valuation, the Banco de Espa96a reformed its accounting rules on insolvency provisions. The main axes of this reform were the shortening of the periods for recognition of loss due to late payment, the introduction of a criterion for the reorganization of foreclosed assets, already used in inspection practice, and the incorporation of real estate security rights into the calculation of the provision for insolvencies. Going a step further, the Bank of Spain collaborated very actively in the "stress tests" organized at the level of the European Union in the summer of 2010, assuming a degree of transparency much higher than that of the rest of the countries, both by extending the year to the entire Spanish financial sector, compared to the minimum of 50% used by most countries. and for providing additional detailed information. This transparency effort was not limited to stress tests, since in autumn 2010 the Bank of Spain decided to require a more detailed publication of the exposure to the construction and promotion sector at the end of the year, of the mortgage portfolio with individuals and of the financing strategies. The sector's response to this deterioration in asset quality was manifested in a significant effort to clean up, especially in real estate portfolios, and to raise capital. In this sense, and although they are already known data, allow me to recall some figures: - The joint restructuring of the Spanish banking sector in the last three years has been 96,000 million euros, around 9.5% of GDP. - The sector has also significantly strengthened its own resources in this period: the excess of capital over core own resources has increased by 53,000 million, 5% of GDP. Both strengthening efforts add up to 15 points of GDP. - If we focus on the exposure to construction and real estate development of savings banks, at the end of 2010, this reached 217,000 million, of which 100,000 million were reflected in accounting as "potentially problematic" assets, a concept that groups doubtful assets, normal assets under special supervision and those received in payment of debts. Constituted provisions account for 38% of this exposure. If we add to this the natural safety net provided by the average "Loan to Value" of the portfolios, located at around 62%, it can be said that the expected loss of these problematic investments is covered at a reasonable level. - Finally, the combination of liquidity shortages and non-performing loans is leading to worsening profitability. Given the imbalances mentioned, which had been affecting external confidence in the sector, despite the fact that most of its entities continued and continue to show good levels of solvency and efficiency, a new instrument was created, the well-known Fund for Orderly Bank Restructuring (FROB), to promote and facilitate its reorganization. I would like to highlight the main actions of the FROB since its creation: - Intervened in the restructuring process of CajaSur, after the replacement of its directors agreed by the Bank of Spain in May 2010. The agility with which the new Fund can face the management of cases of non-viable entities allowed this process to be concluded in just 55 days, through the award, in a competitive procedure, of the business to the BBK, with final aid of 392 million, instrumented through an "asset protection scheme". - Supported throughout 2010 the realization of eight processes of integration of savings banks through the subscription of preferred shares for an amount of 11,167 million. But this has not been the only legislative movement. The Savings Banks Law was amended to include corporate alternatives that would improve the access of these entities to new sources of capital and promote the professionalization of their management. In general, this new regulation opened the possibility of the "indirect exercise" of the activity through a banking entity to which the financial business is contributed, either maintaining the status of credit institution, or transforming into a foundation. Likewise, the requirements to be met by those who hold a position in the governing bodies of the savings banks were regulated and a regime of incompatibilities was established. The problems seemed reasonably limited at the beginning of the fourth quarter of last year, when a second episode of the sovereign debt crisis, located in Ireland and then in Portugal, generated a new escalation of uncertainty in the markets that especially affected Spain. As a reaction to this situation, the Government approved in February 2011 and Parliament validated in March a substantive reform of the solvency framework of credit institutions through Royal Decree-Law 2/2011, whose forecasts are currently being put into practice. I would like to comment on the main characteristics of this new regulation and the moment in which we are in its implementation. In the first place, it establishes the requirement of a new main capital ratio of 8% for all deposit institutions, which will be 10% for those entities most dependent on wholesale financing, which also do not have at least 20% of their capital on the stock market or in the hands of third parties. This new capital requirement introduces a very high level of solvency, since it revolves around the "main capital", a concept in which only the elements of the highest quality are computed, in line with the "common equity Tier 1" of Basel III in its composition scheduled for 2013, and since the required level of 8-10% is still higher than the 7% that will be requested when the implementation of this agreement is completed in 2019. Secondly, the capacity of the Fund for Orderly Bank Restructuring (FROB) to strengthen the own resources of viable entities is strengthened. The main novelty lies in the type of financial support it can provide. Compared to the previous rule, the new regulation only allows the subscription of ordinary shares, forcing the transformation of savings banks into banks, in the event that the FROB has to support their capitalization. The provision of aid will be linked to the presentation of a recapitalization plan that must be approved by the Bank of Spain and will include a detailed adjustment plan. The subscription price shall be calculated according to the market value of the institution and based on what is determined by one or more independent experts appointed for that purpose, if there is no relevant transaction data in the previous five months. The FROB is finalizing the applicable methodology for setting the value of entities. Among the effects that will be associated with the granting of aid, it is worth highlighting: - The appointment of the FROB as a director to guarantee compliance with the recapitalization plan with the proportional representation that corresponds to it in the Board of Directors. - In the case of savings banks, the transfer of the financial business to a public limited company. - The establishment of minimum rules aimed at improving corporate governance. The Bank of Spain published on March 11 the list of entities that did not reach the new required levels: 8 savings banks, 2 Spanish banks and 2 subsidiary banks of European entities. The additional capital needed to reach the new minimums is 15,152 million euros. This does not mean, obviously, that it is only public capital, since, previously, the entities are collecting private capital. The final figure may also be amended to reflect the requirements arising from the June 2011 stress tests. Until March 28, these twelve entities have had a deadline to present their strategy and implementation schedule to the Bank of Spain. Note that, after the breakup of the SIP of "Banco Base", there will finally be thirteen entities concerned. Strategies may include different types of measures, basically: (a) placing capital to third parties; (b) special transactions assessed (sale of units or portfolios, sale of networks, etc.); c) support from the FROB. A new integration process may also be considered. Tomorrow the Bank of Spain will make its decisions on these strategies and calendars, and, in the event that FROB aid is foreseen, before the end of this month of April the entities must present the specific recapitalization plans. The measures will have to be implemented by 30 September 2011. The Bank of Spain may grant an extension of three months for objective reasons of procedures that have been complicated (six months in the case of the IPO), always on objective bases. I would like to conclude by mentioning some of the remaining challenges for the coming months. First, the swift and responsible completion of the effects foreseen by the new legislation. In cases where the FROB provides public aid, the recapitalization plans must be prepared quickly, including the commitments to be assumed. From there, there must be rigorous compliance, both in scope and timing, of the measures envisaged. Secondly, the conduct of the stress tests organised by the new European Banking Authority (EBA). This year's tests are even more demanding than those carried out last year, both for the definition of the target capital (5% of core capital) and for the severity of the scenarios, with which it is expected that the results will have a high degree of credibility. Spain will once again be the European country with the largest number of entities subject to the scrutiny of supervisors, since all savings banks and all listed banks will be included. Third, it is essential that all credit institutions exercise extreme caution in their credit risk management practices, strive for efficiency and implement responsible risk, asset and liability pricing, cost rationalisation and problem asset management policies, in order to continue to effectively provide the financial intermediation services required by citizens and businesses. Fourth, by the end of 2011 it would be optimal for at least two or three banks, from former savings banks, to have started trading on the stock exchange. This milestone would mark a clear commitment to the "market discipline" of a sector that is irreversibly obliged to obtain financial resources in it, both in the form of external financing and in the form of capital. This would represent a very relevant advance in the consolidation of savings banks as a significant sector within the Spanish banking system. A tough year is coming for the income statements of the entities. I would ask everyone to face the exercise with determination, agility and rigor, but also with confidence, because, as Cervantes said, "in the shrunken spirits the good joy never took place". Thanks a lot.
text_original: 13 de abril de 2011 La consolidacin del sector financiero espaol Jornada Vilogos Javier Arztegui Subgobernador del Banco de Espaa Me gustara comenzar agradeciendo a Banca Cvica su invitacin para estar hoy en Pamplona y poder exponer mis ideas sobre la consolidacin del sector financiero espaol. Mi agradecimiento es doble por la oportunidad que supone regresar a Navarra, el lugar donde tengo mis races y cuya visita, ya sea por motivos personales o profesionales, es siempre un motivo de satisfaccin. Quisiera comenzar con una precisin terminolgica. El concepto consolidacin del sector financiero puede ser entendido en un doble sentido: como concentracin del sector, o proceso de integracin entre entidades para reducir el nmero de participantes y aumentar su tamao medio; y, en un sentido ms ligado a la propia etimologa del trmino, como proceso de refuerzo de la solidez del mismo. Aunque estn relacionadas, cada perspectiva destaca un aspecto diferente de la cuestin. Esta interrelacin de eficiencia y solvencia es muy notoria en la reestructuracin del sector de cajas de ahorro. En el primer sentido, la consolidacin del sector bancario espaol se ha acentuado en los dos ltimos aos. No es, sin embargo, un fenmeno novedoso, sino que ha sido una constante desde la liberalizacin del sector financiero iniciada en la transicin democrtica. A este respecto cabe recordar que las entidades protagonizaron un intenso proceso de concentracin a partir de 1988, que se extendi a lo largo de los 90, con fusiones entre los grandes bancos que supusieron la ruptura del statu quo. La integracin de la banca favoreci una fuerte expansin internacional de los principales grupos resultantes. En los ltimos dos aos ha llegado el turno a las cajas de ahorros. Quizs lo distintivo de esta transformacin es que se ha registrado en una coyuntura especialmente difcil, con un conjunto de fuerzas presionando a la vez sobre la situacin de las entidades: las tensiones financieras internacionales, la crisis econmica en Espaa, la burbuja inmobiliaria, la exacerbacin del riesgo soberano, la crisis de confianza, etc. Por eso, lo caracterstico de este proceso de concentracin de cajas es que ha tenido que ser animado con medidas regulatorias, incluidos apoyos pblicos, para proteger la estabilidad financiera interior y, desde luego, ha sido impulsado por el Banco de Espaa como una condicin necesaria para afianzar el futuro. La concentracin entendida como aumento de tamao no debe ser un fin en s mismo, sino que ha de ir acompaada de una profunda reestructuracin interna de las entidades, que reduzca costes, genere sinergias y mejore la rentabilidad. Esta idea enlaza con el segundo significado de la consolidacin del sector bancario, como mejora de su solidez, de su solvencia. En este sentido, el fin ltimo del actual proceso es garantizar la viabilidad a largo plazo de este sector. Conseguir que adece su estructura al volumen de negocio previsible, su eficiencia a las exigencias del mercado y su solvencia a las demandas de inversores, contribuyentes y reguladores. Estos tres agentes quieren que en el futuro las entidades acten con un nivel de capital sustancialmente mayor. En este punto, cabe realizar la siguiente pregunta por qu era necesario afrontar este proceso de concentracin en las cajas de ahorros? Para contestar vamos a remontarnos un poco en el tiempo. Nos situamos a principios de este siglo XXI, cuando la situacin del sector de cajas de ahorros era muy diferente de la actual. Como entidades muy ligadas a su territorio, la evolucin de su negocio era estable y estaba vinculada a la situacin de la economa espaola. Con el fin de ampliar su base de negocio y para aprovechar las oportunidades que proporcionaba la entrada en el euro y el previsible descenso de los tipos de inters, las cajas de ahorros iniciaron a mediados de los aos noventa una intensa expansin crediticia que culmin en el verano de 2006. Este avance gener un conjunto de desequilibrios con las siguientes caractersticas: - Estaba muy ligado al boom de la vivienda, por lo que fue la exposicin al sector inmobiliario la que creci de forma ms pronunciada. - Su financiacin no poda atenderse nicamente a travs de la red minorista, por lo que las entidades acudieron de manera creciente al mercado mayorista, principalmente por medio de cdulas hipotecarias o titulizando activos. En consecuencia, se multiplic el peso de la financiacin va emisiones de ttulos en los mercados. - El crecimiento del negocio supuso un incremento de los gastos de estructura por la creacin de redes extensas de sucursales que, una vez iniciado el ajuste de actividad, resultaron sobredimensionadas. - En ciertos casos, esta expansin no se fundament en slidas prcticas de gestin del riesgo de crdito. Por desgracia, ciertas entidades privilegiaron el crecimiento por encima de otras variables y, al fijar las condiciones de las operaciones, infravaloraron las primas de riesgo y relajaron los controles. - Por ltimo, la naturaleza jurdica de las cajas de ahorros impona limitaciones para acceder a fuentes externas de capital de la mxima calidad y determinaba un rgimen de gobierno menos flexible que el de las sociedades cotizadas y menos valorado por los inversores. En consecuencia, las cajas disponan de menos capacidad de reaccin y estaban sujetas a una menor disciplina del mercado. Ambos factores se revelaron como una traba importante cuando se conjugaban altas tasas de dependencia de los mercados de financiacin mayorista y un aumento de la incertidumbre propia de cualquier crisis. La mayor o menor influencia de estos factores estableci la vulnerabilidad de cada entidad. Y esto es lo que sucedi a partir del verano de 2007, con el inicio de la crisis de las hipotecas subprime y el cierre de los mercados de financiacin. A todo ello se sum el inicio de la recesin de la economa mundial y el de la espaola. La liquidez de las entidades se resinti, al quedar lastrados los mercados mayoristas. Esta escasez se agudiz especialmente a partir de la crisis de Lehman Brothers. En Espaa, se decidi afrontar la situacin a travs de la creacin del Fondo de Adquisicin de Activos Financieros, diseado para proveer de liquidez a las entidades mediante programas de adquisiciones temporales de valores. Adems, se puso en marcha un programa de concesin de avales pblicos en la emisin de valores. Estas actuaciones no fueron suficientes para cubrir las necesidades de financiacin, por lo que el sector pareci redescubrir las vas de financiacin minorista. Todo ello gener ofensivas comerciales para la captacin de depsitos con condiciones de remuneracin atractivas que aadieron nuevas y peligrosas tensiones en las cuentas de resultados. Por otro lado, la morosidad de las carteras crediticias comenz un rpido proceso de deterioro a partir de finales de 2007, como consecuencia de la recesin econmica y el crecimiento del desempleo. La situacin de partida de las entidades espaolas era razonable para afrontar este deterioro en la solvencia, dado el notable esfuerzo realizado por el sector con la constitucin de la provisin genrica en los aos anteriores. Sin embargo, la existencia de esta provisin no era, en algunos casos, suficiente para detener el lgico impacto del deterioro econmico. En este contexto, las iniciativas adoptadas por el Banco de Espaa fueron de diversa naturaleza. En primer lugar, con el fin de adoptar un enfoque ms prudente en la valoracin de las carteras, el Banco de Espaa reform sus normas contables sobre provisiones de insolvencias. Los principales ejes de esa reforma fueron el acortamiento de los plazos de reconocimiento de la prdida por morosidad, la introduccin de un criterio de saneamiento de los activos adjudicados, ya utilizado en la prctica de inspeccin, y la incorporacin de las garantas reales inmobiliarias al clculo de la provisin por insolvencias. Yendo un paso ms all, el Banco de Espaa colabor muy activamente en las pruebas de resistencia organizadas a nivel de la Unin Europea en el verano de 2010, asumiendo un grado de transparencia muy superior al del resto de pases, tanto por extender el ejercicio a la totalidad del sector financiero espaol, frente al mnimo del 50% que utilizan la mayora de los pases, como por facilitar informacin adicional de detalle. Este esfuerzo de transparencia no se limit a las pruebas de resistencia, ya que en otoo de 2010 el Banco de Espaa decidi exigir una publicacin ms detallada de la exposicin al sector de la construccin y promocin al cierre del ejercicio, de la cartera hipotecaria con particulares y de las estrategias de financiacin. La respuesta del sector a este deterioro de la calidad de los activos se manifest en un notable esfuerzo de saneamiento, en especial en las carteras inmobiliarias, y de captacin de capital. En este sentido, y aunque son datos ya conocidos, permtanme recordar algunas cifras: - El saneamiento conjunto del sector bancario espaol en los ltimos tres aos ha sido de 96.000 millones de euros, en torno al 9,5% del PIB. - El sector tambin ha reforzado significativamente sus recursos propios en este perodo: el exceso de capital sobre los recursos propios bsicos se ha incrementado en 53.000 millones, un 5% del PIB. Ambos esfuerzos de reforzamiento suman 15 puntos del PIB. - Si nos centramos en la exposicin a la construccin y promocin inmobiliaria de las cajas de ahorros, a cierre de 2010, esta alcanzaba 217.000 millones, de los que 100.000 millones estaban reflejados contablemente como activos potencialmente problemticos, concepto que agrupa a los activos dudosos, los normales bajo vigilancia especial y los recibidos en pago de deudas. Las provisiones constituidas alcanzan el 38% de esta exposicin. Si a ello se aade la natural red de seguridad proporcionada por el Loan to Value medio de las carteras, situado en el entorno del 62%, se puede afirmar que la prdida esperada de estas inversiones problemticas est cubierta en un nivel razonable. - Por ltimo, la combinacin de escasez de liquidez y morosidad est provocando un empeoramiento de la rentabilidad. Ante los desequilibrios enunciados, que venan afectando a la confianza externa en el sector, a pesar de que la mayor parte de sus entidades seguan y siguen mostrando unos buenos niveles de solvencia y eficiencia, se cre un nuevo instrumento, el ya conocido Fondo de Reestructuracin Ordenada Bancario (FROB), para impulsar y facilitar su reordenacin. Me gustara resaltar las principales actuaciones del FROB desde su creacin: - Intervino en el proceso de reestructuracin de CajaSur, despus de la sustitucin de sus administradores acordada por el Banco de Espaa en mayo de 2010. La agilidad con que el nuevo Fondo puede afrontar la gestin de casos de entidades no viables permiti concluir este proceso en solo 55 das, mediante la adjudicacin, en un procedimiento competitivo, del negocio a la BBK, con unas ayudas finales de 392 millones, instrumentadas mediante un esquema de proteccin de activos. - Apoy a lo largo de 2010 la realizacin de ocho procesos de integracin de cajas de ahorro a travs de la suscripcin de participaciones preferentes por un importe de 11.167 millones. Pero este no ha sido el nico movimiento legislativo. Se reform la Ley de Cajas de Ahorros para incluir alternativas societarias que mejorasen el acceso de estas entidades a nuevas fuentes de capital e impulsasen la profesionalizacin de su gestin. En lneas generales, esta nueva regulacin abri la posibilidad del ejercicio indirecto de la actividad a travs de una entidad bancaria a la que se aporta el negocio financiero, bien manteniendo la condicin de entidad de crdito, bien transformndose en una fundacin. Asimismo, se regularon los requisitos que deben cumplir quienes ostenten un cargo en los rganos rectores de las cajas y se estableci un rgimen de incompatibilidades. Los problemas parecan razonablemente acotados al inicio del cuarto trimestre del ao pasado, cuando un segundo episodio de la crisis de la deuda soberana, localizado en Irlanda y despus en Portugal, gener una nueva escalada de incertidumbre en los mercados que afect especialmente a Espaa. Como reaccin ante esta situacin, el Gobierno aprob en febrero de 2011 y el Parlamento convalid en marzo una reforma sustantiva del marco de solvencia de las entidades de crdito mediante el Real Decreto-Ley 2/2011, cuyas previsiones estn ponindose en prctica en estos momentos. Me gustara comentar las principales caractersticas de esta nueva regulacin y el momento en que nos encontramos en su puesta en marcha. En primer lugar, se establece la exigencia de un nuevo ratio de capital principal del 8% para todas las entidades de depsito, que ser del 10% para aquellas entidades ms dependientes de la financiacin mayorista, que adems no tengan, al menos, un 20% de su capital en Bolsa o en manos de terceros. Este nuevo requerimiento de capital introduce un nivel de solvencia muy elevado, puesto que gira sobre el capital principal, concepto en el que computan solo los elementos de la mxima calidad, en lnea con el common equity Tier 1 de Basilea III en su composicin prevista para 2013, y puesto que el nivel exigido del 8-10% es todava superior al 7% que se pedir cuando se complete la implantacin de este acuerdo en 2019. En segundo lugar, se potencia la capacidad de actuacin del Fondo de Reestructuracin Ordenada Bancaria (FROB) para reforzar los recursos propios de entidades viables. La principal novedad se encuentra en el tipo de apoyos financieros que puede prestar. Frente a la regla anterior, la nueva regulacin solo permite la suscripcin de acciones ordinarias, obligando a la transformacin de las cajas en bancos, en el supuesto de que el FROB tenga que respaldar su capitalizacin. La prestacin de ayudas estar ligada a la presentacin de un plan de recapitalizacin que deber ser aprobado por el Banco de Espaa y que incluir un plan detallado de ajustes. El precio de suscripcin se cifrar de acuerdo con el valor de mercado de la entidad y basndose en lo que determinen uno o varios expertos independientes nombrados al efecto, si no hay datos de transacciones relevantes en los cincos meses anteriores. El FROB est ultimando la metodologa aplicable para la fijacin del valor de las entidades. Entre los efectos que llevar aparejada la concesin de ayudas, hay que destacar: - El nombramiento del FROB como consejero para garantizar el cumplimiento del plan de recapitalizacin con la representacin proporcional que le corresponda en el Consejo de Administracin. - En el caso de las cajas de ahorros, el traspaso del negocio financiero a una sociedad annima bancaria. - El establecimiento de unas reglas mnimas tendentes a la mejora en el gobierno corporativo. El Banco de Espaa public el 11 de marzo pasado la lista de entidades que no alcanzaban los nuevos niveles exigibles: 8 cajas de ahorros, 2 bancos espaoles y 2 bancos filiales de entidades europeas. El capital adicional necesario para alcanzar los nuevos mnimos es de 15.152 millones de euros. Esto no supone, obviamente, que sea solo capital pblico, ya que, previamente, las entidades estn acopiando capital privado. Asimismo, la cifra final podr modificarse tambin para reflejar las exigencias que se deriven de las pruebas de resistencia de junio de 2011. Hasta el 28 de marzo, estas doce entidades han tenido plazo para presentar al Banco de Espaa su estrategia y el calendario de instrumentacin. Ntese que, tras la ruptura del SIP de Banco Base, finalmente sern trece las entidades concernidas. Las estrategias pueden incluir distintos tipos de medidas, bsicamente: a) colocacin de capital a terceros; b) operaciones especiales tasadas (venta de participaciones o carteras, venta de redes); c) apoyo del FROB. Tambin puede plantearse algn nuevo proceso de integracin. Maana mismo el Banco de Espaa tomar sus decisiones sobre estas estrategias y calendarios, y, en el caso de que se prevean ayudas del FROB, antes de fin de este mes de abril las entidades debern presentar los planes concretos de recapitalizacin. Las medidas tendrn que ejecutarse antes del 30 de septiembre de 2011. El Banco de Espaa podr conceder una prrroga de tres meses por razones objetivas de trmites que se han complicado (seis meses si se trata de la salida a Bolsa), siempre sobre bases objetivas. Quisiera terminar mencionando algunos de los retos pendientes para los prximos meses. Primero, la culminacin gil y responsable de los efectos previstos por la nueva legislacin. En los casos en que el FROB preste ayudas pblicas, tienen que prepararse rpidamente los planes de recapitalizacin, incluyendo los compromisos a asumir. A partir de ah, debe haber un cumplimiento riguroso, tanto en el alcance como en los tiempos, de las medidas previstas. Segundo, la realizacin de las pruebas de resistencia organizadas por la nueva Autoridad Bancaria Europea (ABE). Las pruebas de este ao son an ms exigentes que las realizadas el ao pasado, tanto por la definicin del capital objetivo (5% de core capital) como por la severidad de los escenarios, con lo que se espera que los resultados tengan un alto grado de credibilidad. Espaa va a volver a ser el pas europeo con un mayor nmero de entidades sometidas al escrutinio de los supervisores, ya que se incluir a todas las cajas de ahorros y a todos los bancos cotizados. Tercero, es fundamental que todas las entidades de crdito extremen la prudencia en sus prcticas de gestin del riesgo de crdito, batallen por la eficiencia y apliquen polticas responsables de riesgos, de fijacin de precios de activos y pasivos, de racionalizacin de costes y de gestin de activos problemticos, para seguir prestando con eficacia los servicios de intermediacin financiera que requieren los ciudadanos y las empresas. Cuarto, a final de 2011 sera ptimo que al menos dos o tres bancos, procedentes de antiguas cajas de ahorros, hubiesen iniciado su cotizacin en Bolsa. Este hito marcara un compromiso claro con la disciplina de mercado de un sector que irreversiblemente est obligado a obtener recursos financieros en l, tanto en forma de financiacin ajena como en forma de capital. Esto supondra un avance muy relevante en la consolidacin de las cajas de ahorros como un sector significativo dentro del sistema bancario espaol. Se avecina un ao 2011 duro para las cuentas de resultados de las entidades. Yo pedira a todos afrontar el ejercicio con decisin, agilidad y rigor, pero tambin con confianza, porque, como deca Cervantes, en los nimos encogidos nunca tuvo lugar la buena dicha. Muchas gracias.

Title: Presentation of the Annual Report to the Governing Council of the Banco de Espaa
text: 2010 PRESENTATION OF THE ANNUAL REPORT Speech by the Governor to the Governing Council of Banco de Espa SPEECH PRESENTING THE ANNUAL REPORT TO THE GOVERNING COUNCIL OF THE BANCO DE ESPA84A Miguel Fernandez Ordez GOVERNOR Legal depito: M. 25493-2011 Printing house of Banco de Espa SPEECH PRESENTING THE ANNUAL REPORT TO THE GOVERNING COUNCIL OF THE BANCO DE ESPA84A Ladies and gentlemen counsellors, About a year ago, I began my speech presenting the Annual Report, 2009 highlighting the complexity of the economic situation that was then experienced in Europe, in general, and in Spain, in particular. The EU Heads of State and Government had just approved the programme of financial assistance to Greece and the first steps of a process of profound reform of the European system of governance were beginning to be glimpsed. The Spanish economic policy, for its part, was beginning a shift in the right direction, focusing on fiscal consolidation, the completion of the consolidation and restructuring of the financial system, and the implementation of supply-side structural policies, once the margins for demand-boosting policies had been completely exhausted. When we review what has happened since then, as does the Annual Report, 2010 that I now present to you, attention is drawn to what progress has been made in the processes that were then undertaken, although the situation remains very complex both in Europe and in our country. Over the past year, the recovery process of the world economy has been consolidated, reaching a growth rate of 5%. Europe, and in particular the euro area, also shares this consolidation in growth, although GDP growth is considerably more modest: 1.7% in EMU as a whole, with significant differences between the economies of the Member States. In Spain, after the serious recession of the previous year, a very weak recovery began in 2010, in an external context dominated by tensions in European debt markets, which have added an additional dose of pressure on their own conditions that are already complex and demanding. The sovereign debt crisis is the most serious shock since the founding of the American currency and poses a major challenge for European authorities and Member State governments. The outbreak of the Greek fiscal crisis in May last year and the rapid extension of the difficulties to the whole area clearly highlighted the existence of serious shortcomings in the institutional fabric of the euro. Problems were identified in three main areas: the limited capacity of the Stability and Growth Pact and national fiscal frameworks to ensure the exercise of fiscal policies in line with the requirements of membership of a monetary union; the absence of effective multilateral consultation, coordination and surveillance mechanisms to identify and prevent in good time the accumulation of macroeconomic imbalances in other areas; and, finally, the lack of instruments and procedures necessary to manage and resolve crisis situations which, such as those first raised by Greece and, later, by Ireland and Portugal, have serious repercussions for the stability of the whole area. Over the past few months, significant progress has been made in all three areas. When the European Parliament has completed the legislative initiatives currently under way, the European Union will have emerged from this process with a new and strengthened Stability and Growth Pact, more attentive than in the past to the behaviour of the debt and more automatic in its way of operating, as well as with revised and improved national fiscal frameworks. Europe will also have a new effective system for the detection and early correction of other possible macroeconomic imbalances of a non-fiscal nature and a permanent crisis management mechanism, the so-called 'European Stability Mechanism'. It is to be hoped that, once this process of governance reform is completed, the European Union will have powerful mechanisms to effectively prevent and resolve crisis episodes such as the current one. In the short term, however, the situation in the Irish, Portuguese and, above all, Greek economies poses pressing problems. The transition to the new governance framework is taking place amid the most tense episode in the euro area's short history. It would be a serious mistake to underestimate the risks involved. If the current problems are not resolved, efforts to reshape the institutional fabric of the euro may prove futile. In critical situations such as the current one, which to a greater or lesser degree have marked the process of building the European project, it is important to maintain a historical perspective. Overcoming difficulties has always been the result of the effort, collaboration and open-mindedness of those who had the responsibility of making decisions that were not always easy. If this trajectory continues, European leaders will be able to appreciate the enormous benefits for all member countries of the high degree of economic and financial integration that has been achieved within the European Union and particularly the Economic and Monetary Union, and will set aside short-sighted and short-term approaches that could trigger a setback with unforeseeable consequences. The Spanish economy is by no means alien to this trajectory of the European project that links the future of each of the participating economies to the becoming com. In fact, it was affected with singular severity during the episodes of the sovereign debt crisis in Greece and Ireland, although not so much in April of this year. when Portugal requested financial assistance and the Spanish spread maintained a more primitive behavior than economies such as Italy or Belgium. In any case, difficulties have been persistently present throughout the scam, fluctuations have been constant and sovereign risk premia have remained too high. The cautious attitude of investors reflects the confluence of the instability of the euro area with the elements of vulnerability that the Spanish economy drags as a result of the imbalances accumulated during the long expansionary phase and others that emerged during the crisis. The origin and development of the imbalances that were generated during the long period of expansion are well known. Suffice it to recall here that strong demand pressures, fuelled by falling interest rates, rapid credit growth and the appreciation of real estate assets, could not be offset by the ability of supply to react, and with the persistent excess demand and all its aftermath eventually exhausting the pattern and pace of growth that had been followed until then. giving way to a complex and inevitably costly adjustment process. Very loose monetary and financial conditions created the breeding ground for the appearance of some macroeconomic and financial imbalances that fed each other. On the one hand, the excess of real estate expansion, based on abundant financing of promotional activities, causes rapid indebtedness of the private sector and, in return, the oversizing of the financial system and a growing recourse to international wholesale markets in search of financing. On the other hand, the continuous increase in costs and relative prices for more than ten years was accumulating a competitiveness problem that contributes to shifting spending abroad. The resulting heavy dependence on external financing should be an element of exposure of the Spanish economy to the episodes of mistrust that were unleashed in international financial markets in the wake of the sovereign debt crisis. The recession added difficulties. On the one hand, the destruction of employment reached great intensity as a result of the institutional singularities of our labour market, the poor functioning of which made the burden of adjustments excessively fall on employment. This burdensome differential feature calls into question, among other things, the ability to absorb the surplus employment generated by the housing crisis, to recover long-term growth potential and to ensure the sustainability of the accounts of the accounts, to which I shall refer below. Indeed, the intensity of the contraction in domestic expenditure and the deterioration of the labour market had a significant effect on financial requirements. Despite the favourable starting situation d1 a surplus of close to 3 % of GDP and a debt of 36 % of GDP in 2007 d1 the deficit of the public administrations increased during the crisis to 11.1 % of GDP in 2009, and the debt ratio increased by around 17 pp of GDP, reaching 53.3% of GDP that same year, although still below the average in Europe and in the countries where the sovereign debt crisis would end up hitting hardest. Beyond the factors that led to the speed and magnitude of the deterioration of the fiscal situation, which are discussed in detail in the Annual Report that I am presenting today, it is important to note that this development occurred at a time when market scrutiny focused precisely on detecting any possible problems for the sustainability of finances. So it decisively influences the financial tensions that hovered over the Spanish economy. In the climate of alert, the comparatively low level of debt did not matter so much as its rate of deterioration and the possible consequences of the high levels of private sector indebtedness, the needs of financial sector consolidation or the difficulties for the economy to grow at a sufficiently high rate. In fact, the development of this crisis has once again highlighted that excessive indebtedness, regardless of whether it comes directly from the Public Administrations or the private sector, tends to negatively affect the perception of fiscal sustainability. The crisis also ended up affecting the Spanish financial system which, although it had overcome the impact of the international financial crisis without excessive difficulty, was subjected to a greater pressure when all the components of the macroeconomic crisis itself emerged. The increase in non-performing loans, especially in the real estate development sector, in which a significant part of the loan portfolio had been concentrated, and the tightening of financing conditions in the wholesale financial markets that accompanied the decline in investor confidence in the Spanish economy were particularly demanding for some banks, Savings banks mainly. And, although the difficulties were limited to a limited segment of the sector, market pressures extended at the most acute moments to the system as a whole, relatively independent of the particular situation of each entity. As a result of all these factors, when the sovereign debt crisis erupted in Europe, the Spanish economy was in a situation of high exposure to contagion of financial instability. It was therefore essential to change the orientation of economic policy in order to reaffirm confidence and counteract the speculations that had been unleashed as a result of the mechanical extrapolation of the negative experiences of other countries with serious vulnerabilities. The responsiveness of economic politics and the perception of its firmness were the only barriers that could stop indiscriminate impulses of mistrust. Firstly, and given the origin of the tensions, it is urgent to dispel doubts about the trajectory of the financial envelopes. To this end, a demanding fiscal consolidation plan was approved in May last year, bringing forward to 2010 and 2011 the bulk of the adjustment that had to be made until 2013, and had a decisive impact on the structural component of the deficit and, within this, mainly on plentiful spending. At the same time, the urgency of addressing labour market failures that hampered the absorption of unemployment and the adjustment of the economy became apparent. A process of labour market reform was then initiated, in the first steps of which the collective bargaining system was excluded. In the financial field, the restructuring process that had begun a year earlier is accelerating, profoundly transforming the savings bank sector. All these developments had an impact on the evolution of the Spanish economy, which in the first half of 2010 began a still very weak recovery trajectory, which has lasted with a similar tone in the first months of this year. At the same time, the correction of accumulated imbalances continues to progress at a reasonable pace. The adjustment of the excess of real estate investment continues, with additional cuts in the activity of the sector and in house prices. And also the financing needs of the nation were reduced, although at an increasingly moderate pace, as a result of the negative impact on the trade balance of the increase in oil prices. Core inflation, by timo, remained moderate, taking into account the effect of the increase in indirect taxes from 1 July. The general price index rebounded sharply in the second half of 2010 and in the first months of 2010, driven by the upward trend in commodity prices and changes in regulated prices. Given the transitory nature of many of these impulses, this trajectory should be reversed in the first months, if the effects of the second round are stopped. This is an essential condition for progress in the necessary improvement of competitiveness and to avoid the fact that a lasting increase in the inflation rate would inflict on the constrained spending capacity of households. For its part, the process of restructuring the non-financial private sector, which needs to reduce its debt levels in order to resume the dynamism of spending, is manifesting itself in a slight reduction in the outstanding stock of credit to households and companies, which is contracting at a rate of 1% and 2% per year, respectively. In the case of companies, there is a pattern differentiated by productive sectors in which loans to those most indebted, such as real estate development, fell at a faster rate d1at around 3%, in the first quarter of 2011d1, while the bulk of the debt of Spanish households is materialized in mortgages with significantly long average maturities and predetermined amortization patterns, So it is difficult to expect its volume to shrink rapidly in a context like the current one. On the other hand, financial tensions have resulted in more restrictive criteria in the granting of loans, which have become more effective with the worsening of the sovereign debt crisis and which are affecting to a greater extent the sectors with greater difficulties in proving their ability to repay in the current adverse conditions. It is essential that the process of rebalancing in which the economy is immersed moves quickly so that greater dynamism is restored in the medium term, although it is inevitable that, in the short term, the adjustment itself will restrict the intensity of the recovery. In 2010 and in the elapsed part of 2011, the withdrawal of expansionary fiscal impulses and their replacement by a firm consolidation programme, the correction in the construction sector and the financial consolidation needs of firms and households limit the possibilities for reviving expenditure, as can be expected to continue in the first quarters. Fortunately, these contractionary effects are being offset by the strength of exports, which must act as the main factor in boosting activity and incomes, for which the achievement of additional gains in competitiveness, which, in fact, is the main variable that the economy has to overcome the current difficult situation, will be decisive. When this phase is completed, the improvement of the equity position of families and companies will allow business consumption and investment to be in a better position to sustainably maintain a more dynamic trajectory. In turn, achieving the objectives of the fiscal consolidation programme will help to dispel doubts about the sustainability of our finances. And it is to be hoped that this will result in a normalization of financing conditions, which should also benefit from the completion of the process of restructuring the financial system. However, for this scenario to take hold, it is necessary to overcome the obstacles that, even today, hinder recovery. The drift taken by the sovereign debt crisis will be a major conditioner, which is beyond the control of Spanish economic policy. But the role of our economic policy remains fundamental, in any scenario, to overcome the inefficiencies that have become apparent, to reduce the mistrust that hinders and makes more expensive the essential external financing and to protect the Spanish economy from any incident that may occur in the European sphere. The fiscal consolidation that began in the past has begun to yield its first results, although the effort that lies ahead is considerable and will require great determination to define and implement the necessary measures. In 2010, the deficit of the Public Administrations fell by almost 2 pps, slightly below the projected level (9.2% of GDP). However, the intensity of adjustment and compliance with targets were uneven across administrations. The greatest breakthrough took place in the Central Administration. On the contrary, the deficit of the Autonomous Communities increased slightly, compared to the planned reduction, and there were small deviations with respect to what was programmed in the Local Corporations and in Social Security. Meeting the fiscal targets in 2011 will entail an additional 3 pp reduction in the deficit balance of the Public Administrations, which must come mostly from the structural component, as happened in the past. This is a considerable effort, both from the point of view of the size of the cut and the inertia that some expenditure items have traditionally shown. In the current circumstances, strict compliance with the announced plans is inexcusable, for which a vigilant and preventive attitude must be maintained to prevent the materialization of possible deviations and, in case they emerge, immediately implement the necessary measures to correct them, as the Government has committed to do. All fiscal discipline mechanisms provided by our budgetary framework must continue to be used to correct deviations that may arise. Such is the case of the strict application and without exceptions of the system of debt authorizations of the Autonomous Communities, by which these are conditioned to the fulfillment of the deficit objectives and to the approval of rebalancing plans in case of deviations. The application in our country of some of the ideas that are being considered in the European debate on the most effective budgetary frameworks to ensure fiscal discipline should also be explored. In particular, budgetary frameworks that combine flat deficit rules with specific spending limits appear to deliver the best results, allowing action on the primary sources of fiscal deficits and forcing cyclical overcollections to be used to improve the fiscal position. In this line, the Government has announced its intention to incorporate into the Budget Stability Law a rule according to which the expenditure of the Public Administrations may not exceed the medium-term growth rate of reference of the Spanish economy. It will be of immediate application to the Central Administration of the State and to the local entities and will promote its adoption by the Autonomous Communities. A fiscal rule of this type applied to all public administrations during the years prior to the financial crisis, when tax collection reached very high but largely transitory growth linked to the real estate boom, would have allowed for more far-reaching improvements in the underlying fiscal position and would have avoided the risk of overvaluation of the margin of available expenditure. To maximize its effectiveness, its application at all levels of government must be guaranteed and the mechanism for correcting possible deviations that occur must be made explicit. It is also necessary to strengthen transparency, in particular by extending information on the budgetary execution of the various administrations. On this point, allow me to assess positively the significant progress that has been made since the end of last year in the dissemination of data on the budgetary execution of the autonomous communities. The absence of this information was a historical lack that had proved particularly dangerous at a time when the lack of information could lead to market distrust. Access to it partially fills this gap, but to fully dispel doubts about the state of regional finances, additional steps must be taken. In particular, it would be desirable to have a regular publication of the whole and of each autonomous community, with the same periodicity, degree of detail, lag and ease of access as those of the State. In summary, in order to prevent the risks of non-compliance with the path of fiscal consolidation from materializing, it is essential to involve all administrations in the adjustment process, reiterate the institutional commitment to budgetary stability and strengthen the mechanisms to enforce the rules, increase the transparency of the accounts and strengthen budgetary planning in the medium term. Fiscal consolidation must also be accompanied by an ambitious programme of structural reforms in this area to improve the capacity to generate employment and growth. And not only because in the short term it is vital to boost the growth of tax bases and reduce the spending components most linked to the cycle. But, above all, because in the medium term finance faces important challenges linked, mainly, to the need to finance the growth of budgetary expenditure that will generate the aging of the population. A problem whose order of magnitude may be subject to controversy, but which will undoubtedly emerge in Spain in horizons less and less distant in time, as it has already begun to do in other developed countries. That is why I believe that the proposal for reform of the pension system presented by the government in January of this year is a crucial step towards ensuring the sustainability of our finances, which are reflected in the corresponding legislative rules, and with the necessary precision as regards the sustainability factor, must not be delayed. It is an example of actions that take advantage of the complementarity between the sustainability of finance and the creation of structural conditions on the supply side, and this has been understood by the markets. Regarding the restructuring of the financial system, already in 2009 a transcendental regulatory step was taken with the creation of the Fund for Orderly Bank Restructuring (FROB), which was completed last year with the reform of the legal regime of the Savings Banks and in February of this year, with Royal Decree Law 2/2011, which has accelerated the restructuring process, in addition to demanding higher levels of capital and the highest quality. Since the process began, progress has been made in different areas that make up the transformation strategy of our banking sector. Indeed, since January 2008 institutions have recognised and assumed losses on the value of their assets amounting to db96 billion, equivalent to 9% of GDP. The savings bank sector, which was highly fragmented, has increased from 45 institutions to 18 through integration processes accompanied by plans to reduce their installed capacity, which require reductions in the number of offices, employees and other operating costs. The new requirement for greater regulatory capital forces all Spanish entities to operate with a higher level of capital and encourages obtaining it in the market, either through IPOs or through the entry of private investors. Finally, the practical transformation of savings banks into banks has been carried out, including those entities that, in accordance with Royal Decree Law 2/2011, did not need to increase their main capital. An essential tool for accelerating reform of the sector has been transparency. Spain has published the stress tests of all listed savings banks and banks, which, as is known, no other European country has done. Analysts and media around the world have the information they need to assess the situation of small Spanish entities, something that cannot be done in other countries. In addition, all banks have been required to publish in great detail their exposures to the most problematic assets and the main lines of their financing structure with their maturities. Finally, and unlike what is usual in other countries, the methodologies of valuation and requirement of provisions are plicates. Transparency has drawbacks in the short term, because no one can talk about what they do not know, while, when information is provided, it attracts everyone's attention. However, transparency has proved to be a very useful tool for this reform, because it has helped the opinion to understand the need to transform the sector, helps to dispel doubts about the soundness of the Spanish banking sector and is encouraging managers and authorities to undertake restructuring without delay. The process of recapitalizing savings banks is proceeding at a relatively leisurely pace. This is due to the fact that the strategy followed in Spain has not been limited to a simple recapitalization through the injection of taxpayer resources into banking entities, but has proposed to undertake a profound and lasting transformation of the sector. In addition, the savings banks have been given the possibility of voluntarily disposing and undertaking their restructuring, so that only if the plans presented are not viable, or are not fulfilled, will the entities be assigned to others through competitive procedures. Finally, the fact that priority has been given to private initiatives inevitably consumes more time than nationalisations used in other latitudes, but it should show significant advantages in the medium and long term, in terms of cost for taxpayers and, above all, the solidity and durability of new projects. However, it should be noted that the process is being complied with in the terms and deadlines provided for in Royal Decree Law 2/2011. On March 11, the Bank of Spain published the capital needs of all entities. After the withdrawal of one of the integration projects, thirteen entities turned out to need to increase their capital. On April 14, the Bank of Spain approved the strategies and timetables presented by these entities. Two of them were subsidiary banks of foreign entities that are being recapitalized by their parent companies. Two other Spanish banks strengthened their capital by going to the market. Of the remaining entities d1nine savings banks or groups of themd1, four raised as a priority to increase their capital in the market, with the FROB acting as a subsidiary alternative. Another fund of the nine mentioned has shown its preference to participate in an integration process with another more capitalized entity. Finally, the remaining savings banks have indicated as their preferred option to increase their capital by going to the FROB. Entities that have chosen to go to the market, either through IPOs or through the entry into their capital of private investors, are now in the process of bquest, negotiation and valuation associated with this strategy. For the savings banks that have requested the participation of the FROB in their capital, the business and recapitalization plans are being analyzed, and the valuation processes of the entities have also been initiated by independent experts. In light of the progress made, and if the established timetable continues to be met, by September 30 of this year, without prejudice to the extra deadlines provided for in the Decree, the panorama will have been sufficiently clarified. Banco de Espa considers that the capital requirements required by Royal Decree Law 2/2011 are sufficient to ensure the soundness of the Spanish banking system, not only in the most likely macroeconomic scenario, but also in stressed scenarios with very low probabilities of occurrence. As I can tell, some analysts considered that capital needs could be higher in the future. If that were the case, that is, if the stress tests showed additional capital needs and these were not covered by either the entities or the market, the FROB would provide the additional funds required by such stress tests, as provided for in the Royal Decree. In any case, even the most pessimistic forecasts about the future of the Spanish economy point to requirements for plastic resources that would mean modest increases in Spanish debt that would entail modest increases in Spanish debt lies. Finally, improving the functioning of the labour market remains the most necessary and imperative economic policy task. As I have stressed on many occasions, it is essential to bring our institutional and legal framework closer to the models of other developed countries that combine the obligatory protection of the worker with a flexibility that allows improving the capacity to reallocate employment between companies and sectors. Within the euro, this task has become urgent to consolidate the recovery in the short term and to increase long-term growth and productivity prospects. Without the tool of devaluation, only a profound reform in this field will allow competitiveness to recover promptly without having to pay the very high social costs of letting the mere passage of time generate the necessary productivity gains. Last Friday the Government approved a Decree Law that contains some improvement in the regulation of collective bargaining. However, it is to be hoped that progress will be made in the parliamentary process, above all, in allowing workers and employers to decide what they think is convenient to improve the productivity and competitiveness of their companies, because without it our economy will continue to pay an excessively high price for a long time in terms of unemployment and low growth. And, of course, the importance of this reform of the institutional framework for employment should not lead us to forget that, in order to enhance and accelerate its effects, it should also be accompanied by a deepening of increased competition in the markets for goods and services. In short, we are at a crucial moment, in which the success in the orientation and management of economic policies is decisive for the future of the Spanish economy. Its approval and correct execution would also be Spain's best contribution to solving the euro crisis. If, in addition, the rest of the European countries address with broad vision the problems that threaten the stability of the eurozone, when we meet next year to present the Annual Report, the economic outlook for Spain and Europe could be much more benign and predictable than it is today, in the midst of the crisis. We are able to see. And, one more, I close this intervention by thanking all the staff of this house, and their government supporters, for the effort and work deployed in the fulfillment of the tasks that our country has entrusted to us.
text_original: PRESENTACIN 2010 DEL INFORME ANUAL Discurso pronunciado por el Gobernador ante el Consejo de Gobierno del Banco de Espa DISCURSO DE PRESENTACIN DEL INFORME ANUAL ANTE EL CONSEJO DE GOBIERNO DEL BANCO DE ESPAA Miguel Fernndez Ordez GOBERNADOR Depito legal: M. 25493-2011 Imprenta del Banco de Espa DISCURSO DE PRESENTACIN DEL INFORME ANUAL ANTE EL CONSEJO DE GOBIERNO DEL BANCO DE ESPAA Sras. y Sres. consejeros: Hace ahora aproximadamente un a, iniciaba mi discurso de presentaci del Informe Anual, 2009 resaltando la complejidad de la situaci econica que entonces se viva en Europa, en general, y en Espa, en particular. La poltica econica espala, por su parte, iniciaba un giro en la direcci adecuada, centrndose en la consolidaci fiscal, la culminaci del saneamiento y reestructuraci del sistema financiero y la instrumentaci de polticas estructurales de oferta, una vez que se haban agotado por completo los mrgenes para las polticas de impulso de la demanda. Cuando se repasa lo ocurrido desde entonces, como hace el Informe Anual, 2010 que ahora les presento, llama la atenci lo que se ha avanzado en los procesos que entonces se emprendieron, aunque la situaci sigue siendo muy compleja tanto en Europa como en nuestro pas. A lo largo del pasado ejercicio se consolidel proceso de recuperaci de la economa mundial, que alcanzuna tasa de crecimiento del 5 %. Europa, y en particular el rea del euro, participtambin de esa consolidaci del crecimiento, aunque el avance del PIB resultbastante ms modesto: un 1,7 % en el conjunto de la UEM, y con notables diferencias entre las economas de los Estados miembros. En Espa, tras la grave recesi del a anterior, en 2010 se iniciuna recuperaci muy dbil, en un contexto externo dominado por las tensiones en los mercados de deuda europeos, que han adido una dosis adicional de presi sobre unos condicionamientos propios que ya de por s resultan complejos y exigentes. La crisis de deuda soberana es la perturbaci ms grave desde la fundaci de la moneda ica y supone un reto de primera magnitud para las autoridades europeas y para los Gobiernos de los Estados miembros. El estallido de la crisis fiscal griega en mayo del pasado a y la rpida extensi de las dificultades al conjunto del rea pusieron claramente de manifiesto la existencia de carencias serias en el entramado institucional del euro. Los problemas se manifestaron en tres reas principales: la limitada capacidad del Pacto de Estabilidad y Crecimiento y de los marcos fiscales nacionales para garantizar un ejercicio de las polticas fiscales acorde con los requerimientos que se derivan de la pertenencia a una uni monetaria; la ausencia de mecanismos eficaces de consulta, coordinaci y vigilancia multilateral para identificar y prevenir con suficiente antelaci la acumulaci de desequilibrios macroeconicos en otros mbitos; y, finalmente, la carencia del instrumental y de los procedimientos necesarios para gestionar y resolver situaciones de crisis que, como las planteadas primeramente por Grecia y, ms tarde, por Irlanda y por Portugal, tienen graves repercusiones para la estabilidad del conjunto del rea. Europa dispondr, adems, de un nuevo sistema eficaz para la detecci y la correcci temprana de otros posibles desequilibrios macroeconicos de naturaleza no fiscal y de un mecanismo permanente de gesti de crisis, el denominado Mecanismo Europeo de Estabilidad. En situaciones crticas como la actual, que en mayor o menor grado han jalonado el proceso de construcci del proyecto com europeo, es importante mantener una perspectiva histica. La economa espala no es, en absoluto, ajena a esta trayectoria del proyecto europeo que vincula el futuro de cada una de las economas participantes al devenir com. En todo caso, las dificultades han estado presentes de manera persistente a lo largo del timo a, los vaivenes han sido constantes y las primas de riesgo soberano se han mantenido en niveles demasiado elevados. La actitud precavida de los inversores refleja la confluencia de la inestabilidad de la zona del euro con los elementos de vulnerabilidad que la economa espala arrastra como consecuencia de los desequilibrios acumulados durante la larga fase expansiva y de otros que emergieron durante la crisis. El origen y el desarrollo de los desequilibrios que se generaron durante la larga etapa de expansi son sobradamente conocidos. Basta con recordar aqu co las fuertes presiones de demanda, alimentadas por el descenso de los tipos de inters, el rpido cre cimiento del crdito y la revalorizaci de los activos inmobiliarios, no pudieron ser contrarrestadas por la capacidad de reacci de la oferta, y co el persistente exceso de demanda y todas sus secuelas terminaron por agotar el patr y el ritmo de crecimiento que se haba seguido hasta entonces, dando paso a un proceso de ajuste complejo e inevitablemente costoso. La recesi vino a adir dificultades. Por una parte, la destrucci de empleo alcanzgran intensidad como resultado de las singularidades institucionales de nuestro mercado laboral, cuyo deficiente funcionamiento hizo recaer excesivamente el peso de los ajustes sobre el empleo. Este gravoso rasgo diferencial pone en cuesti, entre otras cosas, la capacidad para absorber los excedentes de empleo generados por la crisis inmobiliaria, para recuperar el potencial de crecimiento a largo plazo y asegurar la sostenibilidad de las cuentas plicas, cuesti a la que paso a referirme a continuaci. Ms all de los factores que propiciaron la velocidad y la magnitud del deterioro de la situaci fiscal, que se tratan con detalle en el Informe Anual que hoy presento, es importante constatar que este desarrollo se produjo en un momento en el que el escrutinio de los mercados se focalizaba precisamente en la detecci de cualquier posible problema para la sostenibilidad de las finanzas plicas, por lo que influyde manera decisiva en las tensiones financieras que se cernieron sobre la economa espala. En el clima de alerta suscitado, no importaba tanto el bajo nivel comparativo de deuda plica como su ritmo de deterioro y las posibles consecuencias de las altas cotas de endeudamiento del sector privado, de las necesidades de saneamiento del sector financiero o de las dificultades para que la economa creciera a una tasa suficientemente elevada. De hecho, el desarrollo de esta crisis ha vuelto a poner de manifiesto co el exceso de endeudamiento, con independencia de que proceda directamente de las AAPP o del sector privado, tiende a afectar negativamente a la percepci de la sostenibilidad fiscal. La crisis terminafectando tambin al sistema financiero espal que, si bien haba superado sin excesivas dificultades el impacto de la crisis financiera internacional, se vio sometido a una presi mayor cuando emergieron todos los componentes de la crisis macroeconica propia. El aumento de la morosidad, sobre todo en el sector de la promoci inmobiliaria, en el que se haba concentrado una parte importante de la cartera crediticia, y el endurecimiento de las condiciones de financiaci en los mercados financieros mayoristas que acompa a la disminuci de confianza de los inversores en la economa espala resultaron particularmente exigentes para algunas entidades, cajas de ahorros principal-mente. Y, aunque las dificultades estaban circunscritas a un segmento acotado del sector, las presiones de los mercados se extendieron en los momentos ms agudos al conjunto del sistema, con relativa independencia de la situaci particular de cada entidad. Todos estos desarrollos incidieron en la evoluci de la economa espala, que en la primera mitad de 2010 iniciuna trayectoria de recuperaci todava muy dbil, que se ha prolongado con un tono similar en los primeros meses de este a. Paralelamente, la correcci de los desequilibrios acumulados siguiavanzando a un ritmo razonable. Continuel ajuste del exceso de inversi inmobiliaria, con recortes adicionales en la actividad del sector y en los precios de la vivienda. Y tambin las necesidades de financiaci de la naci se redujeron, aunque a un ritmo cada vez ms moderado, como consecuencia del impacto negativo en la balanza comercial del aumento en los precios del petreo. La inflaci subyacente, por timo, mantuvo una tica de moderaci, si se descuenta el efecto de la elevaci de la imposici indirecta a partir del 1 de julio. El ndice general de precios repunten cambio con intensidad en la segunda mitad de 2010 y en los primeros meses de este a, impulsado por la senda alcista de los precios de las materias primas y por los cambios introducidos en los precios regulados. Dado el carcter transitorio de buena parte de estos impulsos, dicha trayectoria debera revertirse en los primos meses, si se atajan los efectos de segunda vuelta. Esta es una condici imprescindible para avanzar en la necesaria mejora de la competitividad y para evitar el da que un aumento duradero de la tasa de inflaci infligira a la constreda capacidad de gasto de los hogares. Por su parte, el proceso de saneamiento del sector privado no financiero, que necesita reducir sus niveles de endeudamiento para reanudar el dinamismo del gasto, se est manifestando en una ligera reducci del saldo vivo del crdito a familias y empresas, que se est contrayendo a un ritmo del 1 % y del 2 % anual, respectivamente. En el caso de las sociedades se observa un patr diferenciado por sectores productivos en el que los prstamos a aquellos ms endeudados, como es el caso de la promoci inmobiliaria, retroceden a un ritmo mayor en el entorno del 3 %, en el primer trimestre de 2011, mientras que el grueso de la deuda de los hogares espales est materializado en hipotecas con vencimientos medios notablemente dilatados y unas pautas de amortizaci predeterminadas, por lo que difcilmente cabe esperar que su volumen se reduzca rpidamente en un contexto como el actual. Por su parte, las tensiones financieras se han traducido en unos criterios ms restrictivos en la concesi de prstamos, que han cobrado ms vigencia con el agravamiento de la crisis de la deuda soberana y que estn afectando en mayor medida a los sectores con mayores dificultades para acreditar su capacidad de reembolso en las adversas condiciones actuales. Es imprescindible que el proceso de reequilibrio en el que se halla inmersa la economa espala avance con presteza para que se restablezca un mayor dinamismo a medio plazo, aunque sea inevitable que, a corto plazo, el propio ajuste restrinja la intensidad de la recuperaci. En 2010 y en la parte transcurrida de 2011, la retirada de los impulsos fiscales expansivos y su sustituci por un programa firme de consolidaci, la correcci en el sector de la construcci y las necesidades de saneamiento financiero de empresas y familias limitan licamente las posibilidades de reanimaci del gasto, como cabe prever que siga pasando en los primos trimestres. Afortunadamente, estos efectos contractivos se estn viendo compensados por la pujanza de las exportaciones, que han de actuar como el factor primordial de impulso de la actividad y las rentas, para lo cual resultar determinante la consecuci de ganancias adicionales en la competitividad, que, de hecho, es la principal variable con que cuenta la economa para superar la difcil coyuntura actual. Cuando culmine esta fase, el saneamiento de la posici patrimonial de las familias y de las empresas permitir que el consumo y la inversi empresarial estn en mejores condiciones de mantener de manera sostenible una trayectoria ms dinmica. A su vez, la consecuci de los objetivos del programa de consolidaci fiscal contribuir a disipar las dudas sobre la sostenibilidad de nuestras finanzas plicas. Y cabe esperar que todo ello redunde en una normalizaci de las condiciones de financiaci, que deberan beneficiarse tambin de la culminaci del proceso de reestructuraci del sistema financiero. Sin embargo, para que este escenario se afiance es preciso superar los obstculos que, todava hoy, dificultan la recuperaci. La deriva que tome la crisis de la deuda soberana ser un condicionante de gran entidad, que est ms all del control de la poltica econica espala. Pero el papel de nuestra poltica econica sigue siendo fundamental, en cualquier escenario, para superar las ineficiencias que se han puesto de manifiesto, para reducir la desconfianza que entorpece y encarece la imprescindible financiaci exterior y para poner a cubierto a la economa espala de cualquier incidente que se pueda producir en la esfera europea. La consolidaci fiscal que se iniciel a pasado ha comenzado a dar sus primeros resultados, aunque el esfuerzo que queda por delante es considerable y requerir gran determinaci para definir y concretar las medidas necesarias. En 2010, el dficit de las AAPP se redujo en casi 2 pp, situndose ligeramente por debajo del nivel proyectado (9,2 % del PIB). No obstante, la intensidad del ajuste y el cumplimiento de los objetivos fueron desiguales entre las distintas administraciones. El mayor avance tuvo lugar en la Administraci Central. Por el contrario, el dficit de las CCAA se incrementligeramente, frente a la reducci prevista, y se produjeron peques desviaciones con respecto a lo programado en las Corporaciones Locales y en la Seguridad Social. El cumplimiento de los objetivos fiscales en 2011 supondr una reducci adicional de 3 pp del saldo deficitario de las AAPP, que ha de provenir en su mayor parte del componente estructural, tal y como ocurriel a pasado. Se trata de un esfuerzo considerable, tanto desde el punto de vista del tama del recorte como de la inercia que han mostrado tradicionalmente algunas partidas de gasto. En las circunstancias actuales el cumplimiento estricto de los planes anunciados es inexcusable, para lo cual se ha de mantener una actitud vigilante y preventiva que impida la materializaci de las posibles desviaciones y, en caso de que estas emerjan, instrumentar inmediatamente las medidas necesarias para corregirlas, tal y como se ha comprometido a hacer el Gobierno. Se deben seguir utilizando todos los mecanismos de disciplina fiscal que proporciona nuestro marco presupuestario para corregir las desviaciones que pudieran surgir. Tal es el caso de la aplicaci estricta y sin excepciones del sistema de autorizaciones de endeudamiento de las CCAA, por el cual estas se condicionan al cumplimiento de los objetivos de dficit y a la aprobaci de planes de reequilibrio en caso de desviaciones. Tambin debe explorarse la aplicaci en nuestro pas de algunas de las ideas que se estn barajando en el debate europeo en torno a los marcos presupuestarios ms efectivos para garantizar la disciplina fiscal. En concreto, los marcos presupuestarios que combinan reglas de dficit plico con lmites especficos al gasto parecen ofrecer los mejores resultados, al permitir actuar sobre las fuentes primarias de los dficits plicos y obligar a que los excesos de recaudaci por causas cclicas se destinen a mejorar la posici fiscal. En esta lnea, el Gobierno ha anunciado su intenci de incorporar a la Ley de Estabilidad Presupuestaria una regla seg la cual el gasto de las AAPP no podr superar la tasa de crecimiento a medio plazo de referencia de la economa espala. Ser de aplicaci inmediata a la Administraci Central del Estado y a las entidades locales y promover su adopci por parte de las CCAA.
