Entre los puntos fuertes cabe sealar, adems de la ausencia de productos complejos asociados a las hipotecas subprime estadounidenses, que las entidades de mayor tamao eran slidas y estaban bien diversificadas, un elemento que ha sido clave para la estabilidad de nuestro sistema en los ltimos aos. Pero la crisis financiera hizo aflorar una serie de debilidades, concentradas principalmente en un conjunto bien definido de cajas de ahorros pequeas y medianas:  Se puso de manifiesto que este sector estaba excesivamente fragmentado, con un gran nmero de entidades demasiado pequeas para lograr financiacin en los mercados en el nuevo contexto internacional y para afrontar los cambios regulatorios articulados en respuesta a la crisis;  asimismo, se hizo evidente que exista un exceso de capacidad agregado, que era necesario reducir para acomodar la cada brusca en los niveles de actividad del sector bancario;  la expansin de sus balances bancarios haba venido, adems, acompaada de una excesiva concentracin de los riesgos en el sector inmobiliario;  por otra parte, la crisis revel los riesgos de una excesiva dependencia de la financiacin de los mercados financieros internacionales, aunque en el caso de las entidades espaolas sta se concentraba en los plazos ms largos;  la crisis tambin hizo evidentes las debilidades de carcter estructural especficas del sector de las cajas de ahorros, derivadas de su particular estructura de propiedad, control y gobierno corporativo, que impeda a estas entidades captar capital de la mxima calidad en los mercados de capitales, entorpeca su gobernanza y la profesionalizacin de sus rganos de gobierno y haca imposible su sujecin a la disciplina de mercado;  por ltimo, existan diversas debilidades en el marco regulatorio e institucional vigente en Espaa que dificultaban la gestin de una crisis de una intensidad y duracin como la que hemos experimentado. Entre ellas cabe destacar la regulacin en materia de resolucin de entidades, que no estaba adaptada a las exigencias de la Unin Monetaria que prohbe la financiacin monetaria-, ni estaba diseada para resolver potenciales problemas en las cajas de ahorros. 2 La respuesta de las autoridades Con todas estas debilidades estructurales, el sector bancario espaol ha tenido que enfrentarse, primero, a la crisis financiera internacional; a continuacin, al desarrollo y profundizacin de la crisis especficamente espaola, que trajo consigo desequilibrios adicionales como el rpido aumento de la tasa de desempleo y la ampliacin del dficit pblico; y, finalmente, a la crisis de la deuda soberana del rea del euro, alimentada tanto por los desequilibrios internos de algunas economas del rea, como por las deficiencias en el propio marco institucional de la Unin Monetaria. Esta sucesin de crisis concatenadas ha exigido un importante esfuerzo tanto a las entidades como a las autoridades, cuya respuesta se ha basado, en trminos generales, en unos principios rectores relativamente estables aunque, al mismo tiempo, la persistencia de la crisis y la naturaleza cambiante de los acontecimientos por ejemplo el inicio de la crisis de la deuda soberana en la primavera de 2010  el reciente deterioro generalizado de las perspectivas de crecimiento- han obligado a irlos modulando y aplicando con flexibilidad. Entre estos principios generales cabe destacar los siguientes:  para corregir el excesivo tamao y fragmentacin de nuestro sistema, se han incentivado procesos de integracin y reestructuracin;  para hacer frente al deterioro de la calidad de los activos relacionados con la actividad inmobiliaria, se ha incidido en primera instancia en el saneamiento de los balances las entidades, con el convencimiento de que recapitalizarlas sin antes obligarlas a reestructurarse y a limpiar de sus balances los activos problemticos hubiera supuesto perpetuar los problemas estructurales de nuestro sistema y habra conducido a un uso inadecuado de los recursos pblicos;  para restablecer la confianza en nuestro sistema bancario, se ha puesto el acento en el fomento de la transparencia haciendo pblicas las exposiciones potencialmente problemticas e incluyendo todas las entidades relevantes en los stress tests- y en el reforzamiento la solvencia, mediante un aumento de capital de la mxima calidad;  para resolver las debilidades estructurales de las cajas de ahorros, se han adoptado los cambios regulatorios necesarios para transformar su estructura de gobernanza y de propiedad, incentivando su transformacin en bancos;  por ltimo, entre los principios que han guiado la actuacin de las autoridades desde el inicio de la crisis, debe destacarse el objetivo de minimizar el coste de la reestructuracin bancaria para los contribuyentes, favoreciendo, siempre que ha sido posible, soluciones alcanzadas en el mbito del sector privado. La aplicacin de estos principios ha ido configurando la respuesta de la poltica econmica a los principales retos del sistema bancario espaol. En este sentido, es importante destacar que la opcin escogida por los gobiernos espaoles no ha consistido en aplicar una recapitalizacin generalizada a todas las entidades, sino que se opt por una estrategia basada en promover el saneamiento de los balances y en impulsar soluciones privadas que permitiesen minimizar el uso de recursos pblicos. Pero esta estrategia tiene el inconveniente de que es mucho ms compleja y requiere ms tiempo. No obstante, ha permitido acometer una reestructuracin profunda del sector y, al mismo tiempo, ha ahorrado a los gobiernos tener que inyectar un volumen de recursos pblicos de una magnitud que habra podido poner en peligro la sostenibilidad de las cuentas pblicas, como efectivamente ocurri en algn otro pas del rea del euro. En cualquier caso, la aplicacin de estos principios ha permitido lograr, con una utilizacin de recursos pblicos muy limitada, avances muy importantes. As, desde el inicio de la crisis hasta principios de este ao se han constituido provisiones por ms del 10% del PIB; las entidades han reforzado su solvencia aumentando significativamente su capital, tanto en relacin con sus activos como en trminos absolutos; la gran mayora de las cajas de ahorros se han convertido en bancos; ha desaparecido un gran nmero de entidades que se contaban entre las ms dbiles, quedando su gestin en manos de otras ms slidas y eficientes (en un proceso, todava activo, en el que han desaparecido dos bancos y 28 cajas) y el tamao medio de las entidades, medido por el volumen de sus activos, se ha multiplicado por dos. A todos estos avances se aaden las medidas adicionales adoptadas ms recientemente. Ms all de las actuaciones del Banco Central Europeo, en particular las LTRO, que han sido claves para mitigar significativamente los riesgos de financiacin y liquidez en el corto y medio plazo, cabe destacar la aprobacin en febrero de 2012 de un Real Decreto-Ley con el que se daba un importante paso para mejorar la confianza en el sector financiero espaol, y en particular, para mitigar las dudas relativas a los activos relacionados con la actividad inmobiliaria, mediante un significativo aumento tanto de las provisiones constituidas desde el inicio de la crisis (hasta alcanzar un 14% del PIB) como de los niveles de capital exigidos a las entidades. Sin embargo, lo hecho hasta ahora no ha sido suficiente para recuperar la confianza de los inversores en la solidez de nuestro sistema bancario, especialmente por la persistencia de las dudas acerca de la calidad de los activos relacionados con la construccin y promocin inmobiliaria, en un contexto, adems, marcado por el deterioro de las perspectivas macroeconmicas, por la prolongacin de los efectos de la crisis de la deuda soberana y por la necesidad de adoptar medidas de calado tanto en el plano de la poltica presupuestaria como en el de la adopcin de medidas estructurales para recuperar el crecimiento. 3 ltimas medidas Por eso hace dos semanas se aprob un nuevo conjunto de medidas adicionales que abordan de forma especfica las principales fuentes de incertidumbre que persisten en relacin con el sector bancario espaol. Se ha decidido intensificar y acelerar el saneamiento de los balances de todas las entidades y reforzar su solvencia, con el objetivo de disipar las persistentes dudas en relacin con la cartera inmobiliaria. As, se han elevado sustancialmente las provisiones para los activos relacionados con la construccin y promocin inmobiliaria clasificados como no problemticos, para tener en cuenta el impacto de potenciales deterioros adicionales en esta cartera. Adems, en el caso de que, como consecuencia de este saneamiento, las entidades experimenten un dficit de capital, debern reforzar su capital bien acudiendo al mercado o bien solicitando el apoyo financiero del FROB, que en todo caso estar condicionado a unos planes de reestructuracin. Por ltimo, con el objetivo de despejar las dudas acerca de la valoracin de los activos, se ha realizado un importante esfuerzo en el mbito de la transparencia. En este sentido, se han aprobado los cambios necesarios para hacer posible la separacin de los activos inmobiliarios problemticos adjudicados del balance de las entidades y asignarlos a unas nuevas Sociedades de Gestin de Activos, lo cual, externamente, contribuir a mejorar la claridad de la informacin a disposicin de los stakeholders e internamente permitir a los gestores de las entidades concentrar sus esfuerzos en otros captulos su balance. Adicionalmente, en este mismo mbito de la transparencia, se ha decidido impulsar una valoracin por parte de expertos de independientes de toda la cartera de activos del sector bancario. 4 Conclusiones En definitiva, recientemente se han adoptado medidas que ahondan en algunos principios que han regido hasta ahora la reforma financiera reestructuracin, saneamiento, reforzamiento de la solvencia y aumento de la transparencia-, y que intentan despejar las dudas que persisten en torno al sistema bancario espaol. En primer lugar, porque el incremento de la transparencia debera llevarnos a disponer de un diagnstico comn, compartido por todos los agentes relevantes, sobre la calidad de los activos del sistema bancario espaol. Y en segundo lugar porque la magnitud del saneamiento y el reforzamiento de la solvencia derivado de estas medidas debera ser suficiente para garantizar su solidez bajo cualquier escenario razonable sobre la evolucin de la economa espaola y sobre los desarrollos del riesgo de crdito. Las medidas ms recientes, junto con la finalizacin de los procesos de integracin y reestructuracin en marcha, deben contribuir a completar este largo y complejo proceso de transformacin del sector bancario espaol que, en el corto plazo, debe permitir remontar la ola de desconfianza que todava afecta a Espaa y que, en ltimo trmino, debe permitir contar con un sistema bancario slido y capacitado para jugar el papel que le corresponde en la recuperacin de nuestra economa.

Title: Inauguration speech as governor of the Bank of Spain
text: June 26, 2012 Inauguration speech Luis M. Linde Governor Ministers, secretaries of state, dear friends and comparos, you will be and beings: First of all, I would like to thank His Majesty the King and the Prime Minister for my appointment. And I extend my thanks to the Vice President and to all the members of the government of the nation. It goes without saying that without the trust, friendship and encouragement of the Economy and Finance Ministers I would not be here today. And, of course, thanks to the representatives of the parliamentary groups that, in accordance with the provisions of the Law of Autonomy of the Bank of Spain, considered in the Congress of Deputies the government's proposal for my appointment and welcomed it. I would like to place on record my appreciation to Miguel e7ngel Fern87ndez Ordez and the two deputy governors who have collaborated with him. I have known Fern87ndez Ordez, Vils and Ar92ztegui for many years and I know very well their absolute personal integrity, their competence and their dedication to the placid service. I extend my thanks to all the Directors-General and all the directors of the Bank, among whom I would like to highlight the members of the Executive Committee, which is the heart of the government of this House: Angel Luis Lez Roa, who is now in his second term; Vicente Salas, who recently finished his; and Ana S87nchez, a great economist, and a better person, who has dedicated her entire working life, with great efficiency and discretion, to the Bank of Spain. And I also want to welcome Maximino Carpio, our new advisor, thanking him very sincerely for accepting that responsibility. And, finally, in this chapter of thanks, thank you, once again, to President Rajoy and his government, which, in agreement with the first opposition party, accepted my proposal to appoint Fernando Restoy Deputy Governor. The Bank thus recovers a truly outstanding professional, with a magnificent academic record, extensive experience and a deep knowledge of the Spanish and international financial system. I confess that I feel emotion for the trust that has been placed in me and for the responsibility I assume. I started working for the State more than 40 years ago and, except for a period at the Inter-American Development Bank, an institution in which I had an exciting job and of which I have the best memories, I have had no other employer than the State. Throughout these more than 40 years I have met magnificent people, whose example and friendship have been very important to me. My memories go to Juan Antonio Garc92a D92ez and Leopoldo Calvo-Sotelo, to whose denes I had the honor and pleasure of working in the aces, not easy and already so distant, of the Transicin; and they also go to Mariano Rubio and Luis e7ngel Rojo, builders and inspirers, to a large extent, of the modern Banco de Espa. As some veterans of this House know, I have reason for grateful remembrance: they both taught me many things, exercising with me, abundantly, in the difficult virtue of patience. Really, I never imagined that at the end of my career I would have a destiny d0 to use the language of officials d0 so important, so honorable and so difficult. Being Governor of the Bank of Spain has always meant assuming a great responsibility, even greater, it seems to me, in the current circumstances. I would summarize in three points, two of substance and one of procedure, the priorities and urgent tasks of the Bank today. First, the most obvious thing: we must clean up and strengthen our banking system so that confidence is restored, normal financing flows are restored and activity and employment in Spain recover as soon as possible. The economic and financial crisis we are going through can be overcome with a major effort to reform, save and rationalise our finances and a great effort on the part of our credit institutions to clean up their balance sheets and strengthen their capital base, counting, in a number of cases, on the help of the State and the resources that the European Union is going to put at our disposal; and, also, contributing to the implementation, within the framework of the Monetary Union and the entire European Union, of new initiatives to advance in fiscal coordination and banking and financial integration. Secondly: starting from the experiences and lessons of the crisis that began in 2007, without neglecting its traditional functions, and just as other central banks in our environment and the European Central Bank itself are doing, the Bank of Spain has to start thinking in terms of what we call, for short, "financial stability", adapting its competences and its organization to that objective. I do not know when this work can be completed, which will be complicated and long, but we have to start it now. And, thirdly: the Banco de Espa carries out its functions within a legal framework of autonomy and independence, obliged, in any case, by our membership of the European System of Central Banks. All political forces participate in this consensus and this gives the Bank great strength. But this strength naturally has trade-offs: it accentuates our responsibility and forces us to strive to ensure that what we do and why we do it is well understood. In short, those of us who work in this House have to show that we use well that capital of trust that the political forces have given us. Banco de Espa is a strong institution, a great machine, well organized, with a lot of experience, with magnificent professionals, proud of their work. But we need the understanding and help of everyone: political parties, economic agents and the media. And, from now on, I dare to ask for that help and understanding. I don't have to ask anything of my comparos at the Bank. I know that they will do everything in their power to ensure that the Bank of Spain continues to be an exemplary institution at the service of all the spallets, at the service of Spain. And, finally, I am going to allow myself a literary reference that wants to introduce a pinch of relaxation and a message of confidence in this solemn meeting, in these difficult moments: Josep Pla, the ico of our great writers concerned about understanding economics d0 it is true that he had in his friend Juan Sard87, so linked to this House, an exceptional private professor -, said Pla, and I return to the thread, that one of the worst things that could happen to the espales was that the Bank of Spain failed. Well, that's not going to happen, we're not going to fail. The spirit of Pla, who watches us closely, will have nothing to reproach us. Thank you all very much for your presence at this event and for your attention.

Title: Inauguration speech at the Council of State
text: July 12, 2012 Inauguration speech at the Council of State Luis M. Linde Governor Mr. Chairman of the Council, Counselors, Lawyers, ladies and gentlemen, First of all, I would like to thank Landelino Lavilla and Miguel Herrero for agreeing to be my godparents at today's ceremony. For me it is a great honor to take office as an ex officio member of the Council of State, the supreme consultative body of the Government and one of the institutions with the greatest historical tradition in our country. As we all know, this is a time of serious difficulties for the Spanish economy, but also for the construction of Europe. These difficulties are, today, really, the main subject of my work, as Governor of the Bank of Spain and as a member of the Governing Council of the European Central Bank. We will be surprised if you have chosen as the subject of my speech the prospects for monetary union, and for the European Union as a whole, the broad frame of reference for our problems, for dealing with and overcoming them. For decades we have witnessed a progressive consolidation of the idea of unity as the best way open to build the future of Europeans. It is true that, in most cases, progress has been laborious. It is also true that the most far-reaching qualitative leaps, including the creation of the euro, have been more the exception than the rule. But it is undeniable that, when considered in historical perspective, the European project has made substantial progress. At the moment, however, a negative perception is gaining weight in some areas, which tends to see Europe, its institutions and its working methods as a risk factor, not only for the economic well-being of its own citizens but even for the international community, beyond the borders of the Union. What are the reasons behind this change in perception and what challenges do they pose to those of us who believe in the need for more, not less, Europe? Times of crisis subject the structures on which economies and the societies that suffer them are based to a degree of tension that ends up revealing their fissures and weaknesses. Europe's sovereign debt crisis is no exception. The origin of the current crisis is likely to be closer to the difficulty of governments in accepting the demands arising from membership of a monetary union than to its structural weaknesses. In any case, the crisis has revealed that the foundations that were laid to support the edifice of the euro, in the Maastricht Treaty, twenty years ago, need to be strengthened if we are to guarantee its stability. But the stability of the euro requires going beyond the set of institutions agreed at Maastricht. Various member countries of monetary union, including our own, face serious difficulties in controlling and reducing the tensions to which their economies are subjected. This task can hardly succeed in lasting its duration if it is not part of a broader process to define and agree on what we could call "the model of economic coexistence" of the member countries of the Monetary Union and of the entire European Union, a "model of economic coexistence" that will inevitably be, increasingly, a model of political coexistence. A fundamental piece of this future "model" will be the financial system and will go through achieving a degree of integration in our banking systems comparable to that achieved in the field of monetary policy, with three main components. The first is the establishment of a single European banking supervisor. As in the case of monetary policy, the new authority could combine the necessary centralisation of the most important, or more general, decisions with a reasonable degree of decentralisation to maximise the experience and expertise of national supervisors. The second element would be a common deposit insurance scheme which, as in the case of the supervisor, should combine centralisation and national elements. Third, the design should also include an integrated mechanism for the treatment of non-viable entities. But whatever agreements may be reached on the financing of both the common guarantee fund and the resolution mechanism, these two new parts of the system cannot be fully effective without the support of a financing mechanism which, in one way or another, can only arise from greater fiscal integration. a very complex political terrain. The range of options between the current situation and the opposite extreme - which would be characterised by a single fiscal authority, a common treasury and a centralised budget - is very wide. I would just like to point out two aspects that seem relevant to me. First, any strategy designed to move towards greater fiscal integration must combine the surrender of national sovereignty with a degree of pooling of financial risks, what we call the "mutualization" of sovereign risks. Secondly, the transfer of sovereignty in the fiscal field has an impact on particularly sensitive political aspects, so it is necessary to accompany the process with a permanent effort of pedagogy and transparency. Just a few weeks ago, the Heads of State and Government of the euro area and the European Council adopted a series of decisions, including some of which have a direct bearing on the issues to which I referred in my speech. There is undoubtedly a long way to go, but the one that began a few weeks ago is an important support for the continuity of monetary union. The success or failure of monetary union will not, for the European Union, be just another incident on a path begun more than half a century ago. It is unrealistic to think that monetary union will fail d0 failure can take various formats d0 and that everything else can remain the same. The failure of monetary union would imply a major slowdown and a fundamental change of course for all European countries, at least in any foreseeable horizon. On the contrary, the success of monetary union, its continuation, will be a decisive impetus on the road to European unity. This is the position and perspective defended by Spain and there are many reasons to trust that monetary union will be able to overcome the current crisis and will remain one of the fundamental axes of the European political process. I would like to conclude by expressing my hope that I will be able to be useful to the Council by offering my cooperation in the important tasks entrusted to it. Thank you very much for your presence at this event and for your attention.

En segundo lugar, la cesin de soberana en el mbito fiscal incide sobre aspectos polticos particularmente sensibles, por lo que es preciso acompaar el proceso con un permanente esfuerzo de pedagoga y de transparencia. Por el contrario, el xito de la Unin Monetaria, su continuidad, ser un impulso decisivo en el camino de la unidad europea. Esta es la posicin y la perspectiva que defiende Espaa y hay muchas razones para confiar en que la Unin Monetaria podr superar la crisis actual y seguir siendo uno de los ejes fundamentales del proceso poltico europeo. Title: Reflections on the banking sector
text: 23.07.2012 Reflections on the banking sector "The reconfiguration of the Spanish banking sector in the face of the new financial regulation. Scope and impact of the crisis". Summer Courses 2012 of the Complutense University of Madrid Fernando Restoy Deputy governor 1 Introduction It is a source of satisfaction to participate for the first time in these summer courses of the Complutense University, University of which I was a student and, later, a teacher. I would therefore like to thank the organisers for their kind invitation. Today I will share with you some reflections on the foreseeable evolution of the institutional framework in which the European banking sector operates. I would also like to take this opportunity to address some issues of a more immediate nature, such as the implications of the agreements recently reached between the Spanish and European authorities, with the participation also of the International Monetary Fund, for the provision of financial assistance for the recapitalization of Spanish entities that require it. 2 On the banking union The history of European construction follows a rather linear thread of argument. The dynamics of the process initiated after the Second World War have led to successive surrenders of sovereignty as the only way to guarantee the progress made over the years. The proven inadequacy of the process of tariff disarmament initiated in the fifties of the last century revealed the need to facilitate the mobility of productive factors and to harmonize national regulations to create a true integrated market. And trade integration led to an attempt to avoid the distorting effects on competition of exchange rate fluctuations. Faced with the obvious difficulty of achieving the stability required by intervention in the foreign exchange markets, the idea of making national currencies disappear, adopting a common currency and monetary policy and thus creating a monetary union, which has been operating satisfactorily for a decade, broke through. Recent events, and in particular the crisis in sovereign debt markets, have shown that the proper functioning of the monetary union requires measures to contain the perception of country risk and thus restore the European Central Bank's control over the financing conditions of agents throughout the euro area. And this entails agreeing on restrictions on the ability of national authorities to undertake autonomous economic policies, establishing centralized surveillance mechanisms and expanding the scope for action of the European institutions. Again, deepening integration appears to be the best way to preserve what we have already achieved. One area where these developments seem particularly urgent is banking. It is clear that a monetary union can only work if financial institutions are in a position to exchange liquidity through lending or deposit operations on similar terms across the euro area. To that end, the counterparty risk should be limited and should not depend significantly on the location of the borrowing institution. Well, the crisis has shown that the ability of banks to obtain financing is today strongly linked to the perception of sovereign risk in their country of origin. In turn, the sovereign risk listed in each State is connected to the general perception of the financial situation of banks in that country, since the use of available public resources to clean up entities in difficulty is discounted. This perverse link between sovereign risk and domestic banking risk is a major breakdown of the foundations on which the proper functioning of the monetary union rests. It is therefore necessary to look for formulas that strengthen the centralised control of national banking risks. To this end, it is essential to agree on common effective measures to contain these risks, and centralized decision-making mechanisms for their monitoring and mitigation. It is therefore necessary to move forward with the creation of a centralised banking supervisor in monetary union. As you know, its creation is a necessary condition for accepting the possibility for the future European Stability Mechanism to provide financial assistance directly to banks. It is clear that this is a potentially very effective tool to weaken the link between financial and sovereign risk. Naturally, the institutional design of the European supervisor will be of paramount importance in ensuring its effectiveness. Experience shows that banking supervision should be the responsibility of central banks. Recent events have shown that any conflicts between the various objectives of central banks with oversight powers over the banking system are much less relevant than the synergies generated between their role in controlling the aggregate liquidity of the system and the preservation of financial stability. It is therefore reasonable that, in the euro area, it should be the European Central Bank that should be responsible for the supervision of banking institutions that are decided to be transferred from national to European level. Furthermore, the definition of the scope of the tasks that the ECB should undertake is not a simple matter. It seems pertinent to design a roadmap with progressive gains of responsibilities on the part of the ECB that is based on three basic elements: first, centralized decision-making, at least, for systemic institutions at the level of the euro area; secondly, the maintenance, at least in the short and medium term, of decentralised supervision of essentially national entities, albeit on the basis of highly harmonised schemes and principles; and finally, the adoption of a federal organization that favors, in any case, the intensive use of the experience, knowledge and technical capacity of national supervisors. However, it should be borne in mind that, however effective central supervision may be, the complete breaking of the destabilising link between domestic banking risk and sovereign risk requires the adoption of effective centralised mechanisms for managing banking crises and mutualising the costs they generate for the public purse. In other words, banking union will never be a complete reality without the design of an integrated deposit insurance scheme and a common crisis resolution scheme. The establishment of both mechanisms is essential to ensure the denationalization of banking risk as an essential part of the strategy to strengthen the monetary union. Of course, no one can hide the fact that its implementation requires the adoption of agreements that are highly complex technically and, above all, politically. 3 About the Memorandum of Understanding In any case, our priority right now is to face d0 with the instruments we currently have d0 the challenges posed by the process of recapitalisation of some segments of the Spanish banking sector in which we are immersed. The roadmap for this process is included in the Memorandum of Understanding that has recently been agreed by the Spanish and European authorities, with the participation of the IMF, in the framework of the request for financial assistance. On 8th June in its assessment of the Spanish financial sector the IMF pointed out that the core of the Spanish banking sector was made up of solid and well-managed institutions with the capacity to resist very adverse developments in macroeconomic and financial conditions. At the same time, it indicated that the sector showed some elements of vulnerability that need to be eliminated. This analysis, shared by the Bank of Spain, is the basis for the strategy to strengthen the national banking sector included in the Memorandum. The strategy contains three main ingredients: firstly, the identification of the capital needs of institutions and their coverage, if necessary, through the provision of public funds, for which a financing line of up to one hundred billion euros is available. Secondly, the establishment of requirements for entities requiring public aid in order to ensure their viability and the proper use of budgetary resources. And, finally, the adoption of reforms and legal changes that strengthen the banking system as a whole. Therefore, the first thing required by the Memorandum is the identification of the entities that will require capital and the estimation of their amount. As you know, a first step was the stress tests carried out by two independent consultants. which were made public on June 21. The main data provided by these exercises is the estimation of potential capital needs for the sector as a whole in a very adverse scenario and using conservative assumptions, which was between 51 billion and 62 billion euros. In a second phase, currently under way, the accounting treatment of problem assets is being reviewed in detail and their valuation is being reviewed. This information will allow for further individualized resistance exercises, which will result, which we expect to make public in September, in an estimate of the capital needs of each entity. With these data and the plans that must be presented by all entities that require additional capital, entities can be classified into different groups depending on whether or not they need capital and, if they need it, whether they can generate or obtain it on their own or, on the contrary, they will require public support. A separate group is made up of the four entities that, at the moment, have the participation of the FROB and where, in all likelihood, the greatest needs of public funds will be concentrated. Those entities that are going to receive public aid will have to design restructuring plans d0 which must be approved by the Bank of Spain and the European Commission d0 that will have to meet some specific conditions. These are, essentially, of three types: the design of a solvent business plan, the transfer of problematic assets off their balance sheets and the sharing of the burden with the aim of minimizing the cost borne by taxpayers. The business plan will be evaluated according to the relative size of the aid required and the specific situation of each entity. Its objective must be to demonstrate that the entity is viable in the long term, without specifying the indefinite maintenance of public aid. Thus, business plans, in general terms, must incorporate ambitious actions that enable an adequate balance of sources of financing, the rationalization of business lines, efficiency gains in the operational structure and the strengthening of corporate governance. The restructuring plans should include, as I have anticipated, the transfer of problematic assets to a newly created asset management company, which will involve the complete segregation of these assets from the balance sheets of the entities. The value at which the assets are transferred shall be equal to their long-term economic value; value to be established in accordance with the bank balance sheet review exercises to which I have referred previously. The asset management company will have public and private capital and will issue, for the financing of its asset purchases, debt instruments that will be guaranteed by the State. This segregation of problematic assets d0 such as those linked to real estate development d0 will allow a thorough restructuring of entities that require public support. At the same time, it will limit the future risk assumed by the public sector, which will only materialize if the evolution of the price of the transferred assets deviates permanently downwards from the long-term economic value which, as I have pointed out, will determine the price at which the asset management company will acquire them. The third type of conditions to be assumed by entities that require public support in their restructuring processes is the adoption of burden-sharing schemes between the owners of the entities and the public sector. Supported entities should, as far as possible, use their own resources, for example by selling holdings in assets that are not of a strategic nature; avoiding its expansion by ways other than those of organic growth; and restricting directors' remuneration and dividend payments. Burden-sharing arrangements shall also include the absorption of losses by shareholders and, to the extent determined, by holders of hybrid equity instruments. In particular, these instruments may be converted into shares at the time when the public capital enters, or repurchased by the entity at the appropriate discounts. If it is determined that any entity is not viable, it would proceed to its orderly restructuring, as has been happening until now, ensuring, in any case, the protection of customers. Finally, the third component of the strategy to strengthen the banking system contained in the Memorandum is the improvement of regulation and the institutional framework relevant to banking activity. Thus, the Memorandum calls for an increase in capital requirements to 9% of risk-weighted assets, and reforms aimed at improving the treatment of concentration risk; to design stable rules on provisions; to review the role of savings banks as shareholders of banks; to increase the transparency of financial information; and to increase customer protection in relation to the marketing of complex products. Likewise, among these horizontal requirements there are also several that specifically affect the Bank of Spain. In particular, the Memorandum calls for strengthening the operational independence of the Institution by increasing its powers in the areas of sanctions, banking licensing and issuing binding guidelines and interpretations. On the other hand, the Memorandum proposes a review of supervisory practices in two aspects: on the one hand, the improvement of decision-making procedures and, on the other, the strengthening of the link between macroprudential analysis and supervision. Naturally, the Bank of Spain has already set to work to fulfill in a timely manner the commitments it assumes directly and collaborate with the Ministry of Economy and Competitiveness in the development of all the tasks that are part of its area of competence. 4 Conclusions In summary, I believe that the measures and reforms outlined will certainly contribute to strengthening our financial system as a whole, building on the exceptional strength shown by the group of entities that constitute its core today, even in the adverse conditions caused by the crisis. It is clear that the work ahead is far-reaching and that the resulting changes in the organization and regulation of the industry will be substantial. It is also clear that we do not have the capacity to distribute reforms autonomously over time, as might perhaps have been advisable in other, less demanding circumstances. But experience shows that urgency is sometimes a good ally of determination, and that, therefore, the current circumstances constitute, above all, an exceptional opportunity to place the Spanish banking sector on a path that ensures its active contribution to the solution of the considerable challenges facing the Spanish economy at the moment. Thanks a lot
text_original: 23.07.2012 Reflexiones sobre el sector bancario La reconfiguracin del sector bancario espaol ante la nueva regulacin financiera. Alcance e impacto de la crisis. Cursos de Verano 2012 de la Universidad Complutense de Madrid Fernando Restoy Subgobernador 1 Introduccin Es un motivo de satisfaccin participar por primera vez en estos cursos de verano de la Universidad Complutense, Universidad de la que fui alumno y, despus, profesor. Por ello quiero agradecer a los organizadores su amable invitacin. Hoy compartir con ustedes algunas reflexiones sobre la evolucin previsible del marco institucional en el que el sector bancario europeo desarrolla su actividad. Asimismo, querra aprovechar esta oportunidad para abordar algunas cuestiones de carcter ms inmediato como son las implicaciones de los acuerdos recientemente alcanzados entre las autoridades espaolas y las europeas, con la participacin tambin del Fondo Monetario Internacional, para la provisin de asistencia financiera para la recapitalizacin de las entidades espaolas que as lo requieran. 2 Sobre la unin bancaria La historia de la construccin europea sigue un hilo argumental bastante lineal. La dinmica del proceso iniciado despus de la segunda guerra mundial ha ido provocando cesiones sucesivas de soberana como nica forma de garantizar los avances realizados a lo largo de los aos. La constatada insuficiencia del proceso de desarme arancelario iniciado en los aos cincuenta del siglo pasado desvel la necesidad de facilitar la movilidad de los factores productivos y de armonizar regulaciones nacionales para crear un autntico mercado integrado. Y la integracin comercial condujo al intento de evitar los efectos distorsionadores que sobre la competencia ejercan las fluctuaciones de los tipos de cambio. Ante la dificultad evidente de lograr la estabilidad requerida mediante la intervencin en los mercados cambiarios se abri paso la idea de hacer desaparecer las divisas nacionales, adoptar una moneda y una poltica monetaria comn y, de este modo, crear una unin monetaria, que ha estado operando satisfactoriamente durante una dcada. Los acontecimientos recientes y, en particular, la crisis en los mercados de deuda soberana han puesto de manifiesto que el adecuado funcionamiento de la unin monetaria exige la adopcin de medidas que permitan contener la percepcin de riesgo pas y, de este modo, restaurar el control del Banco Central Europeo sobre las condiciones de financiacin de los agentes en toda la zona del euro. Y ello conlleva acordar restricciones en la capacidad de las autoridades nacionales para acometer polticas econmicas autnomas, establecer mecanismos de vigilancia centralizados y ampliar el margen de actuacin de las instituciones europeas. De nuevo, la profundizacin de la integracin aparece como la mejor forma de preservar la que ya hemos alcanzado. Un rea donde estos avances parecen especialmente urgentes es el mbito bancario. Es evidente que una unin monetaria solo puede funcionar si las entidades financieras estn en disposicin de intercambiar la liquidez mediante operaciones de prstamo o depsito en condiciones similares en toda la zona del euro. Para ello, es preciso que el riesgo de contrapartida est acotado y que este no dependa significativamente de la localizacin de la entidad prestataria. Pues bien, la crisis ha evidenciado que la capacidad de los bancos para obtener financiacin est hoy fuertemente ligada a la percepcin de riesgo soberano en su pas de origen. A su vez, el riesgo soberano cotizado de cada Estado est conectado con la percepcin general sobre la situacin financiera de las entidades bancarias de ese pas, pues se descuenta la utilizacin de los recursos pblicos disponibles para sanear entidades en dificultades. Este vnculo perverso entre riesgo soberano y riesgo bancario nacional supone un quebranto importante de las bases sobre las que se asienta el adecuado funcionamiento de la unin monetaria. Por tanto, es preciso buscar frmulas que refuercen el control centralizado de los riesgos bancarios nacionales. Para ello resulta esencial acordar medidas efectivas comunes para la contencin de estos riesgos, y mecanismos de decisin centralizada para su vigilancia y mitigacin. De este modo, resulta preciso avanzar en la creacin de un Supervisor bancario centralizado en la Unin Monetaria. Como saben, su creacin resulta una condicin necesaria para que se acepte la posibilidad de que el futuro Mecanismo Europeo de Estabilidad proporcione directamente ayuda financiera a las entidades bancarias. Es evidente que esta es una herramienta potencialmente muy eficaz para debilitar el vnculo existente entre riesgo financiero y soberano. Naturalmente, el diseo institucional del supervisor europeo tendr una importancia capital para asegurar su eficacia. La experiencia demuestra que las tareas de supervisin bancaria deben recaer en los bancos centrales. Los ltimos acontecimientos han mostrado que los eventuales conflictos entre los distintos objetivos de los bancos centrales que tienen competencias de vigilancia del sistema bancario son mucho menos relevantes que las sinergias generadas entre su papel de control de la liquidez agregada del sistema y la preservacin de la estabilidad financiera. Por ello, es razonable que, en la zona del euro, sea el Banco Central Europeo la institucin que asuma las competencias en materia de supervisin de las entidades bancarias que se decida transferir desde el mbito nacional al europeo. Asimismo, la definicin del alcance de las tareas que debera asumir el BCE no es una cuestin sencilla. Parece pertinente disear una hoja de ruta con ganancia progresiva de responsabilidades por parte del BCE que se asiente sobre tres elementos bsicos: en primer lugar, la toma centralizada de decisiones, al menos, para las entidades sistmicas a nivel del rea del euro; en segundo lugar, el mantenimiento, al menos en el corto y medio plazo, de la supervisin descentralizada de entidades de mbito esencialmente nacional aunque sobre la base de esquemas y principios altamente armonizados; y finalmente, la adopcin de una organizacin federal que favorezca, en todo caso, la utilizacin intensa de la experiencia, conocimiento y capacidad tcnica de los supervisores nacionales. Sin embargo, debe tenerse presente que, por eficaz que resulte la supervisin centralizada, la completa ruptura del vnculo desestabilizador entre riesgo bancario domstico y riesgo soberano exige la adopcin de mecanismos centralizados eficaces de gestin de las crisis bancarias y de mutualizacin de los costes que estas generan para el erario pblico. En otros trminos, la unin bancaria nunca ser una realidad completa si no se disea un sistema de garanta de depsitos integrado y un esquema comn de resolucin de crisis. El establecimiento de ambos mecanismos resulta bsico para asegurar la desnacionalizacin del riesgo bancario como pieza esencial de la estrategia de fortalecimiento de la unin monetaria. Por supuesto, a nadie se le oculta que su implantacin requiere adoptar acuerdos que revisten una elevada complejidad tcnica y sobre todo poltica. 3 Sobre el Memorando de Entendimiento En todo caso, nuestra prioridad ahora mismo es hacer frente con los instrumentos de los que disponemos en la actualidad- a los retos que plantea el proceso de recapitalizacin de algunos segmentos del sector bancario espaol en el que estamos inmersos. La hoja de ruta de este proceso est recogida en el Memorando de Entendimiento que recientemente ha sido acordado por las autoridades espaolas y las europeas, con la participacin del FMI, en el marco de la solicitud de asistencia financiera. El 8 de junio, en su evaluacin sobre el sector financiero espaol, el FMI sealaba que el ncleo del sector bancario espaol estaba conformado por entidades slidas y bien gestionadas y con capacidad de resistencia ante desarrollos muy adversos en las condiciones macroeconmicas y financieras. Al mismo tiempo, indicaba que el sector mostraba algunos elementos de vulnerabilidad que es preciso eliminar. Este anlisis, que comparte el Banco de Espaa, es el que sirve de base a la estrategia de fortalecimiento del sector bancario nacional que recoge el Memorando. La estrategia contiene tres ingredientes principales: en primer lugar, la identificacin de las necesidades de capital de las entidades y su cobertura, en el caso de que sea preciso, mediante la aportacin de fondos pblicos, para lo que se dispone de una lnea de financiacin de hasta cien mil millones de euros. En segundo lugar, el establecimiento de requisitos a las entidades que precisen ayuda pblica con objeto de asegurar su viabilidad y la adecuada utilizacin de los recursos presupuestarios. Y, finalmente, la adopcin de reformas y cambios legales que permitan fortalecer el sistema bancario en su conjunto. Por lo tanto, lo primero que requiere el Memorando es la identificacin de las entidades que precisarn capital y la estimacin de su cuanta. Como saben, un primer paso lo constituyeron las pruebas de resistencia realizados por dos consultores independientes que se hicieron pblicas el da 21 de junio. El principal dato que proporcionaban estos ejercicios es la estimacin de las necesidades potenciales de capital para el conjunto del sector en un escenario muy adverso y usando hiptesis conservadoras, que se situaba entre 51 mil y 62 mil millones de euros. En una segunda fase, actualmente en curso, se est procediendo a revisar de manera pormenorizada el tratamiento contable de los activos problemticos y a revisar su valoracin. Esta informacin permitir realizar nuevos ejercicios de resistencia individualizados, que darn como resultado, que esperamos hacer pblico en el mes de septiembre, una estimacin de las necesidades de capital de cada entidad. Con estos datos y los planes que debern presentar todas las entidades que precisen capital adicional, se podr clasificar a las entidades en distintos grupos dependiendo de si necesitan o no capital y, en caso de necesitarlo, de si lo podrn generar u obtener por su cuenta o, por el contrario, requerirn apoyo pblico. Un grupo aparte lo constituyen las cuatro entidades que, en estos momentos, cuentan con la participacin del FROB y en donde se concentrarn, con toda probabilidad, las mayores necesidades de fondos pblicos. Aquellas entidades que vayan a recibir ayudas pblicas tendrn que disear planes de reestructuracin que debern ser aprobados por el Banco de Espaa y la Comisin Europea- que habrn de satisfacer algunas condiciones especficas. Estas son, esencialmente, de tres tipos: el diseo de un plan de negocio solvente, la transferencia de activos problemticos fuera de sus balances y el reparto de la carga con el objetivo de minimizar el coste soportado por los contribuyentes. El plan de negocio ser evaluado en funcin del tamao relativo de la ayuda requerida y la situacin concreta de cada entidad. Su objetivo debe ser demostrar que la entidad es viable a largo plazo, sin precisar para ello el mantenimiento indefinido de las ayudas pblicas. As pues, los planes de negocio, en trminos generales, habrn de incorporar actuaciones ambiciosas que posibiliten un equilibrio adecuado de las fuentes de financiacin, la racionalizacin de las lneas de negocio, ganancias de eficiencia en la estructura operativa y el fortalecimiento del gobierno corporativo. Los planes de reestructuracin debern contemplar, como he anticipado, la transferencia de activos problemticos a una compaa de gestin de activos de nueva creacin- que implicar la segregacin completa de estos activos de los balances de las entidades. El valor al que se transfieren los activos equivaldr a su valor econmico de largo plazo; valor que se establecer de acuerdo con los ejercicios de revisin de los balances bancarios a los que me he referido con anterioridad. La compaa de gestin de activos tendr capital pblico y privado y emitir, para la financiacin de sus compras de activos, instrumentos de deuda que contarn con la garanta del Estado. Esta segregacin de los activos problemticos como los ligados a la promocin inmobiliaria- permitir un saneamiento profundo de las entidades que requieran apoyo pblico. Al mismo tiempo acotar el riesgo futuro asumido por el sector pblico, que solo se materializar en caso de que la evolucin del precio de los activos transferidos se desve a la baja de manera permanente del valor econmico de largo plazo que, como he sealado, determinar el precio al que la compaa de gestin de activos los adquirir. El tercer tipo de condiciones que debern asumir las entidades que requieran apoyo pblico en sus procesos de restructuracin es la adopcin de esquemas de reparto la carga entre los propietarios de las entidades y el sector pblico. Las entidades que reciban ayudas habrn de utilizar, en la medida de lo posible, sus propios recursos, por ejemplo vendiendo participaciones en activos que no sean de carcter estratgico; evitando su expansin por vas distintas a las del crecimiento orgnico; y restringiendo las remuneraciones de los administradores y el pago de dividendos. Asimismo, los mecanismos de reparto de la carga incluirn la absorcin de las prdidas por los accionistas, y, en la medida que se determine, por los tenedores de los instrumentos hbridos de capital. En particular, estos instrumentos podrn ser convertidos en acciones en el momento en el que entre el capital pblico, o bien recomprados por la entidad con los descuentos pertinentes. Si se determinara que alguna entidad no es viable se procedera a su reestructuracin ordenada, tal como ha venido ocurriendo hasta ahora, asegurando, en todo caso, la proteccin de la clientela. Finalmente, el tercer componente de la estrategia de fortalecimiento del sistema bancario que contiene el Memorando es el perfeccionamiento de la regulacin y del marco institucional relevante para la actividad bancaria. As, el Memorando suscita el aumento de los requisitos de capital hasta el 9% de los activos ponderados por riesgo, y reformas encaminadas a mejorar el tratamiento del riesgo de concentracin; a disear una normativa estable sobre provisiones; a revisar el papel de las cajas como accionistas de los bancos; a incrementar la transparencia de la informacin financiera; y a aumentar la proteccin de la clientela en relacin con la comercializacin de productos complejos. Asimismo, entre estas exigencias de carcter horizontal se sitan tambin varias que afectan especficamente al Banco de Espaa. En particular, el Memorando plantea el reforzamiento de la independencia operacional de la Institucin aumentando sus poderes en materia de sanciones, concesin de licencias bancarias y emisin de directrices e interpretaciones vinculantes. Por otra parte, el Memorando plantea una revisin de las prcticas supervisoras en dos aspectos: por un lado, el perfeccionamiento de los procedimientos para la toma de decisiones y, por otro, el estrechamiento del vnculo entre el anlisis macro prudencial y la supervisin. Naturalmente, el Banco de Espaa se ha puesto ya manos a la obra para cumplir en tiempo y forma los compromisos que asume directamente y colaborar con el Ministerio de Economa y Competitividad en el desarrollo de todas las tareas que forman parte de su rea de competencias. 4 Conclusiones En resumen, creo que las medidas y reformas sealadas contribuirn con toda seguridad a reforzar el conjunto de nuestro sistema financiero construyendo sobre la excepcional fortaleza que han mostrado el grupo de entidades que constituyen hoy su ncleo, incluso en las adversas condiciones provocadas por la crisis. Es evidente que el trabajo que tenemos por delante es de gran envergadura y que los cambios resultantes en la organizacin y regulacin de la industria sern sustanciales. Es tambin claro que no disponemos de la capacidad para distribuir autnomamente en el tiempo las reformas como quizs podra haber sido aconsejable en otras circunstancias menos exigentes. Pero la experiencia demuestra que la urgencia es en ocasiones un buen aliado de la determinacin, y que, por ello, las circunstancias actuales constituyen, sobre todo, una excepcional oportunidad para situar al sector bancario espaol en una senda que asegure su contribucin activa a la solucin de los considerables retos que tiene planteados la economa espaola en estos momentos. Muchas gracias

Title: Reform of the Spanish banking sector: measures to strengthen financial stability
text: 15.11.2012 Reform of the Spanish banking sector: measures to strengthen financial stability1 Seminar of central bankers of Banco Santander Fernando Restoy Deputy governor Translation from the original in English 1 Introduction I am very pleased to be able to participate in this International Banking Conference organized by Banco Santander. As you all know, the Spanish banking system is undergoing an unprecedented restructuring and recapitalisation process. Important steps have already been taken and we hope that this process will be completed in a few months. I believe that this conference provides us with an excellent opportunity to review what has been done so far and to examine the main challenges that remain. 2 Initial measures to strengthen confidence in the Spanish banking sector: 2008 to mid-2012 The main problems of the Spanish banking sector stem from the imbalances accumulated in the prolonged period of expansion that preceded the financial crisis. During this period, credit to the private sector, and especially to construction and real estate development, registered strong growth. This credit growth could not be fully financed by retail deposits and banks therefore increasingly turned to international wholesale and interbank markets. This increased the vulnerability of Spanish banks to possible disturbances in financial markets. The importance of the vulnerabilities cited became apparent over the course of the crisis. Consequently, between 2008 and 2011, the Spanish authorities adopted a number of measures, mainly aimed at supporting the liquidity of institutions, promoting the consolidation and restructuring of the most fragile institutions (especially savings banks), and increasing capital and provisioning levels, in particular to cover risks arising from the real estate sector. However, these measures failed to fully restore confidence in the soundness of a segment of the Spanish banking system. Indeed, perceived signs of vulnerability increased in 2011 and early 2012, reflecting persistent uncertainty about the quality of assets related to construction and real estate development. These signals were evident in an environment marked by a deterioration in the macroeconomic outlook (a double recession), the prolonged and worsening effects of the sovereign debt crisis, and the challenges facing budgetary policy. For this reason, important additional measures were taken during the first half of 2012 to mitigate uncertainty regarding the valuation of assets related to construction and real estate development. In particular, in February and May, the Government passed two Royal Decree-Laws, which required a significant increase in provisions for damaged loans and assets foreclosed or received in payment of real estate debts. In addition, measures were taken to address concerns about the evolution of healthy assets, requiring banks to introduce a general provision of 30% for the loan portfolio. classified as standard to take into account the possible migration from the normal portfolio to the problem loan portfolio. In general, the clean-up of balance sheets resulting from these measures leads to a sharp increase in provisions in the face of possible additional losses in the financial system. In fact, when these measures have been fully implemented, the provisions accumulated by the Spanish banking sector from 2007 to 2012 will amount to more than 200,000 million euros (around 20% of GDP). 3 The ongoing restructuring of the Spanish banking sector These measures contributed to improving the perception of the situation of the Spanish financial sector. However, additional measures were needed to address the remaining uncertainty in the markets. The Spanish authorities therefore adopted two important new decisions: - Firstly, in May, they decided to carry out an independent assessment of the solvency and business prospects of the Spanish banking system. In particular, an exercise was carried out to assess the resilience of banks in the event of a further deterioration in the economy and to determine the level of capital that would ensure the long-term viability of banks. - And secondly, at the end of June, the authorities requested external financial assistance. The recapitalization and restructuring of the banking sector required support measures by the public sector to ensure that potential capital needs were met. However, given the situation in sovereign debt markets, it was felt that the establishment of such backstop measures using only domestic resources could have further strengthened the relationship between sovereign and bank risks, thereby aggravating the potential negative feedback effects between the two sectors. Thus, on 20 July 2012 the Eurogroup approved financial assistance of up to db100 billion, as part of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) agreed by the Spanish and European authorities, with the participation of the IMF. The MoU includes specific conditions for banks in need of public sector support and horizontal requirements for the banking sector as a whole and the regulatory and supervisory framework. The ultimate objective of this agreement is to strengthen the resilience of our banking system and establish the confidence necessary to normalize access to international financing markets. The Memorandum of Understanding establishes a clear roadmap for the recapitalisation and restructuring of the Spanish banking system. The key component of the programme is the review of the most vulnerable segments of the banking sector, with three main elements: - First, the identification of the capital needs of each bank through a comprehensive review of the asset quality of the banking sector and a disaggregated, bank-by-bank stress test exercise carried out by an independent external consultant. - Secondly, the recapitalisation, restructuring or resolution of the most vulnerable institutions, through the implementation of plans to address the capital needs identified in the stress test. - And finally, the segregation of problem assets into entities receiving public aid for their recapitalisation, and their transfer to an external Asset Management Company. These three elements constitute the core of the strategy we are pursuing to conclusively restore confidence in the solvency of the Spanish banking system in its entirety. Let me now elaborate on what has happened recently in these three areas. 3.1 Asset quality review and stress testing The first phase of this process consisted of the assessment of the capital needs of Spanish banks, which has been carried out in two stages. The first was the top-down test. The results of this year, published at the end of June, showed that, in an initial approximation, the Spanish banking system could need between 51,000 million and 62,000 million euros to maintain the capital ratio or Core Tier 1 of 6% in a very adverse macroeconomic scenario. This exercise helped to narrow down the magnitude of the potential capital needs of the system as a whole, which were estimated to be well below the db100 billion financial assistance agreed with the European authorities. In addition, this aggregate exercise also provided information on the distribution of capital requirements among different categories of institutions. Specifically, the results showed that the bulk of the capital needs were concentrated in a group of 4 entities already owned by the Fund for Orderly Bank Restructuring (FROB). The exercise also showed that larger banking groups would not need additional capital even in a very adverse scenario. However, while the information used in this exercise enabled us to obtain a reasonable estimate of the capital requirements of the banking system as a whole, it was not sufficiently granular or detailed to provide an individual bank-by-bank estimate. Therefore, after completing the aggregate exercise, a disaggregated analysis was carried out from the beginning of July to the end of September. This analysis involved, as a first step, a thorough due diligence review and a detailed analysis of specific banks' portfolios. The results of this preliminary work were then used in a second round of stress tests to determine the capital requirements of each institution. To ensure consistency with the aggregate exercise carried out in June, the same macroeconomic scenarios were used and the exercise was applied to the same set of banks, which included 17 banking groups representing around 90% of the Spanish banking system. I would like to highlight three characteristics of the exercise, which illustrate the rigor with which it was carried out: - Firstly, the completeness of the information used. The exercise was carried out by the consultancy Oliver Wyman, which had access to individualized information on loans from databases of credit institutions and the Bank of Spain, as well as the business plans of each banking group. In addition, the four main audit firms verified the quality of data on the loan portfolio and assets foreclosed or received in payment of real estate debts, and the adequacy of the accounting classification and the levels of provisions. Finally, six national and international real estate valuation companies carried out an exhaustive review exercise of real estate assets. Second, both the scenarios and the assumptions considered are very conservative. For example, the adverse scenario envisages a sharp cumulative fall of 6.5% of GDP over a three-year period. In addition, the probability of default considered in the adverse scenario was extraordinarily high, reaching, in the case of some portfolios, a level equivalent to five times the current default rates. Also, in this scenario, a loss of 64% was assumed for assets foreclosed or received in payment of real estate debts. Finally, in order to ensure the quality and consistent application of the methodology, a strong governance structure was established to monitor the exercise. Two committees, composed of experts and representatives of national and international authorities, were responsible for making the main strategic decisions and monitoring the exercise. In addition to the Spanish authorities, the European Commission, the European Central Bank (ECB), the European Banking Authority (EBA) and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) participated very actively in the work of these committees. The results of the disaggregated exercise were presented on September 28 and show that in the most likely scenario d0 the baseline scenario d0 only banks already owned by the FROB would need a significant volume of additional capital to meet the minimum capital ratio required of 9%2. The capital ratio was set at 9% in the baseline scenario and 6% in the adverse scenario. These figures are in line with the ratios established in other countries. In the adverse scenario, 7 banking groups, representing 62% of the loan portfolio analyzed, would not need additional capital. In the case of these groups of In the absence of additional measures, although all of them are already making significant efforts in terms of provisions, in accordance with the requirements established in the Royal Decrees-Laws approved in the first half of this year. The remaining banks included in the year, representing 38% of the loan portfolio, would need additional capital in the adverse scenario to meet the minimum required capital ratio of 6%. The estimated capital needs for the system as a whole would amount to db59 billion, without taking into account the tax effects and impact of ongoing integration processes. These capital requirements are in line with those estimated in the previous aggregate year in June and are well below the maximum support under the financial assistance programme. It should be noted that up to 86% of the capital needs of the sector, in the adverse scenario, correspond to the 4 entities in which the FROB has a majority stake. For all other banks, the capital needs, the need for public aid and, where applicable, the exact amount of this public aid will be determined following a detailed analysis of the recapitalisation and restructuring plans submitted by each bank. It is important to note here that the public support provided to banks will not, in general, coincide with the capital needs estimated in the stress test. In particular, the need for support will depend on a number of measures that institutions can take to reduce their final capital needs. In particular, institutions may divest assets or lines of business; transfer them to the Asset Management Company; carry out burden-sharing exercises involving the assumption of losses by holders of hybrid or subordinated debt instruments or raise new private capital on the markets. 3.2 Restructuring and recapitalisation plans Once the capital needs of each bank have been determined, the next step in the roadmap set out in the MoU is the recapitalisation and restructuring of the weaker institutions. In the case of entities already owned by the FROB (Group 1 entities), the Spanish authorities have been working on recovery or resolution plans jointly with the European Commission since the end of July 2012. We hope that these plans will be approved before the end of November. The remaining banks with capital needs under the stress test have recently submitted their recapitalisation plans. After a preliminary analysis, we have concluded, in agreement with the services of the European Commission, that two of these entities (Banco Popular and Ibercaja) will be able to cover their capital needs by their own means, at the latest, by the end of December 2012. It is expected that the remaining four entities will have to use public aid to meet their recapitalisation needs. It is important to underline that entities receiving public aid will launch a restructuring process compatible with European regulations in this area. Such restructuring plans will place greater demands on institutions in need of more public support and this could entail requirements in terms of resizing, elimination of non-core activities or unprofitable business segments, rebalancing of funding structures, improvements in governance, rationalisation of branch networks and staffing levels, as well as burden-sharing exercises that would affect holders of hybrid and subordinated instruments. The restructuring plans of these entities are expected to be approved before the end of the year. They will be granted assistance as soon as the Bank of Spain and the Commission approve such plans. Once the operation has been agreed, the European Stability Mechanism (ESM) will transfer the funds to the FROB, which will then inject them into the entities to strengthen their capital ratio. 3.3 Segregation of impaired assets Finally, one of the main elements of the recapitalisation and restructuring process will be the segregation of impaired assets of institutions requiring public aid d0 assets mainly related to the real estate sector d0 through their transfer to an external Asset Management Company (EMS). Very important steps have recently been taken in this direction. In particular, it is expected that two legislative measures establishing the legal status of the Asset Management Company, to be called 'Sareb', will be adopted shortly, and which is mainly characterised by the following: Firstly, with regard to its capital structure, Sareb will be designed in such a way that ownership will basically remain in the hands of private investors, while the Spanish authorities (the FROB) will have a non-majority stake. Sareb's own resources, part of which will take the form of subordinated debt, will represent approximately 8% of total assets. It should be noted that credit institutions transferring their assets will not be shareholders of Sareb nor will they be represented on its board of directors. In exchange for the assets contributed, these entities will receive debt issued by Sareb and guaranteed by the State. In general, Sareb will have three main sources of financing: (i) the issuance of preferential debt with State guarantee, which will be subscribed by credit institutions transferring assets; (ii) subordinated perpetual debt and (iii) common shares. Secondly, as regards the perimeter of the Asset Management Company, it will include assets foreclosed or received in payment of real estate debts, whose net book value exceeds 100,000 euros, loans to real estate developers, whose net book value exceeds 250,000 euros, and controlling shareholdings linked to the real estate sector. We have also determined the maximum size of the company, which will not exceed 90,000 million euros. Based on current information, the volume of assets to be transferred by credit institutions in which the FROB has a majority stake is estimated at 45,000 million euros. This amount would increase to about 60,000 million euros once the assets of the rest of the entities that require public aid are transferred. The transfer price of these assets shall be based on two distinct elements. First, the actual economic value of the assets, which will be determined using the detailed information and expected losses of the baseline scenario used in the disaggregated stress test. Second, additional downward adjustments will be made, which will vary across asset classes. These adjustments will be intended to take account of the very particular characteristics of this operation, for example: the bulk acquisition of assets; taking into account the costs of managing and administering the assets to be transferred; the outlook for the timing of divestment of assets, and other factors related to the risks involved in Sareb's specific activity. As a result of these one-off adjustments, the transfer price of the assets to Sareb does not constitute a valid reference for the valuation of other bank assets that have not been transferred to Sareb. Therefore, final transfer prices will be very conservative and will vary between asset classes. The average valuation haircut with respect to gross book values will be 63% for assets foreclosed or received in payment of real estate debts and 45.6% for loans. We have already prepared an interim business plan for Sareb, which is currently being discussed with potential private investors. This plan has been designed for a 15-year horizon and contemplates the macroeconomic and financial evolution of the Spanish economy, in particular, that of the real estate market. Taking this scenario into account and considering the market's absorption capacity, based on the different asset classes and their geographical location, Sareb is expected to obtain an attractive return on equity under normal circumstances. However, given the economic outlook and the time horizon of this activity, the results could be rather modest in the first years, when a large volume of assets have to be financed, while sales still represent only a limited part of the stock. In line with our expectations, the Asset Management Company should be fully operational by December, when the first Group 1 assets are expected to be transferred. 4 Next steps To summarize, in the space of a few months great progress has been made in the restructuring of the Spanish banking sector and the process is expected to be completed shortly. What are the main measures to be taken from now on? With regard to capitalization, we expect that the plans of Group 1 credit institutions d0 that is, those in which the FROB has a majority stake d0 could be approved by the end of this month. As for the other entities that require public aid, their plans will be approved in December. Therefore, we expect that the funds necessary for the recapitalisation of all entities requiring such support will be available before the end of this year. As regards the asset separation process, we hope that the new legislation will enter into force as soon as possible. At this time, the management team is being recruited and the review of the assets to be transferred by Group 1 (nationalised) credit institutions has already begun. The first assets will be transferred to Sareb in December and we expect that the assets of Group 2 entities (entities that require recapitalisation with public aid) could be transferred at the beginning of 2013. 5 Conclusions Overall, we have a clear roadmap for the restructuring and recapitalisation of the Spanish banking system, with a number of well-defined milestones. So far, significant progress has been made, as recently acknowledged by the IMF and the European authorities. We are on the right track and, by the end of this year, most of the process should be completed. I am sure that this will make a significant contribution to strengthening confidence in the Spanish banking sector as a whole. Thanks a lot.
text_original: 15.11.2012 Reforma del sector bancario espaol: medidas para reforzar la estabilidad financiera1 Seminario de banqueros centrales del Banco Santander Fernando Restoy Subgobernador Traduccin del original en ingls 1 Introduccin Me complace enormemente poder participar en esta Conferencia Bancaria Internacional organizada por Banco Santander. Como todos ustedes saben, el sistema bancario espaol se encuentra inmerso en un proceso de reestructuracin y recapitalizacin sin precedentes. Se han dado ya pasos importantes y esperamos que este proceso termine en algunos meses. Creo que esta conferencia nos brinda una oportunidad excelente para hacer un repaso de lo que se ha hecho hasta el momento y para examinar los principales desafos an pendientes. 2 Medidas iniciales para reforzar la confianza en el sector bancario espaol: 2008 a mediados de 2012 Los principales problemas del sector bancario espaol tienen su origen en los desequilibrios acumulados en el prolongado perodo de expansin que precedi a la crisis financiera. Durante este perodo, el crdito al sector privado, y especialmente a la construccin y a la promocin inmobiliaria, registr un fuerte crecimiento. Este crecimiento del crdito no se pudo financiar totalmente con depsitos minoristas y, por lo tanto, los bancos recurrieron de forma creciente a los mercados mayoristas e interbancarios internacionales. Este hecho aument la vulnerabilidad de las entidades de crdito espaolas ante posibles perturbaciones en los mercados financieros. La importancia de las vulnerabilidades citadas se puso de manifiesto en el transcurso de la crisis. Por consiguiente, entre 2008 y 2011, las autoridades espaolas adoptaron varias medidas, orientadas bsicamente a apoyar la liquidez de las entidades, promover la consolidacin y reestructuracin de las ms frgiles (especialmente de las cajas de ahorro), y aumentar los niveles de capital y de provisiones, sobre todo para cubrir los riesgos derivados del sector inmobiliario. No obstante, estas medidas no lograron restablecer plenamente la confianza sobre la solidez de un segmento del sistema bancario espaol. Efectivamente, las seales de vulnerabilidad percibidas aumentaron en 2011 y principios de 2012, como consecuencia de la persistente incertidumbre sobre la calidad de los activos relacionados con la construccin y la promocin inmobiliaria. Esas seales se pusieron de manifiesto en un entorno marcado, adems, por un deterioro de las perspectivas macroeconmicas (una doble recesin), por la prolongacin y agravamiento de los efectos de la crisis de la deuda soberana y por los retos a los que se enfrenta la poltica presupuestaria.
