Por este motivo, durante el primer semestre de 2012 se adoptaron importantes medidas adicionales para mitigar la incertidumbre relativa a la valoracin de activos relacionados con la construccin y la promocin inmobiliaria. En particular, en febrero y mayo, el Gobierno aprob dos Reales Decretos-Leyes, que exigan un aumento significativo de las provisiones para los crditos daados y activos adjudicados o recibidos en pago de deudas inmobiliarias. Adems, se tomaron medidas para hacer frente a la inquietud por la evolucin de los activos sanos , exigiendo que las entidades de crdito introdujeran una provisin general del 30% para la cartera de prstamos clasificada como estndar a fin de tener en cuenta la posible migracin desde la cartera normal a la cartera de prstamos problemticos. En general, el saneamiento de los balances resultante de estas medidas conlleva un acusado aumento de las provisiones frente a posibles prdidas adicionales del sistema financiero. De hecho, cuando estas medidas se hayan aplicado totalmente, las provisiones acumuladas por el sector bancario espaol desde 2007 a 2012 ascendern a ms de 200.000 millones de euros (en torno al 20% del PIB). 3 La reestructuracin en curso del sector bancario espaol Estas medidas contribuyeron a mejorar la percepcin sobre la situacin del sector financiero espaol. No obstante, era necesario adoptar medidas adicionales para hacer frente a la incertidumbre que an persista en los mercados. Por consiguiente, las autoridades espaolas adoptaron dos nuevas e importantes decisiones: - En primer lugar, en mayo, decidieron realizar una evaluacin independiente de la solvencia y de las perspectivas de negocio del sistema bancario espaol. Concretamente, se llev a cabo un ejercicio para evaluar la resistencia de las entidades en caso de un deterioro adicional de la economa y para determinar el nivel de capital que garantizara la viabilidad a largo plazo de los bancos. - Y, en segundo lugar, a finales de junio, las autoridades solicitaron asistencia financiera externa. La recapitalizacin y reestructuracin del sector bancario exiga medidas de respaldo por parte del sector pblico para asegurar que las posibles necesidades de capital quedaran cubiertas. Sin embargo, habida cuenta de la situacin en los mercados de deuda soberana, se tuvo la impresin de que el establecimiento de tales medidas de respaldo utilizando solo recursos internos podra haber reforzado ms an la relacin entre los riesgos soberanos y los riesgos bancarios, agravando con ello los posibles efectos de retroalimentacin negativos entre ambos sectores. As pues, el 20 de julio de 2012 el Eurogrupo aprob una asistencia financiera de hasta 100.000 millones de euros, como parte de un Memorando de Entendimiento (MoU) acordado por las autoridades espaolas y europeas, con la participacin del FMI. El MoU incluye condiciones especficas para las entidades de crdito que necesiten apoyo del sector pblico y requerimientos horizontales para el conjunto del sector bancario y el marco regulador y supervisor. El objetivo ltimo de este acuerdo es reforzar la resistencia de nuestro sistema bancario y establecer la confianza necesaria para normalizar el acceso a los mercados de financiacin internacionales. El Memorando de Entendimiento establece una hoja de ruta clara para la recapitalizacin y reestructuracin del sistema bancario espaol. El componente clave del programa es la revisin de los segmentos ms vulnerables del sector bancario, con tres elementos principales: - En primer lugar, la identificacin de las necesidades de capital de cada entidad de crdito mediante una revisin exhaustiva de la calidad de los activos del sector bancario y un ejercicio de prueba de resistencia desagregada, banco por banco, llevada a cabo por un consultor externo independiente. - En segundo lugar, la recapitalizacin, reestructuracin o resolucin de las entidades ms vulnerables, mediante la aplicacin de planes que permitan hacer frente a las necesidades de capital identificadas en la prueba de resistencia. - Y, por ltimo, la segregacin de los activos problemticos en las entidades que reciban ayudas pblicas para su recapitalizacin, y su transferencia a una Sociedad de Gestin de Activos externa. Estos tres elementos constituyen el ncleo de la estrategia que estamos persiguiendo para restablecer de manera concluyente la confianza en la solvencia del sistema bancario espaol en su integridad. Permtanme explicar ahora con ms detalle lo sucedido ltimamente en estas tres reas. 3.1 Revisin de la calidad de los activos y pruebas de resistencia La primera fase de este proceso consisti en la evaluacin de las necesidades de capital de los bancos espaoles, que se ha llevado a cabo en dos etapas. La primera fue la prueba de resistencia agregada (top-down). Los resultados de este ejercicio, publicados a finales de junio, mostraron que, en una aproximacin inicial, el sistema bancario espaol podra necesitar entre 51.000 millones y 62.000 millones de euros para mantener la ratio de capital o Core Tier 1 del 6% en un escenario macroeconmico muy adverso. Este ejercicio ayud a delimitar la magnitud de las necesidades de capital potenciales del sistema en su conjunto, que, segn las estimaciones, se situaban claramente por debajo de la ayuda financiera de 100.000 millones de euros acordada con las autoridades europeas. Adems, este ejercicio agregado tambin proporcion informacin sobre la distribucin de las necesidades de capital entre distintas categoras de entidades. Concretamente, los resultados mostraron que el grueso de las necesidades de capital se concentraba en un grupo de 4 entidades ya participadas por el Fondo de Reestructuracin Ordenada Bancaria (FROB). Asimismo, el ejercicio mostr que los grupos bancarios ms grandes no necesitaran capital adicional incluso en un escenario muy adverso. No obstante, si bien la informacin empleada en este ejercicio nos permiti obtener una estimacin razonable de las necesidades de capital del conjunto del sistema bancario, no era lo bastante granular o detallado para ofrecer una estimacin individual banco por banco. Por consiguiente, tras completar el ejercicio agregado, se llev a cabo un anlisis de carcter desagregado desde principios de julio a finales de septiembre. Este anlisis supuso, en una primera etapa, efectuar una revisin exhaustiva de debida diligencia y un anlisis detallado de carteras de entidades de crdito especficas. Los resultados de este trabajo preliminar se utilizaron despus en una segunda ronda de pruebas de resistencia para determinar las necesidades de capital de cada entidad. Para garantizar la coherencia con el ejercicio agregado llevado a cabo en junio, se utilizaron los mismos escenarios macroeconmicos y el ejercicio se aplic al mismo conjunto de entidades de crdito, que inclua 17 grupos bancarios que representan en torno al 90% del sistema bancario espaol. Me gustara destacar tres caractersticas del ejercicio, que ilustran el rigor con el que se llev a cabo: - En primer lugar, la exhaustividad de la informacin empleada. El ejercicio fue realizado por la consultora Oliver Wyman, que tuvo acceso a informacin individualizada de los prstamos procedente de bases de datos de las entidades de crdito y del Banco de Espaa, as como a los planes de negocio de cada grupo bancario. Adems, las cuatro principales firmas de auditora verificaron la calidad de los datos sobre la cartera de prstamos y los activos adjudicados o recibidos en pago de deudas inmobiliarias, y la adecuacin de la clasificacin contable y los niveles de las provisiones. Por ltimo, seis sociedades de valoracin inmobiliaria nacionales e internacionales realizaron un ejercicio exhaustivo de revisin de los activos inmobiliarios. - En segundo lugar, tanto los escenarios como los supuestos considerados son muy conservadores. Por ejemplo, el escenario adverso contempla una fuerte cada acumulada del 6,5% del PIB en un perodo de tres aos. Adems, las probabilidades de impago consideradas en el escenario adverso fueron extraordinariamente elevadas, llegando, en el caso de algunas carteras, hasta un nivel equivalente a cinco veces las tasas de impago actuales. Asimismo, en ese escenario, se supuso una prdida del 64% para los activos adjudicados o recibidos en pago de deudas inmobiliarias. Por ltimo, a fin de garantizar la calidad y la aplicacin coherente de la metodologa, se estableci una slida estructura de gobernanza para supervisar el ejercicio. Dos comits, integrados por expertos y representantes de las autoridades nacionales e internacionales, se encargaron de adoptar las principales decisiones estratgicas y de hacer un seguimiento del ejercicio. Adems de las autoridades espaolas, participaron de forma muy activa en las tareas de estos comits la Comisin Europea, el Banco Central Europeo (BCE), la Autoridad Bancaria Europea (EBA) y el Fondo Monetario Internacional (FMI). Los resultados del ejercicio desagregado se presentaron el 28 de septiembre y muestran que en el escenario ms probable el escenario base- solo los bancos ya participados por el FROB necesitaran un volumen significativo de capital adicional para cumplir la ratio de capital mnima exigida del 9%2. La ratio de capital se fij en el 9% en el escenario base y en el 6% en el escenario adverso. Estas cifras estn en consonancia con las ratios establecidas en otros pases. En el escenario adverso, 7 grupos bancarios, que representan el 62% de la cartera crediticia analizada, no necesitaran capital adicional. En el caso de estos grupos de entidades, no se precisar la adopcin de medidas adicionales, aunque todos ellos ya estn realizando importantes esfuerzos en materia de provisiones, de conformidad con los requerimientos establecidos en los Reales Decretos Leyes aprobados en el primer semestre de este ao. El resto de las entidades incluidas en el ejercicio, que representan el 38% de la cartera de prstamos, necesitaran capital adicional en el escenario adverso para cumplir la ratio de capital mnima exigida del 6%. Las necesidades de capital estimadas para el conjunto del sistema ascenderan a 59.000 millones de euros, sin tener en cuenta los efectos impositivos y el impacto de los procesos de integracin en marcha. Estas necesidades de capital estn en lnea con las estimadas en el anterior ejercicio agregado llevado a cabo en junio y se sitan claramente por debajo del respaldo mximo contemplado en el programa de asistencia financiera. Conviene destacar que hasta un 86% de las necesidades de capital del sector, en el escenario adverso, corresponden a las 4 entidades en las que el FROB tiene una participacin mayoritaria. Para el resto de bancos, las necesidades de capital, la necesidad de ayuda pblica y, en su caso, el importe exacto de esta ayuda pblica ser determinada tras un anlisis detallado de los planes de recapitalizacin y reestructuracin presentados por cada entidad. Aqu es importante sealar que las ayudas pblicas proporcionadas a los bancos no coincidirn, en general, con las necesidades de capital estimadas en la prueba de resistencia. En particular, la necesidad de ayudas depender de varias medidas que las entidades pueden adoptar para reducir sus necesidades de capital definitivas. Concretamente, las entidades pueden desprenderse de activos o lneas de negocio; transferirlos a la Sociedad de Gestin de Activos; llevar cabo ejercicios de distribucin de la carga que suponen la asuncin de prdidas por parte de los tenedores de instrumentos hbridos o de deuda subordinada, u obtener nuevo capital privado en los mercados. 3.2 Planes de reestructuracin y recapitalizacin Una vez determinadas las necesidades de capital de cada entidad de crdito, el siguiente paso en la hoja de ruta establecida en el MoU es la recapitalizacin y la reestructuracin de las entidades ms dbiles. En el caso de las entidades ya participadas por el FROB (entidades del Grupo 1), las autoridades espaolas llevan trabajando en los planes de reestructuracin o de resolucin conjuntamente con la Comisin Europea desde finales de julio de 2012. Esperamos que dichos planes queden aprobados antes de finales de noviembre. Las entidades restantes con necesidades de capital segn la prueba de resistencia han presentado recientemente sus planes de recapitalizacin. Tras un anlisis preliminar, hemos concluido, de acuerdo con los servicios de la Comisin Europea, que dos de estas entidades (Banco Popular e Ibercaja) sern capaces de cubrir sus necesidades de capital por sus propios medios, a ms tardar, a finales de diciembre de 2012. Se prev que las cuatro entidades restantes tendrn que recurrir a las ayudas pblicas para hacer frente a sus necesidades de recapitalizacin. Es importante subrayar que las entidades que reciban ayudas pblicas pondrn en marcha un proceso de reestructuracin compatible con la normativa europea en esta materia. Esos planes de reestructuracin supondrn mayores demandas para las entidades que necesiten ms ayudas pblicas y ello podra entraar exigencias en trminos de redimensionamiento, eliminacin de actividades no esenciales o segmentos del negocio no rentables, reequilibrio de las estructuras de financiacin, mejoras en la gobernanza, racionalizacin de las redes de sucursales y de los niveles de personal, as como ejercicios de distribucin de la carga que afectaran a los tenedores de instrumentos hbridos y subordinados. Se espera que los planes de reestructuracin de estas entidades estn aprobados antes de finales de ao. Se les otorgar asistencia tan pronto como el Banco de Espaa y la Comisin aprueben dichos planes. Una vez que se haya acordado la operacin, el Mecanismo Europeo de Estabilidad (MEDE) transferir los fondos al FROB, que, posteriormente, los inyectar en las entidades para reforzar su ratio de capital. 3.3 Segregacin de los activos deteriorados Finalmente, uno de los principales elementos del proceso de recapitalizacin y reestructuracin ser la segregacin de los activos deteriorados de las instituciones que requieran ayudas pblicas activos relacionados, fundamentalmente, con el sector inmobiliario mediante su transferencia a una Sociedad de Gestin de Activos (SGA) externa. Recientemente se han dado pasos muy importantes en este sentido. En particular, se prev que en breve se adopten dos medidas legislativas por las que se establece el rgimen jurdico de la Sociedad de Gestin de Activos, que se denominar Sareb y que se caracteriza principalmente por lo siguiente: En primer lugar, en lo que respecta a su estructura de capital, la Sareb se disear de tal forma que la propiedad quedar, bsicamente, en manos de inversores privados, mientras que las autoridades espaolas (el FROB) tendrn una participacin no mayoritaria. Los recursos propios de la Sareb, parte de los cuales adoptarn la forma de deuda subordinada, representarn el 8% de los activos totales, aproximadamente. Cabe sealar que las entidades de crdito que transfieran sus activos no sern accionistas de la Sareb ni estarn representadas en su consejo de administracin. A cambio de los activos aportados, dichas entidades recibirn deuda emitida por la Sareb y garantizada por el Estado. En general, la Sareb tendr tres fuentes principales de financiacin: i) la emisin de deuda preferente con garanta del Estado, que suscribirn las entidades de crdito que transfieran activos; ii) deuda perpetua subordinada y iii) acciones ordinarias. En segundo lugar, por lo que respecta al permetro de la Sociedad de Gestin de Activos, incluir activos adjudicados o recibidos en pago de deudas inmobiliarias, cuyo valor contable neto sea superior a 100.000 euros, prstamos a promotores inmobiliarios, cuyo valor contable neto sea superior a 250.000 euros, y participaciones accionariales de control vinculadas al sector inmobiliario. Hemos determinado tambin el tamao mximo de la sociedad, que no exceder de 90.000 millones de euros. Sobre la base de la informacin actual, el volumen de activos que habrn de transferir las entidades de crdito en las que el FROB tenga una participacin mayoritaria se estima en 45.000 millones de euros. Esta cantidad se incrementara hasta unos 60.000 millones de euros una vez que se transfieran los activos del resto de entidades que requieren ayudas pblicas. El precio de transmisin de estos activos se basar en dos elementos diferenciados. En primer lugar, el valor econmico real de los activos, que se determinar utilizando la informacin detallada y las prdidas esperadas del escenario base empleado en la prueba de resistencia desagregada. En segundo lugar, se realizarn ajustes adicionales a la baja, que variarn segn las categoras de activos. Estos ajustes tendrn por objeto tomar en consideracin las caractersticas muy particulares de esta operacin, por ejemplo: la adquisicin en bloque de activos; la consideracin de los costes de gestin y de administracin de los activos que se hayan de transferir; las perspectivas en cuanto al momento de la desinversin de los activos, y otros factores relacionados con los riesgos que entraa la actividad especfica de la Sareb. Como resultado de estos ajustes singulares, el precio de transmisin de los activos a la Sareb no constituye una referencia vlida para la valoracin de otros activos bancarios que no hayan sido transferidos a la Sareb. Por consiguiente, los precios finales de transmisin sern muy conservadores y variarn entre las distintas categoras de activos. El recorte de valoracin medio con respecto a los valores contables brutos ser del 63% para los activos adjudicados o recibidos en pago de deudas inmobiliarias y del 45,6% para los prstamos. Ya hemos preparado un plan de negocio provisional para la Sareb, que se est discutiendo actualmente con los posibles inversores privados. Dicho plan se ha diseado para un horizonte de 15 aos y contempla la evolucin macroeconmica y financiera de la economa espaola, en particular, la del mercado inmobiliario. Teniendo en cuenta este escenario y considerando la capacidad de absorcin del mercado, basada en las distintas categoras de activos y en su localizacin geogrfica, se prev que la Sareb obtenga una atractiva rentabilidad de los recursos propios en circunstancias normales. No obstante, habida cuenta de las perspectivas econmicas y del horizonte temporal de esta actividad, los resultados podran ser ms bien modestos en los primeros aos, en los que hay que financiar un gran volumen de activos, mientras que las ventas solo representan todava una parte limitada del stock. Conforme a nuestras expectativas, la Sociedad de Gestin de Activos debera estar funcionando plenamente en diciembre, cuando se prev que se transfieran los primeros activos del Grupo 1. 4 Prximas medidas Para resumir, en el plazo de unos pocos meses se han logrado grandes avances en la reestructuracin del sector bancario espaol y se prev concluir en breve el proceso. Cules son las principales medidas que habr que adoptar a partir de ahora? Por lo que respecta a la capitalizacin, esperamos que los planes de las entidades de crdito del Grupo 1 es decir, aquellas en las que el FROB tiene una participacin mayoritaria podran estar aprobados a finales de este mes. En cuanto a las otras entidades que requieran ayudas pblicas, sus planes se aprobarn en diciembre. Por lo tanto, esperamos que los fondos necesarios para la recapitalizacin de todas las entidades que requieran dichas ayudas estarn disponibles antes del final de este ao. En lo referente al proceso de segregacin de activos, esperamos que la nueva legislacin entre en vigor lo antes posible. En este momento, se est contratando al equipo gestor y ya se ha iniciado el examen de los activos que habrn de transferir las entidades de crdito (nacionalizadas) del Grupo 1. Los primeros activos se transferirn a la Sareb en diciembre y esperamos que los activos de las entidades del Grupo 2 (entidades que requieren recapitalizacin con ayudas pblicas) podran ser transferidos a comienzos de 2013. 5 Conclusiones En conjunto, contamos con una hoja de ruta clara para la reestructuracin y la recapitalizacin del sistema bancario espaol, con una serie de hitos bien definidos. Hasta ahora, se han logrado progresos significativos, como han reconocido recientemente el FMI y las autoridades europeas. Vamos por buen camino y, para finales de este ao, debera estar concluido la mayor parte del proceso. Estoy seguro de que ello supondr una significativa contribucin para fortalecer la confianza en el sector bancario espaol en su conjunto. Muchas gracias.

Title: Speech of the XIV Rey Juan Carlos Economy Prize
text: December 4, 2012 Speech at the XIV King Juan Carlos Economics Prize Luis M. Linde Governor Your Highness, Minister, Ladies and Gentlemen, Allow me to say my first words to His Majesty the King, who has always accompanied us in this event since 1986, when we celebrated it for the first time at the Banco de Espa96a. I would like to ask you, Your Highness, to convey to Your Majesty our most respectful and cordial remembrance and our wish for a speedy and full recovery. This is the first time, Your Highness, that you preside over the delivery of the King Juan Carlos Economy Prize, but it is not the first time you have visited this House. You did it for the first time in March 1989, as part of a group of students from the Autonomous University of Madrid. And, on a second occasion, in October 2001, when sharing a working day with our Executive Committee. We are very honored by your presence today. The King Juan Carlos Economy Prize was instituted by the Jos8e Celma Prieto Foundation, whom I want to thank, in the person of its President, Don Jos8e Celma, who is with us today, for his generous and tenacious work of patronage. The Award aims to recognize the academic or professional career in the field of Economics of a Spanish or Ibero-American personality. The Banco de Espa96a is honoured to host an award ceremony whose prestige is measured by the stature of the personalities who have received it: Pedro Schwartz (2010), Joaqu92n Muns (2008), Gonzalo Anes (2006), Xavier Sala Mart92 (2004), Juan Velarde (2002), Guillermo Calvo (2000), Enrique Fuentes (1998), Salvador Barber87 (1996), Gabriel Tortella (1994), Miguel Mancera (1992), Julio Segura (1990), Andreu Mas-Colell (1988) and Luis e7ngel Rojo (1986). According to the statutes governing the award, the Governor of the Banco de Espa96a chairs the Jury, which in this 2012 edition was composed of Mr. Jos8e Ram97n e7lvarez Rendueles, Mr. Gonzalo Anes, Mr. Rodolfo Mart92n Villa, Mr. Andreu Mas-Colell, Mr. Aurelio Men8endez and Mr. Juan Velarde. This jury decided on September 28 to award the 2012 King Juan Carlos Economics Prize to Professor Jaime Terceiro Lomba. The list of winners I have just read shows the variety of dedications of the winners, with the only common denominator of excellence. The academic and professional contribution of Professor Jaime Terceiro adds to this list a new and brilliant profile. Professor Jaime Terceiro holds a PhD in Aeronautical Engineering, with an extraordinary award, from the Polytechnic University of Madrid. After focusing on economics, he graduated in Economics from the Autonomous University of Madrid, also with an extraordinary prize. And in 1980, he won by opposition the Chair of Econometrics and Statistical Methods of the Complutense University of Madrid. In his role as a mathematical economist, Jaime Terceiro was one of the introducers in Spain of the dynamic models of the equation of states, whose translation of the framework of engineering to economics has given and continues to bear important fruits in the fields of economic prediction, dynamic analysis between variables and estimation of unobserved components. These techniques are a fundamental tool for analysis and prediction in most research services (including that of the Bank of Spain) and university departments with lines of research in these fields. Professor Terceiro himself has applied these techniques to the Spanish economy in several works on prediction of the consumer price index, the relationship of liquid availabilities, credit and industrial production and causality between macroeconomic variables. A part of the teachings and research of Professor Terceiro in that decade of the 80s are collected in the monograph published in 1990 by the Springer-Verlag publishing house, in English, focused on the application of dynamic macroeconomic models when there are measurement errors in the variables. Going back a few years, Professor Terceiro's professional activity began, as soon as he finished his engineering studies, in Germany, in the Department of Simulation and Control of Messerschmitt-B9alkow-Blohm where he worked on procedures for the identification, estimation and control of complex systems, a work that is at the origin of his contributions to econometrics that I have just mentioned. Upon his return to Spain, Professor Terceiro held various management positions in financial institutions, beginning a career that would culminate, in 1988, with his appointment as Executive Chairman of Caja Madrid. Under his presidency, Caja Madrid undertook a stage of financial and technological expansion and modernization. These were also the years of the creation of the Caja de Madrid Financial Corporation and the Caja de Madrid Foundation, which significantly increased the Fund's resources for its social work. They were, in short, years of intense modernization of Caja Madrid, in tune with the general modernization of the Spanish financial system. Soon Professor Terceiro transcended his role as manager, developing a new vision for savings banks in which he disagreed with the then dominant thought, according to which the high solvency and capacity to generate profits of the savings banks in those years validated the system. In his analyses, Professor Terceiro pointed out that the apparent strength of the sector was due to strong regulation and the existence of geographic markets protected by barriers to entry. For Professor Terceiro, the really relevant issue was the ability of savings banks to compete with other entities in the environment that was emerging from the process of liberalization of the banking system and Spain's entry into the European Union. In short, Professor Terceiro was ahead in the analysis of the problems of savings banks and was an early advocate of the reform of the sector. In this same context, Professor Terceiro made significant contributions in the area, today so topical, which we know as "governance". Examples of this are his study on the institutional problems of savings banks, published by the Royal Academy of Moral and Political Sciences in 1988 and his work "Las Cajas de Ahorro en la d8ecada de los 90", published by the El Monte Foundation in 1994. These works They constitute a pioneering analysis of the problems of the savings banks associated with the lack of definition of their legal form and their property rights and, consequently, of the weaknesses in their governance. Knowledge and action, theory and practice, effectively combined, are the two poles of Professor Terceiro's personality, which should be recognized throughout his outstanding and exemplary academic and financial career. Reiterating my gratitude to His Highness Prince Felipe for his presence at this event, I can only stand, with your permission, Your Highness, to ask the winner to take the stage so that you can present him with the 2012 King Juan Carlos Economy Prize.

Title: Opening of the exhibition "The new face of the euro"
text: March 25, 2013 Keynote address Opening of the exhibition "The new face of the euro"/Banco de Espa96a Fernando Restoy Deputy governor Good morning. I would like to begin these brief words by thanking all of you for your presence today at the opening of the exhibition "The New Face of the Euro" and, in particular, Yves Mersch, Member of the Executive Board of the European Central Bank, with whom we have the honour today to share this event in one of his first visits to a Member State. following his recent appointment. For the Bank of Spain it is a source of satisfaction to host this traveling exhibition on euro banknotes, which makes Madrid the first stop on the planned route of the exhibition, after having been open to the public for two months at the Archaeological Museum in Frankfurt. This is an excellent opportunity for citizens to learn more about the banknotes that we have been using daily as a means of payment for eleven years. As you can see, this careful exhibition offers not only useful practical information, but also games and curiosities about the history of the metallic currency and banknotes, which I trust will interest both adults and young people who begin to discover the meaning of money. I also consider that the timing of this exhibition is of particular interest. On the one hand, more than a decade after euro banknotes and coins were put into circulation, the European Central Bank has decided to begin the renewal of these banknotes, with the release of a second series, under the appropriate name of Europe. This series, which incorporates the most advanced security measures and technology, will be released on May 2, when we can start using the first copy of the new series, the new 5 euro banknote. The new series of banknotes was born at a time when Europe is going through a complex stage where, after a long period of expansion, many citizens suffer the consequences of the lack of economic growth and the increase in unemployment. However, although it may sometimes be difficult, the current intense crisis must not make us lose sight of the enormous benefits that European integration brings to economic prosperity and stability in Europe. In particular, for Spain, the introduction of the euro has been an anchor of macroeconomic stability that boosted the development and modernization of our country towards the standards of the most advanced economies. In difficult times, the common currency has also been a shield that has protected us from the many episodes of turbulence that have affected international markets since the beginning of the current century. There is no doubt that membership of the single currency requires us to make a continuous effort to keep our commitments and achieve the flexibility and efficiency that our economy requires to maintain its competitiveness within an increasingly commercially integrated common monetary area. However, I believe that no one can reasonably argue that the efforts needed to ensure economic prosperity could be lighter outside monetary union. Having said that, we have important challenges ahead in the European integration project, as has been shown in the crisis that began in 2010. If we have learned anything during this crisis, it is that the only way to restore stability and growth and preserve the integration achieved is precisely to continue moving towards more Europe, without allowing ourselves any step backwards. That is why the steps taken towards the creation of a banking union in Europe are an excellent example of the overall strategy to strengthen the European Union. And no one better to conclude this act than Yves Mersch, member of the Executive Board of the ECB. Mr Mersch has extensive experience as a public servant and, in particular, as a central banker, having remained a member d0 I would say a prominent member d0 of the Governing Council of the ECB, in his capacity as Governor of the Central Bank of Luxembourg, since its foundation in 1998. Yves is currently assigned important areas of responsibility at the ECB, such as banknotes, information systems and coordination d0 together with Vitor Constancio d0 of the preparation of the single supervisory mechanism. Let me then welcome Yves Mersch. Yves, thank you very much for being here today in Madrid in your first visit to Spain as an ECB Executive Board Member.

Title: Lessons of the Crisis for Research Agendas in Economics
text: 16.04.2013 Opening remarks at the CEMFI 25th Anniversary Conference Lessons of the Crisis for Research Agendas in Economics Fernando Restoy Subgobernador I would like to thank Rafael Repullo, the director and founder of CEMFI, who has been kind enough to invite me to participate in this special 25th Anniversary celebration for CEMFI. It is a great pleasure to introduce this conference in which outstanding academic economists like Christopher Sims and Andrei Shleifer will be offering presentations that, I am sure, will be of great interest. Unquestionably, CEMFI has played an essential role in the development of the highest quality teaching and research in economics in Spain. This role was especially important in its early years, when CEMFI was virtually the only option for receiving a top-level education in Spain in financial and monetary economics. Over the past twenty five years, CEMFI has not only managed to retain the spirit of its early years; it has also broadened its horizons, becoming an international point of reference as an academic centre. By way of example, CEMFI receives more than 250 applications every year from students from the leading universities in more than 50 different countries. The applications undergo a rigorous selection process until they are narrowed down to a limited number per course, at times as low as 20. Of course, this could not be possible without the excellent nucleus of professors CEMFI boasts. Throughout the years, CEMFI has been blessed in being able to attract and retain renowned researchers of the stature of Manuel Arellano, Samuel Bentolila, Rafael Repullo and Enrique Sentana, who together with a new generation of excellent economists, make up one of the best Departments of Economics in Europe. Among CEMFIs many contributions in the past twenty five years, let me emphasise the role it has played in improving the standard professional quality of the economists employed by both the public and private sectors. The Banco de Espana has naturally been one of the entities to benefit most from this. Currently, we are fortunate to have 60 CEMFI graduates working for the Bank and, in several cases, occupying substantially senior positions. But the contribution CEMFI has made to the profession does not just stop at improving human capital. Through its publications and seminars series, CEMFI participates prominently in both the academic and the policy debates on an equal footing with other outstanding academic institutions. Indeed, the role of economic research in policy-making is a recurrent topic for discussion in the profession. Let me use the rest of my time to offer some brief remarks on this. Taking policy decisions typically requires addressing analytical questions and/or conceptual problems on which economists have often accumulated knowledge by developing models and gathering and interpreting data through the lenses of well-established empirical methodologies. However, the research input does not always noticeably feed the policy decision process. In particular, it is often the case that we lack a sufficient degree of consensus on the right model and the relevant empirical evidence to justify a particular decision. Moreover, quite frequently, the available analysis of policy alternatives falls short of taking into account all the political and social constraints involved. In addition, when gaps between available knowledge and policy needs are apparent, the timing of policy-making is not always compatible with that of research, as there are decisions that cannot be delayed until the research comes up with new results, new insights and new evidence. During the crisis, we have witnessed a clear manifestation of these problems. Policy-makers have been under pressure to address questions that required urgent answers and action, for which available models, among them a wide variety of DSGE models in use at central banks, were not well-suited. Having been designed for other uses, DSGE models have not yet been able to fully incorporate relevant complex links between the real and financial sectors of the economy. Yet it is no less true that from time to time policy-makers have not paid sufficient attention to policy-relevant available economic research I mean good economic research- and that, by doing so, they have contributed to increasing the probability of making policy mistakes. Let me give an example. By looking at all the relevant deficiencies in the institutional design of EMU that the crisis has uncovered, it is natural to wonder whether somebody had already told us this but we did not want to hear. Frankly, despite the opportunistic proliferation of ex-post prophets, I believe that nobody fully anticipated the nature and, much less so, the magnitude of the current European crisis. More importantly, nobody really put forward at the right time a magic solution to prevent it. Yet, it is also clear that a few academics wrote insightful pieces many years back that would have merited careful reading and consideration by European leaders. One example is, obviously, one of our guests this afternoon, Professor Chris Sims. In an outstanding article written in 1999, he identified what he called the precarious fiscal foundations of EMU whose consequences have unfortunately become very real and have prompted a large-scale policy reform which is yet to be fully completed. In any case, it is simply unfair to ask academic economists to deliver solutions to complex institutional deficiencies which are largely rooted in political constraints or, more generally, in behavioural patterns of relevant agents that involve a departure from economic rationality. Nevertheless, let me highlight a few issues that I believe are, and will continue to be, among the most instrumental ones for the current conduct of policy-making in Europe. The first issue and the order is not at all random- is the identification of the best policy strategy to end fragmentation in European markets. This development is very much associated, as we all know, to the destabilising link between banking and sovereign risk, which is severely damaging the monetary policy transmission mechanism. We are still struggling in Europe to identify and naturally to implement- the right combination of initiatives in three different fields: domestic policies, monetary policy and institutional design. In connection with this latter area, the design of an effective resolution regime for troubled financial institutions in a multi-country monetary union context would very much benefit from a deeper economic analysis of the relevant trade-offs involved. Another area where further knowledge would be most welcome is fiscal policy, in general and with regard to its interactions with monetary policy. At present, a fierce debate rages between those who believe in expansionary fiscal austerity and those who, on the contrary, are convinced that fiscal consolidations, in the current context of depressed private demand, are self-defeating. The economic literature has illustrated this debate with a wide variety of new estimates of the so-called fiscal multipliers which, to a large extent, are taken as sufficient statistics of what fiscal policy can and cannot achieve. From my perspective, biased by the Spanish situation, I fail to extract sufficient guidance from this literature on how best to approach the debate in a country with no monetary autonomy, relatively high private indebtedness and subject to the adverse impact of still-excessive sovereign and redenomination risk. In any case, I think that in order to understand the effects of fiscal policy in the current complex economic set-up we need much more than extending the set of estimates of fiscal multipliers, even under new methodological approaches. Finally, a third set of issues on which deeper academic analysis would be welcomed is the interaction between regulatory reform and potential growth. I had the privilege of viewing the slides that Andrei Shleifer is expected to use in his presentation later on. I trust I will not be unveiling any confidential information if I anticipate that he will be arguing most convincingly that the neglected risk by both public and private players is one of the most powerful factors behind the crisis. That of course speaks quite loudly in favour of more stringent capital and liquidity requirements for financial institutions. Yet, we still need to fully understand the overall macroeconomic effects of a tougher prudential policy with a view to fine-tuning the different available regulatory instruments and, if needed and possible, to adjusting other policies in order to offset potentially adverse effects on the availability of financing. In any event I find that, beyond what research can do to optimise policy design, researchers themselves and, more generally, economists with deep-rooted training in advanced economic analysis, can and do contribute to making policy mistakes less frequent and severe and to improving the management of both public and private projects. That is why we at the Banco de Espana, as the sponsors of CEMFI, are so proud of the support provided to this academic centre over the years. Such support has been substantially vindicated by the numerous outstanding contributions CEMFI has made to the Bank itself, to the economics profession and to the country at large. So, happy anniversary.

Title: Presentation of the book "The institutional architecture of the refoundation of the euro"
text: 10.05.2013 Presentation of the book "The institutional architecture of the refoundation of the euro" Fundaci97n de Estudios Financieros/ICO Auditorium Fernando Restoy Deputy governor It is a pleasure to share with you the presentation of the report "The institutional architecture of the refounding of the euro". I would not like to start without thanking the Foundation for Financial Studies and, in particular, its President Juan Carlos Ureta for his kind invitation, as well as Rom87n Escolano, President of the ICO, for allowing us to hold this event in this auditorium. I believe that the study presented today, aimed at reflecting on the initiatives under way to improve the design of EMU, could not be more timely. Throughout their seven articles, the authors offer contributions of great interest with concrete proposals to move decisively towards a genuine banking, fiscal and economic union in EMU. Let me take this opportunity to join in these reflections on the reforms needed to address the weaknesses that EMU has shown in recent years. There is no doubt that these reforms require a balanced combination of measures at national level and measures at European level. I believe that in Spain, as in other countries, relevant steps are being taken to adopt measures that will improve the economy's ability to adjust in the event of idiosyncratic developments, to strengthen its competitiveness and to reduce the probability that, in the future, marked macro-financial imbalances may be generated. These measures at national level are essential to strengthen the functioning of monetary union. It is clear, however, that, at the same time, we need an institutional strengthening of Economic and Monetary Union, in order to prevent any hint of uncertainty about its own continuity which, as the recent past shows, can be very destabilising. In fact, I will focus my presentation on what is undoubtedly one of the most ambitious institutional reforms, the project to create the Banking Union. Introduction The crisis that the Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) is going through has its main manifestation in the fragmentation of its financial markets, understood as the re-emergence of a component of country risk in the cost of financing of issuers and borrowers whose magnitude depends on their location. As you know, this fragmentation of markets is rooted in the budgetary difficulties of various States in a context of the absence of effective risk mutualisation mechanisms at European level. These budgetary difficulties have been fuelled by the impact on economic activity of the sharp correction of certain macrofinancial imbalances, experienced by those national economies that suffered a very pronounced expansionary effect after the adoption of the single currency and that lacked sufficiently flexible product and labour markets to absorb this impact in a balanced way. These imbalances have acquired a particularly destabilizing dimension when they have ended up affecting the banking industry in those countries where the size of the sector, its solvency position or the very situation of public finances, made it difficult to use national budgetary funds for the preservation of financial stability. This feedback between banking and sovereign risk is, therefore, at the base of the current crisis, so overcoming it involves eliminating it or, at least, containing it effectively. As I pointed out earlier, it is clear that the solution to these problems is to take measures at the national level to contain structural fiscal imbalances, mitigate macrofinancial imbalances and increase the strength of the banking sector. At the same time, EMU needs to be institutionally strengthened so as to promote greater integration of the economies that are part of it. This entails the creation of centralized mechanisms for the coverage of contingencies and, in return, a greater transfer of sovereignty in the policies that are relevant to prevent and manage them. I believe that European leaders have largely learned their lesson, as shown by the remarkable progress made in recent years in reforming the institutional architecture of EMU. In particular, progress in improving the procedures established for monitoring a wide range of national policies in situations of macroeconomic imbalances represents a significant step forward. In particular, budgetary policy surveillance mechanisms have been significantly strengthened, especially following the introduction of the so-called 'Fiscal Compact'. In addition, resources have been allocated to the detection and monitoring of systemic risks with the creation of the European Systemic Risk Board (ESRB). Finally, with the establishment of the European Stability Mechanism (ESM), a permanent vehicle has been established to channel financial assistance to euro area countries that may need it. In any case, the progress made during the early years of the crisis was not sufficient to tackle market instability in the euro area. This became evident during the summer of 2012, when tensions reached a great intensity caused by the perception of a risk of redenomination, which included the eventuality of a breakup of the euro. The answer here was, as has traditionally happened in the past when the European Union has experienced acute problems, a qualitative leap towards a new and strengthened Union, which began to take shape in the agreement reached in June 2012 by the Heads of State and Government of the euro area. Among the various measures agreed, the Banking Union project is the key element in limiting the perverse interaction between sovereign and banking risks that we have witnessed during this crisis. Towards a banking union: the single supervisory mechanism An essential step in the development of the project is the creation of a Single Supervisory Mechanism, which is possibly the most far-reaching institutional reform agreed in the EU since the introduction of the euro. I would like to mention three features of the design of this mechanism. 1 Integrity Firstly, the assignment to the Single Supervisory Mechanism of all relevant supervisory responsibilities for all credit institutions. This is clearly the best option to ensure the widespread application of the highest supervisory standards and to reduce distortions that could result from the coexistence of different supervisory regimes for institutions sharing the same market. Although, in principle, the ECB will only directly supervise significant institutions d0 those whose balance sheets exceed db30 billion d0 the Single Supervisory Mechanism actually covers all banks in the euro area and possibly also those in countries outside the euro area that are willing to enter into cooperation agreements with the ECB. Naturally, establishing a strong internal organisation within the ECB for the new supervisory capacity is a complex and demanding task. In particular, it is important to strike a good balance between managing potential conflicts of interest and exploiting synergies within the ECB. One of the concerns in this area is to mitigate any potential friction between the objectives of supervision and the ECB's monetary policy tasks. To this end, the Regulation stipulates an organisational scheme - which pivots on a newly created Supervisory Board - which should ensure that monetary policy decisions are not tainted by supervisory considerations. 2 A unified system benefiting from national experiences The second aspect I would like to highlight concerns the involvement of national competent authorities (NCAs) in the Single Supervisory Mechanism. The Single Supervisory Mechanism is far from being a federation of national supervisors or a macro-college of supervisors. Indeed, it has been established as a system in which the supporting role of national supervisory authorities is clearly defined: to contribute to the preparation and implementation of decisions that will always be taken centrally. To this end, NCAs shall assist the ECB in preparing and implementing all types of supervisory-related tasks, including regular on-site inspections. Based on these principles, and in order to ensure a smooth and effective transition from purely national to one developed by the Single Supervisory Mechanism, the change should be made following a step-by-step approach, which implies that, at least during the early stages of its operation, particularly meaningful involvement of NCAs will be necessary in order to avoid discontinuities that damage the effectiveness of supervisory work. 3 Accountability Thirdly, in order to have a solid institutional set-up of the Single Supervisory Mechanism within the ECB, it is important, of course, that it has the necessary public acceptance at both European and national level. As always, the counterpart to independence, guaranteed in this case by the ECB Statute, should be the exercise of accountability, both to legislative and governmental authorities, taking into account the possible effect of supervisory actions on public finances. However, it is important to remember that, unlike monetary policy, supervisory policy does not pursue a macroeconomic objective at euro area level d0 such as price stability d0 with which to justify the measures it takes. In fact, supervision involves the application of specific measures for each bank and its success will be evaluated in each country, entity by entity. This means that the ECB will have to have much greater visibility to citizens in different countries and interact frequently with national authorities, parliaments and interest groups. Single Resolution Mechanism However, despite the importance of establishing a Single Supervisory Mechanism, a genuine banking union also requires an effective Single Resolution Mechanism and possibly also a Common Deposit Insurance Fund. Without these ingredients, institutional reform is unlikely to be instrumental in radically breaking the vicious circle between bank risk and sovereign risk. Indeed, the basic objective of a banking union is to prevent banks' liabilities from having a different value or risk, depending on where they are located. Unified supervision undoubtedly helps to this end. However, supervision cannot and probably should not seek to nullify the likelihood of banking crises. Therefore, to the extent that crises persist that may affect the viability of individual institutions, the bank liabilities affected should be treated similarly across jurisdictions. In other words, the existence of heterogeneous national crisis resolution schemes is incompatible with a banking union. In addition, the establishment of unified oversight without a common resolution regime could give rise to certain operational risks. In particular, European supervision with national resolution systems could lead to problems of compatibility of incentives affecting the proper conduct of supervision. In addition, it could undermine the legitimacy of supervisory actions vis-88-vis national citizens. In this respect, it may not always be easy to ensure that citizens accept the use of national public funds to support credit institutions whose vulnerability has been exposed by supervisory action by an institution that is not formally accountable to national authorities. The existence of a common resolution framework for financial institutions is therefore a necessary complement to the creation of a genuine banking union. Let me briefly outline the main features that, in my opinion, a unified resolution system should have. Firstly, harmonised regulation of the resolution regime is urgently needed. In this area, the advanced state of the new Credit Institution Resolution Directive is encouraging. I hope that the final text will live up to expectations and provide a comprehensive resolution system that can be applied uniformly across jurisdictions. In particular, the resolution framework should be designed in a sufficiently harmonised manner, with common rules and approaches, leaving minimal scope for possible exceptions at national level. Otherwise, if the Regulation allows relevant exceptions or specificities in national resolution schemes, involving differentiated treatment of creditors of similar typology, it could weaken their ability to correct market fragmentation by promoting arbitrage between instruments and jurisdictions. In my opinion, this element of coherence and harmonisation is possibly even more relevant than the debate d0 moreover quite intense d0 on the specific treatment of different types of bank liabilities in private investors' loss-making exercises (bail in). Second, to achieve uniform application of regulation, a joint resolution authority is necessary, at least, for countries participating in the Single Supervisory Mechanism. Half-baked solutions, based on a possible network of national resolution authorities, do not seem the right option for crisis management at European level. The common resolution authority should be independent and have the means to take the necessary decisions as soon as the situation demands. At the same time, the resolution authority should maintain a close relationship with the single banking supervisor in order to benefit from its knowledge of institutions and facilitate decision-making in crisis situations, where a wide range of financial stability-related factors have to be taken into account. In principle, it seems preferable to advocate the creation of a specific resolution authority, with a scope similar to that of the Single Supervisory Mechanism. I am of course aware that establishing a new authority at EU level it could require complex amendments to the EU Treaty, which would delay the process excessively. Other pragmatic ways of creating a common resolution system d0 possibly based on one of the currently existing institutions d0 should therefore be explored and ideally should become operational before the Mechanism is scheduled to become operational in the summer of 2014. I am sure that the proposal to be presented by the European Commission in the coming months will contain ideas that will bring us closer to achieving this objective. Finally, a common resolution framework also requires a financing system at euro area level. Resolution rules, based on the principle of minimising the burden on taxpayers, should establish a homogeneous framework of conduct incorporating the corresponding assumption of losses by the holders of the different instruments that may be subject to bail-in exercises. This could, in principle, be sufficient to ensure in many cases the orderly resolution of credit institutions. However, as experience shows, additional funds are often needed to support the resolution of vulnerable banks, even when they are not especially large or complex. These funds do not have to be provided entirely by governments, as industry could also contribute through the timely design of resolution funds. Indeed, it might be feasible to design mechanisms in which the expected contribution of taxpayers to the resolution could be minimized and even reserved for exceptional scenarios. But, frankly, if we believe in the establishment of an effective banking union, which can make a significant contribution to combating fragmentation, I see no alternative but to envisage the adoption of support measures financed by a common scheme, containing the participation that is considered appropriate from both the private and public sectors. And I finish. There is no doubt that we are making great progress in strengthening the institutional design of EMU, the completion of which will enable us, together with the introduction of the necessary measures at national level, to have a sufficiently solid institutional framework to prevent and effectively manage developments that could destabilise monetary union. As I was saying, the Banking Union project is a clear example of this. Moving towards more Europe is the only effective way to tackle the problems of the current crisis. I therefore reiterate my thanks to the authors and editors of the Report for their contribution to enriching the debate on such a relevant topic. Thank you for your attention.
text_original: 10.05.2013 Presentacin del libro La arquitectura institucional de la refundacin del euro Fundacin de Estudios Financieros/Auditorio del ICO Fernando Restoy Subgobernador Es un placer compartir con ustedes la presentacin del informe La arquitectura institucional de la refundacin del euro. No quisiera empezar sin agradecer a la Fundacin de Estudios Financieros y, en concreto, a su Presidente Juan Carlos Ureta su amable invitacin, as como a Romn Escolano, Presidente del ICO, por permitirnos celebrar este acto en este auditorio. Considero que el estudio que hoy se presenta, destinado a reflexionar sobre las iniciativas en marcha para mejorar el diseo de la UEM, no podra ser ms oportuno. A lo largo de sus siete artculos los autores ofrecen contribuciones de gran inters con propuestas concretas para avanzar decididamente hacia una autntica unin bancaria, fiscal y econmica en la UEM. Permtanme que aproveche esta ocasin para unirme a estas reflexiones sobre las reformas necesarias para hacer frente a las debilidades que la UEM ha evidenciado en los ltimos aos. No cabe duda que estas reformas requieren de una combinacin equilibrada entre medidas de mbito nacional y medidas en el mbito europeo. Creo que en Espaa, como en otros pases, se estn dando pasos relevantes para adoptar medidas que mejorarn la capacidad de la economa para ajustarse en caso de desarrollos idiosincrsicos, para reforzar su competitividad y para reducir la probabilidad de que, en el futuro, puedan generarse desequilibrios macro-financieros acusados. Estas medidas a nivel nacional resultan imprescindibles para fortalecer el funcionamiento de la Unin Monetaria. Es evidente, no obstante, que, al mismo tiempo, precisamos un reforzamiento institucional de la Unin Econmica y Monetaria, con objeto de impedir cualquier atisbo de incertidumbre sobre su propia continuidad que, como muestra el pasado reciente, pueden resultar muy desestabilizadores. De hecho, centrar mi exposicin en la que es, sin duda, una de las reformas institucionales ms ambiciosas, el proyecto de creacin de la Unin Bancaria. Introduccin La crisis por la que atraviesa la Unin Econmica y Monetaria (UEM) tiene su principal manifestacin en la fragmentacin de sus mercados financieros, entendida como la reemergencia de un componente de riesgo pas en el coste de financiacin de los emisores y prestatarios cuya magnitud depende de la localizacin de los mismos. Como bien saben, esta fragmentacin de los mercados encuentra su origen en las dificultades presupuestarias de diversos Estados en un contexto de ausencia de mecanismos eficaces de mutualizacin del riesgo a nivel europeo. Estas dificultades presupuestarias se han visto alimentadas por el impacto sobre la actividad econmica de la aguda correccin de determinados desequilibrios macrofinancieros, experimentados por aquellas economas nacionales que sufrieron un efecto expansivo muy pronunciado tras la adopcin de la moneda nica y que carecan de mercados de productos y de trabajo suficientemente flexibles para absorber de forma equilibrada ese impacto. Estos desajustes han adquirido una dimensin especialmente desestabilizadora cuando han terminado afectando a la industria bancaria en aquellos pases donde el tamao del sector, su posicin de solvencia o la propia situacin de las finanzas pblicas, dificultaban el uso de los fondos presupuestarios nacionales para la preservacin de la estabilidad financiera. Esta realimentacin entre riesgo bancario y soberano est, por lo tanto, en la base de la crisis actual por lo que su superacin pasa por eliminarla o, al menos, contenerla de modo efectivo. Como sealaba antes, es evidente que la solucin a estos problemas pasa por tomar medidas a nivel nacional que permitan contener los desajustes fiscales estructurales, mitigar los desequilibrios macrofinancieros y aumentar la fortaleza del sector bancario. Al mismo tiempo, la UEM debe ser reforzada institucionalmente de modo que se impulse una mayor integracin de las economas que formen parte de ella. Ello conlleva la creacin de mecanismos centralizados para la cobertura de contingencias y, como contrapartida, una mayor cesin de soberana en las polticas que resultan relevantes para prevenirlas y gestionarlas. Creo que los lderes europeos han aprendido en gran medida la leccin, como muestran los notables avances realizados en los ltimos aos en la reforma de la arquitectura institucional de la UEM. Concretamente, los progresos en la mejora de los procedimientos establecidos para el seguimiento de una gama amplia de polticas nacionales, ante situaciones de desequilibrios macroeconmicos, suponen un significativo paso adelante. En particular, los mecanismos de vigilancia de la poltica presupuestaria se han fortalecido de forma notable, especialmente tras la introduccin del denominado Fiscal Compact. Adems, se han asignado recursos a la deteccin y el seguimiento de los riesgos sistmicos con la creacin de la Junta Europea de Riesgo Sistmico (ESRB, en sus siglas en ingls). Finalmente, con la constitucin del Mecanismo Europeo de Estabilidad (MEDE) se ha establecido un vehculo permanente para canalizar la ayuda financiera a los pases de la zona del euro que pudieran necesitarla. En cualquier caso, los avances realizados durante los primeros aos de la crisis no fueron suficientes para atajar la inestabilidad de los mercados en la zona del euro. Esto se hizo evidente durante el verano de 2012, cuando las tensiones alcanzaron una gran intensidad propiciada por la percepcin de un riesgo de redenominacin, que recogan la eventualidad de una ruptura del euro. La respuesta en este caso fue, como ha ocurrido tradicionalmente en el pasado cuando la Unin Europea ha atravesado problemas agudos, un salto cualitativo hacia una Unin nueva y reforzada, que se empez a perfilar en el acuerdo alcanzado en junio de 2012 por los Jefes de Estado y de Gobierno de la zona del euro. Entre las distintas medidas acordadas, el proyecto de la Unin Bancaria resulta el elemento fundamental para limitar la perversa interaccin entre los riesgos soberanos y los riesgos bancarios que hemos presenciado durante esta crisis. Hacia una unin bancaria: el mecanismo nico de supervisin Un paso esencial en el desarrollo del proyecto lo constituye la creacin de un Mecanismo nico de Supervisin, que posiblemente supone la reforma institucional de mayor calado acordada en la UE desde la introduccin del euro. Me gustara mencionar tres caractersticas del diseo de este mecanismo. 1 Integridad En primer lugar, la asignacin al Mecanismo nico de Supervisin de todas las responsabilidades relevantes en materia de supervisin del conjunto de entidades de crdito. Esta es claramente la mejor opcin para garantizar la aplicacin generalizada de los estndares supervisores ms rigurosos y para reducir las distorsiones que podran derivarse de la coexistencia de diferentes regmenes supervisores para las instituciones que comparten el mismo mercado. Aunque, en principio, el BCE solo supervisar directamente entidades significativas aquellas cuyos balances superen los 30.000 millones de euros, el Mecanismo nico de Supervisin abarca realmente todas las entidades de crdito de la zona del euro y posiblemente tambin las de pases de fuera de la zona que estn dispuestos a suscribir acuerdos de cooperacin con el BCE. Naturalmente, establecer dentro del BCE una organizacin interna slida para la nueva capacidad supervisora es una tarea compleja y exigente. En particular, es importante encontrar un buen equilibrio entre la gestin de los posibles conflictos de intereses y el aprovechamiento de las sinergias en el seno del BCE. Una de las preocupaciones en este mbito es mitigar cualquier posible friccin entre los objetivos de la supervisin y las funciones de poltica monetaria del BCE. A tal efecto, el Reglamento estipula un esquema organizativo -que pivota sobre un Consejo Supervisor (Supervisory Board) de nueva creacin- que debe facilitar que las decisiones de poltica monetaria no se vean contaminadas por consideraciones supervisoras. 2 Un sistema unificado que se beneficia de las experiencias nacionales El segundo aspecto que me gustara destacar se refiere a la participacin de las autoridades nacionales competentes (ANC) en el Mecanismo nico de Supervisin. El Mecanismo nico de Supervisin dista de ser una federacin de supervisores nacionales o un macrocolegio de supervisores. En efecto, se ha establecido como un sistema en que el papel de apoyo de las autoridades supervisoras nacionales queda claramente definido: contribuir a la preparacin y a la puesta en prctica de las decisiones que se adoptarn siempre de forma centralizada. A este fin, las ANC asistirn al BCE en la preparacin e implantacin de todo tipo de tareas relacionadas con la supervisin, incluidas las inspecciones regulares in situ. Sobre la base de estos principios, y para garantizar una transicin fluida y eficaz, desde una supervisin puramente nacional a una desarrollada por el Mecanismo nico de Supervisin, el cambio debe hacerse siguiendo un enfoque gradual, lo que implica que, al menos durante las primeras etapas de su funcionamiento, ser necesaria contar con una participacin especialmente significativa de las ANC con objeto de evitar discontinuidades que daen la eficacia de la labor supervisora. 3 Rendicin de cuentas En tercer lugar, para disponer de una slida configuracin institucional del Mecanismo nico de Supervisin en el seno del BCE es importante, como no puede ser de otro modo, que cuente con la necesaria aceptacin pblica tanto a nivel europeo como nacional. Como siempre, la contrapartida de la independencia, garantizada en este caso por el estatuto del BCE, debe ser el ejercicio de rendicin de cuentas, tanto ante las autoridades legislativas como gubernamentales, teniendo en cuenta el posible efecto de las actuaciones supervisoras sobre las finanzas pblicas. No obstante, es importante recordar que, a diferencia de la poltica monetaria, la poltica supervisora no persigue un objetivo macroeconmico a escala de la zona del euro como la estabilidad de precios con el que justificar las medidas que adopte. De hecho, la supervisin supone la aplicacin de medidas especficas para cada banco y su xito se evaluar en cada pas, entidad por entidad. Ello significa que el BCE habr de tener una visibilidad mucho mayor ante los ciudadanos de los distintos pases e interactuar con frecuencia con las autoridades, los parlamentos y los grupos de inters nacionales. Mecanismo nico de Resolucin Con todo, pese a la importancia de establecer un Mecanismo nico de Supervisin, una autntica unin bancaria exige adicionalmente un Mecanismo nico de Resolucin efectivo y posiblemente tambin un Fondo de Garanta de Depsitos Comn. Sin estos ingredientes es improbable que la reforma institucional resulte decisiva para romper de manera radical el crculo vicioso entre riesgo bancario y riesgo soberano. De hecho, el objetivo bsico de una unin bancaria es evitar que los pasivos de las entidades de crdito tengan un valor o un riesgo diferente, dependiendo de dnde estas estn radicadas. Una supervisin unificada ayuda indudablemente a este fin. Con todo, la supervisin no puede y no debe, probablemente, tratar de anular la probabilidad de aparicin de crisis bancarias. Por lo tanto, en la medida en que persistan crisis que puedan llegar a afectar a la viabilidad de entidades concretas, los pasivos bancarios afectados deben tener un tratamiento similar en todas las jurisdicciones. En otras palabras, la existencia de esquemas nacionales heterogneos de resolucin de crisis es incompatible con una unin bancaria. Adems, el establecimiento de una supervisin unificada sin un rgimen de resolucin comn podra dar lugar a ciertos riesgos operacionales. En concreto, la supervisin europea con sistemas de resolucin nacionales podra provocar problemas de compatibilidad de incentivos que afectasen al buen desarrollo de la supervisin. Adicionalmente, podra deteriorar la legitimidad de las actuaciones supervisoras ante los ciudadanos nacionales. En este sentido, podra no ser siempre sencillo asegurar la aceptacin por la ciudadana de la utilizacin fondos pblicos nacionales para apoyar a entidades de crdito cuya vulnerabilidad ha sido puesta de manifiesto por una actuacin supervisora llevada a cabo por una institucin que no rinde cuentas formalmente ante las autoridades nacionales. La existencia de un marco de resolucin comn para las instituciones financieras es, pues, un complemento necesario en lo que se refiere a la creacin de una verdadera unin bancaria. Permtanme que esboce brevemente las principales caractersticas que, en mi opinin, debera reunir un sistema de resolucin unificado. En primer lugar, se necesita urgentemente una regulacin armonizada del rgimen de resolucin. En este mbito, resulta esperanzador el avanzado estado de la nueva Directiva de resolucin de entidades de crdito. Espero que el texto final est a la altura de las expectativas y ofrezca un sistema de resolucin completo que pueda aplicarse uniformemente en todas las jurisdicciones. Concretamente, el marco de resolucin debera disearse de manera suficientemente armonizada, con normas y enfoques comunes, dejando un margen mnimo para posibles excepciones a nivel nacional. De lo contario, si el Reglamento permite excepciones o especifidades relevantes en los esquemas nacionales de resolucin, que impliquen un tratamiento diferenciado de acreedores de tipologa similar, podra debilitar su capacidad para corregir la fragmentacin en los mercados al promover el arbitraje entre instrumentos y jurisdicciones. En mi opinin, este elemento de coherencia y armonizacin es, posiblemente, incluso ms relevante que el debate  por otra parte bastante intenso- sobre el tratamiento especfico de los distintos tipos de pasivos bancarios en los ejercicios de asuncin de prdidas por parte de los inversores privados (bail in). En segundo lugar, para lograr la aplicacin uniforme de la regulacin, es necesaria una autoridad comn de resolucin, al menos, para los pases que participan en el Mecanismo nico de Supervisin. Las soluciones a medias, basadas en una posible red de autoridades de resolucin nacionales , no parecen la opcin adecuada para la gestin de crisis a escala europea. La autoridad de resolucin comn debera ser independiente y contar con los medios para adoptar las decisiones necesarias tan pronto como lo demande la situacin. Al mismo tiempo, la autoridad de resolucin debe mantener una relacin estrecha con el supervisor bancario nico para beneficiarse de su conocimiento de las entidades y facilitar la toma de decisiones en situaciones de crisis, cuando se ha de tener en cuenta un amplio conjunto de factores relacionados con la estabilidad financiera. En principio, parece preferible abogar por la creacin de una autoridad de resolucin especfica, con un mbito de actuacin similar al del Mecanismo nico de Supervisin. Naturalmente soy consciente de que establecer una nueva autoridad a escala de la UE podra requerir complejas modificaciones del Tratado de la UE, que retrasara el proceso excesivamente. As pues, convendra explorar otras maneras pragmticas de crear un sistema de resolucin comn posiblemente residenciado en alguna de las instituciones actualmente existentes que, idealmente, debera comenzar a funcionar antes del momento en que est previsto que empiece a operar el Mecanismo, en el verano de 2014. Estoy seguro que la propuesta que, al respecto, debe presentar la Comisin Europea en los prximos meses contendr ideas que permitirn acercarnos al cumplimiento de este objetivo. Por ltimo, un marco de resolucin comn tambin requiere un sistema de financiacin a escala de la zona del euro. Las normas de resolucin, basadas en el principio de minimizar la carga de los contribuyentes, deberan establecer un marco de conducta homogneo que incorpore la correspondiente asuncin de prdidas por parte de los tenedores de los distintos instrumentos que puedan estar sujetos a ejercicios de bail in. Esto podra bastar, en principio, para garantizar en muchos casos la resolucin ordenada de las entidades de crdito. Sin embargo, como muestra la experiencia, a menudo se necesitan fondos adicionales para apoyar la resolucin de los bancos vulnerables, incluso cuando no son especialmente grandes o complejos. Estos fondos no tienen por qu ser aportados en su totalidad por los gobiernos, pues la industria podra tambin contribuir a travs del diseo oportuno de los fondos de resolucin. De hecho, podra ser viable disear mecanismos en los que la contribucin esperada de los contribuyentes a la resolucin pudiera minimizarse e incluso reservase para escenarios excepcionales. Pero, francamente, si creemos en el establecimiento de una unin bancaria eficaz, que pueda contribuir significativamente a luchar contra la fragmentacin, no veo otra alternativa que contemplar la adopcin de medidas de respaldo financiadas con un esquema comn, que contenga la participacin que se considere apropiada tanto del sector privado como del pblico. Y termino. No cabe duda que estamos logrando grandes avances en el refuerzo del diseo institucional de la UEM cuya culminacin nos permitir, junto con la introduccin de las necesarias medidas a nivel nacional, disponer de un marco institucional suficientemente slido, que permita prevenir y gestionar de manera eficaz los desarrollos que puedan desestabilizar la unin monetaria. Como les deca, el proyecto de Unin Bancaria es un claro ejemplo de ello. Avanzar hacia ms Europa es el nico modo eficaz de afrontar los problemas de la actual crisis. Por ello, reitero mi agradecimiento a los autores y editores del Informe por su contribucin al enriquecimiento del debate sobre un tema tan relevante. Gracias por su atencin.

Title: Closing speech of the Seminar "Competitiveness and Brand Spain"
text: 21.06.2013 Control of Regulators Closing of the Seminar "Competitiveness and Brand Spain/APIE UIMP Fernando Restoy Deputy Governor of the Bank of Spain Good morning. Thank you very much Michelangelo for your presentation and thank you for the invitation. It is a real pleasure to be able to close this year the course organized by the APIE at the UIMP. As you know, this is not the first time I have participated in the course. I have had the opportunity to do it for several years as Vice-President of the CNMV, but this is the first year, and I hope not the last, in which I do it as Deputy Governor of the Bank of Spain. Today I will share with you some reflections on the situation and prospects of the Spanish financial sector, which I trust will be of interest to you. First I will dwell on the situation of the Spanish economy, then review the progress in the reform of the banking sector and end by pointing out the challenges that lie ahead, with particular attention to the project of the European Banking Union. Macroeconomic environment As far as the macroeconomic outlook is concerned, as you all know, the Spanish economy is mired in a double recession, largely associated with two distinct but interrelated factors. Firstly, the sharp contraction in spending, precipitated by the deep crisis in the housing market, which has led to a pronounced destruction of employment. Secondly, the fragmentation of European financial markets which, despite the improvements observed recently, incorporate a country-risk component that is affecting the availability and cost of financing for the Spanish private sector. Despite the current severe situation, the considerable adjustment capacity that our economy has been showing should be highlighted, as shown by the pace at which the imbalances accumulated during the expansionary phase that preceded the crisis are being corrected. In particular, the current account balance has recorded a surplus for the first time in more than 25 years and forecasts suggest that this positive trend in the current account balance will consolidate in the coming years d0 we expect a surplus of around 4% of GDP for next year. It is true that this trend is partly related to the contraction in imports, as a result of weak domestic demand, but the improvement in the balance is also attributable to the positive performance of exports. In fact, Spanish companies are gaining shares in international markets, especially in countries outside the European Union (EU) with high growth potential. As regards price competitiveness, the adjustment is also very evident. The flexibility gained in the labour market following the recent reform is favouring the adjustment of wages to prevailing economic conditions. Last year was the first in decades in which compensation per employee was reduced. This moderation, coupled with productivity gains, is leading to a Sustained decline in relative unit labour costs. Thanks to this process, we have now recovered 75% of the competitiveness losses, relative to the euro area average, that had accumulated since the start of EMU. We expect the gap to close completely next year. As regards public finances, there is no doubt that the deterioration since the beginning of the crisis has been rapid and pronounced, but at the same time there has been a notable reaction in the area of fiscal policy. This has made possible a structural adjustment of more than six percentage points in three years. This is an almost unprecedented intensity adjustment in the EU. Unlike the public sector, in the private sector there is a reduction in debt ratios of both households and non-financial corporations. However, given the recessionary situation and the low inflation rate, the bulk of this adjustment has been carried out in the most burdensome way, that is, through a reduction in credit, which in turn limits the speed of the process. Banking sector reform In this macroeconomic context, our banking system is undergoing unprecedented reform, consisting of a deep recapitalization of vulnerable banks, a rigorous consolidation of bank balance sheets and the implementation of ambitious restructuring processes. The reform is being carried out according to a clear roadmap, with well-defined milestones, set out in the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) agreed in July last year with the European authorities.
