Let me take a few minutes to review the work already done. First, the most vulnerable banks have been recapitalised, meeting the capital needs identified in last summer's rigorous stress tests. These capital deficits were highly concentrated in some credit institutions d0 mainly those that were already under the control of the FROB at the time of the year, while the core of the banking sector d0 more than three quarters of it d0 did not require public aid. Following this process, all Spanish banks now meet d0 and in general quite comfortably d0 the requirement of a principal capital ratio of 9% of risk-weighted assets. As you know, the total amount of public aid required by national banks amounted to EUR 39 billion. It is pertinent to recognize that the volume of support provided by the public treasury was reduced by the burden-sharing exercises carried out by the FROB, following the guidelines established in the MoU, and that affected capital instruments, preferred shares and subordinated debt. Allow me to comment on these hybrid instrument management exercises. These exercises are required by the criteria of the European Commission to authorize state aid to banks and have recently been incorporated into our legislation. The principle on which they are based is the following: to the extent that public aid has as its ultimate objective to avoid the insolvency of entities that may affect financial stability, holders of hybrid instruments d0 which would have foreseeably lost practically all their investment in a liquidation event d0 should not be rescued by the taxpayer but, on the contrary, they must contribute to ensuring that the support required from the State is as little as possible. This has also been the experience in other countries. For example, in Ireland, cuts of more than 70% were imposed on subordinated debt and, more recently, in the case of a bank undergoing restructuring in the Netherlands, the cuts meant the complete loss of investment. The ongoing debate on the European resolution directive seems to go even further, broadening the base of instruments concerned. The Spanish case is certainly of a relevant singularity, in so far as a significant proportion of the holders of hybrid instruments were regarded as retail investors. Therefore, in our case, burden-sharing exercises may have a particularly strong impact on the customer base of the entities concerned. Despite this, the legislation prevents discrimination between investors on the basis of their nature. Therefore, the task of the authorities has essentially been to exploit as much as possible the margin of flexibility provided by national and European regulations to moderate the impact on retail investors. This has been pursued basically through three types of actions in which the Bank of Spain has been involved: i) first, negotiating with the European Commission the acceptance of more moderate cuts than initially planned, in exchange for assuming that the value recoverable by investors materialized in shares. This made it possible to satisfy the objective that these instruments contribute as much as possible to the capitalisation of the institution without requiring the complete loss of the investment; ii) secondly, establishing, through the Deposit Guarantee Fund, a mechanism to grant liquidity to the shares delivered in exchange for hybrids in the case of unlisted entities, iii) and thirdly, offering arbitration procedures in the entities controlled by the FROB, which comply with the criteria established by a Monitoring Committee created for this purpose by means of a legal norm. These procedures make it easier for investors harmed by poor marketing to be compensated through more agile formulas, but formally equivalent to judicial channels. In addition to the recapitalisation process, the second pillar of the strategy was the clean-up of banks' balance sheets. This objective has been achieved mainly through two tracks: first, through a considerable increase in provisioning requirements; in particular, for risks related to real estate development and construction and, secondly, through the transfer of problem assets from credit institutions that required public aid to an external asset management company (SAREB). As a result of both processes, the net exposure of the banking sector as a whole to the real estate sector was reduced by more than 50% in 2012. Finally, I would like to stress that credit institutions that have received public aid are undergoing a demanding restructuring process involving significant reductions in staff, offices and assets. These measures are essential to comply with public support rules and reduce the overcapacity of our financial system. In addition, the resolution authority, the FROB, is carrying out a divestment strategy that will additionally contribute to the consolidation of the sector. So far, we have sold two nationalized banks, promoted two additional corporate operations and boosted the listing of a fifth entity. Currently, four entities remain under the control of the FROB, of which we plan to sell two of them, which are immersed in a resolution plan, in the relatively near future, to the extent that market conditions allow. In short, as the European authorities publicly pointed out a few weeks ago, we are fulfilling all the commitments made at the MoU on time. I therefore believe that we can say with a reasonable degree of confidence that the unique problem of the Spanish banking sector d0 consisting of excessive exposure to the real estate sector and the lack of sufficient capital in various banks to cope with the deep contraction of that sector d0 has been successfully addressed. That said, there is no doubt that a number of uncertainties, mostly related to the macroeconomic environment, remain. In particular, the adverse economic situation, the deleveraging process and the adjustment of the economy will inevitably continue to affect the volume of activity and profitability of Spanish banks in the immediate future. To better analyse the impact of the macroeconomic environment, we recently conducted an exercise to update Oliver Wyman's stress tests last year, using the most up-to-date information available, including actual balance sheet data as of December 2012. This year's results d0 which were recently published in the Financial Stability Report d0 show that, for all loan portfolios, actual defaults in 2012 have been significantly lower than expected in Oliver Wyman's adverse scenario. In fact, the observed defaults are similar and, in some cases, lower than those estimated in the baseline scenario. In addition, the 2012 data show a better-than-expected profit before provisions, even in the baseline scenario, suggesting that we have started 2013 in a somewhat more comfortable situation than expected in Oliver Wyman's fiscal year. On the other hand, we have also carried out a prospective analysis in order to estimate the expected losses, profits and, ultimately, capital ratios of the sector in the period 2013-2014, incorporating not only the latest available data but also the most recent macroeconomic projections. As you know, the economic outlook has deteriorated since last summer, as a result of adverse developments in certain variables, such as the unemployment rate and house prices. However, other relevant variables, such as GDP or interest rates, are behaving more or less in line with the baseline scenario or, even, in some cases more favourably. The net result is that the expected delinquency for the coming months, according to the most up-to-date macroeconomic projections, is somewhat higher than that estimated by the consultant in its central scenario, but is still far from that corresponding to the adverse scenario. This evolution of expected NPLs, given the expected recovery in profits, is consistent with the fact that the solvency ratios estimated for the end of 2013 are comfortably above the regulatory limits. On the whole, we can say that these exercises d0 which we will conduct on a regular basis in the future d0 offer us a certain margin of comfort that, of course, we treat with great caution. As it cannot be otherwise, our efforts are focused on continuously promoting and monitoring that institutions offer the highest possible level of transparency and maintain the necessary solvency levels. The most visible initiatives we have taken in this regard d0 but not the only ones d0 have been the new transparency requirements on relevant exposures and refinanced loans, measures related to the remuneration of deposits or, more recently, the guidance on accounting policies for refinanced loans. Allow me, in the last part of my speech, to share with you some thoughts on the institutional reform of EMU, which is key to being able to address the various shortcomings that have become apparent during the crisis. It is clear to all of us that the fragmentation of financial markets in Europe remains one of the main manifestations of this crisis and the main impediment to the proper functioning of monetary union. Among the various measures agreed to date to address these imperfections, the Banking Union project is at the heart of the reform agenda. The first ingredient of the Banking Union project is the creation of the Single Supervisory Mechanism (SSM) under the leadership of the ECB, whose launch, after building a rapid consensus on the matter, is a clear cause for satisfaction. The relevance of the SSM is hard to exaggerate. In the case of Spain, more than 90% of our financial system will be under its direct responsibility, which means that the Spanish banking sector will be the third in importance within the SSM. As you can imagine, the Banco de Espa96a is participating intensively in the preparations that are being carried out in a coordinated manner between the ECB and the rest of the national supervisors. In this regard, we are confident that the SSM will be able to start operating effectively within just one year. Undoubtedly, this mechanism will help to harmonise supervisory practices, promote their convergence towards the highest standards and facilitate competition on a level playing field in the euro area banking market. In any case, in addition to the Single Supervisory Mechanism, a genuine banking union also requires an effective Single Resolution Mechanism (SRM) and, possibly, a Common Deposit Insurance Scheme. The SRM is an essential component to facilitate the perception that the risk associated with banks' different liability instruments does not depend on where banks are located within the monetary union, which is not the case at present. Moreover, the establishment of unified supervision without a common resolution regime could lead to problems of compatibility of incentives for supervisors and call into question the legitimacy of supervisory actions vis-88-vis national citizens. In my opinion, a well-defined single resolution mechanism should have the following characteristics: Firstly, a common resolution framework with uniform rules that would leave a minimum margin for exceptions at national level. Secondly, a single resolution authority that can ensure the homogeneous application of the common rules. Indeed, unambitious solutions, based, for example, on a network of national resolution authorities, do not seem the right option for crisis management at European level. Finally, the establishment of a common system for financing bank resolution processes, at least for the countries that are part of the SSM, including a hedge fund that draws on the contributions of the European banking industry. At this stage, it is still uncertain how much progress we will have made on establishing a common resolution system when the SSM becomes operational. I am confident that a satisfactory consensus will be reached in a short period of time to clear up these uncertainties. In any case, substantial progress has already been made on the future Institutions Recovery and Resolution Directive. This directive will radically change the way financial crises will be managed in the future and thereby change the behaviour patterns of investors and customers of financial institutions. I sincerely hope that the regulatory framework designed for entity resolution processes will contain a reasonable compromise between four objectives: (i) minimising taxpayer participation; (ii) adequate protection of deposits; (iii) affordable financing costs for credit institutions; As regards the other two elements, the single resolution authority and the common funding system, the European Commission will present a legislative proposal in the coming weeks. The challenge here is to find a pragmatic compromise that allows for effective centralised management of resolution processes and the availability of a common backstop mechanism that does not require a review process. This process would be complex to manage and have an uncertain outcome. And I finish. The Spanish economy is facing a complex economic situation, a consequence of the significant internal imbalances accumulated during the years of expansion that preceded the crisis and whose destabilizing effect has been exacerbated by the fragmentation of European financial markets. Internally, I sincerely believe that an ambitious reform agenda is being undertaken, both in the area of economic policy and the banking sector. This is making it possible for the adjustment of the most important imbalances in the Spanish economy to be carried out relatively quickly, which will undoubtedly contribute to triggering a sustainable recovery soon. Naturally, from the Bank of Spain we insist that there is no room for complacency. On the contrary, the challenges facing our economy require keeping the reform momentum unchanged. However, an important battle of the war is fought outside the Spanish borders, on a European scale. I consider it essential that the efforts being made to strengthen EMU and eliminate financial fragmentation soon yield significant results, especially as regards the creation of a full banking union in the near future. Thanks a lot.
text_original: 21.06.2013 El Control de los Reguladores Clausura del Seminario Competitividad y Marca Espaa/APIE UIMP Fernando Restoy Subgobernador del Banco de Espaa Buenos das. Muchas gracias Miguel ngel por tu presentacin y gracias por la invitacin. Es un verdadero placer poder clausurar este ao el curso que organiza la APIE en la UIMP. Como saben, no es la primera vez que participo en el curso. He tenido la oportunidad de hacerlo varios aos como Vicepresidente de la CNMV, pero este es el primer ao, y espero que no el ltimo, en el que lo hago como Subgobernador del Banco de Espaa. Hoy compartir con ustedes unas reflexiones sobre la situacin y las perspectivas del sector financiero espaol, que confo sern de su inters. Primero me detendr en la situacin de la economa espaola, revisar despus el progreso en la reforma del sector bancario y terminar apuntando los retos que tenemos por delante, con particular atencin al proyecto de la Unin Bancaria Europea. Entorno macroeconmico En lo que respecta a las perspectivas macroeconmicas, como todos ustedes saben, la economa espaola se encuentra sumida en una doble recesin, asociada en gran medida a dos factores distintos aunque interrelacionados. En primer lugar, la aguda contraccin del gasto, precipitada por la profunda crisis del mercado inmobiliario, que ha ocasionado una pronunciada destruccin de empleo. En segundo lugar, la fragmentacin de los mercados financieros europeos que, a pesar de las mejoras observadas recientemente, incorporan un componente de riesgo- pas que est afectando a la disponibilidad y al coste de la financiacin para el sector privado espaol. A pesar de la severa situacin actual, debe destacarse la notable capacidad de ajuste que viene mostrando nuestra economa, como muestra el ritmo al que se estn corrigiendo los desequilibrios acumulados durante la fase expansiva que precedi a la crisis. En particular, la balanza por cuenta corriente ha registrado supervit por primera vez en ms de 25 aos y las previsiones sugieren que esta trayectoria positiva del saldo corriente se afianzar en los prximos aos -esperamos un supervit en el entorno del 4% del PIB para el prximo ao-. Es cierto que esta evolucin guarda relacin, en parte, con la contraccin de las importaciones, como consecuencia de la debilidad de la demanda interna, pero la mejora del saldo es tambin atribuible al positivo comportamiento de las exportaciones. De hecho, las empresas espaolas estn ganando cuotas en los mercados internacionales, especialmente en los pases no pertenecientes a la Unin Europea (UE) con alto potencial de crecimiento. En cuanto a la competitividad en trminos de precios, el ajuste es tambin muy evidente. La flexibilidad ganada en el mercado de trabajo tras la reforma reciente est favoreciendo el ajuste de los salarios a las condiciones econmicas prevalecientes. El ao pasado fue el primero en dcadas en el que se redujo la remuneracin por asalariado. Esta moderacin, sumada a las ganancias de productividad, est propiciando un descenso sostenido de los costes laborales unitarios relativos. Gracias a este proceso, hemos recuperado ya el 75% de las prdidas de competitividad, en relacin con la media de la zona del euro, que se haban acumulado desde el inicio de la UEM. Esperamos que la brecha se cierre totalmente el prximo ao. Por lo que respecta a las finanzas pblicas, no cabe duda que el deterioro registrado desde el inicio de la crisis ha sido rpido y pronunciado pero, al mismo tiempo, se ha producido una reaccin notable en el mbito de la poltica fiscal. Esto ha posibilitado un ajuste estructural de ms de seis puntos porcentuales en tres aos. Se trata de un ajuste de intensidad casi sin precedentes en la UE. A diferencia de lo que ocurre con el sector pblico, en el sector privado se registra una reduccin de las ratios de endeudamiento, tanto de los hogares como de las sociedades no financieras. No obstante, dada la situacin recesiva y la reducida tasa de inflacin, el grueso de este ajuste se ha llevado a cabo de la manera ms gravosa, es decir, mediante una reduccin del crdito, lo que limita a su vez la velocidad del proceso. Reforma sector bancario En este contexto macroeconmico, nuestro sistema bancario est siendo objeto de una reforma sin precedentes, consistente en una recapitalizacin profunda de las entidades vulnerables, un riguroso saneamiento de los balances bancarios y la implementacin de procesos ambiciosos de reestructuracin. La reforma se est realizando conforme a una hoja de ruta clara, con hitos bien definidos, establecidos en el Memorando de Entendimiento (MoU) acordado en julio del ao pasado con las autoridades europeas. Permtanme dedicar unos minutos a revisar el trabajo ya realizado. En primer lugar, las entidades ms vulnerables han sido recapitalizadas, cubriendo las necesidades de capital identificadas en las rigurosas pruebas de resistencias realizadas el verano pasado. Estos dficit de capital estuvieron muy concentrados en algunas entidades de crdito principalmente en las que ya se encontraban bajo control del FROB en el momento del ejercicio, mientras que el ncleo del sector bancario ms de tres cuartas partes del mismo no precisaron de ayudas pblicas. Tras este proceso, todas las entidades de crdito espaolas cumplen actualmente y, en general, con bastante holgura el requisito de una ratio de capital principal del 9% de los activos ponderados por el riesgo. Como saben, la cuanta total de la ayuda pblica requerida por los bancos nacionales ascendi a 39 mil millones de euros. Resulta pertinente reconocer que el volumen de apoyo proporcionado por el erario pblico se vio aminorado por los ejercicios de reparto de la carga efectuados por el FROB, siguiendo las pautas establecidas en el MoU, y que afectaron a los instrumentos de capital, a las participaciones preferentes y a la deuda subordinada. Permtanme un inciso sobre estos ejercicios de gestin de instrumentos hbridos. Estos ejercicios vienen exigidos por los criterios de la Comisin Europea para autorizar ayudas de estado a la banca y han sido recientemente incorporados a nuestra legislacin. El principio en el que se apoyan es el siguiente: en la medida que la ayuda pblica tiene como objetivo ltimo evitar la insolvencia de entidades que puedan afectar a la estabilidad financiera, los tenedores de instrumentos hbridos que hubieran previsiblemente perdido prcticamente toda su inversin en un supuesto de liquidacin- no deben ser rescatados por el contribuyente sino que, por el contrario, deben contribuir a que el apoyo requerido del Estado sea el menor posible. As ha sido tambin la experiencia en otros pases. Por ejemplo, en Irlanda se impusieron recortes superiores al 70% a la deuda subordinada y, ms recientemente, en el caso de un banco en restructuracin en Holanda, los recortes supusieron la prdida completa de la inversin. El debate en curso sobre la directiva europea de resolucin parece ir incluso ms all, ampliando la base de instrumentos afectados. El caso espaol reviste, ciertamente, una singularidad relevante, en la medida en que una parte importante de los tenedores de instrumentos hbridos tenan la consideracin de inversores minoristas. Por ello, en nuestro caso, los ejercicios de reparto de la carga pueden tener repercusiones especialmente acusadas sobre la base de clientes de las entidades afectadas. A pesar de ello, la legislacin impide realizar discriminaciones entre inversores en funcin de su naturaleza. Por ello, la tarea de las autoridades ha consistido esencialmente en explotar al mximo el margen de flexibilidad que nos proporciona la normativa nacional y europea para moderar las repercusiones para los inversores minoristas. Ello se ha perseguido bsicamente mediante tres tipos de actuaciones en las que ha estado involucrado el Banco de Espaa: i) en primer lugar, negociando con la Comisin Europea la aceptacin de recortes ms moderados que los previstos inicialmente, a cambio de asumir que el valor recuperable por los inversores se materializase en acciones. Ello permiti satisfacer el objetivo de que estos instrumentos contribuyeran lo mximo posible a la capitalizacin de la entidad sin exigir la prdida completa de la inversin; ii) en segundo lugar, estableciendo, a travs del Fondo de Garanta de Depsitos, un mecanismo para otorgar liquidez a las acciones entregadas a cambio de los hbridos en el caso de entidades no cotizadas, iii) y en tercer lugar, ofreciendo procedimientos de arbitraje en las entidades que controla el FROB, que se ajustan a los criterios establecidos por una Comisin de Seguimiento creada a tal fin mediante norma de rango legal. Estos procedimientos facilitan que los inversores perjudicados por una deficiente comercializacin puedan ser resarcidos mediante frmulas ms giles, pero formalmente equivalentes a la va judicial. Adems del proceso de recapitalizacin, el segundo pilar de la estrategia consisti en el saneamiento de los balances de las entidades de crdito. Este objetivo se ha alcanzado principalmente a travs de dos vas: primero, mediante un incremento considerable de los requisitos de provisiones; en particular, para los riesgos relacionados con la promocin y la construccin inmobiliaria y, segundo, mediante la transferencia de los activos problemticos de las entidades de crdito que necesitaron ayudas pblicas a una sociedad externa de gestin de activos (SAREB). Como resultado de ambos procesos, la exposicin neta del conjunto del sector bancario al sector inmobiliario se redujo ms de un 50% en 2012. Por ltimo, deseara subrayar que las entidades de crdito que han recibido ayudas pblicas estn llevando a cabo un exigente proceso de reestructuracin que entraa significativas reducciones de plantilla, oficinas y activos. Estas medidas son esenciales para cumplir las normas de las ayudas pblicas y reducir el exceso de capacidad de nuestro sistema financiero. Adems, la autoridad de resolucin, el FROB, est llevando a cabo una estrategia de desinversin que contribuir adicionalmente a la consolidacin del sector. Hasta ahora, hemos vendido dos bancos nacionalizados, hemos promovido dos operaciones corporativas adicionales y hemos impulsado la cotizacin en bolsa de una quinta entidad. Actualmente permanecen bajo control del FROB cuatro entidades, de las cuales tenemos prevista la venta de dos de ellas, que se encuentran inmersas en un plan de resolucin, en un futuro relativamente prximo, en la medida en la que lo permitan las condiciones del mercado. En resumen, como han sealado pblicamente hace unas semanas las autoridades europeas, estamos cumpliendo puntualmente todos los compromisos asumidos en el MoU. Por consiguiente, creo que podemos afirmar con un grado de confianza razonable que el problema singular del sector bancario espaol consistente en la excesiva exposicin al sector inmobiliario y la falta de capital suficiente en diversas entidades para hacer frente a la profunda contraccin de dicho sector se ha abordado con xito. Dicho esto, no cabe duda de que an persisten varias incertidumbres, en su mayora relacionadas con el entorno macroeconmico. En particular, la adversa situacin econmica, el proceso de desapalancamiento y el ajuste de la economa continuarn, inevitablemente, afectando en el futuro inmediato al volumen de actividad y a la rentabilidad de las entidades de crdito espaolas. Para analizar mejor el impacto del entorno macroeconmico, hemos realizado recientemente un ejercicio para actualizar las pruebas de resistencia desarrolladas el ao pasado por Oliver Wyman, utilizando la informacin disponible ms actualizada, que incluye datos reales de los balances a diciembre de 2012. Los resultados de este ejercicio que se han publicado recientemente en el Informe de Estabilidad Financiera muestran que, para todas las carteras de prstamos, los impagos efectivos en 2012 han sido significativamente inferiores a las previstas en el escenario adverso de Oliver Wyman. De hecho, los impagos observados son similares y, en algn caso, inferiores a los estimados en el escenario base. Adems, los datos de 2012 ponen de manifiesto un beneficio antes de provisiones mejor de lo esperado, incluso en el escenario base, lo que sugiere que hemos comenzado 2013 en una situacin algo ms cmoda que la prevista en el ejercicio de Oliver Wyman. Por otra parte, tambin hemos llevado a cabo un anlisis prospectivo con objeto de estimar las prdidas esperadas, los beneficios y, en ltima instancia, las ratios de capital del sector en el perodo 2013-2014, incorporando no slo los ltimos datos disponibles sino tambin las proyecciones macroeconmicas ms recientes. Como saben ustedes, las perspectivas econmicas se han deteriorado desde el verano pasado, como consecuencia de la evolucin adversa de algunas variables, como la tasa de paro y los precios de la vivienda. Sin embargo, otras variables relevantes, como el PIB o los tipos de inters, se estn comportando ms o menos en lnea con el escenario base o, incluso, en algn caso de modo ms favorable. El resultado neto es que la morosidad esperada para los prximos meses, de acuerdo con las proyecciones macroeconmicas ms actualizadas, es algo mayor que la estimada por el consultor en su escenario central, pero sigue quedando lejos de la correspondiente al escenario adverso. Esta evolucin de la morosidad prevista, dada la recuperacin esperada de los beneficios, resulta coherente con que las ratios de solvencia estimadas para el cierre del ejercicio de 2013 se siten holgadamente por encima de los lmites regulatorios. En conjunto, podemos afirmar que estos ejercicios que conduciremos de manera regular en el futuro- nos ofrecen cierto margen de confort que, por supuesto, tratamos con gran cautela. Como no puede ser de otro modo, nuestros esfuerzos se centran en fomentar y vigilar de forma continua que las entidades ofrezcan el mximo nivel de transparencia posible y mantengan los niveles de solvencia necesarios. Las iniciativas ms visibles que hemos adoptado a este respecto que no las nicas han sido los nuevos requisitos de transparencia sobre exposiciones relevantes y prstamos refinanciados, las medidas relacionadas con la remuneracin de los depsitos o, ms recientemente, las guas sobre las polticas contables de los prstamos refinanciados. Permtanme que, en la ltima parte de mi intervencin, comparta con ustedes unas reflexiones sobre la reforma institucional de la UEM, que resulta clave para poder hacer frente a las diversas deficiencias que se han puesto de manifiesto durante la crisis. Todos tenemos claro que la fragmentacin de los mercados financieros en Europa sigue siendo una de las principales manifestaciones de esta crisis y el principal impedimento para el adecuado funcionamiento de la unin monetaria. Entre las distintas medidas acordadas hasta la fecha para hacer frente a estas imperfecciones, el proyecto de la Unin Bancaria es el elemento fundamental del programa de reformas. El primer ingrediente del proyecto de la Unin Bancaria es la creacin del Mecanismo nico de Supervisin (MUS) bajo el liderazgo del BCE, cuyo lanzamiento, tras la construccin de un rpido consenso al respecto, constituye un claro motivo de satisfaccin. La relevancia que tendr el MUS es difcil de ser exagerada. En el caso de Espaa, ms del 90% de nuestro sistema financiero estar bajo su responsabilidad directa, lo que significa que el sector bancario espaol ser el tercero en importancia dentro del MUS. Como podrn imaginar, desde el Banco de Espaa estamos participando intensamente en los preparativos que se estn llevando a cabo de forma coordinada entre el BCE y el resto de supervisores nacionales. En este sentido, confiamos en que el MUS pueda empezar a operar de modo efectivo dentro de, apenas, un ao. Sin lugar a dudas, este mecanismo contribuir a armonizar las prcticas supervisoras, a propiciar su convergencia hacia los estndares ms rigurosos y a facilitar la competencia en condiciones de igualdad en el mercado bancario de la zona euro. En cualquier caso, adems del Mecanismo nico de Supervisin, una autntica unin bancaria requiere tambin de un Mecanismo nico de Resolucin (MUR) efectivo y, posiblemente tambin, de un Sistema de Garanta de Depsitos Comn. El MUR es un componente esencial para facilitar la percepcin de que el riesgo que cabe asociar a los distintos instrumentos de pasivos de las entidades de crdito no depende de dnde estas estn radicadas dentro de la unin monetaria, algo que no sucede en estos momentos. Por otra parte, el establecimiento de una supervisin unificada sin un rgimen de resolucin comn podra provocar problemas de compatibilidad de incentivos para los supervisores y cuestionar la legitimidad de las actuaciones supervisoras ante los ciudadanos nacionales. En mi opinin, un mecanismo nico de resolucin bien definido debera reunir las siguientes caractersticas: En primer lugar, un marco de resolucin comn con normas uniformes que dejase un margen mnimo para excepciones a nivel nacional. En segundo lugar, una autoridad nica de resolucin que pueda garantizar la aplicacin homognea de las normas comunes. En efecto, las soluciones poco ambiciosas, basadas, por ejemplo, en una red de autoridades de resolucin nacionales, no parecen la opcin adecuada para la gestin de crisis a escala europea. Por ltimo, la constitucin de un sistema comn de financiacin de los procesos de resolucin bancaria, al menos para los pases que forman parte del MUS, que incluya un fondo de cobertura que se nutra de las aportaciones de la industria bancaria europea. En este momento, resulta todava incierto el grado de progreso que habremos podido alcanzar sobre el establecimiento de un sistema de resolucin comn en el momento en que el MUS empiece a operar. Confo en que en un plazo breve de tiempo se logre un consenso satisfactorio que despeje estas incertidumbres. En todo caso, se han logrado ya avances sustanciales en relacin con la futura Directiva sobre recuperacin y resolucin de entidades. Esta Directiva cambiar radicalmente la forma en que se gestionarn las crisis financieras en el futuro y, con ello, se modificarn los patrones de comportamiento de los inversores y los clientes de las entidades financieras. Espero sinceramente que el marco normativo que se disee sobre los procesos de resolucin de entidades contenga un compromiso razonable entre cuatro objetivos: i) la minimizacin de la participacin de los contribuyentes; ii) la proteccin adecuada de los depsitos; iii) unos costes de financiacin asumibles para las entidades de crdito, y iv) el rechazo a las especificidades y excepciones nacionales. En cuanto a los otros dos elementos, la autoridad nica de resolucin y el sistema de financiacin comn, la Comisin Europea presentar una propuesta legislativa en las prximas semanas. El reto en este caso es encontrar un compromiso pragmtico que permita una gestin centralizada efectiva de los procesos de resolucin y la disponibilidad de un mecanismo de respaldo comn que no requiera un proceso de revisin de los actuales Tratados de la UE, pues este proceso sera de gestin compleja y de resultado incierto. Y termino. La economa espaola se enfrenta a una situacin econmica compleja, consecuencia de los significativos desequilibrios internos acumulados durante los aos de expansin que precedieron a la crisis y cuyo efecto desestabilizador se ha agudizado por la fragmentacin de los mercados financieros europeos. A nivel interno, pienso sinceramente que se est asumiendo una agenda ambiciosa de reformas, tanto en el mbito de la poltica econmica como del sector bancario. Ello est posibilitando que el ajuste de los desequilibrios ms importantes de la economa espaola se est llevando a cabo de una manera relativamente rpida, lo que sin duda contribuir a desencadenar pronto una recuperacin sostenible. Naturalmente, desde el Banco de Espaa insistimos en que no hay ningn margen para la complacencia. Por el contrario, los retos a los que debe hacer frente nuestra economa exigen mantener inalterado el impulso reformista. No obstante, una batalla importante de la guerra se libra fuera de las fronteras espaolas, a escala europea. Considero fundamental que los esfuerzos que se estn realizando para reforzar la UEM y eliminar la fragmentacin financiera rindan pronto resultados significativos, especialmente en lo que respecta a la creacin de una unin bancaria plena en un futuro prximo. Muchas gracias.

Title: Appearance before the Subcommittee on Bank Restructuring and Financial Sanitation of the Congress
text: APPEARANCE OF THE PRESIDENT OF THE GOVERNING COMMISSION OF THE FROB BEFORE THE SUBCOMMITTEE ON BANK RESTRUCTURING AND FINANCIAL RESTRUCTURING OF THE CONGRESS September 10, 2013 Mr President, ladies and gentlemen, Complying with the control mandate contained in article 56 of Law 9/2012 on the restructuring and resolution of credit institutions, of November 14, I appear before this Subcommittee on Bank Restructuring and Financial Sanitation as President of the Governing Committee of the Fund for Orderly Bank Restructuring (FROB), in which it constitutes my third appearance, to report on the activities carried out by the FROB since April 24, the date on which I last appeared. Prior to the presentation of the specific situation in each of the institutions, you will allow me a brief general introduction on the evolution of the financial restructuring process as a whole. INTRODUCTION I would like, first of all, to recall that at the beginning of July the conclusions of the third revision of the Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) were made public. Well, the reports issued in this regard by the European Commission and the International Monetary Fund agree that the measures provided for therein are being correctly applied, achieving the objectives set. With regard to compliance with the restructuring plans, the reports positively assess the significant progress made to date and highlight the reinforcement that this has meant for the equity position of the Spanish banking system as a whole. Specifically, it highlights the good execution of the divestment programs imposed on the entities in their respective plans, the correct compliance with the capacity adjustment programs, the readjustment of balance sheets that they have made and the improvement that this has meant in the indicators of efficiency, liquidity and solvency. In fact, I would like to highlight that to date the three fundamental measures for restructuring and financial restructuring included in the plans of the entities of groups 1 and 2 have been implemented, according to the nomenclature of the MOU that refers respectively to the banks majority owned by the FROB and to the entities with capital deficit that cannot face this deficit without public aid. Thus, and after the injection of funds to the aforementioned entities for a total of 39,078 million euros and the transfer to the Asset Management Company from the Bank Restructuring (Sareb) of real estate assets for a net amount close to 51,000 million euros, measures on which I already reported in my previous appearance, Burden-sharing exercises have been completed. These have been implemented through the implementation of the management actions of hybrid equity and subordinated debt instruments d0 with the exception of Banco Gallego, which is expected to be carried out in the coming days d0 which have generated additional capital for the entities for a gross amount of approximately 13,600 million euros. The burden-sharing exercises respond to the fundamental principle enshrined in Law 9/2012 and in the MoU of minimizing the use of public resources in restructuring and resolution processes. This implies that holders of hybrid equity and subordinated debt instruments should contribute to the recapitalisation of the entities affected by these processes, but should do so in accordance with the ranking of their securities and, in any event, once shareholders have incurred losses to the extent possible. The shareholders have assumed losses as a result of the reduction of their participation in the entities based on the economic valuation of this determined by the FROB and the dilution caused by the capital injections made by it. Management actions for hybrid equity and subordinated debt instruments, on the other hand, have involved the application of certain haircuts on the nominal value of the securities and the subsequent reinvestment of the remaining value in shares or other similar equity instruments. The actions of the FROB, like those of the rest of the authorities involved, have been aimed, however, at making compatible the principles of burden sharing indicated with the mitigation as far as possible of the costs borne by the most vulnerable investors. To this end, arbitration processes have been undertaken in nationalized entities for investors affected by poor marketing of hybrid instruments and liquidity mechanisms have been implemented to facilitate the cash conversion of assets received in exchange processes. Thus, I would like to inform you that the deadline for submitting claims in arbitration proceedings for the commercialization of preferred shares and subordinated debt initiated by the entities Bankia, NCG Banco and Catalunya Banc (CX) has ended, and that it is expected that the analysis of them will be very advanced by the end of this year. As I pointed out and I told you in my hearing on 24 April, the need to alleviate the particularly unfavourable situation of investors affected by the burden-sharing exercises they receive in the exchange of their preferred shares and subordinated debt unlisted shares, without this situation being expected to change within a reasonable time horizon, motivated the design of mechanisms for the provision of liquidity to these instruments. Specifically, Article 2 of Royal Decree-Law 6/2013, of 22 March, on the protection of holders of certain savings and investment products and other financial measures, provides for the possibility of subscription or acquisition by the Deposit Guarantee Fund (FGD) of ordinary shares not admitted to trading on a regulated market issued by entities that have received public support, within the framework of the aforementioned actions for the management of hybrid instruments and subordinated debt. In compliance with this provision, the FGD by agreement of its Management Committee dated June 4 and 7, 2013, in accordance with section four b) of the fifth additional provision of RD-Law 21/2012, made a voluntary offer for the acquisition of the shares not admitted to trading on a regulated market of the entities NCG Banco and Catalunya Banc, subscribed within the framework of the management actions of hybrid instruments and subordinated debt. This offer was aimed exclusively at those who, on March 23, 2013, held preferred shares and subordinated debt, and in which the status of retail clients concured, in accordance with the provisions of article 78 bis of Law 24/1988. This offer to acquire ordinary shares was made under the terms and conditions published on the websites of the issuing entities, the FGD and the National Securities Market Commission, through a relevant event, as well as in a newspaper of national diffusion and another of the Autonomous Community of the registered office of the issuing entity. The conditions of the offer to acquire shares, as well as the results thereof, will be set out below when carrying out the analysis of each of the entities. The management exercises of hybrid instruments of each of the entities have some common features, while the valuation rules of the securities, as well as the criteria followed in determining the discounts to be applied according to their category, are coincident. Notwithstanding the foregoing, there are substantial differences that I will analyse in detail for each entity, and which respond to the commitments assumed with the European institutions, to the requirements imposed by the recapitalisation plans on the percentages of participation of the holders of these securities in the share capital, to the minimum thresholds of acceptance of the exchange or to the generation of a minimum amount of principal capital as a result of its implementation. Allow me to explain to you the specific actions that have been undertaken by the FROB in relation to the resolution and restructuring plans since last April to date in each of the entities of the so-called Groups 1 and 2, as well as those referred to Sareb. I will also report on the current situation of the arbitration proceedings relating to the marketing of preferred shares and subordinated debt, the status of the legal proceedings initiated by the FROB in relation to different credit institutions and, finally, on the financial situation of the FROB, whose annual accounts were approved last July. NCG BANCO, S.A. Ladies and gentlemen, as you will recall, NCG Banco's resolution plan recognised the bank's initial capital needs, which stood at EUR 5 425 million after taking into account the effect of the transfer of assets to Sareb and hybrid management shares. These 5,425 million euros were injected through ESM funds by Resolution of the Governing Committee of the FROB of December 26, 2012. The transfer of real estate assets to Sareb also became effective on 31 December. For its part, the implementation of hybrid management actions was reflected in the Resolution of the Governing Committee of the FROB of June 7, 2013. The management actions of hybrid instruments implemented were addressed to the holders of these NCG Banco securities, which represented an outstanding balance of 2,047 million euros. The average cut applied for all emissions was 30%. The shares exercised included the repurchase, subject to application of the corresponding haircuts, of the preferred shares and perpetual subordinated obligations, and the reinvestment of the repurchase value in ordinary shares of the entity. Holders of the subordinated term bonds were given the choice between reinvesting in shares of the entity with the established haircut or doing so, with a higher haircut, in a senior debt security with the same maturity date as the repurchased security and with a yield of 2% payable at maturity. The implementation of these actions to manage hybrid equity and subordinated debt instruments has had a positive impact on the entity's equity of approximately 1,959 million euros, excluding taxes, which has served to reduce the need for public funds. Naturally, the final impact on the estate could vary depending on the outcome of the judicial and arbitration proceedings initiated or that may be initiated in the future. Currently, after the deadline for submission of arbitration requests, which began in July 2012, a volume of requests amounting to 497 million euros has been accepted, giving an alternative solution to the hybrid management exercise to an approximate number of 58,000 customers, representing 49.8% of the total. On the other hand, and as I have already pointed out, the Deposit Guarantee Fund (FGD), exceptionally, made a voluntary offer to acquire ordinary shares of NCG Banco, subscribed within the framework of the management shares of hybrid instruments and subordinated debt, and addressed exclusively to those who, on 23 March 2013, held preference shares and subordinated debt and in which the status of retail clients was present, in accordance with the provisions of article 78 bis of Law 24/1988. The offer was formulated as a purchase and sale of shares and with a cash consideration per share received by the seller, which resulted from applying an illiquidity discount of 13.8%. This discount was determined on the basis of an independent expert report in accordance with Article 4 of the Fifth Additional Provision of Royal Decree-Law 21/2012. The deadline for acceptance of the aforementioned offer ended on July 12. The offer was attended by holders of the shares representing 25.6% of the share capital of NCG Banco, which represents 89% of the shares to which the offer was directed, and represented a total cost for the FGD of 801.7 million euros. Once the above operations have been carried out, the FROB is the main shareholder of the entity with 62.75% of the capital, the FGD owns 25.57% and the rest is in the hands of the previous holders of hybrid products and subordinated debt. As you know, another of the actions that institutions must undertake in accordance with their restructuring plans, and which is fundamental for the success of the recapitalisation process, relates to divestment processes. Thus, with regard to the actions carried out by NCG Banco to reduce the structure of the entity, in this period 66 branches have been sold to Banco Etcheverr92a, and yesterday the award was made public for a figure of 60 million euros, and through the corresponding competitive process, from the EVO Banco business unit to the US entity Apollo. This business unit will be constituted, with the prior authorization of the Bank of Spain, as an independent financial institution through the segregation of the banking business of the 80 branches of NCG Banco that are currently operating under the EVO Banco brand. Parallel to these processes, during the month of July, the FROB arranged to hire BNP Paribas to carry out a detailed analysis of the assets (portfolios and business units) to estimate the price that the FROB could reasonably obtain in its case for the sale in a competitive process of the shares of NCG Banco. At present, the analysis process prior to making the decision on the start of the possible competitive process, which is expected to begin in the last days of this month of September, is practically completed. GALICIAN BANK As I had occasion to explain in my previous appearance, originally the resolution of Banco Gallego was contemplated within the resolution plan of NCG Banco, which required its sale before April 30, 2013 or, in another case, the orderly liquidation of the entity. As you will recall, following the transfer of assets to Sareb and the simultaneous capital reduction and increase that was agreed and executed in January and February, a competitive process of divestment of NCG Banco's stake in Banco Gallego began. To this end, NCG Banco contracted Mediobanca as an investment bank and, on April 19, 2013, the Governing Committee of the FROB agreed to the award of Banco Gallego to Banco Sabadell because it considered that its offer was the most competitive according to the established valuation criteria and in order to optimize the use of public resources. The details of the offer, which involves an injection of capital by the FROB amounting to 245 million euros, as well as additional guarantees, with obvious advantages over the settlement alternative estimated at a cost of more than 930 million euros, were already exposed in my previous appearance, so now I will limit my presentation to inform of the actions that are being taken to complete it. On April 23, 2013, a resolution plan was approved for Banco Gallego, including both the forecasts previously included in NCG Banco's resolution plan and the new commitments arising from the purchase agreement. As part of the sale process, on May 9, 2013, the Governing Committee of the FROB proposed to the Bank of Spain the provisional replacement of the administrative body of Banco Gallego and the appointment of FROB itself as provisional administrator. On 17 May 2013, the Executive Committee of the Banco de Espa96a approved both Banco Gallego's resolution plan and the provisional replacement of its administrative body. On May 22, 2013, the Governing Committee of the FROB agreed to the appointment of Mr. Jos8e Manuel Oliver Mart92nez as the natural person who, on behalf of the FROB, will exercise the administrative functions of Banco Gallego. With regard to the exercise of the management actions of hybrids of capital and subordinated debt, the Governing Committee of the FROB, on July 4, 2013, and the Executive Committee of the Bank of Spain a day later, approved the modification of the resolution plan of Banco Gallego in order to introduce a change in the mandatory exercise of management of hybrid instruments and subordinated debt with respect to the one initially planned. This perfectly combines the mandatory exercise in which the subscription of Banco Gallego's senior debt would be imposed, with the alternative that the buyer, Banco de Sabadell, would present to offer the subscription of capital instruments of that entity. Once approved by the European Commission this new resolution framework for Banco Gallego at the end of last July, the implementation of the hybrid and subordinated debt management actions is expected for the next days of September, which will allow Banco Sabadell to be fully effective. CATALUNYA BANC, S.A (CX) Catalunya Banc's resolution plan recognised the bank's initial capital needs which, after the transfer of assets to Sareb and the consideration of hybrid management shares, amounted to db9,084 million, which were injected through ESM funds through a Resolution of the FROB Governing Committee of 26 December 2012. The transfer of real estate assets to Sareb became effective on 31 December 2012, in accordance with the forecasts of the aforementioned plan. On the other hand, the management actions of hybrid equity and subordinated debt instruments were carried out by Resolution of the Governing Committee of the FROB of June 7, 2013. These management actions of hybrid instruments implemented were aimed at holders of securities representing an outstanding balance of 1,818 million euros, with an average cut for total issues of 25%. The shares exercised consisted of the repurchase, after the application of the cuts of the preferred shares and the perpetual subordinated obligations, and their reinvestment in ordinary shares of the entity. Holders of the subordinated term bonds were given the option of reinvesting in shares, after applying the corresponding discounts, or doing so, with a higher haircut, in a debt security with the same maturity as the repurchased security and with a yield of 2%. The management actions of hybrid instruments have had a positive impact on the entity's assets, without taking into account taxes, of approximately 1,676 million euros, an amount that could vary depending on the outcome of the judicial and arbitration proceedings initiated or that could be initiated in the future. Currently, after the deadline for submission of requests for arbitration that began in October 2012, a number of claims corresponding to 28,474 clients of the entity have been admitted by the independent expert, representing 36% of the total and representing an amount of 259 million euros, having obtained so far positive award 13,135 holders, representing a volume of EUR 158 million. As in the case of NCG Banco, the Deposit Guarantee Fund (FGD), exceptionally, made a voluntary offer to acquire ordinary shares of Catalunya Banc, subscribed within the framework of the shares of management of hybrid instruments and subordinated debt, addressed exclusively to those who, on 23 March 2013, held preference shares and subordinated debt, and in which the condition of retail clients concurs, in accordance with the provisions of article 78 bis of Law 24/1988. The offer was made under the same conditions and with the same requirements as for the acquisition of the common shares of NCG Banco, so you will allow me to refer to the above. The offer was attended by holders of the shares representing 32.3% of the share capital of Catalunya Banc, which represents 97.1% of the shares to which the offer was directed, and represented a total cost for the FGD of 1,000.9 million euros. Once the recapitalization, the hybrid management exercise and the FGD offer have been completed, the FROB is the main shareholder, with 66% of the capital, and the FGD owns 32.3%. On the other hand, and within the procedure of reorganization of the management body, on May 10, 2013, the cessation of Mr. Adolf Tod97 Rovira and Mr. Jaume Masana i Ribalta as President and CEO of the entity respectively became effective, and Mr. Jos8e Carlos Pla was appointed as President of the entity. Finally, to inform you that in July the Governing Committee of the FROB, after processing a competitive procedure, awarded the company N 1 Corporate Finance a contract for the analysis and possible sale of Catalunya Banc, whose purpose is the detailed study of the assets (portfolios and business units) that allows estimating the price that the FROB could reasonably obtain in its case for the sale in a competitive process of the shares of Catalunya Banc. Once the value of these assets has been estimated, the FROB, based on the weighting of the data and the valuations obtained, will decide on the advisability or not of initiating a competitive sale process since the plan provides for the resolution of the entity within a maximum period of five years. BFA-BANKIA The capital needs for the entity recognized in the restructuring plan motivated the injection of ESM funds amounting to 17,959 million euros, which was made by Resolution of the Governing Committee of the FROB dated December 26, 2012, although on September 3, 2012 the entity was also the recipient of an initial advance with funds from the FROB amounting to 4,500 million euros. After that, and as you will recall, the Governing Committee of the FROB, on April 16, 2013, issued a Resolution containing the necessary agreements to complete the recapitalization of the BFA-Bankia Group. These agreements consisted of a capital reduction through a reduction of the nominal value of the shares from 2 euros to one cent, an operation to ensure the normal price of the shares, and two capital increases, a first with preferential subscription right and guaranteed by the FROB through BFA, for an amount of 10,700 million euros, and a second for an amount of up to 5,210 million euros to cover the exercise of the management actions of hybrid equity and subordinated debt instruments. The management actions of hybrid instruments implemented were directed to the holders of these securities representing an outstanding balance of 6,911 million euros. The exercise of these has had a positive impact on the entity's equity of approximately 6,669 million euros, without taking into account taxes, an amount that significantly reduces its capital needs, on the one hand generating profits from the nominal value cut and on the other through reinvestment in capital. The shares exercised in this case have the same scheme as in the case of the previous entities, although, in accordance with the criteria of the European Commission on the percentages of participation of the FROB and the new shareholders, the reinvestment of the amount in ordinary shares of the entity has been made at the same subscription price as the FROB. This implies the absorption by holders of hybrid equity and subordinated debt instruments of the proportional share of the negative economic value of the institution. After the complete execution of the FROB agreements referred to above, and therefore the full recapitalization of the group, BFA, an entity of which the FROB remains its sole shareholder, became the owner of 68.39% of Bankia's shares. Finally, ladies and gentlemen, I would like to inform you that BFA-Bankia began, on 18 April, the deadline for receipt of applications for claims in the arbitration procedure on the marketing of preference shares and subordinated debt that ended on 16 July. With the most recent data, a number of complaints corresponding to 108,425 clients of the entity have been admitted by the independent expert, which means the admission so far of claims for 37% of clients, representing a total of 821 million euros. The positive arbitration awards issued to date represent a volume of 84 million euros, corresponding to 18,737 clients. The entity expects that the arbitration process, taking into account the experience of this period, will extend until the end of 2013, and may even last during the first half of 2014. GROUP 2 ENTITIES Continuing with my presentation, I will now go on to detail the latest actions carried out in relation to the entities integrated in the so-called Group 2, those that without being initially participated by the FROB had to resort to public aid to overcome their capital deficit, and which is formed by Banco Mare Nostrum, Banco CEISS, Banco Caja3 and Liberbank. As you will recall, the plans of the Group 2 entities were approved by the European Commission on 20 December, after the national authorities (FROB and Banco de Espa96a) had done so. I will break down the latest actions carried out in each of the Group 2 entities and their specific implementation: a5 Banco Mare Nostrum (BMN) BMN's recapitalisation plan recognised a final capital requirement of db730 million, which was covered by the subscription in March 2013 by the FROB of the entity's newly issued ordinary shares. Once its assets were transferred to Sareb, the Governing Committee of the FROB, on May 27, issued the Resolution implementing the management actions of capital hybrids and subordinated debt. These actions were addressed to holders of securities representing an outstanding balance of 449 million euros. The average cut for all emissions has stood at 26%. The implementation of the management actions of hybrid equity and subordinated debt instruments has had a positive impact on the entity's equity, of 425 million euros, via capital increase and nominal cut. As a result of the recapitalization operations of the entity, the FROB has a 65% stake in the capital, the rest being owned by the founding savings banks and third parties. Finally, to inform them that within the divestment process that the entity must undertake in compliance with the plan, on May 31, 2013, the sale of the Caixa Pened8es network to Banco Sabadell became effective. This sale was a fundamental action in the recapitalization of the entity, since it has allowed it to reduce the perimeter of its balance sheet by about 10,000 million euros (of which 9,500 million euros correspond to loans) and the transfer of 462 offices and 2,019 workers. a5 CEISS Bank As you will recall, in my last appearance I informed you about the analysis that the FROB and the Bank of Spain together with the European authorities were carrying out on a possible corporate operation with Unicaja Banco, which had delayed the injection of public funds amounting to 604 million euros, foreseen in the plan pending the final terms of the offer and its inclusion as part of the Plan of Resolution of the entity. This delay is justified by the benefits that the operation can bring to the affected entities and the public treasury. Given the urgent need of the entity to strengthen the first category own resources, and while proceeding to process the modification of the plan, it was necessary to undertake on April 24 said injection of public funds. However, in order to make it more compatible with the offer that might be submitted, it was implemented instead of by subscribing to ordinary shares of Banco CEISS, as contemplated in the initial plan, through the subscription of contingently convertible bonds. These instruments establish a pattern for the repayment of public aid, which contributes to reducing the risk borne by the taxpayer. On 9 and 10 May 2013, the FROB and the Executive Committee of the Banco de Espa96a, respectively, approved the amendment to the Resolution Plan of Banco CEISS of 19 December 2012 in order to adapt it to the offer that the Unicaja Group would present for the purchase of Banco CEISS, S.A. On 13 May 2013, the European Commission validated this amendment. The Governing Committee of the FROB, by resolution of May 16, agreed on the bulk of the recapitalization that included most of the exercise of the management shares of hybrid equity and subordinated debt instruments. This year was completed on July 15 with the exchange of the only two subordinated debt issues that remained to be managed, once Unicaja finalized the terms of its offer and the estimate of the entity's capital needs was updated. The shares exercised presented a singularity derived from the conditions of Unicaja's offer. Thus, wholesale holders had to reinvest in the subscription of shares, while retailers had to do so in another equity instrument, namely bonds necessarily and contingently convertible into shares of Banco CEISS. The actions implemented affected an outstanding balance of 1,433 million euros and have had a positive impact on the entity's equity amounting to 1,351 million euros. On July 15, Unicaja Banco announced the terms of the offer that it plans to address to 100% of the shareholders and holders of bonds necessary and contingently convertible of Banco CEISS, excluding the FROB. Unicaja will offer institutional investors newly issued Unicaja Banco shares in exchange for CEISS shares and a combination of contingent obligations (Cocos) and mandatory convertible bonds (ManCocos) of Unicaja Banco to retail investors of Banco CEISS. This offer is conditional on a minimum acceptance of 75%. Likewise, Unicaja's offer would include a commitment to request admission to trading on the Spanish stock exchanges within a maximum period of three years from the execution of the exchange offer, which would mean a medium-term liquidity horizon for the holders of CEISS instruments that attend it. As foreseen in the resolution plan, in the event that this offer is not formalized or does not obtain the minimum acceptance established, the FROB would proceed to acquire a controlling stake in the entity, by converting the contingently convertible bonds it holds into shares. In any case, the established calendar foresees that the offer can be authorized by the CNMV next month. a5 Banco Grupo Caja3 The restructuring plan of Banco Grupo Caja3 is developed within the framework of the integration of the entity with Ibercaja Banco. On May 23, 2013, Ibercaja Banco and Banco Caja3 signed the definitive integration agreement that has involved the acquisition by Ibercaja Banco of 100% of Banco Grupo Caja3 through a share exchange process. To this end, Ibercaja Banco agreed to a capital increase amounting to 325.5 million euros that were subscribed by the three member savings banks of Banco Grupo Caja3, contributing as consideration the entire share capital of the group. The process will conclude at the end of 2014 with the merger by absorption of Caja3 by Ibercaja Banco. Since July 25, 2013, the shareholders of Banco Grupo Caja3 (CAI, C92rculo Cat97lico Burgos and Caja Badajoz) have had a joint stake of 12.2% of Ibercaja Banco. As you will recall, Banco Grupo Caja 3 was the recipient of public financial support amounting to EUR 407 million, which materialised with the subscription by the FROB of necessarily convertible bonds. Once the transfer of assets to Sareb had been carried out, the entity had to undertake, in accordance with the recapitalisation plan, a hybrid management exercise of capital and voluntary subordinated debt, conducted by the entity itself, aimed at the holders of those securities, which in this case were all wholesalers. In the event that this year does not obtain the percentage of acceptance or generates a minimum of capital, a mandatory exercise should be imposed by the FROB. The hybrid instrument management actions for both financial years were adopted in June 2013. The shares agreed by the FROB affected a single issue whose holders of the securities did not attend the voluntary exchange proposed by the entity. The exercise of these has had a positive impact on the entity's equity of approximately 44 million euros, via capital and capital gains obtained in the exchange of subordinated debt for senior debt. a5 Liberbank In my previous appearance, the entity Liberbank had implemented the management actions of hybrid instruments, both the voluntary one carried out by the entity and imposed in its restructuring plan, and the mandatory one agreed by the FROB when the entity did not obtain the percentage of acceptance imposed by the aforementioned Plan. However, the process of recapitalization of Liberbank foresaw for its completion the listing of its shares. On May 16, Liberbank's IPO was carried out through a procedure of , and therefore without the need for a public offer. The initial trading price of the shares was 0.40 euros, with their price currently slightly above 0.44 euros. In order to compensate for the risk of fluctuating in the price of the securities delivered in that year, the founding savings banks -Grupo Cajastur, Caja Extremadura and Caja Cantabria- have offered a loyalty plan aimed at retail customers previously holding the securities that were affected by the exchange. This plan implies that the savings banks assume with their own assets a part of the risk of loss of value of the securities acquired in the exchange by investors who have undertaken not to dispose of them for two years. SAREB Let me refer briefly to the Company for the Management of Assets from Bank Restructuring (Sareb), which, as you know, is one of the cornerstones of financial reform. Sareb was formally constituted on 28 November last year and on 31 December received the assets of Group 1 entities which, in accordance with Law 9/2012, were to be transferred to that company. This transfer was completed on February 28 of this year with the assets from the entities of the so-called Group 2. In total, 50,781 million euros of real estate and loans for real estate development. The FROB holds 45% of the company's capital and a similar percentage of its subordinated debt, with the rest of Sareb's equity in private hands. Since its establishment, the company has made an appreciable effort to quickly achieve fully operational conditions. This has allowed Sareb's commercial activity to make rapid progress in the sale of real estate and financial assets in the three planned channels: sale of wholesale portfolios, sale of singular assets and retail sale through transferor entities. With regard to the company's financial information, it should be noted that Sareb's annual accounts for 2012 were approved by the company's General Meeting held last May. They cover the financial year from November 28 to December 31, 2012, have been audited by PricewaterhouseCoopers and present a clean opinion. The result of the year was losses amounting to 5.5 million euros, mainly due to external services and financial expenses. In addition, in accordance with the provisions of RD 1559/2012, Sareb will publish its first half-yearly activity report for the first half of 2013 in the coming weeks. For Sareb, 2013 is a year full of logistical and financial challenges: in addition to the need to make rapid progress in the implementation of systems, in the knowledge and control of portfolio management and the implementation of the different marketing channels, we must add the fact that Sareb bears the financial burden of a full year while commercial activity has actually started from the second quarter of the exercise. JUDICIAL PROCEEDINGS AND PROTOCOL OF PREVIOUS ACTION Regarding the legal proceedings promoted by the FROB, you are already aware that the FROB assumes an active role in the detection of any irregular conduct in those entities in which it has been appointed provisional administrator or to which it has provided financial support. As I have already had the opportunity to comment in previous appearances, in order to debug possible criminal responsibilities and minimize the costs of these processes, the FROB commissioned independent experts to analyze the irregular operations or operations of dubious economic rationality carried out by the previous managers of these entities. This has made it possible to launch up to ten criminal cases against directors or former directors of the entities and third parties in which alleged crimes related to real estate traffic and their remuneration are investigated. As a result of the experience accumulated in these criminal proceedings, during this quarter the Governing Committee of the FROB approved the protocol of action for the investigation and analysis of the operations carried out in the last five years, which have had an impact on the entity for a significant amount and present indications of irregularity or do not respond to a logical economic purpose. The protocol was communicated to the different entities at the beginning of May, each of them having adopted the necessary measures for its implementation through the investigation of suspicious transactions. Currently, the FROB is analyzing the reports prepared or in the preparation phase by the internal audit departments of the entities with the suspicious operations detected, to assess the relevance of hiring external third-party services specialized in forensic analysis so that, where appropriate, the investigation work continues and allow the increase of judicial cases to debug possible responsibilities. In the coming months, this activity will constitute one of the fundamental axes of the action of the FROB, so that the principles and objectives of the resolution can be complied with, among which it plays a main role that managers, administrators or third parties who have generated costs or damages contribute in accordance with the applicable legislation to bear the costs of restructuring or resolution. This, however, is done with the utmost respect for the principle of legal certainty that must characterize the actions of the FROB, and in particular, compliance with the deadlines necessary to have sufficient information, vestiges and evidence to allow a well-founded judgment on the alleged irregularity of the conduct. FINANCIAL SITUATION OF THE FROB The Governing Committee of the FROB, at its meeting on July 18, approved the annual accounts of the Fund for 2012, prepared in accordance with the General Accounting Plan, having issued an audit report without qualifications. The accounts of the FROB are very influenced, as it can not be otherwise, by the moment of the restructuring process in which we find ourselves, in which the entities have already been recapitalized and the foundations have been laid for their restructuring, but whose temporary execution contemplates a horizon of several years. Therefore, the evolution of the accounts of the FROB will depend to a large extent on the result of the divestment processes and, more generally, on the evolution of the financial sector. The 2012 accounts include financial support to Group 1 entities (BFA-Bankia, Catalunya Banc, NCG Banco and Banco de Valencia), which has led to a sharp increase in the size of liabilities to finance these injections. In December 2012, the State granted the FROB a loan for 39,468 million euros, an amount that covers the recapitalization of Group 1 and Sareb entities. However, it does not include those of Group 2, since the injection of funds into it was made in February 2013. The Treasury loan to the FROB materialized in the form of ESM bonds, since European assistance was channeled through this instrument. The result for the year reflects losses of 26,000 million euros. This figure is mainly due to the accounting, following a principle of prudence, of significant impairments in the value of investments, resulting from the valuation reports entrusted, under Article 5 of Law 9/2012, to independent experts, and based on the financial assumptions contemplated in the plans. These valuations do not prejudge the recoverable value in the divestment processes and, therefore, do not constitute the recognition of losses or benefits derived from a possible disposal of the interests in the different entities. These can only be determined once the restructuring and resolution processes have been carried out, and after the divestment by the FROB in each of the entities in whose shareholding it is currently present. As a result of the high impairments in value, net assets stood at -21,831 million euros, a figure that incorporates the increase in the FROB's equity endowment amounting to 6,000 million euros, made by the State in June 2012. In order to restore the equity position of the FROB, progress is being made in its recapitalization through the conversion of the loan granted by the Treasury into equity for an amount of 27,000 million euros, for which the mandatory authorization of the ESM is already available. In any case, the FROB has an adequate cash position to meet its commitments in the short and medium term. At the end of June 2013, the amount of uncommitted cash of the FROB amounted to 12,137.5 million euros, invested in State Debt and liquid deposits in credit institutions and in the Bank of Spain. With regard to operating or operating expenses, the reconfiguration of the FROB after the entry into force of RD-Law 24/2012 (now Law 9/2012), which grants it the status of resolution authority, with a huge range of administrative and commercial powers, determined the need to provide it with a structure and means appropriate to its functions. Therefore, throughout the first quarter of 2013 a recruitment process was carried out to provide the Fund with an adequate minimum staff, as well as a transfer of the FROB from its original headquarters to one according to its new size. This has led to an increase in operating expenses in items such as personnel costs or leases. I must, in any case, show that throughout this process of design and implementation of the new FROB has always been based on the principle of austerity, taking advantage as far as possible of the human resources present in the public sector. In the same way, the selection of the new headquarters of the FROB has proceeded taking advantage of the best opportunities and prices of the market, finally choosing a building of ownership Public. Finally, the growth of the workforce and its specialization in a matter as complex as the resolution of credit institutions, allows and will allow the reduction of costs for contracting external services, previously necessary due to the lack of human resources. In terms of contracting services and supplies, it has been based on the maximum respect for the principles of public procurement, with the specialties of the FROB and its double submission to public and private law, which has determined access to third-party services, indispensable on the other hand in accordance with Law 9/2012, that requires the services of valuers, independent experts, the organization of divestment processes with advisors and investment banks, etc., at competitive prices derived from the greatest possible competition. In short, the creation of the resolution authority has been consistent with the current context and with the principle of rationality in spending, but always bearing in mind the need for such a specialised and relevant task to have adequate means. CONCLUSIONS I conclude, ladies and gentlemen, As I highlighted in my speech, since my last appearance in this Subcommittee, the activity of the FROB has continued to be very intense and has focused from the administrative point of view on the implementation of hybrid management exercises, which is practically completed the recapitalization of the entities provided for in the plans contemplated in the Memorandum of Understanding. In the field of management, the FROB after an internal reflection that had the collaboration of a consultant has initiated an analysis process to lay the foundations of the divestment processes of banks with a public majority, NCG Banco and CX, which must necessarily be sold in a finite horizon according to their resolution plans. I believe, therefore, that the FROB continues to advance in the execution of the restructuring program of our financial system in line with the planned schedule and with fidelity to the principles that have been guiding its actions. These are none other than minimizing the costs of the process for the public treasury and maximizing its contribution to the adequate development of public policies in the financial sector. And, without further ado, I remain at your disposal.
text_original: COMPARECENCIA DEL PRESIDENTE DE LA COMISIN RECTORA DEL FROB ANTE LA SUBCOMISIN DE REESTRUCTURACIN BANCARIA Y SANEAMIENTO FINANCIERO DEL CONGRESO 10 de septiembre 2013 Seor Presidente, Seoras Cumpliendo con el mandato de control recogido en el artculo 56 de la Ley 9/2012 de reestructuracin y resolucin de entidades de crdito, de 14 de noviembre, comparezco ante esta Subcomisin de Reestructuracin Bancaria y Saneamiento Financiero como Presidente de la Comisin Rectora del Fondo de Reestructuracin Ordenada Bancaria (FROB), en la que constituye mi tercera comparecencia, para informar de las actividades desarrolladas por el FROB desde el pasado 24 de abril, fecha en la que comparec por ltima vez. Con carcter previo a la exposicin de la situacin concreta en cada una de las entidades, me van a permitir una breve introduccin general sobre la evolucin del proceso de reestructuracin financiera en su conjunto. INTRODUCCIN Quisiera, en primer lugar, recordar que a principios del mes de julio se hacan pblicas las conclusiones de la tercera revisin del Memorando de Entendimiento (MOU, en sus siglas en ingls). Pues bien, los informes emitidos al respecto por la Comisin Europea y el Fondo Monetario Internacional coinciden en sealar que se estn aplicando correctamente las medidas previstas en el mismo, consiguindose alcanzar los objetivos fijados.
