The intense work carried out in recent months has allowed us to obtain the first results of this tool, based on three macroeconomic scenarios: a base scenario, determined from the current projections of the Bank of Spain, and two alternative, less likely, characterized by a more unfavorable evolution of the main magnitudes for the period 2013-1015. The first alternative scenario, called the unfavorable scenario, foresees a stagnation of GDP over the coming years, with a more negative evolution of variables such as unemployment or house prices, in line with the forecasts of the International Monetary Fund and which are less optimistic than those of the consensus of analysts. The most adverse scenario, of very low probability, would imply a new relapse of the Spanish economy, which would enter what would be the third recession of the crisis. Based on these scenarios, the results of the year carried out for all 15 entities analysed show a solvency position in 2015 that was quite comfortable at an aggregate level. Even in the most adverse scenario, the loss-absorbing capacity exceeds the expected losses by about db30 billion. Thus, the capital ratio in 2015, using Basel III first-class capital as a benchmark, is reduced from levels above 11% in the baseline scenario, and to levels of 10.8% and 10.2% in the adverse and adverse scenarios respectively. Although this tool does not allow to accurately calculate the solvency situation of each entity at the end of the horizon, it follows from the exercise that all the entities analyzed would comfortably exceed the regulatory minimums, even in the most adverse scenario. As I said at the beginning, the results I have mentioned to you constitute a first application of a new analytical tool that, from now on, will be part of the set of supervisory instruments of the Bank of Spain and that, of course, will also be used in due course within the scope of the Single Supervisory Mechanism. Thank you very much for your attention.
text_original: 06.11.2013 El sistema bancario espaol: situacin y perspectivas Central Bankers Day /Grupo Santander Fernando Restoy Subgobernador Muchas gracias por la invitacin y por las palabras de presentacin. Me complace mucho participar de nuevo en este seminario de bancos centrales organizado por el Banco Santander. De un tiempo a esta parte, el entorno econmico y financiero ha cambiado notablemente. Hace apenas un ao, en esta misma Conferencia, dediqu gran parte de mi intervencin, que se produca a los pocos meses de la aprobacin del programa de asistencia financiera para nuestro sector bancario, a explicar el proceso de reestructuracin del sector bancario espaol, detallando la revisin de la calidad de los activos y las pruebas de resistencia realizadas, los planes de recapitalizacin y reestructuracin de las entidades y el proceso de segregacin de los activos deteriorados mediante su transferencia a una sociedad de gestin de activos externa. Este ao, me van a permitir que intente poner en valor el trabajo realizado, sin por ello dejar de mantener ciertas cautelas respecto a los retos que se avecinan en los prximos meses. Para ello, durante los prximos minutos sealar, en primer lugar, los desarrollos recientes que considero ms positivos para el sector bancario espaol. Me detendr despus en los principales retos a corto y medio plazo, tanto desde una perspectiva nacional como europea, y comentar las actuaciones que como supervisor bancario estamos llevando a cabo para hacer frente a estos retos. Aprovechar, entonces, para presentar los resultados de un ejercicio prospectivo sobre la situacin de solvencia de la banca espaola que hemos hecho pblicos hoy. Desarrollos recientes favorables Como les deca, la reforma sin precedentes a la que se ha sometido el sector bancario espaol en respuesta a la crisis financiera est dando sus frutos. En particular, son varios los elementos positivos que quisiera sealar. En primer lugar, uno de los resultados ms significativos de la reforma financiera ha sido la apreciable reduccin de la exposicin al sector inmobiliario por parte del sector bancario espaol. Para recuperar la confianza sobre la solidez del sistema bancario, ha sido clave facilitar el saneamiento de los balances bancarios y eliminar as el que era uno de los principales elementos de vulnerabilidad del sector financiero espaol. Este proceso de saneamiento se ha llevado a trmino mediante dos actuaciones distintas: por una parte, el aumento de las exigencias en materia de provisiones para cubrir exposiciones al sector inmobiliario y, por otra, en el caso de las entidades que recibieron ayuda pblica, la segregacin y transferencia de los activos relacionados con el sector inmobiliario a una sociedad de gestin de activos externa. Como consecuencia de estas actuaciones, la exposicin del sector bancario espaol a los riesgos inmobiliarios se ha reducido drsticamente. Los 240.000 millones de exposicin neta de provisiones- que haba a finales de 2011 se redujeron en torno al 50 % en 2012 y, para finales de este ao, esperamos que esta cifra apenas se site ligeramente por encima de los 100.000 millones. Un segundo desarrollo positivo ha sido la evolucin del margen de explotacin del sector bancario. Aunque el dbil pulso de la actividad econmica, los bajos tipos de inters y la fragmentacin de los mercados siguen presionando sobre la capacidad de generacin de rentas del sector, los mrgenes han evolucionado de modo ms favorable que lo esperado. En particular, el margen de explotacin de los negocios en Espaa durante 2013 se situar previsiblemente por encima del estimado tanto en el escenario adverso como en el escenario base de las pruebas de resistencia efectuadas el ao pasado. El tercer elemento que quiero sealar es la mejora de los ratios de solvencia del sector, tanto de las entidades que no requirieron ayudas pblicas en torno al 80 % de la industria- como de las que accedieron a fondos del Estado para aumentar su capital en la cuanta requerida segn los resultados de las pruebas de resistencia efectuadas. La solvencia de estas ltimas se vio adems beneficiada de los ejercicios de gestin de instrumentos hbridos de capital y deuda subordinada, que redujeron apreciablemente el coste para el erario pblico de los planes de recapitalizacin de las entidades vulnerables. Actualmente, todas las entidades cumplen con los requisitos de capital del 9 % segn la definicin EBA -requisitos ms exigentes que los vigentes en otras jurisdicciones- y, en general, con un margen de holgura apreciable. De hecho, esperamos que el ratio de capital para el conjunto del sector se site por encima del 10 % en 2013. Por ltimo, los avances en el proceso de recapitalizacin y reestructuracin del sector bancario estn siendo apreciados en los mercados, en un contexto de mejora generalizada de las valoraciones de los instrumentos pblicos y privados emitidos en Espaa. Esta mejora se ha reflejado en los ltimos meses en una revalorizacin de la bolsa espaola -y, en particular, de los ndices del sector bancario-, al tiempo que el diferencial de la deuda pblica espaola a 10 aos frente a la deuda alemana se ha reducido de forma progresiva respecto a los mximos que observamos a mediados de 2012. La mejora en la percepcin de los mercados puede observarse tambin en la valoracin que hacen los inversores de las entidades, de acuerdo con la relacin entre el valor de cotizacin de las entidades y su valor contable (price to book value). Actualmente, la valoracin del mercado sita a los principales bancos espaoles cotizados en una posicin medio-alta en relacin con las entidades comparables a nivel europeo. Esto ilustra no solo el incremento de la confianza en las perspectivas de rentabilidad de nuestra banca sino, tambin, en la calidad de sus activos, tal y como se refleja en los estados contables pblicos. No cabe duda, por tanto, que la reforma del sector bancario espaol est siendo bien valorada. De hecho, como muestran los informes publicados por la Comisin Europea y el FMI con ocasin de las revisiones peridicas del proceso, los objetivos se estn cumpliendo siguiendo el calendario previsto, de modo que prcticamente la totalidad de las medidas establecidas en el Memorando de Entendimiento pueden darse ya por completadas. En todo caso, a pesar de lo avances realizados, es evidente que tenemos por delante retos muy importantes que paso a comentar a continuacin. Retos para el sector bancario Probablemente, los desafos ms relevantes a los que debe hacer frente la industria bancaria espaola se derivan del entorno de debilidad econmica en el que an estamos inmersos, a pesar de la mejora que muestran los ltimos datos publicados. Tras dos aos de descenso continuado del PIB, la economa espaola habra superado, durante el tercer trimestre, la segunda recesin de la prolongada crisis econmica. Segn los ltimos datos disponibles, el PIB habra crecido durante el tercer trimestre un 0,1 % respecto al segundo, lo que supondra el primer aumento de la actividad tras nueve trimestres consecutivos de contraccin. Con todo, el pulso de la actividad econmica contina siendo dbil y se mantendr previsiblemente as en el corto plazo. En particular, a diferencia del dinamismo que muestra el sector exterior, el gasto privado se sigue contrayendo, como consecuencia de los elevados ratios de endeudamiento, la cada de la riqueza de los hogares y el continuado descenso de la renta disponible, derivado de la destruccin de empleo que, no obstante, ha empezado a desacelerarse. No obstante, ms a medio plazo, la aguda correccin que estn experimentando los desequilibrios que acumul la economa en la etapa de expansin y la primera parte de la crisis -me refiero al desajuste del sector exterior, las prdidas de competitividad, los dficit fiscales estructurales y el elevado endeudamiento privado-, apoyan las expectativas sobre una recuperacin sostenida de la actividad econmica, cuyo alcance se ver ampliado en la medida que las autoridades mantengan el impulso reformador. En segundo lugar, a pesar de la mejora observada en los mercados financieros de la zona del euro en los ltimos meses, estos no se han normalizado completamente, como refleja el volumen de actividad del interbancario, que se mantiene en niveles reducidos y el mantenimiento de un componente de riesgo pas en los precios de los activos en funcin de la localizacin del emisor. En este contexto, la disponibilidad de liquidez contina siendo un foco de atencin para las entidades bancarias. De hecho, las entidades espaolas han seguido recurriendo aunque de una manera decreciente- a la provisin de liquidez que ofrece el Eurosistema en cuantas abultadas. No obstante, la situacin de la liquidez de las instituciones bancarias ha mejorado sensiblemente en el ltimo ao. As, desde finales de septiembre de 2012 hasta finales de septiembre de 2013, las entidades espaolas redujeron su apelacin bruta al Eurosistema en 142 miles de millones de euros; una reduccin del 37 %. Por otra parte, los bancos han reducido tambin la dependencia de la financiacin mayorista en su estructura de financiacin, incrementado de modo muy pronunciado el peso relativo en sus balances de los depsitos minoristas en un contexto de cada de los prstamos a empresas y familias. De hecho, la continuada contraccin del crdito, que contina con la senda iniciada en 2009, es otro de los riesgos a los que se enfrenta la economa espaola, de particular relevancia si tenemos en cuenta la fuerte bancarizacin de nuestra economa y la preponderancia de la actividad crediticia tradicional en el modelo de negocio de las entidades espaolas. De hecho, segn los ltimos datos disponibles, el crdito al sector privado residente en Espaa registr una cada del 13 % en septiembre de 2013, si bien estos datos estn todava afectados por el traspaso de los activos asociados a promocin inmobiliaria a la Sareb -la sociedad de gestin de activos externa-. El anlisis de los factores explicativos de la evolucin contractiva del crdito reviste una cierta complejidad. La evidencia disponible muestra que esta responde a importantes factores de demanda, entre los que cabe sealar la necesidad de las familias y empresas de reducir su elevado endeudamiento. No obstante, tambin se observan restricciones por el lado de oferta que pueden estar, en el margen, dificultando el acceso al crdito de algunos prestatarios solventes, en particular en el segmento de pequeas y medianas empresas. Dicho esto, a pesar del descenso continuado del crdito desde 2010, los datos recientes apuntan a una moderacin de la intensidad de la cada. De hecho, si se excluyen las entidades que han estado sujetas a procesos de recapitalizacin y reestructuracin/resolucin (grupo 1 y 2 en terminologa MoU), la cada del crdito se produce ahora con menor intensidad que en el pasado reciente. Por otra parte, si se analiza la evolucin del crdito desde el principio de la crisis, se observan elementos que apuntan a una discriminacin saludable por parte de los bancos entre prestatarios, en funcin de su situacin financiera. As, el proceso de desapalancamiento parece haberse concentrado en aquellas empresas que presentaban mayores necesidades de saneamiento, como consecuencia de que haban alcanzado unos niveles de endeudamiento mayores. De hecho, mientras las compaas ms endeudadas registraron reducciones de casi del 10 % desde las cotas mximas alcanzadas en 2007, las empresas menos apalancadas aumentaron su nivel de deuda en ms de un 33 % entre 2007 y 2011. En cuarto lugar, se mantiene la presin alcista sobre el volumen de activos dudosos del crdito al sector privado en Espaa. La ratio de morosidad del conjunto del sector ha seguido aumentado durante la primera mitad de ao, hasta niveles del 13 % segn el dato ms reciente correspondiente al pasado mes de septiembre. Este aumento de la morosidad se ha producido de forma generalizada entre las distintas ramas de actividad, siendo las actividades de construccin y promocin inmobiliaria las que alcanzan unas ratios superiores, prximas al 30 %. Varios son los factores que subyacen tras el aumento de la tasa de morosidad que, previsiblemente seguir aumentando en el futuro prximo, habida cuenta de los desfases habituales entre el ciclo econmico y la evolucin de los impagos. No obstante, la cada del volumen de crdito, esto es, la reduccin del denominador de la ratio de morosidad, es uno de los factores explicativos cuya importancia a lo largo de los ltimos meses est ganando peso. Esto es, la tasa de morosidad aumenta porque aumentan los activos dudosos, pero tambin, y cada vez en una proporcin mayor, porque se reduce el volumen de crdito. Este efecto es especialmente importante en el caso de las entidades sujetas a planes de reestructuracin y resolucin. Finalmente, el ltimo reto que quera sealar hace referencia a los nuevos requisitos de capital basados en Basilea III, destinados a reforzar la solvencia de las entidades en respuesta a la crisis financiera internacional, a los que las entidades debern hacer frente en los prximos meses. Estos requisitos, que han sido adaptados a la normativa europea a travs de una Directiva y un Reglamento, se irn endureciendo progresivamente desde su aplicacin el prximo enero de 2014, siguiendo un calendario de implantacin gradual que se extiende a lo largo de diez aos. De este modo, a pesar de que, tal y como he comentado, el nivel de capital ha aumentado apreciablemente en el conjunto del sector, este deber adaptarse a los nuevos requisitos que contemplan no solo un aumento de la cantidad del capital exigido, sino una importante mejora de su calidad. En concreto, la nueva regulacin endurece de forma significativa los requisitos de elegibilidad de los instrumentos computables y ampla las deducciones; por ejemplo, las correspondientes al fondo de comercio, las participaciones significativas o los activos fiscales diferidos. Asimismo, la nueva regulacin introduce controles prudenciales suplementarios para reforzar la capacidad de resistencia de los bancos y del conjunto del sistema. Las entidades bancarias espaolas disponen de suficiente holgura para hacer frente a los nuevos requisitos. En trminos agregados, teniendo en cuenta los nuevos requisitos, los niveles de capital principal segn Basilea III en enero de 2014 podran situarse en niveles prximos al 10 %, muy superiores, por tanto, a los mnimos regulatorios establecidos por la normativa, respetando el calendario previsto de deducciones. Prioridades supervisoras Nos encontramos por tanto en un contexto en el que, a pesar de los avances que he comentado al principio, es evidente que el sector bancario espaol tiene importantes retos por delante derivados del entorno macroeconmico nacional, los mercados europeos y los cambios regulatorios. En este marco, el Banco de Espaa debe velar, como no puede ser de otro modo, por la preservacin del capital de las entidades y el mantenimiento del rigor en el reconocimiento del deterioro de los activos con el fin de fortalecer la credibilidad de la industria bancaria y asegurar la estabilidad del conjunto del sistema financiero. Djenme que, en este mbito destaque algunas actuaciones recientes del supervisor. El pasado mes de abril el Banco de Espaa public un conjunto de directrices sobre las polticas de refinanciacin y restructuracin de prstamos y sobre el tratamiento contable de las operaciones afectadas. El objetivo no era otro que el de garantizar una aplicacin homognea y consistente de la normativa y, en particular, asegurar una adecuada dotacin de provisiones a las exposiciones que no pudieran calificarse como de riesgo normal. Tras la publicacin de los criterios, las entidades han tenido hasta el pasado 30 de septiembre para revisar la clasificacin contable de las carteras refinanciadas o reestructuradas con el fin de garantizar la homogeneidad de la aplicacin de los criterios. Los datos preliminares recibidos en el Banco de Espaa, como resultado del trabajo de revisin llevado a cabo por las entidades, apuntan a un reconocimiento del deterioro del riesgo de crdito que implicara un saldo adicional de provisiones prximo a los 5 mil millones de euros, si bien esta cifra est sujeta a revisin. Asimismo, el pasado mes de junio publicamos una recomendacin del Banco de Espaa en relacin a la poltica de distribucin de dividendos de las entidades de crdito, para que esta se ajuste al principio de cautela y se oriente a asegurar en todo momento un adecuado nivel de capitalizacin. As, durante 2013, se ha recomendado limitar el reparto de dividendos que, en todo caso, no deben exceder del 25 % del beneficio consolidado atribuido. Con todo, una parte creciente de nuestro trabajo como supervisor se centra en los trabajos preparatorios para la puesta en funcionamiento del Mecanismo nico de Supervisin que, tras su aprobacin reciente, debe comenzar a operar de modo efectivo dentro de un ao. El Banco de Espaa est intensamente involucrado en el complejo trabajo de elaboracin de las normas, procedimientos e infraestructura que requiere el desarrollo de este complejo proyecto. Al mismo tiempo, en el mbito domstico, una de nuestras prioridades es asegurar una preparacin adecuada de las entidades que a partir de finales del ao prximo pasarn a estar directamente supervisadas por el Mecanismo nico bajo el liderazgo del BCE. Un primer reto lo constituyen las pruebas sobre perfil de riesgos, revisin de calidad de los activos y pruebas de resistencia a las que el nuevo mecanismo someter a todas las entidades europeas sobre las que ejercer una funcin supervisora directa. Anlisis prospectivo de la banca espaola En este contexto, en el Banco de Espaa hemos desarrollado una nueva herramienta supervisora que nos permitir realizar de forma regular anlisis prospectivos para la evaluacin de la solvencia de las entidades espaolas ante diferentes escenarios macroeconmicos. Esta nueva herramienta no debe entenderse como una previsin de las ratios de capital de las entidades, sino como una evaluacin de la sensibilidad de la solvencia ante un conjunto determinado de perturbaciones a lo largo de un determinado horizonte temporal. El FLESB (acrnimo de su terminologa inglesa, Forward Looking Exercise on Spanish Banks) se ha desarrollado a partir de modelos propios del supervisor. Esta perspectiva top-down se ha enriquecido con numerosos elementos granulares al nivel de prstamo (bottom-up). Este grado de detalle ha sido posible gracias al uso de las bases de datos del Banco de Espaa que ofrecen informacin muy especfica sobre diversas variables, como las que valoran las garantas y el riesgo asociado a cada prstamo. El funcionamiento de este tipo de herramientas es el siguiente: a partir de unos escenarios macroeconmicos determinados, la herramienta computa las prdidas esperadas en la cartera de crdito que se comparan con los recursos disponibles por parte de la entidad para absorber estas prdidas: provisiones existentes, generacin de beneficios y exceso de capital disponible. La proyeccin de prdidas esperadas se obtiene a partir del clculo de tres elementos esenciales: las probabilidades de impago, las prdidas en caso de impago y la exposicin en caso de impago. El intenso trabajo realizado durante los ltimos meses nos ha permitido obtener los primeros resultados de esta herramienta, sobre la base de tres escenarios macroeconmicos: un escenario base, determinado a partir de las proyecciones actuales del Banco de Espaa, y dos alternativos, menos probables, caracterizados por una evolucin ms desfavorable de las principales magnitudes para el perodo 2013-1015. El primer escenario alternativo, denominado escenario desfavorable, prev un estancamiento del PIB durante los prximos ejercicios, con una evolucin ms negativa de variables como el desempleo o el precio de la vivienda, en lnea con las previsiones del Fondo Monetario Internacional y que resultan menos optimistas que las del consenso de los analistas. El escenario ms adverso, de probabilidad muy reducida, implicara una nueva recada de la economa espaola, que se adentrara en la que sera la tercera recesin de la crisis. Sobre la base de estos escenarios, los resultados del ejercicio realizado para el conjunto de las 15 entidades analizadas muestran una posicin de solvencia en 2015 bastante confortable a nivel agregado. Incluso en el escenario ms adverso, la capacidad de absorcin de prdidas supera a las prdidas esperadas en unos 30 mil millones de euros. De este modo, la ratio de capital en 2015, usando como referencia el capital de primera categora de Basilea III, se reduce de niveles superiores al 11 % en el escenario base, y a niveles del 10,8 % y del 10,2 % en el escenario desfavorable y adverso respectivamente. Aunque esta herramienta no permite calcular con precisin la situacin de solvencia de cada entidad al final del horizonte, del ejercicio se desprende que todas las entidades analizadas superaran con holgura los mnimos regulatorios, incluso en el escenario ms adverso. Como les deca al principio, los resultados que les he comentado constituyen una primera aplicacin de una nueva herramienta analtica que, a partir de ahora, formar parte del conjunto de instrumentos supervisores del Banco de Espaa y que, como es lgico, ser tambin utilizada en su momento en el mbito del Mecanismo nico de Supervisin. Muchas gracias por su atencin.

Title: Appearance in the Commission of Economy and Competitiveness of the Senate
text: APPEARANCE OF THE PRESIDENT OF THE GOVERNING COMMISSION OF THE FROB BEFORE THE COMMISSION OF ECONOMY AND COMPETITIVENESS OF THE SENATE December 4, 2013 Thank you, President. You would be. I want to thank you for the opportunity to appear for the first time before the Senate Committee on Economy and Competitiveness as President of the Fund for Orderly Bank Restructuring (FROB). I do so with great pleasure, being aware of the responsibility that the FROB has contracted with citizens and their representatives, given its role in the preservation of a public asset as relevant as financial stability and the management that, with this objective, it carries out a very high volume of taxpayers' resources. 1. INTRODUCTION As you know, the FROB was born in 2009 through Royal Decree-Law 9/2009, of June 26, in order to facilitate the management of the solvency and liquidity problems of some Spanish financial institutions that emerged as a result of the international financial crisis, which began in 2007, and the beginning of the recessionary phase of our economy. The regulation provided the FROB with various instruments to facilitate intervention in vulnerable entities and, in particular, the provision of aid in the framework of restructuring processes. These instruments were extended in RD-l 2/2011, of February 18, which included the possibility for the FROB to subscribe ordinary shares of the affected entities. With these tools, the FROB carried out various actions in seven banks, all of them created from savings banks, which had shown appreciable solvency weaknesses. These actions undoubtedly contributed to avoiding a generalized crisis of confidence in the sector. However, the deepening of the economic crisis in Spain, with the entry into the second recessionary phase, from the second quarter of 2011, in a context of intense turbulence in the European debt markets, exacerbated the weakness of part of our financial system, while a significant deterioration in financial responsibilities became evident. The confluence of these factors generated a destabilizing feedback between the perception of sovereign risk and bank risk, by introducing uncertainty about the ability of the Spanish treasury to guarantee the stability of the banking sector. As a reflection of this situation, by mid-2012, as you recall, the interest rate on long-term Spanish debt reached 630 basis points above the German benchmark. This is the context of the origin of the external financial assistance program approved by the Eurogroup on July 20, 2012, which included the availability of European funds for a maximum amount of 100,000 million euros and a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) agreed by the Spanish and European authorities d0 with the participation of the IMF d0 which included a strategy to strengthen our banking system. An essential part of the strategy was to strengthen the powers of the FROB in order to enable the restructuring of the weakest part of our banking system. Specifically, with the approval of Law 9/2012 of November 14 d0 which validated RD d0 24/2012, of August 31 d0 the FROB obtained the necessary legal and operational framework to facilitate the restructuring and, where appropriate, the orderly resolution of credit institutions. This regulation is among the most advanced in terms of resolution, anticipating a large part of the measures that are included in the draft European Directive on Bank Recovery and Resolution, which is expected to be approved primarily. Specifically, the aforementioned rule provides the Fund with the commercial and administrative powers that allow, for the achievement of a higher objective, such as the defense of financial stability, the replacement of the General Meeting of Shareholders or the Board of Directors of an anima company. This facilitates the adoption and execution in a short period of time of agreements such as capital increases or reductions, statutory modifications, etc. Likewise, the FROB is granted the possibility of implementing actions for the management of hybrid equity and subordinated debt instruments, in order to minimize plastic support and make effective the principle of contribution of shareholders and creditors to the costs of restructuring or resolution. These powers have allowed the FROB to manage bank rescues, achieving a reasonable compromise between the adequate protection of bank customers and the minimization of the cost for taxpayers. The FROB should therefore be understood as a product of the economic crisis and an effective instrument to preserve financial stability with the lowest possible price. Their actions have been decisive in bringing to fruition the reform of the banking system initiated with the signing of the Memorandum of Understanding a year and a half ago. The timing of this Senate appearance could not be more timely. Just a few weeks ago the Eurogroup certified compliance with the commitments set out in the programme and confirmed its completion in January 2014 on the basis of assessments issued by the European Commission, the ECB and the IMF. Therefore, I consider that this is a good opportunity to review before Your Series the main milestones of the reform carried out and, in particular, those in which the FROB has been involved, seal the most relevant tasks at the present time and, finally, comment on the effects of the process undertaken on the current situation and the prospects of the Spanish financial system. 2. THE REFORM PROGRAMME STRATEGY The components of the reform strategy contained in the programme were essentially five. . Firstly, the identification of the specific own funds needs of each entity. . Secondly, the adoption of plans to cover the capital shortfall through actions by the institutions themselves and, where necessary, by public aid. . Thirdly, the clean-up of the balance sheets of all vulnerable institutions, through the transfer of assets linked to the real estate sector to an external asset management company. . Fourthly, the approval of restructuring or resolution plans for institutions with subsidies, in order to strengthen the efficiency of viable institutions and to promote the orderly disappearance as independent entities of non-viable banks. . Finally, the program included the adoption of a set of reforms and legal changes aimed at strengthening the banking system as a whole. The FROB has played an important role throughout the process, always acting in coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Competitiveness, the Ministry of Finance and Administrations and the Bank of Spain. If I may, I will briefly summarize the main actions at each stage of the strategy, with the exception of regulatory reform as unnecessary since this chamber has participated directly in it as part of the legislative branch of the State. 3. IDENTIFICATION OF CAPITAL NEEDS The first step of the strategy was to identify the capital needs of the Spanish banks. This was based on an exercise conducted by an external consultant and with the collaboration of the four main auditing firms and companies specialized in the valuation of real estate assets. The exercise was structured in two phases: firstly, a thorough review of the quality of the banking sector's assets and their accounting treatment and, secondly, a stress test or a disaggregated stress test, bank by bank. Although it was conducted with a high speed d0 barely three months d0 it was possible to meet the best standards of rigor. This reflects the broad scope of the exercise, which covered 90% of the system, the completeness of the information used, the severity of the macroeconomic scenarios considered, and the well-known governance structure with direct participation of the national and international authorities to which the contracted external consultants regularly reported. I believe that it is illustrative of the rigor of the analysis carried out that the European Central Bank has used it as a reference for the design of the valuation exercise of European banks, which must be carried out prior to the start of the activities of the Single Supervisory Mechanism in cousin a, in accordance with the recently approved Community Regulation. As Your Lords will recall, the results of the stress test were presented in September 2012. These results revealed that the capital needs of the system as a whole, in an adverse scenario, amounted to just under db57 billion, well below the maximum support provided for in the financial assistance programme. Likewise, almost 90% of these needs were concentrated in the four entities in which the FROB already had a majority stake. Thus, the exercise revealed that the Spanish financial sector d0 almost 80% of it d0 did not require additional capital or could obtain it without public assistance. I believe that this fact has not been emphasized enough: that is, the solvency position of most of the Spanish banking system, despite the deep crisis that our economy has gone through and the collapse of its real estate sector. This has meant a significant qualitative difference with respect to the generalized banking crises experienced in other jurisdictions, which has moderated the scope of the crisis and significantly facilitated the management of the reform process. 4. RECAPITALISATION Once the capital needs of each bank had been identified, the next step in the roadmap was to proceed with the process of recapitalizing the banks that needed it. As you know, the aid finally disbursed has been lower than the needs estimated in the stress test, as a result of the ability of institutions to generate capital by their own means, the effect of the segregation of assets to Sareb and, mainly, the assumption of losses by holders of hybrid instruments (preference shares and subordinated debt) to which I will refer later. In compliance with Law 9/2012 and according to the terms of the MoU, the recapitalization strategy was included in the plans presented to the Bank of Spain and the European Commission for approval. The resolution plans for the entities of the so-called Group 1 .majority owned by the FROB and composed of BFA/Bankia, Catalunya Banc, NCG.Banco and Banco de Valencia.were prepared by the FROB and approved by the Bank of Spain first and then the European Commission in November 2012. The plans of the entities of the so-called Group 2 d0 that is, banks not owned by the FROB that required state aid such as Banco Mare Nostrum, Grupo Banco Caja3, Ceiss and Liberbank d0 were approved during the month of December 2012. The aid finally disbursed amounted to a total of approximately 39,000 million euros, corresponding to 36,976 million euros to Group 1 and 1,865 million euros to Group 2. The choice of the instrument to channel financial support d0 ordinary shares or convertible instruments computable as principal capital d0 depended on the equity situation of each entity. Specifically, Group 1 entities received the funds through the subscription of newly issued ordinary shares. All of them had negative economic and accounting values and, consequently, high capital requirements. On the other hand, of the four entities of Group 2, three of them received financial support through the subscription of instruments convertible into shares (CoCos), while in the fourth (BMN) the FROB subscribed a capital increase. In all cases, the shareholders of the institutions contributed to the costs of restructuring by absorbing losses before the injection of plastic funds and bearing a very pronounced dilution effect. The scope of these actions was very broad, to the point that the savings banks that controlled the rescued banks of Group 1 lost all their participation in them. It should therefore be inferred that the plic funds contributed have not been used to rescue the former owners of the supported entities, but rather to protect depositors and other creditors of the institutions in order to preserve the stability of the financial system. However, at this point it is necessary to ask, what has been the total cost to the taxpayer of these actions of the authorities in relation to the stability of the banking system? Allow me to try to answer this question by taking advantage of the detailed information that the Bank of Spain has been publishing on the subject. Under the MoU, as I have detailed, the total amount of aid required by national banks was EUR 39 billion. Prior to the MoU and since May 2009, tenders were provided in various forms through the FROB, either under the program of the so-called FROB 1, established by RD-l 9/2009, of June 26, or by the so-called FROB 2, established by RD-l 2/2011, of February 18. In total, the aid implemented by these two programmes amounted to EUR 14 404 million. Finally, the aid provided by the Guarantee Fund for the Provision of Credit Institutions in the case of Unimm, CAM and CCM, amounted to 7,884 million euros. In total, the total contribution of public funds stands at approximately 61,366 million euros, committed in various forms of capital since May 2009. This figure does not take into account the volume of guarantees granted by the State to entities, nor the contingent support formalized through asset portfolio protection schemes (EPA) in some integration processes. The aid referred to is therefore at a premium of 6% of GDP. This is a very significant figure, but it does not stand out too much than that registered in other European countries affected by the financial crisis. In fact, public aid granted in Spain accounts for approximately 15% of the total of the European Union since 2008. In terms of GDP, aid in Spain is at levels comparable to those made in the United Kingdom, Belgium, Holland and Portugal, and substantially below the figures reached in countries such as Cyprus, Greece or Ireland. 5. SUBPARAGRAPH: ACTIONS FOR THE MANAGEMENT OF HYBRID INSTRUMENTS One of the most sensitive and complex components of the reform process has been the hybrid instrument management exercises whereby equity holders Preferred and subordinated debt have assumed a significant part of the costs of recapitalizing institutions. As established by the MoU, and in order to lighten the burden on the taxpayer, after assigning losses to shareholders, the application of measures was required to distribute the burden among holders of hybrid capital and subordinated debt, either through voluntary or mandatory exercises. In summary, the implemented shares involved a haircut on the nominal value of the securities, and their subsequent reinvestment in shares or other equity instruments. Holders of maturing subordinated debt had, in general, the option of choosing, as an alternative to shares, the reinvestment of their securities d0 subject to the appropriate haircut d0 in a senior debt product, with the same maturity as subordinated instruments, and with a 2% coupn payable at maturity. However, the treatment of the securities d0 both in terms of the haircut and the asset offered in exchange d0 varied depending on the instrument of origin, the interest rate of the issue and the maturity date, in accordance with the requirements established by the European Commission. In total, the years of assumption of losses by holders of preferred shares and subordinated debt have affected a total volume of 14,750 million euros, which has resulted in a significant reduction in the cost of bank recapitalization for the taxpayer. However, the Spanish case is of particular importance, insofar as a significant part of the holders of these instruments were retail investors. Specifically, 83% of the volume invested in hybrid instruments was in the hands of 611,500 retail investors at the time of the execution of the exercises. This singularity, together with the existence of bad marketing practices of these instruments d0 as has been evidenced in administrative and judicial proceedings d0 has significantly increased the social costs of hybrid management exercises and deteriorated the value of the franchise of the affected entities. The strategy of the Spanish authorities has therefore been, on the one hand, to exploit all the margin allowed by Community and national legislation in order to alleviate the burden on retail customers and, on the other, to facilitate the restitution of the damage in the case of those investors who have been harmed by poor marketing. This strategy has essentially taken the form of three actions: (i) reducing as far as possible the haircuts to be applied; (ii) the establishment of a liquidity mechanism for investors in securities of unlisted entities; The execution of the hybrid management exercises has meant an average cut of 26% on all the issues of preferred shares and subordinated debt of the entities that have received full support. Although these are significant losses in value, these are lower than the cuts applied in other countries, such as Ireland, where cuts to subordinated debt were more than 70%, or the Netherlands. Moreover, it is foreseeable that once the future Bank Recovery and Resolution Directive enters into force, the balances issued of hybrid instruments should, as a general rule, be fully used to recapitalise vulnerable institutions before any injection of funds outside the institution. In order for the European Commission d0 in compliance with its State aid criteria d0 to accept more moderate cuts than initially planned, the value recoverable by investors was materialised in ordinary shares eligible as premium capital. In the case of Bankia, for example, shares were received at a subscription price of 1.35 euros, which have been quoted in the period of time elapsed after their admission to trading at a maximum of 1.18 euros per share, that is, at 87.4% of the acquisition price. Naturally, the exchange rate implemented was particularly burdensome for investors in entities such as NCG Banco (NCG) and Catalunya Banc (CX), whose shares are not listed on liquid markets. To alleviate this cost, a liquidity mechanism was established through the Depitos Guarantee Fund. Thus, RD-l 6/2013, of March 22, granted the Depitos Guarantee Fund (FGD) the ability to acquire, at market prices, the unlisted shares resulting from the mandatory exchanges of hybrid equity and subordinated debt instruments. Pursuant to this rule, the Management Committee of the FGD, at its meetings of 4 and 7 June 2013, agreed to make a voluntary offer for the acquisition of the shares of NCG and CX, subscribed within the framework of the shares of management of hybrid instruments or subordinated debt, addressed exclusively to holders who had the status of retail clients. The deadline for the acceptance of the aforementioned offer ended on July 12 and resulted in a great acceptance. The offer for the acquisition of NCG Banco and CX securities was accepted by holders representing 88.3% of the shares to which the offer was addressed in the first case and 97.1% in the second. The total cost of the operation amounted to just over 1,800 million euros, which will be borne by the industry through its contributions to the Depitos Guarantee Fund. It will be the latter that assumes in the same term the risk related to a possible depreciation of the shares acquired until the moment of their disposal. Finally, to deal with cases in which there had been a deficient commercialization of hybrid instruments, voluntary arbitration mechanisms have been established in the entities owned by the FROB that in the past had placed these instruments among their retail clientele. These arbitrations have been executed in accordance with the criteria published on April 17, 2013 by the Monitoring Committee of hybrid equity and subordinated debt instruments, created by RD-l 6/2013, of March 22. To date, 427,802 investors have attended the arbitration processes opened at NCG Banco, Catalunya Banc and BFA-Bankia, representing 80% of the holders entitled to arbitration, or 70% of the global amount. In total, there are already 144,189 investors who have received a positive award in arbitration, equivalent to 34% of the holders who have requested it. It should be borne in mind that although the process is already completed in NCG, where 62% of the investors who requested arbitration have recovered 100% of the investment as a result of the positive award, the an process is underway in CX and Bankia, which is the one that began later, although it has already reached a percentage of favorable awards on the total of applications of 30%. Taking into account the NCG reference, it is expected that, when the ongoing processes are completed, more than half of retail investors will be able to recover their initial investment thanks to the favorable award on possible marketing defects, obtained in the arbitrations conducted by the entities controlled by the FROB. For the rest of the retail investors, taking into account the aforementioned cuts, and the liquidity measures implemented, we can estimate that a large majority have recovered or been able to recover d0 in the form of cash or liquid shares d0 more than 50% of the investment, and that only a fairly small percentage will recover an amount less than 25%. Clearly, these data provide little relief for investors who consider themselves most harmed. They do seem, however, illustrative of the fact that, at the very least, the measures taken have been able to alleviate a far-reaching economic and social problem. 6. SANITATION: SAREB Let me now briefly refer to the Bank Restructuring Asset Management Company (SAREB), an essential element in the reform of the banking sector, since it has contributed to one of its fundamental objectives: the clean-up of the balance sheets of the most vulnerable credit institutions. Sareb was established on 28 November 2012 with a global objective consisting of the management and divestment within a period of fifteen years of the assets received, seeking to obtain the maximum value for them. 45% of Sareb's capital is owned by FROB, the rest being in the hands of private entities: fourteen national banks, two foreign banks, four insurers and one electricity company. Its equity amounted to db4,800 million (8% of total assets), of which db1,200 million correspond to capital and db3,600 million to two issues of contingently convertible subordinated unsecured debt subscribed by shareholders. Its effective activity began on December 31, 2012, the date on which the assets of the entities classified in Group 1 (BFA-Bankia, Catalunya Banc, NCG Banco and Banco de Valencia) were transferred. On February 28, 2013, the company's balance sheet was completed with the transfer of the assets corresponding to Group 2 entities (Liberbank, BMN, CEISS, Caja3). In total, the volume transferred was 50,781 million euros in real estate and loans for real estate development. After a complex foundational stage, the company is now fully operational. In fact, Sareb's commercial activity has been advancing rapidly in the disposal of real estate and financial assets through the three planned channels: sale of wholesale portfolios, sale of singular assets and retail sale through transferor entities. The cash flow figure in the first half amounted to db842 million, of which db674 million came from financial assets and db168 million from real estate assets. By mid-November, the company had sold 6,500 real estate assets. In its first year, Sareb is expected to achieve gross revenues of more than db2 billion. 7. RESTRUCTURING AND RESOLUTION Finally, allow me to say a few words about the process of restructuring and resolution, which is a component of reform that I wanted to tell you. In order to optimise the effectiveness of the support provided, it is necessary to demand in parallel the reduction of the sector's capacity, through processes of thinning the most vulnerable entities and through the promotion of integration processes that improve the organization of the banking industry. In fact, the restructuring or resolution plans of the entities that have received aid include an average reduction in the number of offices of 35%, a reduction in staff of the order of 30% and an average balance sheet counter-estimate of close to 35%. The degree of progress achieved so far puts the reductions at 16% of branches, 17% of staff and 12% of assets. The process takes on different degrees of intensity depending on the volume of aid received by the entity and its qualification as an entity in restructuring or resolution. The term "resolution" is reserved for those processes in which the credit institution is not viable and, therefore, the full return of the aid received is not foreseen. Resolution plans provide for the exit from the market as an independent entity (for example, through takeover by another entity) within a limited period of five years, through fmulas that preserve customer protection and financial stability. The term "restructuring" applies, strictly speaking, to entities that require public financial support to ensure their viability, but which have the capacity to repay such financial support within the time frames foreseen for each support instrument. The restructuring of a credit institution may also be considered if its resolution would foreseeably have seriously detrimental effects on the stability of the financial system. Based on the above criteria, Catalunya Banc, Banco de Valencia, CEISS and NCG Banco and Banco Gallego, a subsidiary of the previous one, were considered entities in resolution. For their part, BFA/Bankia, BMN, Liberbank and Caja 3 were classified as entities undergoing restructuring. The strategy followed so far by the FROB on the entities receiving bids, and which I will comment on below, can be summarized in the sale of two nationalized banks, the promotion of two corporate operations and the promotion of the stock market listing of another entity. In addition, four entities remain under the control of the FROB, two of which are expected to be sold primarily, provided that acceptable offers are received. Thus, with regard to the banks in resolution, the FROB ordered the sale of the shares of Banco de Valencia and Banco Gallego, which were sold to Caixabank and Banco de Sabadell, respectively. As for NCG Banco (62.75% owned by the FROB), the formal auction process of the entity has recently begun, which will be developed, in principle, in two phases and which we expect to conclude around the end of the year. In the case of Catalunya Banc (with a 66% stake in the FROB), its sale process is in the analysis phase. Once the potential buyers have been identified, they will be provided with the necessary information so that they communicate a possible price range at which they would be willing to acquire the entity. This price will be used as the main decision criterion on the launch of the second phase of the process, consisting of the formal sale of the entity. The third entity under resolution, Banco CEISS, which is part of one of the two corporate transactions mentioned above, has been the subject of an acquisition offer by Unicaja. The offer is aimed at the former holders of hybrid instruments of Banco CEISS who, after the hybrid management exercise carried out by the FROB, are holders of shares and convertible securities of the bank. Once the prospectus of the offer has been approved by the CNMV on November 26, these investors have a period of thirty calendar days to accept it. The acceptance of the offer entails the waiver of any type of judicial action against Unicaja Banco or Banco CEISS. For this reason, the FROB has offered retail holders of hybrid instruments of Banco CEISS who accept Unicaja's offer the possibility of submitting to a mechanism to review the marketing processes by which they acquired, at the time, preferred shares and subordinated debt. This review will follow criteria equivalent to those used in the arbitrations carried out in NCG, CX and Bankia. Therefore, this mechanism avoids the prejudice that would be detrimental to CEISS retail investors if they accept the offer d0 in relation to the treatment of investors in other entities in resolution d0 while promoting the success of a transaction that is prudential and allows the saving of an appreciable volume of public funds. With regard to the entities under restructuring, in two of them, Bankia and BMN, the FROB is the majority shareholder, since the public aid was implemented through capital injections. In both cases, the divestment of the FROB is not foreseen in the short term, since the two entities are following the marked roadmap, with effective management systems that should translate into an increase in their economic value. In fact, in the case of Bankia (68.4% owned by the FROB through the Banco Financiero y de Ahorros), the accin is currently trading at 0.93 euros, 63% above the 0.57 euros at which it closed on May 28, the first day on which the new shares were put on the market, as a result of the agreement of the Governing Committee that executed the management and hybrid exercise and recapitalized the entity. As for BMN (in which the FROB owns 65% of the capital), it has already completed the main milestones of the restructuring plan, largely thanks to the sale of the network of the former Caixa Pened8es to Banco de Sabadell. The plan envisages the IPO before the end of 2017. The other two entities in restructuring, Liberbank d0 which went public last May d0 and Caja 3 d0 about to complete its integration process with Ibercaja d0 received aid through the subscription, by the FROB, of contingently convertible bonds, which are expected to be returned within the deadlines established in their respective restructuring plans. In summary, it can be said that the plans designed for each of the entities that have received full support are being satisfactorily fulfilled, while a reordering of the Spanish banking system is being promoted, with fewer but more solvent and better managed entities. 8. RESULTS AND CHALLENGES For all these reasons, I believe that the effort made in developing the programme for the reform of the Spanish banking system has significantly strengthened the sector, which is timely, given the important challenges it will have to face in the future cousin. In the last part of my speech I will refer to the current situation of the banking sector and its prospects. In the recent past, there has been a significant improvement in the main indicators. These include rising profitability in the sector as a whole, despite sluggish activity, low interest rate levels and the persistence of a significant degree of fragmentation in euro area financial markets. After the losses associated with the extraordinary provision effort made in 2012, the results have returned to positive territory in 2013 and it is foreseeable that, for the year as a whole, earnings before provisions will be above the levels contemplated in the stress test scenarios carried out last year. On the other hand, there has been very significant progress in the clean-up of banks' balance sheets and, in particular, in reducing their exposure to risks arising from the real estate sector. This has been possible thanks to stricter provisioning requirements, as well as the segregation of assets transferred to Sareb by entities that required grants. In fact, the net exposure of provisions to real estate risks has gone from 240,000 million euros at the end of 2011 to just over 100,000 million today. In addition, there has been a significant improvement in the sector's capital ratios, especially for entities in so-called groups 1 and 2, whose solvency has been strengthened not only by the financial assistance provided to them but also by the management exercises of hybrid equity and subordinated debt instruments. Consequently, to date, all institutions have core capital ratios above 9%. In fact, it is expected that for the sector as a whole this ratio will be above 10% by the end of a. These developments have contributed to improving the perception about the soundness of the banking sector in our country, as shown by the increase in the prices of the main entities since the middle of last year. The ratio of the market price to the book value of listed banks is higher than the European average for a set of institutions of comparable size, reflecting improved confidence in the profitability prospects of the banks and the quality of assets they hold on their balance sheets. However, the progress I have just mentioned to you must be taken in due order, because, as I was saying, the Spanish banking system still faces challenges of great importance. These include, first of all, the weakness of the economic situation. The Spanish economy has just overcome its second recession in less than five years and the most recent data point to a prolongation of this trend towards improvement. However, the intensity of the recovery is very moderate and can be expected to remain so in the short term, in a context in which private spending will continue to be weighed down by high levels of indebtedness, as well as by the evolution of disposable income and household wealth. More in the medium term, the ongoing process of correcting the main imbalances in the Spanish economy supports the expectation of a sustained recovery, the intensity of which will depend, among other factors, on the extent to which the reform momentum is maintained. Another of the main challenges for the Spanish economy is the continued contraction of credit. The available evidence suggests that this evolution is largely explained by demand factors, such as the process of deleveraging households and firms, although there are also certain supply-side constraints, such as those linked to the fragmentation of financial markets in Europe, which may be making it difficult for some creditworthy borrowers to access credit. especially small and medium-sized enterprises. However, recent data reflect a change in the patterns observed since the beginning of the crisis, which is most evident in the case of companies, for which the rate of loan contraction has tended to decline since the summer. On the other hand, the volume of doubtful assets of credit to the private sector has continued to increase and the NPL ratio, which has increased across the board for all branches of activity, stands at around 13% for the sector as a whole. Given the usual lag between the economic cycle and the evolution of non-performing assets, the NPL ratio is expected to continue to rise in the first few months. Finally, the challenge to which I would like to refer concerns changes in the regulation and supervision of the banking sector. The new Basel III capital framework, incorporated into European legislation through the Capital Requirements Directive and Regulation, will introduce, from January 2014, new requirements for institutions that will be progressively tightened in the first cousins. The new rules pose a major challenge, as they include a significant increase in the amount of capital that will be required of institutions and an improvement in their quality, that is, their ability to absorb losses. In any case, it should be noted that Spanish institutions generally have sufficient scope to meet the new requirements. In fact, ordinary capital levels as defined in Basel III could be at 10% by January 2014, clearly above the required minimums. In addition, the Spanish banking system will have to face the challenges posed by the process of moving towards the Banking Union in Europe. In particular, the creation of the supervisory mechanism will require institutions to adapt to new rules, criteria and procedures for interaction with supervisors. As a preliminary step, the Spanish institutions that become directly supervised by the new ICO mechanism d0 more than 90% of our banking system d0 will have to be subjected, like the rest of the significant European banks, to a thorough analysis that will include the review of the quality of assets and a new stress test. Although the details of the exercise, especially with regard to the stress test, have not yet been fully defined, the Bank of Spain has recently developed a tool that allows prospective solvency analyses to be carried out in different scenarios. The first results, recently published in the Financial Stability Report of the Bank of Spain, show that the set of entities analysed presents a fairly comfortable solvency position, given that their capacity to absorb losses would exceed the expected losses even in quite adverse scenarios. These results indicate that the Spanish banking system is d0 after the reform carried out and the actions undertaken by the institutions themselves d0 well positioned to face the challenges associated with the implementation of the new European supervisory framework. This, obviously, does not alleviate at all the intensity with which financial institutions must be used to maintain rigor in the accounting reflection of the evolution of the quality of assets, in the implementation of improvements in their efficiency and, above all, in the preservation of capital. Thanks a lot.

INTRODUCCIN Como saben, el FROB naci en 2009 mediante el Real Decretoley 9/2009, de 26 de junio, con objeto de facilitar la gestin de los problemas de solvencia y liquidez de algunas entidades financieras espalas que emergieron a raz de la crisis financiera internacional, iniciada en 2007, y del comienzo de la fase recesiva de nuestra economa. La confluencia de estos factores gener una retroalimentacin desestabilizadora entre la percepcin de riesgo soberano y de riesgo bancario, al introducir incertidumbre sobre la capacidad de la hacienda plica espala para garantizar la estabilidad del sector bancario. Como reflejo de esta situaci, hacia mediados de 2012, como recuerdan, el tipo de inters de la deuda plica espala a largo plazo lleg a situarse a 630 puntos bsicos por encima de la referencia alemana. Ese es el contexto en el que se inscribe el origen del programa de asistencia financiera externa aprobado por el Eurogrupo el 20 de julio de 2012, que inclua la disponibilidad de fondos europeos por un importe mximo de 100.000 millones de euros y un Memorando de Entendimiento (MoU) acordado por las autoridades espalas y europeas con la participacin del FMIdonde se recoga una estrategia de fortalecimiento de nuestro sistema bancario. Una parte esencial de la estrategia consisti en reforzar los poderes del FROB con objeto de posibilitar la restructuracin de la parte ms dbil de nuestro sistema bancario. En concreto, con la aprobacin de la Ley 9/2012 de 14 de noviembre que convalidaba el RDl 24/2012, de 31 de agostoel FROB obtuvo el marco legal y operativo necesario para facilitar la reestructuracin y, en su caso, la resolucin ordenada de las entidades de crdito. Esta normativa se sita entre las ms avanzadas en materia de resoluci, anticipando gran parte de las medidas que estn recogidas en el proyecto de Directiva europea de Recuperacin y Resolucin Bancaria, que se prev sea aprobada primamente. En concreto, la mencionada norma dota al Fondo de las facultades mercantiles y administrativas que permiten, para la consecucin de un objetivo superior, como es la defensa de la estabilidad financiera, la sustitucin de la Junta General de Accionistas o del Consejo de Administracin de una sociedad anima. Ello facilita la adopcin y ejecucin en breve plazo de tiempo de acuerdos como aumentos o reducciones de capital, modificaciones estatutarias, etc. Asimismo, se otorga al FROB la posibilidad de implementar acciones de gestin de instrumentos hbridos de capital y de deuda subordinada, con el objeto de minimizar los apoyos plicos y hacer eficaz el principio de contribucin de los accionistas y acreedores a los costes de la reestructuracin o resoluci. Estas facultades han permitido al FROB gestionar los rescates bancarios, logrando un compromiso razonable entre la proteccin adecuada de los clientes bancarios y la minimizacin del coste para los contribuyentes. El FROB debe entenderse, por tanto, como un producto de la crisis econica y un instrumento eficaz para preservar la estabilidad financiera con el menor coste plico posible. Sus actuaciones han resultado determinantes para llevar a buen puerto la reforma del sistema bancario iniciada con la firma del Memorando de Entendimiento hace ahora ao y medio. El momento en el que se produce esta comparecencia en el Senado no podra ser ms oportuno. Hace apenas unas semanas el Eurogrupo certific el cumplimiento de los compromisos recogidos en el programa y confirm su finalizacin en enero de 2014 basndose en las valoraciones emitidas por la Comisin Europea, el BCE y el FMI. Por lo tanto, considero que esta es una buena oportunidad para revisar ante Sus Seras los principales hitos de la reforma efectuada y, en particular, aquellos en los que el FROB ha estado involucrado, selar las tareas ms relevantes en el momento presente y, finalmente, comentar los efectos del proceso acometido sobre la situacin actual y las perspectivas del sistema financiero espal. 2. Entre ellos, cabe destacar el aumento de la rentabilidad del conjunto del sector, a pesar de la atona de la actividad, de los reducidos niveles de tipos de inters y de la persistencia de un apreciable grado de fragmentacin en los mercados financieros de la zona del euro. Tras las prdidas asociadas al esfuerzo extraordinario de provisiones realizado en 2012, los resultados han regresado en 2013 al terreno positivo y es previsible que, en el conjunto del ao, los beneficios antes de provisiones se sitn por encima de los niveles que se contemplaban en los escenarios de las pruebas de resistencia que se realizaron el ao pasado. Por otra parte, se ha producido un avance muy significativo en el saneamiento de los balances de las entidades y, en particular, en la reduccin de su exposicin a los riesgos derivados del sector inmobiliario. Ello ha sido posible gracias a unos requerimientos de provisiones ms estrictos, as como a la segregacin de los activos transferidos a la Sareb por parte de las entidades que requirieron ayudas plicas. De hecho, la exposicin neta de provisiones a los riesgos inmobiliarios ha pasado de 240.000 millones de euros a finales de 2011 a poco ms de 100.000 millones en la actualidad. Adems, se ha producido una mejora significativa de las ratios de capital del sector, especialmente para las entidades de los denominados grupos 1 y 2, cuya solvencia se ha visto reforzada no solo por la asistencia financiera que se les prest sino tambin por los ejercicios de gestin de instrumentos hbridos de capital y deuda subordinada. En consecuencia, a da de hoy, todas las entidades tienen ratios de capital principal superiores al 9%. De hecho, cabe esperar que para el conjunto del sector dicha ratio se site por encima del 10% a finales de a. Estos desarrollos han contribuido a mejorar la percepcin acerca de la solidez del sector bancario de nuestro pas, como muestra el aumento de las cotizaciones de las principales entidades desde mediados del pasado a. La ratio entre el precio de mercado y el valor contable de los bancos espales cotizados es superior a la media europea para un conjunto de entidades de tamao comparable, lo que refleja una mejora de la confianza en las perspectivas de rentabilidad de los bancos espales y en la calidad de activos que mantienen en sus balances. No obstante, los avances que acabo de comentarles deben tomarse en su justo trmino, porque, como les deca, el sistema bancario espal sigue teniendo por delante retos de gran importancia. Entre ellos cabe destacar en primer lugar la debilidad de la situacin econica. La economa espala acaba de superar su segunda recesin en menos de un lustro y los datos ms recientes apuntan a una prolongacin de esta tendencia a la mejora. Sin embargo, la intensidad de la recuperacin es an muy moderada y cabe esperar que contine sindolo en el corto plazo, en un contexto en el que el gasto privado se seguir viendo lastrado por los elevados niveles de endeudamiento, as como por la evolucin de la renta disponible y de la riqueza de los hogares. Ms a medio plazo, el proceso en marcha de correccin de los principales desequilibrios de la economa espala apoya la expectativa de una recuperacin sostenida, cuya intensidad depender, entre otros factores, de la medida en que se mantenga el impulso reformador. Otro de principales retos para la economa espala es la continuada contraccin del crdito. La evidencia disponible parece indicar que esta evolucin se explica en su mayor parte por factores de demanda, como el proceso de desapalancamiento de familias y empresas, si bien tambin se observan ciertas restricciones por el lado de oferta, como las vinculadas a la fragmentacin de los mercados financieros en Europa, que pueden estar dificultando el acceso al crdito de algunos prestatarios solventes, especialmente peques y medianas empresas. Con todo, los datos recientes reflejan un cambio en las pautas observadas desde el inicio de la crisis, que es ms evidente en el caso de las empresas, para las que la tasa de contraccin de los prstamos ha tendido a reducirse desde el verano. Por otra parte, el volumen de activos dudosos del crdito al sector privado se ha continuado incrementando y la ratio de morosidad, que ha aumentado de forma generalizada para todas las ramas de actividad, se sita cerca del 13% para el conjunto del sector. Teniendo en cuenta el habitual desfase entre el ciclo econmico y la evolucin de los activos dudosos, cabe esperar que la tasa de morosidad contine todava aumentando en los primos meses. Finalmente, el timo reto al que me gustara referirme se refiere a los cambios en la regulacin y supervisin del sector bancario. El nuevo marco de capital Basilea III, incorporado a la normativa europea mediante la Directiva y el Reglamento sobre Requerimientos de Capital, introducir, a partir de enero de 2014, nuevos requisitos para las entidades que se irn endureciendo de forma progresiva en los primos as. Las nuevas normas suponen un desafo importante, en la medida que recogen un aumento significativo de la cantidad de capital que se exigir a las entidades y una mejora de su calidad, esto es, de su capacidad para absorber prdidas. En todo caso, debe destacarse que las entidades espalas disponen, en general, de un margen suficiente para hacer frente a los nuevos requisitos. De hecho, los niveles de capital ordinario segn la definicin de Basilea III podran situarse en enero de 2014 en niveles primos al 10%, claramente por encima de los mnimos exigidos. Adems, el sistema bancario espal deber hacer frente a los desafos que supone el proceso de avance hacia la Unin Bancaria en Europa. En particular, la creacin del mecanismo ico de supervisin exigir a las entidades adaptarse a nuevas reglas, criterios y procedimientos de interaccin con los supervisores. Como paso previo, las entidades espalas que pasen a ser supervisadas directamente por el nuevo mecanismo ico ms del 90% de nuestro sistema bancariodeber ser sometido, como el resto de los bancos europeos significativos, a un anlisis exhaustivo que incluir la revisin de la calidad de los activos y una nueva prueba de esfuerzo. Aunque los detalles del ejercicio, en especial en lo que se refiere a la prueba de esfuerzo no han sido todava plenamente definidos, el Banco de Espaa ha desarrollado recientemente una herramienta que permite realizar anlisis prospectivos de la solvencia en diferentes escenarios. Los primeros resultados, publicados recientemente en el Informe de Estabilidad Financiera del Banco de Espa, muestran que el conjunto de entidades analizado presenta una posicin de solvencia bastante confortable, dado que su capacidad de absorcin de prdidas superara las prdidas esperadas incluso en escenarios bastante adversos. Estos resultados indican que el sistema bancario espal se encuentra tras la reforma realizada y las acciones acometidas por las propias entidadesbien posicionado para afrontar los retos asociados a la puesta en funcionamiento del nuevo marco supervisor europeo. Ello, evidentemente, no alivia en absoluto la intensidad con la que las entidades financieras deben emplearse en el mantenimiento del rigor en el reflejo contable de la evolucin de la calidad de los activos, en la implementacin de mejoras en su eficiencia y, sobre todo, en la preservacin del capital. Muchas gracias.

Title: Lunch in honor of Enrique Iglesias, Ibero-American Secretary General
text: 30.01.2014 Luncheon in honor of Enrique Iglesias, Ibero-American Secretary General Bank of Spain Luis M. Linde Governor Dear Enrique, dear friends, In September 2005, on the occasion of the events organized at the Inter-American Bank in Washington to bid farewell to Enrique, there was a meeting of the Board of Executive Directors at which the Directors glossed his great contribution to Ibero-American politics and economics. I said then that the political and public personality of Enrique Iglesias could be drawn with four ideas. You will allow me to summarize them now. The first, a personal note that involves almost everything Enrique has done. Enrique Iglesias does not know how to be rhetorical. My impression is that, simply, he does not know how to express himself in what in French is called "langue de bois", a wooden tongue, which serves to express what is not felt, what is not thought, just because it is what the majority thinks, what is politically correct, which allows us to muddle through by provoking little resistance. And this is difficult to find in someone with so much political visibility and so many years of being and acting under all possible spotlights. Enrique Iglesias has an outstanding ability to expose and link ideas with a lot of content and intelligent simplicity and those who know him well affirm that it is not easy to hear him say what he does not think. And this, I believe, is the secret of his effectiveness as a communicator: his own conviction, simply and sincerely expressed. The second point concerns the economy. Over the years at the IDB and SEGIB, the dominant economic and political ideas have not always been the same. But Enrique has always remained in a position that I would call, I don't know if he likes the expression, of "centrist realism". He led the IDB in the years of the disappearance of the so-called "real socialism" and the rebirth of the market as a mechanism for allocating resources, with what this has meant, in a political and economic sense, throughout the world. But it has been able to assume these changes without dogmas, extreme positions, or imitations, always in a balanced and critical way. This critical vision, always somewhat distanced from the dominant economic paradigm, is another lesson that Enrique Iglesias has been leaving wherever he has worked. The third idea is political. The turn of the 90s towards the market model has not occurred in a political vacuum: what we could call the democratic demand has taken a lot of force, which can be specified in two priorities, always present in the work of Enrique Iglesias: the strengthening of the rule of law and that of public and private institutions that are essential for sustained economic development. He himself has summed it up in the motto: more market and better government, with which many of us can feel identified. The fourth idea refers to the history of the Ibero-American continent, which is also the history of Spain. I would dare to say that the most profound inspiration of Enrique Iglesias' actions, the feeling that has ultimately sustained his long and dedicated effort at the head of the IDB and SEGIB, has been the ideal of continental unity, through the great avenues of development, economic integration and political cooperation. On one occasion, I heard him refer to the process of fragmentation, at the beginning of the nineteenth century, of what we now call Ibero-America or Latin America. Latin America, calling it a great historical drama. For him, unity is there, you just have to know how to see it. I would say that this vision, oriented to unite wills, militant against division and sterile confrontations, is, truly, that of a Spaniard "from both hemispheres", as the C87diz Constitution said. I'm done: I said at that event in September 2005 that Enrique Iglesias was not retiring, because that was an ontological impossibility. Well, today, the same. I have been told that you plan to live between Madrid and Montevideo, that you will continue to have an office in Madrid, and we do not doubt that you will continue working for what you have dedicated your political and professional life to: the Ibero-American Community of Nations.
