Title: Appearance in the Commission of Economy and Competitiveness of the Congress of Deputies
text: APPEARANCE OF THE PRESIDENT OF THE GOVERNING COMMISSION OF THE FROB IN THE COMMISSION OF ECONOMY AND COMPETITIVENESS OF THE CONGRESS OF DEPUTIES June 24, 2014 Mr President, ladies and gentlemen. In compliance with the control mandate contained in article 56 of Law 9/2012 on the restructuring and resolution of credit institutions, of November 14, I appear before this Economy and Competitiveness Committee as President of the Governing Committee of the Fund for Orderly Bank Restructuring (FROB). The purpose of this appearance is to report on the activities carried out by the FROB since February 5, the date on which I last appeared before this Commission. I would like to mention, first of all, that in March and April a team composed of experts from the European Commission, in coordination with staff from the European Central Bank (ECB), made the first visit to Spain in the context of the mandatory reviews following the end of the financial assistance programmes. The visit allowed the experts to verify the important progress made in the restructuring of the Spanish banking sector, recognizing the effort made and, in turn, adequately identifying the challenges that still remain, many of them shared by the European banking system as a whole. Not surprisingly, ladies and gentlemen, as you know, the ECB is carrying out, in collaboration with national supervisors and prior to the assumption of supervisory tasks in November 2014, a comprehensive assessment of the European banking system that will affect all Spanish banks that have received public aid. On the other hand, as you know, it has been agreed to make a voluntary early repayment of the loan to the European Stability Mechanism (ESM) for an amount of EUR 1 304 million, which will be made shortly. This amount, as well as the costs associated with the amortization, will be assumed by the Public Treasury and the FROB, in proportion to the part that corresponds to them of the loan whose nominal is going to be reduced. Therefore, the FROB must contribute to the amortization for 30.62% of the amount, equivalent to 399.27 million euros, the remaining part corresponding to the Public Treasury. In my speech, I hope to convey to you that the activity of the FROB maintains the intensity required to adequately meet its objectives. The phase in which we find ourselves has not required new restructuring and resolution measures but, above all, actions derived from the execution of the current plans and, particularly, from the disposal of state shares in entities that required public support. In the first part of my speech I will detail the measures taken in relation to divestment processes and the promotion of corporate operations. I will refer, first, to the entities declared as not viable alone, whose resolution plans imposed the sale of the entity within a pre-established period, that is, NCG Banco and Catalunya Banc. I will also comment on the partial divestment of the FROB's stake in Bankia, indirectly, through Banco Financiero y de Ahorro (BFA), carried out recently. Given its relevance and impact, I would like to give you a relatively detailed explanation of this process. Finally, I will inform you of the terms in which the corporate operation of Banco CEISS and Unicaja Banco has finally been carried out. In the second part of my speech I will analyse other actions of the FROB, within the framework of the functions that it has legally established, such as the monitoring of plans and arbitration processes, judicial proceedings, initiatives undertaken for the identification of irregular actions by former managers of entities that required public aid and the evolution of Sareb. Likewise, I will offer some brushstrokes on the patrimonial situation of the FROB and I will review the public funds used in the actions carried out since its creation. Finally, ladies and gentlemen, I will devote the last part of my appearance to informing you about recent European regulatory developments in bank resolution. Next, I will now present the divestment processes of the FROB's participation in credit institutions. 1. SALE PROCESSES OF CREDIT INSTITUTIONS IN RESOLUTION a. NCG BANCO I start with NCG Bank. As you will recall, within the framework of the contract for the analysis of the management strategies of the entities owned by the FROB, which included NCG Banco, the accelerated divestment of the entity was proposed as the most respectful alternative for the purposes of the restructuring, since it was the one that ensured the least loss to public assets. Consequently, a competitive divestment process was initiated that culminated in the award, on December 18, 2013, to Banco Etcheverr92a-Grupo Banesco of 88.33% of the shares of NCG Banco, as its offer was the most competitive in accordance with the established valuation criteria. The effectiveness of the contract of sale was conditional on compliance with the legally established requirements and obtaining the required authorisations by the national and Community authorities. Indeed, in recent months the technical teams of the Directorate-General for Competition of the European Commission, the FROB, the Bank of Spain and the Banesco Group have been working intensively to adapt the current resolution plan to the new circumstance of the integration of the entity into the Banesco Group. The modification of the plan has been approved by the Executive Committee of the Bank of Spain, at the proposal of the FROB, on June 18 and by the European Commission two days later. In this way, once the purchase contract is made public in the coming days, the resolution process of NCG Banco can be concluded, having fulfilled the objectives established and the commitments acquired within the framework of the financial assistance program. b. CATALONIA BANK (CX) Turning to Catalunya Banc, as I told you in my previous speech, the Governing Committee of the FROB, taking into account the result of the report prepared by the consulting firm McKinsey within the framework of the analysis of the management strategies of the entities in which the FROB has a stake, and after a bidding process, agreed to award the contract for the analysis and eventual sale of Catalunya Banc to N1 Corporate Finance, S.A. The contract established that the process should be structured in two phases: a first analysis of the economic and financial situation of the entity and market contrast, and a second stage, more limited in time, in which the sale process would be executed, where appropriate. In the development of the first phase, the consulting firm Ernst & Young has been responsible for the preparation of financial, labor, tax and legal due diligence, while N 1 has informally contacted different investors to press the appetite of the market, trying to guarantee the greatest possible concurrence. The main recommendation that emerges from the N1 report is to proceed, first, to proceed with the sale of a loan portfolio with modest commercial value. This sale would improve the quality of Catalunya Banc's assets and, predictably, increase competition in the entity's sale process. Consequently, Catalunya Banc has initiated a process of segregation of a loan portfolio of approximately 6,500 million euros, composed mostly of mortgage loans to individuals. On May 27, Catalunya Banc received the first expressions of interest from more than a dozen candidates, who presented their non-binding offers on the portfolio for sale. The bank, with the advice of the investment bank, has carried out the analysis of the offers, and has selected five candidates who have moved on to the next phase and who, in accordance with the rules of the process, will submit their binding offers at the beginning of July. Likewise, it is expected that during the month of July the FROB will proceed with the sale of the entity. In fact, its Governing Committee has already agreed to start the divestment process in the Catalan entity, which will be developed through a competitive, transparent and objective procedure, in order to ensure the most efficient use of public resources. Interested entities must submit their binding offers by 14 July. Additionally, as part of the divestment strategy for non-strategic activities contained in the resolution plan, Catalunya Banc has sold to Aigon Capital, after a competitive process, a portfolio of non-performing loans for an approximate amount of db1,500 million, which were fully provisioned. It has also sold the real estate asset management platform, CatalunyaCaixa Inmobiliaria (CXI), to the Blackstone fund. In addition, the entity initiated a competitive process in order to sell the offices located outside Catalonia. After having received two binding offers, and not being the same satisfactory, the entity has determined the closure of the process. Therefore, these 43 offices will remain in the scope of sale of the entity. 2. DIVESTMENT PROCESS IN BANKIA Allow me to turn now to the divestment process in Bankia. As honourable Members will recall, since I had the opportunity to refer to it in my last appearance in this Committee, the FROB decided a few months ago to carry out an analysis on the most appropriate strategy to optimize the return of the taxpayer in the process of alienation of the shares owned by BFA d0 100% owned by the FROB d0 in Bankia. For this purpose, the investment bank Goldman Sachs was hired as strategic advisor in this operation. In addition, following a competitive process, BFA engaged Rotshchild as tactical advisor in the process of determining the design, structure, schedule and documentary requirements of the transaction. In light of the reports received, on February 19, 2014, the Governing Committee of the FROB approved the divestment framework in Bankia S.A. shares through BFA following the recommendations of the strategic advisor of the FROB and the tactical advisor of BFA. These reports highlighted the good market conditions and the appreciable gain in value of Bankia's shares, particularly since the presentation of the results for 2013 on February 3 of this year. Thus, Bankia traded at that time significantly above the value of the subscription made by BFA (db 1.35) and at prices that represented around 1.5 times its book value, well above the average of the sector in Spain and Europe. In addition, the reports showed the gain in depth of the stock market supported by its re-entry into the IBEX 35 at the end of 2013. In operational terms, the recommendations of both advisors pointed to a multi-stage market process and accelerated placement among institutional investors as the best alternative for the first divestment operation, which should affect a volume of shares compatible with the absorption capacity of the market. In accordance with the recommendations of the advisors and the framework approved by the Governing Committee of the FROB, the first divestment operation in Bankia was carried out through an accelerated placement under the agency execution format, for a maximum volume of 10% of the capital to be carried out in the first quarter of 2014. The choice of Thursday, February 27, 2014 as the launch date of the operation was based on the analysis carried out by Rothschild on the situation of the European equity markets, the Spanish stock market and the behavior of Bankia's shares. In view of the fact that there had been no special shocks on the day, at 5:00 p.m. on February 27, the decision was made to carry out the operation at the close of the market. It was also decided to accept the tactical advisor's recommendation to place the final volume of the placement at 7.5%, based on its analysis of the market's absorptive capacity according to the observed trading volume. For such a large operation, Rothschild recommended using a syndicate made up of three placement agencies. The criteria applied to the pre-selection of potential placement banks were based on the recent experience of potential candidates. The entities selected were Deutsche Bank, Morgan Stanley and UBS. After the closing of the trading session, UBS was asked to draft, together with the legal advisor, the relevant event relevant for submission to the CNMV, after whose publication books could be opened. This publication occurred at 6:56 p.m. on February 27, 2014. The price range was only specified early on February 28, 2014. After conducting rounds of approach to investors, Rothschild recommended the allocation of shares at the price of db 1.51 per share, the price at which the order book closed at 9:15 a.m. That price also allowed the allocation of a large volume of shares to long-term institutional investors as opposed to hedge fund investors, which should promote greater price stability. At a price of db1.51 per share, BFA received db1,304,337,458 from the sale of 7.5% of Bankia's capital (863,799,641 shares). This represents a capital gain of 301 million euros for the BFA Group. The FROB, as the sole shareholder of BFA, benefits from this greater equity value of the entity. The operation has, in principle, no impact on either the deficit or the public debt. However, when BFA distributes dividends to its shareholder or amortizes capital, the operation may have a positive indirect impact on the stock of government debt to the extent that the cash raised could be used to write down liabilities or reduce the need to issue new debt securities. After the partial divestment, BFA's stake in Bankia was reduced from 68.395% to 60.89%, with no plans to carry out a new divestment in the short term. 3. CORPORATE OPERATION UNICAJA-BANCO CEISS Allow me now to explain the latest actions carried out for the completion of the Unicaja-CEISS corporate operation. Taking into account the commitment assumed by the FROB on the coverage of the negative impact of the claims of Banco CEISS investors who did not attend Unicaja's offer, and in accordance with State aid regulations, the resolution plan of Banco CEISS was modified, in order to recognize the new restructuring commitments that had to be assumed by the bank. The approval by the European Commission of the new plan became effective on March 13, 2014. After that, Unicaja proceeded to announce the fulfillment of the conditions required in its offer by means of a relevant event published in the CNMV. Finally, on April 2, the exchange was carried out in the terms provided. As you will recall, in order not to prejudice the acceptors of the offer who renounced litigation in relation to the initial marketing of their preferred shares and subordinated debt, the FROB decided to assume the judgment of an independent expert (PwC) who had been hired so that, applying regulatory and judicial criteria, it reviewed the integrity of the process of selling the aforementioned products to CEISS retailers. As of today, the expert's review has been completed and the FROB has made all the corresponding payments that represent 188 million euros to retail clients, who have thereby recovered 100% of the economic value of their investment. To date, and once Unicaja's offer has been settled, Banco CEISS has been resolved with full guarantees through its integration into a solvent entity and minimizing the use of public resources because, according to the estimates made by independent experts, the non-completion of the process would have been much more burdensome for the taxpayer. 4. ARBITRATION PROCESSES AND MONITORING OF PLANS After concluding the comments regarding the divestment operations carried out and the corporate operations promoted in the entities with aid, I would like, in the second part of my speech, to refer to other actions of the FROB carried out within the framework of its competences. I will briefly comment, first of all, on the situation of the arbitration processes in which the FROB participates, as well as the progress in the restructuring and resolution plans of the sector. to. Arbitral proceedings The situation of the arbitration proceedings initiated by the credit institutions owned by the FROB (BFA-Bankia, NCG Banco and Catalunya Banc) in relation to the marketing among retail customers of preferred shares and subordinated debt has constituted, as it could not be otherwise, a recurring point of my interventions before this Commission. The concern, both institutional and social, arising around the deficient commercialization among the retail clientele of hybrid products, prompted the search for formulas for the adequate resolution of the conflicts generated. This is the response to the creation of the Monitoring Committee for hybrid equity and subordinated debt instruments which, in addition to carrying out analysis and monitoring functions of the incidents detected, had the task of determining the basic criteria to specify, in the case of entities in which the FROB has a stake, the cases in which these entities had to offer their clients to submit to an arbitration procedure. These criteria were approved by the Monitoring Committee on April 17, 2013 and have been applied in all cases, although the processing of arbitration processes has not been parallel in time. Thus, NCG has concluded the arbitration process initiated in July 2012, having issued a positive award for more than 58,000 clients representing 62% of those who requested arbitration, representing a disbursement for the entity of 496 million euros. In the case of Catalunya Banc, the process, which began in October 2012 and has a deadline for submitting applications in July 2013, is expected to be completed in the second half of this year. So far, the independent expert has admitted the claims of nearly 69,000 holders, 67% of all those submitted, representing an amount of 465 million euros. Finally, in BFA-Bankia, the independent expert has so far admitted the applications corresponding to 177,000 holders, 77% of those submitted, representing an amount of 2,296 million euros. The awards continue to progress at a good pace: proceedings have already been resolved favourably to the client for a volume of 1,990 million euros, corresponding to more than 163,000 clients. The entity expects the arbitration process to end this month In conclusion, the independent experts have accepted the requests of more than 300,000 clients, representing 57% of retail investors who had access to arbitrations and more than 70% of those who have requested it, who have already been compensated or will soon be compensated for an amount equivalent to the nominal amount of their investment. These figures will still increase somewhat in the coming weeks as ongoing procedures are completed. b. Recovery and resolution plans Next, I would like to refer to the restructuring and resolution plans, an essential element for the rationalisation of the banking sector, which impose demanding requirements on entities that have received public aid in terms of capacity reduction. These requirements translate into average reductions in branches, personnel and balance sheets of the order of 35%, 30% and 25%, respectively. The latest available data, referring to the first quarter of 2014, confirm the progress in the fulfillment of these plans, having already achieved decreases of 29% in offices, 26% in staff and 18% in assets. I would like to highlight in this chapter the fact that some of the entities in which the FROB has a stake have once again issued securities on international markets. Thus, Bankia has placed two issues of 1,000 million euros, one of senior debt on January 9 and another of subordinated debt on May 13, this last issue having closed with a high demand, after receiving requests for 4,200 million euros. With this issue, Bankia's total solvency ratio under the Basel III criterion rises 103 basis points from 11.29% in March to 12.32%. For its part, BMN placed at the beginning of the year an issue of mortgage bonds for 500 million euros, at more favorable prices than initially expected and with a demand three times higher than the supply. Finally, and as you will know, another entity receiving public aid, Liberbank, agreed on April 29 to execute a share capital increase that has been successfully completed for a total amount of 575 million euros. These operations illustrate the progress made, not only in the material fulfillment of the restructuring plans, but also in the satisfaction of the fundamental objective of these plans, which is none other than to restore the capacity of the restructured banks so that, generating a profitable and sustainable commercial activity over time, they can meet their financing needs by their own means. 5. LEGAL PROCEEDINGS AND EXECUTION OF THE PROTOCOL OF PRIOR ACTION Another issue that I would like to comment on refers to the demand for responsibilities from the previous managers of the entities that have received public aid for the damages caused. As you know, the FROB has been assuming an active role both in the detection of irregular conduct and in the exercise of judicial proceedings derived from such investigations. In the last quarter, the FROB has appeared in different processes in order to guarantee the correct defense of the public interest it represents and, in particular, to ensure adequate reparation of the damage. So far, the FROB has initiated or is involved in 18 criminal cases, in which alleged crimes related to real estate trafficking operations or the irregular remuneration of former directors of entities that have received public support are analyzed and investigated. An example of the first results, which we hope will be followed by many more, is the Sentence issued in the criminal trial followed against former managers and directors of Caixa Pened8es, which has allowed the recovery of a significant sum of money for BMN in which the FROB holds 65% of the capital, in addition to a criminal conviction. In this process the FROB exercised the private accusation. Likewise, in accordance with the protocol of action for the investigation and analysis of suspicious or irregular operations carried out in the last five years by the entities, after having completed the phase of detection and preparation of reports by the internal audit departments, the FROB has promoted the realization of 90 forensic analyses, for which it has proceeded to the hiring of external expert services. These analyses aim to identify those irregular operations on which the FROB could exercise legal actions in order to achieve adequate reparation for the damage. The work of external third parties is in the completion phase in most cases, which should allow for further court proceedings next autumn. 6. SAREB I now proceed to refer briefly to the financial data of the Company for the Management of Assets from Bank Restructuring (Sareb), in which the FROB owns 45% of its capital. On 9 April 2014, Sareb approved its 2013 annual accounts. During that year, the management and divestment of the assets generated charges amounting to 3,800 million euros, which allowed the entity to close its first operating year with a gross operating result (Ebitda) of 1,195 million euros. The net result for the year was negative by 260 million euros, after having recorded the financial cost (1,221 million euros) and the write-down of part of the financial assets received (259.4 million euros). In any case, Sareb has been able, in its first year of life, to generate a cash surplus for debt repayment amounting to 1,998 million euros. On the other hand, the entity has started 2014 with a new organizational structure, with the aim of enhancing value creation and increasing its revenues. In fact, despite the significant challenges it faces, Sareb seems to be approaching cruising speed, with its portfolio management and divestment activity having significantly intensified, in accordance with its objectives and in line with its business plan. 7. FINANCIAL SITUATION OF THE FROB: VOLUME OF AID PROVIDED In relation to the accounts of the FROB for the year 2013, given that the approval of the same by its Governing Committee has not yet occurred, I beg you to apologize for not being able to offer you detailed information about them. However, if I would like to point out the broad features of the current patrimonial situation of the FROB. As you know, the accounts of the FROB in December 2012 reflected negative equity of almost 22,000 million euros, as a result of the high write-downs that had to be carried out in that year. To correct this situation, in 2013 the partial conversion of the loan granted by the Treasury to the FROB, intended for the execution of the European financial assistance program for the recapitalization of Spanish credit institutions, into a contribution to the equity endowment of the FROB and for an amount of 27,170 million euros, which has allowed to restore a situation of positive own funds. I would also like to indicate that the write-downs that are expected to be reflected in the accounts of the FROB for the year 2013 for its participations in credit institutions and other concepts, are of much lower amount than those registered the previous year, so the FROB maintains a positive accounting equity. In this chapter and, probably, anticipating the questions of the honourable Members, allow me to try to quantify the cost borne by the FROB d0 and, ultimately, by the taxpayer d0 in the process of restructuring and recapitalization of our financial system since the beginning of the crisis, relying on the figures recently made public by the Bank of Spain. In fact, the direct cost to the taxpayer of the aid provided to banks could be estimated by adding to the amounts disbursed by the FROB in the entities, the expected cost of the EPAs granted by this body (Banco de Valencia and Caja Sur) and other guarantees and coverage offered by the FROB within the framework of the resolution processes. That is, to calculate this cost we should compute the funds disbursed by the FROB to acquire shares or contingently convertible obligations amounting to 53,553 million euros, and add the estimated cost of the EPAs and other guarantees granted in the resolution processes which, according to the available valuations, stands at 2,087 million euros. To this should be subtracted the recovery of the amounts paid through the amortization of convertible bonds subscribed by the FROB or the sale of the shareholdings of the FROB in the entities helped. In this section we must already account for the 1,760 million euros from the sale of NCG and the return of the aid granted to Banca C92vica by Caixabank. In addition, it is expected with a high probability that the convertible bonds subscribed by the FROB will be amortized before 2017 into Caja3 -absorbed by Ibercaja-, CEISS -absorbed by Unicaja- and Liberbank, which will imply the return of 1,135 million euros. Finally, it is expected that in the near future the 1,300 million euros obtained from the divestment of BFA in Bankia can be accounted for, once this amount is paid to the sole shareholder of BFA. The most uncertain element of the calculation is, logically, the estimate of the result of the sale of Catalunya Banc, currently underway, and the divestment in BFA/Bankia and BMN, when this is completed. However, it is likely that these disposals imply an appreciable moderation of the cost to the taxpayer of the consolidation of the financial system, which, in any case, in terms of GDP is below that required in many European countries. The above calculations do not include the investment of the FROB in the Sareb, for an amount of 2,192 million euros, as it does not constitute financial aid to banks. Likewise, it does not seem appropriate to count liquidity support provided through guarantees or credit lines as a cost to the taxpayer. In the first case, more than 69% of the guarantees d0 whose disposition required the payment of the corresponding fee d0 are already canceled and the rest will disappear with a high probability as the corresponding emissions expire. In the second case, all available liquidity has already been returned and available and undrawn liquidity has been cancelled following the integration of the beneficiary entities into other banking groups. Note also that in order to estimate the total aid required, it would be necessary to account for the almost 15,000 million euros contributed by the industry through the Deposit Guarantee Fund (FGD) in the form of direct capital injections, acquisition of shares under the liquidity mechanism for retail investors in NCG and CX, and coverage of the EPAs of CCM, CAM and Unnim. 8. EUROPEAN RESOLUTION RULES Finally, I would ask Members to allow me to conclude my presentation by referring to European regulatory developments in bank resolution, as these will condition the FROB and, in general, the activities that are carried out in this area in our country in the future. One of the fundamental pillars on which the Banking Union is based, in addition to the creation of the Single Supervisory Mechanism, is the Single European Resolution Mechanism (SRM) which, together with the Recovery and Resolution Directive that will enter into force next year, will create a true European framework for banking crisis management. The Directive is committed to strengthening crisis prevention mechanisms and, above all, to minimising the public cost of future resolution processes for non-viable entities, following the large bill that the banking crisis that began in 2009 has caused for European taxpayers. To this end, it requires the involvement of shareholders and creditors in the coverage of losses or capital deficits in the entities under resolution before resources outside them can be used. It also establishes the obligation to create resolution funds provided by industry to cover deficits that are not covered by the holders of liabilities of the entity. The Single Resolution Mechanism, to which the countries that are part of the Single Supervisory Mechanism d0 in principle those belonging to the euro area d0 will join, means adding to the single rules imposed by the Directive, the creation of a common body that will be responsible for implementing them and a common fund that, fully endowed by contributions from the European banking industry, It will face the needs that cannot be covered by the entities in resolution, after the mandatory involvement of shareholders and creditors. These advances represent an important transfer of sovereignty of the Member States that will favor the homogeneity between jurisdictions in the treatment of the different types of bank liabilities. This will go a long way towards restoring the integration of financial markets in Europe and defusing the links between financial and sovereign risk, while reducing the foreseeable cost that bank bailouts will have on taxpayers in the future. The launch of the new European resolution framework is expected to involve some adjustments in the organisation of resolution activities at national level. In our case, as you know, the FROB develops two types of activities that are affected differently by regulatory developments at EU level. Thus, a relevant part of the actions of the FROB d0 perhaps the most important at the present time d0 has to do with the management of the State's participation in some of the entities that have received public support, including the divestment strategy in them. This type of activity, related to the management of public assets in the financial sector, is not affected by the new European resolution rules and should continue to develop, logically, with the direct involvement of government authorities. The resolution actions, consisting of the determination of the non-viability of the institutions and the preparation, approval, execution and monitoring of the plans -which are currently divided between the FROB and the Bank of Spain- will be more affected by the transfer of powers to the Single Resolution Mechanism and by the adoption of a regulatory scheme where the need to use the public budget in the processes of resolution. In most of the main countries around us, formulas have been put in place, or are in the process of being adopted, that place the resolution activities themselves in an independent unit, within the scope of the banking supervisor, while establishing a functional organization and, sometimes, a decision-making system that ensures a sufficient separation between the resolution function and that of the regular supervision of institutions. In any case, at the Bank of Spain we understand that it would be advisable for the model adopted to distinguish resolution activities from those of management of public property of banking entities. In addition, for the first type of functions, a reasonable balance should be sought between the need to functionally separate resolution from supervision and the desirability of taking advantage of the synergies between the two activities, ensuring an allocation of available resources that can be flexibly accommodated to the varying needs in time typically available for the resolution of non-viable entities. It will, of course, be up to the government and this Parliament to determine the most appropriate way of aligning our rules with the new European framework. 9. CONCLUSIONS I shall conclude, ladies and gentlemen. As I said at the beginning, I hope that my speech has served not only to explain the main actions of the FROB in recent months, but also to illustrate that the work done is beginning to bear fruit in terms of the normalization of the functioning of the most vulnerable segment of our financial system. I also believe that the arbitration processes undertaken are managing to mitigate, at least, the serious social problem created by the deficient commercialization of preferred and subordinated debt and that the FROB is acting diligently in the prosecution of irregular management practices in the entities that should have received public support. But, having said that, we are naturally aware of the high volume of public resources that the FROB has had to use in its actions, being our main interest to make the most efficient use of them. We are also aware that significant challenges remain, starting imminently with the participation of all institutions in resolution or restructuring in the assessment exercises that are being carried out under the Single Supervisory Mechanism. Finally, the agreements reached in the European Union in recent months, in particular the creation of the European Resolution Mechanism, as well as the establishment of a Community regulatory framework on the resolution of credit institutions, will require the adaptation of the national resolution scheme in order to preserve its effectiveness in the new environment. Thank you for your attention.

De hecho, a pesar de los importantes retos a los que debe hacer frente, Sareb parece acercarse a su velocidad de crucero, habindose intensificado de forma apreciable la actividad de gestin y desinversin de su cartera, de conformidad con sus objetivos y en lnea con su plan de negocio. 7. SITUACIN FINANCIERA DEL FROB: VOLUMEN DE AYUDAS SUMINISTRADAS En relacin con las cuentas del FROB correspondientes al ejercicio 2013, dado que la aprobacin de las mismas por su Comisin Rectora todava no se ha producido, ruego que me disculpen por no poder ofrecerles informacin detallada sobre las mismas. No obstante, si querra sealarles los grandes rasgos de la actual situacin patrimonial del FROB. Como sus Seoras conocen, las cuentas del FROB a diciembre de 2012 reflejaban unos fondos propios negativos de casi 22.000 millones de euros, consecuencia de los elevados saneamientos que tuvieron que realizarse en ese ejercicio. Para corregir esta situacin, en 2013 se realiz la conversin parcial del prstamo concedido por el Tesoro al FROB, destinado a la ejecucin del programa de asistencia financiera europea para la recapitalizacin de las entidades de crdito espaolas, en aportacin a la dotacin patrimonial del FROB y por un importe de 27.170 millones de euros, lo que ha permitido restaurar una situacin de fondos propios positivos. Tambin me gustara indicar que los saneamientos que estn previstos reflejar en las cuentas del FROB del ejercicio 2013 por sus participaciones en entidades de crdito y otros conceptos, son de importe muy inferior al de los registrados el ejercicio anterior, por lo que el FROB mantiene un patrimonio contable positivo. En este captulo y, probablemente, adelantndome a las preguntas de sus Seoras, permtanme que intente cuantificar el coste soportado por el FROB y, en ltima instancia, por el contribuyente- en el proceso de saneamiento y recapitalizacin de nuestro sistema financiero desde el comienzo de la crisis, apoyndome en las cifras recientemente hechas pblicas por el Banco de Espaa. De hecho, el coste directo para el contribuyente de las ayudas proporcionadas a la banca podra estimarse sumando a las cantidades desembolsadas por el FROB en las entidades, el coste esperado de los EPA concedidos por este organismo (Banco de Valencia y Caja Sur) y de otras garantas y coberturas ofrecidas por el FROB en el marco de los procesos de resolucin. Esto es, para calcular este coste deberamos computar los fondos desembolsados por el FROB para adquirir acciones u obligaciones contingentemente convertibles que ascienden a 53.553 millones de euros, y sumar el coste estimado de los EPA y dems garantas concedidas en los procesos de resolucin que, de acuerdo con las valoraciones disponibles, se sita en 2.087 millones de euros. A ello habra que restar la recuperacin de los importes desembolsados mediante la amortizacin de obligaciones convertibles suscritas por el FROB o la venta de las participaciones accionariales del FROB en las entidades ayudadas. En este apartado hay ya que contabilizar los 1.760 millones de euros procedentes de la venta de NCG y de la devolucin de las ayudas concedidas a Banca Cvica por parte de Caixabank. Adems, cabe esperar, con una elevada probabilidad, la amortizacin, antes de 2017, de las obligaciones convertibles suscritas por el FROB en Caja3 -absorbida por Ibercaja-, CEISS absorbida por Unicaja- y Liberbank, que implicarn la devolucin de 1.135 millones de euros. Por ltimo, resulta esperable que en el futuro prximo puedan contabilizarse los 1.300 millones de euros obtenidos de la desinversin de BFA en Bankia, una vez se produzca el abono de esta cantidad al nico accionista de BFA. El elemento ms incierto del clculo lo constituye, lgicamente, la estimacin del resultado de la venta de Catalunya Banc, actualmente en curso, y de la desinversin en BFA/Bankia y BMN, cuando esta se complete. Con todo, resulta probable que estas enajenaciones impliquen una moderacin apreciable del coste que para el contribuyente ha supuesto el saneamiento del sistema financiero que, en todo caso, en trminos del PIB se sita por debajo del requerido en numerosos pases europeos. En los clculos anteriores no se incluye la inversin del FROB en la Sareb, por un importe de 2.192 millones de euros, por no constituir una ayuda financiera a la banca. Asimismo, no parece oportuno contabilizar como coste para el contribuyente el apoyo de liquidez suministrado mediante avales o lneas de crdito. En el primer caso, ms del 69% de los avales cuya disposicin requera el abono de la correspondiente tasa- estn ya cancelados y el resto desaparecern con una elevada probabilidad a medida en que venzan las emisiones correspondientes. En el segundo caso, toda la liquidez dispuesta ya ha sido devuelta y la disponible y no dispuesta ha sido cancelada tras la integracin de las entidades beneficiarias en otros grupos bancarios. Ntese adems que para poder estimar la ayuda total requerida habra que contabilizar los casi 15.000 millones de euros aportados por la industria a travs del Fondo de Garanta de Depsitos (FGD) en forma de aportaciones directas de capital, adquisicin de acciones en el marco del mecanismo de liquidez para inversores minoristas en NCG y CX, y cobertura de los EPA de CCM, CAM y Unnim. 8. NORMATIVA EUROPEA DE RESOLUCIN Finalmente, ruego a sus Seoras me permitan terminar mi exposicin haciendo una referencia a los desarrollos regulatorios europeos en materia de resolucin bancaria, pues estos condicionarn al FROB y, en general, a las actividades que en esta materia se desarrollen en nuestro pas en el futuro. Uno de los pilares fundamentales sobre los que asienta la Unin Bancaria, adems de la creacin del Mecanismo nico de Supervisin, es el Mecanismo Europeo nico de Resolucin (MUR) que, junto con la Directiva de Recuperacin y Resolucin que entrar en vigor el prximo ao, crear un autntico marco europeo de gestin de crisis bancarias. La Directiva apuesta por fortalecer los mecanismos de prevencin de crisis y, sobre todo, por minimizar el coste pblico que supongan en el futuro los procesos de resolucin de entidades no viables, tras la abultada factura que para los contribuyentes europeos ha supuesto la crisis bancaria iniciada en 2009. Para ello, exige la involucracin de accionistas y acreedores en la cobertura de prdidas o dficit de capital en las entidades en resolucin antes de que puedan utilizarse recursos ajenos a las mismas. Asimismo, establece la obligacin de crear fondos de resolucin dotados por la industria como cobertura de los dficits que no sean cubiertos por los tenedores de pasivos de la entidad. El Mecanismo nico de Resolucin, al que se adherirn los pases que formen parte del Mecanismo nico de Supervisin en principio los pertenecientes a la zona del euro-, supone aadir a la unicidad de normas que impone la Directiva, la creacin de una autoridad comn que se encargar de aplicarlas y un fondo comn que, dotado en su totalidad mediante contribuciones de la industria bancaria europea, har frente a las necesidades que no puedan ser cubiertas por las entidades en resolucin, tras la preceptiva involucracin de accionistas y acreedores. Estos avances suponen una importante cesin de soberana de los Estados Miembros que favorecer la homogeneidad entre jurisdicciones del tratamiento de los distintos tipos de pasivos bancarios. Ello contribuir de manera apreciable a restaurar la integracin de los mercados financieros en Europa y a desactivar los vnculos entre el riesgo financiero y el soberano, al tiempo que reduce el coste previsible que los rescates bancarios tendrn en el futuro para los contribuyentes. La puesta en marcha del nuevo marco europeo de resolucin implicar previsiblemente algunos ajustes en la organizacin de las actividades de resolucin a nivel nacional. En nuestro caso, como saben, el FROB desarrolla dos tipos de actividades que se ven afectadas de manera distinta por los desarrollos normativos a nivel de la UE. As, una parte relevante de las actuaciones del FROB quizs la ms importante en el momento actual- tiene que ver con la gestin de la participacin del Estado en algunas de las entidades que han recibido apoyo pblico, incluyendo la estrategia de desinversin en las mismas. Este tipo de actividades, relativas a la gestin del patrimonio pblico en el sector financiero, no se ve afectada por la nueva normativa europea de resolucin y debe continuar desarrollndose, lgicamente, con la involucracin directa de las autoridades gubernamentales. Las actuaciones de resolucin, consistentes en la determinacin de la no viabilidad de las instituciones y la preparacin, aprobacin, ejecucin y seguimiento de los planes -que en este momento se reparten entre el FROB y el Banco de Espaa- se vern ms afectadas por la cesin de competencias al Mecanismo nico de Resolucin y por la adopcin de un esquema normativo donde se minimiza la necesidad de utilizar el presupuesto pblico en los procesos de resolucin. En la mayor parte de los principales pases de nuestro entorno se han dispuesto, o estn en proceso de adopcin, frmulas que sitan las actividades de resolucin propiamente dichas en una unidad independiente, dentro del mbito del supervisor bancario, si bien estableciendo una organizacin funcional y, en ocasiones, un sistema de toma de decisiones que aseguren una separacin suficiente entre la funcin de resolucin y la de la supervisin regular de las entidades. En todo caso, en el Banco de Espaa entendemos que sera aconsejable que el modelo que se adopte distinga las actividades de resolucin de las de gestin de la propiedad pblica de entidades bancarias. Adems, para el primer tipo de funciones debera buscarse un equilibrio razonable entre la necesidad de separar funcionalmente la resolucin de la supervisin y la conveniencia de aprovechar las sinergias existentes entre ambas actividades, asegurndose un asignacin de los recursos disponibles que se pueda acomodar de modo flexible a las necesidades variantes en el tiempo que tpicamente tiene la resolucin de entidades no viables. Naturalmente, corresponder al Gobierno y a este Parlamento determinar la forma ms adecuada de ajustar nuestra normativa al nuevo marco europeo. 9. CONCLUSIONES Concluyo, Seoras. Como les deca al principio, espero que mi intervencin haya servido no solo para explicar las principales actuaciones del FROB en los ltimos meses, sino tambin para ilustrar que el trabajo realizado empieza a rendir sus frutos en trminos de la normalizacin del funcionamiento del segmento ms vulnerable de nuestro sistema financiero. Creo que la venta de NCG, la culminacin de la operacin de integracin de CEISS en Unicaja, la enajenacin con xito de un paquete de la participacin que ostenta el FROB, indirectamente a travs de BFA, en Bankia, y el avanzado estado del proceso de venta de Catalunya Banc, suponen avances relevantes en la hoja de ruta que tenamos planeada. Estas operaciones, junto con la buena marcha del proceso de reestructuracin de las entidades y la mejora de las condiciones econmicas y financieras generales, estn posibilitando la vuelta al mercado de las entidades apoyadas, que han conseguido emitir instrumentos de capital o deuda en condiciones favorables. Creo, asimismo, que los procesos de arbitraje acometidos estn consiguiendo mitigar, al menos, el grave problema social creado por la deficiente comercializacin de preferentes y deuda subordinada y que el FROB est actuando con diligencia en la persecucin de prcticas irregulares de gestin en las entidades que han debido recibir apoyo pblico. Pero, dicho esto, naturalmente somos conscientes del elevado volumen de recursos pblicos que el FROB ha debido utilizar en sus actuaciones, siendo nuestro principal inters hacer el uso ms eficiente posible de los mismos. Somos tambin conscientes que todava persisten retos importantes comenzando, de manera inminente, con la participacin de todas las entidades en resolucin o reestructuracin en los ejercicios de evaluacin que se estn realizando en el mbito del Mecanismo nico de Supervisin. Finalmente, los acuerdos alcanzados en la Unin Europea en los ltimos meses, en especial la creacin del Mecanismo Europeo de Resolucin, as como el establecimiento de un marco normativo comunitario sobre resolucin de entidades de crdito, exigirn la adaptacin del esquema nacional de resolucin con el fin de preservar su eficacia en el nuevo entorno. Gracias por su atencin.

Title: Intervention at the Day of the Foundation for the Royal Spanish Academy
text: 17.10.2014 Intervention of the governor in the Day of the Foundation pro Real Academia Espa96ola Luis M. Linde Governor Gobera Your Majesties, Minister, Ambassadors, Academics, Ladies and Gentlemen, On this morning of so many important commemorations, allow me to add to them one more celebration: that of the Day of the Foundation for the Royal Spanish Academy, which, with the permanent and fundamental support of the Crown from the honorary presidency, the Governor of the Bank of Spain has the privilege and responsibility of presiding. Since its creation under the auspices of King Juan Carlos, twenty-one years ago d1they are fulfilled in three days, on October 20d1, the Foundation dedicates an annual day to its patrons and benefactors. A special day, and none more solemn than today, to express to all of them our gratitude and recognition for the invaluable help provided throughout these two decades. Individuals, companies and institutions, including the governments of all the Autonomous Communities, have contributed to making viable projects of great relevance for the Academy, which, surely, would not have been possible without their generous support. Thank you, therefore, to everyone, many of them, present here today at this solemn meeting. Like many other institutions in our country, the Royal Spanish Academy has had to adapt to the restrictions imposed by the economic crisis that began in 2008. In these circumstances, it is necessary to highlight the discretion, adaptability and good spirit with which its governing bodies, its Directors and all its members have faced the situation. In 1993, when the Foundation was created, its first president, the then Governor of the Bank of Spain and great university figure, our unforgettable Luis e7ngel Rojo, pointed out that the Foundation for the Royal Spanish Academy was born to support the Academy in all circumstances and, naturally, even more, in difficult ones. It must be recognized that those who had then, with King Don Juan Carlos at the head, as first signatory and first donor, the happy idea of creating the Foundation, were well foresighted. That initiative has provided crucial help to the Academy to move forward, at full capacity, in its different tasks, always with the same purpose: the service to the Spanish language, common heritage of half a billion Spanish speakers. The Academy has overcome difficult times, adverse moments d0 it is enough to approach the History recently published by Don V92ctor Garc92a de la Concha to know the anxieties of the past d0 and we have no doubt: it will always continue to find the most appropriate way to overcome difficulties. Just a month ago, Lord, at the first meeting of the Board of Trustees that you presided, we had the opportunity to analyze with Your Majesty our current reality, in order to lay the foundations that will allow us to face the challenges of the future. You pointed out then something that has also been underlined here today, with the presence of the directors and presidents of the twenty-two corporations that make up the Association of Academies of the Spanish Language: "Collaboration and consensus among all the Academies d0 the foundation of what has been called pan-Hispanic language policy d0 is key for Spanish to continue growing and consolidating itself as a second language of international communication." We all agree on this objective, which is the same one already defended by King Juan Carlos, in the constitutive session of the Foundation, when, referring to the commitment of this House, he said: "Of few institutions can be pointed out such a long delivery in time, and also in space, taking into account the transatlantic projection of academic works." Recently it was four centuries since the publication of the Treasury of the Spanish Language, our first dictionary and, by the way, the first in a Romance language, whose author, Sebasti87n de Covarrubias, gave it to the press in Madrid, in 1611, reigning Philip III. Three centuries ago, the Royal Spanish Academy was commissioned to care for and protect this treasure, which has not stopped enriching and growing, in every way, since then. The Royal Academy has fulfilled the task splendidly and we are sure that it will continue to assume, faithfully and brilliantly, that great responsibility. Our Foundation will remain, modestly, by your side to help in everything that is within its reach. Today, Your Majesty, you have received the twenty-third edition of the Dictionary of the Spanish Language, which arrives in bookstores in America and Spain under a hopeful motto: "The words that unite us". It only remains for me to add: so be it.
text_original: 17.10.2014 Intervencin del gobernador en el Da de la Fundacin pro Real Academia Espaola Luis M. Linde Gobernador Gobera Majestades, Seor Ministro, seores embajadores, acadmicos, seoras y seores: En esta maana de tantas y tan importantes conmemoraciones permtanme que sume a ellas una celebracin ms: la del Da de la Fundacin pro Real Academia Espaola, que, con el apoyo permanente y fundamental de la Corona desde la presidencia de honor, el Gobernador del Banco de Espaa tiene el privilegio y la responsabilidad de presidir. Un da especial, y ninguno ms solemne que el de hoy, para expresarles, a todos ellos, nuestra gratitud y reconocimiento por la inestimable ayuda prestada a lo largo de estas dos dcadas. Particulares, empresas e instituciones, entre ellas, los gobiernos de todas las Comunidades Autnomas, han contribuido a hacer viables proyectos de gran relevancia para la Academia, que, seguramente, no habran sido posibles sin su generoso respaldo. Gracias, por tanto, a todos, muchos de ellos, presentes hoy aqu en esta solemne sesin. Al igual que otras muchas instituciones de nuestro pas, la Real Academia Espaola ha tenido que adaptarse a las restricciones impuestas por la crisis econmica que se inici en 2008. En estas circunstancias, hay que resaltar la discrecin, la capacidad de adaptacin y el buen nimo con los que han afrontado la situacin sus rganos de gobierno, sus Directores y todos sus miembros. En 1993, cuando se cre la Fundacin, su primer presidente, el entonces Gobernador del Banco de Espaa y gran figura universitaria, nuestro inolvidable Luis ngel Rojo, seal que la Fundacin pro Real Academia Espaola naca para apoyar a la Academia en todas las circunstancias y, naturalmente, ms an, en las difciles. Hay que reconocer que quienes tuvieron entonces, con el rey Don Juan Carlos a la cabeza, como primer firmante y primer donante, la feliz idea de crear la Fundacin, fueron bien previsores. Aquella iniciativa ha prestado una ayuda crucial a la Academia para seguir adelante, a pleno rendimiento, en sus diferentes tareas, siempre con la misma finalidad: el servicio a la lengua espaola, patrimonio comn de quinientos millones de hispanohablantes. La Academia ha superado pocas difciles, momentos adversos basta acercarse a la Historia publicada recientemente por don Vctor Garca de la Concha para conocer las zozobras del pasadoy no tenemos ninguna duda: seguir encontrando siempre el camino ms adecuado para superar las dificultades. Hace apenas un mes, Seor, en la primera reunin del Patronato que presidisteis, tuvimos la oportunidad de analizar con Vuestra Majestad nuestra realidad actual, con el fin de sentar las bases que nos permitan encarar los desafos del futuro. Sealasteis entonces algo que hoy tambin se ha subrayado aqu, con la presencia de los directores y presidentes de las veintids corporaciones que forman la Asociacin de Academias de la Lengua Espaola: La colaboracin y el consenso entre todas las Academias fundamento de lo que se ha denominado poltica lingstica panhispnica es clave para que el espaol contine creciendo y consolidndose como segunda lengua de comunicacin internacional. Todos coincidimos en este objetivo, que es el mismo que ya defendi el rey don Juan Carlos, en la sesin constitutiva de la Fundacin, cuando, refirindose al compromiso de esta Casa, deca: De pocas instituciones puede sealarse una entrega tan dilatada en el tiempo, y tambin en el espacio, teniendo en cuenta la proyeccin trasatlntica de los trabajos acadmicos. Hace poco se cumplieron cuatro siglos de la publicacin del Tesoro de la Lengua Castellana o Espaola, nuestro primer diccionario y, por cierto, el primero en una lengua romance, cuyo autor, Sebastin de Covarrubias, lo dio a la imprenta en Madrid, en 1611, reinando Felipe III. La Real Academia Espaola recibi hace tres siglos el encargo de cuidar y proteger ese tesoro, que no ha dejado de enriquecerse y crecer, en todos los sentidos, desde entonces. La Real Academia ha cumplido de forma esplndida con la encomienda y estamos seguros de que seguir asumiendo, fiel y brillantemente, esa gran responsabilidad. Nuestra Fundacin seguir, modestamente, a su lado para ayudar en todo lo que est a su alcance. Hoy habis recibido, Majestad, la vigsimotercera edicin del Diccionario de la lengua espaola, que llega a las libreras de Amrica y Espaa bajo un lema esperanzador: Las palabras que nos unen. Slo me queda aadir: que as sea.

Title: Speech at the award ceremony of the XV King Juan Carlos Economics Prize, awarded to Agustn Maravall by the Jos Celma Prieto Foundation
text: 27.10.2014 Speech of the XV King Juan Carlos Economy Prize Jos8e Celma Prieto Foundation/Bank of Spain Luis M. Linde Governor Your Majesty, Mr. Secretary of State, ladies and gentlemen, First of all, Lord, I would like to thank you for your presence today at this event. Since 1986, when the award ceremony that bears your name was held for the first time in this House, you have always accompanied us, except in the 2012 edition, when Your Majesty could not attend and we had the honor of being presided over by the then Prince, today King of Spain, Don Felipe VI. Your Majesty, to put it plainly as possible, your attendance brings us great joy and honour once again to this House. The King Juan Carlos Economics Prize, instituted by the Jos8e Celma Prieto Foundation, whose president, Mr. Jos8e Celma, who is with us today, I want to thank for his long and generous work of patronage, was established to recognize the academic or professional career, in the field of economics, of Spanish or Ibero-American personalities. The Jury of this 2014 edition, which I had the honor of chairing, was composed of Mr. Aurelio Men8endez, as vice president, Mr. Juan Velarde, Mr. Rodolfo Mart92n Villa, Mr. Andreu Mas-Colell, Mr. e7lvaro Cuervo and Mr. Jos8e Luis Feito. Before moving forward, I would like to express the deep sorrow of all the members of the Jury for the death of Mr. Gonzalo Anes, director of the Academy of History, member of our Jury, as well as, himself, candidate awarded in 2006. And I also want to thank and highlight the long and fruitful collaboration of Mr. Jos8e Ram97n e7lvarez Rendueles, former governor of the Bank of Spain, who has ceased as a member of the Jury by application of the statutory rules that regulate it. In this 2014 edition, the Jury, meeting on July 10, decided to award the Prize to Mr. Agust92n Maravall, valuing his contribution to the field of statistics applied to economics, and, in particular, his work on the statistical and prediction instrument called "time series", a field in which Agust92n Maravall is a very prominent figure in the international arena. The Rey Juan Carlos Economics Prize has always taken into account the academic or professional prestige of the winners and the international recognition of their contributions. On this occasion, the long list of Spanish and foreign universities and institutions that have supported the candidacy of Agust92n Maravall indicates that this tradition has been maintained that, recognizing the merits of the winner, prestigates, in turn, the Prize. Agust92n Maravall holds a PhD in Agricultural Engineering from the University of Madrid and a PhD in Economics from the University of Wisconsin (USA). He worked for three years as an engineer at the Ministry of Agriculture in Madrid. He was an economist at the Governing Board of the Federal Reserve in Washington and, in 1979, on his return to Spain, he joined the Research Service of the Bank of Spain, where he has worked since then, with the parenthesis of the seven years in which he was professor at the European University Institute in Florence. He has been a professor at George Washington University, at the University of Aix en Provence, at the Complutense University, at the Autonomous University of Madrid and at the Center for Monetary and Financial Studies. He has published numerous papers in the main journals of his specialty and several monographs on statistics and mathematical methods applied to economic studies and economic prediction. Agust92n Maravall, who is an honorary member of the American Statistical Association and the Journal of Econometrics, has received several awards, among which we must highlight the Julius Shiskin Prize for Economic Statistics, in 2004, the most important prize granted in its specialty in the United States; and in Spain, the Rey Jaime I Economics Prize in 2005 and the Galician Statistics Prize in 2006. The statistical tool in which Agust92n Maravall is a great master emerged in the 70s, in part, as a response to the failure, in some cases resounding, of prediction techniques based on econometric models. But there is one characteristic of the laureate's academic and scientific contribution: not only has he made basic contributions to the methodology of economic forecasting, especially in the areas of seasonal adjustment and trend estimation, but he has also developed tools for the practical application of this methodology. In fact, different techniques and models that he authored or co-authored are currently used in economic institutions around the world, starting with the most important central banks. But surely the winner will explain to us in his speech, much better and in a more interesting and illustrative way than I could do, what this technique consists of, to which he has contributed so much. Statistics, economic prediction and time series do not exhaust, far from it, the interests of Agust92n Maravall. I hope that he will confide in us in his speech about his scientific and literary hobbies. But I want to tell you something that, it seems to me, Agust92n Maravall is quite proud of, although he would never acknowledge it in public: Maravall is, you can believe me, an excellent ping pong player. It is true that when, for somewhat fortuitous reasons, he could measure his strength with a world champion and with a champion of Spain he left, on both occasions, scoring a score that is not appropriate to remember, although he recognizes that his opponents treated him with, let's say, kind benevolence. Finally, returning to his scientific contribution, Agust92n Maravall is, without a doubt, the most outstanding Spanish expert in statistical techniques applied to economic prediction and one of the most outstanding teachers of this specialty at an international level. For the Bank of Spain it has been an honour and a privilege to have him almost thirty years as a collaborator in its Research Service. Reiterating our gratitude for your presence at this event, sir, I can only have, with your permission, to ask the winner to take the stage so that you can present him with the 2014 King Juan Carlos Economy Prize.
text_original: 27.10.2014 Discurso de entrega del XV Premio de Economa Rey Juan Carlos Fundacin Jos Celma Prieto/Banco de Espaa Luis M. Linde Gobernador Majestad, seor secretario de Estado, seoras y seores: En primer lugar, seor, quiero agradeceros vuestra presencia hoy en este acto. Desde 1986, cuando se celebr por primera vez en esta Casa la entrega del Premio que lleva vuestro nombre, nos habis acompaado siempre, salvo en la edicin de 2012, cuando Vuestra Majestad no pudo asistir y tuvimos el honor de que nos presidiera el entonces Prncipe, hoy Rey de Espaa, Don Felipe VI. Jos Celma, que hoy nos acompaa, quiero agradecer su larga y generosa labor de mecenazgo, se estableci para reconocer la trayectoria acadmica o profesional, en el mbito de la economa, de personalidades espaolas o iberoamericanas. El Jurado de esta edicin 2014, que he tenido el honor de presidir, ha estado compuesto por D. Aurelio Menndez, como vicepresidente, D. Juan Velarde, D. Rodolfo Martn Villa, D. Andreu Mas-Colell, D. lvaro Cuervo y D. Jos Luis Feito. Antes de seguir adelante, quiero expresar el profundo pesar de todos los vocales del Jurado por el fallecimiento de D. Gonzalo Anes, director de la Academia de la Historia, miembro de nuestro Jurado, as como, l mismo, candidato premiado en 2006. Jos Ramn lvarez Rendueles, ex gobernador del Banco de Espaa, que ha cesado como miembro del Jurado por aplicacin de las reglas estatuarias que lo regulan. En esta edicin 2014, el Jurado, reunido el 10 de julio pasado, decidi otorgar el Premio a D. Agustn Maravall, valorando su aportacin al campo de la estadstica aplicada a la economa, y, en particular, sus trabajos sobre el instrumento estadstico y de prediccin denominado series temporales, campo en el que Agustn Maravall es figura muy destacada en el mbito internacional. El Premio de Economa Rey Juan Carlos siempre ha tenido en cuenta el prestigio acadmico o profesional de los premiados y el reconocimiento internacional de sus aportaciones. En esta ocasin, la larga lista de universidades e instituciones espaolas y extranjeras que han apoyado la candidatura de Agustn Maravall indica que se ha mantenido esa tradicin que, reconociendo los mritos del premiado, prestigia, a su vez, al Premio. Agustn Maravall es Doctor Ingeniero Agrnomo por la Universidad de Madrid y Doctor en Economa por la Universidad de Wisconsin (EEUU). Trabaj tres aos como ingeniero en el Ministerio de Agricultura en Madrid. Fue economista de la Junta de Gobierno de la Reserva Federal en Washington y, en 1979, a su vuelta a Espaa, ingres en el Servicio de Estudios del Banco de Espaa, donde ha trabajado desde entonces, con el parntesis de los siete aos en que fue catedrtico del Instituto Universitario Europeo de Florencia. Ha sido profesor en la George Washington University, en la Universidad de Aix en Provence, en la Universidad Complutense, en la Universidad Autnoma de Madrid y en el Centro de Estudios Monetarios y Financieros. Ha publicado numerosos trabajos en las principales revistas de su especialidad y varias monografas sobre estadstica y mtodos matemticos aplicados a los estudios econmicos y a la prediccin econmica. Agustn Maravall, que es miembro de honor de la American Statistical Association y del Journal of Econometrics, ha recibido diferentes premios, entre los hay que destacar el Premio Julius Shiskin de Estadstica Econmica, en 2004, el ms importante premio que se otorga en su especialidad en Estados Unidos; y en Espaa, el Premio de Economa Rey Jaime I, en 2005, y el Premio Galicia de Estadstica, en 2006. La herramienta estadstica en la que Agustn Maravall es un gran maestro surgi en los aos 70, en parte, como respuesta al fallo, en algunos casos estrepitoso, de las tcnicas de prediccin basadas en modelos economtricos. Pero hay que sealar una caracterstica en la aportacin acadmica y cientfica del premiado: no solo ha hecho contribuciones bsicas a la metodologa de la prediccin econmica, especialmente, en las cuestiones relativas al ajuste estacional y la estimacin de la tendencia, sino que, adems, ha elaborado instrumentos para la aplicacin en la prctica de esa metodologa. De hecho, diferentes tcnicas y modelos de los que l es autor o coautor se usan actualmente en instituciones econmicas de todo el mundo, empezando por los ms importantes bancos centrales. Pero seguro que el premiado nos explicar en su intervencin, mucho mejor y de modo ms interesante e ilustrativo de lo que yo podra hacerlo, en qu consiste esta tcnica, a la que l tanto ha aportado. La estadstica, la prediccin econmica y las series temporales no agotan, ni mucho menos, los intereses de Agustn Maravall. Espero que l nos har en su intervencin alguna confidencia sobre sus aficiones cientficas y literarias. Pero yo quiero contarles algo de lo que, me parece, Agustn Maravall se siente bastante orgulloso, aunque l nunca lo reconocera en pblico: Maravall es, pueden creerme, un excelente jugador de ping pong. Es cierto que cuando, por causas un tanto fortuitas, pudo medir sus fuerzas con un campen del mundo y con un campen de Espaa sali, en ambas ocasiones, anotando un marcador que no es del caso recordar, aunque l reconoce que sus contrincantes lo trataron con, digamos, amable benevolencia. En fin, volviendo a su aportacin cientfica, Agustn Maravall es, sin duda, el ms destacado experto espaol en tcnicas estadsticas aplicadas a la prediccin econmica y uno de los ms destacados maestros de esa especialidad a nivel internacional. Para el Banco de Espaa ha sido un honor y un privilegio tenerle casi treinta aos como colaborador en su Servicio de Estudios. Reiterando nuestro agradecimiento por vuestra presencia en este acto, seor, slo me queda, con vuestro permiso, solicitar al premiado que suba al estrado para que le hagis entrega del Premio de Economa Rey Juan Carlos 2014.

Title: Opening remarks at the XIII Germn Berncer Prize Ceremony
text: 03.11.2014 Opening remarks by Deputy Governor of the Banco de Espana XIII German Bernacer Prize Ceremony Fernando Restoy Deputy Governor Ladies and Gentlemen, It is for me a great pleasure to welcome you all and to participate in the Award Ceremony for the 13th German Bernacer Prize at the CEMFI premises, under the presidency of Vitor Constancio, Vice-President of the ECB, and chairman of the Selection Committee for this award. I would like to start by expressing my gratitude to Vitor, for honouring us with his presence today, on the eve of a historic day in the process of the European construction; namely, the beginning of the oversight activities of the Single Supervisory Mechanism (SSM). We have devoted much of our time in the last few months preparing the comprehensive assessment including a stress test for European banks, an extremely absorbing exercise which, in my view has achieved its objectives. You obviously deserve much credit for that. You would agree with me that after all that stress it is particularly pleasant now to be able to take part in an activity relating to the world of intellectual creation such as the recognition of the research of young economists. Naturally, I want to praise the initiative launched by the Observatorio del Banco Central Europeo chaired by Guillermo de la Dehesa to institute this award for outstanding researchers on macroeconomics and finance under the age of 40. I also acknowledge the sponsorship of Banco Santander and welcome Ana Botin to CEMFI and to this ceremony, in her new capacity as Chair of Banco Santander. Let me also thank CEMFI a foundation created and sponsored by the Banco de Espana and its Director, Rafael Repullo, for hosting this ceremony. I could not think of a better place to recognise the work of young economists. The organisation of this event here shows the continued support of the Banco de Espana to this initiative as well as our long-standing commitment to high-quality research and education in economics, such as those conducted by CEMFIs faculty. The Bernacer Prize commemorates a distinguished Spanish economist, the first director of the Research Department of the Banco de Espana. Bernacer was arguably a pioneer of modern monetary theory with seminal contributions that encountered serious difficulties in gaining the national and international recognition they deserved. It is somewhat ironic and also a fortunate decision by the Observatorio that a prize specifically created to recognise excellence in research should bear his name. Finally, let me convey my congratulations to the winner of this edition, Professor Thomas Philippon, who will be introduced by Guillermo de la Dehesa in a few minutes. Thomas Philippon, from NYU Stern School, has developed interesting research on the efficiency of the financial sector, among other areas. By way of example, I was struck by the findings of his recent paper on the matter (forthcoming in AER), which show that not many efficiency gains measured by the cost of intermediation can be identified in the financial industry despite technological progress. As a banking sector supervisor, I can assert that any work that helps us better understand the dynamics of efficiency deserves much attention, particularly in a context in which the banking sector is facing significant challenges associated with low margins and profitability. We are therefore looking forward to your further contributions on the matter. Following the protocol, I believe it is now the turn of Ana Botin, Chair of Banco Santander, to take the floor.

Title: Speech introducing Dr. Jens Weidmann, President of the Bundesbank. Annual Financial Convention 2014, organized by the Financial Markets Association
text: 24.11.2014 Speech by Luis M. Linde, Governor of the Bank of Spain, introducing Dr. Jens Weidmann, President of the Bundesbank Annual Financial Convention 2014/ Financial Markets Association Luis M. Linde Governor First of all, I would like to thank the President of the Bundesbank, Jens Weidmann, for accepting the invitation to participate in the luncheon conference held on the occasion of the Annual Convention of the Financial Markets Association. When Enrique Prado, president of the Association, raised the idea of inviting the president of the Bundesbank to me a year ago, I welcomed it with great interest. Jens Weidmann has a somewhat atypical academic background, but very interesting from the point of view of the European Union as a whole. Jens Weidmann graduated in Economics in France, but received his PhD in Germany. He is a German with a perfect command of French and the culture and history of France. This makes him a true Europeanist, something that, dare I say, has added value in the current circumstances. In 1997, Jens Weidmann joined the International Monetary Fund in Washington. In 1999 he was appointed Secretary-General of the German Council of Economic Experts. In 2003 he joined the Deutsche Bundesbank as Director of the Monetary Policy and Analysis Division and Deputy Director of the Economics Department. Three years later he moved to Berlin to take up the post of Director of the Department of Economic and Fiscal Policy of the Federal Chancellery. While in that capacity, he also acted as the Chancellor's personal representative in the preparations for the G-8 and G-20 global economic summits. Jens Weidmann was appointed President of the Deutsche Bundesbank and member of the Governing Council of the ECB on 1 May 2011. The views of the Bundesbank and its President are always highly relevant to the European Monetary Union and the Eurosystem as a whole. But perhaps they are even more important right now. Monetary union is a great achievement of the European Union, but it is obviously not the automatic and easy panacea to all our problems. We have an open discussion on what fiscal policy can achieve, what structural and institutional reforms are necessary and what is the role of monetary policy in the face of today's problems. There may be different answers to these questions, but I am sure we all agree that our economic policies must generate economic growth and employment, and that if this is not achieved, doubts about the future of monetary union and hostile political views towards it will inevitably increase. For all these reasons, I believe that the presence of Jens Weidmann among us today is truly timely. I would like to thank the President of the Bundesbank once again for being here, and I shall now give him the floor.
