Title: Appearance in the Commission of Economy and Competitiveness of the Congress of Deputies
text: APPEARANCE OF THE PRESIDENT OF THE GOVERNING COMMISSION OF THE FROB IN THE COMMISSION OF ECONOMY AND COMPETITIVENESS OF THE CONGRESS OF DEPUTIES April 14, 2015 Mr President, ladies and gentlemen. In compliance with the control mandate contained in article 56 of Law 9/2012 on the restructuring and resolution of credit institutions, of November 14, I appear before this Economy and Competitiveness Committee as President of the Governing Committee of the Fund for Orderly Bank Restructuring (FROB). The purpose of this appearance is to report on the activities carried out by the FROB since June 24, the date on which I last appeared before this Commission. In recent months, the Spanish financial sector has benefited from the progressive improvement in the economic situation, which has manifested itself in a gradual reduction in the volume of impaired assets. This has made it possible to reduce NPL ratios, which largely explains the improvement in the results that, in general, reflect the annual accounts as of December 2014. This positive evolution is also observed in the entities that remain under the control of the FROB, that is, BFA-Bankia and BMN. In the latter, BMN, profits have exceeded 100 million euros, compared to a practically zero result in 2013. At Bankia, meanwhile, results increased by 90% in 2014, reaching 771 million euros. In fact, Bankia has announced its intention to pay for the first time since its recapitalization a dividend of 202 million euros, of which 127 would be paid by BFA -owned by the FROB 100%-, which is a milestone in the normalization of the operation of this entity, after the intense process of restructuring and restructuring undertaken. However, Spanish banks, like the rest of the European banks, must face an unfavorable environment, derived from the sluggish demand for credit and the low interest rates that put downward pressure on the profitability of the business. To meet the challenges arising from this complex environment, Spanish banks have benefited from the intense process of consolidation, restructuring and recapitalization developed in recent years at the request of the authorities. The positive impact of the measures adopted d0 in whose design and execution the FROB has participated directly together with the Government and the Bank of Spain d0 has been evident in the evaluation exercises of European financial institutions, carried out by the ECB and the national supervisory authorities, as a preliminary step to the start of the activities of the new Single Supervisory Mechanism (SSM). The results of these exercises were published at the end of last October. As you will recall, the evidence revealed that Spanish banks were the ones with the most accurate valuation of the assets contained in their balance sheets and, therefore, it can be said that they offered more rigorous financial information. In addition, the exercises confirmed the appreciable resistance of Spanish banks to very severe shocks, since all of them had at the time of publication of the results a significant margin of capital above the minimum thresholds established for different macroeconomic scenarios. Specifically, Spanish banks subject to resolution or restructuring plans comfortably exceeded the years with data as of December 31, 2013, with the sole exception of Liberbank, which showed a minuscule capital deficit that was already amply covered on the date of publication of the results. Moving on to give you an account of the recent activity of the FROB, allow me to structure my presentation in four sections. Thus, in the first part of my speech I will inform you about the regular actions of the FROB, which cover (i) the divestment processes undertaken, in particular Catalunya Banc, (ii) the work carried out in the follow-up of the resolution or restructuring plans in progress, (iii) the completion of the arbitrations on hybrid products, (iv) the judicial proceedings and investigations carried out and (v) the evolution of Sareb. In the second part I will dwell, due to its obvious relevance, on the actions specifically related to Bankia's Public Offer of Subscription of shares (OPS). Next, in the third part, I will comment on the participation of the FROB in the management of the recent crisis of the Banco de Madrid entity. Finally, ladies and gentlemen, I will inform you of the progress that has been made at European level for the construction of the Banking Union and, in particular, of the implementation of the single resolution mechanism which, without a doubt, will significantly affect the framework for action of the FROB in the immediate future. 1. THE MAIN ACTIVITIES OF THE FROB I pass, then, to expose the main activities of the FROB in recent months. (i) Divestment processes As you will recall, in July 2013, the Governing Committee of the FROB awarded N1 Corporate Finance, S.A. the contract for the analysis and eventual sale of Catalunya Banc. The main recommendation that emerged from the report prepared by the consultant was the prior sale of a specific portfolio, composed of mortgage loans, with a gross value of approximately 6,400 million euros, with little commercial value (Hercules portfolio). This sale would increase the attractiveness of the entity -once devoid of the aforementioned portfolio-, which would be sold in a second phase. This strategy was justified by the potential benefit of attracting two types of investors: on the one hand, companies strictly interested in asset management d0 with an interest in bidding for the Hercules portfolio d0 and, on the other, financial institutions willing to acquire the banking business of Catalunya Banc, once properly healthy. In this way, it was aspired to maximize the return that the FROB would obtain in the whole operation. Consequently, in March 2014, Catalunya Banc began the process of selling the so-called Hercules portfolio, which achieved a high turnout. Thus, and after receiving expressions of interest from more than a dozen candidates, who submitted their non-binding offers, five bidders were selected for the second phase in which four of them submitted binding offers. The sale operation culminated on July 17, with the award of the Hercules portfolio to the Blackstone fund. The operation was structured through the creation of an asset securitization fund that will issue two types of bonds: senior bonds, class A bonds, which will be subscribed by the investor and class B bonds, which will be subscribed by the FROB for an approximate amount of 525 million euros (lower than the initially planned 572 million euros) and which are subordinated with respect to the former. Senior bonuses will be remunerated until reaching a maximum yield of 13%. Any additional return on the portfolio derived from the cash flows obtained will be distributed at 50% between the investor and the FROB. Additionally, the FROB will grant a credit line for a maximum limit of 400 million euros. This line will have market conditions in terms of remuneration and commissions. Overall, the operation entails an estimated financial support from the FROB of about 649 million euros, which means that the portfolio has been sold for approximately 85% of its book value. With regard to the sale of the bank's banking business, which began on June 2, 2014, three binding offers were received. Having analysed these, the Governing Committee of the FROB, in its session of July 21, 2014, decided to award the entity to Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria, S.A. The price offered amounted to 1,165 million euros for 98.4% of the shares of Catalunya Banc, owned by the FROB and the FGD. Together, both operations d0 that is, the sale of the portfolio and the banking business d0 have resulted in a net positive value, after considering the value of the guarantees granted, which amounts to 328 million euros. Once the relevant authorizations have been obtained by the national authorities and the European Commission, it is expected that, in the coming days, both sales contracts will be made public. First, the sale of the portfolio will be closed and, a few days later, the sale of FROB's stake in Catalunya Banc to BBVA. With this, the resolution process of the entity can be concluded, complying with the commitments assumed within the framework of the financial assistance program. (ii) Restructuring and resolution plans The latest available data confirm that the restructuring process of publicly supported institutions continues to progress at a satisfactory pace. Several banks completed balance, workforce and office adjustments in 2014, as required by their restructuring plans. The rest are expected to achieve it on the established dates. I would also like to inform you, in this section, that on December 22, the entity Liberbank, with the prior authorization of the Bank of Spain, and without having expired the deadline for the return of the public aid granted, proceeded to the amortization of the entire issue of contingently convertible bonds, which was subscribed in full by the FROB for an amount of 124 million euros. In other words, that entity has fully repaid the public aid it received in the form of capital instruments. Likewise, in the restructuring process of BFA-Bankia, and in accordance with the forecasts contained in the plan, the BFA entity submitted the waiver of the banking license on October 31, 2014, which was authorized by the Bank of Spain with effect from January 2, 2015. This waiver, although it does not alter the scope of consolidation of the group for the purposes of prudential supervision, is consistent with the consideration of BFA as a holding company without any banking activity. (iii) Arbitral proceedings I now turn to inform you about the follow-up of arbitration proceedings in relation to the marketing of preference shares and subordinated debt to retail clients initiated by some of the entities in which the FROB has a stake. Since the arbitration process initiated by NCG has been concluded several months ago, those corresponding to BFA-Bankia and Catalunya Banc are practically completed. Overall, the independent experts have so far accepted the applications of more than 300,000 clients, who have obtained or will soon obtain compensation equivalent to the nominal value of their investment. That figure represents 57% of retail investors who had access to arbitrations and 72% of those who have requested it. In this way, it can be concluded that the arbitration processes promoted by the FROB and undertaken by the nationalized entities that issued these instruments have been revealed as effective mechanisms to resolve cases of bad practices by issuers. These arbitrations, together with other actions d0 such as the liquidity mechanisms established by the Deposit Insurance Fund to support investors who obtained illiquid shares to Change of their preferred shares and subordinated debt - have allowed, at least, to alleviate the serious social problem generated by the inadequate commercialization of complex products. (iv) Legal proceedings In another vein, I will now explain the progress that has been made in the investigation and analysis of allegedly irregular management practices in the entities that have received financial support. As honourable Members will recall, the demand for responsibilities from the previous managers, as well as the detection of any irregular conduct, has been since the beginning of the bank restructuring one of the main focuses of attention of the FROB. This emphasis is due both to the duty as a public authority to contribute to the clarification of facts that may deserve reproach by the courts of justice, and to the obligation imposed by the rule to act at all times in accordance with the patrimonial interests of the State, seeking when possible the reparation of the damages caused to the public treasury. Currently, the FROB is involved in 20 criminal cases, mostly derived from its own actions to detect irregular practices of former managers. Likewise, in 2013 it agreed on an action protocol, which involved the performance of 90 forensic analyses, for which it has had specialized external services. The investigations carried out focus mainly on two types of actions: (i) those related to operations related to real estate traffic and (ii) those related to remuneration practices. In the section on activities related to the real estate sector, sixteen operations corresponding to Catalunya Banc have been sent to the Prosecutor's Office, with an estimated loss of 900 million euros, in addition to a file relating to a portfolio of retail mortgage loans granted by this entity. Likewise, nine operations corresponding to NCG Banco have been remitted, which could involve an estimated damage of 810 million euros. With regard to operations related to directors' remuneration, the FROB has sent the Prosecutor's Office two files relating to the BFA group or the savings banks that formed it. The first refers to the possible undue perception of remuneration, by directors and executives of Caja Madrid and Bankia in the period 2003-2012, through the use of credit cards, which has led to the opening of a separate piece in the case opened by the IPO of Bankia, to which I will refer later. The second file is related to the possible receipt of irregular compensation, whether in the form of fixed or variable remuneration, compensation for termination of contracts or contributions to pension plans, by directors of Caja Madrid in the period 2007-2010. Likewise, in relation to the entity Catalunya Banc, a file has recently been sent to the Prosecutor's Office regarding the termination of senior management contracts for the period 2008-2009. (v) Sareb To conclude this first section, I will briefly refer to the Company for the Management of Assets from Bank Restructuring (Sareb). In 2014, Sareb achieved a gross margin of 1,599 million euros, achieving an Ebitda of 1,103 million euros. The net result for the year is negative at db585 million, after having recorded a write-down amounting to db719 million corresponding to participative loans (db91 million) and unpaid unsecured loans from companies in bankruptcy (db628 million). These provisions are due to an exercise of accounting prudence, the result of the consultation carried out with the Bank of Spain on the calculation of the impairment of assets, in the period of time remaining until the approval of the circular on valuation of assets that is, at the present time, subject to the mandatory analysis by the Council of State. On the other hand, the entity has approved at the beginning of this year a new organizational structure with the elimination of the figure of the CEO, the maintenance of an executive presidency and the creation of two general directorates. Allow me at this point to recall that in January there was the resignation, for personal reasons, of Bel8en Romana d0 who had held the presidency since the foundation of Sareb in December 2012 d0 and her replacement by Jaime Echegoyen. 2. ACTIONS IN RELATION TO BANKIA'S PAHO In the second part of my speech, I will now comment on the participation of the FROB in the ongoing legal proceedings related to the Public Subscription Offer (OPS) of Bankia shares of July 2011, which have been processed, since June 2012, in the Central Court of Instruction No. 4 of the National High Court. As part of the investigation of the process, and at the request of the court, two expert opinions were issued to inspectors of credit institutions, on which the parties are currently alleging. Likewise, and in the processing of the aforementioned proceedings, the judge has agreed to the provision of joint and several bonds by Bankia, BFA and four directors of the group at the time of the IPO, for a total joint amount of 800 million euros. Against the bail order, the Public Prosecutor's Office, the FROB and some defendants have filed an appeal, which is pending resolution by the Criminal Chamber of the National Court. On March 18, the bond was deposited in cash jointly by BFA and Bankia, although these entities have announced that they will go against the four former directors to claim the part that, if any, could correspond to them. The action of the FROB, personified as an injured party in the process, has been guided by the same principles that have inspired its strategy in the rest of the causes in which it is or has Involved status. That is: the contribution to the clarification of the facts and the defense of the public interest. In the case of Bankia's IPO, in which both this entity and its parent company are charged together with those responsible for both at the time of the OPS, compliance with these objectives required the evaluation of the expert reports, since they could result in consequences that could be very burdensome for the public treasury. Although these reports had been prepared by competent professionals who acted independently and strictly following technical criteria, the FROB considered that some of the central conclusions of the experts' analysis were not sufficiently supported by the evidence shown. In particular, the FROB found questionable elements in the analysis developed in the expert reports in relation to Bankia's IPO financial statements and the process of forming the price of the new shares issued. To reach this conclusion, the FROB benefited both from the contribution made by the members of its Governing Committee and from its own technical services. In addition, in order to complete its analysis, it requested a report from the CNMV on the pricing process in the wholesale tranche of the issue and consulted the Bank of Spain on the proper interpretation of its own accounting circular in some aspects that were relevant for the valuation of the expert reports. As is logical, this technical analysis carried out within the FROB has determined its performance in the process. Thus, this analysis has been used in the participation of the legal representative of the FROB in the hearing of ratification of the experts held between January 12 and 16, and has inspired, in part, the content of the appeal filed by the FROB on February 23 against the order by which the Judge imposes high bails on certain defendants, among which, as I said before, are both BFA and Bankia, both directly or indirectly owned by the State. Likewise, on March 5, the FROB, through its procedural representation, presented to the court a brief of allegations in which the main conclusions of the analysis to which I have referred are collected. At the same time, I must inform you that the volume of claims and civil lawsuits from PAHO-related clients has increased in recent months. The civil proceedings that are being conducted relate to the subscription operations of Bankia shares carried out by retail clients, without any complaint having been received to date from the institutional investors who attended the OPS. So far, 2,424 civil lawsuits have been filed against the entity, representing a total claimed amount of db70 million. From these demands, 236 judgments have been issued, of which 85% are against the entity. The BFA-Bankia group has estimated that the contingency for civil lawsuits could rise to a maximum amount of 780 million euros. Despite the fact that all the lawsuits were directed against the entity that launched the OPS, that is, Bankia, the entity presented to the FROB various legal opinions that indicated the possibility of that a possible claim by Bankia against BFA d0 100% owned by the FROB d0 with respect to part of the costs derived from the aforementioned judgments should succeed. Those opinions were based, in essence, on BFA's relationship with the IPO process of its subsidiary Bankia. The Governing Committee of the FROB, after studying the documentation provided by the entity, and obtaining a report from the State Legal Service confirming the existence of legal arguments for a possible claim by Bankia against BFA for this concept, agreed to recognize the Board of Directors of BFA the power to subscribe, where appropriate, an agreement for the distribution of these contingencies between BFA and Bankia, which would limit any claims between the two entities. Naturally, the Governing Committee imposed a number of restrictions on the distribution agreement to ensure that it complied with the principle of efficient use of public resources and, in particular, with the objective of maximising the return on public support granted for the recapitalisation of the group. In effect, the agreement in no case could involve the injection, by the FROB, of additional public funds and required that the negative consequences that could arise for BFA as a result of it be, as far as possible, offset by the distributable dividend that Bankia may distribute for the lower impact on its accounts of the contingency derived from civil claims. In addition, the eventual agreement should refer only and exclusively to the contingencies derived from civil claims, would reach up to the maximum amount estimated by the entity of 780 million euros, and could foresee that BFA would be charged only a tranche of second loss, being the first liability of Bankia. Likewise, the signing of the agreement should entail Bankia's obligation to adopt all necessary measures to minimize the amount of the contingencies, including the claim against any responsible in the facts, whether administrators, managers, employees, insurers or third parties who have participated in the process. After obtaining the authorization of the FROB on February 27, the Board of Directors of BFA approved a transactional agreement between BFA and Bankia for the distribution of contingencies arising from civil lawsuits. Under the agreement, BFA and Bankia agreed to establish the distribution percentages, within the limit of 780 million euros authorized as a maximum amount, corresponding to Bankia the assumption of a section of first responsibility up to 40%, that is, up to a maximum amount of 312 million euros; and BFA the assumption of costs that exceed that amount, up to the maximum amount of 780 million euros, which corresponds to 60% of the maximum amount to be distributed. These amounts, db312 million in Bankia and db468 million in BFA, have been provisioned by the entities in their respective annual accounts for December 2014. I sincerely believe that this agreement is balanced and favors the stability of the listed entity, which benefits its controlling shareholder who is none other than the State through the FROB. 3. BANK OF MADRID Allow me now to dwell on the recent actions taken in relation to Banco de Madrid. On March 10, the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) announced its decision to consider BPA as a foreign financial institution subject to a major money laundering concern under Section 311 of the USA Patriot Act. Additionally, FinCEN issued a resolution proposal in this regard that would consist of: (i) prohibit U.S. financial institutions from opening or maintaining accounts in the name of BPA or any entity in its group, including Banco de Madrid; and (ii) require U.S. financial institutions to implement special diligence measures to prevent accounts they have opened to other entities from being used to process operations involving BPA or any entity in its group. As a result of this decision by the US authorities, all the group's entities, including Banco de Madrid, which is 100% owned by EPS, saw their operations in dollars severely damaged and their operations in the European wholesale markets significantly affected. In addition, the decision had an acute reputational impact that was significantly aggravated by the arrest in Andorra of the CEO of BPA, who was also the CEO of Banco de Madrid. Additionally, on the weekend that began on Friday, March 13, the press echoed the decision of the Standing Committee of the Commission for the Prevention of Money Laundering and Monetary Offenses d0 chaired by the General Secretariat of the Treasury and Financial Policy d0 to open a disciplinary file against said bank, the board of directors and the secretary general. for possible breaches of current regulations on the prevention of money laundering, derived from the inspection carried out by the Executive Service for the Prevention of Money Laundering (Sepblac). At the same time, Sepblac transferred the file opened to the Anti-Corruption Prosecutor's Office. I am not going to detail here the sequence of events and, in particular, the actions of the Bank of Spain to deal with the situation. The Bank of Spain itself made public last Friday a detailed account of them. However, let me emphasize that the actions of the US authorities and the rest of the news that appeared publicly meant an appreciable destabilization of Banco de Madrid and, in particular, a rapid breakdown of the liquidity situation of the entity. Since March 11, that is, the day after the publication of the news about the performance of FinCEN, the outflow of funds reached 124 million euros in the following three days, that is, more than 20% of total deposits. Thus, the liquidity available on March 16 did not cover the amount necessary to meet the outflows of funds scheduled for that same day, which placed the entity in a state of imminent inviability or insolvency, as it could not meet its obligations. Consequently, on 16 March, the provisional directors of Banco de Madrid requested voluntary insolvency proceedings in accordance with Law 22/2003, of 9 July, on bankruptcy, and decreed the closure of the entity and the suspension of its operations. Subsequently, on March 17, the Commercial Court No. 1 of Madrid sent an official letter to the FROB by which it summoned it, within fourteen days, to inform it if it was going to open a restructuring or resolution process of those provided for by Law 9/2012, of November 14, on the restructuring or resolution of credit institutions. And this in compliance with the provisions of the aforementioned Law, which requires suspending the processing of the application for the contest until the FROB rules on the appropriateness or not of the resolution of the entity in question. To facilitate the response of the FROB to the Court, and taking into account the distribution of competences regarding the opening of resolution processes of credit institutions, on March 18 the Executive Committee of the Bank of Spain informed the FROB that it was not appropriate to open the resolution process ordered because the reasons of public interest whose concurrence requires article 19.1 of Law 9/2012 for this purpose were not appreciated. The Governing Committee of the FROB reached the same conclusion regarding the inadmissibility of the opening of a resolution process of the Banco de Madrid entity within the framework of Law 9/2012 and so communicated it to the judge, on March 20; that is, after consuming only two of the fourteen working days available. This made it possible that, a few days later, on March 25, the Court issued the order declaring bankruptcy. The opening of a resolution process of a financial institution, as a substitute for bankruptcy, requires two fundamental conditions: (i) the classification of the entity as non-viable and (ii) the assessment of the existence of a public interest in need of protection and whose defense is not safeguarded in an ordinary bankruptcy liquidation process. The resolution is therefore presented as an alternative to ordinary insolvency proceedings in cases where the application of insolvency law to non-viable entities could pose problems for the stability of the financial system or other harmful effects on the general interest. The extreme reputational impact suffered by Banco de Madrid as a result of the various news in the press about its activities and those of the group to which it belongs affected its operations and business in such a way that, despite its comfortable solvency ratios, it determined its imminent non-viability; concurring, therefore, the first of the conditions required for the opening of a resolution process. However, the second of the conditions had yet to be met, since it could hardly be concluded that a possible liquidation of the Banco de Madrid could significantly affect the stability of the system. In fact, Banco de Madrid's balance sheet only represents 0.04% of the sector's total assets and barely presents financing from other credit institutions. On the other hand, its operations are quite unique in being specialized in the asset management business, which differentiates it from the commercial banking model that predominates in the rest of the sector. Therefore, the chances of contagion were very small, as the facts have since confirmed. In addition, critical functions that the entity developed and that could impact on the real economy were not detected, nor were sectors or regions identified in which the disappearance of the entity could have a relevant impact. Likewise, the declaration of the entity in resolution would have required the maintenance of its operations, for which it would have required the immediate contribution of public funds in the form of liquidity support by the FROB, given the impossibility for the Eurosystem to continue financing entities considered non-viable. That is, in a resolution process, the State should have lent funds to the entity, thus increasing the risk assumed by the public treasury, which would only have been possible in the presence of an overriding public interest to safeguard, which was not the case in this case. In the days following the declaration of Banco de Madrid's bankruptcy, it has been found that there are no significant collateral effects in the rest of the sector. In any case, the speed with which the Bank of Spain and the FROB have proceeded, has allowed the Deposit Guarantee Fund to initiate the procedures for the satisfaction of the guaranteed amounts (with a maximum of 100,000 euros per holder), which will be completed in the coming days. In this way, more than 14,000 depositors of the entity will soon be able to recover all of their investment, while about 500 will be temporarily affected by exceeding their deposits the maximum guaranteed volume. In any case, with the information available today, depending on the equity situation of the entity, it is very likely that the latter can also recover almost all of their investment within the framework of the bankruptcy process. For their part, the participants of the investment funds linked to Banco de Madrid, must wait, after the replacement by the CNMV of the manager or depositary as the case may be, for their operations to be restored, which, as reported by the CNMV itself, is expected to happen in a short period of time. 4. EUROPEAN RESOLUTION RULES Turning to the last part of my speech, I inform you of the latest developments that have been made in the framework of the constitution of the Single Resolution Mechanism (SRM). Most Member States of the European Union are currently immersed in the process of transposing the European Directive for recovery and resolution. As I said in my previous hearing, the directive entails a fundamental change in the strategy for managing banking crises, as it imposes the main assumption of the costs of resolution on shareholders and creditors, so as to minimise the need to provide public resources to avoid damaging financial stability. This strategy requires preventive action by banks, so that their corporate organization and the structure of their balance sheet facilitate the maintenance of their essential activities, without the help of external resources, in cases where the entities reach the point of non-viability. In Spain, the transposition of the Directive will be carried out through the approval of the Bill for the recovery and resolution of credit institutions and investment services companies, a project that, as you well know, was submitted by the Government to this same Economy Commission on March 10. The project separates the attribution of the competences in matters of preventive resolution or resolution planning, which will correspond to the Bank of Spain and the CNMV (each in its field of action), from the competences in matters of executive resolution, which will correspond to the FROB. From the approval of the standard, it will be led by an executive president with full dedication to this task. This scheme of sharing resolution actions across more than one agency is unique in the European context, as all resolution powers at national level are usually assigned to an autonomous unit or agency located within the prudential supervisor. However, in the Spanish case, the formula adopted in the Bill constitutes a reasonable balance between the convenience of taking advantage of the experience acquired by the FROB in the execution of restructuring and resolution plans in recent years and mitigating, at the same time, the risk of the appearance of inefficiencies and coordination problems with the actions of prudential supervisors. Given that these risks are presumably more located in preventive resolution functions than in executive ones, the assignment of the former to the Bank of Spain, in the case of banks, contributes to increasing the efficiency of the model. However, given the relative complexity of the scheme, it will be essential to maintain adequate coordination between the different agencies involved. In any case, the relevant resolution policies for most of the Spanish banking sector will have to be adopted within the framework of the Single Resolution Mechanism, which became operational on 1 January 2015 and will have full powers from next year. At the moment, the appointment and incorporation of its President, Vice-President and the four Directors of the Single Resolution Board (SRB), provided for in the regulations, has already taken place, and the recruitment of the necessary staff to correctly carry out their functions is in the process of being completed. Allow me at this point to emphasize the good news that has meant the appointment of Antonio Carrascosa -General Director of the FROB, until a few weeks ago- as one of the directors of the SRB, and to point out the appointment as the new Director General of the FROB of Jaime Ponce, who meets all the requirements for the proper performance of the responsibilities that he must assume. 5. CONCLUSIONS And I conclude, President. As you have seen from my speech, since my last appearance, the activities of the FROB have continued the tendency to concentrate on aspects related to the management and eventual disposal of its shares in financial institutions and collaboration with justice in the Identification of possible irregular practices by the former administrators of the entities that should have received public support. In this way, the normalisation of the situation of our financial system has allowed the actions of the FROB more directly related to its resolution powers, such as those that the FROB had to carry out in the framework of the intense process of reorganization, recapitalization and restructuring of our financial sector, to lose relative weight. In any case, I believe that, a few months before this Parliament approves the rule that will introduce a relevant change in the framework of action for bank resolution policies in our country, it is not a bad time to take stock of the work done. Of course, it is not for me to assess the performance of the body I have chaired since June 2012. However, I believe that today it can be considered an objective fact, especially following the overall assessment of the European banking system made by the ECB and the national supervisory authorities to which I referred at the beginning of my speech, that the strategy followed has fulfilled its fundamental objectives, by contributing to improving the structure of our banking system. strengthen its equity position and increase its resilience to adverse developments, which is essential to preserve such an important public good as financial stability. However, the challenges that the FROB will have to face in the near future are not minor. In particular, the successful completion of the ongoing divestment process, of which only the sale remains, at the moment in which market conditions are propitious, of the stakes that the FROB holds in Bankia and BMN, will be essential to reduce as much as possible the bulky volume of public resources that have had to be used to strengthen the system. In addition, in the coming months, the FROB must adjust its structures and internal organization, in accordance with the tasks assigned to it by the standard in process and its role in the new Single Resolution Board to whose implementation and effective development of its functions it must contribute with the maximum possible determination. Thanks a lot.

Adems, los ejercicios constataron la apreciable resistencia de las entidades espaolas a perturbaciones muy severas, pues todas ellas disponan en el momento de la publicacin de los resultados de un margen significativo de capital sobre los umbrales mnimos establecidos para distintos escenarios macroeconmicos. En concreto, las entidades espaolas sometidas a planes de resolucin o restructuracin superaron holgadamente los ejercicios con datos a 31 de diciembre de 2013, con la nica excepcin de Liberbank, que arroj un dficit minsculo de capital que estaba ya sobradamente cubierto en la fecha de la publicacin de los resultados. Pasando a darles cuenta de la actividad reciente del FROB, permtanme que estructure mi presentacin en cuatro apartados. As, en la primera parte de mi intervencin les informar sobre las actuaciones regulares del FROB, que cubren (i) los procesos de desinversin acometidos, en particular Catalunya Banc, (ii) la labor desarrollada en el seguimiento de los planes de resolucin o reestructuracin en curso, (iii) la culminacin de los arbitrajes sobre productos hbridos, (iv) las actuaciones judiciales e investigaciones efectuadas y (v) la evolucin de la Sareb. En la segunda parte me detendr, por su evidente relevancia, en las actuaciones especficamente relacionadas con la Oferta Pblica de Suscripcin de acciones (OPS) de Bankia. LAS PRINCIPALES ACTIVIDADES DEL FROB Paso, entonces, a exponer las principales actividades del FROB en los ltimos meses. i) Los procesos de desinversin Como sus Seoras recordarn, en julio de 2013, la Comisin Rectora del FROB adjudic a N+1 Corporate Finance, S.A. el contrato de anlisis y eventual venta de Catalunya Banc. La recomendacin principal que se desprenda del informe elaborado por el consultor era la venta previa de una cartera especfica, compuesta por prstamos hipotecarios, con un valor bruto aproximado de 6.400 millones de euros, con escaso valor comercial (cartera Hrcules). Esta venta permitira aumentar el atractivo de la entidad -una vez desprovista de la cartera mencionada-, que se enajenara en una segunda fase. Esta estrategia se justificaba por el beneficio potencial que representaba atraer a dos tipos de inversores: por un lado, sociedades interesadas estrictamente en la gestin de activos -con inters en pujar por la cartera Hrcules- y, por otro, entidades financieras dispuestas a adquirir el negocio bancario de Catalunya Banc, una vez adecuadamente saneada.
