Title: Keynote address at the XI Meeting of the Banking Sector, organized by IESE
text: 10.12.2015 Keynote address XI Meeting of the Banking Sector/IESE Luis M. Linde Governor Good morning, everyone. First of all, I would like to thank IESE and its president, Professor Toribio, for their invitation to the opening of this XI Meeting of the Banking Sector, an outstanding and always very interesting annual event in our financial calendar. With the end of 2015 approaching, I think it may be appropriate to draw up a balance sheet of the current situation of our banking system. I will review the main milestones of its recent evolution, its current situation and deal with the perspectives and challenges we face. I can begin by recalling that the Spanish banking system was not affected by different destabilizing practices widespread in other banking systems, such as the storage of risks in "vehicles" outside the scope of the supervisory review, or the investment in complex products, of low liquidity or inadequate valuation, or not always clear distribution of risks, factors that, as we know, They were instrumental in triggering the global financial crisis starting in 2007. However, this strength did not mean that Spanish banks were free of a series of risks that, together with tensions in the euro zone and turbulence in European debt markets, explain the crisis in the sector from 2010 onwards. These risks were essentially four: an oversizing of the sector, the result of an accelerating, clearly unsustainable, expansion of credit investment, favoured by a loose context of interest rates; excessive and also unsustainable exposure to the real estate sector; insufficient own resources to cover the risks assumed; and, finally, weaknesses in corporate governance systems in a relevant segment of the sector, savings banks. With the perspective that the intervening years give us, we can remember and assess the most important decisions that were taken to face the crisis and undertake the reform of the sector. In 2008, shortly after the outbreak of the crisis in the United States, the Financial Asset Acquisition Fund was created, and in mid-2009, the Fund for Orderly Bank Restructuring (FROB), with the aim of facilitating processes of integration of viable entities, strengthening the solvency of the resulting entities and providing a quick solution for non-viable entities. In 2010 the legal regime of savings banks was reformed and in 2011 additional steps were taken to strengthen the level of solvency of Spanish credit institutions, demanding higher minimum levels of capital of maximum quality, with the formula, which is already history, of the requirements of "main capital". However, the second recession that affected our economy from 2011, the magnitude of the risks assumed in the previous years of expansion and the contagion effects of the euro area crisis made the measures adopted insufficient. This forced us to undertake, with the help of the European Union, a more radical and transparent process of restructuring and reordering our banking system that was embodied in the Memorandum of Understanding of July 20, 2012 with two basic chapters: the recapitalization and restructuring of the Spanish banking sector and an important reform agenda. The first of these chapters was carried out in three lines of action: first, the determination of the capital needs of each institution through an analysis of the quality of the assets and a stress test in an adverse scenario; secondly, the recapitalisation, restructuring or orderly resolution of weaker institutions, based on plans designed to address identified capital shortfalls; and finally, the segregation of damaged assets related to exposures to the real estate sector. To identify capital needs, two stress tests were carried out involving the main Spanish banking groups that together represented around 90% of the sector's assets. The first of these, of an aggregate nature, was carried out in June 2012 and served to limit the capital deficit of the system. Subsequently, between July and the end of September 2012, the second test was carried out in order to determine the capital needs of each entity. The results of this second test showed maximum capital needs, that is, hypothetical needs in the worst case scenario, of 57,000 million euros. Finally, the volume of public aid provided by the FROB and financed through the European Stability Mechanism within the framework of the Financial Assistance Programme was lower than the identified needs. Of the 10 entities with capital needs, 2 were able to cover them by their own means, through capital increases, repurchase of subordinated debt and liquidation of assets. A number of measures were applied in the remaining banks, including the assumption of losses by shareholders and holders of hybrid instruments, the segregation of real estate assets and the divestment of other assets. After these adjustments, public aid stood at 39,000 million, of which 37,000 million were allocated to entities majority owned by the FROB. The recapitalisation of the banking sector was completed in the first quarter of 2013. The granting of public aid was subject to compliance with strict conditions set and supervised by the competition authorities of the European Commission, so the entities had to submit restructuring and resolution plans that included commitments to reduce offices and employees, reorient the business model and divestment in non-strategic assets. Overall, since 2007, the number of banking groups has fallen by 40%, the number of branches has fallen by 30% from 2008 peaks and there has been a 25% reduction in the number of employees. An important element of the reform was the clean-up and reduction of banks' exposure to the real estate sector, which was achieved by increasing the already stringent provisioning requirements and by transferring real estate assets to the Bank Restructuring Asset Management Company (Sareb). The total amount of assets transferred was 51,000 million euros. As a result, at the end of 2014, the level of exposure of Spanish depository institutions to real estate development activity, net of provisions, had been reduced since 2011 by around db150 billion, around 62% of the exposure existing at that time. As regards the second chapter of the Programme agreed with the European Union, important reforms were carried out in the regulation of the banking sector. Of particular note is the new crisis management framework established in 2012, later replaced by the harmonised European framework of the Recovery and Resolution Directive, and the 2013 reform of the savings bank sector. It should also be remembered that in seven years, between 2008 and 2014, the sector endowed, against results or reserves, provisions for more than 280,000 million euros. If this figure is added to the capital increases carried out in the same period, a total increase in own resources is achieved between 2008 and 2014, excluding public aid, of 330,000 million euros, which represents more than 30% of our average GDP for that period and gives an idea of the effort made by the sector. The process of restructuring the banking system was completed in January 2014, after the European Commission, the ECB and the IMF verified that the objectives and conditions set out in the Memorandum of Understanding were met and it was, let's say, endorsed or ratified a year ago d0 we have experienced so many events that it seems that more time ago, but only one year has passed d0 in November 2014, with the conclusion of the balance sheet analysis and stress test exercises prior to the launch of the Single Supervisory Mechanism. Of all this process, it is only pending to carry out the exit and sale strategy of the entities in which the FROB participates. Current situation of the financial system The Spanish banking system is currently in a solid and solvent situation. We may recall that the ECB's comprehensive assessment exercise of banks a year ago, as part of the preparatory work for the implementation of the Single Supervisory Mechanism, revealed, judging by the minor shortcomings in valuations or provisioning, that, in general, The balance sheets of Spanish banks rigorously reflected the risks arising from their activity. Thus, the incidences found in this review implied an average reduction of 14 basis points in the ordinary capital ratio (CET1) of Spanish banks, compared to an average impact three times higher in the participating European banks. The other component of this ECB's global assessment exercise, the stress test in the face of an adverse macroeconomic scenario, also showed satisfactory results for the Spanish banking sector. On average, the adverse scenario would have meant a reduction of 144 basis points on the CET1 capital ratio of Spanish banks. In the case of European entities, this impact would have amounted to 300 basis points. This positive development has continued over the past year. Fundamentally, as a result of the capital increases carried out in the period, capital ratios have increased by more than 80 basis points compared to their level in June 2014, comfortably exceeding the regulatory minimums. The highest quality capital ratio, ordinary equity tier 1 (CET1), of all Spanish depository institutions stood at 12.4% last June; and the total capital ratio reached 14.3%. Another indicator of the improvement in the soundness of the Spanish banking system is the reduction of assets classified as non-performing loans. In June 2015 they accounted for 4.9% of the balance sheet, when a year earlier this percentage was 6%. If we focus on business in Spain, total non-performing assets fell by almost 20% between June 2014 and June 2015, in line with the recovery in economic activity, which has allowed the NPL ratio to fall to 11.2%. And refinanced or restructured credit to the resident private sector is also being significantly reduced. The most recent profitability data confirm the trend towards normalization of the sector. Following losses in 2012, driven by the sharp increase in impairment provisions, depository institutions recovered positive results in 2013 and have continued to improve since then. The total consolidated results of Spanish depository institutions in the first half of 2015 confirm this recovery, reaching more than 11,000 million euros, representing an increase of close to 39% compared to those registered in the same period of 2014. All margins improved by more than 10% year-over-year, including net interest income, as a result of the greater fall in the average cost of liabilities compared to the average return on assets. Likewise, following the trend of recent quarters, the decrease in non-performing loans in most entities has reduced provisions for impairment of assets, which contributes to the improvement in results. However, it must be borne in mind that part of this improvement is due to the results of the business outside Spain. The profitability of the activity in Spain is subject, like that of other countries in our environment, to significant pressures. In terms of funding, Spanish depository institutions net-banks reduced their appeal to the Eurosystem. On the other hand, private sector deposits in Spain experienced a slight decline, highlighting the response of families and companies to low interest rates, which is translating into a recomposition of their savings between deposits and other types of investments. With regard to credit to the resident private sector, it continued to show negative year-on-year rates of change in October, although with increasingly lower figures in absolute terms, that is, approaching a zero variation, which means that credit volumes can stabilize in 2016 for the first time since 2011. Perspectives and challenges The environment in which the banking business develops today is characterized by technological changes, regulatory developments, growing competitive pressure and, of course, low interest rates. Of the many challenges facing banking, I will focus on low profitability and adaptation to the new regulatory framework, which are obviously not exclusive problems of the Spanish banking system. Firstly, the profitability of the activity in Spain. Although the consolidated results of the Spanish banking system have improved significantly compared to the significant losses recorded in 2012, the current levels of return on equity in the business in Spain, at around 5%, are below the estimates of the cost of capital, although we all know that these estimates have, Inevitably, a fairly wide margin. There are three main elements of pressure on the income statement of the business in Spain. In the current environment of very low interest rates, the spread between asset and liability interest rates is historically very low at close to 1%. The sustainability over time of net interest income in situations such as this, in which the rate differential is so demanding, depends to a large extent on the existence of a level of activity that allows to compensate -via quantities- the scarce contribution to the income statement that occurs via prices. This is not the case at present, as the level of banking activity is still low, which is the second element of pressure on the income statement. The third of these factors is the still significant volume of non-performing assets (NPLs and foreclosed) that remain on banks' balance sheets, although, as I noted earlier, NPLs are declining significantly since the economy has recovered growth rates to around 3%. But Spanish banks have alternatives to adjust their strategy and increase their profitability: First, the Spanish banking system still maintains a density of branches higher than the European average, so this process may still have some travel. Second, our banks, like those of other developed countries, can and will undoubtedly deepen their efforts to innovate technology and digital adaptation; and, thirdly, it is clear that the path of consolidation cannot be considered closed or exhausted, not only in Spain, but in the area of the Single Supervisory Mechanism as a whole. The second challenge I wanted to refer to is adapting to the new standards of regulation and supervision. The introduction of new liquidity and leverage ratios, higher capital requirements, or new resolution requirements are some of the main regulatory requirements that make up the new scenario. I am going to dwell for a moment on the introduction of new requirements in the field of the resolution of entities, given that the G-20, at its summit last November, approved the proposal for requirements of what we all call, for its acronym in English, TLAC (Total Loss Absorbing Capacity) designed by the Financial Stability Board of whose Steering Committee the Bank of Spain is a member. This new regulation will apply to the 30 banks considered to be of systemic importance globally, and will begin to enter into force, even with some exceptions in a first phase, in 2019 and in a second phase, already with the calibration that may be the final one, in 2022. The TLAC requirements determine a minimum volume of eligible liabilities for loss absorption and recapitalization of institutions, available in the event of resolution of the entity, and constitute a requirement similar, although raised in other terms, to the requirement called MREL (Minimum Requirement for own funds and Eligible Liabilities), introduced into European legislation through the Directive on the Recovery and Resolution of Credit Institutions, already transposed into our legal system through Law 11/2015 and its Development Decree, published last November. The Directive, together with the Single Resolution Mechanism, which became operational on 1 January this year, establish a common European framework that should allow for orderly resolution with uniform criteria for all institutions under its jurisdiction. This new resolution framework represents a fundamental change in the banking crisis management strategy, as it imposes the main assumption of resolution costs on shareholders and creditors, thus minimising the possibility that it would be necessary to provide public resources, while trying to preserve financial stability. The new European rules will cause changes in the structure of the balance sheet of institutions, since they must have not only a minimum volume of instruments computable as regulatory capital, but also a minimum volume of other liability instruments capable of absorbing losses in the event of resolution. On the other hand, from the supervisory point of view, one year has just passed since the launch of the Single Supervisory Mechanism, and it is expected that supervisory harmonisation (by approaching the best practices in each area) will generally tend to increase the level of demand for all European banks. And I conclude. After the intense clean-up process carried out since mid-2012 and the improvement achieved in asset quality and liquidity and solvency, our banking sector is ready to face the challenges that arise. But we must recognize that the picture is very different from the one that existed before the crisis: today it is more demanding, more competitive, more subject to uncertainties and difficulties caused by technological changes, including payment systems, regulatory innovations, reputational problems and the demand for improvement in relation to customers. plus a long etcetera. Therefore, the motto under which this Meeting has been placed, "Banking in the new competitive environment", could not be more relevant and timely. Thank you very much for your attention.
text_original: 10.12.2015 Discurso de apertura XI Encuentro del Sector Bancario/IESE Luis M. Linde Gobernador Buenos das a todos. En primer lugar, quiero agradecer al IESE y a su presidente, el profesor Toribio, su invitacin a la apertura de este XI Encuentro del Sector Bancario, una cita anual destacada y siempre muy interesante en nuestro calendario financiero. Estando prximo el cierre del ejercicio 2015, creo que puede ser oportuno esbozar un balance de la situacin actual de nuestro sistema bancario. Repasar los principales hitos de su evolucin reciente, su situacin actual y tratar de las perspectivas y retos a los que nos enfrentamos. Puedo empezar recordando que el sistema bancario espaol no estuvo afectado por diferentes prcticas desestabilizadoras extendidas en otros sistemas bancarios, como el almacenamiento de riesgos en vehculos fuera del alcance de la revisin supervisora, o la inversin en productos complejos, de escasa liquidez o inadecuada valoracin, o no siempre reparto claro de riesgos, factores que, como sabemos, jugaron un papel decisivo en el desencadenamiento de la crisis financiera global a partir de 2007. Sin embargo, esa fortaleza no supona que la banca espaola estuviese libre de una serie de riesgos que, junto con las tensiones en la zona euro y las turbulencias en los mercados de deuda europeos, explican la crisis del sector a partir de 2010. Estos riesgos eran, esencialmente, cuatro: un sobredimensionamiento del sector, fruto de una expansin acelerada, claramente insostenible, de la inversin crediticia, favorecida por un contexto laxo de tipos de inters; una excesiva y tambin insostenible exposicin al sector inmobiliario; unos recursos propios insuficientes para cubrir los riesgos asumidos; y, por ltimo, debilidades en los sistemas de gobierno corporativo en un segmento relevante del sector, las cajas de ahorro. Con la perspectiva que nos dan los aos transcurridos, podemos recordar y valorar las decisiones ms importantes que se adoptaron para enfrentar la crisis y acometer la reforma del sector. En 2008, poco despus del estallido de la crisis en Estados Unidos, se cre el Fondo de Adquisicin de Activos Financieros, y a mediados de 2009, el Fondo de Reestructuracin Ordenada Bancaria (FROB), con el objetivo de facilitar procesos de integracin de entidades viables, reforzar la solvencia de las entidades resultantes y aportar una solucin rpida para las entidades no viables. En 2010 se reform el rgimen jurdico de las cajas de ahorro y en 2011 se dieron pasos adicionales para reforzar el nivel de solvencia de las entidades de crdito espaolas, exigiendo mayores niveles mnimos de capital de mxima calidad, con la frmula, que ya es historia, de las exigencias de capital principal. No obstante, la segunda recesin que afect a nuestra economa a partir de 2011, la magnitud de los riesgos asumidos en los aos anteriores de expansin y los efectos de contagio de la crisis de la zona euro hicieron que las medidas adoptadas resultasen insuficientes. Esto oblig a acometer, con la ayuda de la Unin Europea, un proceso de saneamiento y reordenacin de nuestro sistema bancario ms radical y transparente que qued plasmado en el Memorando de Entendimiento de 20 de julio de 2012 con dos captulos bsicos: la recapitalizacin y reestructuracin del sector bancario espaol y una importante agenda de reformas. El primero de esos captulos se llev a cabo en tres lneas de actuacin: en primer lugar, la determinacin de las necesidades de capital de cada entidad mediante un anlisis de la calidad de los activos y una prueba de resistencia ante un escenario adverso; en segundo lugar, la recapitalizacin, reestructuracin o resolucin ordenada de las entidades ms dbiles, sobre la base de los planes diseados para abordar los dficit de capital identificados; y por ltimo, la segregacin de los activos daados relacionados con exposiciones al sector inmobiliario. Para la identificacin de las necesidades de capital, se realizaron dos pruebas de resistencia en las que participaron los principales grupos bancarios espaoles que representaban, en conjunto, alrededor del 90 % de los activos del sector. La primera de ellas, de carcter agregado, se realiz en junio de 2012 y sirvi para acotar el dficit de capital del sistema. Posteriormente, entre julio y finales de septiembre de 2012, se llev a cabo la segunda prueba con el fin de determinar las necesidades de capital de cada entidad. Los resultados de esta segunda prueba arrojaron unas necesidades mximas de capital, es decir, necesidades hipotticas en el escenario ms adverso, de 57.000 millones de euros. Finalmente, el volumen de ayudas pblicas aportadas por el FROB y financiadas a travs del Mecanismo Europeo de Estabilidad en el marco del Programa de Asistencia Financiera fue inferior a las necesidades identificadas. De las 10 entidades con necesidades de capital, 2 fueron capaces de cubrirlas por sus propios medios, mediante ampliaciones de capital, recompra de deuda subordinada y liquidacin de activos. En el resto de entidades se aplicaron una serie de medidas, incluida la asuncin de prdidas por parte de accionistas y tenedores de instrumentos hbridos, la segregacin de activos inmobiliarios y la desinversin de otros activos. Tras estos ajustes, las ayudas pblicas se situaron en 39.000 millones, de los que 37.000 millones se destinaron a las entidades participadas mayoritariamente por el FROB. La recapitalizacin del sector bancario se pudo dar por terminada en el primer trimestre de 2013. La concesin de ayudas pblicas estuvo sujeta al cumplimiento de estrictas condiciones fijadas y supervisadas por las autoridades de Competencia de la Comisin Europea, por lo que las entidades tuvieron que presentar planes de reestructuracin y resolucin que contemplaban compromisos de reduccin de oficinas y empleados, reorientacin del modelo negocio y desinversin en activos no estratgicos. En conjunto, desde 2007, el nmero de grupos bancarios se ha reducido en un 40 %, el nmero de oficinas ha descendido un 30 % con respecto a los mximos de 2008 y se ha producido una reduccin del 25 % en el nmero de empleados. Un elemento importante de la reforma fue el saneamiento y la reduccin de la exposicin de las entidades al sector inmobiliario, que se logr mediante el incremento de los ya exigentes requisitos de provisiones y mediante el traspaso de activos inmobiliarios a la Sociedad de Gestin de Activos Procedentes de la Reestructuracin Bancaria (Sareb). El importe total de activos traspasados fue de 51.000 millones de euros. Con ello, a finales de 2014, el nivel de exposicin de las entidades de depsito espaolas a la actividad de promocin inmobiliaria, neto de provisiones, se haba reducido desde 2011 en unos 150 mil millones de euros, cerca de un 62 % de la exposicin existente entonces. En cuanto al segundo captulo del Programa acordado con la Unin Europea, se llevaron a cabo importantes reformas en la regulacin del sector bancario. Cabe destacar el nuevo marco de gestin de crisis establecido en 2012, -sustituido posteriormente por el marco europeo armonizado de la Directiva de Recuperacin y Resolucin-, y la reforma del sector de cajas de ahorro de 2013. Cabe tambin recordar que en siete aos, entre 2008 y 2014, el sector dot, contra resultados o reservas, provisiones por ms de 280.000 millones de euros. Si a esta cifra se le suman las ampliaciones de capital llevadas a cabo en ese mismo perodo, se alcanza un reforzamiento total de los recursos propios entre 2008 y 2014, sin contar ayudas pblicas, de 330.000 millones de euros, lo que representa ms del 30 % de nuestro PIB medio de ese perodo y da idea del esfuerzo realizado por el sector. El proceso de reestructuracin del sistema bancario concluy en enero de 2014, despus de que la Comisin Europea, el BCE y el FMI constataran el cumplimiento de los objetivos y las condiciones recogidas en el Memorando de Entendimiento y qued, digamos, avalado o ratificado hace ahora un ao hemos vivido tantos acontecimientos que parece que hace ms tiempo, pero slo ha pasado un ao- en noviembre de 2014, con la conclusin de los ejercicios de anlisis de balances y pruebas de resistencia previos a la puesta en marcha del Mecanismo nico de Supervisin. De todo este proceso queda pendiente slo llevar a cabo la estrategia de salida y venta de las entidades participadas por el FROB. Situacin actual del sistema financiero El sistema bancario espaol presenta en la actualidad una situacin slida y solvente. Podemos recordar que el ejercicio de evaluacin global de las entidades bancarias realizado por el BCE hace ahora un ao, en el marco de los trabajos preparatorios para la puesta en funcionamiento del Mecanismo nico de Supervisin, revel, a juzgar por las menores insuficiencias en las valoraciones o en la dotacin de provisiones, que, con carcter general, los balances de las entidades espaolas reflejaban de forma rigurosa los riesgos derivados de su actividad. As, las incidencias encontradas en esta revisin implicaron una reduccin media de 14 puntos bsicos de la ratio de capital ordinario (CET1) de los bancos espaoles, frente a un impacto medio tres veces superior en los bancos europeos participantes. El otro componente de ese ejercicio de evaluacin global del BCE, la prueba de resistencia ante un escenario macroeconmico adverso, mostr tambin resultados satisfactorios para el sector bancario espaol. En media, el escenario adverso habra supuesto una reduccin de 144 puntos bsicos sobre la ratio de capital CET1 de los bancos espaoles. En el caso de las entidades europeas este impacto habra ascendido a 300 puntos bsicos. Esta evolucin positiva ha continuado en el ltimo ao. Fundamentalmente, como consecuencia de las ampliaciones de capital realizadas en el perodo, las ratios de capital se han incrementado en ms de 80 puntos bsicos respecto a su nivel en junio de 2014, superndose con holgura los mnimos regulatorios. La ratio de capital de mayor calidad, el capital ordinario de nivel 1 (CET1), del conjunto de entidades de depsito espaolas se situ en junio pasado en el 12,4 %; y la ratio de capital total alcanz el 14,3 %. Otro indicador de la mejora en la solidez del sistema bancario espaol es la reduccin de los activos clasificados como dudosos. En junio de 2015 suponan el 4,9 % del balance, cuando un ao antes este porcentaje era del 6 %. Si nos centramos en los negocios en Espaa, los activos dudosos totales descendieron casi un 20 % entre junio de 2014 y junio de 2015, en lnea con la recuperacin de la actividad econmica, lo que ha permitido que la ratio de morosidad se reduzca hasta situarse en el 11,2 %. Y tambin se viene reduciendo de modo significativo el crdito refinanciado o reestructurado al sector privado residente. Los datos ms recientes de rentabilidad confirman la tendencia a la normalizacin del sector. Tras las prdidas registradas en 2012, motivadas por el fuerte aumento de las provisiones por deterioro de activos, las entidades de depsito recuperaron resultados positivos en 2013 y han continuado mejorando desde entonces. Los resultados consolidados totales de las entidades de depsito espaolas en la primera mitad de 2015, confirman esa recuperacin, alcanzando ms de 11.000 millones de euros, lo que supone un incremento cercano al 39 % respecto a los registrados en el mismo perodo de 2014. Todos los mrgenes mejoran ms del 10 % respecto al ao anterior, incluido el margen de intereses, como consecuencia de la mayor cada del coste medio del pasivo frente a la rentabilidad media del activo. Asimismo, siguiendo la tendencia de los ltimos trimestres, la disminucin en la mayora de las entidades de la morosidad ha reducido las dotaciones de provisiones por deterioro de activos, lo que contribuye a la mejora de los resultados. No obstante, hay que tener en cuenta que parte de esa mejora se debe a los resultados del negocio fuera de Espaa. La rentabilidad de la actividad en Espaa est sujeta, como la de otros pases de nuestro entorno, a importantes presiones. En cuanto a su financiacin, las entidades de depsito espaolas disminuyeron en trminos netos su apelacin al Eurosistema. Por su parte, los depsitos del sector privado en Espaa experimentaron un leve descenso, poniendo de manifiesto la respuesta de familias y empresas a los bajos tipos de inters, que se est traduciendo en una recomposicin de sus ahorros entre depsitos y otro tipo de inversiones. Por lo que respecta al crdito al sector privado residente, segua mostrando en octubre tasas interanuales de variacin negativas, si bien con cifras cada vez menores en trminos absolutos, es decir, acercndose a una variacin cero, lo que significa que los volmenes de crdito pueden estabilizarse en 2016 por primera vez desde 2011. Perspectivas y retos El entorno en el que se desarrolla hoy el negocio bancario se caracteriza por los cambios tecnolgicos, las novedades regulatorias, la presin competitiva creciente y, desde luego, los bajos tipos de inters. De los muchos retos a los que se enfrenta la actividad bancaria voy a centrarme en la baja rentabilidad y en la adaptacin al nuevo marco regulatorio que, evidentemente, no son problemas exclusivos del sistema bancario espaol. En primer lugar, la rentabilidad de la actividad en Espaa. A pesar de que los resultados consolidados del sistema bancario espaol han mejorado de manera notable respecto a las significativas prdidas registradas en 2012, los niveles actuales de la rentabilidad sobre fondos propios en el negocio en Espaa, en torno al 5 %, se sitan por debajo de las estimaciones del coste del capital, aunque todos sabemos que esas estimaciones tienen, inevitablemente, un margen bastante amplio. Son tres los principales elementos de presin sobre la cuenta de resultados del negocio en Espaa. En el entorno actual de tipos de inters muy bajos, el diferencial entre los tipos de inters de activo y los de pasivo se encuentra en niveles histricamente muy reducidos, cercanos al 1 %. La sostenibilidad en el tiempo del margen de intereses en situaciones como sta, en la que el diferencial de tipos es tan exigente, depende en buena medida de la existencia de un nivel de actividad que permita compensar -va cantidades- la escasa aportacin a la cuenta de resultados que se produce va precios. Esto no sucede en la actualidad, ya que el nivel de actividad bancaria es todava reducido, lo que constituye el segundo elemento de presin sobre la cuenta de resultados. El tercero de estos factores es el todava significativo volumen de activos improductivos (dudosos y adjudicados) que permanecen en los balances de las entidades, aunque, como seal anteriormente, los activos dudosos se estn reduciendo de manera significativa desde que la economa ha recuperado tasas de crecimiento en el entorno del 3 %. Pero la banca espaola dispone de alternativas para ajustar su estrategia y aumentar su rentabilidad: Primero, el sistema bancario espaol mantiene todava una densidad de oficinas superior a la media europea, por lo que este proceso puede tener an cierto recorrido. Segundo, nuestra banca, como la de otros pases desarrollados, puede profundizar, y va a hacerlo, sin duda, en su esfuerzo de innovacin tecnolgica y adaptacin digital; y, en tercer lugar, es evidente que la va de la consolidacin no puede darse por cerrada o agotada, no solo en Espaa, sino en el conjunto del rea del Mecanismo nico de Supervisin. El segundo desafo al que quera referirme es la adaptacin a los nuevos estndares de regulacin y supervisin. La introduccin de nuevas ratios de liquidez y de apalancamiento, mayores requerimientos de capital, o nuevas exigencias en materia de resolucin son algunos de los principales requisitos regulatorios que conforman el nuevo panorama. Voy a detenerme un momento en la introduccin de nuevos requisitos en el mbito de la resolucin de las entidades, dado que el G-20, en su cumbre del pasado noviembre, ha aprobado la propuesta de requerimientos de lo que todos llamamos, por sus siglas en ingls, TLAC (Total Loss Absorbing Capacity o Capacidad Total de Absorcin de Prdidas) diseada por el Consejo de Estabilidad Financiera de cuyo Comit Director es miembro el Banco de Espaa. Esta nueva normativa se aplicar a los 30 bancos considerados de importancia sistmica a nivel global, y empezar a entrar en vigor, an con alguna excepcin en una primera fase, en 2019 y en una segunda fase, ya con la calibracin que puede ser la definitiva, en 2022. Los requerimientos de TLAC determinan un volumen mnimo de pasivos elegibles para la absorcin de prdidas y la recapitalizacin de las entidades, disponibles en el caso de resolucin de la entidad, y constituye una exigencia similar, aunque planteada en otros trminos, al requisito denominado MREL (por sus siglas en ingls, Minimum Requirement for own funds and Eligible Liabilities), introducido en la legislacin europea mediante la Directiva de Recuperacin y Resolucin de Entidades de Crdito, ya transpuesta en nuestro ordenamiento jurdico mediante la Ley 11/2015 y su Decreto de desarrollo, publicado el pasado mes de noviembre. La Directiva, junto al Mecanismo nico de Resolucin, que entr en funcionamiento el 1 de enero de este ao, establecen un marco europeo comn que deber permitir una resolucin ordenada y con criterios uniformes de todas las entidades bajo su jurisdiccin. Este nuevo marco de resolucin supone un cambio fundamental en la estrategia de gestin de las crisis bancarias, ya que impone la principal asuncin de los costes de resolucin a los accionistas y acreedores, minimizando, as, la eventualidad de que fuera necesario aportar recursos pblicos, tratando, al mismo tiempo, de preservar la estabilidad financiera. La nueva normativa europea provocar cambios en la estructura del balance de las entidades, ya que debern contar no slo con un volumen mnimo de instrumentos computables como capital regulatorio, sino tambin con un volumen mnimo de otros instrumentos de pasivo susceptibles de absorber prdidas en caso de resolucin. Por otra parte, desde el punto de vista supervisor, se acaba de cumplir un ao de la puesta en funcionamiento del Mecanismo nico de Supervisin, y es de esperar que la armonizacin supervisora (al aproximarse a las prcticas ms rigurosas en cada mbito) tienda, en general, a aumentar el grado de exigencia para todos los bancos europeos. Y concluyo. Despus del intenso proceso de saneamiento llevado a cabo desde mediados de 2012 y la mejora lograda en la calidad de los activos y en liquidez y solvencia, nuestro sector bancario est en disposicin de afrontar los retos que se plantean. Pero hay que reconocer que el panorama es muy diferente del que exista antes de la crisis: hoy es ms exigente, ms competitivo, ms sometido a incertidumbres y dificultades provocadas por los cambios tecnolgicos, incluidos en los sistemas de pagos, las innovaciones regulatorias, los problemas reputacionales y la exigencia de mejora en relacin con la clientela, ms un largo etctera. Por ello, el lema bajo el que se ha puesto este Encuentro, La banca en el nuevo entorno competitivo, no poda ser ms pertinente y oportuno. Muchas gracias por su atencin.

Title: Presentation of the critical edition of "Lessons in Political Economy", by Knut Wicksell. Speech at the headquarters of the ICO Foundation
text: 25.02.2016 Presentation of "Lessons in Political Economy" by Knut WickselI ICO Foundation Luis M. Linde Governor First of all, I want to congratulate the ICO Foundation and its president, Emma Navarro, for persevering and maintaining this initiative, the "Classics of Economics" collection. And I want to thank you for your invitation to close this event. Today we remember Knut Wicksell, whose contributions to economic theory, political economy and their applications in the fields of fiscal and monetary policy are still present a century later. After the presentation of Professor e7lvarez-Rendueles, the first governor in my long life at the Bank of Spain -who has coordinated the work and has written a great introductory study on the life and contribution of Wicksell- my intervention is quite difficult. I will be very brief and try to bore you as little as possible. In his early retirement, Wicksell was an advisor to the Swedish government and the Swedish Central Bank and had, like Alvarez-Rendueles in his introduction, a decisive influence on the committee that proposed the abandonment of the gold standard in 1931 and its replacement by the establishment of inflation targets in the implementation of monetary policy. Wicksell was a multifaceted person, introverted and, in some respects, very radical. Francisco Cabrillo, in his book "Extravagant Economists d0 Etchings Portraits", narrates the belligerent anti-religious attitude of Wicksell, which takes him to spend two months in prison, at the not early age of sixty aces. However, Professor Cabrillo tells us, he enjoyed certain privileges and a civilized treatment that allowed him to write during his stay in prison on the theory of interest for a book of homage to the Austrian economist von Wieser. The Hispanic context that vivimarcsus works and their way of thinking. It faced the social crisis that Sweden was going through at the end of the nineteenth century with a markedly Malthusian approach, concerned with population growth as a brake on the improvement of general welfare. Wicksell, as Professor Alvarez-Rendueles has recalled, was concerned with combating alcoholism and prostitution, as well as with birth control with measures that even Malthus had not come to defend. Wicksell, precursor of modern economic theory In academia, Wicksell was an economist with original ideas, largely a pioneer of contemporary macroeconomic analysis. He developed the formulation of the theories of utility and marginal productivity, framing these works of a "microeconic" optimizing character in a Walrasian framework of general equilibrium. In the fields of economic policy and fiscal theory, it may be recalled that James Buchanan, in his Nobel Prize acceptance speech in 1986 for his work on election theory, praises Wicksell as one of the main inspirers of his analysis. In Buchanan's opinion, Wicksell is the most important precursor of modern theory of choice, which consists of three foundations: methodological individualism, homo economicus, and politics as exchange. Wicksell advocated determining the level of spending in conjunction with the level of income to assess the welfare gains of flat spending for citizens/taxpayers, and arguing for the need for consensus in decision-making, to more accurately reflect the preferences of individuals. Among his contributions to economic theory is his statement on the distribution of income among the factors of production, based on the marginal productivity of each factor. To this result, of a theoretical nature, it adds an assessment in terms of distribution and inequality, giving the Treasury a relevant role in the redistribution of income and wealth. Consequently, he considered that the marginalist mechanism of factor remuneration was not socially efficient and was in favour of a progressive tax system that also taxed capital. Concern about inequality and the role it gives to intervention mark it as a precursor to the welfare state. Wicksell in the field of monetary policy In the field of monetary policy, its contribution was very remarkable. Wicksell's work is at the origin of the evolution of monetary theory after World War I. It can be said that the debates between Keynes and Hayek started from the contributions of Wicksell; In fact, it seems that both considered themselves his heirs. The monetary policy of the major economies between 1870 and the First World War was governed by the more or less strict application of the gold standard. The gold standard promoted price stability. Money does not play an active role in determining real variables, it acted, rather, as a lubricant for economic machinery. By the end of the nineteenth century, the risks of deflaci and stagnation far exceeded those of a hypothetical sustained rise in inflation. This case was dealt with under exceptional circumstances, in particular in the event of a relaxation in the application of the standard, normally due to the financing needs of some administration in the event of war. But Wicksell's thinking went further. His analysis of the interdependence between interest rate and price movements was an innovative and very important contribution. He introduced the concept of "the natural rate of interest," the rate that equalizes the demand for loanable capital and the supply of savings. Wicksell compares the natural rate with the market interest rate of bank loans, so that price stability is achieved when both coincide. If the market rate is below the natural rate, prices will tend to rise until banks raise the interest rate on loans, or the natural rate of interest is reduced by a lower return on capital. The natural rate being an unobservable magnitude, Wicksell proposed keeping the banks' interest rate unchanged as long as prices did not change; If prices rose, the interest rate had to be raised and in the event of a fall in prices, the interest rate had to be lowered. Wicksell presents, therefore, a precedent of monetary policy rules. Thus, it anticipates the approaches of authors such as J. Taylor who in 1993 developed his well-known rule according to which the federal funds rate set by the Federal Reserve Bank responds positively to both inflation and the output gap. This rule, with its limitations, is, as we know, a widely used benchmark today in the evaluation of monetary policy. Wicksell on current monetary policy What would be Wicksell's recommendation if he could sit on the Governing Council of the European Central Bank that will be held in a couple of weeks in Frankfurt? The risk of very low inflation or even a de-anchoring of inflation expectations would not sound strange to him. But, like that, I'm not sure I can answer the question. Throughout the twentieth century, faced with periods of high inflation, partly the results of expansionary policies aimed at promoting activity and employment, a double consensus crystallized in the monetary sphere. First, around the benefits that low and stable inflation represents for economic growth, employment and welfare maximization. Second, about the interest rate as a regulatory instrument of monetary policy, as opposed to a policy based on quantitative objectives. The inflation targeting and use of interest rates as an instrument of monetary policy should be welcomed by Wicksell. Moreover, giving the central bank autonomy to achieve its objectives has constituted an ilsynthesis between rules and discretion which, by straining anti-inflationary credibility, allows greater flexibility in adapting monetary conditions to economic and financial circumstances. I don't think Wicksell objected here either. He advocates compliance with the rules of fiscal balance and the gold standard, although with a certain discretion in the face of exceptional transitory circumstances. The recent international financial crisis has led central banks to rethink this inflation-targeting model and to incorporate considerations relating to financial asset price developments and financial stability in general. In addition, the limits of conventional monetary policies and the instruments used by the monetary authority (basically the interest rate) and the risks of falling into the so-called "liquidity trap" (a possibility already postulated by Keynes in the General Theory) in situations of low inflation rates have also been revealed. Major central banks have sought to address this problem through unconventional monetary policies, interest rate cuts, even to negative rates, and policies aimed at growing their balance sheets through purchases of financial assets, including debts of governments and private institutions. It is worth questioning whether this new monetary paradigm would be too provocative, even for someone with a character as innovative as Wicksell's, or not, but it is the one that has been built during the scams. Again, many thanks to the ICO for their initiative and to all of you for your attention.
text_original: 25.02.2016 Presentaci de Lecciones de Economa Poltica, de Knut WickselI Fundaci ICO Luis M. Linde Gobernador En primer lugar, quiero felicitar a la Fundaci ICO y a su presidenta, Emma Navarro, por perseverar y mantener esta iniciativa, la colecci Clsicos de economa. Y quiero darles las gracias por su invitaci para clausurar este acto. Hoy recordamos a Knut Wicksell, cuyas contribuciones a la teora econica, a la economa poltica y sus aplicaciones en los mbitos de las polticas fiscal y monetaria siguen estando presentes un siglo despus. Tras la exposici del profesor lvarez-Rendueles, primer gobernador en mi larga vida en el Banco de Espa -que ha coordinado la obra y ha escrito un estupendo estudio introductorio sobre la vida y la aportaci de Wicksell-se hace bastante difcil mi intervenci. Voy a ser muy breve y tratar de aburrirles lo menos posible. En sus timos as, ya jubilado, Wicksell fue asesor del gobierno sueco y del Banco Central de Suecia y tuvo, como sela lvarez-Rendueles en su introduccin, una influencia decisiva en el comit que propuso el abandono del patr oro en 1931 y su sustituci por el establecimiento de objetivos de inflaci en la implementaci de la poltica monetaria. Wicksell fue una persona polifactica, de carcter introvertido y, en algunos aspectos, muy radical. Francisco Cabrillo, en su libro Economistas extravagantes  Retratos al aguafuerte, narra la beligerante actitud antirreligiosa de Wicksell, que le lleva pasar dos meses en prisi, a la nada temprana edad de sesenta as. No obstante, nos cuenta el profesor Cabrillo, disfrutde ciertos privilegios y de un trato civilizado que le permitieron escribir durante su estancia en la crcel sobre la teora del inters para un libro de homenaje al economista austraco von Wieser. El contexto histico que vivimarcsus trabajos y su forma de pensar. Afrontla crisis social por la que atravesaba Suecia a finales del siglo XIX con un enfoque marcadamente maltusiano, preocupado por el crecimiento de la poblaci como freno a la mejora del bienestar general. Wicksell, como ha recordado el profesor lvarez-Rendueles, estuvo preocupado por combatir el alcoholismo y la prostituci, as como por el control de la natalidad con medidas que ni siquiera Malthus haba llegado a defender. Wicksell, precursor de la teora econica moderna En el mbito acadmico, Wicksell fue un economista con ideas originales, en gran medida un pionero del anlisis macroeconico contemporneo. Desarrollla formulaci de las teoras de la utilidad y de la productividad marginal, enmarcando estos trabajos de carcter optimizador microeconico en un marco walrasiano de equilibrio general. En los mbitos de la poltica econica y de la teora fiscal se puede recordar que James Buchanan, en su discurso de aceptaci del premio Nobel, en 1986, por sus trabajos en la teora de la elecci plica, elogia Wicksell como uno de los principales inspiradores de su anlisis. En opini de Buchanan, Wicksell es el precursor ms importante de la teora moderna de la elecci plica, que consta de tres fundamentos: el individualismo metodolico, el homo economicus y la poltica como intercambio. Wicksell defendideterminar el nivel de gasto conjuntamente con el nivel de ingresos para evaluar las ganancias de bienestar del gasto plico para los ciudadanos/contribuyentes, y defendila necesidad de consenso en la toma de decisiones, para reflejar de manera ms fiel las preferencias de los individuos. Entre sus aportaciones a la teora econica destaca su enunciado sobre la distribuci de la renta entre los factores de producci, basada en la productividad marginal de cada factor. A este resultado, de carcter teico, le ade una valoraci en trminos de distribuci y desigualdad, otorgando a la Hacienda Plica un papel relevante en la redistribuci de la renta y de la riqueza. En consecuencia, considerque el mecanismo marginalista de retribuci de los factores no era eficiente socialmente y se mostrpartidario de un sistema impositivo progresivo que tambin gravara el capital. La preocupaci por la desigualdad y el papel que otorga a la intervenci plica le selan como precursor del Estado de bienestar. Wicksell en el mbito de las polticas monetarias En el mbito de la poltica monetaria, su contribuci fue muy destacable. Los trabajos de Wicksell estn en el origen de la evoluci de la teora monetaria despus de la I Guerra Mundial. Puede decirse que los debates entre Keynes y Hayek partieron de las aportaciones de Wicksell; de hecho, parece que ambos se consideraban sus herederos. La poltica monetaria de las principales economas entre el a 1870 y la primera guerra mundial se rega por la aplicaci, ms o menos estricta, del patr oro. El patr oro promova la estabilidad de los precios. El dinero no desempeba un papel activo en la determinaci de las variables reales, actuaba, ms bien, como lubricante de la maquinaria econica. A finales del siglo XIX, los riesgos de deflaci y estancamiento superaban ampliamente los de una hipottica elevaci sostenida de la inflaci. Este timo caso se contemplaba bajo circunstancias excepcionales, en particular, en caso de relajaci en la aplicaci del patr oro, debido, normalmente, a las necesidades de financiaci de alguna Administraci Plica en caso de guerra. Pero el pensamiento de Wicksell fue ms all. Su anlisis de la interdependencia entre los movimientos del tipo de inters y los de los precios fue una contribuci innovadora y muy importante. Introdujo el concepto de la tasa natural de inters, la tasa que iguala la demanda de capital prestable y la oferta de ahorro. Wicksell compara la tasa natural con el tipo de inters de mercado de los prstamos bancarios, de forma que la estabilidad de precios se alcanza cuando ambos coincidan. Si el tipo de mercado se sit por debajo de la tasa natural, los precios tendern a subir hasta que los bancos aumenten el tipo de inters de los crditos, o se reduzca la tasa natural de inters por un menor rendimiento del capital. Siendo la tasa natural una magnitud inobservable, Wicksell propona mantener la tasa de inters de los bancos inalterada mientras no cambiasen los precios; si los precios suban se deba subir el tipo de inters y ante una cada de precios se deba rebajar el tipo de inters. Wicksell presenta, por tanto, un antecedente de reglas de poltica monetaria. Se anticipa, as, a los planteamientos de autores como J. Taylor que en 1993 desarrollsu conocida regla conforme a la cual la tasa de los fondos federales que fija el Banco de la Reserva Federal responde positivamente tanto a la inflaci, como a la brecha del producto. Esta regla, a con sus limitaciones, es como sabemos, un referente muy utilizado hoy en la evaluaci de la poltica monetaria. Wicksell ante la poltica monetaria actual Cul sera la recomendaci de Wicksell si pudiera sentarse en el Consejo de Gobierno del Banco Central Europeo que se va a celebrar en un par de semanas en Frankfurt? El riesgo de una inflaci muy baja o, incluso, de un desanclaje de las expectativas de inflaci no le sonara raro. Pero, a as, no estoy seguro de poder responder a la pregunta. A lo largo del siglo XX, frente a perodos de inflaci elevada, en parte resultados de polticas expansivas que pretendan promover la actividad y el empleo, cristalizun doble consenso en el mbito monetario. Primero, en torno de los beneficios que una inflaci baja y estable representa para el crecimiento econico, el empleo y la maximizaci del bienestar. Segundo, acerca de la tasa de inters como instrumento regulador de la poltica monetaria, en comparaci con una poltica basada en objetivos cuantitativos. El establecimiento de objetivos de inflaci y el uso de los tipos de inters como instrumento de poltica monetaria deberan ser acogidos con satisfacci por Wicksell. Adems, dotar al banco central de autonoma para alcanzar sus objetivos ha constituido una il sntesis entre reglas y discreci que, al forzar la credibilidad anti inflacionista, permite una mayor flexibilidad para adaptar las condiciones monetarias a las circunstancias econicas y financieras. No creo que Wicksell pusiera reparos tampoco aqu. l aboga favor de cumplir las reglas de equilibrio fiscal y el patr oro, si bien con una cierta discrecionalidad ante circunstancias transitorias excepcionales. La reciente crisis financiera internacional ha llevado a los bancos centrales a replantearse este modelo de objetivo de inflaci y a incorporar consideraciones relativas a la evoluci del precio de los activos financieros y la estabilidad financiera en general. Adems, tambin se han puesto de manifiesto los lmites de las polticas monetarias convencionales y los instrumentos usados por la autoridad monetaria (bsicamente el tipo de inters) y los riesgos de caer en la denominada trampa de la liquidez (posibilidad ya postulada por Keynes en la Teora General) en situaciones de reducidas tasas de inflaci. Los principales bancos centrales han tratado de resolver este problema a travs de polticas monetarias no convencionales, descensos de los tipos de inters, incluso a tasas negativas, y polticas orientadas al crecimiento de su balance mediante compras de activos financieros, incluidas deudas de los gobiernos y de instituciones privadas. Cabe cuestionarse si este nuevo paradigma monetario sera demasiado provocativo, incluso para alguien con un carcter tan innovador como el de Wicksell, o no, pero es el que se ha venido construyendo durante los timos as. De nuevo, muchas gracias al ICO por su iniciativa y a todos ustedes por su atencin.

Title: Introductory words at the ECB Focus Session
text: 08.04.2016 Focus Session  Introductory words BCE/Banco de Espana Luis M. Linde Gobernador I am very pleased, on behalf of the Bank of Spain, to welcome you and to host the first Focus Session that we are going to hold on today. The Focus Sessions  an initiative of the ECB in the field of market infrastructures and payments  are intended as a forum where the Eurosystem and financial players can exchange information and views on issues of common interest. Our programme today features several topics related to market infrastructures. The Eurosystem plays a provider role for TARGET2 and T2S  the two settlement services for payments and securities. Moreover, the Eurosystems recently launched Vision 2020 initiative enhances the current services and extends the benefits of integration to other areas, such as Eurosystem collateral management. Discussions will focus on the T2S Programme, which reached an important point just two weeks ago, with the successful migration of its second wave. I take this opportunity to congratulate all the teams participating in this project for their commitment and success in what is a significant achievement. On a national note, but still in the T2S context, the Spanish securities market reform will be discussed afterwards. The Banco de Espana, together with the National Securities Market Commission, has promoted and supported this reform, in close cooperation with the Spanish securities industry. Much work has been done and, in a few weeks time, the first milestone of the reform will be reached as Iberclears new T2S-compatible system for equities is launched; this is a crucial step before the migration to T2S in September 2017. Implementing the reform in parallel with the adaptation to T2S, which is in itself a complex project, entails significant challenges and the schedule for its completion remains tight. At this juncture, the Spanish community should commit itself to the additional resources and the final push needed to bring about a timely and successful migration to T2S. Other key issues such as harmonisation of market practices or the degree of consolidation of the market infrastructures across Europe will also be discussed. We expect this forum to help improve awareness of what has been achieved and to reflect on what still lies ahead. The emergence of new change drivers is also important. One of these is the so-called Distributed Ledger, a technology that is arousing a lot of interest in the financial community owing to its potential applications in the fields of cash and securities clearing and settlement. Much research and debate are under way worldwide on this and other innovative, promising technologies. It is probably too early to arrive at any conclusions as to which of these promises will materialise into effective products, but the topic merits attention. To conclude, I would add that central banks are monitoring market initiatives closely, so that when the time is ripe we can be in a position to anticipate their implications for oversight, for supervision and for financial stability. We can also play a role as catalysts and facilitators of those initiatives that have the potential to be of value to the market and the entire society. You will contribute with your views, your concerns and your experience to turn each challenge into an opportunity, so as to achieve our common goal, which is, indeed, improving our financial services for the benefit of all European citizens. I wish you a fruitful Focus session today and to our visitors a very good stay in Madrid.

Title: Opening remarks at the XIV Germn Berncer Price Ceremony
text: 13.05.2016 Opening remarks XIV German Bernacer Prize Ceremony Luis M. Linde Governor Ladies and Gentlemen, It is a pleasure for me to welcome you all and to take part, with some introductory remarks, in this Award Ceremony for the 14th German Bernacer Prize at the CEMFI premises. Due to unexpected circumstances, our dear friend and colleague Vitor Constancio, Vice-President of the ECB and Chairman of the Selection Committee of this award, will not be able to be with us today. I would like to express our gratitude for his commitment and contributions to the Prize. I would also wish to congratulate the organizers, as well as the sponsors of the Prize, for their support, and to thank the CEMFI for hosting the event. The prize is named after German Bernacer, an outstanding Spanish economist, appointed head of the Servicio de Estudios of the Bank of Spain in 1930, with a deep interest and knowledge of monetary theory, acquired during his studies in Germany, where he came into contact with the work of Wicksell. The Prize was created in 2001 by the Observatory of the European Central Bank, to foster macroeconomic and financial research among young economists in the euro area. On this edition of the Prize, the winner is Ms. Veronica Guerrieri. She is an Italian Economics professor, who earned her bachelors degree summa cum laude and a masters degree in Economics from Universita Commerciale Luigi Bocconi, in Milan, and a PhD in Economics from the Massachusets Institute of Technology. Veronica Guerrieri holds an impressive record of recognition. She won the Carlo Alberto medal for the best Italian economist under 40 in 2013; the Alfred P. Sloan Research Fellowship in 2011; the Excellence Award in Global Economic Affairs in 2010 from the Kiel Institute for the World Economy; and the Excellence in Refereeing Award in 2008 and 2012 from the American Economic Review. Guerrieri is a research associate of the National Bureau of Economic Research, an associate editor both for the American Economic Review and the Journal of Economic Literature and consultant at the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago since 2014. She has extensive academic experience, MIT, Yale an LSE among others. Currently, Ms.Guerrieri is Professor of Economics at the University of Chicago Booth School of Business. Her work covers search theory, labor and financial market frictions, dynamic contracting and growth theory, and has been published in leading journals including the American Economic Review, Econometrica and the Journal of Political Economy. Particularly relevant from a central bank perspective are her publications on financial frictions, liquidity traps and flights to quality. I would like to highlight her research to explain the emergence of illiquidity and fire sales in different asset markets. Her contributions are useful, for instance, to understand the potential impact of asset purchase programmes, a non conventional monetary policy instrument not precisely far from the interests and practices of the central banking community nowadays Congratulations Ms Guerrieri!

Title: Speech of delivery of the XVI Prize of Economy King Juan Carlos to D. Jos Luis Garca Delgado
text: 17.11.2016 Speech of delivery of the XVI Prize of Economy King Juan Carlos to D. Jos8e Luis Garc92a Delgado Bank of Spain Luis M. Linde Governor Your Majesty, Madam Secretary of State, ladies and gentlemen, First of all, Lord, I want to thank you for your presence at the Banco de Espa96a, one more year, at the ceremony of the presentation of the Economics Prize that bears your name. You have accompanied us in the presentation of this Award for three decades and today your presence once again honors this house and makes us proud. The King Juan Carlos Economics Prize was instituted by the Jos8e Celma Prieto Foundation in 1986. Since then, it rewards every two years the academic and professional career, in the field of economics, of Spanish or Ibero-American personalities. I want to thank, once again, the Foundation and its president, Mr. Jos8e Celma, for their long and generous work of patronage. The jury that I have had the honor of chairing, has been composed of Mr. Aurelio Men8endez as vice president, Mr. Juan Velarde, Mr. Rodolfo Mart92n Villa, Mr. e7lvaro Cuervo, Mr. Jos8e Luis Feito and Mr. e7lvaro Rodr92guez Bereijo. On July 11, the jury decided to award the Prize, corresponding to this year, 2016, to Mr. Jos8e Luis Garc92a Delgado, for his contributions to the study of the transformation and economic modernization of contemporary Spain, for his dedication to the training of university professors and, in general, for his contributions to the stimulation of academic activity in the field of economic and social studies. Professor Garc92a Delgado is Professor of Applied Economics, has taught for 49 years and is Doctor Honoris Causa by the Universities of Oviedo, Lima, Buenos Aires and Alicante. He obtained the Medal of Honor from the Complutense University of Madrid, is a Full Member of the Royal Academy of Moral and Political Sciences and, in 2015, received from His Majesty, Don Felipe VI, the Pascual Madoz National Research Prize for his historical-economic analysis of the great events of the twentieth century in Europe and Spain. The work of Garc92a Delgado has been collected in books and articles whose enumeration would be too long to be done here. He has also stood out as director and founder of economics journals, - "Investigaciones Econ97micas", "Revista de Econom92a Aplicada" and "Revista de Econom92a" -, and in the development and promotion of discussion and analysis forums. Jos8e Luis Garc92a Delgado has been a very outstanding academic manager. He has held the positions of director of the Department of Economics of the Pontifical University of Comillas, director of the Department of Economic Structure and Industrial Economics of the Complutense University, dean of the University of Economic and Business Sciences of the University of Oviedo, vice-rector of the Complutense University and rector, for 10 years, of the Men8endez Pelayo International University. He is currently the holder of the "la Caixa" Chair in Economics and Society, through which he continues to promote academic initiatives of great interest in the field of economics and social sciences. With a horizon that goes beyond the strictly economic field, Professor Garc92a Delgado has delved into central themes of contemporary Spanish history. In his book "The economic modernization in the Spain of Alfonso XIII", - a subject to which he dedicated his doctoral thesis and on which his speech of admission to the Royal Academy of Moral and Political Sciences was devoted -, he shows a reality that defies the pessimism characteristic of the Spanish intellectuals of that time, pointing out that Spain has not been, against a widespread vision, a singular reality, isolated from what is happening in Europe, nor in the world. It is appropriate to recall the intervention of Garc92a Delgado in the Academy of Moral and Political Sciences, on the occasion of the centenary of the famous conference that Ortega gave in March 1914, "Old and new politics". Garc92a Delgado faced, I believe with courage and independence of judgment, that Orteguian vision that presented the regime of the Restoration as a system that was distinguished in the European political scenario by its corruption, a system dominated by the caciquismo and the rigged turn of the parties, a regime that, in the opinion of the Ortega of that time, it had to be rejected, practically, in its entirety. Garc92a Delgado understood d0 and I think the historical perspective proves him right d0 that Ortega, like other intellectuals of the time, was exaggeratedly pessimistic, that he underestimated the positive aspects of the Restoration, both politically and economically, and that his famous sentence, launched in 1910, "Spain is the problem and Europe the solution". it was somewhat overshadowed when, shortly after, in 1914, the Great War began, the origin of the disasters and sufferings that were to befall Europe during the following decades. In a different field, another contribution of Professor Garc92a Delgado that should be highlighted is the collection of books that, under the sponsorship of the Telef97nica Foundation, has been published on the economic value of the Spanish language, a great asset of our country that is often overlooked. This collection deals with aspects such as the role of Spanish as a language of scientific communication, its use in international relations and in the development of Spanish companies in global markets, proposing a promotion policy that reinforces its international status. Finally, I want to point out that Jos8e Luis Garc92a Delgado is also a person very interested in artistic and literary issues, something that helps us to know his personality better. In particular, he is a great fan of cinema, a great connoisseur of the seventh art and an appreciated film critic, within canons, dare I say, very classic. I do not know if he planned to make any confidence in this matter but, just in case he had decided to exercise extreme discretion, I have gone ahead. I'm sure he forgives me. It only remains for me, Lord, with your Majesty's permission, to ask the winner to take the stage so that you can present him with the 2016 King Juan Carlos Economy Prize.

En un terreno diferente, otra aportacin del profesor Garca Delgado que debe destacarse es la coleccin de libros que, bajo el patrocinio de la Fundacin Telefnica, se ha venido publicando sobre el valor econmico de la lengua espaola, un gran activo de nuestro pas que, frecuentemente, se pasa por alto. En esta coleccin se tratan aspectos tales como el papel del espaol como lengua de comunicacin cientfica, su utilizacin en las relaciones internacionales y en el desarrollo de las empresas espaolas en los mercados globales, proponiendo una poltica de promocin que refuerce su estatus internacional. Finalmente, quiero sealar que Jos Luis Garca Delgado es tambin una persona muy interesada en cuestiones artsticas y literarias, algo que nos ayuda a conocer mejor su personalidad. En particular, es un gran aficionado al cine, un gran conocedor del sptimo arte y un apreciado crtico cinematogrfico, dentro de cnones, me atrevo a decir, muy clsicos. No s si l tena pensado hacernos alguna confidencia en esta materia pero, por si acaso hubiera decidido extremar su discrecin, yo me he adelantado. Seguro que me perdona. Solamente me queda, Seor, con permiso de su Majestad, solicitar al premiado que suba al estrado para que le hagis entrega del Premio de Economa Rey Juan Carlos 2016

Title: The future of Spanish banking
text: 15.12.16 The future of Spanish banking Opening of the 12th Meeting of the Banking Sector, "Banking in the future", IESE (Madrid) Fernando Restoy Deputy governor I am very grateful to the organizers, and IESE in particular, for inviting me to participate in this prestigious annual event. Circumstances have meant that, in all likelihood, this is my last public appearance before my departure from the Bank of Spain to take over, from January, the presidency of the Financial Stability Institute, in Basel. This is therefore a good opportunity to reflect on the current situation and the challenges facing our banking sector - to which I have logically devoted an important part of my work as Deputy Governor - in the area of its membership of the banking union. 1 The general situation of the sector A simple observation of the data on the situation of European banks shows the considerable vulnerability shown by the sector. All European institutions have very low returns on capital d0 slightly below 6% on average d0 which are below any reasonable estimate of the cost of capital in the market, despite the technical difficulty involved in the rigorous assessment of the latter concept. This low profitability of the sector is the consequence of depressed net interest income and, in many cases, the accumulation of non-performing assets on bank balance sheets. The potential of commission income to mitigate the deterioration in the profitability of the brokerage business does not appear to have been exploited so far. In fact, during the first half of 2016, such revenues were approximately 5% lower than those recorded a year earlier. Similarly, the increase in solvency requirements and the emergence of new resolution requirements d0 which extend the requirements on the availability of loss-absorbing liabilities d0 constitute additional elements of pressure on the sector's profitability. It is clear that some of the factors that explain the low profitability of banks, such as the extremely low level of interest rates, are cyclical in nature and that their foreseeable deactivation in the future could be a factor of relief. However, it is possible to anticipate that, even as monetary conditions normalize, secular downward factors on interest rates, increasing competition in the market for transactional and portfolio management services, the likely development of capital markets as an alternative source of financing to bank credit, and the consolidation of a considerably more demanding regulatory environment than in the past, They will put continued pressure on the banking business as a whole. It is therefore not difficult to predict that the banking sector will generally be smaller in the future and that its component entities will perhaps be less profitable, but probably also safer. This will necessarily lead to important changes in the structure of the industry and will generate natural selection processes from which not only those best adapted to the new environment will emerge successfully, but also those who are better adapted to the new environment. that, not being so, they are able to manage with clairvoyance their integration into potentially more solid projects. In particular, I believe that the new economic and regulatory conditions could allow the survival of small credit institutions that take advantage of the proximity to very specific customers and that are able to maintain sufficient regulatory capital, especially if they do not necessarily have to remunerate it in market conditions. The business model of these institutions must be adjusted to their status as non-systemic institutions that, in a possible situation of failure, would be liquidated through an ordinary insolvency process, with no external protection other than that provided by the Deposit Guarantee Fund for covered deposits. However, beyond a certain size threshold d0 for example, the one that marks the status of significant institution directly supervised by the Single Supervisory Mechanism (SSM) d0 capital requirements and liabilities convertible into own resources will normally oblige institutions to participate actively in capital markets and therefore to remunerate these instruments in accordance with the conditions laid down therein. In an environment of low interest rates and increasing regulatory and competitive pressure, hedging the cost of liabilities will require very high levels of efficiency. But it does not seem that this alone is enough. It is foreseeable that the profitability required to meet costs can only be maintained in a stable manner over time if the entity has suitably diversified sources of income. This affects both the location of their credit exposures and their ability to generate revenue through the provision of a sufficiently wide range of financial services. The latter requires entities not only sufficient capacity to withstand the competition of non-bank Fintechs, but also agility to perfect their product offer through the intelligent and agile use of new technologies. Thus, it seems likely that the reduction in the overall size of the industry and its average profitability, which I mentioned earlier, will be accompanied by fewer entities that will normally be more capitalized, more efficient, more technologically advanced and more active in capital markets, and that will develop a more diversified business model. 2 How do Spanish banks face these challenges? I think that today it is a commonplace to appreciate the work done in Spain in recent years to restore the solidity of its financial system. Compared to the situation at the beginning of the crisis, today we have a more consolidated, much healthier and better capitalized banking sector. Thus, since 2007, the number of banking groups has been reduced by 44%. In addition, more than 60% of the net exposure to the real estate sector in 2011 has been removed from individual bank balance sheets and, since 2008, approximately 300 billion new provisions have been made for outstanding and foreclosed loans. Although the volume of non-performing assets remains high, it is promising that, between June 2015 and June 2016, non-performing assets fell by 18%. Finally, sanitation so Sharp achievements have not hindered an intense recapitalization, which has reached 70 billion euros since 2008, at a consolidated level. On the other hand, the regulations relating to savings banks have been thoroughly reformed, adjusting the structure and operation of these entities to the usual corporate models in the industry, preserving, in turn, the social function they perform. You will allow me to take advantage of this very special intervention to highlight the work done in this process by the institution to which I belong. Indeed, as you know, the Banco de Espa96a participated from the outset, advising the government, in the negotiations of the financial assistance programme approved by the European authorities in July 2012 and with the participation of the IMF and the ECB, among others. In addition, it contributed significantly to the capital needs identification exercises and approved the recapitalisation and restructuring plans for the weaker banks, which set out requirements for the transfer of assets to Sareb, capacity reduction plans and burden-sharing exercises affecting shareholders and subordinated creditors of the institutions that received public support. This had to be done after complex negotiations, in particular with the European Commission. These actions were developed, from the summer of 2012, in an environment of high instability and in the face of very critical situations for some entities, which had to be solved expeditiously without counting, at that time, with the confidence of the markets. In parallel, relevant actions were carried out in different areas that contributed to increasing the solidity of institutions and restoring investor confidence. Remember, for example, the guidelines or recommendations issued on the transparency and proper accounting of refinanced credits, the remuneration of deposits or the distribution of dividends. More recently, the amendment of Circular 4/2004, or accounting circular, will further refine the way in which the quality of bank assets is reflected in the financial statements. When I emphasize these actions of the Bank of Spain, I would like to emphasize, above all, that these are pieces that are part of a State strategy that required close cooperation between different instances. The Bank has always acted in coordination with the Government d0 responsible for promoting, among other actions, regulatory changes d0 and, in particular, with the Ministry of Economy, either through bilateral interaction, or through the participation of both institutions in the FROB, a fundamental tool of the process, of whose Governing Commission it is also a member. the Ministry of Finance. It is also worth mentioning the participation of the industry as a whole in the effort to clean up and recapitalize the most vulnerable segment of the industry. Through the Deposit Guarantee Fund, the banking sector has provided aid for a volume close to 20 billion euros, through capital subscriptions or the assumption of asset protection schemes, in the first part of the crisis and, later, in the form of purchases from retail investors of shares from the conversion of hybrid instruments into equity. At the same time, most banks decided to participate in Sareb, which has played an essential role in the process of restructuring the sector. However, the most important effort has been made by the taxpayer who, in an adverse period for growth and employment, had to contribute very large resources, amounting to close to 5% of GDP. It must, in any case, be emphasized that these funds have not served to alleviate shareholder losses but, essentially, to protect depositors and restore financial stability, a public good of primary necessity. For all these reasons, I believe that the reform and restructuring of our financial system has been, above all, the result of a collective effort, involving the authorities and private institutions, as well as society as a whole.
