Title: Speech at the Conference "The challenges of European banking: profitability and business models"
text: 10.04.18 "The challenges of the financial system" Speech at the Conference "The challenges of European banking: profitability and business models", organized by Cinco D92as and Abanca (Madrid) Javier Alonso Deputy governor Good morning. I would like to begin by thanking the organizers for their invitation to participate in this conference entitled "The challenges of European banking: profitability and business models". My public interventions over the last fifteen months have been revolving around the different challenges facing European banks and it is a pleasure to be able to continue sharing my reflections on this today, here, with you. At the same time, I would not want to repeat excessively the content that I have already developed in previous speeches, not because I have changed my mind but because I think it is already well known that I believe it is necessary to continue exploring ways to improve efficiency and continue with the orderly correction of excess capacity. Nor would I want to overlap with the round tables that follow and that will focus exclusively on profitability, the first, and business models, the second. The first is likely to mention, among others, aspects related to low interest rates, the still significant volume of non-performing assets, adaptation to recent regulatory changes that have led to an increase in capital requirements, or new technologies. The second can be oriented in different ways, but I understand that, ultimately, the debate will revolve, in one way or another, around the sources of income and financing that define the different business models. In any case, both round tables are closely related, since a key aspect in relation to a business model is that, to be sustainable, it must be profitable. It must generate sufficient returns to hedge its risks on the basis of a stable funding structure. In this context, in my speech today, I would like to make a brief mention of new technologies, as an aspect that affects the traditional banking business in Europe in a transversal way. In addition, and from the point of view of banks' traditional sources of funding, I would like to take this opportunity to highlight some regulatory changes underway in Europe in the area of covered bonds and securitisations. New technologies With regard to new technologies, it is clear that technological development has favoured the emergence of new service providers which, in some cases, compete with traditional banking in specific market niches. In addition, as a result of the possibilities offered by these new technologies, the behavior patterns of users of banking services are changing profoundly. Traditional banks react to this change in different ways: (i) taking advantage of the advantages derived from cooperative initiatives at the sectoral level, (ii) allying with new agents, (iii) incorporating new technologies and changing the way in which they develop their activity to become more competitive and give more emphasis to aspects such as the "customer experience" or (iv) pressuring the authorities to open the door to Innovation through, for example, the creation of controlled test spaces with tempered regulatory requirements. To analyze and understand all these changes, the central bank and regulators have to transform. In this sense, at the Banco de Espa96a, we have recently proceeded to the creation of a new Deputy Directorate-General with the intention of strengthening the analysis of these changes and the implications they have for the financial sector and for the public policies that must be carried out. In this sense, the work of this new area must be transversal within the Bank of Spain, given the multiple dimensions that are affected: payment systems, market conduct, regulation, supervision, financial stability, research and studies, or authorizations, among others. It must also maintain a fluid dialogue with other authorities - such as the CNMV and the General Secretariat of the Treasury and Financial Policy - and with the market, both through established forums and through bilateral meetings. And not only will it try to understand the implications of the emergence of new agents and new ways of operating among Spanish entities, but it must necessarily have a global vision, since one of the characteristics of the change we face is the transnational dimension of many of the new initiatives and the speed with which successful ways of operating that are developed in any country end up spreading to others. Jurisdictions. In this sense, it is not surprising that, among the lines of action of the European program called Capital Markets Union, actions related to these new agents are included in which it is sought, precisely, to promote an orderly reaction at European level. Legislative reforms in the area of sources of funding Let me now turn to two legislative reforms, which are also part of the Capital Markets Union, and to which I think it is important to pay attention because they relate to two traditional sources of funding for banks that are expected to regain prominence when the ECB's targeted longer-term refinancing operations mature (TLTRO II, for its acronym in English). These include reforms on covered bonds and securitisations. These reforms aim to promote deeper and more efficient European markets for such financial products, thereby helping to improve the financing of credit institutions and thus their ability to mobilise resources towards the real economy. The reform of the securitisation framework also aims to help investors assess the risks related to securitisations, thereby contributing to risk management. Both legislative reforms will result in changes in the practices currently followed by banks and will therefore require some adaptation effort on the part of both issuers and investors. I shall now briefly refer to each of them. Covered bonds Starting with covered bonds, on March 12, the European Commission published a proposal that seeks to harmonize its regulation in Europe. This type of bond, which includes the case of Spanish mortgage bonds, is characterized by the fact that banks issue securities (bonds) whose repayment is guaranteed by a set of assets. In this way, the issuing banks retain the risk in their balance sheets (the collateral) and the investors in the bonds are doubly protected in case of default: on the one hand, they have direct recourse over the hedging assets of the covered bond program, and on the other hand they have recourse against the issuing entity as ordinary creditors. This protection, known as double recourse, together with the high quality required of collateral, means that it is a type of instrument of high quality and liquidity, and that the investment of entities in this type of bonds receives preferential treatment in terms of regulatory requirements. In Europe, there are several countries where this type of product has traditionally been regulated and where there are important markets. Among others, Germany, Denmark, France and Spain stand out. As is known, in our country mortgage bonds have had a remarkable importance as a source of financing for credit institutions. However, the different local European covered bond markets have their particularities, and their regulations differ from each other. For example, in the Spanish case, a very substantial difference with respect to other countries is that mortgage bonds are backed by the entire mortgage portfolio, despite which they have not traditionally been considered better than other similar securities in which the guarantee of the bonds is significantly lower. Given the differences observed at European level, a fundamental objective of the recent proposal of the European Commission is to advance in the harmonisation in Europe of the regulation of covered bonds. The proposal includes a Directive, specifying the basic elements of covered bonds, which will thus be eligible for the label of "European Covered Bonds"; and a modification of prudential banking regulation, which strengthens the conditions for banks investing in these products to benefit from lower regulatory capital requirements. The Directive provides a definition of covered bond, stressing the need for dual recourse, and continues the tradition of limiting the issuance of this product to credit institutions. It introduces, among others, requirements for the segregation of assets that serve as collateral for bonds, liquidity requirements, and several criteria to ensure the quality of assets, including the possibility of the existence of an external reviewer of collateral. The Directive also requires the need for public supervision, which aims at greater investor protection. The modification of prudential regulation strengthens the requirements for a lower regulatory capital requirement for banks investing in these products, including, among other issues, a minimum level of excess collateral (i.e. a minimum level of over-collateralization), in general terms, of at least 5%. Once the Commission's proposal is adopted, the Directive should be transposed so that banks can start issuing instruments as soon as possible that benefit from the benefits of obtaining the European covered bond label. In this regard, I would like to point out two points. First, I believe that a transposition of the Directive should be addressed that allows a reform to be undertaken that makes a financing market traditionally so relevant for Spanish entities even more efficient and solid. And second, during this transition period, banks must properly manage their issuance programs so that, when the Directive has been transposed, they are in a position to issue according to the best practices required of European covered bonds. Titulizaciones As far as securitisations are concerned, this financial product, unlike covered bonds, has performed poorly during the international financial crisis. Moreover, its inappropriate use within a banking model known as "originate to distribute" is considered one of the elements that contributed to it. The stigma of this product has not been confined to the US, but has also affected, perhaps more unjustifiably, Europe. However, the European authorities have considered that securitisations, which are properly regulated and well structured, can help diversify funding sources, promote better risk management, and ultimately mobilise more resources towards the real economy. For these reasons, on December 28, two Regulations were published in the Official Journal of the European Union that modify the regulatory framework applicable to securitisations, in an attempt to obtain their benefits, limiting the risks derived from their improper use. One of these Regulations establishes a general framework for all securitisations, and creates a specific framework for what are to be called "simple, transparent and standardised" (STS). The other Regulation transposes the new Basel III framework by introducing changes to prudential regulation for credit institutions and investment firms, both for securitisations in general, and for simple, transparent and standardised securitisations, which will benefit from better treatment. As regards the specific framework for STS securitisations, without going into the specific details, the regulation lays down a number of specific requirements. To be simple, for example, the underlying exposures are required to be homogeneous in terms of the type of asset, and its contractual and credit risk characteristics. In order to be transparent, it establishes, inter alia, the minimum information to be provided to investors, which will facilitate due diligence. To be standardized, a series of contractual requirements are determined that the transaction must meet. Finally, reporting obligations are required for the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA), while public oversight of these criteria is required. This new, simple, transparent and standardised securitisation framework recently approved, and which will apply from the beginning of next year, is an opportunity to revive a market that has been stigmatised and penalised by the recent international financial crisis, but which can offer advantages for banks in terms of improvements in their funding and risk management opportunities. Efforts should be made to converge towards such practices. Conclusion And I finish, going back to the beginning. Let us not lose sight of the challenges posed by new technologies, but neither are aspects related to the traditional financing of institutions that will regain importance as the liquidity granted by the ECB matures.
text_original: 10.04.18 Los retos del sistema financiero Discurso en la Jornada Los retos de la banca europea: rentabilidad y modelos de negocio, organizada por Cinco Das y Abanca (Madrid) Javier Alonso Subgobernador Buenos das. Quisiera comenzar agradeciendo a los organizadores su invitacin a participar en esta jornada que lleva como ttulo Los retos de la banca europea: rentabilidad y modelos de negocio. Mis intervenciones pblicas a lo largo de los ltimos quince meses han venido girando alrededor de los distintos retos a los que se enfrenta la banca europea y es un placer poder continuar compartiendo mis reflexiones al respecto hoy, aqu, con ustedes. Al mismo tiempo, no querra repetir en exceso el contenido que ya he desarrollado en discursos anteriores, no porque haya cambiado de opinin sino porque creo que ya se conoce sobradamente que considero que es necesario seguir explorando vas para mejorar la eficiencia y continuar con la correccin ordenada del exceso de capacidad. Tampoco querra solaparme con las mesas redondas que vienen a continuacin y que se centrarn de manera exclusiva en la rentabilidad, la primera, y en los modelos de negocio, la segunda. En la primera es probable que se mencionen, entre otros, aspectos relacionados con los bajos tipos de inters, el todava significativo volumen de activos improductivos, la adaptacin a los recientes cambios regulatorios que han supuesto un aumento en los requerimientos de capital, o las nuevas tecnologas. La segunda puede orientarse de distintas maneras, pero entiendo que, en ltima instancia, el debate girar, de una manera u otra, alrededor de las fuentes de ingreso y de financiacin que definen los distintos modelos de negocio. En cualquier caso, ambas mesas redondas estn ntimamente relacionadas, ya que un aspecto clave en relacin con un modelo de negocio es que, para que sea sostenible, debe ser rentable. Debe generar suficientes rendimientos para cubrir sus riesgos sobre la base de una estructura de financiacin estable. En este contexto, en mi intervencin de hoy, quiero hacer una breve mencin a las nuevas tecnologas, como aspecto que afecta de manera transversal al negocio bancario tradicional en Europa. Adicionalmente, y desde el punto de vista de las fuentes tradicionales de financiacin de las entidades, me gustara aprovechar esta oportunidad para poner de manifiesto algunos cambios normativos en marcha en Europa en el mbito de los bonos garantizados y de las titulizaciones. Las nuevas tecnologas Por lo que respecta a las nuevas tecnologas, es claro que el desarrollo tecnolgico ha favorecido la aparicin de nuevos proveedores de servicios que, en algunos casos, compiten con la banca tradicional en nichos concretos de mercado. Adems, fruto de las posibilidades que ofrecen estas nuevas tecnologas, los patrones de comportamiento de los usuarios de servicios bancarios estn cambiando de manera profunda. La banca tradicional reacciona ante este cambio de distintas maneras: (i) aprovechando las ventajas derivadas de iniciativas cooperativas a nivel sectorial, (ii) alindose con los nuevos agentes, (iii) incorporando nuevas tecnologas y cambiando la forma en la que desarrollan su actividad para hacerse ms competitivos y dar ms nfasis a aspectos como la experiencia del cliente o (iv) presionando a las autoridades para abrir la puerta a la innovacin mediante la creacin, por ejemplo, de espacios de prueba controlados con requisitos regulatorios atemperados. Para analizar y comprender todos estos cambios, el banco central y los reguladores han de transformarse. En este sentido, en el Banco de Espaa, hemos procedido recientemente a la creacin de una nueva Direccin General Adjunta con la intencin de reforzar el anlisis de estos cambios y las implicaciones que tienen para el sector financiero y para las polticas pblicas que en su caso deben ser realizadas. En este sentido, el trabajo de esta nueva rea debe ser transversal dentro del Banco de Espaa, dadas las mltiples dimensiones que se ven afectadas: sistemas de pago, conducta de mercado, regulacin, supervisin, estabilidad financiera, investigacin y estudios, o autorizaciones, entre otras. Debe tambin mantener un dilogo fluido con otras autoridades - como la CNMV y la Secretara General del Tesoro y Poltica Financiera - y con el mercado, tanto a travs de foros ya establecidos como a travs de encuentros bilaterales. Y no solo va a tratar de comprender las implicaciones de la aparicin de nuevos agentes y nuevas formas de operar entre las entidades espaolas sino que, necesariamente debe tener una visin global, ya que una de las caractersticas del cambio al que nos enfrentamos es la dimensin transnacional de muchas de las nuevas iniciativas y la rapidez con la que formas exitosas de operar que se desarrollan en cualquier pas acaban extendindose a otras jurisdicciones. En este sentido, no resulta sorprendente que, entre las lneas de accin del programa europeo denominado Unin del Mercado de Capitales, se incluyan actuaciones relacionadas con estos nuevos agentes en las que se busca, precisamente, fomentar una reaccin ordenada a nivel europeo. Reformas legislativas en el mbito de las fuentes de financiacin Permtanme que pase ahora a referirme a dos reformas legislativas, que tambin se enmarcan dentro de la Unin del Mercado de Capitales, y a las que considero que es relevante prestar atencin porque tienen que ver con dos fuentes tradicionales de financiacin de las entidades que es previsible que recobren protagonismo cuando vayan venciendo las operaciones del BCE de financiacin a plazo ms largo con objetivo especfico (TLTRO II, por sus siglas en ingls). Se trata, en particular, de las reformas relativas a los bonos garantizados y a las titulizaciones. Estas reformas pretenden promover unos mercados europeos ms profundos y eficientes para dichos productos financieros, contribuyendo con ello a mejorar la financiacin de las entidades de crdito y, por tanto, su capacidad para movilizar los recursos hacia la economa real. Asimismo, la reforma del marco de titulizaciones persigue ayudar a los inversores a evaluar los riesgos relacionados con ellas, contribuyendo de este modo a la gestin del riesgo. De ambas reformas legislativas se derivarn cambios en las prcticas que actualmente siguen las entidades de crdito y, por lo tanto, exigirn un cierto esfuerzo de adaptacin, tanto por parte de los emisores como de los inversores. Me referir a continuacin brevemente a cada una de ellas. Bonos garantizados Comenzando con los bonos garantizados, el pasado 12 de marzo, la Comisin Europea hizo pblica una propuesta que persigue armonizar su regulacin en Europa. Este tipo de bonos, entre los que se incluye el caso de las cdulas hipotecarias espaolas, se caracterizan porque los bancos emiten ttulos (los bonos) cuyo repago queda garantizado por un conjunto de activos. De este modo, los bancos emisores retienen el riesgo en sus balances (los activos de garanta) y los inversores en los bonos quedan doblemente protegidos en caso de impago: por una parte, tienen recurso directo sobre los activos de cobertura del programa del bono garantizado, y por otra parte tienen recurso contra la entidad emisora como acreedores ordinarios. Esta proteccin, conocida como doble recurso, unida a la elevada calidad que se exige a los activos de garanta, hace que se trate de un tipo de instrumento de alta calidad y liquidez, y que la inversin de las entidades en este tipo de bonos reciba un tratamiento preferencial en trminos de exigencias regulatorias. En Europa, hay varios pases en los que tradicionalmente se han regulado este tipo de productos y en los que existen mercados importantes. Entre otros destacan Alemania, Dinamarca, Francia y tambin Espaa. Como es sabido, en nuestro pas las cdulas hipotecarias han tenido una importancia notable como fuente de financiacin de las entidades de crdito. Ahora bien, los diferentes mercados locales europeos de bonos garantizados tienen sus particularidades, y sus regulaciones difieren entre s. Por ejemplo, en el caso espaol, una diferencia muy sustancial con respecto a otros pases es que las cdulas hipotecarias quedan respaldadas por toda la cartera hipotecaria, a pesar de lo cual no han sido tradicionalmente consideradas mejores que otros ttulos similares en los que la garanta de los bonos es significativamente menor. Ante las diferencias que se observan a nivel europeo, un objetivo fundamental de la reciente propuesta de la Comisin Europea es avanzar en la armonizacin en Europa de la regulacin de los bonos garantizados. La propuesta incluye una Directiva, en la que se especifican los elementos bsicos de los bonos garantizados, que podrn de este modo obtener la etiqueta de European Covered Bonds; y una modificacin de la regulacin prudencial bancaria, que refuerza las condiciones para que los bancos inversores en estos productos se beneficien de unas menores exigencias de capital regulatorio. La Directiva ofrece una definicin de bono garantizado, destacando la necesidad de la existencia del doble recurso, y contina con la tradicin de limitar la emisin de este producto a las entidades de crdito. Se introducen, entre otros, exigencias para la segregacin de los activos que sirven de colateral a los bonos, requerimientos de liquidez, y varios criterios para asegurar la calidad de los activos, incluyendo la posibilidad de la existencia de un revisor externo de los activos de garanta. La Directiva exige, adems, la necesidad de una supervisin pblica, que persigue una mayor proteccin de los inversores. La modificacin de la regulacin prudencial fortalece los requisitos para una menor exigencia de capital regulatorio para los bancos que inviertan en estos productos, incluyendo entre otras cuestiones, un nivel mnimo del exceso de garanta (es decir, un nivel mnimo de sobre-colateralizacin), en trminos generales, de al menos un 5%. Una vez que la propuesta de la Comisin sea aprobada, se deber transponer la Directiva, de tal modo que los bancos puedan empezar a emitir lo antes posible instrumentos que se beneficien de las ventajas de obtener la etiqueta de bono garantizado europeo. En este sentido, querra sealar dos cuestiones. Primero, considero que se debera abordar una transposicin de la Directiva que permita acometer una reforma que haga todava ms eficiente y slido un mercado de financiacin tradicionalmente tan relevante para las entidades espaolas. Y segundo, durante este perodo de transicin, los bancos debern gestionar adecuadamente sus programas de emisin para que, cuando la Directiva se haya transpuesto, estn en disposicin de realizar emisiones siguiendo las mejores prcticas exigibles a los European covered bonds. Titulizaciones Por lo que respecta a las titulizaciones, este producto financiero, a diferencia de los bonos garantizados, ha tenido un mal comportamiento durante la crisis financiera internacional. Es ms, su uso inadecuado dentro de un modelo bancario conocido como originar para distribuir, se considera uno de los elementos que contribuyeron a ella. El estigma de este producto no se ha circunscrito a EEUU, sino que tambin ha afectado, quiz ms infundadamente, a Europa. Ahora bien, las autoridades europeas han considerado que las titulizaciones, adecuadamente reguladas y bien estructuradas, pueden contribuir a diversificar las fuentes de financiacin, a favorecer una mejor gestin del riesgo, y, en ltima instancia, a movilizar mayores recursos hacia la economa real. Por estos motivos, el pasado 28 de diciembre, se publicaron dos Reglamentos en el Diario Oficial de la Unin Europea que modifican el marco regulatorio aplicable a las titulizaciones, en un intento de obtener sus beneficios, limitando los riesgos derivados de su uso inadecuado. Uno de estos Reglamentos establece un marco general para todas las titulizaciones, y crea uno especfico para las que van a llamarse simples, transparentes y normalizadas (STS, por sus siglas en ingls). El otro Reglamento traspone el nuevo marco de Basilea III introduciendo modificaciones en la regulacin prudencial para las entidades de crdito y empresas de inversin, tanto para las titulizaciones en general, como para las simples, transparentes y normalizadas, que se beneficiarn de un mejor tratamiento. En lo relativo al marco especfico de las titulizaciones STS, sin entrar en los detalles especficos, la normativa establece una serie de requisitos concretos. Para ser simples se exige, por ejemplo, que las exposiciones subyacentes sean homogneas en cuanto al tipo de activo, y sus caractersticas contractuales y de riesgo de crdito. Para ser transparentes, se establece, entre otras cuestiones, la informacin mnima que se debe facilitar a los inversores, lo que facilitar la diligencia debida. Para ser normalizadas, se determinan una serie de requisitos contractuales que debe cumplir la transaccin. Finalmente, se exigen obligaciones de notificacin a la Autoridad Europea de Valores y Mercados (ESMA, por sus siglas en ingls), al tiempo que se exige la supervisin pblica de estos criterios. Este nuevo marco de titulizaciones simples, transparentes y normalizadas aprobado recientemente, y que ser de aplicacin desde comienzos del ao prximo, supone una oportunidad para reactivar un mercado que ha sido estigmatizado y penalizado por la reciente crisis financiera internacional, pero que puede ofrecer ventajas para las entidades bancarias en trminos de mejoras en sus oportunidades de financiacin y de gestin del riesgo. Convendra hacer los esfuerzos necesarios para converger hacia esas prcticas. Conclusin Y termino, volviendo al principio. No perdamos de vista los retos que suponen las nuevas tecnologas, pero tampoco aspectos relacionados con la financiacin tradicional de las entidades que recobrarn importancia a medida que vaya llegando a vencimiento la liquidez otorgada por el BCE.

Title: Appearance before Congress in relation to the General State Budget Project for 2018
text: 16.04.2018 Appearance of the Governor of the Bank of Spain before Congress in relation to the General State Budget Project for 2018 Luis M. Linde Governor Ladies and gentlemen, In my appearance before this Commission, framed in the process of discussion and approval of the General State Budget and Social Security for 2018, I will begin by referring to the current macroeconomic context and the prospects of the Spanish economy, and then comment on the main aspects of the budget bill approved by the Government on March 27, and conclude with some reflections on the challenges that, in the opinion of the Bank of Spain, the current design of fiscal policy faces. The external environment of the Spanish economy The international economic context has been characterised in recent quarters by the recovery in global economic activity, supported by very favourable financial conditions and improved business and consumer confidence. While growth has spread to most geographical areas, it is worth noting the gain in dynamism in advanced economies in general and the euro area in particular, which experienced the highest GDP growth rate since the start of the crisis in 2008 in 2017. This favourable environment has led to a stable behaviour of the international financial markets over the last year, which, however, was interrupted last February by an episode of volatility, related to the possibility of a faster normalisation of the Federal Reserve's monetary policy in the face of the prospects of improvement in activity and a rise in inflation in the United States. Due to its possible global impact, the announced change in the orientation of some economic policies in the United States is also relevant. On the one hand, the tax reform approved last year and the budget agreement reached at the beginning of this year accentuate the expansionary nature of fiscal policy. On the other hand, the announcement of tariff increases warns of a shift in its trade policy towards protectionist positions, with potentially serious consequences, at a global level, for trade and economic activity. In the euro area, the improvement in economic activity in 2017 was notable and extended to all countries. According to the most recent information, the expansionary tone would have been maintained in the first quarter of this year, 2018. This advance in the euro area economy led, according to available estimates, to the closing of the negative output gap arising from the crisis. The most recent forecasts, made by the ECB in March, point to the maintenance, in the medium term, of the dynamism observed in the most recent period, supported both by domestic demand and by the strength of exports. Despite this dynamism, a relatively moderate inflation scenario persists in the euro area, so that growth in its core component d0 which excludes the most volatile elements d0 stood at 1.2% in February. More in the medium term, the ECB's projection exercise, published last March, forecasts a very gradual increase in inflation, reaching a level of 1.7% in 2020. Given this context of contained inflation prospects in the euro area as a whole, monetary policy in 2017 and at the beginning of this year has maintained a strongly accommodative tone. The Governing Council of the ECB decided last March not to modify the reference interest rates and reiterated its commitment to maintain net purchases of securities under the asset purchase program at least until next September. Evolution and prospects of the Spanish economy I now turn to the evolution and prospects of the Spanish economy. The Spanish economy grew by 0.7% during the fourth quarter of 2017 and the most recent information suggests that this rate of growth could have continued in the first months of 2018, which has allowed the current level of GDP to exceed that registered just before the crisis. For 2018 as a whole, according to the Bank of Spain's forecasts, published on 20th March, GDP is expected to grow by 2.7%. Although this figure is somewhat below last year's figure (3.1%), if this forecast is met, the Spanish economy would maintain, for the fourth consecutive year, a greater dynamism than the euro area as a whole. Growth over the coming quarters will continue to be supported, above all, by the expansion of domestic demand, although the foreign sector is expected to maintain its positive contribution. In particular, favourable developments in employment and household disposable income, together with favourable conditions for access to credit, will continue to boost household consumption and the recovery in residential investment spending. For its part, business investment will continue to be supported by strong demand and increased utilization of productive capacity, within a very favourable framework of financing, both domestic and external. According to these projections, the current phase of growth of the Spanish economy, which began at the end of 2013, would continue over the next few years, supported by a favourable international context, comfortable financial conditions and the continuation of the process of improving competitiveness. All this would make it possible to continue making progress in correcting the imbalances accumulated in the previous expansionary cycle and during the last recessionary period. As for the behavior of prices, the known data for 2018 continue to show moderate progress, with a year-on-year growth of the CPI, until March, of 1.2%. A slight recovery in inflation is expected for the coming months, which will continue to be influenced by the base effects of energy prices, so that, for 2018 as a whole, the latest projections by the Bank of Spain anticipate average inflation of 1.2%. For the following years, a gradual rebound in prices is expected, as a result of the progressive reduction of the cyclical slack of the Spanish economy. The main risks and elements of vulnerability Despite the dynamism of the Spanish economy that I have just pointed out, there are elements of vulnerability and possible obstacles to long-term growth. On the external front, we cannot rule out further episodes of volatility in financial markets during the process of monetary policy normalization in advanced economies. On the other hand, we must consider the effects of possible political disturbances, as well as the possible consequences on trade and world growth of the protectionist turn recently adopted by the US administration. These risks may alter the favorable scenario for the global economy that underlies our projections. Internally, political tensions in Catalonia could generate episodes of lack of confidence, as happened in the last quarter of last year. On the other hand, the growth of economic activity in recent years has been favoured by the contribution of factors of a transitory nature, such as a very accommodative monetary policy, a clearly expansionary fiscal policy in 2015 and 2016, and a favourable evolution of oil prices. It is conceivable that as these effects lose relevance, their contribution to the growth of the economy will decrease. Therefore, sustaining sustained growth may require reforms to replace the temporary boost recently provided by the above-mentioned transitory factors and monetary and fiscal policies. The need for reforms seems most pressing in an economy like ours, which has low productivity growth, lack of competitiveness in some sectors and still significant inefficiencies in the labour market. These factors, in an environment of intense population ageing, impose limits on potential growth in the medium and long term. Allow me to go on to review the main lines of the General State and Social Security Budgets for 2018. Budgetary policy in 2018 The macroeconomic forecasts accompanying the draft Budget represent the extension of the current growth phase. Specifically, they project an increase in real GDP of 2.7% in 2018, which would be accompanied by an increase in prices, so that the increase in nominal GDP would stand at 4.3%. The macroeconomic picture on which the draft Budget is based is, in general, compatible with the scenario I have described above, in which the latest projections of the Bank of Spain are framed and, more generally, with the scenario of consensus among analysts of private institutions. However, the nominal GDP growth expected for this year in the macroeconomic table of the budget is higher than projected by the Bank of Spain (4.3% compared to 3.8%). The deficit target for all the Public Administrations stands at 2.2% of GDP for 2018, which is compatible with the requirements of the Stability and Growth Pact, and represents an expected reduction of 0.9 pp of GDP, compared to the previous year, marking, if the transitory impact of financial aid is excluded, the ninth consecutive year of improvement in the public accounts, since the maximum deficit of 11% of GDP, recorded in 2009. For its part, the draft Budget places public debt at 97.6% of GDP in 2018, which would imply a reduction in this ratio of 0.7 pp of GDP compared to that registered in 2017, maintaining the slightly downward trend of recent years, from the maximum of 100.4% reached in 2014. In the current macroeconomic context, the improvement in the deficit in 2018 would be mainly due to the good cyclical performance of the economy and the reduction in interest payments on public debt, in a context of general moderation in public spending, determined by the expenditure ceiling, despite some measures to increase spending and reduce taxes incorporated into the draft budget. Thus, the tone of fiscal policy, measured by the change in the primary structural balance, could be neutral or slightly expansionary, compared with the neutral tone of 2017. Consequently, there would be no progress in reducing the still high structural deficit of Spanish public administrations in 2018. By subsectors, the draft Budget includes the stability objectives approved by the Cortes in July last year. For the Central Administration and Social Security, the public deficits expected for 2018 stand at 0.7% and 1.1% of GDP, respectively, compared to 1.9% and 1.5%, respectively, recorded in 2017. For their part, the objectives of the territorial administrations are a public deficit of 0.4% for the Autonomous Communities (0.3% in 2017) and budgetary balance for Local Corporations (compared to the surplus of 0.6 pp of GDP of the previous year). Compliance with the public deficit target incorporated in the Budget is based on two fundamental elements. First, in an evolution of spending in line with the limit imposed by the State spending ceiling approved by Congress in July of last year; secondly, in the significant advance of public revenues that is assumed. Among the most notable spending measures, it is worth mentioning the increase in 2018 of the fixed remuneration of public employees by 1.75% (plus 0.2% of additional funds to increase the wage bill), in line with the agreement reached between the Government and the main trade union organizations. As for public employment, the draft Budget gives continuity and expands in 2018 the hiring policy of the last two years. Specifically, the replacement rate of 100% of the staff at their service is generalized to most sectors of the Public Administrations, allowing in some cases, increases above this value, and additional actions are incorporated in terms of working hours and temporality. For the whole of 2018, these measures would lead to a 5.4% growth in wage expenditure in the State Budget, compared to the 2.3% decline observed in 2017. On the other hand, the restriction of current expenditure on goods and services is maintained, which is reduced by 4.1%. With regard to public investment, investment in the consolidated budget of the State, Social Security and the public business sector is expected to increase in 2018, around 15%, when compared to the initial budget of the previous year. In 2017 this figure was a reduction of 3.3%. Among the measures framed in the Social Security budget, the increases in minimum and widowhood pensions stand out, of 3% and 2%, respectively, and that of the lowest contributory pensions, in the range of 1 to 1.5%, which, as a whole, will increase contributory pensions by 1%, compared to 0.25% established in the revaluation formula. These measures, together with the demographic determinants, related to the evolution of the number of pensioners and the substitution effect of the new pensions with respect to those that are cancelled, will increase spending on contributory pensions this year by 3.5%. Thus, the weight of expenditure on pensions over total consolidated expenditure by the State and Social Security will increase to 40.9% (compared to 40.5% in 2017). It is also worth noting the reduction in spending on unemployment benefits, which incorporates the Draft Budget, of 10%, which should be consistent with the decreases assumed for the unemployment rate and for the coverage rate of the unemployed. On the income side, the main measures incorporated in the budgets are concentrated in the field of personal income tax, and are the increase of the minimum exempt from taxation of this tax from 12,000 to 14,000 euros gross per year, and other measures that reduce the taxation of net income from work, the creation of birth checks and nursery, and the expansion of existing family cheques. Overall, it is expected that tax revenues, before the transfer to territorial entities, will increase by 6.0% in 2018, and that social contributions will increase by 5.1%, which given the macroeconomic forecast and the impact of the aforementioned regulatory changes, would mean a response of the collection to the activity higher than that observed historically. The latter will make it advisable to continuously monitor the evolution of revenue during the year, so that it can react in time, both on the expenditure and revenue side, in case the risks to meeting the deficit target materialize. It should also be remembered that Spain is a country with a highly decentralised structure of competences in matters of public expenditure, where more than 40% is carried out by territorial administrations. In this way, the budget that affects the State and Social Security shows only a partial vision of the budgetary policy of all public administrations. In this context, the Update of the Stability Programme that will be published in the coming days, which consolidates the budgets of the administrations dependent on the central government with those of the Autonomous Communities and Local Corporations, becomes relevant. It is this document that should allow a full analysis of the budget forecasts. The importance of budgetary consolidation Before concluding, I would like to mention some of the challenges facing public finances in Spain. First of all, I would like to highlight the most immediate. Spanish Public Administrations are subject to an "Excessive Deficit Procedure", which was put in place march in April 2009, under the so-called "corrective component" of the Stability and Growth Pact. At the moment we are, with France, one of the two countries of the Union subject to this procedure. The deadline set by the Council of the European Union to overcome this situation is this year, 2018. It should be recalled, however, that, once this objective has been exceeded, the consolidation process will have to continue until budgetary balance is achieved in structural terms, which is essential to recover the margins for manoeuvre of fiscal policy in the event of adverse growth scenarios. Taking into account that, according to the European Commission's estimates, the structural deficit of Spanish general government would still stand at around 3% of GDP in 2017, the pending budgetary adjustment is still significant. In this context of consolidation, it is also essential to reach sustainable consensus over time on the reform of regional financing. Our administrative structure is based on strong decentralisation, so that the involvement of territorial administrations is essential to ensure budgetary stability. There is broad agreement that the current system of financing these administrations should be reformed to improve their transparency, ensure that their resources are adapted to spending needs and increase the degree of fiscal co-responsibility. Additionally, the Autonomous Communities should once again access the capital markets as a fundamental way of financing their budgetary imbalances, leaving the different State funds, developed during the crisis, as an emergency resource in exceptional circumstances. In any case, while these mechanisms are operational, it is necessary to apply the elements of conditionality they have. In the medium term, the main challenge in the area of public finances is the persistence of a high level of public debt, whose ratio to GDP stood at 98.3% in 2017. Although high nominal output growth has allowed this ratio to be reduced slightly from the peak reached in 2014, maintaining such a high level of public debt may affect the functioning of the economy, such as the absorption of resources that could have more productive uses, a greater dependence on external financial conditions, or reducing fiscal policy room for manoeuvre in the face of adverse shocks. If we add to these factors the normalization of financial conditions expected for the coming years and, even more importantly, the impact of demographic trends on spending in the medium term, it becomes clearer that the process of public deleveraging must be a priority. Given its relevance in several key dimensions, allow me to emphasise the impact of population ageing on public spending in the medium and long term, a major challenge for the sustainability of public finances. If the most recent estimates were met, public spending on pensions, health and long-term care would increase by 1.5 to 2 percentage points of GDP per year over the next three decades, peaking at over 21% of GDP around 2050. In the case of the pension system, the application of the sustainability factor, which links the initial pension to the increase in life expectancy, and, above all, the annual revaluation index of pensions, which links its increase to the balance between income and expenditure of the system, would, in favourable macroeconomic contexts, gradually reduce the current deficit, which reached 1.5% of GDP at the end of 2017, and counteract the effect of the expected increase in the dependency ratio in the long term. However, in the absence of additional revenue increases, the adjustment would occur mainly through a decrease in the replacement rate of public pensions. Looking ahead, the key is to strike a balance between the replacement rates of our pension system that are intended to be secured and the income needed to ensure the sustainability of the system. From the available analyses, it can be concluded that maintaining the current replacement rates, which are high in international comparison, would require very significant increases in the system's revenues. In any case, it is desirable that any reform strategy chosen increases the transparency of the system, strengthens the relationship between contributions and benefits, and maintains an adjustment mechanism that guarantees financial balance. For these reasons, it should be stressed that the fiscal consolidation process must be anchored in a medium-term programme detailing the measures to achieve the budgetary objectives, as well as in a prudent forecast of macroeconomic developments and government revenues. In the current environment, the composition of the adjustment is particularly important, so as to favour a greater contribution of public finances to the potential growth of the economy. In this sense, progress must continue in the rationalization and efficiency of public spending, as well as consider a review and definition of the tax basket that allows obtaining in a stable and efficient way the revenues necessary to finance the desired level of public spending. Conclusions And I'm done. The Spanish economy continues to show solid growth in output and employment, anchored in the strength of the foreign sector. This economic strength is expected to continue over the next few years, although it is likely to do so at a somewhat slower pace, in a context in which non-negligible risk elements persist. Despite this favourable reading and recent progress, the Spanish economy has significant imbalances, such as high public debt, external financing needs and the persistence of still very high levels of unemployment. For this reason, fiscal consolidation policies and reforms, aimed at underpinning the confidence of the various actors in the economy and increasing growth potential, are essential conditions for correcting these imbalances and allowing for continued growth in economic activity and job creation. Thank you very much for your attention.

La poltica presupuestaria en 2018 Las previsiones macroeconmicas que acompaan al proyecto de los Presupuestos suponen la extensin de la actual fase de crecimiento. Ese documento es el que debe permitir un anlisis completo de las previsiones presupuestarias. La importancia de la consolidacin presupuestaria Antes de terminar querra mencionar algunos de los retos a los que se enfrentan las finanzas pblicas en Espaa. En primer lugar, me gustara destacar lo ms inmediato. Las Administraciones Pblicas espaolas se encuentran sujetas a un Procedimiento de Dficit Excesivo, que se puso en marcha en abril de 2009, bajo el llamado componente correctivo del Pacto de Estabilidad y Crecimiento. En este momento somos, con Francia, uno de los dos pases de la Unin sometidos a este procedimiento. El plazo fijado por el Consejo de la Unin Europea para la superacin de esta situacin es este ao, 2018. Hay que recordar, no obstante, que, superado este objetivo, el proceso de consolidacin deber proseguir hasta lograr el equilibrio presupuestario en trminos estructurales, lo cual resulta fundamental para recuperar los mrgenes de maniobra de la poltica fiscal ante eventuales escenarios adversos de crecimiento. Teniendo en cuenta que, de acuerdo con las estimaciones de la Comisin Europea, el dficit estructural de las administraciones pblicas espaolas se situara todava en alrededor del 3% del PIB en 2017, el ajuste presupuestario pendiente es todava significativo. En este contexto de consolidacin, resulta asimismo imprescindible alcanzar consensos sostenibles en el tiempo sobre la reforma de la financiacin autonmica. Nuestra estructura administrativa se basa en una fuerte descentralizacin, de manera que el concurso de las administraciones territoriales resulta esencial para garantizar la estabilidad presupuestaria. Existe un acuerdo amplio en el sentido de que el actual sistema de financiacin de estas administraciones debe reformarse para mejorar su transparencia, conseguir la adecuacin de sus recursos a las necesidades de gasto e incrementar el grado de corresponsabilidad fiscal. Adicionalmente, las CCAA deberan volver a acceder a los mercados de capitales como va fundamental de financiacin de sus desequilibrios presupuestarios, dejando los distintos fondos del Estado, desarrollados durante la crisis, como recurso de emergencia ante circunstancias excepcionales. En todo caso, mientras estos mecanismos se encuentren operativos resulta necesario aplicar los elementos de condicionalidad con los que cuentan. A medio plazo, el principal reto en el mbito de las finanzas pblicas es el que plantea la persistencia de un elevado nivel de deuda pblica, cuya ratio sobre el PIB se situ en el 98,3 % en 2017. Si bien el alto crecimiento nominal del producto ha permitido reducir esta ratio ligeramente desde el mximo alcanzado en 2014, el mantenimiento de un nivel de endeudamiento pblico tan elevado puede afectar al funcionamiento de la economa, como por ejemplo por la absorcin de recursos que podran tener usos ms productivos, una mayor dependencia de las condiciones financieras exteriores, o la reduccin de los mrgenes de maniobra de la poltica fiscal ante perturbaciones adversas. Si a estos factores aadimos la normalizacin de las condiciones financieras prevista para los prximos aos y, an ms importante, si cabe, el impacto de las tendencias demogrficas sobre el gasto en el medio plazo, resulta ms evidente que el proceso de desendeudamiento pblico debe ser una prioridad. Dada su relevancia en varias dimensiones clave, permtanme que insista en el impacto del envejecimiento de la poblacin sobre el gasto pblico en el medio y largo plazo, un reto de primer orden para la sostenibilidad de las finanzas pblicas. Si se cumplieran las estimaciones ms recientes, se incrementara, por este concepto, el gasto pblico en pensiones, sanidad y cuidados de larga duracin entre 1,5 y 2 puntos porcentuales de PIB anuales durante las prximas tres dcadas, alcanzando un mximo superior al 21 % del PIB en torno a 2050. En el caso del sistema de pensiones, la aplicacin del factor de sostenibilidad, que liga la pensin inicial al incremento de la esperanza de vida, y, sobre todo, del ndice de revalorizacin anual de las pensiones, que vincula su incremento al equilibrio entre los ingresos y los gastos del sistema, lograran, en contextos macroeconmicos favorables, reducir de forma gradual el actual dficit, que alcanz el 1,5 % del PIB a finales de 2017, y contrarrestar el efecto del incremento esperado de la tasa de dependencia en el largo plazo. Ahora bien, en ausencia de incrementos adicionales de los ingresos, el ajuste se producira principalmente a travs de una disminucin de la tasa de sustitucin de las pensiones pblicas. De cara al futuro, la clave consiste en alcanzar un equilibrio entre las tasas de sustitucin de nuestro sistema de pensiones que se pretenden asegurar y los ingresos necesarios para garantizar la sostenibilidad del sistema. De los anlisis disponibles se puede concluir que el mantenimiento de las tasas de sustitucin actuales, que son elevadas en comparacin internacional, exigira incrementos muy significativos de los ingresos del sistema. En todo caso, es deseable que cualquier estrategia de reforma elegida aumente la transparencia del sistema, refuerce la relacin entre contribuciones y prestaciones, y, mantenga un mecanismo de ajuste que garantice el equilibrio financiero. Por las razones apuntadas, hay que subrayar que el proceso de consolidacin fiscal debe anclarse en un programa de medio plazo en el que se detallen las medidas que permitan la consecucin de los objetivos presupuestarios, as como en una previsin prudente de la evolucin macroeconmica y de los ingresos pblicos. En el entorno actual, adquiere especial importancia la composicin del ajuste, de forma que se favorezca una mayor contribucin de las finanzas pblicas al crecimiento potencial de la economa. En este sentido, se debe seguir avanzando en la racionalizacin y eficiencia del gasto pblico, as como considerar una revisin y definicin de la cesta de impuestos que permita obtener de forma estable y eficiente los ingresos necesarios para financiar el nivel deseado de gasto pblico. Conclusiones Y ya concluyo. La economa espaola contina mostrando un slido crecimiento del producto y del empleo, afianzados en la fortaleza del sector exterior. Se espera que esta pujanza econmica se prolongue durante los prximos aos, si bien es probable que lo haga a un ritmo algo menor, en un contexto en el que persisten elementos de riesgo no desdeables. Pese a esta lectura favorable y a los avances recientes, la economa espaola presenta importantes desequilibrios, como el elevado endeudamiento pblico, las necesidades de financiacin del exterior y la persistencia de niveles todava muy elevados de desempleo. Por esta razn, las polticas de consolidacin fiscal y la realizacin de reformas, destinadas a apuntalar la confianza de los distintos agentes en la economa y a aumentar el potencial de crecimiento, son condiciones esenciales para corregir estos desequilibrios y permitir el crecimiento continuado de la actividad econmica y la generacin de empleo. Muchas gracias por su atencin.

Title: Keynote speech at the NABE/Banco de Espaa symposium
text: 16.04.2018 Keynote address NABE-Banco de Espa96a Symposium Luis M. Linde Governor Welcome to the Bank of Spain. It is a real honor for us to host the fourth international symposium of the National Association for Business Economics (NABE). This edition is entitled "Global Recovery: the Good, the Ugly and the Bad", a suggestive title to highlight the challenges facing the current economic recovery. Over the next two days, a select group of panelists and guest speakers, along with the rest of the participants, will have the opportunity to discuss the origins, weaknesses and risks of the current recovery. Today we will begin the discussion with an overview of the main determinants of the current global recovery, followed by three sessions on various relevant issues. These issues will range from the role of the banking sector, as opposed to capital markets, in financing the real economy to the challenges central banks face in fulfilling their price stability mandate. During tonight's reception dinner, we will have the opportunity to learn about the vision of the global recovery of a very distinguished speaker: Peter Praet, Member of the Executive Board of the ECB. The symposium will continue tomorrow with Jordi Gual, Chairman of CaixaBank, who will present his views on current developments in the banking business. After several panels in which various topics, both interesting and timely, will be discussed, we will conclude with the speech on the main features of US economic policy by John Williams, president of the Federal Reserve of San Francisco and, starting next June, president of the Federal Reserve of New York. I believe that the format of the symposium will ensure a fruitful debate. Undoubtedly, the interaction between economists from the world of central banking, business, finance and academia, representing so many international institutions and entities, will provide us with varied and enriching perceptions about the world economy. But before starting with the debates, allow me to share with you some reflections on the current situation of the global economy and briefly summarize the recent developments and the main challenges facing the Spanish economy. In 2017, global growth was stronger than initially expected and broad-based across regions. The incipient recovery of investment and the expansion of international trade explain a significant part of this positive surprise, which reveals, once again, the role of international trade as a source of growth and prosperity. Therefore, referring to the words of the conference title, I think it would be accurate to say that the intense pace of world trade has been the 'good' thing during the recent period. However, the current positive tone of the world economy should not make us complacent. Indeed, the international economy faces significant risks. Specifically, there are three "ugly" global risk factors that, if they materialize, could lead us to some really "bad" scenarios. First, there is the rise of protectionism, which is becoming evident with the approval of new tariffs and the threats of trade wars. Economic history has amply demonstrated the costs of trade wars around the world and their implications in terms of economic, financial and political instability at the international level. We know that in trade wars there are no winners, only losers, as my colleague on the ECB's Governing Council, Beno94t Ccfur8e, pointed out a few days ago. Secondly, the uncertain outcome of the Brexit process entails risks not only for the European Union, but also for the global economy. A disorderly exit, with consequent financial instability and economic isolation from the United Kingdom, would have serious negative effects for the European economy as a whole, which would quickly spread to the rest of the world. The economic slowdown experienced by the United Kingdom in 2017, in an environment of strong global growth, should be interpreted as an indicator of these risks. Finally, the current calm in international financial markets, in a context of high asset valuations, low levels of volatility and risk premia, and strong investor appetite for risk, warns us of the risk of a potentially sharp adjustment. Indeed, we already received some warnings a couple of months ago, when global markets overreacted synchronously and synchronously to the news published about the US economy. Undoubtedly, the recent resurgence of certain geopolitical conflicts should, if anything, raise awareness d0 among both policymakers and market participants d0 of the risks and vulnerabilities that lie in the way of recovery. Allow me to link these reflections with some brief comments on the recent experience of the Spanish economy. Few economies have suffered the harsh consequences of the global recession that began in 2008 like Spain. Between 2008 and 2013, real GDP fell by 9% and the unemployment rate exceeded 27%. All in all, Spanish exports demonstrated an astonishing resilience. Following the collapse of world trade in late 2008 and early 2009, Spanish exports of goods and services grew by 28% between 2009 and 2013, largely cushioning the fall in domestic demand. The opening of the world economy and the security provided by belonging to the euro area were the essential levers of the recovery of Spanish sales abroad and, consequently, of our economic activity and job creation in our country. In Spain, the ratio of exports to GDP grew from 23% in 2009 to 34% in 2017. The greater internationalisation and competitiveness of the Spanish economy made it possible to convert the current account deficit in 2007, which was close to 10% of GDP, into the surpluses recorded since 2013. There is no doubt that protectionism and isolationism would only have worsened the economic and financial crisis in Spain and prevented its strong recovery. In addition to the significant contribution of the foreign sector, Spain's recovery has benefited enormously from the normalisation of its financial outlook, thanks to the combination of national and European initiatives. The recapitalisation and restructuring of a significant part of our financial sector was complemented by the still incomplete construction of the European banking union. The measures taken in these areas facilitated some of the conditions for recovery: the normalisation of capital and credit markets, and the gradual elimination of financial fragmentation in the euro area, an objective to which the ECB's monetary policy contributed crucially. In this context, Spanish non-financial corporations and households were able to reduce their debt by 63 points of GDP until the end of 2017, with a contained contractionary effect on aggregate demand. Now, as I have already said, there is no room for complacency. In addition to the factors of uncertainty for the world economy mentioned above, to which our country is certainly not immune, the Spanish economy faces its own challenges, among which the rapid aging of the population, a relatively low level of productivity and the need to considerably reduce the level of public debt in the coming years stand out. The comments and reflections of all of you on these and other issues will be very valuable to all of us. Let me conclude my statement by thanking the panelists, panellists and organisers for their contribution and wishing you all a fruitful and productive debate, as well as a happy stay in Madrid. Thank you.
text_original: 16.04.2018 Discurso de apertura Simposio NABE-Banco de Espaa Luis M. Linde Gobernador Bienvenidos al Banco de Espaa. Es para nosotros un verdadero honor acoger el cuarto simposio internacional de la National Association for Business Economics (NABE). Sin duda, la interaccin entre economistas procedentes del mundo de la banca central, empresarial, financiero y acadmico, que representan a tantas instituciones y entidades internacionales, nos proporcionar percepciones variadas y enriquecedoras sobre la economa mundial. Sin embargo, el actual tono positivo de la economa mundial no debera hacernos caer en la complacencia. De hecho, la economa internacional se enfrenta a riesgos significativos. Concretamente, existen tres factores de riesgo feos de carcter global que, si se materializan, podran conducirnos a algunos escenarios realmente malos. En segundo lugar, el incierto resultado del proceso del Brexit entraa riesgos no solo para la Unin Europea, sino tambin para la economa global. Una salida desordenada, con la consiguiente inestabilidad financiera y aislamiento econmico del Reino Unido, tendra efectos negativos graves para la economa europea en su conjunto, que se extenderan rpidamente al resto del mundo. La desaceleracin econmica que experiment el Reino Unido en 2017, en un entorno de fuerte crecimiento mundial, debera interpretarse como un indicador de dichos riesgos. Por ltimo, la calma que reina actualmente en los mercados financieros internacionales, en un contexto de elevadas valoraciones de los activos, niveles de volatilidad y primas de riesgo reducidos, y fuerte apetito de riesgo de los inversores, nos advierte del riesgo de un ajuste potencialmente brusco. Sin duda, el reciente resurgimiento de determinados conflictos geopolticos debera, si acaso, concienciarnos ms tanto a las autoridades como a los participantes en los mercados sobre los riesgos y vulnerabilidades que acechan en el camino de la recuperacin. Permtanme que enlace estas reflexiones con algunos breves comentarios sobre la experiencia reciente de la economa espaola. Pocas economas han sufrido como Espaa las duras consecuencias de la recesin global que comenz en 2008. Entre 2008 y 2013, el PIB real cay un 9% y la tasa de paro super el 27%. Tras el desplome del comercio mundial a finales de 2008 y principios de 2009, las exportaciones espaolas de bienes y servicios crecieron un 28% entre 2009 y 2013, amortiguando en gran medida la cada de la demanda interna. No cabe duda de que el proteccionismo y el aislamiento no habran hecho ms que empeorar la crisis econmica y financiera en Espaa y habran impedido su fuerte recuperacin. Adems de la significativa contribucin del sector exterior, la recuperacin espaola se ha beneficiado enormemente de la normalizacin de su panorama financiero, gracias a la combinacin de iniciativas nacionales y europeas. La recapitalizacin y reestructuracin de una parte importante de nuestro sector financiero se vieron complementadas por la construccin an incompleta de la unin bancaria europea. Las medidas adoptadas en estos mbitos facilitaron algunas de las condiciones necesarias para la recuperacin: la normalizacin de los mercados de capitales y de crdito, y la eliminacin gradual de la fragmentacin financiera en el rea del euro, un objetivo al que la poltica monetaria del BCE contribuy de forma crucial. En este contexto, las sociedades no financieras y los hogares espaoles fueron capaces de reducir su deuda en 63 puntos del PIB hasta finales de 2017, con un efecto contractivo contenido sobre la demanda agregada. Ahora bien, como ya he dicho, no hay lugar para la complacencia. Adems de los factores de incertidumbre para la economa mundial mencionados anteriormente, a los que sin duda nuestro pas no es inmune, la economa espaola se enfrenta a sus propios retos, entre los que destacan el rpido envejecimiento de la poblacin, un nivel de productividad relativamente bajo y la necesidad de reducir considerablemente el nivel de deuda pblica en los prximos aos. Los comentarios y las reflexiones de todos ustedes sobre estas y otras cuestiones resultarn muy valiosos para todos nosotros. Permtanme que concluya mi intervencin agradeciendo a los panelistas, ponentes y organizadores su contribucin y desendoles a todos un debate fructfero y productivo, as como una feliz estancia en Madrid.
