Title: Introduction to John Williams at the NABE/Banco de Espaa Symposium
text: 17.04.2018 NABE/Banco de Espana Symposium Introduction to John Williams Luis M. Linde Governor Dear participants, We are fortunate to be able to close this symposium with an eminent speaker, John Williams. John is one of the most influential economists in the United States, with an outstanding record both as a scholar and as a policy-maker. After completing his PhD in Economics from Stanford University, John began his career as an economist at the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, where he contributed to bringing traditional macro models towards what is now considered the state of the art. Subsequently, John joined the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, later becoming Director of Research. Under his leadership, the San Francisco Fed became one of the leading research hubs of the Federal Reserve system. In 2011 John took over from Janet Yellen as President of the San Francisco Fed. And just a few weeks ago, he was named as the successor to William C. Dudley as New York Fed president. He will occupy a permanent seat on the Federal Open Market Committee, the Federal Reserves monetary policy-making body. Congratulations, John, and, we wish you the very best of luck on your new appointment. John Williamss research features significant contributions on a wide range of topics in modern macroeconomics, from the analysis of monetary policy under uncertainty, to the study of innovation and productivity. Crucially, his research has brought back to the attention of policymakers the role of the natural interest rate, a concept which dates back to the contribution of Wicksell a century ago, and which has gained greatly in importance in the analysis and conduct of monetary policy. John has popularised the idea that the natural interest rate is not constant or even stationary. His research reveals that the bulk of the fall in the natural interest rate can be attributed to a slowdown of trend productivity growth, a view that has gained ground in academic and policy circles. That is related to the risk of a a low economic growth scenario, at least in the advanced economies, an idea that has been present in your discussions during the symposium. On behalf of the organisers of this conference, the National Association for Business Economics and Banco de Espana and, also, on a personal note, I would like to warmly thank John Williams for joining us here today.

Title: Closing address of the Workshop "La Revolucin Fintech"
text: 23.04.18 "Central banks and new technologies in the financial sector" Closing of the workshop "The Fintech Revolution", organized by Garrigues and IEAF-FEF Javier Alonso Deputy governor Good morning. I would like to begin by thanking the organizers - Garrigues, the Spanish Institute of Financial Analysts (IEAF) and the Fundaci97n de Estudios Financieros (FEF) - for their invitation to close this workshop dedicated to analysing the effect that technological development is having on the provision of financial services. I think you will agree with me that the changes that this development brings with it are profound, they go beyond what would be a mere adaptation or a simple investment, and may end up affecting both the number and type of agents participating in the market, as well as the groups that access certain products or the way in which certain services are used. In this context, I would like to focus my statement today on two parts. In the first part, my objective is to explain how at the Bank of Spain we are paying increasing attention to a phenomenon whose breadth, global dimension and pace of transformation exceed the parameters that used to characterize changes in the banking sector. In the second part, I would like to share with you some considerations in relation to a particular product: that of crypto-assets. A certain "informative exuberance" has been generated about him in recent months and I would like to highlight some aspects that I consider important to take into account. Organizational changes to address the challenge of financial innovation Starting with the first part, as I have pointed out, technological development is altering the financial system in several dimensions. On the one hand, new service providers are emerging that, in some cases, compete with traditional banking in specific market niches and, in other cases, offer innovative financial products or aimed at groups that previously only had access to a very limited number of financial instruments. Traditional banks are reacting to this change with different types of strategies. Some of these strategies are based on cooperation, for example, on the use of blockchain technology to make digital identification processes more efficient. Others rely on alliances or investment in new entities. You know examples of joint projects developed between banks and new fintech companies and investment platforms promoted by banks to invest in new companies in this field. There are also strategies that simply try to incorporate new technologies in the way in which entities carry out their activity to put more emphasis on aspects such as improving accessibility to banking services through mobile or the proliferation of online applications of banks to advise us in a personalized way on how to manage the current expenses of a household. Finally, I cannot fail to mention the systematic request of the entities for an "intense dialogue" with the authorities to redefine the regulatory framework, understanding that they are not in equal conditions to compete with new companies. And Both these and the banks raise the need to create test spaces, or, if you prefer, sandboxes. Sandboxes that, in any case, would be applicable to initiatives that bring improvements to society and not only profits to the entrepreneur at the expense of greater risks. All this transformation represents a real modification of the financial ecosystem to which central banks and financial regulators must react. The nature of these trends means that several areas of action of the authorities are affected, including, among others, consumer protection, control and risk management, the process of authorizations to carry out reserved activities, data protection or the prevention against money laundering and terrorist financing. In this regard, it is not surprising that the first reaction of many authorities has been to organize coordination committees, both internally and between authorities, to assess the impact of financial innovation. At the Bank of Spain we have not been oblivious to this trend and, in February 2016, we created the so-called Financial Innovation Group in which all the Directorates-General were represented. This first effort was in the right direction but, probably, it was insufficient since, in addition to strengthening coordination and sharing information, it is necessary to dedicate specific resources to: (i) try to understand the dimension of the change that is taking place, (ii) analyze the consequences that may end up having aspects such as blockchain technology or the use of artificial intelligence, (iii) and, be in permanent contact with authorities from other jurisdictions to share experiences and coordinate responses, taking into account the global nature of this transformation. For this reason, at the Banco de Espa96a we have recently created a new Deputy Directorate-General with the intention of strengthening these aspects. This area will necessarily have to work transversally, given the multiple functions of the central bank that are affected. Additionally, it will maintain a fluid dialogue with other Spanish authorities d0 such as the CNMV or the General Secretariat of the Treasury and Financial Policy d0 with the market, both through already established forums and through bilateral meetings, and with international institutions, particularly European ones, to share experiences and improve information on the importance of some of the trends. The ultimate objective is to develop an overview of the main characteristics and challenges that the provision of financial services will face in the near future, including the consequences for established entities. In this sense, I am convinced that new technologies d0 and new intermediaries d0 will offer the possibility of improving the quality of the services provided, increasing efficiency in many of the processes currently used by traditional entities and reducing costs. However, these changes are also likely to necessitate a review of the body of legislation, to determine whether reforms are needed in such essential areas as the information requirements that new entrants must provide to authorities or supervisory intensity in aspects related to security, data protection or consumer protection. Criptoactivos Let me close my speech with a few brief reflections on what is popularly known as crypto-assets or cryptotokens (which could be translated as "crypto-vouchers"). As you know, a joint statement has recently been published by the CNMV and the Bank of Spain on this particular with which we have tried to alert the public about the limitations and dangers associated with this type of investment. In particular, we have stressed that they are not legally considered money or deposits and therefore do not benefit from the protections and guarantees contemplated in the regulations on banking or investment products. We have also highlighted their speculative nature, the absence of support from supervisory bodies and the vulnerabilities they present both on the side of fraud and possible price manipulation. Finally, we have taken advantage of this statement to highlight the liquidity problems they may present. However, given that interest in the subject remains high, I think it is appropriate to insist on this matter again. Since the appearance of Bitcoin in 2009, the number of crypto assets has increased steadily to exceed 1,500 initiatives. In addition, its market value has multiplied by five in the last year. Both circumstances and, above all, the breadth of the modalities of its commercialization - directly, through contracts for difference or through other structured products such as futures contracts or swaps - favour a greater diversity of uses and make economies around the world increasingly exposed to their risks. While it is true that their relative weight is still small (barely 1% of global GDP), it is noted that cryptoassets are gaining attractiveness among retail investors. This fact, together with their extreme volatility and the heavy losses they have experienced as a result of operational failures and other cyber threats, paints a picture on which it is urgent that the authorities take a stand. And not only in terms of improving our level of information and knowledge but, especially, in terms of undertaking possible public policy actions. As regulators and supervisors, our main concern is their potential impact on financial stability, not forgetting the ramifications they may have on customer protection, data protection, market integrity, tax evasion or avoidance of money laundering controls. In short, it is about being able to adopt adequate safeguards without losing the necessary flexibility to take advantage of the potential benefits that could be brought by the underlying technologies, especially distributed ledgers. As this is a global phenomenon, the effectiveness of any measure depends on a cooperative approach, an issue in which we are fully involved both in Europe and in other multilateral forums. Specifically, one of the outstanding commitments of the Financial Stability Board (FSB) and the The European Commission for the year 2018 is, precisely, the identification of information needs and the formulation of appropriate indicators that allow us to strengthen the tasks of monitoring and measuring emerging risks. This effort to increase the transparency and traceability of the operations that take place with crypto-assets should be seen as a first step in a more ambitious strategy that aims to more accurately assess the possible risks, without ultimately ruling out regulatory changes that respond to the vulnerabilities detected, eliminate opportunities for arbitrage and provide a solid foundation for the development of an industry compatible with a safe global financial system. In my view, the answer to this challenge lies not in seeking groundbreaking approaches but, rather, in identifying existing parallels with other financial instruments and, where this is not possible, in applying the current guiding principles of international financial regulation. Consequently, the resulting framework should be focused on ensuring a homogeneous treatment of equivalent situations, adapting the requirements to the specific risk profile of both the economic functions performed by each family of crypto-assets and the activities that take place around them. In this sense, it is reasonable to extend to this sector the provisions of the regulation on the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing, but also others related to operational risk management and transparency and protection of the rights of the user of financial services. In conclusion, I would like to refer briefly to two issues. The first of these is central bank digital currencies. The possibility of central banks issuing digital money, employing technology similar to that used by some cryptotokens, has sparked growing interest. It is true that new technologies open the opportunity to redesign traditional functions assigned to central banks, even some as established as the issuance and distribution of money. However, it is clear that, beyond the purely operational questions about the technological capacity to digitally record the transactions that are currently made with cash in its physical form, the implications of issuing money digitally are far-reaching in many areas. Central banks have begun to analyze this issue, paying attention to the main implications and the different aspects that need to be addressed. In this sense, the report that the Bank for International Settlements recently published (in March) with the title of "Central Bank Digital Currencies" is a good reference on the current state of the discussions that central banks are having, still of a preliminary nature. It is a reading that I recommend to those who have an interest in this topic. I encourage you, in particular, to consider carefully the scope and complexity of some of the issues raised there. Personally, I have many doubts about the future viability of this initiative. The second of the issues I want to address briefly is the situation of crypto assets in Spain. Although, in the absence of official data, it is difficult to get an idea of the real size of this market in our country, we are aware of the existence of a certain level of activity involving people residing in our territory. For the most part, this is done through providers located abroad, which provide a range of services ranging from exchange platforms, to cryptocurrency loans, or brokers that mediate between buyers and sellers of contracts for differences. In addition, we know of the existence of more than twenty initiatives of "initial cryptocurrency offerings" or ICO (Initial Coin Offerings) by the hand of Spanish promoters that, in their entirety, are being carried out from countries such as Switzerland, Singapore or Estonia or territories such as Gibraltar. Due to its potential implications, the Banco de Espa96a is already working on improving the quality and volume of the information we currently have, for which we have opened channels of cooperation, at all levels, with other national bodies and authorities. We are confident that this dialogue will soon bear fruit in visible results. Conclusion In conclusion, let me highlight that, as in other transformation processes that we have seen in history, opportunities open up to increase efficiency, improving, in this case, financial services. But it should not be forgotten, however, that changes also pose significant challenges in the form of new risks. Little is said about these. That is why I paid a lot of attention to them during my speech, because it is in our DNA. We are for innovation but we are regulators, supervisors and custodians of financial stability. Thank you very much for your attention.

Algunas de estas estrategias estn basadas en la cooperacin, por ejemplo, en el uso de la tecnologa de blockchain para hacer ms eficientes los procesos de identificacin digital. Otras se basan en las alianzas o en la inversin en nuevas entidades. Ustedes conocen ejemplos de proyectos conjuntos desarrollados entre bancos y nuevas empresas fintech y de plataformas de inversin promovidas por entidades bancarias para invertir en nuevas compaas de este mbito. Existen tambin estrategias que, sencillamente, tratan de incorporar las nuevas tecnologas en la forma en la que las entidades realizan su actividad para poner ms nfasis en aspectos tales como la mejora en la accesibilidad a los servicios bancarios a travs del mvil o en la proliferacin de aplicaciones online de los bancos para asesorarnos de modo personalizado sobre la forma de gestionar los gastos corrientes de un hogar. Por ltimo, no puedo dejar de mencionar la sistemtica peticin de las entidades de un dilogo intenso con las autoridades para redefinir el marco regulatorio, al entender que no se encuentran en igualdad de condiciones para competir con las nuevas empresas. Y tanto estas como los bancos plantean la necesidad de crear espacios de prueba, o, si lo prefieren, sandboxes. Sandboxes que, en todo caso, seran aplicables a las iniciativas que aporten mejoras a la sociedad y no slo ganancias al emprendedor a costa de mayores riesgos. Toda esta transformacin supone una verdadera modificacin del ecosistema financiero ante la cual los bancos centrales y los reguladores financieros hemos de reaccionar. La naturaleza de estas tendencias hace que sean varias las reas de actuacin de las autoridades que se ven afectadas, incluyendo, entre otras, la proteccin al consumidor, el control y la gestin del riesgo, el proceso de autorizaciones para realizar actividades reservadas, la proteccin de datos o la prevencin frente al lavado de dinero y la financiacin del terrorismo. En este sentido, no resulta sorprendente que la primera reaccin de muchas autoridades haya sido la de organizar comits de coordinacin, tanto internos como entre autoridades, para evaluar el impacto de la innovacin financiera. En el Banco de Espaa no hemos sido ajenos a esta tendencia y, en febrero de 2016, creamos el denominado Grupo de Innovacin Financiera en el que se encontraban representadas todas las Direcciones Generales. Este primer esfuerzo iba en buena direccin pero, probablemente, era insuficiente ya que, adems de reforzar la coordinacin y compartir la informacin, es necesario dedicar recursos especficos para: (i) tratar de comprender la dimensin del cambio que se est produciendo, (ii) analizar las consecuencias que pueden acabar teniendo aspectos como la tecnologa del blockchain o el uso de la inteligencia artificial, (iii) y, estar en contacto permanente con autoridades de otras jurisdicciones para compartir experiencias y coordinar las respuestas, atendiendo a la naturaleza global de esta transformacin. Por ello, en el Banco de Espaa hemos procedido recientemente a la creacin de una nueva Direccin General Adjunta con la intencin de reforzar estos aspectos. Esta rea deber trabajar, necesariamente, de modo transversal, dadas las mltiples funciones del banco central que se ven afectadas. Adicionalmente, mantendr un dilogo fluido con otras autoridades espaolas -como la CNMV o la Secretara General del Tesoro y Poltica Financiera- con el mercado, tanto a travs de foros ya establecidos como a travs de encuentros bilaterales, y con las instituciones internacionales, particularmente las europeas, para compartir experiencias y mejorar la informacin sobre la importancia de algunas de las tendencias. El objetivo ltimo es desarrollar una visin de conjunto sobre las principales caractersticas y desafos a los que va a enfrentarse la provisin de servicios financieros en el futuro prximo, incluyendo las consecuencias para las entidades ya establecidas. En este sentido, estoy convencido de que las nuevas tecnologas- y los nuevos intermediarios- ofrecern la posibilidad de mejorar la calidad de los servicios prestados, aumentar la eficiencia en muchos de los procesos actualmente empleados por las entidades tradicionales y reducir costes. No obstante, tambin es probable que estos cambios hagan conveniente una revisin del cuerpo normativo, para determinar si son necesarias reformas en aspectos tan esenciales como los requisitos de informacin que los nuevos participantes deban suministrar a las autoridades o la intensidad supervisora en aspectos relacionados con la seguridad, la proteccin de datos o la proteccin al consumidor. Criptoactivos Permtanme que cierre mi intervencin con unas breves reflexiones acerca de lo que se conoce popularmente como criptoactivos o criptotokens (que podra traducirse por cripto-vales). Como saben, recientemente se ha publicado un comunicado conjunto de la CNMV y del Banco de Espaa sobre este particular con el que hemos tratado de alertar al pblico sobre las limitaciones y peligros asociados a esta clase de inversiones. En concreto, hemos subrayado que no tienen la consideracin legal de dinero ni de depsitos y que, por tanto, no se benefician de las protecciones y garantas contempladas en la normativa de productos bancarios o de inversin. Hemos destacado, igualmente, su carcter especulativo, la ausencia de respaldo por parte de los organismos supervisores y las vulnerabilidades que presentan tanto por el lado del fraude como por el de la posible manipulacin de precios. Finalmente, hemos aprovechado este comunicado para hacer hincapi en los problemas de liquidez que pueden presentar. No obstante, dado que el inters por la materia sigue siendo alto, creo oportuno volver a insistir sobre este asunto. Desde la aparicin de Bitcoin en el ao 2009, el nmero de criptoactivos ha aumentado de forma sostenida hasta llegar a sobrepasar las 1.500 iniciativas. Adems, su valor de mercado se ha multiplicado por cinco en este ltimo ao. Ambas circunstancias y, sobre todo, la amplitud de las modalidades de su comercializacin -directamente, a travs de contratos por diferencias o por medio de otros productos estructurados como contratos con futuros o swaps- favorecen una mayor diversidad de usos y hacen que las economas de todo el mundo estn cada vez ms expuestas a sus riesgos. Si bien es cierto que su peso relativo sigue siendo pequeo (apenas el 1% del PIB mundial), se constata que los criptoactivos van ganando atractivo entre el inversor minorista. Este hecho, unido a su volatilidad extrema y a las fuertes prdidas que han experimentado a consecuencia de fallos operativos y de otras amenazas cibernticas, dibuja un panorama ante el que resulta apremiante que las autoridades tomemos postura. Y no slo en trminos de mejorar nuestro nivel de informacin y conocimiento sino, especialmente, en lo que se refiere a emprender posibles actuaciones de poltica pblica. Como reguladores y supervisores, nuestra preocupacin principal se centra en sus potenciales repercusiones para la estabilidad financiera, sin olvidar las ramificaciones que puedan tener sobre la proteccin de la clientela, la proteccin de datos, la integridad del mercado, la evasin fiscal o la elusin de controles sobre el blanqueo. Se trata, en definitiva, de ser capaces de adoptar salvaguardas adecuadas sin perder la flexibilidad necesaria para aprovechar los potenciales beneficios que pudieran reportar las tecnologas subyacentes, especialmente los registros distribuidos. Al tratarse de un fenmeno de carcter global, la efectividad de cualquier medida pasa por apostar por un enfoque cooperativo, cuestin en la que estamos plenamente involucrados tanto en Europa como en otros foros multilaterales. En concreto, uno de los compromisos destacados del Consejo de Estabilidad Financiera (FSB, por sus siglas en ingls) y de la Comisin Europea para el ejercicio 2018 es, precisamente, la identificacin de las necesidades de informacin y la formulacin de unos indicadores adecuados que nos permitan reforzar las tareas de seguimiento y medicin de los riesgos emergentes. Este esfuerzo por aumentar la transparencia y trazabilidad de la operativa que tiene lugar con criptoactivos debe ser visto como un primer paso dentro de una estrategia ms ambiciosa que aspire a evaluar con ms precisin los posibles riesgos, sin descartar en ltima instancia que se produzcan cambios normativos que den respuesta a las vulnerabilidades detectadas, eliminen las oportunidades para el arbitraje y provean un fundamento slido para el desarrollo de una industria compatible con la existencia de un sistema financiero global seguro. A mi juicio, la respuesta a este reto no se encuentra en buscar planteamientos de carcter rupturista sino, ms bien, en identificar los paralelismos existentes con otros instrumentos financieros y, donde esto no sea posible, en aplicar los actuales principios rectores de la regulacin financiera internacional. En consecuencia, el marco resultante debe ir enfocado a garantizar un tratamiento homogneo de situaciones equivalentes, adaptando las exigencias al perfil de riesgo especfico tanto de las funciones econmicas que desempea cada familia de criptoactivos como al de las actividades que se desarrollan a su alrededor. En este sentido, es razonable extender a este sector las disposiciones propias de la regulacin de prevencin del blanqueo de capitales y financiacin del terrorismo, pero tambin otras relacionadas con la gestin del riesgo operativo y la transparencia y proteccin de los derechos del usuario de los servicios financieros. Para cerrar mi intervencin quisiera referirme, brevemente, a dos cuestiones. La primera de ellas es el dinero digital de banco central (central bank digital currencies). La posibilidad de que los bancos centrales emitan dinero digital, empleando una tecnologa similar a la que usan algunos criptotokens, ha despertado un creciente inters. Es cierto que las nuevas tecnologas abren la oportunidad para redisear funciones tradicionales asignadas a los bancos centrales, incluso de algunas tan asentadas como la emisin y distribucin del dinero. Sin embargo, es evidente que, ms all de las cuestiones puramente operativas sobre la capacidad tecnolgica de registrar de modo digital las transacciones que en la actualidad se hacen con el efectivo en su forma fsica, las implicaciones de emitir dinero de forma digital son de gran calado en multitud de mbitos. Los bancos centrales hemos comenzado a analizar esta cuestin, prestando atencin a las principales implicaciones y a los distintos aspectos que deben ser abordados. En este sentido, el informe que el Banco de Pagos Internacionales public recientemente (en marzo) con el ttulo de Central Bank Digital Currencies es una buena referencia sobre el estado actual de las discusiones que los bancos centrales estamos manteniendo, todava de carcter preliminar. Es una lectura que recomiendo a quienes tengan inters en este tema. Les animo, en particular, a que consideren con detenimiento el alcance y la complejidad de algunas de las cuestiones que all se plantean. A m, personalmente, me crean muchas dudas sobre la viabilidad futura de esta iniciativa. La segunda de las cuestiones que quiero abordar brevemente es la situacin de los criptoactivos en Espaa. Aunque, en ausencia de datos oficiales, resulta complicado hacerse una idea del tamao real de este mercado en nuestro pas, somos conscientes de la existencia de cierto nivel de actividad que involucra a personas residentes en nuestro territorio. En su mayor parte, sta se realiza a travs de proveedores situados en el extranjero, los cuales proporcionan un rango de servicios que abarca desde plataformas de intercambio, a prstamos en criptomonedas, o brokers que intermedian entre compradores y vendedores de contratos por diferencias. Adems, sabemos de la existencia de ms de una veintena de iniciativas de ofertas iniciales de criptomonedas o ICO (Initial Coin Offerings) de la mano de promotores espaoles que, en su prctica totalidad, se estn llevando a cabo desde pases como Suiza, Singapur o Estonia o territorios como Gibraltar. Por sus implicaciones potenciales, desde el Banco de Espaa ya estamos trabajando en mejorar la calidad y el volumen de la informacin de que disponemos en la actualidad, para lo que hemos abierto vas de cooperacin, a todos los niveles, con otros organismos y autoridades nacionales. Confiamos en que este dilogo fructifique pronto en resultados visibles. Conclusin A modo de conclusin djenme resaltar que, como en otros procesos de transformacin que hemos visto en la historia, se abren oportunidades para incrementar la eficiencia, mejorando, en este caso, los servicios financieros. Pero no debe olvidarse, sin embargo, que los cambios tambin plantean importantes desafos en la forma de nuevos riesgos. De estos se habla poco. Por eso les he dedicado bastante atencin durante mi intervencin, porque va en nuestro ADN. Estamos a favor de la innovacin pero somos reguladores, supervisores y cuidadores de la estabilidad financiera. Muchas gracias por su atencin.

Title: Intervention in the presentation of the Financial Competence Survey. Event organized by the CNMV and the Banco de Espaa
text: 25.05.2018 Financial Skills Survey (ECF) Luis M. Linde Governor Good morning: I want to start this intervention by expressing my satisfaction for participating in this event in which we presented the Financial Skills Survey (FCS). The event will take place in two parts. First, the President of the CNMV and myself will intervene to frame and describe this statistic and its importance. The characteristics, methods and results of the survey will be presented in more detail below. The presentation in this second part will be given by Olympia Bover, coordinator of the study and author of the Main Results Report, together with Laura Hospido and Ernesto Villanueva, economists of the General Directorate of Economics and Statistics of the Bank of Spain. The Financial Skills Survey is part of the Financial Education Plan, a project initiated ten years ago by the Bank of Spain and the National Securities Market Commission, to which the Ministry of Economy, Industry and Competitiveness, through the General Directorate of Insurance and Pension Funds, and the Ministry of Education, subsequently joined. Culture and Sport. The continuity of the Plan highlights the importance that its promoting authorities attach to improving the basic financial skills of citizens. Savings, insurance and financing vehicles are key tools for families to plan their main economic decisions throughout their lives. However, several international studies in neighboring countries such as France, Italy, Germany or the United States show that large segments of the population seem to be unfamiliar with financial concepts that are essential to be able to adequately face some of these decisions. For example, according to the latest results of the International Financial Education Network of the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD), in countries such as France, Germany or Italy, at least 30% of the population believes that inflation does not reduce the real purchasing power of money. Similarly, when calculating the evolution of an amount saved in a deposit, more than 40% of the people interviewed in these countries do not take into account that the interest rate is also applied on interest generated in the past. Likewise, it is not uncommon to find savers who do not know if the risk associated with an investment is greater or lower according to the increase in the number and variety of actions in which it is invested. A limited understanding of relatively elementary concepts, such as inflation, compound interest rate or risk diversification, makes it difficult to compare products with different returns, risks or maturities, which leads to the adoption of decisions that are not optimal by many families. In fact, internationally available evidence suggests that households that are unaware of these basics tend to be more indebted and save less. It is pertinent to ask, therefore, why financial knowledge differs between different groups of the population. There is some consensus that this type of knowledge is acquired gradually throughout life, partly during the formative stage and, also, during adult life, from one's own experience. And there are well-founded reasons to consider that our country does not constitute an exception to the pattern detected in other developed countries. As an example, in Spain a high percentage of citizens in various age groups have completed only primary education, something that limits the possibility of acquiring certain basic numerical knowledge in the education system. In fact, the limited evidence available suggests that Spain does indeed largely share the problems mentioned above. Why is it necessary to try to measure the degree of development of financial skills? Understanding the context in which households make their savings and debt decisions requires a reliable measure of financial literacy from representative samples of the population. Measurement must also cover a broad range of subjects, which go beyond knowledge of, for example, inflation or interest rates, and which must extend to the type of savings or borrowing vehicles they know, which they own and, when choosing between different savings or debt products, What are the sources of information used. Similarly, it is also important to understand how households use different financial products. For example, there is little evidence on what percentage of individuals choose to save in demand accounts, cash or using a term tax. Similarly, there is also little information about how Spanish families finance the specific mismatches between their expenses and their current income, including the frequency with which they obtain credit from relatives or, alternatively, with which they use their credit card. Several countries in our environment are asking these same questions and for this reason, in 2015, the OECD launched an initiative coordinated among more than thirty countries to measure financial knowledge, attitudes towards savings and financial behavior of the population between 18 and 79 years. It is in this context that the Bank of Spain and the National Securities Market Commission have prepared the Financial Skills Survey, within the framework of the Financial Education Plan and included in the National Statistical Plan, which demonstrates its importance. This survey will also be the Spanish contribution to the international effort in this area coordinated by the OECD. This study, which has been carried out for the first time between 2016 and 2017, through personal interviews, has had the valuable and essential collaboration of the National Institute of Statistics, which has developed a large sample of adult individuals, selected at random, representative of the entire Spanish territory and each of its Autonomous Communities. The main novel elements of the Financial Skills Survey The survey has several novel elements, which I would like to highlight. Firstly, as we know, in Spain educational competences are decentralised. Since financial competencies vary sharply with the educational level of individuals, the project has representative samples for each of the Autonomous Communities. Secondly, the Survey does not only include individual financial skills, but also those of the household in which you reside. This is especially important in Spain, a country where, as a relatively high percentage of young people live with their parents, individual financial skills may not be reflected in household decisions as a whole. To this end, the Survey collects information on the financial situation of the household as a whole. In particular, it includes a module on the main dwelling, which provides information on the household's decision to acquire or not a home, the reasons why you opt for buying or renting, as well as expectations about the future evolution of the price of the family home. Finally, decisions such as the acquisition of a financial product are affected by non-strictly financial skills, such as reading, numerical or even those related to the ability to understand graphic elements. The survey contains internationally validated questions aimed at measuring these competencies. In addition, questions have also been included to measure knowledge on some key issues in the understanding of basic macroeconomic phenomena, such as inflation and money. I mention these novel elements of the survey to indicate that the availability of these data will allow, in addition to guiding the future efforts of the Financial Education Plan, to analyze the influence of financial competencies on the savings, indebtedness and insurance decisions of families. In the presentation that will take place in the second part of the event, by Olympia Bover, the results of the survey will be shown in detail. However, before giving the floor to the President of the CNMV, I would like to conclude by thanking all the people and institutions that collaborate, directly or indirectly, with the Financial Education Plan, and, in particular, all the people who have been involved in the preparation of this Financial Skills Survey and, above all, to the citizens who have agreed to answer the survey. Without their collaboration this study would not have been possible. Thank you very much for your attention.
text_original: 25.05.2018 Encuesta de Competencias Financieras (ECF) Luis M. Linde Gobernador Buenos das: Quiero comenzar esta intervencin manifestando mi satisfaccin por participar en este acto en el que presentamos la Encuesta de Competencias Financieras (ECF). El acto se desarrollar en dos partes. En primer lugar, intervendremos el Presidente de la CNMV y yo mismo para enmarcar y describir esta estadstica y su importancia. A continuacin, se presentarn con ms detalle las caractersticas, mtodos y resultados de la encuesta. La presentacin en esta segunda parte correr a cargo de Olympia Bover, coordinadora del estudio y autora del Informe de Principales Resultados, junto con Laura Hospido y Ernesto Villanueva, economistas de la Direccin General de Economa y Estadstica del Banco de Espaa. La Encuesta de Competencias Financieras forma parte del Plan de Educacin Financiera, un proyecto iniciado hace diez aos por el Banco de Espaa y la Comisin Nacional del Mercado de Valores, al que posteriormente se adhirieron el Ministerio de Economa, Industria y Competitividad, a travs de la Direccin General de Seguros y Fondos de Pensiones, y el Ministerio de Educacin, Cultura y Deporte. La continuidad del Plan pone de manifiesto la importancia que sus autoridades promotoras otorgan a mejorar las competencias financieras bsicas de los ciudadanos. Los vehculos de ahorro, de seguro y de financiacin son herramientas clave para que las familias planifiquen sus principales decisiones de ndole econmica a lo largo de su vida. No obstante, varios estudios internacionales en pases de nuestro entorno como Francia, Italia, Alemania o Estados Unidos muestran que amplios segmentos de la poblacin parecen no estar familiarizados con conceptos financieros que son esenciales para poder afrontar adecuadamente algunas de estas decisiones. Por ejemplo, segn los ltimos resultados de la Red Internacional de Educacin Financiera de la Organizacin para la Cooperacin y el Desarrollo Econmico (OCDE), en pases como Francia, Alemania o Italia, al menos un 30% de la poblacin considera que la inflacin no reduce la capacidad adquisitiva real del dinero. De modo similar, a la hora de calcular la evolucin de una cantidad ahorrada en un depsito, ms del 40% de las personas entrevistadas en estos pases no tiene en cuenta que el tipo de inters se aplica tambin sobre los intereses generados en el pasado. Asimismo, no es infrecuente encontrar ahorradores que no saben si el riesgo asociado a una inversin es mayor o menor segn aumenta el nmero y variedad de acciones en las que se invierte. Una comprensin limitada de conceptos relativamente elementales, como la inflacin, el tipo de inters compuesto o la diversificacin del riesgo dificulta la comparacin de productos con distintas rentabilidades, riesgos o plazos de vencimiento, lo que provoca la adopcin de decisiones que no son ptimas por parte de muchas familias. De hecho, la evidencia disponible a nivel internacional sugiere que los hogares que desconocen estas nociones bsicas tienden a estar ms endeudados y ahorran menos. Es pertinente preguntarse, por tanto, por qu los conocimientos financieros difieren entre distintos grupos de la poblacin. Hay cierto consenso sobre que este tipo de conocimiento se adquiere paulatinamente a lo largo de la vida, en parte, durante la etapa formativa y, tambin, durante la vida adulta, a partir de la propia experiencia. Y hay razones fundadas para considerar que nuestro pas no constituye una excepcin al patrn detectado en otros pases desarrollados. A modo de ejemplo, en Espaa un alto porcentaje de ciudadanos en varias franjas de edad ha completado nicamente la educacin primaria, algo que limita la posibilidad de adquirir ciertos conocimientos numricos bsicos en el sistema educativo. De hecho, la limitada evidencia disponible sugiere que, en efecto, Espaa comparte en buena medida los problemas anteriormente mencionados. Por qu es necesario tratar de medir el grado de desarrollo de las competencias financieras? Para entender el contexto en el que los hogares toman sus decisiones de ahorro y endeudamiento es preciso obtener una medicin fiable de los conocimientos financieros a partir de muestras representativas de la poblacin. La medicin debe, adems, abarcar un conjunto amplio de materias, que van ms all de los conocimientos sobre, por ejemplo, la inflacin o los tipo de inters, y que deben extenderse al tipo de vehculos de ahorro o endeudamiento que conocen, cules poseen y, a la hora de elegir entre distintos productos de ahorro o de deuda, cules son las fuentes de informacin utilizadas. Del mismo modo, resulta tambin importante entender cmo utilizan los hogares los distintos productos financieros. Por ejemplo, hay poca evidencia sobre qu porcentaje de individuos escoge ahorrar en cuentas a la vista, efectivo o utilizando una imposicin a plazo. De modo similar, tampoco abunda la informacin acerca de cmo financian las familias espaolas los desfases puntuales entre sus gastos y sus ingresos corrientes, incluyendo la frecuencia con la que obtienen crdito de familiares o, alternativamente, con la que hacen uso de su tarjeta de crdito. Varios pases de nuestro entorno se estn haciendo estas mismas preguntas y por esta razn, en 2015, la OCDE lanzuna iniciativa coordinada entre ms de treinta pases para medir los conocimientos financieros, las actitudes ante el ahorro y el comportamiento financiero de la poblacin entre 18 y 79 aos. Es en este contexto en el que al Banco de Espaa y la Comisin Nacional del Mercado de Valores han elaborado la Encuesta de Competencias Financieras, en el marco del Plan de Educacin Financiera e incluida en el Plan Estadstico Nacional, lo que demuestra su importancia. Esta encuesta ser, adems, la contribucin espaola al esfuerzo internacional en esta rea coordinado por la OCDE. Este estudio, que se ha realizado por primera vez entre 2016 y 2017, mediante entrevistas personales, ha contado con la valiosa e imprescindible colaboracin del Instituto Nacional de Estadstica, que ha elaborado una muestra amplia de individuos adultos, seleccionados al azar, representativa de todo el territorio espaol y de cada una de sus Comunidades Autnomas. Los principales elementos novedosos de la Encuesta de Competencias Financieras La encuesta tiene varios elementos novedosos, que querra resaltar. En primer lugar, como sabemos, en Espaa las competencias educativas estn descentralizadas. Dado que las competencias financieras varan de manera acusada con el nivel educativo de los individuos, el proyecto cuenta con muestras representativas para cada una de las Comunidades Autnomas. En segundo lugar, la Encuesta no recoge nicamente las competencias financieras individuales, sino tambin las del hogar en el que reside. Esto es especialmente importante en Espaa, un pas en el que, al convivir un relativamente alto porcentaje de jvenes con sus padres, las competencias financieras individuales pueden no reflejarse en las decisiones del hogar en su conjunto. Para ello, la Encuesta recoge informacin sobre la situacin financiera del conjunto del hogar. En particular, se incluye un mdulo sobre la vivienda principal, en la que se obtiene informacin sobre la decisin del hogar de adquirir o no una vivienda, las razones por las que se opta por la compra o el alquiler, as como las expectativas sobre la evolucin futura del precio de la vivienda familiar. Finalmente, decisiones como la adquisicin de un producto financiero se ven afectadas por competencias no estrictamente financieras, como puedan ser las de lectura, las numricas o, incluso, las relativas a la capacidad de comprensin de elementos grficos. La encuesta contiene preguntas validadas internacionalmente destinadas a medir estas competencias. Adems, se han incluido tambin preguntas destinadas a medir los conocimientos sobre algunas cuestiones clave en la comprensin de fenmenos macroeconmicos bsicos, como pueden ser la inflacin y el dinero. Menciono estos elementos novedosos de la encuesta para indicar que la disponibilidad de estos datos permitir, adems de guiar los futuros esfuerzos del Plan de Educacin Financiera, analizar la influencia de las competencias financieras en las decisiones de ahorro, endeudamiento y aseguramiento de las familias. En la presentacin que tendr lugar en la segunda parte del acto, a cargo de Olympia Bover, se mostrarn con detalle los resultados de la encuesta. No obstante, antes de darle la palabra al Presidente de la CNMV, quisiera terminar agradeciendo el trabajo y el esfuerzo a todas las personas e instituciones que colaboran, directa o indirectamente, con el Plan de Educacin Financiera, y, en particular, a todas las personas que han estado involucradas en la elaboracin de esta Encuesta de Competencias Financieras y, sobre todo, a los ciudadanos que han accedido a responder la encuesta. Sin su colaboracin este estudio no hubiera sido posible. Muchas gracias por su atencin.

Title: Opening speech at the main event of Financial Education Day
text: 1.10.2018 Opening of the main event of the Financial Education Day CNMV Headquarters Pablo Hernandez de Cos Governor I want to begin by expressing my satisfaction for participating in this act with which we formalize the celebration of Financial Education Day. This is the first Financial Education Day that I attend as Governor and I would like to confirm the commitment of the Bank of Spain with the activities and objectives of the Financial Education Plan that we developed jointly with the National Securities Market Commission. The objective of this Conference is to raise awareness in society about the importance of improving and expanding financial knowledge and, more generally, basic economic knowledge, to facilitate decision-making that affects many facets of our lives. On previous occasions, it was mentioned in these same days that we still knew little about the true level of financial knowledge of the adult Spanish population. While there was concern that citizens in Spain were generally not sufficiently prepared to face many of the savings and investment decisions they must make throughout their lives, much of the available evidence was based on limited information.1 1 Available sources come from international studies of samples from about 1,000 individuals. See Leora Klapper, Annamaria Lusardi and Peter van Oudheusden (2015): "Financial Literacy Around the World: Insights from the Standard and Poor's Ratings Services" (telephone survey), or Allianz (2017): "When Will the Penny Drop?", International Pension Papers 1/2017 (computer survey). On this occasion, however, we already have a somewhat more precise vision of the financial and economic knowledge of the Spanish population, as well as their interaction with the financial system. I am referring to the recent completion of the Financial Skills Survey (ECF), an initiative of the Bank of Spain and the National Securities Market Commission within the framework of the aforementioned Financial Education Plan, whose main results we published last May. The survey is a very large study in which several thousand adults were interviewed about their financial knowledge, about their ownership and acquisition of financial products, as well as about their job expectations or attitudes towards consumption and savings. Additionally, it contains information, among other aspects, about the reasons that motivated the owners to buy their home, about how they financed it or about their expectations about its future value. Finally, the survey also measures skills that, although not strictly financial, can affect their decisions in this area, such as their degree of reading comprehension or their ability to understand certain graphic elements. This survey represents the most complete source of information available on the financial skills of Spaniards for several reasons. Firstly, thanks to a large population sample, provided by the National Institute of Statistics, the Financial Skills Survey is representative of all people residing in Spanish territory and of each of its autonomous communities. A second feature of interest of the ECF is that it is part of an international project coordinated by the International Financial Education Network under the auspices of the OECD. As a result, the main results of the PCE can be compared with those of other countries in our environment. Based on the information provided by this new survey, I would like to highlight below some of its results that are more closely related to initiatives that are part of the Financial Education Plan. In particular, I will refer to those relating to citizens' financial knowledge, their degree of financial inclusion, what financial products they acquire and what sources of information they use in this process. In relation to the financial knowledge of the population, the results of the survey show that a very large group of Spaniards is not familiar with basic concepts such as inflation (42%), the compound interest rate (54%) or risk diversification (51%), which are essential for making informed investment or debt decisions. In any case, these shortcomings are common to those of the countries around us. The lack of financial literacy is most noticeable among the youngest and those over 65. In the case of this last group, that of the elderly, they have comparatively higher levels of wealth, so financial knowledge can be particularly relevant when managing their assets and, therefore, the most worrying deficiencies in financial knowledge. In view of this situation, it is particularly appropriate that this Financial Education Day is celebrated precisely coinciding with the International Day of Older Persons and that, within the Financial Education Plan, emphasis has been placed on the preparation of informative material focused on the elderly. Conversely, in the case of those under 35 or those individuals who live with their parents, they tend to delegate their financial decisions to others. Let me make a specific comment about the lack of knowledge about the concept of diversification. Even when considering the third of the population that has some financial asset d0 which are usually investment funds, pension plans, stocks or bonds d0 the percentage of incorrect answers to this question is still 40%. This would indicate that a large group of financial market participants seems unaware of the advantages of a fundamental aspect for risk reduction in financial decision-making, such as diversification in investments. Answers to other questions about general economic knowledge similarly show that large groups of the population are unfamiliar, for example, with the effects of a change in the inflation rate on the real value of fixed-rate mortgage payments. This ignorance is the majority among those under 45 years of age and very pronounced among the youngest. Given that in these ages the acquisition of mortgages is frequent, doubts arise, again, about whether all the relevant financial factors are being taken into account when financing the purchase of a home. With regard to levels of financial inclusion, a basic measure is the holding of a bank account. According to the results of the survey, the percentage of people who have a current account in Spain is 97%, one of the highest in the countries of our environment. The lack of ownership of this financial product is It concentrates on low-income households (6% do not have a bank account) or immigrants (8% do not). On the other hand, the possession of other savings vehicles (such as a savings account or a pension plan) is significantly lower, around 40%, although with significant variability between autonomous communities. In addition, we know from other sources that the holding of savings instruments such as pension plans or investment funds is lower in Spain than in other countries around us. On the contrary, both the percentage of households that own their main home (around 80% in Spain) and other real estate properties (around 40%) are higher. In relation to borrowing decisions, the percentage of households with some outstanding debt (such as a mortgage or a personal loan) is 50%2, in line, in this case, with that of other developed countries. 2 This percentage of indebted households comes from the Bank of Spain's Household Financial Survey, with the percentage of individuals (not households) with debt being 40% according to the Financial Skills Survey. 3 Although there is a clear negative relationship between financial literacy and net wealth level, the direction of causality is not evident d0 for example, see V. Stango and J. Zinman (2009) "Exponential Growth Bias and Household Finance" Journal of Finance; and T. Jappelli, and M. Padula (2013) "Investment in Financial Literacy and Saving Decisions" Journal of Banking and Finance 37: 2779-2792. Finally, regarding the process of seeking information from those who purchase a financial product, the results of the survey reveal that the percentage of individuals who compare alternative products or search in different entities is very limited. In fact, just over a third of those who have purchased a savings, credit or insurance vehicle have compared between products offered by various entities. These guidelines depend on the instrument considered. For example, the majority of those who purchased a mortgage in the two years prior to the survey did weigh the options offered by various entities. However, even in this case, in which the payments of the product will be made for more than a decade, a third of those who mortgaged only considered a single alternative or chose among those offered by a single entity. In addition, when interviewees were asked which were the sources of information that most influenced when acquiring a savings, debt or insurance vehicle, the majority answer was that provided by the company that offers said product. The use of comparators is still a minority, which hinders the process by which savers or those who take out a mortgage or insurance find the most appropriate product. This brief summary of the main results of the Financial Skills Survey offers a first overview of what the financial knowledge of Spaniards is and how they interact with the financial system. However, from the presentation of the results themselves, questions arise about the relationship between the financial knowledge of Spaniards and their savings, spending and investment decisions. For example, we still do not know to what extent the lack of financial knowledge may be affecting financial decisions.3 On the other hand, we observe marked differences between population groups in the possession of financial products. However, we do not know if these differences are due to a lack of knowledge about the existence of of specific products, that it is difficult to understand their profitability or cost, or that different people have different preferences for savings or risk. Alternatively, individuals may perceive that there are non-financial investments that are more profitable than participating in financial markets. Access to reliable statistical sources is an essential step to understand these and many other questions about how citizens make their financial decisions and the importance of financial education. The Bank of Spain's recent initiative to provide researchers with disaggregated survey data will make it easier to answer these questions and help design the most appropriate public policies. On the other hand, I consider it crucial to underline the importance of systematically evaluating the measures adopted in the Financial Education Plan to identify and prioritize those that are most effective in raising the financial knowledge of the Spanish population4. The systematic development of the evaluation of public policies is one of the pending tasks in our country and all institutions must contribute, from our areas of action, to advance in this area. 4 Experimental studies such as the one carried out by O. Bover et al. (2018) "The Impact of High School Financial Education on financial Knowledge and Choices: Evidence from a Randomized Trial in Spain", Working Paper 1801, Bank of Spain, show the persistent impact of financial education on savings choices as well as its positive effects on the acquisition of other skills. To conclude, I would like to join the President of the CNMV in the sincere and deep gratitude for the work and effort, in all these years, to all the people and institutions that collaborate, directly or indirectly, with the Financial Education Plan. On this occasion I would also like to extend my thanks to the citizens who have agreed to respond to the survey. Thank you very much for your attention. I hope you enjoy this Financial Education Day.
text_original: 1.10.2018 Apertura del acto central del Da de la Educacin Financiera Sede de la CNMV Pablo Hernndez de Cos Gobernador Quiero comenzar manifestando mi satisfaccin por participar en este acto con el que formalizamos la celebracin del Da de la Educacin Financiera. Este es el primer Da de la Educacin Financiera al que asisto como Gobernador y me gustara confirmar el compromiso del Banco de Espaa con las actividades y los objetivos del Plan de Educacin Financiera que desarrollamos conjuntamente con la Comisin Nacional del Mercado de Valores. El objetivo de esta Jornada es concienciar a la sociedad acerca de la importancia de mejorar y ampliar los conocimientos financieros y, ms en general, los conocimientos econmicos bsicos, para facilitar la toma de decisiones que afectan a muchas facetas de nuestras vidas. En ocasiones anteriores, se mencion en estas mismas jornadas que an sabamos poco acerca del verdadero nivel de conocimientos financieros de la poblacin espaola adulta. Si bien exista la preocupacin de que los ciudadanos en Espaa no estuvieran, en general, suficientemente preparados para afrontar muchas de las decisiones de ahorro e inversin que deben tomar a lo largo de su vida, mucha de la evidencia disponible se basaba en informacin limitada.1 1 Las fuentes disponibles provienen de estudios internacionales de muestras de alrededor de 1.000 individuos. Vase Leora Klapper, Annamaria Lusardi y Peter van Oudheusden (2015): Financial Literacy Around the World: Insights from the Standard and Poors Ratings Services (encuesta telefnica), o Allianz (2017): When Will the Penny Drop?, International Pension Papers 1/2017 (encuesta por ordenador). En esta ocasin, sin embargo, ya disponemos de una visin algo ms precisa de los conocimientos financieros y econmicos de la poblacin espaola, as como de su interaccin con el sistema financiero. Me estoy refiriendo a la reciente realizacin de la Encuesta de Competencias Financieras (ECF), una iniciativa del Banco de Espaa y de la Comisin Nacional del Mercado de Valores en el marco del mencionado Plan de Educacin Financiera, cuyos principales resultados publicamos el pasado mes de mayo. La encuesta es un estudio muy amplio en el que se entrevist a varios miles de personas adultas sobre sus conocimientos financieros, sobre su tenencia y adquisicin de productos financieros, as como sobre sus expectativas laborales o actitudes ante el consumo y el ahorro. Adicionalmente, contiene informacin, entre otros aspectos, sobre las razones que motivaron a los propietarios a la compra de su vivienda, sobre cmo la financiaron o sobre sus expectativas sobre su valor futuro. Finalmente, la encuesta mide tambin competencias que, si bien no son estrictamente financieras, s pueden afectar a sus decisiones en este mbito, como son su grado de comprensin lectora o su capacidad de entender determinados elementos grficos. Esta encuesta representa la fuente de informacin disponible ms completa sobre las competencias financieras de los espaoles por varias razones. En primer lugar, gracias a una muestra de poblacin amplia, proporcionada por el Instituto Nacional de Estadstica, la Encuesta de Competencias Financieras es representativa tanto del conjunto de las personas que residen en el territorio espaol como de cada una de sus comunidades autnomas. Una segunda caracterstica de inters de la ECF es que forma parte de un proyecto internacional coordinado por la Red Internacional de Educacin Financiera bajo los auspicios de la OCDE. Como consecuencia, los principales resultados de la ECF se pueden comparar con los de otros pases de nuestro entorno. A partir de la informacin proporcionada por esta nueva encuesta, querra resaltar a continuacin algunos de sus resultados que se encuentran ms estrechamente relacionados con iniciativas que forman parte del Plan de Educacin Financiera. En concreto, me referir a los relativos a los conocimientos financieros de los ciudadanos, su grado de inclusin financiera, qu productos financieros adquieren y qu fuentes de informacin utilizan en este proceso. En relacin con los conocimientos financieros de la poblacin, los resultados de la encuesta muestran que un grupo muy amplio de espaoles no est familiarizado con conceptos bsicos como la inflacin (el 42%), el tipo de inters compuesto (54%) o la diversificacin del riesgo (51%), que resultan esenciales para la toma de decisiones informadas de inversin o endeudamiento. En todo caso, estas carencias son comunes a las de los pases de nuestro entorno. La falta de conocimientos financieros resulta ms notable entre los ms jvenes y entre los mayores de 65 aos. En el caso de este ltimo colectivo, el de las personas mayores, estos poseen niveles de riqueza comparativamente ms elevados, por lo que los conocimientos financieros pueden ser particularmente relevantes a la hora de gestionar sus activos y, por lo tanto, las carencias en conocimientos financieros ms preocupantes. A la vista de esta situacin resulta particularmente apropiado que este Da de la Educacin Financiera se celebre precisamente coincidiendo con el Da Internacional de las Personas Mayores y que, dentro del Plan de Educacin Financiera, se haya puesto el nfasis en la preparacin de material informativo enfocado hacia las personas de mayor edad. Por el contrario, en el caso de los menores de 35 aos o de aquellos individuos que viven con sus padres, estos tienden a delegar en otros sus decisiones financieras. Permtanme hacer un comentario especfico sobre la falta de conocimientos acerca del concepto de diversificacin. Incluso cuando se considera el tercio de la poblacin que tiene algn activo financiero -que suelen ser fondos de inversin, planes de pensiones, acciones o bonos-, el porcentaje de respuestas incorrectas a esta pregunta es todava del 40%. Esto sera indicativo de que un grupo importante de participantes en los mercados financieros parece desconocer las ventajas de un aspecto fundamental para la reduccin del riesgo en la toma de decisiones financieras, como es la diversificacin en las inversiones. Las respuestas a otras preguntas sobre conocimientos econmicos generales denotan, de forma similar, que amplios grupos de la poblacin no estn familiarizados, por ejemplo, con los efectos de un cambio en la tasa de inflacin sobre el valor real de los pagos de una hipoteca a tipo fijo. Este desconocimiento es mayoritario entre los menores de 45 aos y muy acusado entre los ms jvenes. Dado que en estas edades es frecuente la adquisicin de hipotecas, surgen dudas, de nuevo, sobre si se estn tomando en cuenta todos los factores financieros relevantes a la hora de financiar la compra de una vivienda. En lo relativo a los niveles de inclusin financiera, una medida bsica es la tenencia de una cuenta bancaria. De acuerdo con los resultados de la encuesta, el porcentaje de personas que tiene una cuenta corriente en Espaa es del 97%, uno de los ms elevados de los pases de nuestro entorno. La falta de tenencia de este producto financiero se concentra en los hogares con rentas bajas (un 6% no tiene una cuenta bancaria) o los inmigrantes (un 8% no la posee). En cambio, la tenencia de otros vehculos de ahorro (como pueda ser una cuenta de ahorro o un plan de pensiones) es significativamente menor, en torno al 40%, aunque con importante variabilidad entre comunidades autnomas. Adems, sabemos por otras fuentes que la tenencia de instrumentos de ahorro como planes de pensiones o fondos de inversin es menor en Espaa que en otros pases de nuestro entorno. Por el contrario, es superior tanto el porcentaje de hogares que poseen su vivienda principal (en torno al 80% en Espaa) como otras propiedades inmobiliarias (en torno al 40%). En relacin con las decisiones de endeudamiento, el porcentaje de hogares con alguna deuda pendiente (como una hipoteca o un prstamo personal) es del 50%2, en lnea, en este caso, con el de otros pases desarrollados. 2 Este porcentaje de hogares endeudados procede de la Encuesta Financiera de las Familias del Banco de Espaa, siendo el porcentaje de individuos (que no hogares) con deuda de un 40% conforme a la Encuesta de Competencias Financieras. 3 Aunque existe una clara relacin negativa entre conocimientos financieros y nivel de riqueza neta, la direccin de la causalidad no es evidente por ejemplo, vase V. Stango and J. Zinman (2009) Exponential Growth Bias and Household Finance Journal of Finance; y T. Jappelli, y M. Padula (2013) Investment in Financial Literacy and Saving Decisions Journal of Banking and Finance 37: 2779-2792. Finalmente, respecto al proceso de bsqueda de informacin de quienes adquieren un producto financiero, los resultados de la encuesta revelan que es muy limitado el porcentaje de individuos que compara productos alternativos o busca en distintas entidades. De hecho, poco ms de un tercio de quienes han adquirido un vehculo de ahorro, crdito o aseguramiento, ha comparado entre productos ofrecidos por varias entidades. Estas pautas dependen del instrumento considerado. Por ejemplo, la mayora de quienes adquirieron una hipoteca en los dos aos anteriores a la elaboracin de la encuesta s sopesaron las opciones ofrecidas por varias entidades. No obstante, incluso en este caso, en el que los pagos del producto se harn durante ms de una dcada, una tercera parte de los que se hipotecaron slo consider una nica alternativa o escogi entre las ofrecidas por una nica entidad. Adems, cuando se pregunta a los entrevistados cules fueron las fuentes de informacin que ms influyeron a la hora de adquirir un vehculo de ahorro, deuda o seguro, la respuesta mayoritaria fue la proporcionada por la empresa que ofrece dicho producto. El uso de comparadores es an minoritario, lo que dificulta el proceso por el que los ahorradores o quienes contratan una hipoteca o un seguro encuentran el producto ms apropiado. Este resumen somero de los principales resultados de la Encuesta de Competencias Financieras ofrece una primera visin de cules son los conocimientos financieros de los espaoles y de cmo interactan con el sistema financiero. No obstante, de la propia presentacin de los resultados surgen preguntas acerca de la relacin entre los conocimientos financieros de los espaoles y sus decisiones de ahorro, gasto e inversin. Por ejemplo, an no sabemos en qu medida la falta de conocimientos financieros puede estar afectando a las decisiones financieras.3 Por otro lado, observamos diferencias acusadas entre grupos poblacionales en la tenencia de productos financieros. Sin embargo, desconocemos si estas diferencias se deben a una falta de conocimiento sobre la existencia de productos concretos, a que es difcil comprender su rentabilidad o su coste, o a que diferentes personas tengan distintas preferencias por el ahorro o por el riesgo. Alternativamente, es posible que los individuos perciban que existen inversiones no financieras ms rentables que participar en los mercados financieros. El acceso a fuentes estadsticas fiables es un paso imprescindible para entender estas y otras muchas preguntas sobre cmo toman los ciudadanos sus decisiones financieras y la importancia de la educacin financiera. La reciente iniciativa del Banco de Espaa de proporcionar a los investigadores los datos desagregados de la encuesta facilitar responder a estas cuestiones y ayudar a disear las polticas pblicas ms apropiadas. Por otra parte, considero crucial subrayar la importancia de evaluar sistemticamente las medidas adoptadas en el Plan de Educacin Financiera para identificar y priorizar aquellas que resultan ms eficaces para elevar el conocimiento financiero de la poblacin espaola4. El desarrollo sistemtico de la evaluacin de las polticas pblicas es una de las tareas pendientes en nuestro pas y todas las instituciones debemos contribuir, desde nuestros mbitos de actuacin, a avanzar en este terreno. 4 Estudios experimentales como el realizado por O. Bover et al. (2018) The Impact of High School Financial Education on financial Knowledge and Choices: Evidence from a Randomized Trial in Spain, Documento de Trabajo 1801, Banco de Espaa, muestran el impacto persistente de la educacin financiera sobre las elecciones de ahorro as como sus efectos positivos en la adquisicin de otras competencias. Para terminar, quisiera unirme al presidente de la CNMV en el sincero y profundo agradecimiento por el trabajo y el esfuerzo, en todos estos aos, a todas las personas e instituciones que colaboran, directa o indirectamente, con el Plan de Educacin Financiera. En esta ocasin quisiera hacer extensivo tambin mi agradecimiento a los ciudadanos que han accedido a responder a la encuesta. Muchas gracias por su atencin. Espero que disfruten de este Da de la Educacin Financiera.

Title: Governor's speech at the 2018 Annual Convention of the Financial Markets Association
text: 19.11.2018 Governor's Intervention Annual Convention 2018/Financial Markets Association Pablo Hernandez de Cos Governor Ladies and gentlemen I want to thank Enrique Prados del Amo for his kind invitation to present today at the Annual Convention of the Association of Financial Markets the President of the National Securities Market Commission, Sebasti87n Albella. In this first Annual Convention of the Association that I attend as Governor allow me to begin by reiterating the support of the Bank of Spain to its activities. I would also like to congratulate both the Association and its President for the excellent work they are doing to promote collaboration and the exchange of views between professionals and institutions linked to the financial markets. Equally noteworthy is the Association's commitment to disseminating the functioning and regulation of markets, as well as to promoting initiatives aimed at achieving a better and more effective functioning of the markets. Traditionally, the Conference rapporteur for the Annual Convention of the Association has been the Governor of a Eurosystem central bank. However, this year, in which the first Securities Market Law has turned 30, the Association has invited the President of the National Securities Market Commission. I think this invitation is very pertinent. Not only because of the role that our rapporteur played in its drafting but, above all, because of the growing importance of the stock markets in today's financial system. In fact, the growing disintermediation in the financial markets is a competitive challenge of the first magnitude that requires the adaptation of all market operators and that, of course, also affects banking entities. It is, therefore, an honor and a pleasure for me to present Sebasti87n Albella, president of the National Securities Market Commission since November 2016. Reflecting the interdependent international financial system in which we live, Sebastian is also a member of the Executive Committee and Board of Supervisors of the European Securities Markets Authority (ESMA), the Board of the International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO) and the Standing Committee on the Implementation of Standards of the Financial Stability Board (FSB). His long and brilliant professional career has been developed in both the public and private sectors. After going from his native Castell97n to study in Navarra and graduating in Law from the University of Navarra, Sebasti87n Albella began his professional career in 1984 as a State lawyer, being Head of the Legal Department of the General Directorate of the Treasury and Financial Policy between 1986 and 1988. Allow me to refer to Sebasti87n Albella at this stage of his career as one of the "fathers" of the first Securities Market Law in Spain, as he was not only part of its drafting team, but was also the first Secretary of the Board and responsible for the legal services of the CNMV. He held these positions from its inception in 1988 until moving to the private sector in 1991. His link to the CNMV continued over time since, subsequently, from the private sphere, he was a member of its Advisory Committee on two occasions. But Sebasti87n Albella is not only the architect of the first Securities Market Law; He has also held various positions of responsibility in the private sector for more than 20 years. Thus, prior to his appointment as Chairman of the CNMV, Sebasti87n was Senior Partner in Spain of the international law firm Linklaters and a member of its global board. Before joining Linklaters in 2005 he was one of the founding members of Ram97n y Cajal Abogados, and for twelve years held the position of legal advisor to the Spanish Banking Association (AEB). He also has extensive international experience in the private sector, having been a member of the Legal Committee of the European Banking Federation and a member of the committee of experts on the securities market of the European Commission. For all these reasons, I wish you a fruitful and interesting conference on your part. I want to thank Sebasti87n Albella for his presence here, but not before referring to the good relationship and close collaboration between the National Securities Market Commission and the Bank of Spain in different areas that I consider very relevant for the future development of financial markets in Spain. The two institutions are currently collaborating on a major European initiative, the Capital Markets Union. This is a major project of particular importance for achieving greater integration of capital markets in the European Union. In addition, there are great synergies between the Banking Union and Capital Markets Union initiatives. Together they aim to improve the private financial sector's capacity to absorb financial shocks and its international diversification. And the role of the Capital Markets Union is vital to achieve developed capital markets and strengthen their cross-border vocation, especially in equity markets, which are the most relevant to increase the power of risk-sharing channels in a Monetary Union. Another area of institutional collaboration is related to the promotion of the Spanish financial system in the current context of great competition between markets and financial centers before the exit of the United Kingdom from the European Union. In the macroprudential area, there is also a fruitful dialogue between supervisors and other authorities to create the institutional framework of a macroprudential authority in Spain. This will provide economic policy in our country with the necessary tools to strengthen the capacity for early identification of risks and vulnerabilities for financial and macroeconomic stability. On the other hand, it will provide the authorities with the necessary response capacity to mitigate these risks and prevent them from materializing in the future. I do not want to conclude my words without mentioning the collaboration of both institutions within the framework of the so-called Financial Education Plan. This initiative seeks to improve the financial culture of Spaniards in order to make informed savings and investment decisions that improve their well-being and protection as customers. And, without further delay, I will now give the floor to the President of the CNMV, Sebasti87n Albella.
text_original: 19.11.2018 Intervencin del gobernador Convencin Anual 2018/Asociacin de Mercados Financieros Pablo Hernndez de Cos Gobernador Seoras y seores, Quiero agradecer a Enrique Prados del Amo su amable invitacin a presentar hoy en la Convencin Anual de la Asociacin de Mercados Financieros al Presidente de la Comisin Nacional del Mercado de Valores, Sebastin Albella. En esta primera Convencin Anual de la Asociacin a la que asisto como Gobernador permtanme comenzar reiterando el apoyo del Banco de Espaa a sus actividades. Asimismo, quiero felicitar tanto a la Asociacin como a su Presidente por la excelente labor que desarrollan para promover la colaboracin y el intercambio de opiniones entre profesionales e instituciones vinculados a los mercados financieros. Resulta igualmente destacable el compromiso de la Asociacin con la divulgacin del funcionamiento y regulacin de los mercados, as como con la promocin de iniciativas orientadas a lograr un mejor y ms eficaz funcionamiento de los mismos. Tradicionalmente el ponente de la Conferencia con ocasin de la Convencin Anual de la Asociacin ha sido el Gobernador de un banco central del Eurosistema. Sin embargo, este ao, en el que la primera Ley del Mercado de Valores ha cumplido 30 aos, la Asociacin ha invitado al Presidente de la Comisin Nacional del Mercado de Valores. Esta invitacin me parece muy pertinente. No solo por el papel que nuestro ponente tuvo en su redaccin como, sobre todo, por la creciente importancia de los mercados de valores en el sistema financiero de hoy. De hecho, la creciente desintermediacin en los mercados financieros es un reto competitivo de primera magnitud que requiere la adaptacin de todos los operadores del mercado y que, cmo no, tambin afecta a las entidades bancarias. Es, por tanto, para m un honor y un placer presentar a Sebastin Albella, presidente de la Comisin Nacional del Mercado de Valores desde noviembre de 2016.
