Title: Intervention in the 23rd edition of the "A" Awards of the ARCO Foundation for Collecting
text: 26.02.2019 23rd edition of the "A" Awards for Collecting ARCO Awards Pablo Hernandez de Cos Governor Mr President of the Community of Madrid, Mr Minister for Culture and Sport, authorities, ladies and gentlemen. When in 1784, in the middle of the Age of Enlightenment, the General Meeting of Shareholders of the Bank of San Carlos, predecessor of the current Bank of Spain, commissioned the portraits of the first directors of the banking institution, the seed was being set, without knowing it, of the creation of one of the most unique corporate art collections in the country. The enlightened ideas had a lot to do with this initiative, which sought as its main purpose to highlight and reward the work of those citizens who had made some contribution to public life. For this purpose, therefore, the first commissions to various artists of the time responded (among others, Francisco de Goya, who signed six splendid canvases for the institution, origin of the great portrait gallery that today preserves the Bank of Spain, and that already in the twentieth century would be enriched with the acquisition of two other portraits of the same author). Enlightenment thought is also responsible for the reflection on the importance of patronage, expressed by the chamber painter Anton Raphael Mengs, who already warned at that time that "if the nobility, the rich and the opulent communities of a country do not enter into the idea of making works [of art], and of spreading with them the taste of the Arts in the Nation, These will be extinguished for lack of food." The Banco de Espa96a Collection is, therefore, the result of an artistic heritage accumulated over more than 200 years of history. It is a very wide set of works, whose number is estimated at around 5,000 and which can be divided into a classical part and a contemporary part. The classic collection begins with the funds from the Bank of San Carlos, of which we must highlight the set of portraits due to the masterful hand of Francisco de Goya. During the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, the official gallery continued to grow, and today brings together examples of the most illustrious painters of each period (Esteve, Esquivel, Madrazo, Vicente L97pez, Zuloaga, Sorolla or Carmen Laff97n, whose brushes have left some of the most outstanding portraits of recent governors). The other relevant set in terms of number of works and quality of the pieces corresponds to the twentieth century. One of the most consistent lines of force in this contemporary section is that of abstraction (with works by T88pies, Saura, Millares, Chillida, Palazuelo and Oteiza, among others). Belonging to the eighties and nineties are the creations of artists such as Gordillo, Campano, Quejido, Sicilia and Barcel97. With the integration of the Bank into the Eurosystem, already in the twenty-first century, the incorporation of creators from the European and Latin American spheres begins, who, together with other current Spanish artists, draw a rich panorama of the most recent art. There is no doubt that the Bank's first obligation with respect to this heritage complex is its conservation. This function is a primary objective, which we consider unavoidable and which obliges us to adopt the necessary measures to ensure that this collection can be enjoyed in the present and bequeathed to future generations. To carry it out, we also have the invaluable collaboration of the Museum's Conservation Departments. Nacional del Prado and the Museo Nacional Centro de Arte Reina Sof92a, to whom I would like to express my gratitude for their continued collaboration. But the Bank's historical-artistic heritage, conceived as a public good, today poses new challenges. In this sense, its future is to establish a more direct link with society, which must understand the existence of this heritage as part of its history and its cultural heritage. For this reason, the Banco de Espa96a has proposed to provide all social sectors with the knowledge and enjoyment of the heritage it preserves, intensifying the dissemination strategies used so far (loans mainstays, publications and heritage visits) and initiating new ones, such as the start-up of an exhibition hall at our headquarters in Cibeles, in the middle of Paseo del Arte, which will allow the presentation of different selections from the collection, and the launch of a heritage website. To these actions we will add this year the publication of a catalogue raisonn8e that will collect the detailed study of some 1,800 works from the collection. These instruments will make it possible to share the Bank's rich historical-artistic heritage on a global scale. For all these reasons, the fact that the Arco Foundation has made us worthy of this "A" Award for Collecting 2019, highlighting precisely the effort that the Bank of Spain is carrying out to make these cultural resources available to society, fills us with pride and drives us to continue on this path. A collective effort that reflects not only the work of patronage of the institution, but also the care and attention that the Bank's human teams carry out in favor of its conservation and maintenance. I would like to finish by showing my gratitude to the Arco Foundation for distinguishing us with such a prestigious award, to the Fair and its director, Carlos Urroz, and to all the administrations involved in this event, which has been highlighting contemporary art in our country for many years.

Title: Intervention at the colloquium of the University of Navarra. "Independent institutions: conditions and challenges"
text: 29.04.2019 "Independent institutions: conditions and challenges" Colloquium University of Navarra (Madrid) Margarita Delgado Subgobernadora Good morning and many thanks to the University of Navarra for this kind invitation. I am delighted to be here with my esteemed colleagues at this colloquium on the conditions and challenges facing independent authorities. Both the economic literature and practical experience in different countries underline the idea of the independence of economic authorities and supervisors as something particularly relevant. Independent "economic supervisors" have, in fact, a long tradition in developed countries and constitute a fundamental pillar of their institutional structure. That is why I think we all agree that independence is a value that we must not only preserve, but strengthen for the benefit of those objectives. Of course, independence is not an end in itself, but a necessary means to effectively achieve the general interest objectives entrusted to us institutions. In any case, it is very important that independence is inseparable from other principles: responsibility and accountability, which make it possible to assess the adequacy of the actions of independent authorities with their mandates, strengthening their credibility and, ultimately, also their effectiveness. Of course, independence also means living up to the highest standards of transparency, integrity and governance. The question of how to make independence effective is very relevant, but before answering it I would like to briefly ask a preliminary question: why is it necessary to give independence to economic supervisors? I think it is important to give that previous answer because, as I said, independence can never be an end in itself. Finally, I would like to briefly cover the need to balance independence with the necessary accountability. Reasons for independence The operation of "economic supervisors" is governed by mandates inspired by the general interest and entrusted to them by the public authorities. Simplifying a little, in the specific case of the Bank of Spain, we have a mandate of price stability, as a monetary authority, integrated into the Eurosystem, as well as monitoring the health of the financial system and protecting customers in financial services. In relation to the mandate of price stability, it should be noted that the role of expectations, in the behavior of economic agents, justifies the delegation of inflation control to an independent body, to avoid monetary policies aimed at continuously stimulating aggregate demand in the short term and that end up translating only into higher inflation. Empirical studies tend to corroborate that a greater degree of independence is correlated with a lower level of inflation, without this having entailed costs in the form of lower economic growth. With regard to the mandate of banking supervision and consumer protection, we also note that conflicts of interest between governments and supervisors, the need to avoid actions linked to the electoral cycle, problems of temporal and geographical inconsistency in the EU or the eminently technical nature of the performance of supervisory functions, also justify that this is exercised by an institution independent. This was reflected in the assumption by the European Central Bank of supervisory responsibilities for significant European financial institutions from 2014. In short, the delegation of these tasks to independent bodies aims to achieve more effectively the tasks of general interest entrusted to those institutions. Independence helps efficiency to the extent that it allows its actions to be impartial, in defense of the general interest and protected from the influence of both government and private interests. As I have already mentioned, the value of independence is particularly important when the effects of its action are only observed in the medium and long term and even entail short-term costs. It is clear that assuming this long-term vision may be more difficult for the Government, which may be tempting to prioritize considerations linked to its possibility of re-election and, therefore, in the short term. An additional point, very relevant for the entire public administration, is related to the need to avoid the so-called "supervisory capture". Obviously, the supervisor must be independent not only of the Government, but also of the entities under its supervision, so it must always act in the general interest, without attending to pressures or particular interests of specific entities or the sector as a whole. Of course, acting independently is not the same as acting arbitrarily or unfairly. Another problem that I have already mentioned and which is clearly associated with the lack of independence of the institutions is that known as "temporal inconsistency". If the validity of a regulation depends on the will of the government of the day, it may lack incentives to maintain previous commitments, which may mean that regulatory decisions do not have the desired consequences if economic agents anticipate that they could be reviewed in the future. These problems are reduced with independent regulators, since their managers are usually appointed for a period of time longer than the electoral cycle and with long-term objectives. Measures to ensure effective independence Focusing on the main issue of this colloquium, I wanted to point out that, for independence to be effective: (i) it must be formally recognized and (ii) it must affect different dimensions of the body: institutional, legal, functional, organizational, financial and personal of its leaders. The independence of the Banco de Espa96a is established in the Law of Autonomy of 1994, in the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, in the Statute of the European System of Central Banks and in the Regulation of the Single Supervisory Mechanism. This independence is not a mere legal formula, but is fully recognized: 1. First, institutional independence empowers governing bodies to act autonomously. In fact, and as provided for in its Law of Autonomy, the Government cannot give instructions to the Bank of Spain, nor can it collect or accept them, in the exercise of the functions derived from membership of the European System of Central Banks. These principles also apply to the functions exercised within the Single Supervisory Mechanism. 2. Legal independence is not only reflected in the legal personality of the body to act on its own behalf, but also in the ability to issue legally binding decisions within the scope of its competences. In this regard, suffice it to point out that the Banco de Espa96a has its own legal personality, distinct from that of any other administration or institution. 3. The personal independence of their highest representatives requires that the appointment, exercise of their mandates and termination of office must be provided for in advance and explicitly provided for and subject to a series of safeguards to protect them from interference. Both the figure of the Governor, and my own, have reinforced their independence with respect to the political powers and the supervised sector, among other measures, through: (i) the duration of our mandate is set at six years (longer than the electoral cycle) and without the possibility of renewal; (ii) the establishment of assessed causes for the dismissal of the office of Governor, Deputy Governor and non-ex officio councilors; (iii) the regime of incompatibilities to which the Governor, the Deputy Governor and the directors are subject, and (iv) the prohibition of exercising professional activity related to credit institutions or securities markets in a period of two years after the cessation of office. 4. Functional independence guarantees the ability of the body to exercise all the functions and powers entrusted to it in order to fulfil its mandate. 5. Financial independence is essential to ensure that the Agency has sufficient financial and human resources and that these are organized and structured in the manner most appropriate to the fulfilment of the mandate. In this sense, the Banco de Espa96a has its own budget that allows it to obtain the necessary economic resources for the development of its functions. 6. As regards organisational independence, the Banco de Espa96a enjoys autonomy in establishing its internal organisation and, in particular, its staff policy. It should be emphasized in any case that the Bank of Spain, by legal imperative, selects its staff respecting the principles of equality, merit, capacity and publicity and that it is linked to the Bank by a relationship of labor law. Therefore, it can be concluded that the level of financial and organisational independence of the Banco de Espa96a is appropriate for the achievement of its objectives. Accountability as a counterweight to independence I would like to conclude by reflecting briefly on the importance of accountability. In a democratic state, any independent body or authority must be required to be transparent and accountable for its decisions, as essential elements to grant it legitimacy. It is a fact that the global financial crisis has led to increased demands on central banks in this area, given that, on the one hand, monetary policy has extended its instruments with more complex measures and, on the other hand, central banks have assumed more responsibilities in the area of financial stability, in particular with regard to macroprudential supervision. Accountability for the actions and activities of independent bodies and authorities should preferably be made to Parliament. In this respect there is direct parliamentary control over the Budget of the Bank of Spain and over its Balance Sheet and Income Statement; Reports and Reports are also sent regularly to the Cortes Generales, such as, for example, the Annual Report, the Institutional Report, the Supervision Report or the Sanctioning Actions. Within this exercise of accountability before Parliament, the appearance of the Governor before the Economy Commission of Congress is also established, to present the Annual Report and to analyze the proposals of the General State Budget. Beyond accountability, institutional transparency is also a basic principle in the proper functioning of independent public bodies, particularly since trust and credibility in these institutions underpin their effectiveness. The Banco de Espa96a has a long tradition in publishing reports that enjoy a recognized rigor and prestige and that cover different areas of the institution's activities, always trying to reach a wide spectrum of audiences. It is also our objective to increase the Bank's participation in those academic, professional and social forums, where our presence can be beneficial, as well as the use of new communication tools, such as the recent opening of a Twitter account, or regular contacts with the press in which it is intended to explain the content of our reports in a more accessible way. The Bank has also increased the level of information on the Transparency Portal, incorporating greater detail in the agendas and appearances of both the Governor and myself, as well as those documents that make up the framework of ethical action of senior officials. In this regard, both the Governor and myself, as representatives of the Governing Council of the ECB and the Single Supervisory Mechanism, respectively, have just signed a new code of conduct that increases our personal commitment to the highest ethical standards in order to guarantee our independence from the public and private sector and avoid potential conflicts of interest. Finally, I would like to point out that the Bank is in the process of preparing a strategic plan, the completion date of which is expected in the second half of this year and the essential content of which will be made public. Beyond the importance of this exercise from an internal point of view, I believe that the preparation and publication of this plan is a fundamental element in increasing transparency, which will facilitate the assessment of the effectiveness of the Bank's actions.
text_original: 29.04.2019 Instituciones independientes: condiciones y retos Coloquio Universidad de Navarra (Madrid) Margarita Delgado Subgobernadora Buenos das y muchas gracias a la Universidad de Navarra por esta amable invitacin. Los supervisores econmicos independientes tienen, de hecho, una larga tradicin en los pases desarrollados y constituyen un pilar fundamental de su estructura institucional. Por ello creo que estamos todos de acuerdo en que la independencia es un valor que no solo debemos preservar, sino reforzar en beneficio de esos objetivos. Por supuesto, la independencia no es un fin en s mismo, sino un medio necesario para alcanzar de manera eficaz los objetivos de inters general que las instituciones tenemos encomendados. En todo caso, es muy importante que la independencia sea inseparable de otros principios: la responsabilidad y la rendicin de cuentas, que permitan evaluar la adecuacin de las actuaciones de las autoridades independientes a sus mandatos, reforzando su credibilidad y, en ltima instancia, tambin su eficacia. Por supuesto, la independencia implica tambin estar a la altura de los estndares ms altos de transparencia, integridad y gobernanza. Los estudios empricos tienden a corroborar que un mayor grado de independencia est correlacionado con un menor nivel de inflacin, sin que ello haya conllevado costes en forma de menor crecimiento econmico. Por lo que respecta al mandato de supervisin bancaria y proteccin del consumidor, constatamos tambin que los conflictos de intereses entre gobiernos y supervisores, la necesidad de evitar actuaciones ligadas al ciclo electoral, los problemas de inconsistencia temporal y geogrfica en la UE o el carcter eminentemente tcnico del desarrollo de las funciones supervisoras, justifican tambin que esta sea ejercida por una institucin independiente. Reflejo de todo ello fue la asuncin, por parte del Banco Central Europeo, de las responsabilidades de supervisin de las instituciones financieras significativas europeas a partir de 2014. En definitiva, la delegacin de estas tareas en organismos independientes tiene como objetivo alcanzar de manera ms eficaz las funciones de inters general que estas instituciones tienen encomendados. La independencia ayuda a la eficacia en la medida que permita que su actuacin sea imparcial, en defensa del inters general y protegida de la influencia tanto del gobierno como de los intereses privados. Como ya he mencionado, el valor de la independencia es particularmente importante cuando los efectos de su actuacin solo se observan en el medio y largo plazo e incluso conllevan costes a corto plazo. Es evidente que asumir esta visin de largo plazo puede resultar ms difcil para el Gobierno, que puede estar tentando a priorizar consideraciones ligadas a su posibilidad de reeleccin y, por tanto, de corto plazo. Un punto adicional, muy relevante para toda la administracin pblica, se relaciona con la necesidad de evitar la denominada captura supervisora. Evidentemente, el supervisor debe ser independiente no solo del Gobierno, sino tambin de las entidades bajo su supervisin, por lo que debe actuar siempre en defensa del inters general, sin atender a presiones o intereses particulares de entidades concretas o del sector en su conjunto. Por supuesto, actuar con independencia no es lo mismo que actuar de modo arbitrario o injusto. Otro problema que ya he citado y que est claramente asociado con la falta de independencia de las instituciones es el conocido como de inconsistencia temporal. Si la vigencia de una regulacin depende de la voluntad del gobierno de turno, este puede carecer de incentivos a mantener los compromisos anteriores, lo que puede generar que las decisiones regulatorias no tengan las consecuencias deseadas si los agentes econmicos anticipan que aquellas podran ser revisadas en el futuro. Estos problemas se reducen con reguladores independientes, ya que sus responsables suelen ser nombrados por un periodo de tiempo superior al ciclo electoral y con objetivos a largo plazo. Medidas para asegurar que la independencia sea efectiva Centrndome ya en la cuestin principal de este coloquio, quera sealar que, para que la independencia sea efectiva: (i) debe de estar formalmente reconocida y (ii) debe afectar a distintas dimensiones del organismo: la institucional, la legal, la funcional, la organizativa, la financiera y la personal de sus responsables. La independencia del Banco de Espaa viene establecida en la Ley de Autonoma de 1994, en el Tratado de Funcionamiento de la Unin Europea, en los Estatutos del Sistema Europeo de Bancos Centrales y en el Reglamento del Mecanismo nico de Supervisin. Esta independencia no es una mera frmula legal, sino que est plenamente reconocida: 1. En primer lugar, la independencia institucional confiere capacidad a los rganos rectores para actuar con autonoma. De hecho, y tal y como prev su Ley de Autonoma, el Gobierno no puede dar instrucciones al Banco de Espaa, ni este puede recabarlas o aceptarlas, en el ejercicio de las funciones que se derivan de la pertenencia al Sistema Europeo de Bancos Centrales. Estos principios son aplicables tambin a las funciones que se ejercen en el seno del Mecanismo nico de Supervisin. 2. La independencia legal no slo se plasma en la personalidad jurdica propia del organismo para actuar en su propio nombre, sino en la capacidad de emitir decisiones jurdicamente vinculantes en el mbito de sus competencias. En este aspecto baste sealar que el Banco de Espaa tiene personalidad jurdica propia, distinta de la de cualquier otra administracin o institucin. 3. La independencia personal de sus mximos representantes requiere que el nombramiento, el ejercicio de sus mandatos y el cese del cargo deban estar previa y explcitamente previstos, as como estar sujetos a una serie de garantas que los preserven de toda injerencia. Tanto la figura del Gobernador, como la ma propia, tienen reforzada su independencia con respecto a los poderes polticos y al sector supervisado, entre otras medidas, mediante: (i) la duracin de nuestro mandato se fija en seis aos (superior al ciclo electoral) y sin posibilidad de renovacin; (ii) el establecimiento de causas tasadas para el cese del cargo de Gobernador, Subgobernador y consejeros no natos; (iii) el rgimen de incompatibilidades al que estn sujetos el Gobernador, el Subgobernador y los consejeros, y (iv) la prohibicin de ejercer actividad profesional relacionada con las entidades de crdito o con los mercados de valores en un perodo de dos aos posterior al cese en el cargo. 4. La independencia funcional garantiza la capacidad del organismo para ejercer todas las funciones y competencias que le han sido encomendadas para cumplir su mandato. 5. La independencia financiera es imprescindible para garantizar que el organismo cuente con los recursos financieros y humanos suficientes y que estos estn organizados y estructurados de la forma ms conveniente para la consecucin del mandato. En este sentido, el Banco de Espaa cuenta con un presupuesto propio que le permite obtener los recursos econmicos necesarios para el desarrollo de sus funciones. 6. Por lo que se refiere a la independencia organizativa, el Banco de Espaa goza de autonoma para establecer su organizacin interna y, especialmente, su poltica de personal. Conviene recalcar en todo caso que el Banco de Espaa, por imperativo legal, selecciona a su personal respetando los principios de igualdad, mrito, capacidad y publicidad y que el mismo est vinculado al Banco por una relacin de derecho laboral. Por tanto, cabe concluir que el nivel de independencia financiera y organizativa del Banco de Espaa resulta adecuado para la consecucin de sus objetivos. Rendicin de cuentas como contrapeso de la independencia Quisiera finalizar reflexionando brevemente sobre la importancia de la rendicin de cuentas. En un estado democrtico, a todo organismo u autoridad independiente se le debe exigir transparencia y rendicin de cuentas respecto a sus decisiones, como elementos imprescindibles para otorgarle legitimidad. Es un hecho que la crisis financiera global ha provocado que aumenten las exigencias de los bancos centrales en este campo, dado que, por una parte, la poltica monetaria ha ampliado su instrumental con medidas ms complejas y, por otra, los bancos centrales han asumido ms responsabilidades en el mbito de la estabilidad financiera, en particular en lo relativo a supervisin macroprudencial. La rendicin de cuentas de las actuaciones y actividades de los organismos y autoridades independientes debe realizarse preferentemente ante el Parlamento. A este respecto existe control parlamentario directo sobre el Presupuesto del Banco de Espaa y sobre su Balance y Cuenta de Resultados; tambin se remiten de manera regular a las Cortes Generales Informes y Memorias como, por ejemplo, el Informe Anual, el Informe Institucional, la Memoria de Supervisin o de actuaciones sancionadoras. Dentro de este ejercicio de rendicin de cuentas ante el Parlamento tambin est establecida la comparecencia del Gobernador ante la Comisin de Economa del Congreso, para presentar el Informe Anual y para analizar las propuestas de los Presupuestos Generales del Estado. Ms all de la rendicin de cuentas, la transparencia institucional es tambin un principio bsico en el correcto funcionamiento de los organismos pblicos independientes, en particular dado que la confianza y la credibilidad en estas instituciones son la base de su eficacia. El Banco de Espaa tiene una amplia tradicin en la publicacin de informes que gozan de un reconocido rigor y prestigio y que cubren diferentes mbitos de la actuacin de la institucin, tratando siempre de llegar a un amplio espectro de pblico. Tambin es nuestro objetivo aumentar la participacin del Banco en aquellos foros acadmicos, profesionales y sociales, donde nuestra presencia pueda resultar provechosa, as como la utilizacin de nuevos instrumentos de comunicacin, como la apertura reciente de una cuenta de Twitter, o contactos regulares con la prensa en los que se pretende explicar el contenido de nuestros informes de una manera ms accesible El Banco ha incrementado tambin el nivel de informacin del Portal de Transparencia, incorporando un mayor detalle en las agendas y comparecencias tanto del Gobernador como mas, as como de aquellos documentos que integran el marco de actuacin tico de los altos cargos. En este sentido, tanto el Gobernador como yo misma, como representantes del Consejo de Gobierno del BCE y del Mecanismo nico de Supervisin, respectivamente, acabamos de firmar un nuevo cdigo de conducta que incrementa nuestro compromiso personal con los estndares ticos ms elevados con el objetivo de garantizar nuestra independencia del sector pblico y privado y evitar posibles conflictos de inters. Por ltimo quera sealar que el Banco est en proceso de elaboracin de un plan estratgico, cuya fecha de finalizacin se prev para la segunda mitad de este ao y cuyo contenido esencial se har pblico. Ms all de la importancia que supone este ejercicio desde el punto de vista interno, creo que la elaboracin y publicacin de este plan resulta un elemento fundamental de incremento de la transparencia, que facilitar la valoracin de la eficacia de las actuaciones del Banco.

Title: Opening speech at the Conference "The role of investors in the energy transition model", organized by Expansin
text: 30.04.2019 Keynote address Conference "The role of investors in the energy transition model"/Expansion Margarita Delgado Subgobernadora Good morning and thank you very much to the newspaper Expansi97n for its kind invitation to open this conference on the role of investors in the energy transition model. Introduction The fight against climate change is a recurring objective of international institutions, at least since the United Nations Summit held in Rio de Janeiro in 1992. After the Paris agreement of 2015, this objective acquires greater concreteness and momentum, also setting a deadline for compliance in the so-called 2030 agenda. In any case, it is noteworthy that it is in the Paris agreement where the importance of the financial system is explicitly recognized to channel, in an efficient way, the resources necessary to transform the economy towards a sustainable model. We can affirm that the energy or ecological transition and, more specifically, the role that finance can play in this transition, is an issue that is gaining visibility and importance on the agenda of international financial organizations. Among others, we could mention various initiatives within the scope of the G20, the United Nations, the Financial Stability Board, or the OECD. At EU level, it is worth noting the relevance of the European Commission's action plan on sustainable finance, and in our country the draft Climate Change Law affects us directly. Specifically in the environment of central banks and banking supervisors, I would like to highlight the work of the Network for Greening the Financial Sector (NGFS), a network in which the Bank of Spain actively participates and which has just published its second report, which includes the best practices to promote the role of the financial sector in compliance with the Paris agreement. The report is highly recommended not only because of its informative nature, but above all because it is a call to action. The 6 recommendations of the report, addressed to central banks, supervisors, regulators and financial institutions, represent an important starting point to start acting in a coordinated manner. Colloquially speaking, it could be concluded that sustainable finance is 'fashionable'. In fact, looking at my own agenda, I note that, since the middle of last month, I have had 4 interventions focused on this topic: I have opened a conference on green finance that we organized in the Bank of Spain together with the Ministry of Ecological Transition, representatives of banks and academics; I participated in the recent NGFS plenary in Paris, where the aforementioned report on sustainable finance was approved; I have been part of a panel in which the potential role of Central Banks as a driver of the ecological transition was discussed; And finally, today I have the honour to open this day. I believe that this accumulation of events on sustainable finance is good proof of the growing attention that this issue raises. On the other hand, in addition to arousing interest, I believe that the ecological transition towards a sustainable economic model is a need that, fortunately, is also being shared by an increasingly large part of society. Although it is a somewhat topical phrase, it is worth remembering that what we do today will determine the type of world in which we will live tomorrow. Of course, the change of production model is an issue of capital importance, which has systemic implications and which, therefore, must be carried out in a careful and gradual way if we want to avoid unwanted economic and social consequences. The objective is to achieve what has come to be called a just transition, although it is not convenient either. Forget that this type of change also brings opportunities that must be seized. In any case, it is clear that, in order to be successful, any transition must include very wide-ranging measures and instruments, affecting virtually all economic operators, not just credit institutions; Proof of this is the varied composition of the round table that will take place after my intervention. The question therefore arises as to what the role of the financial system is in this process. I would like to highlight two elements: (i) firstly, as providers of the credit necessary for economic activity to develop, it is clear that any change affecting economic agents also directly affects banks; (ii) second, both institutions and investors can and should play an active role in such a transition. This second facet is what is reflected, rightly in my opinion, in the title of this day, and will be the main object of my speech today, in which I will also refer to the work of the financial system as a potential catalyst for the process of ecological transition. Finally, I will mention what, in my opinion, are the elements that are still missing so that finance can truly act as an engine of change, among which I will highlight the need to have a clear and functional taxonomy that can be used by all economic agents. Role of institutions and supervisors As I have already indicated, the solvency of credit institutions may be affected by the ecological transition process. More specifically, due to the materialization of two types of risks: (i) on the one hand there are the so-called physical risks, caused by the direct effects of climate change, such as the effect of droughts or floods, (ii) on the other hand there would be the so-called transition risks, that is, the effect on bank borrowers of measures aimed at transforming the economy in a sustainable way. The supervisor has the obligation to monitor these risks as well as articulate measures to encourage banks to assess, assess and mitigate these risks. These measures can be of different kinds, including aspects such as: . collecting detailed information on aspects such as the physical location of assets or the efficiency strategies of companies receiving funding; . the implementation of stress tests around different ecological transition scenarios; . the development of macroeconomic models to assess the potential impact of certain transition scenarios on the economy; or . The development by entities of risk models that take climate change into account. It is worth asking where exactly we are in relation to these measures. As I will describe below, we are still in an early, somewhat incipient phase, in which both the supervisor and the supervisees are raising the level of knowledge and awareness on this subject. While there have been significant advances, we must admit that we are still building the methodologies and governance structures necessary to meet this challenge. Qualitative measures Among the topics currently being discussed at the NGFS is the so-called Environmental Risk Assessment (ERA), which refers to the methods and practices used to quantify environmental impact in the financial sector. These evaluations have both qualitative and quantitative elements. With regard to the qualitative elements, I would highlight governance first. In this regard, it is essential that supervisors engage in dialogue with institutions to analyse how they are dealing with environmental risks. Obviously, the consideration of environmental risk is something very new and entities that already contemplate it in an explicit way have tended to include it within their areas of social responsibility; however, we must verify that the entities are incorporating it, in addition, in their strategies and risk analysis and monitoring, and that the information generated internally reaches the entity's own Board. The supervisory expectation in the short and medium term is that institutions understand the implications of this risk and are able to identify and measure it, always in proportion to its size and complexity. In this sense, they must be able to evaluate how it can affect their business model as well as integrate it within their risk appetite framework, for which they are expected to use stress analysis and hypothetical scenarios, since, by definition, if only historical data is used it is not possible to capture events that have not occurred in the past, at least since we have a reliable record. It is also important that the analysis of this risk is carried out considering a medium and long-term horizon, higher in any case than that usually used in the measurement of financial risks. Quantitative measures On the other hand, the quantitative elements seek to measure and reflect the physical and transition risks that may affect the accredited of the institutions. This quantitative environmental risk assessment should be carried out in institutions' own risk models. Obviously, there are methodological challenges and difficulties in incorporating these factors into internal risk models, for example, the horizon over which the effects of physical risk are observed may be much longer than that generally used in risk assessment. However, I wanted to point out that, although these elements are novel, institutions have historically been subject to this type of transition risk, although it may not have been called that so far. We all have in mind examples of solvent and strong companies, many of them international leaders, that have disappeared in a short period of years because they have not been able to adapt to a change in technological or consumer behavior. The analysis of potential changes in the environment, in order to assess the possibility of business failure, is an essential part of the evaluation and management of risks in the financial system, regardless of whether such change in the environment has a technological, customer behavior, regulatory or environmental origin. In any case, I would like to emphasize that, if institutions identify, and properly quantify these risks in price and capital needs, they would not only be improving risk sensitivity, contributing to guarantee the stability of the system. financial as a whole, but also, indirectly, would become a driver of change, by encouraging financing to reach those activities that contribute most to the sustainable transformation of the economy, while discouraging those activities that may be more harmful, by passing on environmental costs to the price of financing, that until now remained hidden. Role of the supervisor As regards the role of the supervisor, we also face significant challenges in quantifying these risks for the financial sector as a whole. For example, we must be able to assess financial institutions' exposures to high-carbon activities, perform stress exercises for the system as a whole, or define scenarios and methodologies to be applied by individual institutions. This is a new type of initiative, but the Single Supervisory Mechanism (SSM) itself has included for the first time the risks linked to climate change as an element to be considered among its priorities for 2019. To carry out this type of analysis in a centralized way, it is essential to have sufficiently detailed and disaggregated information on credit risks, for example, by type of activity, sector or geographical location. In this sense, Banco de Espa96a has traditionally been a reference in terms of credit information collection, counting for decades with a Risk Information Center (CIR) widely used in supervision, statistics and remote monitoring. Very recently, the Bank has been one of the few authorities in Europe that has completed the implementation of the SSM project known as 'Anacredit', which allows obtaining a greater level of detail of exposures to companies, which will make it possible to carry out this type of analysis in a more exhaustive and precise way. Additionally, supervisors must advance in the development of models that contemplate the macroeconomic effects of different ecological transition scenarios, in order to know the potential impacts of climate change on certain economic sectors, industries or even companies, as well as on variables of a more aggregated nature, such as growth or inflation. This is the perspective from which we must view measures to promote a just transition. In any case, it is clear that, both the institutions and the supervisor himself, need to increase, or even sometimes begin to 'build', the technical knowledge necessary to be able to understand and adequately measure these risks. On the other hand, as knowledge about these risks increases, so does the integration of these risks into the supervisory culture. Role of investors Returning to the title of this day, I would also like to refer to the role that investors can play in this process of ecological transition. It should be noted that in capital markets, there has been some discrimination in the valuation of companies with lower levels of exposure to climate change, although still to a limited extent. Additionally, a certain proliferation of 'green bonds' issuances is beginning to be observed, even by the public sector, as we have seen recently with an ICO issue, placed in general with a much higher demand and at costs. lower than equivalent standard emissions. Clearly, the attractiveness of green bond issues among investors is an indication of growing concern about the effects of climate change, but it should also reflect lower underlying risk. Logically, this discrimination in the valuation of traded financial instruments would allow us to estimate the 'financial' value of the risks associated with climate change and, as already mentioned in the case of bank financing, should act as a catalyst for change towards certain sustainable activities. Taxonomy However, for transmission mechanisms, whether through the assessment of risk by institutions or the differential valuation of issues in the markets, to function properly, a common 'language' is required, which can be used by both debt issuers and potential investors to consistently catalogue risk. allowing these markets to reach a 'critical mass', while increasing transparency regarding sustainable investments. To achieve these objectives, initiatives developed within the framework of the European Commission are fundamental. The Commission, within its action plan presented in May 2018, includes a proposal for three regulations: (i) Regulation to establish a framework to facilitate sustainable investments; (ii) Regulation on disclosure relating to sustainable investments and sustainability risks; (iii) Regulation to create low-carbon and positive carbon impact benchmarks. The three regulations stress the need to provide greater transparency and homogeneity to this type of investment but, among the three, I would highlight the first, which establishes precisely the creation of a 'taxonomy', that is, a technically sound classification system that provides clarity on what is 'ecological' or 'sustainable' (green assets) as opposed to 'polluting' assets (also known as brown assets). Obviously, once this taxonomy is established, it would be possible to carry out a much more consistent analysis of the spread in risk between green or brown assets, whether measured in terms of delinquency (solvency), price (differential required to finance) or price (green bonds). It would also facilitate the risk analysis in a consolidated way by the supervisor, the development of macroeconomic models to evaluate the effects in the medium and long term, and the consistent articulation of stress exercises. Finally, it is clear that this risk taxonomy is also needed if we want to provide clear and homogeneous information to investors and public opinion in general, as required by the Spanish law on ecological transition for all listed companies. Of course, we must understand that it is impossible for this taxonomy, or any that can be proposed, to be perfect from day one. Certain categories will need to be adjusted, refined and modified as we better understand the implications and connections between certain activities. It is also true that it is not the same to establish a single category of 'green' activities, than to be able to classify all activities. economic within a green-brown range. The taxonomy initially proposed will therefore be limited, and predictably, will gain in ambition as our knowledge advances. In any case, it is clear that in order to communicate it is much better to have a common language, even if it is limited and imperfect, than not to have a language or that it is not common, as in the current case. Role of central banks as investors Central banks are also active investors in financial markets, both in our monetary policy operations and in reserve-related portfolio management. In this respect, we must recognise that, for the time being, environmental risks are not being incorporated into most ratings of that portfolio, whether internal or prepared by rating agencies. However, we are working to correct this situation. Within the Eurosystem, an intensive review of these risk assessment processes is under way to ensure that all relevant factors, such as environmental factors, are taken into account for the prudent management of the portfolio held by central banks. In addition, I would like to point out that, like the ECB, we strongly support the initiative that, as regulator of rating agencies, has recently been launched by the European Securities Markets Authority (ESMA) to establish guidelines for these entities to make public the way in which they incorporate sustainability elements into their valuations. Again, I think it is clear that the consistent development and implementation of a common taxonomy would allow our efforts to translate into a more robust and robust rating methodology, based on empirical evidence. Conclusions I would like to conclude by reiterating the importance of this challenge and the need to face it realistically but also with ambition. The transition to a more sustainable economy is a challenge that affects virtually all economic agents and sectors, but I believe that the financial sector undoubtedly has a prominent responsibility in this transition. Financial authorities, within the scope of our mandate, can and must do everything in our power to properly assess, manage and mitigate the risks associated with climate change. I hope that the measures promoted in this area from Europe will end up being a reference and standard at international level and that, in this way, we will achieve that the financial sector contributes actively and efficiently to the sustainable transformation of our economy. If we look at the current situation, I think we can see that there are a large number of initiatives that are 'germinating', while others have even begun to 'flourish'; however, it is also true that much remains to be achieved to achieve them in order for them to bear fruit and the commitment of the Paris agreement is not as far back in time as it might seem. Despite all the challenges and difficulties I wanted to end with a positive message. It can be seen that the speed at which the whole process is happening is surprising. It should be recalled that the NGFS was created less than two years ago and that we still do not have national or European legislation in place on sustainable financing; However, progress in less than two years has been very significant and the degree of preparation of institutions and supervisors, who are not exactly agile when it comes to undertaking changes of this magnitude, has increased considerably in this period. I would like to emphasise that it is usual to introduce changes in organisations by going in tow of legislation, whereas, in this case, both entities and supervisors are acting before a standard explicitly requires it. As Victor Hugo said, 'nothing is more powerful than an idea whose time has come'. I sincerely believe that the time for sustainable finance has just begun. Thanks a lot.
text_original: 30.04.2019 Discurso de apertura Jornada El papel de los inversores en el modelo de transicin energtica/Expansin Margarita Delgado Subgobernadora Buenos das y muchas gracias al diario Expansin por su amable invitacin para abrir esta jornada sobre el papel de los inversores en el modelo de transicin energtica. Introduccin La lucha contra el cambio climtico es un objetivo recurrente de las instituciones internacionales, al menos desde la Cumbre de Naciones Unidas celebrada en Ro de Janeiro en 1992.
