Esto explica, tambin, el creciente inters de los organismos internacionales como, por ejemplo, el Consejo de Estabilidad Financiera (FSB, por sus siglas en ingls) o el Comit de Supervisin Bancaria de Basilea (BCBS, por su siglas en ingls) por profundizar en la evaluacin de sus implicaciones potenciales para la estructura y el funcionamiento del sistema financiero. Resulta evidente que la innovacin tecnolgica ofrece oportunidades de mejora para la eficiencia del sector financiero que podramos denominar tradicional. Pero quiz ms relevante es el hecho de que los avances tecnolgicos han permitido separar las distintas funciones tradicionales que efectan las instituciones financieras (realizacin de pagos, transformacin de plazos, comparticin de riesgos, asignacin del capital), de forma que estas pueden realizarse ahora individualmente por nuevos actores no bancarios. En este contexto, y a diferencia de oleadas de innovacin tecnolgica previas, los intermediarios financieros tradicionales parecen estar teniendo ms dificultad que en el pasado para adaptarse y responder con la misma agilidad. La mera observacin de esta realidad puede hacernos pensar que parafraseando el conocido ttulo del trabajo de Reinhart y Rogoff sobre las crisis econmicas esta vez s parece ser diferente. Qu caractersticas del fenmeno fintech lo hacen diferente a oleadas de innovacin previas? El primer elemento distintivo del fenmeno fintech actual es la multiplicidad de tecnologas innovadoras que emergen y maduran a gran velocidad en forma de racimo: banca mvil, inteligencia artificial, identidad digital, registros distribuidos, computacin en la nube y un largo etctera que dificultan a las organizaciones tradicionales focalizarse en un nico elemento tecnolgico innovador, como pudo ser Internet en los aos noventa o la informatizacin en los aos setenta y ochenta. Adems, esta variedad de tecnologas est permitiendo a los nuevos proveedores responder con gran celeridad a las demandas y necesidades especficas de los usuarios, creando nuevos servicios. Por otra parte, el entorno global de creciente digitalizacin al que aluda al principio acelera estos procesos de transformacin. As, un nmero creciente de consumidores se ha adaptado fcilmente y de manera rpida a las nuevas tecnologas y demanda una experiencia de usuario similar en todos los mbitos de su vida, incluidas sus relaciones financieras. En consecuencia, las nuevas soluciones en los mbitos de banca mvil o las plataformas de financiacin alternativa se expanden rpidamente y trascienden las fronteras nacionales. Por poner un ejemplo, el porcentaje de las operaciones de pago al por menor que canalizan las entidades no bancarias en China ha pasado de ser el 59 % en 2013 al 76 % en 2017. Del mismo modo, segn estimaciones del FSB, el mercado global de los prstamos peer-to-peer representa en la actualidad algo ms del 3 % de la cifra de endeudamiento de los hogares, siendo de nuevo China el caso ms destacado. En este contexto se pone de manifiesto otro elemento diferencial del proceso de innovacin tecnolgica actual: la relevancia de los datos. La creciente digitalizacin est haciendo que el volumen de informacin disponible sobre los usuarios aumente de manera exponencial. Desarrollos como el Internet de las cosas no harn sino impulsar esta tendencia an ms. Y ello hasta el punto de que algunas estimaciones1 apuntan a que el stock de datos existente a da de hoy se habr multiplicado por cinco en apenas un lustro. Al mismo tiempo, la mayor capacidad computacional para almacenar y procesar rpidamente toda esta informacin hace posible que aumenten las opciones de nuevos servicios prestados a los clientes. En el mbito financiero, destaca el papel creciente de los algoritmos automatizados en los procesos de decisin en reas como la identificacin y el reconocimiento de clientes, la concesin de crditos o la deteccin de prcticas fraudulentas, entre otros. 1 Data Age 2025: The Digitalization of the World, IDC & Seagate (2018). Estos desarrollos en el terreno de los servicios financieros dan lugar a que, por ejemplo, un volumen considerable de informacin valiosa para estimar la calidad crediticia de los clientes se est generando fuera del espacio de actuacin de los intermediarios financieros tradicionales. Adems, la proliferacin de iniciativas como el open banking, apoyadas en el dinamismo de las application programming interface (API), podran erosionar las ventajas comparativas de los bancos basadas en un diferencial de conocimientos anteriormente no accesible a terceras partes. Este escenario supone un reto para las entidades financieras, dado que su negocio se ha sustentado tradicionalmente, en buena parte, en su capacidad para obtener, almacenar, procesar y explotar la abundante informacin de que disponen, tanto sobre sus clientes como sobre los mercados. Cmo se estn adaptando los intermediarios financieros tradicionales a este nuevo entorno? Es evidente que la nueva ola de innovacin tecnolgico-financiera est alterando las estructuras de costes e influyendo en las economas de escala y alcance del negocio financiero. Esto est llevando a los intermediarios tradicionales, y en particular a la banca, a modificar su modelo de negocio y a ofrecer sus servicios de manera diferente. Ante este reto de adaptacin, los intermediarios financieros tradicionales han ido evolucionando desde una reaccin originalmente ms defensiva hacia posiciones ms proclives a la colaboracin dentro del nuevo ecosistema. La principal excepcin son, posiblemente, las grandes empresas tecnolgicas de los mercados asiticos y, aunque con un alcance menor, la competencia ms directa que se observa entre bancos y empresas fintech en el segmento del crdito a familias y pymes. Los bancos buscan intensificar la colaboracin a travs de distintas vas. As, han desplegado ambiciosos programas de adquisiciones a travs de los programas de aceleracin de compaas tecnofinancieras (ms conocidos como aceleradoras de innovacin). Tambin destaca el creciente papel de las entidades financieras en calidad de inversores de referencia en fondos de capital riesgo especializados. Estos esfuerzos de colaboracin van dirigidos a propiciar que el crecimiento tenga lugar de una manera ms orgnica, facilitando que las aportaciones diferenciales de las empresas fintech acaben por integrarse en la estructura de los bancos de manera ms eficiente. De hecho, un creciente nmero de entidades aboga por la creacin de reas digitales propias que desarrollan una genuina actividad fintech interna como elemento dinamizador de unos ciclos de transformacin tradicionalmente dilatados. Nuevos modelos, nuevos actores, nuevos riesgos En conjunto, la actual oleada de innovacin tecnolgico-financiera ofrece un amplio abanico de mejoras potenciales en la calidad, la cantidad y la inmediatez de los servicios financieros accesibles a los ciudadanos, reduciendo simultneamente los costes de estos servicios. Al mismo tiempo, sin embargo, tambin puede amplificar algunos de los riesgos de carcter financiero u operacional ya conocidos y crear otros nuevos. En primer lugar, desde una perspectiva macroprudencial, debemos sopesar las eventuales implicaciones sistmicas del fenmeno fintech. Ello supone, en primer trmino, evaluar las interrelaciones en el sistema financiero, que podran aumentar de manera significativa en el nuevo entorno competitivo y tecnolgico, incluido el sector bancario, facilitando la propagacin de las perturbaciones. En efecto, la dimensin global de la tecnologa y de muchos de los oferentes de sus componentes esenciales redunda en que el sector financiero se vuelva progresivamente ms interconectado e interdependiente desde el punto de vista operativo. Esto hace tambin ms relevantes las amenazas cibernticas, que se convierten en uno de los principales riesgos para la estabilidad financiera. Adicionalmente, implica tomar en consideracin aspectos tales como el posible contagio reputacional provocado por la prestacin de servicios financieros o tecnolgicos a familias y empresas por parte de las nuevas entidades, que no siempre cuentan con las estructuras de gobernanza y control de las instituciones financieras. Estos costes reputacionales pueden surgir de aspectos tan sensibles como la privacidad y el acceso a los datos individuales o la financiacin de actividades ilcitas. Asimismo, dado que todava no disponemos de un ciclo crediticio completo con estas nuevas tecnologas, desconocemos la potencial influencia de estas, los algoritmos o los nuevos actores en cuestiones bsicas como la relajacin de los estndares de concesin de crdito o en la prociclicidad de las polticas crediticias, lo que podra tener importantes consecuencias macroeconmicas. En el mismo sentido, el incremento de la competencia, la mayor rapidez en las transacciones y el uso de algoritmos comunes podra llevar a un incremento de la volatilidad del sistema financiero, incluidos los depsitos de los bancos. Por otra parte, en principio el fenmeno fintech incrementa el grado de contestabilidad del mercado financiero y, de esta manera, aumenta el nivel de competencia y eficiencia del mismo. No obstante, desde el punto de vista competitivo resulta crucial el papel que acaben desempeando las grandes corporaciones tecnolgicas globales, las famosas bigtech. Algunas de las caractersticas de estas empresas, como sus fuertes niveles de capitalizacin, su capacidad para acceder a una financiacin barata o su amplia cartera de clientes sobre los que acumulan un volumen ingente de informacin, las situaran en una posicin envidiable en el caso de que decidiesen acometer una estrategia de expansin masiva en el sector financiero. La importancia de la informacin en la industria financiera y las fuertes economas de escala en el acceso a los datos podran facilitar esta expansin. De hecho, el acceso a las variables financieras, junto con las mtricas relativas a las circunstancias personales y a las conductas de los agentes econmicos, ha sido, y sigue siendo, un elemento crucial para explicar el inters de las bigtech en incorporar servicios financieros a su cadena de valor. Adems, estas empresas se han caracterizado, precisamente, por sus fortalezas en trminos de capacidades para poder aprovechar, en beneficio de sus otras lneas de negocio, los grandes volmenes de datos que acumulan fruto de las interacciones con sus clientes. Se plantean as nuevos riesgos competitivos y operativos que podran, por ejemplo, adoptar la forma de una gran dependencia respecto de un reducido nmero de proveedores de informacin. De hecho, el mercado de la informacin financiera y de los servicios analticos asociados es uno de los primeros ejemplos destacados, donde, conforme a los anlisis del FSB, dos de las entidades especializadas acumulan cerca del 50 % de la cuota de mercado. En este entorno, las entidades financieras tradicionales corren el riesgo de quedar excluidas de las bases de datos de carcter crecientemente estratgico, como pueden ser los patrones de consumo de los clientes que se generan a travs de las plataformas digitales y que pueden proporcionar informacin valiosa sobre la calidad crediticia de los clientes. A su vez, el grado de dependencia de las entidades financieras en torno a un nmero reducido de proveedores de servicios tecnolgicos, como pueden ser, por ejemplo, los relacionados con la computacin en la nube (que adems, en muchos casos, son proporcionados por estas mismas bigtech con un alto nivel de concentracin, ya que los cuatro proveedores principales gestionan el 60 % del mercado), podra dar pie a la aparicin de nuevos riesgos de carcter sistmico. Retos regulatorios Dados los riesgos identificados, resulta especialmente pertinente valorar la idoneidad del marco regulatorio ante estos nuevos modelos de negocio, tanto desde la perspectiva de preservar la estabilidad financiera manteniendo estndares prudenciales apropiados y la proteccin de los clientes, como desde la necesidad de no limitar indebidamente los potenciales beneficios para la sociedad de los modelos de negocio basados en la tecnologa. Espaa comparte con varios pases de Latinoamrica la caracterstica de tener unos sistemas financieros predominantemente bancarizados en los que las entidades se han caracterizado por ofrecer una amplia gama de servicios financieros. Los nuevos proveedores, sin embargo, siguen una estrategia diferente, basada en la especializacin en ciertos nichos y en la distribucin de productos de terceros. En estas circunstancias, es importante garantizar unas reglas del juego que garanticen un entorno competitivo equilibrado y que favorezcan una transicin ordenada. Por ello, es fundamental asegurar que se cumple el principio de neutralidad, de manera que riesgos similares derivados de actividades similares estn sujetos a las mismas reglas independientemente de cul sea el proveedor. Lamentablemente, este principio, aparentemente sencillo, no est exento de complejidades a la hora de ponerlo en prctica. El primer escollo lo encontramos al tratar de definir el mbito de aplicacin de una norma. La transformacin tecnolgica est difuminando las fronteras funcionales que suponan la delimitacin del mbito de aplicacin de la normativa. De hecho, la innovacin tecnolgica no solo introduce una mayor segmentacin en la cadena de valor estndar, sino que adems promueve la creacin de nuevas cadenas. En consecuencia, podemos encontrar entidades que se centran exclusivamente en un proceso muy concreto, as como otras que combinan la provisin de servicios financieros con actividades al margen de este sector. Cuando las barreras se difuminan de esta manera, la tarea de definir unas normas claras que cubran adecuadamente todas las posibilidades se dificulta de manera considerable. Porque, adems, tambin se estn difuminando los mbitos geogrficos de prestacin de los servicios al amparo de las posibilidades de prestacin remota que brindan las nuevas tecnologas. En todo caso, me gustara aclarar una cuestin sobre la que, en algunos casos, existe un aparente malentendido. Contrariamente a lo que se piensa, no toda la actividad desarrollada por las empresas fintech se halla al margen del exigente permetro regulatorio que caracteriza al sistema financiero. Por un lado, el esfuerzo de los reguladores para disponer de un marco mejor adaptado a esta nueva realidad es evidente en mbitos como el de los sistemas y los medios de pago. Por ejemplo, en la Unin Europea, la reciente Directiva de Servicios de Pago (PSD-2) ha servido, entre otras cosas, para extender el permetro regulatorio, dar cabida a nuevos actores, y darles la posibilidad de acceso a los datos bancarios de sus clientes. Por otro lado, es apreciable el volumen de nuevos operadores que, tras una fase inicial de prueba, han buscado el amparo de una licencia antes de dar el salto a operaciones de mayor escala. En este contexto, hay que destacar el papel de los sandbox o entornos de pruebas controlados. Iniciativas de este tipo (como las que se estn desarrollando o iniciando en pases como Mxico o Espaa, entre otros) tienen como objetivo proporcionar, con todas las cautelas en cuanto a seguridad para los participantes y para el sistema en su conjunto, un marco gil que permita a las entidades analizar si los modelos de negocio basados en nuevas tecnologas tienen viabilidad. Asimismo, permiten a todas las autoridades involucradas aprender de forma prctica su funcionamiento y conocer los nuevos riesgos asociados a sus actividades. A cambio, este conocimiento ms profundo sobre la actividad realizada por estos nuevos actores abre la puerta a que los supervisores puedan explotar plenamente el principio de proporcionalidad contenido en las regulaciones para aquellos proyectos viables que puedan abandonar el espacio de pruebas. Es importante tener presente que se trata de eso, de un entorno de pruebas, y que, por tanto, debe tratarse de una fase temporal, de forma que, para aquellos proyectos que resulten viables, impere el principio general ya mencionado de aplicar una regulacin equivalente para actividades y riesgos similares. Por otra parte, la respuesta regulatoria ante la complejidad derivada del fenmeno fintech pasa, inevitablemente, por lograr una mayor cooperacin y una ms completa coordinacin con otras autoridades, tanto en el mbito nacional como en el internacional. Adems, la necesidad de cooperacin no se limita solo a las fases iniciales de transformacin y cambio del sector, sino que abarca aspectos ms fundamentales. As, cuestiones como la privacidad de la informacin personal, la proteccin del consumidor, la defensa de la competencia o la proteccin ante amenazas cibernticas adquieren especial relevancia en un entorno crecientemente digital. En particular, en relacin con los riesgos cibernticos, resulta esencial abordarlos de forma conjunta y coordinada entre los sectores pblico y privado desde una ptica global, lo que hace imprescindible la cooperacin internacional. Pero adems, ante este tipo de amenazas, debe tenerse tambin en cuenta que cualquier elemento del nuevo ecosistema puede servir como puerta de acceso al conjunto y puede comprometer, de este modo, su seguridad. Por ello, no es posible abordar este riesgo con las mismas reglas de proporcionalidad o gradualidad que rigen para otro tipo de riesgos. En definitiva, resulta imprescindible identificar los puntos crticos del sistema financiero en esta materia, compartiendo informacin y buenas prcticas y desplegando una estrategia de concienciacin dirigida a toda la sociedad. Por otra parte, permtanme recordar que, en el mbito estrictamente bancario, el BCBS public en 2018 un documento de buenas prcticas para los bancos y los supervisores bancarios en relacin con la innovacin tecnolgico-financiera. Sin abordar en detalle el declogo completo de recomendaciones contenidas en dicho informe, s querra destacar dos elementos centrales. En primer lugar, de nuevo, la importancia de la cooperacin supervisora internacional y con otras autoridades (e. g., proteccin de datos, competencia, prevencin del blanqueo, etc.). En segundo lugar, la necesidad de que las propias entidades cuenten con estructuras de gobernanza y procesos de gestin de riesgos adecuados a los nuevos riesgos derivados de la innovacin. En este sentido, siguiendo tambin las conclusiones del informe publicado en diciembre de 2018 por el BCBS sobre prcticas en materia de ciber-resiliencia, quisiera destacar que, si bien el uso de recursos de terceros puede contribuir a mejorar los niveles de resiliencia de los bancos, los supervisores deben garantizar que estos cuenten con prcticas y procesos de gestin del riesgo apropiados para cualquier actividad externalizada o apoyada por terceros. Y esto debe incluir, lgicamente, los servicios prestados por empresas fintech. Por tanto, debemos asegurar que a las actividades externalizadas se les apliquen unos controles de calidad tan estrictos como los aplicados a los servicios que los bancos realizan por s mismos. El documento del BCBS tambin enfatiza el hecho de que algunos de los desarrollos tecnolgicos que estn aplicando las empresas fintech y los bancos podran tambin ser aplicados a las prcticas supervisoras, mejorando su eficiencia y efectividad, por lo que merecen ser explorados (lo que se conoce como suptech). Por ltimo, desde la perspectiva de la gestin de los sistemas de pago hemos de valorar la conveniencia de adaptar las reglas de acceso a dichos sistemas, de modo que faciliten la participacin de un mayor nmero de contrapartidas y proporcionen un entorno favorable en el que poder seguir innovando. No obstante, una decisin de este tipo debe guiarse por la prevalencia de unas reglas que eviten la propagacin de riesgos con consecuencias que podran ser sistmicas. En definitiva, la creciente incorporacin de los nuevos desarrollos tecnolgicos al mbito de los servicios financieros podra generar importantes beneficios en trminos de inclusin financiera, diversificacin de las fuentes de financiacin e incremento de la eficiencia. No obstante, tambin debe reconocerse la existencia de nuevos riesgos, que deben abordarse reforzando la cooperacin de todas las autoridades regulatorias y supervisoras nacionales e internacionales. Muchas gracias.

Title: Keynote speech at the XXVI Financial Sector Meeting organized by Deloitte, Sociedad de Tasacin, and ABC
text: 08.05.2019 Keynote address XXVI Meeting of the Financial Sector "Building the Banking of the Future" Deloitte, Sociedad de Tasaci97n and ABC Margarita Delgado Subgobernadora Good morning I would like to thank Deloitte, Sociedad de Tasaci97n and the newspaper ABC for the invitation to inaugurate this twenty-sixth meeting of the Financial Sector, which is a unique opportunity to discuss the present and future of the sector. If we look at the agenda of this meeting we can see that the words 'challenge' and 'opportunity' are present in the title of almost all the presentations. I will be unoriginal, given that my speech will focus, precisely, on the opportunities and challenges facing the banking sector in our country. First of all, I will refer to the actions that the entities have been developing for some time, not without a lack of pressure from the supervisor, thanks to which they have managed to improve both their solvency and their profitability. I will now look ahead, focusing on the measures that, in my view, need to be implemented in order to seize the opportunities and meet the challenges they face. Looking back. It is fair to underline that, in the last five years, Spanish banks have carried out an intense process of consolidation, recapitalization and restructuring that has significantly improved the situation of the sector in basic parameters such as the quality of their assets or their levels of profitability and solvency. Indeed, between December 2013 and the end of 2018, the reduction in non-performing loans and foreclosed real estate assets has been very notable. Non-performing assets to the private sector have declined 60% since their peak in 2013. Foreclosed assets have followed a similar pattern, falling by 40% from the peak reached in 2012, although most of this reduction has occurred over the last two years. In particular, during 2018 important steps have been taken in this regard, as Spanish banks have been very active in the sale of damaged portfolios and foreclosed properties, which has allowed them to improve the quality of their assets and save on management costs. The process of reducing the volume of non-performing assets is taking place at a pace similar to that observed during the recovery from the previous crisis, which began in 1994. Thanks to these efforts, as of December 2018, the average level of non-performing loans (NPLs) was in the average of the countries of the European Union. The economic recovery has contributed to this process but, as I have already pointed out, the reduction in non-performing assets is largely explained by the active management of banks. However, it should not be forgotten that such active management has been, to put it mildly, 'encouraged' by the supervisor. In particular, the Single Supervisory Mechanism (SSM) has set out and communicated its supervisory expectations through the publication of supervisory guidance in March 2017. This guide was supplemented by an addendum published a year later. Based on To these expectations, each entity has set an ambitious but credible strategy of divestment of non-performing assets. In addition to this reduction in non-performing assets, we can see that there has been an improvement in the profitability of Spanish entities. Since the collapse in 2012, when it was in negative territory (reaching 'minus' 25%), the return measured on equity stood at 8.5% during 2018, a level clearly higher than the 6.9% observed on average for the euro area. For its part, the return on total assets reached 0.6% in 2018, which is also higher than the 0.5% average registered in all entities under the supervision of the SSM. In any case, it should be stressed that, although profitability has returned to positive values and is above the European Union average, it remains below pre-crisis levels and is lower than the cost of capital demanded by investors. The low average profitability generated by Spanish entities is especially evident in their business in Spain. This low profitability is explained by several factors. Firstly, the still high volume of non-performing assets has a direct negative impact on banks' income statement via reduced interest earned, higher provisions for impairment and expenses associated with the maintenance and management of these assets. In fact, if we compare the period 2015-2017 with 2003-2005, we can see how the decrease in net profit of the business in Spain is mainly due to impairment losses. Second, current interest rate levels have had an impact on the compression of banks' interest margins. Finally, the low profitability is also explained by the significant drop in income associated with the private sector deleveraging process. In fact, it is estimated that two-thirds of the fall in net interest income in Spain is due to the contraction in credit. On the cost side, the effort to adjust operating capacity stands out, which has allowed operating expenses to maintain a downward trend in recent years. As is well known, this adjustment in operational capacity has materialized in a significant reduction in the number of employees and offices in Spain. Since the peaks reached in 2008, the reduction of branches exceeds 40%, while that of employees clearly exceeds 30%. With regard to international activity, mainly of our two large entities, it should be noted that it has allowed us to obtain higher returns, although it is not without challenges, as evidenced by the recent difficulties that have occurred in some of the emerging economies to which our entities are exposed. Despite these difficulties, it can be said that the geographical diversification of banks is a source of added value and stability in the medium and long term. The low correlation of activity between countries ensures more recurrent income and less subject to specific crises. On the other hand, the lower degree of maturity of banking markets in emerging countries has made it possible for our international entities to have higher margins. As regards solvency, I have already pointed out that our banks have also strengthened their capital levels. Specifically, the average ratio, measured on CET1, has gone from showing levels of 9.8% in 2014 to reaching 11.5% in 2018. Although the improvement is clear, it is no less true that Spanish banks would currently be the 'red lantern' in a hypothetical European classification of average solvency levels. In fact, the distance between the average CET1 of Spanish and EU banks has gone from 200 to 300 basis points in the last 4 years, which implies that European banks have strengthened their capital comparatively more than that of our country. However, in terms of leverage, Spanish banks are in a better situation than the European average, especially in relation to that observed for the 'comparable' countries of our environment (that is, the United Kingdom, France, Holland, Germany and Italy). This lower leverage has been maintained since 2016, although the distance with the European average has decreased. This 'divergence' in the classification of solvency levels, measured in terms of leverage and capital ratio, would be explained by several reasons. On the one hand, it should be remembered that, during the crisis, there was a worse relative performance of some credit segments in the Spanish market; On the other hand, the greater capital allocated to assets in certain economies skews upwards the requirements for our two large international entities. Additionally, the higher relative density of Risk-Weighted Assets (PRAs) is related to a lower use of domestic models for capital consumption, compared to other Eurozone countries. As a positive effect, this lower use of internal models allows requirements to be less cyclical. It also means that Spanish banks are not affected by the future introduction of capital floors based on the standard approach, established in Basel III, unlike what will happen with other European competitors. Therefore, although Spanish banks need to strengthen their capital ratios, it should be noted that they have certain comparative strengths, in terms of leverage and geographical and economic diversification. Looking to the future Let me now turn to the challenges that, in my opinion, our financial system must face in order to remain profitable, in an environment of increasing regulatory demand and competitive pressure. Reduction of non-performing assets As I have already indicated, it is fair to underline that during 2018 Spanish banks have been very active in the sale of damaged portfolios and foreclosed properties, which has allowed them to improve the quality of their assets and save on management costs. Despite this, according to internal estimates of the Bank of Spain, by 2020 the NPL ratio could still be around 4%, in the absence of wholesale portfolio sales. The average coverage of all non-performing assets has also fallen, from levels close to 45% at the end of 2013, to below 39% at the end of last year. Recovery of profitability I have already pointed out that improving profitability, and its long-term sustainability, is one of the main challenges facing the sector for the future. The correction of impaired assets to which I have just referred is key, since, in addition to strengthening solvency, it allows profitability to be improved in several ways. On the one hand, resources are freed, now destined to finance non-productive assets. Secondly, all costs associated with maintaining the portfolio, which are particularly burdensome in the case of real estate assets, are eliminated. Thirdly, it allows to reorient the activity towards profitable businesses. Therefore, the reduction of non-performing assets continues to be a challenge for the sector but, at the same time, it is an opportunity to improve solvency and profitability. Not surprisingly, among the SSM's supervisory priorities for this year remains the requirement for institutions to persevere in implementing actively managed policies. On the side of cost reduction, it can be seen in the graphs how, over the last 10 years, the sector has significantly reduced its operational structure, Despite this, Spanish entities continue to have clearly higher levels of bank branches in relation to the euro area and other economies. Therefore, there would still be some potential for cost reduction in this way. On the contrary, if we look at the evolution of the number of employees per 100,000 inhabitants, we can see that Spanish banks would present the lowest levels among comparable European countries, and internationally would only be surpassed by Japan. This is a reflection of the high number of branches with few employees that our entities maintain, as a result of the dispersion of population. The risk of financial exclusion is a topical issue and, obviously, the closure of bank branches in small centers of dispersed population is seen as a worrying issue. However, I wanted to point out that a more widespread use of mobile banking and the internet and, in general, mobile applications will prevent this risk from materializing or mitigate its effects. As can be seen in the graph, according to OECD data we have enormous potential in this area. In any case, it should be noted that, in terms of cost efficiency, Spanish banks continue to be comparatively better than entities in neighbouring countries, particularly if we look at the results for large European economies, such as Germany, France, the United Kingdom or Italy. Future business model In any case, given the interest rate environment in which we find ourselves, as well as the emergence of new technologies and the emergence of new non-banking competitors (fintech and big tech), banks must necessarily evaluate and adapt their strategy and business model with a view to setting medium and long-term objectives that allow them to generate recurring results. The starting points of the entities are very different, so each one must find its own way. In fact, a recent thematic review carried out by the SSM on profitability and business models shows that there is no optimal business model in terms of profitability and solvency. According to this review, the most Profitableists maintain very different business models. Therefore, each entity must analyze its strengths as well as potential areas for improvement. Regardless of the path chosen, it is of the utmost importance that entities always apply an appropriate pricing policy at the product or service level. Those policies should be consistent, comprehensive and rigorous to ensure that the price charged for a product or service corresponds at least to its total cost, including the risk premium inherent in each type of transaction. From the supervisory point of view, it must be stressed that the search for profitable businesses cannot be carried out at the expense of rigour in the granting of credit. Historical experience has shown that the relaxation in concession practices ends up translating into notable increases in late payments in the future. As evidence of the importance of this issue, the SSM has included the revision of lending standards among its priorities for 2019. Impact of technology The impact of technology is a fundamental element to consider in the design of the future business model. I do not discover anything new when pointing out that the emergence of new competitors, agile and with little cost structure, poses a threat to the traditional banking business model, as can be manifested with the implementation of PSD2, but it is no less true that digitalization and technological innovation introduces new opportunities in terms of efficiency, accessibility and immediacy, new businesses and more dynamic ways of accessing customers. As I have pointed out before, Spanish banks have a relatively high number of branches and we have great potential for improvement in terms of access to banking services through the internet or mobile applications. Therefore, institutions should explore this path to continue gaining efficiency without losing customers, although in the short term it implies the need to undertake investments in systems. This is an adaptation challenge, which poses new risks, such as over-reliance on solutions provided by so-called big tech. Possibly, medium and small entities will have to evolve from defensive positions to others more prone to collaboration with fintechs. Reputation and conduct Another aspect to highlight in relation to the future business model refers to the necessary integration of the customer protection framework. The current concern about the risk of conduct is well known. As an illustration, the number of customer complaints to the services of entities has multiplied almost by 6 between 2014 and 2017. With regard to those received in the Bank of Spain, the figure has also increased considerably, many of them related to mortgage operations. It is often pointed out, not without reason, that entities have had inappropriate behavior with their customers in the past. However, because they are entirely fair, it should also be stressed that the rules on customer protection have changed significantly in the Recent years. As a result of these changes, what was appropriate in the past is no longer appropriate today. Traditionally, the regulation had focused on ensuring that the client received the appropriate information and that, at least formally, he stated that he understood and accepted the conditions that were going to apply to him. The financial crisis has led to more demanding legislation, regulations that require entities not only to inform, but to act honestly, impartially, transparently and professionally, taking into account the rights, interests and needs of their clients. A good reflection of this new philosophy is found in the recent real estate credit law. In my opinion, a very positive aspect of this new approach, which seeks to ensure the protection of customers, avoid conflicts of interest and promote real transparency in transactions, is precisely that it promotes legal certainty and significantly reduces the risks of future litigation. It should not be forgotten that litigation is one of the main costs that the sector has been bearing. In this sense, I believe that customer protection, far from being a disadvantage for the operation and profitability of institutions, is a central element of a viable and sustainable banking business model in the long term. On the other hand, the judicialization of claims implies a not inconsiderable increase in the workload and costs associated with the judicial system, in addition to ending up harming the clients themselves, since the need to cover future court costs inevitably makes credit more expensive. I must emphasize that the implementation of this new approach to customer relations implies a cultural change, which cannot prosper unless it has decisive support within the organization, starting with the involvement of the Board itself. Improvement of the solvency ratio With regard to the solvency ratio, we are at the tail end of the entire Eurozone. Regardless of the strengths and peculiarities that qualify and explain this objective data, it is undeniable that this situation puts pressure on our entities to improve their capital levels. In order to strengthen the solvency ratio, it is obvious that institutions can take measures that act on the numerator, increasing capital, or on the denominator, seeking to reduce or limit the growth of the APRs. Starting with the denominator, apart from the elimination of unprofitable business lines and the reduction of non-performing assets already mentioned, some entities have begun to explore the possibility of using internal models. While one of the main explanations for a higher density of APRs relates to the lower use of internal models, institutions should be aware that the level of demand on the supervisor is very high with regard to the use of such models. Proof of this has been the TRIM project (or 'Targeted Review of Internal Mode') which has involved the review, based on a methodology developed by the SSM, of the internal credit, market and counterparty models applied in the Eurozone. A fundamental aspect is that the use of models implies significant improvements in risk management, data quality, as well as in its governance framework. Of course, this process is not at all simple and it is not ruled out that for various credit segments capital consumption will rise instead of falling. On the numerator side of the ratio, the most obvious way of strengthening capital comes through the organic generation of reserves, which leads me again to highlight the importance of profitability and, related to the latter, the policy of capital remuneration. Shareholder remuneration policies must be adapted to the organic capital generation needs of each entity. In this regard, the variability of the average pay-out that has occurred during the last years is striking. As can be seen, this rose significantly in 2017 to reach 48% on average, although it returned to 41% last year. To a large extent, this variability of the pay-out is a consequence of the communication policy of the entities, which transfer dividend forecasts expressed in the form of money per share, rather than in terms of pay-out. It should be remembered that equities are not fixed income. Thus said it seems obvious, however, the reality is that on many occasions the forecasts communicated by the entities have generated a market expectation, excessively rigid, regarding the amount to be paid as a dividend. The variability of the result must translate into dividend variability. Obviously, there will always be expectations in the markets; However, we must not go so far as to treat such expectations as if they were quasi-contractual clauses. For example, there have been recent situations in which it was 'discounted' that entities were going to voluntarily replace certain issues with new ones, in which a higher interest rate would be paid. Of course, exercising the option to pay more for the same type of financing is completely irrational from an economic point of view. In this sense, it is spoken A lot of 'market discipline', but I think this discipline should be a two-way street. In my opinion, when it is economically rational, entities should 'disappoint expectations' in order to discipline the market. Mergers In the context of seeking profitability and strengthening solvency, it is almost inevitable that the issue of bank mergers will arise. As has been said repeatedly, our role as supervisors is not to decide which mergers are desirable and which are not, but to assess to what extent a merger process creates a more solvent entity, with a solid business model, allows structural costs to be significantly reduced and, ultimately, generates value as a whole. It is important to note that mergers are long and complex processes and, sometimes, lead to more problems than initially anticipated. In any case, banks continue to have a heavy cost structure, particularly compared to new banking competitors, which base their business almost exclusively on mobile banking. Therefore, in the current context of low interest rates and high competition, mergers appear as a clear alternative to improve profitability and gain efficiency. A much-discussed fact is that, at least for now, there have only been mergers at the national level. The absence of cross-border mergers is widely seen as a sign that the banking union is not working as it should. We must recognise that several elements of the banking union are still lacking, most notably the common Deposit Insurance Fund (EDIS), as well as a recapitalisation fund with real capacity to act in the event of significant banking crises; On the other hand, the regulation affecting the sector is still too heterogeneous between jurisdictions. In addition, certain European projects, such as the Capital Market Union, are still pending development. However, without dismissing or ignoring these reasons, which would partly justify this lack of European consolidation, it seems that the banking sector's own overcapacity would be acting as a barrier to entry for entities from other jurisdictions, given that the potential gain in costs and synergies can only be obtained if entities with duplication of networks and services are merged, This happens almost exclusively in the case of entities located in the same jurisdiction or those that have a business model that allows vertical savings. Governance I would like to conclude by referring to the importance of institutions having an adequate governance framework. Governance is an issue that has been on the agendas of international organizations for some time. Thus, the OECD issued the first principles of corporate governance in 1999. For its part, the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision adapted the OECD Principles in 99 and issued its own in 2006. Subsequently, it has updated them several times, the last of them in 2015. For its part, the SSM published recommendations on governance and risk appetite in June 2016. Governance does not usually grab headlines and probably does not occupy a prominent place among the challenges to be faced by the sector, which will be discussed today and tomorrow during this meeting, but it is a precondition for everything to work. Throughout my speech I spoke about the need to change the business model of institutions, to introduce new customer relationship policies, the possibility of using internal models to improve risk management and capital consumption, etc. None of these measures is likely to work properly without assured governance. Unfortunately, in Spain we have witnessed the impact that structural deficiencies in the legislative framework of governance of some entities can have not only for the entities themselves but for society as a whole. Therefore, beyond compliance with the various prudential ratios, I consider that establishing solid governance mechanisms in financial institutions is an essential necessary condition to guarantee their future soundness. As you know, this issue has gained prominence on the SSM agenda, which assesses various aspects of banks' internal governance. The outcome of these reviews is not limited to mere recommendations for improvement, but has a direct impact on the capital requirements arising from the supervisory review process. While considerable progress has been made in recent years, I would like to highlight two elements on which we need to continue to work: (i) the functioning of the boards; and (ii) implementation of risk appetite frameworks. There is room for improvement on boards in terms of independence, dedication and succession plans. Many entities have carried out self-assessment processes of the functioning of the council, and have taken action in this regard, but there is still some way to go. In particular, boards must act as real supervisory bodies, not only as formal approvers of decisions taken at lower levels, but as real supervisors of managers. For this, it is necessary that its composition includes people with a variety of profiles, who have experience and knowledge of the different technical issues subject to decision. Of course, the quality of data and risk information is essential in determining strategy and decision-making. Finally, the risk function must be adequately represented on the board and have weight in the entity's decision-making. In addition, the integration of the risk appetite framework into management should be improved. Conclusions I would like to conclude by acknowledging the efforts made by the entities in recent years. We are in a much better situation than five years ago in terms of solvency, profitability and asset quality in the sector. However, as the entities are well aware, there is no room for complacency. The search for profitability, the reduction of non-performing assets and the strengthening of solvency will continue to be the workhorses over the coming years. In an increasingly competitive environment, improvements in management and cost rationalisation remain key levers for improving solvency and profitability. In order to face these challenges, it will be key for entities to analyze their business in detail in order to enhance their strengths and correct those elements that may hinder their viability in the medium term. In this sense, a clear and ambitious response to technological changes, as well as a new customer relationship policy, must always be part of a viable and sustainable business model. Obviously, the implementation of profound changes in organizations is doomed to failure if there is no adequate governance framework. Paraphrasing the title of this meeting, I trust that entities and supervisors will make the necessary efforts today to be able to build the banking of tomorrow. Thanks a lot.
