Jansen (2018), Market insertion of youth: evidence from Madrid, mimeo. 7 P. Font, M. Izquierdo y S. Puente (2017), d2Subsidising mature age employment or throwing coins into a wishing well: a quasi-experimental analysisd3, Documentos Trabajo, n.a1 1740, Banco de Espa96a. This evidence, to which is added the need to face the aforementioned phenomena of globalization and digitalization, should lead, in my opinion, to a rethinking of the institutional design of the Spanish education system, as well as the learning system and the content of the educational curriculum itself, with the aim of modernizing it and providing students with tools such as the capacity for innovation. of reaction and entrepreneurship to face a more technological and changing environment. With regard to vocational training, it is essential to assess and adjust the system as the needs of the business world evolve. In this sense, the first studies that have examined Dual Vocational Training in Spain do not present conclusive results6, which highlights the difficulties of adapting a system that has worked in other countries, such as Germany or France, to the specific reality of our economy and our education system, especially with regard to the combination of general training and practical training. Therefore, it is important to carry out pilot programs to determine which design is the most appropriate in our case. Finally, in relation to the group of unemployed, it would be advisable to prioritise expenditure on training and guidance activities, and to reduce the impact on active employment policies of general recruitment subsidies that may have high efficiency losses d0 or deadweight7. In addition, an evaluation of the effectiveness of current training measures is essential to ensure that they effectively improve the chances of finding a job. Labor regulation In terms of labour regulation, the latest reform, adopted in 2012, increased the possibility for companies to adjust working conditions, particularly wages, in the presence of adverse disturbances. This reduced the real rigidity of wages and allowed for some differentiation of wages between firms. However, in the recovery, this differentiation between companies has not been maintained. In addition, hiring and firing patterns have hardly changed, in the sense that both new contracts and dismissals focus primarily on the group of workers on temporary contracts, regardless of their productivity. In practice, this means that fluctuations in employment are disproportionately concentrated among younger people, with potentially persistent effects, since, as I mentioned, accumulating experience during the first years of working life is key to productivity in the rest of working life. The reduction of the temporary employment ratio in Spain would require new regulatory measures that would increase the attractiveness of permanent contracts for companies, while ensuring the necessary flexibility to adjust labour costs in the face of negative shocks and thus avoid excessive job destruction in recessionary phases. Finally, there are different policies that aim to directly increase the incomes of workers with fewer resources, such as, for example, the increase in the minimum interprofessional wage or wage supplements. The effectiveness of any of these measures depends, on the one hand, on the fact that they do not have a disproportionate fiscal impact and, on the other, on the fact that they do not end up reducing the ability of the affected groups to accumulate experience because they hinder their employability. Housing policies The limited income-generating capacity of young people, described above, is aggravated by the recent tightening of conditions for access to the housing market. This is particularly the case for the rental market in large cities, where cumulative price growth since 2014 has been close to 40%, in a context where the proportion of young people8 living in rental has increased significantly, from 30% in 2007 to over 50% in 2017. 8 Emancipated households with a head of household under 30 years of age. These recent developments in the housing market and job instability have contributed to the fact that the age of emancipation of young people has not decreased over the past five years, despite the economic recovery. In this context, it is important that the Public Administration promotes access to housing. In particular, priority should be given to those public policies aimed at promoting the supply of rental housing. Intergenerational equity and the demographic challenge Let me end this speech by taking a few minutes to the demographic challenge, because how this challenge is met will have important intergenerational consequences. The phenomenon is well known. Socioeconomic and health advances have allowed life expectancy in Spain to increase continuously and has exceeded 83 years of age in 2017, when 40 years ago this figure stood at 74 years. This increase in life expectancy, which is expected to continue in the future, together with the low birth rates observed, will generate a very substantial increase in the dependency ratio9, which, even in the most optimistic demographic projections, will reach 50% in our country by the middle of this century, that is, double the current rate. 9 Measured as the proportion of people over 65 in relation to the working-age population. 10See Chapter 4 of the Bank of Spain's 2018 Annual Report, "Economic consequences of demographic changes". It is foreseeable that this demographic scenario will have profound macroeconomic consequences, affect consumption and savings patterns, and even generate a negative effect on the evolution of productivity and, therefore, on the growth potential of our economy10. But, above all, population ageing will have d0 is already having d0 a significant impact on public finances. In the particular case of the pension system, it will tend to be subject to particular pressure, to the extent that the number of pension recipients increases more intensely than that of contributors, which will force the approval of far-reaching reforms to guarantee its sustainability. These reforms should, in my opinion, take hold. on two fundamental pillars: the financial and social sustainability of the system, on the one hand, and its contributiveness, predictability and transparency, on the other. The reform of the public pension system must also achieve an equitable distribution of its costs and benefits between current and future generations. Indeed, reforms of the public pension system generally have distributional implications among different individuals, depending on how they are designed and implemented. In particular, the way in which changes in the pension system are graduated over time has implications for the distribution of the cost of reform across generations. In this sense, delaying the necessary reforms of the public pension system could contribute to this distribution having to be done in a less equitable manner and at the cost of greater uncertainty, which harms the savings and labor supply decisions of current generations. I would like to conclude these reflections by stressing the importance of young people taking an active part in the debate on the economic reforms that the country needs. And you, by your formation, are specially qualified for it. In fact, one of the main personal challenges you are facing from this very moment is, precisely, to discover how to better channel your talent and knowledge to contribute the maximum to those around you. Some of us decide to do it with a direct vocation of public service, others will do it as entrepreneurs, as professionals, in academia ..., or in other ways that may not even have been conceived yet and that you will create. We trust in you, in your talent, effort, knowledge and good work. So much so as to predict that in another 26 years one of you will illustrate, in an act very similar to this, another generation of graduates about all that Spanish society will have done to offer a future of prosperity and opportunities to the young people of tomorrow. You are already the present. Thanks a lot.
text_original: 14.06.2019 La juventud en Espaa: retos y oportunidades Cierre del ao acadmico en CUNEF Pablo Hernndez de Cos Gobernador Excelentsimo rector magnfico, seor presidente de la Asociacin Espaola de Banca, seor presidente y directora general de CUNEF, claustro de profesores, estimados alumnos, seoras y seores, quiero comenzar mostrando mi agradecimiento a CUNEF por la invitacin a participar en este acto de cierre del ao acadmico, que me brinda la posibilidad de felicitar a los jvenes que hoy se gradan, particularmente a aquellos que van a recibir un reconocimiento a su esfuerzo y desempeo acadmico. Para m, este acto tiene un importante componente emocional: me trae a la memoria mi propia graduacin en CUNEF, hace ya 26 aos. Muchas cosas han cambiado desde entonces; otras, como la liturgia de los actos acadmicos, afortunadamente, no tanto. Una nueva promocin de jvenes acaba de completar sus estudios universitarios y se dispone a empezar su carrera laboral. Esta transicin est sujeta a retos importantes, en parte derivados de las tendencias sociales y econmicas que se han ido observando en las ltimas dcadas, y en parte como consecuencia de una crisis econmica profunda, que a su vez ha provocado cambios que han afectado especialmente a los jvenes. El entorno de referencia relevante para estos estudiantes que hoy se gradan es global, no solo porque es probable que algunos de ellos busquen fuera de Espaa su primera o posteriores experiencias profesionales, sino porque el fenmeno de globalizacin que ha caracterizado la economa mundial en estas ltimas dcadas genera una interdependencia muy estrecha entre las distintas economas. Y Espaa, evidentemente, no ha sido ajena a este fenmeno, como muestra el hecho de que el grado de apertura de la economa al exterior, medido a travs del peso de las exportaciones y las importaciones sobre el PIB, se ha incrementado en casi 40 puntos porcentuales en todo el perodo democrtico. Pues bien, este entorno global se ha tornado ahora ms complejo e incierto como consecuencia de diversos factores, entre los que destacan, como elementos novedosos recientes, los conflictos comerciales o la debilidad de algunas economas emergentes, en particular por su tamao la de China. Las tensiones comerciales ponen, de hecho, en cuestin algunos de los pilares sobre los que se ha asentado el desarrollo econmico mundial de las ltimas dcadas: la integracin econmica y el multilateralismo. Este entorno ms incierto se ha hecho sentir especialmente en la economa del rea del euro, nuestro principal socio comercial y financiero, como consecuencia de su elevado grado de apertura exterior y de diversas perturbaciones negativas, que han sido particularmente intensas en algunos pases, como Italia y Alemania. Tambin ha puesto de manifiesto algunas de las debilidades estructurales de los pases europeos, como los elevados niveles de endeudamiento de algunos pases, la fragilidad de determinadas entidades bancarias, las perspectivas demogrficas y los bajos niveles de productividad. La economa espaola est mostrando un elevado grado de resistencia a este entorno adverso. Una resistencia que se asienta en la correccin de algunos de nuestros desequilibrios previos, como el desendeudamiento del sector privado y la mejora de la competitividad. Sin embargo, no debemos olvidar que nuestra economa mantiene importantes retos y vulnerabilidades, que exigen ser afrontados si se quiere favorecer un crecimiento sostenible y equilibrado. Algunos son consecuencia de la profundidad de la ltima crisis, como el elevado endeudamiento pblico, y otros son el resultado de transformaciones econmicas y sociales, como el fenmeno del envejecimiento poblacional. Pero tambin podemos identificar un grupo de retos que son reflejo de problemas estructurales que han estado presentes a lo largo de las ltimas dcadas y que no hemos sabido afrontar, entre los que destacan la alta tasa de paro y la reducida dinmica de la productividad de nuestra economa. En este contexto, me gustara aprovechar la ocasin para hacer balance de la situacin de nuestros jvenes en relacin con el mundo laboral y analizar el papel que algunas polticas econmicas pueden desempear en la mejora de sus perspectivas profesionales y vitales. Juventud y mercado de trabajo Cmo se enfrenta esta nueva generacin de jvenes al mercado de trabajo? Como bien sabemos, la crisis econmica gener un fuerte incremento del desempleo en nuestro pas, que fue particularmente elevado en el caso de los jvenes: en el colectivo de entre 16 y 24 aos lleg a alcanzar el 56 % en 2013. La recuperacin econmica ha permitido reducir esta tasa hasta el 33,5 % en el cuarto trimestre de 2018; en cualquier caso, todava lejos del nivel anterior a la crisis, cercano al 20 %, y del observado en la media de los pases del rea del euro (16,3 %). Como respuesta a estas dificultades laborales, se produjo una reduccin de la tasa de participacin de estos jvenes en el mercado laboral e incluso un ligero aumento de las salidas anuales de jvenes al extranjero, que llegaron a alcanzar las 10.000 personas, para un total de 6 millones de jvenes de entre 16 y 30 aos. En la actualidad, la tasa de participacin se sita en el 53,2 %, cuando a comienzos de la crisis estaba ligeramente por debajo del 70 %. La mayora de estos jvenes se dedicaron a formarse. De este modo, la proporcin de jvenes que ni estudian ni trabajan, que experiment un acusado ascenso al principio de la crisis, hasta alcanzar el 25 %, ha venido registrando descensos desde 2013, de forma que ya se ha alcanzado un nivel similar al de antes de la crisis, en el 15 % de la poblacin menor de 30 aos. Esta reduccin ha venido causada, principalmente, por un descenso general del desempleo, as como por un incremento de la proporcin de jvenes inactivos que estn embarcados en actividades de formacin. Por otro lado, las condiciones laborales de los jvenes espaoles que han conseguido encontrar trabajo son, en la actualidad, ms precarias que en los pases de nuestro entorno. En particular, la ratio de temporalidad de los jvenes de entre 16 y 24 aos se sita en el 70 %, frente al 52,6 % del rea del euro. En este contexto, resulta interesante comparar las condiciones laborales de los jvenes actuales con las de las generaciones anteriores. De esta comparacin se puede deducir que, antes de la crisis, cada nueva generacin alcanz, de media, ingresos laborales anuales superiores a los de la previa. Esto se debi tanto a la mejora educativa como al incremento de los ingresos laborales de los colectivos con menor nivel de estudios. Adems, en cada generacin se produca un aumento continuo del salario por hora a medida que los trabajadores acumulaban experiencia laboral y, con la misma edad y formacin, se observaba una relativa estabilidad en el salario por hora entre diferentes cohortes. Con la crisis, el colectivo de jvenes menos formados fue el que sufri una mayor cada en sus ingresos anuales totales. Adems, los salarios reales por hora de cada nueva generacin redujeron su ritmo de avance con la acumulacin de experiencia, e incluso llegaron a caer ligeramente para aquellos trabajadores con ms ingresos. Las razones que explican este deterioro de la situacin laboral de los jvenes durante la crisis son mltiples, entre otros los derivados de algunos problemas de la regulacin laboral espaola, que provocaban que, ante las crisis econmicas, las empresas utilizaran el empleo y, en particular, el de carcter temporal (que afecta principalmente al colectivo de jvenes y, en especial, a los de menor formacin) como mecanismo de ajuste. En la actual expansin, estas generaciones estn viendo que sus ingresos laborales van recuperando los niveles que se observaban con anterioridad a la crisis. Esta recuperacin est siendo, no obstante, lenta por diferentes motivos. En primer lugar, de acuerdo con la evidencia disponible, las situaciones de desempleo al inicio de la carrera laboral pueden generar efectos bastante persistentes, lastrar, por ejemplo, la productividad del trabajador a lo largo de toda su carrera laboral y dificultar, por tanto, la recuperacin de sus rentas, frente a generaciones anteriores que no sufrieron esas situaciones tempranas de desempleo1. 1 L. Jacobson, R. LaLonde y D. Sullivan (1993), Earnings losses of displaced workers, American Economic Review, 83(4), pp. 685-709. En segundo lugar, el desajuste entre las habilidades de las personas desempleadas y aquellas que demanda el mercado aument notablemente con la crisis y se mantiene muy elevado a pesar de la recuperacin. Asimismo, la incidencia del desempleo de larga duracin, que dificulta la empleabilidad como consecuencia de la prdida asociada de capital humano, se mantiene elevada y se concentra en los colectivos con los niveles educativos ms bajos. En tercer lugar, como sealaba, los jvenes, especialmente los menos formados, presentan una tasa de temporalidad muy elevada, lo que dificulta la acumulacin de capital humano en el trabajo durante los primeros aos de carrera laboral, que depende, crucialmente, de la estabilidad de la relacin laboral. La reduccin de la duracin de los contratos temporales que se ha producido en los ltimos aos estara agravando este problema. Finalmente, se observa asimismo una tendencia creciente de los trabajos a tiempo parcial, generalizada para todos los grupos de edad y niveles de educacin, que tambin estara afectando a los jvenes. Algunas de estas tendencias podran tener, adems, un cierto componente estructural. En concreto, los cambios en la demanda de trabajo, que parecen perjudicar, sobre todo, a trabajadores de formacin media y baja, reflejan al menos en parte el impacto de la globalizacin, la digitalizacin, la robotizacin e incluso el envejecimiento de la poblacin2. En el mismo sentido, no es descartable que algunos de estos factores hayan permitido que las empresas necesiten en menor medida establecer relaciones estables con determinados trabajadores, lo que ha favorecido la reduccin de la duracin de los contratos y el incremento de la parcialidad. 2 Vanse, por ejemplo, D. Acemoglu y D. Autor (2011), Skills, tasks and technologies: Implications for employment and earnings, Handbook of Labor Economics, n. 4, pp. 1043-1171; R. Feenstra y H. Gordon (1999), The impact of outsourcing and high-technology capital on wages: estimates for the United States, 1979-1990, The Quarterly Journal of Economics, 114(3), pp. 907-940, y D. Comin, A. Danieli y M. Mestieri, Demand-driven labour market polarization, mimeo. 3 J. Hall y A. Krueger (2016), An Analysis of the Labor Market for Uber's Driver-Partners in the United States, NBER Working Papers, n. 22843. Por otro lado, las nuevas posibilidades tecnolgicas y la actividad en plataformas colaborativas tambin pueden haber modificado las decisiones de participacin en el mercado laboral de determinados colectivos, especialmente el de los jvenes, lo que habra incentivado su participacin laboral, que anteriormente se podra haber visto limitada por unos esquemas tradicionales ms rgidos en trminos de horarios y calendarios3. En resumen, podemos concluir que los jvenes que ahora se incorporan al mercado laboral, a pesar de pertenecer a una generacin especialmente formada, se enfrentan a algunos retos ms exigentes que los que encararon las generaciones pasadas. Concretamente, los jvenes de hoy tienen que enfrentarse al desafo que supone haberse incorporado al mercado laboral tras la crisis financiera, lo que ha dificultado su capacidad de adquirir experiencia en los primeros aos de carrera profesional, especialmente en el caso de los trabajadores con menor grado de formacin, y verse comparativamente ms afectados por la temporalidad y la parcialidad. El papel de las polticas econmicas Dada esta evidencia, resulta crucial identificar qu polticas econmicas pueden resultar ms efectivas para mejorar la situacin laboral de nuestros jvenes. Formacin y sistema educativo Una de las primeras cuestiones que se han de abordar es la relativa al sistema educativo. Es cierto que la generacin actual es la que ha alcanzado un mayor nivel educativo medio, en comparacin con las anteriores cohortes. Por ejemplo, el porcentaje de la poblacin joven con estudios superiores o medios es hoy del 89 %, frente al 20 % del inicio del perodo democrtico. Sin embargo, a pesar de la convergencia del capital humano hacia el promedio de la Unin Europea, todava estamos lejos de alcanzar los niveles educativos medios de los que disfrutan los pases de nuestro entorno. Adems, tenemos evidencia de que nuestro sistema educativo tiene deficiencias. En este sentido, uno de los retos ms importantes del sistema educativo espaol sigue siendo acabar con el elevado abandono escolar, que afecta al 18,3 % de los alumnos de entre 18 y 24 aos. Asimismo, nuestros estudiantes, incluidos aquellos que poseen un ttulo universitario, presentan resultados comparativamente bajos en los exmenes estandarizados a escala internacional4. La evidencia disponible muestra que estos resultados tienen que ver no solo con los conocimientos relativos de los estudiantes, sino tambin con sus habilidades no cognitivas (como el deseo de innovar, el autocontrol o la capacidad de concentracin)5. 4 Ministerio de Educacin, PIAAC: Programa Internacional para la Evaluacin de las competencias de la poblacin adulta. 2013. Informe espaol. Anlisis inicial, vol. I. 5 Vase G. Zamarro, C. Hitt e I. Mndez (206), When Students Don't Care: Reexamining International Differences in Achievement and Non-Cognitive Skills, EDRE Working Papers, n. 2016-18. 6 Vase S. Bentolila, A. Cabrales y M. Jansen (2018), Market insertion of youth: evidence from Madrid, mimeo. 7 P. Font, M. Izquierdo y S. Puente (2017), Subsidising mature age employment or throwing coins into a wishing well: a quasi-experimental analysis, Documentos Trabajo, n. 1740, Banco de Espaa. Esta evidencia, a la que se une la necesidad de afrontar los fenmenos mencionados de la globalizacin y de la digitalizacin, debera llevar, en mi opinin, a un replanteamiento del diseo institucional del sistema educativo espaol, as como del sistema de aprendizaje y del propio contenido del currculum educativo, con el objetivo de modernizarlo y de dotar a los estudiantes de herramientas como la capacidad de innovacin, de reaccin y de emprendimiento para enfrentarse a un entorno ms tecnolgico y cambiante. Respecto a la formacin profesional, resulta esencial evaluar y ajustar el sistema a medida que evolucionan las necesidades del mundo empresarial. En este sentido, los primeros estudios que han examinado la Formacin Profesional Dual en Espaa no presentan resultados concluyentes6, lo que subraya las dificultades de adaptar un sistema que ha funcionado en otros pases, como Alemania o Francia, a la realidad especfica de nuestra economa y de nuestro sistema educativo, especialmente en lo relativo a la combinacin de formacin general y formacin prctica. Por ello, es importante realizar programas piloto que permitan determinar qu diseo es el ms adecuado en nuestro caso. Finalmente, en relacin con el colectivo de desempleados, sera conveniente priorizar el gasto en actividades de formacin y de orientacin, y reducir la incidencia en las polticas activas de empleo de las subvenciones generales de contratacin que pueden tener unas prdidas de eficiencia o peso muerto elevadas7. Adems, resulta fundamental una evaluacin de la eficacia de las medidas formativas actuales para asegurar que estas permiten mejorar de manera efectiva las posibilidades de encontrar un empleo. La regulacin laboral En cuanto a la regulacin laboral, la ltima reforma, aprobada en 2012, aument la posibilidad de que las empresas ajustaran las condiciones laborales, en particular las salariales, en presencia de perturbaciones adversas. Esto redujo la rigidez real de los salarios y permiti una cierta diferenciacin de salarios entre empresas. Sin embargo, en la recuperacin, esta diferenciacin entre empresas no se ha mantenido. Adems, los patrones de contratacin y de despido apenas se han modificado, en el sentido de que tanto los nuevos contratos como los despidos se centran fundamentalmente en el colectivo de trabajadores con contratos temporales, independientemente de su productividad. En la prctica, esto implica que las fluctuaciones del empleo se concentren de una forma desproporcionadamente elevada entre los ms jvenes, con efectos potencialmente persistentes, en la medida en que, como he mencionado, acumular experiencia durante los primeros aos de la vida laboral es clave para la productividad en el resto de la vida profesional. La reduccin de la ratio de temporalidad en Espaa requerira nuevas medidas regulatorias que incrementaran el atractivo de la contratacin indefinida para las empresas, a la vez que aseguraran la flexibilidad necesaria para ajustar los costes laborales ante perturbaciones negativas y evitaran as una excesiva destruccin de empleo en las fases recesivas. Finalmente, existen diferentes polticas que tienen por objetivo incrementar directamente las rentas de los trabajadores con menores recursos, como, por ejemplo, la subida del salario mnimo interprofesional o los complementos salariales. La eficacia de cualquiera de estas medidas depende, por una parte, de que no tengan un impacto fiscal desproporcionado y, por otra, de que no acaben mermando la capacidad de acumular experiencia de los colectivos afectados porque dificulten su empleabilidad. Las polticas de vivienda La limitada capacidad de generar ingresos por parte de los jvenes, ya descrita, se agrava a raz del endurecimiento reciente que han experimentado las condiciones de acceso al mercado de la vivienda. Este es el caso, en particular, del mercado del alquiler en las grandes ciudades, donde los crecimientos de precios acumulados desde 2014 han sido cercanos al 40 %, en un contexto en el que la proporcin de jvenes8 que viven en rgimen de alquiler ha aumentado significativamente, desde el 30 % registrado en 2007 hasta situarse por encima del 50 % en 2017. 8 Hogares emancipados con un cabeza de familia menor de 30 aos. Esta evolucin reciente del mercado de la vivienda y la inestabilidad laboral han contribuido a que durante los ltimos cinco aos no haya disminuido la edad de emancipacin de los jvenes, a pesar de la recuperacin econmica. En este contexto, es importante que la Administracin Pblica promueva el acceso a la vivienda. En particular, se debe dar prioridad a aquellas polticas pblicas dirigidas a favorecer la oferta de vivienda de alquiler. La equidad intergeneracional y el reto demogrfico Permtanme que acabe esta intervencin dedicando unos minutos al reto demogrfico, dado que la manera en que se afronte este reto tendr importantes consecuencias intergeneracionales. El fenmeno es de sobra conocido. Los avances socioeconmicos y sanitarios han permitido que la esperanza de vida en Espaa se haya incrementado de manera continuada y haya superado los 83 aos de edad en 2017, cuando hace 40 aos esta cifra se situaba en 74 aos. Este incremento de la esperanza de vida, que se espera que contine en el futuro, junto con las bajas tasas de natalidad observadas, generar un incremento muy sustancial de la tasa de dependencia9, que, incluso en las proyecciones demogrficas ms optimistas, alcanzar en nuestro pas el 50 % a mediados del presente siglo, esto es, el doble de la tasa actual. 9 Medida como la proporcin de mayores de 65 aos en relacin con la poblacin en edad de trabajar. 10Vase el captulo 4 del Informe Anual 2018 del Banco de Espaa, Consecuencias econmicas de los cambios demogrficos. Es previsible que este escenario demogrfico tenga profundas consecuencias macroeconmicas, afecte a las pautas de consumo y de ahorro, e incluso genere un efecto negativo sobre la evolucin de la productividad y, por tanto, sobre el potencial de crecimiento de nuestra economa10. Pero, sobre todo, el envejecimiento poblacional tendr est teniendo ya un impacto significativo sobre las finanzas pblicas. En el caso particular del sistema de pensiones, este tender a verse sometido a una particular presin, en la medida en que el nmero de perceptores de pensiones se incremente ms intensamente que el de cotizantes, lo que obligar a aprobar reformas de calado para garantizar su sostenibilidad. Estas reformas deberan asentarse, en mi opinin, sobre dos pilares fundamentales: la sostenibilidad financiera y social del sistema, por un lado, y la contributividad, la predictibilidad y la transparencia de este, por otro. La reforma del sistema pblico de pensiones debe lograr, adems, una distribucin equitativa de sus costes y beneficios entre las generaciones actuales y las futuras. En efecto, las reformas del sistema pblico de pensiones tienen, por lo general, implicaciones distributivas entre distintos individuos, en funcin de cmo se diseen y se implementen. En particular, la manera en la que se graden en el tiempo los cambios en el sistema de pensiones tiene consecuencias para la distribucin del coste de la reforma entre distintas generaciones. En este sentido, retrasar las necesarias reformas del sistema pblico de pensiones podra contribuir a que dicha distribucin tenga que hacerse de manera menos equitativa y con el coste de una mayor incertidumbre, lo que perjudica las decisiones de ahorro y de oferta de trabajo de las generaciones actuales. Quisiera terminar estas reflexiones resaltando la importancia de que los jvenes tomis parte activa en el debate sobre las reformas econmicas que necesita el pas. Y vosotros, por vuestra formacin, estis especialmente capacitados para ello. De hecho, uno de los principales retos personales al que os estis enfrentando desde este mismo momento es, precisamente, el de descubrir cmo canalizar mejor vuestro talento y conocimientos para aportar lo mximo a quienes os rodean. Algunos decidimos hacerlo con una vocacin directa de servicio pblico, otros lo haris como emprendedores, como profesionales, en la academia, o de otras maneras que a lo mejor ni siquiera se han concebido todava y que vosotros crearis. Confiamos en vosotros, en vuestro talento, esfuerzo, conocimientos y buen hacer. Tanto como para augurar que dentro de otros 26 aos alguno de vosotros ilustrar, en un acto muy parecido a este, a otra generacin de graduados sobre todo lo que la sociedad espaola habr hecho por ofrecer un futuro de prosperidad y de oportunidades a los jvenes del maana. Vosotros ya sois el presente. Muchas gracias.

Title: Opening speech at the II Banking Forum "The banking sector facing the challenge of digitalization", organized by El Economista
text: 18.09.2019 The banking sector in a new context: calibrating the challenge of digitalization II Banking Forum "The banking sector facing the challenge of digitalization"/ El Economista Margarita Delgado Subgobernadora Good morning. First of all, I would like to thank El Economista for its invitation to open this II Banking Forum, which will address the challenge of digitalization. Sometimes digitalization is spoken of as a future challenge, which must be undertaken to improve efficiency and provide a better service to customers, but, while it is true that the future seems to be digital, it should not be forgotten that it is a central element of our present. Digitalization: a continuous challenge for banking Digitalization is already here, it is a fundamental part of the environment in which the financial sector operates. Increasingly widespread access to the online world, particularly through smartphones, is having a major impact on our environment and the way we do things. It is surprising how the mobile has become a key tool for many of our daily activities and it is difficult to deny that, despite its drawbacks, having a mini computer permanently connected to the internet in our pocket, facilitates our day to day. In fact, you only have to look at how quickly they have become widespread. According to the figures of 2018, 59% of Europeans, and 72% of Spaniards, have a smartphone. In the case of Spain, this represents almost 100% of people who have a mobile phone. That is, in just over 10 years since its launch, smartphones have managed to almost completely replace previous terminals. Users want to make their financial transactions with their mobile, anytime, anywhere, quickly and easily. That is, with the same user experience which they enjoy in other areas. This explains the growing use of banking apps. According to a survey conducted by MasterCard, almost three out of four Spaniards use mobile banking. On the other hand, some bank users seem willing to adopt the services of non-banking companies if they offer them a solution more adapted to their needs. In this sense, it seems very relevant to me that, according to various studies, around 10% of Spanish users of banking apps are also users of fintech apps. It would be a not inconsiderable percentage and much higher than that of other countries in our environment, such as Italy, France or Germany. Of course, this does not mean that all users have switched to operating with their bank through digital channels. The advance of new technologies should not make us forget that there is still a significant part of the population that, for various reasons, prefers to resort to traditional channels to communicate with their entity. Thus, one of the studies to which I referred earlier reveals that 20% of Spaniards do not usually use online banking to manage their finances. This segment of customers depends to a large extent on the necessary service provided by traditional banking. In any case, the increase in competition resulting from the entry of non-bank actors is one of the most distinctive features of the new environment. With digitalization, the barriers to entry into the financial services market have decreased significantly, giving entry to new companies, not only domestic, but also foreign. According to the figures compiled by Finnovating, the number of fintech startups offering their services in Spain amounted to 358 last July. Normally, these new players do not try to offer a complete catalog of financial services, but usually take advantage of the possibilities offered by new technologies to direct their services towards very specific niches. This often results in a disaggregation of the value chain. In other words: we have gone from a situation in which many users interacted, almost exclusively, with a single financial institution, to a context in which, for example, a user can have an account in an entity, order their payments through the interface provided by another provider and use the payment instrument provided by a third party. Potentially, this situation could lead some banks to lose contact with customers, being relegated to performing typical back-office tasks. I am not going to analyze all the consequences that would derive from this, but I would like to dwell on one of them, which seems to me especially relevant since it compromises one of the competitive advantages that characterize financial institutions. Of course, I am talking about customer data, which is the raw material on which the so-called Fourth Industrial Revolution rests. It can be said that financial institutions are in a good starting position, having accumulated over the years a large amount of information about their customers, but obviously they need to maintain this access to data, for which it is necessary to preserve high standards of compliance with the rules and best practices of privacy and information management. Naturally, it is not only a question of having the information but also of being able to process it in order to be able to offer quality services to its clientele and compete on an equal footing with the new players, in particular, with bigtech, which I will talk about later. I am aware that it is not an easy task. It requires changes at many levels: remodeling the computer architecture, establishing efficient governance in data management, having access to or being able to develop the necessary analytical tools or incorporating experts in the field, among many others. All this in a context of tightening margins and high competition, in which cost control and the correct discrimination of transactions by risk and price are essential to remain competitive. The challenge is further complicated if we take into account that the current environment is characterized by the multiplicity of technologies that are emerging, or re-emerging: big data, artificial intelligence, distributed ledgers, cryptography, biometrics... There is no doubt that keeping up to date with all the news is a great challenge, both for the variety and for the speed with which they happen. Banks are making significant progress in adapting to this new environment. Proof of this are the empowerment of digital channels or the new solutions that we are seeing in recent times. They are also making investments internally in order to redesign their computer systems, deepen their knowledge of new technologies and make structural changes towards a more transversal and customer-centric organization. But these changes are profound and take time, so despite the efforts made so far, there is still a long way to go. According to the Funcas Financial Information Barometer, 72% of managers approve of their entity in terms of digitalization, but the most repeated score is a modest 6 out of 10, with the average standing at 5.55. The to-do list is long but can be summarized in three key issues: capitalizing on strengths, changing mindsets and betting on cooperation. Regarding the first, we must not forget that the entities have the trust of customers, providing service in Spain to practically the entire population. I have already pointed out that institutions must have extensive and comprehensive databases, although they must be able to exploit that information adequately to capitalize on this strength. With regard to the second issue, the change of mentality, it is clear that a market in continuous movement, such as the current one, requires a change in the way we work towards greater flexibility, creativity and dynamism. The culture of each entity should also reflect these changes. In relation to the third question, I have no doubt that the spirit of cooperation, both between banks and with fintech companies, is key to being able to face these challenges. It has moved from defensive positions to ones more prone to collaboration through different channels, such as acceleration programs for fintech companies (also known as "innovation accelerators") or investment in specialized venture capital funds. The Observatory of Innovation and Fintech Trends 2018 estimated around 75% the number of fintech companies that maintain an active collaboration with banks. We must not forget, in addition, that in order to compete in the new environment it is not only necessary to adapt, but to do so quickly. We are all aware of the increasing speed at which technological change is occurring. The growing importance of bigtech As I mentioned a moment ago, one of the biggest challenges that digitalization poses for the financial sector is the greater competitive pressure and, in particular, the greater transformative role that companies such as Google or Amazon could play; That is: the so-called bigtech. Although, unlike other branches of activity, the area in question has not been as exposed as others to this disruption, the signs that seem to announce an imminent structural change are beginning to accumulate. The most striking sign would be the recent announcement of "Libra", Facebook's cryptocurrency to which I will dedicate the last part of my speech. However, this is not an isolated case. In recent years, the number of areas that register remarkable activity by digital giants has been increasing, and has done so unquestionably. Indeed, the top ten technology companies now have more than 50 classes of financial services in their portfolio, to which should be added an increasing number of alliances and collaboration agreements with countless entities around the world. Thus, a complex and often opaque ecosystem of interrelationships is taking shape for the authorities, whose potential implications for financial stability, competition or consumer protection seem profound. In this sense, what differentiates bigtech from other emerging competitors are, fundamentally, three major keys: (a) the transversality of its operations, (b) the geographical breadth of its scope and, (c) its proven ability to increase its scale very quickly. These characteristics allow us to equate some of the bigtech, in their capacity as potential providers of financial services, to the figure of banks of global systemic importance, making evident the need to design a strategic and regulatory response capable of rising to the occasion. China is a paradigmatic case of what I have just said. In just four years, the share of non-bank agents in the retail payments market has risen from 59% to 76%; A situation that has motivated the adoption of the first specific regulatory measures. It is clear that the globality of these issues makes it impossible to address them unilaterally. In this sense, Banco de Espa96a has been collaborating closely with other authorities within international organizations such as the FSB or the BIS, to give two outstanding examples. These efforts reflect our growing concern about the phenomenon. One of our biggest concerns has to do with the lack of competition and the level of concentration that could result from a greater presence of bigtech. In principle, the emergence of bigtech is associated with greater market dynamism, which would facilitate access, innovation and reduce friction points. However, the strong economies of network, scale, scope and learning that characterize these ecosystems imply an uncertain future. Specifically, scenarios can be imagined in the that the consolidation of the dominant position of bigtech in financial services threatens the possibility of effective rivalry. Regardless of the implications that this fact could have for competition policy, as a financial authority our main concern should focus on ensuring that the transformation that occurs in the provision of financial services maintains adequate levels of stability, security and customer protection, while allowing the incorporation of the efficiency gains provided by new technologies. For this, it is important to have rules of the game that guarantee a balanced competitive environment, always complying with the principle of neutrality, so that similar risks derived from similar activities are subject to the same rules, regardless of the supplier. Logically, this challenge is not easy in a context of the emergence of new agents and new types of interdependencies and interrelationships that can create systemic vulnerabilities. Think, for example, of the level of exposure generated by the outsourcing of certain advanced technological resources, such as cloud computing services or certain analytical capabilities. Imagine the problems that could cause its total or partial unavailability. It is, in this sense, essential to move forward in a framework that equates these modern dependency formulas to more traditional outsourcing in terms of transparency, audit rights and control by regulators or portability options; A path that we have already begun to travel. Another example is the financial links that may arise between traditional intermediaries and new entrants. Again, the case of China is very illustrative, while the financing of banks has begun to depend increasingly on the funds they receive from large technology platforms that, in turn, distribute savings products among retail investors, competing with the supply of bank deposits. Additionally, as intermediaries, bigtech companies seek to take advantage of the synergies between financial services and business generation without having to bear the associated risks. In practice, this implies the generalization of formulas that guarantee its transfer, such as portfolio securitisations, or loan syndications, giving rise to the consolidation of new "originate to distribute" models where the volume could prevail and not necessarily the quality of the underlying asset. It should be remembered that, without adequate supervision, this type of business model, in which 'intermediaries' do not assume any responsibility for the successful completion of transactions, can entail systemic risks, as we had the misfortune to see with the outbreak of the financial crisis. To finish with this chapter of risks, and without wishing to be exhaustive, let me dwell, for a moment, on the controversial aspect of the data. As you know, bigtech companies are characterized by being information-intensive companies that bet, openly, on the accumulation of records in order to build value on them. The incorporation of elements of a financial nature does not constitute a minor contribution since it reveals key facets of the behavior of individuals that allow improving both the quality of the analysis and the effectiveness of the commercial action. Although still in its infancy, the use of this type of information by combining alternative statistical techniques to those traditionally used can alter the way in which certain financial services, such as the granting of credit, are provided. Potentially, the accumulation of this information in a few technological platforms can place them in a situation of competitive advantage in the provision of a wide range of services, including financial ones. In this regard, it could be asked whether, as has happened with banking and transaction data, payment, the possibility that, with the consent, other companies can access this information should also be regulated in order to balance the initial situation. I would not want to close this section without first making sure that my words are interpreted correctly. The authorities are aware of the benefits that bigtech could bring in terms of modernization and development of the financial system. However, there are concerns arising from the entry of these agents into the financial space, to which the authorities should respond. It is, therefore, a complex path that cannot be covered by traditional formulas and strictly national approaches but, as the BIS has pointed out, requires a new approach to design and implement public policies. The proposed measures must be tailored to the objectives pursued, the approach must be proportionate and particular attention will have to be paid to the transnational dimension of the necessary actions, with the enormous practical complexities that this entails. Libra: a new global currency? In this journey, from the most general to the particular, I would like, finally, to share with you some reflections about the Libra project. Both in terms of its concept and its theoretical design, Libra raises many and very diverse questions; all of them interesting. Are we facing a means of payment? Is it rather a financial instrument? Or, as the authority of the Swiss financial markets, FINMA1, should we assimilate it to a financial market infrastructure? 1 See / Truth be told, the answers are currently unclear. From the details that have been released, we know that Libra presents important differences with respect to, for example, Bitcoin. On the one hand, it is expected to have a single known issuer: the Libra Association, based in Switzerland, and in which Facebook will participate along with other prominent companies and organizations from various sectors. In addition, it aims to be a stable medium of exchange whose value does not suffer sudden oscillations as is the case with other cryptocurrencies. To this end, their issues will be backed by a basket of financial assets denominated in the main international currencies. This basket will be managed by a network of trusted custodians, with experience in this task, being the Association who will establish the management policies of said reserve. In addition, the ecosystem will be completed with a number of liquidity creators, trading platforms, digital wallet providers and institutions that will offer trading and custody services to end users. In light of the above, Libra emerges as a compendium of many already known realities and, at the same time, it seems to be something completely new that will require, from all of us, a deep exercise of previous analysis: the challenge is of such magnitude that we cannot wait passively to determine its effects, since it could become a destabilizing element of the economy. As a global phenomenon that it aspires to be, Libra demands, first of all, a coordinated international action that is truly effective, consistent and that eliminates the slightest opportunity for arbitration. Hence, from the G7, a working group has been launched with the aim of defining, for this next autumn, a clear roadmap. Among its priorities, it already points to the need to subject Libra to demanding regulatory and supervisory standards. It also seems urgent to deploy mechanisms to ensure that the management of reserves is transparent and consistent with the nature of the obligations assumed. But what does this mean in more concrete terms? Without pretending to anticipate the conclusions that the G7 may reach, let me point out several aspects of the Libra project to which, I believe, it would be worth paying special attention. In particular, I would like to point out some of its most prominent risks which, moreover, are not exclusive to this initiative but can be extended in general to the phenomenon of so-called stable currencies. From a micro perspective, consumer protection issues stand out. It is not evident that the contractual arrangements governing the operation of Libra are sufficiently transparent to allow its users to fully understand the risks to which they are exposed, not least because such services may be being provided from outside the EU. In the same vein, it is reasonable to doubt the effective safeguarding of privacy since the accumulation of large amounts of economically valuable information constitutes a clear incentive for cyber criminals. On the other hand, we cannot forget that the recent history of one of its promoters has not been characterized, precisely, by carefully exploiting personal data. In addition, the international nature of Libra transactions poses significant challenges for the purposes of adequate prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing. To give an example, there are still many uncertainties to be cleared about how the behavior of the different actors in the system is coordinated and integrated. It is also problematic to detect criminal behaviour early, when international transactions can be executed so quickly. Along with these concerns, the potentially systemic dimension of Libra contains other concerns, of a more macroeconomic nature, that do not go unnoticed. Thus, for example, in terms of the stability of the financial system, Libra could be a factor that amplifies the volatility of financial markets, also affecting the payments business and the deposit-taking activity of banks with the consequent erosion of their income statement. In another order of things, a massive use of Libra for the operation of large payments or for the granting of credit could, in turn, limit the effectiveness of traditional tools for the execution of monetary policy. On the other hand, being based on a basket of international currencies would make it easier to spillover between the monetary conditions of different countries. Additionally, the fact that Libra does not have access to mechanisms for extraordinary provision of emergency liquidity could aggravate the tensions that may cause various problems on the financial system, such as those of operational origin or loss of confidence in it. Finally, with regard to payment systems, Libra could mean the emergence of parallel circuits for the mobilization of the financial resources of economies. This would weaken the current role of the euro and other hard currencies as a safe settlement asset and, if adequate supervisory mechanisms are not applied, would jeopardize the ability of financial authorities to control and intervene today over infrastructures that are fundamental to the functioning of our economic system. Conclusions As I have done on other occasions, I would like to close this talk by re-emphasizing the importance that, for the future of banking, it has to face technological change with responsibility and urgency. The magnitude of the challenge is great and increases, without a doubt, with the arrival of bigtech. These represent a new disruptive factor that contributes to adding more pressure to the existing one and before which it does not seem possible to remain on the sidelines. It is a phenomenon that has two faces, on the one hand it can contribute to expanding the offer of financial services, improving both innovation and levels of access, on the other, it harbors significant risks, which may even have a systemic nature. In the specific case of Libra, the potential consequences are of such magnitude that we must maintain all kinds of caution while there is any doubt. At Banco de Espa96a we are fully aware of these circumstances, having firmly committed ourselves to the international effort being made to identify the challenges, take advantage of the opportunities and, at the same time, deploy the appropriate risk containment measures. Regulation should aim to be the most neutral, fair and symmetrical possible, allowing innovation while ensuring equal opportunities. The financial sector is called to reinvent itself to remain relevant. In this challenge, the importance of data stands out above all. The future of the banking business involves access, management and exploitation of available information in order to capitalize on the competitive advantages that the sector currently presents.
