Title: Closing speech at the 2nd Green Finance Workshop on the incorporation of climate risks by rating agencies, organized by the Bank of Spain
text: 15.11.2019 Closing remarks 2nd Green Finance Workshop on the incorporation of climate risks by rating agencies/Bank of Spain Margarita Delgado Subgobernadora Good morning and thank you very much for attending this second workshop on green finance organized by the Bank of Spain. As you will have had the opportunity to see, the Banco de Espa96a has a genuine interest in promoting debate on the challenges of climate change. In particular, we want banks to be aware of the repercussions of this change for their business model and, also, we intend to explore the ways through which the financial system, as a channel of resources, can contribute to the transition towards a more sustainable economy, while trying to avoid the most dramatic effects that such a change can produce. Surely you know that, as deputy governor of the Bank of Spain, I am part of the plenary of the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), a network of central banks and supervisors with 46 members and nine observers, whose objectives are to strengthen the global response required to meet the objectives of the 2015 Paris agreement. As I have just pointed out, the banking sector is a key element in achieving such compliance; To this end, it must deepen and improve the management of the environmental risks of its portfolio, which would facilitate the mobilisation of capital for green and low-carbon investments. The three lines of action in which we are working in the NGFS would be: (i) the identification of macroeconomic and financial risks linked to the climate, (ii) the analysis of the practices that supervisors must use to ensure the solvency of credit institutions in the face of these risks and (iii) the development of financial markets that enable channeling, in an efficient way, of the resources necessary to transform the economy towards a sustainable model. I believe that we will all agree on the need to undertake these three objectives and I also believe that all those present, banks, supervisors and rating agencies, can contribute to their achievement. As you can imagine, I meet regularly with banks, so I will take advantage of the presence of the rating agencies in this workshop to briefly address them. Specifically, I will try to explain how they can contribute in one of these three areas. - Firstly, it is clear that identifying climate risks is a considerable challenge, as we are facing an unprecedented situation (therefore no data). In fact, if we limit ourselves to looking at the default rates in the Spanish economy during the last crisis, we would see how the sectors that we could qualify as "brown" are those that produced the least defaults. Actually, I think this is not surprising, because they are very mature sectors with wide margins. However, it is well known that the so-called transition risks are reflected in situations of abrupt change in the environment, to which certain companies do not know or can adapt. In this context, we must not lose sight of the fact that the environmental transition is, in fact, planned and announced. The European Commission has set the goal of achieving a fully decarbonised economy by 2050, so we have projections on what may happen, even if there is uncertainty about how. Obviously, the analysis of potential changes in the environment that may affect business solvency is an essential part of the assessment and management of risks in the financial system, with Regardless of whether this change in the environment has a technological, customer behavior, regulatory or environmental origin, but, without a doubt, it is also an element to be analyzed in external ratings. Secondly, in relation to banking supervision, we must ensure that climate risks are being properly incorporated into banks' asset portfolios. The challenge is enormous, because we do not have all the necessary information to calculate these risks, at least in a sufficiently granular way, at the company level. Of course, we must also be aware of the difficulty that this type of analysis implies for the banking industry. It is not the same to evaluate the carbon footprint or climate risk of a large loan to one of the main Spanish companies, than to do it for loans to SMEs, although there are several tools that can be useful. Thus, for example, in the case of mortgages, the deeds incorporate energy efficiency certificates. There are also initiatives based on new invoice and supply recognition technologies to be able to calculate the carbon footprint of even the most modest SME. Finally, in order to assess whether or not to introduce the so-called Brown Penalization, or Green Supporting Factors, it is necessary to understand how entities incorporate climate risks in cost and capital, or how they are considered in credit ratings. Again, the role of credit rating agencies is very important in this debate. - The third of the NGFS working groups aims to analyse how financial markets can contribute through financing to the achievement of a sustainable economy. In this regard, last month, during the autumn meetings of the International Monetary Fund, we presented the manual for incorporating sustainability and responsibility criteria in the management of central bank portfolios, in the drafting of which we have had an active participation. Of course, while the handbook is primarily aimed at central bank managers, useful lessons can be drawn for the entire industry. Obviously, the development of investment strategies in green bonds requires a much more developed market than the current one, with greater homogeneity on which assets are green and which are not, something for which initiatives such as the Taxonomy being developed by the European Union is fundamental. At the moment, green bonds are only a niche of the global fixed income market. If financial markets are to play a truly vigilant role in the face of climate change, sustainability and responsibility criteria need to be applicable to all outstanding bonds. Once again, the development of efficient financial markets requires the correct assessment of climate risks, starting with the one that rating agencies must make. Of course, in addition to the list of duties for rating entities and agencies that I have just mentioned, supervisors also have a good number of tasks to do. As a member of the NGFS, the Bank of Spain has committed to making progress in four areas, responding to four key recommendations included in its first comprehensive report. First, we must make progress in integrating climate-related risks into financial stability monitoring and supervision. In this regard, the Bank of Spain is already working on the implementation in the near future of stress tests around different ecological transition scenarios, promoting that entities develop risk models that contemplate climate change. In addition, the draft Law on Climate Change and Transition provides for the Bank to prepare an annual report on the impact of the financial system on the environment. A second recommendation of the NGFS report concerns the integration of sustainability factors into portfolio management. In this area, the Banco de Espa96a is incorporating environmental sustainability as a strategic objective of reserve management. In addition, we have recently participated in the creation of a new green bond investment fund launched by the Bank for International Settlements. Third, the report recommends that central banks close gaps in information and data relevant to climate risk assessment. In this regard, the Banco de Espa96a is already collaborating within the Eurosystem working groups to develop homogeneous methodologies to assess the degree of sustainability of its own portfolios, as part of a broad project that aims to advance the integration of green principles in reserve management. Finally, the fourth area in which the Bank of Spain is working would respond to the NGFS recommendation to create awareness and intellectual capacity on sustainable finance, promoting technical assistance and knowledge exchange. This would include both this workshop and the one held last month, with ESG (Environmental, Social and Governance) data providers, as well as the development of specific publications on sustainable finance and the holding of thematic meetings with industry. The hearing of this workshop shows that there is genuine concern on the part of the financial industry, both issuer and investor, and a real need for data, models and guidelines for risk measurement. From the Bank of Spain we have also raised this challenge, as the activities I have mentioned show, and as this workshop exemplifies. I do not want to end without recalling that next month the World Climate Summit will be held in Madrid. In Madrid, the main experts and world leaders will be presented, and the eyes of the whole world will be on us. I believe that this occasion should serve as an opportunity to analyse what we are doing, whether we are moving in the right direction and whether it is sufficient. I hope that the conference that the Bank of Spain will organize on December 11, as part of the events surrounding the Summit, can serve as a framework to reflect on all these issues and, above all, to continue advancing in them. I would like to conclude by stressing once again the important role that rating agencies can and must play in the face of this new challenge. Undoubtedly, their experience in risk modelling is especially relevant in this context, so we hope to develop a fruitful collaboration. I stop stealing more of your time this Friday. I hope that the day has been profitable, and that we will see each other soon in another new workshop.
text_original: 15.11.2019 Discurso de clausura 2 Taller de Finanzas Verdes sobre la incorporacin de los riesgos climticos por parte de las agencias de rating/Banco de Espaa Margarita Delgado Subgobernadora Buenos das y muchas gracias por asistir a este segundo taller sobre finanzas verdes organizado por el Banco de Espaa. Como habrn tenido ocasin de comprobar, el Banco de Espaa tiene un inters genuino en fomentar el debate sobre los retos del cambio climtico. En particular, queremos que las entidades sean conscientes de las repercusiones de este cambio para su modelo de negocio y, tambin, pretendemos explorar las vas a travs de las que el sistema financiero, como canalizador de recursos, puede contribuir a la transicin hacia una economa ms sostenible, a la vez que tratamos de evitar los efectos ms dramticos que dicho cambio puede producir. Seguramente saben que, como subgobernadora del Banco de Espaa, formo parte del plenario de la Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), red de bancos centrales y supervisores con 46 miembros y nueve observadores, cuyos objetivos son fortalecer la respuesta global requerida para cumplir con los objetivos del acuerdo de Pars de 2015. Como acabo de sealar, el sector bancario constituye una pieza clave para lograr dicho cumplimiento; para ello debe profundizar y mejorar en la gestin de los riesgos medioambientales de su cartera, lo que facilitara la movilizacin del capital para inversiones verdes y bajas en carbono. Las tres lneas de actuacin en las que estamos trabajando en el NGFS seran: (i) la identificacin de los riesgos macroeconmicos y financieros ligados al clima, (ii) el anlisis de las prcticas que los supervisores debemos usar para velar por la solvencia de las entidades de crdito ante estos riesgos y (iii) el desarrollo de unos mercados financieros que posibiliten la canalizacin, de un modo eficiente, de los recursos necesarios para transformar la economa hacia un modelo sostenible. Creo que todos coincidiremos en la necesidad de acometer estos tres objetivos y creo tambin que todos los presentes, bancos, supervisores y agencias de calificacin, podemos contribuir en su consecucin. Como pueden imaginar, me reno con regularidad con los bancos, as que voy a aprovechar la presencia de las agencias de calificacin de riesgos en este taller para dirigirme brevemente a ellas. En concreto, tratar de explicar cmo pueden contribuir en una de estas tres reas. - En primer lugar, es evidente que la identificacin de los riesgos climticos supone un reto considerable, pues nos enfrentamos a una situacin sin precedentes (por tanto, sin datos). De hecho, si nos limitamos a mirar las tasas de impagos en la economa espaola durante la ltima crisis, veramos cmo los sectores que podramos calificar como marrones son los que menos impagos produjeron. En realidad, creo que no se trata de algo sorprendente, pues son sectores muy maduros con mrgenes amplios. Sin embargo, es bien conocido que los llamados riesgos de transicin se reflejan en situaciones de cambio abrupto en el entorno, ante el que determinadas empresas no saben o pueden adaptarse. En este contexto, conviene no perder de vista que la transicin medioambiental est, de hecho, planificada y anunciada. La Comisin Europea ha establecido el objetivo de alcanzar una economa completamente descarbonizada en 2050, por lo que contamos con proyecciones sobre qu puede ocurrir, aunque haya incertidumbre sobre el cmo. Evidentemente, el anlisis de potenciales cambios en el entorno que pueden afectar a la solvencia empresarial es una parte esencial de la evaluacin y gestin de riesgos en el sistema financiero, con independencia de que dicho cambio en el entorno tenga un origen tecnolgico, de comportamiento del cliente, regulatorio o medioambiental, pero, sin duda, se trata tambin de un elemento a analizar en las calificaciones externas. - En segundo lugar, en relacin a la supervisin bancaria, debemos asegurarnos de que los riesgos climticos estn siendo correctamente incorporados a las carteras de los activos de los bancos. El reto es enorme, pues no contamos con toda la informacin necesaria para calcular estos riesgos, al menos de manera suficientemente granular, a nivel de empresa. Por supuesto, debemos ser tambin conscientes de la dificultad que este tipo de anlisis implica para la industria bancaria. No es lo mismo evaluar la huella de carbono o el riesgo climtico de un prstamo de gran envergadura a una de las principales empresas espaolas, que hacerlo para los crditos a las pymes, aunque existen varias herramientas que pueden ser tiles. As, por ejemplo, en el caso de las hipotecas, las escrituras incorporan los certificados de eficiencia energtica. Tambin existen iniciativas basadas en las nuevas tecnologas de reconocimiento de facturas y suministros para poder calcular la huella de carbono de incluso la pyme ms modesta. Finalmente, con objeto de evaluar la conveniencia de introducir o no los llamados Brown Penalizing, o Green Supporting Factors, es necesario entender cmo las entidades incorporan los riesgos climticos en coste y capital, o cmo se consideran en las calificaciones crediticias. De nuevo, el papel de las agencias de calificacin de riesgos resulta muy importante en este debate. - El tercero de los grupos de trabajo del NGFS tiene por objetivo analizar cmo los mercados financieros pueden contribuir a travs de la financiacin al logro de una economa sostenible. En este sentido, el mes pasado, durante las reuniones de otoo del Fondo Monetario Internacional, presentamos el manual de incorporacin de criterios de sostenibilidad y responsabilidad en la gestin de las carteras de los bancos centrales, en cuya redaccin hemos tenido una participacin activa. Por supuesto, aunque el manual se dirige principalmente a los gestores de bancos centrales, cabe extraer lecciones tiles para toda la industria. Evidentemente, el desarrollo de estrategias de inversin en bonos verdes requiere un mercado mucho ms desarrollado que el actual, con una mayor homogeneidad sobre qu activos son verdes y cules no, algo para lo que iniciativas como la Taxonoma que est desarrollando la Unin Europea resulta fundamental. Por el momento, los bonos verdes son solo un nicho del mercado global de renta fija. Si queremos que los mercados financieros jueguen un papel verdaderamente vigilante frente al cambio climtico, es necesario que los criterios de sostenibilidad y responsabilidad se puedan aplicar a todos los bonos en circulacin. Una vez ms, el desarrollo de mercados financieros eficientes requieren la correcta valoracin de los riesgos climticos, empezando por la que deben hacer las agencias de calificacin. Por supuesto, adems de la lista de deberes para las entidades y agencias de calificacin que acabo de referir, los supervisores tenemos tambin un buen nmero de tareas pendientes. Como miembro del NGFS, el Banco de Espaa se ha comprometido a avanzar en cuatro reas, respondiendo a cuatro recomendaciones clave incluidas en su primer informe integral. En primer lugar, debemos avanzar en la integracin de los riesgos relacionados con el clima en el monitoreo de la estabilidad financiera y la supervisin. En este sentido, el Banco de Espaa ya est trabajando en la implementacin en un futuro prximo de pruebas de resistencia en torno a distintos escenarios de transicin ecolgica, promoviendo que las entidades desarrollen modelos de riesgo que contemplen el cambio climtico. Adems, el anteproyecto de Ley de Cambio Climtico y Transicin contempla que el Banco elabore de forma anual un informe sobre el impacto del sistema financiero sobre el medio ambiente. Una segunda recomendacin del informe del NGFS se refiere a la integracin de factores de sostenibilidad en la administracin de carteras. En esta rea, el Banco de Espaa est incorporando la sostenibilidad medioambiental como un objetivo estratgico de la gestin de reservas. Adems, hemos participado recientemente en la creacin de nuevo fondo de inversin en bonos verdes lanzado por el Banco de Pagos Internacionales. En tercer lugar, el informe recomienda a los bancos centrales cerrar brechas de informacin y datos relevantes para la evaluacin de riesgos climticos. En este sentido, el Banco de Espaa ya colabora dentro de los grupos de trabajo del Eurosistema para desarrollar metodologas homogneas que evalen el grado de sostenibilidad de las carteras propias, dentro de un amplio proyecto que pretende avanzar en la integracin de principios verdes en la gestin de reservas. Por ltimo, la cuarta rea en la que est trabajando el Banco de Espaa dara respuesta a la recomendacin del NGFS de crear conciencia y capacidad intelectual sobre las finanzas sostenibles, fomentando la asistencia tcnica y el intercambio de conocimiento. En este mbito se encuadraran tanto este taller como el celebrado el mes pasado, con proveedores de datos ESG (Environmental, Social and Governance), as como la elaboracin de publicaciones especficas sobre finanzas sostenibles y la celebracin de reuniones temticas con la industria. La audiencia de este taller muestra que existe una genuina preocupacin por parte de la industria financiera, tanto la emisora como la inversora, y una verdadera necesidad de datos, modelos y pautas para la medicin de riesgos. Desde el Banco de Espaa tambin nos hemos planteado este reto, como las actividades que he mencionado muestran, y como este taller ejemplifica. No quiero terminar sin recordar que el mes que viene se va a celebrar en Madrid la Cumbre Mundial del Clima. En Madrid se van a presentar los principales expertos y los lderes mundiales, y sobre nosotros van a estar los ojos del mundo entero. Creo que esta ocasin debe servirnos de oportunidad para analizar lo que estamos haciendo, si vamos en la buena direccin y si es suficiente. Espero que la conferencia que el Banco de Espaa organizar el da 11 de diciembre, como parte de los eventos aledaos a la Cumbre, pueda servir de marco para poder reflexionar sobre todos estos temas y, sobre todo, para continuar avanzando en ellos. Quisiera finalizar subrayando de nuevo el importante papel que las agencias de calificacin de riesgo pueden y deben jugar ante este nuevo reto. Sin duda su experiencia en la modelizacin de riesgos resulta especialmente relevante en este contexto, por lo que esperamos poder desarrollar una colaboracin fructfera. Dejo ya de robarles ms tiempo de este viernes. Espero que la jornada les haya sido provechosa, y que nos veamos pronto en otro nuevo taller.

Title: The reform of international banking regulation and current and future challenges
text: 18.11.2019 The reform of international banking regulation and current and future challenges Financial Markets Association 2019 Annual Convention Pablo Hernandez de Cos Governor Good afternoon: I would like to thank the Financial Markets Association and its president, Enrique Prados, for their invitation to participate in this annual convention, as well as Sebasti87n Albella, president of the National Securities Market Commission (CNMV), for his kind words of introduction. On this occasion, I would like to share with such a distinguished group of financial market professionals an overview of the current priorities of the work programme of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, which I have had the honour to chair since March. I would also like to highlight the main challenges and risks that are perceived for financial stability both globally and in Spain. A decade of regulatory reforms in the international banking system... The Basel III reform package addresses the shortcomings identified in the regulatory framework prior to the global financial crisis, with the aim of strengthening international regulation, supervision and banking practices in the interest of financial stability. Basel III is the result of a decade of work and protracted negotiations within the Basel Committee, under the leadership of my predecessors in the presidency, Nout Wellink and Stefan Ingves. The Committee's response to weaknesses in the banking system has led to an increase in both the minimum capital levels required of institutions and improvements in its definition, giving greater importance to the highest quality capital, Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1). The objective is to improve the ability of institutions to absorb losses for as long as the institution is viable. In addition, a set of requirements have been introduced that complement each other: an internationally harmonized leverage ratio, two liquidity standards, limits for large risks, and a new macroprudential dimension. Although many of these reforms are well known, let me review some of their main features. The objective of the leverage ratio is, on the one hand, to contain the excessive accumulation of indebtedness in the banking system and, on the other hand, to supplement capital requirements independently of risk measurements. It includes both a minimum requirement for all internationally active banks and an additional buffer for global systemically important institutions (G-SIBs). The latter buffer has been designed to maintain consistency between risk-weighted requirements and leverage ratio requirements applicable to G-SIBs. For the first time, international liquidity requirements have been incorporated with two ratios: one short-term and the other more structural. These requirements make banks more resilient to potential short-term distortions in access to finance, while favouring a more stable funding structure. In order to mitigate the risk of excessive concentration, a high-risk framework, which also includes macroprudential consideration, has been introduced as it imposes stricter limits on exposures between global systemically important banks. The financial crisis also showed that the microprudential approach alone is insufficient to identify and ultimately prevent or mitigate the accumulation of systemic risks. As a result, the need for macroprudential instruments to help safeguard the stability of the financial system as a whole became clear. The new macroprudential dimension introduced by the Basel Committee has been an important step in this direction. To this end, and in addition to the elements mentioned above, different capital buffers have been incorporated into the prudential framework, such as the buffer for institutions of global systemic importance, which seeks to address the externalities generated by this type of institutions, or the countercyclical buffer, which seeks to prevent and mitigate the systemic risks associated with excessive credit growth at the aggregate level. In addition, another of the main objectives of the reform package has been to reduce the excessive variability of risk-weighted assets (PRAs), which constitute the denominator of the regulatory capital ratio. To this end, a floor added to the capital (floor to output) has been introduced, which establishes a minimum permissible for the APRs resulting from the application of internal models, calculated as a percentage of the APRs resulting from applying the standard methods. This floor to output has been set at 72.5%. In addition, flooring has been introduced to some parameters of the internal models that entities can use to calculate APRs. These reviews aim to restore credibility in the calculation of APRs and improve the comparability of risk-weighted capital ratios declared by different institutions. In guiding the reforms, the Committee has sought to maintain a balance between comparability and simplicity of the prudential regulatory framework, while retaining risk sensitivity. To this end, a comprehensive review of the standards for credit, market and operational risks, among others, has been carried out in order to increase the robustness and risk sensitivity of the standard methods, as well as strengthen comparability and reduce the complexity of internal models. "New" risks, such as those arising from banks' exposures to central counterparties, have also been incorporated. In addition, and with the aim of strengthening market discipline, the Committee has substantially reformed the transparency requirements, which now cover a broader set of risks and disclosures, and include a greater degree of standardisation in the way such information is transferred to the market in order to promote comparability between institutions. These reforms are complemented by those put in place by the Financial Stability Board (FSB). With regard to the banking sector, it highlights the introduction of a set of requirements on total loss-absorbing capacity for global systemically important institutions, in order to ensure additional loss-absorbing and recapitalisation capacity in the event of resolution. These requirements are based on the FSB's document "Fundamental elements for the Effective Resolution Regime of Financial Institutions", which defines the essential aspects for authorities to resolve institutions in an orderly manner, without having to resort to taxpayers' money, in the event of idiosyncratic crises, even for the largest banks, complex and interconnected on a global scale. In the case of the European Union, these total loss-absorbing capacity requirements also apply to entities other than G-SIBs in the form of MREL (Minimum Requirement for own funds and Eligible Liabilities) requirements. ... has generated a significant increase in the resilience of the global banking system Predictably, the Basel III reforms have resulted in a significant strengthening of the resilience of the global banking system. Since 2011, Common Equity Tier 1 resources of internationally active banks have increased by 91% to over db3.7 trillion. And the average risk-weighted CET1 capital ratio has risen from 7.2% to 13%. High-quality liquid assets have increased by more than 50% during this period to over db13 trillion. The average leverage ratio of banks' Tier 1 capital has increased from 3.5% to 6%. In addition, these figures are likely to continue to grow in the coming years, given that the implementation of some of the Basel III reforms will not be completed until 2022, with a transitional period for soil to output that limits the variability of APRs between standard methods and IRB, which may last until 2027. Are all these reforms leading us towards adequate levels of capitalization in banks? One way to answer this question is to draw on the existing results of the economic literature that analyzes the marginal macroeconomic impact of increases in the capital ratios of financial institutions. A paper published by the Basel Committee1 last June reviews the recent academic literature on the macroeconomic costs and benefits of higher capital requirements. This paper concludes that the net macroeconomic benefits of capital requirements are positive within a wide range of capital levels. The comparison of Basel III with these estimates shows that the minimum requirement of 4,5 % for CET-1 in Basel III is clearly in the lower range of 1 Comit8e de Supervisi97n Bancaria de Basilea (2019): d2The costs and benefits of bank capital d0 a review of the literatured3, junio, disponible en . capital levels showing positive net benefits according to the estimates of these studies. If the capital conservation buffer is added, we approach the midpoint of the range and when the additional buffers for systemically important institutions are included, and the countercyclical capital buffer is assumed to activate to a maximum level of 2.5%, the end result is that total capital requirements are still within the range of capital level estimates that show a positive net macroeconomic contribution. Taken together, therefore, Basel III reforms can be said to result in capital levels that are within the range of estimates pointing to positive net macroeconomic benefits for society as a whole from the increased financial stability and shock-absorbing capacity they provide. In summary, there is no evidence to suggest that we have exceeded the calibration of capital requirements in Basel III. The current priorities of the Basel Committee are the full and timely implementation of the reforms and their evaluation... Given this regulatory effort, we are often asked whether the financial reform process can be terminated. Indeed, the completion of Basel III is an important milestone and, in this regard, the priority must now be for jurisdictions to fully implement these rules, within the agreed timeframes and consistently, as G20 leaders have repeatedly stated. Precisely, an important part of the current work of the Basel Committee is to support this objective through its programmes for assessing the implementation of reforms, the so-called RCAP (Regulatory Consistency Assessment Programme). SPCRs have contributed - and continue to contribute - decisively not only to evidences deviations from locally implemented norms from the standards agreed in the Committee, but, even more importantly, to reduce these deviations. This will continue to be the objective of these programmes in the future, and, in fact, we are going to carry out an evaluation of these programmes to identify ways in which we can increase their effectiveness. Beyond the necessary implementation of the agreed standards, this is also the time to start evaluating, without preconceived positions, the effectiveness and impact of the reforms. In my opinion, it is imperative for any body responsible for the development of public policies, including, of course, the Basel Committee, to evaluate the measures and reforms it approves. These evaluations should consist of providing a rigorous and transparent analysis and assessment of the impact of reforms after their implementation. In this way, they constitute a fundamental element in strengthening the credibility and accountability of institutions. To this end, the Basel Committee has launched a comprehensive evaluation programme of the agreed standards, which includes assessing the effectiveness of each of the individual reforms, their interrelationships and the coherence between them, as well as their macroeconomic and structural impacts. It is a multi-year programme that will be based on rigorous empirical analysis, complementing the cross-sectoral evaluations being carried out by the FSB, in which the Basel Committee is also actively involved. Evaluation exercises should not be understood as a door to relaxation in the requirement of agreed standards. In fact, one of the main objectives that I have set myself during my term as chairman of the Basel Committee is to fight against what has come to be called the "regulatory cycle", according to which - and there is empirical evidence to confirm this - over time memories of crises and their negative effects tend to disappear. Pressure from special interests is growing and the temptation to relax regulatory standards is growing. Having said that, we must remain open to the results of evaluations. If we find conclusive empirical evidence suggesting the need to review certain elements of the regulatory framework, either because undesirable effects are observed or because the objectives pursued are not achieved, we should certainly review them, including the adoption of new measures, if necessary. In short, the reforms adopted are enormous, and now is the time to implement them and address their evaluation. ... as well as the close monitoring of new risks associated with the banking sector, such as those associated with financial disintermediation, the technological revolution or climate change Beyond these objectives, the Committee should continue to continuously monitor the risks and vulnerabilities to which the global banking sector is exposed and take, where appropriate, the necessary measures. Today, in fact, there are many challenges facing the international financial sector. Allow me to share with you some thoughts that illustrate these new risks about which we must be vigilant. First, it is clear that the post-crisis financial landscape has changed. In particular, in some jurisdictions, such as the euro area and China, the share of assets in the banking system in relation to the total assets of financial institutions has declined steadily. Thus, in China the weight of the banking system over the financial system as a whole rose from 93% in 2006 to 75% in 2015. In the case of the euro area, the decline was somewhat smaller, but also significant - from 53% to 45% - over the same period. On the other hand, in jurisdictions where banks have traditionally played a relatively minor role in financing the economy, such as the United States, this percentage has not changed significantly. In this context, it is important to ensure that the risks associated with so-called "non-bank financial intermediation", and those arising from its interlinkages with the banking sector, are appropriately regulated and supervised. This requires, among other aspects, closely monitoring the regulatory perimeter of the entire financial system, ensuring that market participants operate under the principle of regulatory neutrality. Secondly, and partly related to the above, the impact of technology on the financial sector is having very significant consequences. In particular, in recent years we have seen a growing interest on the part of global technology companies, known as "big tech", in the provision of financial services. It is clear that their size, their customer base, their small cost structure and the large amount of data they have, together with their technological capacity, make these companies have the potential to modify the current structure of the financial system. In this context, it should be borne in mind that, although "big tech" can contribute to an improvement in the provision of some financial services, they can also generate risks for financial stability, consumer protection, competition and data privacy, among others. Therefore, it is necessary to analyze these potential risks in depth and, if necessary, modify the regulatory framework to mitigate them. On the other hand, these developments can affect banks in different dimensions, ranging from a possible risk of excessive dependence on a few technology service providers, to additional pressures on their profitability, to implications for their current business models. An example of the disruptive capacity of technology in the financial field is the development of the so-called cryptoactives, and in particular the so-called stablecoins, of which project Libra is the one that has received the most attention. As the G72 has identified, these types of innovations generate different legal, regulatory and supervisory issues. To provide an adequate response to these challenges, the FSB plans to analyze in the coming months the current supervisory and regulatory approaches and determine if they are adequate to face the considerations of financial stability and systemic risk that may arise due to specific characteristics of a stablecoin or by its joint operation. Following this review, and if deemed necessary, multilateral responses would be proposed, including the development of approaches. 2 G7 Working Group on Stablecoins (2019), d2Investigating the impact of global stablecoinsd3, octubre, disponible en global supervisors and regulators to address these issues of financial stability and systemic risk. The Basel Committee is currently assessing the implications for banks and supervisors of an increase in the use of stablecoins, both in terms of the possible role that banks could play in a stablecoin ecosystem and in relation to the risks that could arise. Specifically, the question of whether supervisors have adequate resources and a regulatory framework conducive to monitoring them will be analyzed. In relation to crypto-assets, the Committee will shortly publish a discussion paper that allows for diverse views on what their prudential treatment should be, and we will continue to analyse what the implications of these developments are for banks and supervisors. Finally, the Committee is deepening its analysis in different aspects related to technology such as the use of artificial intelligence and so-called machine learning, the dependence of banks on unregulated third-party providers and data governance. On the other hand, it is evident that the increasing use of technology exposes financial institutions to cyber-incidents with greater frequency, severity and sophistication. In fact, according to recent surveys, 80% of bank risk managers consider cyber risks a priority issue, up from just 10% in 2013. In this regard, the Committee published in December last year a report describing and comparing different practices of banks, regulators and banking supervisors in relation to cyber risk management3, and is currently revising the principles and guidelines related to operational resilience to better reflect the risks associated with technological innovations. The third of the challenges facing the banking sector that I wanted to refer to is related to environmental sustainability and climate change. On the one hand, the banking sector is exposed to both physical and transition risks arising from climate change, which encompass credit, market or operational risks. On the other hand, the financial system can play a crucial role as a provider of the financing necessary to make the investments required to achieve a more sustainable economy. In this context, the Basel Committee joined a few months ago, as an observer member, the Network for Greening the Financial System of which the Bank of Spain was already a member. This network will allow regulators and central banks to share experiences and best practices in the assessment and management of risks arising from the ecological transition in banks and at the level of the financial system as a whole. In the same area, at the end of last October, the Committee decided to start various works on the financial risks associated with climate change. 3 Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (2018), "Cyber-resilience: Range of practices", December, available in In a more uncertain global macroeconomic environment, low bank profitability and growing risk appetite are some of the main risks for banks Beyond these structural challenges for the financial sector, allow me to also mention some of a more circumstantial nature, related to the global macro-financial situation. Over the past year, global growth prospects have deteriorated and become more uncertain; and, as a result, interest rates are likely to remain at low levels for longer in a large number of countries. In addition, global indebtedness is at an all-time high. This macro-financial context introduces risks of different nature to financial stability. On the one hand, the macro-financial environment to which I have just referred, together with the additional pressure imposed by some of the structural changes mentioned above and the existence of some legacies of the crisis, is causing the banking sector to find it difficult in many jurisdictions to generate levels of profitability that exceed the cost of capital. It should be remembered that the ability to generate results is not only the first line of defense of financial institutions against the materialization of risks, but insufficient levels of profitability make it difficult to strengthen their solvency. In this context, it is necessary for institutions to continue working on improving the quality of their balance sheets and increasing their efficiency, considering the adaptation of their business models to technological change, among other factors. On the other hand, the current situation of low interest rates and pressures on bank profitability may encourage banks to take greater risks. Thus, the high levels of high-yield corporate debt, and the participation of banks and other financial intermediaries in the financing of this market segment worldwide, can be a paradigmatic example of this type of trend towards greater risk-taking. Specifically, the available information suggests that the volume of high-risk debt materialized in leveraged loans (leverage loans) and their securitizations (CLO) remains at high levels at international level and vulnerabilities in this market segment have increased in recent years, as these products incorporate lower levels of credit protection and changes in the structure of the market have made it more complex and opaque. In addition, the available information also suggests that banks are among the main direct holders of this type of product. These global developments need to be analyzed in greater depth to definitively understand their potential systemic implications. In any event, in the environment I have described, the capital and liquidity requirements of the Basel III framework help to prevent and contain the effects of excessive risk-taking. Microprudential supervisors also have an important role to play. In this respect, the Basel Committee is a forum in which cross-border cooperation in the area of micro-prudential supervision can be enhanced through the exchange of supervisory approaches and techniques. For their part, macroprudential instruments should also contribute to mitigating the potential accumulation of risks to financial stability in a global macro-financial context such as the current one. Risks to financial stability that are shared by the Spanish economy... Allow me to end my speech with a mention of the assessment we make at the Bank of Spain of the risks to financial stability in our country. As you know, we published our autumn Financial Stability Report on 31 October. The report highlights, consistent with what I have just mentioned for the global economy, a certain deterioration in the balance of risks to financial stability in our country. The sources of the risks identified for financial stability in Spain are also similar to those identified on a global scale. On the one hand, it identifies the risks arising from the global economic slowdown and geopolitical uncertainty, which is affecting Europe and emerging economies more intensely. Less economic dynamism and an eventual materialization of geopolitical risks may have implications for financial stability in Spain through different channels. First, it can lead financial market participants to reassess their perception of risk. This would cause the risk premia of financial instruments, currently highly compressed, to increase, which would reduce the valuation of assets and, therefore, the wealth and value of collateral. These developments could further affect the most vulnerable segments such as debt with lower credit quality and markets with high valuations, and could extend to other assets. Second, it can affect agents' income flows, with implications for their consumption and investment spending decisions. For households, they could reduce job creation and wage growth. In the case of non-financial corporations, the advance of their profits would decrease. The public sector would also see its balance of income and non-financial expenses affected by the operation of automatic stabilizers. This would mean that both private and public debt levels could end up being higher than expected, with additional implications for both spending decisions and financial markets' perception of the path of debt sustainability. Logically, a possible deterioration in the macroeconomic context would also affect depository institutions. The decrease in the value of some of its assets would be joined by a lower demand for credit. In addition, the quality of the asset could worsen, since the ability to pay of its borrowers would be negatively affected. They would also find it more difficult to continue to divest their non-performing assets. As a result, their profit and loss accounts would come under downward pressure. This is particularly relevant in a context, such as the current one, in which banks' profitability is low. This is, in fact, the second risk for the financial stability identified in our report. Again, it is not something specific to the Spanish financial system either. Although the profitability of Spanish banks is higher than the European average, this is still lower than the cost of capital which, as I mentioned, makes it difficult to strengthen their solvency. Precisely, one way to assess the adequacy of the solvency levels of institutions is to subject them to stress tests. The Bank of Spain carries out this type of exercise annually for all Spanish entities. To do this, it takes as its starting point very granular data from the balance sheet of the entities at the end of the previous year and defines a central macroeconomic scenario, which coincides with the forecasts of the Bank of Spain available at the time of the year, and another stressed, which tries to collect the effect of the materialization of the risks previously identified. The difference between the two scenarios reflects the degree of stress of the exercise, which, in the one carried out this year, is slightly higher than the previous year due to the intensification of the risks to which I have referred. The results obtained in relation to the resilience of all Spanish banks are, in general, positive. The capital needs that occur in the adverse scenario are moderate at the aggregate level, although there is considerable heterogeneity between entities. In particular, the reduction in the CET1 capital ratio for large institutions with significant international activity is 0.4 percentage points (pp), 2.7 pp for the rest of the institutions supervised by the SSM and 0.6 pp for less significant institutions. These results are, in general, more favourable than last year, since banks have taken advantage of the last year to reduce their exposure to changes in the prices of some assets, such as foreclosed assets. Specifically, banks have divested significant packages of foreclosed assets during 2018 and so far in 2019. The last source of risk identified in the report has to do with the operational risk of financial institutions. Operational risk represents 9.3% of the volume of risk-weighted assets of Spanish depository institutions, slightly below the European average (10.5%). In any case, the deterioration in solvency associated with an operational risk event may be high according to historical experience. In the Spanish case, the potential materialization of costs associated with legal risks continues to contribute to the operational risk of deposit institutions. The processes linked to past litigation such as the floor clauses have had an estimated cost for the sector of more than 2,200 million euros until June 2019. In addition, there are other relevant legal processes pending resolution. In any case, legal risk and some other factors related to the conduct of entities have had a significant impact on the reputation of the banking sector, and not only in Spain. In this sense, it should be remembered that the reputation and trust of customers are the fundamental elements on which the banking business is based. Institutions should therefore strive to reverse this trend by providing their customers with financial products and services appropriate to their needs and capabilities, as well as providing relevant information in a clear and transparent manner. ... which will be strictly monitored by the Bank of Spain In this context of potential risks, and after a technical analysis that combines quantitative indicators with qualitative information, the Bank of Spain has maintained in the fourth quarter of 2019 the percentage of the Countercyclical Capital Buffer (CCA) at 0%. In particular, the set of quantitative indicators guiding CCA decisions includes indicators that seek to capture the evolution of the credit cycle of the non-financial private sector and its excessive growth, the position of the business cycle, the potential overvaluation of house prices, the effort involved in paying interest and repaying the principal of loans to households and enterprises (debt service), the external imbalance; The technical analysis assesses the recent evolution of the indicators, their current situation and also their expected behavior in the coming quarters consistent with the macroeconomic forecasts prepared quarterly by the Bank of Spain. The prospective analysis is particularly relevant in this context, since, if the CCA is activated, the entities have twelve months to comply with the requirement. In particular, the credit cycle indicator continues to show values below the activation thresholds (taking into account the credit-to-GDP ratio, which remains below its long-term trend value), although it is gradually converging to equilibrium. On the other hand, the production gap has been positive since the beginning of the year, and forecasts for its future evolution maintain a growing outlook. Some complementary quantitative indicators also point to an increasing trend over the next two years. Overall, the analysis carried out covers the maintenance of the CCA at 0%, although it points out the need to continue a strict monitoring of both short-term risks and the evolution and projections of the indicators. Conclusion In summary, returning to the legitimate question that many ask about whether we can conclude the financial reform process, the most appropriate answer I can give by way of conclusion is that, once the Basel III regulatory framework is finalized, the main challenge is to carry out a full and timely implementation of it in all jurisdictions. at the same time it is necessary to evaluate its effects. In parallel, we must remain alert and react to the new risks facing the banking system, such as those associated with growing financial disintermediation, technological disruption, climate change, or those derived from the macro-financial environment and their consequences on the business models and risk appetite of institutions. The objective of our work must remain the same: to safeguard and strengthen financial stability through the use of macro- and microprudential instruments within a framework of cooperation and coordination between supervisory authorities at national and international level. text_original: 18.11.2019 La reforma de la regulacin bancaria internacional y los retos actuales y de futuro Convencin Anual 2019 de la Asociacin de Mercados Financieros Pablo Hernndez de Cos Gobernador Buenas tardes: Quisiera agradecer a la Asociacin de Mercados Financieros y a su presidente, Enrique Prados, su invitacin a participar en esta convencin anual, as como a Sebastin Albella, presidente de la Comisin Nacional del Mercado de Valores (CNMV), sus amables palabras de presentacin. El objetivo perseguido es mejorar la capacidad de las entidades para absorber prdidas mientras la entidad sea viable. Adems, se han introducido un conjunto de requerimientos que se complementan: una ratio de apalancamiento internacionalmente armonizada, dos estndares de liquidez, lmites para los grandes riesgos, y una nueva dimensin macroprudencial. Aunque muchas de estas reformas son bien conocidas, permtanme que repase algunas de sus principales caractersticas. El objetivo de la ratio de apalancamiento es, por una parte, contener la acumulacin excesiva de endeudamiento en el sistema bancario y, por otra, complementar los requerimientos de capital con independencia de las mediciones del riesgo. Este ltimo colchn ha sido diseado con el fin de conservar la coherencia entre los requerimientos ponderados por riesgo y los requerimientos del coeficiente de apalancamiento aplicables a G-SIBs. Se han incorporado, por primera vez, requisitos internacionales de liquidez con dos ratios: una de corto plazo y otra de carcter ms estructural. Dichos requisitos dotan a los bancos de una mayor capacidad de resistencia frente a posibles distorsiones a corto plazo en el acceso a la financiacin, al tiempo que favorecen una estructura de financiacin ms estable. Con el fin de mitigar el riesgo de concentracin excesiva, se ha introducido un marco de grandes riesgos, que tambin incluye una consideracin macroprudencial, puesto que impone lmites ms estrictos a las exposiciones entre bancos de importancia sistmica mundial. La crisis financiera tambin puso de manifiesto que el enfoque microprudencial es insuficiente por s solo para identificar y, en ltima instancia, evitar o mitigar la acumulacin de riesgos sistmicos. Por ello, se hizo patente la necesidad de contar con instrumentos macroprudenciales que contribuyan a salvaguardar la estabilidad del sistema financiero en su conjunto. La nueva dimensin macroprudencial introducida por el Comit de Basilea ha sido un paso importante en esta direccin. Para ello, y de forma adicional a los elementos sealados anteriormente, se han incorporado al marco prudencial distintos colchones de capital, como el colchn para las entidades de importancia sistmica global, que busca tratar las externalidades generadas por este tipo de entidades, o el colchn anticclico, que busca prevenir y mitigar los riesgos sistmicos asociados al crecimiento excesivo del crdito a nivel agregado. Para ello, se ha llevado a cabo una revisin exhaustiva de los estndares para los riesgos de crdito, mercado y operacional, entre otros, con el fin de aumentar la solidez y la sensibilidad al riesgo de los mtodos estndar, as como reforzar la comparabilidad y reducir la complejidad de los modelos internos. Asimismo, se han incorporado nuevos riesgos, como los derivados de las exposiciones de los bancos a las entidades de contrapartida central. Adems, y con el objetivo de reforzar la disciplina de mercado, el Comit ha reformado sustancialmente los requisitos de transparencia, que ahora abarcan un conjunto ms amplio de riesgos y de informacin, e incluyen un mayor grado de estandarizacin en el modo en el que esa informacin se traslada al mercado con el fin de fomentar la comparabilidad entre entidades. Las prioridades actuales del Comit de Basilea son la implementacin plena y a tiempo de las reformas y su evaluacin Dado este esfuerzo regulatorio, se nos pregunta con frecuencia si se puede dar por finalizado el proceso de reforma financiera. En segundo lugar, y en parte relacionado con lo anterior, el impacto de la tecnologa en el sector financiero est teniendo consecuencias muy significativas. En concreto, en los ltimos aos hemos observado un creciente inters por parte de las empresas tecnolgicas globales, conocidas como big tech, en la provisin de servicios financieros. Por otra parte, estos desarrollos pueden afectar a las entidades bancarias en distintas dimensiones, que abarcan desde un posible riesgo de excesiva dependencia de unos pocos proveedores de servicios tecnolgicos, a presiones adicionales sobre su rentabilidad, pasando por implicaciones en sus modelos de negocio actuales. En relacin con los criptoactivos, el Comit publicar en breve un documento de discusin que permita recabar diversas opiniones sobre cul debe ser su tratamiento prudencial, y seguiremos analizando cules son las implicaciones de estos desarrollos para bancos y supervisores. Finalmente, el Comit est profundizando su anlisis en distintos aspectos relacionados con la tecnologa como son el uso de la inteligencia artificial y el denominado machine learning, la dependencia de los bancos de proveedores terceros no regulados y la gobernanza de los datos. Por otra parte, es evidente que el uso creciente de la tecnologa expone a las entidades financieras a ciber-incidentes con mayor frecuencia, severidad y sofisticacin. De hecho, de acuerdo con encuestas recientes el 80 % de los responsables de riesgos de los bancos consideran los ciberriesgos como un tema prioritario, frente a tan solo el 10 % en 2013. El tercero de los retos a los que se enfrenta el sector bancario al que quera referirme es el relacionado con la sostenibilidad ambiental y el cambio climtico. De un lado, el sector bancario est expuesto tanto a los riesgos fsicos como a los de transicin derivados del cambio climtico, que abarcan tanto riesgos de crdito, como de mercado u operacionales.
