Pese a que el esfuerzo ha sido evidente, es posible que el proceso de consolidacin no se pueda dar todava por finalizado. En todo caso, cabe subrayar que, en trminos comparativos, nuestro grado de avance es muy superior al de pases de nuestro entorno. Por otro lado, en paralelo a este proceso, durante los ltimos cinco aos el sector ha logrado mejorar notablemente su situacin en parmetros bsicos como la calidad de sus activos o sus niveles de rentabilidad y solvencia. Estoy convencida que los representantes de las entidades coincidirn conmigo en que el entorno en el que se desarrolla el negocio bancario es cada vez ms complicado. A la necesidad de continuar con la reduccin de activos no productivos se une la presin por mejorar los niveles de solvencia. Todo ello en un entorno de persistencia de tipos de inters negativos, que presionan los mrgenes, y en un contexto crecientemente competitivo, con la irrupcin de nuevos actores no bancarios. Adems, el sector sigue arrastrando problemas del pasado en forma de litigiosidad y prdida de reputacin por determinadas actuaciones pretritas. Todos estos retos y dificultades configuran un entorno muy complicado y competitivo al que debe responder la banca. En la segunda parte de mi intervencin hablar sobre los cambios que, a mi juicio, deben introducirse en el modelo de negocio bancario como respuesta a este difcil entorno. Pero permtanme que, antes de hablar del futuro, comparta con ustedes algunas reflexiones respecto al pasado. Lecciones de la crisis bancaria Ya he sealado el papel clave de la iniciativa empresarial para lograr la creacin de riqueza. No obstante, tambin es cierto que, para poder desarrollarse, la actividad empresarial precisa financiacin, y que sta depende de la banca, al menos en ausencia de mercados de capitales profundos3. 3 En la UE se est tratando de desarrollar el denominado mercado de capitales unido (CMU) pero an estamos lejos de poder contar con un canal de financiacin verdaderamente alternativo a la banca, salvo para las grandes empresas. Por qu el papel de la banca sigue siendo muy relevante para lograr un desarrollo econmico sano y sostenible? Pues porque al analizar y evaluar el riesgo antes de la concesin de financiacin, el sector bancario acta como un filtro esencial para el funcionamiento de la economa, permitiendo la correcta asignacin de los recursos financieros disponibles al discriminar aquellos proyectos con alta probabilidad de xito de aquellos que no son viables a medio plazo. Naturalmente, se pueden producir errores en esa evaluacin del riesgo. De hecho, es inevitable que se produzcan, incluso en aquellas entidades que mejor gestionan el riesgo de crdito. Unos estndares de concesin excesivamente estrictos pueden actuar como un freno a la innovacin y el crecimiento, pero debemos reconocer que a los supervisores nos tiende a preocupar ms el caso contrario; cuando los estndares de concesin se relajan excesivamente se acaban financiando demasiados proyectos inviables. En este sentido, la crisis nos ha vuelto a recordar alguna leccin que nunca debimos olvidar. La financiacin de proyectos de dudosa viabilidad es, a medio plazo, un psimo negocio para todos: lo es para el cliente, que ve comprometido su futuro por una mala decisin personal o empresarial. Sin duda, lo es tambin para el banco, que tiene que soportar las prdidas de un prstamo dudoso. El sistema judicial tambin sufre las consecuencias, al aumentar su carga de trabajo, lo que dificulta su funcionamiento. Por ltimo, lo es para la sociedad en su conjunto, al dejar dolorosas secuelas en forma de despidos y desahucios. Estarn pensando que esta leccin es bsica. Bueno, ciertamente lo es, pero tambin es cierto que en plena expansin econmica, particularmente cuando esta expansin se prolonga en el tiempo, es fcil olvidarnos de ella. Por otro lado, no debemos menospreciar la presin ejercida por la competencia y las expectativas de mercado. La aplicacin de unos estndares estrictos implica la obligacin de decir no en muchas ocasiones ante solicitudes de financiacin, lo que en momentos lgidos de crecimiento tiene muy mala prensa y resulta difcil de asumir por la entidad que dice no, particularmente si la competencia est siendo laxa en la concesin de riesgo. Por otro lado, el crecimiento desbocado del crdito y la consiguiente acumulacin de desequilibrios no tiene consecuencias negativas aparentes durante una etapa expansiva, sino que permite mejorar la rentabilidad de las entidades, retroalimentando la toma de riesgo. En ocasiones, el propio supervisor puede caer en esa falsa sensacin de seguridad, crecimiento y beneficio que solo nos estara conduciendo al desastre. Quisiera subrayar este punto: debemos evitar a toda costa caer en esta trampa. Tanto supervisores como reguladores debemos mirar las cosas siempre en negativo. As dicho parece un poco triste; en la vida es casi obligatorio ser optimista y, desde un punto de vista econmico, sin optimismo la actividad se ralentiza y las inversiones se detienen; el ndice de confianza empresarial es una variable clave de la economa. Pero siendo esto cierto, la regulacin debe redactarse sin perder nunca de vista lo que sucede en poca de crisis. Por ejemplo: la evaluacin de determinados activos inmateriales, o la cantidad de capital necesario deben hacerse contemplando un contexto estresado. Evidentemente, la supervisin debe realizarse bajo una perspectiva similar. Por tanto, cabe plantearse cules han sido los cambios introducidos en la regulacin prudencial y en el marco institucional de supervisin y resolucin, para evitar que situaciones del pasado vuelvan a suceder. Nuevo marco regulatorio Comenzando por la regulacin y, ms en concreto, por la normativa de solvencia, el marco de capital de Basilea ha sido reformulado en su prctica totalidad para incorporar las lecciones de la crisis. Los cambios normativos han afectado a todos los elementos que configuran la conocida ratio de capital: (i) la definicin de capital en el numerador es mucho ms exigente, aumentando su calidad y capacidad de absorcin de prdidas a la vez que se endurecen las deducciones por activos inmateriales; (ii) en el denominador se ha fortalecido el modo en que los riesgos bancarios se traducen en activos ponderados, introduciendo tambin cautelas respecto al uso de modelos internos; por ltimo, (iii) el propio nivel exigible de la ratio ha subido considerablemente, contemplando colchones adicionales para, entre otros, cubrir los riesgos que presentan las entidades sistmicas. La prctica totalidad del marco prudencial ha girado tradicionalmente en torno a esta ratio. No obstante, la crisis ha mostrado que centrarnos solamente en una mtrica puede ser contraproducente. Se han introducido otros elementos complementarios al clsico de la solvencia relativos a la liquidez o al grado de apalancamiento de las entidades. Tambin se han implementado lmites y restricciones a la poltica retributiva de las entidades de crdito, con el objetivo de corregir o, al menos, paliar determinados incentivos perversos. Nuevo marco institucional de supervisin Adems de la regulacin, la supervisin ha cambiado tambin de modo radical. Desde el punto de vista institucional hemos abrazado una supervisin verdaderamente europea, como paso fundamental hacia una Unin Bancaria que dote de una mayor seguridad al conjunto del sistema financiero europeo, favoreciendo con ello un crecimiento sostenible de la economa. Como he manifestado en otras ocasiones, an nos queda camino por recorrer para completar la Unin Bancaria; contamos con dos pilares ya constituidos: los mecanismos comunes de supervisin y resolucin, pero nos falta an el tercero: un fondo garanta de depsitos verdaderamente europeo. En todo caso, la direccin del proyecto es clara y parece que se podran estar dando los pasos para alcanzar un acuerdo que desbloquee este tercer pilar bsico de la Unin4. 4 Tambin resulta importante el impulso de la denominada Unin de Mercado de Capitales, que resultara complementaria a la Unin Bancaria a la hora de favorecer la integracin y el desarrollo de un mercado financiero verdaderamente europeo. Supervisin micro y macroprudencial A pesar de todos estos cambios institucionales creo que el papel bsico de la supervisin sigue siendo esencialmente el mismo. La supervisin bancaria ha sido, y sigue siendo, eminentemente preventiva. Nuestra capacidad de accin como supervisores es muy limitada una vez que la crisis bancaria ha estallado. Al inicio de mi intervencin me he referido al proceso de reconversin y redimensionamiento que el sector bancario ha llevado a cabo en los ltimos 10 aos. Dicho proceso ha sido necesario debido a fallos en la gestin de muchas de las entidades as como en las previsiones econmicas que se manejaban. Pero, lamentablemente, es reflejo tambin de un fallo en la evaluacin de riesgos por parte del supervisor y de la carencia de instrumentos adecuados. Algo que resulta particularmente perturbador es el hecho de que las entidades no incumplieron en ningn momento la normativa de solvencia durante la formacin de nuestra burbuja inmobiliaria. Como acabo de sealar, la normativa ha cambiado con objeto de corregir y evitar determinados incentivos, pero no es en absoluto descartable que se puedan volver a acumular desequilibrios estructurales en los balances de la banca tal y como ocurri durante la etapa previa al estallido de la crisis. En este contexto surge la denominada poltica macroprudencial, que complementa la supervisin tradicional, tambin llamada microprudencial. La poltica macroprudencial tiene como objetivo potenciar la estabilidad financiera mediante la prevencin y mitigacin de los denominados riesgos y vulnerabilidades de carcter sistmico, evaluando tambin la existencia de potenciales desequilibrios o sobrevaloraciones que puedan afectar a un sector determinado. Por tanto, los riesgos se pasan a evaluar de un modo agregado. Desde 2014 el Banco de Espaa ya realiza esas tareas de identificacin y seguimiento de vulnerabilidades en el sistema financiero y cuenta tambin con la posibilidad de introducir colchones anticclicos de capital. No obstante, hemos adquirido recientemente la posibilidad de usar herramientas adicionales a la mera activacin los colchones de capital. Estas herramientas son mucho ms especficas, y deben permitir actuar de modo focalizado en el segmento de crdito dnde se puedan concentrar desequilibrios. Por supuesto surgen dos preguntas: - Cmo detectar la acumulacin excesiva de desequilibrios? - Cundo debemos actuar para corregirlos? Quiero resaltar que este tipo de medidas son muy novedosas, incluso se podra decir que su aplicacin est todava en paales. Las metodologas para detectar sobrevaloraciones o desequilibrios estn todava en desarrollo, junto a los criterios a seguir a la hora de activar y desactivar estas medidas. No obstante, ello no debe ser excusa para no actuar. Se nos ha dotado de unas herramientas que hubieran sido muy tiles para corregir o paliar la crisis que hemos padecido. Evidentemente debemos actuar con responsabilidad, pero tambin con prudencia. Cambios en el marco de resolucin Algo que tambin nos ha recordado la crisis es que, pese a todos los esfuerzos, las crisis de entidades puntuales pueden seguir ocurriendo. Particularmente, en un entorno tan complicado como el actual, por lo que debemos contar con los mecanismos adecuados para evitar una transmisin o contagio al resto del sistema, a la vez que minimizamos el riesgo de tener que usar fondos pblicos. En consecuencia, el marco de resolucin y liquidacin de entidades ha sido tambin modificado de modo radical. La planificacin de la resolucin por parte de las propias entidades es un elemento clave de este nuevo marco. Parece claro que un entorno de crisis no es el ms propicio para la improvisacin. Aunque cada crisis sea distinta y resulte casi imposible anticipar todas las circunstancias que pueden acaecer, todo lo que se haya trabajado de antemano ayudar en el proceso de gestin de cada crisis individual. El otro elemento clave se refiere al cambio de paradigma de resolucin, pasando del rescate externo, en gran medida a travs del uso de fondos pblicos (bail-out) al rescate interno, soportado por los accionistas y acreedores de la entidad (bail-in). Este ltimo elemento ha implicado la introduccin de los nuevos requerimientos de pasivos elegibles, conocidos como MREL por sus siglas en ingls. Evidentemente, la emisin de estos pasivos elegibles es difcil para entidades con limitado acceso a los mercados, a la vez que aade presin a la cuenta de resultados. En este sentido, parece que la creciente solvencia de las entidades podra reducir algo esta presin, ya que a mayor nivel de ratio de capital CET1, cabe observar unos menores costes de emisin de deuda. Cambios a introducir por las entidades Tras cubrir todas las transformaciones ocurridas en los marcos regulatorio, supervisor y de resolucin, permtanme que me refiera brevemente a los cambios que no dependen del sector oficial, sino que solo pueden acometer los propios bancos. Creo que tanto supervisores como supervisados operamos con un objetivo comn: ambos queremos que las entidades sigan abiertas, dando servicio a su clientela y contribuyendo al desarrollo econmico. En cualquier caso, las claves de la sostenibilidad del negocio bancario en el largo plazo estn en las manos de las propias entidades. Quisiera hablar de alguna de esas claves internas. En concreto, me referir a la gobernanza, as como a aquellos aspectos en los que se debe incidir a la hora de replantear el modelo de negocio bancario. Gobernanza Como saben las entidades, la gobernanza es un tema que est recibiendo una atencin creciente por parte del supervisor. No se trata en absoluto de algo nuevo. Sin embargo, ha adquirido una importancia crucial a raz de la crisis. En un momento complicado desde un punto de vista del negocio tradicional de la banca, con una gran presin en mrgenes y entrada de competidores no bancarios, es relativamente sencillo que la mejora de la gobernanza se vea como algo secundario; quiz deseable, pero no una prioridad. Evidentemente, la mejora de la gobernanza no contribuye en el corto plazo a ensanchar los ingresos o a controlar los costes; antes al contrario, puede implicar la necesidad de contratar personal con determinado perfil o acometer reformas que pueden suponer costes adicionales. Por qu entonces esta fijacin supervisora? La gobernanza es una de esas claves fundamentales a las que antes me refera que permiten asegurar la viabilidad del negocio a largo plazo. No es, desde luego, una condicin suficiente para dicha viabilidad, pero creo firmemente que s se trata de una condicin necesaria. Sin una adecuada gobernanza, las entidades no pueden gestionar los conflictos de inters inherentes a la actividad bancaria. El ms evidente de ellos sera el que se produce entre la bsqueda de beneficio a corto plazo y la sostenibilidad y viabilidad de la entidad en el largo. Un triste ejemplo lo tenemos en el crecimiento desaforado del crdito que se produjo, junto con el debilitamiento en los estndares de concesin, antes del estallido de la crisis. Modelo de negocio y relacin con la clientela En este mismo contexto de sostenibilidad del negocio a largo plazo, querra reflexionar sobre la reputacin de las entidades y el modelo de relacin con la clientela. La banca, tanto o ms que los supervisores, se enfrenta al reto de recuperar su imagen ante la opinin pblica y su reputacin ante la clientela, cosa que resulta complicada mientras afloran casos del pasado. Durante los ltimos aos, la normativa de proteccin a la clientela ha cambiado de modo significativo, en paralelo con la evolucin de la sociedad. Ambos elementos implican un claro incremento del nivel de exigencia en cuanto a la transparencia, diligencia, rigurosidad y honestidad que se espera de la banca. Un buen reflejo de esta nueva manera de actuar se encuentra en la reciente Ley de crdito inmobiliario. Podramos afirmar que hemos pasado de la regulacin de la transparencia formal a la regulacin de conducta, lo que implica que prcticas consideradas adecuadas en el pasado han dejado de serlo. Algo muy positivo de este enfoque es la mejora de la seguridad jurdica, que permite cimentar la reputacin futura del sector. Al igual que sucede en el caso de la gobernanza, se trata de un elemento que resultar clave a medio y largo plazo, aunque en el corto implique renunciar a determinado tipo de negocio. Por supuesto, para que se implante con xito es fundamental que se produzca un cambio cultural en el conjunto de la organizacin, para lo que se debe contar con el apoyo decidido de la alta administracin y de los equipos gestores de las entidades. De nuevo, hablamos de gobernanza como precondicin para que se produzca el cambio. Por ser positivos, creo que se observa un cambio de actitud en las entidades, pese a que quede mucho por hacer. En este sentido, el pasado ejercicio se observ una cada de las reclamaciones presentadas. Segn la Memoria de Reclamaciones 2018 del Banco de Espaa el nmero de reclamaciones tramitadas el ao pasado ha descendido ms de un 50 % en relacin a las de 2017. Finanzas sostenibles Otro cambio evidente en la sociedad es el relativo al llamado reto medioambiental. Es palmario que existe una creciente concienciacin social en relacin a la contaminacin y sus potenciales efectos sobre el clima. De hecho, segn una reciente encuesta del Real Instituto Elcano, el 97 % de los espaoles est de acuerdo en que el cambio climtico existe y un 92 % cree que los humanos somos sus principales responsables. Desde un punto de vista regulatorio, la transicin ecolgica est ganando visibilidad e importancia en la agenda de los organismos financieros internacionales. Existen multitud de iniciativas oficiales en este momento. En el mbito de la UE destaca el plan de accin sobre finanzas sostenibles y en nuestro pas, debemos referir el anteproyecto de Ley de Cambio Climtico. En el entorno de los bancos centrales destacan los trabajos de la Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), cuyo objetivo fundamental es el de impulsar el papel del sector financiero en el cumplimiento de los Acuerdos de Pars. Evidentemente, el cumplimiento de estos objetivos implica necesariamente cambios muy sustanciales en nuestro modelo productivo, que afectaran prcticamente a todos los agentes econmicos. Creo que, de nuevo, debemos emplear aqu la palabra reconversin. Pese a no formar parte de los sectores con altas emisiones contaminantes, el sector bancario puede y debe jugar un papel importante para tener xito en el reto de la transicin ecolgica. Al inicio de mi intervencin hablaba sobre el papel fundamental de la banca como filtro necesario para discriminar los proyectos econmicos viables. Del mismo modo, si las entidades incorporan a su anlisis los riesgos derivados de la transicin ecolgica, pasan a convertirse en motor del cambio al favorecer que llegue financiacin a aquellas actividades que, adems de ser econmicamente rentables, contribuyan a la transformacin sostenible de la economa. La consideracin de los factores de sostenibilidad en las inversiones es un cambio muy relevante que ya est sucediendo. Cada vez ms entidades se estn sumando a iniciativas de banca tica o responsable, adhirindose a principios internacionales. Tambin se estn fomentando el desarrollo de los llamados bonos sostenibles, muy demandados por inversores. Conviene no olvidar que, conforme al plan de accin de la UE antes citado, para lograr los objetivos en materia de clima y energa se estima que se precisar una inversin anual de alrededor de 180.000 millones de euros durante el periodo 2021-2030. Como se suele sealar, la transicin ecolgica acarrear riesgos que el sector deber controlar y gestionar, pero tambin oportunidades que la banca debe aprovechar. Cambio tecnolgico Permtanme que me refiera brevemente a un elemento que surge cada vez que se discute el futuro del modelo de negocio bancario. Por supuesto, estoy hablando de la tecnologa. El cambio tecnolgico es un tema fundamental para afrontar el futuro pero, a la vez, es un tema que est ya totalmente presente. Debemos ser conscientes de que la adaptacin tecnolgica exige realizar significativas inversiones en sistemas, lo que es difcil en un contexto de reduccin de costes. No obstante, estas inversiones hoy sern clave para la cuenta de resultados futura. La mayora de transacciones bancarias en nuestro pas se sigue realizando a travs de cajero automtico y ventanilla, pero el porcentaje de usuarios online crece todos los aos. Conforme a esta tendencia, el potencial de ahorro de costes es significativo. Con independencia de estos potenciales ahorros de costes, lo cierto es que la tecnologa debe formar parte esencial de la reflexin sobre el modelo de negocio de las entidades y su sostenibilidad en el largo plazo. Las entidades cuentan con una fortaleza muy significativa en esta nueva era digital. Naturalmente estoy hablando de los datos de la clientela, materia prima bsica de esta cuarta revolucin industrial. Se suele hablar mucho de la parte transaccional, la calidad de las apps y la experiencia del cliente, pero, sin negar su importancia, quiero resaltar que es an ms trascendente focalizar esfuerzos en el cambio tecnolgico interno. Es esencial que las entidades sean capaces de extraer, explotar y analizar los datos de su clientela. Evidentemente esta informacin debe usarse en las decisiones sobre concesin de riesgos y en la fijacin de precios. En un entorno tan competitivo como el actual, las entidades deben discriminar cada transaccin en trminos de riesgo y coste. Es evidente que la banca precisa repercutir los costes y riesgos asumidos en cada nueva operacin, por lo que la poltica de precios debe incorporar esa informacin. Tambin es fundamental analizar la rentabilidad conjunta para cada cliente. En este campo queda muchsimo potencial de mejora. De hecho, no est totalmente demostrado que se est explotando adecuadamente la informacin para trasladar el riesgo subyacente al precio. Esta deficiencia de gestin parece ser comn para muchos bancos de la eurozona, as que, por hacer una lectura positiva, dira que nos hallaramos ante una palanca clara para mejorar la eficiencia bancaria. Como conclusin, quiero subrayar que no es lo mismo contar con la informacin que ser capaz de explotarla. Esta ltima cuestin ser crtica en el futuro. Si la banca no aprovecha esta ventaja hoy, otros competidores nuevos lo harn maana. Conclusiones Permtanme concluir. Desde 2009 el sector bancario ha atravesado un drstico proceso de reestructuracin y ajuste, una verdadera reconversin que ha permitido reducir su sobrecapacidad y purgar, en gran medida, los excesos cometidos en el periodo de acumulacin de desequilibrios que precedi al estallido de la crisis. La regulacin, supervisin y resolucin bancarias han pasado tambin por otro proceso de transformacin radical, incorporando lecciones y pasando a tener un mbito verdaderamente europeo. Se nos ha dotado a los supervisores de herramientas macroprudenciales, que deberemos usar de modo responsable y prudente. Conviene no olvidar el pasado si queremos construir un futuro mejor. La reconversin industrial result traumtica y dej profundas huellas en el Pas Vasco, algunas de las cuales son an visibles, pero permiti sentar las bases sobre las que se ha desarrollado su economa actual. Del mismo modo, el proceso traumtico que ha atravesado el sector financiero debe servir como campamento base para escalar hacia el futuro. El nuevo entorno, extremadamente competitivo y difcil, obliga a revisar el modelo de negocio bancario para responder a la nueva realidad econmica, tecnolgica, medioambiental y social. Slo as se podrn sentar unas bases slidas de futuro. Muchas gracias, Eskerrik Asko.

Title: Situation and prospects of the Spanish financial sector. XXIV Meeting of Economy S'Agar: "Where the world is going", organized by the Olof Palme International Foundation
text: 29.11.2019 Situation and prospects of the Spanish financial sector XXIV Meeting of Economy S'Agar97: "Where the world is going" International Olof Palme Foundation Margarita Delgado Subgobernadora Thank you very much for the invitation to participate in the twenty-fourth edition of the meeting of Economy SAgar97. There are 24 editions many, which is undoubtedly a sign of the importance and relevance of this meeting, although, obviously, the privileged environment in which this meeting takes place surely helps to maintain interest every year. The title of this edition is "where the world is going", consequently I will talk about the future of banking, but to talk about the future we must know our present starting point and, for this, we must understand our past. If we look 10 years ago, I think the word that would best define the situation of the banking sector would be "oversizing", caused by an excessive process of previous expansion of credit, in particular, developer credit. This excessive credit was accompanied by a significant relaxation in the concession conditions, in many cases linking it to the value of the guarantee rather than to the ability to pay. The negative effects soon appeared: an unprecedented rise in non-performing loans and a continued adjustment in the volume of credit. Consolidation As a result of these adjustments, there was a drastic process of bank consolidation. To give some figures, since 2009 there has been a reduction of more than 30% in the number of entities. The number of offices has decreased by more than 40% (about 20,000) while the number of staff has decreased by more than 30% (about 90,000 fewer employees). Although the effort has been evident, it is possible that the consolidation process cannot be completed yet, particularly when the reduction of structural costs is one of the few "levers" available to improve the income statement. Present The representatives of entities that are with us today will agree that the environment in which the banking business is developed is increasingly complicated. The need to continue with the reduction of non-performing assets is compounded by the pressure to improve solvency levels. All this in an environment of negative interest rates that pressure margins (in which it has gone from talking about "low for long" to "lower for longer"), as well as in an increasingly competitive context, with the emergence of new non-bank actors. In addition, the sector continues to drag problems of the past in the form of litigation and loss of reputation for certain past actions. All these challenges and difficulties make up a very complicated and competitive environment to which banks must respond, but how? The answer would lie in the business model of the entities. A key point of that future model is that it must be sustainable, another fundamental element refers to the central role that technology must play in it. Starting with the sustainability of the model, it is worth remembering how, before the crisis, certain banking operations were apparently very profitable; Unfortunately, that same operation produced huge losses once the crisis erupted, both in the form of insolvencies and due to conflicting judicial decisions for questionable actions. The model applied by banks before the crisis was undoubtedly profitable but, also undoubtedly, unsustainable. To summarize, short-term gains turned into massive losses in the medium and long term. Clearly, this should be a powerful reminder when looking to the future. Future How to prevent this type of short-term behavior from happening again? In my speeches I always like to refer also to two key elements: governance and customer relations. Both are long-term elements, fundamental to guarantee the sustainability of the future business although they do not imply an immediate improvement in the income statement, quite the contrary, so in an environment as complicated as the current one it is easy for them to be seen as something secondary. However, without adequate governance, banks cannot manage the conflicts of interest inherent in banking activity, among which the one between the search for short-term profit and the sustainability and viability of the entity in the long term stands out. Observing the unbridled growth of credit, and the weakening in concession standards, I think it is easy to conclude that, unfortunately, before the outbreak of the crisis, short-term incentives prevailed over long-term ones. In relation to behavior, I wanted to briefly point out two reasons why a change in the customer relationship model will be key in the medium and long term, although in the short term it implies giving up a certain type of business. On the one hand, the banking business is based on trust and reputation, which is an intangible asset, but certainly very valuable. Reputation is built over a long time but can be lost very quickly. The bank faces the challenge of recovering its image while cases from the past surface, which seems very complicated. However, it is precisely today's conduct that will cement tomorrow's reputation. Secondly, in addition to the need to recover the image, the implementation of this change is necessary from a purely economic point of view. The cost of litigation in the long term far exceeds the eventual benefit that some entities may have obtained in the short term through questionable behavior. Let me refer to the challenge of technology, which is one of the points that focus the debate of this meeting, in my opinion in a very right way. Obviously, technology is part of the response that must be given today to the growing competition of non-banking entities but it must also be part of the reflection on the business model of entities and their sustainability in the long term. To summarize it in one sentence, technology is a central element for business strategy, positioning against the competition, cost savings and improvement in risk management and profitability of operations with customers. I believe that the digital revolution has two dimensions, both very significant. On the one hand there would be the "outward" dimension which, if you will allow me the analogy, would be the tip of the iceberg that is visible externally and that, therefore, determines something as important as the perception that the clientele has of the entity. User interactivity, app quality and user experience are key aspects today, and will be even more so in the future. But, continuing with the analogy, we must not forget that about 90% of the iceberg is submerged. This hidden part is even more transcendent, since without it it is impossible for the visible 10% to work. Speaking of consolidation and mergers, it should not be forgotten that practically all current entities are the result of integration processes, and, surprising as it may seem, it is possible in many cases to still find computer applications in use that come from entities that long ago disappeared. The existence of applications without technical support, which cannot be used in the cloud and for which in some cases there is no alternative or planned replacement, is unfortunately a common reality, except of course for the so-called "neobanks". Consequently, it is key to also carry out this technological change "inward". It is public that the sector has announced large investments in this field over the next few years, which is a sign of the strategic importance of technology. Clearly, making significant investments in systems is particularly difficult in a context of cost reduction. However, these investments today will be key to the future income statement. It seems clear that in the future efficiency gains will be closely linked to technological change. Most banking transactions in our country are still carried out through ATMs and branches, however the percentage of online users grows every year. In line with this trend, the potential for cost savings in this way can be significant. In addition to all the above, there is another key aspect of the future business that also depends on technology. Of course I am talking about data, which is the basic raw material of this fourth industrial revolution. It is often said that the interest of the so-called bigtech in banking has more to do with data than with the banking business itself, hence the potential threat implied by the entry of the PSD2 directive, but, to verify a no-brainer, it is the entities that have the data at the moment. However, if banks do not take advantage of this advantage today, other new competitors will do so tomorrow. In this sense, it is not the same to have the information than to be able to exploit it. Access to information is useless if banks do not extract, exploit and analyse their customers' data in their day-to-day management and, in particular, in the granting of operations and pricing. In an environment such as the current one, the granting of operations at a loss is not viable. It is necessary to discriminate each transaction in terms of risk and cost. This point is both worrying and hopeful. Worrying because, based on preliminary analyses of the European supervisor, for practically the entire sector, there would be no correlation between the price of operations and their underlying risk. Hopeful, because the bad starting situation allows us to have another 'lever' to improve efficiency and gain in profitability, a real workhorse of the sector in the current rate environment. One last challenge for the future that I do not want to fail to mention is the environmental one. I would like to point out two things: on the one hand, the consideration of sustainability factors in the granting of credit is a very relevant change that we are actively promoting from the supervisors and that the entities are gradually incorporating. More and more banks are joining ethical or responsible banking initiatives, adhering to international principles, and supervisors are making an important effort to adapt our analytical structures and methodologies to cover this change. On the other hand, in addition to the risks that the sector will have to control and manage, the ecological transition also implies opportunities that banks must take advantage of. To give a concrete example, according to the EU action plan on sustainable finance, it is estimated that an annual investment of around db180 billion over the period 2021-2030 will be required to achieve the climate and energy objectives. Thanks a lot. I am sure that in the round of questions we will have the opportunity to delve into these and other issues that my fellow panelists have pointed out.
text_original: 29.11.2019 Situacin y perspectivas del sector financiero espaol XXIV Encuentro de Economa SAgar: Hacia dnde va el mundo Fundacin Internacional Olof Palme Margarita Delgado Subgobernadora Muchas gracias por la invitacin para participar en la vigesimocuarta edicin del encuentro de Economa SAgar. 24 ediciones son muchas, lo que sin duda es signo de la importancia y relevancia de este encuentro, aunque, evidentemente, el entorno privilegiado en el que se desarrolla este encuentro seguro que ayuda a mantener el inters cada ao. El ttulo de esta edicin es hacia dnde va el mundo, en consecuencia voy a hablar del futuro de la banca, pero para hablar del futuro debemos conocer nuestro punto de partida presente y, para ello, debemos entender nuestro pasado. Si nos situamos hace 10 aos, creo que la palabra que definira mejor la situacin del sector bancario sera sobredimensionamiento, causado por un proceso excesivo de expansin previo del crdito, en particular, el crdito promotor. Este excesivo crdito vino acompaado de una relajacin importante en las condiciones de concesin, en muchos casos ligndolo al valor de la garanta en vez de a la capacidad de pago. Los efectos negativos no tardaron en aparecer: repunte sin precedentes de la morosidad y ajuste continuado en el volumen de crdito. Consolidacin Como consecuencia de estos ajustes se produjo un drstico proceso de consolidacin bancaria. Por dar algunas cifras, desde 2009 ha habido una reduccin de ms de un 30 % en el nmero de entidades. El nmero de oficinas ha disminuido en ms de un 40 % (unas 20.000) mientras que el personal ha descendido ms de un 30 % (unos 90.000 empleados menos). Pese a que el esfuerzo ha sido evidente, es posible que el proceso de consolidacin no se pueda dar todava por finalizado, particularmente cuando la reduccin de costes de estructura es una de las pocas palancas disponibles para mejorar la cuenta de resultados. Presente Los representantes de entidades que nos acompaan hoy coincidirn en que el entorno en que se desarrolla el negocio bancario es cada vez ms complicado. A la necesidad de continuar con la reduccin de activos no productivos se une la presin por mejorar los niveles de solvencia. Todo ello en un entorno de tipos de inters negativos que presionan los mrgenes (en el que se ha pasado de hablar del low for long al lower for longer), as como en un contexto crecientemente competitivo, con la irrupcin de nuevos actores no bancarios. Adems, el sector sigue arrastrando problemas del pasado en forma de litigiosidad y prdida de reputacin por determinadas actuaciones pretritas. Todos estos retos y dificultades configuran un entorno muy complicado y competitivo al que debe responder la banca, pero cmo? La respuesta estara en el modelo de negocio de las entidades. Un punto clave de ese modelo futuro es que debe ser sostenible, otro elemento fundamental se refiere al papel central que la tecnologa debe jugar en l. Empezando por la sostenibilidad del modelo, conviene recordar cmo, antes de la crisis, determinada operativa bancaria era en apariencia muy rentable; desgraciadamente, esa misma operativa produjo enormes prdidas una vez que la crisis estall, tanto en forma de insolvencias como debido a resoluciones judiciales contrarias por actuaciones cuestionables. El modelo aplicado por las entidades antes de la crisis era, sin duda, rentable pero, tambin sin duda, insostenible. Por resumir, los beneficios del corto plazo se convirtieron en prdidas masivas en el medio y largo plazo. Evidentemente, esto debe constituir un poderoso recordatorio a la hora de mirar hacia el futuro. Futuro Cmo evitar que este tipo de comportamientos cortoplacistas vuelvan a ocurrir? En mis intervenciones me gusta siempre referirme tambin a dos elementos claves: la gobernanza y la relacin con la clientela. Ambos son elementos de largo plazo, fundamentales para garantizar la sostenibilidad del negocio futura aunque no impliquen una mejora inmediata en la cuenta de resultados, antes bien al contrario, por lo que en un entorno tan complicado como el actual es fcil que se vean como algo secundario. Sin embargo, sin una adecuada gobernanza, las entidades no pueden gestionar los conflictos de inters inherentes a la actividad bancaria, entre los que destaca el que se produce entre la bsqueda de beneficio a corto plazo y la sostenibilidad y viabilidad de la entidad en el largo plazo. Observando el crecimiento desaforado del crdito, y el debilitamiento en los estndares de concesin, creo que es fcil concluir que, lamentablemente, antes del estallido de la crisis los incentivos del corto plazo prevalecieron frente a los del largo. En relacin a la conducta, quera sealar brevemente dos razones por las que un cambio en el modelo de relacin con la clientela resultar clave a medio y largo plazo, aunque en el corto implique renunciar a determinado tipo de negocio. Por un lado, el negocio bancario se basa en la confianza y reputacin, que es un activo intangible, pero ciertamente muy valioso. La reputacin se construye a lo largo de mucho tiempo pero se puede perder muy rpidamente. La banca se enfrenta al reto de recuperar su imagen mientras afloran casos del pasado, lo que parece muy complicado. No obstante, es precisamente la conducta de hoy la que permitir cimentar la reputacin de maana. En segundo lugar, adems de la necesidad de recuperar la imagen, la implementacin de este cambio es necesario desde un punto de vista meramente econmico. El coste de la litigiosidad a largo plazo sobrepasa con creces el eventual beneficio que algunas entidades pudieran haber obtenido en el corto plazo a travs de comportamientos cuestionables. Djenme referirme al reto de la tecnologa, que es uno de los puntos que centran el debate de este encuentro, a mi juicio de modo muy acertado. Evidentemente la tecnologa forma parte de la respuesta que se debe dar hoy ante la creciente competencia de entidades no bancarias pero tambin debe formar parte de la reflexin sobre el modelo de negocio de las entidades y su sostenibilidad en el largo plazo. Por resumirlo en una frase, la tecnologa es un elemento central para la estrategia de negocio, el posicionamiento frente a la competencia, el ahorro de costes y la mejora en la gestin de los riesgos y rentabilidad de las operaciones con la clientela. Creo que la revolucin digital tiene dos dimensiones, ambas muy significativas. Por un lado estara la dimensin hacia fuera que, si me permiten la analoga, sera la punta del iceberg que es visible exteriormente y que, por tanto, determina algo tan importante como la percepcin que la clientela tiene de la entidad. La interactividad con el usuario, la calidad de las apps y la experiencia de usuario son aspectos claves hoy, y lo sern an ms en el futuro. Pero, siguiendo con la analoga, no hay que olvidar que cerca del 90 % del iceberg est sumergido. Esta parte oculta es ms trascendente si cabe, dado que sin ella es imposible que el 10 % visible funcione. Hablando de consolidacin y fusiones, conviene no olvidar que prcticamente todas las entidades actuales son el resultado de procesos de integracin, y, por sorprendente que pueda parecer, resulta posible en muchos casos encontrar todava aplicaciones informticas en uso que provienen de entidades que hace tiempo desaparecieron. La existencia de aplicaciones sin soporte tcnico, que no se pueden utilizar en la nube y para las que en algunos casos no hay alternativa ni recambio planificado, es lamentablemente una realidad comn, salvo por supuesto para los llamados neobancos. En consecuencia, es clave llevar tambin a cabo este cambio tecnolgico hacia adentro. Es pblico que el sector ha anunciado grandes inversiones en este campo a lo largo de los prximos aos, lo que es seal de la importancia estratgica de la tecnologa. Evidentemente, la realizacin de significativas inversiones en sistemas es particularmente difcil en un contexto de reduccin de costes. No obstante, estas inversiones hoy sern clave para la cuenta de resultados futura. Parece claro que en el futuro las ganancias de eficiencia estarn muy ligadas al cambio tecnolgico. La mayora de transacciones bancarias en nuestro pas se sigue realizando a travs de cajero y oficina, no obstante el porcentaje de usuarios online crece todos los aos. Conforme a esta tendencia, el potencial de ahorro de costes por esta va puede ser significativo. Adems de todo lo sealado anteriormente hay otro aspecto clave del negocio futuro que depende tambin de la tecnologa. Por supuesto hablo de los datos, que son la materia prima bsica de esta cuarta revolucin industrial. Se suele afirmar que el inters de las llamadas bigtech por la banca tiene ms que ver con los datos que con el negocio bancario en s, de ah la potencial amenaza que implica la entrada de la directiva PSD2, pero, por constatar una obviedad, son las entidades las que cuentan con los datos en estos momentos. No obstante, si la banca no aprovecha esta ventaja hoy, otros competidores nuevos lo harn maana. En este sentido, no es lo mismo contar con la informacin que ser capaz de explotarla. De nada sirve el acceso a la informacin si los bancos no extraen, explotan y analizan los datos de su clientela en su gestin diaria y, en particular, en la concesin de operaciones y fijacin de precios. En un entorno como el actual no es viable la concesin de operaciones a prdida. Se precisa discriminar cada transaccin en trminos de riesgo y coste. Este punto es a la vez preocupante y esperanzador. Preocupante porque, en base a anlisis preliminares del supervisor europeo, para prcticamente todo el sector, no existira correlacin entre el precio de las operaciones y su riesgo subyacente. Esperanzador, porque la mala situacin de partida nos permite contar con otra palanca para mejorar la eficiencia y ganar en rentabilidad, verdadero caballo de batalla del sector en el entorno de tipos actual. Un ltimo reto de futuro que no quiero dejar de citar es el medioambiental. Quiero sealar dos cosas: por un lado, la consideracin de los factores de sostenibilidad en la concesin de crdito es un cambio muy relevante que estamos fomentando activamente desde los supervisores y que las entidades van poco a poco incorporando. Cada vez ms entidades se estn sumando a iniciativas de banca tica o responsable, adhirindose a principios internacionales, y los supervisores estamos haciendo un esfuerzo importante en adaptar nuestras estructuras anlisis y metodologas para cubrir este cambio. Por otro, adems de los riesgos que el sector deber controlar y gestionar, la transicin ecolgica implica tambin oportunidades que la banca debe aprovechar. Por poner un ejemplo concreto, conforme al plan de accin de la UE sobre finanzas sostenibles, se estima que se precisar una inversin anual de alrededor de 180.000 M. de euros durante el periodo 2021-2030 para lograr los objetivos en materia de clima y energa. Muchas gracias. Estoy segura que en la ronda de preguntas tendremos oportunidad de profundizar en estos y otros temas que han sealado mis compaeros de panel.

Title: Intervention at the informative breakfast: "The European Banking Union". Club Dilogos para la Democracia. Dialogues for Democracy Club
text: 14.01.2020 "The European Banking Union" Dialogues for Democracy Club Margarita Delgado Deputy Governor Good morning Thank you very much Miguel for your kind words of introduction and, of course, to Unicaja and the Dialogues for Democracy club, in particular its president Antonio Gavilanes, for their invitation to participate in this colloquium today. As you know better than I do, Dialogues for Democracy was founded in 1976, as a forum for debate that sought to provide solutions and ideas to the multiple problems that arose in a society that, at that time, was in transition to democracy. Obviously, societies are evolving, and new problems arise that we must face, so this type of forum is still as necessary today as it was then. Undoubtedly, in the time that has elapsed since our democratic transition, one of the most important historical milestones was our entry into the then called European Economic Community, on January 1, 1986, that is, more than 34 years ago. As I say, the importance of this milestone in shaping our society and our economy is enormous. Despite this importance, I believe that knowledge in Spanish society of the institutions and the European regulatory framework is, in many cases, scarce. For this reason, I am very grateful for this opportunity to discuss a European project that I consider very relevant, the Banking Union. Let me start by acknowledging that this is an issue on which I am somewhat biased. As many of you know, 5 years ago I had the privilege of participating in the creation of the Single Supervisory Mechanism (SSM), which is one of the central, although certainly not the only, elements of this Banking Union. I say that this experience was a privilege, because it is very rare to be able to participate in the creation of a new body from scratch. The SSM is made up of people from the 28 countries of the Union (i.e. not just the 19 in the Eurozone), each with their own culture, language and way of approaching supervisory work. As you can imagine, the task of achieving a single monitoring framework is not easy when starting from such diverse points of view. Adopting a new culture and new supervisory practices implies renouncing practices that we considered as our own, accepting that, possibly, other methodological approaches may be more appropriate, which is not easy. Despite these difficulties, I believe that in these 5 years we have managed to move towards truly European supervision. Although there is still a long way to go, in my opinion, the result to date is very positive. In the ensuing debate we may be able to delve into what the SSM has meant to date for our work as supervisors and for the functioning of the European banking sector, but, as the title of this paper rightly says, I now intend to go beyond the SSM to talk about the Banking Union project. In particular, I wanted to reflect with you on the reasons that motivated the launch of this project and what it has meant to date, in terms of safeguarding the euro. and greater integration, but I also intend to cover those elements that, in my opinion, are lacking in order to achieve an integrated, truly European and cross-border banking sector. On the other hand, I will refer to an even broader objective, that of achieving a real 'Financial Union', of which the Banking Union would be part, but which would encompass other elements, such as the so-called 'Capital Markets Union'. European integration I think it is fair to point out that, since its creation, the EU project has improved the lives of millions of European citizens, not only in economic terms, but also in terms of rights and living standards throughout the Union. Of course, the success of this common project cannot be evaluated solely in terms of its economic performance, but we must also consider its other initial objectives, namely to increase the level of political integration, to promote peace, its values and the well-being of its peoples. Something that should not be forgotten is that the European Union was born with the aim of ending armed conflicts between neighbouring countries, after the horror of two World Wars. The creation in the 50s of the European Coal and Steel Community was the first step of an economic and political union of European countries, with the ultimate goal of ensuring a lasting peace. The success in achieving this original objective was reflected in the awarding of the Nobel Peace Prize to the European Union in 2012 for 'having contributed over six decades to the advancement of peace and reconciliation, democracy and human rights in Europe'. I believe that, in reality, the objectives of ensuring peace and promoting integration and economic development are related. As the World Trade Organization reminds us, the trade war unleashed during the Great Depression contributed to the outbreak of the Second World War. In this sense, a very positive consequence of trade between nations is that it contributes to transforming "rival" nations into "partners", which share interests, instead of having conflicting interests. Undoubtedly, since the founding of the European Coal and Steel Community in 1952, the economic and political integration of the EU has reached very remarkable levels, although the process has not been linear, nor gradual. During its almost seven decades of history, the European project has gone through long periods of stillness in which little or nothing remarkable happened, interrupted by 'transformative periods', which have contributed decisively to its development and its current configuration. Normally, these profound transformations have been the result of long reflective and negotiating processes, being carried out in a more or less orderly manner. Introduction of the single market and the euro For example, the launch of the Single Market was the result of lengthy negotiations that officially began in 1985, although the idea had already been set as an objective since the European Community was founded in the Treaty of Rome in 1957. Circulating, trading, establishing or providing services in any EU country seems obvious today but the single market did not come into force until 1993. As most of the things that seem obvious to us, we may not be valued in their proper measure, but certainly the free movement of goods, capital, services and people is one of the EU's great achievements. At the beginning of the process, in 1985, some 300 measures were identified to achieve this objective. A whole series of internal barriers and borders were progressively disappearing. Changes were introduced in the decision-making mechanisms to achieve progress, introducing qualified majority voting as opposed to the unanimity required until then. A minimum rather than total harmonisation of national regulations was chosen, which are now recognised as equivalent between the partners. The history of the single market shows that, as Voltaire said, the perfect is often the enemy of the good. The lack of progress in completing the single market before 1985 was undoubtedly due to anti-competitive practices maintained by national authorities, but also to the difficulty of reaching unanimous agreements in the Council and the search for too detailed legislative harmonisation. The situation was unblocked after opting for objectives that, a priori, were less ambitious. In fact, certain administrative barriers persist, for example in the area of the provision of professional services, so we could not even consider the single market to be completed. In addition, the creation of the single currency has meant another key transformation on the road to greater integration. The euro represents the most ambitious process of economic integration in the world since the end of World War II. It was in Maastricht in 92, just before the entry into force of the single market, that 12 Member States decided to exceed this initial economic objective and plan a monetary union. Like the single market, the euro was also the result of lengthy debates, negotiations and preparatory phases, which were not always fully successful, in fact opt-out clauses of the Economic and Monetary Union had to be established for the United Kingdom and Denmark. Despite these difficulties, the euro was introduced in 1999 and, following the introduction of euro banknotes and coins in 2002, has been a tangible reality for all citizens. In fact, according to the latest Eurobarometer, its popularity is at an all-time high in all 19 eurozone countries1. 1 74% of citizens are in favour of the Euro. Creation of the SSM and the SRB However, although the introduction of the euro was seen as a success, it is clear that its institutional design suffered from certain problems which the crisis that erupted a decade ago clearly revealed. Twenty years ago, Christian Noyer pointed out that the introduction of the euro should act as a catalyst for further reform and further integration. Ultimately, the reforms took place, as predicted by the then Vice-President of the ECB, but I think it is fair to conclude that further integration was, de facto, a precondition for the proper functioning of the euro, rather than a consequence of it. It was the crisis that led to the realization that there was a need for a common and strengthened framework for banking supervision and resolution that would help break the link between banking risk and sovereign risk. As is known2, this link is reciprocal and feeds back. On the one hand, in a context of banking crisis, the combination of states' support for their national banking systems and lower tax revenues put pressure on public finances, deteriorating the solvency of the country itself. On the other hand, banks' high exposure to their country's sovereign debt compromises their own solvency, which can raise recapitalization needs. Memory is somewhat fragile, so I would like to emphasize the magnitude of that crisis. To give some data, the spreads demanded by Greek sovereign debt exceeded 1,500 basis points in June 2011, while those of Portugal and Ireland were around 700. As you know, the crisis hit Spain hard a year later, in July 2012 the market demanded more than 7% to finance us for 10 years. We must therefore recognise that, unlike the single market or the adoption of the euro, the Banking Union was not the fruit of a vision shared by EU leaders on the need to improve banking supervision and resolution across the eurozone, but the result of bold, if defensive, reactions. to preserve the single currency in the context of the financial and sovereign debt crisis that threatened to break up the euro. As a result, the creation of the Single Supervisory Mechanism (SSM) was formalized in 2014, while in January 2015 the Single Resolution Board (SRB) became operational, which, for now, are the key components of this Banking Union3. Today, the reasons for the creation of the SSM and the SRB seem obvious, although before the outbreak of the European sovereign crisis, few pointed to the risks arising from a fragmented banking supervision environment in the euro area. These institutional weaknesses are perfectly reflected in the so-called 'Five Presidents' Report'4, published in June 2015, which indicates the pending measures to achieve the completion of the European Economic and Monetary Union. 2 See for example Reinhart and Rogoff, 2011 3 Another important development related to the Single Resolution Mechanism materialised in December 2018, when the European Stability Mechanism was recognised as a backstop to the Single Resolution Fund, both for solvency and liquidity 4 The report rightly points out that, since the vast majority of money is created through bank deposits, the currency can only be truly unique if confidence in the safety of such deposits is the same regardless of the Member State in which a bank operates. EDIS as the third pillar of the banking union I think this phrase perfectly sums up a fundamental problem of the Euro. A common currency must reflect a single financial system; therefore, the same euro deposited in different banks must have the same support and confidence, regardless of the Eurozone country in which each entity is domiciled. In this respect, the implementation of the SSM and the SRB is an important achievement, but we must recognise that as long as deposits do not have identical support throughout the Banking Union, we cannot consider the building to be completed. It is well known that we still lack one of its three fundamental pillars, the European Deposit Insurance Scheme (EDIS). Any construction requires at least three pillars to ensure its structural strength. Similarly, I believe that EDIS would contribute to increasing the stability of the Banking Union, particularly in times of stress, when the resilience of structures is put to the test. EDIS would have a strong impact on citizens' confidence, but in addition, the increased degree of risk mutualisation in the euro area would help align financial responsibility with the pan-European decision-making process, which has already been put in place in the areas of banking supervision and resolution. The current situation is such that the ultimate backstop for securing deposits in a failed institution depends on national institutions, while responsibility for supervision and resolution lies with other pan-European institutions. Shortly after the outbreak of the financial crisis, Mervin King ironically pointed out that international banks tended to be global in life, but always ended up being national at their death. This phrase still seems to be applicable in the Eurozone. In a true banking union, banks should be a European issue, both during their lifetime and in their death. As you know, the debate on EDIS was revived in November last year, due to an article5 by German Finance Minister Olaf Scholz, in which he advocated its implementation, which, in his own words, was 'no small step for a German finance minister'. Of course, the German proposal referred to the introduction of a European reinsurance scheme instead of a fully mutualised EDIS, in addition to being subject to various conditions. In any case, it is clear that the debate is still open and differences persist between the various European partners, but I hope and hope that, as on previous occasions, 5 Ver FT Let us achieve a consensus that will allow us to finalize this third basic pillar, introducing a truly common EDIS, and therefore fully mutualised. European banking consolidation and integration Let me now turn to the degree of integration of the European banking sector. I have already indicated that the Banking Union has fulfilled one of its key objectives: to help weaken the link between banking risk and sovereign risk but, additionally, when it was launched it was assumed that the Union should lead to a more integrated banking system. However, so far, the increased degree of institutional integration has not been accompanied by an increase in cross-border activity in the sector. The share of domestically owned banks in national banking systems remains high, at around 83%, the same level as in 2014, prior to the establishment of the SSM.6 We must therefore recognise that bank consolidation across jurisdictions remains minimal, and most companies and individuals in the eurozone continue to rely on their national financial systems. Economic operators can see on a daily basis the benefits of the single market and the euro, but unfortunately, there are currently no tangible benefits, in terms of increased price competition and financial services, from the Banking Union. The reality is that European citizens and businesses still face barriers to investing in European markets. Pensioners and domestic investors have access to different investment products and their rights differ as a result of different local insolvency laws. Finally, I have already pointed out that the banking sector remains mainly national, and remains closely linked to its sovereign risk. The fact that there are no cross-border mergers is seen by many as proof that we still have a long way to go in terms of market integration and diversification. In any case, the lack of cross-border consolidation is symptomatic, particularly in a context of clear overcapacity of the European banking sector. In relation to this issue, it should be noted that, in its latest stability report7, the ECB has published a study on the degree of overcapacity of the sector in Europe and its potential implications for the banking business. According to the conclusions of this study, excess capacity can lead to operating below margins in the face of very high competition, which would make it impossible to make investments necessary for the future of the entity and its adaptation to new technologies and new operators, such as systems, creating a kind of 'zombie banks' that drag the profitability of the sector even lower. 6 CGFS (2018) 7 Financial Stability Review d0 noviembre 2019 The study points to those entities that present a return on equity (RoE) below the median of 6% for 3 years, but the most worrying group would be that of entities with a profitability of less than 3%, no less than around 25% of the total. The study concludes with the need to face restructurings and mergers, showing a clear preference for pan-European mergers (cross-border) over national ones. In relation to the always controversial issue of mergers, I have already said on several occasions that our role as supervisors is not to decide which mergers are desirable and which are not, but to assess to what extent a merger process creates a more solvent entity with a more solid business model, allowing to reduce structural costs in a significant way and, in short, generating value as a whole. In my opinion, the lack of cross-border mergers can be partially explained by the overcapacity and fragmentation of the financial sector in Europe. Indeed, the benefits of synergies, potential cost reductions and efficiency gains are mainly seen in mergers between entities in the same country, thanks to the elimination of duplication in branches and central services. In this sense, the radical consolidation process that the Spanish banking system has carried out since 2009 is well known. To give some figures, there has been a reduction of more than 30% in the number of entities. The number of offices has decreased by more than 40 per cent (about 20,000) while the number of staff has decreased by more than 30 per cent (about 90,000 less). However, given the extremely competitive environment in which we operate, I would like to stress that the map of national mergers may not yet be closed, particularly when the reduction of structural costs is one of the few 'levers' available to improve the income statement. In the case of most cross-border mergers, economic rationality is more difficult to justify, although there would be potential gains in competitiveness for those entities that have a business model that allows vertical savings. However, as the ECB points out in its study, in addition to the potential reduction in costs, there is another aspect to consider in bank consolidation: the improvement of geographical diversification, both from the point of view of revenues and the risks assumed. I fully agree with this conclusion of the study. Certainly, cross-border mergers have the advantage of increasing diversification, which undoubtedly improves resilience in times of stress and allows for greater stability and recurrence of revenues, as was evident during the last crisis. In this sense, I believe that the lack of explicit recognition of diversification as a risk-reducing factor may be a factor that is limiting this type of transnational integration. It may be useful to reflect in depth at European and international level on the regulatory treatment of diversification, and its potential beneficial effect on the risk profile of institutions. In any case, it is important to note that mergers are always long and complex processes and, in many cases, lead to more problems than initially anticipated. On the other hand, national barriers persist that hinder mergers of entities from different jurisdictions. Persistence of national barriers We must admit that, despite progress, there are still certain cultural, institutional and regulatory obstacles that hinder the creation of a truly European banking market. The resistance to removing these obstacles contributes significantly to maintaining national barriers (ring fencing), which limit or even prevent the free movement of capital or liquidity between the different jurisdictions of the Eurozone. In my view, after achieving a significant reduction in risks in the financial sector, the time has come to urge an end to these national supervisory barriers, which are detrimental to financial integration and therefore limit the ambition of the Banking Union as a single jurisdiction. It does not seem reasonable that the implications, in terms of capital and liquidity, for a banking group that has a subsidiary in a Latin American country are very similar to those that would exist if the subsidiary were located in another Eurozone country. Naturally, the full introduction of a truly European deposit insurance scheme would complement and greatly facilitate this progress in integration. On the other hand, from a regulatory perspective, the absence of a sufficiently homogeneous legal basis in the euro area stands out. Just as certain national rules needed to be harmonised, or recognised as equivalent, in order to enable the creation of the single market, certain rules that impede the development of a truly single financial services market need to be changed. Full harmonization may not be possible, but it is probably not necessary. There are some critical areas, such as anti-money laundering, fitness rules and insolvency rules in banks, where a common set of rules across the euro area would boost market integration, which would also improve the efficiency of supervision and resolution. The importance of ending these barriers and harmonizing regulations is also gaining prominence. In fact, in the aforementioned article, the German finance minister also refers to the need for a common insolvency framework for all banks in the Eurozone, while acknowledging the existence of national barriers, which should be removed to avoid a fragmented financial market. Financial union Allow me to look beyond the Banking Union in the final part of my speech, to refer to Financial Union. I have already pointed out the importance of introducing a genuine deposit insurance scheme, removing national barriers and harmonising certain regulatory areas but, in addition, other elements are needed to make further progress towards a genuine Financial Union. In this regard, the development of deep and integrated capital markets undoubtedly strengthens the euro area's capacity to cushion macro-financial shocks. Of course, I am talking about the Capital Markets Union (CMU), a project that would complement the Banking Union, promoting a cross-border financial sector that allows economic agents to mitigate asymmetric national shocks. The Capital Markets Union project was launched in 2015 with the aim of 'unlocking financing for Europe's growth', i.e. favouring not only the development but also the integration of European capital markets with the ultimate aim of diversifying available sources of finance. However, the project has languished until recently. Proof of this would be the fact that the year scheduled for its entry into operation was, originally, 2019. Obviously, this objective has not been achieved, although the importance of this project has only increased since 2015, particularly in the context of Brexit. Although somewhat paradoxical given the slow pace of progress, the objectives of attracting institutional investors, improving resource allocation, introducing a safe European asset and strengthening the international role of the euro are more relevant than ever. Although limited, at least some progress has been made. For example, most of the work in terms of harmonising investment and savings products across the EU has already been agreed, including the definition of a pan-European personal pension product. However, the complexity of the project requires greater efforts at regulatory and fiscal harmonization, particularly in relation to capital taxes. Among other things, there are still more than 90 types of forms in different languages for tax refunds in the EU. It may seem inconsequential, but these administrative hurdles are often mentioned as a major obstacle to investment by market participants. In this context, it is noteworthy the report published in October 2019, during the Finnish presidency, of the so-calledNext CMU group'8, formed by high-level representatives of the industry who, at the request of EU finance ministers, have evaluated the progress of this project, proposing a series of measures to relaunch it9. 8 9 The report also suggests renaming the project the 'Sustainable Savings and Investment Union', which emphasises the role of financing in fostering the transition to a more sustainable economy. Conclusion Let me conclude. Throughout its history, the EU has progressed towards a higher level of economic and political integration which has brought clear social and economic benefits. However, the pace of progress has not been steady. The analysis of some of the main achievements of the Union, such as the creation of the single market or the euro, tells us that it is often better to be pragmatic and move forward with less ambitious solutions, rather than persist in the deadlock when we cannot reach the perfect agreement. The Banking Union is an important step in this direction and has been key to tackling the euro crisis, even though the absence of a European deposit insurance scheme reminds us that the process is not over. On the other hand, it is necessary to introduce certain regulatory and institutional elements to obtain the economic benefits resulting from an increase in cross-border banking activity, thus achieving a true 'Financial Union'. As the Five Presidents' Report, to which I referred earlier, points out: 'Economic and Monetary Union is like a house built over several decades, but only partially finished. When the storm raged, its walls and roof had to be quickly stabilized. Now it's time to strengthen its foundations." I think this sentence illustrates very well what the reform process is like on many occasions in the EU. It is in the middle of the storm when the political pressure rises to undertake the reforms that allow to prevent the house from collapsing, however, we will agree that the best time to undertake this type of work is when the sun is in the sky. In assessing our capacity to deal with future financial crises, we must not forget that the institutional framework has not yet been completed. Certainly, the foundations are not fully strengthened, and we must avoid complacency. We cannot forget that, as memories of the crisis fade, political pressure to undertake reforms also tends to fade. Thanks a lot.
text_original: 14.01.2020 La Unin Bancaria Europea Club Dilogos para la Democracia Margarita Delgado Subgobernadora Buenos das Muchas gracias Miguel por tus amables palabras de presentacin y, por supuesto, a Unicaja y al club Dilogos para la Democracia, en particular a su presidente Antonio Gavilanes, por su invitacin para participar hoy en este coloquio. En el debate posterior quiz podamos profundizar en lo que, hasta la fecha, ha significado el MUS para nuestro trabajo como supervisores y para el funcionamiento del sector bancario europeo, pero, como bien dice el ttulo de esta ponencia, ahora pretendo ir ms all del MUS para hablar del proyecto de la Unin Bancaria. Construccin europea Creo que es justo sealar que, desde su creacin, el proyecto de la UE ha mejorado la vida de millones de ciudadanos europeos, no solo en trminos econmicos, sino tambin en lo que respecta a los derechos y los niveles de vida en toda la Unin. Creo que, en realidad, los objetivos de garantizar la paz y fomentar la integracin y el desarrollo econmico estn relacionados. Como bien nos recuerda la Organizacin Mundial del Comercio, la guerra comercial desencadenada durante la Gran Depresin contribuy a que estallara la segunda guerra mundial. Sin duda, desde la fundacin de la Comunidad Europea del Carbn y del Acero en 1952, la integracin econmica y poltica de la UE ha alcanzado niveles muy notables, aunque el proceso no ha sido lineal, ni tampoco gradual. Durante sus casi siete dcadas de historia, el proyecto europeo ha atravesado largos perodos de quietud en los que poco o nada destacable suceda, interrumpidos por perodos transformadores, que han contribuido de manera decisiva a su desarrollo y a su configuracin actual. Normalmente, estas profundas transformaciones han sido resultado de largos procesos reflexivos y negociadores, llevndose a cabo de manera ms o menos ordenada. Introduccin del mercado nico y del euro Por ejemplo, la puesta en marcha del Mercado nico fue el fruto de largas negociaciones que se iniciaron oficialmente en 1985, aunque la idea ya se haba planteado como objetivo desde que se fundara la Comunidad Europea en el Tratado de Roma en 1957.
