Como la mayor parte de las cosas que nos parecen evidentes quiz tendamos no se valore en su justa medida, pero, ciertamente, la libre circulacin de bienes, capital, servicios y personas constituye uno de los grandes logros de la UE. Al inicio del proceso, en 1985, se identificaron alrededor de 300 medidas para lograr la consecucin de este objetivo. Toda una serie de barreras y fronteras interiores fueron desapareciendo progresivamente. Se introdujeron cambios en los mecanismos decisorios para lograr avanzar, introduciendo la mayora cualificada frente a la unanimidad requerida hasta ese momento. Se opt por una armonizacin mnima, antes que total, de normativas nacionales, que pasan a ser reconocidas como equivalentes entre los socios. La historia del mercado nico demuestra que, como afirm Voltaire, lo perfecto es en muchas ocasiones enemigo de lo bueno. La falta de avances en la consecucin del mercado nico antes de 1985 se debi sin duda a prcticas anticompetitivas mantenidas por autoridades nacionales, pero tambin a la dificultad de alcanzar acuerdos por unanimidad en el Consejo y a la bsqueda de una armonizacin legislativa demasiado minuciosa. La situacin se desbloque tras optar por unos objetivos que, a priori, eran menos ambiciosos. De hecho, determinadas barreras administrativas persisten, por ejemplo en el mbito de la prestacin de servicios profesionales, por lo que ni siquiera podramos considerar que el mercado nico est finalizado. Adicionalmente, la creacin de la moneda nica ha supuesto otra transformacin clave en el camino hacia una mayor integracin. El euro representa el proceso de integracin econmica ms ambicioso del mundo desde que finaliz la Segunda Guerra Mundial. Fue en Maastricht en el ao 92, justo antes de la entrada en vigor del mercado nico, cuando 12 Estados miembros decidieron sobrepasar este objetivo econmico inicial y planificar una unin monetaria. Al igual que el mercado nico, el euro fue tambin el resultado de prolongados debates, negociaciones y fases preparatorias, que no siempre fueron plenamente exitosas, de hecho hubo que establecer clusulas de opt out de la Unin Econmica y Monetaria para Reino Unido y Dinamarca. Pese a estas dificultades, el euro se introdujo en 1999 y, tras la puesta en circulacin de los billetes y monedas en euros en 2002, ha sido una realidad tangible para todos los ciudadanos. De hecho, conforme al ltimo Eurobarmetro, su popularidad se encuentra en un nivel mximo en los 19 pases de la eurozona1. 1 El 74% de los ciudadanos se muestra a favor del Euro. Creacin del MUS y de la JUR No obstante, pese a que la introduccin del euro se consider como un xito, es evidente que su diseo institucional adoleca de determinados problemas que la crisis que estall hace una dcada puso claramente de manifiesto. Hace veinte aos, Christian Noyer seal que la introduccin del euro deba actuar como un catalizador de nuevas reformas y de mayor integracin. En ltima instancia, las reformas tuvieron lugar, tal y como predijo el entonces vicepresidente del BCE, pero creo justo concluir que la mayor integracin era, de facto, una precondicin para el correcto funcionamiento del euro, ms que una consecuencia del mismo. Fue la crisis la que llev al convencimiento de que era necesario contar con un marco comn y reforzado para la supervisin y la resolucin bancarias que ayudara a romper el vnculo entre riesgo bancario y riesgo soberano. Como es conocido2, este vnculo es recproco y se retroalimenta. Por un lado, en un contexto de crisis bancaria, la combinacin del apoyo de los estados a sus sistemas bancarios nacionales y los menores ingresos fiscales ejercen presin sobre las finanzas pblicas, deteriorando la solvencia del propio pas. Por otro, la elevada exposicin de los bancos a la deuda soberana de su pas, compromete su propia solvencia, lo que puede elevar las necesidades de recapitalizacin. La memoria es un tanto frgil, por lo que me gustara recalcar la magnitud de aquella crisis. Por dar unos datos, los diferenciales exigidos por la deuda soberana griega superaban los 1.500 puntos bsicos en junio de 2011, mientras que los de Portugal e Irlanda rondaban los 700. Como saben, la crisis golpe de lleno a Espaa un ao ms tarde, en julio de 2012 el mercado exiga ms de un 7% para financiarnos a 10 aos. Por tanto, debemos reconocer que, a diferencia del mercado nico o de la adopcin del euro, la Unin Bancaria no fue el fruto de una visin compartida por los lderes de la UE sobre la necesidad de mejorar la supervisin y la resolucin bancarias en toda la eurozona, sino el resultado de las reacciones, audaces, si bien defensivas, para preservar la moneda nica en el contexto de la crisis financiera y de deuda soberana que amenazaba con romper el euro. Como consecuencia, en 2014 se oficializ la creacin del mecanismo nico de supervisin (MUS), mientras que en enero de 2015 comenz a funcionar la Junta nica de resolucin (JUR) que, por ahora, son los componentes clave de esta Unin Bancaria3. Hoy en da, las razones que justificaron la creacin del MUS y de la JUR parecen obvias, aunque antes del estallido de la crisis soberana europea, pocos sealaron los riesgos derivados de un entorno de supervisin bancaria fragmentado en el rea del euro. Estas deficiencias institucionales quedan perfectamente reflejadas en el denominado informe de los cinco presidentes4, publicado en junio de 2015, en el que se indican las medidas pendientes para lograr finalizar la unin econmica y monetaria europea. 2 Ver por ejemplo Reinhart and Rogoff, 2011 3 Otro avance importante relacionado con el Mecanismo nico de Resolucin se materializ en diciembre de 2018, cuando el Mecanismo Europeo de Estabilidad fue reconocido como respaldo del Fondo nico de Resolucin, tanto para solvencia como para la liquidez 4 https://ec.europa.eu/commission/sites/beta-political/files/5-presidents-report_es.pdf El informe seala acertadamente que, dado que la gran mayora del dinero se crea a travs de depsitos bancarios, la moneda solo puede ser realmente nica si la confianza en la seguridad de tales depsitos es la misma con independencia del Estado miembro en el que un banco opere. El SEGD como tercer pilar de la unin bancaria Creo que esta frase resume perfectamente un problema fundacional del Euro. Una moneda comn debe ser reflejo de un sistema financiero nico; por tanto, el mismo euro depositado en distintos bancos debe contar con el mismo respaldo y confianza, con independencia del pas de la Eurozona en que est domiciliada cada entidad. En este sentido, la puesta en marcha del MUS y de la JUR supone un logro importante, pero debemos reconocer que mientras los depsitos no cuenten con un respaldo idntico en toda la Unin Bancaria, no podremos considerar que el edificio se ha completado. Es conocido que seguimos careciendo de uno de sus tres pilares fundamentales, el Sistema Europeo de Garanta de Depsitos (SEGD). Cualquier construccin precisa al menos tres pilares para asegurar su solidez estructural. De manera anloga, creo que el SEGD contribuira a aumentar la estabilidad de la Unin Bancaria, en particular en pocas de estrs, que es cuando la capacidad de resistencia de las estructuras se pone a prueba. El SEGD tendra un fuerte impacto en la confianza de los ciudadanos, pero, adems, el mayor grado de mutualizacin de riesgos en el rea del euro contribuira a alinear la responsabilidad financiera con el proceso paneuropeo de toma de decisiones, que ya se ha instaurado en las reas de supervisin y resolucin bancarias. La situacin actual es tal que el ltimo respaldo para asegurar depsitos en una institucin fallida depende de instituciones nacionales, mientras que la responsabilidad de la supervisin y resolucin recae en otras instituciones paneuropeas. Al poco de estallar la crisis financiera Mervin King seal irnicamente que los bancos internacionales tendan a ser globales en vida, pero siempre acababan siendo nacionales en su muerte. Esta frase parece ser todava aplicable en la Eurozona. En una verdadera unin bancaria, las entidades deberan ser una cuestin europea, tanto durante su vida como en su muerte. Como conocen ustedes, el debate en torno al SEGD se reaviv en noviembre del pasado ao, debido a un artculo5 del ministro de finanzas alemn, Olaf Scholz, en el que abogaba por su implementacin, lo que, en sus propias palabras, no era un paso pequeo para un ministro de finanzas alemn. Eso s, la propuesta alemana se refera a la introduccin de un esquema de reaseguro europeo en vez de un SEGD plenamente mutualizado, adems de estar sujeta a diversas condiciones. En cualquier caso es evidente que el debate sigue abierto y persisten diferencias entre los distintos socios europeos, pero espero y deseo que, como en ocasiones anteriores, 5 Ver FT https://www.ft.com/content/82624c98-ff14-11e9-a530-16c6c29e70ca logremos un consenso que nos permita finalizar este tercer pilar bsico, introduciendo un SEGD verdaderamente comn y, por tanto, plenamente mutualizado. Consolidacin e integracin bancaria europea Djenme que me refiera ahora al grado de integracin del sector bancario Europeo. Ya he indicado que la Unin Bancaria ha cumplido con uno de sus objetivos clave: contribuir a debilitar el vnculo entre riesgo bancario y riesgo soberano pero, adicionalmente, cuando fue lanzada se asumi que la Unin deba conducir a un sistema bancario ms integrado. Sin embargo, hasta ahora, el mayor grado de integracin institucional no ha ido acompaado de un aumento de la actividad transfronteriza en el sector. La cuota de los bancos de propiedad nacional en los sistemas bancarios nacionales sigue siendo alta, aproximadamente un 83%, el mismo nivel que exista en 2014, antes del establecimiento del MUS.6 Por tanto, debemos reconocer que la consolidacin bancaria entre jurisdicciones sigue siendo mnima, y la mayora de empresas y particulares en la eurozona continan dependiendo de sus sistemas financieros nacionales. Los agentes econmicos pueden constatar diariamente los beneficios provenientes de la existencia del mercado nico y del euro, pero lamentablemente, no se percibe en estos momentos beneficios tangibles, en trminos de mayor competencia en precios y servicios financieros, provenientes de la Unin Bancaria. La realidad es que los ciudadanos y las empresas europeas siguen teniendo que enfrentarse a barreras para invertir en los mercados europeos. Los pensionistas e inversores nacionales tienen acceso a diferentes productos de inversin y sus derechos difieren como resultado de leyes locales de insolvencia diferentes. Por ltimo, ya he sealado que el sector bancario sigue siendo principalmente nacional, y sigue estando muy vinculado con su riesgo soberano. Muchos consideran que el hecho de que no se produzcan fusiones transfronterizas es una prueba de que todava nos queda un largo camino por recorrer en trminos de integracin y diversificacin de los mercados. En cualquier caso, resulta sintomtica la escasa consolidacin transfronteriza, particularmente en un contexto de clara sobrecapacidad del sector bancario europeo. En relacin a este tema, cabe sealar que, en su ltimo informe de estabilidad7, el BCE ha publicado un estudio sobre el grado de sobrecapacidad del sector en Europa y sus potenciales implicaciones para el negocio bancario. Conforme a las conclusiones de este estudio, el exceso de capacidad puede llevar a operar por debajo de mrgenes ante la muy elevada competencia, lo que imposibilitara realizar inversiones necesarias para el futuro de la entidad y su adaptacin a las nuevas tecnologas y nuevos operadores, como por ejemplo en sistemas, creando una especie de bancos zombis que arrastran an ms hacia abajo la rentabilidad del sector. 6 CGFS (2018) 7 Financial Stability Review  noviembre 2019 El estudio seala a aquellas entidades que presentan una rentabilidad sobre recursos propios (RoE) inferior a la mediana del 6% durante 3 aos, pero el grupo ms preocupante sera el de entidades con una rentabilidad inferior al 3%, nada menos que alrededor del 25% del total. El estudio concluye con la necesidad de afrontar reestructuraciones y fusiones, mostrando una clara preferencia por las fusiones paneuropeas (cross-border) frente a las nacionales. En relacin al siempre controvertido tema de las fusiones, ya he dicho en diversas ocasiones que nuestro papel como supervisores no es decidir qu fusiones son deseables y cules no, sino valorar en qu medida un proceso de fusin crea una entidad ms solvente y con un modelo de negocio ms slido, permitiendo reducir costes estructurales de un modo significativo y, en definitiva, generando valor en su conjunto. En mi opinin, la falta de fusiones transfronterizas puede explicarse parcialmente por el propio exceso de capacidad y la fragmentacin del sector financiero en Europa. Ciertamente, los beneficios de las sinergias, las posibles reducciones de costes y las mejoras de la eficiencia se observan principalmente en las fusiones entre entidades del mismo pas, gracias a la eliminacin de duplicidades en sucursales y servicios centrales. En este sentido, es bien conocido el radical proceso de consolidacin que el sistema bancario espaol ha llevado a cabo desde 2009. Por dar algunas cifras, ha habido una reduccin de ms de un 30% en el nmero de entidades. El nmero de oficinas ha disminuido en ms de un 40% (unas 20.000) mientras que el personal ha descendido ms de un 30% (unos 90.000 menos). No obstante, dado el entorno extremadamente competitivo en el que nos movemos, quiero subrayar que el mapa de fusiones nacionales puede no estar todava cerrado, particularmente cuando la reduccin de costes de estructura es una de las pocas palancas disponibles para mejorar la cuenta de resultados. Para el caso de la mayora de las fusiones transfronterizas la racionalidad econmica es ms difcil de justificar, aunque existiran potenciales ganancias de competitividad para aquellas entidades que cuenten con un modelo de negocio que permita ahorros verticales. No obstante, como seala el BCE en su estudio, adems de la potencial reduccin de costes, existe otro aspecto a considerar en la consolidacin bancaria: la mejora de la diversificacin geogrfica, tanto desde el punto de vista de los ingresos como de los riesgos asumidos. Coincido plenamente con esta conclusin del estudio. Ciertamente, las fusiones transfronterizas tienen la ventaja de incrementar la diversificacin, lo que mejora sin duda la resistencia en momentos de estrs y permite dotar de mayor estabilidad y recurrencia a los ingresos, como se puso de manifiesto durante la ltima crisis. En este sentido, creo que la falta de reconocimiento explcito de la diversificacin como factor reductor del riesgo puede ser un factor que est limitando este tipo de integracin transnacional. Quiz pueda ser conveniente una reflexin profunda a escala europea e internacional sobre el tratamiento regulatorio de la diversificacin, y su potencial efecto beneficioso sobre el perfil de riesgo de las entidades. En cualquier caso, es importante resear que las fusiones son siempre procesos largos y complejos y, en muchas ocasiones, acarrean ms problemas de los inicialmente previstos. Por otro lado, persisten barreras nacionales que dificultan las fusiones de entidades de distintas jurisdicciones. Persistencia de barreras nacionales Debemos admitir que, pese a los avances, persisten todava determinados obstculos culturales, institucionales y regulatorios que dificultan la creacin de un mercado bancario verdaderamente europeo. La resistencia a eliminar estos obstculos contribuye notablemente a mantener barreras nacionales (ring fencing), que limitan o incluso impiden la libre circulacin de capitales o liquidez entre las distintas jurisdicciones de la Eurozona. A mi juicio, tras lograr una reduccin significativa de los riesgos en el sector financiero, ha llegado el momento de instar a poner fin a estas barreras supervisoras nacionales, que son perjudiciales para la integracin financiera y, por tanto, limitan la ambicin de la Unin Bancaria como jurisdiccin nica. No parece razonable que las implicaciones, en trminos de capital y liquidez, para un grupo bancario que tenga una subsidiaria en un pas latinoamericano sean muy similares a las que existiran si la filial estuviera localizada en otro pas de la Eurozona. Naturalmente, la introduccin plena de un esquema de garanta de depsitos verdaderamente Europeo complementara y, en gran medida, facilitara este avance en la integracin. Por otro lado, desde una perspectiva regulatoria, destaca la ausencia de una base jurdica suficientemente homognea en la eurozona. Al igual que se necesit armonizar, o reconocer como equivalente, determinada normativa nacional para posibilitar la creacin del mercado nico, se precisa cambiar determinadas reglas que impiden el desarrollo de un mercado de servicios financieros verdaderamente nico. Puede que no sea posible lograr la plena armonizacin, pero es probable que no haga falta. Existen algunas reas crticas, como la prevencin del blanqueo de capitales, las normas sobre idoneidad y la normativa sobre insolvencia en los bancos, en las que un conjunto comn de reglas para toda el rea del euro impulsara la integracin del mercado, lo que tambin mejorara la eficiencia de la supervisin y la resolucin. La importancia de terminar con estas barreras y de armonizar la normativa es un tema que va tambin ganando protagonismo. De hecho, en el artculo antes mencionado, el ministro de finanzas alemn se refiere tambin a la necesidad de contar con un marco de insolvencias comn para todos los bancos de la Eurozona, a la vez que reconoce la existencia de barreras nacionales, que habra que eliminar para evitar un mercado financiero fragmentado. Unin financiera Permtanme que en la parte final de mi intervencin levante la vista ms all de la Unin Bancaria, para referirme a la Unin Financiera. Ya he sealado la importancia de introducir un verdadero esquema de garanta de depsitos, eliminar barreras nacionales y armonizar determinadas reas regulatorias pero, adicionalmente, se necesitan otros elementos para seguir avanzando hacia una verdadera Unin Financiera. En este sentido, es indudable que el desarrollo de unos mercados de capitales profundos e integrados permite reforzar la capacidad del rea del euro para amortiguar perturbaciones macrofinancieras. Por supuesto, estoy hablando de la Unin de los Mercados de Capitales (UMC), proyecto que complementara la Unin Bancaria, promoviendo un sector financiero transfronterizo que permita a los agentes econmicos mitigar perturbaciones nacionales asimtricas. El proyecto de la Unin de los Mercados de Capitales fue lanzado en 2015 con el objetivo de desbloquear la financiacin para el crecimiento de Europa, es decir, favorecer no solo el desarrollo sino tambin la integracin de los mercados de capital europeos con el propsito final de diversificar las fuentes de financiacin disponibles. Sin embargo, el proyecto ha languidecido hasta recientemente. Prueba de ello sera el hecho de que el ao previsto para su entrada en funcionamiento era, en origen, 2019. Evidentemente, no se ha logrado este objetivo, aunque la importancia de este proyecto no ha hecho ms que aumentar desde 2015, particularmente en el contexto del Brexit. Aunque resulte algo paradjico teniendo en cuenta la lentitud en los avances, los objetivos de atraer inversores institucionales, mejorar la asignacin de recursos, introducir un activo seguro europeo y fortalecer el papel internacional del euro estn ms vigentes que nunca. Aunque limitados, al menos se han logrado determinados avances. Por ejemplo, la mayor parte del trabajo en trminos de armonizacin de productos de inversin y ahorro en toda la UE ya ha sido acordado, incluyendo la definicin de un producto paneuropeo de pensiones individuales. No obstante, la complejidad del proyecto requiere mayores esfuerzos de armonizacin regulatoria y fiscal, en particular en relacin a los impuestos sobre el capital. Entre otras cosas, siguen existiendo en la UE ms de 90 tipos de formularios en diferentes idiomas para las devoluciones tributarias. Puede parecer poco trascendente pero, a menudo, estas trabas administrativas se mencionan como un gran obstculo a la inversin por parte de los participantes del mercado. En este contexto, es reseable el informe publicado en octubre de 2019, durante la presidencia Finlandesa, del denominado Next CMU group8, formado por representantes de alto nivel de la industria que, a peticin de los ministros de finanzas de la UE, han evaluado la marcha de este proyecto, proponiendo una serie de medidas para lograr relanzarlo9. 8 https://nextcmu.eu/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/The-Next-CMU-HL_DO.pdf 9 El informe tambin sugiere rebautizar el proyecto como Unin de Ahorros e Inversin Sostenible , lo que enfatiza el rol de la financiacin para favorecer la transicin hacia una economa ms sostenible. Conclusin Permtanme que concluya. A lo largo de su historia la UE ha progresado hacia un mayor nivel de integracin econmica y poltica que ha aportado claros beneficios sociales y econmicos. No obstante, el ritmo de avance no ha sido constante. El anlisis de alguno de los principales logros de la Unin, como la creacin del mercado nico o del euro, nos indica que muchas veces es mejor ser pragmtico y avanzar con soluciones menos ambiciosas, en vez de persistir en el bloqueo al no poder alcanzar el acuerdo perfecto. La Unin Bancaria es un paso importante en esta direccin y ha sido clave para hacer frente a la crisis del euro, pese a que la ausencia de un esquema de garanta de depsitos europeo nos recuerde que el proceso no ha concluido. Por otro lado, es necesario introducir determinados elementos regulatorios e institucionales para obtener los beneficios econmicos resultantes de un aumento de la actividad bancaria transfronteriza, logrando as una verdadera Unin Financiera. Como seala el informe de los cinco presidentes, al que me he referido anteriormente: la Unin Econmica y Monetaria es como una casa construida a lo largo de varias dcadas, pero solo acabada parcialmente. Cuando arreciaba la tormenta, haba que estabilizar rpidamente sus muros y su tejado. Ahora toca reforzar sus cimientos. Creo que esta frase ilustra muy bien cmo es en muchas ocasiones el proceso reformista en la UE. Es en medio de la tormenta cuando sube la presin poltica para acometer las reformas que permitan evitar que la casa se venga abajo, sin embargo, estaremos de acuerdo en que el mejor momento de acometer este tipo trabajos es cuando el sol est en el cielo. Al evaluar nuestra capacidad para afrontar futuras crisis financieras no debemos olvidar que el marco institucional an no se ha completado. Ciertamente, los cimientos no estn totalmente reforzados, y debemos evitar caer en la complacencia. No podemos olvidar que, a medida que los recuerdos de la crisis se desvanecen, la presin poltica para acometer las reformas tiende tambin a desvanecerse. Muchas gracias.

Title: Basel III: the implementation imperative
text: Basel III: the implementation imperative Speech by Pablo Hernandez de Cos Chairman of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision and Governor of the Bank of Spain Keynote address at the 15th BCBS-FSI High-level Meeting for Africa on Strengthening financial sector supervision and current regulatory priorities Cape Town, 30 January 2020 Introduction Good morning, and welcome to the 15th BCBS-FSI High-level Meeting for Africa. Let me start by thanking Governor Kganyago and the South African Reserve Bank (SARB) for hosting this meeting in Cape Town. As the global standard setter for banks, the Basel Committee places great importance on reaching out to a wide range of stakeholders to inform its work. Events such as these high-level meetings are of particular value to the Committee in seeking the views of central banks and supervisory authorities across different regions of the world. With a population of over 1.2 billion and a median age of 19 years, Africa will play an increasingly important role in shaping the future world economy. The average annual GDP growth in Africa has exceeded the global average over the past several years, and six of the worlds 10 fastest-growing economies hail from this continent.1 1 Signe and Gurib-Fakim (2019). 2 McKinsey (2018). 3 Ibid. 4 Hernandez de Cos (2019c). These growth prospects are also reflected in Africas banking systems, which are among the fastest-growing and most profitable of any region. During the period 201217, African banks revenue grew at a compound annual rate of 11%, and these institutions are projected to continue to be among the fastest-growing banking systems over the coming years (Figure 1).2 Indeed, with a retail banking penetration of just under 40% of GDP, there is incredible potential for African banks to continue to grow.3 And Africa has been at the forefront of using technology for banking services, long before fintech become a household term.4 Whether it is established fintech companies such as Kenyas M-Pesa mobile money service or Nigerias Interswitch digital payments  which were set up over 15 years ago  or more recent fintech startups, there are now over 250 active fintech companies operating in sub-Saharan Africa (Figure 2). There is much that we can learn from Africas rich history of fintech. But these tantalising prospects for Africas banking systems will require a robust and resilient regulatory foundation. Such a foundation helps deliver sustainable and healthy banking systems that can serve the real economies at all points of the financial cycle. So, my remarks today will focus primarily on the imperative of implementing the Basel Committees post-crisis reforms. Im pleased to note that the SARB takes this imperative seriously: it has a strong track record of implementing the Basel III standards in a timely and consistent manner. And Governor Kganyagos chairmanship of the Financial Stability Boards Standing Committee on Standards Implementation underscores the SARBs commitment to this imperative. I will frame my remarks around four questions: (i) Why does implementation matter? (ii) What has the Basel Committee done to meet the implementation imperative? (iii) What have we seen to date among our members? (iv) Where does this leave us? Why does implementation matter? At face value, the answer to this question may appear obvious. Any global regulatory standard will have no durable impact if it is not actually implemented! But the response to the question is deeper than this in at least two ways. Implementation is integral to policymaking First, implementation is a core element of any policymaking cycle (Figure 3). While the features of such a cycle may differ across organisations, they generally comprise the following sequential elements: (i) identifying a policy issue/objective; (ii) developing and appraising possible policy options; (iii) implementing and monitoring the finalised policy measures; (iv) evaluating the effectiveness of the policy measures and the extent to which they meet their objectives; and (v) incorporating any insights and lessons learned for future policymaking. So, only by implementing global regulatory standards can we reap their full benefits, understand and assess their impacts, and draw any takeaways for future policymaking. I have previously discussed the increasing focus of the Committee and other international forums on evaluating post-crisis reforms.5 But such evaluations can only be conducted in a rigorous manner after the relevant reforms have been implemented. 5 Hernandez de Cos (2019b). 6 Hernandez de Cos (2019a). 7 Schoenmaker (2011). Implementation and global financial stability Second, safeguarding financial stability is a matter of global collective responsibility.6 In a world with cross-border capital flows, no jurisdiction can preserve financial stability domestically through its own policies.7 Preserving global financial stability requires jurisdictions to cooperate in identifying and mitigating risks to the financial system. The costs of the global financial crisis of 2007-09 were profound and are still raw. Estimates from the IMF suggest that output levels remain below pre-crisis trends in more than 60% of economies.8 And the broader societal impact of the global financial crisis is no less jarring  we have yet to full the full impact of these changes.9 8 International Monetary Fund (2018). 9 Hernandez de Cos (2019a). 10 Ibid. 11 Carstens (2019). In response to the global financial crisis, Basel Committee members developed a comprehensive package of post-crisis reforms collectively known as Basel III. These reforms seek to address some of the glaring fault-lines in the banking system exposed by the global financial crisis, including unsustainable levels of leverage, insufficient high-quality loss-absorbing capital, excessive variability of banks modelled risk-weighted assets, a mispricing of liquidity risk and the build-up of system-wide risks. In developing the Basel III reforms, the Committee carefully weighted the costs and benefits of regulation. There is strong empirical evidence suggesting that the net macroeconomic benefits of capital requirements are positive over a wide range of capital levels (Figure 4). The benefits of Basel III accrue both to society as a whole, in the form of reduced frequency and impact of banking crises, and to banks directly, in the form of lower funding costs and better-quality lending.10 But the benefits to global financial stability of Basel III can only be fully realised if these global minimum standards are implemented across jurisdictions based on the following criteria: Full implementation: the full scope of globally agreed reforms are expected to be implemented. The Committees post-crisis reforms collectively enhance the robustness of the regulatory framework. These reforms are complementary in nature, as they seek to address different fault-lines exposed by the global financial crisis. A selective implementation of Basel III will result in a frail regulatory foundation, exposing banks and the real economy to vulnerable pockets of unmitigated risks. Timely implementation: the reforms are expected to be implemented no later than the agreed implementation dates (Figure 5). For example, for the recently-finalised Basel III reforms, that means an implementation date of no later than 1 January 2022. Consistent implementation: the reforms are expected to be implemented in a faithful and compliant manner. This means meeting both the letter and spirit of the standards (while allowing for any non-substantive drafting variations for the purpose of domestic legislation).11 Failure to meet this implementation imperative could undermine global financial stability and the provision of credit to the real economy. Global cross-border bank claims exceed 30 trillion, which includes claims on not only other banks but also non-bank counterparts (Figure 6). If certain parts of this globally interconnected banking network are not subject to the same degree of resilience provided by Basel III, this could result in a build-up of risks in certain banking systems, which could ultimately impede the continued provision of credit across jurisdictions. Importantly, the implementation imperative refers to the minimum standards set out in the global Basel framework. Jurisdictions are free, and encouraged, to go beyond this baseline if the size and structure of their banking system and the associated risks warrant additional measures. Such measures only reinforce global financial stability. A non-consistent implementation of Basel III across jurisdictions could also result in market fragmentation and cross-border regulatory arbitrage. As noted in a report by the Financial Stability Board on this topic, which drew on inputs from the Committee, the potential impact on market fragmentation as a result of a non-consistent Basel III implementation could include: creating an unlevel playing field among banks that can result in a race-to-the-bottom in terms of regulatory standards and/or supervisory practices, which in turn can have adverse consequences for the safety and soundness of the banking system; overstating the capital and liquidity ratios reported by banks in jurisdictions that have not implemented Basel III consistently, which would erode comparability across banks and impair market discipline; and adding operational costs and complexity for internationally active banks.12 12 FSB (2019). 13 BCBS (2018). 14 BCBS (2017). 15 See BCBS (2019b) for the latest report. What have we done? So, what has the Committee done in practice to help meet the implementation imperative? Commitment to implementation First, the Committees Charter explicitly notes that members are committed to implement and apply BCBS standards in their domestic jurisdictions within the pre-defined timeframe established by the Committee.13 The Committee does not possess any formal supranational authority, and its decisions have no legal force. The power of the Committees standards lies therefore in the common willingness and understanding that member jurisdictions will adopt them into domestic laws or regulations. This commitment was most recently reaffirmed by the Group of Central Bank Governors and Heads of Supervision when finalising the outstanding Basel III reforms in 2017.14 And G20 Leaders have repeatedly and unequivocally stated their commitment to a full, timely and consistent implementation of Basel III. Regulatory Consistency Assessment Programme Second, the Committee set up the Regulatory Consistency Assessment Programme (RCAP) in 2012 to achieve three objectives: (i) monitor the timely adoption of standards by members; (ii) assess the completeness and consistency of the standards adopted by members; and (iii) evaluate the outcomes of the application of these standards. Let me say a few words about what has been done thus far to meet those objectives. The Committee submits semiannual monitoring reports to G20 Leaders on the implementation status of Basel III.15 These reports provide a high-level overview of Committee members progress in adopting all of the Basel III standards. The publication of these reports provides an incentive for member jurisdictions to adopt the Committees standards in a timely manner. In addition to periodically reporting on the status of adoption, all Committee members undergo an assessment of the completeness and consistency of their domestic rules with the Basel standards. The jurisdictional assessments consist of peer review exercises that assess the extent to which domestic regulations are aligned with the minimum Basel standards and identify any deviations from the Basel framework. The assessment reports are published and include an overall compliance grade, which provides an incentive for member jurisdictions to take any corrective actions to address findings identified in assessments. The Committee also publishes follow-up reports to track the actions taken by member jurisdictions after the publication of the RCAP report. To date, the Committee has published assessment reports for all its member jurisdictions regarding their implementation of the capital requirements, Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) and global systemically important bank (G-SIB) framework.16 In 2018, the Committee started assessing the consistency of implementation of the Net Stable Funding Ratio (NSFR) and the framework for measuring and controlling large exposures. The review of the implementation of these standards for all member jurisdictions is expected to be completed in 2021. The Committee will then commence its review of members implementation of the leverage ratio framework and the revised risk-weighted capital framework. 16 The reports are available at . 17 The reports are available at . With respect to evaluating the outcomes of the application of Basel standards, the Committee has published a series of thematic reports on the consistency of risk-weighted assets for credit risk, market risk and counterparty credit risk.17 These reports highlighted a material and worryingly large degree of variability in banks risk-weighted assets (Figure 7) and in turn motivated the recently finalised Basel III reforms that seek to reduce this excessive variability. What have we seen to date? Where do we stand with the implementation of Basel III? On the timeliness of implementation, Im pleased to note that all member jurisdictions have implemented the initial (2010) Basel III capital standards and the LCR (Figure 8). And most jurisdictions have implemented the leverage ratio framework on time as well. But we are seeing increasing signs of delay with regard to the implementation of some of the other standards. For example, only 70% of jurisdictions have thus far implemented in a timely manner core reforms such as the Net Stable Funding Ratio and the large exposures framework. And a similar pattern can be seen with regards to various reforms related to the risk-weighted capital framework, including the standardised approach for measuring counterparty credit risk, the revised securitisation framework and capital requirements for banks exposures to central counterparties. From a consistency perspective, the Committees RCAP reports on the implementation of the Basel III capital framework found that, of the 19 member jurisdictions, 15 have been assessed as compliant, three were largely compliant, and one was materially non-compliant (Figure 9). With respect to the LCR, 16 jurisdictions have been assessed as compliant and three were largely compliant. Finally, the RCAP reports on the G-SIB framework found that all jurisdictions in which the G-SIBs are headquartered were compliant. And the RCAP reports conducted thus far on the NSFR and large exposures framework for seven jurisdictions have found them all to be compliant. Importantly, most member jurisdictions have actively rectified observed deviations by amending their domestic regulations in the course of the RCAP assessments. The assessments of the capital framework, LCR and G-SIBs framework identified a total of 1,450 deviations, of which around 60% were rectified during the assessment. Of the remaining deviations, 85% have been assessed as not material, ie not expected to give rise to concerns related to financial stability or an international level playing field. This is evidence of the tangible benefits derived from the Committees RCAP. Where does this leave us? So, where do we go from here to meet the implementation imperative? I will offer two observations. The regulatory cycle and excessive complexity First, it is concerning to see signs of delays in implementing the outstanding Basel III standards among some member jurisdictions, and even more worrying to see indications of potential deviations in a few instances. In my view, such delays and potential inconsistencies are a result of two broad factors: (i) the unfortunate dynamics of the regulatory cycle; and (ii) the significant volume and excessive complexity of some of the post-crisis reforms. I have previously discussed the concept of the regulatory cycle, whereby memories of banking crises fade over time, vested interests start to gain momentum, and the fallacy of this time is different recurs.18 It tests our will to persevere with the implementation of post-crisis reforms. And we convince ourselves that some reforms may no longer be needed or warranted, or even that rolling back reforms may be the key to achieving other short-term economic objectives. 18 Hernandez de Cos (2019a). There are worrying signs that we may be entering the later stages of this cycle. For example, it is disconcerting to hear claims made by some that a jurisdiction or region needs to adapt Basel III to suit its domestic circumstances. This points to a lack of understanding or misrepresentation of how the Basel standards are developed. The Committee has a comprehensive approach to designing its standards, which includes: (i) an extensive outreach with a wide range of stakeholders through a transparent and structured consultation process; (ii) rigorous empirical analyses of the impact of any proposed policy measure, with the results of many quantitative impact studies made public; and (iii) discussions among Committee member jurisdictions regarding the final design and calibration of any standard. So, the Committees approach to finalising its standards already takes into account any relevant differences in viewpoints among its members or different structural features across its jurisdictions. For example, during the finalisation of the recent Basel III standards in 2017, over 50 adjustments were made by the Committee during its development of the standards relative to the proposals that it initially consulted on. A related cause for delayed implementation is the excessive complexity and volume of post-crisis reforms. Both banks and supervisors are facing operational challenges in implementing some of the standards. In some instances, some of this complexity reflects relentless lobbying efforts by some stakeholders to continuously seek further fine-tuning of Basel III, which would purportedly result in greater risk sensitivity. Instead, it has increased the operational obstacles for banks to implement the standards in a timely manner. When combined with the length of the domestic legislative process in some jurisdictions, this further undermines the ability to meet the implementation imperative. This underscores the importance of ensuring that standards are designed in a simple and robust manner.19 Such an approach is in the interest of all stakeholders, as it facilitates the ability to meet the implementation imperative in a timely manner, and provides a resilient regulatory foundation that stands the test of time. In finalising Basel III, the Committee reviewed the appropriate balance of simplicity, comparability and risk sensitivity in the regulatory framework.20 It is important that we continue to ensure that the right balance is struck going forward. 19 Ingves (2015), Coen (2018). 20 BCBS (2013a). 21 BCBS (2012). 22 BCBS (2019c). Proportionality and the Basel framework My second observation relates to the role of proportionality in helping to meet the implementation imperative. The Core Principles for Effective Banking Supervision embed the role of proportionality, including that supervisory practices should be commensurate with the risk profile and systemic importance of the banks being supervised.21 These principles are relevant for all banks and jurisdictions around the world, and provide the basis for a resilient banking system. The Committee supports the use of proportionality in implementing the Basel framework in a manner consistent with the Core Principles.22 The Basel framework includes a range of approaches, from simpler standardised approaches to advanced approaches. Accordingly, proportionality can take different forms, including, but not limited to, the following: implementing the most appropriate approaches among those available in the Basel framework (ie among the range of standardised and internally modelled approaches) for internationally active banks in member jurisdictions. There is no expectation  even for internationally active banks  that they must use internally modelled approaches; and implementing standards for banks in non-BCBS member jurisdictions that are broadly consistent with the principles of the applicable Basel standards. A proportionate framework should not reduce the resilience of banks or dilute the prudential regulatory framework, but rather reflect the relative differences in risk and complexity across banks and the markets in which they operate. Crucially, a proportionate framework should also consider supervisory capacity and resources, particularly when implementing more complex standards. Going forward, the Committee will continue to exchange views on the role of proportionality in the Basel framework, and whether any additional work is needed at the global level. I would encourage jurisdictions in Africa to pursue a proportionate approach to their implementation of the Basel framework along these lines, where relevant. And I look forward to hearing your views on how proportionality can best be used in your jurisdiction to provide a resilient and robust regulatory framework for African banks. Committee work programme and outlook Before I conclude, let me say a few words about the Committees current work programme. In addition to its unremitting commitment to meeting the implementation imperative, the Committees work programme comprises three broad strands of work. First, the Committee is undertaking a targeted set of policy initiatives related to topical issues including: operational resilience and cyber risk; the prudential treatment of crypto-assets; the regulatory impact of benchmark rate reforms; and the implications of expected credit loss accounting for banks regulatory capital requirements. Second, the Committee is continuing its efforts to promote strong supervision, including with regard to assessing the implications of financial technology for banks and supervisors and mitigating climate-related financial risks. Third, while the Basel III reforms are being implemented, the Committee will be devoting a substantive part of its agenda over the next few years to carefully evaluate the impact and effectiveness of its post-crisis reforms. Conclusion To conclude, the Basel Committees post-crisis reforms, centred around Basel III, are a comprehensive and wide-ranging set of measures that seek to fix the many fault lines in the pre-crisis regulatory framework. But the benefits from Basel III can only be enjoyed if these standards are implemented by all Committee member jurisdictions. The time for adaptation is passed, and the focus should now be on adoption. This is of particular importance for those jurisdictions and regions with the biggest banking systems. More than ever, it is in their interest to lead by example and contribute to global financial stability by implementing Basel III in a full, timely and consistent manner. Title: Intervention at the bell ringing of the Madrid Stock Exchange for gender equality
text: 04.03.2020 Intervention in the ringing of the bell of the Madrid Stock Exchange for gender equality Spanish Stock Exchanges/Global Compact Margarita Delgado Deputy Governor Good morning: I am very honored by the invitation of Spanish Stock Exchanges and Markets and the Global Compact to carry out this bell ringing for gender equality, which in Spain is going through the 6th edition and which, in anticipation of International Women's Day next Sunday, is celebrated today simultaneously in more than 85 exchanges around the world. As you are well aware, International Women's Day commemorates the struggle of women for their participation, on an equal footing with men, in society and in their full development as individuals. I believe that the struggle for equal opportunities summarizes the set of demands of this day. Whenever we talk about equality, we use statistics, which continue to show that women are at a disadvantage compared to our male colleagues. The vindictive nature of this day invites us to focus on these signs of inequality and to correct them. That is all well and good, but I think we should also welcome what we have made progress in a short period of time. To give a fact, the Global Gender Gap study of 2020, carried out by the World Economic Forum since 2006, has classified Spain in the eighth position of the 153 countries analyzed for its degree of progress in gender equality, ahead of countries such as Germany, Denmark, France or the United Kingdom. Naturally, this does not mean that everything is done; even Iceland, which leads the ranking of the most egalitarian countries, continues to have some deficit. Throughout my professional career I have been able to see this progress. When I started working, a few years ago, at Banco de Espa (well, not so many either) to be an inspector of credit institutions was to be a rara avis. It is not that there were explicit restrictions that prevented or hindered women's access to inspection; It was simply a profession within the financial sector that was considered male. However, the picture today is very different. It is paradigmatic that, in the two promotions of Inspeccin, two thirds of the incorporations have been women. There have been no quotas, no policies involved, we have simply found that they have been better than the rest. This evolution has also occurred in the rest of the Bank; in fact, last year, women became the majority in the workforce for the first time, and, although full parity has not been achieved, the presence of women in middle management and senior management of the Bank is increasingly relevant. This type of evolution has also happened in Spanish society. If I can give a personal reference, my two daughters have decided to study technical and scientific careers, and they have done so completely independently, without their father or I having encouraged them to follow that path. However, I think there are still too many children who give up considering whether they like, are interested and motivated to study certain careers. or pursue certain professional achievements. The lack of stimuli and, in many cases, of female references in which to be inspired conditions the image they have of themselves. I think we cannot afford to give up so much talent. We need more scientists, more engineers, more economists, more deputy governors and, why not, more governors. And for the record, I'm not saying it for myself, I'm not looking for a promotion. It is clear that our work from public powers, companies and society must be, precisely, to encourage each person, whether man or woman, to make, on an equal footing, the decisions that affect their lives without external conditions. I am firmly convinced that it is necessary to break this unconscious bias, which too often limits career progression, preventing the presence of women among the middle managers of organizations. This is a difficult but essential cultural change. Of course, not all women want to move towards technical careers and not all women, nor all men, aspire to move up in organizations, especially if it means giving up their personal or family life. People can and should freely choose their interests and their level of professional ambiction, but it is clear that organizations must make an effort to avoid that there may be people who have to give up their career for reasons other than professional. Conciliation, both for men and women, is a basic pillar of society and I believe that this is one of the areas in which we still have great potential for improvement. In conclusion, despite the evident progress, we must continue to make progress in removing the barriers, visible and invisible, that prevent women from making decisions freely. I believe that there is a lot of potential to improve work-life balance, favouring the full development of a professional career compatible with a full personal and family life, which undoubtedly also implies sharing family responsibilities between men and women. To sum it up with one sentence, we have to level the playing field. Let those nis and, of course, children, who wish to do so, develop their full potential. It is not only a matter of justice or equity, but is of interest to all. We cannot give up the talent of half of our society. Thanks a lot.
text_original: 04.03.2020 Intervenci en el toque de campana de la Bolsa de Madrid por la igualdad de gnero Bolsas y Mercados Espaoles/Pacto Mundial Margarita Delgado Subgobernadora Buenos das: Me siento muy honrada por la invitacin de Bolsas y Mercados Espaoles y de Pacto Mundial para realizar este toque de campana por la igualdad de gnero, que en Espa va por la 6 edicin y que, como anticipo al Da Internacional de la Mujer del prximo domingo, se celebra hoy de forma simultnea en ms de 85 bolsas de todo el mundo. Creo que la lucha por la igualdad de oportunidades resume a la perfeccin el conjunto de reivindicaciones de esta jornada. Est bien que sea as, pero creo que tambin debemos celebrar lo que hemos logrado avanzar en un plazo escaso de as. Por dar un dato, el estudio Global Gender Gap de 2020, que realiza el Foro Econmico Mundial desde 2006, ha clasificado a Espa en la octava posicin de los 153 pases analizados por su grado de avance en igualdad de gnero, por delante de pases como Alemania, Dinamarca, Francia o Reino Unido. Naturalmente, esto no significa que todo est hecho; incluso Islandia, que lidera el ranking de pases ms igualitarios, sigue presentando alg dficit. A lo largo de mi carrera profesional he podido constatar este avance. Cuando empec a trabajar, hace ya unos cuantos as, en Banco de Espa (bueno, tampoco tantos) ser inspectora de entidades de crdito era ser una rara avis. No es que hubiera cortapisas explcitas que impidieran o dificultaran el acceso de mujeres a la inspeccin; sencillamente, era una profesin dentro del sector financiero que se consideraba masculina. Sin embargo, el panorama hoy es muy distinto. Resulta paradigmtico que, en las dos timas promociones de Inspeccin, dos tercios de las incorporaciones hayan sido de mujeres. No obstante, creo que sigue habiendo demasiadas nis que renuncian a plantearse si les gusta, les interesa y les motiva estudiar determinadas carreras o perseguir ciertos logros profesionales. La falta de estmulos y, en muchas ocasiones, de referencias femeninas en las que inspirarse condiciona la imagen que tienen de s mismas. Creo que no nos podemos permitir renunciar a tanto talento. Necesitamos ms cientficas, ms ingenieras, ms economistas, ms subgobernadoras y, por qu no, ms gobernadoras. Y que conste que no lo digo por m, no estoy buscando un ascenso. Es evidente que nuestra labor desde los poderes pblicos, las empresas y la sociedad debe ser, precisamente, fomentar que cada persona, ya sea hombre o mujer, pueda tomar, en pie de igualdad, las decisiones que afectan a su vida sin condicionantes externos. Soy una firme convencida de que se precisa romper ese sesgo inconsciente, que limita en demasiadas ocasiones la progresin en la carrera profesional, impidiendo la presencia de mujeres entre los mandos intermedios de las organizaciones. Se trata de un cambio cultural difcil de lograr, pero esencial. Por supuesto, no todas las mujeres quieren encaminarse hacia carreras tcnicas y tampoco todas las mujeres, ni todos los hombres, aspiran a ascender en las organizaciones, especialmente si ello implica renunciar a su vida personal o familiar. Las personas pueden y deben elegir libremente sus intereses y su nivel de ambicin profesional, pero es evidente que desde las organizaciones se debe hacer un esfuerzo para evitar que pueda haber personas que tengan que renunciar a su carrera por motivos distintos a los profesionales. La conciliacin, tanto de hombres como de mujeres, es un pilar bsico de la sociedad y creo que esta es una de las reas en las que todava tenemos un gran potencial de mejora. En conclusin, pese a los avances evidentes, debemos continuar avanzando en la eliminacin de las barreras, visibles e invisibles, que impiden que las mujeres tomemos decisiones de modo libre. Creo que existe mucho potencial para mejorar la conciliacin, favoreciendo el desarrollo pleno de una carrera profesional compatible con una vida personal y familiar plena, lo que, sin duda, implica tambin repartir las responsabilidades familiares entre hombres y mujeres. Por resumir con una frase, tenemos que lograr nivelar el terreno de juego. Permitamos que aquellas nis y, por supuesto, nios, que lo deseen, desarrollen todo su potencial. Title: Intervention of the governor at the signing of the Agreement of the Financial Education Plan with the Ministry of Education and Vocational Training and the CNMV
text: 07.09.2020 Signing of the Financial Education Plan Agreement with the Ministry of Education and Vocational Training and the CNMV Pablo Hernandez de Cos Governor Madam Minister, Mr. President; Ladies and gentlemen, good afternoon everyone. It is an honour for me to represent the Banco de Espa96a in the signing of this Financial Education Plan Agreement jointly carried out by the Ministry of Education and Vocational Training, the National Securities Market Commission and the Bank of Spain itself. We thus project into the future the work that began in May 2008 when, based on the recommendations and principles of the European Commission and the OECD to contribute to the improvement of the financial culture of citizens, a collaboration agreement was signed by the CNMV and the Bank of Spain, for the development of a financial education plan. Subsequently, in September 2009, the collaboration agreement was signed with the then Ministry of Education, in order to implement financial education in the teaching system. Since that signing, we have worked intensively, jointly, on that objective. The identification of the training needs of students, the development of training resources and the implementation of a Financial Education Program can be cited as actions carried out under its protection. And all this will have contributed to the progressive inclusion of financial competence in the curricular itineraries of primary and secondary education, as well as to the consolidation of the contents of economics, business and finance in baccalaureate and vocational training. Undoubtedly, the signing of this Agreement renews that commitment and represents a new step forward in the process of consolidating the Financial Education Plan. It is well known that financial education plays a fundamental role in the responsible management of household and small business economies, as well as in the protection of the user of financial services, and by extension in the maintenance of financial stability, since it balances the relationship between suppliers and demanders of these products. It is, therefore, a competition whose promotion must continue to be promoted in coordination by public and private organizations. Precisely at times like the present, in which our country suffers the effects of the Covid19 pandemic, institutions must focus on promoting and carrying out long-term reforms. As I have stressed on several occasions, in order to increase the productivity of the Spanish economy, it is essential to improve human and technological capital. I firmly believe that the financial education of the population, focused on young people but without losing sight of vulnerable groups, is and will be a fundamental piece in this process. As recommended by the OECD, the Financial Education Plan is aware of the need to give special importance to training in financial skills from an early age. The promotion of financial education in schools is also considered as a relevant aspect. In this regard, the main objective is that students in Primary and Secondary Education, as well as those in Vocational Training and Baccalaureate, receive minimum contents that guarantee adequate competence in financial education. It is a fact that the child population begins to relate in one way or another to money at increasingly younger ages. In addition, in a society with very high levels of financial inclusion, we can be sure that citizens will have permanent relationships with financial institutions in their adult lives: the possession of a current account or a credit card are practically universal in Spain. Therefore, in their educational process they must acquire basic skills so that during their adult life they are able to make responsible financial decisions adjusted to their personal and family characteristics. To increase financial skills, it is considered essential that financial education begins as early as possible and is integrated into a coordinated strategy where a learning framework is established that sets objectives and teaching results, content and, of course, evaluation systems. In this last sense, I would like to highlight the importance that I believe Spain's participation in the evaluation of financial competence would have in future editions of the International Program for Student Assessment PISA, with the next one in 2021. For this, there is excellent training of teachers responsible for teaching financial education. The CNMV and the Bank of Spain, in coordination with the Ministry of Education and Vocational Training and the Ministries of Education of the different Autonomous Communities, actively collaborate by making available to teachers educational materials and resources adapted to each of the training cycles, as well as to teacher training itself. In conclusion, in order to achieve the new challenges in the field of financial education, I would like to highlight the importance of the signing of this Agreement that updates and reinforces the collaboration developed by the Ministry of Education and Vocational Training, the CNMV and the Bank of Spain in the field of financial education. Experience shows that results can only be expected in the long term, since financial education is, in short, a tool for changing and improving citizens' behaviours and behaviours. Thanks a lot.

Title: Delivery of the III Carlos Humanes Prize for economic journalism
text: 05.10.2020 Delivery of the III Carlos Humanes Prize for economic journalism Association of European Journalists/BME Pablo Hernandez de Cos Governor Good afternoon, everyone. Allow me to say a few words to close this event. A few words that are directed, first of all, to thank the Association of European Journalists and its president, Diego Carcedo, who have thought of me, again, to deliver this award. I say 'again' because, in previous editions, previous commitments, unfortunately, did not make it possible, so it is a real pleasure to be here this afternoon. Thanks that I extend to Bolsas y Mercados Espa96oles, for allowing us to meet here, at the Palacio de la Bolsa, where Carlos Humanes began his journalistic career about 40 years ago, and where his press room has been and is the cradle of many economic journalists. Without going any further, some of the members of the communication team of the Bank of Spain have thrown their first teeth here as professionals. And, above all, congratulations to Rosa Mar92a S87nchez for this III Carlos Humanes Award. An award that highlights professional careers and journalistic works related to economic, financial and/or stock market information. Rosa receives this award for being a good example of the values of rigor and veracity, which should govern the exercise of the profession of any journalist. But also for its work teaching young journalists, something of incalculable value for economic and financial information to continue contributing in the future to greater education and training of society in these disciplines. This combination of rigor and truthfulness, on the one hand, and teaching ability, on the other, is particularly important in this unprecedented crisis generated by the pandemic and, particularly on a day like today, when we celebrate Financial Education Day. In a context of so much uncertainty as the current one and so complex at the same time for everyone, given the unprecedented moment we are living, good economic journalists have a very important job to rigorously transmit what is happening. As I have said many times, this work is particularly relevant for the economic authorities because the measures we take and the motivation for them reach the citizens through you. In this situation, in which a good part of these measures aim to offer peace of mind to citizens and reduce uncertainty, that this information is transmitted properly is crucial. From my point of view, this work of rigorous and demanding journalism is also positive because it obliges the authorities to explain ex ante the arguments behind the decisions and requires ex post that they make an assessment of whether the proposed objectives have been achieved. All this results in greater rationality in the action of economic policy, at least to the extent that citizens judge these actions on the basis of these assessments. In addition, as I said, today we have celebrated Financial Education Day. This act of epilogue to this Day may well serve. You translate a language that is sometimes very complicated into understandable terms, which often incorporates an element educational, which contributes to increasing the financial education of citizens. In short, good journalists are able to inform and teach at the same time. A good example of all this is the article signed today by our award-winning in El Peri97dico, in which in just under 500 words she dissects the latest IMF statement in the context of the so-called article IV in relation to the economic policy recommendations that this international institution defends at this time for Spain. In the dissection, Rosa not only describes the main recommendations of the IMF to face this crisis, but also assesses the changes in emphasis of the institution compared to past crises and even identifies and underlines what she considers its main message: to prevent the health and economic crisis from being joined by a financial component. which would aggravate it greatly. I recommend this article to you and not only because, in relation to this last issue, this is a message that I have also been emphasizing since the beginning of this crisis. For all this, Rosa, congratulations. Thank you all very much and good evening
