En este sentido, cabe recordar que diferentes estudios acadmicos indican que las reformas de Basilea III han dado como resultado unos requerimientos de capital que se encuentran dentro del rango de estimaciones que apuntan a beneficios macroeconmicos netos positivos, derivados de la mayor estabilidad financiera y de la mejor capacidad de absorcin de perturbaciones proporcionadas por tales requerimientos3. 3 Vase Comit de Supervisin Bancaria de Basilea (junio de 2019): The costs and benefits of bank capital  a review of the literature. Los beneficios de la implementacin de Basilea III no se limitan a las economas y sistemas financieros de los pases miembros del Comit de Basilea, sino que tambin son relevantes para otras jurisdicciones. Entre ellas, Amrica Latina, tanto por el efecto sobre los sistemas bancarios a escala local como por la influencia de los bancos internacionalmente activos que operan en la regin y que adems influyen en el ciclo financiero de un modo global. Basilea III contribuir a reducir la probabilidad de que se produzcan futuras crisis y, en caso de haberlas, minimizar su impacto. Sin nimo de ser exhaustivo, las reformas del marco de capital, los nuevos requerimientos de liquidez y la introduccin de un enfoque macroprudencial ayudarn a aumentar la capacidad de reaccin y de resistencia de los sectores bancarios de la regin, contribuyendo adems a lograr un terreno de juego competitivo ms nivelado.  En segundo lugar, debemos ser conscientes de que la reforma regulatoria no est finalizada: an quedan aspectos cruciales por completar en la implementacin de Basilea III. Las reformas acordadas que todava estn pendientes de implementar, y que contienen una serie de estndares dirigidos a potenciar la robustez y credibilidad del marco de activos ponderados por riesgo, solventan defectos que continan siendo tan importantes hoy como antes de la pandemia. En especial, en la medida en que refuerzan la comparabilidad entre entidades, que tiene un claro efecto sobre el terreno de juego competitivo, y limitan la variabilidad de los requerimientos de capital. Cada vez est ms claro que las reformas de Basilea pendientes de implementar servirn de complemento al marco regulatorio actual y a su impacto neto positivo sobre la economa real. Por ejemplo, anlisis recientes del Banco Central Europeo muestran que los costes de la implementacin de las reformas en Europa en trminos de producto interior bruto son modestos y transitorios, mientras que sus beneficios contribuirn a reforzar la resiliencia econmica ante futuros shocks. Adems, la elaboracin de estos estndares se benefici de un minucioso proceso consultivo. No implementar estas medidas de manera completa, puntual y consistente, tal y como han acordado los lderes del G-20 en distintas ocasiones, dejara sin atender las restantes debilidades y fragilidades estructurales, lo cual conlleva un coste significativo para la economa y la estabilidad financiera global. El COVID-19 ha puesto de relieve la vital importancia que supone disponer de los mecanismos necesarios antes de la emergencia de un shock; esto tambin es aplicable, sin duda, a los estndares prudenciales y a la seguridad y robustez del sistema bancario. Permtanme recordar, en este punto, que el objetivo de implementacin completa, consistente y en plazo para los bancos internacionalmente activos no es incompatible con la aplicacin de un marco proporcional acorde con los Core Principles for Effective Banking Supervision, en los que se establece que las prcticas supervisoras deben ser conmensuradas con el perfil de riesgos y la importancia sistmica de los bancos supervisados4. Ms all de eso, el Comit tiene en marcha iniciativas para promover el rol de la proporcionalidad en la regulacin y supervisin bancarias, incluyendo el desarrollo de guas prcticas sobre el uso y el diseo de un marco regulatorio y supervisor proporcional, que estar disponible para las jurisdicciones para su uso de manera voluntaria5. 4 Vase Comit de Supervisin Bancaria de Basilea (2012), Core Principles for effective banking supervision. 5 Comit de Supervisin Bancaria de Basilea, Basel Committee work programme and strategic priorities for 2021/22.  En tercer lugar, y en paralelo al programa de evaluacin que tiene en curso el Comit, es fundamental adoptar un enfoque supervisor con una visin prospectiva, para identificar, evaluar y mitigar los riesgos emergentes y las tendencias estructurales que impactan en el sistema bancario global. Algunos de estos riesgos y tendencias incluyendo la digitalizacin de las finanzas, los riesgos financieros relacionados con el clima, y la evolucin y sostenibilidad de los modelos de negocio bancarios ya haban sido identificados antes de la pandemia, y el COVID-19 ha subrayado an ms la importancia de abordarlos. Concluyo ya. La implementacin de Basilea III responde a un inters global y colectivo. Tanto la lucha contra enfermedades infecciosas como la salvaguarda de la estabilidad financiera son bienes pblicos globales que no conocen fronteras y que requieren colaboracin entre pases. La pandemia no finalizar hasta que cada uno de nosotros estemos a salvo. Del mismo modo, los beneficios globales de Basilea III no se lograrn si no se respeta el compromiso de implementacin completa, consistente y en plazo alcanzado en el G-20 y en el Grupo de Gobernadores y Jefes de Supervisin.

Title: The financial sector in the post-Covid context
text: 30.09.2021 The financial sector in the post-Covid context XVIII Deloitte/ABC Financial Sector Meeting Margarita Delgado Subgobernadora Good morning First of all, I would like to thank Deloitte, Sociedad de Tasaci97n and the newspaper ABC for the invitation to open one more year the second day of this meeting of the Financial Sector that already reaches its twenty-eighth edition. The last time we met at this very event we were still immersed in a deep crisis unprecedented from any point of view. Today, almost a year later, I think it is a good time to analyze the situation in which we find ourselves and consider what the future may hold so that we can face it from a solid position and with the best tools. Introduction In the last meeting we were still suffering the consequences of the second wave of the pandemic without being fully aware that we would live three more. Fortunately, today we face the future with more optimism thanks to the rapid pace of vaccination. This unusual situation of successive ups and downs in sanitary conditions has led to the adoption of extraordinary measures of all kinds that have affected, as it cannot be otherwise, the country's economy. It is not my intention in this forum to analyze the actions that have been taken to alleviate the effects of this crisis. There is already abundant literature on this. Therefore, I will focus more on the current situation and on emphasizing aspects that I consider relevant to face the near future that, without reaching the extreme of the uncertainty of last year, does not yet have the visibility that we would all like. Current analysis: profitability and solvency Figure 1 Decomposition of the result raiation Figure 2 ROA distribution The first point I would like to address because of its relevance is that of profitability. A business is not sustainable if it does not generate sufficient resources. The accounts of Spanish entities in the first half of the year have been very positive compared to those of the same period last year. Even without considering the extraordinary results that some entities have had for relevant corporate operations, the outlook at the moment seems hopeful. It is true that 2020 was a totally anomalous year in which entities made an effort to increase provisions for the health crisis. It seems that the current trend of banking results is approaching that of 2019, something that is in line with macroeconomic developments and existing forecasts for the coming months. However, we must remember that we have not yet recovered pre-pandemic levels of wealth and there are still uncertainties. Even without taking into account the extraordinary results of the last two years, the return on assets (ROA) has improved to June 2021 compared to a year earlier. If in this graph we had represented the situation of June 2019, we would also observe that the last data would be slightly higher than that of that date. Given this scenario in which banks seem to have recovered the level of profit generation prior to the pandemic, we as supervisors have to show our prudence and warn of the risks of excessive optimism, even more so when there are still uncertainties on the horizon. There is no need to be in a hurry when it comes to reversing the provisions provided last year until we have full confidence that the loan portfolio is evolving as expected. Gr87fico 1 - Evolution of CET ratio % FL Figure 2 - Rate of change of CET1 and risk-weighted assets In terms of solvency, the process of strengthening banking since 2014 is noteworthy. In addition, as I have said on other occasions, the basis for calculating current solvency ratios is defined in a much more solid way than we had in the past thanks to the regulatory reforms of Basel III. In fact, the banking system has been better placed to deal with a systemic crisis, even such as this one of an exogenous nature. The full implementation of Basel III will undoubtedly make the sector even more resilient. Capital ratios increased in the last year, especially in the second half of 2020. The improvement in capital indicators, despite the outbreak of the pandemic, was largely due to the measures adopted by the authorities to mitigate the effects of the health crisis. The extraordinary modification of the CRR, called quick fix, had a positive impact of about 55 basis points on the solvency of Spanish significant institutions. It should also be noted that the recommendation to limit the distribution of dividends had an additional positive effect of 17 basis points. This recommendation, which was undoubtedly extraordinary, was deemed necessary at a time of total uncertainty, but time has proved its necessity and effectiveness. However, in view of the progressive economic recovery, it has been considered appropriate to withdraw this recommendation. However, we must not be complacent. Spanish banks have to continue making efforts to continue strengthening their solvency position because the differential with the rest of European entities not only continues to exist, but has increased. It is true that there are reasons that partly explain this differential, such as the lower use of advanced internal models for the calculation of capital requirements. In addition, the business model of Spanish entities, mainly the most international, is characterized by a recurring generation of results. This fact constitutes the first line of defense in the medium term to guarantee a solvent business. Current analysis: asset quality Figure 1- Loans to the resident private sector Graph 2- Breakdown of business and household credit growth Continuing with the analysis of the current situation, there has been a growth in total credit investment destined to non-financial companies in the last year. This fact is related to the momentum of operations guaranteed by the ICO during the first part of the pandemic. However, this growth has been moderate in recent quarters. In contrast, household dynamics have been much flatter. In fact The stock of financing to households has remained stable despite the increase in mortgage operations in recent months. That is what I shall come back to later. It is noteworthy that, despite the current situation, there has not yet been an increase in NPL ratios. In fact, both in companies and especially in families this continues to fall. Figure 1 - NPLs to the resident private sector. Figure 2 - NPLs to non-financial corporations and households Figure 3 - NPL ratio The huge package of aid made available to companies and families may undoubtedly be having a mitigating effect on their liquidity and solvency needs, which allows the delinquency figures to remain contained. In addition, the potential consolidation of the economic situation will help prevent potential liquidity tensions from materialising and to the financial sector. Something I want to emphasize is that we must be cautious and monitor the evolution of those loans granted under one of the protective umbrellas or support measures approved during the pandemic. Even more so because these operations are concentrated in the sectors potentially most affected by the crisis. Banks have a wide range of early warning tools to detect situations in which borrowers, without being classified as doubtful, have weaknesses in their ability to meet their financial obligations. The use of these early warnings is crucial in these circumstances for the correct detection and management of potentially problematic assets. Although assets under special surveillance have increased in recent quarters, at the Bank of Spain we have observed that these assets still remain at a relatively low level, even in those sectors most affected by the pandemic. Therefore, it will be necessary to maintain vigilance on the evolution of these portfolios in the coming months, both for the end of the moratoriums that remain, already few, and for the behavior of the exposures endorsed by the ICO, since they also have extended grace periods, in many cases, under Royal Decree Law 34/2020. Figure 1 - Credit investment coverage Non-financial corporation Figure 2 - Credit investment coverage Households As I mentioned earlier, Spanish banks made a significant effort in 2020 in terms of provisioning to deal with possible contingencies of problematic loans. This has allowed the level of global coverage to improve substantially compared to pre-pandemic times even despite the increase in credit investment mentioned. This accumulation of provisions has been especially relevant for those operations with a significant increase in risk (the so-called stage 2, in accounting terminology). However, as I have already pointed out, we will have to be very attentive to the evolution of the quality of the loan portfolio in the coming months and check that the level of coverage remains at adequate levels at all times. Figure 1- Evolution of the credit balance for construction and real estate development Figure 2- Evolution of the mortgage credit balance for housing purchases Another point I want to comment on is the dynamism of the real estate sector. The number of housing transactions and the annual variation of new mortgage credit has reached high levels. The quarter-on-quarter increase in house prices between April and June 2021 has been the highest in the last six years. We must analyze the causes of these increases and see if it is a tendency to consolidate or, on the contrary, they are due to circumstantial reasons, such as the postponement of purchase decisions due to the pandemic together with the accumulation of savings by households in those months. That said, we don't see any signs of imbalance in the market. At the moment, the behavior of this type of credit is still much more moderate than in other European countries. In fact, the volume of mortgage amortizations in these quarters has been able to compensate for the new credit granted, so the stock remains stable. The pandemic has "forced," we might say, households to save, and resident private sector deposit balances continue to rise at annual rates. Our forecasts assume that this accumulated savings will be reduced only partially and the final destination of this savings remains to be seen. Future challenges Figure 1- Evolution of the number of employees and offices 2001/2020 Figure 2 - Evolution of the number of entities Once the current situation has been analyzed, it is time for us to look towards the most immediate future: How are entities going to operate in a post-pandemic environment? What changes should they make to adapt to the new situation? The main challenge remains profitability. The financial sector operates in very tight return on capital ranges and, it is in the interest of all and financial stability that the banking business is sustainable. This goal can be achieved by combining several elements. On the one hand, it can be achieved with a reduction in operating costs and, on the other, through the transformation of the business model towards another that generates value in the medium term. With regard to the reduction of operating costs with more immediate effects on the income statement, the Spanish financial sector has made significant efforts to adjust the their structures. We've seen it in mergers, downsizing, or branch closures. After the recent processes of bank concentration, it seems that the path in this direction is more limited. However, as we have commented on other occasions, the level of concentration is not worrying if we compare ourselves with other countries in our environment since we are at a moderate level according to the Herfindahl index. Internationally, what we do see is a growing trend of pan-European business acquisitions rather than cross-border bank mergers. This dimension is growing in importance by fostering greater integration within the Banking Union and highlighting the benefits of geographical and business diversification. Speaking of business model transformation, I cannot fail to mention digitalization. In fact, during the pandemic it has accelerated with new actors and products, which is producing changes in the competitive landscape of the financial system. This digital transformation will require a strategic decision to invest in technological and human capital in the short term that will bear fruit in the medium and long term. Therefore, it seems inevitable that banks will take steps in this regard. On the one hand, reducing its operating costs to guarantee its sustainability and on the other in the structural transformation that guarantees the business. In short: banks have to be profitable if they want to ensure their existence. Another element that I would like to highlight in this discussion about profitability is that of commissions. From the Bank of Spain we have been observing that income from bank commissions has more and more weight in the income statements of the entities. Everything indicates that the collection of commissions for services that were previously free is a practice that will spread as a result of the search for new sources of income. Additionally, we are observing in this process of banking transformation, a trend towards businesses with a greater generation of recurring commissions, which constitutes a strength that complements the traditional banking business. Allow me to refer to the transparency that should govern the relationship between the bank and the customer. The collection of financial commissions is subject to a regulation of conduct subject to supervision and is linked to the effective provision of the service. No one likes to be charged commissions. But it must be recognized that, when receiving a financial service, entities incur costs. Therefore, it is necessary to make an effort of transparency and strict compliance with the regulations. This is a key exercise for good customer relationship and bonding. This point leads me to talk about the reputation of entities. Reputation and governance Since the outbreak of the last financial crisis, the reputation of the sector has been in question on numerous occasions. There are many issues in which banking has been in the focus of media attention and in the spotlight of public criticism. Governance is therefore a key element that in recent years has been emphasised not only by supervisors but also, more importantly, by banks themselves. Robust governance is key, among other things, to strengthening a good reputation. So is doing self-assessment work to see how and in what sense it can be reinforced. Strict compliance with existing regulations coupled with the exercise of best practices is essential to build a solid reputation. I trust that the entities are aware of this. Proof of this is the strategic protocol to reinforce the social and sustainable commitment of banking that the main associations of the sector have assumed. Institutions d0 both public and private d0 are increasingly aware of the impact that their actions have on society. We must bear in mind that this commitment, which covers aspects as varied as social or environmental, will increasingly be subject to scrutiny by all actors. An example of this is the stress exercise on climate risks that will be carried out next year. Climate risk This climate test stress exercise will include a self-assessment by entities on their exposures to climate change and their preparedness to face it. The objectives of this exercise are diverse: to check the capacity of entities to assess climate risks, understand the stress tests of climate risks that entities may have designed internally, identify vulnerabilities, evaluate the incorporation of these risks into management, provide guidance and improve data availability. The main obstacle that supervisors and the industry currently face is the definition of adequate metrics and, above all, the non-existence of data with sufficient depth and granularity. These points are essential to make robust analyses and identify clear and concrete strategies. As I have pointed out, this type of risk is relatively new and we do not have sufficient experience in identifying key data that can define climate risks. In relation to this, the essence of this new stress exercise is to familiarize us all, supervisors and entities, with the identification, quantification and management of a new type of risk that will become increasingly relevant. The stress test will not have a direct impact on capital requirements, but will certainly provide additional information for the assessment of other risks. The guidance published by the European Central Bank in November 2020 on climate-related risks reflects supervisory expectations for climate-related risk management and serves to improve the sector's awareness and preparedness of climate-related risk management. All sectors, including the financial sector, must adapt their business models towards an environment in which concern for the environment takes on greater prominence and towards an economy that is transforming towards more sustainable models. The Bank of Spain, for example, has adhered to the agreement adopted by the Eurosystem for the establishment of a common position for sustainable investment and already, in 2019, decided to add sustainability and responsibility criteria in the investment policy of its own portfolios, among other measures. For its part, the European Central Bank has presented an action plan to include climate considerations in its monetary policy strategy. The sustainability to which I refer must not only be confined to the environmental aspect, but also to the social and governance aspects. ESG stands for a concept that will become increasingly familiar to us. Finally, let me return to the topic of digitalisation because of its great relevance towards the future. Digitalisation and digital euro Figure 1- Percentage of users of online banking services 2006/2019 Figure 2- Evolution in the use of payment methods with the COVID-19 crisis One of the outstanding transformations of the financial industry as a result of the pandemic has been the promotion of digital tools to offer banking services. Many of these tools already existed, but their use has become much more common these days. The growth of users of online banking services, digital payments and financial applications has been constant in recent years and has been boosted during the pandemic. The banking industry has accelerated planned digital innovation processes to adapt to this new context. Digital circuits are now much more frequent, not only for carrying out simple transactions, such as ordering transfers or checking balances, but also for more complex activities, such as receiving financial advice or Hire new products. The pandemic has pushed us all to make greater use of technology, from the virtual credit card called wallet to payment by Bizum. To the extent that it is already a structural trend, new key challenges for the future of the sector arise. In addition, as mentioned above there are new competitors, digital banks and fintech. First, it is essential that banks seriously reflect on what their optimal strategy should be and devote their efforts to implementing it without further delay. In other words: they have to decide d0 with some urgency d0 what technologies to incorporate, at what pace to do it and, above all, how to carry it out. Digitalization entails the realization of non-negligible investments, but it also implies cost reduction in the medium and long term and puts them in a competitive position in the market. Within the strategy, another element to take into account is the decision on whether the necessary technological developments are carried out internally, alliances with external players are sought or a combination of both strategies. Each has advantages and disadvantages that need to be examined very carefully. In addition, entities must also comply with the issues that most press the authorities, for example, ensuring effective control of external technology providers. Secondly, digitalization undoubtedly impacts the business model. In an environment in which speed and simplicity are qualities valued by all, the possibility of making more and more transactions digitally increases bank customer satisfaction. In addition, it allows to incorporate new sources of income or customers and exploit information in a massive way to extract value from the data. Incidents reported in 2019 and 2020 by quarters Thirdly, it must be recognised that the digitalisation process also carries risks. By increasing reliance on technology, technological risk increases. Special mention must be made of cyber risk. The increase of interconnections, both With third parties as with customers, the likelihood of attacks increases, as evidenced during the pandemic. This transition to digital also entails the task of training employees in new tools and processes. Undoubtedly, the profile of the bank employee will undergo a reorientation towards skills more related to technology and data management. Finally, the authorities must recognize and support the digitalization programs of banking, thus assisting the sector in its modernization process. An example is the creation in November 2020 of the Sandbox. In the first wave, 67 projects were received and analyses of the first pilots admitted to the controlled test environment are beginning. The deadline for applications for the second wave began on September 1. The Law for the digital transformation of the financial system that regulates the Sandbox aims to facilitate the innovative process and ensure that financial authorities have adequate control instruments in the digital context. Digitalization also implies a firm commitment to strengthen the training of our staff and undertake actions that enhance the use of new technologies for the best performance of our functions and skills. The Banco de Espa96a's Strategic Plan is committed to promoting technological innovation, accompanied by other no less important initiatives within the framework of the Eurosystem. One of them, as everyone knows, is the digital Euro. The Eurosystem continues to deepen its analysis in order to be prepared for its issuance, if it is so decided. After a year and a half of conceptual study and experimentation, last July the Governing Council of the ECB agreed to launch a research project. Thus, over the next two years, we will analyze in detail different characteristics and configurations in order to determine what the digital Euro should look like. That is, what is the optimal combination of the different design options that manages to respond to the needs of users and, at the same time, minimize the effects on financial and monetary stability. Some of these issues are already clear, as is the case with the distribution model of this currency. Details such as the specific role of supervised entities remain to be finalized. But we are heading towards an intermediated model in which entities are responsible for bringing the digital Euro to users. Therefore, the digital Euro is not intended to compete with banking, as is sometimes heard, but is expected to open opportunities for banks to offer new or novel services on a secure and common basis throughout the euro area. Conclusion Let me conclude. In my speech I reviewed the main challenges and supervisory concerns present in the short term, based on an analysis of the current situation of the financial sector. I believe that Spanish entities are in a solid position to face the uncertainties to which this pandemic has accustomed us. However, the evolution of the different assets will have to be monitored to detect as soon as possible those exposures that may show some signs of impairment. Taking action as far in advance will be key to avoiding possible greater evils in the future. In addition to this imminent task, the financial sector has the challenge of adapting to a new, more digital environment, with new competitors and in which new risks such as climate risks will take center stage. To face this scenario, entities must reflect on their business models and how to reorient them to adapt to this framework also seeking the much-needed profitability. I also wanted to put a lot of emphasis on digitalization. As I have pointed out, establishing a clear strategy in this regard is key, as is allocating the necessary resources in an environment of tight margins. Let's turn these challenges into opportunities to grow more and in a balanced, fair and sustainable way. We have a very interesting road ahead of us. Thanks a lot
text_original: 30.09.2021 El sector financiero en el contexto post-Covid XVIII Encuentro del Sector Financiero Deloitte/ABC Margarita Delgado Subgobernadora Buenos das, En primer lugar, quisiera agradecer a Deloitte, Sociedad de Tasacin y al diario ABC la invitacin para abrir un ao ms la segunda jornada de este encuentro del Sector Financiero que ya alcanza su vigsimo octava edicin. La ltima vez que nos reunimos en este mismo evento todava estbamos inmersos en una profunda crisis sin precedentes desde cualquier punto de vista. Hoy, casi un ao despus, considero que es un buen momento para analizar la situacin en la que nos encontramos y plantear qu nos puede deparar el futuro para que podamos afrontarlo desde una posicin slida y con las mejores herramientas. Introduccin En el pasado encuentro estbamos todava sufriendo las consecuencias de la segunda ola de la pandemia sin ser del todo conscientes de que viviramos otras tres ms. Afortunadamente, hoy afrontamos el futuro con ms optimismo gracias al rpido ritmo de vacunacin. Esta situacin inslita de sucesivos vaivenes en las condiciones sanitarias ha llevado a adoptar medidas extraordinarias de todo tipo que han afectado, como no puede ser de otro modo, a la economa del pas. No es mi intencin en este foro el analizar las acciones que se han tomado para paliar los efectos de esta crisis. Sobre ello ya existe abundante literatura. Por ello, me centrar ms en la situacin actual y en enfatizar aspectos que considero relevantes para encarar el futuro prximo que, sin llegar al extremo de la incertidumbre del ao pasado, no tiene an la visibilidad que todos desearamos. Anlisis actual: rentabilidad y solvencia Grfico 1 Descomposicin de la raiacin del resultado Grfico 2 Distribucin del ROA El primer punto que quisiera tratar por su relevancia es el de la rentabilidad. Un negocio no es sostenible si no genera recursos suficientes. Las cuentas de las entidades espaolas en el primer semestre del ao han sido muy positivas comparadas con las del mismo periodo del ao pasado. An sin considerar los resultados extraordinarios que algunas entidades han tenido por operaciones societarias relevantes, el panorama de momento parece esperanzador. Cierto es que 2020 fue un ejercicio totalmente anmalo en el que las entidades hicieron un esfuerzo para incrementar las provisiones por la crisis sanitaria. Parece que la tendencia actual de resultados de la banca se aproxima a la de 2019, algo que va en lnea con la evolucin macroeconmica y las previsiones existentes para los prximos meses. No obstante, hay que recordar que todava no hemos recuperado los niveles de riqueza previos a la pandemia y an existen incertidumbres. An sin tener en cuenta los resultados extraordinarios de estos dos ltimos ejercicios, la rentabilidad sobre activos (ROA) ha mejorado a junio de 2021 en comparacin con un ao antes. Si en este grfico hubisemos representado la situacin de junio de 2019, tambin observaramos que el ltimo dato sera ligeramente superior al de aquella fecha. Ante este panorama en que los bancos parece que han recuperado el nivel de generacin de resultados previo a la pandemia, nosotros como supervisores tenemos que hacer gala de nuestra prudencia y alertar de los riesgos de un excesivo optimismo, ms an cuando todava existen incertidumbres en el horizonte. No hay que tener prisa a la hora de revertir las provisiones dotadas el ao pasado hasta que no se tenga plena confianza de que la cartera crediticia evoluciona segn lo previsto. Grfico 1 - Evolution of CET ratio % FL GRfico 2 - Tasa de variacin del CET1 y los activos ponderados por riesgo En cuanto a la solvencia, es destacable el proceso de fortalecimiento de la banca desde 2014. Adems, como he comentado en otras ocasiones, las bases de clculo de las ratios de solvencia actuales estn definidas de una manera mucho ms slida que las que tenamos en el pasado gracias a las reformas regulatorias de Basilea III. De hecho, el sistema bancario ha estado mejor situado para afrontar una crisis sistmica, incluso como esta de carcter exgeno. La completa implementacin del acuerdo de Basilea III har, sin duda, an ms resistente al sector. Las ratios de capital aumentaron en el ltimo ao, especialmente en la segunda mitad de 2020. La mejora de los indicadores de capital pese a la irrupcin de la pandemia, se debi, en gran parte, a las medidas adoptadas por las autoridades para mitigar los efectos de la crisis sanitaria. La modificacin extraordinaria de la CRR, llamada quick fix, tuvo un impacto positivo de unos 55 puntos bsicos en la solvencia de las entidades significativas espaolas. Tambin hay que sealar que la recomendacin de limitar el reparto de dividendos tuvo un efecto positivo adicional de 17 puntos bsicos. Esta recomendacin, sin duda extraordinaria, se estim necesaria en un momento de total incertidumbre, pero el tiempo ha demostrado su necesidad y eficacia. No obstante, ante la constatacin de la progresiva recuperacin econmica se ha considerado adecuado retirar dicha recomendacin. Con todo, no hay que ser autocomplacientes. Las entidades espaolas tienen que seguir haciendo esfuerzos para continuar fortaleciendo su posicin de solvencia porque el diferencial con el resto de entidades europeas no solo sigue existiendo, sino que ha aumentado. Bien es cierto que hay razones que explican en parte este diferencial, tales como el menor uso de modelos internos avanzados para el clculo de requerimientos de capital. Adems, el modelo de negocio de las entidades espaolas, principalmente de las ms internacionales, est caracterizado por una generacin recurrente de resultados. Este hecho constituye la primera lnea de defensa en el medio plazo para garantizar un negocio solvente. Anlisis actual: calidad de los activos grfico 1- Prstamos al sector privado residente grfiuco 2- Desglose del crecimiento de crdiro a empresas y hogares Siguiendo con el anlisis de la situacin actual, se observa un crecimiento en la inversin crediticia total destinada a empresas no financieras en el ltimo ao. Este hecho est relacionado con el impulso de las operaciones garantizadas por el ICO durante la primera parte de la pandemia. No obstante, este crecimiento se ha visto moderado en los ltimos trimestres. En contraste, la dinmica de los hogares ha sido mucho ms plana. De hecho, el stock de financiacin a hogares ha permanecido estable a pesar del incremento de operaciones hipotecarias en los ltimos meses. A esto me referir posteriormente. Llama la atencin que, a pesar de la coyuntura vivida, todava no se haya observado un incremento en las ratios de morosidad. De hecho, tanto en empresas como especialmente en las familias esta sigue bajando. grfico 1 - prstamos dudosos al sector privado residente. grfico 2 - prstamos dudosos a sociedades no financieras y hogares grfico 3 - ratio de dudosos El ingente paquete de ayudas puestas a disposicin de las empresas y familias sin duda puede estar teniendo un efecto mitigador en las necesidades de liquidez y solvencia de las mismas, lo que permite que las cifras de morosidad permanezcan contenidas. Adems, la potencial consolidacin de la situacin econmica contribuir a que las posibles tensiones de liquidez no se materialicen y trasladen al sector financiero. Algo que quiero recalcar es que hay que ser cautos y vigilar la evolucin de aquellos prstamos concedidos bajo alguno de los paraguas de proteccin o medidas de apoyo aprobados durante la pandemia. Ms an porque estas operaciones se concentran en los sectores potencialmente ms afectados por la crisis. Las entidades cuentan con un amplio abanico de herramientas de alerta temprana para detectar aquellas situaciones en las que los acreditados, sin estar clasificados como dudosos, presentan debilidades sobre la capacidad para hacer frente a sus obligaciones financieras. El uso de estos indicadores anticipados (early warnings) es crucial en estas circunstancias para una correcta deteccin y gestin de activos potencialmente problemticos. Aunque los activos en vigilancia especial han aumentado en los ltimos trimestres, en el Banco de Espaa hemos observado que dichos activos se mantienen todava en un nivel relativamente bajo, incluso en aquellos sectores ms afectados por la pandemia. Por lo tanto, habr que mantener la vigilancia sobre la evolucin de estas carteras en los prximos meses, tanto por la finalizacin de las moratorias que restan, ya pocas, como por el comportamiento de las exposiciones avaladas por el ICO, ya que tambin cuentan con periodos de carencia ampliados, en muchos casos, al amparo del Real Decreto ley 34/2020. Grfico 1 - Cobertura de inversin creditica Sociedad no financieras Grfico 2 - Cobertura de inversin crediticia Hogares Como he mencionado anteriormente, las entidades espaolas hicieron un esfuerzo significativo en 2020 en cuanto a la dotacin de provisiones para hacer frente a las posibles contingencias de los prstamos problemticos. Esto ha permitido que el nivel de cobertura global haya mejorado sustancialmente con respecto a tiempos anteriores a la pandemia incluso a pesar del incremento de la inversin crediticia comentado. Esta acumulacin de provisiones ha sido especialmente relevante para aquellas operaciones con incremento significativo de riesgo (las denominadas stage 2, en terminologa contable). No obstante, como ya he sealado, habr que estar muy atentos a la evolucin de la calidad de la cartera crediticia en los prximos meses y comprobar que el nivel de cobertura se mantiene en niveles adecuados en cada momento. grficoi 1- Evolucin del saldo crediticio a la construccin y promocin inmobiliaria grfico 2- Evolicin del saldo crediticio hipotecario para la comptra de viviendas Otro punto que quiero comentar es el dinamismo del sector inmobiliario. El nmero de transacciones de viviendas y la variacin anual de nuevo crdito hipotecario ha alcanzado niveles altos. El incremento inter-trimestral del precio de la vivienda entre abril y junio de 2021 ha sido el ms elevado en los ltimos seis aos. Hay que analizar las causas de esos incrementos y ver si se trata de una tendencia a consolidar o, por el contrario, se deben a motivos coyunturales, como el aplazamiento de las decisiones de compra por la pandemia unido a la acumulacin de ahorro por parte de los hogares en esos meses. Dicho esto, no observamos ningn signo de desequilibrio en el mercado. De momento, el comportamiento de este tipo de crdito es todava mucho ms moderado que en otros pases europeos. De hecho, el volumen de amortizaciones de hipotecas en estos trimestres ha sido capaz de compensar el nuevo crdito concedido, por lo que el stock permanece estable. La pandemia ha forzado, podramos decir, a los hogares a ahorrar y los saldos de depsitos del sector privado residente siguen aumentando en tasas anuales. Nuestras previsiones asumen que este ahorro acumulado se reducir solo de forma parcial y est por ver el destino final de este ahorro. Retos futuros Grfico 1- Evolucin del nmero de empleados y oficinas 2001/2020 Grfico 2 - Evolucin del nmero de entidades Una vez analizada la situacin actual es hora de que pasemos a mirar hacia el futuro ms inmediato: Cmo van a operar las entidades en un entorno post pandemia? Qu cambios deberan realizar para adaptarse a la nueva situacin? El principal reto sigue siendo la rentabilidad. El sector financiero opera en unos rangos de rentabilidad sobre capital muy ajustados y, es en beneficio de todos y de la estabilidad financiera que el negocio bancario sea sostenible. Este objetivo se puede alcanzar mediante la combinacin de varios elementos. Por un lado, se puede lograr con una reduccin de costes operativos y por otro, a travs de la transformacin del modelo de negocio hacia otro que genere valor en el medio plazo. En cuanto a la reduccin de costes operativos con efectos ms inmediatos en la cuenta de resultados, el sector financiero espaol ha realizado importantes esfuerzos en el ajuste de sus estructuras. Lo hemos visto en las fusiones, reducciones de plantillas o cierres de sucursales. Tras los recientes procesos de concentracin bancaria, parece que el recorrido en este sentido es ms limitado. No obstante, tal y como hemos comentado en otras ocasiones, el nivel de concentracin no es preocupante si nos compararnos con otros pases de nuestro entorno ya que nos situamos en un nivel moderado segn el ndice Herfindahl. A nivel internacional, lo que s se observa es una tendencia creciente de adquisiciones de negocios paneuropeos ms que de fusiones transfronterizas de bancos. Esta dimensin est creciendo en relevancia fomentando una mayor integracin dentro la Unin Bancaria y poniendo de manifiesto los beneficios de la diversificacin geogrfica y de negocios. Hablando de transformacin del modelo de negocio no puedo dejar de mencionar la digitalizacin. De hecho, durante la pandemia esta se ha acelerado con nuevos actores y productos, lo que est produciendo cambios en el paisaje competitivo del sistema financiero. Esta transformacin digital requerir una decisin estratgica de inversin en capital tecnolgico y humano en el corto plazo que dar sus frutos en el medio y largo. Por lo tanto, parece inevitable que los bancos tomen medidas en este sentido. Por un lado, reduciendo sus costes operativos para garantizar su sostenibilidad y por otro en la transformacin estructural que garantice el negocio. En resumen: los bancos tienen que ser rentables si quiere asegurar su existencia. Otro elemento que me gustara resaltar en esta discusin sobre la rentabilidad es el de las comisiones. Desde el Banco de Espaa venimos observando que los ingresos por comisiones bancarias tienen cada vez ms peso en las cuentas de resultados de las entidades. Todo indica que el cobro de comisiones por servicios que antes eran gratuitos es una prctica que se extender como resultado de la bsqueda de nuevas fuentes de ingresos. Adicionalmente, estamos observando en este proceso de transformacin bancaria, una tendencia hacia negocios con una mayor generacin de comisiones recurrentes lo que constituye una fortaleza que complementa al negocio bancario tradicional. Permtanme que al hablar de comisiones bancarias haga referencia a la transparencia que debe regir la relacin entre el banco y el cliente. El cobro de comisiones financieras est sometido a una normativa de conducta sujeta a supervisin y va ligada a la efectiva prestacin del servicio. A nadie le gusta que le cobren comisiones. Pero hay que reconocer que, al recibir un servicio financiero, las entidades incurren en unos costes. Por eso, es necesario hacer un esfuerzo de transparencia y cumplimiento estricto de la normativa. Este es un ejercicio clave para la buena relacin y vinculacin del cliente. Este punto me lleva a hablar sobre la reputacin de las entidades. Reputacin y gobernanza Desde el estallido de la ltima crisis financiera la reputacin del sector ha estado en entredicho en numerosas ocasiones. Son muchos los asuntos en los que la banca ha estado en el foco de atencin meditico y en el punto de mira de la crtica pblica. La gobernanza es, pues, un elemento clave en el que en los ltimos aos se ha hecho hincapi no solo por parte de los supervisores sino tambin, y lo que es ms importante, por parte de las propias entidades. Una gobernanza robusta es clave, entre otros cometidos, para afianzar una buena reputacin. Tambin lo es hacer un trabajo de autoevaluacin para ver cmo y en qu sentido se puede reforzar. El cumplimiento estricto de la normativa existente unido al ejercicio de las mejores prcticas es esencial para construir una slida reputacin. Confo que las entidades son conscientes de ello. Prueba de esto es el protocolo estratgico para reforzar el compromiso social y sostenible de la banca que las principales asociaciones del sector han asumido. Las instituciones -tanto las pblicas como las privadas- somos cada vez ms conscientes del impacto que sus actuaciones tienen en la sociedad. Tenemos que tener presente que este compromiso, que abarca aspectos tan variados como los sociales o medioambientales, va a ser cada vez ms objeto de escrutinio por todos los agentes. Una muestra de ello es el ejercicio de estrs sobre riesgos climticos que se llevar a cabo el ao que viene. Riesgo climtico Este ejercicio de estrs test climtico incluir una autoevaluacin por parte de las entidades sobre sus exposiciones al cambio climtico y su preparacin para afrontarlo. Los objetivos de este ejercicio son diversos: comprobar la capacidad de las entidades para evaluar los riesgos climticos, entender los estrs test de riesgos climticos que las entidades hayan podido disear internamente, identificar vulnerabilidades, evaluar la incorporacin de estos riesgos a la gestin, proporcionar orientaciones y mejorar la disponibilidad de datos. El principal obstculo al que los supervisores y la industria nos enfrentamos actualmente es la definicin de mtricas adecuadas y, sobre todo, la no existencia de datos con la suficiente profundidad y granularidad. Esos puntos son esenciales para hacer anlisis robustos e identificar estrategias claras y concretas. Como he sealado, este tipo de riesgo es relativamente nuevo y no tenemos la experiencia suficiente en la identificacin de datos clave que pueden definir los riesgos climticos. En relacin a ello, lo esencial de este nuevo ejercicio de estrs es ir familiarizndonos todos, supervisores y entidades, con la identificacin, cuantificacin y gestin de un tipo nuevo de riesgo que ir cobrando cada vez ms relevancia. El estrs test no tendr impacto directo en los requerimientos de capital, pero sin duda proporcionar informacin adicional para la valoracin de otros riesgos. La gua publicada por el Banco Central Europeo en noviembre 2020 sobre riesgos relacionados con el clima refleja las expectativas supervisoras en materia de gestin de este tipo de riesgos y sirve para mejorar la concienciacin y preparacin del sector respecto a la gestin de los mismos. Todos los sectores, incluido el financiero, deben adaptar sus modelos de negocio hacia un entorno en el que la preocupacin por el medio ambiente cobra mayor protagonismo y hacia una economa que se va transformando hacia modelos ms sostenibles. El Banco de Espaa, por ejemplo, se ha adherido al acuerdo adoptado por el Eurosistema para el establecimiento de una posicin comn para la inversin sostenible y ya, en 2019, decidi aadir los criterios de sostenibilidad y responsabilidad en la poltica de inversin de sus carteras propias entre otras medidas. Por su parte, El Banco Central Europeo ha presentado un plan de actuacin para incluir consideraciones climticas en su estrategia de poltica monetaria. La sostenibilidad a la que me refiero no solo debe circunscribirse al aspecto medioambiental, sino tambin al social y a la gobernanza. ESG son las siglas en ingls de un concepto que cada vez nos resultar ms familiar. Por ltimo, permtanme volver a tratar el tema de la digitalizacin debido a su gran relevancia hacia el futuro. Digitalizacin y euro digital Grfico 1- Porcentaje de usuarios de servcios de banca online 2006/2019 Grfico 2- Evolucin en el uso de medios de pago con la crisis del COVID-19 Una de las transformaciones destacadas de la industria financiera a raz de la pandemia ha sido el impulso de herramientas digitales para ofrecer servicios bancarios. Muchas de estas herramientas ya existan, pero su uso se ha hecho mucho ms habitual en estos das. El crecimiento de usuarios de servicios de banca online, pagos digitales y aplicaciones financieras ha sido constante en los ltimos aos y se ha visto impulsado durante la pandemia. La industria bancaria ha acelerado procesos de innovacin digital planificada para adaptarse a este nuevo contexto. Los circuitos digitales resultan a da de hoy mucho ms frecuentes, no solo para la realizacin de transacciones simples, como ordenar transferencias o consultar saldos, sino tambin para realizar actividades ms complejas, como recibir asesoramiento financiero o contratar nuevos productos. La pandemia nos ha empujado a todos a hacer un mayor uso de la tecnologa, desde la tarjeta de crdito virtual llamada wallet al pago por Bizum. En la medida en que ya es una tendencia de carcter estructural surgen, por tanto, nuevos desafos clave para el futuro del sector. Adems, como se ha comentado anteriormente hay nuevos competidores, bancos digitales y fintech. En primer lugar, es fundamental que las entidades reflexionen seriamente acerca de cul debe ser su estrategia ptima y dedicar sus esfuerzos a implantarla sin ms dilacin. En otras palabras: les toca decidir -con cierta urgencia- qu tecnologas incorporar, a qu ritmo hacerlo y, sobre todo, cmo llevarlo a cabo. La digitalizacin conlleva la realizacin de inversiones no despreciables, pero tambin implica reduccin de costes en el medio y largo plazo y les pone en una posicin competitiva en el mercado. Dentro de la estrategia, otro elemento a tener en cuenta es la decisin sobre si los desarrollos tecnolgicos necesarios se realizan internamente, se buscan alianzas con jugadores externos o una combinacin de ambas estrategias. Cada una presenta ventajas e inconvenientes que han de examinarse con sumo cuidado. Adicionalmente, las entidades deben, asimismo, dar cumplimiento a las cuestiones que ms apremian a las autoridades, por ejemplo, asegurar un control efectivo de los proveedores externos de tecnologa. En segundo lugar, la digitalizacin impacta, sin duda, en el modelo de negocio. En un entorno en el que la rapidez y sencillez son cualidades valoradas por todos, la posibilidad de realizar cada vez ms transacciones de manera digital aumenta la satisfaccin del cliente bancario. Adems, permite incorporar nuevas fuentes de ingresos o clientes y explotar informacin de forma masiva para extraer valor de los datos. Incidentes reportados en 2019 y 2020 por trimestres En tercer lugar, hay que reconocer que el proceso de digitalizacin tambin conlleva riesgos. Al aumentar la dependencia en la tecnologa, se incrementa el riesgo tecnolgico. Hay que hacer una mencin especial al ciberriesgo. El aumento de interconexiones, tanto con terceros como con clientes, aumenta la probabilidad de ataques, como se ha evidenciado durante la pandemia. Esta transicin hacia lo digital conlleva tambin la tarea de formar a los empleados en las nuevas herramientas y procesos. Sin duda, el perfil del empleado bancario sufrir una reorientacin hacia aptitudes ms relacionadas con la tecnologa y manejo de datos. Por ltimo, las autoridades hemos de reconocer y apoyar los programas de digitalizacin de la banca, asistiendo as al sector en su proceso de modernizacin. Un ejemplo es la creacin en noviembre de 2020 del Sandbox. En la primera oleada se recibieron 67 proyectos y estn comenzando los anlisis de los primeros pilotos admitidos en el entorno controlado de pruebas. El 1 de septiembre empez el plazo para presentar solicitudes para la segunda oleada. La Ley para la transformacin digital del sistema financiero que regula el Sandbox pretende facilitar el proceso innovador y garantizar que las autoridades financieras disponen de instrumentos adecuados de control en el contexto digital. La digitalizacin implica tambin una decidida apuesta por reforzar la capacitacin de nuestro personal y emprender acciones que potencien el uso de las nuevas tecnologas para el mejor desempeo de nuestras funciones y competencias. El Plan Estratgico del Banco de Espaa est comprometido con el fomento de la innovacin tecnolgica, a lo que se acompaan otras iniciativas no menos importantes en el marco del Eurosistema. Una de ellas, como todos saben, es el Euro digital. Desde el Eurosistema seguimos profundizando en su anlisis a fin de estar preparados para su emisin, si es que as se decidiera. Tras ao y medio de estudio conceptual y experimentacin, el pasado mes de julio el Consejo de Gobierno del BCE acord poner en marcha un proyecto de investigacin. As, durante los prximos dos aos, analizaremos con detalle distintas caractersticas y configuraciones para poder determinar cmo debera ser el Euro digital. Es decir, cul es la combinacin ptima de las distintas opciones de diseo que consiga dar respuesta a las necesidades de los usuarios y, al tiempo, minimizar los efectos sobre la estabilidad financiera y monetaria. Algunas de estas cuestiones ya estn claras, como es el caso del modelo de distribucin de esta moneda. Falta por ultimar detalles como, por ejemplo, el papel especfico de las entidades supervisadas. Pero nos dirigimos hacia un modelo intermediado en el que las entidades sean las encargadas de hacer llegar el Euro digital a los usuarios. Por tanto, el Euro digital no pretende competir con la banca, como se escucha a veces, sino que se espera que abra oportunidades para que las entidades ofrezcan servicios nuevos o de manera novedosa sobre una base segura y comn a toda la zona euro. Conclusin Permtanme concluir. En mi intervencin he hecho un repaso a los principales retos y preocupaciones supervisoras presentes en el corto plazo, partiendo de un anlisis de la situacin actual del sector financiero. Considero que las entidades espaolas se encuentran en una posicin slida para afrontar las incertidumbres a la que esta pandemia nos tiene acostumbrados. No obstante, habr que vigilar la evolucin de los distintos activos para detectar lo antes posible aquellas exposiciones que puedan presentar algn signo de deterioro. Tomar medidas con la mayor anticipacin ser clave para evitar posibles males mayores en el futuro. Adems de esta tarea inminente, el sector financiero tiene el reto de adaptarse a un nuevo entorno ms digital, con nuevos competidores y en el que riesgos nuevos como los climticos cobrarn protagonismo. Para afrontar este panorama, las entidades debern reflexionar sobre sus modelos de negocio y cmo reorientarlos para adaptarse a este marco buscando adems la tan necesaria rentabilidad. Tambin he querido poner mucho nfasis en la digitalizacin. Como he sealado, establecer una estrategia clara en este sentido es clave, como lo es tambin destinar los recursos necesarios en un entorno de mrgenes ajustados. Convirtamos estos retos en oportunidades para crecer ms y de una manera equilibrada, justa y sostenible. Tenemos por delante un camino muy interesante que recorrer. Muchas gracias

Title: Governor. Financial Education Day
text: 04.10.2021 Financial Education Day Ministry of Economic Affairs and Digital Transformation, National Securities Market Commission and Bank of Spain Pablo Hernandez de Cos Governor of the Bank of Spain H.E. First Vice-President of the Government and Minister of Economic Affairs and Digital Transformation, Secretary of State for Education, President of the National Securities Market Commission, Director General of Consumer Affairs, other authorities, ladies and gentlemen, It is a pleasure for me to celebrate this central event of Financial Education Day at the Bank of Spain. As every year, we meet this first Monday in October to reiterate our institutional commitment to the promotion of financial education among Spanish citizens and our support for the action of the Financial Education Plan. This year the focus has been on sustainable finance. The concept of sustainable finance or "green finance" is of great importance from the perspective of citizens and should therefore be a priority in our financial education agenda. Let us take the main risks arising from climate change and the fight against climate change. On the one hand, the so-called physical risks are those that, if we do not act to prevent global warming, will materialize as permanent alterations of the climate, with increasingly frequent natural disasters and with economic damage probably also greater. In fact, there is evidence that these risks are already materializing to some extent: according to FSB1, global economic losses associated with weather-related catastrophes have doubled since the 1990s. 1 V8ease Financial Stability Board (noviembre de 2020): The Implications of Climate Change for Financial Stability. These physical risks are relevant for the valuation of real estate assets and may particularly affect certain sectors, such as agriculture or tourism. In addition, its incidence will be unequal by geographical areas and could even generate migrations of activities and even of the population. And, of course, it would also affect the financial sector. In parallel to physical risks, the transition to an environmentally sustainable economy entails a broad transformation of production technologies and a reallocation of activities between different sectors and companies. Indeed, such restructuring will mean that, in the short term, some sectors will increase their profits while others will incur losses, with implications for the financial system and its stability. These changes will occur as a consequence of the need to adapt to greener ways of producing, due to changes in investor and consumer sentiment, public regulation or taxation. Climate change could also have a direct impact on inflation and economic activity. It is highly likely that policies aimed at promoting Transition to a carbon-neutral economy, such as carbon taxes, affect the volatility of headline inflation, which includes energy prices. And, to the extent that producers of carbon-intensive non-energy goods and services in their production pass on the costs of increased carbon taxes and other interventions to their consumers, considerable upward pressures on core inflation could also be observed. Similarly, climate change could have negative effects on productivity, resulting from the impact of higher temperatures on labour supply and the destruction of capital associated with natural disasters. While the transition to a more sustainable economy will require substantial investment in green technologies, which could raise trend productivity growth, The potential impact on all these economic variables is, in fact, the reason that justifies the enormous analytical efforts that are being developed in the community of financial supervisors and central banks in understanding the impact of climate risks on the economy in general and, in particular, on the financial sector. Thus, an important part of the recent review of the monetary policy strategy that we have developed at the European Central Bank (ECB) has focused on incorporating climate change considerations. And in response to this challenge we have designed an ambitious agenda in this area. A first step has been the ECB carrying out a stress test exercise, the results of which were published last September, which analyses the impact of climate change on more than 4 million companies globally and 1,600 banking institutions under three different climate policy scenarios. At the Bank of Spain we are developing an ambitious analytical instrument to incorporate climate risks into our analyses and, in particular, into stress tests, the first results of which will be published this autumn. This analytical effort is crucial to introduce climate considerations into the actions of financial supervisors and central banks in pursuit of our financial stability or price stability mandates. And it must also serve as a spearhead for the rest of the financial system to do the same and develop the data, methodologies, markets and financial instruments that allow internalizing the climate costs in the prices of the different products offered to customers. In this way, the concept of sustainable finance is closely related to individual financial decisions: climate change and the fight against it will affect the profitability of the products in which citizens invest. In addition, our actions, including those related to the management of personal finances, impact the environmental and social sustainability of our planet. From this perspective, citizens' savings decisions can crucially help to achieve the objectives we have set ourselves in this area. And financial education must contribute to this objective of making citizens aware of the risks, but also of the opportunities, associated with climate change. Result therefore, it is particularly pertinent that the focus of this Financial Education Day is placed on this occasion on sustainable finance. On how to achieve this, let me highlight four points. First, we must highlight the importance of the decision to incorporate the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Digital Transformation into the agreement of the Financial Education Plan 2022-2025 and to become a promoter of it together with the Bank of Spain and CNMV. With this decision, the National Financial Education Strategy is powerfully reinforced, which, among other aspects, will allow us to expand the network of collaborators and achieve greater capillarity in our actions. Secondly, as I have already pointed out on several occasions, the promoters of the Plan have the obligation, as in any public policy, to support our actions on empirical evidence that supports the effectiveness and efficiency of our actions. In this regard, I would like to highlight that the Bank of Spain will carry out the second wave of the Financial Skills Survey in the coming months. Without information, there can be no evaluation. And, in coordination with the OECD, work has just been completed to assess financial skills among our small and medium-sized enterprises. Thirdly, given the educational reforms currently under discussion, we should not miss the opportunity to deepen the incorporation of economic and financial knowledge into the school curriculum in both secondary and primary education, as recommended by international institutions. Finally, and beyond the academic cycle, it is important that we continue to put a special focus on our financial education actions in groups with specific needs, such as the population in vulnerable situations, immigrants or the elderly. And that we adequately address from the public sector the problems of financial exclusion that may arise as a result of recent demographic and economic trends. Undoubtedly, these are exciting challenges for the next four years that we hope to be able to share here every first of October. Thanks a lot.
text_original: 04.10.2021 Da de la Educacin Financiera Ministerio de Asuntos Econmicos y Transformacin Digital, Comisin Nacional del Mercado de Valores y Banco de Espaa Pablo Hernndez de Cos Gobernador del Banco de Espaa Excma. Sra. vicepresidenta Primera del Gobierno y Ministra de Asuntos Econmicos y Transformacin Digital, Sr. secretario de Estado de Educacin, Sr. presidente de la Comisin Nacional del Mercado de Valores, directora general de Consumo, resto de autoridades, seoras y seores: Es para m un placer celebrar este acto central del Da de la Educacin Financiera en el Banco de Espaa. Como cada ao, nos reunimos este primer lunes de octubre para reiterar nuestro compromiso institucional con la promocin de la educacin financiera entre los ciudadanos espaoles y nuestro apoyo a la accin del Plan de Educacin Financiera. Este ao el foco se ha puesto en las finanzas sostenibles. El concepto de finanzas sostenibles o finanzas verdes es de gran importancia desde la perspectiva de los ciudadanos y, por tanto, debe ser objeto prioritario en nuestra agenda de educacin financiera. Tomemos los principales riesgos que se originan como consecuencia del cambio climtico y de la lucha contra el cambio climtico. Por un lado, los denominados riesgos fsicos son los que, si no actuamos para evitar el calentamiento global, se materializarn como alteraciones permanentes del clima, con catstrofes naturales cada vez ms frecuentes y con daos econmicos probablemente tambin mayores. De hecho, existe evidencia de que esos riesgos ya se estn materializando en cierta medida: segn el FSB1, las prdidas econmicas globales asociadas a catstrofes relacionadas con fenmenos meteorolgicos se han duplicado desde la dcada de 1990. 1 Vase Financial Stability Board (noviembre de 2020): The Implications of Climate Change for Financial Stability. Estos riesgos fsicos son relevantes para la valoracin de los activos inmobiliarios y pueden afectar particularmente a determinados sectores, como la agricultura o el turismo. Adems, su incidencia ser desigual por reas geogrficas y podra incluso generar migraciones de actividades e incluso de la poblacin. Y, por supuesto, tambin afectara al sector financiero. En paralelo a los riesgos fsicos, la transicin hacia una economa sostenible desde una perspectiva medioambiental conlleva una amplia transformacin de las tecnologas de produccin y una reasignacin de actividades entre los distintos sectores y empresas. De hecho, esa reestructuracin significar que, a corto plazo, algunos sectores aumentarn sus beneficios mientras que otros incurrirn en prdidas, con implicaciones para el sistema financiero y su estabilidad. Estos cambios se producirn como consecuencia de la necesidad de adaptarse a formas de producir ms verdes, debido a cambios en el sentimiento de los inversores y los consumidores, de la regulacin pblica o de la tributacin. El cambio climtico podra tambin tener un impacto directo sobre la inflacin y la actividad econmica. Es altamente probable que las polticas dirigidas a promover la transicin hacia una economa neutra en carbono como los impuestos sobre el carbono afecten a la volatilidad de la inflacin general, que incluye los precios de la energa. Y, en la medida en que los productores de bienes y servicios no energticos con un uso intensivo de carbono en su produccin repercutan los costes del aumento de los impuestos sobre el carbono y de otras intervenciones a sus consumidores, podran observarse tambin considerables presiones al alza en la inflacin subyacente. Del mismo modo, el cambio climtico podra tener efectos negativos sobre la productividad, derivados del impacto de unas temperaturas ms elevadas sobre la oferta de trabajo y la destruccin de capital asociada a las catstrofes naturales. Si bien, la transicin hacia una economa ms sostenible exigir una inversin sustancial en tecnologas verdes, que podra elevar el crecimiento tendencial de la productividad, El potencial impacto sobre todas estas variables econmicas es, de hecho, la razn que justifica los enormes esfuerzos analticos que se estn desarrollando en la comunidad de supervisores financieros y bancos centrales en entender el impacto de los riesgos climticos sobre la economa en general y, en particular, sobre el sector financiero. As, una parte importante de la reciente revisin de la estrategia de poltica monetaria que hemos desarrollado en el Banco Central Europeo (BCE) se ha concentrado en incorporar las consideraciones de cambio climtico. Y en respuesta a este reto hemos diseado una ambiciosa agenda en esta materia. Un primer paso ha sido la realizacin por parte del BCE de un ejercicio de stress test, cuyos resultados se publicaron el pasado septiembre, en el que se analiza el impacto del cambio climtico sobre ms de 4 millones de empresas a escala global y 1.600 instituciones bancarias bajo tres escenarios de polticas climticas diferentes. En el Banco de Espaa estamos desarrollando un ambicioso instrumental analtico para incorporar los riesgos climticos a nuestros anlisis y, en particular, a los stress test, cuyos primeros resultados se publicarn este otoo. Este esfuerzo analtico resulta crucial para introducir las consideraciones climticas en las actuaciones de supervisores financieros y bancos centrales en aras de la consecucin de nuestros mandatos de estabilidad financiera o de estabilidad de precios. Y tambin debe servir de punta de lanza para que el resto del sistema financiero haga lo propio y se desarrollen los datos, metodologas, mercados e instrumentos financieros que permitan internalizar los costes climticos en los precios de los diferentes productos que se ofrecen a los clientes. De este modo el concepto de finanzas sostenibles se relaciona estrechamente con las decisiones financieras individuales: el cambio climtico y la lucha contra el mismo afectarn a la rentabilidad de los productos en los que invierten los ciudadanos. Asimismo, nuestras acciones, incluidas las relativas a la gestin de las finanzas personales, impactan en la sostenibilidad medioambiental y social de nuestro planeta. Desde esta perspectiva, las decisiones de ahorro de los ciudadanos pueden ayudar crucialmente al logro de los objetivos que nos hemos marcado en este mbito. Y la educacin financiera debe contribuir a este objetivo de que los ciudadanos conozcan los riesgos, pero tambin de las oportunidades, asociadas al cambio climtico. Resulta, por tanto, particularmente pertinente que el foco de este Da de la Educacin Financiera se site en esta ocasin en las finanzas sostenibles. Sobre cmo lograrlo, permtanme que subraye cuatro cuestiones. En primer, hay que destacar la importancia de la decisin de incorporacin del Ministerio de Asuntos Econmicos y Transformacin Digital al convenio del Plan de Educacin Financiera 2022-2025 y de convertirse en promotor del mismo junto al Banco de Espaa y CNMV. Con esta decisin se refuerza poderosamente la Estrategia Nacional de Educacin Financiera, lo que, entre otros aspectos, nos permitir ampliar la red de colaboradores y de alcanzar una mayor capilaridad en nuestras acciones. En segundo lugar, como ya he sealado en distintas ocasiones, los promotores del Plan tenemos la obligacin, como en cualquier poltica pblica, de apoyar nuestras acciones en las evidencias empricas que avalen la eficacia y eficiencia de nuestras acciones. A este respecto, me gustara destacar que el Banco de Espaa va a realizar en los prximos meses la segunda ola de la Encuesta de Competencias Financieras. Sin informacin, no puede haber evaluacin. Y, en coordinacin con la OCDE, se acaba de concluir un trabajo para valorar las competencias financieras entre nuestras pequeas y medianas empresas. En tercer lugar, ante las reformas educativas que se encuentran actualmente en discusin, no deberamos dejar pasar la oportunidad para profundizar en la incorporacin de los conocimientos econmicos y financieros en el curriculum escolar tanto en educacin secundaria como en primaria, como recomiendan las instituciones internacionales. Finalmente, y ms all del ciclo acadmico, es importante que sigamos poniendo un especial foco en nuestras acciones de educacin financiera en los colectivos con necesidades especficas, como la poblacin en situacin de vulnerabilidad, inmigrantes o personas mayores. Y que abordemos adecuadamente desde el sector pblico los problemas de exclusin financiera que puedan surgir como resultado de las tendencias demogrficas y econmicas recientes. Sin duda, son retos apasionantes para los prximos cuatro aos que esperemos poder compartir aqu cada primero de octubre. Muchas gracias.

Title: L'Agefi Global Investment Forum. From the review of the ECB's strategy in 2021 to the possible return of inflation, what macroeconomic prospects do European investors face? Notes for intervention
text: 06.10.2021 First plenary session: From the review of the ECB's strategy in 2021 to the possible return of inflation, what macroeconomic prospects are facing European investors? Notes for intervention Global Investment Forum, meeting organized by L'AGEFI Margarita Delgado Subgobernadora Outlook for the euro area economy after COVID - We are witnessing a strong recovery in economic activity in the euro area, as the reopening of the economy continues following the progress of vaccination campaigns. According to the latest ECB staff macroeconomic projections, euro area real GDP is expected to exceed the pre-pandemic level by the end of this year. Going forward, strong growth is also expected for next year, at 4.6%, followed by a fall to levels slightly above 2% in 2023. - There is also a sharp increase in inflation in the euro area, which reached 3.4% in September, according to the estimated growth. You have to go back to 2008 to find levels like these. A debate has been opened as to whether or not this high inflation is transitory, and indeed we are very likely to deal with this issue later, but let me tell you now what I think about it. My personal view is in line with the ECB's position, which believes that the high level of inflation is largely due to transitory factors, such as supply bottlenecks, increases in energy prices and the reversal of the VAT cut in Germany. Part of this inflation should therefore be reabsorbed over the medium term. This view is also shared by ECB experts, who expect the inflation rate to exceed 2% on average this year and then fall to 1.7% in 2022 and 1.5% in 2023, well below our 2% target. - However, there is no doubt that this central scenario is subject to risk. A worsening of the pandemic due, for example, to the emergence of new variants of the virus, could slow down the economic recovery. On the inflation front, if supply bottlenecks prove to be more persistent than expected, high inflation could eventually be passed on to the new collective agreements and thus reinforced by second-round effects. And, of course, we have yet to see how the Evergrande crisis evolves, as a hypothetical disorderly collapse could have an adverse impact on global financial markets. - Finally, from a longer-term perspective, I believe that successful implementation of the NGEU fund will be essential for the euro area economy to grow substantially in the coming years. To this end, it is obviously necessary for Member States to make appropriate use of these funds, selecting investment projects that favour growth with the maximum use of digital technologies and that are also respectful of the environment. Effects of the COVID crisis and the policy mix applied during the pandemic on potential growth and inflation. - In my opinion, the question of how the pandemic will affect potential growth is very complex, as many unknowns still need to be cleared. I see all kinds of effects in different directions. Some of the sectors that have been most affected by the pandemic may never regain the dynamism prior to the pandemic crisis. I'm referring to the retail sector, as online shopping has skyrocketed during the pandemic, and to work travel, due to the more intensive use of technology to Organize meetings. I don't think they're going to disappear completely, but our lifestyle is changing and the pandemic has accelerated this process somehow. On the other hand, I see the NGEU d0 a public policy initiative that would not have existed without the pandemic d0 as an excellent opportunity to raise the EU's growth potential. Ultimately, everything will depend on how these opposing forces materialize. - Another question is how inflation will evolve after the pandemic. What matters here is not potential growth, but real growth relative to potential, or more specifically, the level of real GDP relative to potentiald1what we call the output gap. In a context of economic reopening and rapid demand growth such as the current one, and given that supply cannot adjust at the same pace, it is normal for the output gap to widen and, therefore, for inflation to also increase. This is basically the situation we are in right now. Ultimately, however, this intense demand growth will stabilise and supply will also tighten, so the widening output gap should be reduced to some extent. In principle, these developments should cause inflation to fall again in the medium term. - This is not to say, of course, that things can't happen differently. If supply bottlenecks drag on longer than anticipated, high inflation could end up being passed on to new wage agreements, which would increase firms' production costs and could eventually translate into higher prices. Through these second-round effects, the current high inflation could become very persistent. This is a scenario we cannot rule out at all. - But I would like to end with a positive message. It has become clear over the past decade that central banks in advanced economies find it very difficult to combat low inflation, as monetary policy is constrained by the lower bound of nominal interest rates. But this limitation does not affect the battle against high inflation, since, in principle, central banks can raise their interest rates as much as necessary to curb the rise in prices. For this reason, and because the ECB has a clear inflation target of 2%, I am convinced that the high inflation figures we are currently experiencing will not become a persistent phenomenon in the future. - I am aware that high levels of public debt raise doubts about possible fiscal dominance, as a result of which central banks may not raise interest rates as much as necessary to control inflation. But, honestly, I don't think this is a relevant issue for the ECB. The European Central Bank has a comprehensive set of tools that can be optimally combined and used flexibly to raise interest rates as much as necessary without causing turbulence in sovereign bond markets. The optimal mix of economic policies for the future. Will central banks ever be able to raise interest rates again? - On the first question, I believe that monetary policy and fiscal policy should continue to work together for the duration of the pandemic. This means that monetary policy needs to continue to maintain favourable financing conditions and that fiscal authorities need to continue to support businesses and households, although, as the economy reopens, this support needs to be increasingly targeted. - A much more complex aspect is how to reduce monetary and fiscal support once the pandemic crisis ends. In my opinion, one of the few things that is clear is the need to avoid cliff effects. When the time comes to withdraw policy support, it should be done in a gradual and predictable manner.
