Los pases que superan este umbral en cualquiera de estas categoras se definen como terceros pases materiales por ser pases fuera de la UE, donde el mbito de las polticas macro y microprudenciales no est definido por normativas comunes y donde la reciprocidad de ciertas medidas no est garantizada. En caso de detectarse riesgos cclicos en un tercer pas, un equipo de trabajo especializado de la JERS realizara una evaluacin cuantitativa y cualitativa detallada. Dicho anlisis recomendara la activacin o no de un colchn de capital anticclico para las exposiciones europeas a ese pas. En 2021, se identificaron 8 pases materiales, 5 de los cuales se encuentran en Amrica Latina (Brasil, Mxico, Chile, Colombia y Per)3. De hecho, las exposiciones a Amrica Latina suponan, a finales de 2020 un cuarto del total de exposiciones de la banca fuera de Espaa, incluida la UE. Esa proporcin es, incluso, superior a la de las exposiciones a economas de la propia Unin Europea. Por todas estas razones, el Banco de Espaa realiza un seguimiento cercano de los riesgos macrofinancieros y del entorno geopoltico y econmico de estos pases denominados materiales. Se pretende con ello prevenir su transmisin al sistema bancario espaol y mitigar sus consecuencias. En este sentido, como bien saben, la situacin econmica de Amrica Latina se ha visto particularmente afectada por la pandemia de COVID-19. El PIB promedio de la regin se contrajo un 7% en 2020, con una elevada heterogeneidad entre pases. Esas diferencias reflejaron, en buena medida, el diverso grado de severidad de las restricciones adoptadas por las distintas autoridades, las diferentes estructuras productivas y vinculaciones comerciales y el distinto apoyo de las polticas econmicas. La nota positiva recientemente es que la recuperacin de la actividad parece haberse consolidado en el tercer trimestre, especialmente en las economas andinas, gracias a un fuerte repunte del consumo privado. Esa recuperacin se ha visto apoyada por los programas de estmulo fiscal y monetario, aunque en un entorno de elevada incertidumbre internacional. Adems, la regin ha acelerado el proceso de vacunacin, alcanzado un porcentaje superior incluso al de Estados Unidos. Todo ello ha llevado a que el FMI proyecte un crecimiento de 6,3% para el conjunto de Amrica Latina y el Caribe para 2021, y que el PIB de economas como la chilena, la colombiana y la peruana se haya situado por encima de su nivel previo a la pandemia en el tercer trimestre de 2021. En paralelo a la recuperacin de la actividad, y tambin como consecuencia del encarecimiento de la energa y los alimentos, la inflacin ha aumentado significativamente en toda la regin, situndose por encima de los objetivos de los bancos centrales, en algunos casos hasta niveles mximos de una dcada. Ello ha llevado a algunos bancos centrales a iniciar el ciclo de endurecimiento de la poltica monetaria para evitar que las expectativas de inflacin de medio plazo, aun relativamente ancladas, se separen de estos objetivos. Con todo, el tono de la poltica monetaria sigue mantenindose, en general y por el momento, en terreno netamente expansivo. Ms a medio plazo, las perspectivas de crecimiento de la regin se encuentran sujetas a un elevado grado de incertidumbre. Se ven condicionadas tanto por factores externos, como la evolucin de China y EEUU y las caractersticas de la normalizacin monetaria por parte de la Reserva Federal de EEUU, como internos. En cuanto a estos ltimos, cabe destacar los desafos que plantea el bajo crecimiento potencial de Amrica Latina comparado con otras reas emergentes y la elevada desigualdad en la regin. Los avances en la agenda de reformas estructurales de medio plazo siguen siendo tmidos y se encuentran sujetos a una elevada incertidumbre, en un contexto de tensionamiento social y poltico. Asimismo, los esfuerzos para consolidar los elevados dficits fiscales y reducir la carga de la deuda suponen un reto importante. Ms an en un contexto de elevada inflacin y, potencialmente de endurecimiento de las condiciones de financiacin. Pese a estas dificultades en el mbito econmico, el sector bancario de la regin se ha mantenido slido y saneado durante la crisis sanitaria, a diferencia de lo que habra sido la norma en la regin, que ha sufrido numerosas crisis bancarias a lo largo de su historia. En parte, dicha resiliencia se deriva de la buena situacin de partida de las entidades, con altos niveles de capital y provisiones, y de una generalizada gestin prudente de los riesgos. Pero, sobre todo, es fruto de la aprobacin de medidas de apoyo al sistema financiero por parte de las autoridades. As, desde el inicio de la pandemia, los gobiernos y las autoridades competentes (bancos centrales, reguladores y supervisores) han aprobado numerosas medidas para asegurar la liquidez en el corto plazo y sostener el flujo de crdito a los agentes econmicos mediante el establecimiento de lneas de crdito garantizadas por los estados y la flexibilizacin de las condiciones de financiacin. Adicionalmente, otro de los objetivos fue reducir el impacto del riesgo crediticio para las entidades financieras. Una de las principales medidas, en ese sentido, consisti en la promocin de la aplicacin de moratorias sobre los crditos existentes a hogares y empresas, lo que ha permitido flexibilizar los criterios de reclasificacin y dotacin de dichos prstamos. Adicionalmente, estas moratorias se han combinado frecuentemente con modificaciones de las condiciones de pago (reestructuracin y refinanciacin de crditos)4. 4 Buesa, A., Elena Vidal, Jos Luis Puente y Alberto Flores (2021), Medidas de apoyo al crdito y al sector financiero en los sistemas bancarios con relevancia material para Espaa, Nota Econmica del Banco de Espaa octubre 2021. Por ltimo, las autoridades de la regin tambin han adoptado numerosas medidas regulatorias y prudenciales, en lnea con las adoptadas por el resto de pases, que han permitido mitigar el impacto de la recesin en la solvencia de los bancos. Entre ellas destacan la limitacin del pago de dividendos, la reduccin temporal de los requerimientos de capital o la flexibilizacin de dichos requerimientos para bancos que concedieran crdito. Tampoco debe olvidarse la puesta en marcha en algunos pases, como Chile y Colombia, de programas de compras de activos similares en su instrumentacin a los llevados a cabo en las economas avanzadas y con el objetivo exitoso de reducir la volatilidad en los mercados financieros por primera vez en la historia de la regin. Se puede sealar sin temor a equivocarse que las medidas puestas en marcha han dado resultado. As, al inicio de la pandemia el crdito no solo no se desaceler, sino que registr, con carcter general, un fuerte repunte, aunque no en todos los pases. Las ratios de capital y liquidez no se deterioraron, y la rentabilidad, aunque descendi, se mantuvo, en general, por encima de los mnimos histricos. Los bancos tampoco registraron problemas de financiacin, toda vez que los depsitos aumentaron sustancialmente debido al ahorro forzoso provocado por las restricciones a la movilidad. Adems, algunos de ellos mantuvieron el acceso a los mercados internacionales de renta fija. Finalmente, los prstamos impagados se mantuvieron en niveles bajos y, gracias a los programas de moratorias de prstamos, incluso descendieron en algunos pases. A medida que se han ido retirando los programas de apoyo, se ha observado una desaceleracin en el crecimiento del crdito que, no obstante, ha empezado a repuntar a partir de mediados del ao a medida que la actividad se recuperaba. Adems, se han registrado mejoras de las ratios de capital en los dos primeros trimestres de este ao, al seguir en vigor la mayor parte de las medidas anteriormente mencionadas. Igualmente, la rentabilidad de las entidades financieras ha aumentado gracias al incremento de los mrgenes de intermediacin -explicado, en parte, por el comienzo de la normalizacin de los tipos de inters oficiales-, mientras que las provisiones continuaron aumentando. En sentido negativo, a medida que se han ido retirando estos programas se ha observado cierto deterioro de la calidad de los activos, aunque la tasa de morosidad sigue todava en niveles poco preocupantes. En definitiva, y con ello querra cerrar mi intervencin, Amrica Latina es una regin muy relevante para la banca espaola y, por tanto, para el Banco de Espaa. La regin ofrece, a da de hoy, grandes oportunidades. Hay 646 millones de latinoamericanos, conformados en una sociedad madura, con un significativo peso de las clases medias. Adems, las entidades financieras latinoamericanas han demostrado tener una notable fortaleza al superar las condiciones extremas generadas por la pandemia gracias, en buena medida, a las respuestas de las autoridades competentes. El reto que se presenta de cara al futuro es que sean capaces de adaptarse a una situacin en la que, si bien la recuperacin econmica se est afianzado, las medidas de soporte van a ir desapareciendo paulatinamente en un contexto en el que an persisten desequilibrios macroeconmicos y sociales importantes y en el que no acaban de definirse las reformas estructurales que necesitan estas economas. Muchas gracias por su atencin.

Title: Closing of the II National Congress of Banking Law of the ICAM
text: 29.04.2022 Closing of the II National Congress of Banking Law ICAM Margarita Delgado Subgobernadora Good morning The calendar has meant that the closing of this Congress coincides with two events related to dispute resolution mechanisms in the financial field. My initial intention was to refer to one of them, the 35th anniversary of the entry into operation of the claims service of the Bank of Spain, but the recent opening of the public hearing process of the Draft Law of the Independent Administrative Authority for the Defense of Financial Customers leads me to include some references to it. The importance of the conduct of entities As is known, the financial sector is subject to strong regulation justified by the important role played by financial institutions in the process of money intermediation. Banks capture and guard deposits from the public and, together with other financial actors, provide the credit necessary for the proper functioning of the economic system. And, in addition, they manage payment services and the circulation of cash. The regulation of the sector and its consequent supervision by public authorities is a guarantee of stability and is based on two fundamental pillars. One of them is the establishment of prudential requirements that seek to guarantee the solvency of financial institutions, through the imposition of levels of own resources linked to the risks assumed by the entity. The other pillar is that of adequate protection of the financial customer through detailed regulation of the relations between institutions and their clients. The fluidity and transparency of this relationship and the maintenance of the necessary trust of citizens are a basic component for the functioning of the financial services market. It is also for the very survival of the entities, so that, for all these reasons, it constitutes a reason for preferential attention on the part of the supervisors and, naturally, of the Bank of Spain. It is to this pillar that we refer when we talk about the conduct of entities. Indeed, the banking business is based on the trust that customers place in the entities and that generated by the entities among themselves, which gives rise to a system whose operation depends, to a large extent, on an intangible value such as appropriate conduct. It should be borne in mind here that this adaptation should not be limited to mere regulatory compliance, but also involves entities implementing a culture of good practices and appropriate treatment of their customers throughout the organization. In short, banking malpractice can undermine the foundations of banking activity, damaging confidence in banks and in the system in general. For this reason, the Bank of Spain, like the rest of financial regulators and supervisors, has intensified its supervisory and regulatory work in order to ensure that entities have internal procedures that guarantee the proper conduct and protection of their customers. The main role of the complaints service, individual dispute resolution... The work of the Bank of Spain is not only focused on supervised entities, on the offer of financial products, but also has certain functions assigned with respect to the applicants of these products, the customers. Prominent among these features is our dispute resolution mechanism, which provides customers with a system to analyze and resolve disputes regarding banking products and services, resolve queries and promote financial education. This public service, a pioneer in Europe, was born within the framework of the process of liberalization of interest rates and commissions which, initiated in 1981, culminated in the Ministerial Order of 3 March 1987, a direct antecedent of the current regulation. The general principle of this rule was the freedom of prices of banking products and services. This principle was complemented by a range of rules to protect customers with the ultimate aim of promoting competition and facilitating comparison through the reinforcement of pre-contractual information. Among other aspects, the aforementioned order provided for the creation in the Bank of Spain of a claims service, responsible for receiving and processing claims that may be made by customers of deposit institutions. The order also empowered the Bank of Spain to regulate its organization and operation and marked the beginning of its actions on September 1, 1987. The satisfactory experience of this claims service was key to subsequently regulate the operation of homonyms in the National Securities Market Commission and in the General Directorate of Insurance and Pension Funds. In this way, the complaints services of the three financial supervisors were subject to the same regulation, under the principles of independence, transparency, contradiction, efficiency, legality, freedom and representation. The complaint to supervisors is useful for citizens who have not received a satisfactory response from the customer services of financial institutions, since they are free, more flexible and faster than judicial processes and do not require legal assistance. Thousands of customers come to these processes every year. While it is true that the decisions of the claims services are not binding on the parties, it is also true that the entities comply with them in a high percentage of cases and that, very often, the criteria they establish inspire subsequent judicial decisions. Specifically, the Claims Service of the Bank of Spain, throughout its almost 35 years of existence, has resolved more than 350,000 claims and almost 600,000 queries (written and telephone), with annual peaks of 40,000 and 50,000, respectively. ... In addition, it is a key piece for the development of other functions related to the conduct of entities Beyond the mere singular resolution of disputes, it is also worth highlighting the enormous contribution of the complaints system to the processes of conduct monitoring and transparency, insofar as its detailed observation and, in particular, its repetition, often reveals the existence of regulatory breaches or bad banking practices in supervised entities. In this sense, the Bank of Spain takes advantage of the information obtained from the claims files to guide its supervisory activity, achieving greater efficiency in the control of the conduct of the entities. This closes a circle in which, on the one hand, the processing of complaints provides valuable information to the supervisor on the areas of improvement in customer service and marketing of each entity and, on the other hand, through supervisory action, contributes to the reduction of conflict by attacking inefficiencies at their source. On the other hand, and as a complement to its supervisory utility, the criteria of good practices developed in the resolution of individual disputes, have become, over the years, a basic reference in terms of banking transparency. This activity has generated a powerful para-regulatory tool, which, in many cases, has inspired the elaboration of positive law rules, crystallizing in specific precepts included in the banking and payment transparency regulations. The complaints reports published annually reflect the criteria of good practice. In addition, they constitute a tool used by the entities themselves, the Bank of Spain, the courts, consumer associations, law firms, consultants or consumer service networks. But, in addition, it is frequently consulted by financial customers themselves, thus becoming a training tool, to the extent that it also contributes to financial education. In this sense, the value of the complaints system as a repository of banking operations commonly carried out by citizens and to detect gaps in citizens' knowledge and possible problems of understanding the products and services offered by banking and payment intermediaries is undeniable. All this makes the complaints mechanism a key element for the design and implementation by the Bank of Spain of actions related to the financial education of citizens. The Bank of Spain is currently working on the preparation of the Claims Report corresponding to 2021. I can tell you that, during that year, the number of complaints submitted by users of banking and payment services exceeded 34,000, that is, 55% more than in the previous year. This figure is a good example of how citizens often continue to resort to this way of resolving their disputes as a preliminary or alternative step to submitting them for resolution by the courts. On the future of financial claims resolution As I have explained, in the area of conflict resolution we continue to deploy our best work, without losing sight of the fact that we are immersed in a transition phase towards the creation of a new Independent Administrative Authority for the Defense of Financial Clients that reinforces extrajudicial channels of conflict resolution in the financial sector. Since the approval of Law 10/2014, of June 26, on the organization, supervision and solvency of credit institutions, the need to establish effective institutional systems for the resolution of individual conflicts was already pointed out, a need that has been reiterated in different legal regulations and that has culminated in the mandate contained in Law 7/2017, on alternative resolution of consumer disputes, which imposes the creation by law, of a single entity, for "the resolution, binding or not, of consumer disputes in the financial sector". Thus, the creation of this authority was foreseen in the Recovery, Transformation and Resilience Plan presented by the Government of Spain on April 30, 2021 and, finally, on April 5, the Government has approved the draft law to create the Independent Administrative Authority for the Defense of the Financial Client that is located, on this date, in the public hearing phase. The Bank of Spain, while underlining the importance and usefulness of the current dispute resolution system, has also been expressing the need to review the regulation of the claims resolution system so that it becomes more effective. We have traditionally advocated a system of separation between prudential and conduct supervision, in which each of these functions is exercised in a unified manner for the entire financial system in separate institutions. The system that has finally been opted for, however, is that of the creation of an independent Authority that can also be valid. The preliminary draft provides that the Independent Management Authority resolves claims not only for breaches of the rules of conduct or good financial practices and practices, but also has the capacity to enter into issues such as, among others, the abusive nature of contractual clauses in the banking field. The resolutions will be free for citizens and will be binding on the financial institution when the amounts claimed are less than 20,000 euros, all financial institutions being obliged to participate in the procedures before said authority. Currently, the Banco de Espa96a is evaluating the preliminary draft to contribute, in the public hearing phase, with its comments and suggestions based on its long experience in resolving claims in the banking sector. In any case, for the Banco de Espa96a the necessary collaboration that must exist between the new authority and the financial supervisors is fundamental, exchanging information related to individual conflicts, because of the special importance that, as I have pointed out, it has for the exercise of its supervisory and regulatory functions. Such coordination is also necessary because the institutional system of customer protection is based on the proper functioning of the customer services of each entity, which is subject to the supervision of the financial authorities. Finally, and I will finish, I am sure that this new authority was born to give continuity to the work carried out by the Bank of Spain, for almost 35 years, incorporating new tools to achieve the objectives of efficiency and public service that have guided, since its creation, the activity of the claims service of the Bank of Spain.
text_original: 29.04.2022 Clausura del II Congreso Nacional de Derecho Bancario ICAM Margarita Delgado Subgobernadora Buenos das, El calendario ha propiciado que la clausura de este Congreso coincida con dos acontecimientos relacionados con los mecanismos de resolucin de litigios en el mbito financiero. Mi intencin inicial era referirme a uno de ellos, el 35 aniversario de la entrada en funcionamiento del servicio de reclamaciones del Banco de Espaa, pero la reciente apertura del proceso de audiencia pblica del Anteproyecto de Ley de la Autoridad Administrativa Independiente de Defensa del Cliente Financiero me lleva a incluir algunas referencias al mismo. La importancia de la conducta de las entidades Como es conocido, el sector financiero est sometido a una fuerte regulacin justificada por el importante papel que desempean las entidades financieras en el proceso de intermediacin del dinero. Los bancos captan y custodian los depsitos del pblico y, junto con otros actores financieros, proporcionan el crdito necesario para el adecuado funcionamiento del sistema econmico. Y, adems, gestionan los servicios de pago y la circulacin del efectivo. La regulacin del sector y su consiguiente supervisin por parte de las autoridades pblicas es una garanta de estabilidad y se basa en dos pilares fundamentales. Uno de ellos consiste en el establecimiento de exigencias prudenciales que buscan garantizar la solvencia de las entidades financieras, mediante la imposicin de unos niveles de recursos propios ligados a los riesgos que asuma la entidad. El otro pilar es el de la adecuada proteccin del cliente financiero mediante una regulacin detallada de las relaciones entre las entidades y sus clientes. La fluidez y la transparencia de esta relacin y el mantenimiento de la necesaria confianza de los ciudadanos son un componente bsico para el funcionamiento del mercado de servicios financieros. Tambin lo es para la propia pervivencia de las entidades, de manera que, por todo ello, constituye un motivo de atencin preferente por parte los supervisores y, naturalmente, del Banco de Espaa. Es a este pilar al que nos referimos cuando hablamos de conducta de las entidades. En efecto, el negocio bancario se sustenta en la confianza que depositan los clientes en las entidades y la que generan las entidades entre s, lo que da lugar a un sistema cuyo funcionamiento depende, en gran medida, de un valor intangible como es una conducta adecuada. Conviene aqu tener presente que esta adecuacin no debe limitarse al mero cumplimiento normativo, sino que tambin pasa por que las entidades implementen en toda la organizacin una cultura de buenas prcticas y trato apropiado a sus clientes. En definitiva, una mala praxis bancaria puede socavar los cimientos de la actividad bancaria, daando la confianza en las entidades y en el sistema en general. Por ello, el Banco de Espaa, al igual que el resto de reguladores y supervisores financieros, ha intensificado su labor supervisora y regulatoria con el fin de asegurar que las entidades disponen de procedimientos internos que garanticen la adecuada conducta y la proteccin de su clientela. El papel principal del servicio de reclamaciones, la resolucin individual de conflictos La labor del Banco de Espaa no se centra solo en las entidades supervisadas, en la oferta de productos financieros, sino que tambin tiene asignadas ciertas funciones respecto a los demandantes de estos productos, los clientes. Y entre estas funciones ocupa un lugar destacado nuestro mecanismo de resolucin de disputas, que pone a disposicin de los clientes un sistema para analizar y dirimir sus conflictos relativos a productos y servicios bancarios, resolver sus consultas y fomentar la educacin financiera. Este servicio pblico, pionero en Europa, naci en el marco del proceso de liberalizacin de los tipos de inters y de las comisiones que, iniciado en 1981, culmin con la Orden Ministerial de 3 de marzo de 1987, antecedente directo de la regulacin actual. El principio general de esta norma era la libertad de precios de los productos y servicios bancarios. Este principio se complementaba con un abanico de reglas para proteger a los clientes con el objetivo ltimo de fomentar la competencia y facilitar la comparacin a travs del refuerzo de la informacin precontractual. Entre otros aspectos, la orden citada dispuso la creacin en el Banco de Espaa de un servicio de reclamaciones, encargado de recibir y tramitar las reclamaciones que pudieran formular los clientes de las entidades de depsito. La orden facultaba adems al Banco de Espaa para regular su organizacin y funcionamiento y marcaba el inicio de sus actuaciones el 1 de septiembre de 1987. La satisfactoria experiencia de este servicio de reclamaciones fue clave para regular posteriormente el funcionamiento de los homnimos en la Comisin Nacional del Mercado de Valores y en la Direccin General de Seguros y Fondos de Pensiones. De este modo quedaron sometidos a una misma regulacin los servicios de reclamaciones de los tres supervisores financieros, bajo los principios de independencia, transparencia, contradiccin, eficacia, legalidad, libertad y representacin. La reclamacin ante los supervisores resulta til para los ciudadanos que no han recibido una respuesta satisfactoria de los servicios de atencin al cliente de las entidades financieras, puesto que son gratuitos, ms flexibles y rpidos que los procesos judiciales y no requieren asistencia letrada. A estos procesos acuden cada ao miles de clientes. Siendo cierto que las resoluciones de los servicios de reclamaciones no tienen carcter vinculante para las partes, tambin lo es que las entidades las acatan en un elevado porcentaje de casos y que, con mucha frecuencia, los criterios que sientan inspiran ulteriores resoluciones judiciales. En concreto, el Servicio de Reclamaciones del Banco de Espaa, a lo largo de sus ya casi 35 aos de andadura ha resuelto ms de 350.000 reclamaciones y casi 600.000 consultas (escritas y telefnicas), con puntas anuales de 40.000 y 50.000, respectivamente.  adems, supone una pieza clave para el desarrollo de otras funciones relacionadas con la conducta de las entidades Ms all de la mera resolucin singular de disputas, tambin hay que destacar la enorme contribucin del sistema de reclamaciones a los procesos de supervisin de conducta y transparencia, en la medida en que, con frecuencia, su observacin detallada y, singularmente, su reiteracin, revela la existencia de incumplimientos de normativa o de malas prcticas bancarias en las entidades supervisadas. En este sentido, el Banco de Espaa aprovecha la informacin obtenida de los expedientes de reclamaciones para orientar su actividad supervisora, logrando una mayor eficacia en el control de la conducta de las entidades. Se cierra as un circulo en el que, por un lado, la tramitacin de reclamaciones aporta una valiosa informacin al supervisor sobre las reas de mejora en la atencin a los clientes y en la comercializacin de cada entidad y, por otro lado, a travs de la accin supervisora, se contribuye a la reduccin de la conflictividad atacando las ineficiencias en su origen. Por otro lado, y como complemento a su utilidad supervisora, los criterios de buenas prcticas elaborados en la resolucin de las disputas individuales, se han convertido, a lo largo de los aos, en una referencia bsica en materia de transparencia bancaria. Esta actividad ha generado una potente herramienta pararregulatoria, que, en muchos casos, ha inspirado la elaboracin de normas de derecho positivo, cristalizando en preceptos especficos recogidos en la normativa de transparencia bancaria y de pagos. Las memorias de reclamaciones publicadas anualmente recogen los criterios de buenas prcticas. Adems, constituyen una herramienta utilizada por las propias entidades, el Banco de Espaa, los rganos jurisdiccionales, las asociaciones de consumidores, las firmas de abogados, las consultoras o por las redes de atencin a consumidores. Pero es que, adems, es frecuentemente consultada por los propios clientes financieros, convirtindose as en una herramienta formativa, en la medida en que tambin contribuye a la educacin financiera. En este sentido es innegable el valor que aporta el sistema de reclamaciones como repositorio de las operaciones bancarias comnmente realizadas por los ciudadanos y para detectar lagunas en los conocimientos de los ciudadanos y eventuales problemas de comprensin de los productos y servicios que ofrecen los intermediarios bancarios y de pagos. Todo ello convierte al mecanismo de reclamaciones en una pieza clave para el diseo y la implementacin por parte del Banco de Espaa de acciones relativas a la educacin financiera de los ciudadanos. Actualmente el Banco de Espaa est trabajando en la elaboracin de la Memoria de Reclamaciones correspondiente a 2021. Les adelanto que, durante ese ao, el nmero de reclamaciones presentadas por los usuarios de servicios bancarios y de pago ha superado las 34.000, es decir, un 55 % ms que en el ao anterior. Esta cifra es un buen exponente de cmo el ciudadano sigue recurriendo con frecuencia a esta forma de resolver sus disputas como paso previo o alternativo a someterlas a resolucin por los rganos jurisdiccionales. Sobre el futuro de la resolucin de reclamaciones financieras Como he explicado, en el rea de la resolucin de conflictos continuamos desplegando nuestro mejor hacer, sin perder de vista que estamos inmersos en una fase de transicin hacia la creacin de una nueva Autoridad Administrativa Independiente de Defensa del Cliente Financiero que refuerce las vas extrajudiciales de resolucin de conflictos en el sector financiero. Desde la aprobacin de la Ley 10/2014, de 26 de junio, de ordenacin, supervisin y solvencia de entidades de crdito, ya se apuntaba la necesidad de instaurar sistemas institucionales eficaces para la resolucin de los conflictos individuales, necesidad que se ha ido reiterando en distintas normas de rango legal y que ha culminado en el mandato recogido en la Ley 7/2017, sobre resolucin alternativa de litigios en materia de consumo, que impone la creacin por ley, de una nica entidad, para la resolucin, con carcter vinculante o no, de litigios de consumo en el sector financiero. As, la creacin de esta autoridad se previ en el Plan de Recuperacin, Transformacin y Resiliencia presentado por el Gobierno de Espaa el 30 de abril de 2021 y, finalmente, el pasado 5 de abril el Gobierno ha aprobado el anteproyecto de ley para crear la Autoridad Administrativa Independiente de Defensa del Cliente Financiero que se encuentra, en esta fecha, en fase de audiencia pblica. El Banco de Espaa, al tiempo que ha venido subrayando la importancia y la utilidad del actual sistema de resolucin de disputas, tambin ha venido expresando la necesidad de revisar la regulacin del sistema de resolucin de reclamaciones para que ganara eficacia. Hemos venido abogando tradicionalmente por un sistema de separacin entre la supervisin prudencial y de conducta, en el que cada una de estas funciones se ejerza de forma unificada para todo el sistema financiero en instituciones separadas. El sistema por el que finalmente se ha apostado, sin embargo, es el de la creacin de una Autoridad independiente que tambin puede ser vlido. El anteproyecto prev que la Autoridad Administrativa Independiente resuelva reclamaciones no slo por incumplimientos de las normas de conducta o las buenas prcticas y usos financieros, sino que tambin tenga capacidad para entrar en cuestiones como, entre otras, el carcter abusivo de clusulas contractuales en el mbito bancario. Las resoluciones tendrn carcter gratuito para los ciudadanos y sern vinculantes para la entidad financiera cuando los importes reclamados sean inferiores a 20.000 euros, quedando obligadas todas las entidades financieras a participar en los procedimientos ante dicha autoridad. En la actualidad, el Banco de Espaa est valorando el anteproyecto para contribuir, en la fase de audiencia pblica, con sus comentarios y sugerencias basados en su larga experiencia en resolucin de reclamaciones en el sector bancario. En todo caso, para el Banco de Espaa es fundamental la necesaria colaboracin que debe existir entre la nueva autoridad y los supervisores financieros, intercambiando la informacin relacionada con los conflictos individuales, por la especial trascendencia que, como he sealado, tiene para el ejercicio de sus funciones supervisoras y regulatorias. Dicha coordinacin es necesaria, adems, porque el sistema institucional de proteccin al cliente se basa en el adecuado funcionamiento de los servicios de atencin al cliente de cada entidad, funcionamiento que se encuentra sujeto a la supervisin de las autoridades financieras. Por ltimo, y ya termino, estoy segura de que esta nueva autoridad nace para dar continuidad a la labor realizada por el Banco de Espaa, desde hace casi 35 aos, incorporando nuevas herramientas para la consecucin de los objetivos de eficiencia y servicio pblico que han guiado, desde su creacin, la actividad del servicio de reclamaciones del Banco de Espaa.

Title: III SANFI Alumni Meeting. "European funds and Spain's recovery after the pandemic"
text: 03.03.2022 European funds and Spains post-pandemic economic recovery* III SANFI Alumni Meeting Margarita Delgado Deputy Governor *English translation of the original speech in Spanish. Good afternoon. First of all, I would like to thank SANFI Alumni for their kind invitation to inaugurate this meeting, where we will have the pleasure of witnessing a debate between these highly respected participants in a few minutes. Naturally, I would like to take this opportunity to publicly congratulate, as I did in private several days ago, the facilitator of this debate, Alejandra Kindelan, on the announcement of her forthcoming appointment as Chairwoman of the AEB. To begin with, let me point out that we are at present subject to the quiet period that precedes monetary policy meetings of the ECB Governing Council. This means that I cannot refer to subjects that may anticipate future monetary policy decisions. Therefore, my thoughts should not be interpreted as insight into the monetary or economic outlook that might shape expectations regarding these decisions. Accordingly, in my speech today I will not touch on certain topical issues that it would otherwise be important to address. It is a pleasure and an honour to have the opportunity to participate for the second time in a row (although not the second consecutive year due to the pandemic) in the SANFI Alumni meeting. This meeting is an ideal forum to reflect on the economic future of Spain. Against this backdrop, I can think of no timelier subject than that which the organisers have chosen for discussion today. This event takes place as Spain, after two long years, is finally emerging from this prolonged period which has been so painful in terms of loss of income, of economic activity and, above all, of human lives. With all the due caution that the unfolding of the pandemic has taught us to exercise, this may well be the beginning of the end of the health crisis. We will always be confronted with new, and sometimes severe, shocks, as last weeks invasion of Ukraine by Russia reminded us. But, precisely because we will never be immune from such shocks, we must be as prepared as possible to respond to them. This means we need to make the best possible use of the economic policy instruments at our disposal. This will allow us to strengthen the recovery in activity we are currently in the midst of, while promoting a structural transformation of the economy that will enable Spain to emerge from this crisis with higher levels of well-being for all. To achieve these ambitious goals, we now have a new tool that was not available to us in previous crises: the Next Generation EU (NGEU) European funds. This programme has a major role to play not only in the post-pandemic economic recovery of Spain and the other European economies, but, above all, in the structural transformation of the Old Continent. That said, it is very important that we understand that all these benefits will not be obtained automatically, but as a consequence of the proper use of these funds. 1 The genesis of the programme lies in the acknowledgement of the fact that this crisis has been exogenous and has affected the different EU countries asymmetrically depending on their sectoral structure. Thus, economic developments have been more unfavourable in countries with a greater exposure to the productive sectors most affected by the pandemic containment measures, such as those related to tourism, food service activities, cultural activities and leisure in general. In designing the NGEU, these asymmetrical effects have been rightly taken into account. The distribution of funds among the individual Member States has been determined according to the impact of the crisis on variables such as unemployment or income in each country, thus including an element of cross-country solidarity. These funds will be implemented mainly through the Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF), complemented by other additional instruments, including most notably the REACT-EU initiative. The RRF allocates 70 billion to Spain in grants, which the Spanish Government has requested through the Recovery, Transformation and Resilience Plan (RTRP), and another 70 billion approximately in loans (to which the authorities have not yet resorted for the time being). It should be recalled that the NGEU is being developed in parallel to the usual programmes within the Multiannual Financial Framework, such as the cohesion or rural development funds. As I already mentioned, given their envelope and the design of their main action lines, NGEU funds are to fulfil a dual purpose: to help repair in the short term the damage caused by the crisis and to bring about structural transformation. This is a unique opportunity for Spain, but significant challenges lie ahead. 1 The REACT-EU amount is in addition to these amounts. 2 As regards the first of these two objectives (the use of NGEU funds as a mechanism to cement the recovery), the main challenge is synchronising the implementation of these funds in the real economy and cyclical needs. The ability to absorb and manage NGEU funds is a huge challenge due to three factors: (i) its sheer size; (ii) evidence on the use of other European funds in the past; and (iii) their simultaneity with the EUs regular programmes. The volume of funds provided by NGEU is unprecedented. It is comparable to the total amount of structural funds that Spain has received in the past three decades (see left-hand chart). In the event that Spanish authorities decide to apply for the full amount available in the form of both grants and loans, we would be talking about a stimulus of close to 12% of GDP spread over six years. Managing these amounts, which includes project design, ex ante evaluation and an ex post evaluation mechanism to ensure accountability, is a challenge for the designated public organisations, which will probably even have to be adapted accordingly. Additionally, one aspect that may help NGEU be used as a macroeconomic stabilisation tool is the fact that European fund revenues and disbursements are deficit-neutral in national accounts. Therefore, the use of the programme is not affected by the foreseeable reinstatement next year of the fiscal rule framework under the Stability and Growth Pact, after appropriate modifications. This is another reason why the projects undertaken using the programmes funds should materialise in public investments that avoid as far as possible generating recurrent expenses in the future. Rather, they should broaden the economys productive capacity and, therefore, the tax base. 3 These considerations highlight the even greater importance of the second objective of the programme: to drive the structural transformation of the Spanish economy in the medium and long term. The significance of this objective is underlined by the considerable challenges posed by the growing digitalisation of activity, the green transition and population ageing, among other dynamics. These challenges are largely common to all of our European peers. However, their scale is greater in Spain given the composition of government expenditure in this country: as compared with our fellow European countries, we invest less in items that have a critical impact on the accumulation of physical and human capital in the economy and, therefore, on productivity. Specifically, in 2019 public expenditure on education and public investment stood at 4% and 2.1% of GDP, respectively, 0.9 pp and 1.5 pp less than in the EU. The build-up of this negative gap over the years is generating a physical and human capital deficit that should be corrected, even if only partially, using the NGEU funds. This would help the Spanish economy to contend with the structural changes already under way from a position of greater resilience. However, the main challenge that we face in this respect relates to the selection and specific design of those projects that will help to transform the economys productive system and optimise potential output. In turn, this objective can only be met if that project selection and design process is transparent and grounded on ongoing assessment in real time. This would allow any deviations from the established goals to be corrected. In addition, the process should be completed with a rigorous ex post assessment, endorsed by independent bodies, to identify those initiatives that have come closest to meeting their goals. In my view, there are three relevant factors that can help to maximise the benefits of the NGEU programme: (i) the need to accompany the budgetary stimuli with structural reforms; (ii) the importance of selecting projects that harness synergies between public and private investment; and (iii) capitalising on the opportunity that these funds offer to cover a portion of the substantial investment requirements aimed at mitigating the adverse impacts of climate change. 4 As regards the first of these three factors, I would like to emphasise the potential that a broad range of structural reforms would have in terms of optimising the transformative capacity of the NGEU funds. At present, aspects of our institutional framework may stymie the reallocation of resources between firms and sectors. A recent study by the Banco de Espana pointed to very strong complementarity between (i) structural reforms geared towards reducing the rigidities in the labour market and the barriers to competition and (ii) NGEU-related spending programmes. In other words, the medium and long-term expansionary effect of the European funds will be substantially amplified if they come alongside policies that reduce the inefficiencies in those markets (see right-hand chart). Turning to the second of the factors, the extent to which the use of the NGEU funds is successful in expanding the economys productive capacity will largely depend on how effective it is in mobilising private investment. The economic literature provides theoretical arguments and empirical evidence that, depending on the circumstances and the specific implementation, private and public investment can act both as complementary and substitutive forces. That said, under the Recovery, Transformation and Resilience Plan a substantial portion of government investment must be tied to private investment, evidencing a conscious decision to ensure ex ante the complementarity of the two types of spending. The specific instruments used to this end are known as Strategic Projects for Economic Recovery and Transformation. They are selected based on the identification of spaces where public investment, far from crowding out private initiatives, provides the incentives for these to prosper. The evidence available internationally indicates that the most successful industrial policies are those that complement private investment by upskilling workers and fostering the improvement and modernisation of the physical capital stock. The third and final factor that, in my view, could allow us to make optimal use of the NGEU funds is gearing a substantial portion of the investments towards meeting Spains ambitious medium and long-term climate targets, in line with those also adopted by the other EU members. The Climate Change and Energy Transition Law passed this year intends to mobilise more than 200 billion in investment over the course of this decade. A significant portion of that investment will have to be implemented by general government. Against this backdrop, the NGEU funds will play a central role in meeting the objectives of that law. However, it is important to acknowledge that government spending must be supplemented by fiscal measures. In 2019, environmental tax revenues (including taxes on energy, transportation, pollution and the extraction or use of natural resources) were appreciably lower in Spain than the EU average. This suggests that there is scope to gradually raise such taxes in the years ahead. Not only would this contribute to meeting the established climate goals, but, as a welcome side effect it would also further the necessary consolidation of public finances. 2 S. Albrizio and F. Geli (2021), An empirical analysis of the determinants that can boost Next Generation EUs effectiveness, Analytical Articles, Economic Bulletin 4/2021, Banco de Espana, 3 A. Terzi, A. Singh and M. Sherwood (2022), Industrial Policy for the 21st Century: Lessons from the Past, Discussion Paper 157, European Commission. 5 I should also mention a further aspect that underscores the importance of the NGEU programme, this time from a pan-European perspective rather than from a national standpoint. Beyond its contribution to shoring up the recovery in activity and to modernising the productive system of the various European economies, the launch of the NGEU programme could be the germ for a permanent macroeconomic stabiliser that goes a significant way towards cementing the European project. The benefits of such a mechanism in the future would be manifold. First, a centralised fiscal capacity would allow for greater risk-sharing among the different euro area economies. This would help to attenuate the impact on countries of idiosyncratic shocks stemming from exogenous factors. In addition, a macroeconomic stabiliser tool would help define the fiscal policy stance within the euro area, which would complement the monetary policy stance. Lastly, equipping this centralised fiscal capacity with the ability to issue debt would help to relieve the scarcity of euro-denominated safe assets. Financial institutions would thus have access to higher volumes of financial instruments eligible as collateral for monetary policy operations. All of which throws into sharper relief the importance of successfully implementing the projects under the NGEU programme, insofar as this can help to create the right environment in Europe for the eventual introduction of a permanent macroeconomic stabilising mechanism. Allow me to conclude by touching on the recent sad and troubling events. Russias invasion of Ukraine will affect the prices of energy and many other commodities. This, in turn, is bound to have repercussions for the income of firms and households alike, the extent of which remains to be seen. While we wait for confirmation of the specific effects on prices, wages, margins and economic growth, it appears more critical than ever to use the NGEU funds to maximum advantage. These funds will be critical to consolidating the economic recovery and, above all, to adapting our economy to the medium and long-term challenges, driving its competitiveness and smoothing the transition to more sustainable models. Sound use of the programme will ultimately further the overall and lasting well-being of our citizens. 6 Let us hope that the terrible conflict on Europes eastern border is resolved soon, without endangering any more human lives. Thank you. 7

text: BANK OF SPAIN Eurosystem 27.01.2022 Business Conference: "Strategic Sectors for the Economy Spanish" The Economist Margarita Delgado Deputy Governor Good morning everyone, Today we are attending this conference organized by elEconomista in which a frankly relevant current issue will be discussed: the economic future of Spain from a sectoral point of view. Before going into the subject, I would like to thank elEconomista, [in the persons of Amador G. Ayora, its director, and Gregorio Pena, its president] for inviting me to participate in this event, in which the choice of the topic of discussion could hardly be more appropriate. Perhaps the first issue that must be addressed in order to channel the debate is the definition of what we understand at the Bank of Spain by strategic sector. This is a very complex and controversial issue for which, unfortunately, there is no single approach. I believe that it is appropriate, therefore, that this intervention begins by delimiting the perimeter of what we could understand as a strategic sector. The criteria for deciding the degree of relevance of a branch of activity can be multiple and interconnected. These criteria can be economic, geopolitical, social cohesion  who could deny the strategic nature of education or health?, territorial cohesion or otherwise. In this intervention I am going to focus on the purely economic ones, although I will provide some brushstrokes on the geopolitical criteria, insofar as they can interact with the economic ones. We are all aware that, from a geopolitical point of view, substantial changes have been taking place in recent years that are altering the rules of the game in the global economy. As can be seen in this slide, the economic elements we use to define a sector as strategic are productivity, resilience and centrality. Productivity is a multidimensional concept in which we include the innovative capacity of a branch of activity, human capital as an essential element in the production and assimilation of new ideas and, finally, the potential for the reallocation of resources. Resilience is a concept that also has several dimensions and is related to the ability of a sector to withstand the impact of shocks and recover quickly from such impact. In this case, I believe that the three main changes to which our economy is subject are digitalisation, climate change and the ageing of the population. Finally, centrality refers to the importance of a sector for its interactions with others and for its contribution to the value chain, as well as for its importance in the economy as a whole both in terms of employment and in terms of the number of companies or weight in exports. Let's briefly develop each of these elements. First, for a sector to be considered strategic, it must have a high potential to contribute to aggregate productivity growth. This is crucial because we know that productivity is the variable that determines sustained long-term growth and the level of social welfare. I would like to emphasise that in a low-growth economy there are more obstacles to economic policy being able to undertake structural reforms that lead to a better redistribution of wealth. In this scenario, it is more difficult to have the necessary resources to strengthen social safety nets and to cushion the impact of these reforms on the affected groups. I think we can agree that without reforms there would be lower growth in per capita income in the future. A vicious circle can therefore arise that is difficult to break, in which low productivity growth makes reforms less likely and the lack of reforms, in turn, leads to lower productivity dynamism. Therefore, it does not seem controversial to say that achieving a more dynamic behavior in productivity is one of the most important challenges for the Spanish economy. Even more so because it has exhibited very modest growth in the last three decades, as we can see in the graph. From a sectoral perspective, this low dynamism is explained both by the greater weight of the branches of activity with lower productivity growth and by the lower productivity compared to other countries in practically all sectors. Herein lies one of the main problems of the Spanish economy. This conclusion can also be extrapolated if we compare it with other major European economies. Secondly, as I have mentioned, the strategic nature of a sector must be determined by its contribution to the resilience capacity1 of the economy in the face of shocks of different kinds. Particularly, in the face of the main ongoing structural challenges, such as the process of technological change  especially that associated with digitalisation  population ageing and climate change.  We can understand the concept of resilience as the ability of the economic system to, on the one hand, resist the impact of shocks (static resilience) and, on the other hand, recover quickly after them (dynamic resilience). Some sectors occupy a privileged position within the productive structure due to very different reasons. These may include, for example, the use of the country's comparative advantages  broadly understood, not only in terms of labour or capital endowments, but also in terms of natural resources, geographical position, ... etc.. An obvious example would be the tourism sector. But, in addition, the strategic nature of a sector may be due to the fact that its activity generates relevant externalities for the rest of the economy or its ability to provide essential infrastructures or inputs to companies in other branches. For this reason, two examples of sectors of high economic centrality are the branches of electricity supply and financial services. Let me highlight two important issues related to centrality. Firstly, factors unrelated to those I have just mentioned, such as mere historical inertia or the exploitation of various distortions, should not qualify a sector as central because it exhibits a high weight in the economy in terms of employment, number of companies or production. Second, the centrality of a sector is not static, as both comparative advantages and inputs or essential infrastructures evolve over time. A few decades ago, mobile phone or 5G networks didn't even exist. Today it is unthinkable not to consider them as essential infrastructures. Climate and the sun have been and are a source of comparative advantage, but within a few decades climate change could erode this source of competitiveness. It is obvious that the existing uncertainty in this regard is enormous, but it does not seem that we can rule out, today, an adverse scenario with a future of severe droughts, desertification or rising sea levels. At the Bank of Spain we have recently been working on the classification of the different sectors of activity according to their relative positioning according to these three dimensions that I have just described: productivity, resilience and centrality. To this end, we have built a taxonomy of the branches of activity by combining a wide range of indicators that capture different elements of the aforementioned dimensions. I would like to highlight two main messages from this work. The first is that the sectors best classified to contribute to productivity growth and resilience are those that, at present, have low centrality and low relative weight in the Spanish economy. As we can see in the slide, the professional activities sector and the information and communication sectors have low centrality. To this we add that unproductive sectors such as hospitality, commerce, construction, extractive industries or real estate have great centrality in our economy. The second message is that, in terms of some of the most advanced countries, many of the sectors with the best relative position in terms of productivity and resilience have a lower weight in the Spanish economy than that observed in these countries. The sectors to which I refer are the aforementioned services of professional, scientific and technical activities; information and communications; or the manufacture of computer and electronic products. These results are certainly thought-provoking. So far we have not taken into account geopolitical factors, but would this scenario change in any way with its inclusion? GEOPOLITICAL ASPECTS Kj Orp & Orp & BANK OF SPAIN BANK OF SPAIN In recent times, the debate has grown on the strategic nature of certain branches of activity from a geopolitical point of view. Some countries have put on the table measures that could lead to a tightening of restrictions on the free movement of products, investments and ideas, with a potentially detrimental effect on global welfare. Perhaps one of the most relevant geopolitical risks emanates from the growing rivalry between the United States and China, given their ability to alter the rules of the game on a global scale. These two powers have drawn up plans to identify those sectors that are considered a priority for their economies. These coincide precisely with those that in our analysis we have identified as best positioned in the categories of productivity and resilience. Unfortunately, these sectors are not, in general, the ones that, in Spain, have a greater relative weight both compared to the rest of the branches and compared to the most advanced countries. And at the European level, what do we think about geopolitical risks? The European response to these challenges has been the introduction of Open Strategic Autonomy. This is a framework for coordinating a broad set of policies to boost the EU's external projection and strengthen its economic and financial resilience. Among these actions, special attention is paid to the industrial policy strategy, which was revised in May 2021 to incorporate the lessons learned during the Covid-19 crisis. The overall objective is to ensure that EU industry can lead the way in the transition to a green, digital and resilient economy . Both the Covid-19 crisis and the bottlenecks in global supply chains and frictions between China and the US have highlighted the importance of addressing the EU's strategic dependence on areas such as critical raw materials  such as rare earths or silicon  batteries, some active pharmaceutical ingredients, hydrogen, semiconductors and cloud computing technologies  which are key to the deployment of 5G. artificial intelligence or the Internet of Things. I do not think I need to repeat that our relative position  and that of most of our European partners  in most of these areas is room for improvement. Hence, it is essential to make the most of the opportunity that the Next Generation EU program gives us. It is an economic policy lever with a high transformative potential in the design of which all these considerations have been taken into account. Not surprisingly, more than half of the funds (57%) must be allocated to digital transformation and the ecological transition, which, as I mentioned, are the two essential factors behind the design of the European industrial policy strategy. Allow me to conclude this speech by recalling that all these sectoral policies must be accompanied, in order to strengthen their economic and social impact, by more horizontal measures. By this I mean those that improve the overall economic environment for all sectors and companies at once. The catalogue of reforms that the Bank of Spain has been defending is widely known, so I will not dwell on detailing it. However, I would like to stress the need to pay special attention to those measures that favour the reallocation of productive factors between the different branches of activity, since the future sectoral composition of the Spanish economy is shaping up to be different from the one we are currently experiencing. New actors, different ways of relating to customers, unprecedented technologies and a less stable and predictable environment are essential elements that will shape the sectoral scenario of the future. And let us not forget that in order to ensure the success of this process of sectoral restructuring, it will also be necessary to assess where existing social safety nets need to be strengthened. These processes often entail transition costs that are concentrated in certain groups and perhaps in certain geographical areas. In conclusion, the sectors best positioned to face the challenges of productivity and resilience have a relatively small weight in our economy, even more so if we compare ourselves with other economies around us. In addition, sectors that are more central have low productivity, such as hospitality, or are vulnerable to the new scenarios we are facing, such as the energy sector in the face of climate change. Therefore, we are at a crossroads that requires us to adopt transcendental strategic decisions in order to position ourselves properly in this new global environment. We need to pay attention to reallocation between sectors, which is undoubtedly a complex process as well as necessary if we want to improve the ability of our economy to adapt to new scenarios. Policymakers, business associations and institutions must be prepared to meet these new challenges and those that lie ahead in order to achieve sustained, sustainable and inclusive economic growth. Thank you very much for your attention. BANK C SPAIN For different reasons, it is expected that these challenges will have a very heterogeneous impact among the different productive branches. For example, the degree of exposure to potentially disruptive technologies such as artificial intelligence is not the same in, say, agriculture as it is in the financial sector. But I would like to emphasize that both can and should benefit from this kind of knowledge. An illustrative example applied to agriculture is the development of intelligent irrigation or fertilization tools, or the use of robotic machinery to harvest on a large scale with greater precision and speed2. And there is nothing better than the information services branch itself to illustrate the transformative power of digitalisation. It could be said that the business model of the written press hardly underwent any major changes during the nineteenth and twentieth centuries3. On the contrary, in the last 20 years it has had to adapt at breakneck speed to the changes demanded by the digitalisation of society. As an example, a button: our host today, elEconomista, was born 16 years ago both in print and on the internet as a way of facing the transformations that were already underway at the time. Nor would the impact of the physical risks associated with climate change be similar in all sectors. For example, the impact on the tourism sector or on the construction of infrastructure would be much greater than that experienced by the chemical industry. And if we look at the changes in consumer preferences motivated both by the aforementioned climate change and by the process of population ageing, we can expect greater alterations in demand for branches such as residential construction or vehicle manufacturing than in branches such as water collection, purification and distribution activities. En primer lugar, factores ajenos a los que acabo de mencionar, como la mera inercia histrica o el aprovechamiento de diversas distorsiones, no deberan cualificar a un sector como central por el hecho de exhibir un elevado peso en la economa en trminos de empleo, nmero de empresas o produccin. En segundo lugar, el carcter central de un sector no es algo esttico, ya que tanto las ventajas comparativas como los inputs o las infraestructuras esenciales evolucionan con el tiempo. Hace unas dcadas, las redes de telefona mvil o de 5G ni siquiera existan. Hoy es impensable no considerarlas como infraestructuras esenciales. El clima y el sol han sido y son una fuente de ventaja comparativa, pero dentro de unas dcadas el cambio climtico podra erosionar esta fuente de competitividad. Es obvio que la incertidumbre existente al 5 respecto es enorme, pero no parece que podamos descartar, a da de hoy, un escenario adverso con un futuro de sequas severas, desertificacin o aumento del nivel del mar. En el Banco de Espaa hemos estado trabajando recientemente en la clasificacin de los distintos sectores de actividad segn su posicionamiento relativo de acuerdo con estas tres dimensiones que acabo de describir: productividad, resiliencia y centralidad4. Para ello hemos construido una taxonoma de las ramas de actividad combinando una amplia batera de indicadores que captan distintos elementos de las mencionadas dimensiones. Me gustara destacar dos mensajes principales de este trabajo. El primero es que los sectores mejor clasificados para contribuir al crecimiento de la productividad y a la capacidad de resiliencia son los que, a da de hoy, presentan baja centralidad y peso relativo bajo en la economa espaola. Como vemos en la diapositiva, el sector de actividades profesionales y los de informacin y comunicacin poseen baja centralidad. A esto aadimos que sectores poco productivos como hostelera, comercio, construccin, industrias extractivas o sector inmobiliario poseen gran centralidad en nuestra economa. El segundo mensaje es que, en trminos comparados con algunos de los pases ms avanzados, buena parte de los sectores con mejor posicin relativa en trminos de productividad y resiliencia tienen en la economa espaola un peso inferior al observado en dichos pases. Los sectores a los que me refiero son los mencionados servicios de actividades profesionales, cientficas y tcnicas; informacin y comunicaciones; o la fabricacin de productos informticos y electrnicos. Estos resultados, sin duda, invitan a la reflexin. Hasta ahora no hemos tenido en cuenta los factores geopolticos, pero cambiara en algo este panorama con su inclusin? ASPECTOS GEOPOLTICOS kJ Orp & BANCO DE ESPAA BANCO DE ESPAA 4 Fernndez y Montero (2021): Un anlisis sectorial de los retos futuros de la economa espaola. DO no. 2133, Banco de Espaa. 6 En tiempos recientes ha crecido el debate sobre el carcter estratgico de ciertas ramas de actividad desde el punto de vista geopoltico. Algunos pases han puesto sobre la mesa medidas que podran desembocar en un endurecimiento de las limitaciones a la libre circulacin de productos, inversiones e deas, con un efecto potencialmente perjudicial sobre el bienestar global. Quiz uno de los riesgos geopolticos ms relevantes emane de la creciente rivalidad entre Estados Unidos y China, dada su capacidad para alterar las reglas del juego a escala global. Estas dos potencias han elaborado planes para identificar aquellos sectores que se consideran prioritarios para sus economas. Estos coinciden precisamente con aquellos que en nuestro anlisis hemos identificado como mejor posicionados en las categoras de productividad y de resiliencia. Desafortunadamente, estos sectores, no son, en general, los que, en Espaa, presentan un mayor peso relativo tanto frente al resto de ramas como frente a los pases ms avanzados. Y a escala europea, qu pensamos de los riesgos de ndole geopoltica? Pues la respuesta europea a estos retos ha sido la introduccin de la Autonoma Estratgica Abierta5. Este es un marco de coordinacin de un conjunto amplio de polticas para impulsar la proyeccin exterior de la UE y reforzar su resiliencia econmica y financiera. Entre estas actuaciones, se presta una atencin especial a la estrategia de poltica industrial, que se revis en mayo de 2021 para incorporar las lecciones aprendidas durante la crisis del Covid-19. El objetivo general persigue garantizar que la industria de la UE pueda liderar el camino en la transicin hacia una economa verde, digital y resiliente. Tanto la crisis del Covid-19 como los cuellos de botella en las cadenas globales de suministro y las fricciones entre China y EEUU han puesto de relieve la importancia de abordar la dependencia estratgica de la UE en reas como materias primas crticas  como tierras raras o silicio, bateras, algunos principios activos farmacuticos, hidrgeno, semiconductores y tecnologas de computacin en la nube que son claves para el despliegue del 5G, la inteligencia artificial o el internet de las cosas6. Creo que no hace falta que repita que nuestra posicin relativa y la de la mayor parte de nuestros socios europeos en la mayora de estas reas es susceptible de mejora. De ah que sea fundamental aprovechar al mximo la oportunidad que nos otorga el programa Next Generation EU. Es una palanca de poltica econmica con un elevado potencial transformador en cuyo diseo se han tenido en cuenta todas estas consideraciones. No en vano, ms de la mitad de los fondos (un 57 %) se debe destinar a la transformacin digital y a la transicin ecolgica que, como mencionaba, son los dos factores esenciales detrs del diseo de la estrategia de poltica industrial europea. Permtanme ir concluyendo este discurso recordando que todas estas polticas de carcter sectorial deben venir acompaadas, para reforzar su impacto econmico y social, de medidas de corte ms horizontal. Con esto me refiero a aquellas que mejoran el entorno econmico general para todos los sectores y empresas a la vez. 5 LHotellerie-Fallois, Manrique y Millaruelo (2021): La Autonoma Estratgica Abierta de la UE. Sin embargo, s que me gustara incidir en la necesidad de prestar atencin especial a aquellas medidas que favorezcan la reasignacin de factores productivos entre las distintas ramas de actividad, puesto que la futura composicin sectorial de la economa espaola se perfila diferente de la que vivimos en la actualidad. Nuevos actores, distintas formas de relacionarse con los clientes, tecnologas inditas y un entorno menos estable y predecible son elementos esenciales que conformarn el escenario sectorial del futuro. Y no olvidemos que para asegurar el xito de este proceso de reestructuracin sectorial tambin ser necesario valorar en qu aspectos hay que reforzar las redes de proteccin social existentes. Estos procesos suelen conllevar costes de transicin que se concentran en determinados colectivos y quiz en determinadas reas geogrficas. En conclusin, los sectores mejor posicionados para afrontar los retos de la productividad y resiliencia tienen un peso relativamente reducido en nuestra economa, ms an si nos comparamos con otras economas de nuestro entorno. Adems, los sectores que presentan una mayor centralidad tienen una baja productividad, como la hostelera o son vulnerables ante los nuevos escenarios que afrontamos, como lo es el sector energtico frente al cambio climtico. Por lo tanto, nos encontramos en una encrucijada que exige adoptar decisiones estratgicas trascendentales para posicionarse adecuadamente en este nuevo entorno global. Necesitamos prestar atencin a la reasignacin entre sectores, lo cual es sin duda un proceso complejo a la vez que necesario si queremos mejorar la capacidad de adaptacin de nuestra economa a los nuevos escenarios. Las autoridades econmicas, las asociaciones empresariales y las instituciones debemos estar preparados para afrontar estos nuevos retos y los que estn por llegar con el fin de lograr un crecimiento econmico sostenido, sostenible e inclusivo.
